title: Big Bus London Hop-On Hop-Off Tour and River Cruise
description: Create your own personalized sightseeing itinerary with a Big Bus hop-on hop-off sightseeing pass, the perfect choice for independent travelers. No matter how long you have in London, a 1-, 2-, or 3-day pass allows you to explore at your own pace. Tick off all of London’s landmarks and see the city from a different perspective on an included Thames River cruise. Upgrade to the fast-track London Eye option to get an aerial view of the city aboard the London Eye giant observation wheel.

reviews.usertext:
We have done other hop on hop off (HOHO)bus tours in other cities and always found it a great way to get a general overview of the city and an easy way to get back to sites we want to see. The bus stops were frequent, well signed and most had an employee to help out. The app showing the next bus coming your way was good too. You get packaged ear phones to listen to the audio , you take them with you for the next bus. The audio was surprisingly good for pre recorded. Unfortunately the bus didn’t follow the route on any of the 3 days and we never got to do the blue route or stops 3-10. The stops are numbered on the paper map, app and the actual stops but the bus didn’t announce the stop number The bus was forced to change route once because of traffic, another time it was an accident and the third day they just didn’t follow the route and gave us no explanation. We got off the bus and took the subway to Baker Street because we were told that the buses weren’t running there that day. While having lunch we saw a bus and were able to take it back to the stop closest to the hotel. We were disappointed that the bus didn’t follow the route and that we missed over half if the sites we planned to see. Our tickets also included an evening tour which we never got to do and a river cruise which apparently only runs on the weekend ( fri-sun) and we were there Mon-Wed.
If I were to recommend anything it would be a bus tour that takes you to all the sites, not a HOHO Then use the underground system to get to the places where you want to stop and see. I’m assuming that a bus tour would make all its tourist spots regardless of traffic etc. This HOHO tour could improve by announcing the stop numbers as well as what is near by. Keep people appraised if a detour is required, we were confused on the bus when our gps was saying we were going one way but the bus map said we were supposed to be going somewhere else.

We were fortunate to have Big Steve provide live commentary for our tour. We have taken other open top bus tours in various cities and the speakers, recordings, and whether the bus stops for you to get a good view makes a big difference in the experience. We stayed on the bus for about two hours and saw many of the London architectural highlights. Steve also pointed out places he recommended for a longer visit, museums and other venues to visit inexpensively and stretch the budget, and had a great supply of "dad jokes." Steve and the driver worked very well together to make sure you could line up a great shot.

Later the same day, we were on a Big Bus with only the recorded commentary and there was no comparison.

This is the best way to see a lot of London. The recorded tour commentary was far more hokie than informative, but the ability to get off the bus and experience anything you'd like is what makes this tour bus so amazing. It really is the best experience you can have to get all over the city and see whatever you like on an open-air bus. The reduced pricing for 2 or 3-day tickets is a big perk and with three full routes, it really is a great bus tour for groups on solo.

In two words... don't bother. Generally we have found that a hop-on / hope off bus is an excellent way to either explore a city or a cost effective way to get to popular areas of a city. No company like this can control traffic congestion, however they can be honest about the amount of time a route takes. This company offers a full range of activities knowing that you may never actually be able to complete even a full circuit in a day due to the congestion in Central London. Our experience was over 90 minutes to travel 4 of 26 planned stops, despite being told the full route was just over 2 hours. Undaunted, we tried the 2nd route the next day, having purchased a 2 day pass. Once again, we made it about 4 stops in 90 minutes. The more disturbing thing was the driver continuing to add people to the bus until the seating and standing limit had been vastly exceeded. There were people standing on the stairs and in the restricted area next to the driver. We finally left after sitting in traffic for 30 more minutes. A complete and total waste of money.

The wait between each bus can be up to 1/2 hour. A very inefficient way to spend your time while touring a city. The tickets were not cheap and it would have been cheaper for a family of 5 to just take a cab to the few places we visited.
Unlike the other hop on and off bus tours we’ve done, this one gave very little historical and interesting facts. Instead, if you choose to plug into their system, it plays annoying music such as Prince 1999 which has no relation to London and annoying jokes. 1/2 of the time I had no idea what they were taking about and really wished that they would have pointed out cool aspects of the city.

In Boston, for example, the bus driver was a local and spoke most of the time to give us various facts and stories about the city. We also never waited for more than 10 minutes.

Right now, we are sitting at Baker Street for the part 1/2 hour and still no bus. Please save yourself the money and time.

Saw a “rep” for the the bus tours at Westminster, he was holding the “red tour bus” map so figured he was the guy to ask about tickets. He was very insistent that we buy tickets for the next day as they sell out quickly and a seat on the bus cannot be guaranteed if we don’t purchase them beforehand. So I agreed….£39 EACH!!! He then gave us the tickets and different maps, maps for the big bus company tours. This guy scammed us, we thought we were getting the red city site seeing bus, but we weren’t it was a completely different company. Now I paid £39 because the city bus is £34 online….turns out that this company we went with tickets are £29 on the street and cheaper online. I know this because I asked another “rep” at a different location. The buses were not every 15-20mins more like every 40 mins. And were very very full people were turned away from them as there wasn’t space, so even though we bought our tickets a seat wasn’t guaranteed anyway. Pressurised into buying an overpriced ticket, lied to about which company it was for and then not getting a seat on a bus……

Such a shame this one guy at Westminster spoils it as the drivers are lovely. Please avoid him.

Unfortunately, our experience was not great. We ended up in a traffic jam for over an hour the first day and the second day we got off at Kensington Palace and when we returned to get on a bus it took an hour for one to show up. They kept blaming traffic however the Toot bus company had multiple buses go by in that same time frame. It seems as though they do not have enough buses/ drivers to accommodate travelers. We decided that we may have to take the city bus across the street after 45 minutes of waiting and in the process of that the bus showed up and we had to run back to catch it. The bus driver was the very rude because we said we had one more person on the way and he didn’t have time to wait. We told him how long we waited and said we couldn’t have if we weren’t at the stop. We explained why and he did wait but was vey rude. On top of that they kept stopping and letting people on the bus and you were shoulder to shoulder and couldn’t move. We barely made it to our river cruise on time. We were not the only customer having problems. I was hoping that this was isolated to London because we already had tickets purchased for France, but unfortunately it was not. In France the headphones didn’t work so you couldn’t listen to the history and when each stop was. They had us switch buses because of that. The problem was when we got off a stop for dinner we went back to catch the next bus and were told the buses stopped running at 5:45pm This caused us to miss our sunset cruise by the Eiffel Tower. Since returning home We have emailed the company and the response was we can’t do anything for you because the buses don’t always run on time. They also wouldn’t discuss the Paris tickets with me because of security issues even though I am the one who purchased the tickets. I would not recommend this company.

Overrated and overcrowded. The tour was a waste of money for our family of five. Traffic was so bad in London that the bus barely moved. We were never able to sit in the open air-second deck because they over sold the trips. The tour audio offered very little information. We used our tickets for and hour and a half before we gave up and never rode it again. We wasted two days worth of tickets and hundreds of dollars. Other bus services had the same number of buses around the city with room in the open air. Give them a try.

This was the worst hop on hop off tour we have ever done in the last thirty five or more years of travelling different European cities. The content of the audio on the red Route was very limited for each of the areas the bus passed and in fact for many lovely buildings passed there was no information at all. The content was about 80% music. The content was done between a male and female voice interacting with each other and and the speakers asking questions of the tourists on the bus, attempting to make it somewhat humorous. It flops miserably. I learnt so little about London in 2 and a half hours, our €84 could have been far better spent elsewhere on an educational tour of London. But we like doing the bus tours to get a decent flavour of a city initially and help us decide the spots we’d like to visit in more detail. For example as we passed through Belgravia we did learn about some of the the Rich and Famous who once lived there or still do but it took 5 minutes or more to tell us that as the audio content persons gave certain clues as to the Rich persons who lived there which the bus tourists were to answer. Ok we learned that Sean Connery, Andrew Lloyd Webber, Roman Abramovich bought properties there but that’s about it. Very little on the type of architecture the architects, the period built and some other facts of interest to tourists visiting London, an expensive city to visit anyhow. A really disappointing tour and I’d advise people who read this to spend their hard earned money on an alternative bus tours. This has been the worst value bus tour of our entire lives to date. What a shame to have to give a review like this for one of the Worlds Iconic Cities.

The tour was fine however, I asked for three adult tickets and a ticket vendor who had a Big Bus shirt on, sold me and charged me for 4 tickets. When we boarded the bus, the ticket taker noticed and told me to go back to the vendor who was across the street. The vendor apologized and said that it was his fault. However, he said that he could not refund the charge that his office would have to do it. He took my name and contact info and said I would be contacted that day. Long story short, no one contacted me and when I contacted them with all the info on the receipt, they said they would give me another ticket. I was already back in the states. They will not be sending a refund . They owe me $70. DO NOT use the BIG BUS Co. This is not to be confused with the Big RED Bus. I have been very pleased with them in the past.

Good tour - would recommend. Guide for the walking tours (Julia) was fantastic - just a pity that she couldn’t have been on the bus itself instead of the audio commentary, which we felt was disappointing. Could have provided a lot more information without all the jokes and long intermissions. Dropped a star for this; otherwise good value for money given the unlimited nature of hop on / hop off, 3 walking tours and river cruise. Recommend you get on the first bus of the day at the first stop (Green Park) to guarantee a good seat upstairs as it gets crowded quickly on a busy day. Plus you need a full day if you plan to do everything that’s included.

Great way to see London. We did the 2 day option. The first day we did the Red Line which is the line with the most stops, and the second day we did the Blue line. The stops are very convenient and we had very little wait time for the buses. You can download the app which shows you where the buses are in real time. The app was very helpful in navigating the city and I continued to use the map throughout my visit. The stops are well labeled for Big Bus tours and throughout the city there were Big Bus representatives at many of the major stops who provided direction and were great resources. The river cruise was excellent! After doing the 2 day tour I found it easier to navigate my way around London for the remainder of the trip. There are other hop on tour buses, but Big Bus seems to be the largest with the most buses and representatives. I would highly recommend them if you are thinking of doing a hop on /hop off bus. When I initially booked the London tour I did not realize I previously used them a few years ago while in Washington DC (realized it after I downloaded the app). The DC tour was excellent as well.

On a recent family trip to London, we purchased tickets for the Big Bus Hop-on Hop-off tour with river cruise and the Tower of London admission added. Based on prior experiences, this is the best way to get insights into the historic landmarks of London. The recorded commentary could be a bit more detailed, but within half a day, you can see all major attractions of London without having to walk a step. I highly recommend taking advantage of the complimentary river cruise, as it is offering a different perspective of London and comes with hilarious live commentary that will make you smile.

It went from bad to worse, I paid just over £100 for a family ticket, downloaded the app to find the bus stops, waited at the bus stop at the top of Regents Street for 30 minutes, no bus, checked the app to find all the bus's were on Piccadilly. We walked 20 minutes with 2 young children to find the bus. When we boarded the bus we were told the route had changed, which explained why the bus didn't go down Regents Street, none of this information was available on the website, very poor communication.

When the bus did eventually leave the commentary was less about the sights of London and more about what restaurants and bars we were passing, I'm sure the company is paid for this advertising. We passed many sights, statues and parks with no mention of what they are, at one point we were stationery in Trafalgar Square, no mention of Nelson Column or Admiralty Arch. We stayed on the bus for another half hour and got off.

We felt completely ripped off, I would have rather given a taxi driver £100 and asked him to driver us round London for an hour.

I would seriously avoid this tour operator, there are many other around.

As a Londoner I wanted to learn more about my city and decided to do one of the Tourist Bus Tours. Unfortunately we chose BigBus Tours, never again. The tour was pointless and a total waste of money for 2 day £53 ticket as it was basically a oneway 2 & 1/2 drive around London in heavy traffic with a shocking bad audio tour. I only gave ot 1 star because of the sights but you may aswell buy a London TFL 1 day travelcard & get on a red bus as it was 95% music & silent pauses. I cannot believe the appalling lack of facts and history that this tour provides with lots of rubbish jokes about things like Jenners & Kardashions. I was purplexed that as we drove passing London's rich history, architecture & modern culture we had to listen to music. At one point the Bus drive down Regent street just after it talked about Hamleys toy store. As the audio was not in sync we were still 10 minutes off of Piccidilly circus on Regent Street & it starts talking very briefly about Piccidilly & the staute of Eros, then the recorded info stops and just plays music continually. So as we pass all through Picidilly/The Strand/Leceister Sq/the Lights at Piccidilly (one of the largest Big Screens in the world that only recently upgraded at a huge cost cost and has been constantly lit since the 2nd world war). But no nothing! Instead we had music all the way through Piccidilly and most of the way down to Trafalgar Square. We never bothered using the 2nd day of our pass as we didn't want to spend almost 90minutes travelling a 15minute walk or what we could do in a few tube stops. When we got on outside St Pauls we waited obout 45minutes for the bus (not every 15mins as it says). A massive queue built up behind us and as the bus finally moved on & carried on the tour but. Later I saw the bus hurtle past a lady at another bus stop who clearly had also been waiting a long time judging by the angry look on her face when it never stopped because it was full.
Would never recommend this tour. Save yourself about £40 by listening to your favoursite radio station as you google the facts & buy a London red bus travelcard.
The CityExperience River Cruise by the London BoatStaff were excellent (suggest you buy that ticket seperate). We learnt more in 5mins with them then the whole 2 & 1/2 hrs with BigBus Tour.

Would not recommend. Was double charged with no resolution in site. Tour was average. The lack of live narration really hurt the tour compared to others I've enjoyed.

More detail on the double charge: I initially bought a ticket online through the app, however, I was given an error message, and never received the tickets. Once on board, the ticket agent instructed me that I must buy the tickets again on board the bus and later I would be given a refund by chatting on the website. The on board tickets were more expensive than the online tickets, however, once I chatted with the bigbus representative, I was informed that it was not possible to have the more expensive tickets refunded because they had been used. Obviously, I found that to be unacceptable.

I've been told the issue has been escalated, but so far there has been no resolution, and this whole thing has been way more of a hassle than it should have been.

To summarize, it was an expensive tour, poor value, and the double charge has been a hassle that remains unresolved.

The bus was clean & took you to all the sites. Regular buses although sometimes we had to get off a bus, wait at the stop and get on another to continue the tour. The commentary let the tour down. It played a lot of music rather than telling you more about the history/sites you were passing. I found myself telling my American guest more about London than the tour did (and I’m not that familiar with London) as lots of information missed and music payed instead. I have done bus tours with much better information before. The cost of this is also not worth it as we could have used the tube/buses to see the sites we did. I only chose this tour so we could here the history & have sites pointed out easily.

Booked tickets not knowing there would be road closures due to the platinum jubilee. Noticed within five minutes of booking over half the stops would be closed all day and tried to cancel tickets due to same. Was told this was not a refundable issue as information was available on the website. The information is not available on the main page or when booking tickets. I only noticed when looked more into the stops to try to arrange getting off for a different reservation. Unable to refund or any discount. Charging full price for less than half of the stops on any other given day is ridiculous. Find a different company

Note: I had booked tours with this company before (e.g. Miami, also London) but I have never been as disappointed as this time.
We booked this tour because for some of us it was the first time in London. The tickets (1 day basic) are expensive; we paid about £37/person.
The tour started on time. In the past they had tour guides on the bus who would comment on the sights and tell stories about the city. I found this very entertaining and informative. However, no guide appeared, so I guess the company doesn't have those guides anymore. Instead there are pre-recorded audio commentaries. The style of these recordings (music, conversations etc.) is well done but in my opinion they could be more informative. While driving or being stuck in traffic (I know this can happen) the commentaries were always interrupted and stopped. Therefore we missed some of the information and after a while we were really annoyed and didn't want to listen anymore. Sometimes it felt like the commentaries didn't quite fit the location we were at or at least it was unclear, where the sight they were talking about was to be seen. Also due to the interruptions, the stops were not announced properly. We decided not to finish the tour (red route) and also did not go on the blue tour. It felt like we wasted time being on the bus.
Overall, the price is too high for what you get in the end. There are alternatives that are worth the money, more informative and more entertaining. No recording can replace a real guide. I really don't see how this price is justified. Best would be if I could get my money back. Next time I would rather choose a walking tour or try another company.

Booked this for some of our things to do in London.
We ran out of time to use the river cruise or the day time buses so cannot comment on that so I ended up spending loads on just an evening bus tour 🙈🙈 so the review is just on that element.
The evening tour starts at 6pm and the bus was waiting when we got there at 5-45
We chose to sit down stairs as it was so cold and rainy. Lots of rubbish on the floor so the bus could have been cleaner.
We were just putting our headphones in and were told that we were going to have a live tour instead (can’t remember the guys name but he was great, think the bus driver was called winston)
We really enjoyed it and it was one of our favourite
Parts of our trip we loved seeing lots of the London sights but without the achy feet and seeing it all lit up at night was really pretty.
Would recommend I just wish we had been able to use the other elements of our ticket 😔

We started our morning around 8:30 on the first bus from Gloucester Road, and rode on the top deck. The breeze up there was nice, but there was quite a bit of traffic and it was slow-going. My goal was to get to the Trafalgar Square stop by 10am so that we could do the walking tour. Since we got on 1.5 hours before that, I thought that would be plenty of time. By the time we got to the stop to switch over from the blue line to the red line, the bus was packed, and pretty much everyone got off to switch to the red. We were unable to go back to the top deck after switching, and it was warm on the bottom deck. The overall ride from Gloucester Road to Trafalgar Square felt like forever. We finally made it to the Trafalgar Square stop at 10:04am, and the walking tour had already left. We walked over to Trafalgar Square, and paid to use the restrooms there. Then we walked over to Buckingham Palace to see the changing of the guard at 11am. After this, we headed over to the Victoria tube stop and took it over to the Borough Market. After, we walked over to the river cruise from the Big Red bus, and took the ride over to Westminster from the Tower of London. This was probably the coolest part of our Big Red Bus experience, it wasn't spectacular but better than the misery of the bus that was to come. We arrived at Westminster which was right by Big Ben. So we took some photos with Big Ben and were ready to head back to the hotel, so we hoped back on the bus. The bus was packed, there was only room for us on the bottom. Nobody was getting off the bus, and it was miserable sitting in the heat of the bottom level. At one point we passed on of the competitor hop on hop off buses and it was empty, we wished we were on one of those buses. When we were near Victoria station, we decided we would just take the tube because we were absolutely miserable in this standing room only bus that was so hot. So we got off and it was such a relief to get out of the bus, we were covered in sweat. Then we took the tube back to our hotel, and thank goodness we did because we probably saved an hour of riding in the miserable crowded heat of the Big Red bus. I definitely do not recommend the Big Red Bus, I would recommend just taking the tube to see the sights, or look into the competitor hop on hop off. In retrospect I wish we had just used the tube.

I don't normally leave reviews and am writing this several days after the tour, so this isn't just another disappointed customer with unrealistic expectations sounding off. My family and I make a habit of using open top buses to help orientate ourselves in a new city, and have done so in several European capitals.
This offering from Big Bus London is easily the worst we have experienced by a long way and is an embarrassment to London's tourist industry.
The commentary in particular is a mixture of simplistic half sentences referring to a point of interest either coming up or just past but only rarely at a point when you can actually see it; poorly scripted pathetic attempts at humour delivered by third rate comedians, and mainly old music hits with a vague London connection.
The shame of it is this would be such an easy element of the attraction to improve - I am very aware that different customers will have different tastes in commentary - why not have more than one (eg one for adults, one for teenagers, one for younger kids); may be run it via an app with better geolocation than the bus seems to have. If anyone out there has a small team of developers to write an app like this (maybe they already exist?) you'd have a market.
My strong suggestion to any family of more than about three is to organise a private tour with a private guide - it will cost more, but should be more tailored to the ages and interests of everyone and you'd get so much more out of your precious time. Got kids under about 14? I beg you, don't bother.

I first did the tour about 7years ago and was really looking forward to it but felt really disappointed. I'm sure that last time we were given far more info on the sighs and it was more of a guided tour. This time it felt like we drove around a lot of pointless streets with virtually no info given. To be honest it felt like to were on more of a normal bus than a tour. I think it would be far better with a proper tour guide. We hadn't planned to do the river cruise that came free with the ticket but as we found ourselves close to tower bridge and wanting to get back towards westminster we jumped on and I'm really glad that we did. That brief 20min trip gave us more info that the 2+hour bus ride. The man from the boat was not an official tour guide but did it for fun and he was very funny and entertaining.
Best advice, don't bother with the bus tour, just do the river cruise instead.

I write a good amount of reviews and try to stay positive because I know what it is like to run a business and deal with a diverse population of customers. However I think the tourist traveling to London should be aware of a few things with this company.
1. If you book a ticket for any number of people other than one you need to book separate tickets for everyone because my experience was that the Bigbus person at the Paddington stop would not let any of our party travel at different times even though we all had the QR code that the company gave us when we booked ahead online. He refused to divide our ticket and we ended up having to buy two more tickets so we could jump on and off at different times. That was $150 US we didn’t need to spend … then they double charged me after promising a discount of 25% on the additional new tickets and then saying right after that they could only give 20%.

If you try to contact their customer service there is no published or accessible phone number so I texted them and to date. I response so I am turning over the charges to my bank - so don’t expect any assistance from the company

We were also told by another rep at padding to stop that the rep could have divided the ticket if he wanted to but it was up to him and he said no.

Then when I went to purchase the additional tickets on my phone the rep told me not to and that’s when he offered a 25% discount to which again two minutes later told me could only be 20% - if it wasn’t for the two other people who had the original 4 ticket pass I would have used another company’s hop on and off bus. There are several companies to choose from so I would highly highly suggest using another company. They all have the same types of buses and features - I travel a lot and I know it’s hard to please everyone but this company really does not support or value it’s customers

From the moment we got to our first stop on Gloucester Road the tone was set for our experience with BBT. We were greeted by a rude staff worker who was annoyed that we had all purchased our own tickets.
We got on the first bus of the day at stop 29 and at stop 4 we were rudely made to exit the bus. When I asked why, we were barked at rudely by the driver to say “I’m on a break”. Several passengers were left on the side of the road waiting on another blue bus for about 20 mins. This is not customer friendly, especially when trying to maximize your time in London. Traffic is completely understandable but rudeness is not.

Second point, the commentary on the bus is sad! You are left guessing what you’re looking at or the driver doesn’t coordinate the commentary with what you’re looking at. It leaves customers confused. Also, there is more music than anything. You will get NOTHING from this tour except a waste of your time.

The 4 of us rode the Big Bus on the Saturday before Queen Elizabeth’s funeral and the streets were packed. However, there was no information given to the fact that stops along Westminster could not be visited due to be being closed for vehicles.

The commentary was fun but too much fun. The mix between being informative and fun was poor. We spent too much time listening to jokes or music as we passed historical buildings and drove down streets.

The 4 of us were very disappointed and having used City’s Sightseeing Hop on Hop off tours many times we have no hesitation in recommending the latter.

As much as I hate to leave a bad review for any company in the current climate, I also hate wasting £62 (the cost of 2 tickets) on a 15 minute ride on the lower deck of a hot, sweaty and overcrowded bus.
We boarded the bus at Trafalgar Square and just finding the bus stop was an achievement in itself! Admittedly this was due in part to my poor sense of direction, but also due to a complete lack of signage.
When we (finally) found the bus stop after a lot of wasted time the bus was overcrowded and we were forced to stand up on the lower deck.
There was no limiting of numbers on the bus and no social distancing whatsoever. Ordinarily this wouldn’t be a problem for us but as things stand at the moment we decided it was safer (and quicker) to get off at the next stop and explore London on foot instead.
Such a shame as I’ve used Big Bus in many different cities and have never had this problem before. What an absolute waste of money!

Avoid! Very expensive for essentially a bus ride with free earphones. We chose to do a Hop On Hop Off bus tour as something to do in London whilst I am currently on crutches, however we ended up getting off quickly and going to a museum instead. The busses themselves were uncomfortable and the audio guide was through cheap, plug-in headphones. For the price you pay, there should be live tour guide on the bus - or at the very, very least an audio guide through speakers! The guide itself is unoriginal, simple with limited information, and childish - basically just annoying for anyone over the age of 12. The taxi driver we met later in the day taught us more about London in 2 minutes than this whole tour did! They also play music between episodes of information, which makes it difficult to talk to those around you about what you are seeing. The staff we did meet were lovely and helpful, but that was about it.

After walking through London for the last two days, I wanted to to relax on the Big Bus Tour. Well it wasn‘t relaxed at all..
I downloaded the App where I could the the planned routes, where the Busses are and where I am. Half of the time, the Busses weren‘t on theirs planned routes, sometimes this was announced via audioguide, sometime it wasn‘t.
Then at some point, the Bus on the red route was PACKED (maybe because it was a friday?), a lot of people - including me - were really stressed out. People had to stand in the aisle of the bus in the downstairs part of the bus. You couldn‘t see anything from there let slone plug in your headphones. Speaking of headphones: they were free and you could listen to the audioguide, which disappointed me as well. Most of the time there was music or unnecessairy chatter between three different characters instead of really interesting information. Sometimes when speaking, the voices were suddenly cut of..

The blue line was less packed but shorter and also there was less to see in my opinion.

But the staff members were actually really nice!

I would recommend you try another company, as their busses were mostly empty, as far as I could see.

One of my worst tourist experiences :-(

I’ve taken countless bus tours in cities all over the world because I travel for work. The commentary on this London Big Bus tour is almost an insult to intelligence. I still can’t believe the level of intrascendental comments that were chosen for this in such a majestic city like London with so much history. I wish I could have my money back. Silly comments constantly pointing out how many million pounds this and that costs and totally overlooking dozens of places we passed by, filling time with music and a conversation exchange that attempted to be “funny” in a kind of humor that not a single passenger received as such. In conclusion… discharges a disappointment!

The busses and the tour were pretty good. You go past a lot of essential need-to-see sites. The problem was the logistics. The busses don’t run every 5-10 minutes as we were told, so it seemed there was a lot of waiting every time we wanted to “hop on” after each “hop off”.

First we were told the busses run till 8 pm, but the reality is we had to be back to a certain point on the route by 6pm to switch from a “red” bus route to a “blue” bus by the beginning of the “last run” so we could get back to our hotel. Before we could do that, at the last stop before we thought we needed to switch, we were told they were changing drivers and there would be a 12 minute wait, which was more like 15 minutes. By then it was 6 pm and a number of folks expressed concern. The dispatcher at the stop advised us to go to “stop #4” where we could meet a “blue” bus there at 6:20. When we finally got there, there was no “blue” bus. One of the other drivers at that stop expressed anger at the company for putting us in that situation and said it was about corporate greed, and I’m not sure what that meant…. But he was able to finally get another bus to come for us “blue” route folks. That took roughly another half hour.

So this was unpleasant.

One other big gripe I have is that they gave us a map showing all the stops, and the stops were numbered on the map. However, those numbers are not on the signs at any of the designated stops nor are those stop numbers announced in the recordings on the bus. This is just plain stupid when you’re providing a service to tourists who are not familiar with the city or it’s landmarks.

I will say that the earphones and the recordings were entertaining and interesting.

Hence, I’m only giving this 3 stars. If I were going to do this again, I’d try one of the other hop on hop off companies (there are several).

Incredibly bad recorded commentary. Virtually no information. Full of stupid jokes between “Tammy” or “Taffy” or whatever her name was supposed to be and her fake friend. In between there was HORRIBLE music - if you could even hear what it was, it was so scratchy. Terrible audio quality! The buses all bunched up - 3 or 4 coming within a minute or two of each other. One bus stuffed full (standing room only) and the next almost empty. In fairness we didn’t have to wait long for an emptier bus. Some of the drivers were kind and helpful, and some others must have been having a very bad day. One of our buses on the “red” route started taking the “orange” route without announcing it and I got panicky because I thought we’d miss our reservation at an event on the Red Route. We ended up getting off and taking a taxi for 15 pounds - so I can’t say the bus saved us much money. I’ve been on similar tours in other cities, but the Big Bus in London can’t be compared because it’s just so awful, awful, awful!

The route was great and we were able to see all of the attractions from the bus, take some photos, and get off on stops, walk around, have lunch, and get back on. The boat tour was also really pleasant and nice on a hot day!

However, we checked the schedule and also did the web chat to confirm the time of the first stop of the day at Waterloo station. We were there at 8:25 since the first stop was 8:35. Right at 8:35 we watched the bus drive by without stopping! We had to wait another 20 minutes for the next bus.

In the afternoon the buses got VERY busy. They had staff at the stops telling people to line up, but then they just told everyone to quickly get on the bus and told the drivers to leave. The buses were already crowded and they put more people on the buses then there were seats. We watched a family walk up the stairs to the upper deck, carrying a stroller, just to see it was full, and then have to carry the stroller all the way back down. There weren't seats down there either and people were just standing in the aisles.

There was never any live narration and the pre-recorded narration wasn't great. Luckily our friend was local and she was able to point out a LOT of stuff that the pre-recorded stuff left out.

We didn’t find the but to be worth the money. We bought a 72 hour ticket. On our first day we used it for one short trip because it was raining and the only open seats were on the top level out in the rain. The second day we used it for maybe an hour. Because of all the closures, we weren’t able to use it to make it all the way to any of our desired stops. While that is partially not their fault, the way the bus loops are designed and the placement of their stops that were in use made it very inconvenient to make it anywhere in a reasonable amount of time. We still have the bus for one more day, but we have decided it isn’t worth the time to utilize it since it will take us hours to make it a distance that we could cover by walking in 15-30 minutes. We did not get to experience the night bus but I will say the river cruise was fantastic.

I purchased the Bigbus Premium package. It was mostly worth it as I had only 2 days to see London, and I used the hop on hop off feature to get around London. This was sometimes easier then finding a tube station. It was also more scenic.

The boat tour was great as I planned my day to work up the Thames from Big Ben to the Tower Bridge, and then took the one way cruise back to Big Ben.

I did the included Jack the Ripper tour, which was quite informative. Having an actual tour guide, Julie, was awesome. She added a lot to the walking tour, more then just the general facts about Jack the Ripper. It was definitely worth it, though bring your walking shoes! I really wished we had a live guide on the buses.

If you are using the bus to tour around the city, it would be much more valuable if you is a real tour guide on the bus providing commentary. The pre-recorded Audio does get old quickly, and having the music interludes kind of takes away from the experience.

Yeah give this a miss. The tour is your typical hop on and hop off. The routes are good and extensive. Yet all you really get is prerecorded crap that is not overly informative and leaves you guessing exactly what building or place they are referring to. Oh yeah you also get to see from the upper deck which has no roof which is not what you want when it’s raining. So when the sky does open up everyone and their mother gets back on board and crams the lower deck. When the rain stops there are no towels to dry the seats up top. The thing that we did enjoy was the short boat ride included up the Thames. They did a good job of being interesting. Get off at Tower of London north side of Thames. You need to ask them for your ticket before getting off.

I would save your money and just take the city buses. You just tap your credit card or Apple Pay when you get on and off and there is a limit of what they charge per day like 6 or 8 pounds. Hop on and hop off no worries. I didn’t try it but someone on the web even sells an app you can listen hopefully to more interesting stuff about London.

Anyway save your money this is not a premium tour.

We've enjoyed many hop-on hop-off buses on other cities like Barcelona and Paris, however BigBus in London was the worse by far.
We bought a premium ticket that included a river cruise return ticket and an evening tour. But when we got here it turned out that the river cruise return ticket was no longer included in the premium package.
Supposedly on the evening tour and both lines some buses include a live guide, but we never got one and the prerecorded commentary is uninformative and full of cringy humor. The buses also go much slower than expected and the were only 3 buses on the blue line, so good luck arriving on time to any of the attractions.
Download an audio tour and use the underground if you'd like to have a good experience and not waste money or time.

What a poor experience. We took this tour on the Sunday of the jubilee weekend. The route taken was not as advertised and a number of the generally very poorly sign-posted stops were closed. Inexplicable 10 minute stops in dirty dingy backstreets around Waterloo and other areas proved to be of no entertainment or interest. The driver seemed to be incapable or unwilling to explain delays and detours. A city that has a history of such diverse culture and rich tapestry of life deserves far better commentary than a recorded delivery aimed at the lowest common denominator. The only surprise was that the voice over did not contain canned laughter. How this company had the gall to charge full price just supports the commonly held belief about "rip off London".

We decided to take an open top bus tour around London to see the sights and got our tickets from a lovely gentleman outside of Victoria Station with a Big Bus. For £39, we were told buses ran every fifteen minutes and that we would get through at least half the tour before we would have to depart the tour to get to our evening show. This was not the case. Though it was not the fault of the bus that it was caught in traffic, we barely saw even a quarter of the tour. This is because we were instructed to swap buses as soon as we reached the next stop on the tour, and then repeated the same section of the tour we had just been on. We decided to try again the next day, and reached the busstop for 10am. Our bus, despite them starting tours at 9.30am, did not reach us until 10.50am. Whilst waiting, three other bus tour companies had passed us at least three time each before our bus arrived. By this time, we knew we would not be able to complete the full tour, but made plans to leave the tour at Tower Bridge to catch the ferry cruise down to Westminster pier. We then could no longer do this because the bus was late to the Tower pier, and we missed the ferry. We once again made a new plan to leave at the next stop, which was near Temple, to be able to catch the tube and get to our matinee show. The bus completely missed this stop despite us pressing the bell and it being on the tour, meaning we once again had to make a new travel plan and were once again almost late for our show. For the price of this tour, I absolutely expected more, and I expected the buses to be on time. Instead, we got late buses, with commentary that did not match where we were on the route and repeated itself three or four times.
Really not impressed.

Do not waste your money. This was shockingly awful! The pre-recorded commentary was cringeworthy and out of date. So much so that as we passed Westminster Abbey it referred to the most recent funeral of Princess Diana! During tourist spots the commentary was nothing more than slap and tickle awful dialogue, with music. We paid for the full tour - yet the drive missed 5 stops due to London traffic. We did not get the produce or service we paid for. They take your money, but don't deliver. After lengthy back and forth emails stipulating my complaints they absolutely refused to refund any money. I'm sure this is illegal - advertise a service, take your money then don't deliver! This is not only money you won't get back, but time.

Brilliant way to a great swathe of London's Tourist attractions in one go. It's gone up in price, the big thing I think is due to petrol costs, it's a bus that's constantly circulating the main hotspots in London. You can hop on and off at conveniently placed his stops, right outside the Tower of London, Buckingham Palace and many others trademark hotspots. You can even stay on all day if you like. The seats were really comfortable, the bus drivers are attentive and careful and it's a really pleasant experience. We got a lovely set of seats at the top with an open top roof. There is also a river cruise that was included with our ticket but we didn't have much time to actually go on that one.

I downloaded the BigBusTours app and we could pinpoint each stop and when the next bus would be arriving. We booked the two day ticket, including cruise, through Wowcher - we only used the voucher on the Saturday but it was worth the spend as took us across the city. Could have done with more visable BigBusTours staff though as I struggled to locate to redeem the voucher. The cruise was through City Cruises at Westminster Pier and the live commentary was utterly fabulous, a proper Londoner who knew how to engage an audience with the interesting facts about London, a tradition passed down by mariners over the years. The bus ticket all the boxes even if the prerecorded commentary was a little cheesy! Brilliant overall experience.

I thoroughly enjoyed my time on the Big Bus. For most of the journey my friend and I were the only ones on the bus since everything in London is a bit quiet these days. This was a blessing! It meant that we had the brilliant tour guide Tiffany all to oursleves. She was really engaging, and evidently passionate about the history of london from her infectious excitement. Tiffanys knowledge on central london was wide and she managed to answer most of the questions we asked about the buildings we passed by. She also knew all the spots to take the best photos! We got some amazing memories to keep and lots of fun trivia facts. I also recommend going on the bus at sunset time, that was beautiful especially when crossing the river Thames.

After explaining that we were time limited we were told the next bus would be a few minutes, after paying we waited 25 mins for a blue route bus. No-one explained that there were earphones available for the audio until after we got off! The route barely went near all the marked sights, you needed to get off and walk each time to see anything of any great interest. After sitting at stop 4 for almost 10mins we were all told to get off as the driver had finished his hours and another bus would be along in a few minutes. After another 10min wait we gave up and headed for the tube!
Buy a travel card and hop on & off tube & buses, it will be quicker and cheaper.

First, the pre-recorded narrative for the tour has been dumbed-down to the point that it is almost worthless. Second, when a demonstration in Parliament Square has been scheduled and advertised, one would assume that a bus would not need to sit still in a traffic jam for an hour. At one point, these bus tours were a good way to learn about a city and its history. This was a complete waste of money.

We took the Big Bus tour in Paris and it was great! London, is another story. There are many stops that are closed and those stops are not updated on their site. So, when we are at our hotel and I try to find the nearest site it has been impossible. Also, the driver in Paris stopped at every stop and gave time for passengers to disembark. You have to ring a bell in London and hope the driver hears the bell. It has not been a good experience so far and I would not recommend the tour in London. Also, the people in front of us just now had someone in a wheelchair and the driver told us we would all have to wait for the next bus.

Waited at the #34 stop on the Blue Line only to see on the app that the bus had made a detour. Neither the brochure map nor the app showed the new route. After waiting 20 minutes to see if the next bus would come our way we had to run 10 minutes to catch the bus at #35 stop.

Was terribly disappointed in the audio recording. Other cities have detailed audio guides with information about the history and landmarks. The Red Line tour that we switched to only shared brief information about the sites and then played music the rest of the time (mostly Queen with a little Rolling Stones and Beatles).

I wanted to learn about the great history of London and this tour did not fulfill that promise.

I purchased tickets for my wife and myself on an anniversary trip to London. Unfortunately, we came to the conclusion that due to the amount of traffic in London and the wasted hours sitting in traffic, it really does not pay to ride the Big Bus. We would much rather have taken the tube to our destination and spent the extra time walking to see the various sites. We did enjoy the River Cruise option, but could have just purchased that as a separate ticket. We had no issues with the buses or drivers. Buses were clean and the drivers were polite and competent. Our only real issue was the amount of time spent idling/crawling along in traffic.

STANDING ROOM ONLY - We just threw away over $100 for a family ticket on July 21st. We tried to get on one bus and it was packed, so the driver said to wait for the next bus. We waited about 15 minutes for the next bus to arrive and all the seats were taken, so we decided to get on and wait for people to exit at the next stop. Instead of people exiting, we had a rush of more people hopping on and the whole aisle was full of people (including us) crowded together like sardines and trying to hold on as we were standing. There were even people standing on the stairs leading to second level! We stayed on hoping for spots to open up, but no luck. It was getting so hot inside that we finally gave up and walked instead. This company must just keep selling tickets without worrying about their capacity to actually fit all those people on buses. I tried to find contact information to request a refund, but there was none provided. I will see if our credit card company can try to get this refunded. I highly recommend trying the other bus (red one that has decent reviews). We saw them pass by often and they always had space for more passengers.

Where do I start. I only had one day in London after spending two weeks in Scotland, so I thought doing this tour would be the best option to see the city in a day, as I have done several hop on hop off tours in other cities. This was a huge mistake. First, not one of the drivers I interacted with or witnessed interact with others were friendly or even just polite. Drivers were rude, acted like the riders were an annoyance. Secondly, there is so much traffic, you literally sit in bumper to bumper traffic throughout the entire tour, many people got off in frustration. I was told the traffic is normal. Due to the traffic, I never got off the red line and it took 5 hours to make the loop, you read that right. Additionally, our bus broke down mid way through and it was pouring rain. We were told we had to get off the bus and wait for the next one to arrive, rather then allowing us to wait in the bus. They also have everything pre-recorded and therefore you don't know what you are looking at or which building they are referring to. If you just want a ride around town and have the option to get off, then I would say book this tour, if you are genuinely looking for an experience and knowing what you are looking at, beware. I was so disappointed. Honestly, I could have allowed a bit more grace if only the drivers showed some personality or kindness.

Unfortunately this hop on/off bus tour was not up to par with others we have taken in other cities. We were on for over half an hour and had only gone three stops, most of that time was spent sitting at the bus stop. Tickets were being sold as people were getting on the bus from the driver which held everything up. We ended up getting off and not using it again because it was so inconvenient and slow. We ended up not being able to make it to one of our other tours so we lost those tickets (over $100!) because of the slow bus schedule. Additionally the person giving the audio portion of the tour was terrible, completely uninformative and unprofessional! Instead of providing facts and information he spent the time making crass jokes about ex girlfriends and his second life or telling stories that were clearly made up.
Very disappointed in this tour and in losing the opportunity to take the other tour we had paid for as a consequence.

We enjoyed our Big Bus hop on hop off experience October 2022, in London, England. We were able to pick it up near our hotel in Hyde Park. Our ticket selection was for 24 hrs.
The bus doesn't use a live guide, but pre recorded commentary. I think it takes something away from the experience. In 2010, we experienced live commentary and it was so much more fun. That said, the pre-recorded commentary is available in several languages which is a plus. The boat tour, included in the ticket, had live commentary and it was funny and great.
There are 3 walking tours. The change of the guard at 10am, City of London's past and present at 1pm and Jack the Ripper at 4pm.. You can do all three tours if you have enough time. We did the tour of Jack the Ripper. Our guide, Julia, was excellent. She was very knowledgeable, great sense of humor and patient. She always waited for everyone to gather before providing the information. She was also attentive to people's needs as my wife had difficulty keeping up because of her hip and as a result, a little slow to gather. A big thank you to Julia.
In my book, the live guide experience is second to none.

Been waiting for 75 minutes and still no bus. (Green Line)
One bus is just sitting in traffic and the other drove past us, empty, on the other side of the road.
In the app it says £37 but when it is time to pay for the tickets it is £41. No explanation or anything...

Travelled on the big bus tour yesterday, 25/7/2021. We tried to board the bus at the London Eye but as there was a run on we directed to Waterloo by one of the guides. No problem we joined the bus there till Buckingham palace, all good.
After rejoining the bus is where it all went downhill. We were planning on getting off at Whitehall next but the bus never went anywhere near. In fact the tour never stopped anywhere near this area or indeed any of the more central stops Covent Garden , trafaglar square to name a few.
Yes we weren’t aware there was a run on closing lots of roads in the city on our day of choice but it would have been good to have been advised of the route change before boarding and validating our ticket as we would have changed our plans and done the bus tour the following day.
No one ever mentioned the route change and it wasn’t until my daughter spotted a QR code after travelling for almost 2 hours we realised why we couldn’t figure out where we where on the map, as this showed a very long list of stop closures.
A very expensive disappointing trip when travelling as a family of four. Only one of our planed stops was available. It was my sons first trip to London and we didn’t get chance to show him half of what we wanted to and living over 5 hours away we don’t travel to London regularly.
More communication before boarding should have been given when we exchanged our online ticket ( purchased as part of the Merlin package).
I realise these things happen but communication would have been good so we could have made a choice of whether to swap our itinerary around.

This trip, whilst taking you through a number of historical and achitectuallary important sites in London, has the most useless, childish and patronising recorded commentary ever conceived of. It is fully of (supposidly) funny pieces which are only going to insult tourists. The tour passes loads of important and interesting sites whilst leaving out any commentary about them. At the same time it introduces fatuous 'quizes' of no consequence. Given that this pretty useless tour of this historic city costs £72 for two people, this must be one of the capital's greatest rip-offs. We haven't been on any of the other trips, but any of them must be better than this.

I have to laugh reading these others reviews because I whole heartedly agree that the recorded audio on the busses is complete garbage. The attempts at humor are awful, nothing very educational at all on the history of the city, they're extremely obnoxious, and I finally stopped listening while riding the busses. Live your guides are infinitely better. The reason for my 4 start review is because the walking tours and the boat tour saved the experience. We had Nick for two tours: the changing of the guard and Jack Ripper. He is phenomenal and worth a 10 star rating. Nick was extremely knowledgeable, engaging, hilarious, and a hoot to be around; you won't want the tour to end. I didn't catch the boat tourguide's name, but his humor was brilliant as well. I would still recommend this company because they still give you rides around the city and the tours are a must. Hopefully you get Nick!

The tour itself was great, drivers friendly and helpful. Buses frequent.
However, if you book through trip advisor, beware if anything goes wrong.
Booked the night before, no email with tickets received via email. They have the correct address on my account, I checked.
Tried to call both trip advisor and the your company itself, no reply.
Emailed x 2, no reply.
Had to buy another ticket for just under £100 on the bus as the driver couldn’t accept the confirmation in the app. (Needed the tickets themselves)
Cancelled the first booking, apparently they have emailed, still nothing received by email.
Apparently I will know their decision in a week…
Will not be booking via trip advisor again…

The experience of the bus tour was great and thorough.
The highlight of my trip was Julia during the walking tour. She has a great spirit , understanding of the history and a warm sense of humour that made the experience twice as fun. Julia puts in a lot of hardwork and the insight we got into her work ethic really proves that.
Highly recommend. The buses are great , the tour wonderful and Julia you’re a star
Keep up the good work
Cheers

We pre-booked our tickets and caught the first green line link bus (08:45) from Kings Cross Station. We had our 10 year old grandson with us. The driver was friendly and told us where to get off to catch the red line (central London) bus. We duly got on the red line bus and plugged in our audio head sets. The sound was horrendous, it just kept breaking up so that was a disappointing start. We got off the bus at the Tower of London to do the included river cruise.

We just missed one so had to wait 30 minutes for the next one. However we got front seats upstairs so that was good. We had good views of Tower Bridge and the Tower of London among other sights. The chap who gave the commentary was great, just the right amount of humour and plenty of information. It is just a one-way cruise up to Westminster Bridge (Big Ben) but it was excellent; our grandson thoroughly enjoyed it.

We found the red bus stop easily and luckily there was one waiting. It was very full and the 3 of us had to sit separately for some time. This one had decent audio however which helped. I heard someone say that it had been re-routed but I don’t know why or what we missed. It was hard to follow the route on the map and on the app. Some of the commentary was quite banal and seemed to miss important things out. We only saw Nelson’s Column and Trafalgar Square from the rear and it went nowhere near Buckingham Palace which was a disappointment.

We got on the blue line bus when that tour finished. That was a HUGE disappointment with not many sights to see. There was only a little commentary, nearly all music. The bus driver drove really fast and we were all thrown about. We missed our one chance of a sighting of Kensington Palace. It wasn’t even mentioned. We were glad when that tour finished.

All in all it was a mixture of experiences. They need to sort out the audio on all the buses and improve the blue line audio. The boat trip was brilliant.

I wouldn't even rate this. Staff selling the tickets were good and explained everything. But the bus driver especially ours was rude to his colleague, so much so he started swearing and shouting at his colleague who was only trying to help us get on as he bloody drove straight past us all!.

He then did not follow the red route as stated. The bus tour was ment to be on until late and at 6.30pm we were all asked to leave the bus! Not at our stop we have expected and left wondering where the hell we are and what we are ment to do now!.

Rip off as was £113.00 for 2 adult and 2 young children. No seats allocated. Passengers looked miserable as not getting the experience we had all expected. Passengers were asking to get off the bus as kept driving past the landmarks!! To be told no I'm only stopping at .... I'm not stopping at any others!. Get this bus driver sorted and to top it off he had his music on that was heard over the commentary!

Use the tube! It's quicker and at least you can get off where you want and not be lost in London!. Terrible experience.

Be very wary of this. We paid for 2 x adult tickets and only used the service for 5 mins due to major issues in London's roads. There was a major breakdown and as the roads are single lanes there were significant delays. We were held up for 45 minutes, not moving anywhere and eventually all passengers got off themselves. The driver was fantastic I have to admit. This then cost more as I had to use alternative route transport. On contacting the company was advised London's roads are busy what do you expect. After multiple emails they have offered a, wait for it, yes 15% refund. My advice use public transport.

Would not recommend Big Bus tours around London. We walked most of the time or got the tube. How we went from stop 20 to stop 1 is beyond me. Wanted to go to trafalgar square they did not stop there dropped us off at Green Park. That was the 1st time he stop past T square. got a tube back to T square £6.00 x 4 people no joke. Then walked to leicester square there did not stop there walked down the mall to buckingham palace walked to westminster abbey to the london eye 21,653 steps that cost us over £123.00 for 4 people to use a bus. That did not stop where we needed to go terrible service bus driver did not give a crap. I have more family coming over from canada this summer will not be using this company. would have been cheaper to get a all day tube/bus pass

Unprofessional, mis managed, not at all punctual and horrible customer service.
They blame everything to London traffic. The whole world knows about London traffic and your back tend operations team should be aware of it.
We wasted 3 hours on 6th Oct at Trafalgar Square and adjoining areas (JUST STOP OIL) rally. We asked for compensation and were told that because the ticket is not purchased directly with them, they cannot compensate. I booked 2 tickets through groupon.
Also, we requested an additional day, instead of 2 tickets, they gave us just 1.
Had to haggle and by then we decided to let go. We got the 2nd ticket after a few hours.

It’s better they stop their service.

And for all those going on a hop on hop off- London traffic is horrible and this may not be the best thing for you unless you take this service for 2-3 days

Spent £50 on this for me and my son to take in the sights before a cinema screening which we had booked. Doesn't follow the route on the map they give you!!! I tracked it in the app they suggest you download, and the went all over the place, you never knew where it was actually going as it didn't stick to the route, which is annoying when you've spent that much on something that this company doesn't deliver. There were foreign tourists asking if it was going the route past Buckingham palace (it didn't), others asking what stop we were at (it wasn't clear as it kept changing route randomly). Seemed to go back to the start point more than once to pick up more customers I'd imagine. Eventually got off at Green Park to get the tube to Leicester Square as otherwise we'd have missed our cinema screening, and I was worried about where the bus was going to take us, could have ended up in the West end miles away from where I needed to be. Yes I could have got the tube, but that's not the point. Like other reviews on here, you don't pay all that money to go on a random tour of London.
Also, I hopped on and off about 3 times, and at no point did anyone check if I had a ticket. I could have had a blank piece of paper in my hand and still got on, so in all honesty, save your money and seek an alternative sightseeing trip.

We were a party of 7 yesterday.It's certainly not cheap.The buses are overcrowded and often my students were unable to sit down and hence unable to listen to the commentary in French.We took the last bus from Buckingham Palace to Marble Arch.The bus was extremely overcrowded,hence we were all stood up and crushed in like sardines.We were not the only ones stood up.The bus was carrying way more than any legal limit of number of passengers.One of my students got her feet trodden on by another passenger another got her hand crushed hanging onto a hand rail.This is not the fault of the drivers.There is an insufficient number buses for the number of passengers.Today,I will be sending a letter by recorded delivery to the management.
What was good was the boat trip on the Thames.When we were able to get seats on the bus the recorded commentary is good

I had hyped this tour up to my friends as I had taken similar Hop on Hop off bus tours thru London before. Wow......what a HUGE DISAPPOINTMENT! We got on the bus at 8:35am for the first trip around. They were scheduled to start at 8:45, and didn't start until 9:00am. While that doesn't seem like a big issue, we were trying to get they whole 2:30 tour in before they had to leave for the airport. Then there was an extended stop on Fleet Street. Two other Big Buses stopped and went past us. We ended up having to get off at the Tower of London to take the ferry back and then a taxi to the hotel.

While the commentary was amusing...at times...they didn't mention ANYTHING about several of the big attractions like: The Marble Arch, Cleopatra's Needle, the monument to the Great Fire of London. BUT, they did spend a whole lot of time promoting Madam Tussaud's.

I will not take this particular bus tour again. There are others that are much better.

Friendly, convenient and priceworthy. If you want to go around the tourist attractions easily, these buses are to recommend. They come every 10mins and make for a good and safe transportation around central London and Westminster. We did a 24h package with an amazing boat cruise included for 41£ ppax. Might be cheaper to buy online.

Beware before you book through trip advisor!! Had to cancel this as we were booked in for the day of the queens funeral and a lot of the routes were closed. Was told I would be refunded and it’s now October and I’m STILL waiting. Cannot get in touch with anyone and when I go to my inbox it says the refund was escalated and completed. There is no way for me to reply on there and everytime i message someone by replying to previous chat about the refund I’m never getting a reply so I feel completely stuck and done out of money.I will be taking this further but just wanted to warn anyone who is tempted to book this on here.

I'm a big believer in an overview tour of a city as a way to start off a trip there, to give everyone context and a bit of background before diving into individual sites. I was hoping that this bus tour would provide that background, but it was terrible. The recorded commentary was as often as not totally off-topic and would skip right over buildings and areas we were driving through without giving any information. The music between bits of "information" was annoying. The stops were overly long - at one point seemingly just to give a passenger time to smoke a cigarette - and the information just wasn't there. The app is not nearly as helpful or informative as I was hoping and did not reflect current detours the buses had to take. All in all, a waste of money and time.

I had 3 walking tour with Nick L. Old city, jack the ripper and royal tour. Although i took the tours the day prior to the funeral (everything was very crowded) and we couldn’t reach the palace, Nick explained about the sites and took us to the most available viewing spots. He was funny and clearly has lots of knowledge. Each tour was unique and in different part of the city so i saw different things. I walked a lot that day, but enjoyed every minute of it :)

Worst bus tour company I have ever been on. Rude staff, lengthy waiting for buses to show. So packed you have to stand. Your child gets an elbow to face causing a nose bleed because of the bus being packed. No air conditioning on even though it was one of the hottest days of the year. After standing for 45mins on a bus we had to get off because of my poor daughter. We had to pay another £170 to go with another company because I didn’t want my relatives disappointed because we thought this was the best way for them to see the sights without too much walking due to their age. Thank goodness for the other company. So annoyed I went with this company and I can’t even get my £176 back.

We've undertaken loads of bus tours all over Europe and this is without doubt the worst. The pre-recoded 'Jokey' commentary between 2 presenters was awful. Constantly asking each other stupid irrelevant questions and using ridiculous voices and sounds. Things like , questions about who has stayed at this or that hotel and trying to put on stupid mimic voices. The tour missed talking about dozens of historic sites. I felt so sorry for our Venezuelan relative who I had to try and explain what many buildings were and other land marks like Hyde Park and Regents Park. Very long gaps with awful music when they could have been talking about the sights. There was no guide just a pre-recording. Some stops weren't announced and not one reference to the stop number on the map. At one point we were all thrown off our bus to go on another packed bus and when we complained they said we could stay on our original bus!!! What was that all about? Total waste of money, Never again.

The actual bus tour was okay, the commentary was bare minimum. Would have been much better with a live guide!!

That being said I went to the morning walking tour with a live guide, Julia and it was so great that I spent the rest of the day doing all of the walking tours with her group! She’s so knowledgeable and a great story teller. She also took the time to answer everyone’s questions.

The walking tours are what made the experience worth it, highly recommend those! And hopefully they bring live guides back to the busses soon too!

Over subscribed, waste of money. Managed to get on bus but only on 1st level and people were left standing - we watched every bus from this operator and all were the same. Other tour operator buses were empty. Top level was full and new customers managed to force their way in as others were leaving and get to the top deck, no staff (except the driver) to manage. 1st level view is terrible, would have been better views and cheaper to take a standard double decker bus and sitting at the top. When finally managed to get on top floor it was only for one stop before the bus terminated and everyone had to get off and transfer to another bus. By the time top floor had disembarked the other bus top floor was full. Didn't see any real tourist sites and will never use again. Commentary was intermittent with two of our group of fours not working properly. River cruise was chaotic and no information on what we needed to do. Queued at ticket office only to find out we didn't need to. Had to wait 40 minutes for boat and was told it was a 40 minute journey (it was only a 20 min journey). Queued up in 3 different queues for the boat but they were the wrong boats/ queues, no staff around to ask for help and was becoming a joke. Nearly ended up on a 5hr party boat and an evening dining cruise even though we had two young children with us. Was only upon getting to the front of the queues did we find out they were the wrong boats.

Will not be using again, ever.

We chose Big Bus based on the 4 star rating without reading the reviews. We did another Hop-On/Off bus in 2019 where there was a live narrator. We thought this was the same one and it most definitely was not. The narration on this bus was all with a tape recording that barely provided any history and was just fluff. For instance, the only thing we learned about Westminster, although we passed it twice (and it was barely pointed out) was that it has the oldest door in the world or something like that. No other history about one of the most important churches in the world. They didn't make it clear when we got to Buckinham Palace. They do an entire section of the tour that is a worthless hour plus of time, with a lot of traffic and no movement, in a part of town that is basically just residential and expensive and there was nothing else to see. Choose another service. I have never left a bad review in my life, despite plenty of bad experiences. So that tells you something.

A mixed review. Some elements were fantastic and others could be improved. I came on the tour with my teenage daughter. We bought 3-day tickets and used different parts of it each day.

The changing the guard and Jack the Ripper walking tours were fantastic. Julia was amazing and enthusiastic, providing lots of information and keeping the walks really interesting. The river cruise was also a highlight.

The bus tour was good for seeing many of the sights but the audio would have been massively improved with live commentary. There were occasions when the audio did not tie in with locations, either because the bus had to divert or was delayed. A human would have been far more capable of reacting to a change in circumstances. Traffic is inevitably a part of city life and beyond the control of the big bus company but being stuck in traffic was frustrating. We tried to do the night tour but found this very repetitive, having already done the daytime tour, and (due to time off the year) it was still daylight all the way round. I'm not really sure it is worth operating a separate 'night tour' when it isn't dark!

Overall, I'm glad we did the tour but there are definitely things that could be improved.

Brilliant tour! We visited London with our 6yo son and as it was his first visit we wanted to make sure he saw everything. We initially looked at one of the other tour companies however found a discount code for Big Bus Tours on the National Rail Big Day Out page.
We were not disappointed at all with the tour. There were frequent buses and the free app was great at showing where the stops were and when buses were due. The tour takes you around all the main sightseeing spots.
The river cruise that’s included was also really good. The live commentary was brilliant and provided a different view of London.
Would definitely recommend the tour to anyone visiting London.

The bus trip itself was okay, but the commentary was so badly done, I found it annoying and offensive. They started off about how rich everyone was in a certain area and talked about money, money, money. The commentary wasn't helpful at all and was done like a comedy show, trying to get us to laugh. I just wanted to learn about London! Buses were slow to come at times, but we had no crowding issues like other companies.

Bring back live commentary! The recorded commentary is aimed at kids and has music in-between, great in some ways as have children. However, some of the buses barely played any commentry and others loads (we know this as doubled up on some of the route to get our hotel and noticed a massive difference the 2nd time round). Also, the 'facts' are pretty rubbish to be honest for anyone aged over 10yrs. The river cruise with live commentary was great in comparison and engaging for adults and children alike.
Either book a river cruise with commentry and see the majority of the sights and walk/tube the rest you can't get to from the river (e.g Buckingham palace, st Paul's cathedral) or use another bus company with live commentary.
For the money expect better. Only saving grace for us was the children had a great time but not for adults at all.

We did the open top bus tour and enjoyed it for what it was, although I am not convinced it was the money we paid which was nearly £30 each.

The weather was abysmal that day, obviously not the fault of the company at all but it did take away from it. No live tour guide so we got a headset and got to plug in to listen to some naff cringe worthy comedy tour guide. The traffic in London in parts really did not help with the experience.

In terms of the good points, the hop on and off element was excellent, especially when used with the app they have. You know where the bus is at any time and it made it easy. The river tour didn't get to do, did not feel it was made clear enough how to do it.

It truly wasn't worth our money. Incredibly slow, long waits, and when I asked the driver a simple question about getting to a church, he told me to take a taxi, and he didn't say it in a nice way. The buses are littered with headphones and the bags they come in. Also, our bus didn't follow the route as indicated on the map and made things confusing. We used the bus twice and had to jump off early. Only the ferry was worth it, but I should have just paid for that and saved my money. One last thing, why call it 24 or 48 hour pass if you're only allowed to use it for a 9-10 hour window? You have to get another ticket to use it after 6.

Absolute rip off! I’m a Londoner so have never bothered to get a tour bus in London as I live here.
