However we had friends visiting London and they had booked the bus with their London Eye ticket and asked us to join them and their kids. So £29.50 each and after waiting 30 mins for a bus we get on. The bus was filthy, overcrowded and we were stuck downstairs with the kids as the top deck was full. For some bizarre reason most of the downstairs windows are blacked out so you can’t actually see out. So now we’re stuck on a bus we’ve paid £60 to go on with our kids who can’t see out the windows and theres no commentary anyway and we’re driving round the back streets of Victoria. Also every time the bus gets to a stop you’re there for 10 mins while they pack more people on and take their hard earned cash. The bus was already at full capacity with no seats available on the top deck but they were still letting more people on which not only is unfair to those that are already on the bus and waiting for a seat to become available it’s also worrying when there is a global pandemic. We stayed on until Regent Street by which time the kids were bored and it had taken over an hour to get there. It would’ve been cheaper and more enjoyable to get in a black cab and ask the cabbie to drive us round the sites of London. Honestly don’t bother! Speaking as a Londoner just use your travel card to get around. And if you want to do a river cruise get the Thames Clipper to Greenwich and back it’s a fab experience.

An intended birthday treat for a 5 year old turned into a very expensive mistake. Buses were crammed and few and far between. The recorded commentary consisted mainly of Musak and recommendations of places to eat and drink, and the few places of interest that were graced with a comment were treated to a few banal remarks. And the final indignity was to be dumped at the back of Buckingham Palace only to be told that there would be a 20 minute wait for the next bus. Would recommend visitors to use another tour operator… any other operator!! An expensive lesson learned..

We bought the two day package with walking tours, the bus and a boat ride and it was the perfect way to learn about London. We did two walking tours with Julia and she was very knowledgeable and had a great personality. The boat tour also had a very good guide explaining the history of the city. The busses were a great way to sit back and see the city of London. There were lots of stops to get on and off and many of them were staffed with employees to help you. My only complaint about the busses would be the prerecorded description of sights. It would have been a much better experience with a live guide explaining what we were seeing.Overall, we felt like the Big Bus was well run and a great deal if you take advantage of the walking tours and the boat.

We bought a one day ticket on the Toot Bus for this tour in August 2022 and hopped on after a photo shoot outside Buckingham Palace. We hopped off again at Hyde Park Corner where we had lunch after enjoying seeing Lambeth Bridge, Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament, just some of the sights along the blue route. We hopped on the yellow route for the next stage of our sightseeing tour travelling along Piccadilly to Piccadilly Circus then onto Trafalgar Square finally hopping off at the London Eye. From here we boarded the River Cruise included in the cost of the ticket and enjoyed a half hour cruise along the South Bank to the hilarious commentary by the host. We bought tickets for the London Eye and following a very short wait we boarded the pod and we were not disappointed. The elevated views of London are breath taking and gave us a great photo opportunity . We finished our day with a Toot bus back to the vicinity of our accommodation tired but with happy memories of a remarkable day.

£85 for two tickets

Buses were delayed by two hours when one finally arrived there were no seats then we were stuck in traffic and moved 2 stops in 45 mins. We got off and walked in the end as it was quicker and more comfortable.

Obviously traffic isn't the operators fault but added to the already dreadful experience.

Avoid at all costs- biggest con in London

One star is two too many but did not have a minus option. No talk guide through headphones that are provided. Got an electric shock through plugging the bloody things in tho. Bus went round in a circle in the traffic until we got back to where we started. All wondering why we had just spent £80 per couple to go on a 40minute bus ride when it set off again. This time however it went through some slightly more interesting traffic until finally . we saw the London eye. We all got off to try the inclusive boat trip. The hop off staff told us to go across the bridge to catch the boat. Which we missed by seconds. We then watched as it went over to the other side to pick people up ! Finally got on one. It took us to London bridge which was great. However we were then told that it was stopping there and to find out own way back. Got a £30 cab. Cannot wait to go again

Loved this! Great way to see London learn a little and get your bearings. Being able to jump on and off the bus at different stop was ideal. There was busses all the time. It was made really clear where the busses were going and what you would see. We bought them on the day from a rep for £42 which we didn't think was bad as we had been paying cabs to get around. The traffic was really heavy as there was loads of events on the weekend we were there but you didn't mind too much as it was a lovely sunny day so you could sit and enjoy the view. Would recommend if you dont really know your way around and want to see alot in a short time.

Unfortunately we were really disappointed by this. Although this was very expensive (Around £80 for 2 adults and 1 child), we thought this would be a great way to see all of the sights in London. We were at stop 36 at 11am, in the thought that we would take that bus to stop 1, get off, go see Buckingham Palace then we had planned to do the red route and the rest of the blue route, back to our hotel near stop 36. Both routes have an estimated journey time on the website, so we thought we would have enough time to do all of this. We were on the red route for over 3 hours and only got from stop 1 to stop 19!! We ended up getting off at the London Eye stop and getting the underground back to the hotel, as we had dinner/theatre booked. The bus was very busy and my husband had to stand at one point. The commentary was informative however it kept cutting off mid sentence, which we all found frustrating.
We were sad that we didn't get to finish either of the routes as there were still places of interest that we wanted to see.

Thanks to Big Steve! Having his live commentary took this from a passable experience into something great and memorable!

We rode this bus in the morning a bit and were disappointed by the experience. The recorded audio was poor quality, and basically offered bad jokes and then listed facts and then you had to sit there listening to the same songs waiting for the next one. Not what you expect for $50/each..

In the afternoon, we got lucky and Big Steve came to the rescue! He provided live commentary and it was exactly what we were looking for. Interesting, entertaining, funny, kind and tons of information and local color- he was great and really made our day! His amount of knowledge was really impressive- someone would ask about a random building or thing and he’d immediately have something insightful to add. He engaged everyone on the bus and made people feel comfortable and enjoy themselves. You could tell he loved his job and making people happy and sharing this city with them.

So overall, the ease of the bus was good, the cleanliness was poor, the audio recording was brutal. So I’d give it a 3, but if you get lucky to have Big Steve as a live guide, it’s an easy 5 experience. Thanks Steve for making our trip memorable!

The bus tours were good, a great way to see the city, but pre-recorded commentary gets tiresome after a while. The river cruise was way too short and disappointing. The highlights were the walking tours: did the Changing of the guard and the Jack the Ripper tour with our guide Nick … he was absolutely fantastic!! Informative and funny, he made it all worth it. The staff at the stops were friendly and helpful too.

I’m elderly and frequently fall asleep during recorded just tours. Chris surprised us today with a lively presentation that was informative and entertaining. We highly recommend this HopOn-HopOff tour company - especially with live tour guides!

Representatives were not friendly nor informative. One out of five different drivers was friendly and informative. I feel I wasted my money. Could have hopped on and off on the city buses for less than 10£ versus spending 90£.

Great experience! Fun way to get an introduction to city lay out and attractions to return to. Organized - attendants at the main stops to help with queue and determine how many seats available on the top deck. Andy was very kind and friendly.

Not cheap but you do get a good view of the London sights. We spent the whole day on the bus changing to go on the different routes. Staff were great, really friendly and helpful, stopping buses so you could get onto the different routes. It was good to simply sit on the buses and get a good tour and overview of the city. We also took the river cruise and the evening tour which was all part of the 2 day ticket. Definitely recommend as it was great to see London from up high, however I feel that the recorded commentary needs an update in light of re events in the UK.

The trip was perfect as was a clearn sunny day, driver Scott was almost the best i've had as he never once gave hard brakes and was driving with the recording synchronised. Things got exceptionally good when the live tour guide Chloe came and she explained many small details that we could never had known as were hidden and real time updates about the city. She even was giving nice comments about things as well as had a beautiful warm smile all the way. Soft as could be and answered everyone's questions and gave us a lot to chuckle about. She even had the history of many monuments that are not easily found on the net. Plus she remembered every bit of the trip to smallest bit. The tour bus were absolutely clean and everyone was given covid guideline spaced seating on bus. Chloe can easily grab the tourist imagination absolutely if she wanted to and she did. I couldn't want anything better than her as a guide. Absolutely recommend this to everyone as one of the top attaractions... i mean the hop on hop off tour itself.. it is an attaraction in itself because of the team they manage. 24 hours then take it all you can by dropping off in middle for the free cruise included in it. The joining it again. Planning the time is best, imho get on middle of day on bus the get on cruise and then again next day morning take the tour on bus full on again. See things differently different times. Makes it worth the amount i paid 10 times over. When ever i am in london would surely take this tour again and again.

We booked the Big Bus Tour for 4th January 2022 and took the first bus which we really enjoyed. We went to Boots at 1pm for antigen tests and had planned to resume the tour with the second bus and river cruise after that but unfortunately we both received incorrect positive tests. We knew we were negative because all our home tests were negative, including that day, however we had to abandon the trip and self isolate before going for a PCR with the NHS the following day. We subsequently received negative test results. We were disappointed that we had missed our on the trip and other activities, and the ticket had expired at this point. I contacted the customer care team with Big Bus and explained the situation and Miriam kindly offered us two complimentary tickets which can be used any time in the next 12 months. I really appreciate this kindness and understanding and we look forward to going back in the near future.

The bus tour was very slow. Lots of stops (as expected) but we sat and waited at some stops for a very long time (at one stop nearly 20 mins). The audio recording was interesting and provided some interesting facts but didn’t always line up to the locations we were at. Next time I would skip the bus tour and walk instead.

Bought the one day pass on Feb 26th...bus went out of service before getting to King Kross, bus in front was scheduled to leave in 20 min. When we left KK, had to wait 30 min for the next bus (Big Bus decided to change the wait time from 20 to 30 min on the green line because of the poor weather).When we were ready to take the bus close to our hotel, bus driver and his boss got into an argument over a older couple. Bus driver pulled a 3 point turn in the middle of traffic because he was ordered to turn around and pick them up. Not worth it, take the tube.

We did the bus tour several years ago and decided to do again.
Fantastic.
We did go early, just after 0900 on a Saturday morning.
Traffic quiet.
Headphone commentary very good and informative.
We decided to come off at London tower and take the river cruise up to Westminster, it was simply outstanding with the Captain’s mate providing a very engaging and entertaining commentary, this was the highlight, we loved it.
One, very small, but of advice if it is at all cold, wrap up well for the open top bus.

My brother was over from Australia so we had a family day out with the kids and our parents. We all had a great time, even the teenagers! It was a great way to get to see all the sights of London and all from the comfort of a chair, we all know how tiring city breaks can be. The audio headsets were a great source of information and the guy on the mic on the boat was informative and funny. I would recommend to anyone coming to London and I will defo be doing this again on my next city break. 10/10.

I have done "hop on/hop off" tours in several major cities, this was by far the worst. Ear phones were provided, some of which did not work. The ones that did work initially, stopped working after 3-5 minutes. The audio we could hear was not the bus driver telling us about the area that we were in, but instead a pre-recorded audio of London, in general. There was absolutely no notification of upcoming stops. We missed the stop we wanted to get off at because we thought we were just sitting at a red light.

The Big Bus tours are a great way to see the sights of London! I wish I could give it 5 stars, but I can’t due to the lack of tour guides and having to listen to audio on the busses.

The bus is great and takes you all around the city, on two different routes. One route is all the main sites and the other is more chill, where you will see less but it is still good. The stops are every so often and plenty of times to get off and on. Get the app so you can track where the busses are and know how long exactly before the next is there. It’s a great way to see the sights, I just can’t give it 5 stars because all the information we got came from an audio recording.

We did a walking tour and a river cruise. First, the river cruise. It was amazing! Make sure you remember that it is only one way, it takes you to a different part of the city. It’s great to be able to see sights of London such as the eye, Big Ben, and more via the boat. On our second day, we did a walking tour for the changing of the guards. Julia was our guide and she was AMAZING! If only every bus had a Julia on it giving everyone information. She made sure we got the best spot at changing of the guard. We moved around from place to place in order to see as much as we could in a timely manner. Be aware, this walk is fast paced so if you do not enjoy that, it’s not for you. Julia gave us so much information about everything. We learned so much from her. It wouldn’t have been near as good if we were listening to an audio.

So, I would do big bus tours again, but mainly for the river cruise and walking tours. The busses are a great way to see the city if you can stand listening to a pre recorded audio.

I took my 5 year old daughter on the hop on hop off tour as she’s recently done ‘London’ as a topic at school and was keen to see the sights for real.
Our guide Phil was absolutely fantastic and really made an effort to involve my daughter, making sure to point out Pudding Lane as she is obsessed by the Great fire of London. We had the top deck almost to ourselves.
We loved the river cruise from Tower Bridge to Westminster.
Later on we hopped on a different bus which had no live guide - the audio commentary via the headphones seemed to be mainly patriotic music rather than much history, so I’d definitely recommend picking a bus with a live guide if you can! Phil really made my little girl’s day on our first bus. The drivers were really helpful and let us hop off near Hamleys even though that stop is currently suspended. The staff are really keen to make sure their customers enjoy the experience, and I wouldn’t hesitate to go again. Fantastic value as kids go free at the moment.
It’s a great time to see London when everything is less busy, and feels good to support these tourism companies trying to get going again. Distancing on the buses is easy as they are operating at much lower visitor numbers than usual.

I’m rarely inclined to leave a bad review, usually I’ll accept that an experience was a poor one and won’t repeat it, however on this occasion I feel strongly that others should avoid using this company at all costs.

My family and I booked our bus and river cruise tickets for a visit to London in May 2021, spending almost £200. We initially waited half an hour for the bus to arrive at Tower of London, after being told it would be 15 minutes. The tour commenced with the bus seeming overcrowded and with us having to stand (frustrating as I was 7 months pregnant at the time, but we accepted it). The bus then proceeded to stop at many more stops than necessary, taking almost 2 hours to get to Victoria because, as it turned out, there was a fault and we all had to be removed and transferred to another vehicle. We’d already wasted a lot of time so again, we accepted it and got on the next bus, before witnessing a member of Big Bud Tours staff having. a huge tantrum at Marble Arch, shouting and ranting at his colleague, because a family had been told to complain to him (by another member of the team). He ranted and raved, loudly, in front of all passengers including children (the two year old in our party was intimidated and upset by this). More delays followed, before we eventually had to exit at Regent Street, having seen almost none of the sights intended. We were stressed and felt duped, after wasting hours of our trip and decided we wouldn’t put ourselves through the hassle of using the buses or boat again, despite having paid for them.

Additionally, the audio didn’t work in most sockets (already a poor option in comparison to a live tour), further confirming the poor maintenance and service this company feels it acceptable to offer.

I complained straight away, requesting a refund. It took weeks of chasing before they offered free tickets for a future visit, something we clearly would have no intention of putting ourselves through. Big Bus Tours was aware from the beginning that a refund was expected, but they avoided answering questions for as long as they could.

After further chasing, they came back to me saying that traffic and weather are out of their control and they don’t refund on this basis - clearly a template response and no attempt to even read back through the email and messaging chain. Ridiculous.

After this point, a refund was eventually offered but this still didn’t arrive in my account until they delayed for almost a week again, at which point i questioned the legitimacy of the company. Now, 6 weeks later, the refund has finally arrived and if this had happened within a week of the problem, I wouldn’t have left this review as I’d have seen that as a reasonable resolution, however the lack of professionalism has led to this.

For those still awaiting their refunds, don’t give up. And for those who haven’t booked yet - find an alternative tour provider

We picked this tour because we were going to be in London on a Monday & Tuesday and so much is closed those days that we were worried about finding things to do. This tour has two routes that cover a lot of the city and that's fantastic.

I think one of the challenges is that in the off-season, you're listening to a pre-recorded guide that really can't adapt to route changes - and route changes are inevitable in a city like London. That said, even when we were on the correct route, the audio was largely uninformative. There was a lot of filler from people who I think are radio personalities and at first they were entertaining but then they just got repetitive. There was little context given, if the guide even told us about what we passed. I had the London Architecture map downloaded on my phone & it was far better at filling in the gaps.

We also got on the bus early, at Gloucester Road, and when we got to Marble Arch, the driver stopped and went out of service. It was another half hour before a bus came so it wasted a lot of our available time. We decided not to even use the bus for the 2nd day we'd booked, which is kind of a waste, but other than getting a different viewpoint of the city, I felt like this was kind of a waste. I don't know if other tours are any better, but I don't feel the need to do another one in a city like London that's so spread out with such good public transportation. Even our taxi driver was more informative when we took one.

During the day bus tour it was easy to hop on and hop at which ever stop we liked. For a party of 3 over 48 hours we think it’s good value for money. Our package also included a non stop night tour and a cruise on the Thames. The only disappointment was the traffic congestion at night which lengthened the time to complete the tour.
Enjoyable experience overall which saved our legs and having to use TFL ***

We travelled from Liverpool just for our boys to go on a tour of London and learn where events had taken place that they had been learning about int school.
We got on a packed bus and had to wait 5 stops until we could get seats upstair.
There is ABSOLUTELY NO COMMENTARY when travelling around on the bus therefore we knew nothing of the city's history. The only landmarks we saw were the ones I could follow on Google Maps. My two 9 year olds were bored stiff just travelling round on a bus listening to music on what shoudlve been a commentary. I feel like I've been robbed of £82 for a totally pointless journey round London!

I booked two adult tickets for myself and my 16 year old step-sister online for when we visited London the weekend. I have emailed the company itself and have given ample time to reply so now I feel it fair to write an honest review. We redeemed the tickets next to the London eye from a friendly staff member but from there it went rapidly downhill.

The weather turned and with the rain falling, everyone on the buses that then came went downstairs, and non of the buses we tried had any shelter on the top of the bus so we sat getting wet through (with our coats on and hoods up). We waited for up to an hour on the Sunday afternoon for a bus to arrive which then was full so had to wait even longer and then we were not able to redeem the river ticket the next day, as promised as it is a 24 hour ticket. My sister was extremely disappointed and it was a real dampner on the trip.Additionally the audio commentary was dismal and there were so many music fillers inbetween, the information given was poor and disjointed.

I used this company around 7 or 8 years ago with family and it was a completely different experience. Please do not book with this company, better to get the tube and a guidebook.

My wife and I used to live in London and we used to regularly use Big Bus Tours when our friends were visiting the city and the experience was always excellent, especially with the live tour guides who were on the whole superb. We have since moved abroad and returned to visit London with our children. We were very excited to give them the Big Bus tour and having used the Big Bus in Paris, with its recorded commentary which was very informative, we were hoping the lack of live tour guides wouldn’t be a problem. How wrong we were. The new recorded commentary was dreadful. In between long periods of music, it attempted some silly banter between the 3 characters whilst failing to impart even a minimal level of detail. London is a fascinating city with stories around every corner yet the new tour left out so many wonderful historical monuments and interesting facts that I nearly stood up to tell some of the information to my fellow riders myself. The new recorded tours around London simply do a disservice to the interested tourist and to the history of London itself. I sincerely hope the other tour operators are far better.

On line paying dropped the ball as my daughter and I were overcharged 74 pounds sterling. Monster runaround after that doesn't seem to go anywhere. Minutes ago I was told by on line help that the case was escalated yesterday even though I was told the same thing in London on April 10th. Give me back 74 pounds sterling.

This is a fun way to explore London and see some of the high points of the city in one day. The tour is narrated and you can listen to a fun theatrical narration of all the things you are seeing as you drive-by. My only suggestion is that they announce the number of the bus stop that's coming up. Sometimes it was a little hard to figure out which stop we were approaching. Other than that the drivers, narration and experience were great!

Thought a bus tour would be the best idea to see most of the big sites without the hassle of travel and cost. Driver was rather abrupt as I didn't know to wait to take my ticket off him before I went upstairs (surprise, I've never been on this tour before!) went on top deck which was freezing even in calm weather (wrap up), if you have a delicate stomach I would advise you: don't do this tour, we spent a lot of our time jerking backwards and forwards every time we stopped (and that was a lot due to the traffic) and when you go over a speed bump or pot hole, hold on tight as you might be going for a flight, think our driver was in a rush as I nearly went over the edge when he hit a speed bump. At the end we seam to get lost, weaving in and out of side streets till we arrived near the Ritz Hotel, stopped and engine off to the bemusement of the passengers (we boarded near Tussauds so was expecting it to go in a loop), by this time we where nearly frozen so we decided to get off and get a taxi back, when we came down the stairs the driver was gone, still no idea where he went too. In short, this tour would be great on a warm clear summers day, but if you get motion sickness or have a delicate stomach Id avoid, also have a back up plan if your stranded in a location you don't know.

We did the changing of the guard walking tour with Julia which was excellent. On the first bus, the pre recorded audio your was not great but on the second bus we had a live guide (Steve, I believe) who was excellent. Definitely try to take a bus with a live person. Overall we had a great time!

My family and I bought the ticket and took the ride on a recent trip to London. It was a great investment, allowing us to see the attractions of the city and explore them at our own pace.
We joined a walking tour of Buckingham Palace with super-guide Big Steve - he is a true phenomenon, going the extra mile to ensure that his clients see hidden treasures off the main tourist trek. Who has ever heard of the site of the Embassy of the State of Texas, for instance? Steve is well versed in history, and enthusiastically shares what he knows.
The highlight of the tour was the changing of the guard by the Household Cavalry. Big Steve knew the drill, of course, and made sure that we positioned ourselves to get amazing photos and videos of the guards that other tourists missed.
I thoroughly recommend this bus tour. Big Steve made it even more worthwhile.

The bus tour was very nice. We did not wait long for any bus and very much enjoyed the river cruise at the end of the day. The Jack the Ripper walking tour was a highlight of the day. We very much enjoyed the live guide and hope live guides are put back on the buses as opposed to recorded commentary. Big Bus here us…. Live guides cannot be replaced by scratchy recordings.

Our family of five purchased online tour tickets for this yesterday. Once we arrived at the pick up location it was clear there was a significant problem. A large group was waiting for this tour bus to arrive and waiting and waiting. In the meantime multiple of their rivals buses went past looking spacious and appealing. Once this one turned up it was packed full. I spoke to the driver whom told me that they have a significant problem with getting their fleet staffed so they are not running all their buses. We stayed on it for perhaps a fifth of the circuit but stop after stop showed that their ticket holders were facing long waits to join the few buses running. Don’t do it. For our group it was like a $180 tube ride.

We pre booked the big bus tours hop on hop off tickets before visiting London as the tickets was cheaper if we pre booked on line. There was 4 routes you could take depending on where you wanted to go. We mostly used the red route and the tour guides was brilliant with loads of information about London. Unfortunately some road closures disrupted our plans but this was out of the big bus tours hands. If you are planning to sit at the open top part of the bus you will definitely need some warm clothes 🥶. There was other tour buses operating it the area but the big bus tour buses seemed to be more frequent so you wasn’t waiting long at the stops. We did get stuck in traffic but for us it was an opportunity to take in all that was around. The bus drives was friendly and helped with questions we had about our journey.

We bought these tickets because we had one day to “see the sights” and also because our flight arrived at 6:30am from the US. We thought this would be perfect to sit and relax and get off as we wanted, to cut down on the walking with jet lag. We got on at Kings Cross and there were so many detours due to construction it took almost 45 minutes to get to the stops by the river. We decided to get off and walk and see some more and get back on at a different stop on a different color line. Well that stop was closed and that wasn’t made clear. Then we never found another stop, so just used the underground to go where we wanted next. We are pretty seasoned travelers and I think about how they might have been very stressful for someone who isn’t used to a big city. I just feel like some kind of announcement system would have been helpful as we planned our stops. At least our son got in a little nap!

We got on a bus with a chap called Phil doing a lively and interesting commentary. This part of the journey was 5*. He had something to say about every street we drove down and he kept us engaged. Sadly he got off 2/3 of the way round and we had to switch to the recorded commentary - which very disappointing in comparison. That part of the journey was 2* (basically a very expensive journey round London on a red bus). Apparently on the day we travelled only one of the ten buses working had live commentary - that's a rip off (and we were lucky).
Also for no apparent reason: our bus skipped a section of the route going straight from the London Eye to Westminster, and missing out 3 or 4 stops, so we were "short changed" as well.

The on bus experience is good, if a bit flat on the humor of the patter. But the app is useless. Locating a stop should be easy but it doesn’t work, even when the app doesn’t crash. And forget imputing you’re ticket for a more personal experience, it just treats everyone like they want to buy a ticket. Worthless. After paying for the premium+, it didn’t feel premium at all. Next time I’ll look into one of the competing lines.

Went to London with my Wife and 2 children aged 8 and 11. Booked the Big Bus Tour Hop on and Hop off service. Paid £94. When we got on the bus the driver was rude, didn’t scan our tickets and just barked at us all to “Just Sit Down!” My daughter even commented on how rude the driver was. The headphone sockets didn’t work and we had to move 3 times to find some that did and then the audio commentary was very poor, just announcing each stop and filling in with music. I have experienced other tour companies and the commentary has always been informative, factual and fun. I have since complained and the customer service has been awful. They have offered to extend the ticket, but I am not returning to London again in the future and also offered me to transfer it to another city around the world which I have no chance of visiting. Then they offered a woefully unacceptable percentage as a refund. I will never use this service again and wouldn’t recommend.

Decided to take a tour of London to find out more about the city we live in.
We had the bus almost to ourselves so it felt like a private tour. Our guide Phil was great and funny, his enthusiasm was infectious and you could tell he was passionate about London and all of its history. We now have some great facts to wow guests with when they come to stay with us!
As a local it was great to see London from a different perspective, getting to view the incredible architecture from a new vantage point.
The river cruise that's included was well worth it, although quite short, again great to see the city from a different perspective.
The member of boat crew giving commentary was very funny and we learnt even more facts about the various buildings

Misleading and very poor service with no customer after service help what so ever! With Russian guests we specifically wanted a tour with Russian commentary which this offers on all their leaflets and even behind every seat (tune to channel 7) But once on the bus there are only 5 languages instead of the 12 they promise. Russian is not one. Our guests understood nothing and as another reviewer said may as well have taken a regular bus. Their three tickets alone cost a whopping £87. The advertised tour of 2 hrs 30 minutes lasted 30 minutes before we were told to get off and take another bus. We did not bother as none of their buses had a Russian commentary. The drivers just shrugged their shoulders. When we complained via email this was ignored so we complained via letter and copied this to Trading Standards. The email reply was that we had bought our tickets at the London Eye ticket office so if we wanted any kind of refund we would have to contact them!! Like it was not their bus tour...?! So Don't bother with this rubbish company and take any other tour but theirs. Angry fed up customer.

We bought tickets at our hotel and the bus driver said they were invalid and needed to be redone. At the tower stop the driver and his associate had a fight about using the tickets scanning machine. We then went to another stop and waited for the crews to switch. No one can explain how long it will take, when you will leave, when another bus will come
Skip it. Use the city bus and pay a fraction and you will get the same views at
Fraction of the price.

The routes of the busses are great. When you go in the busy season (as we did), you sometimes have to be a bit smart if you want to sit on the upper deck. Look at the bus coming and if necessary let one pass you by. Usually there are plenty of busses so the wait for the next one isn’t too long.

Having the walking tours included in your ticket is something you should take advantage of for sure! We did the Changing of the Guards tour and the Jack the Ripper tour, both with Julia and both were excellent.

That’s also my biggest comment to the Big Bus company - I’ve done other tours with Big Bus (for example in Hong Kong) where there was live commentary and while I’m sure a lot of time was put into the recorded audio - NOTHING beats a live tour guide. It’s day and night difference for us tourists.

Please make sure you have actual guides on the busses - this would lead me to give 6 out of 5 stars :)

Had a terrible and traumatic experience on the bus as a tourist who had been eagerly looking forward to the tour .
The driver of my tour bus failed to exercise the requisite safety standards when he moved the bus while we were still climbing to find a seat .

I fell backwards, broke my phone screen and my nail!
Days later I was still experiencing pains from that fall .
Prevented me from undertaking a number of my planned activities.

What’s worse? The Supervisor I complained to about the incident pretended to take my details and work on it but didn’t bother . He probably threw my details away .

The company is yet to resolve my complaints. Hopefully they expedite action on it because I’m looking at taking the matter all the way through.

Still one of the best ways to see London ! A day ticket allows you on two routes, the RED and the BLUE , with unlimited times on and off the bus. It also includes a river cruise from Westminster up to Tower bridge. If you sit upstairs you see so much more of London's skyline and architecture and the tour commentary lets you know whats available to see at each stop. I found the commentary upbeat, informative and entertaining. The staff were very helpful and were able to print out tickets from my mobile phone bar codes and offer advice regarding the phone app. The phone app was great as it shows real time where the buses are so you can plan when to be at the bus stop and also see the route the bus is taking. My only suggestion to improve on this already great service would be a slightly bigger map showing more of London's great attractions so you can explore more on foot. We bought our Bus Tickets as part of a package with another attraction which made it very reasonable.

The walking tours and live commentary during the night tour were fantastic. The guides (Julia and Steve) were great. Full of interesting anecdotes as well as historical reference. The hop on / hop off bus ride is a great way to explore a new city.

Waited 15 minutes at first stop to start, bus full on top so had to sit in the bottom which was very hot, every bus was very full while most of the competitors buses had open seats on top. After a few stops and later in the day(4:00) buses were even more full and would skip stops because their was no room for more passengers so we missed our stop and had to walk an extra half mile, plus all company’s use the same stops and we waited for our bus while all the other company’s had at least 2 or 3 buses com to that stop. Advice use one of the other companys

The recorded commentary was absolutely hilarious and informing. There was an option to get off the bus and do a walking tour. Our guide was Julia and she took us through the City of London and shared great stories about the city’s history. Julia was a great conversationalist and even recommended a great restaurant! Would definitely tour with her and Big Bus again!!!

The person we bought our ticket from said the bus ticket was valid till 2pm the following day, however the ticket says 11.59pm the same day. The recorded commentary is ridiculously lacking content. Very expensive for a seat on a slow bus with poor information.

Very disappointed. Visited this weekend with our 7 year olds. Chose to do a tour bus to save their little legs. They was so excited. Bought tickets and joined the bus at tower bridge and got off at Buckingham palace. From their we waited over 40 mins for another bus and still one didn’t arrive. When you are only there for a short time you can’t be hanging round waiting for buses for them not to show. Then obviously the tickets are sold that they are for use over 24hrs. But on Sunday the first bus only starts at 9am from stop 1 so by the time it would get to where you might need it, say stop 17 could be 1-2hours later. So basically we paid £96 for a bus ride from tower bridge to Buckingham palace. Sickening. Save your money and use the tube, or do some research and see that some places are definitely walkable.

The commentary was very limited and in an attempt to make itself relevant to younger generations totally missed the mark on providing any real information about London. The majority of the tour was spent listening to the same 5 or 6 songs on repeat.
The number of buses was also very limited and at one stage we had to wait 40 minutes for a bus on the blue route. Which in turn meant we missed the opportunity to make the river cruise. We also joined a bus near our hotel on 3 occasions only to find out that the bus terminated 2 stops later and we had to get off again and wait on the next bus. Given we only used it for 2 days we were either very unlucky or this is common practice.
As someone who has experienced bus tours in many European cities this one was by far the worst.

We were waiting for about one hour at the bus stop, when the bus arrived, it passed by us without stopping and continue its route.
Two other people were waiting too, we all waved at the driver but he didn't bother to stop. When I complained to the company, they gave me some lame excuses like "maybe the bus had some issues". I think the driver could have stopped to let us know, or a representative should have been there to give us some explanations.

Of course, they refuse to refund the ticket and say they are available for 1 year. There are many other bus tours companies in London, just don't go for that one.

The audio guide tells virtually nothing about the sights and sounds of this wonderful city. We’ve done many tours and enjoyed the potted history and anecdotes about buildings along the route. This guide was mainly old pop music and silly chatter. A hugely wasted opportunity in such a fabulous city.

The Big Bus tours are nice for older people and children who can't walk long distances, but you don't get to see much. Depending on traffic, the bus could either be stuck somewhere for ages or zoom by the things you want to see. They've moved to a recorded system rather than pay a tour guide (who could answer questions); the recording is hokey, but informative. Headphones are available at the entry of the bus. Tip: Start early, as the bus fills up later in the afternoon. We saw people unable to get on the bus at all as it was completely full, meaning they had to wait another twenty minutes for the next one.

This tour was absolutely perfect for my friends and I and gave our tired feet a much needed break. The commentary was lively and filled with music breaks which helped lift our spirits. Busses ran regularly and we were able to sit on the top level which we really enjoyed.

We like hop on hop off tours. We always learn some details about the area that we don't know, regardless of how many times we visited. This tour was weak. We drove for blocks without an explanation of what we were seeing or having buildings identified. The tour was designed to entertain with basic humor versus provide information. If you are looking for transportation around the city with lite information, this is the tour for you.

Allowed far too many people on the bus at 1 time. It was exceptionally dangerous. We were herded on to a full bus, people standing downstairs and on the stairs, it was a rainy day so floors slippery. There was no less than 6 guides standing at the first stop on the red route but not 1 checked that the bus was already full before ushering around 20 people us included onto an already full bus. Awful customer service. We couldn't hear the tour because we couldn't get a seat...total waste of money

We got a multi attraction ticket for the big bus, the london eye and the dungeons via last minute. Com.
Had a great time on the eye and at the dungeons, leaving the Big Bus for our last afternoon.
It said very clearly that to get on the Big Bus we had to show our London Eye ticket which would be scanned.
Refused to let us on and told us we had to go all the way back across town to the London Eye to get our Big Bus ticket. When we bought our tickets initially there was no option on the last minute. Com to print our bus ticket.
I contacted last minute. Com and after spending 40 mins waiting to get through, was told by the rep that I should be able to use my London eye ticket which doubled up for the Big Bus. When I told her that this was clearly not the case, she put me on hold for 10 mins, before coming back to me to tell me that unfortunately I would need to get the ticket off the London eye for the bus.
We had not the time to do this as it was our last afternoon so abandoned it all together.
Last minute and Big bus need to get their act together and either enable one to print the Big bus ticket off at time of purchase or let one double up as it clearly says on the ticket.
What if you want to do the bus trip before the Eye?
Have requested a partial refund but won't get back the 2 hours wasted and the disappointment!

I was skeptical about the Big Bus Tour at first but I was pleasantly surprised. I found it to be a great way to get a quick overview of all the tourist sites in the city and we could get off and explore those of most interest. The busses were frequent so there is not a very long wait at any stop. The guide was recorded, but was very well done and available in multiple languages. The River Cruise was a bonus and offered a unique perspective of the city. This was worth the investment even if you only have a few hours.

We decided to get the big bus tour tickets for London since we got the Paris Pass for our leg in Paris that also included 3 days of the big bus tour in the their package.

We found that the London big bus was well organized and covers lots of ground. It was pretty easy to understand the map and use the app. We really liked that we could use the boat to cross the river as an option which allowed for a nice change of scenery. The worker on the pier was very helpful. The worker at Buckingham Palace not so much. We noticed alot of the earphone jacks on the chairs often didnt work so if you like to listen to the historical parts you might not find a spot available. We really wanted to enjoy that part so we were disappointed. We waited for busses about 20 mins each time.

In comparison to the big bus tour in Paris, we completely utilized every aspect of the busses and tour routes. None of the earphone jacks had issues and the busses came super frequently. No more than a 7 min wait throughout our 3 days in paris.

I would use big bus again in Paris, but I don't think in London. The London underground is just super easy to use and conveniently located in all areas throughout London. The only benefit of big bus would be the historical information but if the ear phone jacks don't work......

On a quiet Sunday morning the tour was promising and a great way to get your bearings, however, the family price should be more like £25. It is insanely over prices. There was no live commentary and later on in the day the buses were rammed and it was impossible to get a seat. Just like a normal bus. You can only listen to the recorded commentary if you're seated and plugged in so it's very disappointing. The sales people are constantly trying to get more people on board even when the buses dont have the capacity to provide a good service.

We purchased a 3 day tour for the two of us that cost £100. They didn’t tell us that they had a reduced schedule on New Year’s Eve day and a re-direct routes on New Year’s Day. We waited for over an hour the bus never came to the bus stop. They advertised that the bus will come every 15 minutes which was a lie. We had planned the day to do some sightseeing and do New Years Eve stuff that day, but our day quickly ruined because of the big bus hop on hop off never came to the bus stop.
I chatted online with the big bus tour associate, and they told me they will open a ticket to resolve this issue. I have been back from London fro a couple of days now, and still haven’t heard anything from big bus hop on hop of bus.Do not use this hop on hop off big bus they will take your money and will not deliver their service!

We haven’t been to London (or the UK) for around eleven years and so bought two-day tickets to reacquaint ourselves with the various ‘tourist locations’. The first day we started on the Blue Bus route (West London, from elegant Kensington Palace, and bustling Harrods, to stylish Notting Hill and famous Paddington station.) and it was a great 1½ hours with a fun, if somewhat slightly cringy at times, commentary.

We then changed to the Red Bus route (Central London from Belgravia in the west, to Tower Bridge in the east.) This route would be around 2½ hours if you don’t get off but we hopped off at Westminster Bridge to go on our 30-mins cruise from Westminster Pier to Tower Pier. It was a lovely way to see both sides of the River in a leisurely way with excellent (and funny) commentary.

We went for a walk, stopped for some lunch, and hopped back on again later in the afternoon for a final trip back to Oxford Street.

We had hoped to use the buses to get to our London Eye trip on the second day but, unfortunately, due to various road closures for the St. Patrick’s Day parade, it was quicker to walk there. This meant that we didn’t get the full benefit of the two-day pass (due to no fault of the company) and we managed to hop back on during the afternoon.

This is an excellent way to get to know the various areas of London and learn some interesting facts along the way. We were totally amazed at how the large buses move around some of the very narrow streets and the road works everywhere.

Travelled all the way from York to London to do the Big Bus tour with my brother and sister for my birthday. The app stated a bus comes every 20 minutes to each stop. We started at London Bridge and waited half and hour with no bus showing. I could see on the app that no buses were moving towards us either. We got the tube to Waterloo and try and hop-on there. Waited 20 minutes and then a bus arrived. We got on but there was no guide, only the bus driver who didn't say anything so we went upstairs and took a seat. The bus went off route and we were stuck in traffic with no sightseeing/tour for 40 minutes however no one told us this until I asked another customer on the bus why we weren't being told any facts, they said it was because of road closures. After 40 minutes of being sat on the bus with no tour/commentary taking place, we ended up back at Waterloo?! Paid £35 each to sit on a bus, in traffic, in silence for 40 minutes. Was so disappointing and a complete waste of time. The Big Bus app and/or bus driver should've informed us of the disturbance to save us being sat in traffic for 40 minutes doing nothing. What a rubbish birthday.

We took the Big Bus tour August 13th. The tour was a near total disappointment. When you get on the bus you receive headphones that plug in so you can hear commentary. The commentary was barely informative at best and often you are just listening to filler music. You will have limited views of many landmarks and no view of Buckingham palace at all which came as a surprise. For approximately 50 USD this tour is a classic tourist trap rip off. Much better to walk around to a few of the landmarks for free.

Really enjoyed the tour bus. It was a very pleasant surprise that they provided free head phones so we could hear the pre-recorded tour guide. The buses were very frequent but very crowded, do not expect to always get a top, outdoor seat. The red tour was great for the main visitor attractions. The App worked very well but the route planner was confusing on the app so I would recommend people to pick up a paper route plan as it clearly shows the route

River cruise was the highlight of the tour! Best way to see London if you either there for a short stay or long stay. Bus tour took us to all of the points of interest, we hopped on at Trafalgar Square and then got off at Tower Bridge to get onto the River Cruise which was absolutely fantastic. Our Host was not only informative but also a really good jovial personality which made the trip so much more enjoyable. We got off at Westminster and walked over the bridge to the London Eye. We literally got our tickets from the booth and went straight on, no queues. We then decided to head to Knightsbridge via the tube from Waterloo station (quick 8minute trip) and then decided to try and get the alternate route back to Trafalgar Square. Unfortunately it was after 6pm and the tour did not operate on the line2 route which was quite disappointing however it was a blessing in disguise as we walked all the way back and the weather was perfect and we got to see more sights. Overall it was a very pleasant day sightseeing, ticks all the boxes

We did not have a great experience and don't recommend this tour. Firstly, when we arrived at the bus stop the ticket seller told us that the London Eye was fully booked that day. He gave us the option to go on it the next day but we weren't going to be in London so he told us to apply for a refund but I still don't know how to do so. My email has not been responded to, two weeks later.

The commentary on the bus is very low-grade, full of ridiculous attempts at humour and does not cover much detail. It was out of sync with the tour as well so was covering sights afte we had passed them. It was the worst commentary on any of the hop on hop off tours I've done in other cities.

The only highlight of the day was the Thames Cruise. We saw so much more, and learnt a lot more detail from the informative, humorous commentary from the captain of the boat. Thank goodness for one silver lining.

Overall, very disappointing, I would not do this again.

Almost the whole time was spent waiting in traffic or waiting for people to get on/off. Most of the time was spent listening to little clips of songs, we literally drove right past the houses of parliament, big ben, and westminster abbey (red line, clockwise) and it said nothing, it was just playing songs. I really couldn't believe that, I am not sure if the driver or someone made a mistake or if there was a glitch.

The recorded commentary, when it does work, was very badly timed, it would say things like "to your right you will see _____, where _______ happened" and you would look to your right and see no sign of what they were talking about, I assume it was a timing issue. But they would roll through one thing after the next and I wouldn't see where most or any of it actually was.

Finally, while trying to hop on to continue the tour, I apparently got on the bus going the wrong way, and repeated part of the tour and had to figure out how to get back. When I got off the bus I saw no sign of "clockwise" or "anticlockwise" etc.

Very easy way to travel round London City. Good value for money because we had a river cruise included which was quite a perk to the trip and the children loved it! We had a very attentive driver to all his passengers at the end of the day. He made sure everyone got to their destination of choice and was very kind, friendly and helpful. His name is Trevor Williams (Snoop Dog). Keep a look out - he’s the best! Thank you for putting the icing on the cake to our trip ☺️.

This was definitely not worth the money paid. The commentary that is played through the headphones was lackluster to say the least. It told you what stop you were at when you were already there and gave maybe 1 piece of information about it but that was it. Otherwise it played the same few songs over and over. On other hop on hop off buses I’ve been on, the drivers provide commentary and act as somewhat of tour guides throughout the ride but that was not the case here.

I will say the app was helpful in knowing when the next bus was coming and how close you were to a stop but that was the best thing about it.

At first it was great. Loved the stops and the audio recordings. But it ended with a bad experience. When we got to stop one we had to get off and the driver said there was another red line right behind him. It turned out he sat there for a long time used as a changing studio of some sort for guys doing a video. That was fine but when I went to ask if the tours were over for the day(it was 5pm) he kept “shooing” me away very rudely. I guess because he was parked there no other BBus stopped to pickup? We waited over 30 minutes and no other bus stopped so after a long day we ended up
Walking back to our hotel -a 45 minute walk. That drivers rudeness just really ruined the whole thing.

Booked tickets that included pass to London Eye. The eye was down to technical issues and advised we contact Big Bus Tours to get new tickets for a different. The only available contact was via chat. Chat was extremely unresponsive, and we have not been able to rebook or get a refund at this point. The tickets also were supposed to include a live guide, but none of busses we were on had anything but recordings. Enjoyed the river cruise.

Rode the Hop On, Hop Off bus through London. Great way to initially explore London, especially when it is raining. Bought a three day ticket would most likely only buy a one day ticket next time. Though did also do the Jack the Ripper walking tour that was included with my tickets.

The routes are nice, but you wait a long time between stops. Our bus had no working sound, so know one knew where we were, or what the points of attraction were, and we missed our stop where we had tickets to the museum. The staff was indifferent, and said we should just get off, wait 20 minutes for a new bus, and ride for an hour back around to the museum. Everyone on the bus was confused and upset. Other bus staff was friendly and helpful on other occasions.

The bus tour was good and the rep who sold us the tickets in the street was fab. But I was horrified at the price considering that due to covid you can only do one basic red route instead of 3 and they have restricted down the stops you can hop on and off at to just 4.
I would defo recommend this excursion for this price on normal service but with all these reductions (buses don't start till 10 now) due to covid, I would have thought it be wiser and more sustainable to offer a reduction until service resumes as normal, for the reputation of the business more than anything. Bit of cheak to charge full price and not offer full service.
Buseses clean, staff wonderful, some of the audio slots couldn't change to other languages aside from English. (FYI the Trip in Cardiff , Madrid & Barcelona is roughly £20 cheaper pp.)

We were lucky enough to have Steve (live tour guide) come on our bus this morning and he’s absolutely incredible and funny! Miss having live guides on these busses. It makes the experience much more personable. Had a much better time with a live guide in London than listening to the audio only on the Big Bus Paris tour.

The worst bus tour ever! Pre recorded commentary which was aimed at a child in way of how it was delivered, all fake voices and ‘beep beep’. No real history/facts about the points of interest, missed certain places on the route out altogether. If all you want is a drive through central London then this is the ‘tour’ for you. Customer services are just as bad, obviously can’t defer from the script. Received a £9.36 refund from the cost of £62.40. Apparently the recorded commentary was updated to this new one after customer feedback, would have hated to see what it was originally like. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

You have to wait a long time for the busses as the traffic in London is very slow moving. Therefor you don't get to see much if you don't want to sit still in traffic the whole time. But the concept is good, as, if you sit on top, you get to see London from a different perspective. The commentators ought to stop trying to be funny, it is very tiresome to listen to.

Driver kept taking us round in circles, missing out major tourist attractions. Driver didn’t tell us anything, it was only when people complained to him that he told us there were road closures. Nobody knew where he was taking us next so we couldn’t plan where to get off or know what we would see next. When I complained I was told I should have been checking online! I paid for a service which in my eyes meant I should have been advised of changes alter all it was big red bus that broke the contract with me not the other way round. It was awful, such a waste of money and time. Never go on one again with this company.

First time we have been with this company, usually go with City Sightseeing, they are far superior. The recorded commentary didn't tell you anything of importance and was full of stupid jokes and inane music. Luckily we knew alot of the places along the way, but visitors to this country missed out so much. A total waste of £82.

Our trip was disappointing due to delays, lack of information, and poor coneectivity with commentary. The worst was that we did not get to the stop planned, and had to get alternative transport to be in time for a theatre performance.
HOWEVER Big Bus have responded well to our complaint, recognising it was their fault, and offered a replacement ticket.
The city cruise part was excellent, and I would recommend that.

We do hop on hop off buses in all new cities. Great way to get a good overview of a city. My problem with this one was the bad naration. It was full of stupid humor in place of more detailed history and did a poor job of directing you to which building they were talking about.

We were fortunate to have Chris for live narration during a hop on hop off bus tour of London. Informative, personable, and thoroughly entertaining. Much better than the recorded narration we had for a different portion of our tour.

We have used hop on and hop off buses in various cities and used different ones in London.
This one was really expensive, if we had had longer we would of done all 4 routes on offer and the boat tour, but time didn't allow for this.
This tour was really weak. They missed lots of information out on really important parts of London like the Cenotaph and other War memorials and more music than chatting going on.
Wont be using this one again.

First visit to London for my grandchildren aged 5 and 9 . This was a great way to see all the sites . Although it was hip on and off we stayed on for nearly the whole tour, getting off at Buckingham Palace to see it from the front .
A bonus on our tour was we have a tour guide rather than the headphones . Her name was Tiffany and she did a fantastic job . She was extremely knowledgeable and our grandchildren learned much more than they would have done with the headphones .

Mixed feelings as very positive is the audio tour, for once it’s not just historical talks, they make it funny as well which is great if you travel as me with three teenagers, perfect mix between informative and fun stories. Less positive is first that our bus skip one part of the tour due to heavy traffic jam, well welcome in big cities as London, you always have traffic jam, and then lots of seating place had broken or inaudible audio button, so you always have to move to one place to the other to finally find a good one. For such high price, it’s for me not really worthwhile but don’t know if it was specific to Big Bus or same for all sightseeing bus tours.

Fantastic way to see London. Straight forward easy access. There are always helpers near the stops to guide travellers. It was disappointing that access to Buckingham Palace was unavailable and therefore this landmark was not seen during the tour.

Everyone was extremely helpful,I am not carrying cash so couldn't tip, but the below need/deserve recognition. On Tuesday 6th September these guys below were especially helpful to myself and others..

Nick did the walking tour and took us to see changing of the guard, was very informative and helpful.

The guy who is from Tunisia who worked outside the Marriott stop 13, all day he was so helpful to me with my hopping on and off, and made sure I got on the evening bus first as I arrived early. He went over and beyond for how I could get home with travel options after the tour ended also.

The driver for the night tour who is from Jamaica, very nice guy!! Very helpful also.

The two boat drivers, they were extremely funny, insightful and energetic. They provided a 15/10 service, could not fault them. Extremely professional.

We selected Big bus because it was the one with a brochure in our hotel lobby. When we went to the nearest stop we waited and never saw a bus, but we saw multiple competing buses. Still, because we knew the pricing and had familiarized ourselves with the route we’ walked to the London Eye stop to buy a ticket. During the three days we used the service we found buses to be infrequent and again several competitors would have two and three buses come by in same time period.

On the last service we were told that the bus will take us and we waited for an hour and no bus was willing to take the people. Every bus told us that the trip had ended and we were left hanging there. However, the Driver Brian from another route was very helpful and stayed to find a bus who could finish the route. During the day everything was great.

We had a great experience. The round trips were long due to traffic but after taking the public bus, they were stuck in traffic too. The guided walking tours were the highlight of the company. Loved the Changing of the Guard at 10:00am since our guide was informative and knew exactly where to be for the best experience. She also gave an informative tour at 1;00 around the financial district with an expansive view from a 15th floor via lift. There were staff at most of the stops who were helpful and friendly. I wish there were live guides on the buses since the prerecorded commentary was not very informative, repetitive and annoying. Big bus tours also gave us the winter map with incorrect bus times. The rides went until 6:00pm when the brochure only said until 4:30. We learned this on day 2 so missed out a bit.

Don't waste your money! I have been on a few hop on hop off bus tours and this was by far the worst. 1st you get on the bus and there are no seats so you stand not being able to hear any commentary because it's all recorded. After about 6 stops with still more people getting on we got off and connected to another route. This time we were lucky to get a seat so now we get to experience the tour. Well forget it, the narration was the worst! It's more like a comedy show with commercials. When they did talk about a site they never said what side of the bus to look out so you had no idea what building or site they were talking about. We were hoping to get off and go into the British Museum for an hour but it was so slow we ended up staying on for our next destination the Tower of London. We got off, had a quick lunch and went on the river cruise. Now that was excellent, full live commentary that was funny, informative and friendly. When we got off that we walked around a few sites and then went to get back on a bus to go towards our hotel and they were finished for the day. Last bus was at 6:30 on a summer evening. So much for 24 hours. So basically we got a bus ride from our hotel to the Tower of London and thankfully the River Cruise. It was our last day in England and my husband said after don't ever talk me into another Hop on Hop off! So save your money and find your own transport to the sights, you'll enjoy your day more than we did.

Bought a ticket on day of travel, not warned of any issues. Checked service problems on the web no issues. On arrival at the departure point found out all departures from that stop were cancelled. Big bus agent at the departure point told us to come back tomorrow, not an option for us. Walked 1.5 miles to anther stop and put on the wrong bus by the Big Bus agent. The commentary was very poor, the promised stopping advice never materialised though we were advised that we should stay seated till we got the advice. Very poor

It was raining all weekend but the big bus tour didn’t kill the mood. We did the river cruise and the night tour. The night tour hosted by Phil ( and Winston driving ) was really great, the amazing commentary, Phil’s enthusiasm, knowledge and entertaining energy made the night. Totally recommended!

We had the pleasure of riding the big bus tour with Wikipedia Will as our guide. He did an amazing job describing all the landmarks and history behind it. My son (7) was paying close attention to Will and learned a lot from him! We were only in town for 2 days and the big bus definitely let us enjoy the city (by hopping on and off) and we also were able to ride the boat tours down the river. Definitely recommended for family. Great experience that we will never forget. Thank you Will & bus driver!!

Spent the afternoon doing the bus tour with our 5 year old daughter, all of us loved it. Nice and convenient, loads of easy stops to jump on and off at key locations, and with an informative audio guide. Very good for children, staff were helpful, friendly and knowledgeable. Special mention here to the river cruise which was possibly the highlight of the day. Nice bonus to have this option, fascinating view of the city encapsulating the history of the river and the landmarks that grew around it. Top marks to the tour guides. Would definitely recommend to families if you're thinking of a full day's entertainment!

We visited London with friends last Saturday , decided that the best way to see city was to take a tour bus, we met this lovely gentlemen Othman at Victoria station. He approached us with the smile, made us feel really welcome, took his time to explain the tour, because English is not our first language. I hope this email will find him, me and my friends wanna say thank to you Othman you made our visit in London absolutely amazing,we really enjoyed Big Bus tour.

We are just back from an absolutely incredible 4 days away in the capital. We travel to london every year, usually for Christmas but this year we mixed things up and travelled during the summer. A few years ago the red route buses were filled with live tour guides and we always had the best experiences on these specific tours. In recent years there are fewer and fewer, and despite the recordings being very informative they are simply not as personal and interactive as a live guides. We were lucky enough to have Phil show us around this year, and even luckier to have hopped on his bus again the very same day, so all in all we got the whole red route with his live tour and it was incredible. Such a lovely funny man and he is a credit to the company. As somebody who uses this company every year, I urge to company to hire more live guides as they really do make a difference. Thank you for a great experience.

This is a great way for Londoners to see London. The great city is alway changing and the best way to see it is by open top bus on a lovely sunny morning. The flexible nature of the of the trip meant that you could board the bus in different places. This was a great day out .

My wife and I enjoyed our hop on hop off experience. However, the most engaged and satisfying experience was the unexpected invitation to the changing of the guard tour with a young lady named Julia. She was well well informed and made our visit all the more satisfying!
Such additional tour opportunities would definitely put big boss well ahead of the crowd in terms of competitors of offerings to tourists like myself and my wife.

I have done all the london bus tours and this is by far the worst. Despite using 3 different buses, not one had a live guide on. The recorded commentary was terrible, basically two people chatting in a very irritating childish way. We passed several points of interest that were completely overlooked.
Not only that but none of their claims regardinding covid safety were observed. I saw no cleaning at any point, and one bus was crammed to full capacity. Last August on the Original Sightseeing Tour the bus was being disinfected at certain points around the route, and seating capacity was limited.
I will never use this company again.

The views from the top of the bus were lovely, however the audio discriptionn of what we were seeing was terrible. It included what I suppose was supposed to be funny dialogue between several characters which had little to do with what we were actually seeing and caused them to miss many of the cities points of interest. It would say something was coming up but never indicate where so you could look at it. At one point it started raining and all the people on top has to come down to the lower deck, that was fine thought there weren't enough seats. The bus stopped at every stop and let more people on even though no one got off. It was overcrowded and unsafe.

Today we went on a big bus hop on hop off tour with River Cruise, we were having trouble finding the bus stop but we suddenly see the bus coming towards us nowhere near a bus stop and we asked Scott the driver where we needed to collect it he very kindly drove to the nearest bus stop and picked us up there which we thought was really lovely of him. When we got upstairs we were greeted by the lovely Chloe she was very friendly and very informative and kept us entertained on the bus. It is the hottest day of the year today but Chloe kept her cool in the searing heat. Would highly recommend this and it was a great thing to do and be socially distanced during lockdown.

The narrated tour recording was basic at best. We purchased this tour, it was closed, so we bought the other one, (CIty Sightseeing) which was so much better. When I was told I could not get a refund from this one, (even though stops were closed and we could not get on) I decided to use it anyway. It was boring and did not give as many details as the other tour. I recommend the other one for a better experience.

Great tour with plenty of stops and 2 routes for you to choose from. Commentary was prerecorded and had lots of"cheeky British humor. Didn't get a chance to do the river cruise since the last boarding is at 4:30pm. Only complaint I really had was that the buses stop running around 5-6pm.

I was quite dissapointed. The bus let me out on some middle station between Picadily Circus and Trafalgar square, and when i waited on the same spot to go on the bus again, the next one didn't even stop there! then i went to trafalgar and had tried chasing the bus, but the bus driver wouldn't open the door (he was about 100m forward of the stop, waiting in line, stopped), so i had to go back to the bus stop and wait at least 25min for another bus! in between i saw 3 citysightseeing buses and 2 TOOT buses. I am really disapointed.
When the bus finally came it was so full (obviously because you have too little buses) that there wasn't any space to sit!

River cruise was fun

The audio commentary was not very informative. Heavy with jokes and entertainment. Many times of just music and not talking about what we were seeing. Very disappointed in the communication. On the brochure it shows stops, yet the red buses do not stop at all red stops. No where was this explained. Bus driver was frustrated, passengers were frustrated. We tried to get off at 2 stops to get on the blue bus. Driver ignored the bell, then when we asked he said he is not supposed to stop at those stops. At the end of the day buses change color and passengers were shifted off the bus without help to find the bus they needed. Drivers had no support and we were all confused. Barely made the right bus to get to our tube.

Don’t waste your money! I bought tickets for this tour after reading very good reviews about it! My experience was totally different and I wouldn’t recommend this tour to anyone!

Busses are so busy, you’ll be lucky to get a seat on the open section of the too deck.
If you hop off and then try to hop on again at the same stop.. it doesn’t guarantee the driver will actually continue the route! We got off at stop 19 after 2 hrs for lunch then on again and the driver just took us back to stop 1!! No warning or anything.

Waste of money!

Just thought this bus tour was 'OKish' You don't get anywhere fast as the roads are absolutely gridlocked. Then to get onto the river cruise at stop 20 then instructed to get off the boat and put out at stop 17 therefore you repeat some of the route again ... no thank you. I would advise anyone else to only buy a ticket if you planned on using it for two days as you just won't have the time to stop off anywhere on one day and If you have the time and mobility my advice would be to use your own map and walk between the landmarks yourself.

We booked onto Big Bus Tours London Hop-On Hop-Off tour on 9th February, the day of Storm Ciara. The weather was ok in the morning, and we were able to enjoy use of the buses from Kings Cross down to Tower Bridge and then back on to near Westminster. However after lunch when we tried to get back on the buses to continue our tour, we discovered that the service had been completed suspended for the rest of the day, even though public buses and other tour companies were running and the bad weather was abating. I'm pleased to say that we have just received a full refund for all our tickets are promised (and I can understand why the safety decision was made to stop the service, though I think it would have been possible to restart the buses later in the day).

Julia's walking tour was amazing. She gave interesting historical facts, had a very positive energy and a good sense of humour. Great way to see the city if you are visiting for a short period of time

commentary was pointless. In a city drenched with history, this tour was abysmal in educating a tourist. The recordings were also hard to hear with headphones (ie poor audio quality). Additionally, the blue bus line had 4 buses going & the red line had a gazillion buses. Had to wait 30 min to transition from red to blue to get to hotel. With years of travel & enjoying many hop/on, hop/off buses, this was the worst experience ever. Save your money & time.

The tour, with audio guide, and route itself was very good. However, when it came to getting on and off the bus it was a disaster.
There was no queuing system and although it is not your companies fault that other passengers were so ignorant to try and push past myself, husband and two children, I do feel that having a competent member of staff at each stop or a system in place with the driver would be beneficial. There were people getting off and on at the same time resulting in tension, stress and a feeling of panic. Unfortunately my little boy panicked, telling me afterwards that he felt scared, tried to rush up the stairs, tripped and grazed his shin.
Such a shame as I have used your company in various countries worldwide and have been impressed with the professional service; unfortunately this was not the case in London.

We used the bus when ride London as on, there was lot of road closures and many of the other operators weren’t running.
