Money well spent for us. Recommendation: Request their route map from their website before you leave home - you can then plan a fabulous day and maximize your 24 hour ticket.

We purposefully made a 10 hour layover at London Heathrow before going to Dublin so I could show the wife a quick glimpse of London. After leaving the airport we went to Piccadilly Circus got on a Big Bus and took a loop around London. Big Ben, Parliment, Buckingham, Trafalgar square, Downing, Westminster, etc. We stopped at Harrod's for some tea, Big Ben/London Eye, Buckingham and had lunch at the Red Lion Pub for some Fish & Chips, Mushy Peas and a Pint. Pictures in a red phone booth before we headed back to the airport with time to spare. Big Bus is the best way to take it all in on a short time schedule. We even took a short taxi ride in a Black English Cab.

Oct 16th.

Me on the phone to this company's office: "You have a nice special online, but I don't have printer to print the tickets"

The manager on the phone: "Do you have a smartphone like iPhone?".

Me: "Yes".

The Manager: "Just purchase the tickets online and bring your phone and show the PDF tickets to our guy at the stop"

Me: "Great!"

17th Oct around 11 AM:

Me (to the Big Bus guy at the Big Bus Stop outside Victoria Station): "Hey! I talked to your manager yesterday and he told me that I could purchase your tickets online and show them to you on the smartphone. So here are my tickets on the iPhone".

The Big Bus Guy (BBG): "I don't care sir. You need a printed paper ticket".

Me: "Umm. I talked to your boss and he said I don't need to. Why don't you call him on that walkie talkie of yours and confirm?"

The BBG: "I won't sir. And in any case, he will tell you the same thing as I am saying. You now need to go away and get those printed tickets. You can run to our office 5 blocks that way and get them printed at office free of charge and you can leave your two kids, your old mother and your wife standing in the rain here while you go do that". (slight dramatization).

Me: "Really? If that is the case, why don't you just call him and let's confirm instead of making me run?"

The BBG: Just stares at me. So I run to get those tickets printed.

17th Oct around 11:30 AM:

Me (panting and soaking with sweat at their office) to the not so friendly lady at the Big Bus Tours office: "So, why would your guy make me run to your office to get those printed tickets instead of accepting them on the iPhone? You know, I did ring beforehand"

The Not-So-Friendly-Lady at the Big Bus Tours Office: Nonchalant shrug.

17th Oct 12 PM:

Me (exhausted, tired and over the tour before it has started): Shove the tickets in the BBG face: "Here! Are these OK?"

The BBG: "Don't talk to me like this. You don't know what I can do to you. I have contacts in this city of mine - you you foreigner!" (yes, this in front of the other customers - threatening me). At this point in time, I am thinking perhaps getting on the bus with the family might not be a good idea. Yet, I get on.

17th Oct, 5:00 PM.

Me, with the family on the last bus that goes towards Harrods, to the driver of the bus: "Is the next stop Harrods?"

The Driver of the Bus (TDOTB): "You need to sit down".

Me (shellshocked) "What?"

TDOTB: "You need to sit down and put those damn ear plugs on. They will tell you everything you need to know".

Me: "Why?"

TDOTB: "Because each time I talk to one of you damn tourists, I lose my concentration and forget to press the brake" (seriously! He was not joking)

Me: "Whoops sorry."

Me (in a whisper to my family): "Next time TDOTB does remember to press the brakes, let's get off".

So we do. Miles away from Harrods, on the other side of Hyde Park. Happy to be rid of this company with the staff with impeccable customer service (not!).

So. Here is my summary to you. There is one other company called "The Original Bus Tour". Both companies have the same product. They both have the same style of buses. They both do the same thing and at the same price tag. But they both have different staff. So if it doesn't matter to you what company you select for your tour of London, then go with "The Original Bus Tour". You may just avoid getting threatened by the staff at the Victoria Checkin or yelled at by a bus driver.

My daughter and I rode the Big Bus Tour on April 4, 2003. The buses were not traveling as frequently then, as it was still early in the season. Overall, the service was quite nice, however, we had a tour guide who memorable in a negative way. Instead of telling us about the city itself, this American expatriate who has adopted London as her new home, told us about her days as a bicycle messenger, her recent purchase of a cell phone, how she used to be a skate boarder. The sites she liked to point out were the hotel where Jimi Hendrix died of a drug overdose and the hotel that cost over 500 pounds a night. We would've gotten off and waited for another bus, but we were short on time and suffered through. I would recommend the bus tour- you also get a boat trip on the Thames in the price of the tour, so that was nice. Just if you have Laura as your tour guide, get off at the next stop!

Just a short note for future UK travelers; during our visit in March, 2006, we bought tickets, 19 pounds each, for the Big Bus Company in London in order to obtain an overview, then plan out our itinerary. First off, upon purchasing the tickets we were notified that they were the only company on that street that was of English origin, then we were asked whether we would tack on additional charges for specific venues, and once we were on the bus, we were asked to transfer twice to different buses. To add to the ordeal, half of the upper deck seats had earphone malfunctions and the bus tended to sit at stops for extended lengths of time. We finally realized the delay in the travel and the transfer to different buses enabled the company to fill the buses. I would not recommend this company for future visitors as it felt like we were herded back and forth, like a flock of unsuspecting sheep. We actually ended up walking, while we referenced our maps and utilized the local taxi service which was much more friendly and efficient.

I hardly ever write reviews but I am writing this to help everyone who is thinking about using this company.
Please if you really have to use them be very careful with what they offer and sell.
I myself bought 2 VIP tickets on the bus for London Eye just to find out on the arrival that they are just vouchers to be exchanged and they run out of tickets for the day, So myself and my family from US had to simply go home. Tried to call the company for 4 days now and there is nobody answering the phone. No reply to email either. I am afraid will not see my money again.
To summerise, please look for a better company to offers hop on/hop off as the idea is great, but don't use them and save yourself trouble, disappointment and money.

You have seen them all around the world. These open top deck busses that whip around town ... these guys from Big Bus Tours have it down to a science. This company has the experience from operating in 16 major cities all over the world so it is no wonder why in general I felt I got a better service and value for money. Boarded it yesterday and this is the best way to see London. Dont think its a 1 hour tour. It can be several hours and the information you get is great. Really the only way to see London if you have never been there. Do take your hat and sunscreen if you are on the open deck. Now for the nitty gritty.

Cost: 1 Single Adult ticket is 32 GBP (Big Bus Tour) vs 1 Single Adult ticket for 29 GBP (The Original Tour). Both give you multiple routes and both give you a cruise BUT the decission factor for me was that Big Bus Tour actually gave you the second consecutive day for free. The Original Tour guide told me YES you get the 2nd day free BUT its until 10:00 am. (When I bought the ticket it was 10:00 am so in essence you get with the Original Tour on 24 Hours of use.... I opted to go for the Big Bus Option obviously.

It has 3 lines - Green, Blue and Red. The Green runs every 20 minutes and in essence is a "link" from the major train stations to join the other 2 lines but it still have a full recorded comentary. Now for the other 2 lines here are the details:

RED LINE - Live comentary in English and the bus runs every 5-15 minutes. They have free ponchos onboard just in case it starts raining.

BLUE LINE - Has the choice of 12 languages and it is the extended tour (I would recomend this over the RED line) The recording is in English, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Chinese, Russian, Spanish, Polish, Hindi, Japanese, Arabic. The first bus operates from Queen Mother Gates at 8:08 am.

I persuaded my family that this might be a great way to see as much as London as possible during our short stay there. The blue route bus stopped right outside our hotel -- what could be more convenient?

It will be a long time before I will live that suggestion down.

The blue bus route provides a pre-recorded commentary that is very short on detail and fails to mention some points of interest at all. There were frequent very long bridges of recorded music by British composers. After about an hour, the same selections from Holst, Elgar and Vaughan Williams get pretty tired.

We spent an inordinate amount of time at Madame Tussauds Wax Museum. First of all we were encouraged to hop off and buy tickets, then we had to disembark and get on another bus.

Overall the tour was proving to be very uninspiring and we were feeling it was certainly not worth the £30/person we had been charged. Then we decided to hop off at Westminster Abby. We had not realized how long we had been sitting on the bus and by the time we arrived at the entrance the Abby, it was closed.

At that point, the real fun began.

We went back to the stop to wait to hop back on the next bus, which should have been along in 15 minutes. After 20 minutes a Red Route bus came by. We enquired as to when the next Blue bus would be along? Oh, the Blue Bus was right behind him -- it would be no more than 7 or 8 minutes, we were assured. The next bus came and it was also from the Red route. Again we were told that a Blue bus would be along directly. When a Blue bus finally arrived it was full. People were packed in and standing. It couldn't accommodate any more passengers. Once more we were promised that another Blue bus would be along with minutes.

We waited at that stop for 45 minutes. We saw only two Blue buses and both were totally packed. One of the drivers told us to take the next Red bus and then transfer at Marble Arch. The next Red bus was full but we boarded the subsequent bus and were told that we couldn't transfer at Marble Arch. The driver took us to another central point where quite a crowd was waiting. It seemed we were not the only people who had been abandoned by the elusive Blue buses.

A customer service person was on the scene and his sole purpose seemed to be as rude and unhelpful as possible. By this time someone in the crowd passed on the information that we had missed the last bus of the evening and we would be on our own finding our respective ways back to our hotels. Whether this was actually true or not was never actually confirmed by the man from the company but he clearly could care less what happened to us. He was particularly offhand with a family who had spent a total of £240 for the tour. A young woman in the group was caring an exhausted preschooler, she was practically pleading with the man to help her family to get back to their accommodations. At this point my adult son, angered by the customer service guy’s attitude, stated that the family should have their £240 refunded. The customer service rep finally gave the woman information about how she could get her money back at the company office the next day. As we were leaving London in the morning, we were out of luck.

We decided to take the tube home. Not a great way to see the sights, but at least it was efficient and reliable.

We booked this through our Hotel and it was the best, most informative hop on hop off bus tour we used through Europe.From the start the customer service was exceptional, they had people located at each stop advising when the next bus was arriving, they had 2 different routes to take so you could see alot of the major tourist attractions around London, and for what it costs was well worth the money with what we got to see., only downside was after 5pm the people are no longer at the stops.The audio worked and the live commentary in english was also really good.

We had a lovely weekend away in London on the Big Bus tour!!!!

;-)

We had a live tour guide Chris and an outstanding driver Paul, who between then kept the laughs and humour going the entire trip =D

All of us had such a great time :-) and learnt so much from the information that was told to us on the tour, it was fantastic =D

Very funny and very informative ;-)

For sure a 5 star vote from us... <3

My wife and I are in London for 2 weeks on vacation and have not had a super positive experience with this company. We were literally told that all we needed was our London Pass after getting on the bus the first day, which was not true. Thankfully we retained the paper receipts that were provided or we would have lost out on 3 days of HOHO bus tours (1 included with London Pass and 2 days paid for). The guys at the various stops feel more like used car salesmen using high pressure sales tactics. One was quite rude with my wife when she told him we had already purchased tickets and did not need any. A few other issues we had: 1) not all buses have live tour operators and the recording is not always in synch with where you are; 2) waiting time at stops can be lengthy despite what their ads say (i.e. repeatedly 30+ min waiting for buses) and buses are not spaced out (i.e. found ourselves in a convoy of 3 buses); 4) there is no such thing as a line or controlled entry to the buses or a max capacity (buses we were on were completely full and they still packed 20 people into the lower floor standing) which inhibits your ability to view sights as you travel through the city.

If you still decided to go with this company, then I recommend the Red and Blue Lines as they seem to cover more of the traditional touristy spots.

We had a very poor experience with Big Bus London on Sunday, March 19, 2017. After purchasing 3 tickets online, we went to catch the Red Bus at pick up point #1. When we got there, the Big Bus employee told us that no buses were leaving from point #1 so we should walk up to point #8. We did so, only to be told that no buses were leaving from point #8. We turned back and walked to point #3. After a bit of a wait, we finally got on one of the Big Buses. It took us one stop – with no commentary – to point #4. Then it stopped for at least 20 minutes. Apparently there was a new driver supposed to take over, but we felt that we were going nowhere. A number of people abandoned this Big Bus at point #4 as no one was able to tell us when the new driver would be arriving. We asked yet another Big Bus employee to refund our money as we’d spent nearly one hour and traveled only one stop. He phoned someone named “Craig”, then informed us that we could only get a refund by sending an email. When we asked we he could not refund us on the spot, he said that because we'd bought our tickets on line and and not from him. It was quite apparent that there would be no driver, no bus, no service and absolutely no customer satisfaction.

Since returning home, we've been trying to contact Big Bus for a refund. We've been ignored. Ironically, the only email they sent us was to complete their survey. So we've complied.

I did research as London has three different hop on hop off bus companies. Big Bus was very good we did not pre purchase tickets bought them just before boarding. I asked them to give me the internet rate for a two day pass and they did. We were able to get to all the sights using the bus and the river boat The 10 am Changing of the Guards walking tour was amazing and free,

Myself and my teenage children decided to go to London for a three day break during May Half Term. As there was lots we wanted see I decided to book the Big Bus Tour for 48 hours.
There are two routes, the red and the blue. The red tour has a tour guide on board and the blue bus tour has earphones to listen to recorded messages. I found that the drivers and guides on the red tours we courteous and friendly, the ones on the blue bus tours were rude, ignorant and very unhelpful.

The first day we took the buses, everything was reasonably fine apart from the majority of the buses being quite packed, on the odd occasion we let one or two pass before we caught another one which looked less busy. Also the stops in-between were quite far apart so a lot of walking was still involved. If you are going to do the full tour without stopping you will need about five hours due to the amount of traffic in central London. On a number of occasions when we were walking we actually overtook the same bus a few times!

On the second day (Thursday 29 May) it was mid afternoon and we stopped at the Tussards Stop and we told we had to get off this bus and change onto another one and there would be a 12 minute wait. We walked to the other bus and the downstairs was completely full so we had to sit on the top deck and it was raining by this time. As we waited the rain got heavier and heavier and we were also getting concerned as we had to get to the Oxford Street stop as soon as possible as we were leaving that day and had to go back to our hotel in Bloomsbury and then to St Pancras Station.

The bus finally left and as our stop on Oxford Street approached people started to get up to leave. When the bus stopped, a whole load of kids jumped on and started coming up the stairs and blocked the stairway so we could not get off and the bus driver started driving again. By this time the rain was heavy and the top deck of the bus was slippery so we had to sit down again. I knew that the Regent Street stop was not too far away so decided we would have to get off here instead even though we would be cutting it fine to get to St Pancras in time.

When we got to Hamleys toy store I knew the stop was fast approaching so we got up as there was no way we could miss this stop with our impending train journey looming. The driver stopped where I thought the stop was so we went down the bus steps, they were drenched wet and I had not noticed but there was some litter half way down as well. Myself and my son descended down the steps safely but as my teenage daughter got half way down she slipped on the wet and litter, and came crashing down to the bottom.

The driver started moving again and I asked him to stop but he said he had only stopped at traffic lights not at the official stop. I tried to explain that my daughter had fallen and was hurt but he just rolled his eyes into the back of his head and tutted at me. He stopped about 20 yards later at the Bus stop.
If he had stopped a bit longer to let us off in Oxford Street in the first place this would never of happened so I was left with my daughter with bruised ribs and having to walk further back to our hotel to collect our luggage to be able to get our train at St. Pancras.

I would NOT recommend this service to anyone as the drivers do not stop for long enough in my opinion and the steps and upstairs are dangerous when it is raining.
Throughout our two days on this bus service I noticed a lot of people getting up too early for the stop as they felt they would also miss the stop and there are a lot of traffic lights in London so on quite a few occasions people thought the drivers were stopping at the official stop and then started setting off again. There was one instance where 8-10 people stood up on the top deck to get off and then the bus started moving again and they stumbled, someone could of been seriously injured.

I used a similar bus service in Rome and found the drivers pleasant, helpful, stopped for the right amount of time and drove carefully.

Oh and also one of the buses got stuck on one of the routes and ran over a parked motorbike!!

I was always interested to discover London by open bus tour when i will go to the UK as i am a tourist. I went to this place today in Piccadilly circus. I had EXTREMELY HORRIBLE service in london in my whole life EVER. When i first come in that place next to piccadilly circus station, there was 1 lady, 1 old guy was sitting. I asked about tour from them and they said that to talk to the guy who was advirtising their tours in outside. Alright, i went to the guy, and he explained me about the tour, and asking me to buy the ticket. I said not now, maybe during the weekend, because i have work to do in LonDOn. Then he was looked upset. I asked how much is the Cirque de soliel Kooza, and phantom of opera, he told me to ask the lady and old man. I went to them and repeated the question. Lady asked me whether i bought the ticket. I said "No" , and could not even finish the sentence. She said to me " GO AWAY"!!!!! I could not believe in my ears. I was looking my eyes bigger, the old man said "GO AWAY" as well..... OMG..... And they were started doing something in the table and didn'teven look at me once again!!!!! I was so shocked, could not even move. Finally, i left this horrible british service.

I advice you to not go to this place. They treat you as a trash or beggar!!!!!!

I am an asian and going back from london with broken heart. SO PATHETIC, HORRIBLE, TERRIBLE service in LONDON.

I dont want to go there again NEVER EVER !!!!!

We actually ourchased our tickets at the Hilton where we were staying as they were good for 48 hours of unlimited daytime travel. The first day we left early and caught the very first bus (we walked West along Bayswater and caught the bus there as the crowds East of Queensway, which was actualy a closer stop for us, were quite large and would eliminate most chances of us getting an upper seat), so a five minute walk and we joined a very small group of fellow ticket holders where we all went to the upper seats and enjoyed the sunshine. Boxes of new ear bud style earphones are supplied in a big box as you step onto the bus along with an easy to understand fold out colour map which further helps one get the "lay of the land". On the first day we made note of attractions/stops that were of interest to us, visited a few interesting looking pubs we spotted and generally just had an easy, long day of riding the bus. The bus stops are plentiful and easy to spot (they are also indicated on the free map) and there was always a bus every 5-15 minutes so you never had long to wait. Some of the buses provided live commetary (indicated by the "red" sign near the driver on the bus) while the majority had the pre-recorded commentary (simply plug your free earphones into the receptacle at your seat and choose the desired language - simple!) indicated by the blue sign. We did not take any of he free guided walking tours that are included in your ticket purchase but we did take the included free river cruise and it was very good, not at all crowded, informative and quite amusing (the commentator was a real comic). All in all an easy, no hassle method of getting aound London. We enjoyed it so much in fact that we purchased tickets a week later and just "cherry picked" some areas we found interesting (the river walk by the the London Eye for instance as we saw an art display we wished to attend, plus the area was just perfect for a lazy day of visiting various exhibits, having a latte, or beer, while people watching along the waterfront). If you are traveling during colder times (it was quite hot in September) you can still ride upstairs as these buses have approximately the first 1/3 covered so if it's raining or the wind is a little cool you can still get that "fresh air exerience".

We had a very expensive experience with this company and were actually left stranded some distance from where we needed to be, we were lied to by a number of staff and there was no care or consideration for the fact I am registered disabled (using a disability scooter) and had a young family with me.

Our trip cost £75, this we were happy to pay in order that the kids could see the sights of London. The member of staff who sold us the ticket outside Harrods appeared most helpful, he advised that buses ran until at least 8pm. Though the "24 hour" ticket is infact, a falicy in that the last bus leaves at 6pm and thats from any stop, so if your not heading the way you need to be heading then you WILL be left stranded after this time.

We hopped on the blue bus at Harrods, we had a good 40 minute wait for the bus to arrive (advertised as every 15-20 mins). The first driver was very good, he helped me and my scooter on and was very friendly, there really is only space for one disabled person using a scooter/wheelchair so please keep this in mind if in this position. We got half way round the whole tour when we were told that we would have to change bus near the Houses of Parliament to continue on our route. By this time, we had been on the bus a fair length of time, a good 1 hour 30 mins, mostly due to traffic, fair enough, this is to be expected, its London after all, though perhaps this company needs to counteract this by putting on more buses in the first place!
We accepted that we needed to change buses, were looking forward to seeing the remainder of the route, sights such as the London Eye and Tower Bridge. When we disembarked at the Houses of Parliament, there was many people waiting, at this point, we were advised that we would have to take the next bus (blue heading west) in order to get back towards our original destination of Harrods. This meant that we would not see the remainder of the tour, the fact we were told that buses "run until 8pm" was a complete lie. When the blue bus heading west arrived, it was busy, the bus driver saw me with my scooter, obviously couldent be bothered making space for me and LIED telling us that there was another blue bus heading west about 4 minutes behind. There was infact NO bus behind and we were left in the position where we were stuck in Westminster and needing to be at Kensington. We complained to the member of staff there, he didnt want to know and basically told us to shut up and just get on the next bus, a red route one, which dropped us off at the far south east side of Hyde Park, from here, we had to walk for 1 hour 30 minutes to get anywhere near to our hotel.

As a disabled customer visiting the city, I am appaulled that we were left stranded in the city by this company. I do plan to take this matter further.

The Big Bus Tour had been advertised and sold to us by Big Bus representatives as a “24-Hour Tour.” Since we only had one afternoon remaining in London, we were disappointed to learn after boarding our first bus from the tour guide that the buses were not, in fact, 24-hours. He also explained that the buses had reduced service after 5:00pm, but would be running until 7:00 pm.

After a brief stop at Buckingham Palace, we boarded a second bus. For the duration of our journey onwards, the live tour guide failed to provide commentary, sat in his seat facing forwards and only spoke with the bus driver. Since this was unsatisfactory commentary (we had paid 37 pounds to learn about the city of London—if we were looking for a double-decker bus ride, doing so with our Oyster cards would have been a more economically sound method) we jumped on a Blue Line bus and rode it to Stop 38. Although we attempted to de-board the bus at Stop 37, we could not. We realized much later that the stop was not in service, but this was never announced or explained.

After a couple of hours at the museums, we decided to re-board the bus around 4:15pm, thinking that we would have ample time to see the rest of the tour, since buses would be running until 7:00pm. Since the closest stop was #37, we headed there to catch the bus. However, after walking to the stop (which was not clearly marked on the map in any way), we discovered that it was not in use/under construction. So we returned to stop #38 to catch the Blue Line bus. When it arrived around 5:00 pm, we were excited to continue onwards with our journey and see the rest of the tour.

At this point, a fifth member of our group decided to join the tour. However, when he attempted to board the bus, the bus driver told him he “couldn’t sell him a ticket” because “the ticket would only be valid for that day” and not good for the following day as well. (Either the bus driver was lying or your “24-hour” advertising is.) He did not, however, explain to any members of our party that this was also because his route would be ending shortly.

At 5:30 PM, the bus terminated at Marble Arch. It was clear that all the other passengers were also confused and had been miscommunicated to. No one on the bus was aware that the tour would be terminating at Marble Arch station, particularly since we had been informed that buses would be running until 7:00 PM. When I politely asked the bus driver if there were any buses continuing onwards, he was clearly annoyed by my question and informed me that ALL the tours were terminating at that time in a manner that I would describe as borderline rude.

(If my math is correct, had it been communicated to us that Stop #37 was not in use, and we had not walked out of the way from one stop to another, or known that we would have to walk the extra distance to Stop 38, we may have been able to complete a longer tour.)

Not only do we feel that we were misled by the company’s advertising and representatives at stops, but we were given incorrect information by live tour guides, treated poorly by one of the bus drivers and received nearly no commentary from one of the “live” tour guides.

From start to finish, the tour was unsatisfactory.

Been all round London on Big Bus Company Buses - joined the tour at Marble Arch - got off at Westminster Bridge and on the River trip to Tower Bridge - back on the bus at the Tower, the guide was really interesting, lots of information - also went on the Blue Bus route (one with headphones)
The Buses we were on had a roof - great with the few showers around
Well worth £20.
Saw lots of the Big Buses around. No waiting at stops

We have have ridden hop-on hop-off buses all over the world and they are a great way to see an area, get some history, and travel around. I booked the Big Bus hop-on hop-off through the London Pass, Getting on the bus and traveling around the city was never a problem, just like every other hoppy-bus we have done. The problem was when it got late in the day, apparently the drivers decide (randomly?), when they are going to stop working or just bypass some of their stops. We were heading back to our hotel near Victoria Station and the Red Line driver decided he was going to bypass 2 stops and head to Marble Arch. Myself and several other passengers spoke up and stated that we didn't want to walk all the way from Marble Arch, back to where he was supposed to drop us off and we got him to stop along the road just to let us out. The next night we were on the Orange Line bus, and on the opposite side of town from our hotel when the driver stopped the bus and started getting out of the bus. There were about 15 of us on the bus and we asked him where he was going. He stated that his shift was done and we could get on another Orange Line bus "down there" (he was pointing down the street. There was no Big Bus within sight. We wandered down the street about a block and I saw a Big Bus (empty with no driver) behind a brick wall. Eventually, the driver showed up and I asked him if he was going to stop 21 tonight (near Victoria Station). He said he would eventually. We boarded the bus and waited about 45 minutes for him to start the bus and finish the Orange Line tour. We got off early (stop 20) because I didn't want to get stuck on the bus again, heading across town. I still enjoyed the Big Bus tours, just not that impressed with the drivers work ethics. Welcome to London!! ;-)

Last week I had some family members visiting us in London from the USA. As they had only 2 days to see London I decided to take them on a bus tour so that they could see as much as possible in a short space of time.
So we all handed over £39! To a very pushy but disinterested ticket seller And boarded a bus. We were met by a grubby and grumpy driver and a packed bus with standing room only. Needless to say we couldn’t see anything. Eventually we managed to get seats up stairs and settled in to enjoy the tour. The tour guide, again very grubby proceeded to mutter into his microphone and due to traffic noise was unintelligible. I pointed out to him that his microphone wasn’t working and he explained we needed to use headphones! Would have been good to have been given these along with the tickets! That is if they worked! Unfortunately they didn’t so we gave up with those and strained to listen to the guide without them. Due to the terrible traffic, I appreciate that is not the bus companies fault, we sat in some very uninteresting parts of the city with silence from the guide and found the whole experience very underwhelming.
My American visitors were very polite and made the best of it but I was extremely embarrassed. Firstly by the extortionate cost secondly by the unprofessional service and finally by the fact that I had inflicted 2 boring hours on them.
If you have visitors and you like them avoided this tour.
Never again!!!

This tour has three bus routes. We have done all three. The most popular route is the Blue route. According to the brochure it has 36 stops and the full circuit time is 1 hrs and 15 min. In my opinion, this took much longer. This route takes you to West London. The Red route has 15 stops according tho the brochure.. The full circuit time is 2 hours and 30 minutes. It takes yoiu to Central London. The Green route is the least popular route. It has 9 stops and it connects Kings's .Cross to Central London The full circuit time is 1 hrs . 15 min. According tho the website there is a route called the Magical Merlink. Well i have not seen that route. Even the staff said, not to pay attention to that because there is no Magical Merlink Route. Some routes cross each other. This makes it easy to switch from routes. The website says that the frequency of the buses is between 5 and 30 minutes (it depends on which route). Sometimes the buses are on time. Sometimes they arrive immediately after each other. And sometimes you will have to wait a long time.

We had a ticket for 48 hours. That included the evening bus tour. We didnt do this tour. We were there in June, and in that period the sun sets about 10pm. This tour that has four stops, has to be done when its dark. So you can enjoy London by night. And the last bus leaves at 9pm, when there is still daylight. Also included in this 48 hour ticket is the River Cruise on the Thames (the yellow route). Its beautiful because you see a part of London from another angle. But cruise is a big word for it. I would say a trip on the Thames. The are different sailings. We did the trip from The Tower of London to the City Center. This lasted about 20 to 25 minutes. There are also bus tour tickets for sale in combination with other tourist attractions, like Madame Tussaud. The tickets are cheaper if you buy them online.

The blue and green route have recorded commentary in 12 languages. The Red tour has live English speaking guides. The website says that the buses have wifi. But some have, some don’t. The buses are wheelchair accessible and you can hire them for private events. The Big Bus Tour Company also has a free Big Bus Tours app. You dont really need it, but it might come in handy (for some passengers). The Big Bus Tours are a good way to see something of London

Ours was a party of 8, ages 8-84. We purchased a 2 day premium, and started our time with the CityCruise from Tower of London to Westminster, which was a big hit with young and old. We had beautiful June weather, a little cooler in the morning than the US, and much less humid.

The upper deck outdoor bus seats will be damp at first, so bring a disposable wipe if you are going to pick up the first buses.

Also, beware that the map has a few errors (you can pick up a Blue Westbound from Westminster Bridge, and stops 25 and 26 were not effective, “diverted” as they say). The 10 or so staff with whom I spoke were all friendly and helpful, and I would give all of them 5 stars. I would advise customers to check with staff on your itinerary to ensure that your expectations from the brochure and website match the reality of the day.

Another warning: the last buses of the day can be quite crowded, so be prepared to stand for several stops.

The audio guides (in 12 languages) on the Blue and Green lines were of good quality, although there was plenty of breaks with the same few English classical musics pieces looping.

I especially enjoyed the live tour guides on the Red line. Of these, Maddie was my favorite, with encyclopedic knowledge, great wit, and a clear and mellifluous voice. I wish my college professors were as communicative and engaged as she is.

Overall, great for first time visitors, multilingual and multigenerational groups.

I had hoped to begin our trip with a big bus tour to get an overview of the city and see some of the iconic sites on wheels. What a disappointment this tour was. We selected the red route because of the live tour guide, but unfortunately it was uninspired. The tour guide pointed out a “classic” Mercedes that we passed by, noted the location of an Aston Martin dealership, and highlighted an old police car that we saw that is used in films. None of which interested me or had anything to do with London and its rich history!!! After switching to the blue line 45 min into the tour, we found the recorded comments to be more interesting but we still decided to change our plans and get off early to do something else.

Note also that there is no heat on the bus, even downstairs. So plan to dress as if you’ll be outdoors the whole time. Or better yet, skip this altogether.

Terrible. Was there last Friday 3/9/2018. The bus drivers are rude, the people are rude, our bus driver on one route hit 3 curbs. In addition - he negotiated a deal for a Rifle with another bus driver while passengers were on board - - - -I cannot make this stuff up!!!!! We immediately disembarked said bus at the very next stop after the Tower of London, and we reported this incident to the corporate offices - that called our claim "alleged". Seriously - - - - A bus driver for their company was negotiating FIREARMS with another city bus driver while we watched in horror!!!!!!!!

We purchased a two day ticket and used it on 30 and 31 Dec.

First day was very good. We used the app and found our way quickly to a stop.

I did not find the app at all useful in working out when the bus was due, so we did have to wait for a little while for it to appear. But this is London and traffic was manic so we shouldn’t be surprised by delays.

A bigger issue was that on our second day the roads were slowly closed down in order to prepare for NY eve which meant the bus had to take detours. That is not the bus companies fault. But our ‘stop’ which was a short walk from our hotel was out of action so we ended up a good distance away.

Perhaps better information could be shared between the local council and the bus company, and then customers could be given better advice as they board the bus. After all, New Year’s Eve happens every year so before next year you could better prepared.

Still an enjoyable way to pass a couple of hours. I enjoyed it.

We paid 35 pounds for a tour hoping it would orientate us to the city. We hopped on only to stand on the lower deck for half an hour as there were no seats left. Then, erratically, just as seats finally became available, the bus stopped and made everyone change out into another crowded bus. It didn’t follow the sequence advertised, was too crowded, and the service was poor by nearly each staff member. Once they took your money they did not care about your experience at all.

Would never do this again and not recommend for anyone.

Sincerely,

It must have been a bad day for the Big Bus Tours Company on Wednesday, July 5, because the day started out with us exiting Victoria Station to witness a BB representative yelling at a prospective customer to go down the street and buy his tickets elsewhere. Apparently he was offended that this guy was trying to price shop and the poor guy set him off.

Then we go to our stop (#22 blue line) right in front of the Grovesnor Hotel. We waited there for 30+ minutes. The BB rep standing at the bus stop with us must have gotten tired of giving customers the same excuse of "it's late due to traffic" (no one was buying it because other bus tours were still coming through for their pick ups), so he left.

The bus then proceeded to pick us up and all seemed fine...until we witnessed the driver getting into a very heated argument with a customer who simply wanted to know how to get to Buckingham Palace. He wasn't sure how to read the map, and wanted to know which color bus line he was on. There was also clearly a little bit of language misunderstanding. I was shocked at how he treated this customer. In the driver's defense, he said to the customer "you've asked the same question 7 times".

I get it. People can be very difficult to deal with, particularly in the service industry. But in my opinion, no matter how many times someone asks you a question, or offends you by price shopping, you must maintain your composure, keep your head, and be the professional that you are.

The rest of the tour went fine, but it was a bit unsettling to witness all three incidents within an hour of each other. The rest of the other personnel/drivers that we experienced were great and very helpful. I'm still on the fence about whether or not I'll give this company another chance.

To summarize, my experience with Big Bus in London was horrendous. After a pleasant experience with Big Bus in San Francisco, I bought a 48 hours ticket on January 16th for its London service. Let me start with the bus stops: you will barely find any around the city. I quickly realized that Big Bus has close to half the number of bus stops as its competitors. Regarding waiting time, I waited once for about 45 minutes to catch a bus when I was close to Big Ben. By no means do the buses run every 10-20 minutes, as they claim. The staff on the bus stops never ask you “how can I help you sir?” or “where are you going sir?”. Instead, their first question is always “are you going to any attraction today sir”? They are all really pushy when it comes to sell you tickets to London’s main attractions and, as soon as you tell them that you are not interested, they immediately ignore you and become really unfriendly.

Now the worst: on my last tour day, the bus stopped around the Marble Arch at 16:30 when the bus driver asked everybody to leave the bus because that was the last stop. I then approached a staff member on the bus stop and asked her about how to get to Waterloo station and she said: “That is up to you. We no longer have buses going there”. When I said: “what a horrendous way of dealing with your clients”, she then said: “If you want to complain, the customer service number is right there on the bus”. This lady was working on Sunday, January 17, 2016, around 16:30 on the Marble Arch stop. I truly hope someone will, at the very least, fire her. Anyway, I truly regret every cent I spent with Big Bus in London and, even though my experience with it in San Francisco was fabulous, I will never ride a Big Bus again in my life.

We are in London and have had the worst experience EVER with Big Bus London! I was closed in the door by a distracted driver, we (everyone on the bus) were suddenly and unexpectedly put off a bus at a random stop and told to board the bus behind us that was PACKED, we were then sent on a detour that caused our half trip around their loop to last nearly THREE hours. We missed our reservations and the last Big Bus back. The cruise is ONE WAY but they do tell you that in the brochure so don't believe the guy on the street in his Big Bus uniform cause he will tell you anything to sell another ticket. We went to Greenwich and it costs us 15 pounds to get back. THEN the night bus tour was 35 minutes late to our stop AND IT IS NOT HOP ON HOP OFF despite what they advertise. IT IS A ONE WAY TOUR around the city, you can get on anywhere but you will not return to the location you boarded. There are three night buses and they all start before any have made it around once so you will get picked up but you will be taken to Marble Arch and LEFT!!!!!! PLEASE PLEASE use "The Original Tour" company, FIVE of their buses passed us tonight at the bus stop while we waited for the FIRST Big Bus to come by. This company just doesn't have a professional standard and lack an ethical code of practice.

These "hop on, hop off" buses are probably the best way for a tourist to see London. We asked at the hotel reception which company had the most popular tour and they recommended the Big Bus Company and we were not disappointed.

Not only was it a great way to see most of London's principal attractionss but several features made the tour even better value for money. For example, there are free walking tours led by a knowledgeable guide. Then there was the one-way river cruise on the Thames. After getting off the river boat it was an easy matter to hop back on another bus. In addition, there was a pack of discount vouchers for use at other attractions.

For anyone spending a few days in London the two-day tour option allows sufficient time to see a few of the more popular attractions around the city, It is also worthwhile planning which attractions to visit beforehand and stick to the plan.

There are plenty of buses around the different colour-coded routes with the more popular ones having an onboard English-speaking guide. Generally speaking they seemed to be very knowledgeable about the places that could be seen along the tour route: although there were one or two 'obvious' slips of the tongue (e.g. the Archbishop of Canterbury is not the spiritual head of the Roman Catholic Church in England and Wales!). If nothing else, the onboard guides provided more than a few laughs and some good entertainment.

Fortunately during the time we were on the tour there were no major diversions due to road closures and relatively little road congestion (for London!). Getting on and off the bus, climbing the stairs and going on any of the associated walking tours may be problematic for those with walking difficulties or those in wheelchairs . So anyone who has a mobility problem might assess beforehand if they can cope with these aspects of the tour. There were family groups, some with young children in buggies, and they seemed to manage fine on the tour.

For anyone with a Smartphone, there is a free 'Big Bus' "app" available with a destination overview, city guide, an interactive map and route / schedule planner. Many of the overseas visitors using the buses seemed to be using this facility although I found the paper guide was adequate for a good day out.

Using the Big Red Bus to get around London and see the highlights is definitely recommended,

Decided to do the Big Bus Tours - London due to a limited time in the city. The tour costs 24 £ per adult for 24 hours, or 30 £ for 48 hours. The buses depart from all around the city and passes all the main attractions in London. It's a hop-on hop-off, so you can leave the bus whenever you want and then board a different bus as many times as you want.
There are two different tours - red line tour and blue line tour. The buses are marked with red or blue. The red line is a bit shorter but cover all the main attractions like House of Parliament, Tower Bridge and Buckingham Palace. The blue line is longer and goes around Hyde Park as well.
The Blue Line Tour has pre-recorded guide information. You are given a headset as you enter the bus. It is pre-recorded in several languages.
The Red Line has a live guide.
Loved this tour and the money was really worth it. Great service. Great bus. Recommended!

Hop On Hop off buses offer a good overview of London in general if you want to get a feel for the city in general. However, if you have specific sights in mind that you want to see and don't need a general overview I would recommend that you skip the bus, since there is traffic (lots of traffic) and thus the bus routes are quite slow (which can suck up limited sightseeing time). For example, to get to the Tower of London we spent over an hour on the bus where we could have spent 10 minutes on the tube. We didn't mind since we had several days in London and I wanted to give the kids a relaxing overview of many of the city sights without having to walk (and listen to the kids whining about walking).

We did a 2 day tour option, and did not use the buses at all the 2nd day- we did, however, take advantage of the walking tour the next day. I would say if you are able to get on the bus before 10:30 or so I doubt you'll need the 2 day option. Better to do the tour, get off on a couple of stops, then back the next day using the tube to see what you need.

As far as selecting a particular company, they have almost the exact same routes (at least as far as the important stuff goes). I would definitely recommend a tour that has a live guide and not a taped tour, since there were always questions we had as we passed something which of course cannot be answered if there is no tour guide! I went with Big Bus because the discount company seemed to have a couple of negative reviews and the river cruise section of the discount bus wasn't as highly rated. Furthermore, Big Bus had a walking Harry Potter tour I was interested in taking. Well, neither the River Cruise nor the Harry Potter tour amounted to much, so you might consider the discounter.

RIVER CRUISE-I liked seeing London from the river, it gave me a different perspective from my previous visits, but I can't imagine the discount company river tour could be any worse than what we took. The commentary was bland and the guy kept insisting over an over again that he wasn't a tour guide, but was trying to comment simply to make our tour better. For his "efforts" he then directly asked for tips and stood in front of the gangway on the way out shaking a bucket for tips. While the views were nice, I don't think the narration was that good and did not appreciate their efforts to pressure people to give them tips. Since the discounter also offers a river cruise, I don't see this as much of a factor. BTW, the tour was maybe 20 minutes with plenty of seating on top of the boat.

HARRY POTTER WALKING TOUR- The family are big Harry Potter fans so I thought it would be fun to see some of the places where some scenes were shot. Unfortunately we only got to see 4 places where scenes were shot, they were places that were unimportant in the movies (maybe 3 seconds of screen time) and looked quite different than in the movie (since there was so much CGI involved). As a result, I wouldn't use this as a factor in deciding what company to use. BTW, this walking tour lasted 90 minutes. The tour stopped by a candy store (not used in the movie at all, but they sold some "Harry Potter" candies- however this was a chain and they are all over the place so no need to take this tour in particular to see the candy store). One of my 3 daughters listed this in her biggest disappointments of the trip.

A generally good experience for a "feel" of the city, but don't use it to get around to the various sights as its too slow and will waste limited vacation time.

Please do not use Big Bus Company, I was completely disappointed.

I went to the London Bridge stop (on Tooley street) at around 11h30 (on the 20th of June) to show the QRcode to the rep who DELIBERATELY ignored me and TURNED his back on me! When he saw I had a QRcode, he just turned his back on me and tried to attract another customer on the street.

So I insisted, and he told me (without looking at me) to show it to the bus driver, which I did. The bus driver then told me to see with the "staff member on the pavement", which is common sense since no driver has a machine to read the QRcode (but I only noticed it later on) ...

Then I went back to see the rep and he said his machine does not work and just put my friends and I in the first bus he saw... without any ticket!

This situation was just intolerable! I guess these staff members get a commission for any ticket sold on the street... but is it a reason to treat this way customers who buy tickets online?!

So again, please do not use this company. I wrote an email to them, no response, no explanation, no apologies.

We were told that the big bus tour would be a great way to see London; unfortunately, they are not able to accommodate mobility scooters due to "safety concerns" over her dry cell battery. My daughters travel scooter has been on numerous airline flights, toured the White House and various other sensitive tourist areas. My belief is that the tour did not want to bother with the scooter in getting it on and off the bus - in any event, if you are traveling with a mobility device please be aware that this tour did not accommodate us (however, the "original bus tours" did accommodate as they have dedicated space for scooters and did not raise any concern).

The buses in general take a long time to get around because of the traffic, so there is nothing they can do about that, but the staff members are liars just to sell sell sell.

One guy by the name of Giammarco told us to our face that if we bought the tickets to the London Eye from them, we would not have to stand in line. So being tourists and knowing that there are a lot of LIARS out there to rip us off, we asked again, do you mean that we dont have to stand in that long line to get on the London Eye, and he said absolutely not. Then he went on to explain that for people to walk right in without waiting in line they have to pay $26, but with their $18.50 tickets we do the same and save money.

So the vulnerable tourists bought the scam. We bought 4 tickets from Giammarco who seemed like an honest guy. When we get to the London Eye, the staff tells us we cannot go in. We explained what Giammarco said and they said "he lied to you".

So, we had to go and exchange the receipt, because it is not a ticket, that he gave us then go back and stand in line like everyone else because Giammarco wanted to make a sale that day and thought what the heck they are tourists, they dont know.

Stay away from buying any tickets from any of these bus companies. If you want to take the long bus ride, not a bad idea, London is a big city, know that you will be sitting in traffic for a LONG time, but if you want to go to other attractions, buy it from the place you go to and DON'T TRUST Giammarco or any of these guys.

We chose Big Bus Tours over the competitors because they were the only ones to offer the Harry Potter Walking Tour as a part of the basic package. It was a great value as some of the HP tours priced separately cost as much or more as the Big Bus Tours does and includes much more.

Purchase your tickets on-line ahead of time for a 30% savings. We got a 48 hour ticket (better value than the 24 hour one, if you buy ahead--starts at the hour of the day you first use it) for 13 pound for a child (only a pound more than the one day ticket bought in person) and about 27 pounds (I think) for adults.

The HP tour leaves Trafalgar Square each day at 2 pm. It lasts about 1 1/2 hour. The guide did a lovely job showing sites related to JK Rowling and places were the movies were filmed or premiered. She had photos to show you the sights actually in the movies. She was professional and informative. We stopped at Hardy's Sweet Shoppes (like Honeyduke's) and got free samples and a discount on purchases. Dumbledore's favorite lemonsherbets and the watermelon things were especially good. The wizard wands were black licorice with pixie stick filling. We had great difficult finding the starting point (it's to the left of the National Theatre when looking up from Trafalgar Square towards the countdown to the Olympics Clock) so it's best to arrive by Big Bus Tours rather than by Tube. But the kind Big Bus Operator raced us to catch up with the group, which had just left. There are 8 or so different avenues from TS so it's hard to know which side of the square the stop is, since it's not easily visible from the main square.

We utilized the City Scenes Boat Ride down the Thames River, which would have cost nearly as much as the Big Bus Tour if booked alone. It was an enjoyable and speedy transportation from Westminister Abbey/London Eye (stops on both sides of the river) to the Tower of London (about 15-20 minutes). I would not book the boat ride alone but since it was included, it was a nice plus. The boat has drinks and snacks for purchase and has an open top deck and sheltered lower seats with big windows for photo taking of Shakespeare's Globe Theatre and the London Bridge. The captain gives an interesting commentary on the ride but over-states his hints for tips for the services of his descriptions. Seriously! Our HP guide served us nicely for an hour and a half and never asked for a tip but the boat captain talks for 15 minutes and stands by the door as you leave with a champagne bucket waiting for tips.

We rode the Big Bus Tour some across town. Unfortunately our first ride was a 20 minute wait for the bus we needed and we entered to find the only seats available in the back half of the upper bus (the only portion that is open air) and IN THE RAIN. We were not offered the free ponchos and free earbuds for the pre-recorded commentary on the blue line until we were leaving. Fortunately we had our own umbrellas and earphones, but it would have been nice of the driver to have told us they were available when we boarded. Our second ride was also on the blue line and we did enjoy the view of the city and the descriptions of what we passed. I would have liked to have ridden the red bus with the live commentary but my son was tired and eager to take the first bus available on one trip and the red line didn't go to where we wanted on the other.

The Big Bus is an easy way to hop on and hop off to many stops around town (wish the Globe Theatre was serviced by the bus) including Buckingham, Westminister, Science/History/VA Museums, King's Cross (Platform 9 3/4--which Original London does not service), St Pauls, Tower of London, etc. It's only a few more pounds for the second day which turned out to be a good value for us, even just for transportation if not riding the bus for the tour. They also include a coupon booklet for Hard Rock Cafe, Planet Hollywood, Globe, Churchill Museum, and more. The booklet is only available at four locations, one of which was Marble Arch. We felt we got our money's worth from the tickets even though we did not ride it as much as we had intended.

Before arriving in the UK we Googled which hop on hop off bus tours were available and decided that once we arrived we would use Big Bus Tours. We got on the Big Bus Tour Bus at Green Park stop on 27th May. The staff were very friendly, however they then wanted to sell us tickets to other attractions. We were told that we would not have to queue at these attractions. We eventually settled on Madam Tussauds and the London Eye thus receiving a discount on entry and confirmed with staff (Bilvana) that we had enough time to visit both Madam Tussauds and London Eye. We confirmed that the bus we were getting on stopped at Madam Tussauds, we were told to get off at Marble Arch and tranfer to the "Red Bus". Once getting on the bus and setting on our way we saw that our bus marked "Red Bus" was in fact not going along the red route and bypassed Madam Tussauds altogether. We were told by Bus Staff that there were no buses going to Maddam Tussauds on that day due to road works. It then took over an hour to get from Regent Street to Trafalgar Square all the while listening to a tour guide laughing at his own jokes and not pointing out any sights. Not satisfied with wasting any more time we got off the bus and spoke to the Bus Company Staff at the next stop who told us that we could receive a refund but that we had to go back to Green Park in order to get one. As it was already nearing 2:30pm and we were close to the London Eye we walked the rest of the distance to the London Eye only to find that we had to queue to exchange our London Eye Bus voucher for an actual ticket and then queue again to get on the London Eye for a 30 minute London Eye ride. Once finished we high tailed it to the Underground to Maddam Tussauds. Again we found we had to queue with everyone else to gain entry. The time this tour wasted and especially the money could not be worse. We could have got to more attractions by using the underground. The bus ticket was 27 pounds and all we got for it was a couple of pounds discount off two attractions that we got ourselves to and rushed around because of the time - thankfully we didn't purchase any other tickets to other attractions as we would have missed them altogether. Although the ticket was valid for 24hours - we were leaving London the following day so we would have been unable to use it.

Unlike some of the other reviewers, my husband and I thought this was the "best bang for the buck" thing we did during our entire week in London. We followed Rick Steves' guidebook and took the tour on a Sunday and caught the 8:30 AM bus near Victoria station. We caught the Red line because we wanted the live tour (the Blue line is pre-recorded). We hopped off at Trafalgar Sq. around 9:30 AM and came back an hour later for the walking tour to catch the changing of the guards. Our tour guide, Phil Harris, was FANTASTIC -- super knowledgeable and funny. We hopped back on later in the day and no problems finding a bus. The longest we had to wait was 10 minutes. Our ticket included a free boat ride on the Thames which was quite fun. We highly recommend making this a "Day 1" activity for any trip to London. Ignore the negative reviews and do the Big Bus tour!

The tour and the guides were fine, but their sales reps go over the line in pushing other attractions. At each stop along the tour there are company reps who will sell you tickets to other London attractions, and indeed their prices are usually a couple of GBP less than at the door. We were interested in possibly going to the London Dungeon, but had an 8 year old boy with us. He likes scary movies and video games, but we had our concern about whether the Dungeon was appropriate for someone that young. The Big Bus rep that we put this question to said, without hesitation, that it was fine for someone his age so we bought the tickets. When we arrived at the Dungeon I checked all the info outside to see if there were any warnings or "may not be appropriate...." messages, but found none. Upon entering you have to exchange your Big Bus voucher for tickets and then wait in line to enter. In the hallway between the ticket counter and the actual entrance there are two displays, one of a man hanging upside down being skinned alive, and another of a guy with a bloody stake through his chest. At this point I went up to the head of the line and asked the gate minder if this was the worst of it, and she told me, with concern, that it got much worse once you enter. We immediately went back to the ticket counter and were told "NO REFUND", though after listening to our concerns they agreed to give us back our BB voucher so we could pursue a refund from them. I have since written to BB twice asking for a refund but have not received a reply. As a person who travels internationally for a living I am used to various approached to dealing with customers, but I did not expect this sort of treatment from two British tourism companies. It's one thing to take the money and run, but it's quite another to mislead customers when a child's mental well being is in question. Our boy could not get to sleep for hours that night as a result of the images in his head. Apparently BB does not understand the power of these review sites. If you agree that these companies should be careful with their recommendations in cases like this then please book your London bus tour with the other hop on-hop off company.

Booked on line for a family of 5 for £72. At 10am on our first pick up outside Royal Mews, Buckingham Gate we were offered £19 for a second days tour, whilst trying to board with 3 children and the driver shouting to other paying customers to hurry up!. When we tried to buy the £19 ticket offer later, when it was practicable & had proper time, we were then told by a Big Bus scout, "Tuff mate! You should have purchased it earlier"! We then called the HO, as we thought there must be a mistake. After 15 minutes we eventually got through to Danielle who also said Tuff!? You'll have to pay another £72.
Go FIGURE?!!

I asked Danielle to explain what difference it made if we purchased the offer a matter of hours later on THE SAME DAY? She said, the sales manager & the computer say NO!
We were Ripped-Off, Misled and Mis-Sold.

Furthermore, throughout the tours NOT ONE member of staff was friendly, they were all curt, impatient and spoke to customers as if they were their enemies. When will Big Bus Tours understand, it starts and ends with the customer! I would never use Big Bus tours again nor recommend them to friends or family.

Loved the Big Bus tour of London this month. Big Steve provided the commentary upstairs on the bus and was fantastic - cracked great jokes, knows so much about the various places around London and answered all our questions - would thoroughly recommend doing this.

We bought tickets with River cruise, and decided to take the last cruise of the day which is at 19.15, we reached the peir at 19.04 and waited till 19.30 still no sight of Big Bus crew nor City Cruises crew. That is not acceptable.. Tried to call but no number to call and when I sent emails to Big Bus company, there is acknowledgement of received of my emails but no response after that. That doesn't seems to be professional at all. Very disappointed..

On visiting London my wife and I decided to leave one of our days free for the famous London open top bus tour, which we did yesterday. The tour itself whisks you around fast enough, in some cases far to fast to take pictures, but I guess the flow of London traffic dictates that to a degree. My main problem was the unhelpful attitude of a few of the staff, they certainly lacked the necessary skills for a customer facing role.. One particular tour guide called Emma took it on herself to introduce her own political bias into her commentary as we passed the home of previous Prime minister Thatcher and then continued to jibe away on some kind of markist rant of envy about the affluence of the people who could afford to live in that area.. I know for sure her comments got the back up off at least a couple more tourists. On the plus side the previous guide Lewis who she had replaced near Buckingham Palace was very helpful and amusing.

We love the hop on bus in any city, and especially here! We found the service to be easily accessible from our hotel by the London Tower. We never waited more than a few minutes for a bus. Saw all the major attractions. We especially enjoyed the red line tour with the fabulous guide, Laura! She was very knowledgeable and added lots of interesting facts to the tour, even making the rush hour traffic more bearable!

We did 3 of the routes over 2 days. The best tours were when we had a live guide and it wasn't raining. London's rains come and go without much warning and we endured on the top of the bus because it was so crowded and stuffy below. One of the best guides was Roland. He had some good gossip on London's past. We were in London for 5 days and this helped us figure out where things were and what we wanted to return to later. Traffic is crazy so never plan on being somewhere at a certain time.

Worst tour company ever. They hire criminals to work for them. We live in NYC and went to London with a baby and a toddler. We got on the first bus at Baker St stop and the tour operator scanned the QR code from email/eticket with his scanner but apparently he didn’t actually scan and it didn’t print any slip. We didn’t know that we would need a slip to get on the next bus. When we tried to get on the next bus, the driver rudely called us liars when we explained that the first bus tour operator didn’t give any slip. He said ‘don’t use little kids’ to try to get a free ride. We carried the babies and stroller off the bus and took the photos of the driver and bus for inquiry in case we need to request a refund since we were denied the tour. The driver ran off the bus to stand towering over me and the kids and attempted to grab my phone to smash it. I was scared for the kids. He calmed down when I said I only took the picture of the bus and left.

We later found another tour operator who scanned the eticket and printed the slip for us to get on the next bus.

This is unacceptable that the company that hires criminals (i guess cheap labor) really needs to do background checks on their job applicants. This guy is clearly MENTALLY DISTURBED and VIOLENT.

We are five Americans that wanted to spend our outing exploring all must-sees in London. We were able to hop on to a bus in the afternoon to start our journey. When we arrived to a stopping bus location, we were introduced to “Big Steve” for a walking tour. “Big Steve” was fun, informative, personable and would recommend him to anyone! We were able to check our bucket list off in the most personable way. We couldn’t have asked for a better experience, thanks to “big Steve”!!!!

It cost us £80 for the tickets in the post office on Gloucester Road. Started off on the Blue line, what a complete waste of time. Seen very little of interest and slow moving in the traffic. We got off all at Trafalgar Sq, and switched to the Red line. Which was fabulous, very interesting, also a good guide on the bus. He was very funny but I don’t think he realise it.
So top tip just do the Red line, Central London attractions. Hop on and off to suit yourself.
I really wanted to take a picture of the staff who gave us the ticket, rude and arrogant. We tourist didnt come here to be insulted by the likes of you . Shame on your service.

I toured on the Big Bus Hop-On Hop-Off touring around London, Emma the tour guide was an exceptional tour guide, she was very informative, knowledgeable, great personality, and funny...I would do it all over again!! I was impressed with the statue of her grandmother on one of the buildings. You can see how proud she is to talk about her grandmother and aunts. Had a great time touring with you!! 🤗🙏🌹

I have done bus tours before and really enjoyed them, but the Big Bus in London was very disappointing. First, we waited about 20 minutes for a bus to come, elbowed our way on, only to have to get back off because there weren't enough seats. Then we got on the next bus and had to take a bottom row seat, which is essentially worthless because you can't see anything. Finally we moved up top, which was better, but our guide was very average in the information he provided. We got off just past Buckingham Palace for a bite to eat. When we lined up to wait for the next bus, the unfriendly man in the picture was waiting beside a Big Bus that sits on the curb apparently just for show because we weren't allowed to enter the bus, despite it being cold and windy. All this man could do was grunt that the next bus would arrive in 12 minutes, then he would resume looking at his cell phone. When 20 minutes went by and still no bus, and we asked again, he got even more rude. Big Bus would do better to have no one than this guy!! He was worthless! Our next bus guide was a little better. His shift ended, and our final guide was actually quite good. If I were to do a London bus tour again, I would try a different company. At least those buses seemed to run much more frequently.

Since we moved to London around 10 years ago we have done the Big Bus Tour 3 times and we always recommend it when we have family and friends visiting us.
With one ticket you can use all their different lines and hop on and off during the day so if you plan your day well you won't need to take the tube or public transport, you can use the bus tour to move around instead (don't try to improvise and start your tour as early as possible... so you have enough time to see everything!).

They have live guides on the red route, but they will give you a pair of headphones when you hop on the bus the first time to listen to the recorded commentary in different languages.

Their tickets include a free River Cruise which is quite fun if you are travelling with kids.

We were in London last week & jumped on the first bus that came by...lucky us! Emma was fantastic-informed & funny, she led us on a great adventure through the Red Line full of facts & stories that interested all.

We loved this tour bus & especially enjoyed Emma’s personality. Great tour, great guide & great city!

We loved our Big Bus Tours and wished we had learned the names of all the tour guides to give them a shout out. With some tour guides we hated to exit the bus at our stop because we were so entertained! We especially loved Lewis and Giles. Thank you for a wonderfully funny and memorable tour around your lovely city!

We booked a full-day bus tour with river cruise and spent all day travelling around London.
The audio guides were good but we particularly enjoyed listening to Joe, who was both informative and entertaining...thank you, Joe (photo attached)!
However, we found that the majority, although not all, of the bus drivers were surly and unfriendly, which was not a great welcome as we got on a bus.
Despite that, I would recommend this company for their extensive route network and additional river cruise, which gives new and old-comers to London a great way to learning and discovering more of London.

We arrive mid afternoon in London on Fri. Aug 3 and thought a shorter night tour would give us a basic lay of the land rather than paying for a full day. The bus pickup options were 8p, 830p, and 9p from Marble Arch - one of 3 pickup locations. Unfortunately, Marble Arch is the last pick up of the 3 stops and all 3 buses were completely full when they arrived to us. We purchased 8 tickets online and were even wondering if it would be available but when the payment was processed and we received our tickets we thought we were all set. There were at least 30-40 people at the same stop in the same situation. The Big Bus Representative said that no other buses were coming and they don’t call in other buses when full. We were advised to contact the company to request a refund. We have made 2 attempts to contact through their website with not response yet. That is $211 or 162 pounds we are waiting on.

From the airport, we took the Heathrow Express to Paddington Station and hopped on from there. We had purchased tickets in advance but they were available on the bus as well. We took the blue route (there are three options of routes) because it was the largest and covered the most places. A really nice surprise is that there is an option to hop off at Big Ben/London Eye and switch to a river cruise. You can take this to London tower and rejoin the bus there. The cruise was fantastic, very informative and an entertaining announcer/tour guide. There is a snack bar and actual bar on that boat. The blue route has prerecorded tour guides. They provide ear phones. The red route has live tour guides. Overall, I would recommend this tour.

We have been to London several times, but had never done the "Hop on, Hop off" bus tour. So today we decided it was time.
While we initially paid for a 24 Hour Ticket that we bought at a store close to our hotel, the Big Bus Tour employee at Paddington Station where we were going to board the bus convinced us to upgrade to a 48 Hour Ticket that included a river boat trip to Greenwich.
What a thoroughly enjoyable day we had. We were away from our hotel for over 9 hours & got to see a lot of London. Tomorrow we will do a different route. Well worth the upgrade.

First time in London. 2 day pass was excellent. Karen who did the commentary on the Red bus was incredible. Excellent communication, checked on passengers regularly and was very helpful. Cruise on theThames was fabulous as well. We really enjoyed the ‘non recorded’ commentary done by a staff member. The Drivers on the buses could have been former precision drivers, the skills needed to navigate the streets of London were excellent.

We came to London for Valentine's Day and booked a bus for one day (with a complimentary 24 hours added). On the first morning, we waited over an hour for a bus to come. We wanted to see Buckingham Palace and Changing of the Guard Tour at 10. We finally took the underground to the stop nearest the Palace. It was 9:25 by this point. We finally found a Big Bus and asked them if they could get us to the appropriate stop for the 10:00 tour. They said they couldn't. They validated our ticket and gave us walking directions to find the tour guide. We finally found him just in time. Jack, the tour guide, did a great job.
Afterwards we found a bus to ride on for a short while, if only to rest our feet. The live commentary was just ok. We only used the bus one more time that day, again to rest. The blue line with audio commentary was actually better than the live.
We intended to ride the bus the next day just to tour the London bridge area, but after waiting another 30 minutes for a bus (there was a bus that kept circling but it was flashing out of service), we just decided to spend our money on the underground. Really hate that we wasted $80 on this service.
I had really studied the different companies and read a lot of reviews and thought I was picking the best one. :(

We visited London two weeks ago and the first thing we decided to do was a bus tour with these guys. The ticket was expensive at £32pp but it looked to be great and the ticket seller was lovely so we said we would give it a go. We purchased our tickets at the bus office at Hyde Park and headed over to the pick up point. This was where it went downhill. Rude staff, arguing with each other and with competitor companies and insanely rude drivers. We got on regardless. The bus was comfortable and the tour knowledgeable but traffic was a nightmare. We got off and explored by foot instead. Once we got on the next bus, we had a live commentator. This should be great we thought, they'll be a lot of fun (as advertised by the company). However, the girl was no more interested in working, informing us of the sites etc etc. All monotones and extremely depressing. We got off at the next stop, which took us 40 minutes to get to with the traffic and I have to say, getting off that bus was the greatest relief. We didn't use our second day of the ticket and out of our whole trip, this was the only experience we truly hated.
