I would also like to mentioned that we stopped at Madame Tussauds for almost 30 minutes while a delivery of bakery items was removed from our tour bus??? Not professional at all. I wouldn't recommend anyone to go on this tour.

We booked our tour of London with this pathetic company and deeply regretted our decision.We waited an hour for our tour bus!!! and were repeatedly lied to that our bus was stuck in traffic.They tried to herd us on to any old bus in order to get rid the problem.We eventually boarded our bus. The tour commentary was boring and uninformative.However we did see the place where Sweeney Todd cut his customers throats. Believe me, when we got off this bus we felt like cutting our own,if you book with this company you will do so at your peril !

The Good: The company offers a Blue line, a Red line, an Orange Line, and a Green Line (see their website map). The Green line is basically a short segmen transport line from Kings Cross Station, with stops that overlap much of the Blue and Red lines, so not much value there. Blue and Red lines cover identical stops. Blue Line (recorded audio) is needed if you don't understand English but otherwise I would avoid the Blue Line. The Red line with a live guide is soooo much better. Our guide was Tony and he was the best. He spoke nearly the full time, pointed out things, told great stories and was enjoyed by all, ages 13-53. You will be very happy if you find yourself on a bus with Tony. Also, he was great for answering questions and was very patient. If you go on a day without rain and can sit on the top with a live guide you will have a great experience. Bring suntan lotion when you sit on the top if you are prone to burning. Up top on the bus the speakers with the live guide are under certain seats. If your hearing is not the best try different seats trying to find one that allows you to hear the best,

The Not So Good:
RAIN!!! Rain will ruin your experience. First, despite the free ponchos and the allowed use of umbrellas the top level of the bus is uncomfortable and you will get wet. Even after the rain ends the seats are wet and water will fall from trees and get blown back from the front of the bus. Staying below is not a great option because people pack in on the lower level like sardines, you can barely see out; if you are standing and on a blue line it is hard to find a place to plug in your headset.

Orange Line!!!! Unless you have a special place you want to see on the Orange Line it was not a very great tour. However, there are a few places worth seeing as long as you are willing to get off and explore, otherwise as just a tour it is not great.

Blue Line!!!! About 75% of your ride is spent listening to music with interspersed small sections of word descriptions. If the live guide gets a rating of A+, I would give the recorded audio on the Blue Bus a C- grade. Also, the audio is not always perfectly timed with the bus location and there is no one to point at the exact area the audio wants you to see.

In summary,if this is your first trip to London, I would suggest, if you have enough time, to ride the Red bus once around with a guide. The rest of the day use either the Red and/or Blue line to take you back to those areas you want to see more, using the bus like an inefficient taxi service that is prepaid, Most importantly, get all you want accomplished before the expected time that rain will begin or better yet pick a day with little or no chance of rain. It rains a lot in London, so it may not be that easy.

My husband and I took the Night tour on May 25, 2016. To be fair, we did see some iconic sights--that was the good part. The tour, however, goes on way too long to hold one's attention. The main reason I wanted to do this particular tour is the return hotel service in certain neighborhoods, which included ours --Kensington (since it's about 10 pm when you get through). I can't speak for every driver but here's what our driver did. He drove a big double decker bus like a bat out of hell. Truly. When it was time to end the tour, I heard him tell one anxious passenger "I don't know how you're getting back to Baker Street, mate" and dropped him and several other passengers at a bus stop. At this point, we're the only two left on the bus. After telling us he'd get us back to our hotel (Crowne Plaza on Cromwell Rd) he drops us off on the edge of Hyde Park in the dark, while laughing "I don't know where your hotel is but go over to that bar and have a drink". This was our first trip to London and we had no idea how to get back to our hotel, not to mention that Hyde Park is reportedly the most dangerous place to be in London after dark. So we began walking and luckily found a couple of people who got us back to our hotel about 2 miles later. I think this is the first extremely negative review I've ever written, so it isn't a habit. Also, I feel like this must not be typical, since the tour gets many good reviews. But buyer beware, the success of your trip depends on the driver you get.

In the two first buses we jumped on the sound did not work at around half of the seats. When we waited at London Tower we saw "reality show" where an employee from big bus got into a discussion with an employee from another bus company. The big bus employee ended spitting at the other man several times, shouting loud and acting very unprofessional. Embarrassing to be part of

The BigBus Tour is a must for sightseeing London. We bought a 24hr ticket that included a boat trip from Tower Bridge to Westminster. Our only regret was that we didn't buy the 48hr pass!! A lot of the time, the bus doesn't move much faster than walking pace because of the traffic and it allows you to view all the sites in comfort, away from the very crowded pavements. The commentary on the red bus is fantastic, made all the better by our guide LEANNE...... AMAZING!!!! Excellent value for money, and a welcome break for tired feet. Definitely recommend

I want to start out by saying that we aren't usually organized tour bus people, but some of our friends convinced us to take the Big Bus, and they were right!

We went to London in March, so it was not busy at all. We bought the 48 hour pass which worked out very well. On day one we took the first morning bus (Red Line) leaving from the Mayfair stop, and did a full loop of the city. It helped us to get our bearings, and when you take the Red Line, you get a live tour guide which is great. We had an awesome tour guide named Charlie, she was really funny! We stayed on the bus the whole loop until we got to Westminster which was good timing to hop off and get to the Changing of the Guard.

On day two we took the bus from Mayfair back to the Tower of London stop, visited the Tower, and then got on the River Cruise (which was free with your Big Bus ticket) and took the River Cruise from the Tower of London back down to Westminster Pier.

I did a hop on hop off tour with a friend visiting from Australia. I live in London so know most of the sites. I was really disappointed with this tour, especially the commentary. It missed a lot of detail about areas in London and it was mainly just classical music. I had to tell my friend about a lot of sites as there was no information given. The staff were incredibly rude on every bus we got on to. I do one of these tours in every city I travel in and I'm ashamed to say London has the rudest staff!

My wife and I recently visited London for the first time. We had always wanted to do a bus tour of the city, and after a lot of research into the three main companies, we decided to go with Big Bus Tours. We definitely made the right decision!

Our tour guide, Jack, was extremely knowledgeable and funny. It was raining most of the day (typical) but he managed to make it an outstanding experience regardless.

We got on the Tour at Green Park and did a full tour before riding back to places we wanted to get off and explore further. We did not take advantage of the free River Cruise or Walking Tours, so I cannot speak to them. However, we more than got our money's worth just with the beautiful tour of the city!

A final word of advice-Big Bus Tours has an App for iPhone that was extremely useful, not only for the tour itself but also when exploring the city. It points out the highlights and gives some information about each, similar to the map given by the company but much more convenient. It's free of charge and helped a ton!

Time: 5:55pm, boarding location: Tower of London, date: 6th October 2014.
I am on a weeks tour of London with my family, wife and 2 children, 6 year old boy and an infant. Must say so far we have had a great time, London has been nice until our experience turned horrific an hour back. We boarded the big bus at the above mentioned time and location with 2 kids and a stroller, with continuous rains. As we made ourselves comfortable on the seats, the driver stopped the bus got off and called out specifically to me, in an extremely rude way, asking if I didn't want to show him our tickets. We had a 2 day valid tickets for each of us. Clearly shouting out indicating that we were unpaid customers. Not only this was insulting but extremely rude in front of fellow tourists. On showing him the ticket he actually insisted that I walk upto him and show him the ticket!! This despite the fact that he saw us board with 2 children and a stroller! I did mention that I didn't hear him, why would I not show him the ticket. We were clearly singled out for this special treatment. Is this the way tourists are treated??? Or is it racism?? Will he do the same to fellow Britishers?? Don't think so...clearly would be put in their place. This has left such a bad taste. With my baby infant tired and crying, we had to get off the bus few stops before our destination to avoid any further insults. We got off before the Westminster bridge in rains with a crying baby! Thank you Big Bus, we have used you across the world but you have ended this relationship with insults rather than a welcome message! Never again! There are a lot more operators who we here offer excellent services...

The entire experience with Big Bus was disappointing. We bought our tickets online and went to the information center as directed to pick up the tickets. We were told to turn left out of the office and head down the street one block to the stop on the corner and wait for the next bus. We were also told that a Big Bus attendant would be there at the stop. We got to the stop and there was no attendant. We waited at this stop for more than 30 minutes before a bus arrived, although the advertised times were 10-15. The bus that arrived was completely full inclusive of the aisles. Understandably, the driver would not let any additional passengers on board. By this time as we were waiting we counted at least 3 of The Original Bus Tour Bus's pass by our location. Tired of waiting and not wanting to wait another 30 minutes for the Big Bust to come by again we went back to the information center to seek a refund on our tickets and stated that we were disappointed with our experience and inability to join a tour. At the information center they stated they were unable to provide a refund. Very poor customer service all around. We left the office and went to buy tickets from the Original Bus Company so we could actually take a bus tour that day. The Original Bus Company was much more pleasant to deal with and had more frequent bus service.

I was so very disappointed in this tour company! After taking a hop on hop off tour with Golden Tour Company I figured big bus would be just as good - I was so wrong! The staff was not helpful. They seemed to just be herding people along. We ordered tickets online and were told to just get on the bus at the stops we boarded then late afternoon we stopped for not having 'validated' tickets and were told off for not taking care of that sooner. If you want to see London I suggest buying all day transportation cards. London has great public transport and it is much easier to get around yourself. If you are worried about getting lost I've found the public transport workers more helpful and friend than Big Bus staff. All the tube stations have several workers to answer questions. Londoners are proud of their public transport system and want to talk about it so don't feel ashamed to ask. Overall, Big Bus Tour was a waste of our time and money! Never again!

We just returned from our visit to Europe. Among our trip we had taken a total of 3 hop on hop off tours, one in each city. When we got to London, we purchased a 48 hour pass for the Big Bus Company. The Big Bus Company was horrible! We waited for over an hour for a bus, the men standing at each stop told you what you wanted to hear, not the truth. That is when they were not rude! We were often told traffic was the excuse, but no other company had that issue. We passed a total of 7 buses not in service yesterday. Most of the bus drivers were nasty or just flat out ignored you, and we were told to get on a specific route to see what we wanted to see. Instead we sat on the bus for 2.5 hours of skipped stops and made up routes. To top it off, our bus driver decided to take a 15 minute break, only to proceed to the next stop and tell us the tour is over we need to switch buses!!!!!! We were so annoyed we got off the bus, walked well over a mile to the office to demand a refund. This part was surprisingly easy! They were nice and helpful. Besides them, and a man named Carlos, standing on a bus stop, everyone else was rude. Take a different company. If you don't you will stand there watching those buses come by one after another while you wait in the rain for your bus!

He recommends this tour as one of several that provide hop-on hop-off service to most major attractions. It gave us a great overview of the many wonderful sights and helped us select which ones to go back to on our own. We rode the entire route, getting off once. We also went on a Sunday, as Rick recommends. The employees were all nice, polite and helpful. The live commentary was excellent, the map provided was excellent, and we highly recommend this particularly to first time visitors.

Took the tour with two children, nine and six. Nine year old enjoyed it seeing all the sights and having a great guide on the bus who talked through many interesting language origins from the gallows, sounds odd but it was interesting. All possibly too long for six year old. He slept throughout the bus journey a blessing.
We stopped to take the boat ride included in the ticket. Quite interesting, however the guide had really done it one too many times and was annoying and not funny.
Possibly the worst of all was when we got to the end of the tour under Big Ben, luckily it was at the same time as the famous chimes, we really wanted to hear them. The guide talked over the whole chimes and more besides asking for money. The whole begging blurb lasted several minutes. Didn't we pay for him in the ticket price?!! On and on he went about needing money for the pub and held an ice bucket for us to put money in as we got off having to negotiate the boat to dock. I'd rather he offered the six year old a hand so he was safer.
So generally pretty good but boat tour guide a real spoiler.

We were staying in Paris and decided to take the train to London and spend six hours in the city. I took my camera and was ready to take as many pictures as possible.

We stopped in the tourism shop inside the train station. We purchased two tickets, walked out of the train station and immediately found the bus. We had to change to a bus "on the main tour route" after 15 minutes. This was expected and they told us this would happen.

We boarded the bus and stayed on the bus for the entire trip. While you can get on and off, we did not have time. Becaue the bus picked us up from the train terminal, we did not have to purchase any other transportation ticket. We saw the major sights:
Big Ben
Tower Bridge
Buckingham palace
Piccadilly Circus
St. Paul’s Cathedral
Westminster Abby (not to be confused with Westminster, CO)
Tower of London
Royal Courts of Justice

There were more sights but these were the primary sights I remember.
I shot hundreds of photos. The driver slowed down when we were in front of a major sight.

Note that during the Olympics, some streets are closed to traffic. If you are arriving during the Olympics, check the tour route. The tour took 3.5 to 4 hours. The timing is not an exact science. Halfway through the tour, they announced that the bus was going to change routes and take a shorter route. For us, we did not care. Others might care. the tour bus company talks about having tours with a pre-recorded device (use earphones provided) and an English speaking tour guide. We waited for four buses and they were all the pre-recorded tours. I wanted a speaking tour guide but could not wait any longer. The bused come every 15 minutes but buses with a tour guide are more infrequent. I did get a lot of good pictures in the 6 hours I spent in London and this was a good way to get my photographs and see London.

Aloha from Kaua'i!

We just got back (2 days ago) from a trip that found us with one full day in London (we had to fly home from Heathrow after a Paris vacation) - and we wanted to make the most of that one day.

After doing the "Royal Day Out" at Buckingham Palace we walked across the street to a bus stop that had about 3 different bus tour stops - I had read about the Big Bus tours prior to going on our trip and they were the only ones that actually had a "salesman" standing there (this should maybe have been a tip - no one else did this) who asked us if we needed a ticket and since I really didn't have a preference (I should have done my homework more) we purchased 2 tickets that ended up costing us well over $50 (I've got to look at the receipts but it was a lot).

Unfortunately as we waited there for the bus to come we realized that it was 4pm and their service ended in a couple of hours! While the other bus company ran 24 hours! Now, I realize that I should have done my own homework and realized that we wouldn't be able to take full advantage of The Big Bus tour in the time we had - but I also think it was somewhat unfortunate that their salesman on the spot didn't think to mention that to us either - but at that point we figured we'd just make the most of the 2 hours we had left and get on the top of the bus and see as much as we could.

The bus came and it was jam packed - cheek to jowel literally. Just like the rush hour on the Underground, nothing like a tour bus. No seats up top, no seats down below - people standing in the heat (it was a very hot day, in the 80's farenheit) hanging onto whatever they could grab onto. No audio tours of any kind that you could (or wanted) to hear for us.

We were so miserable that we got off at the first stop they made (no place close to a visitor attraction) and just wrote it off as a very bad idea. We made our way on foot to Westminster Abbey, Big Ben, the London Eye, etc.

The two things that bothered me the most about this experience was that the salesman obviously knew that there was almost no time left in the day for a tour - but sold us a full ticket anyway with no brochure or explanation - we had to find out afterwards while waiting for the bus. Then when we did board, it was absolutely horrendous conditions - as I noted before, it was simply a hot, jam packed bus with no way to see out the windows for the many standing people and no audio of any kind offered.

I loved the very short time we had in London - the people were unfailingly kind and polite and we saw some amazing things - but the only negative thing we experienced was the sales pitch and short bus ride on "Big Bus Tours".

Hi we was in london over the last weekend and was told the big london bus tour was the best way to see the sights of london and you can hop on and off for a 24 hour ticket costin £27.00 per person. What a total rip off ,we got on near knightsbridge and after a hundred metres the bus stopped for nearly 20 minutes but no one was getting on or off the bus was just parked up with the bus scouts trying to sell tickets to other tourists , next stop same thing and after 90 minutes we had just had enough off this and got off. Trading standards need to look at this problem.

My experience with The Big Bus Company of London was not the best one. It happened on 16th of March 2008. I tried to take part of the walk tour that started at 10:00 at Trafalgar Square. It was raining and quite cold but the prospective to see the guard change at Buckingham Palace was fascinating. I arrived at Trafalgar Square 9:50 and walked around the statue but was not able to spot anything resembling the Big Bus or walking tour. In 10:04 I spot an Indian guy in the uniform of Big Bus who at first asked me to show the ticket and then said that the tour had started already. After walkie-talkie conversation he advised me to catch the group. After my question where should I go he told towards "horsgad". Of course I had no idea what the "horsgad" is and even less how to find it. After looking at map I understood that he was talking about Horse Guards, but had no idea how to reach the spot. Big Bus representative tried to explain me in style go there and turn there, I understood every word but had no idea where I should go – nevertheless for the first time in London and really do not know how the streets or places are named here.

In 10:10 I found another representative of Big Bus but he helped me as much as the first.

After that I walked in the rain down the Whitehall street to Parliament Square Big Bus stop, at least so was written on it. There stopped also competing company The Original Tour. After waiting in the rain and at 5 degree centigrade temperature one hour (60 minutes!) and seeing 4 The Original Tour busses passing by and no Big Bus I took the underground and went to Big Bus information centre at Victoria station. There I talked the story and must say that they gave me voucher that allowed to participate in one walk tour and explained that the route of Big Bus was changed and it was not meant to travel by this street. After me asking why the Original Tour buses traveled by this route I got ice cold stare and was told politely that they had already spent on me 10 minutes of their precious time.

After all that I traveled by Big Bus a route. The map I got from information was old and showed not the route bus traveled. The bus had no heating and at the end after 2,5 hours may people were shivering of cold. At the same time it should be mentioned that the guide did well and it was interesting to listen to him. Altogether - not very pleasant memories.

A visitor from Estonia
16.03.2008

With a day to spare my friends and i decided to use a bus tour as a way of seeing the whole city. We paid £19 for our tickets, got the green line bus to meet the red and blue buses which would bring us around the city.
We were dropped off at a bus stop with 10-15 other passengers to wait for the next buses. We were told it should be there in 15/20mins. It was pouring rain and we were all sqeezing in to fit under the bus stop.
30 mins later another green line bus arrived to drop more people off. I asked the driver if he could check when the bus is coming or if we could stay on the green bus because it was raining. The driver obviously wasn't interested in what i had to say & I was told it would be there in 15-20 mins (same line as before) and that we couldn't wait on that bus because the driver had a "Procedure to follow"
When I pointed out that leaving us standing in the rain for 30mins surely wasn't the procedure he informed me that he wasn't going to check now because i was complaining and that i could fill out a complaint form instead. At this stage all of the other people were standing around waiting for an answer too.
For a service that is targeted at tourists i would have thought they would make more of an effort with their customer service but thinking about it they probably don't care because it's not something you would have repeat business from. We were left to just stand and wait, once we had paid our money we got the impression that they didn't care.
Once we got going the tour itself was fine but the fact that we had been soaked from the rain meant that we were freezing for the rest of the day. We had thought that this was a good way to see London and avoid the rain. This is definitely not something that i would recommend. By the way, while we were standing at the bus stop 2 buses from the Original Bus Tour passed us by :-)

Loved driving around London, seeing different sites,only down fall was when got near Buckingham palace all you saw was the side of it and not a front view unless you got off the bus to go look, other than that we really enjoyed it

We had pre-purchased a 3-day London Pass and chose to start our pass on the Big Bus Red tour (it's the only route with a live guide). Our live guide - Emma - certainly made the trip! We started on the first bus of the day, at 8:10am, for an almost-complete loop to get oriented to the city. We were the only people on board for the first half hour, so Emma sat near us and skipped the mic, and it was like we were on a private tour! As a born-and-bred Londoner she was super knowledgable about her city, and we learnt things about London we hadn't heard anywhere else (such as where the term 'daylight robbery' came from). We didn't try the other routes, but can certainly vouch for the Red route as a good way to learn the ins-and-outs of the city before exploring it yourself.

The tours are easy to book and easy to navigate. We had a couple of different guides and they offered extremely knowledgable commentary and humour. The tours routes ensure you see all of the major attractions in London. The only issue with these 'big bus tours' (not just London) is that they only travel in one direction and normally take 2-2.5 hours for a round trip. This means, if you get off on stop 10 and maybe want to go back to stop 8 for lunch ?, then you need to continue full circle (2hours) before you are back at stop 8. I would recommend getting familiar with the route and planning your full day of where you want to get on and off at and where you'll want to have lunch. But great tour

My tour guide, Emma, is a third-generation Londoner, and she REALLY knows her stuff! Her descriptions of the important landmarks were interesting and filled with humor and wit. She even told us when to get ready to take photos so we’d capture the best angles! Emma is top-notch!

We spent 5-6 hours yesterday on the Big Bus Tour, Tues 17 Sept. We bought our tickets from Peter near Oxford Circus, great guy. We did the audio thing on most buses until the last 2 hours when we got Emma. What a breath of fresh air she was. So fun, so enthusiastic about her job and London, found out so many interesting facts about life in London historically and now. She is a credit to your company. Because of her I did not want to get off the bus but alas it was the last bus of the day. Well done Emma.

We enjoyed a leisurely and informative ride with Emma as our guide today on the Red Line during our visit in London. She shared nuggets of information about the various sites, answered numerous specific questions from guests and had the most delightful personality with a fabulous sense of humor - which made it a very enjoyable ride. Loved her spontaneity!
Additionally, we took the Blue line, which unfortunately had a different experience. The pre-recorded site information was boring at best and we had to wait around for almost half an hour for the bus, not to mention traffic was ridiculously slow!
I might add we were incredibly impressed with the drivers we had on both buses - excellent navigation skills and made some very tight corners, as well as being quite pleasant! Thanks much!
Robbin W.

1. Drivers are not friendly. Not willing to answer tourists' questions.Never smile or say hi to customers.
2. Be careful pickpocketing when boarding Big Bus at Tower Bridge. 4-5 women with nice new Muslim clothes pretending to be tourists to stand at crowded boarding time covering each other to pickpocket one lady in our group.
3. Big bus is better than subway for seniors, less walking.

I feel like we waited more then we rode. Very disorganized. Every time we asked a question before boarding they just wanted to sell us entry tickets. Takes the double amount of time to board than the other buses around us. Cometary on the buses were fine. Just extremely disappointed.

Went on 3 seperate buses with live commentary and have to say Emma and Nick (or Adam 🤔) were both very knowledgable, entertaining and interactive with the people on the bus. Our other guide was knowledgeable, but less interactive. Buses with live commentary are really worth it.

Took the big bus tour on visit to London with friend. The lady who was doing the Live commentary (sorry didn’t catch her name, but her grandmother was an artist with a statue of her on a building) she was excellent with lots of interesting facts, and although there was a detour because of a demo, dealt with it professionally and informed us about the river cruise. Recommend completely and thank you for an enjoyable tour
Ian the live tour commentator was just the best seen a few tour guides over the weekend but none were as funny and knowledgeable as ian, I hope he is paid well , because he is worth it

Went to take the bus at Westminster stop and was waiting for the red bus east bound. When asked the one guy I believe his name was Noel. He kepted covering his name badge. He said you have to wait and it comes when it comes. About 20 min later we asked if it would come soon( this was the longest we had waited and about 10 buses came thru) he started screaming at us and made us feel unsafe.my aunt was feeling ill and he said to her if you are sick stay home from holiday. As we got on the bus he waved at us so rudely.
Enjoyed the big bus tour with my family. Had a great tour guide Emma on the red route, very knowledgable about London and its history. All the staff we encountered were friendly and helpful.

Used the red route and exited at Tower Bridge for the River Cruise. After hanging around for the next boat and queuing, we were told by the staff at The cruise that we could not get on the boat as tickets had not been validated. This is done by staff scanning tickets who sold tickets near bus stops. I had booked in advance and this was not mentioned on any email. This was also not mentioned on the bus. In fact I was never even asked to show tickets, drivers were far too busy and stressed. I could have got on for free.

The cruise staff required me to walk all the way back from the Thames up to the main road by the Tower. I had 4 children with me. It was 10 mins walk. On speaking to the Big Bus staff member and stating I was unhappy to miss the boat and waste over an hour (especially as my family had travelled from New Zealand and we were only there for the day), he replied ‘what do you want me to do about that?’. I advised he was representing his company and was looking for an explanation he stated ‘do you want me to scan your tickets or not?’. An appalling way to speak to a customer with a genuine complaint.

As a result we wasted a large part of our day. We were all very inconvenienced and spent over £200 on tickets for this tour bus. Not worth it at all. I would recommend jumping on the tube instead! There are many other bus companies that run more frequently and have staff that actually treat you with respect.

Big thumbs down to the young man working at the Tower of London bus stop. No manners, no apology and no idea on customer service.

we purchased a two day ticket with the hotel concierge. Paid 90.00 for it and found ourselved (and many others) stranded at a bus stop across town. It was cold and rainy. One of the drivers was decent enough to tell us that they are misleading in telling people that basically between 6-8pm, there is no service! Another bus driver said he was off duty at the time and proceeded to yell at a lady asking questions. The next day, we saw the same driver having a yelling match with a co worker at a stop. Also, this company busses were packed all the time. We wish we had booked with Global One I think they were called. They seemed to be much better

We went for the tour on a rainy day so the outdoor seats were unavailable. That was not the problem.

The issue was the most of the other seats had obstructed views due the adverts that were printed on the outside of the windows. A waste of an afternoon. And a waste of money.

We deliberated which hop on/hop off bus tour company to choose. Glad we chose the Big Bus Tour. Reps at Marble Arch (where we purchased 24hr pass) were brilliant. Friendly and efficient and eager to answer any questions we had. No waiting around for a bus at any of the stops en route to reboard and enjoy all the must see sights of London. Must give special mention to two Nicks who were our knowledgeable guides on board. Also Samira. There was one guide (female)who let the Company down. We therefore took the decision to get off the bus and catch the next bus less than 10minutes later. Credit to the drivers also manoeuvering the busy streets along the way.

I spend over £100 on a two day family ticket and what a waste of money. The buses were so full, at one point my family (which includes a 6 &9 year old) were all sitting in different parts of the bus. We were stationary several times for 20 minutes or more, whilst the drivers were changing shifts and on 2 occasions when we eventually did have a seat upstairs, we were told we all had to get off the bus and get on the one behind. We weren't happy to leave our seats and when we got to the other bus there were no seats and we were standing again. At one point we were told to get off the bus, waited at the stop for 15 mins and then were told to get back on the bus again. This was all on day one, we gave up and bought an Oyster card. On Day 2 we didn't even bother, we used the tube. We knew the river cruise would be a disaster and couldn't face it, so didn't even try. Don't waste your time with spending a fortune, look into public transport instead. Save yourself time, cash and the stress!

Last week I used the Paris Big Bus and it was excellent. Just got off the London Big Bus and it was terrible. They fly by a lot of the attractions so you barely see them. You sure don’t get time to take photos or videos. In Paris they slow down or stop so you can see the attractions and photo/video them for memories. The employees in Paris were friendly and helpful, they are not in London. The buses are overloaded in London. They don’t check to see how many are onboard. There were people jammed into the isles on some of the buses.

Ive been to London many times and the place is absolutely huge. There is no way to soak it all in on foot unless you spend a month walking every borough (which I have) But the Big Bus is by far the best way to get a snap shot of most of the inner city and then you can plan what you want to tackle on foot afterwards. Tower of London and Tower Bridge? They Eye and Westminster? Hyde Park and the Palace? Definitely take the bus and sit up stairs (yes even in winter) and you'll experience them all. I first did the tour in 2006 and of course not much has changed with the iconic buildings, but London definitely has - Now as much construction going on as Sydney! We took our 12 year old daughter on it for the first time and she's more in love with London than ever.

Red Route, Mon, July 22 2019, the last circuit of the day with Neil our guide (or was it Nick sorry mate!) and Jamie our driver. Some great commentary (and bad dad jokes, which were also great haha) made the trip that much better. I was the Aussie music promoter just in front of you.

Enjoy!

Over priced, rude drivers, audio instruments not always working, and dirty buses.

Unfortunately I fell for this scam.

We bought a one day trip the other day. Super busy but we'll worth it. We got on the bluet route at Queensway and transferred to the Red route at Marble Arch - the busiest be part of the tour. We stayed on for the full route then started to hop on and off as we had all day. Stephen and Emma were great enthusiastic guides. We'll worth doing as the City is so big and uber busy.

Bought 2 days pass for my daughter and myself. We did one trip (35 minutes) and we could not get back in the bus because our ticket (like receipt paper thin) got destroyed in my pocket. I did show them the email showing reservation but they said that if ticket is lost or destroyed you loose it all. Tried to contact customer service multiple times and nobody responded. You just get a recording.
This would be unimaginable in the US.
To say something good. Looks like they have lots of buses and the 35 minutes drive we did was good.
In summary, tours are probably good but if you loose or ticket get destroyed you loose it all.

Should have known by attitude of first 3 salesmen that they didn't care. Spent the day sitting in traffic or waiting at bus stops (30 mins and ONE hour) as the other companies buses went past. No wifi on 3 of 4 buses. Only visited St Pauls Cathedral and did not complete a whole circuit. Live audio-guide hit and miss. When we got to River Cruise told that our ticket was not valid. Many of the audio-jack points broken so when bus full you are just sitting in traffic. Golden Tours appeared to be offering much better service and customers a lot happier.

DO NOT PAY TO USE THIS COMPANY! They don’t check tickets so anyone and everyone climbs onboard. Crowded, poor queue management, rude staff give inaccurate information, and impossible to reach customer service. Take the free ride but do not give them your money!

We were hoping to get a good city overview on our first day in London so we bought tickets from one of the BigBus sales people (they are everywhere). After waiting an hour at one stop we walked to another but found there were no seats on any busses. The busses were so packed people were sitting on the stairs. Bus stops had big crowds waiting for busses that never came. We were told some of the buses were out of service and it was just tough luck. This company puts all of its money into the sales force and none into the actual product.
very rude staff... no sence for guests big dissapointment London is still a beautiful city worth visiting

We took this bus the day we arrived after a ten hour flight. It was very informative and helpful as it takes you by all of the major attractions so you can figure out what you want to see the most. We got a 3 day ticket because we thought the hop on hop off experience would be easy to get from attraction to attraction. However, it does take quite a long time to get through the route so my suggestion would be to get a one day ticket, figure out what you want to see and then take the tube or taxi to get around.
Emma did a marvelous job describing London and its history to us. She is an avid reader of history, and it shows. She also was quite helpful guiding tourists to their bus stops. Bravo Emma!

Our first time in London and on this hop on hop off bus. Ian said funny jokes and is knowledgeable on London history. He made the ride on the redline a lot of fun! Thank you very much Ian! The blue line was self-guided, informative, but no personality. Recommend this bus company.

Having done many bus tours all over the world, I would say the London Big Bus tour is one of the more well organized tours I've been in. Unlike my experiences in some other cities, the tour stops in London are well organized and clearly marked. Buses come at greater frequency and reliability than I've experienced in other cities also. I would definitely recommend this tour as a great way to see all that London has to offer in a short time. They actually offer 5 different tours (4 day tours, 1 night tour). Be warned however, the traffic in London is pretty slow (as expected). So be prepared to be sitting in some heavy traffic. You may want to try to tour outside of rush hour times to avoid some of the traffic. Overall a great experience with informative live tour guides. The live tour is given in English with a guide. For non-English speakers you can use plug in headphones (provided complementary with tour) to listen to the tour in 12 other languages.

Walk and use an app (Citymapper) to navigate The Tube, and skip the bus.

We bought a two-day pass and used it for 1 1/2 rides. We jumped off for some shopping, and then jumped back on. The bus was crowded and the only seats were at the very back - where we got to sit on the hot engine and smell the delightful diesel fumes. After 20 minutes and barely moving down the road at all, we jumped off a the next possible stop and spent the rest of the time walking and taking The Tube. Much more pleasant experience. London is a walkable town with some excellent transit options. You'll see more and enjoy it.

The most convenient way to see the major areas of the city.Incase you are staying for long take it in the initial days as it will familiarise you with the city n the major landmarks.
Start early to cover all routes n get off only at places you don’t wish to visit otherwise.

They these guys are in over a hundred cities around the world. In London, they are not only cheaper than taking the tube, but you get fantastic information from the live presenters.

I took all four routes over the course of 5 days. Only the red route had a live presenter so keep that in mind. The information provided was very entertaining and helpful. The routes covered almost all of the cities attractions and offer a great way to see the sights while getting to your destination - far better that using the underground.

I have a tip...

I took each route a different day to maximise my time. For each route, I stayed on the bus for the entire route and planned where I wanted to spend more time. With that list in hand, as the bus restarted its route again, I knew exactly where I wanted to get off and where to get back on the bus.

We were lucky enough to have the amazing guide Emma on our tour. She made the Big Bus trip the highlight of our day! We were supposed to get off half way along the route, but chose to do a full lap of the red route instead because we were having such a great time. Emma was very knowledgeable and shared many interesting and amazing facts about London. It gave us a whole new perspective of London and really made the city come to life.

We had the three day pass so we did the red, orange, green and blue tours. Fantastic way to see any location and some attractions a few times as the tours overlap in a few areas.
Make sure to download a map of the tours before you arrive and plan your tours to suit you. The red tour covers the largest area so is the most crowded but if you plan your movements you can hop on and off at attractions to avoid the worst congestion on the bus.
The guides onboard the buses vary but in general are very informative. We found Danial to be the best on our three days.

Fantastic live commentary from Daniel on the red route. He was very knowledgeable and shared lots of fantastic information and stories bout the city!
Easy to purchase tickets- friendly and helpful staff. Great way to see the sights.

We used the bus tour and river cruise over 2 days. Our guide on the bus was Ricky and driver was Julian. Both very friendly and helpful.
Ricky is a true gentleman and speaks beautiful queens english.
He was engaging, informative and knowledgeable about the sights of London. He asked us where we lived and said what a beautiful place the Lake District is. I am a true English citizen and will always use my manners and wait in line patiently. Can’t say the same for some of the other tourists on the bus. Complaining about not been able to get on the top deck and wanting their money back! Which poor Ricky dealt with in sympathetic and dignified manner.
Also people standing up on the top deck to take selfies of themselves going over tower bridge. No one else could get a decent view from their seats. It clearly states on notices not to stand up! However.... this is no reflection on the bus trip company or it’s staff. Call me old fashioned, but if everyone was more thoughtful then there wouldn’t be a problem.

Enjoyed the tour as a whole. The guides we had were informative.
Lewis was particularly engaging with those on the bus sore throat and what not.
Overall we enjoyed the tour.

We took Big Bus Hop-on-Hop-off tour just for first seven stops, but this little trip was absolutely delightful! Our guide Emma was not only highly knowledgeable, but also charming and funny. It was obvious that she is absolutely in love with her city and wants us to feel the same. We were lucky to have her on our route.
Rina &Joseph, U.S.A.

I bought my 1day pass for tgat same day on TripAdvisor given they say how easy it is to book and redeem. I was sold and wanted to avoid waiting in line or going to a booth to buy a ticket. So i do that and show up at the nearest bus pickup...they say they can't accept my email confirmation. I need to print it out (I'm in the middle of nowhere) and bring the printout to their office( which was miles away from where i was) to exchange it for a valid ticket because the email confirmation has no barcode for them to scan. I had only 1 day to visit and bought the ticket that afternoon with only a few hours left before the last bus....given the huge hassle to get a ticket and time was an issue, i was forced to buy another ticket from them. I asked TripAdvisor for a refund, the answer was NO because it was less than 24hrs before the ticket is expired. paid twice for a 2hr bus ride. Very dissapointed in the TripAdvisor purchase process. The tour company said that i should just buy it on their website which provides a barcode that any stop can validate. TripAdvisor doesn't have that. This was my first purchase with TripAdvisor and definitely my last.

Thanks Tripadvisor

I did this on my last day in London, should have done it day one. This tour is good to get around, see the city and get some narration about where you are going. I got to see a lot in one day. This saves a lot of walking too. Good way to see any major city.

Me, my daughter and nephew, enjoyed the service of the Big Bus, we booked for two days plus a river cruise, no time for the walking tour, also included. We used all the four routes to see all the possible.
A part the bus, we appreciate the City Cruises nice boat and, instead of headphones, ask to the bar a special gadget. Another important thing is that showing the tickets, you can have a prices discount and a preferable way of entrance in a places, as for example Madame Tussauds.
But are not all roses: sometime the waiting from a bus to the next could be very "long"! Well. that's life!

I booked this on a last-minute trip to London, for which I had no time to plan. I flew overnight, and figured this would be a great way to see a lot, especially given that I'd be jetlagged but wanting to push through the day. I was right! I rode the entire circuit of two of the routes. Not only did I see many of the sights, I also got a good orientation to city. Had two different tour guides - one was much better than the other, who yelled a lot, got into a row with a passenger, and otherwise said the bare minimum as we passed sights. I only wish that I had been able to get out again the next day, as the ticket would have been a great way to get around to hop-off at some sights, after I was rested. I will plan to do this on future visits to new cities.

We had a great experience on our Big Bus. Of course it was raining buckets the day we did this; but we toughed it out. Sat on top and inside; just had to be prepared.

I will say that we did have a difficult time finding the location of this bus and we kept being guided in different directions; to the wrong buses; and it was stressful getting onto it. Perhaps we should have selected the more central location near the changing of the guard...? THAT was much easier to deal with - so I guess that's my tip. Also included with our ticket was the London Eye; and that was a fun experience as a combination ticket.

I took the Hop-On Hop-Off Bus Tour, taking the Red Route, 7 January 2019. Although I had planned to use the Hop-On feature, I ended up riding the bus for the entire route, because our guide Emma was phenomenal! Her knowledge of London, including her story of her personal tie to the statuary, made the trip so much more interesting and enjoyable.

I did use the Hop-on Hop off service later in the day, but only after I toured the entire route with Emma. I would highly recommend this tour (get there early for a great seat!) for anyone wanting a quick overview of London.

We had Emma giving us the talk and she was so enthusiastic about London it was a Joy she brighten our day 😊very informative and her love of London was very evident 👍if you get it online you save 10 % and the cruise was something I have always wanted to do and wasn’t disappointed.

Giles, Kathy, and LuAnn all deserve 5 stars. They were great on the live tours. I can say there is a lot to see in London and those guides gave me different views and excellent tips on what are major points to see. I really liked to boat tour with the tower bridge with a great clear view.
Great way to see London! Just the Queen taxes were crazy! Thats nothing against the big bus tour.

If you are planning a trip to London then the best way to see the whole city is by booking a good tour with Big Bus, specially when you have time constraint. It is best to download the app and plan your route beforehand. You can visit all the landmarks. The bus covers up all possible areas. We took the one with a river cruise and could visit Greenwich also. The guides on the cruises are very good and give complete information and history about London. I would highly recommend these tours.

Emma our tour guide was amazing. She was very detailed and knowledgeable of history of the city. She gave tips that the other tour guides did not. She wasn't just speaking like she was reciting things she memorized. She spoke with passion about the city and you could tell she loved her home town.
The other tour guides were okay but not as knowledgeable as Emma.
I wish I knew the bus route she handled to recommend people to take that particular bus.

My wife and I have spent the last two days using this company and we have experienced the full range of service.

Firstly the sublime, today we travelled on the red route from Marble Arch to The Tower with tour host Allie, who gave us a magnificent presentation of facts and items of interest, what a great asset this young woman is to this company.

The Ridiculous, over the two days we experienced other lazy fat male hosts who wouldn't or couldn't stand up to do the presentation and who provided a boring mono syllabic presentation.

One whose trousers were barely covering his bum, sat down and ate during his " so called presentation".

And the grand finale was the arrogant stupid driver who drove past bus stop 32 on the blue route on the Bayswater Road and denied it was a designated stop.

All this despite another young couple who showed him the map provided and our both confirmations that we had got on and off at this stop for the past two days.

There are other companies who provide the same services and I'd strongly recommend not using this one.
Did the tour of London with Laura as our guide. She was fantastic very informative and personable not like listening to Wikipedia.

We usually take a hop on hop off bus tour on the first day of our visit to a new city. We have done this in many cities all over the world so this is not our first time.
We clearly rate the London Big Bus Hop On Hop Off operator as the WORST of it’s kind. Their guides and drivers clearly DO NOT UNDERSTAND the meaning of CUSTOMER SERVICE. They make a joke of their trip schedules and bus routes by making arbitrary changes without explanations. And it’s not just one tour guide & driver team. When the driver and guide parked the bus we were on at the Hyde Park area around 11am, all the tourists were just left on their own. The other Big Bus tour guides, drivers and supervisors hanging around were just as callous about the fate of their paying customers. To prove how terrible the employees of London Big Bus tours were, I only got help for directions from a RIVAL hop on hop off operator. This outfit should be investigated by the London Tourism Board.

One of the highlights of our holiday in London was going to be the Hop On Hop Off tour with Big Bus. My children (ages 11 and 14) and I were really looking forward to it. We read the reviews and although we had seen a number of bad reviews, we had also read some good ones, and decided to go with Big Bus as opposed to Golden Tours, which was our other option with the London Pass. What a monumental mistake! I cannot imagine any HOHO tour could have been any worse. Why? Here's why:

1. My main complaint is with the ridiculously poor live commentary we were given. The tour guide herself was extremely polite and friendly, but her commentary was so infrequent and poor, that I ended up explaining what we were seeing myself to my kids. Her knowledge of both the historical and modern sights was superficial and even though those on board the bus were asking questions, her answers were of the briefest kind, and with the most basic of information. Surely, more can be said about Lambeth Palace than, 'It's where the Archbishop of Canterbury lives'? Especially after I actually had to ask what building we had just passed!!!!! Her commentary on Big Ben was restricted to how long it was going to be covered up for, and how some people had cried when it chimed for the last time before the works began. Surely some information about its creation, architect, cultural significance etc would have been the minimum we should have received? This type of poor commentary was what we were subjected to throughout the whole hour we sat on the bus.

2. On our second journey the same afternoon, we found there was no live commentary. We were disappointed, as we had hoped to get a better guide than earlier, but decided to make do with the audio guide. Yet again, we were extremely disappointed. This time, not only was the standard of the information given on a par with that provided by the tour guide earlier, but 95% of the time we were subjected to classical music, with no commentary whatsoever!!!!! We drove past Belgrave Square with the briefest of explanations. Something on the lines of, 'This is Belgrave Square where some countries have their embassies'.

3. There was no airconditioning on either of the buses we rode on. I would have thought that in this day and age airconditioning in buses in summer would have been standard. Our choice was to roast on the bottom level in the closed area, or fry in the direct sunlight at around 35 degrees celsius. Neither option was at all appealing.

4. At one point, our driver pulled up into the bus lane and stopped the bus. At first we thought we were in a traffic jam, but soon realised that the traffic was moving past us. After about 10 minutes, my children and I decided we had had enough of this terrible tour, and made our way to the bottom level of the bus to leave. When we alighted, we realised that the bus driver was not in his seat, and that he had left the bus without even informing those riding the bus! We were shocked that he had done this, and wondered if perhaps he was feeling ill. As we walked away from the bus, we caught sight of the driver having a chat with some people further down the street! We then proceeded to look for a tube station and having eventually found one, visited the toilets. Once finished, we came out and found ourselves face to face with the bus driver who was going to the toilet himself. This means that the bus had now been without a driver for at least 20 minutes, and the people on board had no idea what was going on! This sealed it for us - We had waste dour time and money on Big Bus, and would have been better off choosing another tour company.

All in all, our experience with Big Bus Tours was terrible. I ask all those who have had similar experiences to write reviews too, as perhaps this will encourage them to get their act in order and provide the service they boast about online:
'Our entertaining and experienced English-speaking guides will offer an exciting and educational commentary throughout the duration of your Red Route (Best of Central London) bus tour. Relax and enjoy fascinating facts and stories about London's rich culture and dramatic history as you pass its famous landmarks and iconic architectural highlights.'
Our live guide and pre-recorded commentary were neither entertaining nor experienced, and we did not 'enjoy fascinating facts and stories about London's rich culture and dramatic history'.

Extremely disappointing:(

Service was irregular and the bus we got on had bad audio. The girl who was the guide on one bus was a star but I think she got irate customers who couldn’t hear anything since the audio system wasn’t working
No safety precautions like seat belts etc and the guys scanning the tickets are only interested in selling you top ups
We had a better experience in San Francisco
You maybe better off taking an Uber and chatting with the drivers

Extremely poor commentary. Back round music very irritating. A few comments from the actual bus driver were the best parts. Sitting in traffic most of the day. Id recommend familiarizing yourself with the tube/ underground and visiting everything that way. Definitely not worth the money. It's only saving grace was the river cruise which was brilliant. The guide on the boat was great fun and really made the whole experience.

I've taken Big Bus tours in 3 cities now, and always end up being disappointed. The tours themselves are great, and very informative, and the live guides are always entertaining. But the advertised lines of "buses run every 15-20" minutes is not always accurate; twice I've waited 45 minutes for buses. On one occasion (in London), several stops were closed for the weekend, but the company didn't bother to post signs at the stops to let us know. And on several occasions, when buses have reached my stop, they've been so full that it's "standing room only", and we had to ride a hot, crowded bus without being able to plug in headphones to hear the recorded commentary. I'm done with this company....gonna try a different tour bus service on my next trip.

Got a 48hr ticket for the Big Bus Tour (which included a free night tour, city cruise and a walking tour). I’ve read a few negative reviews about them but I have to say we didn’t find anything negative. It’s a great way to get around London and to hop off when you want to see certain areas or attractions. Yes they might turn up late at certain stops but what do people expect when they’re driving in a busy city like London!! It’s not the underground or a river cruise! There is traffic!! The commentary is brilliant. We had one French lady called Aude who was very knowledgeable with her history of London. Very enthusiastic too and a friendly lady. Worth doing in my opinion as you get to see a lot of London (I’ve been to London quite a few times over the years and this was the first time doing a bus tour) plus we saw a lot that we’ve never seen before. Highly recommend!

We left our hotel in Kensington at 9.30 to go to St Paul's Cathedral. Road closed till 2pm. Finally found the correct bus after being told the incorrect bus to catch 3 times. We went past Trafalgar Square 4 times. It took us nearly 4hours to get home from Westminster. We passed Marbel Arch 4 times. Red bus driver told us wrong instructions. One commentatry giver was more interested in which pub he had been to. We were told to walk through Green Park to catch next bus.
Too exhausted to get out at St Paul's so stayed on the bus. Then told to catch the Home James Service back to Kensington. Driver was fabulous because he broadcast the stops.
Others did not. It was a shambles. Wouldn't recommend at all.

I've been studying in London for about 3 months, making deliberate trips to sightseeing locations both on my own and for class. It's very easy to discount the hundreds of Hop-On Hop-Off buses that pass you each day as "touristy" and "basic", but we finally got off our high horses to ride one yesterday and had the most fun since arriving. The buses offer a great opportunity to self-guide your own tour: if you want to see Buckingham Palace, great. If you don't want to, just keep riding. The tour guides (Lisa!!) were extremely knowledgable and were able to keep spewing facts even when traffic was awful. I found I was learning lots of cool facts about London I didn't know, despite doing a plethora of research for a history of London course. I would absolutely recommend this service to anyone who only has a little time in the city and wants to get around quickly and scenically. Especially if it's warm and sunny!

A large group of us used this over two days. The bus has no heating and it was very cold. The driver, on one route, the red line, was on his mobile for most of a segment of the trip thus the commentary was lacking!!!!! He did not press the button for the commentary near the required stops. Very disappointed. We also purchased out tickets as a kiosk before the bus stop and the person charged our credit cards for a cash advance when it was a purchase only.

On the 14th December 2017 I purchased two adult tickets at GBP31 per adult (approx AUD$60 each) with high expectations for a fun day out. What a complete debacle it turned out to be and a complete waste of money. The bus kept stopping for prolonged periods for no apparent reason (no customers getting on/off) at each stop, then we had to change buses for at the Madame Tussaud stop and wait another 15 mins, then that bus broke down 2 stops later. The total trip time had so far taken 2.5 hours and we hadn't even arrived at our desired destination and were quickly running out of time to see all the tourist stops we had originally planned. At that point I gave up and spoke to the bus driver requesting a refund. I was told that I would have to apply for one via their website, which I did that afternoon. I promptly received an email stating that my request would be looked into and to date have not received any further response. Ironically, it only took us 10 minutes on the London tube to travel the same distance that had taken us 2.5hours on the Big Bus. Please do yourself a favour and just purchase an Oyster card for the tube - far cheaper, quicker and more reliable! I will never, ever use a hop-on-hop-off bus ever again.

We booked the tour on the 4.10.2017 and we had to wait for the first bus for 45 Minutes in front of Waterloo station where we bought the tickets. On the tour the head phones system stopped working and their was nothing the company did to replace it. In the end we had to wait for another bus which took long time to arrive. We waited more than we enjoyed the tour.
It is far tooo expensive and I would not recommend it at all.

We purchased a 48 hrs ticket for BigBus London and we got on to the bus at 4:30pm as we wanted to do the whole tour - blue bus. Nowhere on the bus leaflet did they mention the timings for the last bus nor the bus driver (who looked as if he was forced to work) told us that the bus will not cover the full tour. In the middle of the tour, a lady came and asked us to get off as the operating hours were over. We were 8 kms away from our Hotel and we had to take a taxi to come back home. You guys need to organise your tours properly by first employing bus drivers who can communicate with the passengers so you don't leave people stranded in the middle.

I had done my research before choosing Big Bus but waited until we actually arrived in London to pay. Sure enough, the reviews were correct. Big Bus has the most stops and the most buses. Yes, some of the ear buds did not work. Just grab another pair. Yes, the traffic in London is like all big cities. The buses have to adhere to the traffic, or anything else that gets in their way.

Just like taking any hop-on-hop-off in a large city, plan your time accordingly. Do not use it as your only source of transportation as it will disappoint you. Get the Travelcard for daily use on the Underground. Remember that the London Underground is the largest subway system in the world. It is extremely easy to navigate.

Use the Big Bus as a first stop in your London tour. Take it and just ride it for a day. You will see all of the major tourist attractions. Then plan the rest of your vacation according to what you want to actually tour.

£54 for two adults includes a guided boat ride on the Thames and 48 hours on the hop on hop off guided bus tour of all the major sights and history of the city of London.

Wether you want to get those classic iconic pictures, learn about the history and places of the city. Then this is the tour for you, the well informed guides will entertain you along the this 2.5 hour tour along the red route. It's stops at all the iconic places. Buckingham Palace, West Minster, London eye, London Bridge, Tower Bridge, TheTower of London, Mayfair and many many more. You can choose to hop off and investigate any of these attractions further.

The guides will also give you various tips and advice on how to save money on theatre tickets and it's a great way to become familiar with this great city. Enjoy 😘

I fractured my ankle so i was on crutches. Only way to see London for me was via a bus tour. We bought vouchers from our hotel for this

We finally got on the bus but the driver was so unwelcoming. We were told those vouchers we bought from the hotel had to be swapped for tickets which the hotel failed to tell us.

During the tour, i could hear the driver swearing....on several occasions. Incredibly unprofessional.

At one point my partner approached the driver with a question and he yelled at her DONT TALK TO ME. SIT DOWN. NEVER TALK TO THE DRIVER.

Nobody likes to be yelled at and you don't need to yell at someone if they are in need of help. Ridiculously rude and uncalled for.

It ruined the experience a bit and i will never recommend this bus company to anyone visiting London

For all those who have been to London would know that London is huge city with loads to see and do, and along with the pros of so many things to see and do, the cons like how to figure out to get from one place to another, figuring out the subway route etc. also come in. The Big bus tour made a lot of sense for me since I was travelling solo and really did not want to get into the hassle of figuring out the routes by myself ( I am a bit lazy that ways) but I am sure there are a lot of people who like to figure out the routes etc and find that quiet exciting, sadly I am not one of those!
This tour made me see the whole of London at a glance first and post that I decided where to get off and what places to see in detail! Frankly speaking I just loved sitting on top of the open roof bus and see London as it drove through the city! Bus stops were not difficult to find and were mostly not more than 5-7 mins walk from all the main destinations. Also the call center people were super helpful. This one time I was not able to find the nearest bus stop, so I called them up and they guided me to the nearest bus stop.

P.S. you do not necessarily need to buy the tickets in advance. You can buy them on the bus itself. I gt it for cheaper on the bus.

DO NOT BOOK WITH THEM!!!! I am currently in London wasting MORE time waiting for busses with this company!!!!! Hundreds of wasted dollars, several wasted hours & the most horrible in person customer service experience. This is NOT how we wanted to spend the few days we had on London; thanks to this company we have lost TWO full mornings trying to even find a bus that is stopping at a designated stop. The guides streetside don't care whatsoever if you get where you're getting. Do yourself a favour and buy up ur tickets with The Original Tour of London, they have reps everywhere and are incredibly helpful...they even helped us find an open stop for this pathetic company without hesitating! We have emailed the company waiting for a response, will be demanding a refund; let's see if they act with a moniker of integrity in the end!!

Got a family ticket on special offer - 48 hours for the price of 24. Very informative and interesting, with good routes taking you to all the main places. Never had to wait long for the next bus, and saw lots of their buses going past at other times.
Included river tour was good, live commentary from knowledgeable Londoner - spoilt only by the large number of other passengers who felt it acceptable to talk over it with no consideration for those who wanted to listen.
Have done the original tour and think big bus is better as less music, more info. Also good that you don't have to pick up ticket from a particular office. We booked online and joined tour at Westminster Bridge.

We bought a day pass and only used it for 2-3 hours making it a very expensive bus trip! We went to the Tower of London then were hoping to get back on the bus to complete the loop. After waiting 15 minutes, we had to walk over to 2 staff who were several metres away from the bus stop texting on their phones and eating KFC. They said the wait would be 5 mins. This happened several times and every time they said the wait would be 5 mins. After 1 interaction with the staff, one of them suggested we go and buy a ticket from the original bus tour if we weren't happy! After 50 mins we gave up and caught a train. A waste of money!!!

Just returned from a lovely 4 day holiday to London where we decided to book a sightseeing tour with Big Bus...the bus was clean and commentary good but the problem came at the end of the tour. We and approx 15 other people were on a blue route bus but were told that we would have to change on to a green route bus at Covent Garden to get back to our hotel (this was approx 7pm) we all got off the bus at Covent Garden as instructed and were told by our bus driver that the bus directly behind us was the green route bus so we all headed for that bus, however the driver of that bus told us that his bus was not in service any more and that a green route bus would be along soon....well, we waited and waited and waited, after 35mins everyone realised that this green route bus was not going to arrive and so people started to disperse. We had to walk back to our hotel which was in Russell Square, quite a distance from Covent Garden, especially with a tired 8 year old and 2 elderly parents in tow! Not good :(

We spent over $250 on a night tour and THEY DID NOT PROVIDE US A SEAT. Had to stand for much of the trip. How much can you see when you are standing in the first level aisle of a double decker bus?? Answer: nothing. And the bus was hot, it was noisy. Plus they didn't even take our tickets.... clearly the bus was being used by London residents for free transportation. We felt -- because we were -- completely cheated. Would have been much more fun, and much less expensive, to simply get a cab and have them drive us to the night spots we couldn't even see on this bus. Which NEVER STOPPED to let us take pictures. Horrible experience. Will never use this bus line again.

We only had a short period of time to see London, so we thought this would be the easiest way to do it. We paid 32£ a piece and got on at Piccadilly. Then we sat. In traffic. For ever. It was at least 20 min in between recorded descriptions of the sights interspersed with the same classical music over and over. Several times the recordings didn't even match the sights. It took us almost 90 min to get to London Bridge when we had enough and decided to get off. We had been told there would be live guides on all the buses or our money back, so I asked for a refund, only to be told then that only the red line had live guides (no one had told us this when we got on). I told the staff at the stop we had a terrible time and felt misinformed. His response was "its not my fault, I didn't do it.". I suggested it would be better customer service if he apologized and stood behind his product. He insisted he would not and asked me " who are you? Why are you entitled to be so critical". I'm a trip advisor member! Save your money or take a different bus line. This was the staff working at the pier stop by tower of London. If anyone from Big Bus reads this, he needs some serious customer service retraining.

The sites were beautiful.The audio tape tour was good, though not always clear about specific buildings being referenced -- a little confusing about the points of reference. The frequency of buses was OK--though the standard line was that the bus we wanted was coming in 5 minutes--not necessarily. As noted elsewhere, music needs modification. The big however was that we were told by a local to negotiate a rate in person. As one negotiation wrapped up near us, we asked for the same deal and we understood that salesman agreed to 19 pounds each (other group had agreed to 19, 19, and 10 for the child on the sidewalk). Since the bus was arriving, the negotiating salesman instructed us to get on the bus. We confirmed the same price of 19 pounds for each of us as we stepped on the bus.Once on the bus, after running our credit card, we discovered that the negotiator had charged us 90 pounds for 3 of us (telling us he was giving us a discount at 90 for 3, not 19 for each). When we objected, he said that the terms he had offered to the other group of 3 did not apply to us--even though we had asked explicitly. Driver told us to go to discuss it at the next stop, where the linking green line switched to the red and blue lines. At that stop, the salesman said he had no authority and that we had to go to the main office -- at Victoria Station to resolve the matter. Given the delays of traffic and our schedule, we had to continue on the trip and did not have time to go to the station.

We visited London in the last week of May just for a day and found the big bus tour online! What a great way to see this amazing city! I booked tickets online in advance for a better rate, we jumped on the bus at the London Eye and proceeded round all three routes the bus tour had - saw all major landmarks / attractions / points of interest all in one day! I took my 15 year old sister who loved it - especially harrods! All the staff are really helpful and have a great sense of humour, their is literally a bus every 10 minutes! Highly recommended and would do this again!

What a great day we had. This tour is amazing value for money. We got on the 'red' route, at Bus Stop No.1, Green Park. The round trip takes about an hour and a half, with an English young man on our bus giving us live commentary which was fun and interesting. The price also includes a half-an hour River Thames boat trip from The Tower of London, down to near the London Eye. We stayed on the boat so had a half-an-hour trip back also. The ticket also includes a free walking tour (3 different ones, at different times of the day, Royal London, Scene in London & Haunted Mysteries. These walks last 1.5 - 2 hours and Royal London starts at 10:20, Scene in London at 2:00pm, and Haunting Mysteries at 6:00pm. Sadly, we ran out of time so did not get the chance to do these, but all of the above for one price. We had a great day. I understand, also, that you can also go on the Blue Route to see Knightsbridge, Royal Albert Hall and Kensington Palace whilst driving around Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens? FANTASTIC value for money.

We (I, wife and two teenage children) took the Big Bus on 10.05.15. The ticket seller (Tickets mention a name Nazrul Islam - don't know if this was the name of the seller) sold us Big Bus tickets (never asked us how many days tickets we wanted - never told us of any options available) for 100 GBP! and also aggressively sold us tickets for various so called attractions totally amounting to GBP 482!!!!! We were told the tickets for the attractions and the Big Bus tickets are valid for 7 days which we later on realised in valid at best for 3 consecutive days. We boarded big bus at 1.30 pm and paid 100 GBP for 2 hours!!!!! Also used only Madame Tussaud's and London Eye vouchers issued by Big Bus. We were booked for Legoland for 11.05 and are booked for Warner Bros a Studio for 12.05. So we have paid 100 GBP for only Big Bus tickets which is a rip off or perhaps daylight robbery and a con job. I am still holding tickets for 3 to 4 attractions which we do not have time to visit only because the Big Bus chap completely misled us. In hindsight I feel that the ticket issuers perhaps enjoy huge commissions on the sales made by them and hence go about defrauding unsuspecting tourists. We could have easily done the same by spending 150 GBP including taxi fare as against 482 GBP charged by the Big Bus guy. Completely avoidable - it should be banned by the British Government. Unscrupulous cheaters and swindlers!

We took a tour around London on one of the big bus tours the tour was advertised at £18 but when we went to pay it was £32 each shocking. The tour was advertised as having a live guide which it did not and we were not given headphones so we could not listen to the recorded Guide £64 spent on a bus ride around London not good value.

Bought tickets for the big bus first impression thinking it was pricey
At £127.00 for three of us, for 3 days, but it was worth every penny, you go all over London and just get on and off as you please , there's 2 bus routs with 2 smaller joining routs, and depending on the area your staying there's also a hotel return service , you'll see and go places you'd never see on foot , I highly recommend this tour , plus you get a free river tour with your ticket & lots of discount in and around London

We decided to book 3 adults & 2 children onto a tour as we felt it would be the best way to see the most of London in one day. The organisation was a complete shambles the green line was re-routed to meet with the next tour at Madam Tussauds. Unfortunately we had to wait for nearly an hour for a bus even though several came and went we were told they were ending their tour. Due to this delay we missed our pre-booked tickets on the London Eye. We tried once more to join the tour at Westminster bridge. We were told a bus would arrive in 6 minutes. The bus arrived after around 25 minutes and by this time there was a queue of angry, pushing people literally fighting their way into the bus which was quite frightening for our children. After this awful experience we abandoned the bus tour in favour of walking.
The best thing about the whole experience was the Thames cruise which was well organised and great fun.
The Big Bus Tour did not provide enough buses for the amount of tickets sold. There was no issue with people who were using the Original Bus Tour company. Their buses were frequent, plenty of spaces on board and only a few people waiting at the stops due to their frequency.
I have contacted the company to complain about our experience. They requested a copy of our tickets, which I immediately emailed. Surprisingly, I have not heard from them since.
