My tip is don't waste your time queuing and fighting to get on this company's buses use Original Tours or walk!

£140 for four adults and two children!!! And for what?

The route was diverted, the automated audio-commentary kept reminding us this for the first half an hour.

The only good thing about Big Bus Tours was getting off!!!

Yes the tickets may be valid for 48hrs, but it'd be cheaper to buy a One-Day Travelcard and see London from a Red Double Decker as you want to see it, not as someone thinks you should see it and then find you've missed practically everything because you're on an unannounced diversion!!!

Wish I'd spent that money more wisely!

I've done both this tour and the Original Tour, so I can give a fair comparison. This tour may be a few pounds cheaper, but I would never take it again.
Instead of giving you actual tickets or wristbands as proof of tour purchase, they give you a skinny little receipt. If you misplace the receipt, they could care less. Never mind that they have proof of your credit card purchase; they will simply tell you "too bad." The female agent at the Green Park station couldn't care a bit that you and your kids are standing out in the cold. She would not allow us back on the bus even to get back to the place where we purchased the tickets. I can't help but feeling that this is a sly tactic to take advantage of foreigners and to keep people's money. I did not give up and disputed the credit card company. We had to take a taxi back to the other side of town. Such tactics would not be allowed in the USA, and I wasn't about to allow them Big Bus get away with theft. The agents do not wear name tags and would not even give me her name so that I can file a complaint with the Big Bus management, TfL (Transport for London), and London police. No one should be treated in this manner. She would not let me talk to a manager. When I took a picture of her so that I could file a complaint both Big Bus, she swiped her walkie-talkie at me. I am filing several complaints, so that no one else has to be treated this way. Even though another agent said that they could confirm that we had paid that morning via a credit card receipt, she would not relent. She wanted us to pay an additional 65 pounds to buy new tickets, that we had not used. That was not going to happen! I contacted my credit card company for an immediate refund.

I've lived in London for nearly 40 years but this was my first Big Bus Tour. I wanted to give 2 visiting American friends an overview of how the city fits together and the Big Bus Tour routes proved to be the perfect way to do that.

First we took the Classic Red Route around the main city sights. Our enthusiastic tour guide Neil was an entertaining mine of information and made our city history lesson fun and highly enjoyable. He obviously loves the city and delighted in sharing it with us. Thank you Neil!

After hopping off for a coffee we then picked up the Blue Route to see some of the more outlying areas and listened to the pre-recorded commentary. This too was highly informative and well produced with music and effects.

We rounded off the afternoon by hopping off at Westminster and taking the City Cruise to Tower Bridge and back. This is included in the price. The City Cruise guide picked up where the Big Bus left off with more illuminating and entertaining commentary.

All in all, a great way to see London and learn some fun and fascinating history at the same time. Even if you've lived here for years, I guarantee you will enjoy learning something new about this great city. Thank you Big Bus!

Cost: Check the Big Bus website for any offers. If you can, pre-book online for the best prices.

We did this our first day in London to get acquainted with the city and felt it was well worth it. We hopped off at the Tower of London so we could take advantage of the river cruise included in the ticket price. What a great way to see the city. The Blue line has a live English speaking guide on board and the red line has headsets with multiple languages. Yes, they even have rain ponchos for the occasional drizzle if you are sitting atop the bus. The bus gives good photos opportunities as well as provides an easy way around town. We found that buying tickets on a Saturday gave us a free day on Sunday too.

We thought the tickets were really expensive for the service we got. The buses were unreliable. Resembled a poorly run and underfunded very basic public transport. We were told to get off the bus after two stops and told it was terminating without any explanation and told another bus would arrive within 5mins. Then we were told the three following buses were also terminating. We were left standing at the bus stop for 30mins with many other unhappy customers! The big bus staff seemed to be flustered. I saw them arguing amongst themselves at the bus stops, unorganised and were very unhelpful, short tempered and failed to engage in appropriate conversation when asked questions. We didn't get an opportunity to see the full tours. Very disappointed and in our view a complete waste of money. They need to lift their game if they want to charge those fees and call themselves tourguides!!!

This bus company has the most buses, the most frequent buses, and also offers a 2-day ticket whereas The Original Bus Tour and the Golden Bus Tours does not. We also purchased the London Eye tickets from the gentleman who sold us the tickets. This gave us the fast track to The London Eye and shortened our time in line. We had a week to use the tickets, which fit into our plans perfectly. They also gave us a river cruise on the Thames as part of the deal. We took the river cruise on the second day and ended up in Greenwich, which was not originally our planned stop. it was planned for another day but we ended up going twice.

The hop on/off red line gives a live commentary throughout whereas the other line of the same company gives an audio tour with headphones. Both were equally fine. The live one was more annimated, but the audio tour gave a few more facts about the places we went past.

The bus stop for this company was very close to our hotel - St. Ermins. There were frequent stops along the route so you could hop off any time you choose.

The first day we rode it all day so we could get the lay of the land, make notes of what we all wanted to return to if it wasn't already on our planned schedule and during the next two weeks we were able to go back to many of the spots noted on our notes.

The second day we used it to just get around from point to point as we had run out of underground time on our Oyster Card and didn't want to use our London Pass Travel card until we started to use the London Pass to get around.

Overall, we found this company to be the best choice of the ones that offer hop on/off services. We would use them again when and if we ever return to London again in the future.

First of all trying to fight the tubes is ridiculous going up and down the stairs, and taking the different lines and fighting for seats with the crowds. The big bus tours have plenty of buses and never waited more than 15 minutes compared to the people waiting for the original tour. Yes sometimes you can't get a seat on the top and have to sit on the bottom but face it this is for transportation to your points of interest. If you are going to do the tour book the 48 hour traffic is sometimes a bear and takes a little longer than expected. Also the buses start at 0845 and most attractions don't open until 9-10 am so start early so you can see more. also their is alot of walking in london and this gives you a little break when getting around the city. This is my 4th time in london and can't believe I didn't do this earlier. Also catch the bus from victoria then you can go up to the arch and take any bus from their to the different routes.

Waste of time due to heavy London traffic - We bought a two day pass for the family on the 10th june 14. However, after spending five hours on the Big bus (without getting off at any sites) seeing only half the sites on the blue line, we decided to get off at St Pauls stop and took the boat cruise back to Westminister. The Big bus drivers were not very friendly and are more interested in competing with the other tour bus companies for customers.
I suggest the boat cruise to visit the sites near the river - The boat cruise was great and covers most of the important sites to see. The live commentry by the boat captain was fun and very informative.

Firstly I apologize for my comments on this same incident where I incorrectly made a reference to the "Original London Sight Seeing Tour" company by mistake and only later realized that I had bought the tickets from Big Bus Tours.

I wrote an email to Big Bus team customer services and there has been no response from them whereas I already got 2 empathizing responses from Original London Sight seeing tour company. So clearly the two companies treat customers very differently. So be warned guys with this "Big Bus Tour".

Now coming to the experience which I want to share with the community members.

I was so excited to take my in laws for a bus tour on 17/05/2014, but that proved to be the worst nightmare. I have 3 major points of complain.

1) The staff they employ are very unprofessional. I was rudely shoved off and told to not enter the bus after purchasing the ticket. The supervisor says - "Don't enter the bus. Go to the person who sold you the ticket. You are not allowed". Is this how you talk to your customers? Where on earth is it specified that the staff member who sells the ticket at the bus stop is the one who decides which bus to board. I'm talking about the staff at Speaker's corner, Marble Arch. And then seemed like they lacked any sense of respect for their customers - obviously I can figure out from their accent that these are non British staff and they hardly showed any etiquette.

2) Why do you allow people to enter the bus when there is no space. We stood for 1 hour and were not allowed to go upstairs. Really there is nothing to see from the lower deck. The driver rudely directed me - "Go down, no standing here". I mean there is something called as customer service. Are you folks working in 18th century.

3) Also these guys charge £32 and this is more expensive than other tour operators. So folks please be careful an watch out before you buy your tickets.

I have stayed in London for more than 10 years and I have used many tourist services, however this Big Bus tours are the worst. So please check before purchasing tickets - there are multiple companies who are offering this London bus tour and some are not having a quality service.

Highly disappointed and will never return and will tell people not to use Big Bus tour service.

Having spent the last 8 years in Australia, whenever I go to a new city I always take the bus tour on day one to get my bearings and see the general sites.

Having just visited Barcelona and done just that, I thought it silly that I had never done my own home town, so this weekend I did just that. Oh dear.

The biggest complaint was that in knowing the general attractions anyway, I was amazed that the audio tape was not in sink with the attractions. On average we were about 300-500 yards too late and some things, like the Monument, which has a fairly obvious story to tell, wasn't even mentioned. If you are doing the bus, there has to be someone better.

The only saving grace was the ferry (included in the price) we caught from the London Eye down to Greenwich. On board was a crafty cockney giving lots of interesting banter about the celebs and pirates from down the years, as well as pointing out the sites.

It also has to be said that even if it had been any good, why it was more than twice the cost of the far superior service in Barcelona, is beyond me.

On Friday, Jan. 17, 2014 my sister & I were directed by our hotel concierge to the bus stop for "The City Sightseeing Tour". When we arrived the purple Big Bus was parked there. We asked the bus driver about the red bus & he told us that they were all the city service buses. He told us about his tour & we asked how long it would take? The answer was 2 1/4 hrs. We paid the 30 pounds sterling or $49.USdollars. At 11AM we began the tour & reached the Marble Arch at 1:45 PM. We disembarked to get a bite to eat & came back to the same stop in one hour. We again got on the bus & at 5PM were still on the tour, we finally got off near Oxford Street & walked back to Russell Square to our Hotel. part of the time was having to get off of one bus & catch another Yes, we did see the RED Buses that do the City Sightseeing tours. I understand they are less money & shorter. It was a very disappointing way to spend a day!!!

Just returned from London this week and wanted to share a friendly tip -- if you like bus tours like we do, use the Big Bus Tour rather than the "Original London Tour" company. Big Bus Tours were less expensive, ran three busses to every ONE of the original busses, had actual tour commentators rather than taped comments we were subjected to, and had later hours. The Original Tour we used left our family stranded on two occasions returning from busy days, and anyone with young kids can appreciate how frustrating that was. When I brought this to their attention we were told the city had closed some roads for a speicial event but didn't bother to re-route their busses so we had to figure out the regular bus system and paid 10 pounds to get back home. The next day the bus was too full to take us and we ended up walking a 1-2 km back to the hotel rather than wait another 30 minutes (and that too might have been full as everyone rides the busses back to their hotels after dinner). The Big Bus Tours have two routes rather than four, but with extra busses on each line it's WAY better and really, once you get off and take in a few attractions these two routes are more than adequate. It was tough watching Big Bus Tours driving by while stranded in a BIG CITY by the Original.

We were travelling with 3 kids six and under so we decided that the hop on/hop off tour would be a good way of seeing the sights with minimal hassle. We bought a family pass for 84 pounds, and got on the first bus. 45 min later we got off and I immediately realized that I had dropped the ticket on the bus. I went straight to the person as soon as we got off the bus and it drove away and explained the situation. We were quizzed about who sold us the ticket, when, where and apparently all our info lined up (as it was true) but she needed approval from a manager to re-issue the ticket. (oh and in the conversation it came out that we had been overcharged by 12 pounds becasue a family pass was only 72 pounds) Anyways, the girl was great but we had to wait for about 30 minutes for her to get a manager to call her back only to deny her to be able to print a new ticket, or do anything about us being overcharrged. All she was authorized to do for us was to sell us a new ticket but at the right fare (72 pounds). Needless to say we passed. There are other options out there please use ones with sensible management that actually look after their customers.

I was a little apprehensive about taking a Hop On Hop Off bus tour after reading bad reviews about various other bus tour companies, however, my parents and I decided to take the risk with this company and we were very glad we did! We took this tour on a Sunday morning in late May 2013.

First, we were worried about the complaints regarding traffic that others experienced in the comments below. However, we had absolutely no problem getting from point A to point B. I believe this is because we went early in the morning. We began our tour from Stop #1 by Hyde Park at 9:30 AM and continued our tour (hopping on and off at various sites along with our Free boat cruise, which is included in the price) until about 2:00 PM. Between these hours, we had no issues with traffic. However, note that after lunch, the bus did begin to fill up as the afternoon wore on and it became a bit difficult to find seats on the top deck. Top tip: Go early!!

Second, the tour guides and bus drivers were extremely friendly and made the experience what it was! Our first guide (I believe his name was Nick) was extremely energetic (especially so early in the morning!), friendly, accommodating of any questions and requests, and knowledgeable. He delivered entertaining stories and we were very satisfied with the tour he provided. Note that the regular Red route *always* has Live guides. However, the Blue route does not, and instead provides you with headsets and recorded commentary (which actually wasn't terrible and provided great information - maximize the value of your ticket by going on the Blue route if you have the time!)

Third, regarding price. We purchased our tickets at the Big Bus Tours office near Victoria Coach station the day before going on the tour. Because we purchased advanced tickets, we paid a discounted price of 23 pounds each (although it might even be cheaper if you purchased in advance online). Note that there is no discount for students. We were then provided a reference number that we took to the bus stop on the morning of our tour and gave it to one of the Big Bus Tour representatives at the stop. They then verified our reference number, and provided us with our validated tickets, which was valid for the next 24 hours. Very easy and convenient. However, if you aren't sure in advance whether you are taking the tour, I believe you can purchase tickets (at a regular price which I believe was 28 - 30 pounds?) at the stop on the day of the tour. Top tip: But, if you are confident you will be taking this tour, purchase your tickets in advance for a discounted price!

Overall, we were very pleased with our Big Bus Tour experience. Our entertaining guide was definitely the highlight. Just make sure you start your tour early to avoid traffic and to easily obtain seats on the top deck!

I echo the comments made by '“Terrible, but friendly tour guide”. As a resident in London, I thought I would take my visiting father from Australia on-board one of these tours. We first boarded the bus and excitingly awaited to begin our journey. The older English gentlemen who was the tour operator for the day began with an old English poem in his thick Queens English. This set the scene for what was appearing to be an excellent couple of hours. But that’s where it stopped. We literally sat in traffic and drove by streets which he named ‘O look there is Oxford Street’ – no ‘guiding’ what-so-ever’. You don’t mind paying the money for the local knowledge sharing but this was such a disappointment. I am afraid the company may be reaching the point where they are too big for their boots and no longer look after the actual customers. With great regret, I must reiterate, it is not worth the money.

I usually do a tour of a city to get the layout when we arrive. We picked this touring bus from the Victoria station tourist information station. We had trouble finding the stop to get on and had to wait for 30 minutes in the freezing cold and wind for the first bus to show up. We saw over a dozen other tour busses pull up and leave while waiting for one of the "Big Bus" tours. We changed over from the red line to the blue line and had a similar wait, again watching multiples of the rival company's busses come and go. We were packed into an over crowded bus without being able to use the audio tour as there were no seats. You HAVE TO BE IN A SEAT TO HEAR THE AUDIO TOUR. The bus was packed solid up to Harod's department store. We missed at least 30 minutes of the audio due to the lack of a seat. The interior was heated but the upper level was freezing. We understand this works fine in the summer but after a full tour, taking over 3 1/2 hours in heavy traffic at freezing temperatures on a Sunday, we were on the verge of hypothermia and shivering. We didn't stand a chance of getting an inside seat, despite repeated attempts to grab an inside seat at each stop. There is absolutely no control over the number of passengers getting on or off the bus. You don't get to hear the audio unless you have a seat. At one point, after we had worked our way up to the front of the upper level on the blue bus, we were stopped and the entire bus was forced to get off one blue bus and move to a different blue bus. Of course, we were back out in the cold at the back of the outside area. After working our way to the front of the covered section on the top of the bus, we were intimidated by several loud young males, shouting to one another in a foreign language, immediately behind us for the last hour of the tour. Everyone else on the upper level left the bus and we were left alone with a group of 5 young males who were shouting to one another so loudly that we couldn't hear the tour over our ear phones. We were so cold and miserable after all the delays on the tour, the repeated changing of buses and the long waits for bus changes, we just desperately wanted to get back to Victoria station. We were frightened to say anything to them to be quiet so we could hear the tour due to the large number of the men, the aggressive attitude and our advanced ages. There is no staff on the bus other than a driver so there was no official person to require them to be considerate of fellow passengers. There are no service people on these busses, no control of the crowd, no schedule, few busses and crazy rules about emptying one bus and switching to another for no reason. I would never again book a tour with this company. I try to give positive reviews but this was incomparably awful and other tourists need to know to choose more wisely than we did.

We were in London for exactly 3 whole days. On our first day after flying in the previous evening on a 9 hours flight, we bought the Big Bus tour tickets after comparing the maps and prices with the Original Tour bus. The OT bus company was $3 cheaper for 24 hours but there was only $1 difference for the 48 hours - either way not a big difference. The reason we ended up buying the Big Bus was because the other one OT routes just seemed more complicated and fragmented. On the other hand OT buses have their last bus at 8.30 while BB has it at 6.30 pm - that is a huge difference Anyway, the 48 hours tickets covered almost the whole of our stay so was very convenient to cover all the major sites. Having to change buses when they reach their last stop was annoying. The buses came frequently - just seemed like there were more of the BB than the OT buses. Otherwise, it was like any other HOHO tour bus - nothing extraordinary nor anything to really complain about - was perfect for a 3 days, first time visit.

We used the Big Bus Tour to get an overview of the city, for transportation, and we even used the bus tour to provide our four year old with a little bit of nap time during our busy days. The narrated tour line was fun. We really liked 2 of the 3 guides we met.

The service was very good and very easy. We never waited more than 10 minutes for a bus. Along with that - there are sections of the tour where this tour and other tour buses are lined up 4 or 5 deep.

On arriving in London my family and I were left with the question of where do we go, and what do we do next. Common questions we have had in any place we have visited, either in U.K or abroad. Our questions were answered as we met and spoke to a sales person working for Big Bus tours. As we chatted about our options it quickly became clear that not only my children, but my wife also wanted to take the Big Bus Trip around London. This was based upon the manner in which the sales person had approached us, not being "pushy" and very helpful with tips and advice we could use during our stay in London.
As we purchased our bus tickets we were also told about the fast entry tickets which were sold to Big Bus passengers, we decided not to bother buying those tickets but were told we could buy them later in the day if we wished. Our main concern was to see London from the top of the bus which we did. Our first bus came very soon after buying the tickets and as we had been warned, it would be quite full as it was nearing the end of it's journey and many passengers would be getting off at the last stop to change buses and use a "Language" tour which had recorded languages on it via a head phone.
We got on the bus and after only 10 minutes we arrived at the point where our tour would begin, with a new bus and guide we sat upstairs and waited to continue our day. Within only a few minute of sitting upstairs, our new guide appeared and made us comfortable, explaining in finer detail some of the things we could do either with our bus ticket or later once our ticket had expired, Phil Harris was our guide and once the tour began, we as a family decided to stay on Phil's bus, and as I saw how much our children were enjoying themselves I knew we had made the right choice on how to spend our day in London. With the river trip on the Thames and all the other options we had with our tickets, such as the guided walks which we didn't have time to do, I thought we had a good value for money day and may well do again next time we go too London with friends.
Yes, I agree there were times later in the day when buses were quite full, but in all our day and in general our stay in London would not have been so enlightening had we not done the Big Bus Tour, I heard how some people had complained that their bus did not have a guide on it, this had been clearly explained to me when I purchased the tickets, that some buses were for different languages with head phones, these buses could also be used with the same ticket and were clearly marked. Each time the bus stopped our guide would take time to explain what we were looking at, had the bus not stopped we would have not had time to see half as much as we did. As Phil mentioned to us, make the most of sitting upstairs and look UP! We did this and were amazed at what we saw, with the different architectural features on various buildings we appreciated the times we had to stop and especially at some places where Phil hardly stopped talking, as he told us the history of the area.

My wife and I waited half an hour in the rain for a bus that was supposed to arrive every 15 minutes. When one finally arrived we thought we would be driven safely and comfortably to the bus stop nearest our hotel; big mistake. We rode for about 20 minutes when the bus stopped and the driver told us that the tours were finished and we had to get out. We were miles from our hotel, it was cold and raining and we were unfamiliar with the area. We had paid for a 48 hour pass and now we had to pay extra to use the Underground to get home. The bus driver was curt and showed no concern for us. The buses should finish the route they started and not leave passengers stranded. There are other tour companies with more buses and more frequent service.

We debated between the Original and Big bus tour companies, and chose Big based on the pick-up stops near our Lancaster gate location. We rode the line with the live tours and lucked out with a cheerful, funny and responsive guide. it was our second day in london and jet-lag had ht us hard, so we loved being able to sit back and take-in the whole city. It helped us finalize where we really wanted to return and what areas/sites we might pass -on. We loved seeing all the amazing architecture and some neighbourhoods that we knew we would not have time to return to. We paid for a two day family deal and later took the green-line to go to Harrods and see Kensington palace. We also did the Changing of the Guard with Phil, their amazing, hilarious, and adorable tour guide who had us at three different prime locations to see different views of the marching bands. We used the boat cruise to go from the tower of London to the London Eye, but the delay in crossing the River was crazy and we would have been better off walking across the bridge. All in all a great value, great tour guides (and if yours is dull, hop-off anywhere and hop on the next bus, it makes a BIG difference!), and a fun way to get around the city and orient yourself. Save a few pounds and book in advance, but you must have a firm date and/or a printer to bring the receipt with you to show the ticket guy.

My husband and I were really looking forward to this tour but from the minute we bought our tickets, we knew we had made a mistake. They sold more tickets then they could accomodate, the buses were scarce if they showed up at all, the recorded nararation didn't work well. At one stop we counted 4 Original Tour buses go by but our Big Bus bus never showed up. We had to take the tube back to our hotel. I wish we had used a different tour bus company. Worst of all, Big Bus was the more expensive tour so we thought it would be the best.

My Partner and I along with our 4 year old son had an amazing day in London thanks to The Big Bus Company. My Partner to quote "saw more of London in one day than I have in my whole life". He was very impressed with the onboard guide and loved hearing the history of the sight's. The hop on and off service was perfect with a small child as it gave you the opportunity for a quick snack or toilet break! We will be back next year and will make another tour with The Big Bus Company. Many Thanks for a wonderful start to the festive season

I recently visited and was considering taking this tour, well what I saw from one of their ticket seller's on Regent Street was as bizzare as it was rude ( English style) While waiting to purchase a ticket the ticket seller was berating an American who had attempted to discuss some issue from the previous day and the ticket seller seem oblivious or not interested in listening, with obvious frustration the tourist walked way only to be followed by the Ticker Seller and I hear loud and clear from the ticker sell " don't you turn your back on me" I write this because you see the discomfort of this poor guy with his family and at that moment I just walked away thinking as an ambassador for this tour this ticket seller was in the wrong business and why he had no interpersonal or customer service skills he should not have been there. Now with that being said I did catch the bus off of Oxford Street by the Marble Arch only to notice the trend of impatient and short tempered ticket sellers ( this can be attributted to the time is money theme) Finally getting on the bus I took both red and blue, enjoyed them got on and off but was hesitant to approach and of the BB Employee's having seen while at different stops a sort of it's more about the $ and filling the bus than responding to questions. So after my 48 hrs I though well I would do it again only next time record what I see, send it to their office and ask? Is this what London bus tours are really all about? So remember who's in charge and don't let the expierence and your enjoyment be ruined by a few when there is so much more and then some to see...

Cheers

we booked this tour in advance of our visit and selected a specific date so availed of a great rate of 66 pounds for 2 adults and 3 children for the day .The reason I chose this tour over its main rival was the Harry potter tour .We had a fantastic day from when we took the bus at 9 am at green park The man who gave us our tickets and the girl standing at the stop before we got our bus were lovely and friendly .We saw some sights from stops 1-10 .we just made it for the royal walk tour at 10 .20 .We had a fantastic young lady tour guide I think her name is Hannah ,knowledgable and enthusiastic and kept us moving along at a fast pace so we didnt miss anything .We went back at 1 pm for the 2nd tour ,Harry Potter led by Hannah again .She was brilliant .I think the key to getting the most out of the day is to go on the walking tours at peak time because ,when we returned to the Haymarket area to go on the Harry Potter tour traffic was heavy around the area and we saw a good few buses from Big Bus Tour and its rival stuck in traffic ,going nowhere .After the HP tour which the kids loved( ,they got to call into a sweet shop along the way -highlight!)we got the bus again we didnt have long to wait .We continued around to stop 22 from where we got the river cruise -free with the big bus ticket got the boat to London or Tower bridge (cant remember which ) and went home exhausted !!A fantastic day ,absolutely well worth the money .Finally ,I also liked the little touch of raincoats when it started to rain (free -as many as you wanted - i got a few extra which lasted us for our holiday !)

During our trip to London we used the Big Bus Company to see as much of London as we could in the limited time that we had.

Our initial experience was pretty poor, our guide was a grumpy man who made everyone on the bus feel awkward (a couple behind us were complaining)... however after we got back on after travelling to the London Eye we had a FANTASTIC guide, unfortunately we can not remember her name, but she was a young lady and was very entertaining and had lots of interesting facts about London. After travelling with her we really enjoyed the Big Bus company and couldn't rave about it enough. The following day our guides were also very good. Our advice would be use the Big Bus company but if you get a bad guide, just get off at the next stop and wait for another bus as you might just have the bad one!

No organization, rude attendants and overcrowded buses. Who wants to stand for the first three hours while your herded on and off the buses trying to figure out which one is the earphone tour for foreign language (the Blue Bus) and which one has the "live" English speaking commentator (the Red Bus)? All the employees at the stops seemed concerned with was selling you a ticket. We were treated rudely when we were confused about the London Eye/River cruise and if you don't get a seat on top, you can't really see anything. Two thumbs down. Try "The Orginial Bus Company"? They can't be any worse.

It happened like six months ago, but my recent trip to London with kids (again) reminded me to write a review about this company. The thing was that it was rather bed weather, I was with two kids, and our ride was interrupted by protest near Parliament.
The very kind bus guide instructed all the remaining passengers aboard to write complaint to HQ, which I did. I wrote the e-mail and scanned my tickets asking for any sort of goodwill compensation. They replied by e-mail that they need original tickets and hard copy complaint being forwarded to their Customers Dept (???, BTW the year is 2009!!!). Ever since then they have not replied in spite of fact that they received my registered mail more than six months ago. DO NOT USE !!! Ever since I use their competition THE ORIGINAL LONDON SIGHTSEEING TOUR, with smile!!!!

I went to London in the off season so my Big Bus Company ticket was good for 48 hours. There fore my husband and I just used the tour bus as a regular bus because you can hop off and on all day. Also the price of our tickets included 5 different walking tours (eg Ghosts of London and Beatles tour) and a Thames River cruise. It was definitely just what we needed after a long flight was to see back and relax. One hint I would recommend doing the tour with an actually guide as opposed to the bus with the recorded tour.

I was in London with my father the first weekend of November 2008. He was traveling for business and I came along to help. He is visually impaired and normally uses a guide dog, but we didn't have time to get her rabies records in order before traveling to the UK.

I wanted to do some kind of tour so he could get the feel for London, but I didn't want to have to be the tour guide myself. Big Bus fit the bill perfectly!

I was a little nervous about choosing Big Bus over Original London because the OL reviews seem to be a little bit better. I chose Big Bus because they run their blue route in the winter and there was a stop within walking distance from our hotel. (According to an email from an OL rep, OL doesn't run their blue route in winter.) Also, with Big Bus you can print your ticket from online purchase and get on at any stop. It seemed easier to just walk to the bus rather than having to take the tube to a starting point.

We got on the blue route bus and it was surprisingly full. We rode on the lower level and listened to the recorded tour for 3 or 4 stops, until we got to a combined Red/Blue route stop. The recorded tour wasn't anything special. It was a little dry and boring.

We hopped off the bus and waited for a Red bus. We waited under 10 minutes. We went up top so we were out in the cool air but could see all of the tops of the buildings easily. Our guide was fantastic. He was british and told lots of jokes interspersed with his facts. We really got a kick out of him, my father especially. We took the whole Red tour and towards the end, they did make us get off and hop onto another Red bus. The guide on that bus was very informative but not as entertaining. We took that red bus to our starting point, then hopped off and headed to a restaurant for lunch.

We hoped to do the haunted pubs tour the next evening, but it was rainy and we had had another long day, so we skipped it.

I feel like this was a great way to get to know London and it was very entertaining for my father to have everything "described" to him. It took a lot of pressure off me. We took the tube all over for the next few days and always felt like we knew where we were because we had been in or near that area on the tour.

So, even though I was nervous because of some of the reviews here, we had a great time on Big Bus.

Big Bus London Hop-on Hop-Off Tour - Big Bus is one of several London tour bus companies. Tours are currently suspended presumably due to Covid-19 related lack of customers, but it was going strong fall of 2020 when we were in London. Four routes took us all around the city on open-topped double decker buses. We were able to get on and off wherever we wanted and found it worthwhile to ride the whole system to see London before deciding where we wanted to do deep dives. We started each route at the Marble Arch stop, which is a common stop to the four routes and to several other tour bus companies. The routes have taped commentaries in 12 languages and when there are many customers, there are live guides who offer commentaries. Some live guides are better than others, and some are better than the tapes. We enjoyed the Red Line the most because of our guide Katherine and driver Joshua, who were superb. Some Big Bus London tickets also include a Thames river boat ride in the price. There is a Big Bus London app for your smart phone that has the route information and locations of the buses along the different routes – essential if you want to know where to get off and walk between buses or routes and locate the Big Bus stops. Caution – be careful as it can get confusing as to which bus stops are for which of the tour bus companies as several companies circulate the same areas and have close, but different stops. Also, we liked the open top double decker buses, but in the late fall it can get rather cold up top and of course you can get wet if it is rainy. Take a coat and a raincoat. Visited late Fall 2019.

Lulu was our walking tour guide to see the Changing of the Guards and the Buckingham palace !!! She was excellent, loads of information and knew exactly where to be so we could take amazing pictures and videos!!! Great job LULU!
Excellent way to see London. Very efficient service. Staff very friendly and buses regular. Didn’t have to wait long at each stop.
Great value for money very informative ,showed all the best spots , Royal changing of the guards ,was a great day enjoyed every minute.

I absolutely LOVED taking the London Big Bus Hop-on Hop-off tour with Louis! He was funny, personable and made sure to welcome each person, find out where they were from and endeavor to greet them in their own language. Not only did this go a long way to make us all feel welcome and involved, after learning it was my birthday he managed to get people from many different places to teach him to say happy birthday in their language for me! Fully brilliant tour! Cheers to Louis!

We went on the hop on hop off red like tour on Jan 22 with our tour guide Julia! We had a great time, even though there weren’t many people on the tour that mooring. Julia was great! She was super personable and chatted with us about extra tidbits of history along the route; she was very knowledgeable and humorous (even when we got stuck in traffic!) She was an excellent tour guide, so if you happen to get her, you’re in for a treat! We laughed so hard during our tour! Would highly recommend!

We were fortunate to be in London right after Christmas, so I feel the tourist volume was a bit lower than usual and we had a really good experience. We rode the bus for about 30 minutes while the tour guide on board pointed out the sights and carried on a conversation with us. From there we went on a walking tour which I would highly, highly recommend. We would have been clueless on our own, but Big Steve was excellent in pointing out all the places of interest, telling us exactly where to stand to get the best pictures of the Trouping of the Colour, and took as many pictures of us with the attractions as we could have possibly asked for. Go with Big Steve if you get a chance to do a walking tour...he was extremely pleasant and entertaining.

Totally unprofessional, they make you waste your time waiting for a bus that never comes , not even the station workers are aware of the exact arrival time of the next bus.
The online exact location is a joke so you can not trust at all when the next bus will come. The 15 min average wait become a 45 or 1hour minimum.
Unpolite personal, not at all interested in finding out solutions to the long delays.
Would never recommend this company.

At each stop, they have a representative come onboard and check every single persons ticket to ensure they have one. Therefore, you sit for about 15 minutes while they do this. We also had to wait over 45 minutes at a stop for the bus to arrive which it never did. There were multiple other tour groups that came through during that time.If you're looking for a FAST way to see the city, I would definitely not recommend this group.
Great tour. Comfortable drive and really cool information about the sights. Wikipedia Will was funny and informative and we stayed on mostly just to listen to his stories!

Only in town for 2 days and bought 24 hour pass.. tried to redeem abt 4pm day 1, but no busses came during torrential rain..so we explored many areas via foot/uber..tried again early day 2 and caught bus at 930.. it went about 7 stops in 90 min. Narrater was chatty but not so informative and the long waits at each stop seemed pointless. We hopped off and never got back on. Complete waste of almost $100.. ugh

Plenty to see and learn about if you choose this hop on tour but if your are bus hopping, it can get confusing. Some tour guides are much more helpful than others and the app isn't the most precise tool. Stick with the red route if you're unsure where to go.

My wife and 3 kids (9,11,15) had a great btime in London last week. We booked a combo ticket for (Madame Tussauds, London Dungeons, London Eye, Big Bus Tour).

We got the bus from outside Tower Bridge and went around for a good tour of the City. Traffic was bad at the time but the guide Louis was great! He pointed out some great spots and told some great stories. We being from Ireland enjoyed when he pointed out the first pub to serve Guinness in London. Also the most haunted church etc etc. He was excellent and we really enjoyed it. Well done Louis. Driver was also very nice. When they were finishing up at 5pm Louis came around and asked the remaining passengers where they would like to go. Very good and recommended. You save alot by getting the combo ticket.
Noted the Big Bus is only for one day, you can extend at a cost for next day.
Good Job guys.

Do not use this company. Don’t often criticize, however this was the absolutely worst experience of our visit to London, drivers are rude, had to wait over 35 minutes at each stop. Ruined and wasted our day.

I purchased two 3 day pass tickets for my husband and I from the time we went to redeem the tickets it was a mess. The company has one stop by our hotel and we thought the service was going to be convenient. We were terribly let down all around. When you redeem your tickets nothing is explained to you, there are no pleasantries or courtesy, you will be treated like cattle being herded into a bus. The job of the staff at the stops is just to print tickets and push people into the next bus as fast as possible. They are not helpfull nor willing to help. The 'tickes' you are handed are printed out on the same paper and style used by stores which makes them super flimsy. During our first very ride our tickets got soaked with the daily London rain. I was able to save mine, but my husband's ticket fell apart by the end of the day. The next day I explained the situation to one of the employee's by my hotel stop and he literally told me that it was my loss. I showed him my receipts and he just kept saying that I lost my tickets because they cannot be reprinted, then attempted to sell me new ones. I was so angry that we just turned around and went back in to our hotel. The next day I did a second attempt with another employee and I received the same care than the first time. As I was sitting down thinking what to do a younger staff member came by and I politely express to her my frustration and what happened with our tickets. She attempted to call the offices, but was busy, so she then called her area supervisor to explain our situation. He authorized her to give us a one day pass and a one way ticket for the river cruise. Although I am appreciative of her help, I am very disgusted with this company. I feel taken advantage off and disrespected. We missed out of a full day and half of the service, the guided tour, and due to the time we were able to get back into the bus and the replacement ticket restrictions, we also couldn't enjoy the river cruise. Big Bus London is a terrible service and ruined my vacation. I will no use them again or recommend them to my friends coming in the next few weeks. Finally, I sent a message fo the company through their site and they haven't bothered to contact us.

Excellent value for money- we bought the 3 day deluxe tour ticket, including walking tour and Greenwich boat trip. We saw tour guide Ian on 4 different occasions,including the walking tour! He was awesome and an absolute credit to the big bus tour company! Funny, informative and very keen to ensure that all passengers had a great experience! He really made our trip to London memorable! Thank you Ian- you will be part of our holiday memories!

We were hard sold this ticket over the original bus tour - promised it is better... we waited a very long time for a bus and then the next 2 busses were completely full - all the while we watch original bus tour busses go by with space.... we bought other tickets and gave up on this one

Bought as a multi ticket with the London Eye & the Hop on Hop off tour bus, the first two honoured the free carer ticket for me pushing the wheelchair but the bus tour did not & wanted an additional £35 for using the bus tour, I refused to pay & as a consequence we lost out, disgraceful in these times of equality.

This may be covered in some small print somewhere but not obvious
Be warned

This was the worst tour I have ever been on! The bus audiotape had no synchronization with where we were. Much of the time it only had music playing. The driver had to divert because of demonstrations and so we missed a lot of what we were supposed to see. I will never use this service in London again.

We paid $125 for the family pass that gave us hop on/off bus and river cruise.
- We spent one day driving all over the city and hopping off where we wanted. We never waited more than 10 minutes for another bus to pick us up. This was a great way to see the city without walking 40 miles. Some busses had live commentary (which was better) but all had at least prerecorded commentary in multiple languages.

-The second day (it's good for two days) we took the river cruise from Tower Bridge to Greenwich. I highly recommend as Greenwich is an adorable retreat from London and it was so cool for our kids to stand on the Prime Meridian. The river cruise had live commentary both ways and since we were the last boat back, we saw the city all lit up at night.

This was a tremendous value for us traveling as a family and wanting to take in all the sites.

We also booked the Tower of London through them- it was the same price as buying them onsite but saved us waiting in line there!

We had the best time doing the big bus tours!While we did the tours there were lots of diversions and road closures but everyone kept us well informed and we still got to see everything we wanted to!
Particularly William was a fantastic live guide on the bus, he told us so many interesting things and was fantastic!
And Joe’s walking tour was excellent! We even got to see the Queen! He came and told us about the Queen being out and about, while we were on the bus and then we joined the walking tour and he got us in a great spot to see the Queen!

My husband and I went to Paris and London for our anniversary and both of us agreed that, by far, London was the most fun! Our first day on the Big Bus we had an amazing your guide, I believe his name was Maxif. He was a very knowledgeable and friendly gentleman. It was freezing and rainy that day and of course my husband wasn't really dressed for it and he very kindly offered him a warm hat. He also recommended a wonderful restaurant to try called Aquachard. He said it had an incredible view of the city and he wasn't lying! It was our last meal of the trip and the most memorable one! Thank you Maxif for the wonderful tour and for helping to make our anniversary dinner so incredible!

My parents and I only had one day to spend in London; this was a great way to see everything. It was my first time visiting, and I loved it! We made a list of everything we wanted to see, then sat down in a cafe and charted our course. This tour company offers a number of lines, so you can easily plan a route that includes all desired stops. The highlight was taking the Red Line with Will as the tour guide. He was charming, hilarious, and upbeat... yet also informative and really knew his stuff. (Not to mention...he's a perfect 10, haha! and he gave me some great music recommendations.) Highly recommend this company to other Americans who want to learn more about London in an efficient and timely way.

Oh, and the boat tour was a great added bonus!

It seems that once u have bought the ticket you are no longer valued. Too many employees at each drop off and seems only focused to sell tickets. Then crowd the buses. Race along the route as they spend too much time at each stop arguing amongst themselves or stopping and talking to their mates. Then race along the route,slam on brakes. Sometimes the commentary doesnt match. Really once u pay for the ticket u just getting a bus service. They act like they doing u a favour but dont realise that customer satisfaction is giving them a job. Management maybe u should take a ride as a tourist and review the process yourself.

The red and blue routes were very good the others not so much. Busses were fine and commentators were helpful. The one way cruise was good and the 24 hour period was helpful using it from noon to noon the next day.

We got the bus by Kings Cross and then transferred to the Red Line. When we boarded the bus, we got fast passes to the Eye.In less than 3 hours we saw the entire city. The highlight was crossing London Bridge and singing "London Bridge is falling down" with our wonderful guide, Emma. This is recommended for everyone, but especially for people with limited time in London. The buses run very frequently, so don't be afraid to hop off. Also, very important, Big Bus personnel are stationed at most of the stops along the route, so you can ask questions that may concern you. They are very helpful.

We booked this combined tour through Tower hotel where we stayed. It was great value, tour guides all really knowledgeable and fun but the icing on the cake was Big Steve's walking tour to see changing of the guard which was all included in the ticket. Steve knew the perfect spots to get up close and take fabulous photos and videos. Extremely informative and enjoyable, we had so much fun. Thank you so much Steve it was a perfect way to end our visit. Top marks Steve and Big Bus. Can highly recommend.

This was our first trip to London and wanted to see as much as possible. We had a couple on the Big Red Bus Hop on Hop Off and it was a wonderful experience and learn so much about London and it’s history. It was so easy to get off at different stops and back on. All of the tour guides we encountered were awesome but especially
Peter and Roland on the Red line! We enjoyed them so very much. We had a girl one afternoon with auburn hair that I sadly forgot her name but she was so nice and helpful! Will definitely use again when we return to London.

Thank you Rob for a very entertaining day on the big bus tour. Your knowledge of London was outstanding. You went above and beyond to help people on the bus and we loved how interactive you were with everyone from the front up to the back of the bus.
We had lots of laughs and will be back tomorrow.

The Guides

Our first tour guide on the Red Line was Joe. He was humorous and energetic. Joe did a great job of mixing travel tips and history of various sites.

Our second guide was Kev. I personally think the BBC should give Kev a chance at narrating a documentary on visiting London. He had a soothing voice that put me at ease.

The Boarding Process

At busy stops, the Big Bus personnel at those stops should take charge and help the driver(s). People getting on and off created a bit of chaos. The bus driver(s) answered questions, validated the pre-booked tickets, and helped people get on and off the bus. In my humble opinion, this slowed the process and made the tour less pleasant.

In sum, it’s a good way to see London, especially if this your first trip. There are competing tours, and your experience will highly depend on the tour guide and the bus driver you meet. The guide and the driver are influenced by the volume of local traffic and the number of tourists. They are working people just like you and me, so cut them some slack. We all have our good days and bad days.

Just back from a red line tour with Emma our tour operator and Scott the driver, what a fantastic tour it was Emma was amazing her knowledge of the different area of london were first class would recommend this trip to anyone visiting london

Great commentary on trip. Red bus takes you to all the highlights of London. We planned to do one circuit and then 2nd time around, hop off at any special place we wanted to visit. Traffic was so bad that the 2 hr became 3 and a half and we still had lots to go. So we got off to take a break. We then walked back to the area we wanted to see which only took about 20 mins. A fact which was pointed out was that in the old days, horse travel averaged 18kmh in London but now the average was 8kmh with vehicles. I suggest it might be about 2kmh. Think the time for the full circuit should be amended to 3 or more hours. Perhaps we did the trip on a particularly bad traffic day.

We decided to relax and take the Big Bus around London. Our guide Emma was wonderful with tons of information about the city. She really made it so interesting. I have lived in London many years ago and I thought I knew a lot. We sat on the top where the view is great. Hop & off it's so easy.

This is a tourist trap. You can pay a fraction to get around using public transport which is also quicker and more environmental friendly.
If you instead want to get stuck in traffic and breath polluted area and waste your money then feel free to use these buses that contribute to make traffic worse and air more polluted.
Keep in mind that there are different lines, it took us ages to get from Kings Cross to the Museum district using these buses.
Around Victoria the bus was so full that we had to stay downstairs, what's the point of paying 9 times the Tfl day bus pass if you can not be in the open deck?
Also, when live commentary was on the language registered one was not working.
Screaming children are your soundtrack most of the time.
Some lines are not busy and it's a shame that the buses are polluted London air and making traffic worse.
However the worse experience was buying the ticket as the seller misled us saying that he would have given 3 tickets for 2 adults and 1 child at the price of 2 adults. When I paid and got the tickets I asked where the child ticket was. He replied that I had to lie when boarding the buses and pretend that the child was younger than 5 years. I asked to cancel the transaction but he tried to ignore me.
Well, a company with great values!
Very good guides and the layout of the routes is convenient. Regular Busses, you never have to wait too long. After their normal schedule they even have an "bring to Hotel" service for drop off.

We were luck enough to have Emma as our tour guide. My first time in London, and on a rainy cool day Emma eagerly shared her extensive knowledge of the sites in London with us. As a life-long resident of London her knowledge of her city as well as her personality made our tour both interesting and fun.

The Big Bus Hop on Hop Off Tour was great. We had purchased a London Pass and got a one day hop on hop off bus tour included. Big Bus had the best routes. We picked up the bus at St. Paul's Cathedral which was near our hotel and it took it to Buckingham, Regent Street, Piccadilly Circus, and then off back at St. Paul's again after a fun filled day. We were in London over a HOT 90 degree couple of days and sitting up top with the breeze felt wonderful.

This bus over the two days with the cruise option was good value. We never waited long times for the bus to arrive and we never had issues on the bus. It was crowded at times and slow due to traffic, but that is to be expected. It was excellent, we were able to see everything we wanted to see, still easy to use even with 4 lines. Would be nice to have some way of getting to Kew Gardens though, we had to catch the train and spend extra money. Really good, live commentary from Emma was excellent and tailored towards the people on the bus. The drivers were excellent too. The buses in good condition.

Excellent tour guide on our trip... EMMA. Very knowledgeable and funny. Would highly recommend. We had the deluxe two day ticket and took advantage of the night tour Md River cruise.
We managed to use the bus to hop on and off to most of the places we wanted to visit.

I would recommend this trip if its your first time in London , there was a lovely tour Guide called " Emma" who knew her stuff about London and was excellent in her Tour guide as everyone looked out at the Big City .

A super experience!! Very informative and easily accessed at all the bus stops. Emma was an excellent guide and was very natural.. so easy to listen to and very friendly making sure all the customers were comfortable and safe. Well done Emma!!

Emma was exceptional. She is an expert on London's history - neat her grandma was a local celebrity. She was likable, personable and warm; resembling someone you would want to call a friend. She sweetly summoned myself and parents from downstairs to join my husband up top when seats became available. I consumed her storytelling. I only wish she would have been able to stay the entire length of our tour. Thank you dear Emma. May this note bring you future cheer. Keeping shining! Hugs from California, Candice T.W.

Got off at the Marble Arch today from the Blue Route and was waiting to change to the Orange Route. The only staff member on was talking to another tour company operator and was very clearly not interested in checking or assisting Big Bus clients who were clearly waiting for busses. The Orange Bus came up but all it said on the bus was “London Eye”. Apparently your staff member yelled out Orange, but neither my sister or I heard him. Every other bus that came has been very clearly marked “Blue” or “Red Eastbound” except this one. I went to query when the next Orange bus was coming only to be told that the Orange one had just been, and that it was my fault I missed it because I didn’t go up to your staff member to check in with him and tell him what bus I was getting. It was my problem because I “ignored him” when I got here. This whole time we have been waiting (almost forty minutes now) your staff member has been taking to the other tour operator and has not approached a single client of yours. Seriously poor service and I wish I had picked Golden Tours instead. Was going to extend our Hop On Hop Off bus ticket for an extra day but will do it with a different company instead.

We booked tickets online and got charged full price. Turned up to one of their stops to find out they closed more than half of their whole routes. Emailed 4 times without any response.
You’re better off jumping on one of the public buses and seeing the city yourself, much cheaper.

On our final leg back to London Eye on the Orange line had the pleasure of having Emma as our guide. Truly exceptional. Her authenticity and passion could only come from a true Londoner. Detailed, explanations and helpful information made sitting in the traffic and rain well worth it!

I was thankful that I started my tour on the Red Line. Unfortunately, the tour was disrupted by demonstrators. Our bus was stuck on the bridge for an hour and thirty minutes! The tour guide Emma kept everyone informed. As others left the bus, she shared much information on the history of her beloved country but also much about the culture. I really feel like I know England much better due to her knowledge and commitment to her trade as an ambassador for the City of London!

The bus driver should be commended as well as he helped many patrons to claim over the bike barrier.

Thanks to each of them for going beyond their job descriptions!!!
Great way to see London. The live commentary is great if you can get on a bus that has it! Otherwise there is audio commentary that explains things very well.

It’s a rainy day in London, which I suppose is expected. We decided to take a bus tour. I am truly impressed with the driving ability of Patrick. London traffic is intensely close and he was able to navigate without problems. He was able to move a very large tour bus in very small spaces. Our tour guide Lionel was humorous and informative. He also handled some difficult passengers with decorum. It was a great way to spend a few hours looking at the city in comfort.

I purchased 4 tickets for me and my family having checked buses were accessible. Arrived with family from Scotland excited to tour London only to be refused access to the bus as I use a power chair. Was told I was pi**ing the driver off by asking about disability access and why I couldn't get on the bus when every other bus in London had no problem taking me. I have a small powered chair not a huge mobility scooter and have never been treated with such awful discrimination and lack of any customer support or care. Avoid big bus company at all costs they clearly care nothing for customers with a disability.

Today I got on a bus near St. Paul's Cathedral, London. I took a seat expecting live audio from an actual human. After five minutes I realized there was no guide and that this is a regular occurrence -- guided routinely don't show up for work. I tried another bus: same thing. Instead of a guided tour I got a bus ride. Don't waste your time or money.

I discovered the idea of the hop on hop off bus tours in NYC. I find then to be a great way to explore a city that you are new to in a comforting way. In London we were blessed to have some very entertaining and knowledgeable tour guides. To be fair some were a bit boring but most were very funny. As I’ve done the tour a few times now I do know that each one shares slightly different facts on each location so don’t be afraid to take it again if you have already.

I’m rating this as a 4 simply because, while I know the British tend to be very straight forward we did encounter a couple of the drivers who were a little on the rude side (even with me looking past the directness of the culture). However the majority of the staff friendly and helpful answering questions I imagine they get 100 times a day. They are especially helpful where it comes to getting you to your point of interest or back to your hotel.

If you are short on time and can’t do all the routes - I recommend the RED one (it is the most popular I think). It has the most stops and is the one with the live commentator - so most entertaining in my opinion. The others, it seems uses recorded information so you get the facts but the live guides and humor to theirs.

Be sure to check the news to see if there is anything happening in the city (marches, demonstrations, etc.), before buying your ticket. It will affect the routes and possibly if you have a live guide. They do a good job of rerouting the busses but through no fault of their own you don’t get the full experience.

Happy touring.
The bus was not ventilated on the bottom floor very small windows in the back very uncomfortable never ride on a warm day
Our tour was great, very informative and fun too. Lewis turned a wet open top bus tour into a great ride. Highly recommended!

My Canadian family very recently used the daily trip, and have asked me to convey their views. They found their day in London was greatly enhanced by the whole experience and wanted to particularly mention Rob and Emma who were very friendly and very informative of the sights of London. All in all they had a terrific day - thank you.

We hopped on and off the Red route a couple of times, beginning at the Tower of London and finishing at Saint Pauls cathedral. All the guides were friendly and helpful, and from all over Europe. Emma really knew London and enriched the script considerably, giving suggestions based upon er own long experience rather than sounding like every hint about what to see was a sponsored advert. The Red route covered most of what we wanted to see. We still preferred traveling on the river to get an overview of the city than through traffic!

So we had one full day to see Central London. We had tried to do a Duck Tour the previous day in Windsor area and it got cancelled by the other company and so we were a bit apprehensive about committing to another tour because we didn’t want to miss twice. I’m happy to say this was the best decision we could’ve made to see London. We have a family of 7, which includes ages from 19yo down to just under 2yo so we needed a lot of seats. I had read negative reviews from people who couldn’t get enough seats up top or missed busses often or whatnot. I can say that we didn’t really have that issue. We went on a Monday during their peak season at end of July. We picked areas to get on their busses where their multiple routes intersected and a lot of busses arrived. By doing this, you’d have groups that would choose to get on a different route because the one they wanted was full. It helped spread out the masses. Secondly, we would all get on a bus and wait till the next stop because we couldn’t always get up top which Is the best viewing. When the bus would stop, we’d move to the top and take spots there. It is really simple and those already on the bus get first dibs at the top level so it works out. All of my kids loved the tour and got some great pics. We had room for our compact jog stroller downstairs and the last bus we were on, we got to hear a live commentator tour guide , Lucas, who was awesome. He had just enough dad-joke type humor that if you were paying attention would make you laugh out loud. Great job. We loved it. I think weekends are probably even busier so I can see that being tougher to get on and set but I will say they had a TON of busses going so even if l, they’d be able to accommodate everyone. Worth every penny

All of the tour guides were excellent, wait time for buses was minimal, buses were clean. The included walking tour was amazing, highly recommend it. We were fortunate to do the tour on a day when there was a changing of the guard at Buckingham Palace and we were able to see the process from start to finish. We also received a free river cruise with our bus passes. If you elect to do the cruise I recommend doing only the portion between Westminster and London Tower. I found the portion to Greenwich to be a waste of valuable sightseeing time.

Overpriced for what we got. We did the bus tour in 4 separate sections, and on 2 of those sections there was a problem with the microphone so there was no live commentary. The pre-recorded stuff was pretty uninteresting so we didn’t learn anything about the history of the city. We might as well have gotten a standard bus ticket around the city. We also didn’t get to go over Tower Bridge or London Bridge as advertised. I wouldn’t recommend this tour at all.

We booked this tour online for the same day. Our original plans had gone astray and we thought this the best way to experience the sights of London without having to walk far in the unusually hot weather with my two children aged 7 & 9. After climbing aboard the first bus we found nowhere to sit, up or downstairs and had to stand with kids on a stuffy overpacked bus. Obviously not much sightseeing could be done. We decided to get off at tower bridge stop where the guide explained where to board the river cruise. On arrival at the pier we were told we didn't have the right kind of ticket as they don't scan mobile tickets, it had to be paper. We were not given any paper ticket on boarding the bus. We returned to tower bridge bus stop looking for a big bus representative but was told by a different tour company guide that they had left at 17.00, (it was now 17.15). As I waited for the next bus I tried unsuccessfully to get through to customer services on the phone (was on hold until it cut off). Finally another overpacked big bus arrived but the driver also did not have the right machine to print us a paper ticket from my phone ticket. The river cruise runs until 19.15 from tower bridge to Westminster but unless you get your printed (not e-ticket) you can't get on it as their company representative leaves at 17.00. We reluctantly got back on the overcrowded bus, again standing. It doesn't end here... By this time it is 18.00. I happened to ask the guide how long it takes to arrive at covent garden stop (we had a return train to catch to Leeds) only to find out that that the bus terminates the service at marble arch after 18.00. Aware of our dilema and unfortunate experience with the river cruise, he advised us to get off at Buckingham palace as it would be the shortest route to walk back with my two children. I have no complaints with the staff I encountered, they were all helpful but the organisation is terrible, not enough frequency of buses and encountered other customers who could not get on as bus was too full. Not the London Tour we were hoping for. I could have spent a lot less money using standard public buses for the same experience. Very disappointed. Would not recommended the big bus tours.

It is a good choice in Hop-On Hop-Off Tour circuit. it offers facilities as we were given preferential treatment at the London Eye and Madame Tussauds. Some of the staff was a little arrogant at Oxford Street. It was not clear in the brochure which time the Last bus starts. I had to find out this. In totality a good Choice

We were really looking forward to this experience. But we have to recommend Golden Tour Buses instead which seemed to be everywhere while we waited interminably for a Big Bus. The ticketing was hard to find around Victoria Station and they don't tell you your tour must be completed by 1800 or take a cab. We found out when the bus stopped and were forced to get a cab. Other buses appeared to continue operating after 1800. The guides were lackluster at best.

We did the red route first, that was so much fun. We had tge most amazing informative Tour Guide, Ruby. WOW she was excellent. I asked her how she remembered everything, she said she trained for two weeks and had only been on the job a week. I was shocked, she's a natural with the history and adding her little stories in. She was fun and kept us entertained, so much so we stayed on the bus a lot longer than we planned to. Thanks Big Bus Tours and a huge thanks to Ruby. You truly made our first visit to London very memorable and we learned a lot from you. GREAT service and GREAT tour.

Visited London with my friend who has never been and decided after having hiked for 20 km up in Scotland that a tour bus could be nice. Had a great experience with the lovely Emma who knew so much about London and it’s history. She had little anecdotes about different streets and places as we were crawling through the busy pre lunch traffic. She took the time to answer the people’s questions and made the tour more personal and alive, which is easier when having a live guide rather than a pre recorded one.

What a great tour bus with a great tour guide. Mehmet made our day with his knowledge of London. He was such a lovely guy who even went above the call of duty and sung happy birthday to my friend in front of all the passengers, he really did make our weekend!! Thanks so much and keep up the good work. We will be sure to book again next time we come.
Didn’t see any of the sites mentioned, no commentary. I waited since 1980, so sad. I would not recommend to my worst enemies

We partook in the hop on and off bus tour. The stop locations were great, and a reasonable price at 50cad per person in peak season (if you order directly off their website). However, I felt the bus was overstuffed. At the beginning of the day there were no issues getting seats up top. However, around 3pm they became so crowded that there were people squishing in and standing overtop of you down the aisle. They just kept cramming more people in! The tour commentators were ok (some better then others),but still not as enthusiastic or talking as often as I would expect. We had a great time but feel we'd book with a different company next time

Big bus rip off!!! My wife and I purchased a “24 hour” ticket at 3 pm today. When we tried to hop on at 7 pm we were told that our ticket was not valid for the “night tour “. If we had known about this policy we would not have purchased the tickets. Save your money or use another company.

I made a big mistake and bought 3 tickets from the street for 40 pounds each. After 10 mn i finally found the station and waited there 20 mn more for the bus to arrive (even thought the guy i bought them from told me i will wait max 20 mn). From the time i hopped i stayed on for 45 mn stuck in traffic before our driver left the bus resulting having to find onother ride. After a 30 mn wait the bus finally arrived and to our suprise it was FULL even so we decided to hop on. We spended another hour standing still stucked in traffic untill i felt sick and decided to exit the bus.
A COMPLETE WASTE OF MONEY!!!
120£ LOST
PLEASE STAY AWAY FROM THIS SCAM

There are a lot of tour bus groups in London. We chose this one because it seemed to have more routes than the other groups. I HIGHLY recommend that you download the Big Bus app on your smart phone when you get tickets. It will show you not only the real time locations of the buses, but ID which ones have live tour guides vs just drivers with pre-recorded tour descriptions. The Red route, which goes through the bulk of the tourist locations; Buckingham, Westminster, Tower of London, etc, is the busiest route. It has more frequent buses and more live tour guides. We had one guide in particular who was stellar; funny, very knowledgable, spoke very clearly and distinctly and even gave us a heads up to get our cameras out when we were approaching something lens-worthy. I wish I had gotten his name. The Blue route went out to the Kensington/Notting hill area, where we were staying. This route does not have a lot of tourist stops on it, nor live guides and does not run very frequently. It was used more as a pick up-drop off route and was frequently over-packed beyond what was really safe. We also had a driver who must have been on his last route for the day; he ran three red lights, almost hit a few motorbikes, and basically drove like a maniac. The last trips are at 6 pm, which I thought was too early, especially at the height of tourist season , when it stays light out until about 9:30 pm. Still, it wasn't the worst way to get around the city and see the sights.

Wouldn't use these again steer clear and use one of the other companies that do the same thing, I've used big bus in many countries where they have been absolutely fine, we visited London a couple of weeks ago and one of there drivers were so rude and offensive we actually left the bus, there own operative rang there offices to complain about him and since we go back I have tried emailing and instant messaging and no one will get back to me about being able to make an official complaint!!!!!
Emma 👍🌞😊 Emma our guide was amasing. 😊👍👍👍👍She is a lexivon. Knows all you need to know about London. She is 4.generation Londoner, she is funny and Nice.

We took the hop on-hop off red line bus on the afternoon of July 12 and it was an excellent kick-off to our one-week stay. The best part was our tour guide Tiffany who has just the right combination of knowledge, personal experience, passion about the city, and sassy wit. The route is smartly plotted to introduce you to the all parts of the central city and all the major attractions you may want to visit. It was highly informative and enjoyable.

Disgusted! Jam packed and more and more people where aloud on. Pathetic couldn't see a thing. Very hot! More and more people piled on after I took this photo. I sent a message to big bus on Facebook, they saw it and never wrote back. Never been so let down it was just pathetic. I never get angry with people I will always just keep it to myself but I couldn't help but say to the driver "this is pathetic!" When I left the bus. I couldn't sit in it, the sweat and B.O from strangers bumping into me while I'm breaking my hip trying to see out the window. I just couldn't believe it. People where standing on the stair case and yet more and more people piled on and the bus driver just let them ! No worries jam yourself on. Couldn't see a bloody thing.

There are many bus companies operating in London- Original Tour, Golden Tour and Big Bus. Big Bus seems to be one of the best value for money.

But don’t get fooled by their marketing.

Big Bus is cheaper because it operates way fewer busses. Typically you have to wait 30-40min for their busses. Compare that to an average of 10min for other companies. In addition, they hire very bad personnel.
