See photos of a long line waiting for the bus while their personnel are chatting with each other far away. In fact, one Original Tour rep answered our questions about Big Bus schedules while the Big Bus operators were avoiding us.

I traveled with a group of six people in May from the U.S. on our way to South Africa and we had a several hours in London before a connecting flight. We decided Big Bus Tours LTD would be a good way to see the city in a short period of time. After purchasing our tickets, and going to the bus stop as directed, we waited for over two hours while one completely full bus after another came and went. Each bus was filled to maximum capacity and the staff kept telling us to wait for the next bus. We finally asked for a refund and we were told to go back to where the tickets were purchased. Upon doing so, we were told that the refund couldn't be processed until the Manager was back on duty a couple of days later, but we were assured that we would get refund. Now, a month and a half later, we are still trying to get the refund!
Will S is a brilliant live tour guide on their red route! definitely recommend taking big bus tours ! Absolutely fell in love with london!

Routes and stops are not satisfactorily explained. If u ask drivers they are rude and tell u to sit down. Too many transfers to get to specific sites. Save your money buy an Oyster card and take the tube. Employees there are helpful as well as maps. These buses are a rip off compared to places like Rome or Dublin. As for getting the access to sites, the cards were for payment only and you still had to stand in long lines. No priority access

We had a tour of london on the 3rd of july. Getting on the buses from the london eye was an actual nightmare. So many people pushing, at this point i was regretting booking the tour and we decided to get a taxi bike to see Buckingham palace.
After seeing Buckingham palace we decided to try the bus tour again from a different stop. Stop 20. We got on and got a seat. We stayed on the buses from stop 20 to stop 1 and then had an entire tour of London from stop 1 and all the way back round to stop 1. We had a lovely tour guide by the name of Valdas. He was very friendly, smiley, very easy to talk to and more than happy to answer any questions, a lovely person who is very good at his job. We really enjoyed the tour with him and by the End of the tour was very glad we booked it after all. Was great seeing london and learning more about the city. Would definately recommend this tour.
The bus was average, but our guide, Emma, was great! Her personal perspective made this a very informative tour of London.

We rode the Hop On Hop Off bus for a day in London. We got on and off several times during that day. When we were on the red line and had a live English speaking guide we found a huge difference in the quality of the guides. The first one was Chris and he was less than helpful and we got off feeling like we didn't know anything more than when we started, except that he is told often that he looks like Bill Clinton. On the other hand, we got on when Matthew was the guide and he was exceptional. We went past several of the same places we had been by with Chris and Matthew gave us detailed and interesting information. He appeared to enjoy it and responded to questions with enthusiasm. The bus is very slow due to traffic and if you have a good guide, at least there are some stories told. There were many times we could have walked much faster than the bus, so if you expect to learn a lot - you're at the mercy of the guide.

We were staying in a hotel nearby to Madame Tussaud’s so decided on this bus tour on Saturday. I asked the ticket seller the cost of the tickets as I read on the shop window 2 adults and 2 children was a total of £90, the seller said ‘no it is £107 for a family ticket’, then she advised she was mistaken the cost for a family ticket is £102. Anyway, I didn’t dispute this as maybe I assumed I had read
the wrong price on an old poster.

We weren’t given any info from the ticket seller just 1 leaflet and a swift ‘get off at the attraction you want to see’: Eventually we fathomed out the leaflet and got off down Oxford Street. After returning to the same spot we discovered we could join the river cruise at The Thames so after a long gruelling journey in the sweltering heat we got off at the River Thames. We then found out that the queue for the cruise was massive and at least a 2 hour wait, we couldn’t put 2 young children through this so went for a wander. Needless to say they were hot and disappointed.

We then got back on the bus on a different stop to be told we could return to Madame Tussards and would be 3 stops then the redline for a further stop and this would take no longer than an hour. We took an hour at least to travel 1 stop to the stop we had got off at the River Thames. After a further 2 stops we were advised to get off and transferred onto another bus, this was by the recorded commentator. We got off the bus and asked a ticket seller what bus we needed, he advised ‘hop on another bus, get off after 2 stops and then get off at Marble Arch and stay on the redline for 1 stop’. He then came back over to us to advise us he thinks it is 3 stops and not 2. We’d had enough by then and knew we were due shortly at the theatre the same evening so we decided to walk there instead.

Aside for the lack of and misinformation, there was no escape from the heat, it was stifling! On some of the journeys the commentary did not work so we were not impressed at all. Aside from this, luckily we managed to get seats but there was many people stood up both up and downstairs which, according to the signs, should only be seating upstairs. Plus trying to get off the bus from upstairs was a battle itself as hoards of people who had just got on tried to squash past us, not allowing anyone downstairs. Each time we thought we were going to miss our stop!

I am aware it was a hot day on Saturday but for goodness sake we are bound to have some hot days in London and really would we go to a cinema for example with no sound or seat?!

I would definitely not recommend. I would thought recommend trying a different company!

The big bus tour was really simple and easy to take. The live guides were great and we loved their dry humour.

Would really recommend this tour and to take at least the 2 day pass so you can take your time with all four routes. Two thumbs up! :)
We took the tour for 2 days and it was amazing. Was lucky that the weather was good. The bus stops at all the important / tourist landmarks. It was easy for us to go around.

Had a really good experience on The Big Bus Red Tour yesterday morning (Monday 24th June 2019). The Tour Guide, Matt, was very informative and pointed out many places of interest to me and my son. But I would like to thank the driver (who said his name was Paul). He was very kind and understanding towards my son who is wheelchair bound. He was very friendly and had a chat with my son to reassure him as the bus was quite full and he was a bit distressed. This helped my son to calm down and he also found it to be very cool that Paul is also in the police! If all the staff at The Big Bus are like this then I would thoroughly recommend it to everyone! Thanks once again!

If you're lucky enough to get Emma, sit down, chuck it on her channel and enjoy! What a knowledgeable and down to earth guide! As it was my parents first trip to London, their comment at dinner "Emma really made our trip" how good is that! Thanks Emma for making us smile and laugh.

Our morning started off on the wrong foot by discovering that The Underground had been shut down. We decided to take the bus instead and it ended up being the best decision ever! Our tour guide Emma was so knowledgeable and you could definitely tell she loves her job. She turned our mess of a morning into a very enjoyable time! We didn’t want to get off!

Our hotel hooked us up with this tour company ( they must give favorable conditions for resell). I have been to may cities and used many hop on hop of busses, but this will go down as my worst experience of them all. They are so good at selling their product that they can't keep up with their demand (at least this was the experience for our day). We had to take the blue line to go to the red line that would go into town and see the main attractions. Getting on the blue bus was difficult (many people waiting, but we managed. We did not have this luck with the red bus - a long line and every bus that pulled up was already full. We cycled through 5 buses with no luck, being the first in line) the crowd was getting angry and the local contact had no good answers referring back to the elusive management. In the end we where unable to use their service and are trying to get a refund. I was a shame, as we had a very limited time in town and this soured our experience. For my opinion, there are too or three other companies that offer similar service and circled around with almost empty buses, while we waited - I will chose one of them the next time I need this service in London.
My advise the the company - get more buses or limit sells per day - stop being greedy and underdeliver your services!

Big Bus is a great way to explore London if you have a lot of time on your hands. They have 3-4 routes and most of them take over an hour.
The red line, a route that takes you to all the main attractions in London includes a tour guide (note that every bus has audio recorded commentary). We were lucky to have Emma in our bus and she was fun, energetic, kind and clearly knew her city well. If you get a good tour guide you will learn many things about London you wouldn't pick up otherwise. If you want to know as much as possible about the city, definitely check Big Bus out.
It is quite expensive though so bear that in mind, for some it isn't worth it as for a two day pass you can get an Oyster card that can easily last a week.

5 buses of “The Original Bus Tour” went by while waiting for our “Big Bus”. Which was completely over crowded
DO NOT RECOMMEND

Famous Double Deckers but do t be fooled there are lots of bus tours. The big red bus tour may be the most economical arnd a great way to get around the city. You can buy multi deay passes and literally cover London from one end the other. Not a big commitment and prices ranged around 26 pounds. Some packages include water tour.

I always love doing the hop-on / hop-off in any place we go. You get such a good perspective of how big the city is and the history and tidbits from the live guides are priceless in my opinion! It's also a great way to get around the city without purchasing an oyster card (if you were that way inclined).

Definitely get a 2-3 day pass if you want to see all 4 routes, however don't let only 1 day in London deter you. This is a must do.

Over crowded, absolutely no crowd management, extremely rude tour guide sitting on the upper deck. He was disrespectful and seemed to spend much of his time YELLING at patrons not to come up. Horrible. We didn’t even realize there was a live tour guide until we managed to get upstairs over an hour into it. No explanations were made. I wouldn’t recommend this company.

Bought a 3 day hop on hop off pass and had a mixed bag of experiences. First time I got on the bus, I had only intended to go 3 stops on the red line, but our tour guide Nick (with his bus driver Dave) was so funny and interesting that I ended up staying in the whole 2 hour loop. That was a five star experience. However, getting on another bus, we didn’t have a guide at all. The next bus we got on had standing room only. So overall, the bus will get you where it needs to go, and if you are lucky, you could potentially end up with a gem of a tour guide

Decent tour with good stops but it was difficult during the rain as the service was inconsistent.
I must say guide (Roland) was awesome, really good and updated commentary.

We bought tickets from the big bus for the bus tour and boat tour, the hop on hop off is open top but we spent most of the day down stairs and at times standing. Then i found out at one of the bus stops by speaking to sales staff of the blue company I think (don't know the name) that the price of tickets are too much there are other companies at better value for money, same tour less money, we pay more to stand up on the bus. Some sales staff are rude for example at victoria.

Decided we would do the big bus tour has we could get it as a package deal with other tourist attractions. We did another bus tour in Paris and thought we would like this one.

We were “greeted” with the bus driver being extremely rude and yelling at other customers. We went into the bus to find a wall of people in the isle. There were so many people on the bus we couldn’t have a seat and the bus driver continued to yell at a guy who was standing on the front blocking his view. The poor guy didn’t have room to move anywhere else! We expected a tour but it was more crowded than any metro bus we were on. After about 10 or so minutes of being squished and hearing others complain we finally got a seat when other people got off the bus. There was no Audio in the lower section as our seats didn’t have head phone jacks for our head phones to listen to the taped tour.
The next stop there was a lot of people waiting and the tour guide yelled to the driver how many are we taking. The tour guide replied with just fill the bus. There was 30+ people squished in the isle and people had to push their way through. There were 2 doors on the bus but the back one was labeled emergency so everyone had to use the 1 at the front. A couple stops later the driver decided to open the rear door to fit even more people. After about an hour a large amount of people got off and we were able to move to the upper section. We could finally hear the guide who was awesome but were very frustrated and not in a good mood. Other tour buses had enough seats for all passengers. Would have been a 5 star review for the guided, maybe a 3-4 with the very rude driver. The amount of money we paid and to not have a seat and not he be able to pick up customers waiting at other stops for 25 min + was unacceptable. I would highly recommend getting s your from another company.

I used Tours with bus Hope on Hope off in many different countries and cities, however this one was very disappointing experience.Auidio recording has very little information, mostly you can hear about advertisement of this company and asking to give them a good reviews.It was very long lines to get in,no seated places available,no cleared marked stations ,when you get in the bus, takes a long time to figure out which line you on ( some stations overlapping ) I had better experience with public transportation

We did this tour today and were a little disappointed. The tour audio is pre-recorded, so no room for inquiries. The red route was extremely crowded (over sold) and we stood for about 5 stops so that meant no audio at all. :( To be fair, we did not have the same issue on the blue route. For what we got, we felt it was a bit overpriced.

Took the bus couple times within 48hours while here in London, had couple tour guides but Louis killed it!!! He was funny and kept us entertained even while stuck in traffic..! Highly recommend!!! :)
Much love from San Diego!!

having a day out in London decided to try the open top bus about lunch time when I asked what the cost, I was quoted £78.00, for two adults I explained it was only for the afternoon I was told £78.00, this is the biggest con I've come across in a long time, when I returned to Hotel to check prices I could not find one costing that came to £78.00 many close to it, but certainly not what I was quoted.
We booked the day before and loved seeing the sights of London with live commentary. We got on and off at several places and didn't have to wait too long for the buses.

My friend and I visited London today. We've bought tickets for Coca-Cola London Eye with Hop off Hop on Big Buses Tours and Boat included at £45/ each on Coca-Cola London Eye website, 2 attractions.
It was a good choice, very good price and our Big Buses ' s live guide was Tiffany whom explained in detail all the important points on the map.
Thank you Tiffany for such a good presentation.
And Thank you to the bus driver for being so polite and sorting out all our route's doubts.
We've met Tiffany in our red route.
We will definitely recommend you!
All the best!
C & G

We had a great time getting around London on the Big Bus hop on hop off. sitting upstairs gave a great perspective of the city and opportunities to take some photos as you drove around. We swapped routes at different times to see different areas, however the highlight was definitely the red route with live commentary. We were fortunate to have Daniel as our commentator on 2 separate occasions. He was engaging, knowledgeable and appropriately humorous in providing great details of the sight we drove by. Also, the staff at each of the stops were friendly and helpful. The buses are well worth the money to for sightseeing or for getting to all the main attractions.

London is such a busy place and this is a great way to get about, see the sights and avoid the crowds. There are some negative reviews on here about the buses being overcrowded and busy. This company cannot prevent this as it is our choice to travel! The buses are frequent so you will always find a bus that has vacant seats and with people hopping on and off you have the opportunity to move around at the various stops. We waited for such a bus and was able to move to the upper deck and at the front - the best seats in the house. It can get a little warm on a hot day but the cover over the front part does give you some shade, a bonus. There was an excellent and informative commentary in English and there are head phones that you can plug in at your seat if required. The seats are plastic and do get warm and rather sticky, take a cushion if you plan a long trip around London. The driver slowed down at certain points around the course for us all to have a good view. He was able to stop completely on some occasions. Do remember your water bottle! We were on the red route but next time we are going to try the blue and orange ones. Note you can also hop off and hop on to experience a water boat trip too. Overall an excellent way to see London. Book ahead to save time and to get a good deal.

My family and I did a big bus tour of London today on the red route and were very entertained by live guide, Emma. She gave excellent relevant entertaining commentaries, was cheerfully funny and went beyond the call of duty, I felt, to help passengers get good seats and provide private recommendations on this and that.

We had thought all the Big Bus live guides were similarly impressive but found out that wasn't so. Emma definitely stands out! Thanks Emma!

Emma was very knowledgeable about her history, being a third generation native. Big bus tour is one of the best way to do sightseeing around London. I recommend this to those who want to see a lot in a short amount of time.

Emma is the best tour guide!! She helped us figure out our day....we had no idea what to do with only one day in London. She advised us to take the London Tour and the river cruise. We took 2 other tours that day and it wasn’t as good as the first (Emma)...we were hoping we would find her again!!
Look forward to next time!!

Emma is an amazing tour guide. It was our first time in London and Emma was very knowledgeable. We had no idea what we wanted to do and Emma helped us fill in our whole day. We loved she was a history buff and that she was a 3rd generation native.

This is a very convenient way to get an overview of sites in London. I liked that we could start the tour at any stop. In our case, it was right in front of our hotel. The Big Bus Tour map shows where you can connect to another route. The taped commentary worked fine for us. If you aren't sure what you want to see in London, this passes by all the major attractions. You can disembark, visit the attraction, then reboard a later bus. Connections are frequent.

Beautiful Morning spent touring Londons sights! Emma our tour guide was terrific! Tower of London was amazing. The tour was super informative! So many interesting facts ... what a fabulous city steeped in history 👍

The tour would be very informative and helpful if everything worked the way it was intended. But sometimes we couldn't figure out what the narration was referring to because it was poorly matched to the scenery. Also in our case at the second half of the tour the narration stopped working all together, constantly repeating half sentences. We alerted the driver twice about it. Nothing changed. When we were leaving the bus the driver told us that he notified the office about the problem. No apology or reimbursement was offered.

So my 13 year old son and I got onto the bus figuring it was a passive way of spending time in our last hours before leaving London. We’ve done Big Bus in other cities and its usually OK or better.

As it turned out Big Steve, who works for Big Bus, gets on and offers to take people on a walking excursion. No extra charge. Walking tour was great. About an hour. Led people back to bus or river tour at the end. He told lots of funny anecdotes. It made our day. Thanks Steve.

After spending a couple weeks in northern England, we had a day near London before flying out of Heathrow. Not having been to London before, we opted for the Red tour to see the major sites of the city. It was a wonderful sunny day and we immensely enjoyed the 3 hours spent touring London.

The guide on our bus was Emma and she was superb. Hi Emma! She knows the city, knows the history, and was very personable and helpful. She did say that she gets a modest tip from the company for every 5-star review she gets and we're more than happy to do this for her. She deserves it. We were only on two buses (one Blue and one Red) and everyone involved (drivers, ticketers, and guide) were helpful and friendly. We purchased tickets online and saved 10%. Worked well for us and we would recommend it.

We did three bus tours but none compares to Emma's tour! Emma provided lots of information on each place we were driven by. We left with the impression that we learnt a lot and would do it again if we have the opportunity. Many thanks to Emma for contributing to this excellent visit to London!

Great for intro to London. Traffic is bedlam so don’t expect it to be fast. Recommend do red blue and orange in 1 go then go back as required. Hopping on and off frequently doesn’t work too well as there are often delays. There were road closures due to protests so check before you pay. The audio was a bit scant on info but we had a live guide for part of the time who was AWESOME. Lots of interesting info. Thanks Sherry. Overall worthwhile but only 1 day.
Great way to get around London and hit the major sites. The tour guides we had, Lionel and Emma were awesome and full of knowledge!! They made the bus ticket worthwhile!

I could go on and on about what an awful day and experience we had but the to sum it up, they sold us a ticket when the buses weren’t running and would not refund money. We spent hours waiting at bus stops and walking all over London! Customer service was terrible!

Emma on the red bus was very entertaining, I give her a 5 star rating! As for the Blue bus, the gentleman commentating was a very good. BUT THE EMPLOYEE AT THE BUS STOP AT HYDE PARK WAS VERY RUDE TO ME AND MY DAUGHTER. Management needs to give some their employees proper customer etiquette.
Remind the rides to what channel the commentator is on.

Despite traffic is an issue in London, the guides and drivers are so helpful and provide an expert advise to assure you can arrive to your destination, always checking were are you going or what are your plans for the day so you can do your best with the time.
The live commentary is relevant and interesting. As soon as you get in the bus you are greeted and the environment is really relaxed, you can focus in taking pictures and enjoy the trip.
Emma is a wonderful and caring guide, I really enjoyed all her comments about art, sculptures and the wonderful places in London but in general all personal is diligent and professional. The Wifi was really convenient.
We mainly used the red line and only the green one the day we visited the British Museum and Convent garden.

When I first arrived I was all set to travel via The Tube to get around. My concierge recommended the Hop On/Off Bus and it was excellent! It makes many stops at all the top Tourist stops allowing you to get back on/off at your own leisures. Buses run frequently so you're never waiting long. Its a long ride consisting of 3-4 routes which do have connecting stops. Well worth the $$ especially if you are short on time. I have done this bus in other cities and always a great experience with everyone very helpful.

Just got off today’s Big Bus tour with the London tour guide Louis, even though the weather was wet, he did an excellent job informing all the riders of the history of the area and I really enjoyed his humor and wit. Had a blast with Louis and people from all over the world. Highly recommended!

After my teenage daughter decided she was sick of walking, we decided to book the Big Bus Hop On Hop Off Premium Ticket which included 2-day pass which allows access to all 3 routes, a round trip River Cruise to Greenwich, and a Night Tour.

Booking on Klook saved a small amount of money but was convenient as I already had the app.

Earbuds are provided on boarding, which you can plug in at your seat and select the language of your choice. From time to time there was a live commentary by an English speaking tour guide.

On the first day we toured from near Euston Station to the Tower of London, where we caught the river cruise to Greenwich then back to Millennium Pier. Then we rejoined the bus until it terminated at Piccadilly due to the Extinction Rebellion protests.

We took the Night Tour the next day, which visits most of the same places, but with a different feel to the city and the illuminated buildings.

I did note that none of the tours went past the front of Buckingham Palace.

Both my teenage daughter and I would definitely recommend.

Our tour guide Emma was amazing. She clearly loved her job and she knew an endless amount of London history and could rattle off date after date of important events. It was great having this tour included in our London Pass, and it was a great way to relax and see the city.

Bought a two day Big Bus Tour ticket and got a bonus river cruise. Was able to see plenty of London on the first day and had an enjoyable river cruise where we had the added bonus of seeing Tower Bridge raised not only once but twice. The second day we were caught in traffic due to the motorbike protest but were still able to get to our stops with a small delay. We enjoyed the service so much we got another one day pass several days later.

Nice way but a little slow for obvious reasons: heavy traffic!
The drivers aren't very nice/simpathetic...
But there s one guy in the ter line named Phillip who gives information and is funny!
Overall it's s good

I got my ticket for the big bus tour through the London pass and it was a really great addition to the large number of things I had access to with the pass. This was my first time in London so the bus tour was a great way to see a lot of things and decide which place to visit first. My tour guide was a lovely lady named Emma — she was kind and friendly and very knowledgeable! I got the sense that she really cared about all of the tour-goers and she knew a lot of fun facts! Would definitely recommend.

Our tour guide Louis did a really great job. He introduced himself and asked where you were from. He then managed to include something that might be about someone or thing from your area. Also due to diverted streets he still managed to keep his banter going with highlights of who lived here and local pub stories etc.
Thanks Louis our bus ride was entertaining educational and fun.

BTW trip advisor needs family category as we had 4 family members no teens no children all adults

Me and my boys boarded the red route at Green Park and were helped with our booking. I booked about 30mins before we wanted to go on the tour. It was so straight forward and the guys on the street were very helpful. The driver welcomed us onboard and Anna Marie provided a very knowledgeable and entertaining tour. She made sure everyone was on the right Channel so we could listen to her telling us all about London.

We got off at stop 16 and then took the boat back as we had a flight to catch. The boat people boarded us nicely, but it was not as enjoyable at the bus tour.

I had three boys aged 10 (twins) and 12 and they all enjoyed the tour. Visit the big bus website so you can see where the various yours take you. They have s great map of the routes.

Book it!

My 3-day pass for BigBus tours was by far the best tourism deal in London! Ideal for those who enjoy people-watching, or those who aren't able to sight-see as well on foot. The routes are extremely complementary with public transport. While traveling on the Red Line, I had the immense privilege to have Ian as a tour guide! Not only is he friendly, hospitable and incredibly knowledgeable, but as a native Londoner was able to offer the most interesting and obscure tidbits about the city. Hop on the Red Line and prepare to be awed :)

Used this service to get around London. We didn’t get the full advantage of it as we were only there for the day and hadn’t time to fit it all in. But they certainly had plenty of places to drive by.
But for the time we did use it...it was fine. It’s the same set of of any other city...there wasn’t really any stress with using this crew..no confusion. There was a crew member at the bus stops...but our first stop was at Kings Cross...and a sign would have been helpful as we couldn’t find the bus stop for a while. We eventually saw the staff member.
What I like about this one was that we got the bus ticket combined with a river cruise and then entry in London Eye. So was a good combination and better value this way. The cruise was worth doing ...
All in all....it worked fine for us.

I took this tour on a rainy and windy cold day recently. I have to admit that I was very pleasantly surprised by the tour: first, I joined the walking tour in the morning and enjoyed the timely visit to the changing of the Horse guards, The guide was very knowledgeable and passionate about History and happy to answer any questions. Then I went on the hop on and off bus and had a great experience: unlike in many cities where you listen to a prerecorded audio-guide, I had the privilege to listen to Mehmet, a real guide who provided lots of information with a great sense of humour and much enthusiasm. I ended up staying on the bus for the whole tour instead of hopping on and off, because the commentaries were so interesting ! Thank you Mehmet ! Keep up the humour !

London's a wonderful city - we all know that. And the evidence of our own eyes tells us how old, varied and special its architecture is. But it takes a great story-teller to bring it to life and elicit chuckle after chuckle as he goes.

Well done, Christopher - great to see a real pro at work. And thanks to today's driver, too (was it Leon?).

A thoroughly enjoyable tour: pricey, but we got plenty from it. Heartily recommend taking the river cruise option, too: we went all the way to Greenwich (of Meantime fame) and the river views were stunning. Greenwich itself if a beautiful 18th century village swallowed up by the city and worth the diversion.

Rather than have the stress of navigating London on public transport we decided to get a day ticket with big bus. We went for the red route. The buses are clean the driver and guides friendly and interesting...special mentions for Molly the guide who was lovely. I would highly recommend downloading the app which gives you directions to the nearest stop and tells you where the next bus is. They come along every 10 mins or so, so there is never long to wait. Our ticket included a river trip, but we didn't do this as we ran out of time on everything else

The wife and I did a hop on/hop off tour while we waited to check into our hotel. We hopped on, but never hopped off. Emma was a ton of fun. Knowledgeable and funny. She gave us great insights and recommendations. A perfect way to start our trip.

What a wonderful way to see London. You can truly get on and off the bus at your leisure to get a closer look at the sights you're Interested in seeing closer. The buses run constantly. We were lucky enough to have Emma (dk last name) a life long Londoner as our guide. She was extremely knowledgeable and witty. I highly recommend sitting on the top tier to get the best views. London was beautiful, but Emma made the tour that much better.

My girlfriend and I were visiting London from the United States on vacation the first week of the new year and really, really loved the big bus tour. We sat on the top deck to increase the quality of the views, but it was super cold (mid winter, so duh). Funny thing, though, the live commentary by our guide, Lewis, was so amazing and good natured and funny that we didn’t even notice the cold. Spent the whole ride getting good information and laughing our *sses off. Seriously, so good.

Thanks, Lewis!

This is a brilliant way to see all the sights of London. I opted to go all around the red route to see what I wanted to hop on and off at. St Pauls cathedral was my favourite stop. Our guide Liam was very informative, entertaining and funny. I shall be using them again when I hope to try the other routes available.

This is concerning the hop on hop off bus tour attended on the 03/11/18. I appreciated the Hindi function for the audio commentary so my parents could understand and appreciate London's rich culture and history.

The guide on the red tour was pleasant and was helpful. However, there was one incident that did slightly annoy me. At Westminster, the tour guide told us to get off at this stop,to get the green line so we could get back to Marblearch. My Dad and I started to get ready to get off, with the tour guide stating "Don't just sit there, get off" in an exasperated tone, maybe unaware that my Dad is an elderly gentleman, who uses a walking stick and has arthritis in both his legs. This really ruined my experience that someone could be quite rude. People have varying physical abilities and this should be appreciated.

There was a demonstration going on and they had no plan. We ended up walking from point to to point with Big Bus employees laughing at us and poiting us in random directions with no service. After having picked it up at stop 14, taking it to Buckingham, we were never able to find another bus to board even though we asked 5 Big Bus employees along the way. Absolutely DO NOT book with this company. It is apparently run by 3rd graders and a bunch of employees who think it's funny they ruined your entire plan for the day. Great vacation guys... really upsetting.
We had a short tour with Jojo. She was wonderful, very personable, and helpful. I wish we had been on her bus longer.

Had a good time riding around the city and learning about the history. Comes with a boat ride, but there were not instructions on how to use it. I was hoping to catch a ride back on it, but apparently you need to get a separate ticket, and there are only certain locations you can get said ticket (they cannot do it on the bus). I was left stranded at the boat station with no way to get a ticket. This was a massive inconvenience.
We had a live commentary by Emma on the Red Line on a Hop-On-Hop-Off tour. She was full of interesting facts and a lot of fun as well.

As it was our first trip to London, we decided to do a hop on/off tour. It was a great way to see the city and use it for getting from one place to another. A water cruise is included, but we didn't end up using it. I think the ride can be better or worse depending on your tour guide. I had one fantastic guide who was funny and told us tons of things, one guide who was pretty good, and one who didn't talk a lot, and then at one point (it was close to the end of the day) he just left and never even said he was done talking! If you think you don't have a great guide, hop off and then get back on again a different bus! Overall we enjoyed it, but it did get very crowded and if you can't be on the top deck it's not as enjoyable because you can't see as much.

Great experience on Big Bus. Have done many of these tours generally with head phones but today we had a guide - Emma who made our day. She did a wonderful job of making it all feel so personal. Highly recommend this company

Big Bus most likely have the best sales people but the worst product. We had to watch competitor busses pass by with plenty of available seats to wait for Big Bus over crowded. It’s the same product, same price so don’t choose this company!

This was a great way to see London and we regret not doing this on our first trip several years ago. We took our teenage daughter, but it would also be suitable for much younger children. The bus accommodates strollers, wheelchairs and people with mobility issues. The driver and tour guide were polite, friendly and professional. One guide went above and beyond for a disabled man - the man had accidentally boarded the wrong tour bus, however the guide said he could stay on and he instructed the driver to help him off at the appropriate stop - this was incredibly compassionate and did not go unnoticed.
This tour company offers several routes which allows tourists to see all of London! The routes are clearly marked and the drivers were incredibly helpful and company reps were at many stops. We were able to see much more of London than we anticipated. Some buses offered a prerecorded narrative and others offered a guide who spoke English. Great tour company - we would definitely recommend it to anyone interested in seeing the sites in London. It may have been a little more expensive than some of the other hop-on hop-off tour bus companies - our hotel concierge booked our tickets so that may have elevated the price? Regardless we were pleased with the tour bus.

We did the big red bus tour on a Monday morning in September. It apparently took longer than usual because there were roadworks going on, but that didn't spoil anything. We had Ian as our commentator who was full of amazing stories and loads of jokes. Julian was our driver. He knew exactly where to slow down on our route to give us ample time to take photos. It was a very enjoyable time and I think everyone should do it at least once when in London.

We decided to spend time riding around on the Big Bus Tours so that we had a relaxing morning to recover from our jet lag but still seeing the city and being “productive.” We booked with Big Bus because of the great reviews and opportunity for a live guide and we lucked out!! Emma was amazing! She is knowledgeable, exciting and excited about her city, easy to understand, and obviously has a true and clear knowledge of the history of London. Emma: if you are reading this with your tea in the morning, thank you for the energy you bring to your groups — I know it can’t be easy doing it day after day, but for once it was only once and you made it worth it 💜 we feel so lucky to have been on your bus!!! Thank you!!!!

6 sept 2018. unplanned trip to London. Took a chance with hop on/off tour.. Very impressed with cleanliness of buses, presentation of staff and all round friendliness of service. Darren/Daniel did the talk on red tour ,10 out of 10. we covered a good few locations and the free boat cruise at the end was an added bonus.no problem recommending for the future.

My 5 girlfriends and I took the 2-day option (highly recommended if you have time...there is too much to stop and see all in one day). Our very first ride started with Emma from the Green Park location. She was kind, funny, and spoke very clear English. Emma had some great information about local attractions that only a local living there would know; she provided knowledge that was not in a history book or program you can buy off the street. I wish we knew how to find her the next day. She was amazing. Unfortunately, we had one bus without a tour guide (but there is an audio recording you can hear in a variety of languages that proved informative) and we had another bus with a tour guide on day 2 (Tim) who believed he knew everything- but the young gentleman bus driver that drove the bus was very nice and knowledgeable. However, Tim was quite unhappy when my friends wanted to get off to shop in SoHo, wouldn't relay the message on which stop to tell my friends that I asked him to from the bottom floor of the bus (he was on the top floor) and began to get upset with my friends to the point my friends believe he was yelling at them. All in all, I would happily take this excursion again- just know when to listen to your wonderful Tour Guide (Emma!!) and know when to listen to a prerecorded message.

We bought 2 day hop on/off - we used the red line extensively and thoroughly enjoyed the live commentaries. The red line for 2 days was worth the money on its own. At each stop we were met and guided by helpful big bus reps. We used the other lines less, although we did move between them, they were good but had recorded commentary and the attractions not quite as exciting.

On top of this there is a night time tour included with the 2 day pass - which is about 2 hours seeing the sights all lit up at night. Very popular and only has 3 departure times so queue early to get up top.

The included free walking tours change depending on the day you go (if it’s a day that changing of the guard is happening or not)

And if that wasn’t enough, with the 2 day pass, use of the city river cruises to go from Greenwich (if you choose) to west minister or tower pier is included along with hilarious (not sure how accurate) live commentary by “the crew” - as many times as you want (1 day tickets only get a single journey)

2 days travel around all London, separate night tour, walking tour and endless use of cruise for £39.60 (10% off the £44 when booked online)

BRILLIANT

Bus was great, when on it! We jumped on the first one we saw after collecting our bus tickets from the London Eye (note - do not book them together via the London Eye website, or you have to go there to collect the bus tickets, before you can get on one!). Anyway, jumped on, all was going well, bus was diverted away from St Paul’s, Monument, Pudding Lane etc (no explanation of why - I thought the driver just didn’t fancy it, but later bus avoided it too).

I went and spoke to the lady giving the tour about getting the boat back, and whether there was time for this before our London eye tickets. We thought there was, so she gave me directions to the pier and off we went. The boat leaves Tower Bridge every half and hour, on the hour & at half past, and they were calling last entry for the boat which looked packed as we arrived at 11.55. But they wouldn’t let us on as apparently we hadn’t got the right tickets! The tickets I had printed at the London Eye said “Big Bus Tour - this is your ticket” across the top, but apparently as it doesn’t actually say “river cruise” that doesn’t count, and they refused to let us on. They said they don’t get paid for it unless we give them the correct ticket. So this meant dragging all 11 of our group back to the bus stop to get the bus round the rest of the tour instead. The bus then went the exact same way back as we had already been diverted, so we saw all the same sights and heard all the same commentary again. By the time the bus arrived (we waited at least 20 minutes) we were already late for our London Eye slot. It was extremely stressful, but we needn’t have worried - the London Eye staff didn’t even look at our time slot, and just told us to join the ENORMOUS queue. 2 of our group did that, the rest went to Macdonalds, where the queue for food and the toilets were both also approx 1/2 an hour long. We only just made it back in time to board the London Eye, as the queue (which stretched a very long way) did move surprisingly fast. We boarded the London Eye and ate our food at approx 2pm (time slot was 12.45). If I could do this again I would have got tickets to display on the phone so we could have got on a big bus at any point, and I would have made sure the first Big Bus person standing by the bus, or the tour guide herself, had given us the boat tickets (I was given them later, but that was pointless!). The boat pier is right under the London Eye, so the boat we missed would have got us there 15 minutes early! Although London Eye tickets say to get there 30 minutes before your slot (presumably to allow time for standing in their massive queue!).

After the London Eye we continued on the red line to Buckingham Palace, walked to Hyde Park Corner and got on the blue line, which took us to Kensington Palace, and near where we had parked our car at work. We did have to sit downstairs on one bus, and migrated up when a load of people got off.

I enjoyed the commentary (both live and recorded) but have marked it down because of the nightmare boat making us late issue - and that was all a result of the bus tour staff not telling us we had to get a different ticket. The boat staff said “this always happens - they are meant to give you a proper ticket”. I’m sure if we’d known to ask they would have, but I didn’t see that on any documentation / info from them.

Good luck!

We bought a ticket on Big bus a Tuesday in July. We thought that it was a good way to see a lot of interesting sights in London. What we experienced was not what we expected. Often when we entered the bus there were no seats so we had to stand without any guide as the connection was occupied by those seated. Also due to heavy traffic it was a very slow way of getting around, so it took a major part of the day queuing at bus stops and standing on a bus in a traffic jam.
The day was a major disappointment and I recommend anyone that want to see London to decide what you want to see and use the underground instead, anyway during the busy time of the year.

I would highly recommend this travel when you first hit London, there are 3 different routes to choose from (we did the 3 eventually). Just relax and enjoy the whole trip then if you want, stay on again and hop off on the Sites you want to explore. We purchased the Tickets from Home, but it was just as easy to buy them at the No. 1 Bus Stop.

We picked up the Big Bus tour from outside Tower Bridge. We chose the red route purely by chance but it was great as it allowed us to see all of the sights in London. Our tour guide Joanne was amazing and so knowledgeable. She was really funny when she was explaining about the sights and giving us some history. She really knew her stuff and she seemed like a real born and bred Londoner not just because of her strong cockney accent but because you could really tell she loved the city. Unfortunately she left us at Marble Arch and another guy took over. Unfortunately he was just nowhere near as animated or knowledgeable as Joanne. There were a couple from Oregon sitting near where he was and that was it, we had lost him for the rest of the journey which was such a shame. We went past some of London's most iconic landmarks and he was too busy asking the couple from Oregon how much rain they had there. You can use headphones on the tour so you can listen to the commentary and whilst we listened intently when Joanne was speaking, we switched off when the new guy came on as he just didn't say anything! We could hear his muffled conversation with the couple near him about the weather, the culture and the length of time it takes to get there. Such a shame as it is not cheap to use this service as it cost us £36 per person so we felt a bit short changed for the second part of our journey. Only saving grace was when we got off the bus, we were told we could use our tickets for the River Cruise the next day. All in all, great first commentary, not so great second commentary.

Visited London today to show Canadian friends around. 6 people cost £150 for a day ticket around city of London. Long ques to catch buses meant waiting times of 30 to 40 minutes only to be sat inside a stifling bus as no room on the open deck on top. Battling London traffic to get nowhere fast means you spend most of the the day either waiting for a bus or sat on a bus as opposed to at the attractions. In 8 hours we got to see Buckingham Palace, Thanes River Cruise and the London Eye. Had we caught the tube between places we would have saved £80 and had much more time to go to other attractions.
Also if you buy a London Eye "fast track" ticket for the London Eye from the Hop On Hop Off staff you still must go i to the ticket office at the London Eye itself to change your paper stubs into actual tickets which can take up to 30 mins to do. Having changed your "Fast Track" stubs i to tickets you then get given a time that you cant join the line before. All in all our fast track ticket required us to wait 1 1/2 hours! Not somfast track after all.
The final nail in the coffin was a bad tempered hop on hop off bus attendant being what can only be described as rude in his answering to simple questions from passengers as to how to get to different locations. He did not have a name badge on otherwise I would have made an official complaint.
All in all, paln where you wNt to go, catch the tube and save yourself time and money to see more during your time in London

Our family of four, has taken Hop-On-Hop-Off Tours in other European cities and enjoyed the experience so we knew this would be part of our London trip. A staff member at our hotel told us not to miss the Red Line because it has live commentary. There's nothing wrong with recorded commentary but Live with Chris and Len really put the tour over the top! Quick wit and the Q & A with Chris made it feel like a family friend was showing you around London.

Booked the two day "premium" tour. "Enjoy free WiFi on our busses" - there is no WiFi whatsoever. "Use our app it's great" - doesn't work and if you use it without the promised WiFi it is a heavy hit on your mobile data. "Use the blue tour, you get info on everything via headphones in 12 languages" - had to change seats 4 times to have working headphone jacks. With four people in our party and in the end always two sharing one set of headphones, out of at least 16 tried only 2 worked. So, as far as we are concerned, not worth the money.

I was excited to see London via a tour as I had previously done in ever other country! Only to discover an app that does not work, a lazy tour guide who kept telling us it’s her second day! Who cares? Buses that never ever arrive at their stops, the only nice thing where the drivers! Waste of money, waste of time , really do not use this tour, walk around on your own better way to see London! 0/10

We should have taken the Original Tour instead. The staff at Big Bus Tours Kondon are rude. Had an extremely disappointing start to our tour from the customer service point of view. It just went downhill from there. Buses are very slow in coming between stops. Everywhere we waited for our bus we would see several Original Tour buses pass by. They had more staff on the ground with friendlier attitude. We bought the 24 hour pass for our family as the first activity of our London holiday and it just gave the worst possible start to our sight seeing. Do not go for Big Bus .

The map on the leaflet was wrong. I think the app didn’t update to the new map as well. And the London traffic is horrible so most of the time I was stuck on the bus.
My plan that day was just ruined.

Have done these elsewhere and enjoyed and very effective way to see a big city. Certainly NOT the case in london. To much traffic makes them ridiculously slow, poor maps are very hard to follow and stops often not well located. Plus rubbish views because bus overcrowded. We literally could walk it faster and in more comfortable and that is what we mostly ended up doing yesterday.
Very bad , waiting for more than 1 he , still waiting, waste of time and money. Blaming it on an accident, but all other tour buses don’t seem to have an issue, would not recommend s

We had a great tour guide day one, but had trouble finding stops. Once we figured out after we left London you could download an application from the App Store it was easy to find stops that we had not gone by or gotten off at.

My wife and I normally take a hop on hop off bus tour when we arrive in a new city, to get an overview of the city and to get our bearing on areas we want to explore. We did this in London and soon realized we had made a big mistake. The streets in London twist and turn and traffic is horrible, with every intersection a bottle neck. The tour was advertised as being 3 hours, after 3 1/2 hours we got off of the bus because we spent most of the time just sitting in traffic. The driver was skipping many of the important sites being mentioned in the narration and we were little more than 1/2 way through the tour.

Went with this company since it was included in the London Pass we bought from Costco. Live guide was good. We hopped off and when we tried to get back on later in Trafalgar Square we could not find a bus. We waited for about 30 minutes to find one at the designated spot across from Canadian embassy but no bus came. We asked two vendors who sold Big Bus passes where to catch the bus and were directed to two different places...still no bus arrived at either place. We ended up taking the tube. If you take this tour, enjoy the live guide and stay on for a full loop. Don't hop off!

Using the bus was an ideal option to see as much as possible. We were told that our ticket was valid for 24hrs from the time we hopped on. We were dissapointed we we ventured into Harrods maze of boutiques and spent more time than expected. We waited outside of Harrods from 18:45 to 20:00 and not a single bus in sight. I approached another bus driver and was told that they were done for the day. We ended up taking a cab back to our hotel. The communication around schedules and times was not clearly communicated on the brochures.was rather dissapointing!

Went for sightseeing today, but this was not good. Like the idea and concept, and been doing this in several cities and London earlier. But London traffic makes this almost impossible. Too slow, takes way too much time. Sorry, but will not recommend this.

Never even made it onto a bus, watched 4 or more pass me by, or not even stop long enough for me to catch one. I can’t run, and there was little or no guidance on where to pick the bus up. I would not bother with this company. Tried calling several times and no one picks up, you just end up in a forever queue... Don’t do it! I am pretty pissed.

This was my first trip to London, we decided to get on the hop on hop off bus which was a fantastic choice, the bus stops at all major landmarks and the guides are entertaining and insightful. I would recommend this to anyone visiting London.

Only problem with routes was trying to figure out which direction the bus was going so not to repeat same route 3 times. Very negative review for last ride of the second day (Apr 8) when driver was well over the speed limit to finish his day and we had to hang on or be thrown around.

We hopped on the big bus tour at St Paul's cathedral and were told that the last stop would be Green Park. On board was Faye, our lovely and knowledgeable tour guide with our driver Josh. Faye made the trip very worthwhile as her commentaries were very informative. She practically knew every landmark along the route and gave us a mobile history lesson! To top it off, we got off at the last stop and struggled to flag down a taxi and guess who came to the rescue? Faye, our lovely tour guide ofcourse with good advice as to where to flag down a taxi. She crossed the road with us and showed us where to stand. Thank you Faye for being so friendly and helpful.
Buses were frequent and clean, and our guide commentators were friendly and informative. Always our favorite way to get oriented in a new city.
Me and my brother took the tour and it was a good experience to travel through the London streets and enjoy the rich and historical artichect of the city... recommended for first time traveller...

This trip was very well done. When I arrived at the train station and saw the bus stop for Big Bus tours I managed to get a ticket immediately and get on the next bus, which came 5 minutes later. It stopped at important sites after giving some really interesting information in an engaging way. I sat on the top deck of the bus, which also had audio guides and a better view! The drivers were very good, even when another bus reversed into us - the bus driver managed to get us onto the next Big Bus going past (literally right behind us). The next driver I had drove me back to my train station at night (very helpful for a young woman), even though it was another 5-10 minute drive to get there and I was the last person on the bus. Very good service, great insightful information and a lot of fun! Highly recommended!

This tour was so confusing to navigate, the blue route didn't seem to follow the map the provided at all. The recorded guide on the blue tour was out of sync with what we were seeing. By the time they talked about it we had already passed it. It also didn't give much information about landmarks etc. Mainly a lot of useless trivia facts and anecdotes that were barely connected with the place they were talking about. However, Robert on the red tour was very knowledgeable and funny! Quite enjoyed his section of the tour, the only part we enjoyed!

We did the bus tour for one day of sightseeing. It was worth the money and it includes the River boat in the price. We did the red line which includes a live tour guide (the others are taped) and Robert was not only knowledgeable, he was very funny. It's worth using if you're not sure where to spend your time as you can see the attractions and get off and use it throughout the day to hop on and move on to another location.

We chose this tour because we had a short time in London. Unfortunately, during the winter, buses are infrequent and we spent a lot of time either waiting for buses or waiting at stops for the bus to move on (Nearly half an hour near the Wax Museum). When we got on, we found that the canned narrative on the earphones was not properly in sync with the route. As a result, we were looking for sites after we had already passed them. We went gone on the included Thames cruise (short but enjoyable, with an actual human being to point out places of interest). Be aware, by the way, that the Thames cruise is a one way trip. You have to rejoin the buses at the Tower of London where we waited nearly another half hour for the next bus. That bus had an actual live tour guide, quite knowledgeable and with an excellent narrative. Sadly we got on at the end of his shift and by the time we were joined by another guide, we had to head back for our flight out (we had a long layover). Be prepared to spend time in the rain and cold if you choose to hop off. I felt as if a huge chunk of my time was wasted in waiting.

Had an amazing ride..just found the business card 9 months later and it made such an impression I had to write a review. Pete A was fantastic. Great sense of humour and super engaging. Loved every minute and saw the sights

We booked a two day premium package specifically to do the river cruise between Westminster and Greenwich. Both days we arrive at the pier asking for that particular boat and are directed to the boarding area by seemingly competent staff. Once on the boat however announcements are made that the boat will only be going part of the way (to Tower Bridge) and that there are no further cruises all the way to Greenwich. As international media in London on a content creation trip I can recommend the bus tour component but will definitely discourage the boat component due to these annoying and very disappointing operational errors. It is the apparent highlight of the package but not done properly you have ruined the entire experience!

We have enjoyed the hop on hop off bus in many European cities - this is the worst
The length of time sitting at a pick-up place is extensive, the routes are convoluted and it just not helpful in any way. Wait time at designated places for buses is not acceptable.
The first time we used this service was in July and we thought the pour service was because of huge crowds. We just used it again in October - not any better. For the price of the day ticket you would be much better to just hail a taxi! Our advice: never ever spend money on this experience!

We got the two day family ticket (pennies of £100) planning to use it to get to specific attractions as well as touring the route to see a bit more.
We picked it up without any problem then spent an hour getting from Covent Garden to the Tower of London. In fairness they can't be blamed for bad traffic... but they could do more to tell you interesting things about the places you are stuck.
After visiting the tower we got the boat up to Westminster Bridge. This was the best (and really the only good) part of the whole experience. We had planned to have a quick walk around the Houses of Parliament and Westminster Abbey before picking up the bus again at the clearly marked bust stop situated on the road between the two. When we got there we discovered that they had closed that bus stop. It said nothing about this on the paper map nor on the 'live' map on the app, which told us that a bus was due there soon!
So we walked our tired children round the route to the next bust top... only to discover that this one was ALSO closed without warning. By this time we were starting to worry that we might miss the chance even just to use the bus to get back to our hotel so we were glad when, at the third bus stop we saw one sitting there.... but it was out of service and the surly driver pointed us to a bus stop on the other side of the road, some distance back that wasn't marked as one for Big Bus Tours. Fortunately we did mamage to get back to the hotel... ut without seeing much of London on the bus.
The floowing day we declined to use the tour to go anywhere in case we got stranded in another 'dead zone' and missed our train home so we walked around Covent Garden adn then tried to take the Big Bus back to the train station. Guess what? The bus stop was closed without warning.
This is definitely the worst sight-seeing experience we have ever had and we will never use this company in any city ever again. Such a huge waste of money.

Decided to purchase this tour due to the ads placed by the London eye tour. Touted as the #1 bus tour company.
It was the #1 bus tour company for poor customer relations, infrequent buses, no maps /headsets given on the first bus we jumped on.
At the first stop by the London eye we waited approximately 40 minutes before the bus showed up , then at the stop near Harrods , the bus driver said we needed to change buses because this one was no longer in service . We then had to wait another 45 minutes before the next big bus showed up. However open tours buses and golden bus tour both had multiple buses pass us waiting on big bus.
Also there were multiple big bus with signs saying "not in service"
The big bus then shut off service at 5:30 pm and we had to take a taxi back to the main attraction area (London eye). No communication from the bus driver that the buses were stopping at 5:30.
Don't waste your time and money on Big bus tours/

We had two days in London so we booked with big bus tours so we could make the most of our time.
Unfortunately we spent most of the time waiting for the busses to turn up and what made it worse was rival bus company busses were arriving at a very frequent rate.
Other people with 'big bus tours' were complaining as many had been waiting longer than us. One couple had been waiting over 1 and 1/4 hours on a route that is supposed to be serviced every 15-20 minutes.
I understand the traffic can delay things but all the companies have the same issues . One company had 10 of there busses turn up at one stop and we still hadn't seen one of 'big bus tours' busses.
Very disappointing

Hubby and I were recently in London for our first time-ever there and at the recommendation of our tour guide rep (Trafalgar tours), we did the Big Bus 48 hour package for hop-on, hop off. We did both the red route and the blue route initially and each of those routes were fine as far as the sight-seeing and guides were concerned. But in making our connections back to where we needed to be from the Marble Arch, is where Big Bus definitely lacked. On 2 separate occasions, we waited a long time - 20-30 min for the blue west route and on the 2nd occasion, it just never appeared and we ended up having to take the subway. On both of those occasions, I kept asking the reps there when the bus would be arriving and I kept getting the brush off - one young man was rude enough to nod in the direction of his supervisor and actually told me to "ask him yourself - I already did". On both of these occasions, I had noted that the reps seemed more interested in counting their money than engaging with the paying customers and offering decent customer service.

And a third example of poor customer service - we had been at the Tower of London and wanted to take advantage of the River Thames cruise that was part of our package. We finally found the bus stop and asked the rep there where we needed to go to do the cruise. He simply nodded down the street and said go down there and turn left. Well that seemed very vague and useless to me so I pushed him for some actual directions and all he said was to keep going until the street ended. Turned out the street kept going much further and we ended up standing on a street corner for 5-6 min trying to get our bearings and figuring out where we needed to go. Again, he had been counting his revenues and wasn't at all interested in being helpful to a tourist who obviously needed help.

Overall, I would not recommend Big Bus tours, mainly for their lack of good customer service.

This is not my first review of big bus tours , we ve used before this year.

Returned to London with my parents , long story short my dad can not walk huge distances ( much to his annoyance ) so the bus tours are ideal .

We were only in London for two days , arriving weds afternoon . We purchased our tickets at Euston , but didn't activate until around 5pm staring in the red route , which has a live tour guide. We had a very nice lady guide briefly , then there was a changeover as her shift had ended.
Our new guide was Nobby , a lovely guy who took us around the tour with lots of interesting information , particularly about the river Thames , the creation of the embankments , how the sanitation system had progressed etc , also lots of snippets of his own observations about the city over the years . Really enjoyed it and my dad who loves hearing historical information loved it !!

Day two we used the ticket for a river cruise ( included in the bus price ) and this was also great - we had been so lucky with the weather , it was glorious , so a nice way to see things from another perspective. This I believe is operated by city cruises - the boat was pretty big with open upper deck . Again guide was great - I'm not sure of his name , so apologies but all credit to him ( this was Thursday afternoon from Westminster pier, he was at a guess late twenties early thirties , fair hair and suntanned ) he gave a live commentary along the Thames pointing out both historical sites and general interest, also pointing out great places for eating and drinking for families .

We got off at tower bridge and then picked up a blue route bus , which was an audio tour but have to say that was Also enjoyable and informative .

Personally I think that the tours cover a lot more ground than is possible on foot during a short trip , and if you want to hop on and off they re so regular it's easy !!

Let me start by saying I read many of the reviews and tried to learn as much as I could about this tour. I had a great experience because I was prepared and knew what to expect and what to do.

First, I ordered my tickets online. I paid €31.50 per person. When I went to the loading area, one of the guys on the sidewalk said he would have sold them to me for €30 and said because my daughter was cute, maybe €28. Not a big difference! This was for a 1 day pass. My goal was to get a good overview of the main London spots that would be good to visit later. This tour also came with a one-way City Cruise trip. It met my objective. I only rode the Red Line because it is the only line that offers a live tour guide on the bus.

Second, my daughter downloaded the app for this company. It tracks all lines of the company, blue, red, and green. And shows you where each bus is at, so you can track if one is near and how long it will take to get to you.

I really enjoyed this tour. Each guide was informative with their distinct style. They were helpful and engaging. They wanted us to ask questions and seemed eager to answer them. I have no complaints and only compliments for my experience.

Not well organized, there were no representatives at each stop, so if you purchased you tickets online you could not validate them when you got on the bus. The driver did not explain that validation could only be done at 3 stops or which stops they were. When we got to the Tower of London, where we could get on the boat tour, we could not get on the boat, because our tickets were not validated, so we had to walk back to the bus stop and get them validated.

During our stay in London there were some road closures, so the busses had to rerouted. The problem was that the drivers had no idea where the detours were, could not help us figure out which stop were in the closure area. We ended up wondering around London trying to guess which stop will be actually serviced. When we finally found a stop ( which by the way are not very clearly marked). All the stops are at the regular London Bus stops - the stop we found was at a building that had scaffolding around it so we - no indication that the bus would not stop there. Al the London busses were stoking there, however the big Bus did not stop - we missed 2 busses until I had to wave the bus down. The driver stopped but said to me that because of scaffolding busses would not be stopping there and we should not have been waiting there. How would I know that! It seemed like all the other busses were stopping. The Bus did not stop at every stop or if it did you had to run for the exit, because the drivers did not stop long enough.

This was not a good experience and considering I bought the 3 day deluxe ticket a real waste of my money. I used Big Red Bus in Paris during the same trip and it was great, but in London it was a disaster.

This was my second time on the Big Bus tour- the first was in September of 2015; the second time was last week. Here are my suggestions: 1) buy a one-day ticket (more on that later) 2) start out as early in the day as you can manage; 3) if you are picking up the bus on the route and not at an obvious tourist stop, make sure you check the website and get as much info re: where the actual stop is located -- we luckily found the Big Bus Gloucester Road bus stop but it's a big intersection and the buses don't necessarily share the same stops; 4) know that taking the bus is slowwww- London traffic is tough, even on a bank holiday, and it took us 3 hours to cover 2/3 of the route- we finally got off at the Tower of London stop- we were done sitting at that point- and took the Big Bus free cruise down the Thames to Westminster Bridge. (That was fun!) Then we got back on the bus and headed back to our hotel in Kensington (with one detour to Harrods which was on the way.)
5) Make sure you check the forecast and bring a hat and wear sunscreen if you want to be in the open air- it can get pretty hot up there.
(I was originally going to buy a 2-day pass but it is a pretty lethargic way of getting around- would recommend saving the cost of a 2-day ticket and use that toward an Oyster card for the Tube- trains come frequently and you can get around easily and cheaply once you get oriented. And there are a number of free London Underground apps that I had downloaded which ended up being very helpful,)
General consensus: Big Bus was a great way to get a scenic overview of London and start the trip.

We got to London late afternoon and chose to take the Bib Bus Tour. We had a live tour and our guide was excellent. She was fun, informative and added tons of tidbits that were fun. Because we bought the ticket late afternoon, we were able to use the Big Bus the next day too. I would not recommend using it for transportation. The Oyster was much more efficient for that. The second day when jet lag kicked in we were happy to have the passive activity to just see the city. We would use it again. We don't know how it compares to other bus tours but we did use it when we went to Paris and enjoyed it there too.

We lost an hour of our precious sight-seeing time to begin with because the stop we chose to start at was no longer in use. Strangely, it is on the map Golden Tour gives out when you pick up your tickets, and there is also a Golden Tour sign at the stop. After 3 families had waited for over a half hour for a bus that should have been coming every 15 minutes, we called the company to find out what the problem was. That's when we were told it was no longer a stop they used. The nearest stop required us to back-track, losing another half hour.

The first time we got off the bus and then were ready to get back on, we found ourselves waiting a long time for a blue line bus and finally ended up taking a red line bus (5 of which had stopped while waiting for the blue line bus).

The live tour guide on the first bus we were on was okay but did not give much narration overall. The pre-recorded narration on the buses without tour guides was not very captivating. A lot of time was spent waiting in traffic. At the end of the day we wished we had taken the advice given to us before we came to London--just choose sites you want to see and take the tube to them--a much more efficient way to see London.

The Big Bus Tour was wonderful! We got to see so much in just one day although you can purchase a two day pass if you're interested( and it's a great deal). The tour also offered a City Cruise down the Thames River which was a great additive. If you're interested in touring the locations that the bus stops at the also offer discounted tickets. The only downside was that we stopped at Madame Toussad's for close to a half an hour and we weren't sure what was going on. Overall it was a great tour.

I booked with big bus at the recommendation of our trafalgar tour guide. I told them that I wanted to see the Tower of London and the London Eye and they sold me vouchers for both. Little did I know that it would be about 2 hours to Tower of London and by the time I was through I had to take the Tube instead to the London Eye but unfortunately they stopped selling tickets at 4 pm and would not honor my voucher ( which was a fast pass). It took me awhile to locate a Big Bus rep and almost an hour for home to arrange a credit which hopefully I will see when I get back home. Additionally they never told me that I had to redeem the voucher for the river cruise with them and I only found out when I went to the dock that they were supposed to give me the ticket. I was unable to find the rep before I had to go and try to make it to the London Eye which ended up unsuccessful as well. They should have told me to do the London Eye first and had given me a better assessment on how to manage the time. The tour is only useful if you don't care about leaving the bus at sites and just want a bus view of the city. For me it was a waste of a vacation day ( only in London 2 days) and I would have been better served by taking the tube to the various sites. Now I only hope the refund for 32 pounds ( for the Eye)come through without a hassle

So many options for the London Bus tour, we opted for the Big Bus, based on reviews. Booked the tickets online. produced the email receipt at the bus stop and received the actual ticket. The tour was fabulous, certainly the best way to see London. The bus es were clean and the audio commentary great. (Note the longest route is the Blue route, audio commentary only. The Red route had onboard commentators)

Great way to see the city!! We went to London with no plans, no itinerary and no knowledge what so ever of the city. The bus tour was the best way to see many of the sights of London and familiarize ourselves with the city. Very convenient and lots of buses if you decided to hop on and off. Commentator was very knowledgeable and helpful.

Found a brochure for Big Bus Tours on a Sunday and decided that we would go on it. Got to London on Tuesday morning at Paddington Station. Walked outside and found the representative for Big Bus Tours. Bought our tickets (35 Pounds) and discounted tickets for the Tower of London (Normally 28 - paid 17). Tour started off good, bus arrived quickly. Rep told us buses are at the stops every 5 - 10 minutes on the blue/red routes. Got off the bus at Piccadilly Circus, walked around a bit and got back on the next bus. We wanted to go to Kings Cross to see Platform 9 3/4 from the Harry Potter movies. That was a mistake switching to the green route. First the rep told us that the bus would be there in 10 - 15 minutes (we ask how often the buses stop - every 20 minutes); 25 minutes later the bus finally arrives. We get on, go two stops and are told this bus is stopping at this time and we need to get on the bus that is waiting there already and it will leave in 15 minutes. What??? Two buses are now standing there not going anywhere. We wait for 20 minutes and the bus finally leaves, we get to Kings Cross and ask the driver how often the buses stop. He tells us every 30 minutes. After our visit to Platform 9 3/4 we get back on the bus and go to the stop where we can get back on the blue/red route. Finally get to the Tower of London, the rep tells us that the last river cruise leaves at 6:05. That gave us plenty of time to tour the castle (closed at 5:30) and make it to the boat. We asked (just in case we got done earlier) how often do boats leave; the rep told us every 30 minutes. We enjoy our time at the castle, decide to go ahead and get on an earlier river cruise. Should be leaving at 5:35, get down to the dock at 5:25. A rep for City Cruise tells us that the boat that is leaving is the last boat and it leaves everyday at 5:20. The final thing is that there where no more buses to take us back. We saw the last bus at the stop as we were leaving the dock area. So you can see why we were so we so disappointed, everyone kept telling us different times for everything. The same company and no one knows what is going on.
