That was our last day in London so it was a big waste of money. You need at least two maybe even three days to do the bus tour and enjoy the sites (getting off the bus). If you have only one day and don't want to tour everything just see it, then stay on the bus and drive around, it will take you a good part of the day to drive the complete blue route, (red route is shorter). We ended up getting tickets to go on the tubes to get back to Paddington Station. I could have planned a trip going on the tubes better than using the Big Bus tours, at least the trains times are reliable.

I would have given this tour 4-5 stars if they would have given me the info I needed. I picked up one of the last buses of the day, heading back to the region of my hotel. I could have walked from there, but, since the bus came, I took it. No info was given when I got on. After about a 20 minute trip ending quite far from where I started (and farther from my destination) the bus suddenly parked and ended its trip. I was told this was the end and I could take public transport back. Well, that was a surprise to say the least. I went where I was directed only to find the buses don't take cash. I was stuck, now 5 miles from my destination rather than 2. I was saved by a lovely couple who helped me out. I'm not one to complain, but forewarning would have prevented this review. Stay away from Big Bus Tours in London near the end of the day. You might not get where you want to go!

We took the hop on hop off Big Bus Tour on our first visit to London. It was an excellent way to get oriented to the city and see the sites. The pass is valid for the entire day and so we decided to take a complete circle first on the bus (about 1.5 -2 hours, depending on traffic) and then started the hop on hop off for the day. The audio narration was quite good and easy to follow. Note though, even though we had visited London in July, the weather was still quite mild and there was a chill in the morning air - so do carry a jacket with you if you plan to sit on the upper deck (which of course has better views) of the Big Bus Tour.

If you speak English take the red tour with the always-amusing live guide. If you're quick enough, grab a seat on top in the front for unparalleled views of London street life. The tour is a wonderful way to place all the landmarks in geographic perspective. You can hop off at any attractions where you want to spend time. Be sure to go early enough in the day so that your favorite stops don't close before you get there. Our tour included a 20 minute cruise up the Thames which was fun, cold but fun.

We purchased a 2 day pass with big bus tours when we arrived and St Pancras station.St Pancras must be affiliated with BB tours as we also purchased Oyster cards to ride the bus and tube.

In hindsite after having to use the tube as the hop on hop off service ended early in winter, we would buy a one day pass and use the underground and normal public transport to get around. It is much more efficient.

For 2 adults and one child it was roughly 65 pounds. 91 including 2 Oyster cards and 15 pounds of credit.

Our first impressions with B B Tours were not favourable. One young British worker for BB Tours who sold tickets at the Tower station pick up was more interested in "tuning" the female tourists arriving, he even put the "attractive" ones on a different tour bus company possibly to win favour. In the mean time we had 2 buses from the red and blue bus services arrive and depart before our bus finally arrived

The BB Tour Bus took ages to arrive, 40 minutes not the 20 advertised. During winter the service stops quite early so have your Oyster cards handy as a back up.

The tour itself was entertaining. The tour guides we had were fantastic, I couldn't stop laughing with either of them. One British bus driver working for the Big Bus Tour company was so helpful, he saved us a huge amount of time and went out of his way giving me advice on how to manage my time better when deciding between Harrods or the museums.

In summary shop around. I feel BB tours are a great way of seeing the sights and deciding what to go and see, use the tube or walk once you've got the lay of the land.

This was a great way to see a lot of London very quickly - there's a lot to see and not always a lot of time. We did this tour the second full day we were in London and we stayed on the bus the entire time. I looked at their schedule online and it unfortunately didn't match up to the bus that showed up. It all worked out ok, but we ended up on the blue route instead of the red. We finally got off at Oxford Street to explore that area and didn't hop back on. We decided that we'd had enough. I was a little disappointed that their schedule didn't match up and it wasn't more obvious that we were getting on the bus we actually wanted (the red line), but still very glad we did this and would recommend it to anyone who wants to make sure they see a lot of the city and still get some of the history.

Upon hopping on the bus tour, we had a staff member approach us asking if we would like to purchase discounted tickets for attractions we would pass, after an extensive conversation around this, confirming original prices and discounted prices & skip the line tickets to make sure it was worth it, we purchased the 2 tickets each after he continued to confirm they were skip the line, the London eye and London tower.
Guess what?!!!! Neither were skip the line, and after the extensive lines to work that out the first time JUST to swap the receipt he gave us for the actual ticket, we then proceeded to wait another 1 to actually get on.
After we hopped on the next bus heading towards London tower, we asked the bus driver about the tickets and he abruptly told us to find another staff member on the pavement, to which he wouldn't wait if I chose to do so.
At the stop for London tower, we approached a staff member as instructed to confirm our next tickets were in fact what we thought we had paid for. After grunting at us twice, he finally stood still and shoved a map in our face circling what he said was the information around the "skip the line" tickets we had bought, rushing us off out of his way. Imagine Our shock to find they didn't even have such a line at this particular tourist attraction.
The whole day as we took different lines and buses, I didn't come across one staff member smile! All when asked questions gave different and mostly incorrect information, so we were better off asking someone off the bus to confirm.
For all the great reviews we've heard, today was a huge let down topped with sour staff!
If people hate their jobs and tourists so much maybe they should reconsider their profession. Especially when people like ourselves try so hard, smile at everyone, have conversations, and show interest! Sad really!
I'm just annoyed I've paid for a 48 hour ticket, as the thought of spending one of my few last days in London dealing with the long faces and sour responses makes me want to crawl into a ball and hide in a dark Room instead!!!

Staying near Paddington Station, noticed that a lot of places offer Big Bus tickets sales. But went online to the official Big Bus site ( designed to trick) and saw the price of 23 Pounds per Adult with "Extra 24 hours FREE" When presented E ticket to Agent at Bus stop, he took the printed E voucher and asked if we wanted extras like Madame Tussauds tickets. When we said "no", he became even more surly and printed our tiny credit card receipt-sized "tickets" and said in an extremely sarcastic and nasty tone, "Enjoy your 4 hour tour, guys!" The next people who got on were told that they got the extra 24 hours fro free. I went to the Bus driver, as the ticket guy was obviously antagonistic, and asked about the 24 hours free ??? I was told that "Oh no, you don't get that with the "Orientation Tour" . Now if you look at the website there is no way any reasonable person would make this conclusion. And in fact Big Bus, which is a very well established company all over the world, has plenty of money to pay people to design their webpage. So there is but one way to see this - they are deliberately false advertising to fool people into this scam. I asked if we could upgrade and pay extra to get that deal and we were told NO. So we went on the tour and did as much as we could. So instead of getting 2 days we got 4 hours. It is a pure SCAM. The tour itself is fine but not worth the price if you get scammed. And I hate supporting companies that trick people. Boycott Big Bus London. Take another tour or just use city buses.

Today I bought a big bus ticket (late morning) which included an extra day plus a river cruise from tower pier to westminster. I deeply regret it as the bus went at a snails pace, stuck in heavy traffic. Took 1 hour 45 minutes to get from Oxford Circus to the Tower of London (blue line) It was hot and stifling especially downstairs, and as we were hardly moving it was also hot upstairs. When I got off at the tower of London, I asked the attendant my above predicament, that I was not enjoying the big bus experience. I asked if he could refund me the amount of money for the next day on my ticket. I was told I would not get a refund and that I could catch the boat to westminster. The attendant did not care one bit. I would recommend using one of the other bus tours like the original London bus tour or goldon yours who appeared to provide a much better service. They didn't seem to get stuck in traffic as much as big bus, have better routes, and more buses and less waiting times. I know this because about 2-3 other buses would arrive per big bus.

Very dissatisfied , having used the Golden Tours bus prior to this .
As we were at London eye we picked up ticket at booth ( no free cruise as advertised), ( no warning that not all buses had guides)no help given here at all to explain maps and alternative lines
Thankfully tour stop was nearby & got us to right stop .
Driver was not helpful in the least , asked for tickets & where we were going.
No guide, no clue where we were going , no working earphones so hopped off . Hopped on again later same " service" .
We were unceremoniously dumped off at Marble Arch , again no warning , no communication simply told by microphone it was last stop& we must transfer .
Nightmare to try to get back on , twice bus was full, after waiting for so long we headed for tube .

Such a difference from other tour, do not waste your money

Took this tour with hubby and our 2 children. We were really looking forward to seeing all the sights of London but found it disappointing and bad value. Had planned to stay on for entire tour to get a feel for everything and then hop on and off as we wished but it took so long to get around due to major traffic delays that we eventually got off after well over 2 hours (and much begging from the kids) and before we got to Buckingham Palace. Even though we had paid for a second day we couldn't persuade the kids to get back on the bus the following day. Saw Buckingham Palace later by foot. Sorry to be so negative but tour was expensive and we really did not get value for our money.

The Big Bus Tour includes a free Harry Potter Walking Tour of Central London. Our guide, Kevin, was outstanding. He is a real enthusiast, and made the film locations come alive with his amusing and well informed commentary. The tour was the highlight of a visit to London with my ten year old nephews, a magical experience!

I chose this company over others after reading reviews on TA. Glad I did! I bought the combo ticket with London eye fast track which worked out cheaper.

Many stops which meant many pick up points and I didn't feel like we stopped too much at all. I do wish that the commentary would include stop numbers as this is what's on the map they give you. Sometimes difficult to tell which stop it is.

There were many busses! Never waited more than 5 mins for a bus and it was a clear London day and as a result very busy.

All the guides were helpful. At my first stop they helped convert my qr code to a paper ticket and explained how to redeem my London eye ticket.

Another confusion is when busses are going East vs West. For a foreigner to London I was lost when the drIver asked which direction I wanted to go. Thankfully I always went the way I wanted to go. Adds to the fun!

Saw the city sightseeing branded busses as well but Big Bus was by far the most. Well worth the money.

We started our visit in London with a Hop on Hop off tour. We felt that this way we would get an idea of what there is to see and then go and explore those things in detail. We purchased our tickets at the welcome center at the airport, so they gave us 48 hours for the price of 24 and it also included unlimited City Cruise along the Thames River. We felt that it was well Worth the money we spent, but we were a little disappointed with the frequency of the buses. The Original Tour Bus had at least 3 times more busses for each one of ours. It was a bit frustrating when we were waiting at the stop and saw so many of their busses pass before ours would come. I do not know if the other bus was more expensive or not, so maybe that could be why they had more busses. It was still a worthwhile expense and we enjoyed the tour on the bus as well as along the Thames.

Having lived in London for two years, my boyfriend and I decided it would be a nice idea to spend Saturday afternoon on a tour bus. Of course, we chose one of the coldest days of the year, but sat upstairs at the front (in the uncover bit). We made sure to get the Red Route (we did accidentally get the blue bus on the Sunday which was basically 3 hours of "Land of Hope and Glory" on repeat!).
Saturday night: we had BIG STEVE, who spoke what seemed like 100 languages, and had the most detailed knowledge on just about everything that you could ever imagine! He was hilarious and had my boyfriend giggling the entire time with his corny jokes.
We will get this bus again in the future, hopefully so that we can leave Steve a big fat tip (as we didn't have any cash on us this time ;-() He is the reason Big Bug gets 5 stars.
Sunday: We got the blue bus (yeah, don't do it!) then another live Tour Guide. I can't remember the second man's name, but he was also fabulous and we learned so much!
We paid £64 but at 4pm on Saturday, so essentially, we got 3 days (48 hours until 4pm Monday) included in the price. You also get free walking tours and the river boat tour included, so if you plan your weekend effectively, it works out at very good value.

After looking at different reviews of hop on hop off buses in London these guys by far got the best reviews so I knew they were the ones we were going to book.
We booked using our phones on the day. You don’t need to print your tickets you can just show them the text message confirmation/bar code. Very handy.
The tour is £26pp and this is 24 hours plus 24 hours free. It includes a couple of walking tours (didn’t do) and the Thames river cruise. The red line is narrated and it was only by chance that we always ended up on the red line buses. The blue line goes a slightly different route and has earphones for you to use. Most of the tour guides were excellent. Only one disinterested man on one of the buses. The tour takes you to all of the major sites you will want to see. We found the service very good. I don’t think we had to wait more than 5 minutes for a bus, maybe we were just lucky!
We done the Thames cruise which is included in the price and I would highly recommend this! This was also narrated and takes you past places you can’t see from the bus. Most of the guides had interesting stories/tips and were very helpful. Would recommend using them.

Was a 5 rating with the live English commentary on two different red line busses. Got off on the cruise which was ok...just to say we cruised the Thames. Problem was trying to get back on the bus. Could not find the bus stop. Their map shows stop 21 at the pier, but maybe that's only for the cruise and we were supposed to stay on the boat and go back to the tower stop, but we thought we could get back in a bus and finish the red line tour. Walked up and down the road where the map showed the stop and nothing. Ended up seeing Big Bus tour busses turning further up the street so basically followed them to the horse guard and Whitehall stop and waiting to get on further back in the tour for stuff we had already seen. Of course nobody at those stops anymore as they're only there in the morning to sell you tickets to other attractions and in the afternoon nowhere to be seen. Was told busses ran until 6, so waited after London Eye at 5:30, gave up after 10 minutes (found out later they stop at 4:30) and not 6 so took the Waterloo tube back to the hotel. Too frustrating at the end.

I've been to London a bunch of times. I even studied at one of the London Unis for a summer term abroad and lived there. So, while I'm not new to the city, I'm no expert, either.

This visit was a short one and we had our two kids (ages 5 and 8) with us. Our first day in London was a half-day - we arrived at lunch time. Our kids moaned and whined at the walking we did (we walked from Paddington Station area south to Hyde Park, across the top of the park and down past the department stores, stopping for a late lunch at House of Fraser. You'd think we'd marched them to the sea with all the complaining we heard! We finished out the evening at Hamley's ("not more walking!") and forked over an obscene amount of money for the tube back to Paddington. That evening we were determined that the next day we'd a) see more of London and b) not listen to so much moaning. We decided that while a tube day-pass was not a bad option, none of would get to see much of London that way and we'd still be stuck walking around top-side.

We settled on a hop-on hop-off tour bus. After checking out reviews here on TripAdvisor, we went with Big Bus. We were very happy with that. We booked online and showed up mid-morning at the main stop by Hyde park just south of Marble Arch (on foot with the little whingers in tow) and waited about 15 minutes for a live-person tour. Some lines have live tour guides, some have recordings. They're color coded and if you want to listen to it, I highly recommend live over recorded. Although, if you're not an English speaker you're better off with recorded (but you're probably not reading this with me rambling on in English!). We rode the bus all through London, across the river several times, learning all kinds of fun facts and obscure trivia ranging in topics from history, architecture, pop culture, and more.

Anyway, we hopped off after crossing Tower Bridge and hoofed it half-way round the Tower of London, ate at Pret a Manger, and then jumped on the included-in-the-bus-tour-ticket river cruise boat. Yep, you can ride the river cruise as many times as you like on the day of your Big Bus ticket. So we cruised down to near Parliament and hopped back on a bus. This time, we hit up a recorded tour bus because that route took us toward the Natural History Museum, which we wanted to visit. We hopped up near Victoria & Albert Museum, walked a couple blocks, visited the museum and came back to get on the bus again. We rode back to Marble Arch around dinner time (in December at least the buses stop running at 5pm or so, or at least new routes won't start after that, the buses in service will finish out their routes).

The kids loved riding the open-top double decker buses (thank goodness we had winter coats, hats, and gloves - it was December after all). I learned a lot of things and was reminded of stuff I forgot. The kids did no complaining about walking too much(!). We all got to see the major (and plenty of more minor) sights. The kids recognized the big stuff from movies (Big Ben, London Eye, Tower Bridge) and the enjoyed the big buildings (the new ones like the Gherkin, Cheese Grater, and the Shard). The cruise was a hit with them too. We got to see most of the main London sights in one day and learned stuff, too. It's exactly what we needed for such a short visit with this age kids. Even with a longer visit, this would be helpful to get an over-view of the city and figure out where to spend more time. Buses were frequent as promised.

We have just returned from a wonderful weekend in London and used the Big Bus Tour over two days. It was very convenient and informative. But what Made our trip was our tour guide "Big Steve". A world of information on London but gave that personal touch and really made the trip for my daughters with lots of facts that would appeal to them also. He even took some great photos for us. Cheers Steve 👍

As a seasoned traveler, I know pretty much what I should expect when I go on a bus tour. The Big Bus Tours in London was "okay" for the first part of the day; truly nothing special. We arrived for our tour at the Paddington Station "bus stop". There was an attendant that issued our ticket and squirreled us into a small space to wait. The wait was a little longer than advertised, but it was a nice day, so we dealt with it. Once on the bus, we were greeted with overcrowding and had to separate to get seats. A couple of stops later that cleared up enough that we were able to get seats together. Sadly, the highlight of our day was not even on the bus, but the “free” boat ride up the Thames. This was a first class boat – probably the nicest on the river! We boarded the next bus later in the day after a ridiculously long wait! I would estimate the wait at the Tower of London to have been 45+ minutes. Other bus companies operate from the same stop, and more than 5 of one companies busses and more than 3 of another companies busses picked-up while we waited, and waited, and waited… When we finally got on the bust we realized that we would need to return to Paddington Station without getting off due to the time. When the bus arrived at the Marble Arch they began combining and reconfiguring the busses to make their final runs of the day. This was around 5:00PM. They asked each of us where we needed to go. We said Paddington Station, and they told us to remain on this bus. Others were asked to switch busses. The bus we were on was a “blue” route bus, so were know it would eventually get to Paddington (in around 12 more stops or 16 minutes if you believe their published route times). After waiting at the Marble Arch for another 15 minutes, we were on our way – we thought to Paddington Station, but apparently we were wrong. Apparently our bus had been changed to a “purple” hotel drop-off bus. Instead of continuing on the “blue” route we went along the north side of Hyde Park. The driver stopped the bus a on Hyde Park Place near the Lancaster Gate tube station and told us to get off here and walk to Paddington. Even after explaining that my fiancé was disabled and could not walk he shoo-ed us off the bus. Using my phone, I located the nearest blue bus stop on Lancaster Terrace and hoped for a bus to come along. In the meantime we looked for a taxi. Fortunately, about 20 minutes later a bus came along. This driver was compassionate and took us right to the entry to Paddington and dropped us off. He is to be commended! The rest of the drivers were not nearly as kind and friendly.
Suffice it to say, I do not recommend this tour company! They abandoned us in an unfamiliar city to fend for ourselves!

After buying an Oyster card in London, was determined to see all the attractions in London by bus. Unfortunately, if you're new to London, this could prove a bit of a challenge. This is where the Big Bus Tour was really helpful, in terms of getting an idea about the tourist spots in London in terms of geographical location, and also more information on each of these.
You can buy the Big Bus pass for 24 hours, 48 hours and also 36 hours. I did the 24 hour tour. I think there are several places you can buy the pass from - I bought mine from the visitor information center at Paddington station which is a few pounds cheaper than from the other places.
The basic idea of the Big Bus tour is that they have a fixed circuit covering the tourist spots, and you can hop on where you like, and then hop on again to the next place. The buses are quite frequent, and there are two ways for the commentary guides - one is through headphones, which I think is also available in a few languages and one is the live guide. If you're an English speaker, the live guide tour is really interesting and fun.
The bus is a double decker, with an open top, so it's a fun way to see London from above the road level - details on buildings are closer and at eye level from the upper deck .

Purchased a ticket outside Victoria station on Sunday 27 Sept. The clerk told us buses come every 5-10 minutes, however we waited for over 30. The clerk continually told us "the delays are due to traffic jams up the road, our bus is just around the corner" ..... But the other two tour bus companies operating from this stop had buses turning up continually. Finally a "big bus" turned up! Hooray, but it was the "blue" route, not the red route we wanted. Anyway we got on it and enjoyed the 5 minute journey up the road where the bus stopped for 20 minutes while the driver and commentator swapped shifts..... Not very impressed. We are a family of 6, here on holiday for a month and will not be using this company again!

I absolutely loved this tour and would recommend it. You have the option of having a live tour guide or a pre-recorded one which available in several languages. The buses run so frequent that you are literally hopping on and off between attractions and never have to wait too long. A ticket also includes a brief river tour and three different walking tours! What a great introduction to London!

This is the bus tour company that was recommended by the two hotels we stayed at in London. The hotels sell discounted tickets, so you are probably better off buying your tickets at the hotel. The first hotel we stayed at was near King's Cross/St. Pancras. None of the tour buses come up there very often.The Big Bus Tour has a green line that comes by more often than the other companies. That said, I would recommend that for whatever tour bus company you take, start at either Victoria station or The Ritz Hotel and get on there. It took me awhile to figure this out because the buses were so scarce at King's Cross, which is a busy tourist area but not on the sightseeing tours. The companies offer an extension service up to King's Cross.

The bus routes mainly go to key historic areas. We were on the Red Line and heard three guides. Ricky, an enthusiastic older gentleman, was the best. He was also the most interested in the riders. The first guide seemed quite bored. The third guide was young, but knowledgeable. Still, this was not a joke filled tour, as there is so much to see as the bus drives by quickly so the tours are mainly facts.

My family was glad we took the bus and sat on top because the perspective was so fascinating. We had walked around a lot, but we saw so much from the higher viewpoint on the bus. But it's cooler and windier up there, so be prepared.

There are at least three tour bus companies in London and the prices vary. I would wait to buy tickets in London, rather than beforehand. Look at the maps carefully to see where the tours go. Read reviews about how often some buses come by. Check out the bus tour hours. Decide if you have time for a boat ride. In the end, you may still end up taking the Underground for part of your exploring, which is less expensive, safe, and easy to use.

I am glad that we took the bus tour. We had a generally good experience. But the cost of the tickets seems rather high. The best deal is the two day ticket with boat rider.

The Big Bus is a great way to see all the sights in London, as well as hop on and off whenever you want. There are about 80 stops, though you won't hit all the stops on the same line. There are a few different bus lines, and you may be required to change lines for different attractions. The London traffic can be bad, which means the bus can't get through either...this is one of the downsides, but still the best way to see everything. The other downside is rain...while you can sit downstairs on the bus, you can't see everything well, so it takes away from the open air view on the top deck. The bus company provides live commentary on the red line or recorded commentary on the blue line. They also provide rain covers, but it's still miserable riding an open air bus in the rain. Your ticket includes a free river cruise, which is a great addition. Buses run into the evening but not into late night, so be sure to get on in plenty of time to see everything. One ticket was 28 Pounds per adult.

We had been touring the entire UK by car for 3 weeks in July/August 2015 and were pretty much exhausted..we only had one day in London while waiting for our flight and wanted to see it all! Well, this tour did not disappoint! We were able to sit on top (in spite of some drizzles) and take in every corner of London...from seeing ordinary London life in the neighborhoods to the major sites like Big Ben and Westminster Abbey, our guide Ollie knew everything about every square inch of London, including when he spotted the Duke of Westminster's blue Bentley! We couldn't have chosen a better way to spend our time and didn't want to hop off until we did the entire tour with Ollie. Not only was he informative, but he set up photo opps in advance and delivered the vast amount of London info with friendliness, humor and finesse! Thanks Ollie, and let's not forget to give a shout out to Dave the driver, too! You guys were the highlight of our day in London, you deserve a raise and the tip of a pint in gratitude for a job well done!

We spent 4-5 hours on the blue line and didn't see the entire line the traffic was so awful (Friday 11am-4pm with one quick stop for food). However, I am convinced that the driver made the traffic seem worse the "original bus tour" kept passing us so they were still moving. My husband loves bus tours (I do not share that love but have been on a number of them--in the name of compromise and this was by far the worst bus/trolley tour I have ever taken!). Seats were NOT comfortable--(I'm young and in shape--this is not something I'd normally notice enough to mention!). The audio guide was boring and superficial, it didn't sync well to the location of the bus the first 30-45 minutes it described sites we had already passed. As we sat in traffic longer it seemed to catch up as we continued to sit in traffic it repeated the same commentary because even the audio guide couldn't believe we were still sitting there. I feel like we wasted a lot of money to be stuck in traffic with uninformative audio guide with way to many advertisements and "elevator music." This is by far the worst recorded audio guide I have ever experienced, I would be shocked if any site other than the Tower of London had 4 whole sentences on the transcript of the audio guide--for the traffic they could record 2+ pages per point of interest! I wouldn't recommend this tour, I do not wish to to discuss it with the tour company, I am just thankful it is finally over! London is well known for charging a fee to drive in the high traffic areas--I truly think the traffic was from the sheer number of buses and taxis.

I chose to use big bus tours to have a look around London, I purchased a two day pass which included a night tour and river cruise. The first day I used the bus to see all the sights and not get off. The second day I got off and on at the sights I wanted to see. This was handy as the tubes were on strike.
The river cruise was nice addition, I didn't use the night tour as I had enough of the traffic of London. I would definitely recommend booking this. Staff were very helpful and friendly. Cheaper to book online.

The Big Bus Hop On-Hop Off buses are a great way to get that first overview of the London. They often provide commentary about the areas through which you are traveling, sometimes with actors who tell you the inside stories. (It was on one of these that we heard about the bombing of London during WWII and felt the pain that was still palpable for many people.) The Big Bus ticket also includes a boat trip, so you don't have to buy a separate ticket. Rain or shine (they provide ponchos), it is a fun way to see the sights.

If you haven't much time OR want an overview of London before you dive in, take the Big Bus! No, it's not the cheapest way to get around London, but it's great for getting photos and that first view into how London is laid out and the sites.

This review is for the red line big bus tour. Not the blue line. The blue line deserves a 3. However, the red line big bus tour was so much fun. The guides were very knowledgeable and funny. We had one bad guide, but theres always a bad apple, right? I am sure he knew his stuff but he was not nice so we got off and on another bus.

We have used this line in other major cities with no problem. This time, we had problems with the credit card transaction. Their fault...even though tickets printed out the employee accidentally cancelled the transaction. He got on the bus to check with his boss if it had gone through, since he was not sure, he pulled us off the bus and had us WASTE 30 minutes of paid tour time while they checked. We asked for compensation, they extended time on our tickets by 2 hours. However we leave early that day.
Also the other tours, BIG BUS, especially have more busses on the road, we would see a couple of these stop before the ORIGINAL TOUR would come around.
Check reviews before you choose a tour company!!!

My 12 year old son and I used the Big Bus Company on 27 & 28 May 2015. I purchased our tickets online before we travelled to London. Very easy to do so - the 2 day pass is great value and the River Thames trip as a free addition was a nice touch. We really enjoyed the experience. The buses run really regularly, are nice and clean and the tour guides were fantastic - and really helpful. They knew their stuff and gave a really interesting commentary that was full of interesting facts and stories that made us laugh. A great 'hop on and hop off' service that is recommended to all.

A great opportunity to get around hop on and off dependent, and coloured routes to choose from to enable you to see everything the capital has to offer. My girlfriend prebooked this as a surprise. It was an absolutely brilliant way of getting around we had stayed in Putney and used the tube to start our journey from Buckingham Palace. We sat up on the top deck on the open top bus to get a better view of the city landmarks...the weather on our visit was intermittent so if you didn't have a coat they would provide a plastic rain mack or move to a small sheltered area at the front of the bus or even back downstairs. We wrapped up luckily and enjoyed it, eventually the sun returned 😉 there is a tour guide providing audio commentary throughout the route which we found very amusing and informative, it wasn't too everyone's taste but it genuinely makes a difference. There is also an audio facility within the seats that enables multi national commentary via headphones sets. There is also a chance to take an additional river cruise which for us we didn't on this occasion but it certainly looked as though it would offer another fresh view of the sights. Needless to say it is certainly one of the great ways to get around. 😉

I've been on several hop on/off tours and loved them, but this one didn't work so well for me. I can only imagine that it was because of the large scale of the city that it covers and the limited hours of operation.

We got on at a green stop near our hotel which was very convenient and appreciated, then transferred to a regular bus. The audio commentary was very good. Our original plan was to ride the entire tour and then get off at a couple of destinations we had already bought tickets for. But the entire tour takes 2-3 hours according to the website. I was afraid that by the time we did that and then made our way back to where we wanted to get off, we would not have time to tour our attractions, so we went ahead and got off early. We never got back on.

We wanted to get back on and continue the tour route, but it was getting later and we wanted to take our free river cruise. So we did that, which took us from Westminster Bridge all the way up to Tower Bridge, but it was the last run of the day so it didn't bring us back. And there were no Big Bus stops on that end of the river. Even if there were, it was nearly 6PM and the tour buses were about to stop running.

So my advice is...if you want to use this as a way to get from attraction to attraction AND get off and tour things, it's not a good idea. There simply isn't enough time. I would do this again but stay on the bus and ride the entire route next time, then maybe plan more carefully as to when I might get off and back on again...if there's time. As it stands, I ended up paying a lot of money for what I could have accomplished on the Tube, really. Live and learn.

This is our third use of the Big Bus-London. Great way to see the highlights of the City, as well as most convenient and economical way to move around the major tourist areas of London. I recommend Big Bus. Excellent service, great frequency at the various stops, and clean and comfortable buses.

Bought a 2 day ticket...its a hop on hop off bus...but in traffic can take a while to get to where your going....we did the whole ride in 2.5 hrs and seen so much of London we would never have seen otherwise.....and used it the next day for getting to places we wanted to go.....well worth the cost of £30 ish per person ( adult )....

Being in London for just one day always seems a bit silly because you never know exactly what you want to do, and when you do know what you want to do its hard to fit everything in usually. After being approached by one of the Big Bus company reps we said we would think about it. After going on the London Eye (which is amazing) we decided we would take the Big Bus tour. Its abou two and a half hours. The tour guide, James, was absolutely brilliant! We enjoyed him alot and we were inpressed by the amount of knowledge he had and how he always kept the atmosphere up! It was great value for money and a great way to get a breif look at all the sights in London. We now definately know what we will be doing next time we visit thanks to the Big Bus!

We joined the tour at Waterloo, and bought tickets at the bus stop. My advice is don't! Book on line because tickets are far cheaper and the very irritable ticket seller will not consider offering the concession price, so probably the £27 we paid more for 3 adults than the internet price was his commission.
The next bit of advice is if you're staying on the bus and not hopping on and off then start at stop 1. We got on at 14 and when we got back round to stop 1 we were told to get off! The bus was full of people who were expecting to continue with the tour, we all had seats on the top deck but apparently the bus was required elsewhere so if we wanted to continue on the tour then we had to get on the other already full bus that was about to start the tour so the bus emptied of lots of annoyed people! We didn't bother getting on the other bus there was no room, we could have waited for another bus but by this time we were fed up of incompetence and and extremely inept customer service!
This aside it is a really good way to see the sites of London but try another company, there are a number and they may be cheaper and provide a better service.

We took the Big Bus in Paris, so we assumed it would be just as good in London. We were wrong. Taking into account that the cities are laid out differently, it was disappointing that the driver took detours around traffic which resulted in some major sites being missed. They also seemed to be more interested in picking up passengers than with the questions and concerns of those already on the bus. We flew by some of the monuments and historical sites -- no time to even snap a photo. At one point we had to change buses. I do not recommend this tour in London. Stick to the Tube.

48 hours should be taken literally. Take advantage of everything included and don’t use the tour bus as a form of transportation. Walking is often faster than the tour bus. I planned where I wanted to go over the two days so that I wouldn't have to sit through any part of the tour more than twice, but still made it between every stop once (to get all of the tour information). The section that I did do multiple times was identical between two different tour live guides.
The blue bus (which has audio prerecorded and not a live tour guide) was the dullest and most boring tour that I have ever gone on. It runs very slowly, to the point where it took more than an hour to drive around a small stretch of area, and not for traffic reasons. It was definitely waste of my time to go around the blue circuit. STICK TO RED.
The included walking tour of the changing of the guard (Royal walking tour) was my favorite experience during my stay in London. The changing of the guard happens every other day, but the tour still runs daily, make sure that you take the tour on the day of the change.
The big bus tour ticket comes free with a ticket on the City Tours river cruise. The river cruise in narrated by the ship staff so you get to hear the “local” version of all of the stories. Because the tickets last 24 hours, and the first river cruise leaves at 10:00 from Westminster Pier, I had my Big Bus tickets validated at 10:05, spend two full days on the big bus circuit and then got a free trip to Greenwich on the third day. Getting back I was on my own, but public transport was very convenient and allowed me to stay longer. Be wary that the cruise takes about 90 minute to get to Greenwich so you won’t arrive until ~11:30.

We took the big bus tours in London and were glad we chose them. Their frequency is very good every 10 minutes and their tour guide was very informative.

Their stops are located conveniently close to major attractions so it's easy to visit attractions. They also have 3 free walking tours which I suggest you should take advantage of. We took the changing of guards walking tour and it was awesome. Our tour guide Kevin was wonderful.

They also sell discounted tickets for other attractions.

Definitely recommend it!

At £32 we initially felt that the price was a bit steep but having a 48 hour validity the ticket ended up offering very good value for money.
For English speakers the Red Tour offer a live commentary which is delivered by very well informed guides who also have a good sense of humour.
The Blue Tour has a headset commentary available in about 9 different languages.
Wit the Hop on Hop off facility it's up to the individual to get the best value for money.
All the main attractions appear to be covered.

We went on this to make use of our tesco points.. so effectively we didn't pay.. you get 48hrs access to the buses and also get a ride on the river boat. Was so worth doing. You can jump on and off when you want as they run every 15 mins. There are 3 different routes you can go on. So worth doing if your a tourist. But I think even if you lived in london you would learn new things on the tour.. but be warned we sat at the back of the bus for photo opportunities and omg when we got off I could not feel my hands or face or legs. So best advise wrap up warm if its a bit cool

Being over in London and having just proposed myself and my new fiance the next day went out sightseeing on this bus. Unfortunately our wonderful host, who's picture I have included, thought it would be great to go round the upper deck of the bus asking nationalities. I said I was Irish there were English, Americans, etc lots of different nationalities.
Then our host started making jokes about the troubles in Northern Ireland and how "Don't worry at least we still have it". What a riot what next eh jokes about the holocaust for Germans? Couldn't believe a tour guide would make jokes about a conflict like Northern Ireland.

If booking online for a trip taken before 28th Feb 15, you get next day free. Excursion includes walking tours and city cruises. We only used the red line and picked up tour at Aldwych near Covent Garden. You can get discounted attraction tickets from guides who wait at each bus stop but we already had ours.
We had planned to stay on a complete circuit , however, the changing of the guard at Buckingham Palace was in progress( only on every other day) so we got off to watch that and then walked down the mall and a big loop round and back on another bus to complete our tour.
We sat in the open section at the top and this gives you a wonderful view of buildings and side streets. You would definitely miss a lot by sitting downstairs but it would be warmer!
We are English and only live 18 miles away but even though we've driven around London many times, being up high gives you a wonderful perspective of the city.
The longest we waited for a bus was 15 mins and our tour guides were great, though some were a bit more informative than others.
We took the city cruise ( boats are a bit tatty but ok) from Tower Pier to Greenwich and then from there back to Westminster Pier. The boats have basic drinks and snacks and a loo.
There is a commentary to listen to and the boatman on board did one from Tower Pier to Westminster and was very funny so give him a big tip as he volunteers to do this.
We didn't have time to do any walking tours.
The red route circuit time will vary depending on traffic conditions, road closures, demonstrations, accidents, diversions etc but would be two and a half to three hours.
We used the bus as our main form of getting about rather than the tube etc. At least that way you can still view things going on your journey. Be aware that the bus steps are very steep and the bus will not always wait for you to reach your seat.
Would definitely use this bus tour again but it will take you much longer than you think and if you get off to do things the time will just fly!
Combine," The London Eye" with," London Dungeon", walk over Westminster Bridge and do the Palace of Westminster , the clock tower that houses Big Ben and Westminster Abbey.
If you exit the bus at The Shard stop you can walk through the station and entrance to Shard viewing point is on your left. If you walk around to the left past The Shangri-La hotel there is an entrance to the bars and restaurant of the Shard on level 33. Don't press the lift button it is automatic!
You can combine The Shard with Bourough Market ( closed on Sunday) with a tour of Clink Prison which was first used in 1144.
The Blue Tour is longer but on our second free day we did this anyway due to a road closure on the red route. This has an audio guide available in 12 languages. Check the front of the bus to make sure you are getting on a blue or red tour and that it says Big Bus. You'd be amazed how many people went to get on the wrong bus!
If you give it a go, have fun and enjoy having a much needed sit down!

So,me and my boyfriend was confused with what to so we went on the big bus tour! It is a great way to see everything and is really good that you can jump on and off at all the stops so you can really see all the sites. Plus you get a free river cruise ticket too. Unfortunately due to really horrendous traffic we missed the last river cruise down the thames.

We booked Big Bus tour ticket from the airport and the good thing that we got a free taxi from the airport to the hotel. The next day we took the Big Bus tour , at the beginning it was fantastic except the traffic jams; by the end of the day we faced trouble to get into the bus once again due to a complete stop of all busses in central London, we had no alternative but to walk back.
If you are young people I would recommend to avoid the big bus tour and make your own tour using the underground, it will be much cheaper if get a daily or even weekly ticket and you will save a lot of time too.

My husband and I only had two days to spend in London. I bought the 48 hour tickets in advance so when we arrived in London we were ready to "Hop On". The first day it was raining so we got on the bus and went upstairs to the top. This was the red line. Only about half of the top was covered so we took two seats that were separated from on another but eventually we were able to move to two fronts seats. We enjoyed a front seat view of the city and the sights between rain drops. On this trip we had a live narrator that gave us information about each of the sights. The second day, we took the blue line which had more sights to see. We hopped off at the London Eye, rode that and hopped back on the Big Bus. On this trip the narrator was taped and you can listen to it in a few different languages. We saw more and again eventually ended up in the front seats upstairs where we had a great view of all the sights. We didn't have time to get out and walk so if you only have a limited amount of time in London, this is the way to do it. Don't confuse the Big Bus with red bus because there are lots of red buses in London.

I rated this a four, only because of the limited covered seats on the top deck.

The tour started off well, got on the green bus and transferred to the red bus. The live guide was good. Waited over 50 mins waiting for a bus at Westminster, during that time there was about 4-5 Original Bus Tours and a few Golden Tour buses. Eventually got on a very crowded blue route bus. Got off at Marble Arch and waited about 20 mins there, during which time a lady was asking one of the Big Bus guys how long the red bus would be and he was very rude and was shouting at her. Later we had a bus pull away from us outside of the National Art Gallery at 18.00 which turned out to be the last bus. There were a number of people waiting for a bus. Eventually after 50 mins we ended up getting a taxi back to the hotel. We had even asked a member of Big Bus staff at Piccadilly Circus where to get the bus but he did not advise there were no more buses. There was a family with young children also waiting to get the bus back to the train station. They also had to get a taxi. I feel this was a massive waste of £93. Would have been better to get an Oyster card or gone with The Original Bus Tours.

Buses did not come every 15min as said it would... my husband and I barely used ours as we always spent 30min waiting for the bus only for it to be over OVET croweded! Spoke to a few others waiting at the stopz the same day as I who were just as unsatisfied.

While we were waiting for the bus I saw 4 golden tours buses come by and 3 original tours bus go by. FOR ANYONE READING THIS please go for the other tours!! Or ull waste ur time waiting at the stops for a extremely over cowded bus! The guys at the stops working for the big bus tours didnt know much either. When asked when the next bus was he just shrugged! Worst experience!!! Would never recommend this to anyone!!

me and my partner have just visited london for a couple of days,and decided to go on the big bus tour.going round the red route i think we got lucky with our guide(nick)i think.he had lots of fun things to talk about and amuse us as well as a lot of very interesting facts.contrast that with the blue route which was a headphone plugged into a recorded message which didnt always work.i would definately go on the red route again,with the hop on hop off sevice and the river boat included is well worth the price.

Traveled with my retired parents, they enjoyed being able to see the city without breaking a leg (figuratively & literally speaking). We bought 24hrs ticket but get a promotional extra day for free. Took the red line on day 1, first commentator was a bit boring but then we had a stop at Green Park and change to another red line bus, that's where it all changes.

Nick, the new commentator is witty, knowledgeable & full of fun facts (like where late-Princess Diana used to host her hen party). Despite being on his third tour of the day, he's still energetic & he always checks with all passengers before each stop to see if anybody wants to get off (he also has some good interaction with the bus driver). We enjoyed his commentary so much that we simply took a complete round of red line tour with him.

The next day, we took the blue line bus & did some hop on/off (now that we know which station the bus stops, the maps are not that great). All drivers maneuver well in the busy streets of London, the wait time is generally 10-15 minutes, the included free river cruise turns out to be another highlight. The buses run late-ish until 8pm+, we could pretty much use the service as substitute for public transport for the first 2 days (with some planning of course).

All in all, would highly recommend Big Bus Tour for anyone who's looking for a ho-ho in London.

Having researched the internet and reviews I decided to book with the "big bus tours". I went online and found that for an extra 15quid I could get a ticket for 48 hours. As we were down in London with the children for a theatre trip (and our first to the capital) Bargino....I thought. Well from arrival at St Pancras where they have a "green" route to take you to meet the main tours we then joined the blue tour which has audio in many languages which you listen to on earphones provided. We had an absolute blast. We took both tours. WELL WORTH THE MONEY. xx

Our flight from Australia landed at Heathrow at 7am. Our hotel room would be ready at 3pm. What to do with that time after about 24 hours in the air? The perfect solution was a hop on hop off tour.

We dropped off our bags at our hotel and got coffee. Sat there wondering what to do for the next few hours that wouldn't be too demanding and would fill in time until we could get to our room. The Hop On - Hop Off bus had stopped across the street. After watching two pass by we realised the problem was solved.

The 24 hour ticket gave us the opportunity to sit through the first complete circuit of the tour and helped us to get our bearings as well as see so many of the sights at least at a distance. After the first 3.5 hour loop we got off had had a walk to Buckingham Palace and a look around, then back on, getting off again for lunch near Harrods. Then onto the bus again, getting off at our hotel. We actually ended up returning closer to 4pm having really enjoyed our look all around the city and making of note of things we wanted to visit again.

Headphones and audio guide is provided and the information is interesting. Staff at each stop were helpful about other stops, exact pick up locations and other queries. In addition to the earphones they also had wet weather plastic ponchos available if required.

By the time we got to our room we had a good sense of where we were, had already photographed some of the key landmarks, and had planned our itinerary for the next two days.
We used the remainder of our 24 hour ticket the next day to start out our travels. Well worth the money. We didn't do the river cruise, but had weather been better we certainly would have done so.

A really good way to orient yourself and pick out the places you want to revisit.

I have been to London a number of time for work, this visit I got to be a tourist, me and my 4 friends decided to do an open top bus tour. We boarded the bus at Kings cross at 11,35am (green link) after a 5 mins wait. this was to take us to the main pick up point at stop 15 (Covent garden) this is where the problem started.

We were told the next bus (red tour) would be along in 5-10 mins we had a time slot of 4 hours to complete the tour and take the river cruise, after a 20 mins wait still no bus, we asked the ticket vendor when it would be here he said 5 mins. After 30 min still no bus, we were then told that there had been mechanical problems, mean while every other bus tour company had there buses passing every 5-10 mins. eventually a bus arrived 50 mins later.

We boarded the over crowded bus and took the tour, unfortunately we had to miss out on the river cruise as we had no time left. I really don't rate this tour as we were left waiting for almost an hour with very poor communication so I really wouldn't recommend this company at all

Big Bus is what you expect from a Hop On Hop Off. You get on the bus, you listen to the commentary, and you get off where you want.
It's fairly easy to buy a ticket, because the vendors are like phone salesmen, very pushy at times. But the ticket vendors in Marble Arch are so so annoying. The Marble Arch hub with several routes crossing each other, and several London bus routes using the same stops. It's not easy finding your way arond that mess. I would suggest that Big Bus makes it easier for tourists to understand the routes and which bus is going in which direction.

Was advised by many expats that the best way to tee off a holiday in London is to do a bus tour so that you can get your bearings around the city. They are absolutely right.

My wife and I did the Big Bus tour today and it was an excellent foundation for our holiday. The bus was clean and the ride was smooth. The commentary was excellent, very informative and rich in history.

You can hop on and off at will and another bus will be along between 5-10 minutes.

This bus ticket also comes with a free ride on the city cruise boat which gives you an excellent journey from Westminster to the London Tower.

Will advise any future first timers to hop on this tour!

Really enjoyed the tour and boat trip. Hopped on and off 3 times.
Our tickets were for two days - which I recommend as if you want to hoho and see many sights, this cannot be done in a day!
Best plan is to take the red (with live guide) route and decide what you want to see (this takes 2 to 3 hours depending on traffic). We did this pre lunch and then stopped for Tower of London and boat trip. Did boat TofL to Westminster - fab bit which kids loved. Massive boats which is important to me! I like nice flat boat trips!!!
Then last hoho for the day round to Aldwych pre tea and show!
Next day did more - London a Dungeon & London Eye, Shard & Buckingham Palaca (Mews). All good.
A couple of things to note. Buses runs to 8.30pm (posters earlier said finish earlier - not sure why?) and there loads of them, so we never had more than 5 minute wait at stop.
Also live guides were excellent but we used the blue route buses for the hoho day 2 as less people on so got round between sites more quickly.
Great time had by all the family!

I took my teenage son on a post-GCSES trip to London - We wanted fun but my son enjoys history so I wanted the trip to be informative too. We picked the bus up at Victoria station and took it to The Embankment (before our lack-lustre experience at The London Dungeon - another story). The guide was fantastic although seemed to have a slightly unnerving admiration of pigeons! 😳 She clearly knew her stuff and was very entertaining. After the Dungeons, we picked up another bus round to the Tower. A different guide this time but he was as good, if not better than the first. After giving us a bit of light-hearted stick for coming on the bus munching our Subways he was informative, funny and very knowledgable being able to answer off-script questions and really engaging with the passengers. I've done other bus trips around London before but this was far and away the best. Being able to hop on and off was excellent as well. We did the free river cruise back to the Embankment from the Tower which added an extra dimension to the trip. All in all, very good value and highly recommended. The only criticism is that the buses stop at 5pm - fine in the winter but I'd have thought they could go on a little longer in the summer.

We've done hop-on, hop-off buses before but the Big Bus was the best. The staff was friendly and helpful. The tour was interesting and audio was clear. Our favorite part was the river cruise though. We spent about an hour cruising the river and then having lunch on board. It was fun and very informative. Would recommend this to anyone. Good value as well. We bought the two-day ticket.

We only had two days in London so we chose the Big Bus Tour to see as much as possible in a short time. They have many stops where you can hop on and hop off then catch another bus. We never had to wait longer than 10 min’s for a bus to pick us up. It hits all the major sites. The red line has English speaking tour guides, the blue line has headphones in all different languages. Our ticket included their boat cruise as well. It is only about a 20 minute cruise but was still fun. A word of caution, your receipt serves as your ticket for the day. We lost our receipt at the very first stop. We walked back to the start and spoke with the lady that had just sold us the tickets about 30 min’s prior. They don’t record your name or credit card number and they made us buy the tickets again! Outside of the ticket issue, it was a great way to see London.

Despite the traditional English weather, the Big Bus Tour was excellent. We were able to see all the attractions of London and were able to walk parts of it and stay longer. Easy the hop-on-and-hop-off over a 24-hour period. Worth the money!

First visit to London and didn't have a clue where anything was. Jumped on the double decker bus with my earphones and off I went. Palace, Marble Arch, Harrods, Tower of London, and the list goes on. All the main sites with informative narration. Bus included offered Tower of London entry at a discount and that also included free boat ride up Thames and Jack the Ripper Tour which was also very good. Highly recommend the bus to do a tour right around then get off when you want.

It's difficult to make me upset but this Big Bus Tour did. At £32 it wasn't cheap, so my husband and I shelled out £64 and once we got off, we never got on again. They provided earphones or the audio tour, which I actually thought was a good idea...until it started to skip and repeat itself. After that, the tour was out of sync...so for example when the audio tour said we were at the American Embassy with a statue of Dwight Eisenhower in front, there was just some ugly office building...this just went on and on and on! No apology, no announcement, no nothing. Then we were greeted with the following: "Listen up, people..you have to get off this bus and get on another bus". I've been on bus tours of London before and they were excellent. This one was a big disappointment and totally ruined the last day of our trip to London.

I'm pretty hard to offend, but the money I spent on this tour this weekend offended me to feel compelled to review my experience. I got on at 9.30 at Greens Park.... To be told bluntly that there was a cycling event on today and that this was only a shuttle bus to another bus. Which didn't really make any sense at the main boarding stop, but hey ho, off we went (to be shuttled to another bus 2 mins away, which then went the route the first bus was supposed to have gone anyway. We then made our first grave mistake... WE
HOPPED OFF the hop on/hop off bus tour. How silly of us. When we went to hop back on 90 mins later, we waited... Nearly 2 hours for a bus, with a whole load other unhappy people. I'd actually gone into a tube station with the day ticket i already had whilst waiting, to try and get to somewhere/anywhere of interest instead of wasting our precious day, but as there were lines shut, I'd gone back out to rejoin the angry waiting group.

We sat on a while enjoying the sights until making our 2nd mistake.... We hopped off again, for about 20 mins.... Cue another 45 min wait for a bus to turn up so rammed that there were people almost sat on the drivers knee. He was an unfriendly chap too and spent the whole vile journey getting out of his cab barking at people that they couldn't stand up upstairs or ordering more compact crammage. So not only could you not see anything on this sightseeing tour (other than someone's shoulders) there was no chance of wangling some blind commentary in an effort to identify where the hell you were whilst your head was stuffed into someone's backpack. So basically, a hop on/hop off bus tour that you'd be stupid to hop off, and have no chance of hopping back on again. And there's a good chance you'll be stuck downstairs unable to see a thing or pointlessly plug your earphones in for audio either. Marvelous waste of 1 day visit to London. Cheers!

I am totally disgusted, Today my extended family wanted to visit the sites of London.
Having worked in London for so long and commuted via Victoria for so many years I always thought the The Big Bus Tours office which is situated directly out side Victoria station would be the most professional. we were 2 adults and 2 children + myself.
I went to buy tickets for the tour and was told the cost for 3 adults and two children would be £88.00. When we asked for a discount, the representative quoted £86.00
and eventually he decided quoted £84.00 all in. At that time we decided that It was too much for a family on a budget and walked away.Momentarily, I came back to the representative and asked if he could bring the price down to £75.00. At that point his superior stepped in and with a very aggressive tone, shouted the discount would not be forthcoming.
I explained that I was quoted £84.00 originally, the supervisor became more aggressive and stated that the representative was unable to make such a discount. When I appealed to him, he refused to discuss it further and would not give me his name. I then asked him how much the actual cost should be and he began by saying "with a discount it would be....." . After a lot of pointless aggravation , he quoted £108.00 for 3 adults and 2 children. again, I asked for his name - which he refused to give. I then went to a colleague of his and got this supervisors details. It would seem this supervisor/operator makes up the prices as they go along. Hardly professional - very rip off Britain.
We decided to go around the corner to another operator - The Original Bus tours and they were happy to get our custom for £75.00 - the children were young and went free.
My advice - Shop around, but don't use this tour company.
I am so annoyed, I have decided to write to the company HQ and BBC watch dog.

As a solo traveler sometimes you hesitate before doing bus tours and things but I have to say I'm so glad I did! The red tour is the one I went on . The tour guide was nothing short of amazing. Our tour guide Steve.M was so full of knowledge and helpful to people in so many languages. Steve made the trip worth being on. So much so I went again! He was funny , kind and his knowledge of local history was amazing. The world should be filled with Steve.M's . Thanks Big Bus Tours and THANK YOU Steve.M . Highly recommend this to any travellers wanting to see London's attractions and historical buildings. 48 hour ticket , free river cruise . Great value for £30 . Oh and don't forget a tip to the tour guide. I tipped and I know it was gratefully accepted .

My son and I just came back from a day trip in London. And the highlight was the open top bus tour by the big bus tour company. Martin was out great driver. But Chris was an amazing tour guide, giving a running commentary on all local attractions, monuments and places of interest. He was funny, factual and entertaining. My son commented on how well educated he was too. He did his job with passion and enjoyment. We were sad when it came to driver and guide change over. Sadly the replacement tour guide was bland and boring, not a patch on Chris. We are considering ourselves very lucky to have had the pleasure of his services for most of the tour. Thank you for a great job and a great experience. Keep up the good work. And Tim you could be doing with taking some tips from your colleague.

On our mid June vacation my family of four signed up with out hotel concierge and were assured that the buses would run until about 8PM and pick up every 15 to 20 minutes at the stops located on the map. Sounded simple. We rode from the Westminster stop to St. Paul's. When we returned to the bus stop we waited over 35 minutes. Competing bus tour line buses and city buses kept coming but by the time the Big Bus came, there were too many people waiting and we had to wait even longer. When we were finally able to board we were crammed in like sardines. Attendants at the bus stop kept saying that there was a strike causing traffic delays which didn't make sense since all the other buses were flowing regularly. A short time later it was the same situation at the Marble Arch station. No big bus buses and we waited for 40 minutes. This time we were told that there were two demonstrations in town slowing traffic-except all the other bus lines and city buses were coming regularly. When asked what the demonstrations were, the big bus attendant had to hesitate and made up some silly answer. When we were able to board a bus we were sardined again. Finally at stop number 42 we waited over an hour for a bus and it picked us up and then it was announced that it would end its run back at Marble Arch as the 6PM daily shut down was approaching. Other riders shared their highly disappointing experience.The attendants at the last stop were nasty when we all said that we were told that the buses would run later and that we all spent so much time waiting. The attendants said that if the buses were to end the run at 8PM, then they had to stop going at 6PM. They were rude and obnoxious-yelling and highly defensive. Highly unprofessional group of attendants that man the larger bus stops. We just wanted to return to the Westminster stop but they would not accommodate. We ended up spending an additional 20 pounds in cab fare to get to where we needed to go. Once billed through on our credit card, the 30 pound per person big bus fare for our family ran up to over $185 US dollars. Please folks, save your money for some other attractions in London and don't take this rip off experience.

After 4 wonderful days in London we decided to pay for a hop on hop off bus tour to ensure that all sights where covered.
We selected the maroon and cream buses (Big Bus Tours) - as the ticket vendor told us they were more reliable than others. This may or may not be true.

If you want the ultimate bad experience at the end of the day choose this tour - remember the buses are maroon and cream.

At 5.30pm we caught the bus at the Harrods stop with a view of ending our trip at London Bridge prior to the 7.00pm cut ff. We rounded Marble Arch and the bus pulled up to the stop. After a 10 minute delay a Mr Graham climbed aboard and told all the passengers that due to drivers hours we had to board a bus further down the road. The time was 6.30pm and the tickets are valid to 7.00pm. We duly alighted the bus together with a large number of other passengers and proceeded down the road to the bus stop. No bus was present and the ticket vendors did not know what was going on.

A similar fate awaited the next three buses and subsequently there was a large number of by now agitated passengers on the footpath demanding what was going on. Mr Graham however by this stage had disappeared his job apparently done in clearing the busses. The only person left was a bemused ticket seller who despite trying his best to solve the situation was none the wiser than all the passengers left on the footpath. At about 6.50pm a bus turned up and they managed to clear half the stranded passengers by pushing as many passengers into it to a more central location. I am sure the number on the bus would not have meet traffic regs. At 7.15pm another bus turned up and once again as many as possible passengers where squeezed in for a very hairy ride to a final destination in Piccadilly.

A passenger remarked that a similar thing happened the night before to her at the Bakers street stop.

To my way of thinking it was a case of having all busses cleared by 6.30pm so the staff could be home by 7.00pm. The tickets purchased clearly state a final time of 7.00pm

I am sure that next time I return to London I will not be using this company. You have been warned.

Have wanted to do this for ages, but as I live in London could never find anyone to accompany me, so my daughter came with me and paid as part of my birthday treats. Luckily my birthday is in July and on the day we had fabulous weather. As this is an open top double decker bus weather can make or break the trip. There are 3 different bus routes that are cleverly colour coded. Red Tours have a guide on board talking who provide a running dialogue of information often with funny comments and unusual facts. Blue tours have information by headphones and cover the West end and Green Tours also have headphone commentary and cover the Kings Cross and Russell Square locations. The yellow tour covers the River boat which we used from Tower Bridge to Westminster Pier and all are very good. You must keep your ticket with you to hop on and off as many times as you like and the buses come along really often, going both ways in many cases so you can go back if you want or stay on and repeat things. We got on at 9.15am when it was empty but it does fill up very quickly. Its great if you want to visit other attractions like the London Tower , London Eye or British Museum as the bus goes right by and you can hop on and off.

We took the Big Bus Tour to give ourselves an overview of London and get ourselves a lay of the land. It definitely helped us get our bearings, and we were able to stroke a few things off of our list, and replace them with a couple different things.

However, it is pretty slow though, and you're definitely in the middle of heavy traffic. If you have limited time and you know what you want to see in London, then this tour probably isn't for you.

Our group of 5 had a great day hopping on and off the bus! We really liked the audio on the headsets explaining the history or culture of each area and major sight. By the end of the day, we had done the whole blue line loop and had seen most of the city. The only disappointment is that the Queen does not allow tour buses on the front side of Buckingham Palace, so one would have to get off at the stop and walk to really see it. It was great otherwise, because we could pass by things and decide what we wanted to take the tube back to the next day when our pass had expired. It was a great first day way to see the city. We went on a Monday and there was quite a bit of traffic, so we didn't move very quickly along Oxford or Regent Streets, so a weekend might be a better choice if you can.

We bought tickets for the Big Bus tour from our hotel concierge. We were on the Blue Line, and kept having to "detour", which meant we were stuck looping in circles around the same sites for HOURS. Finally we had to get off the bus and walk to our other destinations. That meant we only had an hour to see the Tower of London and a museum we wanted to go to. We made our concierge aware of the problems when we returned, but nothing was done about it. It was an expensive disappointment.

We took the 24 hours hop-on, hop-off London tour.
We used both the red line- which was with live commentaries (Thank you Jesse the guide and John the driver! You were the best of the 3 guides we've met in this line) and the blue line- which was with recorded insights.

The pros: The buses are in good condition, the staff on the buses (drivers and guides) is very professional and amicable and the spread of stations around the city is perfect. The frequency of the red line is great and the free river cruise by boat is a very nice addition!
The cons: The frequency of the blue line wasn't great. We wanted to reach the Portobello market in Notthing Hill on Saturday and for some reason were taken off the bus near Hyde park with no explanation. We have waited almost 45 minutes outside (and of course- it started to rain, but that's not their fault) and each time a blue line bus arrived (which was every 10 minutes) the impolite staff outside of the bus (those who sell tickets) wasn't nice and just shouted at us to wait that these buses, although supposed to take the blue route, take the red one instead. That's in addition to the constant red route buses that kept on coming... Weird!
In the time we've waited in the rain we saw around 10 buses (red+blue routes) that passed us- all went to the red route and none to the blue one.

All in all, it's a recommended option to see the city, especially during the first day upon arrival. The Big Bus Tour is a good option. However, this company can aim for a better blue route service.

Me and my friends finally decided to go to London for a long weekend. Only having a few days in such a big city we thought we ought to go on one of the sightseeing buses to see/ learn as much as possible. The bus takes you by all the big attractions and you can hop on and hop off as you please which is great. The bus takes round 2 hours but you learn so much. Our tour guy Rob was such a laugh. He had loads of small funny stories to tell about the attractions besides the "educational" facts. He also had sense of humor which made the bus such a joy to be on and we all had good fun. The tour guides seem to be well trained as when we got stuck in traffic he had came up with so many things to keep us entertained and answered all our weird question to his best knowledge. I thought the bus tours would be a bit of a tourist trap but I was so pleasantly surprised. I'd happily go on one again any time.

All in all, our experience was good. We showed up at the bus stop and was admitted entrance onto the Big Bus right away. The staff was excellent, no complaints there. Our only issue was the amount of time we had to wait until the bus "took off" from a particular station. Each time felt like a long, long time and we felt like we were losing valuable sight seeing time.

On a separate note, we took advantage of the free "Ghosts by Gaslight" tour with tour guide Kevin Russel, which was one of the free walking tours provided by Big Bus. Kevin is hilarious, engaging, charismatic, and just plain awesome. Kevin made our day and we recommend his tours to anyone. He even stayed late afterwards to make sure everyone had directions to their proper tube, bus or walking directions. You can just tell Kevin loves his job, and it shows. Cheers to you, Kevin!! :-)

We were unsure at first if this was going to be worth the cost but decided it was the best way to see London as we only had a limited time here. Our tour guide was a history buff and had a wealth of knowledge about the area and presented it in a very humorous manner. We decided to transfer to the canal tour as it was included. This presented a different angle on all the landmarks which gave us the opportunity to get some great shots. We only did one bus route and the canal tour, but several other routes are available and the ticket was for 48 hours. I recommend anyone coming to London take this tour. It's entertaining as well as educational. Plus it gives you the opportunity to get off and do walking tours and do your own exploring at your own leisure. Best of both worlds.

We arrived in London Friday morning. We chose Big Bus Tours because they said they had buses running every 5 to 15 minutes.
