There were 5 of us altogether including an elderly relative, and it cost just short of £150. The first bus we got on was jam packed and we had to stand until people got off, they had live commentary and we enjoyed ourselves but the traffic was horrendous, so we got nowhere fast. We decided to get off near Buckingham Palace, had lunch, then went to the stop to catch the next bus.

While waiting for the Big Bus Tours, 4 Original Bus Tours and 2 Golden Bus tours passed by - no sign of our bus. One of the other tour opperators laughed and shouted over to us we'd be waiting hours for the Big Bus. The rep from the Big Bus Tours said it would be here in 5 minutes, his attitude towards us was rude and arrogant, after 20 minutes we again asked how long the bus would be, then his excuse was the bus was stuck in an accident, it will be here in 5 minutes, (funny how so many other tours buses managed to pass by!!) These buses supposed to be every 5 to 15 minutes - 45 minutes we waited for it to turn up.

The tours are supposed to last until 6pm. We passed the marble arch 3 times, we seemed to be doing a constant circle instead of the tour printed out on the map. At 5.30 the bus driver stopped and told us to get off. We asked why because we were told it finished at 6pm. He said he didnt know who told us that and to get off. He then drove off with passengers still on the top deck. He was very rude, and unhelpful.

We ended up having to flag down a passing black cab.

After chatting with the London cabbies we found out they have black cabs who know the history behind landmarks, who take you on a 2 hour tour to where you want to go for about £60

The Big Bus tour was an excellent way to see al of London's big landmarks in one day. The hidden gem that really added value was the walking tours including changing of the guards at Buckingham palace one day then changing of the horse guards on the next day as well as a Harry Potter tour with a visit to some of the town sites were brief filming occurred. Our guide, Phil, was absolutely knowledgeable about everything in a very fun, upbeat way. It was fun just to walk with Phil. Phil should be the cornerstone of Big Bus tours in London. He does a fantastic job on his walking tours and I obtained the absolute best views, naked eye and with camera, during my time spent with him! Don't forget to get off the Big Bus and walk with them too!

Booked the tour online for me and my wife for 48 hours. Reached one of the boarding points on Staurday 11 AM and then just sat and listened. The live commentary was amazing, the tour leader (commentator) explained the significancne of various places and had very good sense of humour. He also showed us the spots where we can click pictures. We sat at the open half of the bus at the top. Went to almost all the places in the bus without getting down. As we had booked it for 48 hours so the next day we kept on getting down to the intersting places which we decided during our first day of big bus tour. Found the tour to be great and absolutely worth every penny we spent. We highly recommend it.
A must do. I have visited London many times but i learnt more historical facts on the bus tour, in a few hours than in the last few years of visiting London.

We took the Big Bus for 2 days... Red tour all around and the river cruise and then the following day we took it to see specific stops, got back on and then continued our blue tour. On the red tour we had a guide who was excellent.. I was sad to see him go..but the blue tour ear phones were quite acceptable. I would really recommend anyone who visits London to take this tour, it orients yourself to the city and allows you to figure out what you really want to see. The drivers, the guides and the people on the ground you buy the tickets from are really knowledgeable and 'steer you' in the right direction. Well worth the money!

I've been to London many times and usually walk or use the tube, but the friend I was with particularly wanted to do the bus tour, so off we went! We joined at the Queen Mother's Gates, but you can join the tour at any of their stops. I would thoroughly recommend the tour if you're a first-timer, or would just like to see London with an informed guide. There are two routes, both interchangeable by moving from one bus to another along the route (the buses arrive at each stop very frequently). Our time was limited, so we could only complete the Red Route (about 2hours), the Blue Route takes quite a bit longer. The guide was both informative and humorous and even though I thought I knew London quite well, I too learned things along the way. One thing to note is that the Red Route is English language only,so a non-English speaker would need to use the Blue Route. I thought the ticket rather expensive, even though we received a discount and paid just £27 each, but if you have two days there, it represents very good value (valid for 24hours). Once on the bus you can alight at any of the 50 stops in an area you think you'll find interesting, then reboard another bus when you're ready to continue; you can do this as many times as you wish (just remember to keep your ticket!). The ticket also includes a river cruise and a selection of walking tours, and the reps also sells tickets to places of interest at discounted prices, eg., Madam Tussauds, the London Dungeons, etc. Using these buses enables the tourist to explore and see the sights stress-free (avoiding the crowds and waits when using the Tube or regular buses), whilst familiarsing themselves with the London landmarks. Would particularly recommend if you're in town for 2 days; that way you can use it to its full value.

I was a litlte hesitant to use this company because of some of the reviews but my family and I were really happy with the tour. We took it on a Sunday so the bus wasn't very crowded and we didn't have to deal with a lot of traffic. We took the blue line because it picked up close to our flat it also was a recorded tour but none of us minded it. Our kids liked the tour so much that our last day in England we took it again. This time it was a Monday and the traffic did make a difference but we weren't in a hurry so we didn't mind. It is a great way to get an overview of the city. It does take longer on some stops to load people but if you aren't in a huge hurry and want a relaxing day of hopping off an on the bus, this is the way to go.

We were not impressed. Simple as that. In fact we were pretty badly disappointed.

We bought tickets at mid day and waited for the green route to come by and pick us up, so that we could join the main red or blue. 30 minutes later, we game up and walked to the main routes, where we caught the blue line (the one where you have an audio comentary with headphones. We took the bus up to london bridge, and junped off to look around.

This was our first mistake. Getting back onto the bus, was a nightmare. Not only did it take ages to arrive, there were so many peole wanting to get on that they all piled in and filled the bus to bursting point. As a result, it was crowded, hot and uncomfortable. And because each seat is designed to have the audio commentary, there was nothing for the peole who had to stand.

As we crawled aound london, standing and not seeing or hearing anything, more peole we getting on, and we were geting more and more frustrated. So badly that we have to get off to prevent a major rage. So we got off and took the underground back at the end of the day.

We tried again the next day. We took public transport out to a Holland park, looked around, saw what we wanted to see, and walked to the stop at kensington palace. After 30 minutes we gave up, took the underground and simply finished our day in london in a much more reliable fashion. Good old guide book way, with public transport.

Honestly, the Big Bus Company charged us a high price for something that they failed to deliver. We have complained to the head office.

If you are going to take the Big Bus, and get a seat on one of their busses, then do NOT get off the bus until you have gone once around London. The promise of hop on/hop off is totally wrong.

We took a BIG BUS TOUR (BBT) on our first visit to London, earlier this year. The staff were brilliant and the views were fantastic.

It took us a while to find the stop that we were told sold tickets, but we did find it in the end. When we got here, the staff were very friendly and also extremely helpful. It is always a good sign when employees are enthusiastic about the business that they are part of. Literally, he was almost TOO enthusiastic!

It took about 15 minutes for the bus with the tour we wanted to come, which is about the time that the man at the stop estimated it would take. We sat on the open top deck, near the back. The girl who was talking through the tour was brilliant and was very informative. She knew more than another girl we had when we were just taking a short journey.

One of my favourite things she said was when we were driving past the MI5 Centre (which probably isn't the real MI5 centre). I quote: 'We are going past the MI5 building now, which you will see if you look to the left of us, by the edge of he water. They're scanning us now. Bruuum...bruuuum....bruuuuuum.... That's good, we all got through OK. Now, you've got to look out for spies. He's a spy. She's a spy. That's a spy. She's a spy. He's a spy.'

One things I found with the buses is that there were loads of stops that were very well spaced out. The bus definately had time to speed up significantly between the stops. I was shocked at the speed that we reached on the bus, you could certainly feel it on the top deck.

On the day we went, the weather was good almost all day, with a few showers. To be honest, we were enjoying the tours so much that we didn't really notice the rain. Also, I don't think that the fact that it was raining made the day any better or worse.

When we bought the tickets, we were also given tickets for a boat trip down the river. I really enjoyed this as I hadn't ever really been on a boat before (I don't think!), and so did my sister. On the boat, there was a snack bar where they sold crisps, cake, sweets and drinks. I think that we stayed on the boat for about an hour, though we could have got on and off as we pleased, as with the bus tour itself.

What I liked about the bus tour is that is was not something that we had to stay on all day. At one time, we only stayed on for a few stops. We were able to visit other attractions such as Harrods and Hamleys throughout the day whilst knowing that we had something to do afterwards.

If you decide to go on one of these bus tours (which I highly recommend you do!), then you must remember to bring a camera. Wether you are photographing the sights or creating family memories, you will be at loss without a camera on one of these bus tours! You may also want to take a waterproof coat or poncho as you won't want to get off even if it does start raining! I would definately recommend these bus tours, hope you enjoy them.

Manomanom xxx

Reception recommended this tour since the departure location was no more than 500 metres from our hotel.
Glad they did.
Boarded at 09.30 and other than an hour stop at Harrrods we disembarked at 15.30.
The sights seen are just amazing. London is looking fantastic in the lead up to the Olympics and a tour like this makes you realise just how sprawling a ciy it is.
Our tour had recorded commentary which was just fine (there is another tour which has a live English language commentary).  I have to say that I normally have trouble with ear buds but not this time. The audio quality and bud fit was perfect.
Sat upstairs and loved watching those in the seats not too close to the front, ready to spring forward the minute the front row was vacated. It should almost become an Olympic event.
Didn't have time to fit in the Thames cruise or walking tour (both included in the price).
Can most sincerely recommend the Big Bus Tour Company.

My family of four used Big Bus Tours in London during the first week of April 2012. We pre purchased our tickets on line in the US before we departed for London and took advantage of the good web site discounts. When in London we got on the bus at 8:30 AM and started our tour. We departed the bus at the Tower of London (half way through the tour) and bought our Tower of London tickets from the Big Bus Tours agent that was waiting as we got off the bus. This saved us about 5-10% off the ticket price at the Tower of London ticket booth, but more importantly it saved us 30 minutes of waiting in line to buy tickets. With our tickets we went right into the Tower and had a fantastic tour -- the Tower of London is not to be missed when in London. After touring the Tower we got onto a Thames River Tour boat, which is included in the Big Bus Tours ticket, and had a very nice 20 minute ride down the Thames. Seeing London from the Thames is great. We departed the boat, had lunch and then jumped back onto a Big Bus Tours bus to continue our tour. The buses are all jump-on/jump-off all day! On the red route offered by Big Bus Tours you get a live tour guide who tells you what you are looking at as you drive around the city. Our guy was entertaining, nice and informative. After making one full circle of the city, we got off of the red route bus, walked around a bit and then jumped onto a blue route bus. The blue route buses use pre-recorded narration that you listen to with free headphones. There are seven different languages offered. We actually liked the pre-recorded narration better than the live narration because it was more in depth. Our advice is to take the blue tour. We used the Big Bus Tours on our first full day in London. This worked out great because it gave us a very good overview of the city and allowed us to cover parts of the city we would not have easily gotten to; we saw a lot in a little time. It also allowed us to identify places that we wanted to go back and explore later. I highly recommend using a tour bus very early in a city vacation to get the lay of the land and to see the whole city in one day.

This tour company does it right and having the Thames river tour included was a nice bonus. There were plenty of busses running and we never waited long for one when we got off to explore. Take the Big Bus Tour of London and you will not be dissapointed.

20 pounds each and we got two days of use of the hop-on-bus. There were two routes available. Buses were regular. A trip on the Thames River was included. Some discounts were available to London tourist attractions by showing your Big Bus pass. For example, next to the London Eye, we had free entry to the British Film Museum with our bus tickets. There was a walking tour near Trafalgar Square included in the price, also. The tour guide for this was very knowledgeable and provided a fun and funny tour that lasted for maybe two hours.
From what I understand, the extra day's use of the bus is available at some times of the year - not at peak tourist times.

It was our first time to London, and we chose to do the Big Bus Tour first thing. It is a great way to get your bearings and figure out which sites you want to see. The commentary during the tour was very informative and you get a good overall history of all the sites. The guy doing it had a great sense of humor. I would recommend this to everyone, and I though it was a good value for the money.

I use the Big Bus Company whenever I want to introduce London to someone with limited time. We usually start at the Speaker's Corner stop at Hyde Park. Always sit on top and towards the back for the best views and easiest camera angles.

We usually do the Red tour since it covers what we want (don't care about going to Harrod's but if you do than use the Blue tour.) I find it is best to just take the entire loop and not get off at all. This ride can be about two hours, depending on traffic. If you get off, remember there is no certainty of getting a good seat on the next but. Sometimes we wait and let one pass by until the next comes and we can get back up on top.

This tour hits all the major sites. The problem with using it to get to sites you want to stop at is time. Places like the Tower of London and Westminster Abbey get very crowded very fast. I suggest you do cab, tube, walk if you want to visit major sites. Get there very early then do the Big Bus AFTER you have seen the big sites. If you just want to hop off to eat, wander, or go to the less crowded sites that is fine.

The live tour guides are hit or miss. Some are wonderful and some are reciting wrote phrases and jokes. You may find a mix of quality as you hop on and off.

I usually allocate 4 hours for the Big Bus tour. That includes a couple of stops to wander around. Perfect when someone has one day and wants to take in all of London.

We took the Eurostar from Paris to London for the day, and having heard that a HOHO tour was the best way to see the major sights in a short period of time, we booked a tour on The Big Bus. We only had 6 hours in the city and it was our first time there.

The website for The Big Bus said the red loop tour would take 2 hr and 15 min and that after that we could take a cruise on the Thames. The reality was very different. After 4 hours we still hadn't completed the tour. At Hyde Park we were all kicked off the bus and had to wait at least 30 min for the next bus and we were not even given an explanation. On the way back to St Pancras, we sat on the bus for at least 20 min thinking we were stuck in traffic. We started to get anxious that we would miss our train back to Paris so we decided we should get off the bus and walk there. When we took the stairs down from the upper deck we were shocked to see that there was no driver!!!! We were just sitting parked at the curb wondering why we weren't moving.

In the entire day we did not have time to even complete the hoop, let alone hop off and explore something that interested us or take the complimentary river cruise or walking tours.

This tour company uses their bus to hold tourists hostage while they try to push their "discounted" attraction tickets on them!

The bottom line is even if you don't mind wasting your money DO NOT WASTE your valuable time.

Company offers tours with audio-guide and ear plugs in several languages. They also offer live tour commentary in English. We tried the live tour and got off at the next stop. The driver drove so fast, we couldn't really see anything or take photos. The PA system was terrible, and the live commentator spoke rapidly in a heavily stilted British accent so that we, as native American English speakers, couldn't understand her at all. We were told that the buses arrived every 7-8 minutes. After we got off, we waited 20 minutes for the next bus, which also had live commentary. So we waited another 15 minutes for a bus with audio-guide. So much for the advertised 7-8 minute bus intervals. While we waited, 7-8 buses of the competing tour line stopped at the same location compared to 3 Big Bus busses. Once we got on the audio-guide bus, several of the seats had non-functional audio consoles, so we changed seats more than once. Ear-piercing high pitched painful noises suddenly came through the system. Very unnerving. At one point, we were told to get off one bus and get on another one to continue the same tour. Not sure why. Two of the bus drivers were very curt and brusk. Definitely not customer-friendly.

We decided to travel round London for the day with the Big Bus Company as we have lived in Surrey for 25 years but have never visited all of the sights in London before. We used the hop on hop off service and had 4 different guides threw out the day. We had the best fun with a Scottish girl called Samantha. She was very knowledgeable about London and extra helpful with any questions we had. The tour with the other guides was still really good but Samantha made the experience very interactive and made sure she paid attention to every person individually and really included the children which prevented them from being bored. If you go on a tour with these guys and get Samantha as your guide tell her Karen and Co said hello! Would definitely recommend to friends.

my brother in law from canada came over and we went to london and took this big bus tour. because of obama and road works and construction, we missed about 5 stops. no concessions are available. over 60, disabled, child and me cost 93 pounds! no help with wheelchair, they shoved it between a seat and told me that they couldnt afford to lose seats by putting it in an aisle that would lose 2 seats. at the end of the day ( after hop on hop off) the last one is 6 pm they let everyone on. it was full to bursting upstairs and down with lots of people standing. not a tour bus , a commuter bus! do your homework and take the normal buses to get around. you can get a daytrip ticket which covers any bus, tube or train all day for 6.60. on a good note you get a free river cruise which is really good. but you can get it on its own for about 8.50.

We had previously been on Big Bus Company in London and Dubai and had high expectations. We were disappointed... The headphones for the nonpersonal guided buses were of so poor quality we had problems hearing. After a stop at London Eye and the aquarium we waited for almost an hour before a bus turned up. The buses were running less frequent than they had advertised that we ended up taking a taxi back to the hotel after our last stop (and buses were supposed to keep coming).

My recommendation for London sightseeing? Buy a guide book and a day pass at the tube/ buses and do it yourself :) You will have a much more pleasant day than wasting hours with Big Bus Company.

We love taking bus tours in every city that we travel to. It give us a sense of the city we are in and we become acclimated quite quickly this way. We like to stay on the bus for the duration of the tour and then hop on hop off at another time or the next day. This couldn't really be done when we toured on the Big Bus in London mostly because of the rain. We sat on the first floor of the bus, since the upstairs was full and we were in the back (bus was mostly empty here), but then we realized that all of the windows were fogging up due to the rain so we moved forward and sat in the very front seat facing the driver. But this way, we could look out of the front window with the wipers going and see most things. The disadvantage was that I wasn't upstairs so I didn't have as great as a view. (Also had a little girl WHISTLING and chatting the whole time until I glared at her since her parents weren't doing anything!). The next day I thought about hopping back on just to try and sit upstairs, but I ran out of time, so that is a big regret of mine. Not riding on the double part of a double decker bus. But I couldn't change the weather, and I did enjoy hearing about all of the places that I saw on foot for the next three days.

This bus tour is truly the best one in London. There are several tours offered in London. A local person in London did both bus tours and said NOT to do the Original Bus tour ,but to do the BIG BUS tour. I am glad I took the advice as we were VERY pleased. First, I LOVED the headphones. They were much nicer than some I've used on other bus tours. They weren't the cheap kind other tour companies use. When we first got on we had a "live" tour guide and he did a GREAT job explaining the sites and giving the history of the city and the sites. We got off after two or three stops and when we got back on there was not a tour guide ,but a very informative lesson via a pre recorded tour guide. This Hop on Hop Off bus is great because you can hop on and hop off at your leisure and get a history lesson and tour for a reasonable fee. We stayed at the Westmister Plaza and there was a drop off bus stop very close. I highly recommend this tour. You could take a City bus, but you wouldn't get the great history lesson or have someone pointing out all of the many sites in London. We did both( the City bus and also the BIG BUS tour) and were glad we did the BIG BUS tour in addition to taking the City bus from one point to the next. The tour was just that...a tour , not just a bus ride. Oh and there is a River cruise down the Thames River that is included in the price of your ticket. Just remember the BIG BUS. It's the BEST !!!

WOW I guess everyone experiences different things from the same companys. We just got back from London and went on both the BIG BUS and ORIGINAL BUS tours. Big Bus picked us up and droped us off right by our hotel, Original Bus picked us up at our hotel but because there buses already stop running at 6PM, we had to walk back to our hotel from hyde park, a 30 min walk. We saw at least 3 BIG BUSs pass us by during our walk and checked their schedule and found they run a lot later. While we were on the Original bus we had to get off for a wc break on the blue line and while we waited for the next bus at least 3 BIG BUSs past by. I think one can see that the BIG BUS offers much better service and more bang for buck. We will never take Original Bus again. The driver on the Original bus that left us stranded was also rude.

When I get to a new city i like to get an idea of where things are so usually grab a bus tour. Nice easy way to get familiar with the place unless you use this company. It started well with a really nice driver and a few jokes but in the end the biggest joke was this company and how they treated you.
After doing the "changing of the guard" tour on foot we were advised to come back to visit Buckingham Palace as it was so busy.. we had already purchased the ticket from them so thought ok we will take your advise........ so jump back on a bus, get off the bus, go to get back on the bus but the buses have been "DIVERTED!" we get told to walk to the next bus stop. We have been in London for 12 hours and really dont know our way to your next bus stop!!!!!!!!!!! So get horribly lost ! Resorted to asking a homeless guy for directions ... finally after seeing abour 15 of the competitions buses we found the big bus red tour and got back on. We purchased the tickets for the Tower of London from these idiots too so head on over to via the boat only to arrive at 4:55 ( it closes at 5!) Information only provided by the guys on the boat after tipping them!!!!!!!!!!!! SO get back on the boat to head to Grenwich as the Tower is closed and so is Buckinham Palace so we have wasted the 40? Pounds. Arrive there only to be told you have 5 mins.
Only use this company if you have time to waste as it is really is the most disorganised, unprofessional company we experienced the whole trip.

A dreadful experience. It took the bus two full hours on a Sunday morning - when there is less traffic - to go from Gloucester Road to Madame Trussauds. The bus stopped all the time and it took ages for the driver and his collaborators to process new requests for tickets. Passangers were squeezed in the lower deck as if it were a normal public bus and I wonder how one could possibily think about making people do a sightseeing in these conditions.

Do not take this tour, especially if you are a couple or a family / party of four or more. With the same amount of money you all together pay (it costs 25 pounds for one adult), you could take a taxi and see all attractions. And then you go back with public transport to see the ones you are interested. Hopping on and off this dreadful bus will make you lose one full day for very little.

We tried to take the tour twice and, in both occasions, at the same stop, we were forced to leave the bus as the bus ahead of ours was not completely packed and therefore the Big Bus Company had to sqeeze us all in one bus to earn more money.

It was really a negative experience - certainly not to be repeated.

It is much better to buy a day travel card of London Transport (5.60 pounds for one adult) and to take the buses. Bus number 11 goes via the Westminster Cathedral, the Westminster Abbey and the Houses of Parliament, Trafalgar Square, Aldwych, St Paul's (for the Tate Modern also), etc. It is a very nice sightseeing.

Took a party on the Big Bus 'Blue Tour' on 6 October. The competitor "Original London Sightseeing Tour" appeared to have perhaps twice as many buses operating, so we waited around much longer than their passengers did. But all went well until around 4:15pm when we 'hopped on' at Gloucester Road. The driver said that he was only going as far as Marble Arch (we were going back to London Bridge) and then the service was finished for the day. We pointed out that the brochure/map showed the service as every 15 mins until 6pm. "Ah yes", he said "but that means 'Departure'". What?? Anyway we (and all the other passengers) were abandoned at Marble Arch at 4:45pm, with no rep there to talk to. Not a good finish. The price was OK (book online for a discount) and the commentary was adequate - if a little sparse. But if I did it again, I'd try the "Original" tour next time.

On August 11, 2009 I purchased tickets for the Big Bus Company tour from their Victoria Station sales point. I was told the buses would come every 15 minutes, if we waited at the stop around the corner.

We waited for about a half hour watching bus after bus from the competitor flying by. Finally, when the Big Bus arrived we jumped on, with relief, only to be told one stop later (Marble Arch) that everyone had to get off the bus and get on another bus. We waited again for what I would estimate to be under a half hour before a bus arrived . It went one stop (Madame Tussaud's) and sat for what seemed like another half hour. We and most of our fellow passengers had now spent about 1.5 hours in hot, crowded conditions, only to have made gone two stops. Several passengers politely asked if they could get off and get refunds. They would not do that and said that the bus was sitting there because they wanted it to be on schedule. We got off a stop or two later after realizing that the experience had ruined the day and the ride was not fun. An American freelance journalist on the bus made clear that she was going to write a scathing review about how the company handled this. Although she was over the top in how she handled herself, her complaints about the terrible customer service were valid.

I went the next day to the ticket seller and explained what had happened. I asked for a refund or to have the ticket extended so that we could try again, when our schedule in London permitted. I was told that they could not handle the matter and to go to their office, which I did. When I got there I was told I was to write them a letter enclosing the original ticket and to explain what had happened. Why send someone on their valuable holiday time to the office when all they are going to do is tell you to write a letter? How does that help you resolve the problem while you are still in London and able to hopefully resolve the matter? What to do? With limited time in London, do you buy another set of tickets in the hope they will do a better job the next time or do you skip having a bus tour and write for a refund?

My family did take Big Bus on a prior trip. When it works, the tour is great. I would not risk it again.

I was a little worried about choosing any bus tour given the completely mixed reviews on both this and the original bus tour. I chose the Big bus tour as it was clear that I could pay at most stops using a credit card or debit card.

I chose the green park stop as it was only a few stops from st pancreas station on the victoria line. Buying a ticket from the conductor was very easy, she had a variety of automated card readers on her person and was very pleasant. You end up with a small yellow/white receipt, prebooked customers exchange a brownish ticket for the same receipt.

We went the day after the tube strike so they made it clear that the roads were still busy and it would take 2hrs 40 on the red route. We got back to victoria the last stop at just under that time. Very early in the tour there were longish waits at some stops and the bus was full and only room for singles at some places.

The tour guide was very professional and took time to talk to everyone on the tour, pointing out special photo ops and including history that I didn't know. We saw all we wanted to see in london and for that reason I would recommend the tour. We had a 3 and 5 year old who would have been exhausted if we did the same by tube or walk/regular bus.

The only disappoint for all tours like this is you will not drive in front of buckingham palace but will only park to the side

If you want to do london in half a day this is the way to do it.

I've taken both of the major bus tours in London, and this tour isn't worth the money.

Poor communication/marketing about the routes and times...we wanted to use this tour as hop on-hop off transportation and hopefully gain some information about the city. Instead we left on the side of the street for 10 minutes to switch buses on 2 different occasions and after more than an hour on the bus had not even covered a third of the route that claims to be a 2 hour tour.

No information was provided to us when we got on the blue line that English speakers needed headphones as well, so we went half the trip without audio, and when we finally got headphones there was limited information on major attractions, but plenty on the Big Bus tour center. More time was given to it than any other attraction!

The tour only travels in one direction around the city, leaving you to sit through sections over and over. The only benefit was being able to catch the last one of the day at a stop near Westminster Abbey because many of the buses were running much later than published.

Would recommend the Original tour over this one any day.

Don't take this in the winter because it's far too cold up top, and on the bottom you can't see anything. The only advantage is there are far fewer people and no long lines and they give you two days on the ticket. Also, if you want to get on and off it's great, but if you want to take tours, in the winter the buses stop at 4:30pm so you might be able to get in one tour and maybe a walk or river cruise. Have to get started very early to use the price of the bus ticket. If you get an Oyster Card, the tube would be much cheaper. Also, as one other reviewer said, they dont seem to have any plan B if anything happens. There was a protest at the Israelie embassy and we were literally "dumped' at Trafalger Square and pointed in the direction of a city bus. We Didn't know where we were, there were a million buses, and the driver just said matter of factly that he couldn't get us back to where we boarded the bus. It was below freezing out so that made it worse. And I'm in a wheelchair. They don't tell you to pick up earbuds when you board so we had to go back while the bus was moving to find them. I'm afraid to take a cab as I have no idea of the cost and we were far away. Plus it made me mad the Big bus company just dumped us far away from our hotel. The protest was planned far ahead and besides they should have a plan B because these things happen in London often. I also observed the other buses seemed to be running and making stops. I think it was close to quit work time for the drivers and that was it, they weren't going any further or out of their way as he said at first he was going to try to get us back to our point of origin where we could catch the bus that stopped close to our hotel. But then said he couldnt make it. So that meant the bus company didn't even endeavor to hold the bus or run it later for people who were late in getting to the connecton because of the protest..

These red open top buses can be seen around London as you walk around the City and you can buy the tickets from many outlets and agents all over London. Or you can book in advance via thier own office or website.

They have headsets that plug into the seat in front of yours and this provides an excellent commentary on the sites of London as you pass them by on the bus. Also there are commentaries in many different languages and you just plug the earphones into the Country flag for the one you wish to hear.

If it rains then for the people on the top deck they provide plastic capes with hoods so that you do not get soaked. These are flimsy and will only protect you in a light shower.

You can get on and off the bus at any of the stops and the tickets are valid for 24 hours to hop on and off at any time as you wish.

I found the tour to be interesting and did enjoy the history given as we went by the various places. Big Ben was just chiming as we went over Tower Bridge and that was wonderful.

The tickets were priced at £24 each and to be honest I thought that this price was a little expensive for what is after all a bus ride and they did not provide any extras for that in the way of souvenirs or even a drink on board the bus. A complimentary bottle of water would have been appreciated when the weather is good for instance.

Be warned however that the staff are not helpful bearing in mind that they are dealing with tourists who are in a strange and very big City.I was assured that I would be returned to the same stop that I got on at so that I would know where I was. In fact they stop the bus around 5.0pm and everyone has to get off. In my case I had no idea where I was and the driver did not help at all but just closed his door and walked off. I had to ask help from a mobile cafe owner who told me that he is sick of giving help to passengers left there by that Company.

If you are aware of the above and make sure that you end your journey in good time then it is a good trip and an excellent way of seeing the sites of London.

Date: Fri 23rd May 2008
Review: Having looked at both the "Big Bus Co." and "Original Bus Tours", we chose the "Big Bus Co.". At £24 per person it was a huge mistake, although I do wonder if the alternative would have been any better? The staff were friendly enough at the sales centre (naturally) but when we got to the bus stop and were waiting for the right one to come along, we witnessed scenes between members of staff from each of the companies pushing and shoving each other as they fought over customers as they tried to board their relevant bus. I'm quite sure these scenes were largely in jest, however it looked very bad to the waiting tourists and right from the outset was very offputting. Our tour was the blue route and I must say the buses were very frequent and the staff were friendly enough but when we boarded the bus we were left to figure out where the ear phones were to enable us to listen to the recorded commentary. The commentary itself was pathetic. The quality in the main was so poor, you couldn't make out what the narrator was saying half the time. The commentary, when it was audible, was pretty rubbish and not very interesting. It would stop and start in the wrong places. The majority of the time there was no commentary at all and throughout the tour you were left wondering what places of interest etc you were passing. In all it was a huge waste of money. I came off the bus having learnt very little and could have made the same journey for pennies on normal public transport. I have advised friends due to visit London shortly to give it a miss and would advise anyone else the same.

On my last trip to London I tried the Big Bus Company for some new information about London, but unfortunately I was very disappointed. The staff of the Big Bus was very friendly, but on the tape of the bus are too little information about the places of interest. The "authors" of the tape tried to accentuate their information with some music, but this music was temporarily too loud, so that it was impossible to understand the information. Fortunately the ticket includes some walks in London and a trip from the Tower to Westminster (or vice versa). But I'd never again spend 20 pounds for a Big Bus tour!

My Wife and I were on honeymoon in Dubai.

The Big Bus Company is well worth it, we didnt really do it to its full potential as it was sooooooo HOT at 43 degrees.

The staff were really pleasant, although the content wasnt very consistent. One would say the UK island of the World was bought buy Richard Branson and the next would be different... however totally un-important really.

I would reccommend to sit inside on the bus in the summer months at it is far too hot and you can still get most of the photos you need.

They stop outside of the Jumeira Beach Hotel so you can take photos of the Burj Al Arab.

They give you a free boat tour (Tour Dubai) which goes along the creek.... This is worthwhile as it takes approx 1hr 10 mins and covers some interesting bits about the creek.

It does go through a lot of the building sites and talks about what will be there as opposed to what you really want to see, however it is still fairly interesting as everything they are doing in dubai is soooo vast.

The largest theme park in the world - Dubailand, etc etc.

Definately worth doing though.

We flew into Heathrow at 6am from HK on April 4,2007. Left our bags at our Kensington area hotel (check in not till 2pm), went to a cafe for a snack and hopped on the Big Bus at Gloucester Street stop around 9am.

It was the perfect way to kill time until our room was ready and to get our bearings around the city. Being the 1st bus of the day, it was initially slow going as the driver and the sales people at each stops tried to muster business and trying to sell their add-on sightseeing tickets. We were forced to change buses once at the Marble Arch stop, obviously their hub stop.

If you are running on a tight schedule, this is not for you. But we had the whole day to kill, so it worked wonders for us. We managed to go on the River Cruise(free with Big Bus Co ticket) from Tower of London Pier to Westminster Pier and even rode the London Eye. We did hop off and on several times and never had to wait too long for the next bus.Views from the top deck is great. Yes, there are some earphone jacks that don't work, we just unplugged and looked for another seat. (yes,easier to do when the bus is not full)

We didn't get back to the hotel till 5pm! It was the easiest way to get over jet lag,get lots of fresh air and know where we wanted to return for a closer look on another day. It worked brilliantly for us.

Multiple rude drivers, unscenic routes, overpriced tickets, and mindless audio tour with Brits filling your day with lame impressions of American movies. This used to be the greatest tour in the world but Big Bus figured out how to ruin it.
We had Chris as our guide, he entertained us while explaining the history and the curiosities of the places we were seeing. A very pleasant experience
Did it a couple times with a family of 4 and nobody got bored and there is plenty of spots to get off at. River cruise is also nice but less spots

The bus tour was fine, but the walking tour was outstanding and made the cost of the tour well worth it! We walked with Phil for two separate walking tours. He was the BEST tour guide and absolutely loves his job! Make sure you join Phil on one of his walking tours for an extremely fun and informative time!!

We booked to go on the tour with a guy who seemed very friendly and lovely but it went down from there. We were charged £39 for a ticket that lasted 24 hours including a one way ferry tour. For this price you'd hope you get a lovely trip. We were told buses were every 15 minutes. After 40 minutes we eventually spotted a bigbus which drove past and the driver shook his head as the bus said out of service. We waited a further 10 minutes and were about to give up when one came. In this time we saw at least 3 different open top bus companies who each passed us two or three times. We got on board, happy to finally be going somewhere. Traffic was slow, not their fault, but when we got to the stops we ended up waiting for 10/15 minutes. Not going anywhere. We had a show on that night so had to leave the tour to get there on time. The tour did not stop where it was meant to so we had to double back to get to a station. The following day we came back thinking it would be better and to get our moneys worth. Nope! Big wait time again, and other people waiting for the same bus were also talking about having long wait times, as they had purchased a ticket that lasted a few days and the bus was late every day, so this seems common. Again multiple bus companies passed us three times. Finally saw some pretty views of London though. But many wait times. Because of the waits we pulled up to the ferry at just gone the hour meaning we had missed the ferry and couldn't get on it without waiting a further hour. We could not do this as we had a second show lined up. We were almost late for this show also as the bus completely missed the stop we expected it to stop at, as we had pressed the button and it was the next stop on the tour. This meant we had to re-work our travel plans to get to the theatre on time.

Literally so happy we were able to go to London and enjoy being tourists hoping on and off the bus to see all the sightseeing! We went ordered our tickets online and used the app on my iPhone as well which was really helpful and the app told you were the bus was and when it would be arriving - a little bit like Uber eats when your food is on its way!

Not all the stops were available due to Covid but the main stops were still available to hop on hop off! We got the 48 hour bus with the river cruise - just unfortunately didn’t want to do the river cruise as it was raining so opted out of that but that was fine!

We always use a hop on hop off bus wherever we go as they are the best and easiest way to get around and also we are both abit geeky so we love listening to the tour guide to see what historically happened in the areas! The guide was very modern and up to date and quite funny to be honest which was great!

The tour guide Benedict was absolutely amazing could of been anymore helpful! We never did get to go to fortnum & mason but I’m sure that’s an excuse to come back to London now haha!

Celebrated the weekend away by getting engaged and literally had the best time!

Highly recommend using the bus company to anyone x

Fantastic driver and guide made us feel very welcome.Guide was very knowledgable and gave a running and fact filled commentary for the whole of the tour.
Would definitely recommend

The big bus was great, we set off from cathedral and literally went all around London, we stopped at Buckingham Palace got off for dinner nearby and popped back on when the next bus came around 10/10 very informative and a full 2 hrs to get around staying on the bus.
Friendly staff (Chloe and Dave) made for an enjoyable tour. Dave gave us a smooth ride while Chloe kept up an enthusiastic and entertaining commentary. Would recommend anytime.
A great way to see all the major landmarks in London when you time is limited. The addition of the river cruise added a different dimension to the experience

I wanted to see London from the top of the bus even if it was calling for rain.
The guide was funny and very informative.
I did the whole tour in one go. I took some amazing photo.
This was an interesting and fun experience. you get to see the main attractions of the beautiful city. although it can get busy it is really fun and worth it

I'd been to London several times but as it was the first time for the rest of the family. And while it's easy to find one's way around, we figured a hop-on, hop-off tour would be an ideal way to get our bearings. And with a number of competing tours availble, we chose the one that was most convenient to where we were staying. Starting at Green Park, ours was a 2-hour ride around Westminster, Waterloo and the City although we got off about three-quarters of the way through. We had a guide that provided live commentary did a good job - he was friendly, informative, and witty - and much appreciated.
First day tour guide was wikipedia will.brilliant.2nd day girl with broken English. Fine ! But to host a bus tour around london.wise up company.

Should have paid a little more money and gone original bus. Tour route was repeatedly changed and guides telling us on the fly so when we got off the do by foot what we wanted we could not get back on as 1 bus came in an hour and it didn’t stop as it was too full!
Christopher was absolutely fantastic when we caught this bus around London. Not only was he knowledgeable but he was entertaining and engaging. It was a great way to get a feeling for the city
Phil on the Red Route tour was fantastic- very knowledgeable and humorous! He had the best laugh too!
We did the whole tour with Ian as our guide. He was FANTASTIC! Learned so much about London and got to see a variety of things quickly. Highly recommend it!
Julia was awesome. Loved hearing about the history and interesting facts of London. Headphone audio could have been better.
Big Steve and Phil’s walking tour was amazing! Great way to see London in a different perspective. It was the real deal
The tour was excellent and Iain was exceptionally informative but also humorous which made the tour very enjoyable.
I found the tour funny, informative and very relaxed. Julia was a great host and would 100% recommend for anyone travelling in London!
Julia was an awesome tour guide on our trip. We planned to hop off a few times but couldn’t bring ourselves to leave in the middle of her tour. Wonderful time!

We have travelled a lot with work and when arriving at a new city we always do the double decker buses to get a feel for the city and surrounds. Just a great cheap and effective way of learning the ins and outs quickly

I would say this is a must and

Easy and friendly to ride and view first them go where you have time.

We had a wonderful time on the tour bus, and also in the river cruse. Our guides, Joe and Loulou, gave us a brilliant tour around Trafalgar square and the Buckingham palace. They were friendly, easy-going, super helpful and fun! We recommend their walking tour to everyone! Thank you for everything!
We truly enjoyed the Big Bus Tour our guide Julia did a fabulous job on our tour! Highly recommend taking a tour while in London!

We decided to use Big Bus because it had a stop right outside our hotel. The commentary on the Red Bus had us in stitches right from the start. Lots of great anecdotes and information until we got off.
Hopped on a Red Tour guided by Caron who was extremely informative and very passionate about London, its history, architecture and attractions. Would most definitely recommend.

Really nice bus tour. We did the red route with Julia. She was an amazing tour guide. Really funny.
Viele Grüße aus Deutschland 😊👍🏻
Had Julia as guide and she made it fun and interesting. Excellent way to relax and see London. Would recommend
My buddy and I took the tour on the red line and blue line. Caren was our live guide on the red line and she was very knowledgeable and fun.

Good routes and regular buses, buses were clean and recorded commentary was good. However, I was really looking forward to the live commentary reading the reviews, but our guy appeared very bored never smiled and was very robotic which was a real shame considering the price of a ticket.
Great buses, lots of stops. Some lines have tour guide. Excellent service and very convenient to see all tourist spots.
Day out in London with some friends, we used Big Bus to go around and we had a great guide Lewis! He was very funny and knew so many things about the city, it was very entertaining! Thank you!
The app BigBus is very usefull. Not all the bus have live guide. The best is with the guide you can see in the app

The Bus is a good way to familiarize yourself with the city -- and where the landmarks are clustered. But you must with a capital M use this service sparling and ride the TUBE [with the peeps of London], the experience is worth the trip.

Me and my husband come from Germany and we bought a 2-day tour with the Big Bus and it was a great experience! The weather was extremely bad due to the Ciara Storm, however we could enjoy even so, the guides Julia and Big Steve were extremely friendly and their live commentary had brighten up our experience. Totally recommend it! The cruise is also really beautiful and worth it!

We absolutely loved our weekend away in London using the Big Bus tour! Our second day was fabulous with having a live tour guide Chris and driver Paul, we had such a great time and learnt so much information we stayed on and did the full red route! Funny and informative definitely 5 stars from us!

Very regular service with plenty of stops and lots to see. Joe the commentator was excellent very informative and funny and seemed to enjoy his job. Was an easy was of seeing London would definitely recommend.
We had Lewis doing the guide and he was brilliant made everyone feel welcome and he really knows his knowledge 😀 very enjoyable journey would highly recommend to do it x
We had a 2 day pass, so got dto do all the tours. No need to worry about traffic, or how to get to an attraction. Just jump on and off the bus. EASY and stress free.

Brilliant for getting about London as well as sightseeing.
Tour guide really friendly and happy to answer any questions.
Only had to wait a few minutes before another bus comes along. Would get again!

Our guide Julia was amazing! This tour took us around everything we wanted to see and there was lots of time to get some great pictures! I would definitely recommend it for anyone wanting to sight see in London!

Louis 1 of the commentary guides on the bus was very informative and friendly we actually missed some of the stops as we were that entertained by him
Defiantly deserves a pat on the back from his supervisor/ manager for a job well done
Mark/Mandy from Birmingham....
Julia our tour guide was absolutely amazing. I recommend you ask for her your. We had a wonderful time.
This is a great deal instead off taking a taxi or bus. the only negative about this ride is, if there is a traffic.

We used this to get an overview of the city. Then used it along with the Underground to get from place to place. I actually preferred the routes with the recorded tour rather than the live guide. I think I learned more.
Me and my sister were visiting from Plymouth and really enjoyed this bus tour during our stay in London. Lewis was a fantastic tour guide, he was informative and purely great at making you laugh!

Had a really good time on the bus tour with my sister, we came up from Plymouth. And LEWIS who was are tour guide was really good and funny! I would definitely recommend it!
Regards Charlotte

Enjoyed it, all English commentary was wonderful
Definitely recommend , affordable and fun, learn so much in little time

Just returned from the best new years trip to London and most of our highlights were from the big bus tour and our guide 2 walking tours Big Steve!! On the day tour we got the best views of the changing of the guard ceremony, and so much more. The night tour took us through the best lesser known areas of the city including the last rooftop performance of the Beatles! Steve was hilarious and the time with him flew by! I could not recommend getting the big bus package with the London eye included, the fast track ticket was a game changer! Thank you Steve for making our time in London unforgettable!

An excellent way to preview the city and options for tours at different attractions
We had a 2 day pass, in hindsite, I would definately get a 1 day pass, and run the full loop to preview all the attractions, and then use the tube to see specific attractions after that.
Louis was a fantastic tour guide. His commentary was great. I wish big bus had live guides on all the lines but Louis was a wonderful narrator for the red line. Loved it!

Lewis was super fun and very educational even about seemingly mundane attractions. The way he asked everyone where they were from really bonded the rest of the riders and made the stoplights go a lost faster.
Nick L was a wonderfully informative and entertaining tour guide who made the hours fly by on our trip on Big Bus. Superb!

They did not have enough buses to cover the number of tickets they sell. We waited up to 45 minutes at a time to get a bus. The worse stop is at the London Tower. The buses immediately fill past capacity as soon as they let people on. We had to watch two buses leave before we could squeeze on the third one. They stop service around 5:30 pm, so plan accordingly or you will be stuck across town and have to walk an hour or take a very expensive cab.

Visited London for the day (Dec 30), just had come from the Paris Big Bus Tour. This tour was way better than Paris. Arrived at green park station @9:30 am and the bus was right there and it wasn’t too crowded. The live tour guide Jamie, was really nice and funny and helpful with making sure everyone got headphones and he answered questions. He also announced every single stop and what you could see if you got off at that stop. Everyone was friendly that worked for the company. Rode the red line, was worth it. Didn’t have time for the canal tour unfortunately. Amazing bus driver, don’t know how they do it. Saved us a lot of headaches!

First being mistakenly headed to Blue tour we switched to the Red one containing key highlights of London.
Team was nice and helpful particularly on 26th December when rain was falling (and some tourists began to be painful).
We booked Christmas ticket which was valid for 2 days including Christmas Day, nice and sunny but also convenient when no public transport working.

Nice clean double decker open top busses that take you in circles via different colored-route maps in London city. Tour guide in one particular bus was really hilarious and kept the moody jolly on a wintery cold day in December. Easy drop-off and climb-on to the hundreds of visiting locations in London. Decent frequency and medium wait times. You'll enjoy this, like we did.
Bought two tickets for this just before Christmas when we were in London for a couple of days is it worth it maybe if you use it but we did 1 hour so at over £70 for two that is very expensive

We had a good time on the tour, but it could have been better. First, our tour guide appeared to not really know some parts of the route. He said “it’s been a few months since I’ve worked this route so I’m a little rusty.” It was inappropriate to say all of that. Instead, he should have been prepared like any other job and did the necessary homework before showing up for work. Second, the exact details on where to catch the walking tour were vague at best. The tour guide said “meet at the bus stop at 11:00 am.” My wife and I showed up 15 minutes early, but searched around aimlessly for 30 minutes to no avail. When we finally asked another bus operator and found the right location they said “you just missed them by 15 minutes.” Not good. We were really looking forward to it. They really need to provide a detailed micro-map of exactly where the point of the walking tour starts to avoid confusion. I am sure other people had the same issue. Third, when you get off the bus to catch the river cruise there are no directions or exact map on where you catch the boat. Which side of the Thames is it? Which pier? Well, my wife and I searched aimlessly again before we stumbled upon the proper location after asking three different people. Totally unnecessary. The exact details should be included in the brochure. It should include a micro-map and exact pier location. Once we did get on the boat, the cruise was good with excellent views of London. It was as a nice roomy and comfy boat. Overall, our experience was average at best and could stand for improvement in several key areas. I hope the management addresses these important issues.

Bought 5 tickets on December 23. It was challenging to find the bus stops and when we did, the wait times were extremely long - far beyond the 15 to 20 minutes that were quoted. Other Hop on Hop off buses came by frequently while we waited. Be careful that you understand what the “24 hour” ticket means. We were only able to use about 30 minutes of our tickets due to the long waits. When I expressed concern to the Big Bus customer service- they simply told me all their policies and essentially as a customer you must do a better job reading all the fine print before you buy.

Enjoyed the hop on - hop off tour.
All I would say is, if you are doing this in the winter time, think yo bring a cloth and plastic bag. If you would like to sit up the top of an open bus and it has just rained, the seats are wet with nothing to wipe them with. The plastic bag helps to stow your wet cloth until you can get back to the hotel and hang it up to dry.
Other, travelling up the top is invigorating, dress appropriately, as it can get cold. The sights are fabulous sitting up the top.
Then took the river cruise to Greenwich to the Xmas Markets. Absolutely a great day. Allow an 1 hour to cruise down and about 1 1/2 to cruise back.

The Red Line is fantastic and possibly the only bus route worth the time (worth doing more than once).

The real treat is at 4:30pm where you can meet Big Steve at stop 1. He created a walking tour around Central London to see the Christmas lights and gives you the history of the buildings that you will not see up close on a bus. Some attractions include the Beatles, Harry Potter, Titanic and much more in which I won’t spoil. This is a very easy walk ~1 mile for almost 2 hours. Do not miss out on this!

We have done several of these Hop-on Hop-off bus tours throughout major cities. Generally liked them but found the actual route the buses travel to be long and inconvenient. With limited time to see the city, the loop takes a chunk of time to complete, ended Hopping-off and hired a cab to take us to the attractions we wanted to see.
Took the bus tour with some visiting American friends. We loved our tour guy wiki will, he made our trip very enjoyable.

We enjoyed multiple trips on the Red and Orange routes over the weekend. This is something that really is a must for anyone visiting London. I myself am very familiar with the city however I always enjoy refreshing my knowledge. You will find the live commentary an excellent enhancement to the experience. All guides are brilliant but I just want to say a big thank you to Ian who was commentating on the Red route on Sunday afternoon. We really enjoyed listening to him as he captivated us with his knowledge whilst also providing many laughs.

A HUGE Thank you Big Bus tour . We had a fabulous time in London . Your Bus made it so easy for us to get around & see lots of brilliant sights in London. My Mom and I were there to celebrate my Moms big Birthday & we had simply the Best time . I had planned each route and new which bus we needed to take with the help of your fabulous App . It was real value for Money and we would definitely use you again .
I would like to thank Jamie for his incredible knowledge of London and his friendly Approach, Also Tiffany who was just so lovely , chatted with is for a while and helped us when we had to leave the bus due to an accident down the road . Also Thank you to Paul Aka Father Christmas, we we fortunate to be passengers on the Christmas Bus & you’d really gone to town to make our trip extra special.
If you want to see London this is the company you need , absolutely Fantastic for the 3 days we were with them . Thank you 😊

London traffic was horrific . We started from Gloucester... n ‘patiently’ changed route at mid way to get on the red route ... and sat through till stop 18 to hop off... to go on the River Thames cruise . All these including bad traffic .. we were on the bus for close to 2 hrs .
We could have saved money and time .... and do so much more by taking the train , walking around ... n even covering the river cruise on our own .

We only hop off once at stop 18 for the river cruise. We didn’t hop back on as ... didn’t wanna get stuck on the bus for another 2 hours .

Buses didn’t have any digital indication of up coming stops . We had to tracked them manually or figured out in our own . There were recorded tour commentaries. But info didn’t match the tour map given . Hence it was slightly confusing.

The only lovely part was the Ricer Thames cruise .

After riding the subway for a few days we decided to take the Hop On - Hop Off Bus Tour. We had such a great experience and was able to see so much more of the city. Our host was Kathy and our driver was Wayne. Kathy was very enthusiastic and informative while Wayne was very nice and helpful. We rode with other people but these two stood out from the rest. Thank you for helping to make our trip to a London a lot more pleasurable and relaxing.

Booked the hop-on-off bus with the included Thames cruise. The whole expedition was fantastic. The day prior to us going on the bus there was a violent incident on London Bridge which meant it and surrounding roads and streets were closed. We were well informed of this and still had an excellent tour. The street staff were good and very polite. The on-board guides were fantastic. So knowledgeable. They made the tour well worth it. We even went back on the tour the next day (it’s a 24hour ticket). I would highly recommend this attraction.

After spending a day walking around London on foot, trying to see the different tourist attractions, we decided to get a Big Bus tour instead. Like most tours in major cities, it is a little pricier and we had great difficulty actually finding the stops to hop on and off. This review is mainly for our tour guide, Emma, who made this a five star experience alone. She was kind, well informed, and witty! She had a great knowledge of London history and she will keep you laughing so much, you won't even realize that you are learning!
Emma was great and explained everything as we saw it. Got to see all the sights then decide what we wanted to go back and see in more detail.

We thoroughly enjoyed our time on this tour. Unfortunately because we got a late start, we were only able to enjoy the Red Line and the Blue Line. The Red line has the “Live” guides, the blue line is recorded. Our kids enjoyed the red line better as our guide was witty, and shared details with humor and candor. It was easy to find all the stops and use all afternoon. We would highly recommend this tour, especially to families.

I had the privilege of taking the Big Bus Tour hop on/hop off bus last Saturday. I got on the red line at Green Park station and had the privilege of meeting Big Steve. He mentioned that big bus has a royal walking tour at 10am daily and encouraged i get off the bus to participate as he was delivering the tour. I decided to listen to him and was the best decision i could have made, Big Steve showed me around covent gardens and trafalgar square before the official walking tour began spotlighting the ins and outs of that very fun area.

During the formal tour there was a small group of us and Big Steve took us all around St James Park, and the quaint areas supporting Buckingham palace providing excellent commentary the whole way! The group was having such a great time and we were so sad to see the walking tour come to an end. Big Steve got permission to continue with us and provide us with an afternoon walking tour as well. We walked to Westminster Abbey, saw Big Ben, London eye, St Pauls cathedral, a roman temple and tower bridge area. I learned so much and had such a great time with the small group Big Steve lead. If you get a chance take this tour and make sure you take the walking component with Big Steve - you won't be sorry. He is an absolute super star!!!! If i could give him 6 starts I would :-)

What a great tour guide, Lewis! So much fun and interactive with everyone who was upstairs. He was very informative and obviously loved his job. Would highly recommend asking for the tour with Lewis. Ooh, and the included boat ride was good too.. A good way to view London.

I bought a two-day pass and wish I could rate this tour seperately for each day. The first day the bus (red route) was efficient and the tour guide (Anna/Emma??) was excellent. The second day (blue route), we spent 25 minutes at one stop while a group of 10 was let on the bus apparently without tickets. Instead of politely escorting them off to do the transaction, Adam proceeded to sell them all tickets while the rest of us waited. At one point he even got off the bus himself to get them change from a nearby market. A second bus stopped and left again while we waited. Then when we got to the next stop, it was the begining or ending of the route and we had to change busses and wait another 10-15 minutes for the tour to start again. Terrible start to the day. If that had been my only experience with this tour I would never recommend or book it again.

The traffic was terrible but it's London, the bus were cold I don't know how the drivers does it all day long and when I found a semi warm one we had to change in the middle of the tour. And I lost a glove in the process.

Emma was an awesome guide, I enjoyed the tour so much because of her knowledge on everything London. I would recommend the tour to anyone, they will not regret it at all, and try to get Ms Emma as your guide.

Most of the things to see are within blocks of each other. Your best bet, get an oyster card and ride the underground to Picadilly and walk everywhere from there! We purchased a 2 day and only used it half a day. We were the only ones on the bus and received personal info from the guide. Nice guy, but we should have just walked around.

I took the big bus for 3 days of my London trip. Everything went well, until the guy from st.paul cathedral Double charged my pass. He asked to contact via email/website to refund my credit card, but even with all photos and SS sent to BigBus , they're still refusing to refund the correct value. It's very disappointed being SCAMMED by this company that has such a good purpose for London city.

Very disappointed and not recommended.

Convenient stops, great phone app!
Our guide Rob did a great job with history and lively commentary.

Went with my 12 year old son for weekend to London it was our first trip so thought bus tour we would help as we don’t know the area. Great decision!! Well looked after during every aspect of our tour. Staff are brilliant friendly and helpful. At the bus stops they were so helpful with information and tips, onboard they are friendly and fun and just want to help you enjoy your time in London, learned lots of interesting facts and met lots of lovely people. Bus is clean plenty of headphones and leaflets. Great stops and great routes, no pushy sales people, top marks!!
We also took the river tour which we loved, another great way to see all the sights and I loved that they had a well stocked bar onboard too! again happy friendly staff there too.
I thoroughly recommend this tour bus and look forward to returning. Thank you Big Bus London

Big Red Bus Tours operating guided routes around London including a Thames river cruise. We did all the routes and the outstanding Tour guides were ‘Lewis’ on the Red route, not only funny but very good looking and another gentleman on the Thames river cruise’.
There is also a plug in guided tour in many languages which is great too.
We learnt so many thing.
Only con against it was the employees stood at bus stops around Marble Arch - very pushy to sell tickets to attractions.

I was very excited to take this bus as per the reviews. We hopped on the red line and our guide Lewis was amazing. We then went on the blue line and we were not impressed. No live commentary and the bus driver didn’t even give advanced notice on the upcoming stops. We then got back on a red line and the mic was not working so no commentary again. The reason we chose this bus tour was for a real guide. It was a waste of our time.

We used Big Bus in London, Norway, Ireland and loved each one. London was especially wonderful as we had a great guide. He was very information and so funny!! It is a great way to see London and then even go back on your own to visit a particular location. Totally worth it!

When the bus stop says Buckingham Palace I was under the impression you could see it from the bus but you could see little of any attractions. There was a protest the day we toured so a lot of stops were out of action, not that is was Big Bus fault.

We had the opportunity to spend time with “Rob” today as our tour guide. He was absolutely the best of the best. He was helpful, he was funny, he was informative and made our experience very memorable. The tour was a great way to see the sights of London. We would highly recommend the “hop on-hop off experience “

Thanks Rob!!
Lewis our tour guide was awesome! Very informative and hilarious! Can o only hope we get one as good as him next time

London has a bewildering number of excellent attractions--- so a "hop on/off" tour offers great explanations, and the flexibility to stay as long as one wants. What makes this tour" best"/most traveler friendly is the "package which also allows cancellation (up to 24 hours in advance), one can redeem a voucher at any stop, and, it also includes a river tour and a walking tour (which I truly enjoyed! It stops at most places of interest to travelers-- but it is best to book a 2 or 3 day tour if you want to see london during the day and at night-- on land and water and walking too. The "value added" will become obvious when recalling the many "Joys of London"!

I hope that this Review has been helpful.
Had a great time seeing the city and stopping at most of the mayor not spots. Great way to check out where you want to come back to and visit.

Great way to see a lot of the main city in a short time
lots of places to stop off at and the different routs cover much of what you want to see
sitting up-top is best.

For the benefit of others It was a visit with my Brother to the tour not solo. we are both in our 20's so no other box seemed applicable.

This tour defiantly needs some work. Yes it does take you to the main attractions, however there are a lot of irrelevant stops which makes completing the circuit very time consuming. By the end of the day we felt that we had run out of time to see everything we wanted due to the constant stops at random locations causing big delays. We also did the Big Bus Tour in Paris which offered free rain coats when it was raining, however the London bus did not offer this service.

If you want to see it all, and only have a few days, this is the best way to do that! The buses come every 15 to 20 minutes and the map is very easy to follow! There is an app for your phone as well! You can stop and see what you want or just stay on the bus and view the sites! They have headphones for you to listen to a commentator or a pre-taped message. They tell you in real time what you were looking at and which direction to look! It was very informative and a great way to see a lot of things on a short time frame! There are always workers there to help guide you to get on the right bus! For us, we started with the red line. It’s seem to have the most highlights of London! On the second day we chose the blue line and that took us out to Kensington Palace in Nottinghill.
For us, we started with the red line. It seem to have the most highlights of London! On the second day we chose the blue line and that took us out to Kensington Palace and Nottinghill. You can buy a one day pass or a two day pass! I highly recommend this for anybody who is here for a short period of time and does not want to navigate them selves through the city! Let somebody do it for you and sit back and enjoy!

I was unimpressed with this tour. I had taken The Original Tour years ago and expected a similar experience. We bought this one based on a recommendation from our hotel that said they had the most frequent buses. We did not find this to be the case. All the signs say you will wait 5-20 minutes for a bus but we waited over an hour everywhere which meant we only got to see about half of what we wanted in our one and only day in London. While we were standing there waiting several buses for the Original Tour came and went. The buses were very crowded as well which was disappointing as we could not even plug in our headphones or hear the live guide unless you were lucky enough to get a seat upstairs. This was a weekday in mid-October so we were not expecting standing room only conditions. Some folks with baby carriages were denied boarding because there was no room and told to wait for the next bus (probably an hour away!) and I felt so bad for them with several cranky children in tow. Obviously they were not running enough buses for the amount of tickets they had sold that day. We would have been better off and saved $100 with an oyster card.
We got this tour because it was due to rain that afternoon and it was great. Our guide was Rob and he was excellent. The commentary was great and all the history was extremely interesting.

Bus was very nice.
Day we went there were protests so trip very long as driver had to go around different ways. Streets blocked off. Staff were a bit agitated. However saw sights.

Nothing wrong with the Big Bus Hop On Hop Off Tour which has great routes and well located stops. However, it was undercut by the London traffic which made navigating the city a very long, time consuming affair. This coupled with lots of construction and many detours made it not the best choice to get around. The Underground was a better option of getting to the sights. However, even the "tube" had weekend shutdowns of some lines that hampered access to some areas.

Hopped on the red line tour around 11am and spent the next hour or so in traffic with our fabulous host Emma. She was extremely informative and passionate about her job. Hands down the best tour guide we had while in London. She had information outside of the major checkpoints which made our tour much more exciting. My favorite was the building that still had damage from WWI. Emma knew a lot about the history of London which played a key role in her ability to project information.

I would recommend this tour if you have limited time to visit London. I was only there for a day and a half and this tour exceeded my expectations BUT I only got off the bus once to transfer from the blue to orange line. Upon exiting Paddington Station, I didn’t really know where to go to catch the bus but a Big Bus Tour worker named Dennis was very helpful and FUNNY! He was friendly and kept me company while I waited for the bus. I thought I was going to catch the red line at that stop but he ushered me onto the blue line and told me to get off at the next couple stops to catch the red line. Now, the wait times between trains and the amount of traffic was overwhelming so it’s honestly better to pick a line and stay on the bus because it’s inevitable to get around in a timely manner if you’re pressed for time.

Have used the big bus company many times before and I can say with all certainty that I will NEVER be using this service ever again buses over crowded wait times can be anywhere from 30 to 60mins buses and drivers needing 25min breaks after picking up passengers leaving them to wait that time before taking them to their payed for destination.
