A nice way to see pretty much the same sites you'll see taking the red line, but it's worth it! I recommend trying hopping-on at the London Eye stop so you will be sure to get a seat when it starts. This tour does not seem to have live commentaries.

*River cruise*
The river cruise was great, almost better than the bus. The crew acts as the tour guides and comment on the beautiful views. Don't really know if it is worth going all the way out to Greenwich and Isle of Dogs. I liked it but it takes an extra hour to get there and back.

We just returned from a weekend in London. Since it was Pride day on Saturday there were TONS of extra people in the city and many road closures. The bus guides were amazing at keeping you entertained during the traffic (Chris and our guide from Ireland, I can't remember her name!) and helping you figure out what alternate stops would work for you with the closures. I have two kids (12 and 8) and we decided to do the Little Legs walking tour (completely free with your ticket). This is super cute for kids. Our guide Joe was the best, he rolled with it even though we ended up in the middle of the pride march! He steered us around and even showed us some different things that normally are not on the kids tour. We enjoyed our tour with Joe so much we met up with him Sunday morning for the changing of the guards tour (also included). He knew exactly where to be so we could see the old and new guard up close! Thank you Big Bus for keeping us rolling, entertained, and safe! Definitely see Joe for the walking tours!
Thank you to Valdas (our tour guide) and Inzie (our driver) for a safe and information packed tour on the red line. Great job guys!
Fantastic day, extremely funny guide called Christopher. Kept us laughing throughout. Very knowledgeable. Would definitely recommend.

Our morning (July 5th, 2019) started off by downloading the Big Bus Tours app and going to stop 32 on the blue line early so that we could meet the first bus. However the street that this stop is on is closed, and had been for a couple of days according to the shop owner. However this fact was not listed on the Big Bus Tours webpage, or in their amendment section of their app (though other stop closures were) - awesome.
Also, thought it started working later in the morning, at 8:10 am local time, through 9am (when I stopped checking) their GPS bus locator was not turned on (there was no issue with my mobile phone settings).
So we raced to the next stop, and the bus, which was 10 minutes early according to the apps information of when the first bus would arrive, was pulling away as we arrived.

Another bus would not come for 45 - yes 45 minutes. Every other tour company had multiple buses that came during that time. and that was the story of the day, buses were so slow to come, they were generally already full, which led to frustrated guests and long lines. Every other tour vendor had multiple buses that passed during that time, all had plenty of seats. In the time we waited for another bus to come, there were four Golden tour buses. We ended up having to wait over 45 minutes for a bus while the website advertises a bus arrives every 15–20 minutes. Once on the bus, there were no indications that there were circumstances that should’ve caused such a delay.

The Big Bus tour guide who finally showed up to the stop (Blue line, 33) seemed to have no idea why the app's GPS feature wasn't working for us (or 2 other families waiting to board) and also had no idea why it was taking such a long time for a bus to come.

Also, there is a TON, and I mean a TON of music that plays during the tours. there is actually very little talking or learning about London that goes on compared to the amount of time that you are actually on the bus. If you take the red line, you will likely have a live tour guide, which is great because they can fill in the dead space and keep the tour interesting. On every other line, you will have the pre-recorded tours, which is fine, but there is just so little talking or learning about London compared to how much time you spend on the bus. Obviously there is a lot of traffic in London, and I am amazed that Big Bus Tours doesn't do a better job of "filling in" the dead time with random facts about London - anything, and I mean ANYTHING would be better then listening to the same boring music the entire tour.

Also, on the blue line, the pre-recorded tour seemed to be 5 seconds too slow. The pre-recorded tour would say "and now on the right you'll see..." except that we had just passed whatever it was that they were trying to point out. this was the case for every tour related item on that particular bus we were on for the Blue route.

when you got off the bus, you were generally screwed at that point, because getting back on was a longshot. The buses were generally full (especially along the red route) and most stops had significant lines (though only Big Bus).

In the midst of all of this, our bus had a "ticket check" where a Big Bus employee gets on, and goes around to check everyone's ticket. This is a very long process, where people go back and forth with the Big Bus ticket agent (often in multiple languages) about their ticket status. All the while you swelter in the sun, during this 10-15 minute unannounced stop - oh and more music through the headphones (what a great opportunity to learn more about London and take your mind off the fact you are getting pounded by sun sitting somewhere instead of exploring the city!!)

****The point of a bus tour company is to actually see London, you would be advised to choose another tour company that seemed to have more buses and/or less guests traveling on them.****

The significant amount of money spent on the Big Bus tour felt that it could have been much better used on a different tour company. Golden tours seemed to have way more buses, and empty ones at that, though all of the other tour companies were much better than Big Bus Tours, at least on July 5th.

PS - Fred, the tour guide on the red line, did a very nice job.
Great way to see the sights of London hopping off and on where you please. Never more than 10 mins between buses. We got the 24 hour pass which worked for us.

This is a great way to see any city ,my husband and I frequently use the hop on hop off in any big city where we travel to get a quick easy highlight tour of the city ,and then you can decide where you really wanna spend your time ,and London is no exception. It’s nice to wear the headphones to stay in touch with what you’re actually passing ,although it is a little bit of a solo experience when you do that because you obviously cannot talk to the person you’re traveling next to , I like one in ,one earplug out.

We took the red tour with Mehmet on July 1. It was a great way to spend Canada Day! Mehmet was great - energetic, entertaining and super informative. We followed up on his tip for a great place for High Tea - the Delauney - and loved it. Great value! Thanks, Mehmet for the great tip!
Went on the Big Bus Tour, our first tour guide, Lewis, was GREAT. The trip was fun and exciting. Combine your ticket with other attractions to get more for your money.

Did the red tour and the river cruise. This is our first activity in a new city and the tour served the purpose. Our guide was OK. The traffic in the city makes the tour challenging and would recommend Sunday morning when the traffic is lighter.
Unorganized, packed, hot, not worth the money, like public transportation . The original London bus we saw was less crowded.
Our your guide Roland did a great job of explaining the tiniest trivia. He was very knowledgable and extremely patient.

So disappointing. And a waste of money. The tour guide didn’t speak great English and was very hard to understand. The buses were jam packed full and there was no one to coordinate all the people. We then decided to try a route with a recorded tour guide and the recording barely gave us any information at all. The customer service was terrible. We asked for info on when the orange route was coming and was told ‘just do the red route’ as it was ‘just the same’ as the red route, which we’d already done. No one was helpful or even particularly polite and it was an all round quite stressful experience. I’ve been to London a few times and have enjoyed getting around by public transport more than I enjoyed this tour. This was my Australian husband’s first time in London and I wanted to show him around, and he was very disappointed with the experience. We only had one day in the city and this experience ruined it. I have tried to contact customer service to give my feedback and still haven’t heard back 2 weeks later, no one ever answers the phone and they haven’t responded to my email. I will be letting all our Scottish and Australian friends and family to not ever do this tour. DON’T WASTE YOUR MONEY!
Emma was our tour guide for this Hop-on-Hop-off tour. She was the very best we have ever had on pour ten year use of Hop-on-Hop-off buses.

It was a lovely part of our tour and we enjoyed every bit of it. Great way to know about the complete city and visit a lot of attractions in a day. It is certainly worth taking multiple days tour and enjoy the complete London. This also included one-way Thames Cruise.

What a great way to see London. Nice and sunny day sitting up top of the bus. Emma was an amazing tour guide. Recommend her for any tour. Very knowledgeable with London history. Enjoyed her commentary.
Emma from Big bus tours London was a wealth of knowledge and gave us a wonderful trip around London and some helpful advice Thanks Emma
Our second guide Karen was knowledgeable, witty, interesting and friendly with useful information even beyond the scope of the tour. The prior guide was too distracted by his neighbors.

In February half term holiday, five of us went on the big bus trip, including 2 children who were really looking forward to it. It was quite possibly the biggest waste of £125 I have ever spent. The bus was overcrowded, packed with standing passengers in the gangway. Couldn't sit on top as it had rained and there were no ponchos available and the seats were wet, the 'guide' told us to sit downstairs. The 'commentary' was not relayed downstairs and we only got the occasional shouted out comment from the driver, which was rubbish. We travelled 3 stops and got off and went to Tower of London. When we came to catch the bus later on we were advised by another bus company that 'big bus tours' had finished for the day (around 5.10 p.m.). We had to get a cab back to Marylebone. Since that time I have been in touch with big bus tours by phone and e.mail on numerous occasions. They initially made all the right noises about looking into my complaint, giving us a 'ticket number' for our complaint etc. They then employed stalling tactics like asking us to provide a copy of our bus ticket which we had already done! It is now July (almost 6 months later) and they have completely stopped responding to any kind of communication. E.mails elicit no response and their phone line is never answered. Clearly they have no intention of addressing our complaints and are just hoping that we will get fed up and go away. I'm sure that they do have many happy customers but if you fall victim to a really poor experience, as we did, don't expect much in the way of customer service - you won't get any!! On this basis I really couldn't recommend this company when there are plenty of others to choose from. Be warned.

My family and I absolutely loved our tour guide Emma. What a wonderful, intelligent tour guide! Not only did she know her history, pop culture, and present day information about London; she gave amazing advice on how to plan your day utilizing not only their bus system but also incorporating it with other transportation systems like the ferry. This to me is valuable information for tourists who have limited time in England. Not only that, she would tell us ahead of time when to take pictures and where! Her charisma, enthusiasm, and candor really set the tone for our brilliant day trip in London.
If I could stay on the bus with our tour guide EMMA all day I would, she was amazing and very knowledgeable you become very engaged in the history of London.

We were on the Red Line tour on Friday & Saturday, June 28th & 29th, and were standing for the most of the time, it was our worst experience in London. The first bus on Friday had no commentary, either live or recorded, so we had to change the bus but the guide wasn’t great, he was simply reading by the script, without giving any additional information. Changed buses again and the next bus had a live guide which was excellent. On Saturday morning most of the buses were jammed full so waiting times were so long. Very disappointing.

Was in London for 3 nights. First and last days were travelling days so I had only 2 full days in London. Booked a 1 day pass and intended to spend the second day shopping.
The pass provides for a river cruise, hop on hop off bus tour and entrance to attractions.

Unfortunately, after the river cruise and time needed to travel between attractions, I did not get to visit more than a couple. A 2 day pass would be a minimum to make it worthwhile.

We only had a day to check out London, and riding the London hop-on hop-off bus tour was the best sightseeing tour that we could get at a decent price! We get to see everything there is to see, and we can hop off whenever we want to for more of an immersive experience, and then we can hop on the bus again to the next destination.

There buses come with audio commentary you can listen in with earbuds on each seat. Some buses also have Live Guides that give a more personalized commentary of the places to see.

You can find discounted tickets from supported hotel concierges. We went to the Hilton Hotel by London Euston station, and that’s also the area of one of the buses pick up point. Our tickets also came with the river cruise so we were able to see the sites via the River Thames.

If you’re ever going to visit London for the first time, I recommend taking this tour. Worth the price!

Took the bus on Friday 28th June. Saw most of the major sights and traffic was busy but that what you expect in London. Suggest downloading the app to help find bus stops easier. Our tour guide was Valdas and was very knowledgeable.

Vladaas made the beginning of our London vacation enjoyable and informative. Thank you!! A lot of information given and the drop off options are many. We took it in the afternoon on our first day as a way to orient ourselves. The next day we “hoped” off the really see the different attractions.

THe big bus tours offers you the chance to see all the major.tourist sights and you can come on and get off at any point of the day.
THE red line has a live guide our guide christopher was a lovely man very funny and helpfull we stayed with him for the whole tour and he even gave us tips what to do after leaving the bus
We were on the Big Bus Red line and really enjoyed our guide, Emma. Very entertaining and informative.

Emma was a wonderful tour guide. There was a lot to see on the bus and she had a way to share the most pertinent information without it feeling rushed. The bus itself had some headphones that did not work and the bus was a bit crowded, but besides that the tour was well worth the price. It was a great way to see London on a limited amount of time.
We have done big bus tours in other cities, but the one we did in London with our guide Emma was absolutely amazing. She knows so much and really takes the time to explain everything to everyone

On a trip to London that had so many memorable moments, the Big Bus Tour was the highlight. I went on this tour yesterday and it was fantastic. Our wonderful tour guide, Emma, shared her impressive knowledge of London history while affably conversing with all of us and getting to know us personally. The next time I am in London I will DEFINITELY book this tour again and will recommend it to all my friends and family as well.

Really enjoyed the tour. The driver was good and squeeze through the city traffic!. Trip guide Emma was excellent and brilliant. Her commentaries gave a great deal of information about London and Britan. Wish you a happy birthday Emma.

Venoden from Sri Lanka
Great overall introduction to the city. Emma is a jewel of a live commentator. She clearly loves her home city and is a front of knowledge and wit.

Beautiful day. Great way to see the sights of the city and to plan what you want to explore next. Emma, our tour guide (Happy birthday!) was just the right mix of informative stories and sense of humour. She was also very concerned about passenger safety. Trip was longer than expected due to the traffic, but certainly not the company's fault. Highly recommend

Did the Big Bus tour of London today. Picked it up outside of Victoria Station. Christopher was our tour guide. He was fantastic. Made us laugh and taught us a lot about the city. Highly recommend to folks looking to get a good overview of London.

Got on the tour bus at Victoria after a day to HP Studios. Needed a way to get back to our station and see more of London without walking so much. Emma provided the amazing commentary based on her life in London and family heritage. It was great and added so much to our trip! She is a jewel! She knew exactly when to lift a camera and prepared us for the shot, too!

Our tour guide, Emma, was very entertaining and educational.

Thank you Big Bus! We had a great time.
Great day out. Very informative with great historical touches from our awesome guide Emma. She added an extra dimension to London.
Even when we had to change route because of road closures Lewis was funny and gave us lots of fun facts. His style of commentary was super informative and fun!
Lewis was an exellent guide On our trip with the red line On tuesday 22. June. Nice and funny comments White he pointed out the sights.

I absolutely loved my experience with this company. Emma was delightful and very intelligent. I would definitely recommend seeing the city from the top of a tour bus. It allows for a different perspective. Amazing opportunity while in London.

Original plan to ride the Tube was quashed due to closures and this became our backup for travel around the city. What a happy accident it turned out to be! Our tour guide Emma was exceptional; fun and informative, she was a wonderful guide to the sites of the city.

Everytime you hop in you get a different tour guide. Some guides were a little bit boring, some were entertainting. You can use the underground public transportation to move around town, but by using the Hop-On Hop-Off Tour you get to enjoy the view and learn a little bit about the area.

I hated this tour! The bus stops were not clearly marked on the map or at the sidewalk! They were terrible to try and find. The bus company closed down two of them without notice because of traffic reroutes so people were stranded. They also stop operating extremely early which I don’t understand because after the attractions close it would be a perfect time to take a bus tour but they are probably just trying to sell more tickets. Our tour guide was rude and his cometary was boring. All in all a HUGE disappointment!!!!
When you’re in London, this isn’t worth your money. The attractions are just a mile or two away from each other, it’s better to just walk or take UBER.

This was our first trip to London and we didn’t know where to begin but we knew we wanted to see everything. This bus tour was absolutely great. They have many stops, ours was a block from our hotel. You can hop-on and hop-off anywhere. What I recommend is starting early in the morning, tour the entire city once and then map out where you want to go back to and spend some time. Also the river cruise was great.
I would have given a 5 but the live tour guides weren’t very good. They have a prerecorded tour which I recommend. One of our guides was only speaking to a couple directly in front of him and you could almost never hear him. Another guy barely spoke and wasn’t funny or entertaining at all.
Still, the bus alone is worth it, plus they have free WiFi on the bus which helps you plan your route and find places while you’re on the bus. Lastly, the river cruise is great and I highly suggest doing it. It’s included with your bus pass.

You can ride this bus for free. All you have to do is grab a map and hop on. Our tickets were never checked once. Busses did not run as often as we were told (every 15 minutes). We waited 45 minutes the first day for a bus to come. When busses FINALLY did arrive, they were extremely packed because it took so long to come back around. There was only a guide on the red line (if you were lucky). Drivers were always in a hurry rushing people in and out, that questions weren't even an option. Some stops weren't recognizable because there were no signs or no guide outside for help.

The London Bus Tour were coming around every 10-12 minutes. There was always someone at the stop to ask questions while you waited. I am not sure how much this one was but I would recommend this line over Big Bus.

I got 2 day tickets for 5 people and it was a blast. At stop #1 there were probably 6 or 8 bus people to answer questions and help with tickets, etc. First loop around the Red Line had a live guide speaking into a microphone and we were all issued hear phone plugs to listen. There is also a recorded commentary available at every seat in 13 languages. The 2 day ticket included a guided tour of the changing of the guards and a river boat ride which we did not take because of weather. Overall, I recommend this to anyone (don't listen to complaining grandkids!)

We were in London for only two days. The day we landed, we dropped our stuff off at the hotel and then jumped onto the closest hop on/hop off stop. What's great is we bought a 2 day pass that starts once you activate your ticket at the first stop you get on. We had bought our tickets before we went on vacation and there were agents there to help get everything started. We used many of the different routes based on what landmark we wanted to visit. Make sure to listen to the tour guide They provide ear phones for you and you can select which language or you can listen to the live guide.

We had a hard time finding the first pick up point, Either the bus was very slow getting to Euston station ( we waited 45 min) or it didn't stop there. We ended up picking up our first bus at Kings' cross. Most of the narration is recorded. A couple of the drivers were nice and were helpful when we asked questions, but many of them couldn't be bothered and one was down right rude. When the bus makes a stop it doesn't always tell you where you are getting off, either the stop number or name. If We go back to London we'll try the Underground or a Black Cab.

Do not waste your money on this tour. The frequency of the buses is the worst in all companies, we used to stand there waiting for a bus for 30 minutes, while other companies’ buses passed by like 3-4 times at least. Even when you find the bus, it’s super busy! We were also faced with excessive rudeness from their sales representative.

There was no tour guide during the ride. It was all recording. But the worse part of it all was the ride experience. Majority of the stops had no one there to guide the passengers. The driver didn't do anything to help and the bus was filed with many standing. Three out of four tour bus was not in service. It is a complete rip off
She is amazing!!! Best tour guide so far!!! We have been here for 3 days. Emma had the best energy and most helpful information:))

Spent two days using the Hop On Hop Off Bus in London. We had a very informative tour guide one morning, Gareth, he was very knowledgeable. This is a great way to get around London and see a good portion of the well know sights. Would highly recommend.

We showed up at the end of the day, and particularly wanted a bus with a live person speaking. Emma was great and the tour bus didn't feel like forced tourism. You could tell Emma loved her job, despite the fact that she had to deal with loud Greeks (dad on phone, and 5 year old child just running his mouth making noise for no reason), she kept a positive tone, and made sure we could hear her. And it was raining so in the upper deck people didn't want to sit on wet seats although she had to correct it for safety, Despite all of those problems, she kept it cool and enjoyable. That level of patience and professionalism speaks volumes to fact that she enjoys her work and it shows.

I would still do the hop-on hop-off tour but when it got to be later in the afternoon not all routes were running and it was difficult to figure out how to get to the stop to walk back to our hotel. I do recommend buying admissions tickets from their agents ahead of time

We have used Big Bus tours in both Paris and Rome, and was excited to use it again in London. Unfortunately, we were a little disappointed by the lack of buses, long waits at certain stops, and overcrowding. I do understand that there were road closures and construction going on, but our "real time tracker" reported only 4 buses running on the line at the time. For such a busy city I would expect a few more to accommodate the demand.

In any case, everything else about the tour was exceptional. One of our live commentators CARON was EXCELLENT!! She had a great personality, was quite funny, and very informative! It was nice to hear her live commentary over the prerecorded audio that comes with the tour. Thank you again CARON!!

On all of the buses the audio kept cutting out and the tour guides (who were the only good thing about the experience) couldn’t do their job and we would have to yell to them that it wasn’t working. The staff members were rude and hostile and told us they would not scan our tickets, which meant that we couldn’t access our tickets to the boat tour, which is what our tickets included. One staff member finally begrudgingly scanned our ticket because he said his shift was about to end. Moreover, the last bus was supposed to start at 6 but the staff were falsely saying it was over and discouraging us from getting on the bus.
Also it doesn’t make sense that tickets must be printed (which was not made clear) how are all the tourists supposed to access printers? It’s 2019, all you need is an iphone to scan a bar or QR code.
On a positive note, we had a 40-something caucasian gentleman tour guide who was fantastic-polite, super friendly, passionate about what he was talking about, knowledgeable, fun, and putting a great effort into his job. That man should be running this company. Kudos to him, the only good thing about this experience.
Lewis did a fantastic job as our tour guide on the hop on / off bus tour! Great sense of humour and really made the tour an enjoyable experience!

Audio was pre-recorded, very sparse, and rudimentary content. In short, the bus trip (Red & Blue Route) was extremely boring! Literally a waste of 100+ pounds for 2 adults & 1 child. Very Disappointed! It was our granddaughters first tour of London...ever. What a waste!

Very comprehensive tour with great views of the city, all of the stops are nicely planned and this is an absolutely good way to get around the city because the distances are far too long to just walk around.
During this tour we had live commentary on board from Valdas who stated many interesting facts and in a really efficient way!! He gave us really good insight on the city and its various historical points of interest.

Great trip on this tour, Ian was very knowledgable about the places. We saw so much more than we thought we would.

Buckingham palace was a little disappointing as bus stop at back of place and we didn’t have time to stop at this point.

We got the 48 hour package and got alot of use out of it. We were staying in Shoreditch and were able to walk down to Tower of London and hop on. We used it both for touring and transit. Buses were constant which is impressive considering traffic and tonnes of construction. Good service would recommend.

Big Bus offers great routes through London, and the drivers are courteous and safe. But that assumes you’re able to get ON a bus. It seems Big Bus is overbooked, and undersupplied, so not only do you regularly wait long spans between buses at any given stop, it’s also very likely you’ll have to wait a few buses to get onto the vehicle.

From our experience of standing at various stops, waiting for Big Bus, there are at least two other bus companies that offer more frequent buses, with less people, following the same route.

My boyfriend and myself used the big bus tour for our first time in london. We enjoyed every single route taken on and especially enjoyed tours from roland and josh. Two very different tours but both equally enjoyable and informative.

I loved the tours and especially the live commentary on the Red line from Emma. It was like meeting one's London pen-pal and embarking on a tour. She's an historian and fascinated by why things came to be 'that way'. All the recorded commentaries on the other routes were fine, but it was even more fun to go back and forth on questions like: "why ' The ROYAL Navy' but just 'The Army'?", (when London traffic slowed the bus down). Emma even had family connections to some sights - her grandmother was the model for the lovely lady on the Bank of England pediment (Emma mentioned a more 'arty' depiction of her nan, but I didn't feel proper gazing on a lady's grandmother in that state of 'reveal', especially after only one tour together). And, having just ended a driving tour of Britain, rather than being upset with the traffic I was just relieved somebody else was driving this time. Another nice thing about taking the bus is, if a traveler has difficulty with stairs, as my friend does, the Underground has a lot of them, on the buses the top level is voluntary! I enjoyed similar tours in most of the cities I visited this time, none more than The Big Bus with charming Emma.

Mark Ligget, from Texas

We did the Big Bus for a couple days and loved it. Great way to see the city! We were on and off many times so had several different tour guides but by far the best were Lewis and Tiffany. Only had Tiffany for a short ride but she was friendly and very informative. Took the entire loop with Lewis who went above and beyond in greeting every passenger, asking where they were from, and then greeting them in their native language. He was very energetic, funny, and knowledgeable! Great job!

This tour was perfect for us because we did not have a lot of time. Courtney was very informative and sweet and Lewis was very charismatic and captivating with his presentation. Just what we were looking for!

The information on the stops are incorrect causing us issues and delays. Apparently the large parts of the sign that clearly state which big bus service (eg blue, red service) stops here are updated by transport for London and the hard to see info below it is the up to date stuff. Found the information on the tour to be lacking and repetitive. Was very underwhelming and not worth the price they charge.

We tried taking this tour last week and bought the tickets on a very wet day. We waited for the bus for 30 minutes before we boarded which we were told was arriving in 10 min. The bus was completely full and we ( as well as many others) had to stand in the isles. We couldn’t see anything and there was no live guide on the bus. Once we were able to sit 2 stops later we got to listen to the recorded narrated tour, which turned out to be completely worthless. We got off at our first site of interest but the bus stop was quite a walk away and no one guided us as to where we were supposed to go. We clearly never returned to the bus and used the underground for the remainder of the day. This was absolutely worthless, uncomfortable and a complete waste of time and money.

We got this tour thinking it was the best but after waiting for 30 or more minutes in the rain for each bus and then getting on to a standing room only bus was just not a pleasant experience. We did not get to see much of London at this rate. Best to go with another tour company with more regular buses or less people.

Had a fabulous guide , Emma, on the red line yesterday! Her knowledge of modern day London and historical London was amazing !
I would recommend Big Bus Tours if you are looking for a friendly and helpful London Tours!
Most Accomodating !!!!! Loved Emma !!!!!!!

We were on the tour this afternoon (June 11th 2019), we took the entire 2 plus hour tour to see all the sights before deciding what are all the places we wanted to see.
We had just finished the change of the guards at Buckingham Palace.

Emma was outstanding in ensuring we get a complete overview of history, trivia, humor and comparisons of the various places on the Red Tour.

Her passion and enthusiasm for what she does and how motivated she is to ensure all of us tourists get as much information , in as easy a style to understand as possible, sure did stand out.

Wishing her the very best and all success.
Kudos to Big Bus to have such passionate but professional tour guides

Thank you again Emma
Good wishes
Pradhan Achaiah

First time to London and decided to try a tour bus. OMG give Gigi an award! She is an incredible guide - very knowledgeable but has amazing customer service and banter. We loved her! I got on another bus for another area and was disappointed not to have the same experience with another guide.

This was an awful experience. They had very poor and rude customer service, they lied about times and also sold tickets when the "busses weren't running" We lost an entire day in London trying tot chance down the bus. I would give zero stars if I could.

We did This tour on 09.06.2019 with tour Guide Valdas he did a great job, we enjoyed it a lot!
Thank you Valdas! You‘ve been very nice and very informative!

Today was the first time me and my wife had a bus tour in London. It was really interesting and we had been so lucky to have perfect weather to sit on the top of the bus too! We were especially lucky to have josh as our tour guide!! He was brilliant at his job, and his knowledge of London was very impressive.
He interacted with everyone sitting on the bus, and he was funny too! Making the tour even more enjoyable!

Our whole family loved this experience!! I have no negatives to write! Staff was great. There was someone at every stop helping! Our tour guide in the morning was Louis and he had tons of knowledge, tips, and funny stories! Loved it!!!!

I tend to travel a lot and so i normally take big bus around the world however it wasn’t what I expected it to be it was extremely crowded on the buses and very less stops near the tower side other then that the staff were helpful

We had the 3 day pass and beautiful weather...perfect way to see all the highlights of this fabulous city! My husband is 65 and in good shape, but the bus offered much needed relief to the miles of walking we were doing each day. With limited time in a huge city, these tours just really helped us know how to plan our days.

We bought a single day ticket to see London. It was the first full day of our honeymoon! What great value! Valdas provided real time descriptions/history of the sites as we traveled through the city. He was friendly, always asking patrons if they had any questions and reminding everyone frequently that the bus would be making diversions late afternoon as a result of taxi protests in the city. What a great guide! We would recommend the bus tour for sure!
Rolland was our third guide and by far the best! Had a lot of great commentary and very funny!! We were on the buses on Thursday the 6th.
Took the tour with Emma, very informative and lots of laughs ! Thank you Emma - keep spreading info re London in your fetching style

bought a 3 day pass on Big Bus hop on hop off in London with the intent to use instead of taxis or tube. BIG MISTAKE! First day did the green link and red line to tower of London, took HOURS due to traffic. I know that its not the companies problem with the traffic, however coming back from the tower of London, the driver didn't stop for the most important stop to link back up to the green line. there were about 20 passengers that had to get off at the London Eye stop and walk back, it took so long that we missed the last bus on the green link and had to walk back to the British Museum area. Not good! skip the hop on and take the tube!

We started at 10 am, blah cruise guide, but when we got on Georgina’s bus.... what a refreshing young girl! She was super pleasant, we enjoyed every moment! She made everyone feel welcome. She told funny stories and filled the in between stops with youthful craziness! She was wonderful! Oh, and the bus ride was equally great with the exception of Trumps visit slowing down the buses and the detours. This is your Leo friend if you read this Georgina!! My son is waiting for you!! Lol!

Our walking tour of Buckingham Palace was GREAT! Big Steve was not only extremely knowledgeable, he was fun! When you are on vacation you want people like Big Steve adding energy and excitement to your experience. Our Bus Tour was complete with Caron's expertise and humor!
Big Thumbs up to the Red Line
From
Boston

Total waste of time. Only used this as it was included in the London pass. Much of London is walkable/accessible via tube but really it’s the staff that let this hop on hop off down. We initially were sent in the complete opposite direction after asking a staff member which bus to get. Once we realised, we asked the bus driver where to get off to change. Once we got off, we asked the bus lady which bus to st Pauls and how long till the next one- she told us 8 mins so we started to walk off only to look back and see our bus arriving, so we ran back to jump on after confirming with her and the bus driver. That bus terminated some stops later which no one told us. Finally; an hour later we got to St. Paul’s and missed the last 4pm entry on our London pass. After contacting the big bus company directly they told us that it was London pass’s issue. Umm how??

We did this tour on our first full day (a Sunday) to get an overview. We took the red line, connected to the blue line, got off at Paddington Station to walk to Jason's canal boat trip (strongly recommend) which goes to Camden Locks. We then picked up the green line near St. Pancras station and completed the tour. The busses were not overcrowded and we got seats on the top of the bus. The guides were friendly and helpful. The map was clear and accurate.
Compared to other companies, we noticed significant less frequency of buses in every stop compared with competitors. Buses were crowded and wait times at stops were very long.

I would recommend getting on the bus and riding it all day to see attractions. We didn't do this, we got off to explore places and it took so much time. But what took most of the time was walking around from store to store trying to find a toilet and the guides on the bus have no clue. Its not like living in Canada when bathrooms are everywhere. We ended up getting stuck behind a protest and the bus operators told all the passengers to get off. I didn't think that was right as no one knew where to go. We stayed on for about 30 minutes until it ended and then continued on our journey but it made us way behind. We managed to get to Buckingham Palace but it wasn't until 6 pm. I would not take this bus tour again. We could have seen more doing it ourselves.
Emma was very knowledgeable and interactive. Big bus tour is one of the best way to do sightseeing around London

Very disappointing. We booked a 2 day tour. The Buses were so overcrowded. Impossible to get seats at the top. Bus drivers were very rude and so unhelpful. We bought our tickets at our hotel and found out we had been given an out of date map. This put us off course completely. When we joined the tour we weren’t given any headphones and didn’t receive any explanation about them. The weather was very very hot in London and the buses were not air conditioned. The biggest complaint we had was about the rude, unhelpful drivers. I would recommend us another company.

Having visited London many times before, we decided to treat ourselves to the Big Bus Tour for my birthday last week.
We had been on tours with them in Los Angeles and San Francisco, both of which were faultless and very entertaining, hence we decided to use the same company in London.
We booked the tickets online and easily collected them at Stop 1.
So far, so good, apart from hearing some of the Big Bus Tour staff using foul language whilst we were waiting.
Our first part of the tour was to get up to Marble Arch (stop 4), hop off and join the Orange tour bus up to Baker Street. We had to wait a good 30 minutes at Marble Arch, watching Red Route after Red Route bus go past, plus plenty of other tour company buses with plenty of empty upstairs seats.
Finally an Orange Route bus arrived and we boarded. only to find that there were no empty seats upstairs. Not much of a view from downstairs, but as we were only going a couple of stops, it wasn't a big issue.
Later, we decided to re-join the Orange Route bus at Baker Street and were fortunate to get seats upstairs. We plugged in to the commentary only to be met with Classical music playing on a loop. We set off on the tour and took in the sights, but found the commentary to be sporadic at best and becoming increasingly annoying as it was mainly the piped, irritatingly repetitive classical music and hardly any commentary.
We left the tour at Hyde Park Corner and decided to jump in a cab to the shops, as the Big Bus Tour buses were too few and far between for our liking.
In the evening, we took the 8pm night tour from Marble Arch - this was supposed to be the perfect end to my birthday in London!
When the bus arrived, the top deck was already full so we were forced to sit downstairs. Therein lies the first problem - the night tour is advertised as being Panoramic.... something which is utterly impossible to achieve from the lower deck of a bus.
You would think that, on a pleasant weather day, the tour operators would realise that everyone would want to sit upstairs and lay on extra open top buses?? Something I would imagine is pretty easy to acheive, seeing as they only have 3 tours per night and clearly have more than 3 buses and drivers.....
Regardless, we set off on our 'exciting' night tour and very quickly realised that we were heading for Baker Street again..... this area of London is not supposed to be included in the night tour - we had been expecting to see the bright lights of Oxford Street and Picadilly etc
Eventually, the bus did seem to find its way on to the correct route and we did see glimpses of some of the sights as the bus sped around the streets, clipping kerbs and performing emergency braking manouevres
We arrived back at Marble Arch about 90 minutes after departing and I thought I would just ask the driver about the change in route and why we hadn't seen the West End
The driver was incredibly rude and didn't even look up from his paperwork but just said, with a double helping of attitude, 'Oxford Street is closed'
I asked him why Oxford Street was closed and he, again without looking up, just said 'You'll have to ask the Metropolitan Police'
If he had been civil enough to speak to me like a paying customer, rather than something he was trying to scrape off the bottom of his shoe, I may well have left it at that but seeing as he had been so downright rude, I asked him for his driver number to which he replied 'I don't have a number'. I then asked him for his name and he said 'I don't have a name...... Good night'

We left the bus and I stood in front of it to take a photo of the registration plate and driver - when everyone had left the bus, the driver pulled away erratically and, in my opinion, with unneccessary aggression, as he had done throughout most of the tour.

If you want to start the day hearing foul language, waste a lot of your day in London waiting at Bus Stops, hear piped Greensleeves, Land of Hope and Glory and World in Union (stopping and starting about as often as the London traffic), Experience the lower deck bus view in a totally underwhelming UNpanoramic night tour of selected areas of the city whilst trying to avoid a whiplash injury and wondering whether the driver will actually mount the kerb and take out a pedestrian, finally culminating in being spoken to like dirt, then this is the tour company for you!!

If none of that particularly appeals, then do yourself a real favour and book with one of the other many, undoubtedly more professional, tour operators in the city.

Oh and thanks for partially ruining my birthday Big Bus Tours, thanks a lot.
Went on Big Bus tour, Emma was our guide she was fantastic. She was so knowledgeable really worth the time so much history, struggled to get off bus as it was so I interesting.

I certainly reccomend against using the hop-on-hop-off from Big Bus. They did not have near enough buses running. We had to wait at least 20-30 minutes each time we wanted to hop on. And when the bus did finally come there were not enough seats - we always had to stand. Plus, there were not enough radios to plug in your headsets to hear the audio part of the tour. We saw the other two companies that do the same thing coming and going many times - with open seats - as we all waited forever for our Big Bus to come.

After manny visits to London we finally decidet to take this tour with our 9 y old kid. We had to wait more than an hour for a bus because 2 that came were not taking ppl in ( interval was supposed to be 7-15 min according to the ticket guy) . In the mean time Original Tour and Golden Tours busses were passing by in regular shorter intervals.Taped commentary was "dry" and live commentator was a nice but hardly understendable gentleman.

Don't use this bus, making transfers are so confusing. In addition, they are always late.
Go for other buses like the Original or Golden Tours instead. I noticed that they have more buses and ply the roads more often.

The Big Bus tour was an outstanding experience for me and my wife. Even though we live in the UK in Essex, we never had a chance to go on a guided tour of London. I must admit that we came to know more about London in 3 days of our Hop-on-hop-off tour of the city than we did in the last 4-5 years.

I found the drivers and the guides very helpful. I would specially like to mention Tiffany, and very bright and confident lady with a great sense of humour. She said that it was very first day as a Big Bus tour guide, but she really sounded like a pro. She was very energetic, knowledgeable and witty. It was a pleasure to have had her as our guide.

I would also highly recommend Chris, a smart and helpful gentleman. He was our tour guide for the walking tour on the bank holiday Monday. Even though the planned trip was changed due to the 10K Vitality Run, Chris made it a point to take us to all the interesting and important attractions of the tour, and enlightened us with lots of interesting facts and figures in a very relaxed and informal way.

Both my wife and I would highly recommend the Big Bus Tour.

KD and Soma

Excellent tour guide! Good explanations
Facilities good !
Would highly recommend!
Would do it again!

The Big Bus was very convenient to get around. We had The London Pass and were able to use the Big Bus for 24hrs. All employees were very helpful along the way. When we arrived at the first stop it was about 1pm and the gentleman scanning us in wanted to make sure we knew we only had till 7:30 to ride the bus and were we sure we wanted to use it that day. When we told him what ours plan was he pointed us to another stop down the street and our trip would be faster. He helped us make the most of our hours. When we were done and retuning to the hotel our guide Emma was awesome, she was very friendly fun and entertaining. It was later in the day and she made sure everyone on the bus knew where they were going and help us all get to our destinations. Since it was late our bus was terminating so when we stoped she helped some of us jump on the bus behind us to get us all a little closer to our destinations. Christopher was our guide on the next bus and he was just as helpful. It was an awesome experience all around. Thank you Emma and Christopher. Loved all of Christopher’s jokes too. Corny but very entertaining 😁
The tour was really good and worth every penny! Emma was an incredible guide! Both funny and a great storyteller, familiar with every part of London

There are many sightseeing companies, but we were able to get 24 hour passes on this one for free as part of the London pass which we purchased at King's Cross station. The first time we got on the tour bus, they scanned our London pass and issued us a receipt which we then showed when getting on and off the bus. There are 4 routes (red, blue, orange, and green) which are generally loops to different areas. We were able to ride all four routes in one day. They are good about announcing on the bus when coming to a stop where you may wish to get off and get on the other colored route. We recommend riding on the top for an uncovered beautiful sight of the city and taking photos. Although the busses come along frequently, we think this type of tour does better when riding it all the time. If you were getting off and on frequently to see some attractions, you would use up your time quickly and never get to ride all four routes like we did in one day. Plus you'd spend time waiting for the busses at each stop, even if they come by frequently. We plan to ride the underground to get to attractions more quickly now that we're familiar with the city. Only the red line has a live guide with commentary, which we enjoyed. But all of the lines have earphones which you plug into a speaker in front of each seat (back of seat ahead of you). You can pick which language you want the pre-recorded narration to play in, or on the red line, you can pick the live English guide. Both the drivers and staff at many stops are helpful at answering questions and verifying if you're in the right spot to catch the next bus.
The hop on-hop off experience was amazing! Emma knew quite a bit about the history of London. I've been on a few buses already and she certainly was the best guide. Great fun :)
Great commentary by Emma. She made it very interesting and kept us involved throughout! You are lucky if she is on your bus!
Try and get on Emma’s bus on the red line. She is full of information and Spears to love sharing her knowledge of London.

My friend and I did a 3 week trip around Europe and many tours! This was by far the best one! It was Tiffany’s first day on the job and she was spewing out facts left, right and centre. It was as if she had been touring for years! She was so sweet and the tour was like having a hilarious chat with your best friends! Informative and personable, we loved Tiffany so much! We HIGHLY recommend this tour and Tiffany if you’re lucky enough to have her!

We visited London and had a lot of fun touring several of the local attractions for a few days. Then, my daughter and I came down with a cold and felt really miserable. The bus tour was great for still taking in the sights and learning a few tidbits about London without having to walk around feeling bad. Our guide (either Vauldus or Baldas?) was great-funny and informative.

Cheers to our awesome tour guide, Louis who gave us so much info on all the sights while keeping us laughing throughout the ride. We enjoyed it so much, we booked an extra day! He really knew the city well, and gave us lots of insight and little hints that made our London visit that much better. Patrick, our driver did an excellent job as well easily navigating through the London traffic. I recommend this highly if you want to see all the major sights. Great experience!!

This is most disappointing ! There is hardly any room on bus. People are standing and buses are very rare waiting up to 20min to get next one cause it was too full to hop on. Terrible !!! There are other bus services options to choose from and are free and available

We had a wonderful time with Ronald on the HOHO bus on Tuesday, 21st of May! He was very knowledgable and extremely entertaining for the entire trip. His funny jibes made it ever more exciting. Thanks Ronald! Me, my husband and my sons (22/12) loved it.

The real fun with the bus is its Open terrace seating. The seating below is comfortable and there are audio commentaries available... but you don't get good pictures and views. Infact we didn't even realise there was a live commentary available until we got a seat at the top.

Not to miss... especially for first time visitors.

We used the tour company yesterday, as we was only there for the day we decided to use the yellow line. When looking at purchasing the ticket, the sale guy was pushy (but yes it’s his job)! After buying the ticket he then said “oh we are short staffed and don’t know when the next bus will be!” We waited around 20 minutes, we then missed stops and went via the Strand due to a taxi protest (not the buses fault but again could have told us). We then got off at the Houses of Parliament as they again was restricted, we tried to ask the bus driver when the next bus was and all we got was “well there is traffic, there are protests ... no one knows” again I understand this but why not warn people before spending £96 on 4 tickets and we had to walk majority of it! Which wasn’t helped by the fact we had a disabled Paterson with us as well. In future maybe warn people of the road closures and protests! You clearly knew about them once you took our money and we was clear with the sale rep that we was only there for day etc

We did this the first day. It really shows you around the city. We didn't "hop off" to see anything but we got a great overview of the things the city has to offer. We then went back to various places that we really wanted to see. Great stories from the tour guides and audio. If you do the red, blue, and orange routes, this will be the day and you will have seen most everything. Then you can plan the next day(s) as to where you want to go explore in detail.

Been a good few years since we’ve been on the London tour bus so thought we would try it again!! The amount of roadworks in London is unbelievable!!!! Every other street is getting dug up!!! Our guide was Lewis and he managed to keep everyone entertained during the inevitable hold ups!! Nice touch that he asks everyone coming on where they are from then greets them in their own language and gives a fact about where they live!! Made the bus trip really entertaining!!
We did the red route fir 2+ hours ..what a fantastic tour made so informative by the knowledge, chat and personality of Emma. Will do it again.

Emma our guide was well informed, enthusiastic, proud of her city, and really cared about her passengers. She personally interacted with almost all the passengers asking them if they had any questions and answering them.

I would highly recommend this tour.

We had an amazing time touring in the Big Bus around London. In fact we did it twice as well as the night tour. The buses are easy to find, run frequently and the staff are very helpful and friendly. The live commentary is something we had never experienced before with hop on and hop off buses and was really interesting. The staff were very informative and each one had their own way of presenting it. Particular mention to Valvas ? and Gaybor Hegyi who went well beyond our expectations. Gaybor was particularly helpful with an issue that we had. Highly recommend this tour bus company

There are earphones so you can hear a guided tour with lots of interesting facts. Many languages. If it’s a nice day, go up top. Otherwise, downstairs had no AC, but you can open windows. I’d recommend doing this your first day to get acclimated to the city.

We purchased a 2 day pass and really enjoyed it. We especially enjoyed the live guides! Karen was great as well as Freddie! There was a third older gentleman but I didn’t catch his name. We also enjoyed the boat tour to the Naval Academy. I would recommend this to everyone!

Horrible frequency compared to other operators in London. Better to choose operators like the The original tours or golden tours who has at least 1: 4 in frequency compared to big bus tour.

But what deserves this one star is not the frequency but the rude curt attitude towards curt and down ride rude behavior toward customers.. not once but noticed it 4 times in the day and one of them even called a poor confused customer idiot to his face ... and that has prompted me to write this review.
Emma our tour guide was amazing. Learned a great deal about the city, and helped me figure out where to go next.

I guess it all depends on who your guide is. We boarded in the morning by Marble Arch and stayed on until Tower of London. The guide was OK. We were seated inside the bus as we could not get a seat in the open area. Each time we tried others got there before us and again no room. I mentioned because this because we couldn’t see anything the guide was speaking about. Also he was upstairs and we didn’t know there was a live person until the third stop when he came down to inform us how we could hear him. As I said we disembarked ay Tower of London, which was a good idea to pick up the City Cruise Ferry which is included in your ticket. That was a nice ride to Westminster and a good guide.

So now for the major reason for the poor review. We re-boarded after a walking tour that ended by the Horse Guard, about half way through the nonstop Red route. We thought we would go up top to get a view of what we missed. What we didn’t expected was a very young man for a guide. He was sitting down with little interest in giving information. He was either carrying on a conversation with and another young guy or on his phone texting. If he did speak, it was a brief naming of a building as we passed. At one point there were demonstrators and he was interested in running back in forth on the bus to get pictures of them. He was by far the worst tour guide. If He had given his name out, I would have reported him to the bus where you purchase you the tickets.

To add to this miserable trip, the bus stopped at stop 22, I think, where he just got up and left the bus. His shift was over. Now we sat on the bus for 30 minutes to wait for another guide to board and then wait for another bus to arrive so we could take those passengers. It took us 2 hours to go six stops.

I would not recommend taking a Hop on Hop bus in a London. I have done it many times in other cities but this may not be a good city to do this.

We were lucky to have Lewis as our guide on the red line. He welcomed all the passengers, was professional and had great rapport. He and the driver helped make Tour fun and interesting.
We only had one day and rode the blue and red line. We got off and on each line once. Would have done more if we had time.
Thanks Lewis and your driver.
Loved our time with Emma on our Big Bus tour! So helpful and a great way to see the city easily :) highly recommend!

Me and my sister(with her 4 month old son) decided to take our mum sightseeing today. Thought going on sightseeing bus was the best way to see London. But how wrong we were. As it was a treat for our mum we didn’t mind the very expensive tickets. It wasn’t worth it at all. No AC in the bus. It was boiling hot today. The roof seats were always full. We had to stay on the lower deck and didn’t understand anything. We never understood why the driver kept waiting at each bus stop, just wasting time. One American man had to tell him off. Now he was so angry he wasn’t stopping at all. He went through a very small road which had some sort of repair going on. He bumped the bus as there was a very sharp turn. He never stop, to see the damage he did to the bus and the partitions on the road. We were so scared. There were small babies and so many tourists on this bus. He still didn’t stop at next stop. We had to use the bell which was far from where we were sitting. Waste of time and money. Very disappointed.
Very bad for such a big company. It’s not a sightseeing bus. Will never recommend them to people. Thank you

Included with the London Pass, which is nice. There is really nothing they did wrong, but rather the fundamental issue is that a bus tour in London is subject to the horrible traffic and the changeable weather of London. On the upper deck, on a nice day, I expect this tour could be a nice time. On a mediocre weather day (rainy or cold), on the lower level, you will not be able to see anything of substance, and the Tube will get you from point A to point B a lot faster than idling in traffic. There are also THREE hop on hop off tour operators in London, so it is all but inevitable that you will see multiple buses of the other tour operators before your bus comes along.
Emma our tour guide on May 10th was very knowlegible and thoughtful. I enjoyed the tour and learned a lot.

The red tour route of London was amazing especially because of our tour guide Emma, she really made the trip interesting and memorable. She really took care of the passengers and was very friendly and more knowledgeable than I could imagine. Definitely recommend taking the bus with the live tour guide!!! Especially Emma :) On the tour we got to see all the sights we wouldn’t have had time to get to on our own.
This is a terrible tour and the service is ridiculous. They told us to go f*** ourselves. Just avoid

we had very short time to enjoy London and with the Big Bus Tour we could span all over and make very targeted short walk visits, hopping on and off. In addition we had the cruise on the River Thames. We want to highlight how good and competent were the two local guides VALDAS and MOLLY, we happened to have, on the red route. They gave fulllive english explanations of the city. and were very helpful to give indications and suggestions.
Our amazing guide Emma was great and super informative! I lost the challenge to find something she didn’t know about London! Thanks Emma!
We took the Red line and had Emma as a tour guide she was wonderful, engaging and gave us suggestions for when we were off the bus which we would have never thought of.

We spent the day listening to Louis and Christopher tell us about the sights of this delightful city. They were extremely knowledgeable and personable in their description of London. Also enjoyed the river cruise and it’s access to great pictures of .this city.

In the 72h package we have access to all four lines : red, blue, orange and green. All of these have stops near all the big and main attractions.
Also included : a walking tour every morning at 10h30, a roundtrip river cruise (with City Cruises) on the Thames and a night tour bus.
High point of all these : the morning walk, which will take you see the guard change and take beautiful pictures of Buckingham Palace without all the crowd. Steve, our guided, was brilliant and made us avoid all the people and learned us a few tricks.
Absolutely fantastic!
Emma was a fantastic tour guide that made the experience much more enjoyable! Hope she's on the next ride when we hop back on :)

For our first visit to London, we decided on the bus tour. We rode the bus two days and luckily for us, we had wonderful weather. We rode on the top deck and were able to take some great photos. Our tour guide on Sunday gave us information about the changing of the guard on Monday at Buckingham Palace. Our tour guide on Monday was Adam, who gave us a lot of great information which was helpful for the rest of our time in London. Glad we bought the two day pass.

I've done a bus tour before in Paris and Barcelona.

We've had a really fun day with my parents.
Even though it was quite cloudy it didn't spoil our fun. Really gives you the chance to see London from a whole new perspective.
Emma is a great guide!
Christopher was amazing. Very knowledgeable and entertaining. Answers any questions you have and gives you little insights about hidden locations that he enjoys.
We had a great time today seeing three iconic British sights! Goffrey was a great guide! Wish we would’ve had more time at Stonehenge, but overall a great day!

Joe, our live tour guide was fantastic. He gave us tons of information and was very funny. He really made the tour better than anticipated!! Would highly recommend to anyone visiting London whether it’s your first time or you’ve been here before!!

My husband and I did the big bus tour-walking tour. Our guide Joe was awesome!! Lots of knowledge of the area as well as being a super friendly and bubbly person we had a great laugh and the tour was perfect!

Thank you Joe 😊
Great tour; lots of places to see- great live guides on the Red Line. Emma was fabulous! Very informative and engaging!
I really enjoyed the tour guide Emma she was very knowledgeable and interesting. She also took time out to help us with additional information. See made the experience much more enjoyable.
Fantastic and informative. Emma, our guide was knowledgeable and friendly. Easy access. Thank you very much.
Emma was very friendly and clearly loved her job. She was full of knowledge and made our experience of London very enjoyable. Thanks!

My friend Rosemary is visiting from the states and wanted to see it all in 2 days so this was good to give her an idea of where everything was. The guide s- first Charlie and then David were great. Charlie was informative and quite funny. David was enthusiastic so really enjoyed the bus tour. We stayed on it for the entire red line. Would recommend that first before doing the hop on/off.

We just spent 1.5 hours standing on the bus, a distance we could have walk in 45. And standing means you do not get to listen to the guide, you need earplugs plugged into the wall for that.

The ticket seller "forgot" to tell us about the traffic situation, there were road blocks everywhere. When the bus driver start skipping stops we asked to get off, but weren't allowed to.

The seller also gave us a "good deal" for the London Eye, telling we would pass all lines. That is not true! You have to take the ticket into the ticket office by the Eye, stand in line to get the ticket validated and then stand in line with everyone else to get in the ride.

So, if you are thinking of doing it, at least check traffic on Google. And, are you visiting more than one of the main sights in London you can get better deals online or at the bix office at London Eye.
Emma is a great tour guide she is amazing so happy friendly she is the best tour guide and she is so intelligent

My family enjoyed riding this bus. The commentary was not the greatest, but looking at london, without tiring your legs is my idea of perfection on wheels.

Only thing missing is free snacks/drinks on board.

We went as a family (4 adults and 5 kids) on Big Bus tour in London. Emma was our guide and she was very helping and guiding. It was a lovely day and she gave us a lot of information about places to do shopping and travelling around in London. Thanks a lot Emma.

We got our tickets through trip advisor and they did not have a barcode on them. I didn’t think anything of it. I did think it was interesting that I had to search out all the information via the Big Bus website and app. We found our first stop and presented the trip advisor tickets. The bus driver said that he needed a bar code and did not want to let us on. The tour guide convinced him to let us on. On our next time getting on the bus, there was the live tour guide even though the red line was guaranteed to have a live tour guide. On our third time getting on, it was the same story as the first. THEN, we went to go on the river cruise and they would not let us on without “validated” tickets, and our tickets through trip advisor were not validated (they could not be because there was no barcode). We did not have cell service in London, so we could not call the contact number during the day to ask for assistance. We did have WiFi, but trip advisor help desk is virtually unavailable through the internet. (Trip advisor: we also have another ticket booked to the colosseum 4/21/19 that doesn’t have a barcode. We’d love for someone to contact us for assistance via email or messages, as we do not have phone access to call. If this same thing happens to us at the colosseum we will not be happy.)

Paid 68 pounds for two people. Went four stops on the bus then got off to go on boat trip (no commentary on boat - basically just a water bus) then we had to negotiate the extinction rebellion protests which had diverted the bus route and we had to walk for miles to find out the new route and where the bus stop was. Very chaotic and disorganised. Terrible value for money

My friend and I went on the Big Bus Tour and found it very interesting even though I’m a Londoner I still learnt quite a lot of things! Many thanks to Emma who was a fantastic tour guide and full of knowledge about the city of Westminster, I highly recommended the tour should you like to see plenty of london it’s definitely the best option to do so 👍🏽 perfect in every way
Waited at Tower of London with about 75 people for 1 bus that came 40 mins after scheduled. The other bus companies came and went several times.

Did the Big Bus tour yesterday. Me and the wife enjoyed it. The knowledge and commentry style and technique of Charlie was excellent. We asked him afterwards how ling he was doing it and he replied that it was his second day on the job. We were blown away by this guys knowledge. Great guide great tour.

We went on the red route bus tour today. Emma, our tour guide spotted us before we got on the bus and introduced herself and immediately made us feel extremely welcome and comfortable. Her wealth of knowledge around London made our trip thoroughly enjoyable and extremely interesting! We seen all of the spots we had wanted to see on the red route and look forward to another route tomorrow! Highly recommended, especially Emma who made our trip!!

At the end of a long tiring day in miserable weather it's hard to generate any enthusiasm for right seeing.
Then there was Emma our favourite Big Bus guide. Funny and smart and charming and informative, she gave us a second wind and we thoroughly enjoyed her passion for the job.
Full marks!

We used the big bus tour with our London pass on Saturday 30th March 2019

The weather was lovely and the buses were very busy as we hopped on and off but we managed to get a seat on the top deck a couple of times.

The buses were so frequent, totally opposite to what we encountered with the same company in Budapest where we waited for 40 minutes at times, in London we found the buses came every few minutes.

The guides we had were all great and friendly, helpful and had great stories to tell.

It's a great way to see where everything is and learn about things and places you wouldn't know about by walking around yourself.

The only thing I would say is if you want to see everything on all the routes, I would set aside 2 full days for this.

You can't beat this trip for a first time visitor. We had two, and by the end of the day they had "seen it all." Remember you can't "experience it all" without weeks in the city. But by the end of the day you clearly know where you want to go back to. Buy a pass to the Tower of London. You can use it any time.the bus passes by. Watch out for timed events. Sometimes you sacrifice some good experience trying to figure out how to get to the "scheduled" events." on time.

Although we were told they would come about every 15-20 minutes, it was more like 45 to wait for the initial bus. After that, when we needed to change lines, we waited in a bus for more than an hour. Finally, at the next stop, after waiting about 30 minutes, we decided to just walk. The sad thing is that it wasted so much of our time. We only had a few days in London so we planned everything out pretty carefully, and I thought this would be a good way to efficiently see everything we wanted to on that day. We ended not having time to do things we really wanted to be because we wasted so much time waiting for this stupid bus. Some drivers were ok, some more on the rude side. I love the concept, but it just didn't work. It was late February, so I don't know if the off season affects bus times, but if so they should have warned us. Very disappointed in the experience.

I booked this through the London eye website as a package. If I would have known before I would have chose the Aquarium option in the package. We rode the bus 2 times in the 24 hours we had them. There was too many stops and one we sat for 20 minutes at waiting for people to buy their tickets.

Recommend saving your money and using the tube that’s quicker and only costs 7£ for the entire day of travel.

Big Steve was my guide during my trip. Not only did I hear him speak 5 languages during my time on the bus, he was extremely friendly and knowledgeable! As a solo traveler only in London for a day, I left this tour feeling satisfied that I had seen practically everything on my list! I love Big Steve!

We chose the wrong day for sightseeing as there was a million ppl protesting in Central London. And yet Big Steve made it so much fun for us. He was very welcoming with all the passengers, asking them where they're from, chatting, joking, and smiles. And he new a lot of interesting details you don't find out from travel guides. Well done, Steve! I still feel guilty for not tipping as I had no cash :( It would've been well deserved.

The buses run regularly and stop in many places, and I recommend setting aside two to three hours for this.
We were on four different buses, where two of them had good guides, so if you feel the guide is a bit "lax", change the bus!

Our London Pass allowed either Big Bus or Golden Tours HoHo bus tours. We mistakenly chose Big Bus. We found it difficult to find a convenient bus stop, so we inquired at a Big Bus ticket kiosk and were given wrong information. We waited almost an hour at the stop recommended by the gentlemen at the ticket kiosk. We followed other waiting people to another stop at which point we were informed several of the Big Bus stops, including the one where we waited an hour, had been taken off the Big Bus route. Finally on the bus, the guide was very insufficient. There were long silences in her narrative; started every sentence with "Okay Guys", and told ridiculous family stories as we were driving by historic sites without commentary. We stayed on Big Bus for just 20 minutes when we decided we could do better on our own. We hopped off never to return to Big Bus. I do not recommend Big Bus! In hind sight, I would purchase tickets for The Original London Tour HoHo bus.

Generally a great service, comparable to the City sightseeing Bus service. Drivers are good, the life narrator is also very good - we even had a discussion with one of them concerning work, life and everything else in London. Combined ticket for the City Cruises is a must, as it takes you to Greenwich on the The Thames. The Hop-on Hop-off service did us a great job, as we used it in a couple of rainy days.

My family loved the Big Bus Tours, we started early in the day and snagged the front seats up top with the best unobstructed views. The live commentators on all the buses were fabulous. The last bus we took at the end of the day did not have a live commentator which was a bit disappointing after all the great live tours throughout the day. The tour company did make sure we got back to our hotel at the end of the night which was really nice. Lots of stops and we loved the relaxing river cruise up the Thames to break up the day. Even our teenaged kids enjoyed the bus tours.

We spent a rainy day with Emma as the tour guide. Her knowledge of the history of London and current recommendations were fabulous. She had a welcoming and extremely helpful manner. Would love to ride with her again.

We chose the Big Bus for our hop on hop off, as it was one of the two offered as part of our London Pass. I emailed them initially asking to see if it offers the same benefits as buying original ticket, and they promptly replied: The London Pass Ticket includes all the 4 routes hop on hop off but do not include the walking tour and the river cruise. Just FYI.
We only did the red tour route, and the live commentary was great. Our guide was Ian, and he’s very knowledgeable, have a great sense of humor, and just made you feel very welcomed. He also took his time and gave us lots of great tips. Also, if you go on their main website, it updates you on any stops that would be closed on certain dates. Overall, I will recommend Big Bus if you want to try the hop on hop off bus.

I always book the hop on and off in every location I visit to get an overview. This time I was traveling with hubby on business and he had never been to London. We had one day. The hop on off bus was the way to go. He was able to see all the hot spots and get the best information. We didn’t hop off except to transfer to the other line. Great commentary from a live person and the recorded tour as well. These tours are always a must and well worth the time and money. Certainly recommend taking one regardless if you have one or many days.

Having read other reviews before taking the tour I was sceptical. Ice done many bus tours in cities before and this one was least impressive! We spent alot of the day stuck in traffic and taking diversions due to roadworks. We did hit it lucky and have a live guide on part of our journey who was much more informative than the automated commentary. We found it pricey for what it was even though we had discounted tickets. We wouldn't do tour again and think money would be better spent accessing sites via tube and much quicker too!

The weather wasn't great, so we weren't expecting a great day. Then, when we boarded at Praed Street, we really weren't feeling positive as the driver was more miserable than the weather (and it was bloody miserable).

But, we changed at Marble Arch to do the Red Route, and it picked up from there. Christopher, the live tour guide, was a rwal tonic for the weather, keeping everyone spirits up with some good knowledge and humour. And he even directed me to the free poncho's as the teenagers in tow decided they didn't need a coat 🤷‍♂️

And you really do get to see all of the bits of London that you want to see as a tourist.

So thank you Christopher and the Big Bus tour. We'll be back (perhaps when the weather gets better) 😉

I’ve been living in London for 10 years and have done a few city tours with guests over the years. I didn’t think I had anything left to learn but our guide on the bus - Valdas, was fabulous! He was so knowledgeable and interesting! I was glad to be on the bus and learn more things.

We got the one day pass, and jumped in the blue line near our hotel. The recorded commentary was fascinating and informative. We saw some really charming neighborhoods and noted a couple we would return to for a more in depth visit. We switched to the red tour, which is longer and goes through the really popular areas, like Piccadilly Circus, Westminster, and the Tower of London.
