It also includes live commentary from a tour guide (mad props to our guide Karen, who was informative and entertaining and made sure everyone was keeping up with the stops and insuring people were getting off where they wanted). All in all it was a pleasant experience, and I highly recommend it to anyone visiting London.

This was my second time doing the hop on hop off tour. It was marvelous. We saw so many sites! I loved the live commentary on the red line. I wish all busses had the live commentary. Our guides on the red line busses were so helpful and amazing.

Our tour guide Bill did a great job of entertaining and informing everyone about the historical significance of the sites we saw from our comfy seats on the bus. I found myself laughing several times at his amusing jokes and the stories he told. It was worth the money to get great views of the city and photo-worthy opportunities. The blue line had a higher back seat on the top of the bus which I appreciated. We also jumped back on the bus in the evening to go to the theatre district.

I would highly recommend doing this at the beginning of your trip so that you get the opportunity to see sites you might want to go back to further explore.

We went on the red line tour with Bill on Sunday 17th February. He was so helpful and informative, and was so engaging in his stories about every single thing we passed. I've been on other big bus tours where I've been unimpressed but Bill absolutely made this tour. Thanks!!

Wet and windy day in February and we didn’t know what to do, so we thought if we took a bus where we could get off at any attraction we fancied and the go on to the next one at our timetable speed. Well with perfect seats and a better tour guide we decided to stay on the bus for the full route and I must say it was a great morning. We saw and learnt more about the capital than I ever considered possible. I would certainly recommend this method of seeing London.

As a group in London for business, we decided to enjoy the hop on hop off bus experience. It was a rainy, cold overcast day but our guide Emma made it feel like the sun was shining bright! You just can’t fake her absolute enthusiasm for her city. Facts, stories, laughs...she delivered it all. Thanks Emma, you are wonderful.

Has a wonderful tour of London, despite the bad weather in London. Nice trip in the bus with excellent explanations. Also went for London eye... had an issue with my tickets for the London eye however, with one part of the ticket not printed.
With the help of @Ahmed Abdullahi, the guide at the bridge, the problem was quickly solved though and was able to appreciate the nice views

A great way to see this huge city and get a small taste for what it has to offer and where to spend your time. The tour guide makes all the difference. We had Emma who gave great live commentary and even assisted us personally with some travel difficulties. She was warm, funny, and knowledgeable. One tip: if possible get on the bus at the beginning, we started at stop 17 and that through us off a bit. But didn’t detract from the whole experience.

Our tour guide, Joe, on Monday Jan 28th, makes the rating 5 Star. Loved his insight on the red line part of tour and genuine excitement in showing his city to us. Felt like a personal tour and had he not been there we would have focused more on the cold and the traffic delays. Great job Joe! - your NC friends
Loved touring London via Big Bus tours. Emma was our tour guide. She was quite knowledgeable and made the day absolutely delightful.

Had a great time on the Big Bus tour in London. Best way to get a quick overview of this amazing city. Emma our tour guide was very informative and helped passengers with other questions relating to getting around London.

We had Caron as our tour guide and found her excellent for our first overview of London. She was clearly spoken, highly knowledgeable and had many fascinating anecdotes for all areas. She made the tour wonderfully enjoyable :)
Thanks for all the details and stories Emma. Great time on the red line tour with you, hope to have time to see the other trips next time in London.

The tour itself was fantastic - the bus drivers are skillful and amazing where they can squeeze their busses. We had both live commentary and audio commentary. The commentators were incredibly knowledgeable and ours had quite a sense of humour.
There were staff at all the stops who were very friendly and helpful.
The only thing I would caution you about is buying attractions from them. We purchased 5 skip the line London Eye tickets and once we got there found out they were only vouchers and we had to line up at the ticket office anyway. We then found out there was a 90 minute wait for skip the line and we ran out of time so didn't get to go on it. London Eye wouldn't refund because we didn't buy the tickets directly from them. I'm going to frame our unused tickets as our most expensive mistake.

We had the BEST experience on this tour! My daughter is in London for a study abroad program and we wanted to see the city to get her acclimated to the area and this tour was AWESOME! Driver Gary and tour guide Louis were phenomenal! They stopped for pictures and made the experience so fun. They filled us in on all the local spots as well as places she could go for anything she needs while she is studying in London. I would recommend this tour to anyone who wants to get a great understanding of the city in a short time!! Thank you Louis for the great tips and laughs!!

We got the 3-day deluxe ticket with river cruise, which is the best way to see the city. Especially Emma's live commentary on the red tour were great!
Highly recommended!

A great way to travel and see London. You may choose to sit at the top throughout the bus journey to see the main Central London attractions or you may choose to drop off and take the bus again as a form of transport. End the day with a cruise along the river. Beautiful sight.

We took the red tour (my wife, 5 year old son, 3 year old son and I ), it was pretty good which most probably have made me give it a 4 star but I had to drop it down to two as we were hoping to do full loop from green park to green park but instead we got to marble arch for the second time and got told that's it and off the bus. We went to the person at the bottom of the stairs (it wasn't the driver) and asked which way it was to green park and how far, his reply was 'you're getting no free pass to green park, off the bus!' which we got ushered off, we replied saying 'well how rude is that' to which he just turned back and closed the doors on us. All we wanted was directions and how long so we could work something out as we had our two young sons, not 'a free pass'. I feel like it was a we've got your money so f**k off moment. Such bad customer service!

We purchased the two day ticket for the big bus tour and started our day at Buckingham palace for the changing of the guard. The girls that we purchased the tickets from her so nice and helpful and we have to say that our tour guide, Josh, was so entertaining we ended up staying on the bus for the entire tour rather than getting on and off. We ended up doing that on the second round. We love the tour we loved the information I really appreciate it Josh and his great sense of humor and all the special tidbits he provided. Great job!

Visiting from Australia and was lucky enough to get Lewis as a tour guide two days in row! He was absolutely hilarious and fantastic at interacting with people while also giving an informative tour
I would highly recommend it!
Great way to get around London! Much better having a live person telling us what we were seeing versus the other tours with pre-recorded information. Lewis and Emma were the best!

Lewis was absolutely fantastic. Loved his sense of humour too. I felt that as a tour guide for the bus- Lewis rates as a 5 star guide. He answered all our questions- gave us extra information and this has made our stay such a better experience for first timers. Can’t thank you enough Lewis. Regards Janelle and Warren- the Queenslanders. Xx
It was the best city tour!!! Thank you!!! Lot of jokes and lot of interesting info about perfect and beautiful London!!!
We enjoyed the big bus we liked the weekend where there was a live person narrating - he was funny we saw a lot more than we would have just walking and learned a lot - our 11 year old loved it

My husband and I went to Central as a birthday gift and had a really great time. We had a London Pass which gave us the opportunity to see as much of Central London as we can. We Hopped on the Big Bus Tour and our first tour guide Louis was funny and witty. After we got Cathy and boy did we love Cathy. She was super funny, insightful and caring. If we ever came back to London anytime soon we would definitely do the Big Bus Tour again and hope we have Cathy. She rocks!

Louis was a fantastic guide and is the only reason I’m leaving a 5 star review. He saved the tour for me.

The day before I hadn’t had a live guide at all, but the staff I encountered wasn’t very helpful. They were polite, but when I asked for a map they said “just a moment” and I never was told where they were (this happened twice with different staff members). I finally located the map at the bus entrance, which should be easy to find, but when you board with a mass of people it’s not easy to find these or the headsets. The tour overall was interesting, but not great.

The next day (today) I was on board with Louis and he was a delight. He was knowledgeable and shared great information and stories. He was humorous as well and made an effort to get to know everyone on the bus.

When it was time for Louis’ break we were transferred to another bus and I was so disappointed I just got off after a few stops. The other guide (who didn’t share his name) mumbled the tour, he didn’t share ANY facts, just said “to the left is Marble Arch.” Or “to the right is...” with zero facts about what we were seeing. Additionally, when an elderly couple came upstairs they wanted to sit in the covered section, but the guide was taking up 2 seats in that section with his bag and himself. I had seen Louis stand and even offer his jacket for people to sit on to avoid the damp - while that is above and beyond, the LEAST I expected was for the guide to move his bag to another seat for them!

So, as I said, while my gut said “2 stars”, Louis made the part of my tour that he was on so incredibly enjoyable. I hope that the company takes notice and 1) Rewards Louis and 2) encourages the remaining staff to up their game.

Many thanks to Emma, my tour guide for Nov 26!
I was desperately trying to finish my Hop on hop off bus tour and wanted to see the missed stops, due to getting off to ride the London Eye. (It should be noted that the Hop On bus by the London Eye can pick you up and take you to stop 18 instead of stopped 13!)
Emma was gracious enough to get off the bus, get her manager’s permission, and use her own lunchtime to take me to a different bus stop so that I could finish my route correctly before I had to head back to Heathrow Airport!
many many thanks Emma!!!

Absolutely loved the tour with Liam!!! He was very knowledgable about the history of the city and took the time to answer everyone's questions as we drove by the monuments and sites.

This tour is definitely something you should do on the first day of your trip. Try to do the full tour before hopping off so you can decide what is most important for you to visit.

Thank you Liam!!

Had a lot of fun on the Big Bus tour over 2 days.

When you compare it to other ways of seeing a monster city like London for the 1st time (cab / tube / helicopter etc.) its probably the best way to get a basic view / feel for it - then you can go back to the areas you like and discover them in more depth at your own leisure.
Maybe its time Big Bus adopted new technology to jazz up the experience to better link up the actual bus location with what you are looking at - and mix up the commentary because it sounds a bit 'tired' / dated.
Unfortunately, our bus got redirected and we went around the same streets listening to the same stuff a few times.
The recorded commentary was OK (but I thought a bit ho-hum).

On one bus (red route I think) we had an ex- Kiwi called Ian doing the commentary - he was hillarious.
With great knowledge of the history / places and events, he delivered his presentation with a Rob Bryden type sense of humour. FANTASTIC.

I don't want to harp on but the recorded material could be improved... to combine more interesting content (history/events/snippets of interesting info) that have occurred at the various parts of the city. Obviously there is a huge amount of material.

Traffic is normally so conjested you are sitting there (not a bad thing necessarily for a tourist) for a long time and the recorded commentary could activate some more interesting info to passengers.
Enjoyed it tho. Had a blast.

I had 24 hrs in London and was really wanting to see the most in this short amount of time. This Hop on Hop off tour was THE BEST!! Lewis our guide on the 1st leg was so funny and knowledgeable that I almost didn't want to get off the bus:)
We also encountered a couple really great employees that are available at a lot of the stops to help with questions. Noel (sp) was one of those who was really great. I highly recommend this bus tour. They were on time, well educated on the city and very helpful

Got a one day package as part of the London Pass. Took the red route around central London.

I use bus tours for a photography blitzkrieg, as I usually walk around to try and absorb a place. The quality of the live guided tour, if one is offered, is not always important. But I was impressed and entertained with Liam's live narration of his city, one that is clearly close to his heart. It was wry, understated, and deep, not unlike London itself.

Different stories spanned the Saxons, the Normans, the Middle Ages, the Civil War/Restoration, the Georgian and Victorian eras, into modern history and the present day. We ran the gamut from pop culture to history to much appreciated detail on the architects and engineers that built London's great works.

Despite today being, as they would say here, bloody cold, the open top of the bus is a great platform for sightlines. It helps put some of the density in perspective. Most of the time I've been here has been spent among a sea of people going from canyon to canyon, which has been fine, but it is nice to be able to actually look at things and take photos of them.

I don't know how this company compares to other tour bus companies because I have no need to ride with them, but I thought the experience was a great use of two and a half hours here.

Bought a 2 day pass for £99 for 3 of us Included as many bus sight seeing trips as we could fit in and a boat trip. Both were excellent! The red route bus included a live guide all of which were really good and quite comical. Emma and James were both exceptional. The boat was great too. Really good value for money. Would do again if we went to London again.

We had a great time using the Big Bus hop on hop off. JoJo was exceptional with her live narration on the redline. We all agreed that she made London come alive with her stories. The gentleman who greeted us where the red and green lines meet was an exceptional ambassador for the Big Bus. We also took advantage of the boat cruise and thought it was terrific. Highly recommended!

On the 23rd of October 2018 Emma was our tour gide. She was very nice, had a lot of usefull information and tips. She spoke with passion about London.
She was amazing. Thank you.

Thanks Emma, my brother and I from Chicago loved your narration of London, your home..we spent a rainy Sunday with you hearing about the history of the city and sights, as well as the personal stories. Loved that your family members were models for the statues through the city..LOL. We were so happy to have a seat upstairs that was protected from the rain. But little did we know that we would have a narrator with a great personality. Your love of the city shines through, even on a rainy day..

Myself and my 2 boys had a great day on the Big Bus tour today. Emma was a brilliant tour guide and made us feel very welcome on her bus. We came home with lots of interesting facts about how ‘green’ London actually is and now want to explore parts of London we’d never heard of before today.

We only had one full day in London, so we rode around for an hour, then hopped on and off at the different spots we wanted to explore further from the stops on the list. Obviously one day is not enough in London, but it did give us enough of a taste to want to go back!

The buses come and go often. Pretty full double decker buses. Several routes. Pre-recorded commentary -- part of our route was live.

Too expensive. We paid 37 pounds per person which is not worth it.

London is an easy city to either walk or use the tube.

If this review is helpful then please indicate so below.
Took both guided (Red) and audio (Blue) tours. Emma on Red tour is energetic, funny and informative. Interesting to hear history and fun facts about London.
Not enough buses, too many people. Had to skip a few buses. Getting a seat upstairs sometimes impossible. For what we paid vs what we used, i don’t think it was worth it.

Very disappointed in the London Big Bus Hop On Hop Off Tour we took today. It seemed very disorganized and sloppy. We got on a bus and a few stops later we were told we had to get on another bus, it was at stop 1 of the London Red Route. The bus we were on had the partially covered top floor which my husband and I wanted, the bus they made us move to was completely open. I asked the tour guide on the original bus if we could just stay on the bus and wait until it left and he said he wasn’t sure. So we got off the bus and I asked the Big Bus representative that was flagging the buses on whether to stop and change or stop and keep going at that location if we could stay on our original bus. She shock her head “no” and then I said that the new bus was completely open and she said “yes” and walked away. No explanation, no nothing. It’s the rudest interaction I’ve ever had with a Big Bus representative. Just so Big Bus management knows who this person is, it was a lady working at stop 1 on the red route on Sat, Oct 20 at about 10:40am. Someone with that sort of an attitude should not be working with the public. My husband and I had just dropped £33 each so £66 total (about $85) on this tour and I expected better service than that! So we get on the 2nd bus which was definitely showing it’s wear (I’ve attached a picture of the foam peeling off the front bar) and to boot, my headset was not working. I had to use one of my husband’s ear buds. At one point towards the end of our route, we stopped for quite some time so a Big Bus Rep could check everyone’s tickets. Are you kidding me?! This should be done when everyone gets on the bus. The guides were also not up to par with other guides on Big Bus tours I’ve taken in other cities. The first guide hardly narrated at all. The second one, Josh, was really nice but he kept having off mic conversations with people near him. It was so annoying because you could sort of hear his conversations but it wasn’t on mic or info he was sharing with the entire bus. He would also tell you to look at things, like a particular pub, right when the bus was in front of it so by the time he said it and you turned to look we’d passed it. That being said, at least he did narrate and provide information. My husband rarely does tours like this and he never criticizes anything but he expressed his frustration with the apparent disorganization of how everything was run. We’ve just moved to London and will be having a lot of friends and family visiting and I won’t take them on the Big Bus Tour, I’ll take them on the Original Bus Tour that our hotel had recommended. I went with Big Bus because I’ve been on Big Bus in other cities and always liked it. Another thing, when we checked the website there was a Service Status but when you clicked on it it said their were stop closures on Saturday 10 October so we figured it was outdated since it is October 20 (Photo attached). But apparently it was for this Saturday since there was a march which created many necessary route diversions (stops 1 thru 12 we’re closed). Overall, a horrible tour and a total waste of money! Big Bus is not the only Hop on Hop Off in London, you’ve got The Original Tour Company and the Grayline run Golden Tour. I would take one of those before taking Big Bus especially since both of these tours are cheaper than Big Bus

Although I work in London, I have been thinking for a long time about being a tourist there and going an open top bus tour. I thought it would be OK and I might learn something, but JoJo was fabulous and kept us entertained throughout. I almost didn't want to get off to see the sights as she was so good. Thank you for a great day.

This is a good bus tour that was made even better by the fantastic tour guide Emma who not only provided knowledge, witty and timely information whilst on route but also had time for questions from our young kids which she answered really nicely, they loved it. We experienced a couple of other guides who despite having decent knowledge sadly got no where near Emma’s all round quality. There’s not much between these buses but a really good live guide makes a huge difference.

Great tour!

We picked the wrong day because it was freezing outside.

Nonetheless, this excursion was great. We had purchased the London pass so this tour was included.

We went around London’s most famous monuments, attractions such as the London Eye,London bridge, Westminster bridge.

Suitable for families and kids. They also providw you with earpiece so you can really focus on what the guide is saying. There’s also a channel in French, Chinese, German, Spanish etc for those who do not speak English.

You can catch this bus at any of their stops: you can scan your London pass onboard if you have a mobile pass OR you need to exchange your pass at Piccadilly Circus if you have a confirmation voucher.

Pre booked tour for family . Very disappointed with the quality of the information regarding both the relevant tour facts and historical context of sights and the logistical problem resulting from a demonstration based in Central London. The members of staff had no idea of how to deal with the problem and some of the most iconic sights were missed. No Trafalgar Square, Piccadilly Circus, Whitehall. Wouldn’t pre book again.

I have been to London several times but this was the first time we went on a tour like this. Boarding is easy, just be at one of their stops & hop on. Our first tour guide was Joe. He not only knew his stuff but was funny & very entertaining. He had info on everything from history and dates to Harry Potter stuff. We got off at the Tower and when we got back on we had Liam. He was just as full of info and stories. We had a blast. This is an excellent value, tickets are good for 24 hours.

We had 12hrs to spend in London and filled it comprehensively with the Big Bus Tour...got some valuable information and tips and particularly enjoyed our tour guide Emma who was very entertaining and knowledgeable..
We do recommend this for a brief overview to see the best features and attractions in London. Thank you for the day...

If you read the sales brochure the company stands out. The reality is somewhat different. I booked this tour for my friends over from China as they wanted to see the sights. The initial contact outside Victoria Station was friendly and helpful. We were given directions to the bus stop and told the service was every 5-10mins. It was downhill from there. We waited at the allotted stop for a good 20 minutes as other tour providers came and went. I asked the representative in the Big Bus Tour jacket when we could expect a bus. Without glancing up from his phone he told me "anytime now". The difference in the service provided by the other two reps working at the stop was chalk and cheese. They were patient, helpful and courteous. That difference is what prompted this review. Once the bus arrived, it was packed to the gunnels with the upper floor fully taken. and only standing room on the lower floor. I lasted 2 stops and decided we should all get off. We then went for lunch. After which we got on another bus and completed the tour. The chances of me ever doing this kind of thing again is less than zero. However, the reason for the review is to advise anyone that reads this to use another service. I was irritated by the rep on the phone and the 23 minutes standing around while other tour operators were coming and going far more frequently.

We booked a two day pass for our weekend trip with grandson, thought it would be a great way for him to see the sights.
Once you get your head around the 3 routes you can plan.
On the first route heading to Buckingham palace we were trying to listen to the audio when a chap came on and started doing a guided tour over a microphone making it difficult and his less informed talk was annoying to say the least, we were glad to get off.
The buses say every 10 minutes but we waited 45 minutes at Harrodsburg for a bus and when it came it was standing room only and squashed in like sardines as we only wanted next stop we thought not too bad but he never stopped at next stop or the next despite several requests from passengers.
Eventually he stopped and when we asked why he had not let us off previously he was very rude and aggressive in front of my grandson.
We never used the bus again so waste of £99. Shame on their service would not recommend them and there are other bus services available I,m sure offering a more friendly service

We really enjoyed our day of exploring London on the Big Bus tour. We had never been to London before, and this was a great way to see historical landmarks and famous sites in a day, with the ability to get off the bus to further explore many of these places. A Big Bus tour is an excellent first step in visiting a new city.

I would highly recommend this to anyone who would like to seethe main tourist attractions in London. The commentary from both the prerecorded tour and the live guides was entertaining and informative. The background music during the prerecorded commentary really adds a great addition to the tour and makes you truly enjoy the sites of London even more. All big bus tour staff were friendly and knowledgeable. Thank you Big Bus tours for making my trip to London absolutely perfect!

Bought a MERLINK bus pass through the London Eye and Madame Tussauds website. Arrived on the day to be turned away by a large coloured gentlemen outside Madame Tussauds who said I would have to book a time slot. This wasn't mentioned when I booked the ticket and the London Eye customer services team say is simply not true. THE BIG BUS COMPANY HAVE IGNORED MY EMAILS.
The man who turned me away said that rather than disappoint my daughter I could buy another set of ticket at nearly £60 and then claim it back. I'm not a mug but bought the tickets to save our family day out in London with little hope of recovering the money. This technique is disgusting and Trading Standards have confirmed that they will look into it as an "unfair business practise".
Please be wary of this company - there are no contact details on the website and in my opinion they behave like sharks. There are other options for seeing London by bus - most of which provide contact details should something go wrong.

This was our first time riding the Big Bus London Hop-On Hop-Off Tour. It ran about £75 for two people, and it included a river cruise. Overall, we thought it was a great way to see downtown London. It’s pretty big and busy downtown, so the bus makes it doable to get around relatively quickly and see the major sites. The free headsets allow you to plug into the audio recording and hear interesting facts about parts of the city. The river portion was nice as well, and the boat staff did a great job and the guide was really funny—he made the trip! Finally, although the bus was great, be prepared for crowded buses on rainy days. In the end, we’d definitely use this bus again, so we recommend it for other families.

Had Phil as our guide on 9/19/18. He was friendly and knowledgeable about all things in London. He definitely made the tour worthwhile. We saw a ton of sites in a two hour period when we decided to get off and enjoy lunch at the Albert. It was one of the oldest establishments in town that he recommended.

Basically just got off the big bus tour today on the red line. For 90% of the journey had a blonde female guide (that I would not name) that was absolutely atrocious.
Sadly she made what should have been an excellent service opportunity adjectively poor. For some reason she said rather little about about the history and architecture of the route from tower bridge to Hyde corner. She did inform us however of how much solicitors are overpaid, the price of scallops 50 yrs ago and lots completely irrelevant information that really distorted the experience. When someone who is paid to be a informative tour guide gives a the explanation of Oliver Cromwell that ‘he tried to stop Christmas ‘ I really question their historical knowledge, accuracy and ability.
If you want to know what strange things can be seen by people wearing on Buckingham Palace Road on the weekend it may be for you. Doesn’t help when she shouted at the driver to ‘hurry up and stop driving like a Christian as I’m starving’.
Although I have to say that the young gentleman that replaced this lady for the follow few stops before we got off was excellent.
I would recommend the service but would avoid this guide in the future.

An ideal way to start a London holiday giving you an opportunity to see places and get your bearings to decide where to revisit. Of course there was a time when we were stuck in traffic for at least 15 minutes. This was a great opportunity for the guide to expand on attractions, history etc, however, she said very little. I did appreciate the recorded soundtrack, especially 'Land of Hope and Glory'. Later in the day I encountered another of your guides, Tabea, who kept us entertained when it was necessary for the bus to re-route. Will recommend to family and friends.

Bought tickets online went to use with a mobile device and were told we had to print by an extremely rude street attendant. Forced to go into a nearby hotel then go back from them to scan the same barcode on a paper ticket. Should have went with the original tour as they have better routes and a cheaper price.

After flying into London on a night flight from NYC and waiting for our room, we booked the bus tour and enjoyed the ride around the City along with the awesome commentary despite being tired.

Thank you!

We only had a guide 1 of 3 rides, and were pretty much ignored for the others. At that point we switched to the 'tube'. With all the construction in the city, several stops had moved, and/or had conflicting signage, so we ended up waiting in the wrong place more than once.

NO problems finding the bus pick up points and the staff were really friendly, with the commentation on the sights excellent and informative. However we booked the trip with the 'single'boat trip and got off at the Tower - and were told we could get the boat back, however when we came back we were told we couldn't, so had to get a bus. If we had gone on to Greenwich and got off there, we would have been stuck as there were no buses back from there. It needs to be made clear when you buy the ticket where and when you can get off/on the boat.
Had a lovely day on the bus tour. Thanks to Jo for a great live commentary! And the jokes :). I highly recommend this method of seeing the city especially if you are crunched for time.

Have just spent the last two days showing friends from Canada the sights of London. Although it would have been cheaper to have used public transport, I am so pleased we had Big Bus Tour tickets. We managed to fit in much more than we would otherwise have been able to due to time and sheer exhaustion! The live commentary on the red route is different from bus to bus as there are different people delivering it. They all have their own style and all point out different things. Make sure you tune your sound system to Channel 13 though or you will be listening to a boring, recorded commentary. The river trip was great, with a really informative commentary. Don’t miss it! There are great photo opportunities too. I would advise you to plan your day carefully as the tours end at different times on different routes, and the company need to update their stops as some of them are indicating that routes stop there which no longer do. This is very confusing. Overall though, the best bus tour of London I have done, and I have tried most of them over the years!

This was an amazing tour around london with a very informative tour guide Emma I really enjoyed the look around the city on the red route I would like to thank the driver wayne ( if I remember correctly) and the tour guide Emma for a 5 star tour.

The have a set route, but it is handled by different route colors. That is not bad.
What is confusing is that the buses do not stop at all stops. For example (stop numbers not exact - just to use as example): If you are on the red route, you can follow the stop at 1, 2, 3, then it jumps to stop 6, 7 8, etc. And these are all for the red route, so there is no explanation as to why they did not stop at 4 and 5 locations.
What is confusing is the half pieces of information. At one transfer stop from x color to red color, we told the bus driver and coordinator where we wanted to go. She strongly said to get the Red Route, West. AND, for when we wanted to return, get the Red Route East. So we go west, get to the place we needed to be (had tickets), finished the event and wanted to go back where we were. Go to bus stop, get on red route bus and ask if going East. NOPE. There is no east or west. It only goes one way. NO EAST or WEST. NOPE. Emphatically said. So we talk to the coordinator. Turns out, only the one location has east / west options. Sure would have been more accurate if the bus driver said "from this location, I only go in the one direction. It is another stop that gives the east / west options". (This type of half information was found in several interactions.)
Confusing ... The buses start running at 8:30. Actually no. If you are at some stops, the first bus you will see is going to arrive after 9:00 a.m. BUT if you want about two blocks for the next bus stop, that bus starts at 8:30. Would have been helpful to know that the first bus of the day differs at different bus stops. Oh, I can see this in some stop locations, but on the same street, in the same direction, the closest stop is after 9:00 a.m., but if you walk the two blocks in the same direction the bus would take ... then that location starts at 8:30.
Some employees were extremely helpful, and even would remember our questions when we got on the bus, to when we got off and the employee would give final advice for the things we wanted to visit.
But for every helpful employee, there were the ones that gave the briefest answer or information not quite helpful. For example: it might be: "it is on the right". What would be more helpful: "It is on the right, about two blocks down". Without that last piece of information, we kept wondering if we were overlooking something.
All in all, the hop on / off works well, but it can take a while to get used to the things that are confusing. I don't think we were that stupid to not know these things.

My husband and I enjoyed this tour which we were able to book and pay for at our hotel. We walked to the closest bus stop which was a five minute walk. We were able to take the red line later on and go on to take the cruise up part of the Thames which was interesting. Guides were very knowledgeable. It’s advisable to start early in the morning since there is a lot to see.

We've done bus tours in various locations in the past and always felt they are "ok" for the price paid and this time around was about the same. We usually do bus tours when first visiting a city and/or if we don't have much time. We've been to London once before and only had a 12 hour layover this time around and figured the hop-on hop-off bus would make best use of our time. Pre-purchasing the tickets online saves a little money versus paying on arrival. There are various stops that are close to public transportation - we took the tube from heathrow and stopped at Green Park, walkng from our tube stop to the bus pickup location was less than 5 minutes. The tour has multiple lines/buses and stops. Traffic was much heavier due to some sort of accident so the bus was moving very slow - the weather was hot and the bus has no air conditioning so it was hard to enjoy. After about 2 hours of little movement, the traffic started to clear and the tour was more enjoyable. We hopped off/on only a few times due to time constraints. You didn't have to wait too long for a bus and sometimes the buses were very empty. Unfortunately other times the buses were very crowded or at capacity. If you're unfamiliar with a city and want to get a bearing of the "tourist" spots or you don't have much time to spend in a city, then I would recommend taking a bus tour - although it is a bit pricey. If you have more time to spend and/or have a limited budget, you are better off using public transportation/taxi/uber/walking.

Never take this tour the last week prior to the start of school in London. Traffic was painful. We had to get off.

Our tour guide was easily distracted by guests and often didn’t realize her mic was off. It was a waste of money.

Visited London for the day with family and did the red route bus tour on tuesday.
Ian the tour guide (think he was Australia?) Was information and funny and made the trip-pretty thanks!

This is my review from August 2018. 1. Booking was easy and the routes that these tours take a good. 2. They are overcrowded for the price you pay. on the tour that i got on, the bus was so crowded that I had to stand on the bottom floor like you would on the underground. 2. If you hop off and stay at an attraction like the tower of London you will not get your money's worth. Just get on the red and ride it all the way through and then get on the blue and ride it all the way through. 3. You will not get a seat at the top unless it is later in the day OR after massive amounts of people get off at popular spots like the Tower. 4. Tour guides are good but seriously look at other bus tour companies you will see the same old stuff.

You either love Big Bus Tours or hate them... a lot depends on the type of traveler you are. We did a Big Bus-tour in San Francisco and loved it... so we tried London AND Paris! We had limited time and wanted to see it all. For our purpose Big Bus Tours work well for us. We come to a new city, weary of travel, and jump on a Big Bus tour and ride it around 1 time. This helps us get our bearings in a new town and lets us see shot of everything to decide what we want to do.

Big Bus had many great qualities but there are some issue that can/should be addressed:

Pros:

Usually hits all the major tourist attractions in a city.

Do not have to find “1” meeting place to get a ticket. This places Big Bus ahead of many competitors. Absolutely to get on/ off near where YOU start is huge! Many others have 1 predetermined meeting space and this can be very difficult to find in a new city ( think of the taxi costs to get to their office!)

Based on hours from when you start... not days. This can be huge if you get in the afternoon.

Live commentary is whoever you get.. some are much better than others!

Quick , usually very little waiting time for a new bus. But keep in mind, this is a type of public transport - it may not be there just because you want it too! ( Our longest wait time was 20 minutes - 1 time)

SOME bus drivers are vey considerate in ensuring that you get back to your stop at the end of the night. A few Guides were VERY good at nicely letting people know how far they would run and where they could get to at the end of the night.

Cons:

Taped commentary leaves much to be desired. This is the “bread and butter “ of your business and prerecorded commentary should be the VERY best that you can offer.. not lots of music to fill the time. Fill it up with interesting facts!!

Headphone issues and port maintenance need to be addressed. Many seats did not work and this is just unacceptable on a tour.

Bus should never be unloaded and reloaded unless it is broken. This process towards end of the night robs visitors of their valuable time and just makes everyone angry... if you shut down at 4 pm, shut at that time , do 1 last trip to drop everyone of and that is it! Shutting down uses throughout the day causes unnecessary waits and delays people.

People working the buses should be as helpful as possible and run as close to schedule as possible. The London Big Bus Tours ends fairly early so people should be made aware and be able to choose if this is a good fit for them.

We often saw customers being denied intermittently. At one stop they would say “No, get on another bus” and then the next stop they would let people with the exact same destinations on. Rule 1: no paying customer should EVER and told to get off/ denied entry to a bus. Staff may KINDLY inform customers of how far they can go but if you have a valid ticket staff should NEVER be denied entry. (bus was not full so this was never a space issue- appeared to be a trying to cut the number of buses on a given day/time)

If a bus runs into trouble, and causes delays.. Sorry BIG Bus drivers but you need to do an extra run at the end of the night. Communication between buses is paramount to ensuring that people do not get left off so far away from their stop and left. We had one issue where they ran down lines to less busses meaning we were transferred from bus to bus for no apparent reason causing major delays in our times and then we had to skip tours since the bus drivers would not run longer to correct the error.

This was a incredibly long review but if you manage your expectations Bug Bus is a GREAT tour that I would recommend to everyone. They could be amazing if they fixed some customer service issues.

Is this cheaper than public transportation- NO! But will it get you a great tour of a new city- YES!
Laura was friendly, knowledgeable, and funny! Cheers to making a rainy day interesting! The red tour covers most of the basics, but wish there was a stop closer to London bridge.
Laura was our tour guide and did a marvelous job! London needed the rain and she was a trooper sitting upstairs giving the tour.

I booked this tour for my sister and her grandchildren who were so keen to see London and this looked like a wonderful way to see the sights. We put them on the bus at Tower Hill and waved them off. They were moved on to another bus by staff and ended up seeing the Shard several times and not much else. They report that staff were very uncommunicative and when they asked how to get to Trafalgar Square they were told to get on the tube! I expected staff to be able to advise them on how to see the sights they wanted to see - It wasn't at all clear to them that there were different routes and it should be an easy thing to help them with. I'm really cross that they've wasted their afternoon in London and that I've wasted £67.

I booked on line for the two day ticket. £40. And got a cruise to Greenwich included, great value. 4 different routes to choose from mix and match hop off one hop on another,
easy to see whatever takes your fancy, Drivers were all friendly and let us know our stop had come, Happy me.

Despite it being an extremely hot day our tour guide showed no signs of flagging. We caught a bus at Green Park around 10am with tour guide Daniel who had such a clear English speaking voice. We hopped off, did the river cruise then the London Eye and finally got back on the bus. Daniel was our guide again and was as enthusiastic and informative as before despite the fact we were all worn out.
Such a great way to see the city. The guide on the boat was also very interesting and had a great London accent.

I did this tour today. If I’d stuck to the blue ring I probably would have rated this a 3. Interesting 1-1.5 hour trip.

Alas, I hopped on the red ring. We sat in traffic jams for 4+ hours. The driver kept letting people on board even though the bus was full and we couldn’t even see out the opposite window owing to bodies and back packs.

I feel really sad that I wasted a precious day in London.

Walk the area you’re staying in, hop on the tube. Save yourself the disappointment and angst on sitting on a crowded bus which really doesn’t get close to most of the sites. You’ll be happy if you want to hop on hop off along shopping strips.

I’ve done this tour in other cities and it was excellent. Just don’t bother with the London one.

I thought it was a pretty comprehensive tour of London. If you do all the routes you pretty much see everything. Unfortunately it was 95 and 97 degrees the two days we did the tour and there is NO AIR CONDITIONING. It was way too hot to sit up top. Of course
the weather was not the fault of the bus. My other complaint is that some of the buses were so crowded there were no seats. Maybe they need to add some buses during their busiest times

We always do the hop on hop off tour when we visit a city, this was the worst one we have ever done. Biggest waste of money. We spent our time sitting in traffic, there was also a cycle on so we were diverted which I think we should have been told about before buying tickets. We got off the bus after only seeing the Tower of London in 2 hours on the bus rather than sitting in a traffic jam and got on the river cruise. We then had to queue for 90 minutes for the river cruise because the first boat was full. More boats are needed at the weekend if there going to be included in the ticket price. The only saving grace was the commentator on the river cruise. Listen to the reviews and do not buy the hop on hop off tours and just use the tube to go to where you want. We didn’t bother using our ticket again even though we paid for 2 days. Your time is precious when you’re only in London for a weekend.

I bought tickets for Big Bus tour with our London eye tickets. We got on the bus (stop was about a 10 minute walk from the eye). There was a guide nearby who told us where to go and it was very straightforward. We stayed on the red route and got off at Buckingham Palace and rejoined the bus until Tower Bridge where we got on the boat to do the last leg . Whole experience was fabulous - a great a way to see the capital . We saw all the main sights and the guide provided us with fascinating commentary. We got seats on the top deck without a problem and even though it was a hot day there was a nice breeze to keep us cool. The boat trip was excellent too. We didn't bother with the blue route - that might have been too much to pack in- but overall would definitely recommend. Total price with London eye tickets was £145 for family of 4, which we felt was good value overall. Great experience and really helpful and friendly staff.

The Big Bus Hop on Hop Off tour of London was a bust. I was traveling with my daughter and her baby. After our first hop off, we were not able to hop back on as the next bus was full. After waiting for a second bus, it arrived full as well. Three people were allowed to board but everyone else was told they would have to wait for another bus. We wanted to see London and not spend the day at the bus stop waiting for a Big Bus that would actually have space for us to board, so we decided to forgo the bus and walk instead. The city was lovely, but the extra time spent waiting for busses we couldn't board and walking time we hadn't planned on didn't allow us to see all the attractions we were sold tickets to. I wish I had not wasted my money on the Big Bus London Hop-On Hop-Off Tour. The Hop-Off worked great but the Hop-On was a bad joke.

We opted for the red route, as it covered a lot of the places we wanted to get off and go see anyways. Being tourists without a car - we found the big bus super convenient for the family because we were able to travel, and get a taste of the city's rich culture, heritage, and history.

The guide was funny, witty, and at the same time did not say too much to distract from the tour itself. As we got a 2 day pass, it was very useful to just walk around the town and explore by foot too - and take things at a slower pace than to try and cover everything in 1 day.

We decided that we have never done any sightseeing in London althou we only live 20 odd miles away and we used the big bus 🚌 company as we have used them in New York and we weren’t disappointed at all and had a great day we decided to stay and do the whole loop the red route and the. Got of at the Tower of London

We attempted to buy tickets online for the Bug Bus hop-on hop-off bus tour. Each time we tried to pay for the tickets we got an error page.

In frustration, we eventually bought tickets from a vendor at one of the bus stops. The bus was fun to begin with. We enjoyed the audio guide. However, we had to wait a long time at the bus stops, and the bus routes were just too roundabout. In the end, over two days we took only two bus rides, compared to getting the London Underground five times. The underground was much more convenient and was fun for our kids.

At the end of our first day, we realized that we had been charged each time the website had shown an error. We disputed the charges immediately. A month later, I am still waiting for a refund.

We decided to try this out after using the Big Bus tours in Paris. The tour was good; we visited a lot of landmarks and did plenty of sightseeing. Our tour guide, Maddie, was a delight. She had so much good information to give regarding history, interesting facts and stories, etc. She was also really funny, and a great help regarding any inquiry. All in all, this was an enjoyable experience.

We took the Big Bus tour around inner London. Started at Marble Arch. The trip included a short river cruise. Got to see places we would not have otherwise see when travelling on foot. The traffic was crazy so be prepared for a bit of a stop start ride. Commentary was great but you could tell the guide had said the same things hundreds of times over. We got off at the Thames embankment near Parliament House and walked around, over the bridge and had lunch at southbank. Hopped on again later in the day but ended up repeating part of the the trip again. Also had to swap busses half way through the return journey back to Marble Arch. Happy with the tour even though the city, the bus and the traffic are very noisey.

Started on red route which seemed to be going to all touristy places but got off and then ended up on blue route as all very confusing as to where we should be standing when getting back on. Blue route Jjust went up and around Baker Street for what seemed like hours so got off and waited for red route bus. That was slow but traffic was bad in fairness and we ended up at Tower bridge on the boat trip. That was good fun and took us to Parliament. For money paid was not all that good value as most touristy things can be reached via Charing Cross and a good pair of walking shoes....

The bus tour was average for a big city. For a family of four, it cost £93 which I found a bit expensive for what you get. The tour is nice, passing most of London's main sites, the audio is OK, but there are lots of pauses (due to traffic). To be honest, I found the tour average. The bus was very busy with people standing, so many sites were obscured unless you were the first people on with an upstairs view.
Speaking to the staff - they were excellent and were really friendly and chatty.

We hopped on a blue route bus at the London Eye stop. While the staff was very helpful with issuing the tickets for a pre-booked ride, the traffic was so slow it took 95 minutes to go round the Tower of London and back to the Big Ben intersection. We hopped off and continued our ride on the local double deckers for fear of not getting to Mme Tussauds before the closing time. They advertise the hop on hop off as an enjoyable way of discovering the city but you get faster from one stop to the next if you walk or take a regular bus.

They don't respect the stops on their own map, so it's impossible to predict the next stop, there are very few busses on some on the lines(25 minutes waiting and no appropriate bus came). Also, when we bought the tickets, the guy selling them made some mistake, the money had to be refunded etc... DO NOT GO ON THIS TOUR. I'm not saying other tours are better, but I can say that this one isn't.

The hop-on hop-off guided bus tour was great.
Rob, the tour guide (That's his name.Don't actually rob him!) made the bus ride worth the time and money spent.
First bus we took had no guide, but a recording of music interrupted by a boring man telling short facts about the places we passed. The music wasn't very varied either, so I grew a bit tired of it after a while.
but then we hopped off the bus for lunch and hopped back on another bus (which is a GREAT feature of the bus ride. You get to drive by all the touristy sites and spend as much time as you wish on any of them and just continue the tour as if you were allways there).
But anyways, back to Rob. (Rob, if You're reading this, we're the Norwegians in the back of the bus, behind that lady You helped reached Madamme Tussauds before it closed)
The second bus had this amazing guide. He was funny, smart, had all sorts of different fun facts and textbook facts and I felt smarter leaving the bus. When we were in a small trafic jam, he even took the time to help a lady reach the museum she was going to before it closed. He knew everything. When to leave the bus, which underground to take and where and explained it very good so she could make it in time.

We had originally planned to hop off the bus and take the boat back to our starting position, but decided to stay and listen to Rob instead. And it was great.

We'll have to take the boat ride next time we're in London.

It may seem as if Rob paid me to write this praise but I promise he didn't.
In fact, I felt the need to give him a tip for his service. I did, however, promise to write a review on Tripadvisor. So here I am.

Oh, I did not interact much with the bus driver, but he also left a good impression.

BTW, I brought a pair of headphones from the trip home, but they were not good quality for music, so don't bother doing that. Fair enough for the recording on the bus tho.

We did the HO-HO for London in late May 2018 when we visited there. We got to our first pick-up point at 8:15 am and they did arrive on time. I believe we did the Blue and Red tour in one day. Not much traffic but it was WARM that day. We had a blast. Nice and friendly drivers. This is the one to do for HOHO.

The bus was so crowded, people were sitting on the steps (double decker) and there was nowhere to stand without being pushed. Didn't get to see many of the sights because of this bearing in mind that it cost £33 per person. When I reached out to Big Bus Tours, they did NOT respond. Avoid. Expensive, uncomfortable and awful customer service. They do not care about the quality of your experience once they have your money.

My husband and I rode the hop-on hop-off tour two days while in London last week. The first trip included Kevin as our tour guide - and he was lovely!
We thoroughly enjoyed his anecdotes, and will recommend friends visiting the city seek him out on his tours!

Our experience began when we boarded the BigBus HOHO in Paddington, intending to get off at the Marble Arch. Our driver did not announce the stop nor did he stop for passengers to get off. When we talked to him and asked to be let off, he refused! No matter what either of us said or did, he would not open the door to let us out there or at any stoplight. The HOHO eventually ended at Baker Street, where we were all told to get off and get on a different bus to continue. The driver got off, as well, as apparantly this was the end of his shift, and he scurried away after another confrontation. Be wary if you are a couple of females traveling thousands of miles from home. Because it is a uniformed driver driving a legitimate bus doesn't you can't be held against your will and driven somewhere you don't want to be!

We used this as a way to get to know the city on our first day of our first trip to London. They have three different lines to chose from blue, green and red. We chose to do the red line because that line uses live tour guides and not a prerecorded message. Our guide for the trip was Abby, she did a great job. Had a lot of inside knowledge that really brings the buildings alive with history. She even recommended a great little mom and pop fish and chip restaurant which was awesome. It’s a great way to see the town and use it as a mode of transportation. Even if you back track and drive by the same place twice, each guide has a different take and you’ll probably learn something new.

Very poor experience! The staff was unhelpful and disinterested. Often came acrosss empty buses where the drivers were on a break. When asked where the next stop was they instead asked "where we wanted to go" and then told us how to walk there directly. This happened multiple times. It was the biggest joke, after paying so much for tickets. It's a big change from the Big Bus tour fun experience we had in Paris the previous day. Really had high standards for this franchise but it fell flat. In addition, when we were finally able to board a bus, the audio didn't sync with the location.
This was my first trip to the UK. I highly reccomend using the Big Bus tours to get around. The bus takes you to all of the major sightseeing spots as well as shopping areas around time.

(It's probably excellent for anyone, actually.) Our family enjoyed the Big Bus on-off tour very much. The routes were fun and went by every major attraction we wanted to see. The seats were comfortable, and the upper level provided a great view of the city as you went through. The audio was helpful, although sometimes the music with the audio drowned out the voice, and we lost the information being conveyed by the narrator.

We have seen some reviews say to walk instead, and although this sounds good in theory, these routes are generally too far for all but the hardiest walkers to handle, and you'd end up taking far longer. Unless you have 10 days in London to wander, the bus gives you a wonderful overview of the city on one tour.

We used the tour to get from our hotel to multiple places were wanted to see in detail, and we highly recommend using the Big Bus tour not just as a tour, but as transportation for first-time visitors who might have time to see some sights but not everything.

A hop-on/hop-off bus is a good way to see a city and decide later what to go back to. Hard to really tell the route based on the map. Seemed like for awhile around the Marble Arch that we went around in circles (with the same recorded commentary) about 3 times. Still worth it to see a variety of areas and not have to worry about transportation. It does go to many good spots. Traffic was bad in spots on the day, but can't blame that on the tour bus. The drivers did very well maneuvering through traffic.

Being here for 6 weeks as a study abroad student, I thought I was too good for a bus tour. Boy was I wrong. Maddie (our tour guide) was kind enough to grace us with her wit and unending knowledge on her city. Despite her scoffing at our clubbing events the evening prior, Maddie was otherwise amazing. I learned a ton about the city and learned so many places that I want to go during my six weeks now.

Just went on the Paris Big Bus Tour and enjoyed it so much that I decided to tour London in the same fashion. I’m so glad I did because Maddie (guide) and Joshua (driver) were awesome. Maddie was full of knowledge and tidbits that she delivered with humor quite often. London is crazy busy with traffic so don’t except a quick trip. There were times we just sat in traffic (Queen was in residence and Prince Charles’s birthday was the day prior). I would certainly recommend this bus tour. The price was perfect for the value received.

We did go to London hoping that our journey with three kids on board will be exciting and enjoyable. Choosing your tour company we did expect to make our visit in London easy, pleasurable and memorable.
Instead we were confused with very complicated route system. There were not much help from your drivers and tour guides. We ended rounding all day around Hyde park stuck in traffic for three hours!Changing routes and colours did not help as seems like we just had the same ride around the park!! In the end we had an hour left to our evening coach back home to Southampton. Desperately we did ask one of your guides if he could hep us to choose a bus driving us to Big Ben -this is what my little son wanted to see all day!. He helped us to choose the bus. And when we were nearly there , the bus was diverted! We ended up running on our fours with three kids and a buggy to see a Big Ben and making it 5 minutes to our Coach. If we would know how badly informed and organised are your drivers and guides we could choose a different options for the day, which ended up being very spoilt for us and the kids.

I've been to London before and we wanted to try another couple of BigBus tours of the city. It's a great way to get around and learn things at the same time. There are BigBus folks clearly visible at the stops so easy to truly hop off and hop back on where/when you'd like to.

If you've never been to London before, I'd say a tour like this is essential. If you're a repeat visitor like I am, it's still a great way to get around and connect with some of the most famous areas within London.

Finally, I've found a great sense of professionalism among the many BigBus folks I've encountered. From the drivers to the tour guides to the wranglers (the folks at the bus stops that assist you), everyone is into what they do and make you feel like a customer!

We booked the multi-day pass on the Big Bus. This is an easy way to see London and get around to all the main sights. It was easy to get on/off and the overall tour was good. The two main highlights of the tour was doing the "night" tour and seeing everything lit up and the boat tour all the way to Greenwich is a don't miss. Only downside for the four stars is when you approach the end of their work day (discontinue running) the staff wasn't very clear on the location of the last stop. Unfortunately for us we weren't in the best location when they stopped and had to use the tube (London Underground) to get our way back to where we were staying. It happened again on the night tour but shame on us this time for not asking about the termination point of the tour.

Well organised.Not too expensive 37pounds per person for a day pass.
Better value for longer period passes and family groups.(see the website).
Three tours including a section on the Thames river.Wide number of hop on's hop off locations across the whole of the city all close to the major attractions.
Generally 20 mins between buses arriving at stops.
Commentary in all languages( free earphones and paper guide).
Better than most and seemingly with the majority of buses for tour London.

This is the 3rd time I have used the tour bus service..... absolutely love it! This time I booked a 1 day ticket online by mistake (meant to buy the 48hr) and didn’t notice until we went to board the bus. This was sorted for me immediately for a small upgrade fee with no issue. On such a hot and busy day it was so nice to be greeted by “can do” people.
The hop on hop off service is so convenient and relaxing; we tend to walk on or close to the bus routes and when our feet ache we hop back on! Our main guide this time was Karen, with Patrick the driver. Both were so accommodating and helpful; there was several incidents and marches over the bank holiday weekend which meant the bus was diverted on occasions during the tour. Karen took time to explain this and gave excellent advice on which alternative stops would be best for the main attractions. I would highly recommend the red route with the live talk, Karen was excellent and very knowledgeable..... a good mixture of history and celebrity gossip.
The 48hr ticket includes a return boat trip from Westminster to Greenwich, excellent value with hilarious live talk.
Would definitely recommend Big Bus.

I was so unlucky to ask a driver a question on a blue line. I should not have done that. It resulted in 4-5 angry comments about NOT talking to a driver while driving. One polite reminder to me might have been better... And more service minded.

My question (to the driver who got angry): when was the next stop? (I had a young daughter who needed to pee, so I wanted to know.)

In all fairness I want to balance the review by saying when we actually managed to get on a bus it was nice and the tour guide was decent. Problem lies in the fact that we only got on the bus once. Wait times were very long, and in general the bus was seriously crowded. At the end of the day, after walking for several miles, we were all looking forward to hopping on the bus to relax and head in a direction we had not yet been. Big Bus is in sight and we make it clear by waving we are at the stop and want to get on .... just to see the bus zoom by us and never even slow down. We walk around the corner and spot a few folks in Big Bus shirts, we verified we were at the correct stop and told them about our experience moments before. They proceed to tell us that they've had to report several drivers that day for that exact behavior. Big bummer, hence we walked back to our hotel knowing we would not have time to see more of the city without the bus. As such, I cannot recommend using this tour option!

My wife was working for a few days, so decided to use this to get around London and visit the key sites. Downloaded the app and the two day pass is the best deal compared to the competitors.

The English guided bus was okay, not a lot of commentary and when there was commentary it sounded like she had done it a million times before.

Tried to use the bus to get around a few more sites on day two and in the end waiting for the bus was too much of a hassle.

In hindsight I should have bought the Oyster card earlier and just used the tube to get around it would have been quicker and easier, the tube is not cheap compared to other cities but I think if I had done that it still would be less than the 39pounds they charged for the two days ticket.

If you want proper tour, you should book one, this is a little bit of a half way option.
The live English speaking guide named Angus was witty and the driver Dariusz was really impressing. I’m glad I chose this trip in spite of the horrible wheather.

Yesterday myself and 5 others had the privilege of riding the red route with Kevin and Mike. The experience was enjoyable and Kevin’s knowledge of London was impeccable. As soon as we boarded the bus Kevin took an interest in the sights we wanted to visit and made sure that no one missed a stop. Once we left the tour we felt sad that Kevin wouldn’t be our guide on the next bus. But!!!! Imagine our delight when we boarded the red bus again to find Kevin upstairs waiting to tell us all the history of London and he remembered us.

We are visiting London as part of a Hen Weekend and Kevin made the Bride feel very special - he took an interest in his audience and made it feel like he knew everyone for that small time that they were on the bus. He adapted his tour to suit his audience and delivered his facts in a lighthearted and enthusiastic manner. He was extremely friendly and clearly loves his job. To us he will forever be KEV.I.N the best tour guide in London!

We used the hop on hop on tour bus, and were not disappointed. We used this in Paris and I must say London was much better thanks to our live guide. She was a lovely French girl, Oude, who took the time to make sure everyone knew where they were going. She told us about every area in London and gave recommendations for each stop. Would definitely use this service again, and hope to get her! Send her my thanks.

Also really enjoyed taking the free river cruise.

Big Bus in London is fine, for what it is. Don't be misled by the hype though. The buses are unpredictable. I waited almost an hour for one at Paddington. The taped commentary is repetitive.
OTOH, it worked just fine for the most part. The Big Bus people are mostly helpful, and you do get to see a lot.

I did a 24 hour hop on hop off pass. I rode the green line from St Pancras station into the city, switched to the blue line, grabbed the included boat ride (with live commentary), and then went out exploring on my own for a bit. I met up with the red line after and did The complete loop. The green and blue prerecorded commentary were very informative. Commentary played on time and made sense to the area we were touring. The red line with live English commentary was also really well done. The presenter (Maddie) knew her stuff and was able to answer questions I had that weren't necessarily part of the tour. There is some overlap in all the routes, but it ensures you see the highlights of the city.

It was a bit cold on the top deck as it's open, so dress warmly.

I would recommend this tour for others who have only a short time in London in order to make the most of it.

we booked the tour for 2 days and it was a great way to have a look at the city ,with the London Eye tickets option (which I highly recommend) and a river cruise (we went to Greenwich by train and came back on the boat) everything was amazing and the people were very friendly and helpful.

We thoroughly enjoyed the ride around London. Super convenient for us to jump off on the places we wanted to check out in more depth. We had an even better experience with Gareth who on our ride back home answered all our questions about the sites we saw. Very knowledgeable about each location and filled us in on some extra info and tips!

We visited London for the first time.Big Bus London Hop-Off Tour was an opportunity to see a lot in a short time.
Good tour, we saw everything we had planned A comfortable bus, the opportunity to get off the bus and come back . I can recommend

Bought our tickets at an amazing price, combined with tickets to the London Eye. Got into our first bus (red line) and was very pleased with the humor and friendliness of the tour guide and driver, who made our young son laugh and made us feel comfortable while he acted as little boys do. Got off at a stop to catch the next line, the blue line. Asked the gentleman when the next bus would come and he said 25 minutes, so we saw some of the sights paying attention to time. Not even 10 minutes later we saw a bus for the blue line wiz last without even stopping. Finally, after waiting almost 45 minutes for another bus, we got on and decided it'd be easier to stay and complete the entire tour on this single bus rather than hop on and off and try to catch other busses. The audio guide on the tours are very informative and enjoyable. Not the best tour I've been on, but certainly not the least! Would recommend to others, with some precautions.

Our first day in London we did the hop on hop off tour. It was great because it gave us the lay out of the city and target where to hit the next day. It was also great because we got to know a ton about the history of the city we wouldn’t have otherwise gotten. Our tour guide, Matt, was high energy, funny, knowledgeable and gave us great recommendations for what to do around town! He made the tour. We went on one in Paris and it didn’t even compare to the personal touch the live tour guide gave!

London has a few HOHO bus companies to choose from. After taking the time to compare the three, we went with 'The Big Bus'. This was certainly the right decision as we saw many sights and highlights of London with our 3 day HOHO ticket. The ticket included a return river Thames cruise which we took from Westminster Pier. The cruise took about 45 mins each direction with live commentary. The HOHO bus also gives live commentary on the red line, while both the green and blue we're done by earphones. The bus offers free wifi but it doesn't always work, when it did it worked well and fast. One thing I noticed was the big bus was always around and ran every 10-15 mins. I barely saw the other companies and when I did, it wasn't as frequent as big bus. Overall great experience and now after this experience, I now take hoho sightseeing options worldwide.

Just returned from a trip to London for three days. Spent one day on the Big Bus London tour and was very happy we did!! Really good tour. We took the Blue and Red tours, hopped off at few places including Harrod's and Buckingham Palace. I loved taking this bus! We got to see all the important "must see" London locations. Really good overview and nice fun facts given on the tour. We didn't wait at all at Westminster Bridge stop, and only had to wait about 10 mins in front of Harrod's. I would recommend this tour if you want to see all that London has to offer, but don't have a lot of time to see it! Also loved the Thames River cruise that was included. We took that last cruise of the day so we were able to start the cruise in daylight and end with fantastic views of London Bridge at night!

A highly informative but thoroughly entertaining 2 hour Big Bus Tour with Kevin and Monica. We have experienced bus tours all over Europe and USA but Kevin is by far the most entertaining host ever. Monica’s driving was impeccable throughout. All in all a wonderful start to our London weekend.

Thank you K&M.
Was not happy with their service. Wish I had used a different bus company. Would never use them again.

I took my mother and some elderly relatives from Canada for a day trip to London. We were agressively approached by the rep at the stop by Waterloo station.

When the bus eventually did arrive the guide was not particularly welcoming. He sat in a prime location at the top and front of the double decker, depriving paying passangers the seats. He then proceeded to go on about the second world war with disparaging remarks about Germans and French. Making inappropriate political comments, as a guide, is not acceptable and do not reflect the views of the people they are representing. I was embarrassed and angry.

We then had to change bus at Green Park to another guide who was equally bad, and talked utter rubbish while we went past many interesting things. Often using the phrase "as we like to say!" before saying something idiotic that I (being british) do not say or know anyone who does.

I would not recommend any visitors use this company as there are alternative ones to use. Turn away from any aggressive reps who may approch you, and find one of the other companies.

After waiting 45 minutes for a bus (Waterloo station) to arrive we commenced our tour that took 3 hours. The attendant at the stop was only interested in onselling tickets to other attractions rather than doing something about the non appearance of a bus.I was surprised to have a live guide but the need becomes obvious when you spend 30 minutes in traffic getting through one intersection and they try to keep you entertained by prattling. The bus does not go past Buckingham Palace(only to the side). I have used the same franchise in Paris, Barcelona, San Francisco, Budapest, Malaga, Madrid and elsewhere.This service cannot deliver any value at all in London. Rather I suggest the 70 GBP (for 2) is better spent on a cab where you will see more, inhale less fumes and importantly not go round in circles!!

I took 48 hrs ticket for £38 online, which was £10 more expensive than other bus tours. The reason why I took big bus tour was a feedback I found online. People said that Big Bus was better as no need to wait more than 10 minutes. It is not true!!! I was waiting for 40 minutes yesterday and decided not to use it today after 20 minutes of waiting because didn't want to waste my time on the bus stop. Next time I'll use just underground travel card. Very disappointed

We decided to do a 1 day bus tour of London to get a good idea of London, initially. After sifting through 3 companies, I found that Big Bus tour map suited us well for what we wanted to do.

On the day, we finished London Eye by 11:30, grabbed a quick lunch and moved to the Big Bus stop which was easy to find. Saw a lot more of big buses than other tour companies. Caught the red tour bus (The color of route is shown on the display board at front) to tower bridge, which was fantastic as we got space on the top deck and the live commentary was fantastic. From there we got on the cruise, which had a crowded top deck, hence we went downstairs, which lessened the experience. We got off at Westminster from where we caught the blue bus. But we had to wait around 15 minutes for this and it was totally crowded and we had to sit below. Which is actually a bit boring.

Overall it is a very good way to get a feel of London, quickly. But would advise to start off early to get the best seats.

Visited London in August with my family and decided to go on the Big Bus Tour.  We chatted to the Big Bus rep at Regent Street as well as some reps from other bus tour companies and after hearing their description of the tours it was clear that The Big Bus was the company to use.  The bus arrived within 5 minutes and we were welcomed on the bus by a super friendly driver.  There was ample room to store our stroller and the driver waited until we were safely seated upstairs with our 2 year old until he started to drive off.  The bus provided a map of the tour as well as cleanly packed earbud units.  The bus was very clean and the driver navigated the streets without any sudden breaking etc.  We were very impressed with the recorded information that we listened and felt that a great deal of thought had gone into its content.  We were able to hop off the bus after a few stops and hop back onto another equally clean and smoothly driven bus thirty minutes later.  Although we did not avail of the 24hr usage, we thought that was a facility that would clearly be useful to other tourists.  I would definitely recommend The Big Bus Company London to any person/family in London.  The company provides an excellent level of service not just in London but also in other cities where we have travelled with them such as Hong Kong, San Francisco and Dubai.  Well Done Big Bus on your high standards of customer service, well planned tours as well as your informative and helpful staff.  Would we use you again? Most definitely a resounding YES.

Sent from my Samsung Galaxy smartphone.

Thiis is good for a hop on hop off way around London, but because you pay by the day this becomes a pricey transportation option. The tube and double decker city buses are cheap and easy to use, making them better options.
