The "tour" part is a cheesy recording that tells you not much and the bus goes along quickly so you don't really see anything. The package can include a boat tour and a skip the line ticket for the London Eye. The boat tour is better than the bus as there is a live person, however the wait for the boat is lengthy. Don't plan on using the boat as an efficient means of transportation (they even told us it would be faster to walk). The skip the line ticket for the London Eye is a voucher you have to stand in line to redeem. I am sorry I spent money on this.

I made the mistake of buying a three-day pass for our family of 4, thinking we could use the bus as our means of getting around the city to the various sites we wanted to see. That was a mistake.

The first day was very nice. Got on the red bus with live tour guide -- he was informative and entertaining, and we had a good overview of the city. If I'd left it there we'd have given a five-star rating.

Next day we waited at a stop for a bus that never came (at least not for half an hour, though Big Bus says they are on a 15-20 minute rotation). Lots of City Tours and Original Tour buses went by -- no Big Bus. We finally walked. When we did get a blue bus, we found the recorded tour was light on information (sometimes shared after we had passed the spot discussed) and heavy on music. And we learned that this was a terrible way to get to sites, since you often had to take the entire route (going a different direction) to get to the place you wanted to see.

Third day we waited ... and waited... and waited for the green bus. Again, saw 3 Original Tours buses stop while we waited for 1 Big Bus.

If I was doing it again, I'd buy 1 day, enjoy the overview, then use the Tube or taxis the rest of my visit.

Choose the 2 day pass with Thames cruise.
Did the full Blue tour loop which took 4 hrs but saw so much of the sights all from the top of the bus.
Good commentary but the following day when hopping on and off in the rain, one bus had a tour guide with great local knowledge and humour which I'm not sure everyone got but I thought he was amusing.
Worth it though at first thought it was a bit pricey.
The guys at the stops were friendly and helpful and easy to find the hop on/off points as all clearly signed which makes getting around simple

Excellent my wife, 1 year old and I purchased a day hop on hop off ticket today. The day was going exceptionally good with temp mid 20s had a fantastic day sightseeing until bubs spits her dummy in the Thames. Of course we didn't have another and everything fine until we got back on the bus mid afternoon. Bubs just cried and cried and cried, of course she was tired but couldn't sleep on the bus. We decided to bail out in a hurry and the wife left her phone on the bus with all the photos of our trip. We had about 10 bus drivers on the hunt for it by the time we realised about an hour later after bubs was asleep. The guys were unbelievable the way they radioed ahead to other drivers and the ones on the ground kept us updated. 4 hours later and anxiously waiting the phone was found, bubs was sound asleep and wife was more than happy. Finding her phone even helped with the sad news we just received from home that day that our much loved family dog of 14 years had passed away.

We got our tickets from a gentleman outside Victoria Station, whom also pushed us to buy Madame Tussauds tickets from Big Bus Tours as it was way cheaper and gave us quick access to the attraction to skip the queue outside. In good faith we hopped off on the Madame Tussauds stop, only to discover that these were vouchers that he sold us and gave us nothing but quick access to the back of the line like everybody else. Turns out the actual tickets are cheaper than what this clown outside Victoria sold us as well, so that was a great start of our tour day.

Our tickets also included a boat ride down the Thames. So we wanted to head over there after Madame Tussauds. In good faith we waited at the bus stop with another 10-15 people, only to discover 45minutes later that the buses didn't go anymore that day. Absolutely sublime that was. Seems to be difficult to at least slap a time table on the wall at the bus stop instead of wasting inc on other commercials.

Oh, and the headphones didn't fit into the plugs, so people had to share headphones on the few that were working. Had to explain the problem to an elderly couple whom were quite disappointed.

Giving this a 2/5 rating because the concept is good, and the view from the bus is alright if you sit in the front, but the information, execution and standards are below what is to be expected.

It was raining and we had overslept (jetlagged). Our hotel concierge had an excellent idea to take the Big Bus to get an overview of the city. We walked in the rain to the bus stop. Got on and stayed on for the entire red route. It gave us a good idea of what to see. (Fortunately, it was the day before the race that blocked some of the major streets. We lucked out based on some of the later reviews.) It was nice to stay dry from the rain. The first tour guide was fun and funny. The second one was just okay.

It is a great IDEA to hop on and off the bus and tour around London and see all the sights BUT every tourist, including myself, always forget that central london is like NYC time square, MADNESS. It is more often bumper to bumper traffic 7 days a week. The bus ideally would like to stick to the every 10-15 min stops at each stop but it is absolutely not realistic due to traffic. Even when the bus picks you up, you are still stuck in traffic so the estimated time they say will take for a full tour, you must add an extra 45min.

I think buying 1 day pass is worth it but any more days is not. You really need to dedicate 1 day to taking the bus and you will get your money's worth. If you try to spend 2 days taking the bus, i feel you will loose days where you can take the tube and get to destinations much quicker.

The thing is, every tourist is scrambling for time to see attractions. Taking the big bus takes a lot of time waiting and sitting in traffic. In theory the night bus and the boat bus is nice but there is not enough time in a day to do all this with the insane traffic in Central London.

To leave on a good note, we had an excellent live tour guide - i think his name was Robert. He was funny and very informative.

Poor service with not enough buses on the routes. There were twice as many red buses coming through on the stops. We stood for as long as 55 minutes on some stops instead of the advertised 10-20 minutes. We wasted most of our day standing on bus stops. Never again Big Bus Tours. Next time it will be the Original Red Bus Co. for sure.

The hop-on, hop-off bus tour was decent and went to most of the major attractions. But the guide gave very vague directions about how to get to sights once you got off the bus. In general, the bus tour got you in the vicinity of the sights so I thought it was OK. However, we waited for nearly an hour for pick up after we did the boat tour and no bus ever came. We had to take the Underground back to our hotel.

The main issue I had was with the Thames boat ride, run by City Cruises, that's included with the ticket. First, it's a fairly short ride and it's kind of hard to see a lot of the buildings from the river. That's OK - it is, what it is. But the guide kept making sexist jokes that made at least a few of the women around me really uncomfortable. Jokes about being able to see half-naked women in a health club that's right on the river - saying some days were really enjoyable and others brought horrible sights you couldn't unsee. Making that comment once was unacceptable. But then he kept expounding on it. It was really offensive and inappropriate. He made several other jokes about women that were offensive or insulting. He also spent a lot of time shilling for tips. Big Bus tours needs to disassociate themselves from City Cruises if this is the caliber of commentary they allow on their tour.

We had originally planned on using a different tour company but after being unable to find them, spoke with the BIGBUS agent and booked our trip. We began at Victoria Station, although you can purchase your tickets at almost any stop where they have agents. The agents are also a good reference for questions as you hop on/off. The first agent seemed a bit pushy as he seemed more interested in just making the sale. We walked around Victoria Station and latter came back and the second agent was very helpful. We purchased the 1 day (24 hour) pass, which includes the River Cruise. We added St. Paul's Cathedral, London Tower, & London Eye. The only ticket we didn't pre-purchase was Churchill's War Rooms, it wasn't offered and I forgot to ask. There is a student discount, so don't forget to ask, our agent offered.

There are 2 different tours, labeled Red & Blue. The Red tour is an English Guide-led tour, the Blue is longer but is an audio, in several languages- they provide headphones. We began the tour just down from the station and rode the entire Red route first, only hopping off a couple of times. We prefer this approach as it allows you to hear about everything, then return to the attractions that are of most interest. We stayed on the Red bus and then hopped off for the River Cruise which is a one-way cruise up the river. The guide on the river cruise was good and included several light hearted comments.

We then got back on the blue bus to take it back to our hotel in Kensington. After 7:30 they run the Purple line, a hotel shuttle for drop-off only, which they had us switch to at Marble Arch. While this seemed like the right approach, in hindsight, it would have been much quicker to just pay the £4.00 ticket and take the Underground.

The following day we hopped back on the bus from our hotel around 9:15-9:30 hoping to get to the walking tour by 11. 2 guides told us it was possible but it ended up taking much longer and we missed this tour. We finished the Blue tour through Kensington and Paddington. At this point traffic was at a slow crawl so we opted to walk to St. Paul's, and Tower of London(HIGHLY RECOMMEND). Finally took the bus to the London Eye to complete our 24 hour ticket. (Note: the attraction tickets are valid beyond the 24 hours for the bus ticket).

Buses: Each of the buses we were on was clean and in good shape. We rode -- like nearly everyone -- on the open top section. On the second afternoon we chose to ride on the first level to avoid the sun, but quickly learned the buses are not air conditioned.

The drivers were each safe and navigated the city's narrow streets with ease. While the guides are extremely helpful, we found the drivers to be less so. (The Blue route does not have guides so the driver is the only source of information). This didn't impact our trip but was notable given the strength of the guides.

Schedule: Due to traffic, the schedules can vary widely which is to be expected. They state every 20-30 mins and we found this to be accurate.

App: the tour company has an iPhone app which we found somewhat helpful but also lacking in several key features common in other tour apps we've used.

1) Route maps - it is very effective to look up locations and stops for the bus.

2) Schedule: we had hoped the app would give approximate arrival times by stop. This is common functionality but is not available in the app.

3) Guide: The audio guide is not included on the app, so you plug in each time you hop on the bus (blue). We would like to have had a way to unlock the guide from the app and use our phones.

Overall we gave them high marks for customer service. We would definitely use them again in another city.

We went on the big bus tour red with Matt , he made our journey he was funny and his knowledge was great he made our trip, loved the joke about Big Ben minute hand lol😜 well done he does a great job and seems to really enjoy it thanks again

The best company world wide compare other sightseeing companies! By far Big Bus is the best.

About delays
London is a big city.
Big city means lots of traffic!

And top of that council, road works everywhere that is something beyond big Bus sightseeing.

Guys take my advice check TripAdvisor, and when you go to any BigBusTours stop ask a member of stuff And buy your tickets.

We've been to London many times, but a sore knee made a hop-on, hop-off a good choice for this couple. The bus with the piped-in tour was fine, but would have been better with a more detailed audio presentation.

We switched to a live guided bus and were lucky to have Gareth for our guide. Entertaining, informative, and very kind - helpful to those getting on the bus and those leaving for attractions or meals. Lovely diction - easy to understand. The guided tour - 5 stars!

We had taken the Big bus tour about 20 years ago. I think traffic has gotten so bad in the ensuing years that the Big bus tour felt like an extra long bus ride. We started on the red tour with the live guide but he was difficult to understand. There was a lot of quiet time while riding in traffic. We started the day after 10 on a Thursday. We then jumped to the blue tour with an audio guide. The guide was easy to understand but once again a lot of dead time and a lot of traffic. What could have been a shorter tour ended up riding around in traffic forever. Our kids fell asleep at times for lack of interest.

They had added a boat ride on the Thames. The boat ride was run by another company and the crew now also give a verbal tour which was interesting enough. The kids enjoyed the boat ride.

We were too late to do the live walking tour.

Would not do this tour again. Was very disappointed.

We purchased our tickets before we left the US. Big mistake. We first tried Big Bus in Paris and were very disappointed in the crowded buses and poor service there. We already had pre-purchased vouchers for London so we were stuck with them for that portion of the trip. Their marketing scheme is very good but there are insufficient seats for the number of ticket holders. London was worse than Paris. A bus may come every 10 to 35 minutes but if it is full they will just pass by and you are stuck. The employees are rude unless you are buying something from them. Several of the other hop on off seemed a lot less crowded and seemed to have more buses running. Big Bus was often like riding in the subway with standing room only and no view of the city. Go with another line this one is terrible.

More expensive than City Tours (£35 Vs £23.90)

Bought tickets in one location, then told to walk to another, and from there to yet another and then to another!! More like a walking tour!.

Finally told my ticket covered the Night Tour only to then find that it wasn't valid (I could pay £21 for another ticket)!

Total con.

I've never used Big Bus before, and won't be doing so again.
Book with another compay

I'd like to thank the guys down at big bus tours for the amazing experience. Thanks to this service I was able to see the best parts of London on a super cool bus. I purchased the two day pass. On day one I caught the blue line and just sat on the bus for the entire route which takes about 4 hours. I took note of which bits I'd like to see more closely on day 2. Hopping off and on the bus again is a piece of cake. The recorded narration is also very good and informative. I definitely recommend this company and it's services to fellow travellers.

Don't know it's always or today but we are at Madam Tussauds London waiting outside in a Big Bus for last 40 minutes if not more. Neither is this bus going nor the staff is guiding us to any other Big bus. We got into the bus from Marble Arch at around 2:30 after asking the driver where we want to go to. Along with us we're other people too and the driver said yes to al the places. Then he suddenly stopped in front of Madam Tussauds and did not tell us that he is stopping for a long halt. All people kept on asking and even driver was in the bus but the bus did not depart. So frequency on a Sunday may be 40 min. But saw many buses of Golden Tours and Original tours running and passing by. Also, observed that in many of their buses wifi doesn't work. Took a 3 day tour with them. Initially I thought that there may be some problem but it's consistent that on most buses wifi doesn't work though they say it's on all the buses. They do give rain poly covers. I asked but the driver said that router must be there. Next time will definitely take Golden/ Original Tours but not Big bus.

We bought a 48 hour bus ticket for the family. What an awesome way to see London. We were fortunate enough to have dry weather so we stayed on the top deck of the open bus. The best thing about these buses is that you see everything. They also have multiple routes and you can hop on and off where ever you like (as long as it is a bus stop).

Would recommend this to a first time visitor as it will give you a good overview of London.

The big bus tour of London was perfect to get familiar with London on our first day. It's also a great activity when you're jet lagged; all you have to do is hop on to get a tour of the city highlights. The stops are very convenient to all neighborhoods. We got the combo pass which includes a river tour, and also a ticket to the London Eye, which is not to be missed. The only problem with the river tour is that it has to be used within the same 24 hours, so you have to juggle your activities accordingly. The Eye ticket can be used anytime within 7 days, so it's perfect. I definitely recommend Big Bus to start your London exploring.

My family recently went to London (March 2017) and we had a few days in central London to do the Tourist thing. So we caught a train into Victoria Station (which is the main hub for London Trains), and there was a Big Bus Tour stand just outside the station for us to buy tickets and then the bus stop was literally 50 metres away. We bought a day pass and got a second day for free and a cruise on the Thames.

The Tour takes about 90 minutes to complete the main route (the red route) and all the main tourist attractions are covered. We hopped on and off multiple times, sometimes walking to the next bus stop and enjoying the London experience. The commentary that is provided on the bus was excellent and mostly recorded...but one of the buses we got on had live commentary and that was not only excellent but very entertaining.

We also appreciated the free wifi on every bus.

Overall an excellent experience. I do remember thinking at the time of purchasing the tickets that I thought it was a little expensive...but hey we are on holidays....

The London bus tour is very expensive and way over priced especially if you want to view London as a family.
The ticket tour guides pester you no matter where you are walking throughout London and once you start conversation with them they are unwilling to lower the price to help with the family cost.
It seems the only way you can get any discount at all is if you book you hotel with booking.com and they send you a voucher code.
Most of the headphone ports on the bus didn't work meaning you miss out on the history of London and looking at the amount of buses touring London hardly any had any tour guides on.

Booked online with London Eye, unlike another reviewer we were told at Victoria Station we couldn't exchange our email voucher for an actual ticket and would need to go to London Eye ticket office to collect! We had a young family with us and with cases etc couldn't drag them back across London once we had checked into our hotel to pick up tickets, so we weren't able to use them on the day of our arrival as planned. The following day we went and asked at the nearest stop whether they could exchange tickets, they said no but allowed us to board the bus to go to London Eye to get our tickets, but the man at the stop forgot us and so we waited for three buses to come and go before he directed us onto one we could have got 20 minutes before. Biggest mistake we made, we should have just bought discounted tickets for the bus on the day, as long story short we basically spent most of the day at the Eye, as the prebooked ticket gets you nothing, other people were in and out in 20 mins (having not prebooked), and we waited over an hour in a queue just to pick up tickets. We then got a bus the other side of Buckingham Palace, but waited for 4 buses to come and go before finding a coveted 'red tour' bus with a live English guide. So all in all we were on the bus for around 40 mins (including traffic) of our 24 hour ticket. Very very disappointing and would not do again.

We booked the hop on- hop off bus tour and London Eye Fast Track combination ticket. On arrival at Victoria Station the Big Bus representative exchanged our voucher for our tickets and informed us that at the London Eye we just needed to proceed to the Fast Track entrance and get straight on within 5 minutes - Be warned!!! - This is not the case!!!! We arrived at the Fast Track entrance to be told that the tickets we had received from the Big Bus company had to be exchanged for actual London Eye tickets at the Fast Track ticket office and after queuing for 40 minutes we finally got our "proper" tickets to be told the next avaliable fast track time was at 5pm - 3 hours later which was unsuitable as we had to be elsewhere at that time, we had to return the next day for our visit.

We spent a day with the Big Bus Tours in London. It was nice to be able to move around above the city where you could see everything (as opposed to the underground system), but the bus doesn't move very fast, so a single day wasn't enough for everything there is to see and do in London. We only had a few days there, so this was a big factor for us... but if you've got the time, do this first and take a notebook to write down everything you want to see.

This more or less met my expectations and did what I wanted it to do -- helped us get oriented to London on our first day, and helped us battle some jet lag after our overnight flight, by getting us in the sunshine and fresh air (luckily the weather was beautiful; though the top is windy so wear layers!)

It was a long wait to get on the bus because of an accident, but the other two companies seemed to have many more buses. Perhaps we were just unlucky.

My plan was to ride the entire route and not even take advantage of the hop-on, hop-off. We got on at Covent Garden (#15) and planned to get off at the end, for us, which would have been the London Eye (#14). Instead, it seemed like we wound up at the London Eye in the middle, so we stayed on a bit longer, and then we were just quite confused about where in the world we were. I imagine perhaps the driver was altering the route from the printed map because of driving conditions, but it was confusing to me. The guide was a pleasant woman, but her voice was quiet and she was a fast talker, so we didn't gain much from her.

Still, I am glad we did it. It helped me understand a bit about the layout of where the major sites were in relation to each other, and it definitely helped with the jet lag on our first day.

One more note -- we added on the Fast Track tickets to the London Eye. Turns out what you get is a voucher that needs to be redeemed for tickets. On the original day we wanted to use them, the tickets were all sold out for that day (about 3 hours before closing), so we needed to redeem them and come back another day. Not the end of the world, but something to be aware of.

My friend and I took a tour on a recent trip to London and really enjoyed it - it's a great way to see some of London's top attractions. We took the Classic Red Tour, which has live English commentary (the green and blue lines have audio commentary). Also included in the price of our ticket was a river cruise and guided walks. We decided to opt for just taking in the sights on the Classic Red Tour and found the guides (we stayed on for more than one loop) to be witty and informative, and offered some great advice, including some places to get the best pictures. The hop on/off nature makes this ideal for getting around to specific attractions, or staying on to get a flavour of more of the sights - The London Eye, Covent Garden, the Tower of London, Trafalgar Square etc. depending on how much time you wish to spend. Would recommend to anyone visiting London.

First time visiting London so we booked a 48 hour hop on hop off ticket with Big Bus. This is an excellent way of getting a good taste of what the city has to offer, with the freedom to hop off and explore neighbourhoods that interest you. On day 1 we did the Red tour and our live guide was Chris...excellent job...sprinkled important information with enough humour. On day 2 we did the blue tour...there is definitely some overlap, but we coupled this with the Thames River tour that you get as part of your ticket...Ted was the guide and he was great. You get an entirely different perspective of the city from the river. Ultimately, it's an excellent way to get around some key parts of the city and staying above ground...highly recommended especially for a first timer.

Great intro to London. Recommend the red line for English speakers, as the tour has a live tour guide giving running commentary about the sights as you go. Ours (Nobby, not to be confused with Dobby:) was excellent.

The route is a bit congested, as it is one of the biggest cities in the world after all, so plan on it taking a while. Lots of stops and starts. We also got diverted from the published path a few times due to roadwork and unexpected congestion from the ever-present London taxis.

Overall, well worth it. I've done hop-on, hop-off tours around the globe and they're always a good way to get an overview of a new city.

For some reason I always have issues with these hop-on hop-off bus tours. I took a chance in London and I am not sure if it was the best idea-I purchased the 24 hour Big Bus ticket along with the London Eye fast track combo and while it was definitely worth it from a costing perspective (as well as the fact that the London Eye online and in person tickets were sold out and I was still able to use the Big Bus ticket and get in). Other than this, I wasn’t overly impressed with this service. The closest stop for my mom and I to get on was at the Tower of London. I wasn’t sure where to board the buses at first and when I finally got on one, I was asked very rudely by the bus driver why I got on without showing my ticket. Honest mistake on my part, but no need to be so rude.

I decided to sit up top for some of the ride because it was a nice day out but eventually decided to move inside. I found the routes to be confusing and hard to determine which direction they were heading. We decided that we would take it over to Harrods and hop off. When we wanted to hop back on, we must have waited a solid 30-45 mins. It was absolutely ridiculous. Because it was so delayed, it was towards the end of the day so eventually they just stopped running and we had to get off at some random spot and find our own way back to our hotel area. Not a great way to end our day.

Not sure what other bus providers there are, but I would do some further research before deciding on Big Bus.

This tour is amazing value for money, over two and a half hours taking in London's main landmarks, while being given the opportunity to 'hop off' and explore further at any of the twenty plus stops around the city, our tour guide, 'Nobby', was clearly a historian, and made learning all about London's history fun and informative.

Had a day free to introduce my 11 year old to London and the Big Bus made it not only easy but fun and great value. We hopped on at Victoria at 9am and off to visit Madame Tussaud's - on again to Tower of London to get off and explore there. Took the inclusive boat trip back from Tower of London to Westminster and got the last bus back to Victoria. Excellent way to cover seeing major landmarks with engaging live commentary on the red line buses. Highly recommend if you want to see a lot in a short time. Staff on all the buses were very friendly and helpful and made sure everyone knew what stop they needed.

Decided to do the Big Bus tour for me son to see London for the first time.we paid 40 pounds for the two of us.
We got on the bus and started to enjoy the tour and commentry.
We got off at marble arch to change buses,then on to Buckingham palace,were we managed to time it perfect for changing of the guard,fantastic for my son.we then got back on bus to Westminster to catch the free river boat cruise,which we really enjoyed.after a good day out we got back on bus to go back to our hotel.we got to marble arch were we had to change buses again.only to be told our bus doesn't go after 5 pm.ONLY for the ticket/sales guys around the company to tell you that you can travel round London on the buses upto 8 pm.
When I questioned this no one wanted to know.was not happy to be straded at marble arch.
We did get on another bus,but only to be dropped off at the top of Baker st/ Euston road.were we were left with a good 25 minute walk to hotel.
So be careful when you go on these tours.and haggle with the price as half of these foreign guys who sell the tickets will over charge you,as they are on commission.

For every city trip, I recommend the bus tour. It brings you around to see the city. The London one is great, sometimes at certain stops you are waiting a little bit more than in other places but it's so worth doing.

Maybe it was because it was mid-January but this wasn't a great tour in London. Bus was inconsistent, as we waited up to 30 min. for one bus, while other "on-off" bus tours like "old original" seemed to come more frequently. Plus, the guide could not be heard clearly downstairs and it was too cold to sit upstairs. They should have the sound thru speakers downstairs. When we mentioned this problem to the driver he came to where we were seated and told us he could hear it. 6 of us sitting in that area all looked at each other and couldn't believe he said this.
The river cruise (free w/big bus ticket) was very enjoyable.

This was our first time in London. We purchased the Hop On Hop Off Bus Tour which included an additional 24 hours, 3 walking tours and a river cruise. We went with the live guides and felt the information could have been a bit more in-depth. I guess it all depends on your tour guide. We took the bus the first day we were there and although it gave us a good idea of the cities layout and where the attractions were I wish there would have been a bit more information and history to the places we were seeing. We did the walking tour and saw the Changing of the Guards. Our tour guide was fascinating. He gave us interesting stories about the history of the sites as well as excellent background information of the Changing of the Guards ceremony. We also did the river cruise and had a wonderful guide. We cruised down the Thames River and was given a great introduction to the city and its buildings along the river along with some interesting facts. Overall I would do this tour again. I believe it is a great value for your money.

The bus tour was the first activity we did in London as to orient our daughter to the city. Samantha was great as she put the city in context for her and kept her engaged throughout the tour. Highly recommend - especially with children.

Brilliant two days on the bus and we bought london tower tickets. Te guided tour was not only informative but also very entertaining as the three guides we had on the two buses and the boat were all great fun - even my to little ones enjoyed it !!!

I have used the London bust tours before but must confess that the "big bus" was probably the best except for some of the guides and audio. Poor audio and poor diction is a bad combination. having had my gripe it is still the only way to see London.
The first guide we had from Piccadilly start point was superb. Knowledgeable, bright, entertaining and a real charmer she made our first leg a great start. As a family we would use "the big bus" again

A friend and I visited London from 19-22 December. He had never been to the city, so during our planning I opted to pre-book Big Bus passes online as a way of introducing him to the city.

During the winter months, Big Bus often runs a special rate which gives 24 extra hours on 24 and 48 hour tickets, and we were able to take advantage of this value by waiting until late October to book. Although I do not that the price for 48 hour pass is worthwhile, getting 2 days of access for the 24 hour price is a very good value. This allowed us to take advantage of the buses as both a tour and transportation option at our leisure. We also took advantage of the included City Cruise on the Thames which also added to the value.

We opted to catch the first morning bus from stop #1 on the Red (live commentary) line since it was just a short walk through St. James's Park from our hotel. The top was partially covered and we were able to stay warm while enjoying the breakfast sandwiches we brought along and the best view in the front row. I highly recommend being an early bird. Our guide sat at the top with us and since there were very few others, we could hear him and chat easily. There was also minimal traffic at that time of morning, so the tour flowed very smoothly. We sat back and enjoyed the tour until we reached Horse Guards Parade, where we got off in plenty of time to see the impressive morning Guard Change ceremony.

We used the buses another time to make our way out to the British Museum from the Strand (Green line stop #51 at the Waldorf Hotel). Although I generally do not recommend using the bus as a primary transportation option due to road traffic (Tube is much faster with more frequent stops), this was a quick and easy ride that brought us to the museum for a quick run through then back to the heart of the action near the Strand. We then hopped on the next Red line bus from stop #15 (same as Green line stop 51) and rode out to the Tower of London to catch a Thames River cruise. This is where we paid for our easy trip to the museum, as the traffic was awful. It took an hour to reach the Tower stop, so in hindsight we should have hopped on the Tube.

We finally made it to the Tower Pier and took advantage of the included Cruise. We rode all the way to Westminster Pier and enjoyed wonderful views and great live commentary. Although Big Bus doesn't run the river cruise, it really enhanced the value of our tickets.

Overall, we got our money's worth out of a few hours of riding spread over three or four journeys, and with the addition of the cruise we really enjoyed the experience. I highly recommend booking online ahead of time as you can activate the ticket anytime upon arrival in London. You are not locked into a certain date as was once the case with Big Bus, so the risk of buying ahead is greatly diminished. We did not book any other attractions through the company since we took advantage of National Rail 2for1s, so I can't comment on that. If you are able to get a discount or extra day free with a 24 hour ticket, then you should be able to get a good value for the investment. I would not recommend spending much more on longer passes... once you've gotten the overview, it's best to get out and see the sights themselves!

I will say that we enjoyed our tour 100%, however, If I had not pre purchased our tour tickets, I would have NEVER gotten on the Big Bus. We got on at the Paddington Station stop on December 27th and as we approached the Big Bus representative with a question he wanted nothing to do with us and yelled "Go to the back of the line" I tried to ask a question referance his yelling and all he could do is yell louder. I don't take kindly to being yelled at and when it was our turn to board the bus, he would only talk to my wife and refused to offer us discount tickets like he did the people in front of us.
This one bad apple pretty much ruined my day. We spent 6 hours on the Big Bus and met some fantastic guides and drivers, but nothing could make up for our initial greeting. We purchased a 2 day ticket, but didn't use the second day because of their rude attendant. Best of all this was during their slow season, I would hate to see what this guy would do when they are busy...

we were chatting about this tour and to be honest I couldnt think of nothing worse than sitting on a flipping bus for 2 hours with someone rambling on about buildings, but the kids wanted to do it. I was pleasantly suprised , you can hop on and off as you like, get differant and a ferry tour is also included,

I did this tour with my mom and we enjoyed it a lot. You just hop on hop off wherever you like. Definitely a great way to see the city. Tour guides were super nice too & you eben get a free boat trip!

If you want to see london then you need a hop on hop off bus. The red line for Big Bus has a live tour guide on it. There are four different lines to see with one ticket. A one day pass gave us a second day free plus a premium Thames river cruise. It was a long tour on the red line, approximately 3 hours. The second day gives you a chance to hop on and hop off. If you are in London for one or two days this is a very good way to see the important sites.

I bought a 24hrs+24 BigBus London tour for my family of five on 28-Nov. Your company was highly recommended by my friends and also my wife who joined your tour about a year ago. I joined your Big Bus tour in New York before and it was fine..

As a tourist, I really do not mind to pay a bit more for a premium service. However I am regret to inform you that your service is over-rated.

None of the big buses I took during the two days had WIFI on-board although most of them had the "WIFI on-board" sign on them. To my annoyance, I could connect to WIFI provided by the Grand Tour buses nearby. This is not something you advertise on your website.

Some of your staff are friendly but not the lady staff who I spoke to at Green Park. Her blunt answer to the unavailability of on-board WIFI is "most of our buses are old" then “All our buses are old” when I pointed out to her that all the Big Buses I took had no WIFI.

Clearly you need to improve your services in order to compete with your cheaper and yet providing reasonable service levels. This is not something I would recommend for my friends.

Attempted to do this tour on my recent trip to London. We got to the stop a good ten minutes before the last tour of the day. We waited and a red route bus came up didn't stop even as we waved at the driver. After asking some questions at Victoria station, where we were told that we were at the right stop, we walked to another near by stop and managed to get on the blue route. Was able to enjoy the tour but ten minutes in we were told it was over. We had prepayed online for this and didn't get anywhere near our moneys worth.

We were a bit apprehensive in booking this after seeing some reviews, but went ahead anyway. We were not disappointed though! We booked the 24 hour tour, as only there for the one day of sightseeing, so the added free 24 hours didn't matter to us really. Our hotel was located near Kings Cross station, so we got on there on the green tour & then later swapped to red tour. We hopped on & off when suited us, so ideal to get off when it suits to see things by foot. We didn't seem to wait long for buses & found the bus stops fine. The longest wait was for the green tour bus back to Kings Cross, but they are more limited then red/blue and it was 5pm rush hour by then. In October this is probably the last bus for green. Red tour was great, with live commentary. Eleanor (I think this was her name?) was great and her tip to get off at Tower of London and do the Thames Cruise (inc in price) to Westminster (20 mins) was spot on! There was a lot of traffic about, so it can slow down the travelling, but then we did expect this and it is London! The kids really enjoyed it, as this was their first visit to London & didn't end up with too much walking! Being October it was quite chilly on the open top, so would advise a warm coat. Drivers were all pleasant. We didn't have enough time to do the included walking tours. All in all, I'm glad we booked this!

The Big Bus tour offered service on 3 lines with various routes. 24 hour ticket offered a free one way thames river cruise from the jetty close to the London Eye down to Tower Bridge. It also allows you to purchase tickets for London Eye and Madame Tussauds at a slightly discounted price. I took the london eye ticket and got it for £2 less. Cost of the 24 hour ticket was £26.
Hop on hop off tour with lots of stops at key places. I tried to take the bus with the live commentary as far as possible and it was quite entertaining and informative! Busses usually run every 15-20 minutes but at 1 stop I had to wait 30 mins or more and then a flood of busses came! To be fair it was rush hour so the traffic was probably the cause.
1st bus starts from 8:30am at Tower Bridge and the last bus leaves at 6pm. Last Thames cruise leaves at 6:30pm but these times are subject to change based on the time of year.
Overall an excellent way to see London. Recorded commentary in many languages if English is not yours.

The Big Bus Tour is a great way to see the city and very convenient. Our tour guide Peter was extremely knowledgeable, very charismatic and had the whole bus enthralled and entertained. Ticket prices are very reasonable too. Definitely recommend!

A terribly organised tour with rude staff. No headcounts were done during the tour and as a result we were left on a toilet stop at the tower of London. We had to run to the street and out into oncoming traffic to stop the bus. Following the completion of the tour the itinerary said we were to be dropped at Big Ben for our ride on the London Eye. Once we returned to the bus, the tour guide said we had to go back to the bus station and drop the tour guide off. One hour later we were back to where our last stop was. The tour guide should of told us it would be quicker to walk then drive around the city in a big loop to get back where we started. Very disappointing we wasted money on this.

We decided to do the bus tour during our visit to London, as we knew we wouldn't have the opportunity to see everything we wanted to see in London on foot in the time that we had. The bus tours in London are a little on the pricey end (we paid £32 each), but we found it truly worthwhile and value for money, with the amount of stops included (not to mention what you get to see), and the extra inclusions (river cruise, walking tour). The guide was informative and interesting, without being over the top, which we have experienced in other cities. It was a spectacular picture perfect blue sky day in London when we did our tour, which made for stunning photos and a nice leisurely way to see London highlights. Would definitely recommend.

Having experienced, the week before, a most pleasant Big Bus tour in Rome, I was expecting the same in London. My nightmare started with the ticket issuer at Green Park. With all of the tour add ons, which included the London Eye and a Thames River Cruise, I elected to keep my banknotes and pay by credit card. Things proceeded reasonably well but at a point while operating his hand held ticket machine the ticket issuer's hand, while holding my credit card, surreptitiously dropped down by his side next to a pocket in his coat. Being wary of card skimming, I like to have my credit card visible at all times, I looked to see whether there was any possibility of there being a skimming device in hits pocket. I saw the outline of a box. I did not confront the gentleman at the time but climbed on board the bus wondering what I should do. The next half hour on the bus were spent frantically contacting a colleague in South Africa for her to put a "stop" on my card. This was successfully done, to my relief, but I then had the inconvenience of no credit card and a lot of the sightseeing on the bus was lost. It may be that nothing untoward happened, but I could not take that chance. My advice to Big Bus London is to train their ticket operators to ensure that, at all times, their customers' credit cards are always within sight of their customers. I have the name of the ticket operator should Big Bus want to do any internal investigation.

Don't buy tickets from guys with pop up stands. They don't tell the complete truth about the tours and why theirs is better.
But I walked into this thinking this to a degree... But what really pissed me off was how long I had to wait for the red line busses(only ones with a live tour guide). We waited 45 mins and finally just took a blue line. The staff kept saying it was coming. Finally we hoped on a blue line just to stop wasting time. I have taken other bus tours in London and they are more frequent and friendly. These big bus staff are hustlers and in no way shape or form are about customer service or being friendly.

I could go on and on... But I will leave it at this... Use another bus company. This company has some major training and inspecting to die of their staff.

We got on the Bus on Baker Street and stayed on until Tower Bridge. We then had the river boat trip & got back on the Big Bus at Westminster & went back to Baker Street going westwards. We had a wonderful day & I would recommend the Red Tour as all 3 guides which we had were really interesting & knowledgeable & it was a brilliant experience. The boat trip guide was also great. Each of the 4 guides stamped their own personality on their commentaries which was refreshing & made the day. The sights and information learnt were amazing. I cannot recommend highly enough. The Red & Blue tour Buses were frequent & the Big Bus lady at Westminster was really helpful. We didn't have time to do any of the walking tours also included in the price but would recommend that you allow a full day & take advantage of all the parts of the Tour. Great value for money. Will be doing it again with my granddaughter when she is older.

We went on the red bus tour on the 17th September 2016 it was a present for my husbands birthday from our daughters. We caught the bus at green park and found the staff excellent the tour was great including a boat trip on the Thames. What made it really special was our guide on the bus Kevin he was informative funny and entertaining everyone on the bus joined in and the social interaction he set made the trip really special.i should not forget the driver also called Kevin who was great when he could safely do so he drove really slow for photo opportunities at places like the shard . i would certainly recommend this trip to anyone visiting London good for all ages we had a 24 hour ticket and could get off and on the bus as many times as you want. .

We were only in London for 24 hours and thought that this would be the best way to see all the attractions. We had the 24 hour pass which included a tour of the Thames River. It was worth EVERY PENNY!!! The drivers were very knowledgeable and friendly and provided directions on how to get to certain areas. The buses run very frequently so which was very helpful because we were travelling with our six year old daughter.
The river cruise was wonderful because it allowed me to get great photos of Big Ben, London Eye and London Bridge. We took the cruise the day of the gentlemen's final of Wimbledon and it sounded like all of London was out cheering or Andy Murray! It was a cool experience for us.

I would recommend using this tour especially the river cruise you will not be disappointed!

Could not believe how difficult a hop on hop off bus could be in my country or origin. Did a similar trip in Barcelona and it was fantastic. Bus stops difficult to find, staff could not care less and added to the confusion, waited ages for a bus to come along which was going in the right direction 5 went eastwards, none westwards. I'd try another company if I decided to do this again.

Buses are always overloaded, maps provided are terrible, bus stops dont seem to exist and routes are shortcut. Also on some bus routes the buses just dont ever come (red route). Several times we waited for nearly 30 mins for a bus on blue line. We should have bought a ticket on the golden tours buses as we would see several arrive in the time it took for one big bus. Also dont waste your time ringing their help desk because they dont answer.

We live in London and decided to take our children (aged 7-10) into town for a bus tour. We booked easily online, picked up the tour in Baker Street and enjoyed a great tour as far as the Tower of London, getting seats upstairs so we could see everything.
After our trip to the tower we picked up a red but with live commentary and continued the tour - with a fun commentary up until stop no. 1 outside The Ritz.
At this point we were trying to go back to Baker St and were told to stay on the bus while they changed driver etc.... at this point we were not warned that we would be sitting on the bus for 20-30 mins waiting. Had we been told this we would have got off and gone home from there.
When we finally departed our children were evidently a bit bored and irritated but we continued the tour sitting at the front of the upper deck. At times we chatted quietly to each other but the children were well behaved considering the long day and the unnecessary wait at The Ritz. However, the commentator decided to pass comment to us over the microphone that we were making too much noise and should go and sit at the back of the bus. He repeated this comment in a rude way when we looked at him confused.... and then proceeded to 'storm off' downstairs. This was highly embarrassing for all of us and completely unnecessary. If we were making too much noise then he could have spoken to us quietly, not on the microphone for all to hear. My children were not being unruly, just maybe talking animatedly to each other at times and we were all made to feel embarrassed when we got off the bus at the next stop.
We arrived at Baker St at around 6.10pm on 15th August and won't be recommending this tour to anyone because of this rudeness which is a shame as all the other staff we had encountered had been great.

I went to London on a work trip and decided to do the tour the day I arrived in order to help me stay up and get in sink with the time zone. I LOVED IT!!! What a great and easy way to get around and see the sites in a short amount of time. You can stop and get out whenever you want and just hop back up on another bus. I can't wait to come back with the family!!!

We visit all cities by exploring a hop on hop off bus tour
Sad to say in our own capital city it was poor
No warning of diversions when paying a full price £32. We missed out large areas off the map with no explanation
No tower bridge
No bucking palace
No stop nr Trafalgar Sq
No borough market loop
One bus had no commentary at all for large parts of the trip
The other with an English tour guide who was poor no real interest except repeating what a wonderful city London was. It is so please take pride in what you do learn some facts basic history or points of interest and get a microphone that works and engage the passenger you have a captive audience
I feel sorry for tourists going on this premium choice lots of clueless staff not knowing what buses were moving
I will not be recommending this tour company or revisiting.

sadly our time with Big bus tours- London was the worst!

firstly- we was promised "fast track tickets" to the tower of London as was told if we show our ticket then we can go to another line... arrive at tower bridge to be told that they dont have fast track and that the big bus tour staff are in fact liars and do this to most of the customers!!

secondly, what tour bus do you go on when the tour guide doesn't actually know much and is too busy chatting up the girls? I am thankful that he knew what big ben was however!!

thirdly- we was told at mayfair to exit the bus and get onto the bus in front, no reason given... The bus in front was that packed that people was sitting down stairs. Im not being funny but I dont pay that amount of money to sit on a bus downstairs in 30 degrees heat!!! at this point we gave up all hope with them and decided to take the underground instead.

WASTE OF MONEY AND A WASTE OF MY TIME.

I was in it for the long haul. I decided when I bought the ticket to go the whole way round, which takes about four hours, starting and finishing outside the Rubens Hotel on Buckingham Palace Road. I was on the bus with the ear-phone commentary, which tells you a little bit about each attraction as you pass by. I couldn't really tell which tour I was on - there are several - but I thought the tour was comprehensive and well worth the money. I would have liked better advice from the ticket lady as to which tour to go on. The tickets are valid for two days, which is a snip. I had to swap buses half way round, I'm not quite sure why, and I sat outside on the top deck on both. You can get off at all the main attractions anywhere in the central London and the old part of the City of London. You can also swap onto other Big Tour buses some of which offer a live commentary. The tour is a great way of orienting yourself around London if you are new to it and if it's a nice day, which it was, it's a good way to catch some sunshine. It was a bit slow, but that's not the fault of the tour. It's just that there are so many construction sites and roadworks in London at the moment. The night tour would also be good, I think.

We had only one day in London and wanted a way to get around the city. We especially wanted to take the bus up to the Thames river cruise port to take the cruise included in the tour price. The gentleman who sold us the tickets-we paid 30 pounds each, but the price quoted depends on who you ask, so be careful-told us it would take about 4 hours to complete the loop from our starting point around and back again. This seemed ok, so we booked. It took 4 hours just to get to the Tower Bridge for the cruise! The bus was uncomfortably hot and crowded the whole way with no facilities unless you get off the bus and then wait for another later. It was raining, so we had to change seats, even though we weren't sitting above, to avoid the water coming down through the staircase. When we wanted to get back after the cruise, we had trouble finding the return bus, since the stops aren't clearly marked. We ended up taking a cab back to our hotel. The taxi driver was happy to give us a bit of a tour on the way, so for less than 20 pounds we could have done the same as the tour in less than an hour, not including the cruise part. I wish we had done our homework before wasting so much money and so much of our limited time on this trip.

Our concierge offered no options other than big bus tours - assumably some arrangement. We stood at stops watching original tour and golden tour buses make 2-3 stops for every one big bus. We stood for 20 minutes waiting at a sign saying "big bus" only to be passed by as the bus had stopped 200 feet earlier - at that stop all other bus agencies had representatives helping people - no one from big bus was present (although an empty bus was there).
Do yourself a favor and choose original tour or golden and actually be able to move about the city rather than standing on the street waiting for buses.

The Big Bus tour was just perfect for the few hours we only had in London.

I booked the tickets online and I had no complications at all.
We easily found our starting point and joined the main line which was the red one.
For a couple of stops we had a quite funny guide. He was very amusing, then he finished his tour and we got another guide. This guide was not as funny than the first but much more informative so I was absolutely pleased with both of them guides.
I stayed in the bus for the complete round.
A bit later we joined the blue line to get back to the stop we needed to go.
The blue line was with an audio guide.
The traffic on the blue line was very bad but that has nothing to do with Big Bus. Other HOP ON HOP OFF busses have the same traffic :D

So all together it worked out just great. Nothing to complain about at all and I would go with Big Bus Tours again :)

Great way to get the over view of London. Then just hop on hop off the sites you want to see and hop back on. We used the bus to get around the city. A little pricey but worth the money. The audio was great and much better than Paris. We would recommend the Big Bus in London but NOT the same company in Paris.

We bought the 24 hour Hop-on Hop-off ticket, which included a Thames river cruise and free city walks. We started by riding the entire circuit the bus makes while listening to a live description of the sights along the way. The narrator's knowledge was excellent and he was quite entertaining in his presentation. The recorded commentary on the non-live narrated buses were kind of bland.

We then used the bus to move to the sights we want to investigate more. By buying the 24 hour ticket (only a few Pounds more), we were able to take advantage of getting to the start of the Royal London walking tour the next morning. This tour (about 1 1/2 hours long) took us to the Changing of the Guards at Buckingham Palace. The guide took us to see some of the behind the scenes activities that lead up the the "changing." The tour was timed so we could see various sets of Guards preparing for their marches.

We then took the Harry Potter walking tour. Don't bother doing this. It was a waste of time. The leader basically took us to a few spots where some exterior scenes from the movies were shot.

I travel a lot. My strategy whenever I go to a new city is to take a tour during the first day or two so I can decide what areas of the city I want to go back to explore. In London, the Big Bus Tour is the company to go with and the Red Tour is the best of the best! Live guides, English speakers, and all the top tourist spots. The 48-hour ticket comes with a free boat trip on the Thames, a great trip on a sunny day! Another thing I loved about this bus company is that you can buy tickets to popular tourist spots like the Tower of London and the London Eye – allowing you the opportunity to skip the queue for tickets. We took the Red bus tour and got off at the Tower of London, then hopped on the river cruise to the London Eye and had the most fantastic day!! The biggest tip I can give you is to sit on the upper deck of the bus, under the covered front section, and become friends with the live tour guide by sitting near to him/her. They are for the large part jolly people who are eager to share their love of their city and their wealth of knowledge! With this tour you will get the best views of the city and a great history lesson. We were lucky enough to actually be perfectly situated to capture that elusive British unicorn us tourists always die to see when we are in London – yes, I am talking about the drawbridge going up on London bridge! Definitely money well spent in my opinion! Go give it a try, this bus tour does not disappoint!

I brought my family (parents and brother) for their first visit to London and decided to do a bus tour to get a good feel for the city. The comments on here are pretty accurate in that the live commentary on the red line (I think it was Kevin) was excellent and helpful. They do drive by some places pretty quick so you do need to be on your toes for pictures (but other places they were able to stop to give time for folks to take some really good pics). The traffic was not too bad as it was a Wednesday but there were places that definitely did take a bit longer. Overall the red line was a good experience.

That being said, the green line was a complete different experience. The driver of the bus (and later on another colleague of his that came up on the bus near Russell Square) were both extremely rude. The bus made a stop near Russell Square where an older gentleman (employee of the company) came on the bus and had asked us where we were getting off at. We had mentioned we were going to sit on the bus and loop back around and get off near Holborn Station. He seemed extremely annoyed with my answer and said there isn't really anything to see in a complete rude/unprofessional manner. Whether there is anything to see or not, the green line has a route and we had paid to be on it. We weren't asking them to do anything more than what we had paid for so I don't understand what the problem here was? Also on the way back the stop we needed to get off at was SouthHampton Row - however, the recorded audio clearly stated that "the next stop is southHampton Row" after we left that stop so my family and I assumed it was going to be the stop coming up. When we went down the stairs and the bus driver asked us where we were trying to get off, he had mentioned we had missed it but I explained what had happened. Though he did let us off right after the next lights, he was muttering things under his breath and profanities, which I could hear clearly. I didn't say anything to his face at the time as I did have a couple elderly folks in my group and we needed to get off the bus quickly (as the driver did make an impromptu stop for us) and didn't want him to drive off while we were getting off. I don't know who these two employees are but both were completely unprofessional and left a sour taste in our mouth.

This was the second time on our trip where we decided to see an overview of the city by doing a city tour bus... The concept is wonderful to see the city and figure out what sights you might want visit.

I'm rating this company a little lower because we got on the "blue route" bus and at some point it changed into an "orange route" bus without any notification from the driver or any of the workers.
Another issue is that they give you a map (Amazing and love that.) but they didn't tell us that due to issues and detours we did not follow the route and skipped a whole section.
All of them also provide headsets. On this one the "Red route" had an actual person giving commentary which I think is better, because you get more of the ancillary information versus just the main highlights or when you are sitting in traffic, listening to music only.
If you take the red or blue routes I think it will take you five hours to do the full circuit.
Big bus was a lot more crowded that other we saw running around town and we also had the perception that the other companies also had more busses running. We waited at a stop where three companies stopped and we saw three of one company and two of the others pass us by while we had one bus show up.

I recommend taking the city tour double decker busses and sitting upstairs outside so you can see everything. Big bus had the better ratings, but I would consider one of the others first given an opportunity to do it again.

Our family took the bus tour for our for visit to London. The bus tour was a great way to get around London and see all the major sites. I also enjoyed the free perks that came with our ticket like the Thames River Cruise.

This being the second leg of our trip. We took the high speed train from Paris (Gare Nord) train terminal to London to just spend the day and then took the train back to Paris. We left Paris at about 7:30 am and returned to Paris at about 10:30. It is about a 2 1/2 hour train ride. the train is clean and comfortable with wi fi available. there is also a food car.

Upon arrival we did not know exactly where we were located or where we needed to be. As you come out of the train station onto Euston Road. turn right and walk about 6-7 blocks (10 minutes) to the bus station/Metro located on the same side of the street. You can go into the Metro terminal and purchase Hop-on/Hop off bus tickets and start your adventure from this location. very convenient and we just happened to stumble into it. there are also several restaurants in this location to grab food if you are hungry before you start.

The Big B bus tour has three or four different colored lines that take you to different parts of the city, but you can transfer from one color to the other at certain locations. I think the tickets were about $40-$50 per person for the day.

We left the Metro/Bus station and caught our first hop on/off bus just about a block and a half away. we saw all the main attractions: Big Ben, Parliament, Westminster Abby, Buckingham palace, etc...we stopped at several attractions, bypassed others etc... the buses have ear phones that provide information in several languages during the ride and information about what you are seeing.

We ate a few meals while in London (most expensive meals of the trip) and upon completion of the day we walked back to the train station and got back on to the train. you will have to go through screening before getting onto the train, in both Paris and London. You will have to show your passport.

Its a great hop on, hop off bus tour and the value for money is decent as well. They have lots of buses plying the streets of London, we waited 15 minutes on average for the next bus to arrive. Opt for the Red Route, since they have a tour guide to tell you about the nice interesting facts about the sights and people of London. We saw all the iconic monuments in a day and got tons of photos as well. You have the option to take the river cruise as well if you like, its included in the price. You can buy tickets for the London Eye and Tower of London with them as well and save you time queuing for tickets.

On May 19, 2016 my companion and I traveled far from the Strand Palace Hotel. We had gotten on three buses and walked many miles before we realized we were lost. It was getting late. We were tired and hungry. We stopped people on the street to ask for directions without success. Finally boarding another Big Bus, we were expressing our frustration to the bus driver when Pete, who was headed home from his work day at Big Bus Tours, overhead our conversation. He told us he was going in that direction and would gladly assist our safe arrival back to the hotel. Pete not only walked us within two blocks of the Strand Palace Hotel, but was most informative about London. I am ever so grateful to Pete for assisting us. He is professional, polite and most concerned about customers. He is an enormous asset to Big Bus Tours. With much gratitude...Susan K

I had injured my foot the day before we arrived in London so I needed to rest it up as much as I could, with this in mind we bought a 24 hr ticket at 19.40 at a cost of £67.00, we hopped on the bus and travelled to the far side of London from our hotel, when we tried to hop back on to the bus at 21.20 we were told that the tour was now a "night tour" and that our tickets were not valid, we were left stranded and were forced to get a taxi back to our hotel at a cost of £15.00, not happy at all, luckily we complained to the ticket seller the following morning who extended our tickets until we left the following day so this defused the situation, my only other disappointment was that you can spend an awful long time getting to your destination that is not too far away due to the sheer volume of traffic, great if you have time but if like us time is limited then a tube day rover or Oyster card would be better value, hope this helps anyone who buys in the future as these situations can spoil your trip when time and money is precious

I pre-booked the 48 hour pass. The service was excellent, stops at all the highlights of London, kept on schedule the entire 48 hours. I used the first day and rode around all the routes and then the second day I used the bus as transportation to everything I wanted to hop off and see more closely. The bus stop time at the end of the day came and went and they kept going until you were at your desired stop. That was great customer service. They gave out maps and ponchos, kept us dry and warm for the short time it rained.
Went on the big bus tour yesterday and one of your drivers Trevor Williams was extremely helpful nothing was too much trouble 5 star service

This weekend I visited London and decided to go on a hop on hop off tour. My hotel concierge told the big bus stop is just infront of the hotel and recommended. I checked the prices online, for 24 hours with Thames boat tour £26. But hotel prices £32. I refused and reached the bus stop. One salesman there and quote £32, but when I told about the online prices he agreed for £25! With bonus River Thames tour!!
First I board Orange tour, then the same bus converted as blue tour from Marble Arch. Red tour with live guide, but unfortunately I couldn't got time to catch that bus. Both tours are great with very informative commentaries. Once the tour ends late evening, one of the buses drop off on a particular route, which includes my hotel also. It's fantastic, we can explore the tour without worrying timeline.
The worst experience happen to me at the Harrods stop. It's on Sunday 30.05.16 at 11am. I got down at Harrods stop, but Harrods opening only 11.30 on Sunday's, then I decided to go for another tour and wait for a bus more than 20 minutes. Then I seen a big bus staff and ask about the next bus. He totally arrogant and told me "If a bus comes you can see, I don't know" and left! I couldn't believe. That particular person ruined my whole enjoyment. I stop touring and went back to the hotel.
This type of staff really damaging the good reputation of the company also.

We have visited London previously and seen many of the "must-do" attractions .We had limited time this visit and due to inclement weather we made a last-minute decision to book the Big Bus tour through our hotel and were SO glad we did! All four of us felt so enraptured to see London from this perspective so easily. The 4-hour route was well paced and the 2 guides provided stimulating commentary in real-time. The map was easy to read and we got on and off when we wanted as well as linking up to another bus on the Big Bus route to return to our hotel. Made our day!

I think maybe they have ONE Big Bus.

Seems like we spent more time waiting than touring; at each station the competitors would have 3-5 busses come in the time it took for one Big Bus to show up.

Save yourself the grief and choose another line, the Original Tour and Golden Tours are much better choices.

The Big Bus Hop On Hop Off is a great way to see different area of London. Take the Red Route at least one time, it is a fully narrated tour (English only), the guide we had on our first ride was hilarious - he could have easily been a comedian in a club, lots of information given for the main attractions and lots of fun facts given on different areas. We enjoyed his commentary so much that we stayed on the bus for a full run just for the sheer entertainment value! Tour the city and get off at any attraction that is of interest to you - the bus stops are easy to find. Ride upstairs (double decker bus) if it is not raining - best vantage point for taking pictures and sightseeing in general.
The package that we purchased through the hotel also included a ride on the Riverboat and that was also very interesting - nice to see a different view of the city and to cross under some of London's many bridges. Commentary on the riverboat was also very good.
We tried another bus company on our last two days in London so that we could compare service and value. Extremely disappointed in the Original Bus Company - do not use the Original Bus as the advertised narrated Red Route Tour was the same as the recorded message that one can get on the headphones, only difference was that it was on speakers and it was always behind the attraction it was talking about - also fewer buses operating, long waits. I can easily tell you that the Big Bus Hop On Hop Off offers the best value, gives the best service and has more buses actively working the different routes that are offered. Highly recommend the Big Bus!

We took the Big Bus and it was NOT
good value for the money. We got on and off three times and walked around the different areas - but we paid £70 for that - two adults and a child. You can take busses and subway for half of that. We only managed to get on a English guided tour once - there seemed to be more of the tours with audio guides - not live once. When we got back we had the feeling of having paid way to much for to little. We will not do it again!

We wanted to spend our last day in London with bigbus tour and we checked on the website that we able to get the ticket from the bus(on the spot) but when we arrive on the bus stop, one of the bigbus staff said we can't purchase the Orientation(1day) tour £22 because its not available there and we gotta purchase from the website in advance. They only offer £25 24-hours tour, which we didnt want to buy because we will leave London the next early morning. We didnt find this information on their website. But the guy finally gave us £22 ticket instead of £25. Which is fine. And then we catched the bigbus at vistoria station around 12 noon because its where the blue line stop. We got on that bus which said BLUE line. But after half an hour later, we were confused because the bus didnt follow the blue route on the map, so we were circling around hyde park area, in which we already explored before!! Then we tried to get off the bus and asked the driver about this confusion and he said "Sometimes I can do whatever I like. So i was doing a yellow line route." And we were asking him why did he do that because we took the BLUE line because we wanted to go to where the blue line heading accross the river. And he replied impolitely by saying "if you ask me twice i will give u the same answer. If you like what im doing then u can stay, if not then you can go." So basically we were wasting our time sitting on the bus, going to places we have explored before just because the driver did whatever he likes to do. We are very vey disappointed !!! Travelers must understand how important every minute when you're having your last day of your holiday.

I decided to take my daughter who is 10 years old to London as she has never seen all the sites. Originally I had planned to take her everywhere myself but then I saw all the tour buses and thought this might be easier. It was suggested to me to use the big bus tour company. This was an excellent idea and it turned out our tour guide, Danielle Harte, was absolutely wonderful and very entertaining. In fact she is one of those people who should be an ambassador for this company, she kept everybody very entertained and motivated throughout the journey even though it was very cold, her boundless energy made what was a simple bus journey around London into a fun and exciting adventure. At the end of the tour we learned that Danielle was also doing tours around London visiting sites all to do with the Harry Potter films. So we immediately went on that tour with Danielle and had even more fun. My little girl thought she was absolutely wonderful and wanted to spend the rest of the day with Danielle! Sadly the fun had to come to an end but I highly recommend this company to anyone who is visiting London. Once again, thanks to the lovely Danielle Who really made our experience memorable.

We bought tickets and hopped on this bus with ease. Route was good.

The weather was poor but we sat upstairs and had a great time seeing the sights in ponchos in the rain. There were no seats downstairs had we wanted to keep dry and warm.

Buses were regular and we only had to wait 10 minutes.

By the end of the day my two little ones were so tired after a full day in London sightseeing so we jumped on the bus to head back up to Piccadilly. They had just nodded off and got cosy about 4.30 when we stopped at Marble Arch and a member of staff jumped on to advise 'last stop, everybody off'. There was no explanation for this, the staff member was rude and abrupt. Her customer service skills were poor. My husband asked if we could stay on this bus and why everyone was being asked to get off? Again all we got was 'last stop'.

We carried two sleepy little ones and were directed to the next buses but no seats!? I asked the member of staff is there a bus free with seats? She rudely told me 'go look, I'm here (and pointed to the door in which she was stood) I can't see!! Rude.

Every bus was full, queues galore , end of day so people everywhere.

No seats on any bus. Queues. We took the tram instead. Disappointed with the service and how our fun day had ended.

I think my rating is fair given we'd enjoyed the trip up until this point but reflects the terrible service we received.

It was recommended to us by the concierge. Paid £29.00 per person. Thames cruise included. We did the tour with 2 friends that came to visit us. Was a lovely experience. Got to know a couple of things I didn't know about London. The tide lasts 2 hours non stop. We got off at London Tower and took the boat for the cruise. Ended at Westminster. Then hopped on another bus and continued the tour. I would recommend this.

1) We took the Red Line which was great/showed all the highlights BUT: do not stay on the whole time!! As of 3/12/16, Downtown London had loads of construction which was noisy, ugly, and caused pretty big traffic flow problems. There was a lot of just sitting there, and the tall buildings block the sun so it gets very, very cold! In order to avoid this but still get to see/have a great photo op for The London Eye/Big Ben, I recommend getting off at stop 15 (right after you cross the Waterloo Bridge.)

**On this note!! Be sure you ask the Guide if the stop you're planning on getting off at still exists... After we made the mistake of not getting off at stop 15, and while we were sitting in the construction/traffic and freezing, we decided to definitely get off at the next stop... only to find out that the stop had been taken off the route without notice. Luckily the guide was super nice and talked with the driver to have them make an extra stop for us (lots of other people, who were also over the construction/cold temps in the shade, were glad that we asked and they got off with us)

2) Only go if the weather is decent and you can sit in the open air. I really don't think it would be the same experience inside the bus, but I can see how the top would be frigid on a totally overcast day. We lucked out with a decently nice day and also had front row seats up top, which was awesome because the windshield blocked us from the wind. I really think this made all of the difference. (In order to score this seat, we got on at the second stop.)

3) Despite the distractingly bad sound system, I really enjoyed our Guide. She was funny, knowledgable, and added a lot to the trip. I would say wait for a bus with a guide instead of just using the audio, but, since I didn't do one with the audio, I can't say for sure.

For 15 stops, the 32 Euro price is pretty expensive. Was it "worth it"? Eh. Idk. If you're on a budget and making choices between things, I would say skip it. If you have a little more spending flexibility, I would say go for it as it's a great way to see all of the "stuff you're supposed to see" in London in one fell swoop without actually walking/taking the tube from place to place. I also walked away with some nice pictures which I think would have been hard to get from down on the ground.
