The big bus tour was fantastic. A good way to see all major sites and get on and off the bus as many times as you like. The Thames Water tour is also included and very well organised and clean and tidy on board. The staff are charismatic and a joy to listen to. It was £50 for a 48hr pass for 2 adults which I feel was appropriate. Certainly recommend.

Very busy city, long ques for popular attractions, packed bars and busy streets.
Bus tours are good for getting around however you do have to switch to different buses for different parts of London as it is so big, get a map and plan your visit.

On my last trip to London I used the Original Tour company and thought it was a fantastic way to see the city. Hop on/off, great tour guides, never much of a wait for a bus, just perfect. This time I decided to try the Big Bus because they have multi-day packages. Colossal mistake.

We walked to the Tower this morning and when we were done we went to the bus stop. First problem, traffic was dead stopped on the road, we could see that, but unlike the Original Tour busses which run both ways, the Bug Buss only runs in one direction, no choice but to sit in traffic.

Second problem, they skipped 3 or 4 stops. Didn't even take the route on the map. We're talking Westminster Abby, Parliament, etc, major stops. Third problem, we were unlucky enough to have a recorded guide rather than a human. (Never got a recorded guide on Original Tour). So we're on some back street listening to the 1-2 sentences about site's we are not even going by. The live guides on Original Tour tell you about every statue, etc you go by, the recording on Big Bus just mostly play crappy music.

We jumped off as soon as we could (after skipping at least 4-5 stops). Got lunch and took a walk around. Went to get back on the bus, wanting to make sure we got the bus with live guides. We waited nearly 40 minutes for a bus in the cold. The busses are supposed to come every 10-20 minutes. Luckily we got a live guide this time.

Fourth problem, we then went two stops and the guide told us the bus was going out of service for 30 minutes! That's over an hour of sitting around an waiting in the cold to go 2 stops!!!! At that point we were done. We got off, walked from stop 1 to stop 8 and took the tube home.

I've asked them for a refund, we'll see if I get it or have to dispute the charge on Amex. Either way, never, ever again.

Having booked online we paid almost £50 for 2 tickets. We had started our sightseeing at Buckingham Palace for changing of the guard. We wanted to go to Westminster Abbey next because it closes before St Pauls and so we walked there because the bus goes in the opposite direction so would have taken forever to get there. We then jumped on the bus to go to St Pauls. We got the bus on the other side of Westminster bridge. Again we did this rather than getting the bus outside Westminster Abbey because the bus would have gone the long way round so we would have missed admission to St Pauls). The first tour guide was rubbish. He just talked about drinking. We then jumped back on the bus to Hyde Park Corner. This 2nd tour guide was really knowledgeable and shared loads of information. He also checked that we were on the right bus because it was the end of the day and there would be any/many more. To be honest we had already seen a lot of the same sights by the time we first got on the bus. For us, the way we planned our one full day in London the tour just wasn't worth the money.

We are just back from a short break in London and opted for the Big Bus tour, It was great value for money. We did both the red route and the blue route. You get live commentary on the red route and our guide (I think his name was Robert) was full of interesting facts and snippets of information. Although both routes were very good, if you have to choose then I would definitely go for the live commentary one. It's only in English but we felt it far more informative and up to date compared to the audio one, likewise we did the river trip as well and half of it was audio whilst the other half was from a guide, again the part with the guide was far more informative and we learnt a lot more from him than we did from the pre recorded audio tape, I think that it was a bit out of sync, although for people who don't speak English obviously for them it would have been good as there are several languages catered for. Well worth the money if you are only in London for a short while..

I did this tour twice once in November 2014 and again in July 2015. It was a great way to see London and decide which attractions you want to visit.

The only down side was I got off at Oxford street and the driver said it was a 15 minute walk to the other end and get back on the bus. 3 hours and $$$ later I was able to get the next bus, but this was in November so I skipped the eastern part and the boat tour as I wanted to see Buckingham Palace. Due to the time of the year I missed it as it was dark but after doing the tour again in July you dont get to "see" Buckingham Palace anyway as tour buses are not allowed to go in front of the Palace only pass the side which is covered in trees..

On the bright side doing this tour late in the year in the afternoon you get to see London by night which is amazing also. Would definately do this tour again next time I go.

I even did the same company tour in Windsor which was also amazing.

quickest way to get round London! would be a nightmare getting tubes to all attractions etc.

the bus tour takes you straight to all the places you'd want to go - hop off and explore and rejoin the next one!

the audio guides are phenomenally detailed and so interesting!

only thing is that bus is freezzziinnnggg up top at winter!

free river cruise included which made it beat its competitors, well priced tickets too. £25 ish each I think.

we unfortunately missed the last river cruise but when we return in june to London we will go on this bus tour again as after 5 hours on it we still didn't see all what we wanted to!

The hop on and hop off bus offers a live itinerary and guided tour around the major highlights in London and gives you the opportunity to stop by interesting sights before jumping back on to join the tour.

The pros for me were the tour guide who were lively, entertaining and knowledgeable.

Unfortunately, their other line which offers an extended tour of London is only a recorded commentary (available in many languages) and was incredibly boring (that I fell asleep). I would suggest avoiding this tour unless you want to see the sights not available in the red tour and/or you want the commentary to be in another language.

We had two days on the Big Bus Hop on Hop off in London. Paid £128.00 or about $265.00 Australian. So the positives. Buses are regular, clean and staff friendly and reasonably helpful. Good commentary on the route. The negatives: winter, intermittent rain and the buses are still open topped. Elsewhere we have used them and the top deck had been covered for winter. They are so slow getting around due to traffic. Not their fault but public transport much quicker. The route is very long and takes abour 2-3 hours to get around. They also spend long periods at certain stops and on several occasions we had to get off one bus and change to another for no apparent reason. In short its average. In future, and my recommendation would be to get an Oyster card, put the fare you would pay for the Big Bus on it and use public transport. It is easy to use, safe and probably 4 times faster than the Big Bus. You can also get any money left on the Oyster card as well as the card purchase price refunded at any station or the airport when you are finished with it.

The most comfortable and fun way to get to know London - covers ALL main points of attraction and stops at very convenient locations. I traveled with friends this December, taking advantage of their online offer (paid 48h and had additional 24h for free) Not bad at all, as we used the Bus to visit a number of places, 3 days in a row :)

Buses are always tidy and clean (even if weather is rainy, you can still have a seat on the top open-deck). Had a fun time on the Red Line, with Live commentator who made us laugh all along our journey.

Make sure you go all the way to Tower Hill (Tower of London) - When stopping there, follow road toward St.Katherine's Docks and have a coffee there. Simply magical :)

(Photos attached were taken while on the BigBus Tour) - amazing!

I used Big bus to show my father London - nice experience.
But if you have any complains you will have to wait for months - they don't care about it anyway! Check the expiration date of the rewards voucher before you getting exited as I did.

What a great way to see London we purchased a family ticket for the blue circle tour which shows a lot more sights. We got free headphones with running commentary. Our ticket was 24hrs with 24hrs free and a free Thames cruise. The family ticket was around £73.00 but well worth it as you can hop on hop off

Me and my boyfriend recently visited London for the first time and used the bus tour to get around.
Staff were excellent! There was a rep at every stop to direct you onto the correct bus and give you information on where to go.
Stops aren't the easiest to find so its best to have a map to help you around.
We managed to see everything that we wanted to and with the hop on and off service it meant we could spend time looking round rather than worrying about missing the bus.

This service is defiantly worth the money and I honestly don't think we would have enjoyed our trip as much as we did without the bus service.
Will defiantly be recommending!!

Don't choose this bus company. They left us out in the cold. We chose this bus because that's what came first in the morning at the bus stop. When I asked is we should get off for a specific site the driver said. " you should look at your map". Yes I should but I found the comment rude and then he told us to get off at the wrong stop. That's just not right. On the way back to our hotel in the afternoon we waited an hour, but no Big Bus Tour buses came by. All the buses that passed us at the stop were "The Original Bus Company" . How we wished we'd bought from them. Someone told us later that Big Bus takes some of their buses off in the afternoon as it's busiest in the morning. The next day we waited again at a bus stop near Westminster Abbey for over an hour. We phoned and they said it should be there within 10 minutes. It never came. We walked to St James Park and then on to the Kensington Palace. We ended up walking the whole day, 5 hours. Phoned to complain and get our money back for the one day but they said because we used one day of the 2 day pass they would not refund us. Terrible service. Do not use this company. Rude and not reliable. Pick the "Original Bus Tour". We saw them run frequently, every 10 minutes, all day as we waited at the bus stop for our no show "Big Bus". This bus waisted precious travel time of ours and the other people who stood waiting at the stops with us. Shame on you.

I purchased the buy one day pass get another pass for free so it was great to get the 48 hours tour for the price of 24 hours. The tour guides I encountered were good and added some humor to the commentary. I spent day 1 riding the Red bus from beginning to end to see what I wanted to view the next day. Once day 2 came around I stopped at certain spots that I wanted to see up close. I loved the convenience of getting on and off the bus instead of having to pay for public transportation to get to the locations I wanted to see. I also purchased my London eye ticket from the big bus workers which is cheaper than buying it at the actual location but it's also £1.34 pounds more expensive than buying it online. If you don't get a chance to purchase the London eye ticket online, I still recommend purchasing it through Big Red Bus people since it's still cheaper. I recommend using this company they were great.

We did both routes in full, Red and Blue, we even did the Green route to return to Kings Cross station. The stops are well located for all attractions,the commentary weather automated or live was excellent, we hopped on and off many times and the headphones worked every time for all four of us.
The commentary on the Thames cruise from London Tower to Westminster Bridge was excellent.
We took advantage of the free ghost walk, this was very entertaining and informative at a manageable pace. The only criticism was when hopping on and off if we walked to another bus stop was hard to find on the map, it's not very clear.

Best Value in all of London and Europe. After the first time touring with Big Bus, I was hooked. The tour schedule is so flexible and easy to hop off for photos and touring a site, hop back on to see more. All in one 24 hour price. Fits your schedule and provides quite a bit of touring in just a few hours. Tour guide included.

We enjoyed our experience on the Big Bus tour in London. The gentleman that sold us our ticket was very helpful and started our trip off well. We sat at the top of the buses and our guide (Jack) was absolutely brilliant. You could hop on and off at any of the stops and it is a brilliant way to see and learn more about the city. We took the red and the blue route and would recommend this tour to anyone. It helped us that the sun was shining :)

BBT London is the best tour in London. The hop on hop off availability allows you to see as many places as possible on your own time schedule. Buses came by about 15 minutes apart so you did not have to wait long, employees were very helpful and the red line live commentary was extremely informative.

When booking a trip to london we debated for some time which bus company to use but are glad we chose the big bus tour london.

They seem to have far more bus's on the road than any of the other companies, literally every few minutes.

The bus's are split between those with live guides (in english) and those with recorded guides in multiple languages (headphones are free).

The staff were all helpful and there was someone to help at every single stop that we used.

The live guide was also excellent, and i learnt a fair few things about london from her.

Overall a great way to get around the city and see a lot of attractions with limited time.

We caught the bus right outside our hotel, it took us to Covent Garden where we took the Red Line Big Bus with live English commentary (which was very funny) through the business district crossing Tower bridge past the Tower of London then along the Thames to Westminster.
We hopped off there and walked around the Houses of Parliament, up to Horse Guards Parade along the Mall to Buckingham palace, right round the palace and up to Marble Arch. Had some lunch in an Italian restaurant chain ( the worst pizza I have ever had) missed the bus by seconds to continue our journey through Mayfair,Hyde park etc.

Well, what can I say I booked the big bus tour company on recommendation of my hotel. I was not disappointed at all, I joined the walking tour with Big Steve to see the changing of the guard at 11.00am. He was fantastic, taking us to all the best advantage spots to see the guards, with out the crowds. He was very funny and kept the whole group engaged. Tasmania could learn from him on how to promote tourism. All the other staff where excellent, they were friendly, informative and helpful. Nothing was too much trouble. So much so Big Steve went out of his way to make sure we all had a great time.

Paid for a tour at 16:30 from Westminster Bridge and negotiated a discount but was charged twice so had to cancel credit card when I returned home due to further possible fraud. Had to wait 30 minutes for a bus that was actually doing the full tour even though we had been told it was 10 minutes away when we asked whilst booking.
First part of actual tour was great and first guide really entertaining. Guides changed over halfway through and second guide seemed obsessed with, firstly, the darker side of London (death etc) and then with 'posh' people who are taking over London and ruining it.

We did not know where to start, and how to start our tour of London. So when we visited Westminster, we joined the Big Bus Tour from there. Fee for 2 days Get On/Off anywhere, and with extra River thames cruise was GBP22 each person, down from GBP30 due to competition among the tour bus companies, and there were 6 of us.

To see the lay of the land, this is where one must start his tour of London, and for 2 days we saw most of the attractions that London has to offer. Big Bus Tour has the most number of buses among the bus tour copmanies, so waiting to get on another bus is easier and wait is shorter. They have live tour guides on some buses and audio guides on some buses, both are good. They even provide free Ponchos just in case of the frequent rain. I have no complain, this is the best in London.

If your goal is transportation from one landmark to another while sightseeing in London, the Tube and regular service TFL buses are cheaper and faster. The real value to the Big Bus is in the tour itself. (Reasons for this advice: the bus circuit is one way, buses are infrequent, and during busy times you can't always hop back on the very next bus to come along -- if it's full you have to wait for the next one, or the next one. My suggestion? Hop on, stay on, and complete the circuit -- then go back and visit the sights using public transportation.)

I often take first-time visitors on the classic red tour with live commentary, sitting on the open second deck of the Big Bus double-decker. Everyone gets their first glimpse of all the famous landmarks and it provides a general orientation, giving a feel for the overall layout along the Thames and illustrating just how spread-out the major sights are. The blue route around Hyde Park is interesting but the commentary is recorded and, in my opinion, not as engaging.

Big Bus tours include a voyage on a City Cruises vessel on the Thames; this is extremely worthwhile. The regular tour goes from Westminster Pier to the Tower of London. However, if you select the 48-hour ticket, you can cruise all the way to Greenwich. I highly recommend this option as you'll cruise underneath Tower Bridge. It's a tremendous experience and you'll get marvellous photos.

Tickets purchased on-line, in advance, are cheaper than those purchased on the street at the bus stop. At the moment, open-date tickets are the same price as fixed-date ones so you don't have to lock yourself in (important if the weather is poor). Another advantage of advance purchasing is this: at less busy times there's not always a ticket agent at every stop. With the web voucher, the driver will still let you board the bus and you can meet the agent at the next stop.

Great tour. There are two main routes. The nice thing is that you can hop off and off the bus at whatever stop go check output the point of interest and get back on another bus. The blue route you can listen to the tour via earphones provided the red route has an actually guide. Ours was very funny and shared lots of information. Also with your ticket you can do the river boat tours and I believe a walking tour if you wish. You can sit back and relax and take it the sites and anywhere you want to go check out you can easily get off and then wait for the next bus to come. My son loved it and we done both the red and the blue tour.

The Big Bus Tour is a wonderful service for those that want an overview of London. The best part of Big Bus is the river cruise component. Loved it! The volunteer operators are fantastic and they have great sense of humour. Do tip them as you disembark.

We were on a very short (5 day) trip to London and it was our first time, so we wanted to pack in as much as possible. The bus is a great way to accomplish this. We had a three day pass that was purchased ahead of time on the Viator website. Three day passes are not sold by the Big Bus company, only 24 and 48 hour passes.

We preferred the red line which has a live tour guide. The blue line offers earbuds and taped commentary. A complimentary cruise on the Thames river is included. Traffic is very busy i London and getting around can be slow, but the London Tube is very complicated, so this was the perfect solution. The drivers and staff at each stop were very helpful in guiding you to the various attractions.

I definitely recommend this company.

Yesterday we were terribly let down by Madame Tussaud London as my daughter is in a wheelchair and they denied her access as they claim they only cater for 3 wheelchair users at any given time! Left devastated we came across a lovely woman for the BIg Bus Tours (Norja Christian) and she immediately realised that we needed help to turn the bad experience around for my daughter who was celebrating her 18th Birthday, Norja put a smile back on my daughters face by arranging for us to do the tour of London with them, she really went out of her way by contacting her bosses and have to say what an amazing day we had, Norja you made her day and just wanted to say thank you, Big Bus Tour is highly recommended for wheelchair uses, they are wonderful and so caring!

Booked a 24 hour Big Bus tour ticket on line. Was well worth the money. It is certainly a good way of getting a feel for the highlights of London and getting your bearings. Spent several hours getting on and off at selected points. The Thames River cruise, which is included in the cost, was fantastic. Thoroughly recommended and well worth the cost.

Convenient hop on, hop off whole day valid bus tour. Although I have been to London for more than 10 times. I still introduce this bus tour to my son who has his first trip to London.
Now multi-language audio with free earphones. Live tour guide also available.
A free boat trip from London tower to Big Ben, or vice versa is included.

My family and I visited London on July 25th. We purchased a 2 day package which included The Thames cruise and the Tower tour. This is absolutely the best and most affordable way to see London and enjoy the many sight. We especially like that we were able to hop off and on the bus at any point of interest. Due to no fault of their own (traffic diversion etc) we got to the Tower too late. We later located a Big Bus staff who provided us with the customer support email address. Upon returning to the USA we contact customer service. We had the please of working with Danielle who was able to issue a refund for the Tower tour. She was courteous and professional and for that I definitely recommend and use the services of Big Bus tours.

We booked this tour because we only had a short amount of time in London. Arriving to purchase our tickets, the line-up of people were already upset because the attendant couldn't get the machine to work thus making us miss 3 buses while we stood there. The real problem was that this attendant told us that the bus would run until 10pm, so we were shocked when the bus attendant told us that we would have to walk to our Paddington Hotel because the route was over at 7pm. He assured us it was a 2-3 minute walk but we knew better, confronted him, leaving him to reply that there was nothing he could do. I'd avoid this trip...it's not worth the money!

On a family vacation to London I waisted both our entire day & £77.00 because Of Big Bus Tours. We bought the tickets from the "official" next to the bus stop outside our hotel more than an hour before the changing of the guards. The "official" assured us the bus would get us there in plenty of time - we arrived an hour after the changing of the guards! Two hours on the bus! If we would have just walked or took another bus, or the underground, we would have been able to see the changing of the guards. We then tried to see some of the other sites by using the Big Bus but arrived to late to go inside. We spent most of our day in London at the Big Bus stops, waiting, and waiting, and waiting. Complaining to the officials only responded with the right bus will be here in 5 minutes - yeah right...

Did the Blue Tour recently while in London and it is the only way to see all of London in a short amount of time. The tour is a self listen, hop on hop off and has something like 45 stops. The ticket at £32 is probably one of the more expensive tours but it does give you a free poncho, free earbuds, map and a free river cruise from Tower of London to Westminster or London Eye or vice versa. Bus drivers are a tad rude as were some of the staff although the chap that sold us the ticket was very helpful.

After waiting for 25 minutes for the Red bus line, one finally arrived. The staff member there ran over to the bus with some man, and then let the man on and talked to the bus driver. We were right behind the staff member trying to get on. Before we knew it, the bus started pulling away. We told the staff member that we wanted on that bus. He just said, "oh will, you will have to wait." No apology.
Later in the day we asked one of the staff members at the stop if we could add on another day. She said that we could and it would only cost 7 Euros. We were on our way to a tour so we didn't buy the extra day then, but on the way back, we asked to add on another day with a different staff member. He told us that it would cost 32 Euros each. We told him that we were told it was only 7 Euros more. He then said that he would do us a special favor and only charge us 7 Euros. He went on and on about how nice he was to us. I am not sure how much the extra day really is, but obviously the staff members do not know themselves.
Several of the staff members were downright rude and at several stops there wasn't even a staff member around. At one stop the staff member was far back from the bus eating her breakfast. Most of the tour guides seemed bored and disinterested. However, two of them were great and one of the bus drivers was very helpful, showing us how to get to a location.
There was construction going on in town so we figured the buses would be a bit late, but one day we waited over 35 minutes and the bus never came. We ended up walking to our destination. Even with the traffic, the other hop on bus line seemed to be able to make their stops in a timely manner.
My final complaint is that the bus takes off while people are still climbing up the stairs. I realize that they want to get going, but this can be dangerous. There is a sign up top stating that people are not allowed to stand while the bus is in motion. What are we supposed to do when the bus takes off while we are still getting to our seats? To me, it is clear that this company does not care about the customers. Even the employees seem unhappy.

We used this tour company when we were in London a few years ago and had a wonderful experience. On this return trip, we thought "No worries!" Well...

1. Bought tickets on-line. Printed everything out.

2. Wanted to take the Thames cruise first before the bus tour. Took printout to dock across Thames from the London Eye. Very long line at ticket booth, but large sign said words to the effect of 'those who are pre-paid go directly to dock'. OK - we did that.

3. When handed our pre-paid information, the employee at the dock said no, we needed to go back to the booth to get our tickets. What we had was a voucher. OK - my bad. I must have misunderstood. Told family to wait here and I'll go get them.

4. Went up to long ticket line. Waited. Watched boat sail away. Got to ticket seller and gave them my voucher. Was told 'No, you since you are with Big Bus tours, you have to get your boat tickets on the bus.' Whaaaat?

5. OK - where is the bus? Go up to the street from the dock then about 1/2 block around the corner and down the next street.

6. Found the bus. Steamed, but maintaining civility. Handed employee the voucher. For verification, he needs the credit card I used to purchase the tickets with. Give him the card. His card reader malfunctions and won't read the card. Even though the name on the voucher matches the name on the credit card (aka ME), he tells me I need to go to the next bus stop (across the Thames). Compound-word profanities about Big Bus Tours in my head, but I silently walked away.

7. Found family, who thought I had abandoned them. Found next bus stop, got tickets, and got on boat. Compound-word profanities expressed to adults in the group.

8. Boat and subsequent bus tour was fine.

Please - I want to play by the rules. It makes everyone's life easier. Just tell me what the rules are!!!!! Likely will not use this company again.

We decided to take an Open Top Bus Tour and the service was great from the person who sold the tickets (despite technical difficulties in taking payment) to the bus drivers and the people at the stops were all friendly.
We started with the Red Bus (One with a Tour Guide) from Marble Arch and we had Oli as our guide who was excellent with a mix of History, humour and personalisation as he showed us the sights. We got off at the Tower of London and took the River Cruise which is included in the Ticket back to Westminster.
After lunch because we wanted to go to Harrods we had to get the Blue Bus (Without Guide) which is a lot more disappointing and not worth the money. Automatic commentary which didn't seem to have a friendly tone, but more of boring tone that failed to get you interested as well as not having great timing (I gave up looking for the memorial for animals in war when we saw it much further up the road when the commentary was already talking about the next thing) and far too much hold music.
I would prefer to pay a bit extra to be able to go with a guide to all locations than have to take the Blue Bus again, it would have knocked the overall experience even lower but any lower score would be an injustice to the Red Bus, Oli and the rest of the Staff.

There is no Fast Track for London Tower, do not think you will move ahead of the lines there if you buy your tickets from Big Bus. There is no Fast Track, it's a sales scam. Summer London traffic is stupid and I should have known better. The traffic this summer makes the usual hop on hop off tour a horrible and ineffecient way to get around. Only reason I am doing this in London this year is for the kids and my foot pain. Other than that, Uber to the far locations and start walking back. Plan your routes and maximize your sites. I can not recommend big bus with the traffic, just not worth it.

We took an OAOA (on and off bus) tour of London. Overall, the routes were very informative, however, it was a hot day and there is no air conditioning on the bus. Also, the bus stopped running at about 6 p.m. and we had to run to catch the last bus. The seats are not comfortable and climbing up the spiral stairs to the top deck is not a good idea if you have any back or knee problems.

Make use of their offers of the cruise, walking tour, and the several bus routes included in the ticket. Buses come every 10-15 minutes, and if you don't like the commentator's style (not everyone can have a great day - every day), you can hop off and wait for the next one. Some commentators are absolutely amazing and if you are lucky, you meet Nick - don't change buses if you get him!

we did the Big Bus tour. Well what can I say. This is a must if you want to see all the sights of London. You also get a ride down the Thames. We travelled on The Millenium City and the audio tour was done by Jamie who told us all the places of interest and was very funny. He made the tour enjoyable.

We then got back on the bus tour to finish the tour of the rest of London. You get to see all the great places of interest. I highly recommend this bus tour company..

This revew is for red line. I read the reviews before booking and thought there is not much difference between BIg bus and Original tour. But, it was not a wise choice. Once we got off we had to wait for 40minutes to get the next bus. When we asked the Reps. we were told if we want to complain we should write to company and shouldn't complain to them. By then we saw atleast 5 Original tour buses go pass. All Big bus passengers were crowded around the bus stop no other bus tour passangers were able to get in. Once the bus arrived there were not enough seats that we had to standup and go for few stops before we got a seat. I was so disappointed with the service and will not recommend it to anyone.

I would highly recommend for all first time London visitors to take the Big Red Bus tour when you get to London. It is a great way to get acclimated, see where all the main attractions are, and gain some local knowledge. The great thing about the Big Red Bus is that you can hop off at any of its stops and go exploring and then hop on any of the buses that follow. They come by every 10-15 minutes so waiting is at a minimum. We actually bought our tickets after 4:00 pm on day one and they were good all through the next day. We were able to hop off at several locations and spend an hour or so touring and then hop back on the next bus that came by to continue. One day tickets were $30 pounds for one day (although buy after 4:00 in the afternoon and use all the next day), with steep discounts for 2 and 3 day passes.

What a great experience we had on the bus tour, the guide was brilliant and very knowledgeable of all the sights in London, worth the money as you could hop on and off over 2 days whilst we were there and also included all the different tours plus a free river cruise and also two free guided walks, which we didn't do. Overall a very interesting bus tour.

Big Bus tours is a great easy to use HOHO bus. There are clearly marked signs everywhere showing you where you can get on and off. They have an excellent map which shows all the stops along with the major attractions. We were fortunate to have Big Steve as our tour guide on the red line. He was so informative and friendly and in true London spirit very funny! I would definitely recommend Big Bus!
LOVED the Big Bus Tour. We saw so many sites and got really good background. This was the highlight of our visit to London.

We were very pleased with our decision to go with Big Bus Tours as our Hop-on/Hop-off service - they are a class outfit and our London experience would not have been the same without them.

Even before we arrived in London, we made inquiries about some sites via email and their staff was very helpful in making the most of our schedule and their services.

After arriving, we found their busses to be clean, prompt and adept at moving through tight London traffic. The on-bus staff and at-stop staff were also really, really helpful and friendly. We often found ourselves having casual conversations with them during the brief waits for the next bus.

The Thames river cruise offered with some of their packages is a great experience as well – seeing London from a different perspective. Our tour conveniently ran between the Westminster and Tower of London piers and they let us stay on for a roundtrip.

Overall, we were thoroughly happy with our decision to use Big Bus Tours when we were in London. They will also be at the top of our list when we visit other cities they service as well.

TIP: Depending on weather, the 2nd floor seats just behind the windshield tend to offer the best of both worlds – a great view with a bit of shelter from the elements. Second floor seats tend to offer more legroom as well.

We were in London for about 36 hours and wanted to learn a bit about the city and see the sights. The Big Bus tour company was a great help and the hop on/hop off feature is the only way to get where you want to go for the cheapest price. (The metro, like the rest of the city, is expensive!). Other companies were a bit more expensive, and The Big Bus included a one time tour of the city on a boat cruise (1 hour long). Unfortunately, we did not have enough time to do it, bummer!

The rainy weather did not put a damper on our experience on the tour, as Steve, or "Big Steve", was a fantastic, friendly and knowledgable tour guide. We rode the Red Line for the full 2.5 hours and enjoyed his funny comments and interesting bits of history all around the city. You really do see everything and learn a lot when you do the full tour route first, then decide where you want to get stop.

Big Steve was very helpful to ALL of the guests and made everyone feel welcomed. He was also a great picture taker for me and my husband (he got a great shot of us with the city behind us- so nice of him!) and we were so thankful for allllll his help!

The Red line is best for english speaking only tourist, while the Blue line is great for those who don't speak any english. Bring head phones (or use the provided free sets), plug into the seat connections and find your language- easy! The buses stop at the designated stations every 15 minutes, so you're never waiting long for a bus to come by.

Pros: the best way to get around the city, affordable, knowledgable tour guides, great for all tourists
Cons: none
Hints: make sure to have some money to tip your guides, you WANT to tip them, trust me!

Having passed every other bus company doing the same tour, I'm not sure how ours was better. But it was. We bought tickets ahead of time before we left the states and added the London Eye a small price extra. When we got there they did a great job of trading vouchers for tickets and got us on board in a jiffy. We had the english speaking bus and the girl did a great job pointing out everything. Everything! I think she knew the name of every single building/person/statute we passed and had the secret back story on every one of them. We even found out Jerry's wife was cheating on him (some guy we passed in front of a park). I jest but she did a great job of pointing out all things British trivia and history. We took the tour that eventually took us to the Eye and hopped off. After the eye we hopped back on and got the bus with headphones and prerecorded speeches and you could pick your own language. The girl was more fun. My hat goes off to the driver who was able to thread the double decker monstrosity through traffic without hitting anything. My only regret is the whole time we sat up there, not a single action figure leaped off a bridge onto our bus, and fought off underworld figures or mummies or zombies. Major disappointment. Bottom line, take the bus, it's worth the price. Clean ride, nice folk working it.

As is usually the case there are good and bad things to say about this company. We started out by boarding a green line bus, wanting to connect to the red line. The location for the changover had been changed from what was shown on their maps and not all of their employees seemed to understand this. So, a bit of a negative.

We did end up on a red line bus, with live narration. The person giving the narration was really quite informative and we enjoyed her comments. This portion of the tour was a plus.

Throughout the day we did hop on and off a number of busses. The employees stationed at each stop were in some cases helpful and knowledgeable and in other cases showed no interest in answering enquiries. Mixed feelings on this aspect.

Later in the day we were on a blue bus and wanted to get back on a green line. Arriving at a stop we were told we all had to get off the bus, no explanation given. At this stop we asked the employee how to connect to the green line bus. His answer was that first we needed to be on a blue line bus and I replied that we were just on a blue line bus and were told we had to get off. His answer was that if I would shut up he was trying to tell me what to do next. Sorry but that attitude doesn't work for me.

This individual was working at the Marlybone Arch stop on Friday May 22/15. He was mid twenties, swarthy, dark complexioned. He was also mouthy, arrogant, extremely rude and confrontational. Throughout this exchange he stayed seated and after I walked off got into it with another customer. For me this guy is the straw that breaks the camels back, the company has to know they have a ticking time bomb on their hands, yet nothing is done.

So, sorry to say Big Bus Company, we won't be doing business again and rest assured we will tell this story to anyone who wants to listen

With a preschooler and baby The Big Bus Tour looked to offer an easy way to see London especially with a two day pass. We were going to by our tickets online as we thought they were cheaper but only if you bought them for the next day or beyond. On the first day it took over two hours to get from Bayswater road to the London Eye as the traffic was bumper to bumper. The second day we thought we would give it another go as that may have been a once off, we tried to swap buses at the designated stop but after waiting over 20 minutes (they say they come every 5 to 15) we decided to take the tube as we had a table reservation. We tried again that afternoon but once we hit peak hour traffic it was slow going once again. Would have been cheaper and easier to get an Oyster card.

Ok so I am a bit cheeky, and especially in these situations. Last minute decision, I was at Canada House in London (aka Trafalgar Square/National Gallery) and though ah go on lets treat ourselves (note this was by far the first time I have been on this tour).
Tip - if you don't need to use the language selection, and you are ok with the tour being conduct in English - only and I repeat for dramatic flare - ONLY - jump on the tour that provides live guides. These guides can provide more than the audio and can also help you find some other gems in the city.
Tip - buy the 2 day pass - you will use it if you plan properly.
Tip - hop on the bus and DO NOT hop off until you are back at square one! This way you get to see it all. Then, seeing as you are a Mr./Ms. Smarty-Trousers, redo the tour, hoping on and off at the attractions you want to see. This becomes a great and cheap way to see London.

This particular day, after navigating my way back from Regents Street (which is stupidly easy considering that London is not on a grid system like many NA cities) I hopped on and enjoyed myself immensely. Nuri, our guide and I, were laughing and cracking jokes and making fun and sharing current events which led to others on the bus coming up from downstairs and others joining in the banter. Better craic could not be found!!

Nuri's fromage infused jokes were awfully laughable and she was a wealth of information. All of the guides are well versed in London and know what they are doing. I have yet to be disappointed.

I also have jumped on the competition buses, and while they are good, I am partial and biased towards Big Bus.

I highly recommend doing this regardless of how many times you have been to London.

Nuri - if you see this - thanks from CANADA!!! Remember Vulcan is a town in Alberta with a replica Starship Enterprise.

This sounds bad and it was a disgrace. Two tour representatives from City Tours and Big Bus Tours were behaving in a threatening manner towards each other at the Westminster Bridge stop in front of passengers from both tours and the Original Tour.
It was not obvious what the slight was that caused this but it was totally inappropriate behaviour and I would say constitutes a breach of the Public Order Act as members of the public were clearly distressed by this.

section 5 of the Public Order Act 1986. Section 5(1) provides:

(1) A person is guilty of an offence if he:
(a) uses threatening [or abusive] words or behaviour, or disorderly behaviour, or
(b) displays any writing, sign or other visible representation which is threatening [or abusive],
within the hearing or sight of a person likely to be caused harassment, alarm or distress thereby.

I hope the companies involved take some notice of this, it was reminiscent of the ice cream wars on the 1970's.

Big Bus Tours London – May 15 -17 wonderful! I read all the tour bus reviews on here and was a bit worried that picking the wrong one would leave us stranded. Also of a concern was the cost, knowing we wanted to book for 2 days Big Bus Tours is the only operator offering a two-day ticket and this was by far the best deal. We decided to go with Big Bus and for 2 adults and one child we paid less for two days on Big Bus then for a single day on either of the other two. For the entire two days, we never waited longer than 10 minutes for a bus and never were any of the buses more than 50% full. Big Bus Tours was an EXCELLENT Choice…. An added plus was ALL of the employees were cheerful and helpful!! I will book with them again on our next trip to London.

This was a most wonderful experience. I took my daughter on the BB Bus tour We couldn't fault it.. . We paid for the tea and it was soooooo lovely. We went around London and the sites were spectatcular and the tea and the tour was so good . Id recommend it to anybody. There was sandwiches Dainty pastries and then we had scones Jam and cream. It was well worth the money , furthermore id recommend mother and daughter to go for a treat

We took the Big Bus Tour from Saint Pancras station. The lady at the ticket booth in the basement (the one next to the currency exchange and across from Costa restaurant) told me BBT was the best because the buses come frequently and take you everywhere you want to go in the city. I traveled to London with three babyboomers, so I thought this was a preferable mode to see the London sights since my traveling companions weren't able to take the Tube.

Well, this was a disaster.

The ticket saleswoman lied to me, point-blank. The buses actually run every 30 to 45 minutes, and each bus is crowded beyond belief which means it flies right by you. The "staff" goes out of their way to be unhelpful, and if I hadn't thought quickly and jumped off the bus at Big Ben we would have missed our tour of Westminster Abbey and the Tower of London.

This was a genuine waste of time and money. Just take cabs. They're more reliable and fun.

My friend and I travelled from our homes in Manchester to London for a day-trip on the early May Bank Holiday Monday and agreed that the best way to explore the capital was to take the sightseeing bus and hop off at places of our interest.
Our commentator was 'Big Steve" who was such a pleasure to listen too instead of the recorded voice you hear through the headphones.
I wish more buses had live commentators as they give the experience a personal touch and are able to answer questions and give us extra pieces of information.
Big Steve was a joy to listen too :-) he is knowledgable, friendly and funny.

It was 3 adults and we had Big Steve has our tour guide on the red route! We highly recommend this tour and Big Steve as your tour guide. He's very personable and be sure to ask him to do some of the tour in English-English. Do all of the red tour first at 830am then go back and see what you want to see the most! Thanks Big Steve for a memorable time in London!

I booked a big bus tour and they are a great company! I started at Marble Arch as that was closest to my hotel. I got off at Trafalgar Square and from there mainly walked everywhere so I could stop and take photos etc. I did get back on at Westminister and took the bus over to London Bridge then caught the included boat ride back to Westminjster. Was a great day!

There are several tour buses available, and the Big Bus red double-deckers are actually a lot of fun! Especially for kids and teens.Their stops are convenient, usually w/ the regular city transport & outside Tube stations. The best part is that you really cover a wide swath of the city in a fluid way. It gives you the biggest scope in the most efficient way. I know it's cheaper to take the public bus and you can duplicate the similar routes the Big Bus takes but for me, this would be a brain drain. We just loved the top deck (need to dress properly depending on weather conditions), we stopped wherever it piqued our interest and you barely wait for the next available bus; there's always one at the stop waiting for you! The recorded tour gives you enough information on major attractions, so if you want to return to that spot, you can loop back. The ticket takers are quick, friendly, professional. they offer a price, you may even get a "deal" - we signed up for one day, then the next day when we were waiting at a public bus stop & the BB ticket woman advised me I could go another 24 hours for a relatively inexpensive cost. We took the offer and had more good times! Just one advice: by 18:00, the bus tour is OVER and the buses go back to their depots! Adjust your schedule to make the best use of the Big Buses.

It is an excellent bus tour for hop on and hop off for the travellers having less time to visit the London city. Better to book a ticket online rather than from the counter because it save you a good amount of money. Rest is available from the Big Bus website.

My teenage son and I had a day in London to tour the city. We purchaed Big Bus tickets on line and went to the marble arch to pick up our tickets. We wanted the Red bus, so we asked the sales person where to wait for the Red bus. We waited from 8:35am and we did not see a bus until 9:45am. When I approached the sales person after waiting for 40 minutes, he told me that a bus would be here soon. A blue bus passed us by, but did not stop. Two competitor buses passed us with multiple busses.
The same thing happened when we tried to get another red bus at the Tower of London. We waited for 35 minutes while multiple busses from two other competitor busses went by. After 35 minutes, 3 Red Big Buses came by at the same time. Not sure if they had a dispatcher on duty but they didn't seem like they were paying attention on this day. After waiting 20 minutes at the Tower of London, I approached the sales person at the Tower of London spot and he did not give me much assurances that a bus would be there soon. We wasted quite a bit of our one day in London waiting for the Big Bus.

Three adults, two children. £105. Sat in traffic for two hours barely moving. Guide discussion is generously described as "difficult to understand". Hop-on-hop-off? A laugh. If you get off, good luck finding a bus that isn't full to get back on - often waiting for two buses before you can squeeze on and find a terrible seat in the back.

Save both time and money and buy a £12 1-day tube pass.

I would recommend to buy tickets online - the cheapest way.
We tried just live commentary on red line, and took us 2 to 3 hours with a break.
We got free boat ticket , so we used boat from the Tower of London pier to Westminster Pier, otherwise you would do the same way by bus, so boat gives you a better view, right.
We totally enjoyed our tour day. Hop on hop off works very well

Hop on hop off bus is a great way to see London. All the sites are covered and the Big Bus audio was excellent. Staff were all friendly and informative including the bus drivers (that's a first for me!). I think however the brochure needs to be a little better laid out as we got lost in out bearings a few times and ending up walking quite a bit between stops. More distinctive signposts may be an idea. If your trip comes with a free river cruise - do it. Our skipper - Tommy talked us through the trip in running commentary that was hilarious. Was akin to listening to a stand-up show.
Tip: get off at Buckingham Palace stop as you do not really get a proper view from the bus itself.

I regretted booking our hop on hop off tour in London a couple of weeks ago. The staff are rude, they are more interested in selling you tickets for attractions in London than anything else. They advertise free walking tours included in the price but they are impossible to book and nobody helps you. Incredibly rude people. These tours are useful if you are in town for a short time but do it with somebody else, The Original Tour company is much better.

We booked this tour for our family of four. The guides were excellent and the buses were very nice.

However we had to wait for 30 minutes at our first off-on stop and watch while multiple "original" busses went by.

Perhaps just a fluke but at our next off-on at Oxford circus we had the same experience at 5:00pm. To add annoyance to frustration there was no live tour operator on the bus!! A poor replacement was the headphone auto-guide that we plugged into.

While not horrible I certainly would not recommend big bus to a friend, try one of the other operators... The Original bus tour seemed to have much better frequency.

just a pity i didn't have enough time in london; the big bus is a great way to zip around town and identify key things to see and do.
1 thing to note: just get the fixed date one. I couldnt activate my ticket on the date itself (2nd Feb) but the staff were so nice and helpful about it. In the end i activated it on 3rd feb and the ticket was valid for 3rd and 4th feb.

By using the big bus's stops I was able to get around town really easily and made use of their stops +ticket validity to even skip taking the tube!
I was on the tour myself as my other half was in London for work. It is my first time in London; using the big bus maps as a guide, I had no issues getting around at all.

The guides were knowledgeable and enthusiastic; always willing to share more info and personal quips.
I was freezing my tropical fish toes off on the bus (weather 3deg that day) so wasn't in the jolliest mood, but still received very useful knowledge from the guides.

Use in conjunction with london pass to really take advantage of London has to offer for tourists!

Living in Scotland, I go to London often for a long weekend, and everytime I go I always use the big bus company. Always jump on the red line as like to hear the different drivers stories about london. My most recent trip we had Jeff, a young lad who was an excellent tour guide, very informative and always answered any questions anyone had. Hope to be lucky enough to have him again when I go back in July. The big bus tour is a must while in London.

What can I say, great day with Big Bus, tons of information, our tour guides were brilliant (especially big Steve!) our kids (9 & 6 yrs) loved the tour. If you want to see the worlds best city, there is no better way!

I've taken this company's tours in other cities with great results. That's why i chose to pay a premium to use them in London. The route was extensive and comprehensive. I started on the blue line which was a fairly good tour. My only complaint was the annoying repetitive music in between the recorded narration of the sights. The bus was comfortable and well appointed.

I decided to switch to the red line as that tour offers a guide who narrates in english. I was looking for some additional insights in addition to the basic description offered on the blue bus.
This tour was miserable. The bus was older and creaky. The speaker was garbled and had to be turned up to to almost an uncomfortable level to be understood. The worst part by far was the complete lack of heat. Extremely cold and uncomfortable i estimate the temperature in the bus at five degrees C. This was the first time i did a tour where i opted out early and i did not tip the guide/driver. Could have been so much better.

London is such a huge city that it's impossible to see everything in a day. That is unless you use the Hop on Hop off bus tour. We used the bus tour to get an overview of the City at large. We each had one thing we knew we wanted to visit. We used the bus to go to each of these sights and chose two more to visit as we traveled throughout the city. Next time we visit we will take the tour again but add in the water ferry too.

For a hop-on hop-off tour this is a pretty good one. The Big Buses come most frequently of any of the other London tour buses (The Original or Greyhound specifically) and they are never too crowded to not get a seat. I did almost a full route on the “blue” tour which was good - this is the pre-recorded audio tour that you listen to with headphones available in several languages. In addition, however, we were lucky enough to get on one “red” line tour. The red lines don’t come that frequently unfortunately but they are MUCH better. These are led by a live guide, ours was Robert who was hysterical, super friendly and very knowledgable. I wished that I waited at every stop for a red line to be honest because it makes the entire experience so much better to have a live guide with a few funny jokes rather than the basic audio tour. The loops they make are very comprehensive and give you a good view of the entire city. They stop running around 4:30pm in the winter (though if you’re lucky you can get on a bus half-way through it’s route closer to 5:30pm). The bus also comes with a free canal cruise which is a fun gimmick but not really as great as it sounds. Be careful buying tickets as they do discriminate pricing a bit and you can negotiate or pre-book. You should pay about 25 pounds, though if you buy it from one of the reps on the street, they will charge you 32 pounds day of. The tickets are valid for 48 hours so plan ahead and take advantage of the full 48-hours that its valid for during your visit to London.

Having lived near London for many years we thought it was about time to get out and see the sights so we picked a really lovely winters day wrapped up warm and got on the Big Bus Tour. We took mostly the red route which has a guide on board giving a live commentary and hopped on and off were we liked. If you want a recorded commentary and to listen in a language other than English then take the blue route. It was a great way to get around and as the ticket lasted 48 hours we used it the following day also. We booked on line as it was cheaper paying £27 instead of £32. It was well worth it. The staff were all very friendly and helpful.

The big Bus tour was one of my favourite ways to see London.
I want to start by saying that there is a lot to see in London and it can be very overwhelming at times. where do i go first? what route do i take? what all should i definitely see?
the Big Bus tour is your answer to all of this.
the tour starts from Hyde Park where you can buy tour tickets. Remember that your ticket is valid for 24 hours, which means that you can use this service twice on the same ticket. Just remember to HOLD ON TO YOUR TICKET.
the bus has 2 routes, the red line and the blue line. we did the red line the first day and the blue line the second. I would always recommend to do the red line tour first as it will take you through the main attractions. The blue line's route towards the end is very similar to the red line.
here are some of my pointers:
1. keep your ticket safe : the tour allows you to get off at any of the attractions and once your done you can get onto the next tour bus. All u have to do is show your ticket. You can also buy the whole package which includes tickets to London eye, the tower of london and other such attractions.
2.if ur going in the summer, carry sun screen. it can get quite hot on the top of the bus.
3. watch out for the trees and branches. I saw someone get hit in the face with one, but he was standing, which is not recommended.

what i loved about the red line was the live guide. he provided us with interesting facts through out the tour while engaging with the tourists. the little things really do make a difference.

the bus tours covers all the major attractions in London, its fun and really the best way to get an idea of the city.

NEGOTIATE PRICES, compare and make offers !!!!

There are various hop on buses, this is just one of a few.
I was able to negotiate the price, since the tube system is so good in London,
I took this to orientate my bearings. You can buy an OSTER Card, put in daily
amounts on a single card. Card is returnable for your deposit of 5 Euro.

I have been to London six times in the past few years and cannot thank big bus tours enough for the wonderful friendly service and staff. I do not use the underground ever and to me the price for the tickets is well worth it. I use the buses for getting from A to B and also for the sight seeing. The staff at Green Park where I have purchased my tickets , the friendly drivers and the fantastic kind , funny and very informative guides the whole experience is worth every pound. £32 for 48 hours and a free river cruise. You pay that in cabs in a very short period of time. As I have said the guides are friendly and informative but one stands out if you like his tour his name is Steve if you didn't his name is Arthur and I have to say Steve is great , lots of jokes and he is full of local knowledge. I left the tour with a big smile on my face. Steve was able to greet everyone even the non English speakers in their own language which bought a smile to their faces. What a gem he is to the company there should be more like him. Thank you Big Bus Tours and Thank you Steve.M. I Will certainly be using the bus service again when I am back and recommend it to anyone looking for a great day out o or a good way to get around town . My son got to enjoy seeing London on his visit with me this time too he managed to take some spectacular photos thanks to our guides knowledge of when to aim and shoot! Regards from Australia the land of the real wheatbix 😍

This is a great way to beat jet lag. Most flights from the USA arrive in the morning. Taking a nap upon arrival will seriously mess up your time clock. To stay awake until a reasonable bed time, book a hop on/hop off tour. Purchase in advance, on line, and you get the 2nd day free. 25gbp about $40. Leave your bags at the hotel. Hop on nearest stop. Hop off for a bite to eat or just sit and relax for the entire circuit. Red bus live commentary is best and entertaining (about 2 1/2 hours if not hopping off). Lots of history. Gives you a good idea of the attractions you may want to visit during your stay. Great for first time visitors or as a refresher for seasoned London visitors.

The Big Bus Tours of London are a must do!! This is the absolutely PERFECT way to see the famous attractions of the city how ever you want to by being able to hop on and off at the stops. The complimentary audio guide even further personilizes the tour for you and of course you have the option of sitting on the upper deck or the lower one. I loved that you could still see all the famous sites of London in a much quicker, easier and cheaper way!! Also the Big Bus Tour ticket came with a Thames river boat cruise that was good for up to 24 hours! I recommend this tour very highly!!

Took my eight year old daughter to London, I wanted to show her where I grew up. She had never been to London or England come to that before. I thought the best way to show her the sites was to jump on a open bus tour. Weather was beautiful!! Joined the big Bus tour at Marble Arch, we had a good guide for the first part of our journey, but upon rejoining the tour after a visit to 'Hamleys' we were lucky enough to meet Kevin!!

Not only was he extremely knowledgable, he had a brilliant sense of humour and kept us all highly entertained throughout. He involved over my daughter with his banter, and I was so happy that she was not bored even for a second!!

Kevin my daughter often talks about you. Thanks for helping to make her first trip to London so enjoyable!!

WENT TO LONDON OCTOBER HALF TERM 2014.
Paid £74 for 48 hrs bus tours & free river cruise,20 min walk to green link@ russell square,which will deposit you @
the Strand (West End) to pick up either Red or Blue tour,Blue tour is much bigger & the recorded tour guide is in about 10( ten) languages.
these buses are packed solid so don't wait for the next one expecting an upper deck seat,get on & wait for your chance to pounce on an upper deck seat if you're lucky.
the buses run all day from approx 09:00 till 18:00.
what you won't be informed is that @ the end of day you will not get back to your Green link,& you will be stranded @ marble Arch as we were with about another 40 people who were all moved from their buses onto a mop up bus!!
SAVE YOURSELF THE HASSLE & TRAVEL BY UNDERGROUND IT MIGHT BE EXTREMELY OVERCROWDED BUT YOU WILL NOT LOSE HOURS SITTING IN TRAFFIC & MISS ATTRACTIONS YOU HAVE PAID, FOR WE MISSED TUSSAUDS TWICE, AS WE WERE TOLD YOU WE COULD DO LONDON EYE & TUSSAUDS IN THE SAME DAY. WAITING TIME @TUSSAUDS AVERAGE 3 & 1/2 HRS.LOST OUT ON £60.
iF YOU DO BUY THESE TICKETS YOU FELL OBLIGED TO USE ONLY THE BUSES IT'S A BIG MISTAKE!!!
THIS IS MY OPINION & THESE TOURS DID NOT WORK FOR US WE ARE A FAMILY OF FOUR.

I would strongly recommend using Big Bus. I booked ahead on the Internet for a 24 hour pass with an extra 24 hours for free which was a bonus.
We were staying within the tower bridge area and the nearest stop was only mins away, the collection of the tickets was very easy, simply take your evoucher to a member of staff who are at most of the stops and they print off your tickets. Staff are positioned all around the routes and are very helpful.

We mainly used to red and blue services. The blue service gives you commentary via earphones and is quite popular with overseas visitors, understandably this was very popular on the Saturday so be warned! The red tour gives you live commentary via a member of staff who is on hand to answer any questions you have, they can be at times a bit of a laugh and there is plenty of participation by other passengers.

You get free headphones and maps on each of the buses, I felt that the map was quite confusing to understand at times but as I said there are plenty of staff on hand to assist.

My ticket wasn't checked properly once therefore I could have technically have an out of date ticket.

You get a free ferry journey which I didn't get chance to use I was slightly gutted.

Another great feature of this I felt was the amount of money you save rather then using to underground. I have an Oyster card but simply used the bus to hop on or off facility as well as using it to clean up on knowledge of the city.

I would recommend this company to anyone. Service top notch!

I had the 48-hour ticket and therefore made use of the bus on two separate days. This meant I had the pleasure of two different guides. I've read some of the reviews which showed that some of the guides were less than informative and buses had been crowded. I was therefore very relieved that on both days there was plenty of seating and that both the guides were entertaining and very knowledgeable. In fact Nick and Naz (the driver) on Sunday 19th were so good that I did the full red loop with them. I also took advantage of the boat cruise all the way up to Greenwich which meant that the price of the ticket which included this turned out to be very good value. I had booked my tickets in advance online and therefore appreciated that unlike some of the other operators I was still able to get on at any stop initially and then subsequently get my ticket validated. I would certainly recommend this tour to others considering getting to know London.

First impression wasnt good,the bus tour host was unfriendly and impolite.
Timings which we were given were so out we didnt even have time to do the full route.
Value isnt bad but we were furious to find out the host at victoria station information desk didnt account for the £30 in cash we paid and the other adult ticket on card so we found out later we were charged an extra £30!!!
Beware of this!!!
Hop on n off for 48hrs n the boat trip makes it all not bad value but hope ya get friendly hosts..

However, if you don't, it damned expensive.The ticket includes 48 hour use of the bus which is multi route, multi stops in multi languages. It includes a riverboat trip. All in all, good value for money. But you need to plan this in advance, so do. If you are there in London for just a one day quick sight seeing tour, other cheaper buses are available.
The trip can also be made by your guide. We had a true character, James who was absolutely brilliant. Very knowledgeable, very witty and an absolute gent.

Today we took a big bus tour of London and were very disappointed. We spent more time waiting than actually on a bus. A number of the guys working for Big Bus were sleazy, made us feel uncomfortable and my daughter very embarrassed with the attempts to arrange an evening meeting with one of them. We have a 48 hour ticket but think we will give tomorrow a miss and sort ourselves out. Compared to the big bus tour we did in New York, this one was over priced and not that enjoyable.

We enjoyed our first ride with Nick, who was pleasant, funny, engaging, entertaining and easy to understand. He also offered stories and info other than just the bland tour stuff. But, unfortunately, we caught him at the end of his shift and then got another guide who was so awful we got off. I forget his name. Older man, gruff manner. He kept yelling at people for talking and he had a heavy cockney accent and we couldn't understand a word he said. We got off at some point, and just hopped another bus later. Depends on the guide you get but it's a nice way to check out the city instead of walking all over. We also rode the Big Bus tour in Paris, which was not as good. We heard the Yellow (or Green?) Tour Bus in Paris is better.

I guess it wasn't really our day. We had to wait for an hour to catch the green link. Apparently it was due to one of the buses broke down. When the bus arrived it was already full. I had to stand up while carrying my baby. Luckily one gentleman gave up his seat and 2 stations later it was really cramped inside the bus. Once we got to Aldwych (the starting point of red/blue tour if u take the green link) of course there were too many people lining up for the bus. We decided to wait until the third bus which took about 20 minutes so we didnt have to 'fight' for the upper deck seats. The tour was fine. Traffic was not so bad. But one thing that really made me disappointed was the rude driver. We had a baby with us and a stroller. So it was a bit of a struggle to hop off the bus. I cant remember which stop we were at but i swear the driver had been waiting for not even a minute, and later started to drive away but i quickly rushed to the front door and apologize. Guess what did he say? "Are you kidding me? it took you that long to decide??" He sounded really annoyed, obviously. So much for British hospitality yea? I hope he felt sorry deep inside when he saw my husband pushing the stroller after me. Later after that we just took the black cab back to our hotel. Much better. I think it is better for you to go for the Original Tour or any other companies. Big bus tour is just a hype. Everybody seems to choose this tour, so good luck in getting your 'preferred seat' on top, if you know what i mean.

My husband visited London for the first time last May and with two kids under 5, we decided to take the bus tour. We decided to stay in the bus for a full circle instead of hop on and off which you can do. We really enjoyed the ride. We started from Piccadilly and went around London for about one hour. We saw almost all iconic places in London: big ben, tower bridge, Tower of London, buckingham palace, and other historical sites. Sit on the open second deck when it's not too cold and rainy. You can see much better there. It's money worth spent especially if it's your first time visiting London.

As a major sceptic of any real"touristy" things... I was pleasantly surprised by this tour and what it offers. For the price of 31 GBP you get 48 hours of the best areas of London. Our tour guide "Big Steve" was so great his excitement about the city he grew up in and the love of it , along with his general knowledge of interesting facts on London, was fabulous. I normally have the attention span of a small child, but was truly entertained for the entire loop. I think it was just over 2 hours. Would absolutely do it again. The other nice thing, if you aren't enjoying the guide , hop off and the next one comes along within minutes!!

I visited London with my aunt and sister-who is 21- and decided to go sightseeing as we all had been to London before but never appreciated the tourism. My aunt booked the tickets for us online which made them cheaper, so my advice would be to BOOK TICKETS ONLINE. The hop on hop off was very useful and you could regularly do this at many different tourist points. We got on the blue bus which gave an audio guide- available in german, spanish and many more languages as well as English- which we all found very interesting and informative. My aunt has lived in London for many years and even she found out some new things about our great capital city. The music in between sights really set the atmosphere and made us all feel very patriotic as we drove over tower bridge and past Big Ben to the sounds of Jerusalem and God Save our Queen. We got on the bus at Madame Tussaud's and travelled all the way to Buckingham palace where we got off and visited (see my review on Buckingham palace). There is a bus every 5 minutes so after our visit we hopped back on the bus and carried on round the route. CHECK THE ROUTE YOU WANT BEFORE GETTING ON THE BUS. Although the bus conductors were more than happy to help and were always around at every stop, we found the route hard to follow at points. We were told that one bus would take us back to Madame Tussaud's but when we got on it it looped back round to the same stop that we just got on at which was confusing but not a great problem for us at this time. We were then pointed in the direction of another bus which we had to run to but just pulled away as we reached it. Knowing we had to be back in time for our trains home we then opted to take a black cab to the train station so as not to risk missing our trains. This was a bit disappointing as we did not get to see one or two more sights on the final route, but this did not ruin our trip. We found the whole day and experience very enjoyable and after going on the majority of the blue bus route found, that although some facts were repeated after a while and as we had headphones on did not lead to an easily sociable tourist trip, it was never boring and you were constantly being informed and inspired by the great city of London thanks to the big bus tours (who also provided rain ponchos just in case!!!). I felt truly proud to be British by the end of the day. Would recommend to anyone of any age for a fun and informative tourist day out in London with family, friends or even on your own!!!

We had good luck with using The Big Bus - Hop On Hop Off for our initial introduction to the London city area.

We got the special 2 day pass through our hotel which offered a small discount when purchasing. And we found the tour and routes very useful for not only seeing attractions and landmarks within the city; but to also get a grasp on London and it's different areas because it is a large city and so spread out.

What recommendations we can make are the following:
We lucked out on grabbing a Red line at one point late afternoon after taking it earlier and not having an actual guide. The latter with our guide was quite entertaining worth the wait.
Know where the closest stop is to your hotel.
Realize there are two basic routes that Big Bus uses to go through the city. The Blue and Red lines. There are certain areas that each line goes to only and there are overlapping areas where each seem to cover similarly as well.

Download a map ahead of time and get used to the routes for each color and the arrows (directions) the lines run in.
A couple of more tips that will help; Where there are "I's" on the map for information; these are also usually bigger stops where you may need to change buses because the drivers change out; and or to pick up the correct line, or different bus, drivers do change and the route generally starts over again, from the route start.
Last buses seems to start at varying times after 6pm or 7pm, try to make sure you leave enough time to get to you final point or hotel area. If you are way outside your area come after 6pm, and have to change, there may not be a bus coming through for you to jump back on to your last stop.
The Big Bus signage on the bus isn't the best as others the have scrolling signs saying the stops. (wish BB would get this hint). Anyway look at the front of the bus to see either a blue or red icon on the scrolling message board, to know which color/bus route you are about to board and, always ask if you aren't sure! Beats riding 1 hour out of you way.

I have done Big Bus tours in several cities, and overall would say London's tour is great if you are very short on time, but a waste of money if you have several days to explore on your own.

Since London has a great Underground system that goes to every destination on the Big Bus Tour, the tour seems most logical for tourist like me who are trying to see as much as the city as possible in a day.

During my trip, I had the unfortunate experience to have a tour guide that used the microphone as his personal comedy club, and provided little useful information about the sites. In the future, I would get off a bus with a bad tour guide and hope the next one is better, as my experience with this tour guide has a lot to do with my small dislike for the tour.

We really enjoyed doing this tour and used it for two days to see the highlights of the city. This company offers three routes around the city that come with commentary (one of which is live and in English). The tours highlight parts of the city that tend to be of interest to visitors (such as tower bridge, tower hill, and Buckingham Palace) and provide a hop-on/hop-off option that allows you to stay and see the attractions more closely.

The routes are well driven with busses coming around every 15 minutes or so. At each stop there is a 'Big Bus Employee' (all of which are very friendly) that has lots of information on the tour or other local attractions and are a great resource if you are looking for something in particular (a building or attraction).

On their website you can download digital maps or an application that gives you more specific details such as: attractions hours, cost, accessibility and reviews.

This was a very nice way to become familiar with London. You receive headphones to listen to what you are seeing but there is one bus route that has a person providing the tour information as oppose to hearing it on the headphones. Lots of good stops and it includes what they say is a river cruise. It's more like a large flat boat with only partial seating that is covered from the elements. Don't expect a cute river cruise but the bus part was very good.

It was impossible to find a friendly face at the Big Bus Tours company in London after 5pm. I suppose everyone must have been fed-up after beating London's traffic for a whole day. The answer to simple questions like "do you stop at Madame Tussaud's" was "No". "Could you tell me which bus stops at Madame Tussaud's?" got the response: "you just have to ask the driver of the next bus". The whole thing was simply unpleasant...

We took the Big Bus Blue Tour so that we could see and know about all the tourist attractions without getting down at each and every road and it was absolutely worth the experience! Everything from the recorded guide in different languages to the customer care provided by this tour is amazing!
