Special thanks to Andy Collins for assisting us to get back our luggage that we had forgotten on one of their buses! And to Neil Tyler as well, for assisting us! Kudos to you guys! :D

Truly a value for money deal right here!

Pre booked our 24 hour ticket on line..... when we arrived the man said a special offer was on and it was buy one day get one free which was fantastic so we hoped on straight away.fantastic tour of london on the red route with a live commentry from the guide.you can hop on hop off anywhere you want.also included is a free walking tour and river cruise wgich i highly reccomend.also pre book tickets as we saved a huge amount if money booking on line than we would have if we had payed on the day.also provide ear plugs for the blue route and rain macs for free.will defo be using tjis amazing company again.thank you xxxx

I love this Bus Tour and have used it on a number of visits to London. The fact that there is a live compere on the main route makes it stand out as you get theoppertunity to hear different opinions on the regular sites whilst also enabling you to ask questions. Also they often give you good information on temporary things that are happening. You get a boat tour and a few walking tours included which were great! Couln't recommend this company enough.

We were 'talked in to' using this bus company by a tour operator ..... my original choice was to use the "Original Tour Co" which has far more presence on the London tour. The Big Bus tour is very hard to find once you get off, there needs to be better sign postings & not once but twice on our tour our bus drivers changed & this meant a 10-15 min 'sit' in the boiling hot sun!!! People on board with small children were ripping their hair out. For the amount they charge it is a very amateur service. Proceed with caution.

We had talked about doing this open tp ride for a couple if years, my partner and i both work in London and never really get to relax and see the city. We took our 2 youngest children on the tour and what fun and an education it was. It was well managed, the guides were fun and we had some excellent banter all day long with different guides. Its great to jump on and off, we rode the bus in sunshine, jumped off at Marble Arch had lunch in Hyde Park, jumped back on and had a tour of the city, the free river cruise is great, if a bit busy, but we thoroughly enjoyed the use of the bus and the fun educational facts that came along with it, well worth the money and time, do it LONDONERS see our city!!

We have just returned from a 3 day trip to London and we would highly recommend the Big Bus Tour. We would never have seen half of what we did if we hadnt used these buses.Our drivers were friendly and helpful and yes, although it does take a bit of time to get round all the route, it is due to the level of traffic (and the traffic lights every few yards). Will definately use them next time we are back in London. Thanks to G and all your colleagues for making us so welcome.

We had a 24 hour family pass which covered us basically for 2 consecutive days. We haven't taken the children to London before, and so we wanted to do the whole tourist thing and have some fun along the way. Firstly, it was great to hop on the Green Link bus near our entry point train station and get taken to meet the blue/red routes, although we had to stand all the way there. Bus full of miserable people who wouldn't let our 4 year old have a seat. On the way back despite us asking for a particular stop, the driver didn't stop there, then had a go at us because we 'should have known' where we were. Well sorry mate, but if I knew my way around London I'd be driving myself?.. Wasn't too impressed.

We found the buses very convenient for the places we wanted to visit although there are more Blue buses (automated commentary) than red (live commentary). We did get one blue bus, and were underwhelmed by the very brief and dull commentary. The biggest problem is that there is no link up to the numbers on the map on the blue route so you almost have to 'guess' where you are. Why can't the commentary say 'you are approaching stop 23 on your map' etc?

The red bus guides were FANTASTIC and we learnt so much about London! However to get the most from them you need to not be in a hurry to get anywhere. Also you should know that you are most likely to get a seat on the top deck at lunchtime when most people have got off to have lunch!

After reviewing all the possible options to roam around in London I decided to take the BigBus tour, there were some mixed reviews about BigBus but to anyone reading my review, don't be fooled by negative reviews. It was an amazing experience to witness everything in London. You can hop-on and hop-off at any point and within 3-5min you will see another bus coming in. They have a very big fleet. But if you are planning to travel after 5pm then be ready for some delays because they reduce the number of buses after that. Best time is to take the bus as early in the morning as possible to watch all the attractions and utilize your time to the fullest.

I spent the day hopping on and off the Big Bus Company buses. The "live" guides on the Red line were extremely helpful in adding color to the areas we visited. Just watch the traffic because it can be a long time to get back to your starting point.

Note: I booked a few days in advance online and got a 25% discount. PLUS...because I didn't start my day until after 11 am, they included an extra day onto my ticket. The drive in from Heathrow to our hotel took 2 hrs of the morning due to the traffic. I thought congestion pricing was supposed to cut down on congestion. It doesn't.
Did the hop on hop off bus your it was well worth it money sin most of London on this and the boat trip well good

You can hop on and off these busses if you see an attraction you'd like to explore. We started on a bus with an automated tour. You just plug headphones in and listen to a recording about the buildings you pass. That was extremely boring, and half the time nobody knew what building was being discussed. We bailed on that bus and got on one with a human guide. He was great--very funny and charming and knowledgeable. You also get a boat ride as part of your fare.

The Big Bus tour was very convenient for moving around London. They run often and stop at all the major attractions. We walked a lot but liked having the option of hopping on the bus. We purchased 2 days for the price of 1. The only thing I didn't love is that we couldn't get a clear answer as to the timing of the last bus for the day. It is too bad that they end fairly early.

We decided to go on this bus tour as a means to get to the Tower of London which was on the other side of the city from our hotel....so glad we did.
We were able to purchase the Big Bus Tour tickets from the lobby of our hotel. From there it was less than a five minute walk to one of the pick up locations. We were on the blue line which meant the commentary was pre-recorded as opposed to the live commentary that you receive when on the red line route of the tour. The pre-recorded information was interesting and engaging. I suggest you sit in the upper portion of the bus if you plan on taking photos.... no glass windows to try to shoot through.... nice clear line of sight for awesome photos.

Big Bus Staff work at many of the bus route stops so asking for directions is very simple if you plan on getting on and off the bus as your tour around the city. We actually bought fast track tickets to the Tower of London through the Bus staff so that we didn't have to wait in line when we arrived at our final destination. The Big Bus Tour ticket also included a ride on the River Cruise boat... another great experience.
Only wish for the Big Bus Tour... wish the bus routes were available into the early evening. If we are fortunate to make it back to London again, we would absolutely use this as our form of transportation in seeing the attractions that we didn't have time to explore during this visit.

Partly due to London traffic and partly due to the circuitous routes that these buses take, it took us 3 hours to do 1 loop of the London Big Bus route. We had planned to do 1 complete loop and then on the second, do the hop on hop off thing, but with a short break for lunch, most of our day was taken up doing the 1 loop. Although crowded, the headphone commentary was great, the buses clean and frequent, if you have a map or a basic knowledge of the London Underground trains, it would be quicker to use them to reach the attractions rather rely on the hop on hop off.

This was my first time to travel to London and the first thing I considered was a tour of London. After researching for a bit on the interweb I found Big Bus Tours. What a great find! The tour was a great way to see all of the sites in London while atop the glorious view that is the double decker. Our guide, Nick was excellent in his knowledge of the area plus not to mention a few jokes thrown in now and again for some comedic relief. His knowledge of the sites and random facts about London provided a great experience for myself and my girlfriend. Would recommend Big Bus Tours to any one interested in a great tour throughout London. FYI Dean is also the best bus driver in London! Props to you mate.

We went on the Big Bus Tour. We had a blast! Our first announcer, Garreth, was a blast! He gave us some helpful tips in our tours and made interesting and comical! It was a hop on/off tour; so we took advantage of that to get off and walk around at all the tourists and then get on the bus! I would highly recommend this for anyone! The tour was 31 pounds, but it was worth it! We hopped on and off about six or seven times and we could use the ticket for two days!

The Big Bus has two lines (Red and Blue) that overlap for the most part but the blue covers more area around Kensington Park. The Red Bus is however an all English speaking tour with a live guide. The Blue is with headphones and spoken in about 12 different languages. For around 30 pounds, you get 24 hours of unlimited use of there buses, walking tours, and boat tours. You can get off and on as much as you like so stopping at attractions is easy. The audio portion of the tour is fine, and the seats are a little cramped and hard, but again, the value here is transportation around the two cities (London and Mayfair) with absolute flexibility based upon your preference areas to visit. We would do this again as in addition to site seeing, it allows you a way to stop and shop at all the various stores such as Harrods.

I had friends from abroad staying with me and decided that the Big Bus Tour would give them an opportunity to enjoy the city at a first glance in a convenient way.
The first thing I did was not only mess up our booking once but twice! Patsy, the sightseeing administrator, whom I contacted about my boo-boo was so nice and accommodating that I cannot praise her customer service high enough.
For our first day on the bus we choose the blue tour as it was convenient for my friends who could listen to the commentary in German. Additionally we also did the river cruise which they liked a lot. On our second day we opted for the red tour with a guide who was very knowledgeable and funny, ensuring everyone had a good time. Thanks to him I now know more about the origins of a few English sayings so it was also worth my while although I have been living in London for almost 4 years now.
At least at this time of the year we didn't have a problem getting on a bus. Obviously you have to be prepared to be stuck in traffic but my visitors didn't mind. They agreed that it was a good way to get a first impression of the city and enjoyed it.

Bought two 48-hour tickets to travel all three routes, which allowed us to get an extensive overview of London, hopping off to visit all the major sites, without running our feet off. All staff so polite and friendly, despite probably being asked the same questions day in and day out. Relatively punctual; obviously at the mercy of London traffic. Live commentary on Red Route excellent. Audio commentary on other routes very informative. Took advantage of the free Buckingham Palace Walking Tour, which was a hoot and highly recommended. Did not take advantage of the Free River Cruise, as it would need to be taken within the 48 hours, which was unfortunate. Opted to rather use our bus tickets to their full extent and buy river cruise tickets separately, to use on the third day. Pricey but buy all tickets online in advance and save.

I bought a 24 hour ticket. Make sure you ask for the 48 hour ticket for only 7 more lbs. You will need it! I was able to get to a good portion of the city, but was not able to hop off and explore long enough. The trip includes a free river cruise which i did twice. my first commentator on the river cruise was great and informative. the second trip was a very poor taped commentary. The tour guides on the busses were extrordinarily well informed and full of great little anecdotes.
Overall, a great way to see the sights of London for a relativley cheap price. Although nothing in London is "cheap"!

We had such an enjoyable day out where to start!

The staff member that gave us our tickets was lovely, friendly and funny, that was a great start. They made sure we had seats at the top in the sun!

The tour guide we had (Nori I think her name was) was awesome! She was funny, sweet, knew her facts about London and even made a hat out of a map for one the of passengers that was getting hot! So nice!

The route was brilliant, we got on at green park and stayed on till Tower Bridge but we could have got off before. We saw everything we wanted to!

The river cruise element was brilliant too, such an easy transition from bus to boat. A 2 minute walk to the pier, on to a boat which was 30 mins down to Westminster and was also brilliant!

Oh even the driver on the bus was lovely, chatting to us when we got on and off!

I would recommend this to everyone (even Londoners!!)

What can I say about the Big Bus tours? They do provide narrated and pre recorded audio tours around London. Their buses do give you a general overview of the city and its sights. There buses do NOT run at any great regularity and the people they have working at the bus stops seem more interested in "up selling" entry to other sights (we missed getting on a bus at the Tower of London to be forced to listen to the guy's schpeel"). AND we had pre-purchased tickets. Also they say their buses run until 8 PM however we could not get back on the bus after 6 PM as the bus wasn't going to go all the way back to where our hotel was at Westminster bridge. The ticket price was sort of high for the day (32 pounds) and it's only good for 24 hours. My advice is to say buyer beware. You would be better off purchasing a day travel card for the city buses and underground.

This is a very good concept but marred by the fact that London has a heavy traffic and frequent traffic jams.
I would strictly recommend this for first time travellers who dont have much time on their hands and want to roam around London in 1 day.
we hopped on to the bus on a sunny saturday morning.Waited for half an hour after which the conductor informed us the road ahead was blocked and you have to walk over to another point.
That messed up our schedule and delayed us by 1 hour and an additional half an hour till the driver brought us back on track to another point. We missed ripleys because of that and madam tussaudes would come as the last option which wud be after it would be closed
so we dropped off at tower pier took the cruise (which was free and was very good) to london eye. and then took a cab to tussauds.
in short we wasted our money on the bus trip i.e a cool 27 pounds.
It may have been good if it wud have started on time and followed the schedule.

The best would be to take the tube and go around the city on your own. Its a wonderful city to discover without any tourist guide :)

Like I said strictly for tourists short on time and dont want to go finding ways on your own.

When we travel abroad, I like to take a Hop on/Hop Off bus tour to get my bearings and have a comfy seat to wear off the jetlag before diving into a new place.
Upon arriving to London from Seattle, we did just that. We took the RED line tour, as it has the live tour guide, so you get more interesting stories, facts and they are not going to be on the fritz or out of sync with what you are looking at.
Still, we had the misfortune of being on the last bus of the evening. They parked the bus at Marble Arch and started telling people to get off, without fully explaining what was going on. I was able (just barely) to guess they were switching to hotel drop-off service as their service day had ended, but they did not follow the route printed for the service nor did they actually announce what was going on. The driver went around the bus, basically hollering, "Where are you going?" and then directing them to get off the bus or stay on. I was able to ask if they'd be stop near our apartment rental & stay on, but I was miffed for the poor people that were kicked off the bus into the pouring rain. Some of them were not English speakers and didn't know what was happening at all. It was very bad form.

We decided to book our tickets online before we arrived because it was cheaper . When we arrived at the stop on regent street closest to our yha hostel we presented our our printed paper copies from online. We did not have a problem. We caught the next bus and did the red route all the way around without getting off. Once we completed this route we stopped for lunch and then continued back on the bus to get us to Big Ben where we took the included boat tour. The boat tour ended at the London bridge. There we caught our next bus to keep exploring. We never waited more then 5 mins for a bus and were always able to find a seat on the top level. We started our tour at 850 am for the red route and were the only ones on the bus for the morning so that was nice . Probably not the case
In the summer. In the end we enjoyed the big bus tour. We would recommend it to anyone travelling to London because the sites in London are spread out and the bus makes it easier to see everything in a short amount of time .

We went on the Big bus in April . It was definitely the best way to see London but the highlight of the trip was seeing the changing of the Guard . Our guide Kevin was fantastic he really made our tour fun & informative . Big thanks to him. We did the cruise to Greenwich that was also a really good day out .There was also a young man commentating on the red bus I think his name was Dan he was also very good very informative . Well worth doing .

After some minor difficulty trying to figure out where to catch our initial bus to begin the tour we finally decided on a major stop in Picadilly. The signs indicating the stops for Big bus tour vs. The original tour ( different companies) are not all that obvious on the very busy and sometime excessively signed streets of London. We saw a bus and hailed it down at which point we were greeted by a very pleasant tour employee who also sold us discounted tickets for the London Eye. The tour was a terrific idea and we had purchased the 48 hour ticket previously online so we could take our time seeing the major sights and include the Eye and the Thames river cruise both of which are highly recommended by this traveler. All in all a great way to see all the tops attractions when time and endurance for lengthy walks are an issue.

We received rode Big Bus Tours on our first full day in London. We thought it was a wonderful way to get our bearings in town and see all of the highlights. We didn't hop off until Buckingham Palace - saw the changing of the guard. On the following days, we dove deeper into the sights.

We had bought 24 hour tickets. If I were to do it again, I might suggest the 48 hour tickets. We rode the Tube every day - but I think the quickest way between two famous sites is often the Big Bus Tour. Plan ahead to maximum your use.

Also, there are two versions of this tour - Red and Blue. One of them is a prerecorded tour, available in multiple languages. The other is a live guide in English. If you speak English, I would suggest the live guide - and then sit close to him - ask him questions. If your first guide isn't very good (ours was great), just hop off and catch the next bus. Also, sit upstairs for the best photos.

We arrived in London a day prior to the tour and only had 2 days to spend touring. We hopped on the bus around 10:30 am and after not understanding a word that the guide said, we got off by Downing Street. We went into Westminster abbey and the Churchill war rooms then re entered another bus only to find out that the majority of the rest of the loop could not be continued due to a tragic accident ahead. I understand that the company has no control over this but we asked one of the personnel if we may continue tomorrow since we only spent maybe 30 mins touring. He explained that we saw the "main attractions, so don't worry about it". No accommodations were made for a very expensive 4 person party. We really wanted to see the city and understand the important areas. We used our guide book instead. I won't recommend this to anyone else.

I feel so bad we never remember names which makes this already a shocking review but please look past the forgetfulness!!! This tour is fantastic and if you get the guide who after all his best jokes says "This is good stuff" DO NOT GET OFF THE BUS. He is absolutely fantastic- and completely made our day. He told us to spend the afternoon at the Tower of London- which was amazing! Then by chance we got back on his bus afterwards (complete fluke). This tour was super easy to understand, the buses were great as were the drivers and the other guides and the commentary made for a wonderful introduction to London. Definitely make the most of the 2 day pass if you are travelling in the off season and try and get on the earlier buses in the morning. Make the most of this tour as you will wish you had all week to complete it!

We like to do “hop on, hop off” buses when we visit a new city. They are a very inexpensive and efficient way to get a feel for the layout of the city and where the sights are, and you learn some tidbits about history that you might otherwise not get. We used this bus twice while in London, for two different tours, and both were outstanding. I highly recommend you do this when you first arrive.

We bought one day and got one free on the Big Bus promotion they had going on for the month of February. If you were trying to get from point A to point B in a hurry, then this is not the mode of transportation for you! If you want to sit back, ride for a while, see some sights, and hear some interesting and witty narrative, then....yes, this is your ride indeed! We have rode other hop on hop off bus tours in other cities. This was no different. It IS what you make of it. If you go into anything with a crappy attitude, then a crappy time is what you shall have. (noticed some other reviews complaining) This is not a private tour, but can be a quite enjoyable day or two in London. Some stops are closed due to road construction. (this was the case near our hotel and it made finding a bus to start with a little more challenging) But ask the driver which stops are closed and adjust accordingly and you will be just fine.

Big bus tours is excellent for sightseeing, the only trouble we had was that we ended up going to London on the 2 day tube strike, which was the exact 2 days we were there so it wasn't the best of trips. The traffic was really slow and we barely moved on the buses at some point but they were fantastic when the commentators were on board with the microphones, keeping our spirits up in the cold weather and bad traffic. Steve and Nuri (sorry if its spelt wrong) were our favourite guides, very chatty, very good cheesy jokes and fully enjoyed their tours! We saw everything wanted to and hopped on and off as we pleased to visit places. Every sight we saw was explained in detail with the past history on them and the guides got everyone involved. They were great when tourists were asking advice on sights, transport etc, and even on the last bus they were excellent at getting everyone where they needed to be to get back to their hotels. Very good at giving advice on watching your bags, and the best places to go. Fully enjoyed our 2 day ticket with big bus tours (despite all the traffic from tube strike!) and have a lot of respect for the staff who stand at the bus stops selling tickets and giving advice, as they were cold and soaking wet! But were fantastic. Thankyou to all of the staff! :)

Booked on line and using Quidco website got tickets for £20 each available for use over 48 hrs, which we took advantage of , nicely broke up the tour and we saw all the sights.Choice of Green (short route),Blue Line(multi-lingual audio commentary)or Red Line((English live commentary by tour guide) recommended.February weather was mixed but managed top of the bus for most of the time,which you need for best viewing and 'photos. Tour guides were very good,extremely knowledgeable ,interesting and amusing.Learnt an awful lot about London history and amazed to see so much in just 48 hours. We didn't have time for the free Thames cruise but had done it on a previous visit and it is a must as you get a different perspective and again see a lot in a short space of time.Top Tip- carefully plan your route beforehand so that you can take in all the attractions by 'jumping' off and on and switching from one line to another - you might want to get a tube to start at Green Park and end the tour there with Tea at the Ritz as a final treat

On our rendezvous in London, UK, my fiancee` son suggested to her that we do the "Big Bus" red and blue tours. Open to anything on holiday in London for the first time, we decided do to it and were not disappointed. We took the Tube from our apartment to Green Park station where we bought our two-day passes. The Red tour was our first choice. We took the slightly longer Blue Tour the next day. These double-decker buses offer fantastic vista vantage points for photos of London (especially from the upper deck)! Between the two of us (and with today's digital technology) we must have taken over 500 pictures in two days! Many of them can be seen here at my blog http://achilliad.wordpress.com/2013/11/09/mind-your-head-london-uk-through-our-eyes/
You can "hop on/hop off" the buses at any of the many scheduled stops along the way. The Red Tour featured live tour guides on-mic; the Blue tour has pre-recorded descriptions and you need to use the ear phones which are a slight inconvenience.
We had so much fun and learned a lot during these tours which added to the overall romantic visit to this historic city! I saved the Big Bus Tour paper map and maybe will frame it one day once my fiancee` and I are living under the same roof. I highly recommend this brand also because I left my little camera case aboard the Red Tour bus the first day and one of the workers found it and they held it for me at their offices until I could collect it two days later. It had a five dollar note and a memory card in it and all was still in-tact when I collected it. Bravo!

We have learned, when visiting a new city, that the best way to see it the first time is to take a bus tour. Hop on-hop off are the best (meaning that for a limited amount of time - usually 12 to 24 hours); you can get off and resume the tour at your convenience. This tour gives you a fair amount of information and history and will orient you to the city. We take the tour, getting on and off for a short time at places we like, and also take note of the places, museums, restaurants, parks, etc., etc., that we really like. We go back on our own time to these places later in the trip.

The tour of London via the Big Bus tour company was fine to a point. Live commentaries are always a bonus and the guide for our day tour was good. Knowledgeable and humorous we took his advice and took a later tour to see the Thames in the evening when the river was lit up.
We were the only passengers on the bus at this time of year when we noticed a strong smell of cigarette smoke. From where we were sitting we could not see the driver or the guide so could not tell who was smoking. This occurred twice and I emailed the company to complain. It took a week before I received a reply saying that smoking is not permitted by anyone at anytime on the buses. I acknowledged the email and was awaiting the outcome. After three weeks still no outcome and doubt that there will be. If this is indicative of the value they place on their customers concern then I would not recommend this company, there are others to choose from.

The London hop on/hop off tour is very convenient and you see many landmarks. However, it doesn't have as many stops as you might like and the red route buses run very, very late. The ticket takers at the stops are so fairly rude and uninterested and do not give timely updates. The guides on each of my buses were interesting and informative but that was the only upside. I recommend The Original Tour as those attendees seemed much more satisfied and I would see three of their buses to every one Big Bus Tour bus.

Purchased a two day pass but could nearly have needed a three day pass as so much to see and do. We found the buses rang regularly, never had to wait too long and were clean, very informative and went everywhere including a cruise to Tower of London and Greenwich if you wished to go further. There are different colour buses tours depending on where you wish to go. We spent 2 full days, getting off at most of the significant places and really it wasn't enough time. We ended up leaving Buckingham Palace and doing that ourselves. I suggest that you go to Tower of London early to avoid the long lines to get into crown jewels (about 80 minute wait in freezing cold for us). We learnt so much about things we didn't know about by doing the tour and you get earplugs and can nominate which language you would like to hear the audio in. They even provided Poncho's for the wet London weather...a must in London. It may initially seem expensive but believe me, it was well worth it. We found it hard to find toilet stops sometimes, however we could always find a coffee shop with a clean toilet and warm environment for a break. Harrods is open to 8pm so I would leave that until later in the day and make the most of daylight hours to see other things. It does get dark about 4pm in Winter so daylight hours are limited. We took the cruise from the London Eye to Tower of London and made the mistake of staying on and going to Greenwich, which all round trip took about 3 hours. Greenwich would be good if you had the time but we didn't and wasted an afternoon when we could have been seeing other sights or seeing them without rushing the next day. This is a fabulous way to see and learn about London. Highly recommended and there are other bus companies, however Big Bus Tours were very reliable, clean and easy to use.

I purchased a 2-day ticket which costs GBP30.

Pros : 1) Easy way to get to know London city - bus will go round the city and short brief about the famous landmarks was shared through recorded commentary. Different languages were available. 2) Bus drivers that I met were polite. 3) Its hop on hop off stops were available and easily accessible at most of the tourist attractions.

Cons : 1) London City traffic condition could be hectic. Wasted a lot of time being stuck in the traffic jam. 2) It's an open top double-decked bus. When it rains, we can only sit in the lower deck which is stuffy. 3) Though it stated 24hrs or 48hrs what so ever, the bus was only running from 10:00 to 16:30.

I was so disappointed by this as I had received recommendations from friends who had used this tour earlier in the year.
I purchased a 48 hour ticket and didn't even bother with the second day as I had been left so dissatisfied the previous day! Our bus waited at Green Park for 30 minutes before even starting the tour, then crawled through a bit of London before missing out the part of the tour for Tussauds, Oxford street, Regent Street etc. Then took a detour past Westminister and headed over the river, the tour guide was useless during all of this, just said 'er....I don't know where we are going? We must be taking a detour...?' I asked if we would be going back to the stops we had missed to which he replied,'er... I don't know', said I could get off at the next stop and find an underground back up the other end of central london if I wanted, I asked which was closest and was told 'if you start walking, I'm sure you'll find one'. Gave up and got off the bus and went for the river cruise included instead which was really good (you could learn from your associated company Big Bus Tours!), Got off the boat at Tower of London to catch the next leg of the bus tour for no bus to turn up for half an hour again.
Gave up and got the boat cruise back to Westminister and decided to do London by foot!
Avoid this firm, I believe there are better, more reliable tours operating.

We took this bus tour while in London for a few days, if you don't have much time this is the only way to see the city. allow yourself 2 days as the ticket is valid for 48 hours and their also a boat trip on the river included. the price is abit steep if like us you only had 1 day. The stops are at all the major things to see and a bus come's about every 20 mins. Try and take this trip on a fine day. (I think their is a reduce price if someone with you is from the UK.) ask when you are buying your ticket. we started from Mabble Arch.

Only had one full day in London so this was an excellent way to see the major sites. We didn't even use the tube as it hits every major place during the day. The guides at the stops were very helpful in directing us to the places we wanted to see when we got off. The delays at the stops were a little longer than expected, but not too bas as we had wonderful weather and it was nice to be outside. Bring your own headphones and they will work on the bus for the audio commentary. We didn't get on the bus with the live guide, so I can't comment to that, but there were plenty of buses and no real wait times in between hopping off and hopping on. The buses were clean and the staff very helpful. Made getting around the city very easy.

BEST tour company in London, Do not let the others fool you, cuz they tried it with me.
First, you get 2 full days to hop on and off. You will see all/or most of London with Big Bus. Everything was perfect, from safe driving, to answering questions, to the frequency of arrival and departure.
I did end up stranded after 6pm, but they made sure I end up in a safe place to catch a cab or walk. And I walked - fantastic adventure getting lost. That's the best way to learn a city )

Thank you Nuri!! After dealing with some not so excellent customer service on the ground with Big Bus Tours and a driver that was a bit crotchety, Nuri saved the day by providing the best tour I have yet to experience and also by going above and beyond to fix the bad customer service and making sure our experience was amazing.

We have enjoyed hop-on hop-off bus tours in many cities. In London, we selected the Big Bus Tours because it went all the way to Kensington and stopped near our hotel. BIG MISTAKE!!! Fortunately, we hopped on at the first stop so we got a seat. By the second or third stop the bus was standing room only. That meant that we could only see out one side of the bus. Also, anyone standing could not hear the audio, which requires headsets. It also meant that if we hopped off, we would be standing when we hopped on again. Instead, we took the bus directly to the Tower of London, which took about 2 1/2 hours. On returning, we waited for almost a half hour at a stop where two other bus companies had multiple busses come and go, and we wound up standing for most of the trip back. The next day, in spite of the fact that we had purchased a 48-hour bus ticket, we took the underground, a much better choice. With it, we got from our hotel to Parliament in about 10 minutes and spent the rest of the day seeing the sights!

We arrived in London at 10.30 2 adults a 15 year old and a 7 year old we headed to charing cross then down pall mall for changing of the guards it's on every even day in August best spot is Victoria monument as you can climb the steps or front of Buckingham palace, we chose to go a little left at the end of pall mall as it was really busy and we had a young child we stood on opposite side of road to monument but still had a great view. We then headed left of the palace towards Victoria station to pick up the big bus tours left hand side of the road the guide was a great help only difference from this tour to the original bus tour it only goes one way round London. We got the blue tour which you use headphones was ok but mine kept going off we got off at green park for something to eat then rejoined the tour we got the red tour which had a man telling us all the info we stayed on until Tower of London then got our free river cruise up to Westminster that was excellent the guide was really funny great view of the eye and Big Ben. I must say I have been to London loads of times but learnt more yesterday than ever before about the city definitely best way to get around. If your bus turns up and is really busy upstairs, generally there will be another couple following which will be empty when we got ours at green park they were all empty and this is busy holiday time Victoria was a lot busier i must add. I can't comment on the walking tours as the first one for changing of the guards left charing cross at 10.20 we really wanted to do Harry potter at 1 at Trafalgar Square but again if we had done that we wouldn't have done the bus tour in time as the last bus is 6 p.m. And we wanted to do the river cruise, time just goes so quickly especially when the bus gets stuck in traffic ,longer than they say it is so give yourself plenty of time. So instead to please my 7 year old we went to kings cross train station and got a photo at 9 and 3/4 the guy there is hilarious. I recommend a good 10 hrs to get done what you need to do in a day I now have a different perspective of London and I must say everyone was fantastic even to the doorman at the ritz where we had a photo taken.

This Hop-on off bus was a waste of money and time. The bus schedule was erratic, the commentary was boring and it is exteremely expensive. We basically wasted a day stuck in traffic, listening to elevator music. I would not recommend this tour.

Me and my mom bought 48 hours tour (I recommend everyone to get48hrs tour as its just a couple pounds more!) our guide on the bus on 5 aug 2013 was Andrew. He's the best guide ever as he always smile, friendly and very helpful. The tour includes all u need bus tour, walking tour Nd the Thamr river cruise tour. Therefore 48hours we explored the whole London!! My mom was so enjoy. Actually i have lived in the UK for 2 years already but I just realised after i took the bus sighseeing that Oh! I missed a lot of wonderful places in london!! So i do recommend everyone!!!!
Ps. Get the bus from green park in order to get a good seat :)) have funn!

Oh my Great!!

the walking tour for the changing of the guards was fantastic. the guide really directed you to the best places to stand and you were able to see and march along with not one but two marching bands.It was Great! Th,e other three walking tours included in the price of a 48 hour hop on hop off ticket were not of interest to us. The bus tour itself while allowing you to preview many of the highlighted sites did not always have a guide describing the sites and those busses that did not have live guides on them did not always have recorded tours that worked.The Thames Riverboat cruise which was also included in the price of the 48 hour ticket was also anothe bonus. You could board the vessel as many times as you wanted and it served as an additional means of transportation to various sites in London. It also allowed you to travel by water to Greenwich, the site of the prime meridian.

I took my daughter and her friend on the Red Tour one sunny Thursday morning. We got on at Green Park Tube, having booked online the day before for about £25 each. The personal commentary was exellent, visual lines were great, and over the first 2 hours it was a great way to get to know London.

It definitely helped them get their bearings, and for the rest of the day they "hopped on and hopped off" various places like St Pauls, Hamleys, Covent Garden etc etc.

It can be quite slow but that is just traffic in London for you - heavy traffic. But they thought it was a great day spent.

These buses take you almost everywhere in London to the interesting sites and permit you to "hop on - hop off" at any of their many stops. The recorded as well as the vocal naration is quite informative. Our tour also included a short river boat trip. Worth the money.

This tour is a great way to see all the important sights in London. You can hop on and off the bus for 24 hours at time of purchase. I would recommend staying on the bus for the full tour (2 hours) to hear and see everything then begin hopping on and off as you approach sights you want to see up close. Many sights have long lines so prioritize your stops. Cost was £30 per person.

We had the greatest guide, young blond haired girl who was funny and knowledgeable. What's great about the line is it has a red tour and a blue tour that take you to different places so its interesting. Its good to get an overall look at everything and then go back and get off the bus to see what you want to see. Then just hop back on the next one.

We had Andy (can't remember surname - but he was an extra in Harry potter:)!) as the live guide. He was excellent - worth specifically asking which bus he'll be on when you do the tour! funny and energetic, but also knowledgable. Having said that, other guides we had after hop off/ on were also good. I can really recommend this as a great way to see London, particularly if you are new to the city or you have limited time

We just got back from taking a Big Bus tour today 14th July 2013. Having lived in London for many years its amazing how much we did not know about it. And thanks to the great tour guides of Big Bus our education got updated.
It has been a hot day and for those coming to London its going to stay in the mid to late 20's until the end of July at least.
So being so hot and sunny wear a hat if your planning to ride on their open top buses and of course wear sun screen. And also if you can bring along that airline cushion you have, my only complaint was the seats do give you numb bum after a while.

The tour we took was the red tour which provided us with a tour guide. The green tour gives you ear bugs and a recorded commentary about London.
The live tour is much better for us.
Its a hop on hop off service.
Our first bus had Dave as our guide a very friendly guy who was polite and helpful at all times however he was losing his voice,occupational hazard I assume.
We had to get off at Marble Arch for some reason which wasn't a problem, we wanted a comfort break anyway.

We did not have any waiting time for our next bus on which Andrew was our guide. This man knew his London very well, and even though we were forced off our scheduled route onto roads he had not been on,because of road works,he was still able to give us fascinating facts about the sights on this detour .

Not once on either bus were there long pauses of no commentary. When there were traffic delays the guides filled in the time chatting to passengers or telling us all about this place or that.

We found every member of the Big Bus very helpful and polite,seeking us out to help not make us come to them.

Points to consider. Its hot in London right now.
Bring water,sunscreen and a cushion if you plan to stay on the bus for the full tour.
However if your hoping off and on again that is not a problem. It does not matter which side of the bus you sit on.
You can sit downstairs if you want to, but you'll see a lot more from on high.

Having never been on a city tour bus before we are annoyed we did not take one years ago.
In hindsight we should have gone for the 48hr pass as there is too much in London to see in one day, but if that is all the time you have then a 24 hour pass with this company is, in our humble opinion, the best option

Included with the tickets is a return River Cruise, which we did not take, the queues were too long,(to be expected) as it was so hot.

There are plenty of bus tours to pick from. They all seemed the same with almost identical routes. Big Bus Tours is a comfortable ride up top and a great way to transit around to the various attractions. It is amazing that the buses can squeeze into the tight streets. The drivers are to be commended.

I wish that there were more stops to actually stop at. We drove past many attractions that I would have liked to have stopped at. Travelling through the streets, often at high speeds, it was often difficult to actually get any pictures like I had hoped. When we did hopped off the bus and then back on, they were often crowded and we were forced to squeeze into the bottom level. It was unfortunate as we missed lots of attractions we wanted to view. Sometimes it took up to 20 mins for another bus to arrive to hop back onto. We had originally planned to hop on and off a lot more but we didn't. We didn't want to waste time just standing around waiting for another bus.

I also wished that the live guide would have said what streets we were coming onto before we actually on them. For instance, I wanted to visit Fleet Street and I didn't know we were even on Fleet Street until I saw a sign and we were leaving it. On another bus we listened to the audio tour which was really good. I wondered it the audio tour would have provided more information than the live guide.

We took the boat cruise back from the Tower of London. Once again it was packed and unfortunately we were crammed into the bottom covered level and we only got to see out the windows through tourist bodies. No pictures could be taken. However, the guide was a funny man and provided fabulous commentary which really helped my displeasure being stuck in the bottom level.

Take ANY OTHER tour. Avoid "Big Bus" at all costs. We've been on the bus for over 2 hours already and haven't gotten thru even a third of the route. The stops are too frequent and too long (we're talking 10-20 minutes at each stop!) and the recorded commentary is ridiculous. There's more awful elevator music than actual explanation of what you're seeing! Of course we were disappointed that the live commentary bus was another half hour wait when this one was already late and we chose the recorded...thinking we might learn something!! The commentary doesn't even match what you're looking at! This is a total waste of time and money. I'm generally a huge fan of HOHO bus tours and have taken them all over the world. This is by far the worst experience of any organized tour. Oh and also, they never ever looked at our tickets so if you want to test it, there's a good chance you'll ride 6 hours of awful tour for free!!

Visiting London at the end of June and not knowing the city and having only five days, we decided to take an open-topped tour bus. We walked to a stop and were quickly accosted by the Big Bus ticket sellers. We purchased 48 hour tickets and were told that busses come every five minutes. The first tour went rather well (we just did a roundtrip from Tower Bridge, not getting off until the trip was over).
The following day, we had an appointed at the British Museum and had to be there by 10:00. We were previously told that the first bus was at 9:15. We waited until 9:30. No bus. We had to take a taxi for 20 pounds.
Another problem is that Big Bus stops are hard to find. They give you a map that shows stops but only about 10% of the streets on that map are named
On Saturday, we waited at a stop for well over 30 minutes. Big Bus rep at the stop told us that bus would arrive in 300 seconds! Nope, waited over 1800 seconds. I promised this young man that I was going to review his terrible company on TripAdvisor. He didn't seem to care.
Anyway, DO NOT use Big Bus. All they want to do is sell you a ticket. Shame on me for not consulting TripAdvisor ahead of time. There is much more about this terrible company that I could tell you. Please DO NOT use Big Bus!!!!!

We had a great afternoon on our Big Bus tour which we picked up from Green Park. Luckily we had good weather so we were able to enjoy the open top bus to its max. Our driver Hannah was smooth and Nuri, the guide was really pleasant and entertaining with interesting nuggets of information, gory facts and corny jokes about the places we passed.

Quite good value too considering there was a river trip and walking tour thrown in. The bus was spotless and the whole thing ran smoothly and efficiently (notwithstanding London traffic) with loads of uniformed staff at all the stops who were pleasant and helpful.

I live in London but sometimes you have to experience it like a tourist to re-ignite your enthusiasm for our great city. Our guide and the whole Big Bus experience did that for us.

A very mixed experience. Wrong bus stop listing meant our first 'hop on' went straight by. Finally getting onto a red route bus, the live commentary was barely live, infact I wanted to go and check the guides pulse at one stage. It was all a bit 'mockney reads from a script'.

Hopped off for lunch, and then had over 25 mins waiting to hop back on, so it wasn't quite the frequency I was led to believe. The second guide had a great sense of humour, was really informative, and fielded all questions - well done to him - a great representative of the company.

While waiting for the Big Bus, there seemed to be a much higher frequency of Original Bus Tour buses. This left me with a bit of a 'meh' feeling about Big Bus; and my advice is that once you have hopped on, and it is a decent guide, DO NOT hop off.

I'm a Londoner born, bred and still living here. I had some friends visiting who wanted to see the sights all in a weekend, so having taken city bus tours both in other UK cities and overseas I thought it would be a great way for them to see lots of London.

Big mistake! Whilst the tour does go to many of the main features, it only goes "close" to others (for example Buckingham palace). We passed hugely historic buildings like Westminster abbey and the recorded commentary makes no mention, likewise Eros in Piccadilly Circus. When it did make reference to places there was little history or detail. We passed Hyde park with not a single reference, the high courts of justice without a word.

Would have been much cheaper to get a one day bus pass, a London guide book and I'd have done a much better job at relaying all the facts and figures. Don't waste your money

I wanted to book at 48 hour hop on hop off bus tour for a Saturday and Sunday, so I decided to go with Big Bus Tours as the other providers only offered 24 hour tickets. I booked for 5 people online at £31 pp.
Admin:
When we got to the bus stop, the person who confirms the online tickets took forever to give us our printed tickets- highly inefficient. It was a cold windy day and we waited outside while 3 busses left without us as we waited for our printed tickets.
Number of busses:
There are MUCH more of the Original Bus Company tour busses than there were Big Bus Tour busses. We ended up waiting for longer than the stated 10-20 minutes between busses that is stated on their website.
Tour guide:
The red route has live english commentary. It was difficult to hear the tourguide and he didnt speak very clearly.
The blue route did not have that much commentary on the various attractions we passes- we spent most of our time listening to the filler music.
River cruise:
The river cruise that was included (30 mins) was quite enjoyable.
Experience:
We had such a bad time waiting on our first day that we didnt even use the rest of our 48h ticket that we purchased.

Overall I would higly suggest you do not use this provider- rather go with the Original Bus Company- we have used them on a short previous visit to London last year and they were much more imformative, friendly and they have many more busses.

Me and my girlfriend did a tour with Big Bus company in London last friday, and we thoroughly enjoyed it. We had a excellent tour guide called Jeff (and driver Buzz), and the commentary was very good... informative, well spoken, and humerous!
We were sitting in the open, and had about a 10minute downpour during our tour - but were given free rain poncho's which i thought was good. You've probably got to expect some rain in London i suppose!
The tour was £30 each which i thought was abit expensive, but i realised afterwards that if you go on their website and book in advance then it's just £21 - which i think is very reasonable.
I would definately do this tour again if i visit London in the future.

I have used the Big Bus tour of London before, so booked it for a special treat on Fathers Day. I was shocked by the terrible service I received when I tried to have my prepaid voucher scanned so that I could get our tickets and board the bus. As soon as the reps knew I'd already paid they wouldn't talk to me and wanted me to wait until all the people that hadn't paid had bought their tickets.
When you board a bus with a tour guide, the commentary is great and their knowledge of London if fantastic. I heard a lot of people ooohing and aaahing. However when you board a bus to discover there is no guide, you have no idea where you are. We were on the bus for nearly an hour with no guide, before the bus pulled over and we were all kicked off.
I expect better for £57 for 2 adult tickets and a child.

We had the best tour guide on many of the busses we traveled on in the 2 days we were in London - NURI, the Whoo Hoo girl! She was knowledgeable, friendly and remembered us! Hop on, hop off - great way to see London and hopefully you are lucky enough to have Nuri inform and entertain you along the way! Unfortunately, the weather wasn't cooperative but still enjoy the sites!

Took the tour over school half term.
If your going to the tour with no stops or guided walks - then you are fine
If your going to do any of the guided walks, then on a day pass - you will run out of time - two day pass shouldnt be a problem.

Advantages - all Big Bus appear to have guides that give you a commentary , which for us was very good. Also they give plastic macs if it rains.

Harry Potter guided walk by Ian (guide) is excellent. The ministry of magic as the MOD building fits the MOD perfectly.

Disadvantages - all Dads be prepared to spend money in the Harry Potter sweet shop that the guide talkes you too (£10 per bag) .

For £31 for one adult and child , you might feel as your not getting value for money if you dont do the full tour . However in my opinion, the guided walks made up for it. i would go again.

We visited London and decided to take the bus tour. We approached a guy who was selling tickets and asked if we could pay by credit card he said it was cash only. We paid even though we wanted to retain some of our cash for later. He then pointed us down the road to where the bus left from. Imagine our surprise when we realised that the big bus rep at the stop was selling tickets on credit card. The agent should have told us this was possible. The bus at the stop has several seats downstairs however the rep advised us to wait for the next one. After waiting about 15 minutes another bus pulled in, this was packed and there were.no seats upstaIrs or down stairs so we had to stand. £30 each to stand on a packed bus with no commentary as the headphones had to be attached to a point in front of the seats. The tours had obviously been oversold. However after a very uncomfortable 15 minutes or so we managed to find a seat when people got off the bus. Apart f rom one stop of another 15 minutes which was made because of buses backing up the rest of the trip was good. It was advertised as hop on hop off but we daren't leave our seats once we had them for fear of not getting another. I appreciate it was a busy bank holiday but some system should be in place to stop the trips being oversubscribed.

We pre-booked our Big Bus Tour - unfortunately our flight was delayed and we arrived a day late and missed our scheduled day. When we arrived we went and spoke to the people at the bus - they were awesome. Made a quick call and got us on the bus for the day. We were very thankful that they did that and that we didn't loose out on the tour.

We enjoyed the bus - we rode both lines. The one with the automated guide was actually pretty good. The live guide was excellent. We learned a lot about London and we got to see all the major sites. The buses came quickly and the stops were clearly marked.

Another thing that we were really impressed with was that we were riding the bus at the very end of the day. The staff found out exactly were we (and everyone on the bus) needed to go and made sure that we were on the correct bus. We were on the wrong bus so we were thankful that they double checked and didn't get stranded.

Our experience with Big Bus was very positive and we highly recommend them.

We felt this tour was a smart way to start off our few days in London. We rode the bus with the live commentary around the full loop to help us decide what we wanted to do for the rest of the time in London. The live commentary greatly depends on who you get but all of ours were enjoyable and different.

We started our second day with the boat cruise down to the Tower of London - also very fun and interesting. Obviously the tube is more efficient for transportation but the hop-on-hop-off is really convenient.

Tips:
*Make sure you are buying your tickets from a real employee of the company
*Don't buy London Eye tickets from them - you have to exchange them for the real tickets and end up standing in longer lines than necessary.

We were staying in the Holborn area of London and my wife was in a lot of pain and barely able to walk. Never the less we decided to do a 24 hr. hop on hop off bus tour with Big Bus Tours. We had bought a Oyster Card( bus and train credit card that cost 5 BPS and the 5 BPS refundable with the return of the card and I added 15 BPS as credit to the card) We took the regular bus outside our hotel and got off 3 stops later at the Big Bus Tours bus stop. 10 minutes later at 11 am saw us on the taped bus commentary with earphones that were provided. We sat on the upper deck outside and it was very pleasant. The recordings were both informative and humourist . We brought with us sandwitches and drinks and ate on the bus. After about 11/2 hrs we got off at Waterloo Bridge and took our free boat trip down to Westminster Pier.
Again the boat trip was excellent and the live commentary was very humourist but I did feel sorry for non English speakers as the commentator used a lot of English/ London idioms. Our bus ticket was still valid till 11:30 am(24 hr. ticket) Again in order to minimize walking we took the train from Holborn to Hyde Park station, we stood at a bus stop that had a sign saying Big Bus but after 20 minutes realized the bus stop was around the corner facing the Hilton Hotel. catching the first bus early morning at 8:30 am. Again this was a enjoyable trip and we actually got to do the whole route when we disembarked at the bus stop were we had started the day before.

The Hop-on-Hop-off bus tours are great for a good overview of London Sights. Personally I like the tube better for transportation, but using the tour service for one day is great.

I would recommend starting your day off nice and early and doing a full circuit tour on a Red Line bus (the ones with a actual person providing commentary). A full circuit takes about 2hrs. Then keep using the service as you navigate to and from other attractions. There is no script for the guides, so you may get extra tidbits from each new guide.

There is another Hop-on-Hop-off company called Original Tours which is cheaper. I have not used this company personally, but have been told that Big Bus guides give better commentary.

Arriving at my hotel at 9:00 a.m. after an all-night flight, my room wasn't ready, but they let me store my bags before I headed out to explore the city for the first time ever. Getting a ticket to ride on the top of the open-air double decker tourist bus was the best choice I could have made. Samantha, our Scottish tour guide, was extremely informative and entertaining. Riding the bus gave me a good idea of how the city was laid out and the location of sights on my must-see list. It also helped to sit for 2-1/2 hours to alleviate jet lag. The Big Bus Tour was a perfect start to my London stay.

I went on Big Bus London today and it was great. We stayed on the entire red loop in one sitting. The tour guides were both really good, informative and enthusiastic. It's lovely to be shown London by girls that clearly enjoy their job and their city. They changed over and both were good and gave slightly different slants but that made it personal and more captivating because they clearly were not just sticking to scripts!! It was really fresh and my partner and I really enjoyed the tour. We thought £30 was expensive at first but actually it is good value because you get the city boat tour included for free which was also good and worth doing. You can hop on/off as many times as you want in 24 hrs or you can upgrade to 48hrs for £6 more.Our main tour girl was Nuri and she said go on trip advisor if we liked it so here I am saying I was so not bored and it was fun and interesting and it is down to the live guides because they bring it to life. Have done recorded headphone ones before and been bored and drift off.

We went on-line to buy our 4 tickets for London's 48 hour Big Bus tour which were advertised at a discount. As it turned out, paid full fare for a 24 hour ticket and, once on the bus had to pay additional for the extra 24 hours which we did. We then sent an e-mail to the company explaining the problem and asking for a refund of the difference and NEVER even had the courtesy of a reply!! The tour was good but this soured our experience.

Worse experience ever! Busses ran between 45 minutes and an hour between busses, not 15-20 minutes as advertised. We spent hours waiting in cold and wet for late busses only to be given bad advice and treated rudely. It was heartbreaking to see 5 Original Tour Busses pick up their passengers and no Big Bus Tour Busses to be found. Finally the blue line bus told us to get off at Victoria Station and catch the next red bus to go to the London Eye. No red bus showed up for nearly an hour and then he told us they were closing and he stranded us!

We really enjoyed the big bus tour which also took in a 30 minute rever cruise on the Thames. The sights were fantastic & the guides on the red line were great. We really enjoyed the river cruise.

The only downside is there are very little provision made for buggies. Most buses only have space for either 1 wheelchair user or 1 buggy and some buses as we found, can't accommodate either.

We had gone on one such bus and after travelling half the route with one driver, when a new driver came on the bus, we were asked to leave the bus and wait for another due to health & safety.

Despite this blip, we really enjoyed the tour overall and would recommend it to anyone who does not have a child in a buggy.

We first saw the Big Bus Tour outside of Charing Cross station. The man who was selling the tickets was the only friendly member of staff we came into contact with throughout the day, and i'm sure its for that reason - he's selling the tickets! My family are over from Germany and with only one day in London we decided this would be the best way to see the main sights in the big city. Buckingham Palace was one of the main things they were excited to see but we never saw it, even though it says it on the side of the bus. After being on the bus for 2 hours we realised we had missed it, but the reason we missed it was because it drives down a road at the side of Buckingham Palace, so unless you know where it is (which you wouldn't because if you're on the bus you're probably here visiting) you are going to miss it everytime.

Awhile later the bus pulls up at the side of the road and the driver (who is the only member of staff on the bus) came upstaires and asks every passenger where they want to go, which we found slightly odd. He then said the bus can go either east or west from this point and basically took a vote from everyone on board as to which way he was going to go. We were on the side who lost the vote and we were told we would have to get off and wait for another bus to take us where we wanted to go. I asked the bus driver if it was quicker to walk to our destination and he basically spoke to me like I was an idiot. We got off the bus and then spoke to another Big Bus employee who didnt seem at all interested in having to sort out this mess. There was a bus further down the road and he said to make our way down to that bus and he would radio them and tell them to wait for us before pulling off. As you can probably guess we walked down and just as we were about to board the bus it pulled away. By now we were freezing cold and pretty fed up. Went back to the guy who still acted like he had better things to be doing than helping us out.

While waiting for the last bus of the day we were asking another Big Bus employee about which bus to take to get us back to our starting point and he was so rude aswell. Basically this company have zero manners and no idea on how to be professional at all. They see you as a tourist, not a human being. Use a different company, please!

I'm struggling to see the value of the Hop On, Hop Off concept especially when you pay 30 pounds for a 2 day ticket.

Positives: *Guides were fantastic, *Ground staff were exceptional apart from one (see below)

Negatives: *Spending 20 minutes at some stops when you are told that the bus will leave in 3 minutes, *Allowing more and more passengers on when the bus was already packed to the rafters and nobody wanted to go upstairs in the open because it was snowing, *Pickup from areas where a lot of people stayed but not dropping off in these areas (e.g. Lancaster Gate). Each time I used the bus it cost me 10 pound to get a cab back to the motel....defeat's the purpose.

All in all, I think you would be better off doing some planning on your own of what you want to see and getting a cab or using the public bus system (I didn't do this). It would be cheaper and a lot more effective.

****
There was one nasty incident that occurred today (Sun 24th March) at the Lancaster Gate pickup point. The staff member, who I bought my tickets from the day prior, pushed my wife, disabled son and myself out of the queue when the bus arrived so other people could get on before us. One of the groups that got on was 5 girls and it was blatantly obvious that he wanted to impress them. When I asked him if it was ok for us to get on now, he responded in a rude manner. I then asked him why did we have to be pushed aside, he answered that we can get on now. I did respond that he was more than pleasant the day before when he was taking my money...he just ignored me. I asked for his name and he said that it is on our ticket. I have his name but I won't mention it on here but I am giving it to the management of the Big Bus Tour Company.

This arrogant piece of work is in a service industry and his job is to give assistance to tourists....ALL TOURISTS and NOT JUST PRETTY GIRLS!!!

I mentioned this incident to another ground staff member further down the line and when I told him his name he was, let's say, not surprised.

Great tour on the hop on hop off bus. Unlike other reviewers I didn't have to wait for the bus at any of the attractions I hopped off to see. I ended up with the headphones tour and found the information provided to be very informative. I lived in London for quite a few years and this was the first time I took a tour. I would recommend to all who visit London to take a tour bus, see and hear about the sights then check them out at a later date.
I liked the idea of the ticket lasting 24 hours. I also found the price of the ticket to view all sights as a hop on hop off was a lot cheaper than the tube.

When I was in London almost ten years ago, I took the Original London hop-on, hop-off tour, and I remembered thinking that I wished I'd taken the Big Bus tour instead. I think it was because the tour I was on had recorded commentary and also spontaneously terminated in Soho where we were required to get off and wait for another bus. In any case, when planning a trip to London with my son this time around I decided to give the Big Bus a try. I definitely liked that they have both a main route with live commentary and then the smaller routes (with recorded commentary) that go to Knightsbridge/Kensington/Notting Hill and St. Pancras/etc. And their first stop was at Green Park, which was right by our hotel.

Starting months before our trip, I was emailing back and forth with their reps with all sorts of questions (I'm a total overplanning travel nerd and info junkie) and I found them to be very forthcoming and customer-friendly. Was hesitant to book in advance (which saves a few quid) just in case our flight was delayed or we had bad weather on that first day. But in the end I did book the day before online. They have an ongoing promotion where you buy a 24-hr ticket and get 48 hours. I really like that it's by 24-hr period and not calendar day, since we'd be starting off our tour in the afternoon after arriving in from airport and checking our bags at hotel.

We took the red/main loop first, with live commentary by Simon. We rode the entire loop without hopping off (I prefer to do it that way and then hop off on subsequent rides). Simon was very informative and amusing and it was definitely worth the money. That said, I think I actually prefer the sequence of the Original Tour more. We covered most of the same sights, but in a very different order. Of course, I took the Original Tour a decade ago so their route may have changed, but I recall them doing Buckingham Palace and Big Ben/Parliament early on, which really adds to the WOW factor when you've just arrived in London. They also approached them from a good angle with nice sightlines. The Big Bus Tour hit Big Ben in the middle of the tour (after Marble Arch/Oxford Street/Piccadilly Square/etc.) and didn't get to Buckingham Palace until the very end. And we only saw the side of it, whereas I recall getting at least a glimpse of the front on my prior visit (maybe that's a new security thing?). Also, the approach for many of the sights did not give great views but instead you saw them as you were driving away from them. It seemed each time we passed an Original Tour they were going in the opposite direction of us, so I think they still do cover the sights in the order I recall, with the views on the approach. S
o, while Big Bus seems to cover more ground, I wasn't as crazy as the pacing and order on the main route. Their blue route, which covers the western nabes of Knightsbridge, Kensington/SoKen, Notting Hill and Paddington, was really good and a must-do. (Not sure if the museum loop on Original is the same as Big Bus's blue route so worth asking if you're weighing out the options.)

If you come to London, do this!! We were really overwhelmed by all the pamphlets and advertising telling us what we "must see”. Somebody recommended this tour as the "one stop shop" solution and it really was. we started at Green Park and saw Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, Tower of London, St. Paul’s cathedral, wellington Arch, Marble Arch to name a few. The guy, Simon, doing the commentary was awesome, they he was really enthusiastic and had us in stitches.
You can get off the bus at whatever feature intrigues you the most and just pick up the next open top big bus!! In the summer this would have been even more awesome.

we took the big bus tour for a day.it showed us around london but we had to wait a long long time before we could hop on a second bus after getting down from one.that way we missed the palace walking tour as we sat waiting in the second bus and it slowly picked up passengers. heating inside the bus wasnt very good and we were quite cold even sitting on the lower deck.

1. At every stop someone (Big Bus) was trying to sell you tickets to the attractions.
2. Because tickets can be purchased at each stop and people usually have a 1000 questions, each stop takes for EVER making the trip a lot longer than necessary.
3. The recorded info is very limited...so mostly, one is listening to elevator music.
4. They tell you that the last bus will be at 4:30pm from a certain place and that buses come every 15 minutes. We waited at our stop from 3:45pm (it got cold and dark) but the bus showed up at 4:20 pm at which point the bus driver informed us that he could not bring us to the station with the last bus in time (4 stops away) and instead, basically dropped a bus full of people in the rain at a train station.
Not sure how the other tour buses are in London, but compared to the one in Paris, this was terrible.
On a Positive note: they have lots of stops and they provide you with free ponchos when it rains.

Frankly shocked at how bad this was. BTW, I enjoyed a similar tour in Barcelona. The problems are the following: We were staying in Kensington. It takes easily 1 1/2 hours to get to the attractions in downtown London. Way too much time is chewed up simply getting to where you want to go. At times you must change buses due to "circulation" whatever that means. Also, the buses stop around 4 30 in winter. If your family, like ours, does not get moving early in the AM, you will have very little time to make use of the bus. For example, if you stay at the British Musuem, or the Tower of London, until closing, no more bus when you get out. Also, there is no live tour guide until you get to Convent Garden-another problem. The bus is very expensive for such limited hours. However, the boat ride on the Thames was good. I strongly recommend taking the Underground to get around.

We only had one day to see London, so we opted for the The Big Bus Tour that was recommended by our hotel staff. It was a nice tour. Look for the "red" bus line that includes a live tour guide. We were there on a cold day, we had to go to the lower level for the several stops.

The tour route was bit long... It would be nice if they had a couple of routes so that we could have opted for a shorter trip. Also, it was a bit too expensive.

On our last day in London we went with Big Bus Tours around Kensington Palace up to Baker Street and then over to the London Eye. It was nice to have the hop on hop off option and have the freedom to do it, but they don't tell you is if you get off at Hyde Park and then want to go to Baker street on the Blue Line you have to wait until the proper bus is coming (3 buses later about 25 minute wait). When you look at the map they give you it seems that all buses follow that route, not so. It also took forever to get thru traffic around Oxford, Regent and Trafalger Square. This is not a knock againest the Company as much of it is out of their control, but we found the Tube was the quickest most effcient way around London. This company had lots of buses and the staff at stops and on the buses were great, very helpful. I don't think we would pick this mode of transport next time in London.

We recently visited London and whilst we enjoyed the big bus tour, we actually found the combination of the London Pass and the Oyster Card (for use on the tube & buses) of far better value. The buses often get caught in traffic and we actually jumped off one of ours as it was quicker to walk. A plus of the tour is that you can pre-purchase tickets to other attractions and avoid queues but most of these offer on-line booking anyway. With the tour you also get a river cruise and walking tour but you also get this as part of the London Pass which also gets you into many London attractions as part of the pass including London tower, London bridge and many other popular places to visit. The Oyster card allows you to navigate through the city via the tube with very little difficulty.

We booked the bus tour as they were very helpful on phone? Getting round London with a 2 year old is hard work, the bus tour was great, the tour guides were fantastic. The Scottish girl needs a bonus. How she sounds so enthusiastic from 10 am till 6 pm is beyond me!

the boat trip is also free and a great way to see the city, all the drivers are friendly although the busses can get very busy they always made sure there was space for a buggy.

I would recommend for those with pushchairs, the bus stops everywhere you need it to.

SIMPLE....EASY......INFORMATIVE!

A day in London with the kids and so we booked Big Bus tickets so that we got to see most of the attractions and could hop on hop off when we chose. We had a fabulous guide on the Red tour, he was very amusing and very knowledgable and we also enjoyed the river cruise.

But then we had to get the Blue route so that we could get to the Science museum. On coming out (and wanting to get back to Hamleys) we waited half an hour for the bus which then takes a long (and to be honest, failry boring) route, via Notting Hill, Lanacaster Gate. It was incredibly slow and seemed to do pointless loops.Then the driver parked up, turned the engine off and disappeared for 10 minutes!! Then we went round Marble Arch twice and pulled up again. Finally, at the Wax Works we were rather rudely told to get off, as this bus was terminating and to catch "that bus over there" which would leave in about 10 minutes. By now, totally fed up, we jumped in a taxi and got to Hamleys just before it closed. After a great day, it just left a bad feeling.

I will say- It is good value for money, entertaining in the most and a great way to see the sights. BUT in hindsight, we should have come out of the museum and got a taxi back to the shops from there.

Stick with the RED route.

My daughter and I started out on a Big Bus (recorded) tour on our first day in England. That first bus was just ok. We got off at Piccadilly Circus to eat lunch and afterwards got on another Big Bus. I'll be eternally grateful that we switched buses. The second time around we had a live tour guide, Ashley Wilson, who, in addition to being a font of information is also a wonderful story teller. One of the stories she told was on herself: she had been selected to sing for the Queen as part of a Scottish delegation to England (She is from Glasgow). When she had sung, Queen Elizabeth came up to her and told her she had a lovely voice.

Ashley told us about the experience:

"Half of my brain was saying, 'Ashley, the Queen of England is speaking to you. Ashley the Queen of England is speaking to you. Ashley, the Queen of England is speaking to you.'
