The other half of my brain was saying, 'Ashley, when the Queen of England speaks to you, you have to say something back.' So I racked my brains and said, 'Thank you so very much, Your Majesty. And may I just say that I love your purse?"

That tour was so good that, though we had planned to get off the Big Bus at the Tower of London, we stayed on until the very end (which was also the final run of the day).

Of course I can't say whether the other tour guides are as good, but you should make sure to get on a bus with a live tour guide in any case. And if you can find out which one Ashley Wilson is on, take that!

When in London recently my mother and i only had 2 days to be able to see everything we could. Big Bus Tours was the solution to our problem. The choice of tours and the addition of the free river cruise ticket meant that in just 2 days we were able to see and visit all of the places we wanted to and both the taped audio and live guided tour information was great. I truely suggest looking this company up if your visiting London.

We bought our passes in advance online for specific dates so we got a fair price for them. What they don't tell you is that 48 hours (which we bought), really doesn't mean that. What they should say is 2 days. So if you don't start till 2 pm. on the first day, that time till about 6 when they quit running is all you get (unless you pay more to upgrade it). We were also surprised how early it would quit running. Be aware of that so you don't get stranded somewhere like we did. Some of the buses, the audio didn't work well. If it rains, everyone tries to crowd in any covered areas, and it was hot in the lower portion of the bus. We also got struck in a traffic jam (which I understand is not their fault), but we lost so much touring time just sitting in the bus like that. Instead of giving you general London info in between sites, there was just music. Buses didn't seem to be as frequent as the Original Sightseeing Tours. We waited 1/2 hour a couple of times for Big Bus and their stops don't seem to be as near good locations as some of the other tour buses. Next time I visit London, I plan to figure out which places we want to visit and just take the Tube directly to them. It's much more efficient to tour that way.

The red tour, which has live commentary, was quite good - it was a good way to get my bearings in London and see the sights relatively quickly. It seemed to stop at all the places a tourists would need. The tour guides were friendly and very entertaining.

I didn't enjoy the blue tour, which provides an audio tour. I only took it because it goes around Hyde Park and through areas I didn't think I'd otherwise have a chance to see while in London. A Big Bus employee provided me with incorrect information on where to pick up this portion of the blue tour, so I ended up wasting time to get back to the original stop. Then, worst of all, the audio guide is just boring. Then we had a long wait and then kicked off the bus to transfer onto a different, more crowded bus. I ended up getting off early and walking so I could just leave and have a more interesting time in London.

We really enjoyed the Big Bus tour. We were able to make a loop of the city in about two hours, and then go back and spend more time at the destinations that interested us. We only had one full day to do Lindon, and this was a great choice.

Went on a Big Bus Tour of London.On a Red bus with a spoken human guide.Blue bus is much cheaper(about half price) as it only has the recorded headphone guides.
We had 2 guides on our trip,thesecond one was much better as he had a good sense of humour,the first one much to serious.
Very good to use in London as its a cheap way of visiting lots of sights in 24 hours.

We were visiting London for just 4 nights during the Olympics and were sure we would not have proper time to see the city, aside from the games we had tickets for. We booked a 2-day Big Bus pass and are so glad we did. We enjoyed the tour with the recorded commentary and used the bus to get the lay of the land, see the sights and get from place to place. There were plenty of stops in great locations. We highly recommend and would do this again, in London and in other cities.

My 7 year old and I travelled around with the Big Bus on 2 different routes, as well as the Thames river cruise. I highly recommend this for a first time visit to London! We were able to see so many sights and take lots of fantastic photos. By purchasing a ticket, you can also ride the 2nd day no charge.
There's so much to see and do in London that we also rode the Big Bus the next day to visit the places we couldn't see on our first day. The Big Bus stops at major tourist attractions and shopping districts. It's a good way to get around without having to hail a cab. I didn't want to drive in the city given that I'm used to driving with the steering wheel on the left side of the vehicle and I've heard too many horror stories about drivers not used to driving with the steering wheel on the right side of the vehicle. The Big Bus was a terrific option to see the city. We went before the Olympics so it was wonderful to see the city so dressed up for the big event. You can hop off at any stop you like, then hop on when the next available bus arrives. Had to wait 30 minutes at one stop, but that was ok b/c my son and I just popped into a little souvenir shop. Normally it's a 15 to 20 minute wait for the next bus. We definitely hopped off at the Trafalgar Square stop so we could pop into the National Gallery. My son wanted to see the Tower of London, so we hopped off there too. I wanted to take him to see the waxworks museum (there's a specific hop off to see Madam Tussaud's) but the lines went around the corner so we skipped it. The boat cruise is fun. Be sure to journey down the Thames. The guides were entertaining. The route with the pre-recorded information was ok. My son enjoyed listening to it more than I did. I was more interested in taking photos while listening to the audio recordings. The audio recordings are available in several languages so hopefully your mother tongue will be one of them.

I was not on the original red bus but the more burgubdy color bus. The tour was excellent . There are two distinctly different tours plus a free river cruise which we accessed at the London Eye but it is also accessible at the Towr of London. The buses were clean and so was the boat, The headphones were understandable which is nt the case in many cities and the busse do line up easily for transfering. Cities like Prague need to learn from these folks how to make a tourist bus work.

Originally we wanted to travel on HOHO bus with The Original Tour but the Indian Sales Reps at a souvenir shop (Owner of this shop called himself "Angel" Gabriel) at Trafalgar Square (BBT Stop 11) persisted in selling us tickets for the Big Bus Tour (BBT). Gabriel claimed that for £29 (£3 more than The Original Bus Tour company of £26), we will get a 48 hours tickets. Guess what? The 2 tickets that we bought £58 turned out to be just a 24 hours tickets.
The BBT company should seriously investigate this matter as this tantamount to fraudulent advertising & indeed is deceitful.
Personally, I would advise TRAVELERS to avoid these Sales Reps. WHY? Because you are NOT getting what you have been promised.... Just a bunch of lies!

Two very UNHAPPY International Travelers

I had friends visiting for two days and they wanted to see London. We took the Big Bus Tour and had a great time! It was very convenient to buy the bus tickets online as well as for the attractions you want to visit such as the Tower or London.. Nice not standing in line! The Driver we had was very friendly and the guide was quite good. I like that they point out the unusual as well as the obvious. The only draw back is when you get a poor guide ~ just hop off and get the next bus. Problem solved! Every time we have guests visit, Big Bus Tours is the one use.

After reading reviews before leaving for London I had decided not to do hoho bus but when we got there our Trafalgar tour director suggested we do it. So paid 39 pond each for 2 day pass but found (as other reviewers had said) that the time it takes to get round on the hoho bus wastes valuable time if you have only a few days in London. The underground is a far faster way to see more of London than the hohobuses. We had to wait over 20 minutes for 1 bus and to get to Kensington Palace from the Tower took over an hour! Note that in 1 day we only got to see The Tower of London and Kensington Palace.- 4hrs at the tower and 2 hrs at The Palace- we left our hotel at 8.30am and finished looking at the Palace around 5pm - The Tower took 4 hrs and the Palace 2hrs - the rest was spent on the hoho bus. If you only have a few days in London I suggest you just use the underground and buses - they are extremely easy to use just get an oyster card when you arrive.

Just returned from five days in London; spent as a birthday gift for my 16 year old granddaughter.

I left her to choose what she wanted to see but was at a loss to know how we could cover so much in just five days. The solution was a day pass on the Big Red Bus. This double decker had live commentary and took us from one end of the city to the other. Many of the stops were at locations she had selected so that we got on/off as needed and then continued. It was the perfect answer and meant there was no need to tackle the underground or spend lots of extra money on taxis. Great solution to what I though would be a problem.

If you have a whole day, or 2, to take this tour, you will enjoy it. But don't think you can accomplish much else. This tour shows lots of sites, but is overpriced because of the extreme congestion in the city. We spent 3 hours on the bus/boat and saw maybe 20% of the whole itinerary. They have a 2-for-1 offer, and that's because it will take you 2 whole days to see it. Busses do not come every 15 min so even if you hop on and hop off, you will wait longer than you hoped.

Personnel and tour guides were great and we enjoyed the double decker, live commentary. We just hadn't planned on spending the entire day on a bus.

This was recommended to us as the best bus tour of London. Hopefully that is not the case.
On our first go round we had two different tour guides - one was average, or less than average and the second was very good. We got on the bus later in the day hoping to finish the tour and get back to our hotel. The bus suddenly stopped and said it was not going on. We had to ask the driver what to do next and it was only then that he told us we had to walk up the street to find another Big Bus Representative and find out what to do there. After a while we, and the other passengers found him and 10 minutes later we were on another bus. After two or three stops, the bus stopped completely again and, half an our later decided to go on its way. Finally, after all these stops and starts we got so fed up we got off at Trafalgar Square and walked the rest of the way back.

Me my mum and sister visit london often and we do the bus tour most times we are in the city! I love it! For the 1st time we decided to do 1 of the walking tours that are included in the price. We decided on the ghost tour which was fantastic! Our guide Jessie was very entertaining and made our tour very enjoyable.
People who are complaining about being stuck in traffic should realise that they are in a busy capital city and that should be expected!
Each of the bus company workers that we met were very helpful! I will continue to travel this way every time I visit london because its the best way 2 c all the beautiful sites the capital has 2 offer.

The Big Bus Tour is a great way to see all of the big attractions in London in a short time. If you are an English speaker, I highly recommend the bus with the live commentator rather than the headphones. The live commentator is funny and can point our all sorts of things that come up along the way. If your bus comes and it is the headphone bus, wait for the next one, it's worth it. The Big Bus is a 'hop-on' and 'hop-off' sort of thing where you can either stay on for about three hours and see everything and then decide where to go in the future or you can just 'hop-off' if something appeals to you. The major attractions are all there--London Tower, the shopping district, museums, the works. Once you complete the tour, you will have a good base of knowledge about London to draw from. The river cruise is included in the ticket and I highly recommend getting off for that. Same thing--the commentator is hilarious and makes the ride fun and informative. Overall, good for all ages, rain or shine and if you are a first-timer, I cannot think of a better way to learn about and to see London.

We chose the Big Bus Tour because we could get the tickets from our Concierge at our hotel charge them to our room and for the price of a 24 hour ticket (29 pounds) we got a 48 hour ticket. A good deal.....when we got on the bus we found the 48 hour ticket was 35 pounds. Just know that what you're getting at the hotel is a voucher...you need to exchange it for an actual ticket at the bus stop.

Very pricey compared to other 'tours' done in other countries but still worth doing.
It helps with the layout of a new city and also aids in prioritising attractions and buildings that you may wish (or not) to re-visit. You also get to see places that perhaps were unknown to you or not on your list to visit. Being able to choose between a 24 hour or 48 hour ticket is great. If you intend to hop on/hop off a lot, then go for the 48 hour ticket. The Thames River Cruise stretch was fantastic. Lovely to be able to see the city from a different perspective. The boat captain was hilarious with his information as we passed various landmarks. Very "educational"; learnt a lot of fascinating tid bits from the commentary. However, the headphones provided were a bit dodgy and easily broken. If it starts to rain, free ponchos are provided.
Some of the busier streets became a bit tedious due to traffic gridlock and this 'ate' into the ticket time. But it is a big busy city so has to be expected at times.
Interesting and enjoyable.

We enjoy bus tours as a way to get a quick dose of the sights and smells of a city. Big Bus in London was no exception - credit the well-designed route for that. Our experience was marred because their Blue Line buses were so few and far between. Several of the principal competitor's would pass while we were waiting, then the next Big Bus was often stuffed to the gills or going off duty. We also had one of the worst customer service experiences ever with one of their 'sidewalk superintendents' - the driver later apologized profusely for it. An email to their customer relations address went unanswered - so busy they likely don't care. Also be advised: we stopped at their "welcome center" only to discover it doesn't have toilets. (The agent suggested a walk to Vic Station or a restaurant.) Next time, wherever we are, we'll try a different bus operator, and be sure to start early in the day. Good luck with the Olympics, London!

Big Bus Tours are a great introduction to London. I had expected more from their live guide tours (having really enjoyed similar ones in other cities) but the live guide was rather disappointingly lackluster. I switched to the recorded tour,though, and found it far more enjoyable and informational! I really appreciated the option of buying the ticket online, and being able to get a 48-hour ticket in addition to the 24-hour one. Well worth it!

This has to be one of the first things you do on a visit to London. The tour guides on the bus are informative and will also answer any queries. It must be said that good weather will make the tour moreg enjoyable but as long as you dress for the weather you will still enjoy it. The folks sellingthe tickets at the stops will also sell you tickets for most of the main attractions and are all very freindly and helpfull. The river and walking tours are well worth taking advantge of and my wife and i were well impressed with the changing of the gaurd and the commentry given by a retired teacher working for Big Bus. All in all this is a must for the visitor to London...you wont regret it!

James & Trish

This was our second visit to london and our second bus tour. Ticket sellers were very friendly and gave a lot of information without being pushy. There weren't any seats left upstairs but the tour guide Ashley kept calling down to let us know when places became available. Her information was really interesting and so entertaining. Now I understood why people were reluctant to get off. We made it upstairs and Ashley catered for the different nationalities. There was a large group of Americans on board with several young girls. Ashley was really friendly but always reminded them to sit down and pay attention to safety. She had a lovely manner and a terrific sense of humour. Thanks for making our day. From fellow Glasgow punters.

We toured London on a beautiful but chilly day in March and saw all the major sites. We always found space at the top of the bus in the front where you get an unobstructed view while being protected from the wind. The experience would not have been as good if the bus had been crowded and we had to sit in the lower level.
There was enough buses that hopping back on was not an issue. Our longest wait was 10-15 min at the end of the day.
The drivers were friendly and the driving was not a concern.
The guides explaining the sites on the his microphone was that great. I tuned him out pretty much immediately, but the sounds was not so loud that it was not an issue. The maps they give were good enough to figure out where we were.
The kids really enjoyed it.

I had one day in London at the end of a business trip, since I was by myself and have never before visited London the Big Bus tour was the perfect way to spend the day. Fortunately I had a beautiful, sunny day on the open air, top deck! I started at Paddington Station at 10:00 a.m., got off at the Tower of London, where I picked up the Riverboat cruise, walked through St James Park, viewed Buckingham Palace, got back on the blue line, got off at Harrods. By this time it was about 6 p.m. I had missed the last Big Bus so I took the tube back to my hotel. It was a great day. I think in the summer the busses run a little later in the day.

Although ive been to london many times, this was the first time doing this open top bus tour.

I thoroughly recommend it - you get to see it all and you notice so much more of the buildings etc than I'd every noticed before. Very informative live guides on the red tour.

My Husband and i pre-booked the bus tour before travelling to London so saved a few pennies online. It was good to see you could combine tickets with other attractions and we ended up getting Madame Tussauds and the London Eye aswell all before we left Scotland. We also got lucky they had a buy one day get another free which worked great for us since we were staying for three days.
The stops are easy to locate and the guys waiting at the stops are funny and informative and always happy to help with any recommendations and helping you beat the queues. We went on the red tour for the live guide and weren't disappointed. The guy was hilarious with his own unique way of informing you on all the history of the city and alerting the bus driver when you wanted off which being pregnant was very helpful rather than trying to get down the stairs whilst the bus was moving. After visiting another attraction we were happy to find ourselves back on his bus later on in the day i just wish i could remember his name to give him a special mention. We have done bus tours in other cities but definately found this one to be the most entertaining. We hop'd off and on all over the city and loved the experience over the two days we used the bus.

Great way to see the city, especially if you've never been and get the lay of the land. The tour goes past most of the major tourist sites- the London Eye, Big Ben, Trafalgar Square, over the Tower Bridge, past the Tower of London; and all with an actual guide if you get red route bus.
Bundle up if you're taking the tour in winter, it got a little chilly up top but well worth it!

Talk about a nightmare....you're better off just using the Tube! First of all, there are thousands upon thousands of bus spots in london so finding where they spot is like looking for a needle in a haystack. Second, they are NEVER on time. (And keep in mind that we were their off peak season) We waited not once but three times for a bus more than 40 minutes. However, I did see their competitor the "original bus tour' drive by several times while we waited in the rain. Really...just use the TUBE and forget the BIG BUS BUST.

Spent one day using Big Bus Tours, and enjoyed every minute of it! An excellent way to see the city, with many stops to get on and off at. They also include free walking tours as well, which was superb, as one was a Harry Potter movie location tour, and being a mad fan made the trip more enjoyable. A great mode of transport, and you can choose between having an english speaking guide, or having a commentary in several different languages on a different bus. Would recommend to anyone who may only have a short trip, and would like to see all the popular sites of London.

This is a great way to get a "lay of the land" in London. You can see that many attractions are very close together and decide where you'd like to start.

I did the tour twice - once with a friend and then with my partner when he arrived a week later.

I did the Beatles Walking Tour one afternoon. Our guide Phil was incredible - very knowledgable and absolutely enthusiastic and fun. It was a great time and he supplemented the tour with YouTube footage and photographs.

I caught the Bus at Westminter for both tours. I recommend getting off at the Tower of London and take the ferry back to the Houses of Parliament. It was great to see the skyline from the River Thames. I recommend taking a tour with a live guide as opposed to just the audio tour. All of the guides I experienced were friendly and knowledgable, but some were better than others. We had a younger guide named something like Barclay and he was great.

Grab a complimentary plastic bag type poncho in case it rains later (which is pretty much a certainty in London if you stay for a few days).

The staff was very helpful and friendly and you can purchase tickets to many attractions without having to stand in line for many of them. Don't forget to tip the drivers and staff. They were great.

There are two major hop on/hop off bus companies operating in London. One is the Original Tour which we used with no problem. The other was the Big Bus Tour which was less than adequate. The Big Bus Tour has fewer buses than the Original Tour but the problem we had was getting them to stop for us. We were waiting at a stop to which we were directed by employees of the Big Bus Tour for one of their blue buses. When it finally came down the street we prepared to board, but the bus did not stop and just kept going. We returned to their ticket seller and explained what happened. He said to wait and the next one would definitely stop. We waited, the next bus came and it too passed us by. One of their red buses stopped and when we started to explain our situation, he shut the bus door in our faces and left. We finally took a cab to our destination. I don't know if this has happened to others, but for us, the Big Bus Tour in any city is no longer an option. Stick with the Original Tour.

While on our 'grand tour' of Europe and the UK we went on Hop on Hop off bus tours in every city we could and enjoyed it everytime. But by far the best was Big Bus Tours in London. All of their staff were amazingly friendly and very helpful, whether we were asking their staff for info on the street at a stop, or on bus, they did everything they could to help and to enhance our visit to London. The tour guides were wonderfully entertaining and full of the most amazing and amusing information about their city, they gave us the opportunity to feel very involved in the city. The bus stops were well situated giving us easy access to everywhere we wanted to visit. We loved Big Bus London and are saving up as we would love to go back and do the whole trip again with them.

Hop on hop off which takes you to a number of attractions. Quite a variety of driving skills (combating some horrific traffic) and very mixed guides. One guide was absolutely brilliant but several were pedestrian. The green route was a complete waste of time it took forever (pulled over a 10 minute stop for no apparent reason), i would avoid. But the other lines were pretty good and ran reasonably frequently so easy to hop on and off on. Although a couple of times they did not stick to the route. Good value if you are only in London for a short time and want to see major sights quickly. Also included a Thames Cruise and a few alternative themed walks. We took the Harry Potter walk which kids, parents and grandparents in our group all enjoyed and not too strenuous.

We visited the kiosk at Marble Arch to enquire about the Big Bus Tour, (routes, operating times etc.,). After being reassured by the seller that the buses operated at 10 / 15 minute intervals, and that services didn't finish until 8 pm, we purchased four x 24 hour tickets.

We boarded a Big Bus (Red Tour) and took in the sights from Marble Arch to Westminster, where we took the (included in price) River Cruise. We then rejoined the Bus Tour at the Embankment.

Our plan was to get the Big Bus from Marble Arch at 6pm, and Hop Off at Piccadilly Circus, as we had theatre tickets for a show in Shaftsbury Avenue at 7.30 pm. (we had already "timed" the journey earlier in the day - 30 minutes) - which would give us plenty of time......... we thought.

The Guide at the stop told us we would need a Red Route bus... and we stood at the stop as quite a few Blue buses pulled in and departed, and we saw a few Red route (empty) buses go whizzing by...

By 6.45 people were getting very annoyed and restless, and the Guide was continually getting on her walkie talkie trying to find a bus to pick us all up.
(She had said that the Red buses didn't operate after 6.30.. which is not what we had been told earlier in the day). While at the stop, there were also a number of rain downpours to contend with (when we SHOULD have been on the bus, or even at the theatre)!.

A bus eventualy arrived at 6.50pm, and by the time the driver/commentator had finished chatting, it was 6.55pm before it left Marble Arch.

Suffice to say, that despite our planning to be at the theatre in good time, we ended up missing the beginning of the show because of the unreliable service.

For 27 pounds per person we got into a bus that was full at the top and barely managed to get two seats downstairs. The bus waited for about 30 minutes at Madame Toussaud's. Nearly empty public transportation double deckers passed by. I don't think that the recorded commentaries and the river trip make up for the big price of the ride. Basically there were people standing up that couldn't even use the headphones because they had no seats available. After about a third of the stops some people got out and we managed to get on the top and take some pictures. With the service operating only till 6 PM there is not enough time for properly visiting more than two big attractions. The good thing is that you can extend your ticket to one more day by paying only 5 pounds more. Maybe there was a problem with the service that day, because two years ago their buses were emptier and the ride a bit faster. I would recommend using the public transportation and buying a river cruise separately. London is expensive enough not to waste 27 pounds on a bus ticket.

We had taken the Big Bus Tour from Marble Arch, to Tower Hill, then got on the ferry back to Westminister which worked out great. We then didn't wish to do the whole circuit again and wanted to find the stop that took us to Buckingham Palace. We went and asked your employee at Stop 13 for directions to this stop. He was most unhelpful and very patronising. His manner was disgusting and bordered on harrassment. He was rude, asking us irrelevant questions, when all we wanted to know was the location of the Buckingham Palace stop. We left swiftly and ended up following the map ourselves finding the stop which we could have done in the first place. We just thought we'd ask one of your "friendly" staff (as quoted on the website) to save a bit of time. This was a big mistake. We will certainly think twice about using Big Bus Tours again and recommending your company to friends.

We prebooked tickets for this tour on their website as we knew we wanted to use it and the specfic date of visit. So it cost £21 each per adult. I had done research previous to arival so knew we could get the blue route from paddington and we arrived there and found exit 1 and the bus stop is in the road opposite to the left. It helped that the bus was just pulling up so we jumped straight on and the very helpful guide told me that we needed to get off at marble arch to change to the red route in order to continue the tour. This was very easy and we had approx a 10 min wait there for the next bus. We easily got seats upstairs ( prob varies on time of day) and rode to aldwych ( where we were staying). The 2 friends I was with had never really been to London so it was important that we saw the sights in as little time and effort as possible. This hit the nail on the head. Good information given all the way but not dull. They announce number of each stop and give you plenty of time to get on and off. It was spitting with rain and they handed out free rain capes to all up top. Good maps on the bus so pick them up as they are free and helpful when walking about.
In the morning we continued the tour from the same bus stop and on to the London Bridge experience ( stops outside) so again taking in more sights on the way. We then go back on at same bus stop and carried on till we had almost ( bar 2 stops thru victoria) completed the circuit and got off at Buck Palace and did the rest of what we wanted to see by foot) So we saw every sight that was felt was important for us and travelled for the 24 hr period (not over night) around the city. It was alot more pleasurable for a nice change to up and down hot and dirty tubes all day and we saw more this way. I don't think I would do again purely beaause I saw the sights and next time I would go back to the tube and just go to the places I want to go to.
A good value option if you do our research before hand.

To make a long story short; The tour is great!
I used the Big Bus company to travel around London (which is perfect, since it takes you to every place you want to visit).
But there were two live guides who I want to thank;
Robin and Benedict. Robin is a great entertainer who knows a lot about London and Benedict is a very young guide who managed to get the whole bus cheering! When I saw the next day that Benedict was guiding again one one of the busses, I just bought a new ticket...and I just did the full tour once again!

We have been to London before and taken a full day tour with other companies. We had friends suggest the Hop on Hop off bus tour and so we tried it. It was a disaster from the moment we started. The buses were consistently late, the operators were not helpful, the buses were overcrowded and therefore uncomfortable. And when you are told "On your right you will see the Houses of Parliament" and all you can see are the thighs of the people standing in the aisles, you know you have picked the wrong tour. We waited over 45 minutes for buses and the employees never offered an explanation or information sharing. We complained and did receive a refund.

This bus claims to be hop-on and hop-off. However, once we hopped off it was impossible to get back on. No buses would come by. The company blamed all sorts of things including traffic, crime events, etc... However we saw PLENTY of The Original Tour Buses go by. My suggestion, if you want a reliable tour bus book on The Original Bus Company, do NOT book the Big Bus Company.

We were only in London for 2 full days and wanted to see as much as possible without worrying about getting lost or missing what was going on outside on the streets while we were down in the underground. We stayed at Rubens at the Palace and the Big Bus office was just down the street. We stopped in and bought out tickets - which were good for 48 hours since we were there in February. It was perfect for us. Our hotel room wasn't going to be ready for at least an hour, so we jumped on a "red sticker" bus and did a tour of the entire loop that the bus tour does. The next morning we walked a bit and ended up catching a bus at the London Eye - we also purchased tickets to the Tower of London and Tower Bridge attraction from the Big Bus representative waiting at the stop. We rode the bus to St. Pauls Cathedral and got off (our hotel gave us tickets for this) and after we went to the cathedral, we decided to walk to the Tower of London. Once we were done with the Tower Bridge, we hopped back on a bus and road it back to our hotel. We really enjoyed the guided tour - the tour guide was funny and very nice. We thought all the representatives that we worked with at different stops were friendly and knowledgable as well. We would recommend it and would totally do it again!

The staff who work for this company must be the rude staff ever. I have been on a similar bus tour in Ireland and the staff were funny amusing and would do anything to help. On the Big Bus Tour in London the staff were shouted at numerous customers as they were not doing what they were told. Also the driver called some of the people upstairs Stupid Tourists. The tour guide put on a very good "happy guide" impression for most of the trip until he also shouted at one customer for daring to ask which stop to get off at for Harrods. If you do want to do an open bus tour I would advise to use another company

We took the Big Bus Tour Hop on and off tour in London to get oriented to the city and to learn more about the monuments while at it. Our main goal was to ensure we had a live guided tour (not a recorded one) and to take the 9 am bus so that we could make it to Buckingham Palace in time for the changing of the guard. When we purchased the 25 GBP tickets from the vendor, he assured us that most of their buses were guided - hence our greater surprise when we found the first bus we got on was recorded only and to get a guided tour, we had to jump off and wait at least 15 minutes for one with a guide. When we did get one, he was great - Phill Harris - was one of the few redeeming qualities of the tour. He was engaging and provided off-the-cuff information about the attractions which we all appreciated. Since we were delayed in getting a guide, we had to jump off of the tour and take the tube back to Victoria to try to catch the changing of the guard. Not that big of a deal. Later in the day, after taking some side trips here and there, we decided to jump back on the bus and finish the tour. This time, ironically, we wanted a blue tour (unguided) as it covers a greater area including much of Hyde Park. When we bought the tickets, we were told that buses run every 20 minutes so we were very surprised to find ourselves waiting 45 minutes and watching, literally, 10 Original Bus tours pass us before any kind of Big Bus tour went by. When it did, it was packed to the brim and there was no seating because they just seriously do not operate enough buses. Instead of wrangling a seat and being frustrated, we decided instead to jump on the included river cruise with City Cruises and found it to be a nice diversion. We considered jumping back on the Bus but decided to avoid the frustration and took the tube instead. Perhaps the Original Bus tour is better - it sure seemed like they ran a better operation -- so maybe check that out instead.

I've done the hop on/off bus tours in other cities so I had a benchmark. It wasn't just my experience but also the experience of others on the same tour. Poorly organized, signage lacking, headsets that simply didn't work, time between buses is not as advertised. Toward the end of the day, about 10 of us were told to disembark and get the next bus as our bus was done for the day. Waited for 35 minutes and ended up taking a taxi. Others were simply stuck due to language barriers (no tube for them) and a few members of the group simply started walking as they were close enough to their final destination. There were only a few things I wanted to see and ended up using the tube to get to the sights I wanted. I took the hop on/off bus to be able to hear the commentary and learn more, but alas, the only thing I learned was that this was not a worthwhile experience.

We had arrived from Paris and used the Big Bus there, with great results, so were really looking forward to our outing, expecting the same in London, but were very disappointed. We bought our tickets, were then directed to a stop, only to be told we then had to redeem the vouchers for tickets, so missed that bus, and then waited around 30 minutes for another. The buses definitely don't come as often as they say, and if you get off in the wrong place, or onto the wrong bus, you'll spend hours going in the one direction. At one point, the tour company couldn't follow the designated route because of the football crowds (surely they should have known about it!) so we just went around with no commentary, and consequently had no idea where we were. We gave up in the end, and figured out the Underground for ourselves, or just walked!!!

People who have had a bad experience with something are more likely to want to share their displeasure with others, than a person who has had a good experience is likely to make an effort to share their pleasure with others. Those who are satisfied are likely to just go on about their business, whereas those who are not satisfied seek a soapbox to complain. These observations were instigated by the fact that I was reluctant to go on either of the two London bus tours, given the many negative reviews for both of them on this web site. Well, I bit the bullet, paid my 25 pounds (or "pound" as the Brits say) and took the Big Bus Company Red Tour today. And man oh man, was I satisfied. I had a great experience. The bus hit all the most important tourist destinations, and most importantly, the tour guide was excellent (for the record, he was Alan or Allen) -- he was informative, had a great personality, and was genuinely humorous. I thoroughly enjoyed the tour, and would heartily recommend it to anybody. It was well worth my 25 pounds (or "pound").

The Big Bus tour was a pretty good investment for our trip. At first, the cost was 25 Pounds per person and seemed a little expensive. Considering we were able to get on three different bus routes the company had to offer across the city and a boat ride, I think it was a good route for my three friends and I. We got to see nearly every landmark in the city within a matter of two hours - this was while staying on the bus and not getting off. We could have gotten off at various locations but we really enjoyed our first tour guide. He did a great job and was very knowledgeable. My friends and I had full intentions of just riding the bus around the first go round but due to traffic we decided to get off to take the ferry instead.

After we got back on another bus, the tour guy never lived up to our first. All in all, it was a good tour and I would considering doing it again if I go back to London.

I brought my visitors on the big bus tour thinking it would be great for children. Well, they made us get on and off at several stops with much waiting time between buses. We had 5 children with us who were not happy. At Hyde Park, we were told to get off the bus, get in a queue and then they tried to sell us other tickets to tourist attractions. We waited quite a while for the bus with the live tour guide. When it came, it was a stampede to get on the bus with much pushing and shoving. It was difficult to keep track of five children. The tour guide was okay although overall I did not feel like I learned much about London because of this tour. Also, at some of the stops, the ticket sellers would get on the bus and complain to the driver about other ticket sellers. At one point I complained as she was using many four letter words in front of my three and six year old!

The best part about paying for this ticket was the boat tour. We did have a little trouble finding where the boat left from but once we did, it was no problem. The "tour guide" on the boat was the best, very animated and interesting. The kids enjoyed this the most.

Hey folks, we are American Expats living in London and we take all our visitors on the Big Red Bus Tour - I've done it MANY times. We usually start at the Victoria Station Location. No particular reason, just like that starting point. If you speak English, make sure you get on a LIVE GUIDED tour. The live guides are very good. If you have to listen through headphones - you will be dissappointed - just skip the tour if you have to do headphones. I recommend that you do the whole tour route - the main line that goes by Buckingham, St Pauls, Tower of London. Later you go explore any interesting site separately using the Tube to move around. The top of the bus gives you a great feel of the city and you can see a little of it all while at the same time hearing some of the local history.

We were in London in Sept. 2007 and booked a tour with the Big Bus Company. We experienced 3 tour guides, one of whom was excellent, one was average, and the other obviously hated her job. So, you may get a mixed bag with this tour. We also had to wait longer at stops for the Big Bus while there seemed to be many more of the Original Tour buses stopping for their passengers

While it doesn't hit the lesser known attractions, on my first trip to London in 2005 I found the Big Bus to be a very good cure for jet lag as the bus does all the thinking for you and is entertaining enough to keep someone awake.

The best part that I found was that it's a full day's worth of activities for a relatively (20 pounds or so) small price. Included in the deal I took a ghost walk with a very entertaining guide. The only disappointment with this was that it was a pub tour and we only stopped in one (overcrowded) pub and were rushed out rather quickly. Still the ghost stories were fun, informative, and slightly (just enough) scary.

The tour was small so there was a lot of one-on-one interaction and this particular guide gave tips for "London survival."

This service is not without its flaws, however. The bus drivers sometimes think they're funnier than they are and a lot of the time is spent hawking the tickets they have for attractions (especially the London Dungeon) and giving intro announcements. But I guess the second is just the nature of the tour bus beast.

Still the audio goes to the upper and lower deck so it's a great way to get on "on the fly" introduction to London and take a lot of photos from above most of the traffic (and they give free rain gear for when it will, inevitably, rain).

I remember 13 years ago I took a bus tour and was absolutely mesmerised by the commentary and the stories about every little corner of London. I did not want to get off the bus I was in absolute awe! Today I got the tour again with my little ones and was so sad to hear the most uninspired commentary which did not have ANYTHING interesting to say about ANY of the sights, it was as if the version had been dumbed down and toned down so that all that remains is a mediocre collection of British invasion anthems between incredibly annoying voices that lack any type of cohesive structure while sacrificing ALL OF THE MAGIC THAT IS LONDON… big red bus really, what are you doing?

I chose the Big Bus Tour b/c I've loved them in other cities. This was a debacle. We paid $135 for 2 tix for a 2 day pass. There was no live tour guide on the day we bought them, but they expected one the next day- so we purchased a 2nd day. Turns out there was no live guide the 2nd day. It would have been 100% ok if the audio guide was good- but it was atrocious. It sounded like Mel B and a male giving a 20 second glimpse of the 25 stops that most would know. It was a 2.5 hr bus ride around the city, w/ likely 25 min of worthless sing song jokey commentary and 2 hrs of music. Are you kidding me? If you are not going to have a live guide, at least make your audio tour worthwhile. There was 2 hrs of historical London commentary that should have been on the audio guide. The only saving grace (on a 2 day ticket) was the brilliant tour by Julia at 1pm by the St Paul's bus stop for a 1 hr walking tour of London. She was funny and full of knowledge. It's a must if you have spent money on the rest of the waste of this tour. We also took a 1.5 hr walking Jack the Ripper tour with Nick on the first day at 4pm. He was equally brilliant, but If I could only do one, I'd pick the tour of London because the content is more interesting, but they are equally incredible guides. For the love of tourism- get rid of the current audio guide & have Steve, the beloved narrate the pre- recorded audio tour - nobody should have to pass 100 landmarks without historical/funny information.

Big shoutout to Inzar, the absolute best driver in London! He helped us navigate the City of London and made it a great experience. 10 stars!

Nick was full of energy and stories, very theatrical and engaging; the tour covered a lot of grounds and really helped us appreciate the city much more, always so lovely to hit up the hidden gems. Highly recommend.

We booked the big bus tour as we could get on at Gloucester Road and it dropped off for the red route, which is what we wanted to go on. It was juvenile and uninformative, often we passed sightseeing locations, with no mention of what we were passing. When we got by Downing Street, ding dong the witch is dead was announced over the commentary, an obvious reference to Maggie Thatcher and whatever you think of her was in bad taste. We also didn't see Buckingham palace when announced. Someone obviously had their heart set on comedy, rather than creating informative commentary. Let me assure you the commentary is desperately unfunny, on a par with afull aids diagnosis

Big Bus continued to book tours when London was gridlocked and more than one of their buses were out of service. They "activated" our online purchase at what turned out to be a non-working bus at St. Pancras - in retrospect this smacks of bad faith.

After wasting an hour (personnel walking us to alternate pickup locations) completely unable to get near a bus, we ended up taking the tube to other stops to try and "hop on;" unfortunately all were packed with no room to get on. (All the while their street personnel continued to not just sell tickets, but solicit riders, while fully aware of the overbooking - again, feels like bad faith.) Do yourself a favor: Please SKIP. You can do better. We booked no less than ten (10!) Viator/Trip Advisor tours for a three week vacation. Have written reviews for every other tour - and researched extensively each one. We enjoyed virtually every one - you can read the personal reviews and why. This one - which we booked last minute - was the ONLY BAD TOUR. Truly abysmal. WHY: the audio commentary is lacking in originality, depth, creativity, and is OLD. Bad music abounds while you are riding. Commentary on the audio is inadquate at best, if not truly SUCKED (at least get celebrities, get real tour guides offering good commentary - do not just get voice over actors!!). , and the bus is late and gets stuck OFTEN. It could be SO MUCH BETTER with LIVE COMMENTARY, better communication between buses, and frankly a company that made the necessary upgrades to bring themselves into the 21st century. Instead they are relying on outdated reputation and fooling tourists into thinking the experience will somehow be ok, IT IS NOT acceptable, let alone good.

BOTTOM LINE: SAVE YOUR MONEY FOR A BETTER, MORE PERSONAL TOUR
The changing guards tour with Julia was great. We had the best spots, Julia is a enthuastic guide and we had a great time with her. Thank you!

We made the mistake of selecting the Big Bus service during our 2 day stay in London. We chose the 48 h premium package that included the river cruise and the night tour. Firstly, Big Bus sells as many tickets as people are willing to buy. There is no tracking of how sales relate to available bus capacity. Given that Big Bus sales kiosks are seemingly everywhere, it is highly likely that your bus will be oversold, especially in the Summer.

Moreover, do not select this service if you intent to use this as your primary mode of transportation in London. It takes at least 3 hours to make one loop and so if you are expecting a bus every 20 minutes, as advertised, you will be disappointed. We ended up using the Tube to get between bus stops which is not only cheaper, but also much faster, but makes no sense when you just spent $45/person on bus tickets.

Second, as previously mentioned, expect huge crowds on this bus. Most passengers get on and ride the entire loop so if you don't get on at either the Victoria Station or the Green Park Station stops, you will likely not get a seat. Driving around it was very noticeable that the "Toot Bus" and "London Sightseeing Bus" were not nearly as oversubscribed and almost always had open seats on the top level. So if you actually want a seat during your tour, I would suggest going elsewhere.

Third, the commentary is a joke. Set on a computer most of the audio is Britpop music interspersed with some random facts about important landmarks that may or may not be synchronized with your actual location. The bus also does not go anywhere close to Buckingham Palace, Harrods, Hyde Park or Kensington Palace so if you want to see those you will need to disembark and walk.

The "night tour" which is sold as an additional benefit of the Premium Ticket is a complete joke. There is only one bus that leaves AT 6 PM from the London Eye stop in front of the Marriott Hotel instead of the designated starting point for the day bus at Green Park Station so you need to factor that in to your planning. Also, if you know anything about London in June, it doesn't actually get dark until 10 PM so if anything, this is a "Late Afternoon" tour. Notably, this is exactly the same commentary, and BritPop music as the day tour. The only difference is that the bus doesn't stop and so you can get around in about half the time as the day bus. Big Bus could dramatically improve the experience of the "Night Tour" by leaving later and providing a live guide. After all, it is only one bus!

The river cruise is provided by an affiliate company that includes live commentary that was both entertaining and informative. The perspective from the river is a nice complement to the views from the bus. However, if you don't board at either the Tower of London or the Westminster bridge location, the boat will be similarly crowded and you will not get a seat upstairs. Basically, don't board at the London Eye if you want to sit outside. Also, keep in mind, this is a one-way ticket so you will need to figure on getting back on the overcrowded Big Bus at 2 of its most popular stops.

Overall, this experience cost our family of 4 over $180 which is a complete ripoff given that we spent most of the time either waiting on a bus or standing in a moving bus or riding the tube to get to a bus stop. The bus company has an App that allows you to see the location of the other buses but its functionality would be greatly improved if this also included a measure of how full each bus was. This would tell you if it was worth waiting for the next bus, or standing in the one you have.

I can't speak for the other hop-on-hop-off buses in London but at least if seems that you could get a seat on these which is more than I can say for the Big Bus. I also find it hard to believe that their commentary could be any worse than the Big Bus. Taken together, I would definitely take my business elsewhere.
Don't waste your money, waited 50 minutes and not 1 bus showed up. Decided not to waste our day waiting and decided to explore ourselves.
This is a perfect days tour to see sights driver bus friendly and kept us informed. Wonderful Day.
I did the Red Line tour last week and our driver was Mr Govind. I want to give a huge shout out to him for being so kind and professional- he made the tour much more enjoyable. Thank you again!
Need to announce stop numbers in addition to historic landmarks. Need live person providing information on stops and for questions.

The London bus tour was fantastic, covering most of the important historic sites! We were told on route about a variety of guided walking tours available, and chose to join the “changing of the guard” the following morning, when our tickets were still valid! We were so lucky to witness the dress rehearsal for trooping of the colour, then followed the band from horse guard to Buckingham Palace! The crowd there was massive, so we weren’t able to witness the guards changing, but it was only a “mini-change” anyway, so unimportant in the context of what we had just witnessed.
Our compliments go to our tour guides, who were knowledgeable, informative and enthusiastic! Special mention to Julia and another chap who were outstanding!

My husband and I bought tickets for this 6 months ago but were unable to use it as planned (so we waited for the weather to improve, and did the tour today). We spent the first hour waiting at the Parliament Square bus stop for a bus to appear. The website says that buses run every 15 minutes or so, but given how bad London traffic can be, we were patient. I eventually used the chat function on the app, to be told that this stop (and two others) had been closed - nothing on the website, or the app, or at the bus stop itself to indicate this. We walked to the next stop, got on the bus, and were surprised when it then pulled in at the stop we’d just left….. The chat was pretty hopeless, to be honest - lots of ‘your feedback really helps us improve our service’ but really light on substance, ie why the buses weren’t (and then were…) stopping at Parliament Square. So to be fair, we weren’t in the best frame of mind when we finally got on board.

I know that commentaries have to cater for a diverse customer base - but having done the other London hop-on-hop-off tour years ago, we were looking forward to an interesting couple of hours. I’m sure the recorded chat and ‘banter’ will appeal to some, but it didn’t work for us at all. The tour was really light on information (in London!), talked about Jack the Ripper for no discernible reason (we weren’t in Whitechapel), said virtually nothing about the Houses of Parliament (apart from fun facts….), talked about Buckingham Palace when we were nowhere near it, promoted a couple of shops (is there a tie-in with Hamleys?), and gave very little information on London’s rich and diverse history, or buildings.

We love hop-on-hop-off tours, and have done them in dozens of cities; they’re a great way to gain insight into new (and familiar) places. But this one was just awful - the commentary would probably have worked for families with young children, but not for anyone else. I’m just sorry we wasted our money with this company, when there are other options - and looking at the reviews, we’re not alone.

Don't waste your precious vacation time waiting on the brown Big Buses. We paid for two tickets using the app while waiting for a bus at the stop by Harrod's. The ads for this company state that the app has real-time viewing for buses. It said our bus was to come every 30 minutes. We waited past the 30 mins as stated, and no bus came, and the app continued to say "no live times." There was no explanation anywhere of what "no live times" meant. There are many buses that you can hire; do not choose this brand. First time in London(Saturday 18th)Victoria station best to see around is Hop on hop off bus our tour guide was called Joe he was excellent very informative and funny had a great time by all thanks Joe.

On the tour right now , the driver looks like he’s fed up with his life lol , the guide is ready to answer question , but I was expecting more of the guided part than just answering questions and listening to music on the tour radio .. not worth it

We did the red line tour first off and had Cathy as our tour guide, she was fantastic and made the trip very enjoyable- some jokes and banter along the way made the whole journey fun even for our five year old, we then did the return Thames river cruise to Greenwich and toured the Cutty Sark merchant ship which is a must see well worth the visit and part of history well kept and preserved.on the way home we did the blue line tour which ended our very busy day delightfully.
Our wonderful tour guide Phil led us on a wonderful tour around the changing of the guard. He took us to spots with clear views and gave an interesting and informative tour.
Had the best first day in London all due to big Steve’s amazing walking tour. Thank you!!! He took us on the most amazing changing of the guards tour and took wonderful photos of us

Our tour was super interesting and our live tour guide Juli was very funny! It’s a great way to see a lot of London and get so much information.
We had a live tour guide with Kathy who was amazing, friendly and helpful, highly recommend it to anyone.

We did a bit of research on the different companies when we were in London for 3 nights for new year. We decided to go with big B. What a mistake it caused us more stress than anything on our trip. We decided to go for the 3 day pass to cover our time there. It was very over priced for the 3 day pass but we thought we may get our money’s worth by using it to get around. That did not happen due to the lack of buses and overcrowding. We were there New Year’s Eve & New Year’s Day and I know that is the busiest time of the year for London and there was a lot of road closures and diversions. That of course is not the bus companies fault, but there was so little information on the app and website about the diversions. That we ended up miles out of our way because the bus did not stop at the stop we wanted. There was no information at all about this when we boarded the bus. I was on it so long I actually felt like I had been taken hostage. The guide, nick who thinks he’s some sort of comedian (and believe me he is not) was that busy talking about himself, messing about with other passengers, having conversations about football and being rude about other cities and football teams, instead of doing his job of giving information about the diversions and some actual (correct) information about the sights we were passing. We had the pleasure of nick twice and could not stand his commentary any longer on the 2nd occasion, that we got off the bus earlier than we wanted to. There was an American couple who got off with us and they said that they had got off for the same reason. Then we had a woman guide, I didn’t catch her name but she was so rude, and grumpy. I went to sit in a seat when I got on and she shouted at me, that’s my seat. I was so taken aback by being spoken to like this. I then watched her be rude and shout at other passengers. “Sit down” “don’t be coming up these stairs, I SAID DON’T COME UP THE STAIRS THERE IS NO ROOM” “don’t get up till I say” I felt like I was back at school. Then told everyone on the bus that we would be mad to go to the fireworks on the river for new year. Well that would be 90% of us on the bus then. I am sure that all the guides aren’t like this, but I suspect that this company has a policy of employing a certain type of personality. I just want someone to tell me the correct information about the service & the sights in a polite and professional manner. I don’t want to see failed comedians or to be shouted at. I go to London at least once a year and I won’t be using this company again.

Although it was a drizzly grey London afternoon, this did not dampen the professionalism or enthusiasm of our fantastic guide on the Red Route - Peter. I am local to London and learnt so much history and details on the route, and with Peter's fantastic sense of humour, anecdotes, politeness and professionalism he made sure everyone onboard had the best trip on a open top bus in London! Thanks again.

I've always had positive experiences with Big Bus in the past. It's our go-to tour when visiting foreign cities. Always great routes and informative audio.

I verified, in advance, that Big Bus was running buses on Christmas and Boxing day while we were visiting London. Only to arrive on site and be told my pre-purchased tickets were not valid. Instead, I needed special tickets for the 25th and 26th. Not having any options, I re-purchased tickets for my entire family from the street-side stand. We were one of many groups completely confounded by this last minute change of policy.

Sure, they offered special Christmas/Boxing only tickets, but at no point was I told in advance standard tickets would not be valid. No text, no email, no message through TripAdvisor, etc.

I'm currently working through the refund process and hoping that Big Bus will reconsider how this is handled in the future.

The overall tour was a nice experience for me (given it was a bit expensive) but it gave me an opportunity to tour the city in one day I had for going around. Of course, you need more time to 'fully' explore the city but it suited my taste. I boarded at Tower of London, saw the palace, took the package-included cruise and dropped off at Westminster's.
There I got a chance to take a walking tour with Joe which was very fun, informative and totally worth it.
So all in all, I would highly recommend it to travellers like me, who are contempt in getting an overall feel of the city, in short time, focusing on very important stuff, Start early and you will really enjoy it through the day.
Julia was great. 5/5 stars for her. The live commentary and human was great. The prices are a bit expensive, but you don’t have other options.

It is good to know that the average speed in London is 6 mi/10Km per hour so you don't go very far very fast. Using a week transit pass, we zipped around the city and saw much more than we could have otherwise. There was support personnel in all the subways who always were able to direct us to where we wanted to go. The transit maps are very good. If you act and ask respectfully, that kindness is always returned.

if you want to see a city in detail ,take the hop on hop off buses. You get the tourist version of whats going on ,,,a fast history and if that sounds good get off the bus and see that sight. We laughed at her cool jokes and loved her story of her granmother who was the model for the statue on Barkleys Bank! True! Very well worth it and saves a lot of walking. I was in London 2 weeks ago and had pre purchased tickets. My intent was to start Thursday night around 4PM to just sit and listen as they did a loop around. When I got on the bus the driver said we couldn't get on because we were too late. Even though the stop said it's last pick up was later. We asked him if we could do the final loop just to sit and he said no and we had to be there earlier to get our tickets. As far as I could find there wasn't a time for when I had to get my tickets by listed. If there is I would suggest making it larger. Obviously, this frustrated us and we brought it up to the man at the stop the next morning. He called his manager who told us we could purchase a two day pass and email the company and be reimbursed. We did so immediately, stating exactly what were told to do. The email bounced back the next day. I have tried multiple times to send it to different avenues and nobody has responded or emails are bounced back. Obviously, I am pissed off that I have now been charged twice for my passes. To top it off, the Friday we were there was the horrible London bridge attack. My mom and I were near the cathedral stop when they announced they would not be sending buses that direction. I understood wanting to keep their staff and customers safe and didn't blame them for that, despite the fact both Golden Tours and the Original Tours were still running the stop. But then the following day, they still were not taking people to the stops listed. That was a bit ridiculous. While we were on the bus it was informative and the app was fine, but I am really frustrated with their customer service.
"Wikipedia Will" was one of our guides. We were impressed that he and all our guides knew so much about London. They were friendly and we enjoyed the tour.

We found that the Big Bus HOHO did not come to the stops every 15-20 minutes as advertised. We found ourselves waiting a half hour or more while watching other HOHO buses such as London Original coming much more often. We wish we would have chosen one of the others.

I grew up in London, so this was a repeat journey for me - Still worth it! Great seeing places where had worked, played or actually visited before. Bought back good memories.

Emma was just an amazing guide. Thank you for the informative and entertaining time! She was so good, we decided to stay on the bus a lot long, just to listen to her.

Tiffany was so good and so informative about l o n d o n. She deserves a raise. This was our first time in Europe.

We started with one day passes and ended up purchasing another day (too much for 1 day). Too: start early.

We really enjoyed the bustour! We had a very nice trip with a lovely guide named Rob. He was really engaged and gave us great knowledge of the city.
The next day we used the free offer and took the walking tour with the guide named Steve. It was so awesome! It was a totally fantastic way to explore the city and feel its pulse. Steve really went out of his way to make it a uniqe and pleasent trip for us and took us to places we would have never discovered on our own. It was the highligt of our trip. Definitely recommended!

Took the big bus on the first day of our London trip. Everything went well in the morning, however we waited for over an hour for the bus late in the afternoon. No bus showed up and there was no staff to be found. We ended up taking the subway back to our hotel. Very disappointing.

Good way to see the major sites in the city if first time visiting or don’t have a lot of time. The guides also give you history of the city and sites as you pass by. Hop on and off is really good cause if there is something you really want to see jump off come back later and a bus will be there. Would highly recommend doing first day or two there.
This service was so easy to use and made it so easy to see lots of London! I loved that it came with an app to help find bus stops easily as well as show us the different places near by

We had a 2 day pass for the BigBus hop on hop off.
I have a mixed review for this:
On the plus side, the audio commentary was good, although the same music between commentaries was far too repetitive, and needs variation.
Most stops had a Big Bus representative at the stop so that made it easier to find the right bus stop and ask questions. However when it came to changing to a different colour route that became very confusing, as sometimes the changeover stop wasn't the stop marked on the map they gave out, or the drivers themselves didn't know which colour route they were going to drive on next. So we had times there were queues of people going bus to bus asking are you 'blue" route, are you "red" route and the drivers didn't know either.
Sometimes the buses couldn't follow the routes due to road closures, because of roadworks, or protests, but this wasn't the fault of the bus company.
We found the buses very crowded and in the afternoon, we just had to wait till an emptier one turned up. i guess that's just down to the number of tourists there are, because there were so many different hop on hop off companies and all buses seemed crowded

I very much enjoyed the Big Bus Tours during our trip to London! We utilized the pass not only for the tour aspects, but also as part of or transportation around the city. We got a 4 day pass plus an additional day when we purchased the London Pass. We loved the night time boat tour & the walking tour to Buckingham Palace! Try to make the 10:00 from Lanchaster Square if you can, being part of "Team Joe" really made the experience so great! I would highly recommend this!

First, it was difficult to find where to get on the bus. Once we finally got on, my 10-year-old daughter and I decided to stay on the bus to see the town. We were traveling away from the city thinking that we would eventually loop back but to my surprise the driver stopped and said that was it and that we had to exit. I told him that we paid for the service that runs until late and it was only 5pm. So he left us in the middle of nowhere without any customer service. He could have told us one stop before that the next stop would be the last. He could have apologized and told us how to navigate once we get off the bus. He knew we were tourist and just didn’t care to deal with us. My daughter and I walked 30 minutes back to the city area and saw that the buses were still running. So I realized that it was just his bus, he was done working but made me believe that it was not possible for another bus to pick us up.

On the Red Route we got great commentary from a young bloke named Medwan. He had planned his spiel well and made it amusing. Seemed to have a good bit of knowledge and had done his own research. Was able to keep our interest even at one point when we got stuck on a section of road for some time due to a traffic incident. At the end of my trip on Red Route, Medwan was EVEN able to advise me where some toilets were to use - finding toilets to use in London is like trying to find water in the Sahara Desert.

Well done. Good job. Certainly takes you passed many significant parts of London.

but - the seats are no good, the headsets are no good, the live feed guide are a bit too difficult to understand as the quality of the sound are poor. The first driver we had was good, but when we took the bus again the next day I got yelled at by the driver because I tried to scan my ticket and was so stressed that he just yelled "GET IN GET IN" and waved his arms. He also drove like crazy and almost ran over a woman trying to cross the road at a green light..
Another downside was that when we were in London most of the stops at the red line were closed as they had the Lord Mayor show happening. I would have appreciated that the guy we bought the tickets from had mentioned that..
But its a great way to see London, and I would probably do the tour again.

We took the tour on a dirzzly day in London but still sat on upper level and had Joe as our guide! He was awesome and provided both educational and witty commentary! I am always a big fan of doing these Hop On Hop Off bus tours as a first day in any new city and Joe made it even better for us on our trip! Recommend (we bought the London Pass and the tour was included in the pass)

My tour guides James C and Ian really made this experience special for me and my family.
I would highly recommend it to a friend

For our first trip to London, this proved to be an outstanding way of seeing all of the major sites. No way we see half the things - London Bridge, Trafalgar Square, Big Ben, etc. - without taking advantage of this. Caron was sensational as our tour guide on the bus. She pointed out tons of things, added personal stories and was quite engaging. And taking the Royal Walking tour was - without a doubt - the best way to see everything that goes into the changing of the guard. Being part of 'Phil's Group' was terrific. He put us in the right places at the right times, was extremely knowledgable and was helpful throughout. Hope he gets the recognition he deserves as he approaches 20 years. Taking the Big Bus is the way to go.

First, I would like to mention I have used this company in countless cities and nations with pleasant results however I can NOT recommend the London service.

List of bad things we experienced in a single day:
-AWOL live tour guides.
-Confused employees: drivers, street personnel, and guides.
-Skipping stops with ZERO explanation of what was happening. Went from stop 5 to 7 (flew past 6) then stop 8 went straight to 14 with a different route then what was on the map. No one could explain what happened to stop 6 however there was a parade preventing stops 9-13. I can understand they have no control of a parade however not explaining why a 1/3 of the route disappeared is super important to the 75 tourists on board who are literally paying you to guide them around the city is another. I wonder what happened to the people who tried to 'hop on' at any of those skipped stops. I had to ask 3 different employees before being told there was a parade altering the route. Because of all the confusion an Italian lady who spoke almost no English tailed my wife and I all day because she was so lost with all the disorder. Poor lady was traveling alone and did not understand what was happening, luckily my wife speaks some Italian and we were ending the day at the same underground stop so we acted like her tour guide because Big Bus didn’t want to ;)
-Waited 45 minutes at an active stop for a bus.
-Towards the end of the day they decided to consolidate my almost full bus with another half full bus. Needless to say, a large group of people were forced off BOTH buses and this was the LAST STOP towards the transfer point to make the next loop (where most of the hotels were). I imagine those people were forced to find other transpiration as we were told another bus was NOT COMING as the route ended for the day. Luckily my wife and I were able to get on the new bus and wait for 30 minutes before it finally left.

Good things:
Buses were clean.
Boat ride was nice but the line was really long.
For the price (on a good day) it would be well worth it.

I would have rated this 2, maybe 3 stars however I emailed customer service 3 times and received ZERO replies. Docking points for that.

If you can ask for Big Steve with the Hop On and Off service or through the walking tour, you will not be disappointed. He came to my rescue today and gave me a fantastic tour. Thank you so much for your hospitality and amazing laughs.

Kristen - Florida girl

Too much time at stops.
Takes long time to get places.
We've done hop on hop off in other cities and never experienced these long extended stops up to 3-4 minutes a stop.

The 4 of us bought the 2 day pass
We toured one day...took a break the next day and then did our second day

A wonderful way to tour London and decide if further interest and a re-visit should happen.

We have done this in many cities and London measured up.

We only live 30 miles from London but had never taken a bus tour until yesterday. We ended up with 3 guides, 2 were excellent & had lots of interesting information & stories, the other we switched off & listened to channel 1! Overall a positive experience & will do again in the warmer weather with the grandchildren.

From lack of buses (at one stop we saw 3 other buses from the other companies come by while waiting for ours), to grumpy drivers yelling angrily (yes more than 1 of them today) at passengers who questioned which route or direction the bus was going combined with poor signage on the bus and it appears that you'd be much better off with either of the other 2 hop on/off tours offered in London. It was very disappointing compared with other hop on/off tours I've done in other cities. The final aggravation was getting dropped at the marble gates at 4:15, told by the bus driver to change there and the other buses would be coming only to wait until 5:10 and assume no more buses were coming. For the money and time, you're better off finding your own way around the city or using one of the other companies, Big Bus clearly isn't putting in the effort in London where pure volume of travelers allows them to continue with such poor service.

Pity the real tourists, who want to learn something. We had one good guide and one really dreadful one! Dreadful one (young lady) gave out a lot of rubbish information - e.g. Balmoral is in England, Lady Di is buried in Westminster Abbey !!! And more!
What really concerned me, was that when I fed this back to the company I just got real platitudes like no one cared less ! Not interested in any corrective action/training etc. - just so long as tourists continue to pay them !!
Very interesting information whilst travelling around London. My son aged 12 really enjoyed it. I was hoping for the information to be issued via a tour guide and not through the recorded tape.

We were in London to see the history and landmarks, we got some advice from an information lady a Victoria Station to use big bus tours. Excellent tour routes and great commentary from the guides, also did river tour.

There was a lady called ‘Caron’ who took us on our walking tour guide through Whitehall, Trafalgar and Westminster area, she was very engaging and knowledgeable, it really made our trip, her enthusiasm and intimate knowledge really made this holiday special.

Thanks Caron!
The big bus was ok. Decent value but a couple of issues. the app was not accurate and the bus stops not clearly marked. Some of the guides were better than others.

The HOP-ON-HOP-Off bus tour is good in any city. This tour gives you an overview of London and allows your group to decide what to do next. It was super hot the day we rode through London. Bring water and a hat.
It is worth the money.

This morning Ema was the tour guide on my Red Line tour. It was perfect to put away the earphones and to stop the canned, taped speech to hear her speak about the history and the life of the London streets and buildings. Her breadth of knowledge was tremendous and so natural as she spoke of her city. I particularly loved the description of her grandmother's role as model for statues throughout London. I bought the book. Thank you so much. I wish all the legs of the tour today could have been so great.

I want to give a big shout out to Emma! She was an amazing tour guide. Very attentive to every question we had on the bus. It warmed my heart to hear her talk proudly about her grandmother's contribution to London's art history. I've never had an amazing tour guide like Emma!!!♥️♥️♥️
Joe on the Red Line Big bus tour was the best! He was very informative, informational, personable and hilarious! Wish we could have had him on all of our tours through the city 🖤

We had a two ticket day. First bus and guide Billy where great. Then started to decline. Most of the time the live guides were talking and the bus drivers didn’t put the commentary, like Oliver. So basic you pay a lot to listen to the same classic music again and again.
The drivers are a nightmare. We had two near collisions in the two days and in Nov 4 we actually hit a car. Bus had to stop and wait for police. No apologies nothing. Wasted my whole morning.
