Very expensive for the service a got. Go with another company or take the double deckers. Are cheaper and you don’t get commentary any way.
I am going to NYC in December. I won’t make the same mistake there.
In the picture you Dan see the Mercedes Benz we hit and the driver trying to get out if it do we could carry on.

Bob was our guide and he is AMAZING. Knowledgeable, entertaining and very helpful!! We had a large group and he took great care of us. Shirl's 50th
Thanks Bob

As we only had Three days we took the pass for two days which was to terrific value.
Loved the personal guide instead of only the earplugs.

Wikipedia Will was our bus guide. The sights of London are amazing but was most definitely enriched with the wide knowledge and little add on information he delivered during the trip. The things not always found in the guide books! A thoroughly nice guy and so helpful. I wound recommend this tour at the beginning of your visit to London to give a real feel for history and antidotes of this amazing city.... Peter & Christine Rochdale UK.

We chose the Big Bus Tour out of our London Pass options and we weren’t disappointed. We did the red route which is what I would recommend for anyone who has never been to the city before. All the major landmarks are on this route. The drivers are not the friendliest, but can be easily overlooked once onboard with the tour guide. We started the tour with William and ended the tour with Big Steve. Both guides were excellent, knowledgeable, and went above and beyond to ensure everyone on board had an unforgettable experience. Definitely a highlight of our trip.

We were very lucky weather wise so although cold(ish), it was dry and relatively sunny. We bought a two day ticket which seemed good valueless for money. We travelled 3 of the 4 routes and saw everything we wanted to see but left London wanting more.
I worked in London for 7 years and even I learnt things from the live guides and automated ones.
Buses were regular and not too busy.
We had to move bus stop once as the bus had been diverted due to an accident - these things happen.
I can concur with some of the comments about the drivers’ attitudes. However, I imagine driving a bus through London day in, day out would fray anyone’s nerves.
We would happily take this tour again.

Had two great guides; Lewis, who was entertaining and so inclusive of everyone and Wikipedia Will who was very informative and slid humour in his talk. I really enjoyed that. Great way to see many sights of London especially if you're time is limited. Easy to get off and look around then get back on at the same stop or find another along the route. Highly recommended.
Enjoyed the ride. Cosy and nice especially in a cold and windy day. Used 2 day pass. Allowed us to cover the routes leisurely.

Great way to explore the city in all its beauty. On the plus side, Emma, our tour guide was perfect. She knows a lot about the city and had interesting anecdotes throughout the visit. She also sang some sick tunes.
A must for tourists to see everything and learn so much about the city. Our guide was Emma and she was absolutely perfect! Very funny, available and knowledgeable. I would recommend 100%.
Emma our guide was superb. Very knowledgeable and worth every penny. We did not want to get off in case we missed something...!

I booked this tour a few days before I came to London. We weren’t quite sure what to book on London, so we decided to book this bus tour. Many of my friends recommended this tour and said it was excellent, and I couldn’t agree more. If you buy your tickets in advance, you save 10$. Our commentator was Emma. She was amazing! She gave us a very nice tour on the red line. We didn’t even want to get off the bus for a while because the whole London history was just that interesting to us! The busses run all across the city and have stops at all major points across London. Tour is great! Worth checking out !

I’m so glad my husband and I decided to do the Big Bus Hop on-Hop off in London. It was the perfect way to start our trip. We decided to do that the very day we arrived, it was nice, being we were jet lagged but had to stay up, to be able to see the city and decide where we wanted to get off and explore the next day. Tiffany, our guide, was great! She was super friendly and knowledgeable able the sights we were seeing.

Good bus tour made amazing by our excellent guide, Wikipedia Will.

I'm very happy with the way it turned out, largely in thanks to our amazing guide.
Was really worth to take the tour while traveling with family. Very easy, very convenient. Special thanks for guide Valdas, who took energy while entertaining and answering all the questions!

Took the tour to allow the kids to see more of London, we travelled the red route with an amazing tour guide Emma who kept us all entertained, being a Londoner herself she was full of genuine knowledge of the city and clearly knows her stuff! She was also super helpful. We travelled late afternoon so had beautiful views of the city all lit up as we travelled over tower bridge.
My only moan is the price as being over £100 is quite an expensive bus ride!
Emma was an amazing guide who really gave life to the city as we went through it. She really made the trip a memorable one!

We were only in town for the weekend so were hoping to do the Hop on Hop Off around London to get our bearings and then pick one or two places to see. Unfortunately there was incredible traffic and it was pouring. The entire top of the bus is open so it fits half as many people. You don't reserve tickets for a certain day/time so you are simply out of luck (or very wet). We were on the bus for a few hours and didn't even make it around 2/3 or the red route. We got off and walked. It was pretty crummy overall. On a nice day I imagine it is great. But, wanted to warn others about it in case it is predicted to be rainy - in London.
Wikipedia guy was excellent. He taught me so much. I loved it. He was so good. Would recommend to anyone.

First, Paul is the best guide. He gives live commentary and not only does he give you all the historical facts, he throws humor in the mix and he was GREAT! This bus takes you to all the iconic spots like St Pauls Cathedral, Big Ben, Parliament, the London Eye, the Eurostar station, old architecture, new architecture & everything in between. The Big Bus Hop On Hop Off is a MUST!!

My parents and I had a lovely experience on the Big Bus - London. The service was very convenient and easy. We had several lovely tour guides, Tim and Rob to name a few. Rob in particular was great! He was caring, informative and a great laugh! Extremely entertaining. Rob Also helped with getting that "picture perfect" click. Couldn't recommend Rob enough. Keep an eye out for him if you want the full experience. Will be back from Aussie land to visit again soon and will definitely return.

We have just come back from a London trip with 48 hour big bus ticket. Great fun was had by all. We started with a walking tour to see the changing of the guards, our tour guide Joe was brilliant! Lots of local knowledge and info, great spots to watch the band and patrol, we even marched along with them. Lots of fun facts. We enjoyed it thoroughly. We then did the orange route and the river cruise which again was brilliant. We were lucky enough to have a hilarious commentator for the return leg!. Then onto the red route which is the main one and a great commentator again. Had a great trip! Thanks big bus
Really enjoyed this great tour around the centre of London. Great commentary from Ross who made it a proper fun experience. Defiantly do it again 😊

My wife and I only had a few days in London, so a Big Bus Tour was the best way for us to hit all the spots in just a few hours.
Our big surprise and huge win was our guide, Will. Make it a point to take his bus and he'll make your visit to London that much more enjoyable. Full of charm and wit and interesting history facts on London, Will gave us the best guided tour I've ever experienced (I've had the opportunity to experience tours like these all over the world).

Thank you, Will, you made our trip around London beyond worth our £35!!!

Big Steve led two wonderful walking tours on 19 October – the day a million protesters marched in London. Rather than fight the ever-changing path of the bus, we chose to accompany Steve on the Royal Tour. He led us through some wonderful backways of London from Trafalgar Square to Buckingham Palace. We saw the changing of the guard, and were always in the best place for sights and photos. We saw places we would never have known were there. The morning tour was such a treat, we joined Steve for a tour from St Paul’s Church to the Tower of London in the afternoon. Steve shared history, humorous trivia, and personal stories about the local sights as we traveled through the backstreets to see sights off the beaten path. We enjoyed his knowledge, his entertainment, and his company. Recommend if you get the chance to join Big Steve for a walking tour, you do not want to miss!

We did the Red Tour on our last day in London and it was really nice. Julia, our Guide, seemed to know a lot, it was a very fun ride with her. (JULIA IS THE BEST, GIVE HER A TIP)
Definitely would tanke the Big Bus again. Thanks a lot!!

I can't recommend this enough. It was excellent to see the sights of London. The river cruise was very funny and a great experience. All the staff were very friendly and helpful. Especially our first bus driver, I didn't get his name. Black man, so friendly and helpful. And the last guy white Wikipedia Will was amazing. His knowledge was fab and very helpful on helping us get to our destination. We were a party of three generations and it suited us all very well. Definitely would do it again, well worth the money. We were only in London for a day. So this was perfect to see the sights.

Because of the protests taking place, the bus was diverted several times along the route. Many times, we had no idea where we were. A lot of the things we came to see were detoured around. There was no way to follow the map given us. I know we circled the Marble Arch three times !! BUT the big issue was...no one mentioned any of this when we boarded ! Finally, the bus stopped and we were told, "Everyone get off". Another driver got on the same bus and announced, "This is now the BLUE route". He was rude when we asked if we would be following map. The detours were not their fault, but we should have been notified that we would basically be driving around unknown buildings and would not be able to get off where we thought we would be.

We booked the big bus tour during a 2 day layover in London traveling with an infant and a very fit Grandma. It is a great way to see the city and despite road work and protests we never had to wait more then 7 mins for a bus. The red route brought us past many major attractions and the boat cruise was a lovely addition. We were particularly excited for the live guides although this turned out to be mostly disappointing. Of the 4 buses we rode, 3 guides lacked animation, gave only basic info or were downright grumpy. The shining exception was Dinosaur Joe. He regaled us with stories and delectable historical tidbits. We actually changed our plans on a whim and rode several steps further just to hear him. If we had the time we would have done the whole route again with him. Overall, a worthwhile expense to experience the city on a short timeline.

We went on the bus tour on a Sunday and had two tour guides who were both amazing! We only caught the name of one of the men who was called Lionel and he was brilliant at telling stories and facts of everywhere in London as well as being really friendly and good at keeping everyone safe on board. I would highly recommend this to everyone but remember to wear layers as it gets cold on the top of the bus. The river cruise included in the ticket was also so good with a really funny guy giving the talk. Amazing for the prices and a great way to see the other whole city in a day.

We did a day on the BigBuses hop-on-hop-of routes. Started with the red one which includes live guided tour in English. Our guide, Ian, was very informative and managed to be personal at the same time. Extremely joyable and entertaining tour. Thank you Ian for great experience!
Cheers
The Icelanders

Josh from the blue tour was the best .... Very informative and knowledgeable guy and friendly too....
Will definitely recommend the big bus tour and if you are lucky to be on the bus with Josh it will be a bonus.... 🙏🏼👍🏼
It was a huge pleasure to have a trip with Big Bus. Our guide Mr. Lionel was amazing and he shared with us a lot of facts about London and many stories. Truly recommended

Prompt departure, easy, very informative. Morton and Dan took great care of us with our drive through the Cotswolds, Warwick Castle, Stratford on Avon, and Oxford. We had enough time at all venues and Morton briefed us on each giving advice and suggestions. Morton's walking tour of Oxford was included and should not be missed. We had an elderly woman with us, and they were very accommodating and patient with her. I would recommend tour to anyone. Thank you for wonderful experience!
Such a great tour. The commentary is sooo informative and funny! I had Nigel & Julia as commentators and they were both hilarious!

On the first day there were disruptions due to protests so the bus was stuck in traffic for a long time. Eventually they re routed the bus and we were back on our way. The second day they stayed out of that area and we had a good day seeing the sights

First impression wasn’t great. The bus is not designed very well to see anything if you are not on the top (which you wouldn’t do while it’s raining).
The person checking tickets when we first got on was a bit rude & unorganised.
Sights & info were great, we hopped back on the tour at the Tower of London & there was a live guide, he was fantastic but unfortunately I didn’t get his name. Our tour also included the river cruise and the captain was very informative & interesting to listen to. The tour was well worth the money!

The reason I'm writing this is Wikipedia Will; we got held up by some hippies who were protesting and we were not moving for nearly a half hour but Will just kept going! He just was an inexhaustible supply of genuinely interesting facts and anecdotes. If I was running another tour I would have poached this guy long ago!
We had a really hard time finding the bus stop closest to our hotel, then had to wait almost 30 minutes for a bus. However, once we got on the tour was great and the river tour was nice as well.

A good way to see the area. We were up top which gave us a great view. Good for photos. We liked the opportunity to sit and listen to all of the information about the area. It is good for an overview. You can get off at any area, explore and then get back on. The staff was very helpful when we had questions.

We have loved the hop on hop off bus service all over Europe but today’s experience was really disappointing. Both drivers on the blue and orange line were really rude.

Also we were literally yelled at to get off the orange line bus, only to get told to walk to the end of the street to get another one?

There are a lot of hop on and hop off buses in London and unfortunately I would not recommend this company at all.

Probably a 4/10-having to wait with approximately 100 people for over half an hour to get on any bus was so frustrating, especially when there were 3 empty buses just sitting there at Marble Arch. When asking the staff member how much longer it would be rudely being told 5 minutes an empty bus will come- not the case. A 3/4 full bus came. First time using this company as we usually use the City sightseeing company. Not sure I would recommend or use them again. Had a great young English guy give live commentary however when changing buses ended up with a girl with a strong accent who we couldn’t understand. Other companies seemed to have so many more buses come by with lots of seats available.

A fantastic way to see London. The tour guide was knowledgeable, and entertaining as well. You can get off any any stop and get back on later Need a full day and hop for sunny weather so you can ride on top in the open.
It was abdolutely GREAT! I bought the tickets in advance, and besides the bus Ride, we for the boat tour. Speechless!

Wiki Will was an amazing tour guide whose extensive knowledge of London was impressive. This is a great way to get a feel for London and it’s sights if you have never visited before. Do it early in your visit so you have a perspective of the city. Our teenage kids have never been to London and really enjoyed the entertaining and informative tour.

We took advantage of the royal walking tour and were so glad we did, because we lucked out to have "Big Steve" as our guide, who just blew us away! He was warm, witty and so knowledgeable about the sites. His passion for the city, its history and our experience was just outstanding! We even bumped into Steve later in the day and received an additional and lovely guided tour along the river that capped it all off. We saw sites off the beaten path, heard engaging tales about the past, learned the source of a dozen common sayings and even had Steve's help getting all the great "photo opps". We have used Big Bus in other cities and recommend it here. Do the walking tour on a weekend and see if you can get Big Steve!

This did not work in London. No hop on hop off possible. Not enough busses for all the tourists. Often ist was not possible to get into the busses. Long times of waiting. Frustrating when you see how much space is left in the busses of the other companys which are even cheaper by the way.

But: one of the tourguides was really great, he was very motivated and shared a lot of Information.
You are a hostage to road closures which will significantly impact your plan to swap routes. We use the red route and ended up paying for a taxi due to other routes being closed.

It was bad. The protestors were suppose to only mess up one area causing the bus to not stop at three points according to the guide on 10-10-19. Protestors were not the problem the first part of the red line route, but traffic I guess was thick for a Thursday? The bus moved at a snails pace. The guide seemed nice enough but he didn't talk all that much. So when he wasn't talking there was buzzing on his live channel, so you could switch to canned band music with interspersed info. But you need to keep your eyes on the guide to see when he does choose to speak into the mic. I'm guessing I missed some bit of info about paying attention to the color of the route your bus is on. There are different routes, red, green, orange.. It was so slow going I decided to get off & walk into the Caranby shop area. When I decided to get back on I waited 40 minutes for any maroon colored big bus to show up, but what I didn't know when I got onto the bus is that it was on an orange route & wasn't going back over to the red loop, later in day ~4:00 pm or so. There was no guide just a driver, thankfully he was helpful & explained I need to get off & go on the tube if I was to have any shot at getting back to my red route stop that I needed. There was another couple that had the exact same issue as me, on a wrong color route getting further & further from where they needed to be. If I had a do over I'd have just picked spots I wanted to get to & just walk or use the tube.

I read another review that said there were more Big Buses than other lines and I agree. We never had trouble finding our bus.
There were a few stops that were not in service, including the one right in front of our hotel. This would have been nice to know before we headed out. Someone also said that the live tour guide was better than listening to the recorded tour but I found they were pretty much identical.
As a Canadian, I found that people in London are fairly rude and customer service is not something they pride themselves on. Once I accepted that ,and lowered my expectations, I found the city to be quite a nice place to visit. This was city-wide and not a reflection on the Big Bus staff. We had several drivers who let us off at traffic lights near to our hotel which was very nice and saved us a lot of steps.
Big Ben is covered for renovation, Trafalgar Square was under renovation when we were there
Had a great tour on the red bus with Tiffany and an excellent walking tour with "Big Steve". He made our visit to Buckingham Palace extremely memorable.
This is a really good and smart way of getting around London and at the same time see the many interesting sites London has to offer. A little pricey but its worth the efficiency.
Staff were friendly and helpful, but most of the tour was spent in traffic jams or lines waiting to get on buses or boat
Our tour guide was Rob who was really informative and funny. He was very interactive with people on the bus and very very friendly would highly recommend doing this tour!
Truly the best to get around the city to see all the sites. You can get on and get off anywhere along the route. No worries of parking or traffic, just enjoy the city!

I love to walk so I never, ever used to take a tour bus, but my wife likes them so I began taking them in Barcelona, Lisbon.... What I now like to do is take one of the Hop-On Hop-Off bus tours the first day that I'm in a city to get a big-picture sense of where everything is located and the areas of the city that I'd like to explore more. I spend the rest of the days walking to really interact with the city and its people.

My husband and I went on a trip to London for our one year anniversary. We decided to try out Big Bus— as a way to get around the city as well as tour the city. Our expectations were blown out of the water! We took all four loops as well as the river cruise with the two day pass. The recorded tours were interesting but the BEST were the live tour guides- each with their individual stories and anecdotes to add to their tour. We have to give an extra shout out to Nick— our one tour guide. He was absolutely incredible— kept us on our toes, laughing hysterically— we honestly stayed on the bus longer than we wanted to keep hearing what he had to say! 100% recommend big bus and if you get Nick as a tour guide— stay on!!

We purchased the 48 hour pass and the first day, the buses were excessively crowded. There was standing room only and buses were running mych further than 30 minutes apart. The staff informed up that since it was close to the end of the "season", there were less buses running. The second day was better, but overall an average experience.

We planned to go to Johannesburg with my whole family and my father, who was first time abroad. We ended up in London (thanks to BA and Heathrow) for two days instead of being in South Africa. So we took the chance to stroll through London with my dad, who was never in London before. We took the Hop-on-Hop-off Bus after a busy day in Mme Tussaud etc. We enjoyed especially the tour with Rob who has a fantastic sense of humour and knows a lot about history and London. It was a huge pleasure and we forgot about our nightmare travel.
The bus takes you to all the great spots. Definitely worth the price. Our tour guide Tiffany was very fun and nice!

We hoped on the tour at a point near Trafalgar Square. Lucky for us we have met Nick L. on the bus. Nick was a smart, amusing tour guide who made us laugh and enjoy the entire ride. It was very interesting. We got so much information that we could choose where to go in the following days. Many thanks to the wonderful Nick for a great first day in London.

My first wonderful surprise was finding that they would take my Scottish notes, always something I have to do with caution in England. I decided to be a tourist back on a visit to my own city. The green line is interesting, but not the most exciting for those looking for the real London highlights, but wonderfully close to my accommodation and St Pancras, so I started there. I transferred to the red line as I had hours to kill, and the route was rather good. It took me about 30mins though to clock on to the live audio. I'm so glad that I did. Giles was hilarious and I wish I could have stayed on his tour longer. I jumped a couple other lines, which had good guides but not quite to my humor I guess. Giles should be one of the standard audio tracks in my mind. The prerecorded ones are quite dry, but his storytelling et al, was spot on for me. Lots of interesting points, like where 'hangover' comes from. I wont spoil it for you, go and find Giles on the red line.
At the end of the evening though, it was about 16.00-16.30, so approaching last bus time, I rejoined the red route by the aquarium. The guy on the street was being somewhat bombarded by questions from people and you could see he was getting a little flustered from having to keep reiterating to tourists what they needed to do, where to go etc, and he was handling it like a champ. I wish I got his name. The red line turns up, and there's a family in front getting on the bus, and the driver seems to decide that he wont get to where they want to. The guide insisted that even with traffic, there was plenty of time, and the driver is trying to kick the family off the bus, which was all causing some drama. The guide is trying to handle the situation, the driver is shouting, and the guide was trying to call some manager I assume. I really felt for the guide, he was trying to help, and I feel if this incident came to their management, that it should be noted how reasonable he was trying to be. Later, we came close to Marble Arch, and were all ushered off the bus. I could see the confusion of many, as the driver simply pointed in the direction, which I knew was, Oxford Street. I don't know if this was the drivers usual temperament, but he seemed unwilling to be of any other use, and many other jacketed staff were off, presumably on their way home. After his argument with the previous guide, I wasn't willing to try. I'm sure in the age of smart phones that these tourists aren't still wandering round Hyde Park, but I also wasn't going to be the one to try and lure people with limited English to somewhere I hoped was more recognizable.
If in doubt, find Giles.
Lionel was a tour director on the Big Bus London trip. He was amazing. He knew the city and was able to tell us all about it without reading it from a script. Thank you Lionel.

If you are in London for a short time but have time for a quick tour, this is the way to do it. The London tour was nice. On the longest circuit, there's a guide who talks to you in addition to the recorded guide. They seem to be competing. As a visitor who wants to garner as much info as possible, it was a struggle to listen to the recording and the guide in the bus. It should be one or the other. Further more, the guide was inaudible even though he had a Mic. The recording had more music than info. In one tour, I experienced a delay of over an hour. The staff at the bus stop didn't know how long the delay was and just told us to wait. The tour therefore ended later than I expected. This was the first time I've used Big Bus and wasn't a good experience unfortunately.

I bought the 2 day access with the river cruise. Loved it all! I saw everything I needed to see in London from the comfort of the bus. The app was helpful in tracking the routes and where the next bus was relative to where I was. Several of the tour guides were good, but Luca is the one who stood out. He was knowledgeable and quite funny. Time & money well spent!

Using the Hop on Hop off bus is a great way to see the sites of London & get your bearings. Great value for money. There’s a route to cover anything & everything in London. The guides are knowledgeable & you find yourself learning without even realising it. Top notch.

Very organized tour with guide who loves his job. Totally Enyoied!
Some buses were overgrowded, but that is understroodable, because it was a saturday rush-huor. A Little bit misunderstood the blue Line routes, because sometimes the recorded guide were late or was not telling anything about what was arounding us.
Stayed in London for 2 full days! Took the big bus tours and it was awesome! Took the guided walking tour to Buckingham Palace! Big Steve was amazing and made the entire walking tour worth the time!!

The Hop-On/Hop-Off bus tour itself is convenient to get around the city and see major attractions if you have lots of time. The buses are comfortable and the audio guide is decent (better if the live guide is working) but often the buses are crowded and London traffic lengthens the travel time between destinations.
For the best “bang for your buck” take one of the Walking Tours which are included in the fare. Big Steve was our guide and he took us on the Royal Walk. We saw everything from Trafalgar Square to Buckingham Palace. He shared all of the facts you would expect and also several extra points of interest. He even pointed out a few hidden side sites that he knew our kids would enjoy! The sites were amazing to see but made even better with Steve there to keep us informed and laughing. He also gave us some useful travel tips and made sure everyone in our group knew how to get to their next destinations. We thoroughly enjoyed our walk and wouldn’t hesitate to do another.

The service was so bad. Almost no buses and all of them were always so full. We took 4 buses and 3 of them we were standing downstairs with 20 more people. It looked more like a public transportation bus than a tourist bus. Would not recommend at all.
We highly recommend the tour boat part of this service. Lots of room and peaceful. Not so much the bus.
We had Mehmet as guide on our red line, and he was very nice an funny. We learned a lot about the city. We enjoyed the tour with him!

We had an actual guide called Cliff, a Londoner who knows his stuff, friendly and an interesting guy, even when we were stuck in traffic (which was often) and when we had do divert from the regular route, he still had plenty to tell us when we were on part of the route that deviated form the usual one, and thanks also to our driver bringing us there and back safely.

They didn’t stop!!!
they left us with 2 little children in the comd and they just drove away even if we run after the bus and waved the driver.
Never again!!!!
Good experience but we didn’t quite know how to exchange vouchers for tickets. It would have been so easy if we knew to look for the guys in the red jackets.

Bought a 48 hour premium ticket on line, when we tried to get the tickets, as instructed by the website, the Big Bus operator at the St Pauls Stop came with attitude as we weren't buying from him and became very obnoxious when my son and daughters tickets wouldn't print out.
Thanks to the driver they got on and finally got tickets at the Tower of London stop.
The live commentaries were varied.
Catching a bus was a big hit or miss with demonstrations closing roads but even on Sunday they didn't seem to arrive.
I also used their app which was useless.
The only highlight was the river cruise
I think in theory hop on hop off is a good idea but in practice its a waste of time and money

We have done lots of HOHO tours, the last two in Copenhagen and Barcelona. The London HOHO offered less information than any HOHO I have used. Seemed like the London Big Bus simply played Rule Britannia over and over. The live commentators had little to say and were more crowd control officers. We used one day of our three-day pass. Money wasted! I've always learned a lot from my HOHO experiences. NOT this time.

We had a great ride with Joe and Charlie. Joe said he'd only been doing tours 3 weeks but you could not tell, The trip was very informative and how these drivers get these buses through London traffic is beyond me. Great time and easy way to see the city.
We enjoyed this tour, especially when our guide was Dinosaur Joe. He was informative as well as humorous. We stayed on the bus longer than planned when he was our guide.

This is an excellent Way to see the Great city of London. Friendly, comfortable ride. The Driver was a safe driver and curious. The Tour guide have us great instructions to take tubes. He was a great tour guide that answered our questions. Elisab

Thanks to this bus tour company, we got to see the highlights of London! Our tour guide was exceptional! Her name is Alexis. Even though she’s Canadian, she was very knowledgeable and made the tour very entertaining. We even decided to stay on the bus throughout all the stops because we liked the way she presented history and all sites, after we came back to the first stop is when we decided to get off the bus. She was very cool and made our London stay unforgettable!

Hi
My family and I did the bus tour in london over two days. The bus is convenient and easy to use with all attractions included.
The commentary, enthusiasm, knowledge and attitude of Christopher made the tour that much more enjoyable.
He is a great tour guide to have as he is very passionate about his work.
We had a great tour seeing the sights of London. Tiffany was very knowledgeable and we all enjoyed her humour and the extra information she gave us.

My husband and I loved this! We had a 48 hour pass and rode the blue, red, and orange routes in one day to get to know the city. Sure, it is full of tourists but it was fabulous and a great first day in London on our honeymoon - we saw everything and learned so much! Unfortunately I don't remember our red route tour guide's name but she was hilarious, informative, and even gave us all candy when there was heavy traffic. 5 stars easy and we would 100% recommend this - especially as an easy way to see a lot of London when you are fighting jetlag!

We did the hop
On off tour on our first day and it was perfect as it gave us a sense of what was where and the sheer size of London !
The first guide we had was very good and the second guide was lovely but difficult to understand due to her heavy Spanish accent .
Would definitely recommend this to newcomers to London

Great value for money and the easiest way to find your way around London's must see and do locations and attractions. Incredibly a London river cruise is offered included in the base price of the tour offering you the chance to view the City from the river. Great value for money would highly recommend.

The staff are so unfriendly and unfortunately the bus don’t follow the map, the information on tune wasn’t working. I have used the Big Bus Paris, it was nice, in London I’m disappointed all service and staff couldn’t be better, the staff worked as unhappy people, them just treated the customers like a silly people, that is very bad.

We only had 1-day in London, so we decided this was the best way to see most everything. And it was. The convenience was just as was expected. The Brexit protests were not expected, when diverted some of the bus routes which was a bit disappointing, but certainly not the bus companies fault. The added transfer to the City Cruise was a pleasant options!

We have travelled and done hop on and hop off buses in other cities in Britain, and for the price we paid, what we expected was a tour around the sights of London with engaging and informative commentary telling us interesting things about one of the most historic and fascinating and storied cities in the world. There is so much in London that is interesting, that to spend 5-10 minutes driving with just boring music playing for large sections of the tour is unforgivable. The commentary was largely either advertising, route directions, or boring "you are at X, it was built by Y in Z" which gave little or nothing more. The commentary voice actors were boring, and there were multiple different voice actors. All in all it felt very disorganised and stilted. Would have been better off with Google Maps.

On the other hand the buses were clean, and well organised, the staff were friendly and very helpful. When we did have a live commentator she was very good.

Absolutely brilliant! Roland was the absolute best guide ever!!!! He was so fun and informative. Would absolutely recommend this tour for anyone visiting London and if you get Roland as your guide then you'll have the best time ever !
We are having a wonderful vacation here in London thanks to the Big Bus Tour Company. We would have never been able to cover this much territory by foot.

Well, we didn’t realise we would get a stand up comedian free with our bus ticket.
Christopher was hilarious. But also had so much knowledge of London. We saw him twice and he remembered us and related some of his patter to suit us. I notice he did this with a lot of others too!

The driver with Christopher, Michelle, was also superb. Excellent smooth and friendly driver. Great communication between her and Christopher.

Big Bus is a definite recommendation from us.

Initially, buses seemed as if we wouldn't be comfortable or get seats since there so were many people on the bus. But, once we went through a couple of stops and others got off the bus, we had great seats. The live commentators were enjoyable, especially Chris on the Red Line. Great information delivered in such a dynamic way. You could really feel his love of London. Would return to London and get Big Bus tickets again.

A great way to see the sights and the hop on hop of is handy if you wish to stay in a particular area for some time and then re board the bus. We were fortunate the sun was shining,so a view from the open top was doable, London is very busy and it is inevitable you will spend some time in stop start traffic.
Our 24hour ticket included a cruise on the Thames which was the highlight of the day, it is a must do.
All in all, if you are in London for a short period of time,what better way to take in the famous landmarks?

Bus was nice, but red line, which has the most to see, was very heavily congested by traffic. Lots of time sitting at red lights and moving slowly. Upside was that we found it somewhat easy to navigate routes and our tour guide, Roland, was wonderful and informative.

Purchased ticket online and advised that ticket was not valid.
Contact number provided in email is not staffed.
It was the last day in London and Big Bus ruined it.

Rob was a great narrator and resource. He made the tour enjoyable and also helped us with directions to our next destination.
Thanks for showing us London.

Tiffany and Fred and the Irish girl all made our day by giving us a clear , informative,engaging and entertaining commentaries. We got a good understanding of the cities of London and Westminster. Fred's account of Oliver Cromwell and Charles' statue's facing each other across the street tickled our fancy- one of many gems on the 3 days we gratefully spent with the tour. Thank you for money well spent.
P.S. - We feel that Big Steve's walking tour to Buckingham Palace is not to be missed.

My friends and I went on the Big Bus Tour in London. We had a fantastic time! It took quite a while to actually get on the bus itself, but once we did the fun took off! Our tour guide was amazing. Unfortunately, I don’t remember her name! She was so knowledgeable and had a great sense of humor. It’s a great way to get a glimpse of everything in London and then make a plan on what to go back and visit!

We booked the two day hop on/off bus pass including the walking tour and hop on/off river cruise. All of the tour guides were very knowledgeable and delivered their tours in a humorous and informative style that kept you both interested and entertained. The walking tour around the parks and royal buildings (note: you don't go inside) with 'Big Steve' was one of the highlights of our mini-break in London. Would definitely recommend anyone going to London to do one of these tours early in their stay.
Had a great day all day touring around London on all the lines! Guides and drivers were courteous and helpful. A great way to start your trip to London.

We initially jumped on the blue line but it played only music, no commentary which was disappointing. So we switched to the red line where the live commentary was fantastic. Laura was only a couple of weeks into the job but knew her stuff! We enjoyed spending the day soaking in the sun on the top level! Great way to get your bearings around London.
Great great great he was a great tour guide. The ride was too fast missed a lot of what I wanted to see. But over all a great experience
The personal commentary on the bus was excellent and Karen did a fantastic job on the walking tour which was included, we saw a lot and she was very informative

Hi. We had Big bus tour and it was really cool. You can hop on and hop off from many stops how many times you want and actually dont need metro to reach most femouse manoments you can do everything with Big bus. And when the weather is sunny and nice you just laying back watching the London listining to guide and chilling. Really recomend this trip. Also special thanks for guide Valdas who was really cool guide and who told us many interest things about London and England :)

I know we were in London but honestly £40 per adult!! We were only in London for the afternoon following football and thought we would like to take the open top bus on a round trip but not getting on and off. The young man I asked for the price was most surly and certainly did not inspire me to pay £40. He did not try to explain if any other options or pricing was available and was plain rude. My poor old dad actually thought I had heard wrong and asked another guide the price lol We expected to pay about £18 or £20 each but £40 was just ridiculous.

We had the London Explorer Passes and were able to hop on hop off for a whole day.
It was brilliant with supplied headphones or a member of staff giving a running commentary on all the sights. Thank You Big Bus!

David and Nanette

I chose Big Bus based on reviews. I planned (spending many hours, even days) our entire three day itinerary around the bus stops and perks (included a river cruise, night tour and walking tour). In theory it worked. But not in reality. Due to traffic (which is obviously not the fault of Big Bus), it took too much time between stops so we gave up (even though we had purchased a three day ticket) and learned quickly how to navigate the London Underground. We do Hop-On Hop- Off in most every city we visit (most recently, in addition to London, we also did Liverpool and York) to get our bearings and an overview of the area. Then, we ride and take advantage of the loop for transportation to the sights we want to see in more detail. We didn’t even have time to get to all the routes because of the time limitations. If you want to see high interest sights like the Tower of London, Westminster Abbey, Churchill War Rooms, St Paul’s Cathedral, etc, where the wait time is long, even with pre-purchased entrance tickets, and you only have three days there is not enough time to do all the loop with the hours of the Big Bus. I understand that the drivers have put in a full day of navigating through a busy city and dealing with traffic but that’s no excuse to be rude. We asked a question of the driver after we had to leave the bus at the end of the day. He was extremely rude in his answer. And he wasn’t the only rude driver we experienced. It would be helpful if an estimated time schedule (minutes after the hour of each stop and a “last bus” time) were included with the brochure and map so riders don’t get stranded far from their intended destination. The commentary (we experienced both audio and live, was, at best, mediocre. Doesn’t give enough information. One of our live guides was a young man who was very laid back, giving only the very basics. It would have been nice had he given us a few stories or anecdotes while we were sitting in heavy traffic. Instead, he just stood holding the microphone. Basically no personality or connection to the patrons. Another live guide was an older man who, I must admit, tried. It was during “rush hour”. The bus was full, riders were rude, talking among themselves, not managing their rude children, etc. The guide, never becoming rude, but was obviously frustrated. The City Cruises river cruise was nice. One of the staff gave a commentary as we traveled. He said it wasn’t his job but just shared his personal knowledge and experiences with us. Quite honestly, his was the best commentary we had all weekend. We gave him a generous tip. The walking tour to the Changing of the Guard at Buckingham Palace was a bust for us. I am a bit mobility limited. I can walk but I’m much slower than the average person. The time to meet the guide was 10:00, then a walk to Buckingham Palace. The guard ceremony starts at 10:30ish with the actual “change” coming at 11:00. While I would have loved to hear the commentary, I would have missed the entire event had I taken the walking tour. We would not have been able to see anything (due to the crowd) based on the given location of where the tour was to watch the ceremony. On our own, we arrived shortly after 9:00 and staked out our location on the steps of the Victoria Statue and had an excellent view. In my opinion, the walking tour should begin earlier to allow time for those who are not necessarily young and physically fit to keep up. Not all handicapped persons are in a wheelchair with someone pushing them. So, my opinion of my experience is...average, at best.

We did the walking Tour with Big Steve it was fabulous, his knowledge and placement for perfect photo opportunities still is mind blowing!
He is amazing that’s for sure, would highly recommend him to anyone!
Verry nice trip. You can see many manuments also guides are very helpful and competitive you can hear many interest things about London.

We really enjoyed the hop on, hop off bus. We did it for 2 days. Red tour has a person explaining as you go. Other tours have head phones and audio. Expect diversions around parliament buildings at the moment due to protestors. If you want to get somewhere quickly then use the underground tube. River cruise is great! Didn’t have to wait long for buses.

First time in London. I’m traveling solo as I am here for work so to maximize seeing the sights, I joined the Big Bus Hop On/Off tour. Extraordinary.... not only were the guides fun and education, they were incredibly kind! Major shout out to Big Steve. The stop that I wanted to get off at was temporarily closed due to the Brexit protests, and after walking over 13 miles already, I didn’t want to walk the few miles back to my hotel. Having not used the tube yet, Steve walked me over to the closest entry, helped me buy my ticket and even rode a portion with me. We talked about Britain, the US, the sights and we talked about the kindness of new people we meet. Steve was lovely and I will never forget his kindness as I navigated the city solo. Many thanks Steve and please tell your boss you should get a bonus or a raise - much deserved :) Lynda from PA...

Had a great time seeing London on the Big Bus Tours, we especially loved the walking tour with our guide Karen. She was very insightful on all the Royals and where to get us for the best pictures. She was great!

First time in London, visiting from the States. Big Bus made it easy to get around without any headaches. Shout out to our tour guide Rob for giving us an educational and entertaining ride through the city!

This tour is a great way to see London highlights. They have several lines that cover most of the well known attractions in London. They also have tickets to many of these attractions which can be purchased on the bus tour so you don’t have to queue up for a ticket when you get to the attraction - a real time saver. I bought a ticket to tour the Tower of London from the driver and bypassed the ticket office at the Tower.

Rob was a wonderful tour guide! You could tell he really loved London and it's history. He was very excited to show tourists around the city, and give them suggestions on what to do. He was friendly, funny, and professional. Rob made our experience great.
Great price, and takes you anywhere you want to go. Just hop on the first you see and jump off when you see something you like or planned for

The tour was good, Nobby, the tour guide was very good. we had an option for live or recorded guide. we listen to the live guide, by Nobby. if you purchased one day it is valid for 24 hours, we used it half one day and other half the following day.

We used the London Hop on Hop Off bus to get a good look around the city. They offer a good service with some of the buses having live commentary. Was very pleasant sitting on the top during the summer days. Some of the buses may be very full.

We bought the classic ticket which included 24 hr hop on/hop off stops, walking tours option, 1 way river cruise and 5 different routes. We came in a day before into London and explored a bit, so that we could leverage the hop off/hop on option a bit better.
For those with young children, we did the Little Legs Walking Tour. Which isn’t advertised a lot, but is available. Joe was our tour guide for the walking tour and my 5 year old son enjoyed it as it was accompanied with a scavenger hunt. It kept him engaged and Joe was enthusiastic and knowledgable. It was about 40 minutes.

We did the red route. It was the longest one and figured it would give us the most insight into the typical tourist sites.

Valdas was great...so was Chuck! Highly recommend!
Give yourself plenty of time to explore, what a great city.

WE booked the 3 day hop-on, hop off. The first day we took the routes we were interested in. The 2nd day we took the bus to the Imperial War Museum. It took 2 hours to get there! Then we had to walk an additional 20 Min. to the site. This is valuable vacation time spent on a bus stopping at places you don't want to stop and then waiting and even changing from our bus to another at Victoria Station for some reason. So here is how we would do it in the future
Buy the 3 day pass. Use the first day to ride the bus and see the sights from above. Take the tube to the sights of interest the next day. Take the included river cruise on the 3rd day and even the night tour. Just don't use the bus to get to and from your destinations. They take an eternity compared to the tube. The hop on bus is a great value for the river cruise and to get oriented and see the sights from street level.

We've travelled on the 'Big Bus' op-On Hop-Off bus in many cities and have always recommended it; however, London's tour did not meet our expectations. Part of the issue was out of their control, which were protests and the buses needing to be diverted. As a result two of the four tour routes were duplicates. The staff who were doing the live narrations, on a route that they were not familiar with, were not well briefed on that route; and the audio taped commentaries were not synced to their amended routes. The staff, nor the drivers, communicated any of this to the customers, many of whom were disappointed. If they'd communicated to the customers, they could have known what to expect and potentially taken another tour route, versus spending more than half they day touring the same routes. We are off to Paris next and were going to take the Big Bus, but have decided to try the competition instead.
This tour looks as if London's old tradition. It may have some value for people visiting London the 1st time. IMHO, it is a lot better and enjoyable to walk around, instead of taking this tour.

We have used this for two days and one more day tomorrow. A great way to get to know London. Today we did the walking tour at 10 am and started at stop #1 on the blue line. Caron did an amazing job and we were all so glad we took advantage of this part of our 72 hr pass. Hoping to do the river cruise tomorrow. Thanks again to Caron!

Driver and assistant doing commentator were totally unprepared for several road closures which meant access to over half the stops on the tour weren't accessible. Disappointing that there was no back-up plan.

It was the best choice I made taking our visitors from abroad on this tour of London. It was exactly as advertised and we saw everything at our pace. The hop on and off idea is the best and Big Bus hop on and off tour proved to be as advertised. I’ll definitely do it again. The rover cruise was the icing on the cake

On the positive side, the buses were frequent and we always managed to find seats on the top deck ( v. important with young children!). There were a variety of routes and stops and some special moments, such as crossing Tower Bridge. ON the negative side it was difficult to navigate. Buses sometimes had 'Red Route Westbound' on the front, sometimes something else such as a final destination. The Westbound bus we went on then proceeded to go east. On the return bus we jumped from stop 18 to 11 instead of 19 without warning. Better maps, better ways of announcing stops ( esp. if you are not using headphones- we didn't because we had young children with us) and better labelling of buses ( eg which colour route it was) would improve things. But generally it was a good service and gave us great views of the sites.

Arrived at the bus stop 12 at 7.15pm for a 7.30pm pickup, there were 3 scheduled busses for last night, no 7.30pm bus, no 8.00pm bus and the 8.30pm bus came past at around 8.45pm but the driver simply waved but not stop, what a waste of an evening standing at the bus stop waiting for the bus that never came, I would not recommend, will be trying to get our money back

Purchased the three day pass with discounted tickets for London Dungeon. All in all a good experience. Rarely had to wait longer than fifteen minutes for a bus and the guides were very good. Shout out to Sanya, who was excellent.

If you do anything, you MUST take the big bus tour with Joe. He is funny and incredibly knowledgeable. The ride was great and very fun. I didn't get off the bus just so I could finish the tour with him.
Awesome tour! Medwin did a great job. Very informative and lots of great stories about London! Thanks!!

The first bus has a tour guide that could barely speak any English. The tour consisted of something along the lines of: “This is a statue of King George. He was a pretty cool dude.” Second bus. Mic is not working, the tour guide is shouting and minutes after we get on the bus we are forced to get off and board another bus in front of us. Third bus. Still waiting for the driver OR the tour guide to show up.... I cannot believe I paid over $60 for this “experience”.
Stephen gave a very interesting and entertaining tour - would definitely recommend to anyone visiting London!
Very easy to book. All the staff very helpful. Great route and included a trip on the Thames. Perfect!
Our tour guide, Shanon was one of the nicest people I’ve met. She was funny and considerate and the best person I could ever ask for.

Good trip on the Big Bus London tour today with Lionel our guide and Oti our driver. Lionel was very knowledgeable. We bought our tickets on line which was slightly cheaper and gave us more flexibility as you have a month to use it.

The Big Bus Company has a number of different routes that cover everything you need to see while in London.
the route choices are excellent, the staff is very friendly too.

Visited the tour on our first day in London. We took many of the busses on all of the routes just as a way to get around as well as a way to see some famous sites. We enjoyed the red tour live commentary and Marcus was amazing! We did the royal walking tour today and Chris was our guide, he was informative and shared many facts about the royals as well as some London side commentary which was cool to hear. It was a good way to get oriented with the city and a cool way to see the sights as well as just get around for lunch and dinner, would definitely recommend to anyone visiting the city

Although London has excellent public transportation, it can get quite pricey if you don't want to go through the hassle of getting an Oyster card (4.90 pounds/trip!). We purchased the London Pass which included a Big Bus pass for one day. The one day pass allowed us to travel on any of the Big Bus routes. We chose the red line as it hit the majority of the sights that we wanted to see. Our guide, Will S. did an excellent job of providing great facts and amusing stories throughout the journey.
Nice commentary full of humor and was extremely informational and helpful in our sightseeing experience

Hey, so me and my Girlfriend decided to do the hop on/hop off bus tour through London and wow! We were throughly impressed! Bob & Oliver (driver and tour guide) were both absolutely outstanding! Both such gentleman and also great at there job!
Can't reccomend them enough! Make sure you look our for there names!

We spent a very warm and sunny bank holiday Monday riding various big buses around London. I just wanted to give a big thumbs up to Will on the red route who was fantastic. Lots of very useful and interesting info. ***** for him.
Only minor let downs were an extremely grumpy driver on the orange route who was very rude when we were late getting off due to being stuck behind a small girl on the stairs; and the infrequent river boat service.
Big Steve was great! He was very funny and made our first experience in London very enjoyable. He is very knowledgeable and a great person. Highly recommended!

Went on the bus and took a loop from our hotel near the London Tower Bridge. Easy to get on (an employee was at our stop and guided us through the process). It was a very warm day, but we sat up top and had a nice breeze. Great way to get your bearings in London, especially if it's your first visit.
Anna was a great tour host and gave excellent commentary on the red tour.. Drivers were courteous and the staff at the stops were most helpful

Rude staff... cocky.. up themselves and not helpful at all. Do not recommend!!
Came for couples trip to see if it would be good to arrange a hen party with this company. Won’t be using them now!!
We loved the Hop on Hop Off bus. The tour guides were very knowledgeable and very funny! It was a great way to start off our stay in London - showing us the layout of London!

We were entitled to use the HoHo bus as part of the London Pass. We tried to pick it up at their Buckingham Palace stop to go to the Covent Garden area. The bus stop was very confusing. Lots of people crowding around. Difficult to tell if they were customers or not. Finally, got to the driver to ask if he was going to Covent Garden area as it was not clear what route the bus was for. He said he was not going there and to wait for another bus. Not very friendly or helpful. Then a minute or two later another man appears and says the bus will be going to Covent Garden and to get on. I think he was a supervisor or something as he took tickets but didn’t stay on the his. Anyhow, we got on. The bus, however did not go to Convent Garden or anywhere near. We were told by the driver that the bus was going out of service for the day and to get off. This was at Oxford Street area, I think. We had to switch to another bus. That didn’t go there either so we jumped off Trafalgar Square and walked it. Not happy.
Very interesting tour, tour guide Laura spoke very clearly and had excellent knowledge. She made the tour interesting and fun

Doing the hop on hop off tour in our first time in London, enable us to explore and see what London has to offer. We have seen a lot of major attractions without getting lost in the city. Nice experience especially for the first timers like us. Friendly and knowledgeable staff too. Highly recommended.

Guides are amazing. We had Luca, Will, and the Harry potter look alike William. They all had a different spin on the sights with some wonderful British humour. Definitely go to Greenwich. The market there was the best food selection I have ever seen. Amazing place London. Best way to see it.

I can't recommend this tour enough. We were lucky to have the fantastic Elvis.... and no, not the original.
He had a fantastic knowledge of many things and coupled his guided information with a brilliant sense of humour, including everyone on board.
Thanks Elvis and big bus tours.
Will was great! He was funny, personable and I absolutely loved his dragon voice! I would definitely recommend to friends traveling to London. Also give the poor lad a raise! He deserves it.
Thank you so much will. You were the best. I likeed it how you told everyone what you had for lunch yesterday

We had a lovely time on the walking tour with “Big Steve”. He was extremely knowledgeable and witty. We highly recommend this tour with him as your guide if you’re interested in walking the Changing of the Guards while in London!

I have used a hop-on/hop-off tickets in the past, the one in Rome is the best, but with a different company. I was suckered in by a sale price that I didn't even get, thanks for tricking me. My first bus I got on at Baker, it was the Orange like, my driver's name was Eric, one of the greatest people I have ever met. I stayed on the bus the entire route (it was my first day, I was just checking out London), and when I was getting off the bus, Eric stopped me and asked why I didn't change buses, so we discussed my plans for a bit and he gave me great advice on what to see, where to go, the usual. That is where the pleasantness stops. Later in the evening, I decided to try the Red line with the live audio comments, like nice Eric suggested. HUGE mistake, the guy on the microphone had the microphone so close to his mouth that you couldn't understand him, then when paying customers asked him questions, he was very rude and told then to listen when he was speaking. Then he claimed that the marble arch was his last stop, and his bus driver said that same thing and that no other bus was going to stop, but why five minutes later a bus came by and stopped and picked people up and yes it was a Big Bus bus. Then I asked another worker about the night tours (at a different stop by Parliament Square) and he was rude and non-coherent, I just walked away and scheduled another London by Night tour through a different company. The idea of a hop-on/hop-off is excellent, but this company pulls it terribly. There are several other companies that offer this sort of service go to them. I live near DC and I have family coming to visit and we will be using a different company. Big Bus, I would suggest the you get Eric to train your employees because he was your only saving grace.

I think I got very lucky with the buses- never had to wait more than 10 min for one. I went when there were no closures so I was able to get on and off as I wanted though plan for traffic since sometimes the routes took longer than they claim. My reason for 4 stars instead of 5 was that I had one poor experience with a live commenter. While I met 2 nice ones, there was one who had little insight to share and was simply annoying going on and on joking about every rich man in London being her boyfriend. The other reason was on my very last stop of 3 days, the driver did not speak English and messed up the stop. This resulted in several people including myself getting off early and then having to walk to the next stop by the time we realized it.

Great way to see all the sites in London! We spent the whole day ( 11.00-18.00) so were able to cover all of the routes! Great live tour guide on the red route, pity there is only prerecorded tour guide on the other routes. All of the tour guides on the red route that we encountered were very knowledgeable but were also quite witty so it wasn't boring (shout out to Roland)! Would definitely recommend!

Such a good way of seeing all the main sights without all the walking, great for kids.

Top tip, get on at Green Park tube because the next stop is Park Lane and there's a massive queue that fills the bus, even at 9am.

Very helpful staff.

I went on the Big Bus Tour while on a short break, in London.
The tour guide Rob was very friendly & full of London Knowledge.
Encouraging people to ask questions, his commentary was great.
Rob really made my day.
Great staff, so helpful. Bus stops everywhere and easily accessible and very regular and interesting.
Great day seeing the sights of London Jess S our guide was awesome comentary very informative and buses run all the time

Touring with 14-15 year olds isn’t always easy. This tour was fantastic for everyone. We were able to see the city and stop wherever we wanted. The true gem, however, was our tour guide on the red tour. Nick was fantastic. It turned our tour into entertainment. My teen was laughing and involved even after we had to change lines. Had all our guides been like nick I’d have given this a 5 star rating. The rest were informative, but nothing exceptional.

I only stayed briefly but the tour was wonderful and the tour guide, Will was really great! If you see this, here’s a great pic😊 Thanks again!

-Canada

The route was nice and goes around all the main parts of the city, and our tour guide Rob was great. He interacted with everyone a quite a bit and was very knowledgeable. If you get on the bus, I hope that you get Rob and his funny quips as well!

The red route tour took in all the”must see” London sights albeit negotiating quite heavy traffic at times but our guide, Shannon was ever friendly, helpful and informative. Although, I believe, she is new to the job, only two weeks, she told us some stories and provided information in a captivating and relaxed way. Thank you.
We enjoyed this tour. We did this on a Sunday and traffic was pretty light. It was a good way to start our vacation to get a lay of the land.
We were very impressed with Valdas commentary throughout he has amazing knowledge of London and was able to inform us of all the many sights we were passing on the fly. Amazingly knowledgeable

My experience with big bus tours had a bad start when one of the guys at Green Park told me that the historic royal walking tour would be every 15 minutes. When I came back at 10.22am i was told that no, that walking tour only starts at 10am! Bought a classic bus ticket after all. The first bus on the blue line refused to let me on because of my dog. There is no fixed policy about dogs. But as mine qualifies with most people as "What a cute well behaved little dog" I was wedgie taken aback. After a chat with the green park manager and a phone call to the office I was clear to go. Never had any problems after that, everyone being happy to see a cute quiet "puppy".
For the last stretch of the red line I had Chris aka "Bill Clinton" as live commentator. It wad the best part. very knowledgeable and clearly passionate about his job. Good mix of accurate historic and miscellaneous information. With some humour and open for questions. Highly recommend him and Shannon the driver.

Had a great time with our guide Joe! He was very knowledgeable and, considerate of the age differential of our group (toddlers to seniors!) We got great information and surprisingly saw a ton of the attractions.

I have been to London multiple times, however I never saw it through Karen's eyes. She was extremely knowledgeable and vivacious. Her stories connected London's past to its present. I truly will Hop on the Big Bus next time I am in London.
We bought 3 days adults and they gave us one child and refuse to change it saying it was redeeemed even though they are the ones that messed up.

Spending a week in London, got the two day hop on hop off bus ticket with the cruise included.
Our first guide was LAURA was had exceptional knowledge, such an interesting trip. The next day we didn’t get a guide and were really let down in comparison to day before. Just shows what a difference a knowledgeable guide can make. Especially her history interests and facts.
Thank you.
We really enjoyed ourselves and will be going back to the places she pointed out to us like the Roman ruins discovered near St Pauls

We spent a lovely afternoon in spite of the rain on the red tour. Fascinating route plus, as a bonus, our tour guide Will gave a commentary that was full of interesting details as well as funny and even thought provoking. A great introduction to a great city.
Hello, This tour was helpful going around London especially the 2nd day of my trip familiarizing myself, etc.

Since my daughter and I had both been to London but my husband had not and we were short on time, I booked us on the 24 hour pass tour. Good choice!! This tour is informative and gives you a great layout of the city before you waste time trying to figure out where things are and what you want to see. Since you are able to jump off and on at your leisure, you can see which ever attractions interest you for whatever amount of time you would like! Some things you just want to look at but some you want to explore. This is the best of both worlds!

Fred and James were great, Fred was knowledgeable about the towns and was up to date with all ages and what they would be interested in.
Nick was very entertaining and was very welcoming whilst included everybody in his talks. I felt very lucky to have these guys as my tour guides when I got on at random stops.
Absolutely loved this bus company - the positivity started with the lady whom I bought the ticket from on a whim!! 5 stars!

We absolutely loved our ride through the top attractions of central London. What made the trip extra special was Will our guide. He was very knowledgeable about the city, and a great ambassador for it. Thank you Will

We did Big Bus on our first day in London and I can't give it enough stars. It's a fabulous way to see the city, and our nine year old son had a blast. Rob was an awesome tour guide and made the ride so incredibly enjoyable. This is a must do for anyone who is coming to London for the first time.

We did part of a bus tour but on that particular the cycle race was on so some buses weren't running and when they started they were really packed!

We opted for the walking tour with Big Steve and boy did we get lucky. Steve took us to all the hidden treasures that we never would have seen on the bus. Beautiful hidden views of the city, old streets, beautiful pubs, roman ruins... and some harry potter element sprinkled in too! he was a wealth of information. It ended up being a very special afternoon. So ask for Big Steve and do a walking tour with him. The buses are good too.

First of all, when going to London, doing a hop on, hop off bus is the only way to do it. Once we were about to hop on at St. Paul Cathedral and this rather talk and friendly gentleman from the Big Bus company asked if we would want to do a walking tour. We were reluctant at first but Big Steve was incredible. He made the walk incredible and fun. He was very knowledgeable and witty with his remarks. Big Steve was flexible with the small group we had and asked us throughout our entire walk if we were ok and if we wanted to stop to take pictures. My husband and I are on our honeymoon and because of Big Steve we have more pictures of ourselves together than any other part of our trip. I highly recommend a walking tour with this company and especially with Big Steve. The bus tour itself was less exciting and interactive because it wasn’t personal.

We made the most of our 1 day ticket and managed to get on 3 of the 4 routes. Apart from a hiccup on the morning waiting for the blue bus, we enjoyed our day and found it very user friendly. A great way to get orientated and also see some sights you don’t necessarily want to get off at. Some of the live guides were better than others.

We booked this for 48 hours, to go around London, we've had success in Rome and other places with the Bus tours, but half of the busses we had they were not announcing, and it was so slow along the River Thams. The boat ride that was included was GREAT tho, such a good historian and sights of London. We ended up using the tube more to get around the city than the bus tour.

Totally recommend this tour!! My sister and I had a great time. Easy to figure out and can use it as much as you want! Once the tour is over you could honestly use the bus as simple transportation instead of buying a bus ticket. Took a walking tour with Joe and he was excellent!! Definitely recommend a walking tour. You’re able to really see stuff as well as get more 1 on 1 with your tour guide. Joe was an excellent walking tour guide and was very informative of the city. If I am ever back in London I would do another tour.

Caron, being the absolute legend that she is, gave a wonderful tour, the perfect mix between informative yet entertaining. so good we actually stayed on the bus for the entire ride and then got off (at certain stops) on our second round. would definitely want Caron to live guide me through the hop on/off stops again!

As in all major cities, my husband and I booked a Big Bus tour in London. It never disappoints. We chose the route based on what we wanted to see, including the Winston Churchill War Rooms. A quick and easy walk from the bus stop got us to this location.

Visited London in August which we realized was the busiest time in London!!! Too many tourists!!! The Big Bus Hop-On Hop-Off was a good way to see the city but because it’s part of the London City Pass, they have too much captured audience which made it too crowded on the bus stops. Check other companies before you decide on getting Big Bus. The commentary guide was grouchy, not very accommodating to the queries of the tourist. 😕

I wish that I knew their names, because the entire crew--over the course of several buses--were fantastic! They were extremely attentive for my granddaughter, who occasionally needed her wheelchair. They looked out for her every step of the way, and I'd like to thank them!
Great tour with multiple places to see and very informative . Tour guy was very polite! We are very happy with the service !!!
Lovely tour, great guide, worth the money. Definitely a fun guide . Bring a coat for the open rood tops

Travelled in early June 2019, weather hot, the bus was packed with people standing down stairs waiting for a seat upstairs. The bus driver was lovely , the tour guide was helpful , you need to use the headphones to hear what she is saying. All the buses seemed to be full, so I recommend you get on & stand for a while like we did & then after a while you might get seats upstairs, you can't see out of the bus if your standing trying to hold on.
I thought it was a bit expensive, 4 adults & 1 teen in my group.

thought it might be cheesy, but turned out I really enjoyed the Big Bus tour around London major sites, great way to get the "lay of the land" when I was new to the city.
esp enjoyed the witty and entertaining commentary by tour guide Will. he had much more interesting things to offer, compared to the usual banter.

I’d like to say that I’ve been on a big city bus tour that was really over and above all others. Besides preferring bus tours with live narrators vs a recording, I find there to be little difference between them. So, if you like bus tours, you’re gonna like this one. If you don’t generally like bus tours, you’re gonna regret it.
Us, we like the bus tours. We do one in almost every new city just to get our bearings. Sometimes – sometimes – you even learn some stuff! I’ll give this one a good thumbs up – we got a live narrator and good times were had by all!

The tour was good but not all of the buses have the guide as suggested on the website. I had only 1 guide on the 1st bus tour and during the rest of the tour buses(around 6 to 7 bus change) there were no guide. All passengers had to follow the map and guess where we were, especially for those on the top deck. The driver has to scream every time he has to stop. Otherwise the top on hop off service was good.
day trip ok,heavy traffic forced guide ti eliminate some stops. Dont do night tour too much trafftc ,takes forever!!!
Too Good trips by the Hop-On- Hop - Off bus. Very nice trips. Happy to have this during the best part of the year. It was neither too cold nor warm during this time. Fantastic trip
Good choice with a good variety on the routes. They should have a staff member at each stop location as we got pushed out of the way at the same stop twice trying to get on the bus.

My daughter (12) and myself opted for a day out in London for some school holiday fun. We pre-booked a big bus tour to make sure we saw all the sights and this included a river cruise (and a walking tour, which we didn’t have time for on this occasion).
Really easy to find our bus, friendly welcome and fantastic tour guide - Christopher! We learned loads of stuff about our capital that we weren’t aware of and had brilliant views of everything from the open top deck. Thank you to Shandy our driver - for a smooth and safe journey!!

My family of 4 and I experienced a one day pass on the hop on hop off tour on the pink line. We were able to see London on our own terms. We leisurely strolled through the sights with no fear of where to find transportation. The open-top seating makes the view more exciting. We learned many fun facts with the English speaking guide and audio.

Having been on a few different hop on hop off bus companies, this was our first time in London and after some swift talk from a big bus rep at Tower Hill bus stop we bought a 48 hr ticket each ( 2 adults) The first day was good, sure the buses were packed due to school holidays which was expected in London. But had to wait quite a long time for drivers to change over at bus stops and in one certain time we pulled up at a stop and were told through our headphones to get out for that stop or to stay on for the next stop. We waited for quite some time and decided to go downstairs to find no driver so we got off the bus and found the driver and some staff eating their lunch inside another bus. Bad communication with customers we should of been told. But apart from this incident the bus tour went well. There were diversions and also a 2 day bike event which closed most of London’s streets down confusing both the bus drivers and customers over our 48 hr ticket but the company extended our tickets for another 24 hrs free of charge to cover the shortened routes from the bike race. This company also provides free of charge walking tours in group or individually and my partner and l had the chance to experience this tour which we learnt so much from. Also big bus offer discounted tickets to other attractions and can be bought at most bus stops . I’ve given 5 stars but I’m annoyed with the lack of communication with the drivers and customers when doing a driver changeover or break.

I like hop-on hop-off tours when I first get somewhere new, and in Dublin - it was the smartest thing I ever did on my first visit. It had the right ratio of buses to stops to sights to see. But in London, it's another animal. There is A LOT here, and it's very very busy. Aside from that, things are sometimes quite far from where they can even stop - and it takes a while to get everywhere as many others have said. Also if you kind of stray from "the attraction at this stop" then you aren't going to find a different pick-up point so easily, even with the app, which I downloaded to help with finding stops.
