It would help the company to better serve its customers to see when people are riding and where to.

With only 3 days in London, there will definitely be not enough time to do it all. However, with this tour I made it to know most of the places (famous) in London. Very convenient and accommodate to all kinds of visitors. Even though I have walked most of the stop points I still felt I was embraced with new information and it also gave me an idea where to go tomorrow! Thank you our tour guide Karen, she is very helpful and full of knowledge of London city! Next time I will definitely take an early ride to get to more places!

Bought 6 tickets on TripAdvisor since the price seemed better than some of the other providers. As another reviewer stated, none of the tickets had QR codes (bar codes) that the Big Bus Company people could scan so the Big Bus Company would not issue me my tickets at the Victoria stop where I tried to redeem the 'tickets' TripAdvisor had issued. The 'ticket' TripAdvisor issued through its subsidiary company Viator clearly stated that the ticket would be accepted if you downloaded it to your mobile device OR printed it (not only if you printed it) - I downloaded it to my phone because it didn't have a printer.
So, save yourself the hassle and DO NOT BUY FROM TRIPADVISOR!!! The only contact number I could find on the booking was for the Big Bus Company who I phoned when the first person I spoke to at the Victoria station stop insisted she would lose her job if she issued us tickets from my ticket (and who apparently has no-one more senior to speak to than herself), and who was only able to reiterate that they cannot issue tickets to us unless the ticket has a QR code to scan.
Why am I giving the Big Bus Company a bad review if TripAdvisor caused the problem? Well, firstly, TripAdvisor doesn't seem to have a way to review them (they would have got zero stars for this), but the main reason is the absolute lack of any will or desire to help in any way by the first person I spoke to. 4 adults and 4 kids were standing in front of her and all she wanted to do was tell us there was nothing for us to do except print the tickets (which we had no way of doing). Eventually we spoke to someone else who at least said we could get on the bus but we should find some way of printing off the tickets. When we got off to do the river cruise part of the trip (when we got to the Tower of London) one of the ticket people suggested we go to a local hotel (we were not staying at a hotel, so did not have access to a printer) and ask the concierge if we could print our tickets, which actually worked, but still cost us 15 minutes added to the other 30 minutes that we had wasted arguing at Victoria. Also, the Big Bus Company clearly has a relationship with TripAdvisor in order for TripAdvisor to sell tickets on their behalf, so they should have ensured TripAdvisor (a quite well known travel operator I would think) is not selling hundreds or thousands of tickets that their customers cannot redeem which makes customers like myself furious and causes bad reviews which makes people not choose them. But then, these bus companies seem like companies from another age - they just want to sell you a ticket and get you on a bus ONCE, all while trying to fight off the competition - they don't expect to see you again so customer service isn't really what they do. As we waited for our bus, one of the ticket 'touts' for one of the other bus companies seemed to steal a customer from the Big Bus Company guy and they almost had a bust-up in from of all the people waiting at the stop.
The tour bus was ok, and the river cruise (not operated by the company, but free with the ticket) was good.

I really enjoyed my Hop-On Hop-Off tour of London - sitting on the top tier of the bus, I got to see and enjoy some spectacular London weather (sunny and warm!) and see the beautiful architecture on the Red Route. I can't remember our guide's name (Jillian?) but she was quite knowledgeable about the area, and enthusiastic about showing her city to everyone on the bus. As I visited on March 30th, we had to detour around Trafalgar Square due to a Brexit protest, and that was actually interesting to see, in its own way. I was a little jet-lagged, but the Red Route was perfect for learning more about London, and I managed to Hop-off for my Tower of London tour at the perfect time for the last Beefeater Tour of the day. After that tour, it was very easy to get back to where the bus stand was - so I was then able to see the rest of the Red route, and the driver graciously dropped me back off by the Marble Arch where I knew I could take the tube back to my hotel. I would highly recommend this tour to anyone going to London - it was very good.

We used the red route bus throughout the day and were happy with the tour and commentary. However late in the afternoon we switched to the green route to take us closer to our hotel. This proved a disaster. We had to wait on the bus at stops for prolonged periods, swap buses for no clear reason and had no live commentary. We even missed our stop because it wasn’t announced and the doors only flapped open and shut. We should have walked this route, we would have reached our destination far more quickly.

We had the pleasure today of riding with Big Bus London tours, and specifically Emma on the Red line. Even though it was sprinkling outside, Emma’s personality and knowledge-sharing was pure sunshine. She shared some personal favorites and really made London come alive for us. She took care of the people on the bus and was super helpful with questions & answers. She even helped me by going down to the first level to find my friend Mechell to tell her we had a seat up top for her. Emma is a great tour guide, and Big Bus is lucky to have her. Emma really made everyone feel included during her educating us on the London highlights. Thanks!!
It was a great tour all around. Emma help and provided great information. She truly enjoys her job. Will definitely recommend to anyone who visits.

Had a brilliant trip last Friday (seeing the sights) with my sister and nephew from the States. I have never done this tour before tho they both have and it was great fun. I learnt a lot of new facts and remembered some of the old. The guide Lewis was fantastic fun he had a great rapport with the clients and was very knowledgeable and really made the tour for us. And even managed to make the Black Cab protest which took place and delayed us a little seem fun.

Went on the tour with my family ( family of 6: husband, parents, sister and 3 year old nephew ) there’s student discount, senior discount and children go for free( not sure how young)
We took the red line, as it stretches more around the city. We really enjoyed seeing the city and got off at tower bridge, did a separate visit there and then took the river cruise back to west minister.
Our tour guide on the bus was very friendly, engaging and informative ( 5 star, Louis👌) so was the other one on the cruise.
Enjoyed this very much as a family and would highly recommend it.

We got a family 3-day on-off ticket. The buses were never on time. We waiting close to an hour at a stop in the rain that advertised buses every 20 minutes. It included the city cruise up to Greenwich. The schedule said the last cruise was around 3. The guides told me they haven't updated the schedule and the last cruise was 7 since it was now Spring. They were wrong--both the printed schedule and guides--the last cruise was 6. We wasted a TON of time waiting for buses in the rain. The tube is cheaper and faster!

I've done many hop on/off tours and usually love them. I was disappointed because there was no narriation. The audio head set was working but it simply was not on point. I've enjoyed these tours much more when there was a live human that pointed out the sites and shared the history and significance. Overall very disappointed with the experience and there was not even a hello from the staff.

We purchased a 2-day tour through the TripAdvisor site for March 25 and 26.

This is a good deal - especially if you buy multiple days. We saw a lot of London and we saved money on taxis and ubers. Keep in mind, if your intent is to get from Point A to Point B in a hurry, this is not for you. If you want to take your time and see the city, this works well.

The tour guides, for the most part, are excellent. We had 3 different guides over the 2 days. Two of them were friendly, energetic and informative. The other, it seemed like there were a thousand other places she'd rather be the day - no energy whatsoever.

Unfortunately, we had a dreadful experience at the start of our tour. We got on the bus at the Tower of London stop. We had bought our tickets through Trip Advisor and I guess this is not the type of ticket they are used to getting. The ticket-taker insisted we needed to have a bar-code. We showed him what Trip Advisor gave us and he kept repeating the same "bar code" line over and over. When I asked if we could call his supervisor together, he refused to help. It wasn't because they were busy - we were the only people there. He just couldn't be bothered. I called the Big Bus helpline myself and explained. They put me on hold, called the ticket taker and sorted it out. It worked out ok in the end, but it put me in a foul mood to start my tour. The ticket taker was one of the rudest, most unhelpful people I've dealt with in a long time. If someone from Big Bus would like to contact me, I can give you details so you can pinpoint exactly who "helped" us. He should be fired.

Very impressed with young tour guide Francesca. Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable. My only complaint with BRB is regarding the three day pass which expires within a 72hr period. Today being a washout I will not in future purchase an advanced three day ticket.

I used Big Bus in Rome 2017 and although I didn't have enough Euros to buy the cheaper 5+ hour ticket, I used my card to pay using the portable devices that the conductor staff/tour guides have. Unfortunately, all the machines of several staff didn't work and then caused issues with my card in cashpoint machines, so one of the staff suggested I visit the office located a short walking distance away. The manager was friendly and very apologetic when I showed him all the receipts and then cancellations, offering me a free day pass and free coupons to use in London, on my return to the British Isles. As the Northern hemisphere was in the height of summer, the weather was not suitable for me, so I kept the vouchers and passed them onto friends who were touring London in 2018. The Rome bus tour was fabulous and I stayed on hoping to see all the attractions, before I realised there were several routes and that the bus I was on terminated in the early evening at the start point. I couldn't use the hop on and off part as I was nursing a foot injury from a long walk while nursing my fracture. I would certainly use the Big Bus facility for London as I loved the tour bus ride with tour guide, that operated in 2004.

We did the 48-hour pass and started on our first day when we arrived. We were so tired that we just stayed on the bus to see the city. It was a very nice and relaxing experience. The second day, we hopped on and off. We took it to the Tower of London then we got on the ferry ride (free with the 2-day pass) back. The ferry ride was excellent. Overall, I highly recommend it.
Very disappointed in the tour guides. English is not their first language. They are very hard to understand. Not much fun when you don’t know what you are looking at.

We purchased the 3 day pass with the boat trip from the London Eye location. We had 10 of us and one mobility scooter passenger. The bus supplied a ramp to go on and off with only one operator who gave us a hard time about getting off one bus onto another which is often. You can only take a color route so far and then you transfer to another route of a different color, but you can get off and on at any stop. We enjoyed the comments and information provided on the headphones as we made our way around London. You may want to catch a taxi at some stops as the walk to site could be long (ex the zoo stop is over mile to walk after getting off).

As a rule I dislike negative reviews but if this saves just one person the hassle we had then it’s worth it. We bought our 2 day ticket online along with tickets to Madame Tussaud’s and the London Eye. I rang first to check they were mobile enabled as we weren’t able to print the voucher. Their office told me it was fine just save the pdf. Showed this at the first stop and ticket seller was very rude and said I’ve needed to wait for next bus as he hadn’t time to give me a ticket. Waited for the next bus and driver tried to tell me the same thing until I insisted he dealt with it. Just gave me tickets for the bus element. Then queued for an hour to get into Madame Tussaud’s to be told that what I had was no use as it needed to be on a paper copy so we were directed to an Internet cafe. Given we had queued for over an hour I pleaded for them to help which eventually they did agreeing to let me email them the voucher to print off there. Not easy as the printer was on a different floor and the girl dealing with us was on a crutch but still went up and down the stairs about 3 times trying to print it. She was amazing and the most helpful person we met all day - give this girl a pay rise as she went above & beyond (she does not work for big bus by the way!) Later we were at London Eye - this was a joke. Again we queued to be told that we needed a paper copy. We eventually got this. Queued up again to be told you need to go to the London Eye ticket office to get a pass. Queued there to be told that no we needed to go back to a Big Bus rep on the street to get a print out ticket which you then have to bring back to the ticket office to convert into your London Eye ticket. So it took us nearly 2 hrs of queuing to see the London Eye. After which we had to wait ages for a bus. Once on it we were told that several stops were closed to us because of the marathon. It might have been helpful if this had been pointed out when I had rang initially to book. We abandoned Big Bus and used the underground. Today we will not use our 2nd day of our ticket instead opting for the underground. My advice - buy an Oyster card and use the underground and just pay for attractions when you get to them. Above all - avoid Big Bus!
Very disappointed that Mobil tickets not accepted since there’s no barcode. We had to print out the hard copy. This is not as advertised and very inconvenient and time consuming.

The bus tour was a great experience. It was nice to ride and listen while getting the lay of the land on our first day in London. It was a little confusing getting on the bus. The little building was closed and basically we were supposed to find a guy standing on the corner to turn our digital ticket into a paper ticket. That could have been explained better. Otherwise, it was a lovely experience.

Joe was a great tour guide on March 14, 2019. We weren't sure if we wanted to spend the money on a bus tour or if the tour would be worth the time on our last full day in London. WOW! We are so glad we bought tickets. Joe was full of information, very friendly and inviting. This tour ended up being one of our favorite things we did! Highly recommend!!!
Very easy to use. Excellent services. Best of London attractions included. A must have for your London holiday. Gives you the history of the place you are visiting , location also included. Loved it.
Emma did a great job with her narration of our tour. Much better than a recorded tour. The red tour is a must do. We really enjoyed our time.
We had a very nice excursion and we enjoyed the narators but they changed the cruise's programm and we missed the visit to Greenwich

we are so glad we booked this in conjunction with madame tusauds and got a 30 percent discount. we only had 4days in london with our 9 year old and this activity was truly worth its money. especially if weather is not so good, but even with good weather it takes out alot of the walking from one point of interest to other.
very very good

We will be spending a few months in England and just landed. We wanted to hit the ground running so a hop on hop off bus tour seemed to be the perfect way to get our feet wet. These tours in any city are a great way to get an overall feel of the city and figure out where to spend more time. The buses have an automatic audio roll that explain major sites long the route. The real treat of these tours are the Live guides who are a plethora of knowledge and mix it with their own mix of humor and personality. We used the hop on hop off to get to a few sites and then at the end of the day we got onto the Red Line to ride most of the loop with Lewis. He was great! He interacted with all guests and made everyone feel a part of the tour. He made an extraordinary effort to greet people in their native languages and was able to put a smile on everyone's face. In traffic he was able to use his knowledge to keep the tour going even though we were not moving very fast, he kept us all engaged. Lewis was also able to make great recommendations for food including where to enjoy pancakes for pancake day! If you get on the red line and have Lewis as your guide, you are in for a great tour! Thank you!

This crowd do not deserve your money. I paid £67 for 2 x 1 day tickets. Arrived at St Paul's and waited well over 40mins for first bus, no update from rep at stop. In this time there were over 8 buses fron Golden tours etc. Bus came and packed to the rafters, could not get on. Waited for next bus, got off at Aldwich for Covent garden for lunch, went back to stop, waited 30mins, bus overfill and standing downstairs only. Got on only to get to cruise, this was a lot better and went well. Avoid this crowd, reps don't care at all. I thought paying a little bit more would give a better service, wrong. Golden tours seemed a lot better. Very disappointed. Will definitely not use again. Avoid.

We stayed in London for a few nights and we purchased the Big Bus Tour 48 hour ticket, we used the bus many of times to get to different places. We went on the red route around London and the tour guide (called Fay) was very helpful and polite and she ensured that everybody was able to ask questions, and she knew lots about all the attractions! We found that these tours were a very good way of seeing many different areas of London, and all the Big Bus Tours staff were very helpful and friendly 🙂
Very friendly tour guide -louis- and thanks to him, i now know a lot more about the history of London!

My girlfriend and I took her brother who was visiting London from the US on the Big Bus tour and it was a fantastic way to see and experience London.

Lewis was our guide and he was very charming and charismatic. His deep knowledge of the sights and landmarks made the whole trip worthwhile and his humour really lit it up on a cold, wet day.

We did one of the tours on Feb. 7th.
It was awesome!
We frist planned to hop off and on, but our Guide did an amazing job and it was lots of fun listening to him, so we decided to stay on the bus.
Sadly I don't know his name :(
We hopped on at trafalgar Square around 12.30pm and he took his break around 2pm at hard rock cafe. Meh.

This tour is a great way to see a lot of sights in a short amount of time. And with an awesome Guide like ours its informative and fun! :D

Despite the cold January weather, the bus tour was great! We sat on the top deck and loved listening to our tour guide, Jo. Not only was she extremely knowledgeable, she was funny! I highly recommend this company and tour. And, if you can be lucky enough to have Jo, even better!

Despite the day being bitterly cold we enjoyed the open top tour (half under the shelter at the front of the top deck). Saw all the sites but couldn't take advantage of the river cruise due to our time restrictions that day. Loved the tour and out guide Lewis/Louis was informative and amusing!

We didn't use the Hop-On, Hop-Off bus much but we enjoyed one trip the most and that was with Marlene the live tour guide (not the an audio guide). She was fun and interesting and even sang for us :-)........it was a nice change (to the audio guide) when you are tired and exhausted from seeing the sites. Thanks Marlene!
Took the tour and was lucky enough to get Emma as a live commentator. She was so lovely and very knowledgeable!!

Caron was a great tour guide on our trip- so passionate about the history of the city and made us feel included. I would highly recommend this bus tour for a fantastic viewing of the city and to learn an extensive amount of knowledge. My boyfriend and I, had the best time and would love to thank Caron for that! She made the time great! SO worthwhile!

I did the Hop on Hop Off Red and Blue route with my boyfriend while we were in London last weekend. I learned so much from our tour guide Big Steve. We enjoyed it so much and had such a great time listening to Big Steve that we didnt even get off the bus!! Best part of our trip to London.
Emma is a great guide, thank for a lovely experience, perfect historical knowledge and very cheerful way of presenting information

The Red Line tour was a great way for my daughter, 3 y.o. Grandson, and I to get an overview of the sights in London on our first day here. Emma was our tour guide and she was such fun...very informative and helpful (she even gave my grandson a snack because he was getting hungry and a little grumpy)! We now have a better understanding of London’s history and know the places we want to visit for the rest of our trip! Thank you, Emma!

I was on a quick trip to London for work and had a morning off before getting back to reality, and picked this bus up at the Tower of London stop and did the red route around back to the Tower of London stop; if you don’t get off of the bus but just enjoy the ride, it takes about 2.5 hours. This was a nice way to see some of the major sites, and you can take clear pictures if you are on the upper deck. Make sure you use the provided headphones so you can hear the tour guide give you the local color and history of the sites you are seeing. Overall, this was an enjoyable experience and well worth it.

Our guide Emma was SO knowledgeable and gave really interesting information which really held my attention and that of my 8 year old grandson. She is clearly very passionate about the history of London and she was able to share this and enthuse others too. We had another male guide take over towards the end of our tour and he just told us info in a rather dull and monotonous voice.

I was prepared to give this 5 starts. Until they sold me tickets to an already closed Tower of London, as I got off of their bus at the Tower. Through emails and many calls, I believe they did the right thing and refunded us, as that was our only chance to go to the Tower in London. I believe the tour guide should have know the venue was closed before selling us the ticket on the bus, stating we'd save through buying from them. Otherwise, if you buy the day pass, and hop off at the places you want to explore...the buses ride every 15 minutes. Catch the next and use the 4 routes to your advantage. Don't forget that one free ride on the Themes RIver (behind the Tower of Lodonon - dock) is included. Go on the boat ride. It's nice and included in your price.

My family and I chose the Big Bus company for a sight seeing tour of London. Unfortunately there seems to be no limit to the amount of people allowed on board so what was meant to be a bus tour turned out to be just a bus ride for the princely sum of 185 pounds. It was impossible to see any of the sights on the opposite side of the bus due to the aisles being full of people. In order to return to our accomodation at the end of the day we chose to take a taxi as there was standing room only on buses arriving at St Paul's cathedral. Extremely disappointing. I suggest the company needs to provide more buses for busy periods.

Do not waste your money! The signs at the bus stops were difficult to see from the bus and the drivers did not call out the stops. The cruise was good but you can do it on your own. Information not forthcoming from employees.
Ian was superb with lots of historical facts as well as bits of trivia and of course with that lovely British humour blended in. Well done and I’m glad to highly recommend the tour as well as Ian!
Took the tour in DEC2018, even while quite cold outside the tour was very nice, especially thank to our guide Emma. Thank you Emma, thank you BIG BUS.

Ian led us on a great tour of London, on the Red Line, with his personal antidotes. The tour on Friday, December 21, on a blustery winter day. We can't say enough about how good the tour was. I highly recommend it

Overall great tour, best way to see all the sights in London. However, we were told wrong time by our conductor and then missed the last boat cruise due to being late. Ended up having to pay an extra £6.50 for a trip up towards Westminister and then a taxi back home. Other than that, tour was amazing, really dissapointed how it ended...
Well I certainly learnt a lot and I thought I knew most things. Emma provided details and anecdotes that made it all come alive

I had my week in London all planned out but my plans fell through - I bought a ticket on a whim - and I'm so glad I did. I've done a couple of these bus tours before but never through this company - and it was head and shoulders above the others. Emma was so knowledgable about the city - not just the regular historical facts but little bits and pieces that most people don't get. It was like we got two tours - the official tour and Emma's tips and tricks on the side - places that don't get listed on the everyday tourist attraction list. On top of that, she made sure that everyone on the bus got off at the correct stop, taking time to talk them through maps and plans, helping them work out the right place to disembark. And managed to make it feel like a private tour at the same time. Thank you, Emma - it was a lovely afternoon.

A friend and I visited London the first week of December and enjoyed our Big Bus experience. We had two tour guides giving live commentary on the red line and appreciated both of them very much. JoJo is a ton of fun and made us smile the whole trip with her warm, engaging style and sense of humor. She was also kind enough to show us to the tube after her shift ended, as she was also heading that way. We enjoyed our experience with her so much--she set the tone for a fun afternoon/evening! The next day we rode with a gentleman named Rick/Rich who was a great guide in a different way. He knew a tremendous amount of detail about various locations, his elocution is stellar, and he was quite a lovely gentleman. Please note the guides are most grateful for tips if they have served the riders well; we were appalled to see most people hoping off without acknowledgement.
Lewis was so entertaining and knowledgeable that we didn’t got off at our intended stop, so our visit to London Tower will have to wait for another day.

Taking the last bus on Tuesday, being the only family on the bus, Lewis still made it a very exciting and unforgettable experience for our children educating us on London’s history and landmarks. You are awesome Lewis! Thank you🙏🏻

A nice way to get to know a city and find the most interesting places easily. But traffic in London is so extremely busy that walking and using the underground probably gets you around faster (and cheaper).

I bought a 2 day ticket and spent most of the time in really slow traffic. This is not the fault of the operator but if you want yo get the most out of your time in London, the tube is the best way to get between attractions.

My friends and I purchased a 24 hour pass on our trip to London and it was a waste of time and money. I do not recommend it!! The buses didn't start running til around 9 and ended around 6, we spent more time on the bus getting to stops because of the congested traffic. Our last stop we waited 45 minutes when they are suppose to pick up every 15-20. Its so much faster and easier taking the tube!

We have never been to London before, and decided on our first morning to lean into the touristy piece. The hop on hop off bus was a great way to see the whole city and the major sights. We used the red line only for the bus.

The highlight was our tour guide Emma. She was funny, smart, really friendly and interesting. She had great tidbits about the city that you could never hear about otherwise and she made it very fun. One of the best guides we've had!

The London pass is a bit expensive, but having access to this bus makes it all worth it. My husband and I walked and walked and walked and were so tired of it. When the day came for our London pass to work, we couldn’t wait to use the bus. The tour guides were funny, helpful and kind. We learned a lot and honestly sat on the bus for a few hours taking the different loops. I would HIGHLY recommend this over any kind of other transportation.

My mother and I were so pleasantly surprised by the beautiful experience offered by the Big Bus Tours. Our guide Emma provided us with exquisite knowledge of London, its history and its inhabitants.
warmly recommend

Purchased tickets for the Big Bus tour online as this company had the highest ratings. Found the stop at Victoria Station fairly easily and waited about 15 minutes for a bus to arrive. There was an agent there who took our tickets, but failed to mention anything about a tour guide - only advised that English was on Channel 1. We decided. to sit downstairs due to the rain, plugged in our headsets and waited for the audio tour to begin. After about 10 minutes of hearing only music on every channel, we headed upstairs to discover a guide talking about all the stops. We have no idea why it wasn’t being transmitted downstairs and missed everything from Stop 22 until about Stop 2.

We debated about just giving up, but everything turned around when Emma - Big Bus Tour Guide Extraordinaire - started her last tour of the day with us. She immediately made us feel welcome and had us laughing right away! Emma not only knew all the fun and interesting points of interest — she added spirit and personality to the tour. We were only going to ride for about an hour, but stayed on the entire way back to Victoria Station because of her. Wish she could be our tour guide throughout all of London!

This was very disappointing, as it was not as advertised. First, on a cold rainy day there was no heat on any of the busses. Next, there was NO live commentary or guide on any of the buses we took on the Red Route and third, the recorded commentary was very minimal on history or interesting facts. We would have paid less and learned more from a warm taxi.

I don’t know how it is with other people but Emma was great. She was funny and informative. The tour was perfect.
I will note that traffic can slow things down and if you need to get somewhere in a certain time frame this may not be for you. The subways are amazing her and cheap.
As for the tour, I would advise everyone to do it. The stops are marked. The guide was awesome. We were even able to buy Tower of London tickets off the bus and didn’t need to wait in line. Loved it.
Our tour guide, Emma, was amazing. We wished she could be with us all day. This tour is a must-do in London. Pretty easy to navigate.

We hoped on the red line (central london) three times and 2 of our live tour guides were really excellent. Tabea and Emma - thank you! Your humour and kindness was a real treat. We switched to the blue line (best of the west) at 3pm on a Friday in November. We should have connected seamlessly, but the blue bus drove away just as the red bus arrived! The staff should have prevented that from happening. We waiting 30 minutes for the next blue bus even though it should come every 10-20 minutes. It was rush hour, so perhaps that's the reason. The blue line was not nearly as good since the tour guide was recorded instead of a live person. Overall, we're glad we used the bus tour, it was part of our London Pass and definitely worth it.

Enjoyed the tour very much, was able to see the main sights in a day. What made it great though was our tour guide Emma, she knows her stuff and her passion about London is evident. Really enjoyed her commentary.

Did the tour in November. Our guide, Lewis, was very entertaining and knowledgeable, and engaged every party who got on the bus. He also made sure everyone had headphones and maps. Driver, Leroy, worked some kind of magic navigating the large bus through the narrow streets. Highly recommended. Only suggestion is the bus should keep towels on hand to dry off wet seats on upper level.

Plug in your headphones, sit back, relax and enjoy seeing the sights and sounds of London. Our guide "Memet"(Pictured Below with me) was funny and very knowledgeable he really made the journey for my wife and I. Others on the bus really got a kick out of his humor. We hopped off to have Lunch in Soho and jumped back on afterwards to finish our tour. The price is very reasonable. We will definitely do it again.
Cathy (may be with a K) was the live feed on our bus. She was so enthusiastic and you could tell she loved every moment of sharing London with us. She was the bright spot of our day!! Great tour!!
great way to see the main atractions in london. great live guide too! many things u can only know from local ppl. loved Louis and Martha! very entertaining and so many informations to share!

I had a great time, especially in the buses with live commentary. I remember Kathy and Louis being two of the guides that I loved most because they were so friendly but I also learned so much from them. If I get back to London, I might do this again just because I loved all the guides so much and want to hear more of the them.

We rode the bus two days in row with various tour guides and hands down Ian was the best tour guide so far ! He was very informative, entertaining with great sense of humor. I will definitely use this service again in other countries.

We booked the red bus for 48 hours which we do in each city we visit. We started at about 2.30 on a Wednesday and went around the purple route. We had plans for the evening so that was all we could do that day. We were not worried as we had plenty of time in the next couple of days to explore. We took the bus to Baker street the next morning to visit Sherlock Holmes Museum. It was very wet. After the museum which was fab, we got back on the bus to continue visiting the interesting spots around. The traffic was very hectic and we were stuck in traffic a lot which meant we did not have time to get off and visit The Tower of London as by the time we got there it was very late in the evening. We did get to see most places from the bus. So the next day we knew we would not make it on the bus to anywhere in good time so decided to take the underground to see Buckingham Palace as we were in control of our own time and could get back in time for the airport. So a little bit disappointing but there is nothing the bus could do about the traffic. The drivers were lovely and information good. Some people left the bus when we were stuck in the traffic.

Took the Big Bus Tour while in London for the Eagles game. I've taken these tours in several cities and I find them rather informative and enjoyable. Kathy was our first guide this particular day and she was amazing. Very pleasant, cheerful and informative. I had a great time and enjoyed the tour and information provided very much.

We did this tour last saturday (oct 27th 2018) with 6 adults... We bought the tickets for £210 (£35 each). Big Buscwas the most expensive hopp on hopp off nus in Londen, but also the best one they told us. Als ok they prommised this and was the only company you don't have to wait longer then 5 till 10 minutes for a new bus to comming at a stop. 35 each is expensive, nut not a problem if the tour was great. We were with two pregant lady's so we decided to do the tour.

We started with the red lane on point 23 (Victoria station) and the tour did well. Till we arrived at stop 1. We all have to step out of the bus, and get into another one. This bus was almost full, so we had no other choice then take our seats on the first level, while it was cold. Of course we know the company can do nothing anout the weather, so no problem. We continued the red lane and stepped out by the tower of London. From here we walked to the river cruise, which was great. After this tour we wanted to take the blue lane, and the easiest way to get near the blue lane was continue the red lane from there till we are at stop 4, Marble Arch. It was very very busy at stop 18, from where we wanted to take the bus, and we couldn't catch to first one, because it was full. We have to wait almost 15 minutes for the other one. Unfortunately we couldn't get in these one too... finally the 3th bus wad coming, and we make sure we get in. We ended up standing in the bus, nothing to hear, nothing to see. My sister is pregnant for 31 weeks, and even she had to stand. It was also very busy on the road (not the fould of the company, I know) but it takes 45 minutes to get to Marble Arch, where we wanted to take the blue lane. 80% from all persons in this bus wanted to take to blue lane from t h ere also, and when we stepped out the red lane, we already see a long row of people who were waiting for the blue bus, and many people were joining this row.

We decided to walk from Marble Arch to Bond street station and take the metro to our hotel from there. We were cold, tired from standing in a bus which was way to full, and disappointed in the company... This was our last day in Londen, and whe haven't seen everything...

Did the 3 day tour, great way to see around the town and stops at major tourist attractions, It beats trying to get around in your own vehicle in traffic or walking. There is ALOT of traffic, sometimes you spend a while in traffic on the bus, which takes up a lot of your time. Stops at most major attractions between their different routes, you really only have time to do one route a day, due to traffic etc. There did seem to be enough buses so you don't spend much time waiting at each stop. The buses that have a live commentary are so much better.

We hopped on the Big Bus tour at Marble Arch, and planned to hop on and off all day visiting sites with one member of our party who had never been to London. We stayed on until the Tower of London because Kathy was so great! She was knowledgeable, funny and really seemed to enjoy her guests. Which these Canadians really appreciated!! Thanks again Kathy and hope to catch you again!!

We looked forward to learning about London and its significant buildings and history on this tour. If I recall correctly, the red tour was supposed to have a live guide providing commentary. Instead we were given headsets and mostly listened to music throughout the tour. Occasionally the music was interrupted by a message about which bus stop we were approaching and reminders to take one's belongings as one exits the bus. In the three hours or so we spent on the bus, we heard perhaps five interesting tidbits of information. What a disappointment.

We bought the 48 hours pass which got us on the bus for three days since it's truly 48 hours. We saw so much and used it as transportation for a short period. We loved getting a feel for the city our first few days. Definitely a great way to get oriented and see a lot in a short amount of time.

we really enjoyed our several trips on the Big Bus! It made our stay in London enjoyable and we got to see so much more travelling around than we would have done! Actually saved us money having to get other buses, tube, taxis etc
The guides are amazing, full of knowledge and really friendly! recommend this highly to anyone

This is the second bus tour we've done in our visits to London, and Big Bus Tours is by far the best. Emma, our tour guide, clearly has a lot of knowledge about London and makes the tour even more enjoyable.

Would wholly recommend

We took the T-2 tour which covers the Central London area and the primary tourist attractions. The idea is to get the the "big picture" for the remainder of our stay. It worked again for us this time and it made our subsequent walking tours and city navigation much easier. The visibility from bus is very good even through the window areas. Suggest the tours with a live narrator vice the headphones. Since we did not get off of the bus, cannot comment on the advantages/disadvantages of the bus stop signage. Make sure you understand the numbering system for the various tour options because each bus is labeled accordingly with a front sign. Also, as mentioned in previous reviews, there are numerous operators of bus tours in London so know which bus you are trying to get onto. We heard our driver explaining that fact to several travelers trying to get on the wrong bus.

I was visiting France and wanted to hop over to London on my free day. I was disappointed with how expensive it costs to get there. Based on the way people talk about it I thought it would be easy and cheap. It was not. After the worst British Airways experience my 14hrs in London was cut down to 7. To make the best of a bad situation I got on the Big Bud Tour. This tour saved my day. In the 3hr round trip I got to see all the sights of the city that I knew about and wanted to see. The tour guide was ok and didnt really share many exciting facts, but I had Google.
Thanks Big Bus for making the best of a bad day,

I have been on big bus tours before, but this was definitely the best one yet. Our tour guide was Jo Jo and she was knowledgeable, funny and gave us all kinds of tidbits that I had never heard before. She was simply delightful. Even though it was raining, it was most entertaining! Sadly, we got on halfway through her tour and another guide replaced her at the beginning of the actual route. Jo Jo was the best. Hands down.

I took a ride on the red line with JoJo. It was informative and enjoyable. Truly recommended. Been on a few tourist buses with recorded comments. This is not the same. Jojo's got good British humor too and the tour was interactive

We had high hopes for our 1 day London tour however Big Bus did not deliver. Our tour was on October 9th and buses were few and far between taking upwards of 20 minutes at stops for a bus to arrive. Several of our busses were standing room only therefore we did not have access to headphone ports. On busses where we did have access, the headphone ports did not work. The live guides and drivers were less than pleasant, probably because there were too many people and not enough busses. At one point, our bus stopped at turnaround stop and all the bus guides were mingling around an it appeared none wanted to get on our bus. I am assuming this was because our headphone ports were not working. Another issue we encountered on the busses was that stops were not clearly indicated, it depended on the live tour guide and whether they remembered to announce the stop. Due to the delays in busses and other issues we ultimately decided to get off the tour and just walk to our destinations, this turned out to be much faster and pleasant. This was the most disappointing and poorly run tour I encountered during my 10 day vacation. I will never take another Big Bus tour. Very disappointing.

Jumped on a bus near the end of our London trip and it was a great way to put together all of the parts of London we had seen over the week. Emma was our guide and she was great. Easy to hear and understand and full of facts and insight. If you've walked London and done the riverboat then top it off with the Big Bus for the full experience.

Monday was a well organized trip round the sights round London . Tuesday we used the green link to get to the boat trip that was free with bi bus. things were fine getting to the boat had a lovely trip on the river getting back to kings cross was not as good buses were running very late from Covent garden and there was no big bus colleague there to keep us in formed of situation.

I have always enjoyed the Hop-on Hop-off tours, I feel you get a good feel for the city. Maybe London is just too big or it's just getting too busy, but while the red line was very interesting with a live guide, the other lines suffer from lots of traffic and redundancy. My sister and I consider the Night Tour useless, basically you rode around the city at night with the same audio tour as during the day. Nothing defines this as a special tour. The river cruises were enjoyable and would do this again. I think the company need to look at their routes and see where they can make some changes to make all the different lines more enjoyable for people who pay not an insignificant amount of money. Next time I would probably look for a smaller company that can give a more personal tour. There use to be a couple of different companies doing the hop-on hop-off thing but it seems that they have all been swallowed up by one company. Too bad - maybe a little competition would be a good thing. We did enjoy the live guides and maybe they should put one on every bus especially with the traffic slowing everything down to give more information about one of the greatest cities in the world. I do recommend if you're looking for an overview, but maybe one day so it doesn't get repetative.

Emma was our tour guide! Absolutely the greatest! Funny and very informative! Loud and clear lovely voice, Loved her.
the bus is very comfortable, generally a great way to cover all the London hot spots comfortably =) xx

We purchased two-day hop-on-hop-off tour tickets which were >GBP70. Buses were always slow, delayed, and late. Since we stayed in Kensington we used the Blue line to connect to the other tours. The Blue line felt very neglected - there were never any live tour guides and buses were constantly stopping for 10 minutes at stops while the attendants tried to sell tickets to potential customers. The pre-recorded commentary was sparse and felt like an afterthought. There was one great tour guide we had on one of our Red line buses who was very helpful and actually seemed to enjoy her job.

What was really disappointing and why I'm giving the one-star review was how much we were looking forward to a night tour (included with the 2-day ticket). We planned our entire day around this, showed up to the stop 15min early, and waited. We ended up waiting 40 minutes, no bus showed up, no attendants at the stop, nothing. Called their office but of course nobody picks up because it was 9pm by then. If the tour was cancelled, we should have been given a heads up through either a sign at the stop or drivers on the day tours giving announcements. Just no communication whatsoever, which is a terrible way to run a business. Next time I would just ride the Underground/local buses - cheaper, will get you to your destination faster, and won't leave you stranded at night.
Did the red and green route today. JoJo was our live tour guide on the red route. Very entertaining and knowledgeable. Thanks JoJo.

What an amazing way to get to know London and what an amazing tour guide! Ray was more entertaining than the city!
Would come again simply for the commentary!

Had to stand for most of the way
Should have more busses on. Waiting for a bus is way too long In the end we caught the tube to get to Tower Hill Commentary was funny

What a disappointment! Stuck in traffic, minimal information unless you hop on the bus with an actual person giving information. We even stopped for over 15 minutes for an "unscheduled" stop in which the driver left the bus. Not sure why- bathroom break/lunch break? We hopped off and walked in the rain through Kensington Park rather than wait for him to return. Another day we went to the Westminster stop only to find out it was closed and had to walk to another location. A complete waste of time. I wish we had not bought the pass and instead used the Tube or our own feet (which we did in Paris and explored to our hearts content!). If you have trouble walking, then it is worthwhile. If you can walk or take other transportation- I would not waste time sitting on a bus!
Emma was a great tour guide. Explained the meaning of Soho and even how pirates used to sound. Thank you

Looking forward to the sights and getting off where we chose.
Emma was our tour guide and was exceptional. Her knowledge of the city and her passion for the history made us stay on the bus until the final stop at Tower of London.
Emma gave lots of excellent tips and suggestions to get the most out of our London experience.
Would highly recommend!
Great introductory tour of London with amazing live commentary from Kevin! Everyone seemed to be laughing and enjoying t

We had just arrived in London and it was late in the afternoon. We were on Regent Street at the Gant shop when we bumped into this incredible ambassador of BIG BUS TOURS. He convinced us to forward purchase the premium tickets for 2 days including everything. Whilst we have done this before on other trips, my dad who was with us had not been there and this would be a good way to see the city. His demeanor, sales pitch, humility and friendliness helped us make up our minds. He is a fantastic employee and should be well guarded or he will be recruited someone else.

The tour was also great. We had no issues at all. Well done.

Almost a five... Emma was 5.5/5 but that didn't compensate for some of the other staff who were surly and rude - especially after we had travelled some distance after a long day only to be told that our ticket didn't include the night tour (we only tried to do this on the recommendation of staff who had said it was included). No sympathy from the lady on duty; just made to feel like we had soiled her bus! Lots to see and hear about. Emma is a wealth of knowledge and a great enthusiast. A good overview of London. Best do the Red Tour and then spend your time on the attractions to hear about - more than enough to fit a week!

We took the big bus tour around London and almost went around an entire lap using the pre-made audio which was informative and nice. We got on a 2nd time with the intention of only finishing our lap but we were blown away by the knowledge and information Ellie had about all the sites that we decided to go around a full 2nd time just to hear what she had to say about all the sites!!! Thank you Ellie

I would recommend this tour to anyone who wants to visit the major sights of London. We did the Red tour with our live commentator, Ellie. Ellie was extraordinarily knowledgeable. She kept the tour very interesting. I think it is a great way to get an idea of which places you want to focus your time on and go back to visit...or just hop off the bus and take a closer look!

This was included in our London Pass and I am so glad we did it. It was useful to see the layout of the city and learn about every place before we decided which ones we would tour and explore more of. Super useful in getting around for the day as well.

Awesome guide she is a local and knows many details of this fabulous city. Thank you
She shares many details of famous travelers

It was amazing the open top on the bus you could see so much more than the down stairs (bring a nice and warm jacket though to stay warm, I learned that the hard way) the live commentator Ellie you could tell she knew a lot about the area and she was really nice. Any way definitely recommend it recommend it for anyone that wants to have a really good and detailed look around.

4 of us decided to use big bus for two days. Boarded from Kings Cross station. The guy selling ticket on the bus was friendly and was also selling additional stuff such as Madame Tussad's, London Eye etc. We only bought two day ticket onboard the bus.

Two day ticket included night tour (worth doing it) and one way river cruise (worth it). It is a good way to see London, however we experienced following issues:

Bus gets stuck in traffic at several spots in London. July heat can quickly make that unbearable. Also it quickly adds to the time you are spending on bus rather than seeing attractions.

You get multiple printouts for ticket and one ticket that is valid for two days. No one tells you that you must save that for BOTH days in order to board again. There is no way for BIG BUS to print a duplicate ticket. We unfortunately left ticket at hotel on day 2 and could not board until we went back to get the ticket. We were not the only ones, came across other families in similar situations. May be a good idea for staff to remind tourists to hold on to their tickets for both days.

Other issue was that next day we bought Madame Tussad's tickets onboard - BIG MISTAKE. Although it is cheaper onboard and the guy will tell you that these tickets give you priority entry - there is no such thing when you get to Tussads. You have to exchange those vouchers with actual tickets by standing in a VERY long line at Madam T. It took us 2.5 hours yes, 2.5 hours to get to final ticket window. It is sheer waste of time for tourists. Buy priority tickets onlne at tussad's site. They may be more expensive but will save you TIME.

On Positive side, Big Bus frequency is good. The evening tour is non stop and it is worth it. However our driver never announced when the first night tour ended and 2nd began. as a result lot of tourists ended up remaining onboard for most of 2nd round.

River cruise is also included and it is lot of fun. Our captain was very funny, so he made it even more enjoyable.

We had a one day hopper with the London Pass so we hopped on early and spent the morning touring around seeing some really great sites until we got to Tower of London when we started touring sites. No complaints about this first part of the day but it went down hill after that. Tried to catch a bus near St Paul later using a map the driver gave us and wait about 15 minutes at a spot only to find out there was no bus coming as they were detoured (we were given an old map). So we walked several blocks to find another one. Decided to head out on another bus lines to see some sites but seemed to go around in circles. Finally made it out to the Marble Arch to try and catch the Blue line just to ride it to see the sites. Waited over 45 minutes and one never showed up. It was getting late and we needed to be back at the London Eye by 8pm so we decided to grab the Orange since we had plenty of time. Made it as far the Baker St. where our driver told us to get off and gave us no further instructions on how and where to catch another bus. Saw one waiting up the street so we all ran up there and asked the driver if he was going to the London Eye and he said yes. We proceeded to sit there on the bus waiting for who knows what for another 15 minutes. Finally under way and made it to the London Eye just in time for our slot. Can't believe it took almost 2 hours.

I was hoping for a better experience. Was traveling alone and looking for a way to get around the city sightseeing. The bus stops are not always easy to locate and when you need to transfer to different lines you need to make sure you are getting on the correct bus. Many will stop but some go east or west, etc. They also need to make the announcements for stops more user friendly. They have the stops by number on the map, not by name, but when they announce the stop they announce it by name. You don't know which stop you are at without asking the drivers. Some are friendly, some are not. One thing that helps is they have attendants out on the streets in the busier areas so they can assist you.

Two ways of using the Big Bus. If you just go for one day, don't hop off, unless it is to go to a different route. Complete each loop in the same bus and you'll get to know the City in one day and you see all the must-do's in one seating. This is a good option if you have a single day in town or for the first day in a multi-day trip.
If you plan to use the bus as a means of transportation and hop off in each interesting place, make sure to secure a 2 days ticket, because one day is not enough. You barely will be able to do one of the three routes. Try to get a plan of the routes and plan your stops carefully taking a look at closing times of attractions. We got to the British Museum just in time to see the Rosetta Stone and were immediately rushed out at closing time (5PM!).

Great way to see the city and get a lay of the land. They take you around to all the key sites, and add commentary. Our tour guides were so-so, the first better than the second, but overall not a big deal. Just driving by the sites and seeing where they're located is helpful.
Highly recommend doing this, it's easy and affordable. We bought our tickets directly from a guy selling them on the street by Hyde Park, but you might want to buy in advance.
Make sure to grab headphones when you board, and ask what channel the live narrative is coming from, we had to figure it out when we couldn't hear him talking.

We really used this bus tour as a mode of transportation opposed to taking the tube. We rode the different lines and transferred over to another line as needed. Examine the different routes ahead of time to determine a schedule.
The weather was nice and it was fun to see all the action from above of the crowds around Trafalgar Square and Piccadilly Circus where we had walked the previous day.
Even sitting in traffic was fine, since it allows you to look around and take it all in. The live guide on the Red Line was very interesting and informative.
The only criticism is that we waited a little long then we expected and most of the staff were very good.

Me and my five friends only had one day to enjoy London and we chose the Big Bus Tours. All of the employees at each stop made things easy and fun. The bus was amazing and luckily always had seats available. It can get crowded in the afternoon, but all six of us were always able to get on at any stop. The bus and boat tours allowed for great photo opportunities and lots of interesting commentary. Would definitely recommend!

As part of our visit to London we spent the better part of one afternoon on the Big Bus Tour. Our guide was very knowledgeable and provided great insight to the many historical buildings as we drove through the city.

If there is a downside to a bus tour, photo ops can be tricky. The upside, we saw almost all of London on the Red Line tour.

Highly recommend this tour.
Hopped on and off the bus a couple of times. Both times the guides were very good spoke clearly and were very informative of all the various sightseeing highlights.

Don't buy one day ticket online!! The Concierge at our hotel gave us a brochure on the BigBus tour. It listed an app, which we thought would be cool, but in order to download it, you were required to purchase the tickets first. Rather than wait for the concierge, we purchased over the phone BIG MISTAKE! (Plus, we never even used the app!) While all the tickets online claim one-way river cruise, when they swapped the ticket vouchers for the tickets, the fine print stated it didn't include the river cruise, which we didn't find out until we were ready to step on the boat. (The "controller" claimed that the online classic ticket doesn't include the river cruise, but their website claims it does.) They kept our original receipt, so we have no proof. So very frustrating! Other people at the boat ticket window were having the same issue. Also, we had 3 different guides - two were pretty good - one was terrible - he mumbled and we could never figure out what building he was talking about. Overall, a very disappointing experience with a company we though was reputable.

Kathy was our first and later our last guide for the day and what a bubbly, friendly and helpful person. Thank-you for our introduction to all the wonderful sites and history of London!! You are a super star, please stay the wonderful person you are😘🇿🇦

We bought the 24hr ticket and kicked off with the red tour early in the morning, availed of the river cruise in the mid morning, took a break for lunch and finished off with the blue tour. The red tour had a live London guide - Joe who was great fun + plenty of jokes and banter. The blue line doesn't have a live guide but still enjoyable. Pretty good value.
Emma the tour guide is very informative and pleasure to listen to... very much enjoyed this tour. Thank you Emma!
Jo and Adrian (the tour guides) was so funny and made my first tour & trip to Europe so fun! If you can get them I would suggest it

So disappointed with our expensive Big Bus one day classic tour around London.
We had a guide more interested in talking about her favorite movies than about the sites we were driving through. She really wanted a good review and reminded us several times. I thought she was friendly but not professional and should not have been leading our tour bus!
And though it is not the fault of the bus lines, the construction around the city kept us stalled in traffic for long periods of time. Should have done a walking tour!

We chose to do the Big Bus tour last week while traveling in London, WOW we are so glad we did so. This tour allows you to see all the major destinations of the city and get great insight and history on everything. The buses were clean. We hopped on and off multiple times throughout the day and kept getting tour guide Ellie.

Ellie was a great guide, super funny, personable and very knowledgeable on all the destinations and sites. We enjoyed this tour a ton but even more so could not stop talking about how much we enjoyed Ellie, she is a great asset to this company and if we came back we will definitely seek her out for future tours around London.
We had a great time on the Red Route with Ellie. She was full of great information & made sure we made it to the last blue line bus in time!

We enjoyed our bus trip. It was amazing to sit on top deck and see the sights. Laura was great narrator with interesting facts and fun humor. She was also very gracious about helping people on the bus with directions of where to go as they got off the bus. She was so patient with the riders. Free earphones to use as well. I wish I had more time so i could have done the other routes. We used our London Pass for this, and it worked smoothly. We loved it.

We book a tour on the Big Bus in London when we arrived on Aug. 31, Emma was our guide and was a wealth of information. She was born and raised in London and gave us insight in to the town only a local could. Our trip was was enhanced because of her enthusiasm and knowledge.
great way to see a city pity about the traffic but the tour guide more than made up for this with her enthusiasm faye i think her name was
We enjoyed the Big Bus tour. Ian from New Zealand is a great guide. It’s an easy and fun way to see London.

Absolutely the worst hop on/hop off bus tour I've ever taken. Not really a 'tour'--it was a sad and expensive replacement for public transportation. First of all, the drivers--every single one of them--were extremely impolite and unhelpful. When asked a question they would simply point or say 'down that way to the end'. As for guides, never saw, or heard, one on any of the 6 buses we used. They pointed to a bin full of earphones and told us to take one. Traffic in London is horrific and with the huge amount of commuters and the road construction closures, it took us 3 hours to get from our hotel in Earl's Court to the Tower of London. The ONLY redeeming feature was the Thames cruise that was included with the 2-day ticket purchase. It was pleasant and fairly quick and there was a charming guide. As for day two use of this ticket--NO WAY. We learned to use the Underground and were much happier.

This was great way to see London on trip to the capital.
I used the buses many times over our 3 day stay and the river cruise too.
For the most part the commentary was very informative apart from one trip whete the young guide was being bombarded with questions from a group of American tourists and didn't quite have all the answers so tried to resort to comedy, he failed.
I would certainly recommend this service and go so far as to say it's value for money if you want to see the major parts of the city.
We did get stuck for quite a while on one of the main streets due to building works but the guide kept us interested with various facts

We visited London for a sightseeing weekend, and decided to go for the 2 day pass on the tour - the overall experience was excellent, as part of the 2 day tour you also receive a boat trip down the Thames. The staff both on the buses as well as the support staff at the various stops were excellent - really made our overall sightseeing trip excellent.

I've used HOHO buses in many cities for siteseeing and had very good success. Maybe the 1st week in August is the wrong time of year but the buses were super crowded as was all the sidewalks and street traffic. Maybe that's just London. While aboard the details, directions to look, timing of the pre-recorded Guide - really left a lot to be desired. Travel time to sites due to the traffic left little chance this was an efficient use of our time. Is there a better way? While the advertising indicates you can hop on hop off other routes that was limited to two locations where you could change routes - meaning we spent more time aboard than desired.

We spent 2 days on the hop on, Big Bus. We really enjoyed the live tour guide, James, sitting across from us on the upper deck. He was fun, witty, knowledgeable, and could answer any question you threw at him. We never had to wait more than a few minutes to catch another bus. The weather was wonderful while we were there, so sitting up top with sunshine was really great.
We noticed we were the only couple to give James a tip when we got off the bus. Hey, tip your guides!!

Second city that we’ve used Big Bus (other was Paris), and were well pleased. The various lines covered all the sights in London, and buses were generally frequent at any stop we boarded. Would definitely do again, in available in the next city that we visit.

Buy your ticket online ahead of your visit, and save money off the cost of purchasing same day. Online also has multiple package deals with some other venues.
Emma was a fabulous guide all the way around the tour. A life long history buff herself, she told not only the facts, but lots of interesting anecdotes. Very enjoyable day!

This was a great way to start our vacation in London. We bought a one day pass and hopped on near our hotel, road to the Tower of London, took the related cruise back to Westminister, walked a bit and hopped back on for a full loop back to our hotel.

We had two tour guides and there was a bit of a difference but both were very good. It is obviously better to be seated at the top of the bus, but it took a little waiting on the first bus before we could get up top. Both tour guides gave live commentary and pointed out various spots. If I were to guess, there is a specific set of things each guide covers and then each one adds their own items.

Even if you cannot get to the top, plug in the supplied headphones (or use your own) and you can hear what the guide is saying on Channel 1 (in English).

I can certainly see why there are some negative reviews as I saw one bus driver (not guide) talk rather sternly to some boarding the bus as they did not seem to understand what they were being told. Instead of being patient, the driver was a bit rough with them.

Otherwise, overall a very nice and worthwhile experience.

i think this is the fastest way to see London esp when u travel for the first time in the city. The easiest eay to get to know London then next time u will know where to go next. The live tour guide helps us to get to know the history of the city and all other trivial things and without getting tired at all if u stay on the bus first and decide where to stay next.

Going to London solo for only two days, I found this big bus tour pretty convenient as it has many different lines going through central London. One thing I also enjoyed is the river cruise included in the ticket. However, I believe this is the most popular company and I did notice other hop on hop off companies were less busy. Might consider going with another company if you don't want crowds on the buses and long wait times.

We visited London for the first time for 3 days and decided to buy the 2 day Bigbus tour with the riverboat cruise and boy was it worth it. Being new to London we wanted to see as many of the landmarks as possible knowing that we could only visit one or two in a short time. Bigbus tours with their various routes certainly helped us achieve that. It is easy to do with plenty of buses, the staff are all very nice and more than happy to help and the tour guides are great (Ian was our favourite ). Al in All, we will definately be using Bigbus tours again and highly recommend them.

I used my two day pass to help me navigate my way around a lot of the attractions. Didn't get off at all stops, but checked out what I wanted to see and found the closest stop - saved me quite a bit of walking. Also used the inclusive river cruise to return from Tower of London back to Westminster Bridge thus getting a different perspective of the city.

Love the Big Bus. We always start any new city with a bus ride. To date Philadelphia was the best and Barcelona the worst. The difference? The guide.

Caren was delightful, engaging, and informative. She provided details well beyond the recorded message - details, history, and facts about what we were seeing. She also share what we could do at each stop, how long it would take and how much it would cost.

My only suggestion - check the facts on Mary, Queen of Scots!

O u t s t a n d i n g !

Had a great time on the bus with Maddie and Phil! She was very informative and much appreciated. We did the red line and blue or green (cant remember which other one) and both were good to get an idea of London and where we wanted to re-visit. I also purchased the London eye and cruise tickets with our bus pass. We didnt have time for the cruise, but the London eye was great fun (fast past is the best way to go). would highly recommend Big Bus London

The tour hits most of the highlights of the city. On top of that, Jojo (the tour guide) provided interesting facts on all of the locations. She is a really good story teller, that really gets you engaged, with an occasional touch of humor. Thanks for that!

I thought the hop on/hop off experience was great. We purchased through our hotel and there are a number of stops. We also did the night tour and also the boat tour but we didn't even get the chance to do either because we were pressed for time. It was a 3 day pass, and it may be better to get the pass as I believe it was 37 pounds for 1 day or 50 for 3. It also gives you the time to take your time and explore more. The app was cool that is used and it is pretty efficient when telling you when a bus was nearing you. The only thing I did not like was that it ended at 6pm for the bus tour, other than that I thought it was a great buy and opportunity to learn about London.

I pre purchased a Tour for my family of 6 - we were only going to be in London for one day so we wanted to see as much as possible
we ere delayed at the airport and by the time we got to the London eye it was sometime after 5 pm .
We were told we had to get the representative to get our voucher and were sent on a wild goose chase - they were nowhere to be found . We came home to find we were
charged TWICE. I have tried to contact them and SURPISE no one gets back to you
Find another company - there were several we saw during our short stay ......

Allthough already our 3rd day in London it was priceless to join the Red Line tour on BigBus. We took the complete circle, not to miss any of the interesting, funny and sweepning comments of our fantastic tour guide Emma!
Thanks again for this beautiful and charming tour. We followed some of her "secret" recommendations and had a great times in London.
The Red-line tour through central London is clearly to recommend, the blue line is a nice add-on for the afternoon, but not as entertaining (missing life commentary)

I had booked a tour of London on Big Bus through VisitBritain.com. I was not disappointed: the Red Route of the classic tour was the perfect introduction to the city. Riding the bus upstairs enchanted my 8-year-old daughter, and my wife and I loved being able to see how the city fit together right after we got off the long, overnight trans-Atlantic flight. Barbara, our color commentator, was a delight - she seemed to know everything about every place we drove by, and was full of laughter, good humor, and great stories that kept us all entertained. I thought the tour was good value for money, and a great way to "meet" a new city.

Big compliment to your absolut great guide - we’ve learnt a lot about London and London’s secrets. We got an answer to every question especially about the Royal’s wedding rules.
If Nick will be the guide guide again we will be back!
We have done Big Bus tours all over the world, and this was the best!! Thanks to Emma for a five star tour!! We will be telling all of our friends.

I took the Red Line, which brings you all around Westminster, Southwark, and the City of London. The live commentary by Ian was great--even when we were stuck in traffic for a bit he kept things lively and interesting.

The River Cruise was definitely the best part. Beautiful reviews. Great tour guide. We have mixed feelings about the bus tour. The bus tour guide was sometimes very engaged and entertaining and sometimes not. We got a good overview of everything with the bus tour and good history but in hindsight we probably should have just done the tour from Victoria Station to the Tower of London and then seen the rest on our own. The traffic (no fault of the bus tour) resulted in a tour that was about 3-1/2 hours long. And the second half of the tour seemed to be more traffic than tour.

We have used this company in other countries, were ok but not this time in London. Not enough buses to cope, always full and long time between pick ups. There was a lot of the opposite companies buses driving around.

I purchased two tickets online for a day out in London. We waited at the correct bus stop number 13 but although other bus tour companies were stopping as normal, no Big Bus Tours buses came past in our direction. No staff available to help, although there were staff from some of the other tour companies. Eventually I saw a member of staff on the other side of the road and they explained that due to an incident earlier in the day (not of their making) the buses had been rerouted. They said that their buses going in the other direction were stopping further up the road. I explained that a whole load of people were waiting on the other side and no-one was aware of this change. The app and online map are totally useless as they do not show that the two stops are not opposite each other. Eventually we got on a bus and it was totally overcrowded. There was no room upstairs so we had to sit at the back downstairs. Although I understand they are not supposed to have people standing, there were at least 10 people standing downstairs. While the bus was moving things were not too bad but when the bus stopped in traffic there was no air flow through the bus. People were looking very unhappy and in the end one American party said they were going to give up and use the Subway (Underground); another party got off and grabbed a cab. We got off and did the same.

So my observations:-
Communication with customers was non existent - we are not mind readers.
The app and online real time map are not fit for purpose - they are inaccurate and are not updated in a timely manner.
The driver missed stops repeatedly and because the online real time map was so poor, it was difficult at times to know exactly where we were.
The overcrowding downstairs, exacerbated by people standing, was totally unacceptable and I regard this as a serious safety issue. The lack of air downstairs made this worse.
The view out of the windows downstairs is appalling. You really can't see anything much.
I have not had value for money and will never use this company again. I suggest you look at alternatives.

Conclusion:-
Don't waste your money. Get an Oyster card and grab a regular 'red' bus.

We had the witty Ian as our live guide and 5 stars for his commentary. He was informative and just so much fun. We learnt a lot. However we caught the Orange Link later and that was only recorded info which contained more advertisements than info hence the 4 stars. Thanks Ian.

As a Londoner, I have been meaning to do this for years. Took the family on a tour of London today. Ellie our guide was welcoming, informative and chatty. Her interesting snippets of information helped make for a great day out. Thanks Ellie! We saw London in a while new light!
Good to get your bearings and learn a bit of history while visiting London. Our tour included the river cruise. Recommended.

Got the tour close to my hotel on the Blue route, the recorded information was very interesting. Changed to the Red route at Marble Arch for central London with Nick as the tour guide, Nick was really knowledgeable, very interesting and quite funny which made the experience most enjoyable even when the traffic was congested! Changed over at The Tower of London for the Thames river boat cruise back to Westminster which was included, another amusing and informative commentary on board. Highly recommended!

I always use the Hop-On Hop-Off tours to begin any vacation in a new location. Always convenient and focused on the major sights. The guides can also help you get off for sights not on the tour. Nice and relaxing as well...once your feet get tired and you just want to sit and see things over again.

We landed in London at about 6:30am, so we got on the Big Bus to relax and hear about London. The first bus we got on, we couldn't really hear the tour guide through all the static, and I was very concerned we had wasted our money. However, we switched to another bus and ended up with a great tour guide and very clear sound. The commentary as we took the tour around London was great, and I'm very glad we chose this activity for the first day. As we spent about a week touring around London, we went back and revisited places we had seen on the tour with a bit more knowledge we would have had otherwise. However, I would not use this as a way to see different places (as in, the Hop On Hop Off feature), as traffic in London is awful and it is much faster to walk or use the Underground.

I found interesting, the recorded given information was very useful and they explained many historical things that happened and personally I did not know, however company employees in bus were not very friendly and open to hear you or answer your questions: most of the time they were rude and impacient, not very friendly, I conclude not an experience to repeat...
Was on the tour with Emma and we learned a lot about London and its history! Highly recommend it especially if Emma is the tour guide.
