Got lucky and got on the red route with Emma. She was amazing. Emma clearly loves London, its history and sharing it with others.
Thank you, Emma!!

We did the bus tour two years ago and when we came back to London it was on our list of things to do. The great thing is there are three different tour routes, not counting the link route. These cover most of London, the main tourist locations and you can hop on and off the bus at any time and onto another route. All buses have maps and complimentary headphones for the audio commentary. The red line has live commentary from tour guides and the other routes have pre recorded commentary. It’s informative and also tells you which stops you need to get off to transfer. We also did the river cruise which was really nice, we had great weather, great views and the crew are friendly, helpful and do a commentary while taking you on your cruise. This time we had the return ticket, there are different locations to board the boat and although the queues can be big they move quickly due to the size of the boat and frequency of the service. You can then step off the boat and board the bus again, although keep in mind the last bus times or you’ll have to make your own way back. All the staff on both the boat and the bus tour are approachable and helpful and we found them to be very friendly. I’d recommend getting a map for the tour and looking it over to see which routes you definitely want to take and which stops you’d like to get off and view something. Planning the day can save you some wandering time.

My wife and me enjoyed 2 fantastic days visiting London with Big Bus Tours.
But the best was the professionality of one of the employees ( Mr.Abduallan Kuddache) who solve us a logistic problem providing us an EXCELENT service. I used to travel around the world and very often I 'm not receiving a good service when I'm in trouble for some reason.
In this case this employee make the difference and I just can strongly suggest this company not only for the great bus tours but for the humanity and quality of the staff as well.

If you have never taken this tour in the past, let me put you at ease. Take it. I liked this tour for many reasons:
1. The live tour guide was good in London. Not all tour buses are "live" speakers, rather it's a recording. I do NOT like the recorded tours. They rarely are in synch with what you are driving by at the time. For example, Hamburg, Germany's tour was terrible for this.
2. The bus will drive around to different locations and make (probably) many stops. I say probably because it depends on the route you are taking in the city you are taking the tour. I rode both London (Great) and Hamburg (Good).
3. Some tours last longer than others (London's red line was like 2-3 hrs.) and Hamburg was (2-2.5 hours).
4. Sit up top if it's a sunny day. The bottom (closed section) gets HOT in the Summer. If there is air conditioning, I didn't notice it on both buses. We sat up top and 1) you can see more and better site lines, and 2) the breeze keeps you comfortable. Don't forget to wear sunscreen.
5. There are designated stops. In London they are clearly marked and made it pretty easy to find the bus stop. In Hamburg, good luck...I didn't see any signs...was terrible. They also ONLY took cash. I didn't have it and need to tap the ATM to acquire Euro. They were cool and waited but I really feel like I was ripped off for being a non-German speaking person. Weird they didn't take a credit card!!!!!!
6. I still rate this tour as a 5, why? London was great. The tour guide was awesome. Hamburg's audio stunk. Only German (I get it)...but the audio portion was terrible and out of sync. I'm trying to appreciate your country Germany and it's pretty hard to do that when I can't understand a word and the stuff I'm looking at isn't what is being discussed. Also, the content, to be frank, stunk too...not enough details. I did however like driving around and seeing the various areas of Hamburg. Signage is terrible in Hamburg....I mean it's really bad!

I would definitely recommend the bus tour. Careful when choosing which "version" or "route" you wish to take as some make different stops and speak different languages and offer audio vs. live speakers. Definitely a great tour to get to know the city quickly for future walking and touring. I recommend this as an initial "kick-off" tour when you are first in the city. Also, I'm mentioning now, as you are driving around, the bus will make stops and you can hop-off or hop-on the bus. Some tickets vary, where they expire 24 hours after your ticket is activated initially and others last for days. Pick which one makes sense for you.

Enjoy. I will be taking another one in different cities as I travel in the future.

The big bus London is a good way to see London without walking everywhere, and what I really like about this kinda thing is that you can either sit on the bus for hours and change routes or you can hop
On and off on different spots of interest. There is different types of tickets that you can buy like the 48 hour ticket where night tour and boat cruise is included. The only problem about this thing is traffic, and that you may have to wait for some time at a stop before the bus gets to you, but that is not the company’s fault so whatever. One thing I want to say is that some of the staff are a bit loud and a tad bit creepy in the sense of being big mouthed with each other which makes it less tempting to ask them about stuff, but there is also a lot of nice people in the staff, also they are easy to find around so that you can buy tickets! 🇬🇧

We took the Big Bus Tour with the river cruise. According to the brochure, each red tour is "guaranteed" to have live commentary in English. First ride had it, but information was scant. Second red tour did not have live commentary at all, neither did the 3rd! The blue line only has prerecorded commentary which is boring and mostly consisted of background music instead of information. The final trip on the red line did have live commentary; however information was repeated multiple times, I'm pretty sure word for word. It was difficult to hear and he got upset multiple times because people wanted to get off prior to their stop. The only part of the day that was enjoyable was the live commentary on the river cruise, until the guide announced he was going to hold a bucket for tips before you could get off the boat. I thought it was a joke, but there he stood, bucket in hand blocking the exit! Don't know if the other bus tours would have been any better, but I would probably try a different one! Supposedly 18 people didn't show up for work that day and when I asked whether we'd have live commentary on the 4th ride, I was advised "maybe". So much for a guarantee!!!

our live-guide on the Big Bus today as Ian. He did an excellent job! Due o the cycle-event today the usual routes were partly blocked. The tour took way longer then usual. Ian made the day. He know all sorts of fun things to tell us. He was personal and witty. Much respect for his patience and humor. Thank you Ian.
Rob Anita Frouke
Had done this tour in the past, years ago, and it was great. This trip, not as good. I guess it is luck if the draw. Some of the guides are on it and some are not.
Marta the guide and Rudy the driver did a great job of giving information on the tour, I enjoyed it,

there are a few options for the Hop on Hop off buses for London. At first it was hard to decided. In the end we went with Big Bus and it was a good choice, we noticed there where more Big Bus buses (there are lots of Original Hop on Hop of also, it seemed so they could be good to) than the other brands, you don't want to be waiting for ages for a pick up.
The staff at Big Bus are all really great and friendly and helpful - they could also tell us where the best shopping was other than just sight seeing, when we asked for ideas.

Only faults - it was super hot in London over 30C - sat down stairs as it was too sunny upstairs - I know this is an odd thing for London. It must have been 45C inside the bus - maybe a fan would help move the air.
At times there was a bit of rubbish on the bus - really some people are disgusting - it would be good if there was a bin and maybe some hand towels for people to clean up if they spill something, the team seemed to do their best to clean up when they could.

My husband and I purchased the 48 hour pass. There is so much to see and do if it's your first time in London that a one day pass would just give you a glimpse. Even though this was not our first time, the two day pass was worthwhile. Our favorite part of the tour was the walking tour that comes with the purchase. Our tour guide, Becky, a native of London, was extremely knowledgeable about anything you wanted to know about London's history...especially the monarchy! I would caution that if you would like to do the walking tour, you have to time yourself carefully on the buses as it starts at 11:00 am at a designated spot !

Was in London for the weekend and bought the £33 ticket for the Saturday for myself and 3 friends .. so all in all paid £132 ish ... now I appreciate that there were a few demonstrations this weekend and didn’t have a problem with that .. what I did object to was that when we got to Westminster Pier we found the Big Bus and got the conductor to validate our tickets .. so far so good .. asked if we could get on the bus that was there and was told No we had to walk up to the bus stop a bit further up the road .. again no problem .. went to the bus stop and queued with the other people waiting .. 25 minutes later we are still waiting and suddenly the Bus that we had originally asked about but weren’t allowed on started to let a full school trip on !!! When I went down and asked why seeing as how we hadn’t been allowed on was told .. oh there had been an accident and now they had to use this bus !! But should they not of let those of us that had been waiting for ever board the bus first ! When it did drive down to the stop those of us that had been waiting all got on but were told we could only sit inside because there was no room upstairs because of the school party ... strange then that at the next stop (at which no one from upstairs got off) people that boarded were allowed to go upstairs !!! Not amused to say the least .. we then endured heavy traffic because of the demonstrations and to be honest the worst commentary I have ever heard ... very very boring .. no tour person on the bus apart from the driver.. the tour was also cut short due to road closures. The good part of the trip was the free River cruise at least that was well organised .. for the money paid for this whole package it really wasn’t worth it .. if you do it check everything out first ie is there any demos or road closures and where the best place to board is.

Our family, including two teenagers, all loved the hop-on, Hop-off bus tour. It was our first time in London and it was a great way to see the city. The various guides we had were all informative and most were quite funny. So many sites to see in this wonderful city!

The river cruise was a bit short, but very enjoyable.

We recommend this tour if you want to see the sites and don’t have too much time to do London on your own.

We bought 3 days pass in anticipation that we'll be able to cover most of London city on all routes...Buses move too slow and takes long to arrive at even nearby places...stops are generally far from the attractions/museums. recorded commentary on blue tour is just okay.
only good thing we found was the free stuff...River cruise trip, night tour

I have been to London several times but I had a first timer friend on this last trip. I suggested the Hop On/Off to get in all the sites and then decide which ones she might want to go back and spend more time.

Commentary was out of date and out of sync of the route, confusion reigned when we were told to get off the bus and go to bus in front but there were two buses in front. Poor tour overall and not worth the money.

My sister and I planned our entire first day in London around taking the Big Bus Tour so were extremely dissatisfied when at 6pm on the Blue Line they asked everyone to leave after just making one stop at Hyde Park. The guy said they would create a "purple" line jokingly and we were left to figure out transfers on our own to finish the rest of the tour. We ended up hopping on another bus but missed sightseeing West London because of this unexpected change. We relied on bus times and stops information given on their website and mobile app which were derailed by this sudden stoppage. Really sad we didn't get to see the Kensington area and it was super stressful at the time to figure out an alternative plan!

Did a 5 day Junket to London to see the sights & sounds of London ,& must say I was pleasantly surprised with the sights from the Hop On Hop off bus Tour. For the price it was definitely worth it . takes you thru the heart of down town London & you see all the Historical Bldgs. & monuments, I was amazed as how well they are preserved & upkept. we did not get off the Bus to get a closer look at the Castles or monuments ...Too Crowded, we did however get off for the River Cruise ,which was quite good, we did have a good day out of this tour ,the only downside was to get a clear picture ,without a CRANE in the shot ...Building Galore in the Touristy areas. definitely worth the Cost

We were disappointed with this Big Bus Tour - the route we took did not have a "live" commentator - but a recorded tour instead - and it was very weak - mostly the same 3 songs playing over and over interrupted by a very short comment about a building or sight - not any information or details - just pointing out something ahead.. wish we had selected the "live commentator" tour or a different company all together - Plus they would not run with any type of consistent timing - we waited 90 minutes for another bus at one hop off hop on location -then a bus pulled up and drove away with out letting us board... Think twice about this one...

Our commentary guide Maddie, and driver Julian, on Wednesday July 4th, were brilliant. Enjoyed the sights of London, and were sorry we had to hop off when we did. Thanks from a family of Aussie tourists!!!

An awesome experience! A grand tour of the sites of London atop the Big Bus on a glorious sunny day, complete with informative guided audio tour. Such a pleasure to just sit back and relax! Then an easy transfer to a river cruise up the Thames to Greenwich with an entertaining live tour guide. A very special day!!!

The buses were scheduled to stop every 20 to 30 minutes which didn't happen. The wait for a bus was usually 40 to 50 minutes but there were lots of people at the bus stops trying to sell tickets. They don't have enough buses and the bus drivers stopped to talk to the guys selling the tickets. This usually took at least 5 minutes. The routes are confusing and they are not easy to get around the city. The staff (salesmen, guides & drivers) at Big Bus were not friendly or helpful! The talking guide didn't have much to say - the taped guide was better.
Not worth it - go with a different tour company or better yet, get an Oyster Card.

I live in London and usually do bus tours when I visit other cities abroad and find them a useful way to get a good feel for a city, at least the tourist parts anyway, and a friend from overseas staying with me gave me the opportunity to do this in London and see if I learnt anything. I sure did, but this very much depends on your tour guide, as having hopped on and off three times their knowledge definitely varies. I would particularly recommend Joanne, who spoke clearly, kept control of passengers who boarded and chatted loudly, and she was very knowledgeable and witty.

We joined a red route bus at Westminster Bridge, after doing the London Eye. It soon became apparent why I normally use the underground to get around - traffic was horrendous, and we crawled around almost the whole route. Some of this was down to construction works, but getting around Trafalgar Square took a ridiculous amount of time so don't be in a hurry if you do the tour. There was also an unexplained delay of over 20 minutes when we got to Green Park, and then when we set off again there was no tour guide! The bus waited a few minutes at the next stop for one to join us.

We also did the short (25 minute) cruise that is also included, from Tower Pier to the London Eye, which was fun and the boat was spacious with a bar and toilets etc.

Bought a ticket, sales person told me to that the bus is coming in 10 minutes, we ended up waiting 1 hour, with no bus,. Because the routes were changed that day, but the employee wasn't aware. Ended up wasting 2 hours and taking Uber to different stop. The person said it's not his fault he is sorry and hid in nearby shop.
Busses are sparse, choose a different company, there are better tours in London.

My husband and I bought 2 tickets for the big bus in London last week. It was the perfect and most convenient way to sight see practically all of London. We enjoyed every minute of the tour, especially with our very funny tour guide - Angus. He had us laughing all the time. Such a young and energetic guy. We told him to guess which country we're from. Took him a while until he knew we're from Israel.
We'd love to hop on back in the near future!

We have used this type of bus in other cities, but the traffic in London just bogs these busses down. We missed out of seeing several attractions because we used this bus rather than the subway. Sometimes our headsets worked, sometimes they did not. There are better ways to see London than these tour busses.

Giving 2 stars instead of 1 because part of the issue was a big royal event on a saturday that added a lot of traffic delays..but that is the last part of credit i give them...

We had the 48 hour bus and didnt realize how few buses they have compared to other hop on hop off buses. At one pointed we waited 40 minutes for a bus and when it finally came the driver told my wife and i that it was full as he was letting people on the bus! then he said someone else was coming and we waited 10+ more minutes. he didnt even apologize.

At the end of our second day we were driving the bus to the last stop (or so we thought) and at a random stop without warning the driver told us it was the end of his route. We had to take the tube back and had not planned on that. Would have been really nice to know when that exact bus was going to stop and where. Someone on the bus with us had literally been sold his ticket 45 minutes before he got on and was not informed! the bus driver literally said "nothing i can do about it! write the office!"

I did like the ones with live commentary but they were few and far between. Wish i would have gone with the "original london bus tour" or the "sight seeing" one. we saw those buses much more frequently while we were waiting for our own bus haha.

i still love london but just not the big bus.

I must say this the way to see London in total. Paid for the two days which included a boat tour of the Thames to Greenwich and back. They have the two routes the Red and Blue, the blue longer covering all the main sites but other interesting sites where you may not consider.

We did the big bus tour In early June. This was a great wat to see London and understand the town and get the lay of the land. We recommend this to start any trip to London. Do the whole circuit first and then get off and on. Thanks for the person guide

You cannot use the Big Bus tour to visit all the major sites, just to pass by them - once off the bus to visit an attraction, and although the buses run on 15-20 minute schedules, waiting uses lots of time as often as not. The 48 hr pass includes a river ride to Greenwich, do it! We found Greenwich a better stop than London! Ride the Big Bus routes to see where things are. Beware there are many road diversions throughout London in 2Q2018 and some documented stops might be bypassed without notice! Some buses do not have working wifi and some have lots of inop audio plugs. The recorded commentary is generally pretty good. The staff are generally very good. Big Bus does not make it easy to timely contact them but their customer service works once you do.

We used these buses the first two days in London and it worked well. Got us oriented to the City and gave some good info, especially on the Red buses which are live commentary (English). Blue have recorded information in many languages. In the evenings it is very busy and traffic is slow, so not a great option then. You do a lot of sitting. But would recommend it.

i Bought 48 hours big bus tour tickets from June 4th to 5th 2018. With this ticket you can use a cruise line from London Bridge to Greenwich to see there. there are 3 lines (RED, BLUE and green).
When i used the blue line from the bridge to reach oxford street, the lines' numbers were not in order, and i had to around the city, with traffic in London.

We used Big Bus Tours as part of our 3 day London Pass in June to see the many different sights and attractions from an open top bus. We spent an few hours on the Red bus tour with a great commentary from our lively host and then also spent a few hours on the blue bus tour, with well timed and good audio commentary. We enjoyed the tour and our host was great, the buses were also every frequent, allowing us to get around easily. I would definitely recommend this bus tour company to others whilst visiting London.

Great service and many more stops than some of the other tours. The only thing I would let people know ahead of time is that if you are going to take the boat ride, expect that to take 2 hours bu the time you board the boat and make the several stops and then take the river ride. Then you have to get off the boat to then board another boat to go back.
We took the opportunity to see all the name sites from the bus. Given the traffic in London, this was effective. Knowledgeable guides as well.

we bought the bus and river cruise package was excellent way to see lots and to get around the city. On our last day we didn't make it back to our original destination and since we were on the tour when it ended they took several of us back to the beginning of our hop on stop. Thanks and we very much appreciated that kind of customer service.
Matt was a real treat - an added bonus to the tour. You see all the high spots with commentary, Very convenient and easy.

Enjoyed our initial journey from the London Eye on the red bus route and the points of interest around the financial districts of the city of London and finding out a few facts about the history behind some of London’s most infamous events such as the great fire and the Black Death. Our tour guide was very a very talented young Mancunian who had my dad in absolute stitches which is no mean feat as he has a very selective sense of humour!!

River cruise was fun and again good commentary from one of the boat captains who was very knowledgeable and witty.

I have to say the journey back from Westminster to Victoria was utterly forgettable as my daughter had had enough by then so we got off and headed home.

All in all it was a little pricey for what we received (£83 for 70-plus, adult and one child), but we could’ve probably done a couple more rounds however the traffic was abysmal at this point so just didn’t fancy it! Thanks to the gent at Charing Cross for sorting us out a discount without that we might not have even bothered!!

We have been on many hop on hop off bus tours. London was my least favourite :(
When there was a travel/tour guide we could couldn’t understand them or if we understood them then we couldn’t hear them. When using the ear buds they were off with what we were seeing!
Then near the end we were asked to leave the bus and it was mass confusion as to which bus to transfer too. We did see the sights, however, we would not recommend this bus tour!

What a total nightmare! Stopped outside doubletree Hilton Bayswater road. We had tickets to lion king for my birthday that Saturday evening so asked how long the tour was- told bout 2/3 hours max and would bring us back to the hotel. Sunny day and had done bus tours in New York and bath so felt we should do our home country! Blue route Bus was later than told us and no room upstairs. I walk with a stick and am disabled . Got on till next stop and told best get off and wait for next one. Did that- still packed upstairs and down. Told get off next stop as an empty bus was just coming. Twenty mins later an empty ish bus- hurrah! Sat upstairs and no person givincommentary just told to use headphones. 80% band music with a few tit bits chucked in. We passed what was being referred to by the time we got there. Heavy traffic and ten minute stops supposedly for driver changes. Then got to county hall and told everyone off as the bus had issues. Another twenty mins standing to be herded onto another blue route bus. Driver obviously liked bug ben as we went past it three times?? Didn’t go anywhere next Buckingham palace and then another 15 mins stop at Marble Arch. Still no commentary just crackly band music and couple of sentences describing houses we passed five minutes before. Then instead of going back along Bayswater road we found we were going back again towards Big Ben! We asked driver who just shrugged and said - oh eventually we’ll get back there. By now we had been going over 4 1/2 hours and still miles from the hotel with half hour till leaving for theatre! Cost us £37 each for bus plus £15 for a cab back to our hotel. Total waste of money and time and no live commentary or even good info from headphones. Don’t waste your money there’s other companies.

Our guide, Angus, was phenomenal. He not only pointed out landmarks and gave their historical significance, he made it entertaining without trying too hard or going over the top. He engaged passengers and answered questions. On the occasions where traffic kept us from moving quickly, he provided info on some of the tourist attractions even though not on his route. We also were on a bus with a recorded guide which felt stale in comparison and played more music than providing info. Then we had another guide and he was informative but not nearly as sincere. This tour includes the river ferry and again, the crew member who provided commentary was young, fun, and informative. (I wish I remembered his name.) These are hard working drivers and guides and I felt like I got more than my money's worth!

We got on the bus in late afternoon, just in time for what I assume was some 'rush' hour traffic. We'd already wandered around some by foot, and had some plans a little later in the evening, so we decided to stay on the bus for almost the entire loop of the red route. Our tour guide, Maddie, was entertaining and knowledgeable. We got stuck in several places due to traffic, and she always had more information to share and was helpful with questions and advice to our fellow travellers. Joshua, our driver, seemed to navigate the traffic smoothly and safely. We thoroughly enjoyed our tour with Big Bus London.

We had never done the Hop ON / Hop Off option on prior visits to London. We had always used the tube to get to our destinations. Travelling with another couple who were visiting London for the first time and since we were only going to be there for two days, we agreed to try this option to give them an overview of the city. While at times a bit slow due to the traffic, it did meet the objective of the day - an overview. It whetted their appetite for future visits and at the same time allowed my wife and I an view of London that we had not seen before - as we were always underground. The audio was spotty at times - due to the jack connection. As always, little known facts surrounding each of the sights and neighbourhoods were provided which are always helpful - although you might not always remember them. Good fun and a great way to get an overview.

We have taken Big Bus tours in other cities to get an overall picture of the city. Admittedly London was crowded on Sunday the 20th and credit to the drivers who had to manoeuvre the heavy traffic and diversions. We had trouble finding the bus stops and waited 40+ minutes for a bus and then two would come. The Westminster area was particularly bad. The upstairs was often packed and downstairs doesn’t give much of a view at street level. The commentary on the blue bus is earphones which we often could not hear. It took two hours for us to get back to our accommodation in Paddington in the evening. Tried again the next day and after a 45 min wait, gave up.

First, go to the Marble Arch stop and see Feshi (pronounced "Fezzy"). He is amazing--helpful, friendly, really knowledgeable. We did the 2 day package which included the boat ride and night tour. The flexibility was so convenient. You can stay as long as you want at any particular location. See all you want then hop back on. The boat tour provides a really different perspective of London. We saw things we hadn't seen on the tour. If you're English speaking, the red line has english speaking tour guides. If you get on the blue line, grab a pair of headphones and choose your language. Again, please see our new friend Feshi. He is very knowledgeable about the features of the tour, and he can advise you on what the best deal is. Hope you all enjoy it as much as we did!

On day HOP-ON - HOP-OFF. on 5-13-2018. We started our tour on the blue line in front of our hotel but it didn't arrive until 35 minutes after the posted first stop time on their web site even though it showed a bus stopped at the stop immediately before our stop. We transferred to the red route and had a really great live speaker for our complete round (that's the reason for the "2 eye" rating instead of a one eye. When we went back on the blue bus it stopped and we were told to get off the bus and get on the one in front of the stopped bus. We did and it too was a blue bus but it did not complete the route as mapped both on the paper maps or the web site but repeated much of the route that we had just completed as the driver deviated from the route on the map. When we approached the driver he could have cared less about our concern. The diversion, repeating he same route cost us an hour of lost time. We ended having to get off the bus and walk more than a 1/2 mile to get back to our hotel to make an appointment. In all I am very dissatisfied with the service that was given us.

Went on the Big Bus tour as part of my London Pass the week of April 22, 2018. First driver was nice, audio was informative. Wanted to get off at Madame Tussauds and driver never stopped. There were 8 of us all together who wanted to get off that stop. The people upstairs even rang the stop button. When we all asked why he didn't stop, the driver became very argumentative and belligerent. We had other drivers who were great but later in the day, got back on this driver's bus. Again he failed to stop at the Churchill War Rooms even though we stood up and walked to the front of the bus. We then had to ride to the London Eye and walk back across the river.

We were in London for 4 Day´s, so we bought the 3-Day´s Hop On Hop Off Ticket.
On Our first Day we took the Red-Route so we had Angus as our Guide and Leroy as our Driver ( Angus, when you read this: mandy and Sandy was good too ;-) ) Thanks for the Jokes.
The tour was really good an also his Tips, he gave us was really good, thanks for this.

Really Bad was our last Day from our Ticket: We want to do the Boat tour. With our 3-Day Ticket we had an 2 Way Boat tour. When we were on the pier from the Boat they told us, we musst pay 10 GBR each Person für a Place on the Boat. Or we must wait for 3-4 hours, to get a Free place. We tried zu Talk with the Person and show and explain the Ticket we bought and he said:
You See, the Boat is full. Pay 10 GBR and you get an place, pay nothing and you musst wait. The boat take off, without us and was not even half full.
We were looking forward to the boat tour, which unfortunately we could not do. that was not enjoyable and a pity.

They found multiple ways to make the experience bad. We started in the heart of the city by Westminster Abbey. The tour buses there looked fun, so thought we would try one. After purchasing our tickets, we were given directions to the pick-up location. We went there and waited. We waited about 30 minutes before a bus finally came. After we got on, we got a seat on top, but the audio didn’t work. We changed seats. After a few stops, we were told that we could go back to the heart of the city by getting off and getting on a different bus. Having just waited 30 for a bus, we decided to stay on the bus. We should have switched buses. The blue line went out to some not that interesting sites. When we stopped at the Sherlock Holmes statue, we waited about 10 minutes in the sun. After getting hot, we went to the lower level where a couple of Big Bus employees were arguing with each other. In the lower section, my audio had a short in it causing it to give lousy sound. We finally made it back to the heart of the city where frankly, the audio explanation did a pretty lousy job. We finally gave up and got off the bus after several disappointing hours.

Have done this in several cities now, enjoying using it to get my bearings before striking off on my own. On the Red line, the live commentary is brilliant - Robert especially was hilarious with his patter. Buses are frequent enough that we never waited too long. The two negatives we encountered were 1. getting stuck in traffic and not moving, took 25 minutes to go one block one day, which I know is beyond their control and 2. late in the afternoon, on the way back to my hotel on the Blue route, being unceremoniously dumped off the bus at Hyde Park Corner and told we'd have to wait for another bus with no explanation.

This is a complete waste of time. We waited over 30 minutes for the change of driver/guide. The guide made no mention of the wait. Bad planning of bus schedules, no AC & guide, though knowledgeable was dry. The sales said demeaning things about Golden Tour. Though inclusive in your London pass, you may have better luck with their rival at Golden Tour. Overall, don’t waste your money & time. All the time waiting around for chat & break - which could have been done before the transfer, perhaps.

On our second day in London we took the day pass it was great to see ALL of the major attractions and to hop off at tower of London and take boat down the Thames you are able to see so much then we ended up walking areas as well. We stayed 6 days in London and this made it so easy for the highlights then we would go back to Trafalgar Sq/ Buckingham Palace or any choices after seeing so much on the bus.

We took this trip because we thought it would be the best way to see the key tourist sites in central London during a weekend visit.

Unfortunately, the weather was really cold and wet, so we stayed inside the bus. Unless you are on the top of the bus, the view is very limited, particularly for children.

Than studio commentary was monotone and sparse.

Diversions were unavoidable, but significant and led to long stretches of boredom.

The bus drivers were nice but ground staff were inattentive or hustling - no happy medium there.

On the plus side, buses were plentiful and waits were about 10 - 15 minutes or so.

We did a boat trip, and the London eye and we felt that these were better ways to see the sights - infinitely more fun and economical.

Nice way of seeing London and get to know a bit of its history and main landmarks.
It isn't perfect for photos oef its rainy since the with does from the bus won't let you grab a clean photo. Outside area is nice when not raining or too windy. The guides - at least the ones I got on this trip - were engaging and funny.

Started the bus tour at Tower Bridge with guide Maddy. She was young, bubbly and very knowledgeable on landmarks. Great at her job. Unfortunately the guide changed half way through to Kevin. He was so annoying! Spent most of the tour sending up people on the bus tour and talking very little about what we were there to see. A lot of time was spent in traffic so the humour wore off quickly. It was a shame and ruined the tour for us

Every time we visit a major city in the world we look for a hop on hop off bus tour to give us a flavour of the place. We're from the UK although we live overseas now and wanted to show our young kids around London. After a bit of online research we chose the Big Bus option and bought 48 hr tickets with a boat trip. About £98 for the 4 of us. There are three lines - the main ones are the blue and red ones, the green line is a link route from the Euston area (which happened to be where we were staying and did sway our choice of company). First thing to say is that London traffic is pretty awful, and each route will take much, much longer than you think. At times, walking or the tube would have been far better options. The buses themselves are generally quite clean. Free in-ear headphones, maps and (nice touch) ponchos are on offer. The drivers were all very friendly and have the patience of saints dealing with cheeky taxis, parked up tradies, road works etc etc getting in their way. In addition, extensive road closures for ceremonial reasons during our visit added to the delays - these affecting all bus companies of course. The tickets are pretty flimsy - just printed out receipts. Would be better if they were plastic credit card in nature. That said, we only had our tickets checked twice in two days despite frequent hops on and off. The upper decks are generally open to the air, some buses have the front third covered up. The commentaries are ok, there's a lot of music played in between and you'll get fed up of hearing Rule Britannia and Jerusalem playing. They claim there is a bus every 10-20mins on the red and blue runs but that wasn't our experience over the two days. Frequently two or three buses of the same colour would be travelling together and then nothing for 30-40 mins. Buses were frequently full as well. Very frustrating at times and made you wary to jump off a bus for fear of a long wait to get back on - kind of negating the whole idea. All in all we were disappointed with the Big Bus company - other companies seemed to have more buses operating and at lesser capacity.

I decided to take this tour as I was unable to walk very far at the time and had a visitor from the US who needed to see as much as possible in a short time. It turned out to be a brilliant decision. She was able to take loads of photos from the top deck of the bus, travelled across Tower Bridge and under it and could get off if she wanted a closer, or more in depth, look. The riverboat part was possibly even better. Camera snapping all the time and the guys giving all the history and info on the buildings, sites etc were a hoot. Wish I'd done this on previous trips and relaxed with a drink from the bar instead of wearing myself out on the tube.

This was a great way to get you feel for the city - we did the first full day and was very easy to navigate and nice to be on top for great photos and just beautiful way to see the city. The Headsets where a great asset on the other buses and we got arround great. Was such a treat we did the 2 days in Paris later that week.

Big Steve and Robert were great! Funny and engaging and helpful with local places to go and see. Our bus drivers were safe and helpful.

The ride home at the end of the day was harrowing though, The driver must have been on a time crunch because he was driving pretty fast and wildly. 4/7 and 4/8/18

We went on the red tour route and had the most amazing french tour guide. She was so enthusiastic and fun. We were planning on hop on/off but decided to stay on the entire loop to listen to her stories.

We had been on these tours before in the summer and loved them Unfortunately yesterday this changed. We took the blue tour from Westminster Bridge to Madame Tussards which took 2 and a half hours to get there. No live commentary which is what we like. WE weren't aware of no live commentary on the blue route but since returning home checked online and it is only the red route that has live commentary. In future may opt for other bus services that include return trip on river and childrens perks

Had hop on hop off bus tickets, Bus was OK but they were always crowded no seats, and the stops were far apart. There were not enough buses running to pick up number of people, probably because it was could out a lot of riders??

Fey was our tour guide on the bus and she was AMAZING!!!!! She was very knowledgeable. She was giving us suggestions for places to visit on our vacation. She engaged us in conversation and really made us feel comfortable and at home! I recommend taking her bus while on the tour! She made the experience unforgettable!!!!

I’m sure if we had stayed on, our experience would have been good. We only rode blue line, which was pre- recorded and easily understandable, with pleasant classical music in between sights.
The incredible frustration, however, is, at least by Buckingham Palace, where we got off blue bus, at stop 28, ( which is MISMARKED as stop 20). We crossed street, to catch red line, stop 6 - - only to realize there’s NO stop 6! We used both the paper map AND the Big Bus app to try to find it- - there is NO stop 6. We watched three Big Bus’s go by while we waited-( none of them stopped), exactly where the App directed us. We walked both directions on the street and even tried side streets. Exhausted, after walking for 30 minutes trying to find the nonexistent bus stop, we gave up. So incredibly frustrated. We spent 20 min on bus and waiting/ walking over an hour trying to find the bus. Never again. It’s a great concept, but unless they do better at marking the stops appropriately, or having staff at each stop to assist and direct passengers, I can not recommend this company.

Even if you select one route you have to change. We were told journey was terminating at one point to get on bus in front. That was full. As was the next. I thought once you picked your colour route it would go a that complete route and you hop on and off, not really that straight forward!

This tour was fantastic . The best way to see the city in a short space of time. Our tour guide Ian from New Zealand was a highlight. He was full of funny anecdotes and very entertaining . I would highly recommend this tour .

I used this service back in 2016 and reviewed it giving a lower rating due to issues with the tour. I returned to London recently where I did this tour again. The company reached out after my initial review and offered me a second ride on the bus.

It is a great way to get a nice history overview of the city and ideas of what you want to see. The guide provides some historical tidbits and the driver does their best to slow down to take photos when safe
If you want to take a big bus tour I would go with this company who worked to ensure I got a good experience even if it took nearly two years.

I hadn’t really explored too much of London before despite living in Surrey all my life, so this tour was the perfect way to spend a day! We did this tour yesterday at around 3:30 so it was a ‘little’ bit sunnier! The tour guide- Maddie- was great, and even though the bus had to take a diversion meaning that we missed Trafalgar square, she was really informative about where to get off. She was really funny and had a great personality and great knowledge which made a cold day in London, a great experience! Would recommend this tour to anyone that just wants to get to know London in a bit more depth!

Last week while on our spring break from Phoenix, AZ we were encouraged to do the big bus tour. Somehow I won the lottery when we were lucky enough to get Matt, A sweet cute zappy witty and knowledgeable font of information. Such a gem! I Loved loved loved his love and knowledge of his city and how he relayed his stories and tidbits with his bus. I have to add that there were some big bus guides that seemed like they just were there for the job. I get it. Minimal interaction. I just was spoiled by this Matt. And your drivers kept me in wonder as they navigated the tiny streets and LOOOAAADDs of traffic. My driver with Matt that day gave me and my granddaughter the sweetest of smiles upon entering. I would advise ALL to do the bus tour early in your trip to find your fav must do's while in London. Please extend my Thanks to Matt!

Due to weather our flight to Ireland got delayed two days in London.. this turned out to be pretty great since we got to visit the city! Because we didn't know much about the city or what to do we decided a hop on hop off tour would be the best way to get our bearings. We were not disappointed! Big Steve, our tour guide, was an absolute blast. He was so informative, funny, and helpful! He helped us plan the rest of our unplanned day, and even used part of his 30 minute break between tours to walk with us a bit. It was the perfect way to start off our day, with the perfect tour guide. Thanks Steve!!

Although we have visited London on several occasions my husband and I decided to take the tour. We booked a 48hour trip which included a river cruise.
We were able to jump on and off with no problems even though there were major road works, road closures and detours.
Our tour guide was Steve. He was wonderful. He managed to speak personally with everyone on board. It didn't matter if you were from Wales, Manchester or New York he had a story for you. He made the trip very interesting not only by pointing out all the landmarks but explaining where phrases originated. He gave tips about the best places to find restaurants, tube stations etc without sounding pushy. Although he must say the same thing several times a day, he made it sound fresh and interesting.
The river cruise was excellent & well worth it.
If you are English speaking I would advise taking the personal guided tour rather than the recorded one.

The tour (Hop on Hop off) means you can get onto the bus and leave it for any attraction on the way-then, once you've visited, you jump on the next Big Bus. Choose whether to get a life-guide in English or an audioguide in any language you prefer (you can switch languages on the bus if you change your mind). The tour also involves, if you want so, a short trip on the Themse - try it, it's worthwhile!

For wheelchair users this is a fantastic way of seeing the sights,it includes a river cruise up or down the Thames.The staff are very friendly and commentary funny and knowledgeable.Well worth the £35 per person
We did the tourist thing and bought a 48 hour hop on hop off. it was cheaper than getting a cab every where we wanted to go. so worth it and we learned a lot from the tour they give you.

It's a great way to leisurely se the sights of London! What's more, it gives you the option to view the sights, places that interest you the most at your own pace. Without having to worry about the time or being herded about like cattle. Which is what it feels like, at times, when your on a group tour.

They give you an number of options to see London sights, the buses taking three separate routes , dependent upon what areas interest you the most. From land marks to monuments, museums to markets, it's really up to you. If you have enough time, you may even plan your trip to cover a full three days.

Enjoy London's sights at your leisure. Get a real feel of the city and all it has to offer.

I purchased a 2 day ticket and used the 1st day on Christmas after paying the upgrade. The ticket they printed on Christmas day clearly says 2 day ticket, but I was refused entry on the second day by a very condescending jerk. It ruined my plans for the day, and put a real damper on my trip. He said I'd have to take it up through email, which I tried to do but they never responded. Nowhere on their web site did it say a 2 day ticket would be invalid if used on Christmas, only that an extra 5 pounds needed to be paid. They guy who exchanged my voucher said nothing about it. The guy who refused me entry had only just heard from his supervisor not to let anyone use a 2 day ticket if it was issued on Christmas when I walked up at 11 am, so it seems like something they just made up. Aside from that, the recorded narration was ok, the employees were squabbling with each other and we had to changes buses because the sound broke on the first one. There's lots of other bus companies, find one that won't rip you off.

First time in London with 3 children. Big Bus Tour was really handy for getting around and visiting all the main sights and attractions. Staff were friendly and very approachable, giving good tips on West End shows! Earphones and map provided. Tour talk is informative. Little pricey...but it is London! Great way to take in the sights in one go. Buses are fairly regular so not much waiting around.

Our. First day on the big bus tour. Started great until I lost our ticket tried to explain to a member of the staff who said tough luck we could say where we bought the ticket and how we paid but wasn't interested
So the following day we purchased tickets again only this time on line so we had the app tickets where 35sterling each and on line 31 each
Part from the rude man not wanting to help us or to check our tickets I would recommend this trip to see the sites. Just don't lose your ticket at Marble Arch

We visited in January. The weather was chilly but not bad in the covered portion. We stayed in the warmer area until we wanted to take photos and then returned to the wind cover. We rode the entire blue tour, jumped off for a few attractions and also rode part of the red tour with a live guide. We had Joanna/Michael - they were great!

The river cruise at sunset was spectacular. Beautiful views of the bridge and city.

While waiting for a bus we were able to watch the live update to see the next bus moving our way. Also towards the end of the day we were able to text the customer service team to ensure we were at the right stop and headed in the best direction to make it home. They were quick to respond and even checked in with us to ensure we got home easily the night prior. Great service there.

I would say the busses are fewer than other tours and at all stops we waited at least 20-30 mins. I just recommend the company update the times so expectations are better managed.
I didn't like the tour as its almost to see the historical places on right and left and I felt borring for an hour and with high cost of 35 pound per person. personally I didn't like it.
i used the bus over new year and was very pleased with the service and commentary. the staff were very friendly and helped you reach your destination.

Pros : one funny guide on the red tour (the guy from the brochure)
Cons : everything else
The app is useless. It's more accurate to guess. Bus stops are not the right number, map impossible to read, no buses for 30 minutes then 3 in a row, they make you change buses and then put you going back where you came from. Wasted 4 hours getting swapped on blue line after being told "yep we stop there" and then got railroaded to different route and never made it. Worst worst worst organization ever seen on earth
AVOID AVOID AVOID
by comparison, every time we were waiting for a big bus, the original tours buses had at least 3-4 buses stop while we were waiting for ours. Very disappointed. Won't be back again

Despite some trouble with one or two employees giving inaccurate and misleading information or being overly unpleasant, our experience with Big Bus Tours was great overall. It was the only reliable method of transportation on Christmas day, since public transportation was closed. The live tours were pretty good, but the best part was our unique Christmas day live tour, courtesy of a last-minute intervention by Philip. We had received incorrect information from a Big Bus employee regarding two-day ticket purchases for Christmas, and another employee was giving us a hard time, but Philip stepped in and made everything right. He then hopped on board a bus whose recorded tour system was malfunctioning and gave a live tour himself, despite no tour guides usually working on Christmas day anywhere in the city. The tour was superb - he gave us very interesting information on all the major landmarks along the route, and he had a great sense of humour. We would definitely recommend this company for a convenient and efficient way of seeing London's highlights when time is limited.

Only do this if you have multiple days in London - very disappointing!
While the idea of a hop-on, hip-off ride seems the best when traveling a large metropolitan city, you will waste many precious minutes & hours hoping to get where you want to go and being disappointed.
The time wasted in traffic, and the extremely confusing maps provided don’t really show the order of your trips. There are also stops listed that are never announced or stopped at! I wasted too much time seeing neighborhoods that I didn’t want to see and not enough time seeing the sites!

Spent a lot of time in London over the years, but never took the time to really get to know the city’s history. I felt we were extremely fortunate to get Georgie as our tour guide. A charming and passionate speaker, with a truly infectious enthusiasm for all the little facts and details of this big beautiful city. Thanks to everyone at Big Bus tours! It was such a treat.

Big Steve was our tour guide and he was incredible. By far the best tour guide we have had anywhere in the world! He was funny and informative, he judged his tour group very well and his delivery of the tour reflected that. We were also impressed with how many languages he spoke! He was constantly trying to involve tour members in the discussion and offered a number of suggestions after the tour had finished.

However, had it not been for Big Steve's brilliant commentary and wit, we would have been severely disappointed with the Big Bus Company.
We waited for almost 35 minutes at one bus stop whilst several buses from the other companies drove past. The upstairs of the bus is great on a sunny day but needs wipers on the front as once the rain comes you can't see a thing! The commentary on the earphones was boring and the music was irritating.

Had it not been for Big Steve this would have been a 1 star review.

God Bless Big Steve!

From a Pom, Aussie and a Springbok.

We bought tickets from a street vendor just outside Piccadilly Circus. The seller said the ticket would be scanned at some stage and then we would get 24 hours on the tour from there.
We headed to Trafalgar Square via Lilywhites sports store (we stopped off at Lilywhites and bought up large) and then hours later ended up at the Embankment area. By then we had had enough and realised that our tickets hadn't been stamped.
So the next day we came back, we caught the tube to Buckingham Palace and then jumped on the bus again for the rest of the day - using the ticket from the day before. Bonus!
In the afternoon we took the short river cruise (included with the ticket) from Westminster Pier and it was actually really good. You finish up at the Tower of London and we took the tube back to where we were staying from there.
The deckhand guy was a real character and the commentary was so funny, we loved it.
During the day we bought coffee from Cafe Nero (best coffee chain we found in the U.K.) and food from Pret a Manger - great food for a cheap price

The Big Bus (blue line) was an excellent first day in London. A thorough preparatory tour of all major sights within London and Westminster. Audio accompanying was very useful and insightful. Plan on a full four hours. Highly recommended. Excellent value.

I only had two days to spend touring London so a Hop-on Hop-off tour seemed like the ideal way to see the major sites. Big Bus has three routes. I opted for the Red Route, which includes a live English-speaking tour guide and commentary. During my tour, I did get off and back on, and experienced three different guides. All three had their own style, and I actually travelled some of the same part of the tour twice, with two different guides, and saw/heard something different on both. The next time, if I have more time, I may take all three tours since the other two also visit other sites that the Red tour does not.

Recommended. I took the blue tour & thoroughly enjoyed it. Great to be able to hop off, visit an attraction/site and then get back on the bus. Frequent buses. They were a lot busier than I anticipated so sometimes have to sit downstairs til people get off. But do then go upstairs as you get the best views from there. Commentary was recorded but fairly good. Felt there could be less music and more commentary/info on London.
Staff friendly & helpful.
Red and blue routes were the best! Also the night tour! Live commentary by Nur, Cassue and HW were the best funny and very informative!

This was a great option for seeing as much of London as possible, especially when travelling with someone who can't walk very far. We took the Red Tour with the live commentary by the very lovely JOANNE, who was fantastic. She was so informative, pleasant and polite. We expected the traffic to be bad, it IS London, but we weren't in any hurry. If you are maybe this is not the activity for you. We just sat back and enjoyed the ride.

My family did the Big Bus London tour just two days after doing the Big Bus Paris tour, so it was very easy to compare what a good job Paris does and what a poor job London does.

The main fault of the London bus tour is the number of stops. I came to London to see Buckingham Palace, Westminster, and Tower Bridge. You do see these things. You also get to stop at the Hard Rock Cafe for some reason. And also some hotels that don't seem to have any historical significance. There are stops that are right across the street or a block away. All of these stops, a total of 41 on the red route, takes forever. Like 6 hours of on bus time. I get that traffic can affect the amount of time on the bus, but stopping every block, in every shopping district really does not help at all.

If I had it to do all over again, I would get a bus pass (Big Bus uses public city bus stops anyway. And the public buses run far more frequently), and a good guide book for less money.

We got this recommended and was worth every penny. We hopped on and off in our point of interest. Very nice guided tour if you want to sightsee Lindon at your on pace. We took the red line and blue line. We also cruised the Thames using the pass and was perfect! Lots of nice pictures.

If you don’t want to enter every attraction but instead just take nice pictures 1 day will be enough. Make sure you buy the ticket early and be aware that it ends around 5pm so plan to be at your final destination at that time. You can buy your pass at the hotel front desk (at least in our hotel).

:)

It was 35 pounds per person for 24 hours.
They said the last bus will be at 8:00 (they said around 7:30 PM will be safe to take the last bus )

We bought the ticket at noon.
However the bus was having an emergency door lock trouble.
So they made us wait for 30 minutes in the bus without announcing anything to us.
After that whole lot of waiting they made us take the next bus coming behind all of a sudden.
We all moved to the next bus including a little baby and families.
Then this second bus started having a horrendous siren all along the bus ride.
It was too noisy I was getting a terrible headache.
We were still hearing it until they told all of us to take the next bus behind after a long while.
They did say sorry (When I went in front) but they did not announce this to everybody.(How irresponsible and unprofessional)
So eventually we transfered the bus twice in the end it was on the third bus.

We were told the last bus will be around at 7:30pm when we were buying the ticket.

We shopped around and had late lunch until 5:30, waited for our bus at 5:40 at the bus stop.
We waited there for 50 minutes.
It was close to seven and there was no sign of the next bus coming.
What a BIG waste of money and a big waste of time for tourists who has their time so precious to spend in London.
I will try to get a refund tomorrow morning. They will definitely know what they did. I have captured all of this on video. If they do not give us a refund I will I don't know what I will say or do avout this next. Horrible. Gruesome nightmare in LONDON..!!!!!!!...........

My husband and I had one day to sightsee in London so we thought the hop on/hop off idea would work well for us. We rode all day on the "blue" line. This route has a recorded narration. There is another route that has a live narrator but this one seemed to go to all the places we wanted to see. The problem was that sometimes the narration didn't quite match what we were seeing. For example, the recording would tell us to " get your camera ready" after we went past the sight. Of course, traffic is terrible, like most big cities. So plan on taking the entire day to do this. I think our tickets came with a boat ride on the Thames River but we just didn't have the time to do it. Maybe we can do the river ride when we come again. We heard it was a really nice ride. One other thing to watch is that the busses run at different times at different times of the year. We got off to see Harrods and had to take a taxi back to our hotel because the buses weren't running that late.
The good thing was that we were always able to get on the bus and they came by often at the bus stops.

After taking the Big Bus tour of Paris we decided to do the same thing in London. It was everything we hoped it would be. We took two tours, one with recorded commentary and one with live commentary. Both were excellent but it was especially nice to have a live person doing it. The sound system was excellent. Our only criticism would be the map - - it could be improved in our opinion. The traffic was heavy and there were delays but the drivers do a good job coping with it. We would recommend this tour to anyone considering such a venture.

We had one day in London and, tired after weeks of travelling, thought it would be a good idea to just sit on a bus and relax. It was actually a really frustrating experience. We spent a lot of time just sitting in traffic (not the fault of the company.) However we found the map they supplied was not clear and the stops were certainly not all "clearly marked" in the way they were supposed to be, leaving us wandering around looking for the right stop.
Also there did not seem to be nearly as many buses as they claimed. I don't know if we were just unlucky but twice we waited for a long time at a stop while several buses from the Golden tour company came along.
To be fair the commentary was good, the drivers were very helpful and the river trip was relaxing, but it definitely was not worth the money.

We opted for this all-day tour because of being able to witness the changing of the Guard, a boatride on the River Thames, lunch provided, and a trip on the London Eye. Because of the traffic, the bus trip was very slow, and there was much more walking than I thought there would be. Both of us had very painful feet during the walk to and from the vantage point of the changing of the Guard.

I give high marks to the tour guide we had; his name is GODFREY, and he was fluent in both Spanish and English. He was kind and had his information down pat; I liked that he gave it as if it were still a new and fresh experience for him.

I loved riding the London Eye, even though it was largely spoiled due to a very loud-mouthed woman and her companions acting like it was their private vehicle. It's unfortunate when rude people spoil the ride for others.

This is a great way of seeing the sights in London. We saw everything we expected and more.
The staff were all polite and helpful and the buses were clean with excellent drivers.
At one stop the lady found my 90 year old mother and seat and out her on the bus first, the driver also brought the bus right to the kerb to make it easier for her to board. All without asking.
We weren't sure what to expect from the cruise on the Thames but it was an excellent experience, helped by the sunny weather. Because there was a wait to board the boat at Greenwich of approx. 15 minutes, the lady offered to board us straightway to avoid queuing. Again without asking. The crew were all helpful and gave an excellent and informative commentary with some humour.
I would thoroughly recommend seeing the sights by Big Bus. I also suggest buying tickets online to save on the cost.

I went solo on this tour since my friends would not be in London for a few days after I got there. I bought my ticket at the first stop for the Red Route in outside of Green Park around noon on a Tuesday. The employees were friendly and we chatted for about 10 minutes while I was waiting for the next bus. I decided to get a single day pass because I wanted to get a better idea of which sites to see later. The ticket is valid for 24 hours and includes a river boat tour beginning at the Tower of London (which I didn't have the opportunity to do). Not only was I able to see landmarks that were already on my must-see list, but I saw many more places that I wanted to check out. During the 3-hour tour the weather was decent; sunny/warm at some points and cloudy/cold at others. We were offered ponchos in case the weather turned. I learned a lot about the history of the city, landmarks, and significant people of London from my tour guide, Joanne. She has a great sense of humor and answered any questions. She also speaks French. One of the main reasons that I didn't get off at any of the stops was because I didn't want to leave Joanne's tour. I had an excellent experience with both of them. I only wish time to check out the other routes.

I bought 5 2 day tickes used between 2-3 September. I was travelling with 4 relatives (over 60's) I was hoping this bus would make our visit to London much easier, in fact it caused us a whole lot of stress and frustration, in hindsight we would have been better off spending the money in a few cabs to go from A to B.
I could not help feeling conned by this company. They seem to spend lots of money on advertising but once you've bought the ticket there are barely any busses unless you want to do the same strech of part of the route over and over again. While we were waiting for ours we saw lots of the Official London tour in particular. Customer service was very very ....very poor and the commentaries in the recorded guide were pointless. On one of the journeys they made us change bus twice in a stretch of 30 min? I have no idea why and we were being treated like sheep, just told to change to the bus in front, no apologies for inconveniences....nothing...
In order to get through to the free river cruise they made me search for one of the reps all over Westminster bridge (there were none at the time) to validate our tickets, and I had to literally beg the City Cruises attendant to let us get on board after 45 wasted minutes...
I felt really sorry to have suggested to my family to get tickets for this bus, so I thought I ought to share to warn some people of the risk...

We bought the single day pass on the Big Bus Tour.
Great experience!
They picked us up directly in front of our hotel.
We had easy access on and off at each stop. Busses were on time and we waited only a few minutes for pick up.
We used this tour for transportation around the city.
The blue line tour was about 4.5 hours.
The red line tour took us about 3 hours.
Easy access to change from blue to red or vice a versa. That way we covered all the places we wanted to see.
Busses were clean and comfortable.
Drivers were helpful as to where to get off for sight seeing locations.
Recommend this tour.

Been to London many times but this is the first time we have been on a tour bus. We really enjoyed. Started on the red route with an English tour guide. Very amusing young man. Matt. The blue route was with headphones which seemed a little dull. Too much music.

The hip in hop off concept is something that we are using in many of our trips. It allows to visit a city even with kids, that are not long distance walkers. Principally the trip was nice, but due to traffic we missed a lot of things with in London and even for family (4p), the price 88 GBP) is not a given...

But in the end it is a good way to see the city in a concentrated form, so absolutely fine.

The buses go everywhere you wanna go as a tourst. Fantastic tour guides, free maps, free rain ponchos, free head phones & free WiFi on board! The ticket price includes 3 free guided fantastic walking tours in town that change often (Harry Potter, Haunted tourst etc) PLUS a free boat tour (City Tours company) on the Thames! The BEST unobstructed views of London Bridge, Parliament, Tower of London, Big Ben, etc can be seen from the comfortable large boat. There's a basic snack shop on board as well as toilets. The fuided boat tour will take you as far as Grenwich (about 70 min one way)! As in GMT! Where time for the entire world is based off of!

Take a day trip on the Big Bus and tour all the routes, starting with the red line and then hoping on the blue line. This way you will see most of the major attractions while getting familiar with the different areas and districts of London. I recommend you take an entire leg of a route while enjoying the sites and listening to the audio tour guide. Use the helpful and informative route map provided to make educated choices on where to hop off to enjoy the attraction in that area and then hop on later to continue to the next attraction. The views from the upper deck of the bus can't be beat and even with the congested traffic patterns this is something that you must do. Hope this is helpful. Try it, you'll like it!

We specifically took Big Bus over its competitors. Unfortunately, Big Bus seemed to have a much lighter bus schedule so we did ALOT of waiting at stops compared to other operators. In addition, we opted for the red route because I had read that the live English commentary was better than recorded commentary. Not sure that really was the case as our first guide spent alot of time commenting on how the Brits love pubs and not giving really details that were helpful or informative. Second guide had a wee bit more info but this is definitely "light" compared to other city tour buses.Have taken these tours in the past and BIG BUS was below average, especially for the price. Use it for hop on hop off but don't use it to get much of a sense of the city, its people or history.

Took the tour in London on 8/20---one good live guide Matt, even though he was having terrible time with the microphone--would start to narrate, in the middle his mic would cut out, he handled his frustration well-what a loss, he was actually very good. This happened over and over. Tried the night audio tour, hoping to hear what I had missed--this time, most of the audio outlets didn't work on the bus--in fact, ended up having to sit in the rain if wanted to hear the recorded narration,. Waited about 45 minutes for one bus--watching many busses for other routes and directions go by, when the bus came (was a blue west) so crowded there was standing room only!!! What the heck? If the audio and mics worked, this might be a decent tour--but for the money, a total waste of time and $$ with the lack of maintenance on equipment!

We were very disapointed with the service of the Big Bus in London. Buses are not very frequent, not like other companies such as the Golden Tours. Most of the staff was not helpful at all. Buses stop at stages and take half an hour for the driver to be changed without informing the customers what is going on. Also i don't recommend this service because of the heavy traffic in London. Better to use the underground, which is much cheaper and faster. To go from stop to stop it was taking around 20 mins, which could be easily done on foot for 10 mins.

We wanted to do the "tourist thing" so got tickets for this tour. Did the Red route on first day- very enjoyable especially the guide, Nobby, - his knowledge of London was amazing not just about the sites. His stories of the history of events in London were very enjoyable. We did the Blue route the second day and whilst we saw plenty I didn't enjoy the recorded commentary as much as the human touch the day before. As a bonus we had great weather🌞🌞
Would definitely recommend the Big Bus tour bus.

Had limited time to see the sites so my girlfriend and I took a Big Bus tour. There are several different tours which include a guided tour and an audio tour tour. The bus was a double decker and we sat on the top since the weather was nice. The audio tour seemed very random and really wasn't very interesting. Lots of historical tidbits, but nothing concrete and useful. The bus stops very, very often and it was hard to get into the groove of the tour as people were constantly getting on and off of the bus. The cost was about $40 each and I don't feel like there was value in what we saw versus what we paid. Very much of a tourist trap. Skip this and either walk or take a cab to the places you want to see. It would be cheaper than the bus.

Was it a really bad day? Or is it a really bad service? We booked two adult tickets, which included a 24 hr bus tour and cruise down the Thames. (A bit over $100 AUD). Left mid morning last Sunday. It was a lovely day in London and very busy, however, we waited 25 min before we managed to get a seat, but only on the lower part of the bus - none available up high. At first we just thought it was a busy day - so we gave the staff the benefit of the doubt. However, as the day passed with us jostling just to get a seat at each stop, we couldn't help notice the 'City Tours' and 'Original Tour' buses coming past much more regularly (sometimes 2:1) all with ample of room and seemingly happy customers. We don't mind standing or waiting if the staff are welcoming, but unfortunately the Big Bus staff were rude, non-enthusiastic, and the drivers came across like regular London Bus drivers - not bus tour drivers. Big Bus were efficient with taking our money, but a below par experience all in all. Our strong advice is to go with one of the other operators. Otherwise just use the London transport system which is excellent.

We have used Big Bus tours a number of times in both the UK and the US. The tour guides are fab, the prices were a little high but they are a fab way to tour a capital.
The weather wasnt on our side and our fist driver did a great job and making sure we all stayed safe on the wet upper deck. The second driver we encountered was nothing short of rude! He used hand gestures at us, scowled and barked one word repsonses at us! Will probably consider one of the other tour companies on our next visit.

Typically we love tour buses like this where you hop on, hop off and have a commentary. But I realized that two factors can make or break a hop on, hop off bus tour: One is traffic. The company can't do anything about this, but as a tourist I can consider whether or not it is high season for tourism in that particular city. In July, there was a state visit of the royalty from Spain AND a car race coming up and that meant so many roads were closed that it really would have been easier to walk around London ourselves.
The second factor is really two things to consider: how walker friendly a place is and how willing you are to walk. Lucky for us, London is a fabulous place to walk and so we did get off the bus and simply walked to where we wanted to go. Also, and this is important, we love walking and are healthy enough at 76, 62 and 15 to do all the walking that made this a great trip.
The bus tour did help by pointing out what we might want to see and getting us close enough to walk, so I think it was worth it, but consider the above factors so your expectations are realistic.

The Bus tour (Hop on Hop Off) is the most economical way to see London. The price ranges from 1day to 2 day to 3day. The Bus stops at all the major destinations. During rain they cover on top so no worries.

On a recent trip to London with family we bought some tickets for the Big Bus Tour in London. Firstly we went to Westminster Pier to go on the River Boat cruise ride. This was very good, but I believe this is facilitated by a different company. I would recommend booking on to the cruise separately which you can do at Westminster Pier.

We than did a few other things, and visited the Big Bus Tour stop on Baker Street, only to learn that we had missed the bus. We than went to the Westminster Pier bus stop to get the next bus. Once we got there we waited for almost an hour before a bus turned up. In the meantime other rival bus companies had visited the stop multiple times. I tried to call the Big Bus Tour company to complain, but after an hour I gave up.

FWIW - the bus tour wasn't great. We went on the blue badge tour, and there was audio commentary which was poor. Overall, it was a poor experience, and like other travelers have mentioned, the bus tours aren't worth it and you may as well use the underground to visit different parts of London. Its a lot cheaper and more pleasurable.

Well where can I start. Our main aim was to see Buckingham Palace. The tour guide assured that the big bus London would be passing at a convenient place for us to get off and head straight to Buckingham Palace. Even with the road closures due to the ride London 100. We were assured our aims would be met. It ended up going no where near the palace and cause of the constant traffic stand still, we were left to abandon the tour and spend further monies on the in order to meet our main aim. Extremely dissatisfied and disappointed with the tour and our purchase! Will not be recommending to anyone who is coming to London hoping to see the sights!

We were in London when they had their heatwave so decided to do a Big Bus Tour to save us the walking. The Big Bus staff were all approachable and knowledgable always ready to assist us in our sightseeing. The drivers on all the buses we were on were all excellent and we didn't have any issues there. The routes that they take you on are easy to navigate and really make the most of sightseeing in such a limited amount of time. The commentary was interesting and good quality and volume. Only thing that could've made it better was air con in the bus!! A great service.

I thought I booked premium service with the premium price, but far from it. While waiting on the next Big Bus, almost always there were two buses from Golden Tours passing by, wish I got that ticket for less. And then every second Big Bus plain dismissed us, being out of service or otherwise not diving the tour it seemed to go. We hardly managed to get any your by bus, mostly just walked because we wanted to see London, not just sit around at a bus stop.

Also they cancelled some of the free walking tours advertised in the outdated flyer we got from local tourist information. Can't see any reason why this cost 20% more than comparable tours (with seemingly more buses).

Absolutely not recommended.

Seeing as we were pressed for time, we took the Big Bus Tour to get an overall idea of the great city.
