It was a beautiful sunny day and we completed the entire Blue line, only hopping off once for a quick bite to eat. The only downfall is the traffic in London which meant it took most of the day to complete the Blue line. We started at 11am and only finished at 5.30pm with an hour break for lunch.
All the staff we spoke with from this company were very friendly and helpful. The audio guide was just right, not too much information, but enough to keep you interested.

We took a Big Bus tour in mid June. This time we chose the two day ticket & it was worth the extra few £'s as it included the night tour & river cruise. No problems with purchasing our tickets online in Australia. (Either in AUD or GDP) Our guide, Kevin was brilliant, funny, informative & very personable. Had him in 2015 on the Changing of the Guard walking tour. ..so much knowledge on the Royals. It's a real shame Big Bus are no longer doing these walking tours !! Any chance of these tours with charismatic locals being reinstated ?
If you just want to get from A to B, use the Tube, but if you want to see the sights & people of London, the top of the Big Bus is definitely the way to go !

Kate & Kev
Victoria
Australia

First London bus tour, great way to see all the main London sights, hop on and hop off when you please, we got a two day pass with a cruise included. I will say the tour guides vary, we had a couple of very informative tour guides, and also a few that were a little lax.

The Greenwich cruise was brilliant, couldn't fault the host, true cockney waterman. Learnt a lot from him, weather was beautiful, would certainly recommend.

The walking tours were a complete let down, made our way to the ghost walk one at Trafalgar Square, nobody showed up disappointingly.

This review is specifically for our guide Chris and driver Josh, during our red line tour around London. Chris was friendly, helpful, engaging and entertaining. We learned quite a bit of interesting tidbits about the city during our two hour ride before hopping off. The live commentary was a welcome change from the terrible experience we had with Big Bus Paris. Excellent tour by Chris and Josh, highly recommend.

We went on the big bus tour as we had never been to London. If you buy your tickets straight from the sellers at the stops there cheaper than at the souvenir shops. We got on our tour and the guide was ok. He then got off about 1/4 of the way round. I think the next tour guide was called Matt from Wigan. Very funny lad and because we're from the north we got his humour. But we was so knowledgeable, he said he'd only been doing the job for 5 months but you would never had known. He must be learning all the time because he knew everything about London. Very nice lad and big bus tours have a real gem. Definitely recommend this tour. We stayed on for the whole tour because he was that good and it was the best way to see as much as we could in the day.

These Hop On Hop Off buses have not worked for me in London nor in Paris. In both cities, traffic is always a mess and a lot of times at a standstill. You can walk faster than the bus.

There are at least 4 different HOHO companies in London and each with multiple routes. If you choose to take one, make sure the route has a live person describing the sights. If it is a taped narration, expect dead time or repeats.

Me and my friends absolutely loved the big bus tour! Being new to London we learnt so much from our tour guide Joanne. She was so lovely and made our experience very enjoyable! I wish we booked longer in London. :) Thank you Joanne! Also the boat trip was really cool! The man talking was so funny just like Joanne. :)

Purchased the 48 hour ticket which included the return river boat cruise. The bus tour was brilliant, enabling you to see all the main attractions and being able to hop on and hop off. The best bit for us was the River Boat Cruise - the sun was shining so being able to go up and down the river on the back of the boat with a prosecco which we bought on board was fabulous! The bar is a little expensive however we didn't mind as we were on holiday and it was very enjoyable! The commentator on the boat was really good.

We waited for 45 minutes to get onto the first bus and the guy at the bus stop kept telling us it will come in the next 10-12 minutes when it never did... finally we got on to a blue tour bus which was useless as it only had a recorded commentary which gave very short descriptions and played music the rest of the time... so we decided to get off and get into a red tour bus... again waited another 45 minutes when they say they have buses every 5-15 minutes... the live commentary by Danni was good on the red tour... we got off at the tower of London and boarded the river cruise which was the only highlight of the trip... got off at Westminster and was hoping to catch the next bus into town when none came for the next hour by which time we had given up... we walked towards trafalga square which was actually much more fun than the bus...
they had also marked the bus stops wrong.. first timers would really get confused but luckily my husband had lived in London a few years ago and he knew his way around! While we were waiting for a bus, there were several buses of other tour companies passing by which made us feel even worse! All in all it was total rip off!

We chose this tour as it was the most convenient to book for our location, we can not complain about the service at all, it catered for all aspects of London, however the only thing I would say is that there seemed to be fewer big busses than the other companies working and we were kept waiting for a long time on most occasions, The original tour seem to have the most busses. However the staff on the guided tours were brilliant.

Big bus tours are nice and convenient . There is an app also which you can download. Big bus tickets can be combined with merlin tickets for few other attractions and comes out cheaper. It was lots of fun the bus takes us around all the major places and more.

We opted to spend the day hopping on and off the blue route. Booked using our phone which enabled us to get the online discount. Staff were helpful and friendly.
The recorded commentary was not great. The music was very repetitive, long periods with no information, and the information was out of sync with where we were. We got off at Kensington park and walked through. At the other side had a little trouble finding the stop due to a road diversion but eventually located it. We then waited an hour before a bus came. Fellow passengers were trying to ring to find out if a bus was coming but were left on hold for more than 20 mins - the bus arrived before the phone was answered. We then had to change busses at Hyde Park Corner - no explanation. We didn't complete the route, missing tower if London, this was due to the long wait and heavy traffic as we approached rush hour.
I think the red route which is shorter with live commentary may have been a better option!

On recommendation of our hotel my husband & I decided on Hop on/off Bus in London. We decided on Big Bus Tour because a cruise on Thames was included.
We were directed to Bus pickup at Trafalgar Square unfortunately it was not so easy as Bus Hop on/ off site was extremely difficult to find . Once found , we informed Driver that we would be Disembarking to take cruise. He informed us to get off on 3 rd stop.Unfortunately he bypassed stop & left us across other side of Westminster Bridge. We had to backtrack & walk across extremely busy bridge to get on Cruise dock. At Cruise dock we were informed we would need a Additional cruise voucher ( though no extra payment was necessary) we were directed to street to find Big Bus employee To issue us required voucher. Once at street we searched & waited for a Big Bus employee for about 15 mins to no avail. Other Company Bus Drivers attempted to help us. When finally A Big Bus came by we explained to Tareq ( ?) a very helpful Bus Driver our predicament. He allowed us onto his Bus & took us once again to other side of Westminster Bridge to a Supervisor who Could give us cruise voucher. Supervisor was extremely condescending though he did in fact issue cruise voucher. Once again on foot we crossed bridge to cruise dock. Cruise itself wasn't bad but we were told to Disembark at Tower Bridge. At Tower Bridge we had to pay an additional fee to upgrade in order to get cruise Back to Westminster our original point of Embarkation.
I have traveled extensively throughout the world & find that A Hop on/ Off Bus is a great way to get an overview of the city, that being said this was one of the worst most frustrating experiences I have ever had.! I strongly advised any Tourist to avoid Big Bus Hop on/ off for you will surely be disappointed!!
Susan Gomez- Pizzo

Staff on Big bus tour were helpful and polite. Hot and humid conditions were very difficult. No air con available. Bus tour maps were not useful as road diversions on the day was terrible. I went on automated guide and live guide tours. The locations were interesting. I would suggest that you take bus tours if weather is pleasant and you check routes are not changed from the map.

Although this is a great way to see London and I took this particular bus as the sales agent at Victoria Station was friendly and helpful. The commentary was through headsets and not the most informative tour, I listened to music most of the tour. A live commentary would have been better. We also got changed over to different buses with no explanation, we had to get off and get onto another bus which hardly had any space left to sit. No explanation. It got us from point A to B, and the fast passes we bought with the tickets were helpful, but I did Expect more after the sales pitch we received.

These buses are definitely a good way to get around a town while learning the local land marks and tourist destinations with most people going straight to the top of the bus where only half of the top is covered. The headsets have many languages for describing the history through the city. The "hop on hop off" options works well with navigating the open and shut times of tourist attractions at various locations around the city. I must say that the bus drivers are excellent at getting these big buses through some very narrow and congested streets, while watching out for all the bikes darting out in front of them.The drivers are rather skilled indeed.

Choose to use the option for 48 hour open hop on hop off as was only in london for 2 days.
Honestly 1st day was awful! Started ok when getting on the green link then got onto the blue tour honestly awful experience with one of the drivers his attitude was awful i was so upset i cant even remember his name. The bus was busy and out headset wasnt working so i asked him a question he was very aggressive in his manner and all but told us just to get off the bus! Lucky i could work out the underground to get back to near our hotel.
Was very apprehensive about using the big bus tour on the second day due to the bad experience but luckily we met with some excellent drivers other staff who where friendly and helpful thank god saved the trip and improved moods all round.
Overall the big bus tour is a good introduction to london and with the various routes allows you to plan your journey well
Would use them again however no.

We bought tickets for two days on the Big Bus tour which seem expensive for 3 at £130 but, on reflection it's not bad value.
We arrived on the Tuesday having avoided the late May Bank Holiday Monday travel crowds then leaving on the Thursday night before the horrific events of the Saturday evening at Borough Market.
We bought our tickets near our hotel in Russell Square from the official Big Bus Tours rep who was also helpful in suggesting the route and planning for the two days.
We only traveled on the red route with the live commentary once, due to our already having an idea of the sights. But, to be fair she was very good. The rest of our journeys tended to be courtesy of the pre recorded commentary in our free earphones. You could tell when traffic was heavy as the delays caused longer periods of tracks of patriotic British melodies such as Greensleeves or Rule Britannia.
The buses are clean and staff friendly while being professional. We got our free Thames Cruise choosing to go from Tower Bridge up to Westminster with a witty commentary from the crew member.
The only problem we found was that with the freedom to hop on and off the bus, we could have done with a longer visit as there is way too much to fit in during just 3 days.
How the drivers manage to get through the traffic and narrow spaces, I'll never know but, thankyou to them all for their friendliness and willingness to help.
My tip - do the whole route day one then decide which sights you want to visit for longer from the bus on further days.

I was in town for business and wanted to maximize my sight seeing before my flight home that afternoon. The route was fantastic, went around Hyde Park up to the Tower of London and so much to see in between. The tour is a great way see and prioritize where you'd like to spend more time. I plan to return in the fall so have key areas identified to get off the bus. Can't wait!

Bought a 24 hr ticket .The staff were more than fantastic. Kevin was my tour guide for the Royal Walk and the Harry Potter Tour. Absolutely brilliant on both occasions. Made my short trip to London most memorable. I did the red line and the blue line - was told when and where to get off. Never waited more than 5 mins for a bus- Brilliant

Start off with Philip and Patrick. Big Bus Red Route has live tour guides that explain what the sites are all about. These two guides were outstanding. Great humor. Always had something interesting to say. When you are stuck in traffic, that is when you will really appreciate what they have to offer.

The two day pass includes round trip boat ride on City Cruises to Greenwich.

All of our transportation needs were covered in an entertaining package. Buy online for at their website for a discount over walk up fare.

I am writing on behalf of my parents who had a horrible experience on the bus tour. I recommended the tour to them because i had a great time last year. They felt like they wasted an entire day on their short trip to London. The stops were not properly marked. There weren't enough buses. There was no proper guidance and they had to wait for their bus for ages. Going by other reviews this seems to have happened to others as well. Will not recommend to anyone else again

Myself and three cousins went on a day trip to show them the sites of London. I thought a bus tour with hop on hop off facility would be great. How wrong can you be the big bus company is awful. We got our tickets St. Paul's and couldn't get on the top deck. Got off at the Tower of London and went on the "free" Thames cruise which was the only thing that was any good about the whole experience. We waited at a bus stop until we were told that the bus is not going to stop there anymore today because of the traffic we were told to walk across Tower Bridge to the other side where we waited again on the wrong side of the road, for Buckingham Palace until we were told to go on the other side of the road by very rude guides. By this time we had wasted over an hour of our precious day we got off at Harrods, then decided to call it a day and go home. I only wish that we had just gone on the underground, we would've been able to see much more in a day.

I recently booked the Big Bus for myself and daughter in London. We purchased in advance. The stops were not clearly not marked we had no idea where to pick up the bus. The company does not give a direct place of pickup. Finally we found a bus and literally followed it down the street only to find out it was not the correct one. When we did finally find the correct bus they only were interested in upselling other tours etc. We stopped outside of he Ritz hotel and had to wait 30 minutes before we changed guides. Overall got you around to places but would have been easier to pick out places in advance and take underground to where we wanted to go.

The live commentary was very good, the frequency of buses in some areas was not too good. At some stops the other two hop on hop off bus companies outnumbered the Big Bus 2 or 3 to one plus there there was more rep's for the others. I would try a different company next time.

Traffic is quite conjested in London. If you use this tour to get to a couple of attractions over the space of a few days, the ticket might be worthwhile. It has many stops but the whole route takes 3-4 + hours to complete without getting off. The tour narration is good, available in multiple languages. For an overview of the city it's fine, but traveling around with the tube is much faster and less expensive with the Oyster card. Should sit on top deck for best views. They have free rain ponchos. No free wifi on this bus.

Tour circled same places in a 1 mile radius 3 times and never went by the castle with the guard or Big Ben. They blamed traffic and police as to numerous re routing issues. We then stopped and we're told to get off bus and onto another bus because driver had to have a break. The problem was that the other bus was full so we were told to get back on our original bus again after 15 minutes standing. We sat back on this bus for another 30-40 minutes while our driver took his break and we left again. This bus passed the same things 3 times over and never passed some of what was supposed to be the trip highlights for us to get off and see.
We have been on the same bus company in San Francisco where new drivers would jump aboard the bus when the current driver took break so the customer was not forced to sit idle while employees rested. We never got off the bus because with all the detours, we never felt comfortable with being picked back up again and being left stranded with all their detours and rerouting.
EXTREMELY DISPLEASED AND DISAPPOINTED.

We had the most amazing experience touring the sites of London, with not only an incredible host, but a young man with impeccable knowledge of London and all of its history! We did the 2 1/2 hour tour, and we picked up the bus early in the am, which I highly recommend. This allowed us the opportunity to have a real intimate experience with our guide and ask multiple questions. If you are lucky enough to get Read as your Big Bus Tour guide, you will not be disappointed!!!

Based on reading various reviews of London Hop On Hop Off tour bus companies in London (there are several), we chose the Big Bus. As first time visitors, in London for 6 days, we found this bus tour ideal. We (3) purchased 72 hour tickets (reasonable cost). The map with all the designated stops was very helpful, and the actual stops are signed at street level. All bus routes (3 different) traveled to all major areas of interest in London and Westminster.....parks, sites, bridges etc. We rode them all and saw a lot and learned even more about them. The red line route has a live guide and the other two have an informative audio guide system you use with free earphones (if its rainy, there are free rain ponchos to take). We used the red line several times and found that each different guide provided excellent description of what we saw and also added personal insights which were quite interesting. I suggest you take the red line tour first, in its entirety, to get your bearings of the city in general. We often hopped off a location we wanted to check out in more detail (eg. Trafalgar Square, Buckingham Palace area, Tower of London, St. Paul's) and were easily able to find a stop to hop back on. A cruise on the Thames was also part of the price and we took it from Westminster Bridge Embankment to the Tower of London/Tower Bridge area. One could go further to Greenwich if desired. A return cruise was also possible, and included, on the 3 day ticket. One is also able to purchase at a discount several site tours from the Big Bus sales agents located at several of the more popular spots. Overall, we found the buses most adequate and clean, the upper viewing excellent (we were lucky, no rain when we used it), and quite ideal for a first time visitor. Everyone we dealt with at Big Bus were helpful, courteous, and knowledgeable. We recommend using Big Bus when visiting London!

We'd been on this bus tour in New York, and Washington, DC and decided to continue with the company for England and Philadelphia. It's worth every penny. You couldn't possible see all these sights in a day if you did it alone. We now want to try and visit every country that Big Bus Tours operates in!

We did the hip on hop off tour today,and it was fantastic! If you are an English speaker, take the red line with the live commentary. So many interesting tidbits of information at all times. Highly recommend.

We had a deluxe ticket which included not only the bus tours but also a Thames cruise and walking tours. The Red route has live commentary, and clearly depends on ability and attitude of guide. The blue route has recorded commentary available in many languages. We thought we knew London, but we learned so much and saw so much. A great way to see our great Capital

I took the one day hop on hop off tour with a cruise on the Thames the day I arrived in London. It was a very good way to get an overview of London for any first time visitors.We did not do any hop on hop off, but saw many Big Bus double deckers all over London. The guide did a good job of explaining the sites.

My mom and I bought a one day pass for the Big Bus through our hotel, and hopped on after an excellent tour of Parliament. We had a great guide, Phil, who was personable, knowledgeable, and funny. We were so lucky to have hopped on his bus. A great guide can make or break a tour as we learned on a day trip to Windsor, Bath, and Stonehenge that was booked through another company. We were stuck with an awful guide, which only made us appreciate Phil all the more. His love of his job really came through, and that made all the difference. The hop on hop off bus is a must do for tourists in London, and you should always hold out for a bus that has a live guide, and not just a recorded audio guide.

So easy to use. I would highly recommend that you book your ticket on line before you travel, there are great discounts to be had ! The buses are clean and frequent. No matter where you stand in the city there will be a Big Bus not too far away.The staff on them are very helpful and polite. We booked a 2 day ticket so we could get the most out of the sight seeing tour. I would also highly recommend the Big Bus river boat tour which is free with most tickets and if you have the time to take the trip as far as Greenwich (allow approx. 3 hours).

It is fair to say I was very disappointed with this bus tour. I had pre-booked 2 tickets for my wife and myself ''The London Classic Ticket'' 1 day hop-on hop-off Sightseeing tour on-line before our trip. A Comedy Of Errors!
Unfortunately the traffic was really bad and at a standstill for quite a while due to wreath lying at the Cenotaph ( We found this out ourselves when we got back to our hotel while the bus driver used a whole different reason and thought that singing would help?)
Some roads had been closed and the bus company used a diversion route. This was slow and time consuming as we found ourselves taking back streets and seeing more building sites than London's historic sights!
We decided after our morning had been wasted we got off the bus at Westminster and walked. So glad we did as we saw everything we wanted to see and much more with better camera opportunities than on the bus.
As we had paid so much for the tour tickets and knowing the roads were open now we wanted to board the bus on the side road by Buckingham Palace back to our starting point.
Don't know if they saw us coming but announced that they were changing drivers and headed down a side street not really wide enough to accommodate a bus.
Our driver exchanged a few choice words with a taxi driver and a line of cycles remained upright we were told it would take 15 minutes for the exchange and to remain on the bus ....We got off the blooming thing and got on the tube... wonderful!

This walking tour is short but very good specially if you are a Harry Potter fan like my kids! The best thing is this tour is free! it is part of the Big Bus tour, Patrick was our tour guide and indeed one of the best one we've had! He knows his HP and very good in managing the crowd. This is highly recommended for any HP fans out there, you don't need to plan anything in advance, just give 2-3 hours of your time in London!

I've just returned from a weekend trip to London and used The Big Bus Tour, the staff were friendly and helpful.
Having used Big Bus Tour in other counties I knew I wouldn't be disappointed.
Best way to see the main attractions and find out the most information.

I like Big Bus and I cannot lie
My family and I can't deny
When a bus drives up with two deckers
And audio in your ear
You get happy, want to tour the city

The bus weaves through the city, great narration- we had a live tour guide- and this was an easy way to see all of the city in a short time.

We've done the hop on/hop off in other cities and found them to be fun- this was no different. We got off and walked around Buckingham Palace, then got back on, then went off to Kensington. Found a Tube, check the Big Bus map, and got off at a stop on its line.

We also used the pre-recorded guide and it was great too. Best bet though is that it has Free WIFI, which without a cell plan, made it a wonderful respite between long walks and journeys through the city.

Without it, we would have way too much to plan. With it, we use the Big Bus Map as our guide, get off when we like, supplement it with rides on the Tube, then found a Big Bus Tour line that ended up back near our hotel.

We are big fans of the Big Bus, and would recommend it to anyone visiting a new city. Hell, we'd probably use it again, just because it's an easy transportation method and the free WIFI.

Our family wanted to love this experience. We purchased a 3 day pass and had planned to use the Big Bus much more than we actually did so the value was not there for us. My husband and I had been to London before and booked with another company and loved it. However, this time the experience on the bus was disappointing. First off, we arrived early at one stop on our first day and we were waiting at least 20 mins past the expected arrival time. When we asked a staff member he nonchalantly replied "it'll come soon". We waited another 15 mins or so and then the bus finally came. There were several other buses arriving and departing within that time. I understand things happen that can cause lateness but the total lack of communication was disappointing. The buses themselves were dirty with litter everywhere. Later in the day we were all but thrown off the bus by a lady who came to inform us that the shift was over. Again, a lack of politeness and communication, utterly disappointing. We spent the whole time wishing we had booked with one of the other companies as their buses came and left several times while we waited at each stop. I realize we had come at a peak tourist time, so I am able to overlook the crowding and even not being on time but the lack of communication and respect was appalling. The one redeeming part of the experience was the River Boat Cruise, that was lovely. The staff we interacted with made us feel like we were an inconvenience, even by just getting on the bus at all. The whole experience really could have been so much better with communication to customers while waiting in line and a smile or two.

Over all the tour was pretty decent, with some great points and a few misses.

Highlights
- Great Route: took you to almost all of the attractions you would want to visit
-Ticketing: tickets were easy to buy online (great deal) and trade in at the nearest bus stop
-Customer service: Everyone we interacted with was friendly and caring, all of our questions were answered and they gave us great touring advise

Misses
-Audio Commentary: We took the blue line which had the audio recording and not the live guide. The recording was pretty lackluster, most of the facts were about who owned what neighborhoods and shared far fewer historical facts than I expected. I'm hoping the live guide was better because the recording was boring.
-Bus frequency: The company's map stated bus come every 10 to 20 minutes. Because we were touring on Good Friday I expected some delays, but we were waiting up to 40 minutes at some stops. The freezing London breeze didn't help in the wait, but the ticket did try calling in after the group started becoming very upset. Holiday traffic should be something they take into account, or warn people before purchasing if you will be running with delays.

We chose Big Bus because it had the closest pick up spot to our hotel near Paddington Station. It was fine, however, when we wanted to return to our hotel taking the loop that goes around Hyde Park, it took longer than 30 minutes for a bus to appear and we noticed a number of the other bus companies buses passing through in the meantime...

We did enjoy the boat tour immensely, but don't know that it is unique to Big Bus.

Booked with this company knowing we would only have around 3.5 hours and wanted to see as much as we could before returning home. The time the bus started did not match up to the wait we had. Several other tour buses drew up but no sign of big bus . After 20 minutes I asked one of the reps why we were having to wait so long. The reply was that traffic was busy. This only seemed to affect big bus. One then told me the bus would arrive in 5 minutes, the other rep said 10 minutes. Had to cut our tour short because of this and pay for a subway ticket to get us back to hotel for our luggage.

If you can't get on the top of the bus, you won't see much from downstairs. We couldn't get upstairs in April (boarding at Waterloo), so I hate to think what it's like in July! It took an hour just to go from Waterloo to the Tower of London because of midday traffic. The guide advised us to come back on the boat from the Tower of London to Westminster and continue our tour there. But the bus stop is a good 10 minutes walk from where the boat docks at Westminster, and very hard to find. The second guide seemed only to be interested in where celebrities had lived in London, not the broader history of the city.

The green line shall leave every 10 min but we were waiting for 30 min and no bus appeared. The stopping points are not marked at the green line at all. At travalgar the stopping points are at a different location than marked in the map. It is ok to hop on at same location where you hop off but better not try to find stopping points somewhere else than at the big sights.

We went for a short family sightseeing trip and were mightily impressed with the tour and the guides. Tour was very informative, interesting and we saw all the sights we wanted to see in London in our limited time there.
I must add that two of your guides were almost spoiling us and our children. Lokman whom we met at Marbel Arch 17/4/17 and Fesih at The London Eye, same day.
These guys couldn't have been more helpful, courteous and genuinely interested that we received fantastic service. People like these guys give your company the best of names. I would sincerely like to thank them both. We shared lunch at the London Eye with Fesih and his colleague (didn't get his name) who was also amazingly helpful.
They literally put us on each bus and even came upstairs to make sure we had everything we needed for the trip.
Excellent customer service, happy children and happy mum and dad. First class Big Bus Tours London. These gentlemen need a pay rise!! 👍🏻

We bought the 48 hour big bus tour pass and took all 48 hours to hop on and hop off all the places we wanted to see. Maybe it was spring break and lots of traffic during the weekend but the service was poor. We were picked up from Paddington and 2 stops later they had us transfer to another bus and that wasn't the only time it happened. We actually ended up just using the tube (train) to get around. We ended up no where near Paddington because the service stops at 5p. Never again....I hear Golden Tours is great service.

We took the bus on Good Friday having booked a family ticket on-line & received a 20% discount as part of an Easter promotion, giving great value for what turned out to be full day of entertainment. We travelled on both the Red and Blue Routes hopping off and on about 6 stops on route. We definitely preferred the Red Route buses which were less crowded and gave an excellent live commentary - each guide putting their own entertaining spin on the proceedings.

We never had to wait more than 10 minutes for a bus and staff were friendly and helpful at each of the stops. We then used our bus ticket to take a City Cruises boat tour from Tower Hill to Westminster giving us a different perspective of the river side sites. We took one of the last boats - around 4.30pm so we didn't have to wait too long to board and it wasn't full.

I'd highly recommend Big Bus Tours if you want to get an overview of London. Take the whole day and enjoy the ease and freedom to hop on and off - take the Red Route for informative and entertaining commentary from a real person!

London is too big and the BigBus takes a lot of time, especially if you get caught in traffic or traffic incident (like we did). If you have travelled in a subway before then I recommend saving your money, get a tube map and a Day Travelcard for about 12 pounds (quids as the locals call them) and get around much more quickly - the tube is big but really easy to get around. We did waste other time trying to find pick up / drop off locations and in some cases waited more than 30 minutes before a bus arrived. All the delays added up to 1/2 day wasted time and we only had 3 days to experience some of london's highlights, thanks to BigBus we missed a few.
To be fair, if you haven't travelled before, never been to a big city, never been on a subway then by all means look into BigBus, original London tours or golden tours - these are the three main bus tours and generally offer the same services.

We were very fortunate to have Kevin as our guide and Vince as our driver on our recent trip to London. After being jostled around in Easter holiday makers it was a pleasure to be in Kevin's company and see such an incredible city from the top of a big bus in the sunshine. I just hope Kevin finds someone who actually knows his friend, Ann Butcher!!

We used this big bus tour as our transport round London last week and as usual we were not dissapointed. Plenty of busses and great routes to choose from. You get your own headset to listen in numerous languages as we don't like having a tour guide onboard who thinks he's a comedian 😫. We had booked a 24 hour tour for a family of 4 but upgraded for 20 to VIP 48 hour including river boat cruise. The cruise was also a great way to see some amazing sights from the river - London eye - Westminster - Tower of London and of course tower bridge. The sun shone and the guide on board this trip was very good and very informative.

Right up front, if you're going to London and want to see it, experience it, and learn about it, you can't go wrong with a Big Bus Tour. I was recently in London and we used these buses most of the days we were there. Our favorite tour guide was Samantha out of the many great ones we were with.

You get a free Thames River cruise along with the bus tour but we did not use it this time around. The buses have their own Wi-Fi zones so you take the internet with you along the way. Lots to learn about and the tour guides are tested before they get to run tours. You can get on and off buses when and where you like provided that it's at one of the many bus stops all around the city. Most of the stops also have guides near them that assist you with when the next bus will show up which is rarely more than about 20 minutes.

Most of the tour buses there have partially opened second levels so, weather dependent, you can ride up top and see a lot from that perspective. After you take a tour, you'll never see single-level buses the same ever again!

Over the three days we used Big Bus Tours, I saw through two complete tours without getting bored at all. Lots to see, listen to, and photograph. The service is superb and the people are friendly!

We booked a 1 days pass and we weren't disappointed. This is the best way to see the London Highlights without really getting of the bus. The tour commentary was good. We did hop off and hop on without issues or waiting too long for a bus.

We booked the Big Bus Tour for the 2nd day in London and it was a great way to see the city and decide which areas we wanted to spend more time. We didn't have to wait long for buses at any stop. The kids enjoyed sitting on top of the bus and it was colder up there so be prepared with a hat or scarf. We did quite a bit of walking around the city so this was a nice way to relax and enjoy learning about London. Our live guide was very good. The only reason this wasn't rated as excellent is that the 2x we went by Westminster and Buckingham Palace (on the blue line audio tour) there was only music on the audio, how can they not have anything to say about the history on these 2 places? Everything else was very good and I'm sure the live guide would not have left these out. We did get the 2 day pass which was great because if you want to hop off you may not get thru everything in one day. I do recommend the bus tour!

We took the Hop On Hop Off Tour in London. My bottom line is that this approach is a great first day. You cover a lot of ground and you get to judge how you want to spend your time for more detailed visits. We have taken this tour in London & Paris.
We went to the main office location and got on the bus at that point.

The problem that we had was that we didn't have any idea where to stop for some lunch. So, we took a wild guess and got off at the Victoria & Albert Museum and we found a great deal. The museum has a very nice lunch room mostly for people who are taking time in the museum. (see photos attached) We got into the lunch without any additional charge.The food & the selection were great. I highly recommend it.

Another day we had lunch at the cafe in the basement of St Paul's Cathedral. It was good food in a nice clean place, but not the variety of choice we had at Victoria & Albert's place.
I have heard that Harrods' has good food but it is pricey. I have not been there !

If you are looking for the Afternoon Tea Service, I recommend going to Tea @ The Ritz. Food is good and great ambiance. Cost was not inexpensive, but you got what you paid for.

In my photos, I included a couple of the most unique photos that we took on out tour
Enjoy each day !!

I am going to be very honest with this review. We used Big Bus based on a recommendation from our hotel which is stop # 27 for those of you who have taken the Big Bus Tour its the last stop on the Red Line at Victoria Station. For the most part, my wife and I were happy with the routes and did see a lot and loved the “Hop off/Hop on” approach. The live guides are great, and I would use Big Bus again. The one negative, I would hesitate to buy additional tickets from them to other tourist attractions. The point in question, we were told by the gentleman selling tickets on the Big Bus that if we purchased tickets from them for the London Eye it would be cheaper (it was 2 pounds cheaper) and we would have access to the “Fast Line or Express Lane” ....no waiting on the line he said…FALSE!!! When we got to the London Eye, we were immediately told by the attendant at the gate that we had to exchange the Big Bus ticket for their tickets to get on the Eye and the ticket we got from the Big Bus sales person was for only standard entry, not fast track entry. Fast track entry would cost an additional 10 pounds per person!!!! That pissed me off!!!

Bus stops has been cancelled and bus routes had been changed. No one told us this. They just gave us a map. Wasted nearly an hour waiting for a bus. Eventually walked to another stop. There was a tour guide there who told us the route had been re-routed. No sign or guide at the cancelled stop.

Also, bought tickets for the London eye from the Euston station. Was informed we wouldn't have to queue.... this was a lie!

My advice would be to use one of the other tour bus groups. Or cheaper still, use the subway.

This was a great way to get around town and get a lay of the land. Also a terrific way to get in a bunch of different sights in one day without having to navigate the tube stations, or walk everywhere. I would highly recommend doing this early on during your visit. The convenience of the hop on hop off was great, as we were able to see a lot in a short amount of time. And they provide audio on the bus for additional learning experiences! (one hint: they also offer discount tickets to other attractions, we got tickets to the London Eye, Madame Tussaud's and the Tower of London and ended up saving ourselves a few pounds!)

If you visit london you should definitily get tickets for the hop on and hop off bus! You can really see all the highlights of the city and get a free boat ride on the thames. Make sure if you get on the bus to get the red line, then you will have instead of an audio a real life tour guide which is way more fun! If you are staying at a hotel you can probably buy the tickets for the bus with a discount at the hotel. Have fun!

We got a 48hr ticket £30 each it includes various routes you can hop on and off, gets you around everywhere you need to go, headphones and map provided commentary in lots of different languages, if you have time it also includes a free river boat ride. It really is the best and cheapest way to get around all major tourist attractions in London.

Long time between the busses. The other companies have two or more coaches than Big Bus Tours. In comparison to the other companies no time schedules are published. The waiting time is to long.In the internet and of announcements at the the bus stations the day price is 30 pounds, but the employee had sold the tickets 35 pounds each.

It is our practice to do a hop on, hop off tour on our first day in a city in order to get an overview off the city. Since this was our fifth visit to London, we weren't sure this would be worth our while. We ended up thoroughly enjoying the experience. We rode the Red line with the live English guide and found the refresher on the history and layout of London to be a great experience. The live guides were excellent and the buses go everywhere you want to see. After the Red Line we took the Blue line to the parts of the city we missed on the red tour. The buses were clean, on time and service oriented. I highly recommend the Big Bus Tour.

I purchased the Hop on Hop off in London, and I should have paid the few pounds more and purchased the Original Bus. This bus did not stop at as many places as the Original, and their hours are shorter. No guide on the hop on hop off, like on the Original. We had to use ear buds instead, Very dissapointed. The only good thing was the river cruise came with it.

The buses run quite often, they were not too crowded (February), plenty of seats on the upper deck available. As for the red tour with the live commentary, you need to be a bit lucky. Some guys do their commentary very good, with lots of British humour, others are just average. The ticket includes 3 guided walking tours, but it's almost impossible to do all of them in one day, so a 48hrs ticket is appropriate if you want to do them as well as the (also included) boat tour. When booking a 48hrs ticket, you get a return ride to Greenwich which is definitely worth a visit. Note though, that the last boat from Greenwich leaves at 4:40 pm. A 24hrs ticket will only give you a ride from Westminster Pier to Tower Pier which is still a nice thing to do.
Right now (February 2017), you get an extra 24hrs for every ticket booked.
There's also a special offer for all ISIC-Card holders. You can get a 24hrs ticket with a return boat trip to Greenwich for 22£. Just look for it on the ISIC UK website.
I recommend the Big Bus Tour for all ISIC-Card holders, as it is worth 22£, but not 30£.

We travel on 17 November 2016 to London and I was confuse what company of Hop-on Hop-off company to book.
Finally we book with Big Bus Tours for 24h + 24h free +madame Tussaud.
We enjoy so much the tour but the most important it was all the staff of Big Bus who everybody was professional it was amazing the great job they do.

To all bus stops we will wait maximum 5 minutes

I recommend you if you travel to London and you want to see all attraction book with BIG BUS TOURS and you will have unforgettable holidays

We picked up the bus at the terminus outside the Ritz Hotel. It was a damp morning so we waited to board a bus where there were seats undercover on the top deck.
Seats very narrow and limited leg room.
The bus took off at set time and immediately it was apparent that our guide "Nobby" was not only very informative, but was also very entertaining.
We not only saw the major sites ably described but he also educated us in the derivative of so many words and phrases in daily use.
We stayed on the bus for the entire run ( we had visited all the main attractions on foot previously) of 2.1/2 hours and thoroughly enjoyed the trip from the elevated position.
Nobby reminded us that we were not tourists but were guests of the bus company looking down on the tourists!!
All in all an excellent way to see London despite the seats at the front being not the most comfortable but small price to pay for an excellent view.
Bus very well driven by Russ and an excellent commentary by Nobby.
We hope Nobby got his well deserved pint in the pub after all his talking on the tour.

I buy the ticket 35 pound, 2 days and boat river included. Next day i find out that people have bought the ticket for 27 pounds or 29 pounds!!!
They sayd that it was impossible, go to london eye they cost 27 there! I bought mine in Baker street.
Bus stops are VERY difficilt to find and when you ask them to let you on they say no go to the stop (that i can't find)
We got stuck in traffic 3 times so everybody just got off. Bus 336 driver very very rude!! Idian guy from the aspect i suppose but spoke very good english, very very very very rude.
Busses are freezing cold how can you stay 3 hours on one?
Next day was the day of the womens march so of curse the bus couldnt drive! Thats not the drivers fault but you should give an additional day because i spent my money and didnt use it!
There are other busses that are cheaper!
And the ear phone guide is not on time, you see things and after 4 stops it explains what you saw already 4 stops.
The only part i really enjoyed was the trip on boat on river, going and coning back was very nice and the 'tour guides' were so nice and funny!

We purchased tickets for the Big Bus hop on and hop off tour in London, the bus drivers would stop randomly at green lights, some even texting & others arriving at stops with no passengers getting off or on stopping only to chat to their fellow staff for ages rather than continuing the tour.
I would suggest looking at another company - the only good thing was the wifi

I love these tours and try one wherever I go and this one is a great way to see some of the iconic places in London. I was on the bus with headphone commentary and found there was more music than narrative, which is a shame as there was lots of buildings and places we drove past that I'd like to of been told about but just had a musical accompaniment. I didn't have time to take either myself but there is a free river cruise included in the ticket price and a choice of one of 3 walking tours. Really good value for money

Well worth the £30 each or so for this tour. The tickets are valid for 24 hour but you often get another 24 hours free. A river cruise is included in the price. Very informative whether it be the recorded info on the green and blue routes or the live tour guide on the red route. Never have to wait more than 20 mins for a bus to come along. These are hop on hop off so are ideal to get to an interesting bit, get off and have a look around then get back on the next bus to the next place of interest.

We always like to catch the Big Bus in a new city. This company always offers very good value. We paid 28 pounds each for a 24 hour pass. They offer in that ticket 3 different bus tours, free River tour, free guided walks and discounted tickets to the big attractions. We spent almost 4 hours (went quickly) on the blue line bus. It gave us lots of historical facts and an idea of must see attractions. It was a public holiday so crowds huge. Will go tomorrow. Glad we did this bus tour.

We didn't have a great deal of time in London, so using the Big Bus Hop On Hop Off Blue Route was just fantastic for seeing all the key parts of central London in one go. The trip did take about 4 hours round the 40 stop route but we would miss a minute. Now have a list of placers to go back around. Also all the staff are very friendly.

London is such an amazing city and so much to do and see,and no better way but on the Big Bus Tour, but it was taken to the next level with the interesting informative and humorous instructor Nobby. He was nothing short of brilliant. Cheers Glenn Briers from Perth Australia

This is a hop on and hop off tour around London. It was a great tour for my husband and I as there were many places we wanted to see in a short span of time, as well as getting history of the city. Leanne was our tour guide, she was AMAZING!!! We both recommend this tour as well as having Leanne as your tour guide.

Its expensive and gives only a very brief orientation to the city. There is insufficient time at each of the stops to cover it in a day or two even. All these locations can be reached by the tube. The live guides are funny and friendly, but do not necessarily provide great insights into the city. The website states that 2 walking tours are covered with the Big bus ticket and this was confirmed by the guide as well. They never tell you that the walking tours need to be done on the same day as the bus tour. There's no time to go around even once and do the walking tours that come with it on the same day. The walking tours can't be joined a day later. The buses look great, but it's not worth the price.

I was in London for a few days, what attracted me to Big Bus is when you buy 24 hour Big Bus tour, you get another 24 hours free. Current promotion was very attractive. It turned out to be a total waste of money. First of all, I was on the bus only once. I entered by the Westminster Bridge and traveled to the Tower. Traffic was so heavy that entering a bus at 9.30 am I was at the Tower stop only after 11am. I than wanted to go to St. Paul's Cathedral, realized that I have to walk, since the St. Paul's is one stop before the Tower, and the Bus is going in one direction only. After St. Paul's i walked back to Westminster Bridge with intention to take a Bus and continue from stop 19 onward. I waited for 40 minutes at the stop and other buses from rival companies were passing through (it was 2 pm), not the Big Bus though. I continued walking, went to the Parliament, stop 22, waited another half hour and went further, still not a single Big Bus passed me on my way. They stop running around 6pm. Over 2 days i used the bus only that one time and paid 27 pounds. I realized that i should've just got the underground day pass, and traveled quickly anywhere i needed to go.

I got the 48 hour bus tour, which also included free walking tours and also a river cruise. It was kind of a last minute thing, I was just walking around the Paddington Train Station and decided to go with it, and I am so glad that I did. The bus drivers were very helpful and nice -answering all my questions. I went on the Red Tour for a while as well and they had a live commentary which I thought was quite hilarious and awesome. I also went on two walking tours (Royal & Harry Potter) and both were amazing! We went to places that I personally would not have known to go to if I were to go around London myself. It was very eye opening and also a great experience overall. Big Steve was my walking tour guide and he was the best! He was very funny and knowledgeable and he went the extra mile in making the tour great for me personally as well as the other participants. So Thank you Big Steve, you're the best and thanks for all the photos you helped me take and helping me find the Sherlock Holmes Pub :), and Thank you Big Bus for helping me create such an awesome experience in London! Definitely will be coming back! And would highly recommend it to all travelers!

Let me first advise travelers to purchase tickets from the Big Bus representatives that are walking around at the bus stops.
I went into a shoppe and I was charged more than the standard fare and also advised to choose another tour company. I like Big bus and I've ridden them in multiple countries. That wasn't cool on the shoppe's part. Big Bus is the real deal, don't accept substitutes.
My wife and I met with Richard and he was a fantastic person to work with! The guy went above and beyond, extremely polite, a wealth of information and we like the same TV; and I honestly cannot say enough nice things about him.
Onto the services:
The bus is always clean and the guides always pleasant.
Pro Tip: The Big bus system has mobile WiFi, so you can play Pokemon or surf the internet while you're traveling around the city. A big plus for those who have limited data packages while traveling abroad.
For the most part, the buses have headphones aboard and you can plug in and get a classical music while cruising around.
This brings me to why you're only getting 4 of 5 stars.
There's more classical music on the Big Bus than there is touring information.
You'd think that in a city with SO much history that goes back in time to, well, forever, that there would be so much to say, on every street and every corner but sadly, it's mostly music... Why?
The big bus has a BIG reputation and I was expecting more out of the Bus tours.
However, there is a plus. On one of the lines (Red?) there's a real-life tour guide with a microphone. If you have the opportunity to jump on that one, I recommend it.
Enjoy your touring and try to meet Richard, he's a really nice chap!

First, we were met by a guide who saw us standing in an incorrect place and he took the time to walk us all the way around the park to the meeting spot. Thanks Phil. We like these quick bus tours because they give us an idea of what we might like to see in more detail. it's a great way to start any new city. Although cold, we did see many things and learned a lot about the city. Highly recommend this as a great start to your holiday in London. You can hop on or off when you want. Our hotel was able to give us a 2 for 1 offer, so check with your hotel before heading to the pickup or check online.

Had a fabulous time making our way around London on Big Bus Tours.

The staff were really friendly & helpful. I would really recommend them for visiting the best of London's tourist attractions!

We asked 3 different drivers about timetables for last pickups and got 3 different answers. Consequently, we were left stranded for 45 minutes before we determined that no more buses were coming. The buses stopped arbitrarily at times for up to 25 minutes for no apparent reason. The narrations was minimal or all together missing. Don't waste your time on this hop on-hop off. Taxis would be better and many places can be reached on foot with the exception of St. Pauls and the Tower of London -- which can be rearched cheaply by the tube. We wasted far too much of our time using this service.

The recorded tour is absolutely empty. It is full of strange classical music and Big Bus ads. However, it does not describe London as it supposed to. When we changed the blue line to red (live guide) it was much better. However, the second "guide" was barely speaking English. Also, it takes time to change the bus. One of them did not continue the tour on final stop and the secons was broken

We have done Big Bus in a few other places so we decided to do it here as well. The live tour guide was pretty good and we did get some background information that helped us on our first day in London. We had a plan for routes and places we wanted to get off but we had to get off twice at other stops instead due to the heavy traffic and the bus not moving at all :( The cruise was a nice addition and we did make use of that

I had friends over in London for one day. They wanted to see as much as possible in this day and since one of them is pregnant, we didn't want to exhaust her too much and chose for the Big Bus experience.
When we got on the first bus, the guide was very friendly and came to us for a chat, we liked his style and the jokes he made in between.

We got off at Covent Garden and walked to Leicester Square and Oxford Street to do some Christmas shopping. Afterwards we got back on again and I must say: the second part of our trip wasn't pleasant at all. From stop 16 on, there were fewer things to see from the bus and we were looking forward to the Tower of London and Tower Bridge. Unfortunately we only saw a glimpse of it. When I asked the guide if we were going to drive a bit closer in a few moments he replied that "we should get off if we wanted to see everything". We didn't want to leave the bus anymore because we had other plans in the evening so we stayed on.
The guide talked a lot but not in a very enthusiastic manner, he just seemed like he was rambling on and wanted to get home quickly. When I asked him questions he replied in a very unfriendly manner ("I've just said that"). And gave us a very school-trip-like experience: as if we were being punished for not hearing/understanding what he said.
In short: this could be a fun experience but everything depends on the guide and your expectations. I would advise to get up early and take the bus so you can get on and off a few times to have a good look at the bigger monuments - and so you can experience a different guide if one of them doesn't create a fun tour.

London has much to offer when it comes to things to see and can be very over whelming. The Big Bus Tour allows you to see the city in sections making it easier to consume it all.
Allow yourself at least 2 full days to be able see the sights.
We loved the Big Bus Tours. We didn't have to wait for too long and the ride covered all places of our interest. Highly recommended. By 2yr old son loved it.

Having only ever been to London once I thought what better way to get my bearings and learn a lot at the same time than to do a double decker bus tour and man and I glad I went with Big Bus Tours! The staff are all very knowledgable and are totally happy to help with any questions you have no matter how silly they may seem at the time. I found it super easy to purchase a ticket and to navigate my way between all of the loops. The app is also a fantastic way to find out what's at each stop especially if you don't have wifi to google everything! I will definitely be doing Big Bus Tours in other cities when I visit!

Bought a 24-hour pass, which was automatically upgraded to a 48-hour pass as they were having a promotion on when we bought them. London is such a big city, and this really is the best way to see everything without getting sore feet and having to navigate the tube network! Our tour guide on the bus was brilliant too - really funny!

My friend and I recently visited London and decided to the Big Bus hop on off tour. We were pleased to find as part of the package they offered walking tours. Our tour guide, Steve was amazing. Not only did he give a great tour, but he also offered us suggestions on local places to eat and shop. We couldn't have asked for a better addition to our trip!

My friend and I recently traveled to London and decided to do a Big Bus tour of the city. It was relatively inexpensive for how much area it covered and someone would be on board telling you about the city and places nearby.

When you buy a bus ticket you can also take three walking tours with a Big Bus guide. Our walking tour guide, Steve, was fantastic! He was very informative and he had a good time with his tour group. He provided loads of historical information as well as suggestions for a local pub and/or coffee shop.

Overall - wonderful experience and a great way to see the city!

We bought these tickets for an easy way to see London. We both know London fairly well but bought the tickets for my daughter to see it all and take advantage of the hop on hop off service. We were not disappointed. In fact we will do it again and make sure we're on a route with live commentary as this was fantastic and we learnt a lot. The free river cruise was also fantastic with an excellent guide. Didn't make use of the walking tours. On a side note, we asked advice from a rival company about Big Bus at one of the bus stops - he was more than helpful (we didn't realise his employment till after he told us) but didn't mind at all. the man we asked for advice from at the pier was not so helpful - he told us he didn't work for them and couldn't help - he worked for the pier itself by the looks of it. All in all, whether you know London or not, this is a great way of seeing it and learning all sorts.

Leaving the Tower of London we picked up a red route bus and used it to see some sights we didn't want to go in or wanted to view at a later date.
Great idea but traffic fails the concept. Rome and Paris had good hop on hop off buses but they got there. Some periods on this bus it would have been quicker to walk not a fault of the Big Bus but very frustrating.
Best part if the deal was the opportunity to take a trip up the Thames. We went from Westminster via the Eye to Tower Pier and then on to Greenwich. No queues!!!!!

This is the best way to see Tower Bridge and the Tower of London

I wanted to see the main sites in London but was unsure of the best way to do so. I stumbled upon this group and decided to take a chance. No regrets! This was absolutely awesome. I chose the option with the live guides and they didn't disappoint. It was good to have the context for the various sites and be able to hop off and spend some times and sites which interested you and then hop back on a bus and continue the tour. Tours were well organized and you must take the boat tour on the Thames. I highly recommend this group.

We struck lucky with a wonderful day for October but were glad to have warm coats and thank goodness it did not rain as this would have been miserable. We had a great tour guide in Joanne who was really knowledgeable which overseas visitors in particular benefitted from and very good answering the questions asked by the children on the bus trip with witty and really funny commentary. Leroy was a safe pair of hands as the driver, navigating the busy London traffic. We commenced our trip at Tower Hill and got off at St James Park. We would have happily stayed on the bus and gone round the whole circuit several times but had places that my 9 year old grandchild wanted to see so did not hop on and off as many visitors will want to do. We will definitely want to use the Big Bus Tours again. Value for money and clean vehicles and highly recommend this as great way to see London and so much easier on the feet!

Just got home from a trip to London with my 3 year old - we rode the red route with Joanne and Patrick as our driver. She was brilliant entertainment and factual information first rate. Whole experience was fantastic and would definitely do a longer tour another day and get on and off next time, great way to see London! Bit miffed that I paid for ticked for my little boy only to find out after that under 5s are free, but worth the money all the same! Enjoyable day out and managed to pass Big Ben to hear 12 chimes! What timing. Thank you both for looking after us well xx

Loved the big bus tour. Did the live guide red line tour followed by the blue audio tour the next day. Both tours were informative and interesting, giving us the "lay of the land" of the city. We actually enjoyed the blue line tour more as it was easier to hear.
Make sure to take advantage of the river cruise to get another view of the city!

We were waiting about 20 minutes for the first bus and on arrival it was jam packed. We did eventually manage to get a seat in the open air but the bus didn't seem to move very far for the first hour what with traffic lights, the sheer volume of traffic and road closures! Eventually we did make it to Buckingham Palace where we decided to risk getting off to look around. Perhaps a mistake as we were then waiting for over an hour for the next bus to come along.. We made our way to the Science Museum (slowly) where we had a look around but then had to wait another 40 minutes for a bus to arrive to continue our journey. Not particularly hop on/hop off as advertised. Nevertheless if you can get a seat on the open top you do get to see some of London sights unlike, obviously, the Tube. Tickets aren't cheap and the drivers not the most friendly although that's understandable considering the traffic they have to contend with day in/day out! Not the fastest way around London although it did improve later in the day.

Would recommend doing a hop on hop off bus tour the 1st day in London, this way you get your baring's to where things are and you can get an idea of places you want to return to later on. Made the mistake of taking the tour on the last day of my trip in London so was unable to return to a few places I wanted to see. How the bus tour worked was not well explained when we got the tickets and I would not buy tickets to exhibits if you want to be able to hop on and off at your leisure. Bought 2 tickets for attractions and due to time constraints of Sunday opening/closing times getting on and off the bus to see things was not possible. It takes a very long time to get around on the bus with stopping at every bus stop on the large loop, so take note of places you want to see again so you can take the tube there directly later in your visit. Also, you must use the headphones and listen to the audio guide in order to know what stops are coming up next. The bus is a little confusing and can get very noisy during the day, but if utilized on the 1st day can be helpful in planning the rest of your trip.

Recently travelled to London as a tourist. It was a family of 5. The big bus was a wonderful way to see London. The hop on hop off tour was great. We all enjoyed the tour. Do take the red tour where there is live commentary. Sit on the top deck and you can interact with the tour guide. we had a lovely person. I think he was called Robert.
The 24 hours ticket with an additional 24 is the best. Just try and see all the tours by getting down and joining the walking tours as well.

My wife and I always use these open-top bus tours, if available, when exploring a new European city - It's a great way to get an idea of where everything is, what the neighbourhoods surrounding the tourist destinations are like, and of course to get a little historical information on various things within the city.
From those aspects, this was also a good tour and they also include some walking tours and a short boat tour in the price of the ticket(s). However, London traffic when we were there in September (weekdays) was so bad that buses were delayed 40 minutes for initial pickup in Paddington and portions within the core of London were so unbearably slow that we decided to get off the bus and walk.
Portions where traffic was not too bad were good. Definitely get on the Red over the Blue through the core in order to get the live guide as opposed to the recordings.
Again, too bad the London traffic made this far less enjoyable than it would otherwise have been.

The hop on Hop off bus tour is a great way to see London and many other large cities in the UK and Europe. We like to go one the first day of each see to get the "lay of the land" and see what we would like to go and spend time visiting or seeing. It is also nice as you essentially have pre-paid transportation for the day or two days depending on if you get the 24hr or 48 hr ticket. If you can, always go for the buses with live guides unless you prefer the audio recorded for a language other than English. They have lots of knowledge and can answer just about any questions!

We had a horrible experience with Big Bus in London. After comparing the prices and options between various operators - we went with Big Bus at Marble Arch and agreed a price with the sales agent at the stop. His ticket machine was not connecting with Internet so he got us to hop onto bus as it arrived to complete transaction. After transaction was complete I noticed he had charged considerably more than quoted price (my fault for not double checking) but he hoped off and was gone. I called their help line the next day and quoted all receipt details etc. they got me to email details and despite several emails they are not interested in refund. To make matters worse the Bus was painfully slow taking 3 hours to get to Tower Bridge. What a waste of half a day. Some good commentary but best to avoid and kids bored to tears after first hour Adrian

Since we had a short time in London, we decided to take a bus tour. I'm very glad we chose Big Bus Tours because we had a great experience. Our driver, Julian, and tour guide, Ricky, were both amazing and we got to see so many things we wouldn't have had time to see otherwise along with Ricky's colorful commentary.

The bus is hop on-hop off and we stayed on for the full route and then got off at the Tower of London to walk around there a bit. If we go back and decide to hit all of the tourist spots, we will definitely take advantage of this again because the buses run frequently and stop right in front of all of the most popular attractions - for the convenience alone it is worth the price of the ticket.

We were unsure of which tour company to use Big Bus or Original Tour at the bus stop we were going to ask Original tour first about their sb.ervice only to get intersected by BIG BUS person. He told us how poor they were and that their tour was the best and so convinced us to us it. The tour itself was mediocre at best and the jokes from the guide were poor, they just kept bigging themselves up and how this was the best tour in London. It was overpriced and simple not welcoming either. As we passed other stops it was all the same from their people we are the best. A few months later we went with friends who purchased tickets for us to use Original Tour. We really could say no after all it was a gift. It was the total opposite kind, informative and friendly, no force of sales at bus stops but pleased if you chose them. Don't use Big Bus use Original Tour they have been doing routes for 65 years now that can't be bought.

We had a very short stay in London, so we decided to take a city tour using the Big Bus. There was a bus stop a few blocks from our hotel. We started on one bus route and then transferred to another route to complete the tour. The first bus had an audio narrative that you listened to with provided earbuds. On the second bus route, there was a live guide that pointed out various sights and provided historical background along the way.

The night tour was interesting; however the number of buses was very limited and stopped running at 9pm.

Big Bus Tours is one of several operating in London, they all virtually use the same routes and stop points. It is just a great way to see London, we stay on for the full drive around, then selected the individual hop off points to visit each attraction. Only negative is the London traffic sometimes we only moved 100 mts in 20 minutes.

The Big Bus tours give a good overview of London We took the red tour and took the suggestion of getting off the tour at the Tower Bridge and taking the boat that is also included in the tour down to Westminster. Total time was about 3 hrs.

Great day weather wise & a great tour. We arrived at Trafalgar Square & after a little bit of confusion we found the right place to pick our bus up - there are different colour tours doing different but similar routes. Our blue tour took us around practically everywhere in London we wanted & the weather made the difference, the top of the bus is open so on a wet day maybe not so good - although they do provide ponchos!!!

Grab a set of free headphones on the way onto the bus along with a route map - the commentary makes the journey much more interesting & hop-off & back on again at leisure - the maps identifies the stops. The only gripe was that we nevfer got to go over London & Tower bridges due to road closures forced by the police, but nevertheless a great way to spend a few hours seeing the attractions form the outisde.

Well done BBT - they also provide a free Thames cruise which we didn't take up as part of your ticket & they have assistants at most bus stops to help in case you need it!!

Very informative! Would recommend this tour to anyone who is traveling into London and wants to explore the city. Hop on, hop off. Also included a river tour! The younger tour guides (like Carl, and a few other) are hilarious and informative. We had a couple older tour guides who were decent, but the younger ones brought some real personality to their gig. Good job!
The best way to see sites of london £29 hop on hop off service buses do fab see everything you want hop off at stops ans walk rd see all the famous sites

Big Steve was incredible! He was extremely knowledgable of the London area and sites. He took pictures of everyone and gave us some wonderful laughs. I highly recommend this walking tour and their bus tours.

Spending the day hopping on and off the Big Bus around London was fantastic but the highlight of the day were the free walking tours which come with your Big Bus ticket. I did the Harry Potter tour when I arrived in London and then came back 1 week later to do it again with my kids (and then the kids even went again the next day). They loved it and Big Steve is awesome with his commentary, pictures and terrible jokes. We also did the Royal walking tour with Big Steve and were lucky enough to do it on a Sunday with the road closed and the changing of the guard. Steve made sure we had the best spots for our photos and then even had us marching alongside the guards as the walked towards the Palace-it is something we will remember forever. Thanks Steve! from your Aussie friends

We bought tickets thru the concierge at the hotel. Used the bus ticket to take the boat ride which was very nice. Lots of interesting sites were pointed out as we rode from Westminster Bridge to Greenwich. The next day we went toured the city. Worked very well as we hopped off at St. Paul's, and back on after touring the cathedral and having lunch.

Fantastic way to see tourist spots, you can hop off Any time to see many attractions. As we had previously done a lot of tourist attractions decided to do something different. So we did the 10.20 Royal London walking tour at stop 10 with Patrick. We were the only couple & was given interesting information. He showed us the horse guard, the park & to Buckingham palace.
We used the Big Bus hop on/hop off for a day tour of London and had 3 different guides. Joanne was great! Fun relevant tidbits of information and very informative history.

Found a great hop on hop off bus tour of London. Found plenty of buses that were always available. Got a discount for being a senior which included a boat ride on the Themes. The red buses had live tour guides and they also included free wifi. There was no limit of the amount of data used.

Saw and was informed of so much that I would not have seen otherwise. We were able to hop off anywhere and then get back on but waived the option as we enjoyed the tour and commentary too much!!! I would have done this in other towns also and find you get the worth out of it!!!!

Bought a 3 day London pass which included a day on the big bus. Should not of bothered been on many big bus tours around the world and London was far the worst. The staff were lovely and bus clean. The one huge problem was the terrible traffic in London. It took half an hour to travel 500 metres! London needs to do something about this maybe ban all traffic vehicles in London apart from buses, taxis and delivery drivers. The roads are just to small which as far as I can make out were made years ago for horse and cart.

My partner and I have actually lived in London (Harrow) for the last 11 years but we thought it'd be a fun way to see It and any of the touristy bits we may have missed.

The weather was great, so we enjoyed all of the trip on the open air top deck. This was also good for taking photos as we toured the city (don't even have to get off the bus if you're looking for a whirl wind tour). It was a little difficult to hear the tour guide at points but he (Pete) had a fun approach to letting you know a little bit more about the city.

Recomend ;-)

Nice route and tour if you can get a bus. Waited an hour for a bus at the Tower of London stop. The guy from the company was not helpful at all. The competitors (original tours and golden tours) had buses non stop. Rather use them if you looking for a decent 'hop on hop off' experience.

I have been to London on many occasions, however since buying a day ticket with the big bus tour, I have learnt more about the city and its history. We travelled the red route, this gave us onboard staff who told us about the area and its history. The staff had lovely sense of humour which added to our day

What I like about the Big Bus Tours is that in two to four hours, you can really get a feel for a city, especially if you don't have knowledge, a guide or specific plans; which was the case for us.

We took the Blue Line tour, and compared to Milan and Helsinki, the one in London is head and shoulders above the others. It took about four hours and we completed about 80%. We learned lots and determined where we wanted to spend our time. We didn't take the included river tour though.

A few pieces of advice: sit on the upper level, it really makes a difference; bring your own headphones - theirs are cheap, but you should expect that of free headphones. Make sure you get an outside seat. Sit at the very back. The front will keep the wind and weather out of your face, but the windshield reflects into your pictures. This assumes good weather, which you can't control.

HTH

We utilized the Big Bus Tours during our weekend layover in London. We wanted a simple and convenient way to move through the attractions of London. We ended up mostly walking but it was good to have a framework of bus routes at our disposal. It was particularly easy for us coming from Heathrow via the Express to Paddington station picking the Big Bus Tours right outside the station.
