We also enjoyed tremendously the Thames river cruise which is included in 24h and 48h tickets. They also have E-tickets sent straight to your smartphone. We were a bit improvising during our layover this time but next time will probably get those e-tickets ahead of time for the sake of even more smooth time management.
The buses are standard for Hop-on, Hop-off type services - double decker open top.
We had no complaints about the service and enjoyed our layover in London.

As with other hop on hop off tours, this one gets you to all major sites. Unlike tours of Paris and Rome, the loop is so long and time spent at stops time consuming it is difficult to do the complete loop then go round again to get off at a stop and investigate.
There is an optional boat trip on the Thames.
With heavy traffic and construction the late buses consolidate to get people to drop off points.
Audio good. Knowledge of associates at stops limited. Audio instructs you to ask directions at stop - however guides are best equipped for selling passes.
If you get on the red route, there is live commentary in English

Did the walking tours with "Big Steve" he was excellent
However the bus tour was average as spent a lot of time siting on the bus at bus stops. Not really the hop on hop of experience

We booked our tickets online for 4 people and we got themes boat tour included in the price,
The bus is fantastic you can get on and off as much as you like where and when you need. The staff are friendly and helpful. And the tour guides in the red route bus were extremely knowledgeable and I learnt much from our tour, I would defiantly recommend this company for your sightseeing needs in London.

We used the red route service yesterday and all was going well from Waterloo to the Tower of London and then a river cruise. We then walked around some sights and waited at a bus stop. No Bus - eventually we saw a small note on the stop that said the stop no longer operated there. We walked to the next stop to find that it too was not operating. We then rang the company and the lady there was not at all helpful and only told us to walk to the next stop. She did not offer any apology. At the next stop then when we queried the ticket seller as to any other stops that were not operating he did not have a clue. So after wasting an hour waiting at stops that don't operate and walking to further stops you can imagine how disappointed we were. I would recommend that you avoid this company at all costs if you actually want to take a bus trip and not do a walking tour looking for a bus stop. And greatly over priced for what we got.

We decided to go on an open top bus tour as we we're visiting London and thought it would be a good way to see lots whilst transporting us to where we had planned to go. Using the Big Bus Tour website and maps we had it all planned - which route and where we would pick up the bus etc. Turned out the map and website is not updated with the stops not currently in use - needless to say the stop we used was out of service, along with the next stop too so we had to do lots of walking on what turned out to be the hottest day of the year. When we finally arrived at the third stop attempt we were told the red route wasn't stopping there! Frustrating, annoying and irritating - why BBT do not update their website with this important information baffles me when most people go online to check these details out!
Ended up on the blue route as we were too hot and exhausted to walk any further. £77 for a family ticket and extra adult and totally didn't get what we'd planned.

Have since e-mailed a complaint and have had no response 6 days on. Not impressed.

I had some family staying with me that want to visit London. So we decided to take a day trip to London. Due to the time we had we decided the best way to see the sights was to jump on a bus tour, this would of also been easier as we had four young children with us (aged4to7). They found the tour very exciting as they were on the top deck at the front. The tour for the adults was very interesting and we had a live tour guide.

After we then took advantage of the free boat trip that came with the bus tickets. This was very good and the whole party enjoyed themselves.

After the boat we mounted back up onto the bus again and took the remainder of the tour with we hadn't done earlier. This time there was no tour guide.

But overall an enjoyable day.

I took Big Bus Tours' red tour with live guide. Our guide, Pete, was so amazing that I didn't want to leave the bus! What a pure professional! He was funny, he gave us interesting information about attractions and buildings and small details about London and Londoners ( I will never forget that the Great fire of London started 2nd of September 1666). Not only he spoke, he sang a small song and recited a sonnet from Shakespeare.
What a great guide! And I dont say this easily, because I used to be a tour guide myself. Thank you Pete!

I've lived around London for a few years now and I have seen much of the city on my own but we had friends in from California and they wanted to do the bus tour......so I figured ok I'll give this a shot. If you are over 6' tall you are not going to be comfortable. I could not sit without having my ankles crossed and also had to hug my backpack as the bus was packed to the maximum. No way to really take photos or do anything other then listen to the live guide, which I could only catch about every 3rd word. He asked if we could hear in the back and we all said NO, but he kept on going. The route seems a bit odd and we zig zagged about the city. We hopped off to take the river cruise which was included but when we boarded at the Millennium Pier there were no seats available on the upper deck so we spent the cruise in the extremely hot and humid dining area on the lower deck. If you are handicapped or want to see a lot of the city in ONE day do this. Otherwise the £60 price is not worth it unless you like being uncomfortable for hours on end.

We debated between this bus tour and the Hop On, Hop Off Tour. Ended up choosing this tour, and we were happy with it. We arrived at the stop in the morning, and there was a staff member there to help us. At every stop there were helpful people, and we were able to purchase tickets to different sights as we went along. The audio commentary was great and the experience was relaxing.

The first bus we got from Baker Street was great, good commentary and after the London Eye we got the boat to the Tower of London. That's when it all went downhill. There just were not enough buses on the route! For every one Big Bus there were 3-4 Original Buses and several of another company that I can't remember. At one bus stop near Buckingham Palace, we gave up after half an hour and jumped into a black cab, at yet more expense. We would have gone for another bus company had we known this in advance.

We have used Big Bus tours in Europe and I recommend them with our reservation. Get over your desire to not be a tourist - you're a tourist and being a tourist is fun. I purchased the 48 hour to be used within 7 days and though the workers did not immediately understand how this particular ticket worked they were able to figure it out.
The ticket included a River Cruise (which I used twice) and also guided walking tour with I did not use but I think would have been great.
The buses get around well and you can choose either a live English Tour guide or a pre-recorded earbuds provided tour.

I booked this tour before arriving in London. I have two small children and thought it would be a super way of getting around London to see the sights with minimal walking for two young kids. - how wrong was I?! First we waited nearly an hour for the bus. There were no buses compared to the other tour bus companies. We wanted the red route as it real human being commentators. Finally when a bus did arrive it was the blue route, the man who worked for the company ushered us on explaining it was our best option, however as we got on we realised it was a con as the bus driver and conductor winked and then high fived each other looking at elderly father hobbling up the bus. The joke was at our expense, we were a problem being removed to a different stop. We did finally manage to get on a red route bus and were jogged at snails pace around London. The commentary was dull and the expression "bored to tears" springs to mind. The cruise was ok but you've guessed it - a 45minute queue. My children were exhausted my dreams of London deflated. I will get the tube from now on.

We had decided to go on this some time ago and so when in London once again went to look for the pick up points.

Normally we will plan things but it was more a care free weekend and so that went out of the window. Looking back we lost a fair amount of time by wandering about not really sure where to start on the bus.

The app is OK but needs some familiarising beforehand. If you re in a hurry it is not that much good..

Basically there are set points around the city on a couple of routes, of which some buses are going clockwise and others anti-clockwise. It was not apparent to us initially where these stops are, but they are TfL bus stops and will have Big Bus Tours on the sign although not very prominent. The apps are not always clear as to where they are exactly so you can end up wandering.

Buying on the street just about to get on appears the most expensive at £36.00 for 24 hours ticket and a limited cruise on the Thames. On line is appears to be £18.00 and the app appears to be £26.00 so significant savings can be had by planning.

Depending on where you get on and and off will determine where you sit. We were struggling to want to get up top which is by far the best place if the weather permits but normally its full up top. But all you do is take a seat downstairs (close to the stairs) and at a popular point loads of people get off. This is your opportunity to get upstairs before the new passengers get on. Works every time and you only have to wait a couple of stops before the bus clears again.

We were not offered headphones on entry and so wondered what to to do. There is generally a massive pile of bagged headphones by the doors plus ponchos which are included. It's worth taking a few of these as some do not work.

Some of the routes have a live commentary and some have headphones. The latter is really good as appears to be related to satnav and alters if the route changes. Expect to come across diversions for the various incidents that occur in the city. The commentary is very informative and being at high level you can soak up the architecture of the streets and the long range views too. Using Google Maps in 3D helped a lot too in identify key buildings.

You can get. On and off which is good and buses tend to be every 15 minutes but this is hit and miss. You also need to understand whether you are on the long route or the short as it is always not apparent.

Staff seemed happy.

We were going to use the free ferry ticket which goes from Westminster Pier (close to St Stephens Tower/Big Ben) down to Tower Bridge but you need to check the times. Some trips take some considerable amount of times and the numbers of people queuing for the equally vast ferry is enormous. We ran out of time really as we would not get back to something we wanted to do, so again planning is the key.

All in all it was value for money and with some research and planning and knowing the route a little better would have been really really good.

You do not need to really show your ticket when getting on and off but the ticket is certainly necessary for the ferry. I foolishly lost my first ticket and managed to get a another for half price, so do hold on to your ticket. Sounds obvious but it really does help.

Buses were clean and were clearly under heavy use and the system seems to work well in a bust environment. There are rival bus companies which probably offer similar.

I will be doing it again.

I would recommend getting at least a two day ticket on the Big Bus Tour. Whenever I get to a new city if they have a double decker bus tour I purchase it and ride every line all the way around on the first day. I do this because you get to see pretty much EVERYTHING that the city has to offer. And there are sometimes things that aren't on your radar that once you see them, you want to see. Also, your ticket also **includes** a cruise of the Thames River. This gives you a great opportunity to see the London Bridge and Tower from the river. I love doing this because the point of view is so different than it is from the road and it is relaxing.

If you are disabled, traveling with small children or older people, this is an excellent way to see more than you would by using public transportation. Because the bus tours target tourist destinations they are very close to them so your walking is more limited. And for me, it gives you a feeling of experienced more of the city than the major tourist destinations.

Considering the traffic density in London right now, the Big Bus Tour does its best to get you around town. It isn't easy. And often the bus is very crowded. But the truth is that it is still one of the best ways to get your bearings and feel the city before venturing out on your own. And the photography opportunities on the top level are really extraordinary.

We bought our tickets on the day of our journey from the tourist kiosk at Victoria train station which was slightly cheaper than buying direct on bus. The tour was great, the audio commentary is excellent and kept a small child very entertained. The hop on hop off facility is very good, we used the bus as our means of transport for the whole day around the city and it was therefore pretty good value for money.

Staff were very friendly and courteous. My only criticism is that there is no guidance as to how long different stages of the tour take (or at least I couldn't find it) plus it's not always totally clear which direction bus you're getting and we therefore missed seeing Buckingham Palace, but this could probably have been avoided if we'd explicitly asked the driver so happy to concede this was our error not the tour's!

All in all it was a very pleasant way to see most of the major sights and if we'd had time to do the river cruise too (which is thrown in for 'free' in the price) it would have been fantastic.

Me and my wife took the tour and found it a fantastic stress free way to see the city.

A funny lady was our tour guide, takes a about 3 hours in total and the time flys by.

The hop on hop off is a really good idea. You see somewhere you like you get off and jump on the next bus, maximum 10 minute wait.

If the price online is cheaper show this to the ticket seller and he should give you it at that price, that's how it worked for us.

You even get a free themes boat tour too. Couldn't fault.

Suitable for the whole family.

I researched bus tours ahead of time and decided to use Big Bus Tours for my family's trip to London. It got the job done as far as a basic hop-on/hop-off tour, but I was frustrated by several things that knocked off a couple of points from my rating.
1. The information online describes how they have a live tour (red route) and pre-recorded tour (blue route). They imply that you can pick equally from either. That's not the case - in several days in London (my hotel was right outside one of the Big Bus stops), I estimate I saw only 1 red route bus for every 5-6 blue bus routes. So if you're really interested in the 'live' commentary, you might want to research other options.
2. For large portions of the red/blue route, the bus did not follow the map, and you ended up missing several sites (a big chunk around Tower of London, and another chunk near Buckingham Palace). These were not temporary detours - the bus company knows that the routes are not valid anymore, but they don't tell you ahead of time and they don't give you corrected maps.
3. I looked at the pricing options ahead of time online, but did not buy online because I wasn't sure which day I would take the tour. When I did buy tickets in person as the bus stop, the Big Bus representative acted as if most of the less-expensive options didn't exist. I was basically forced into buying a more expensive option, even though they advertise multiple less expensive options online.

Although our 1-1/2 hour bus tour ended up being closer to 3 hours (due to extremely heavy traffic), it is an excellent way to get an overview of the city and get your bearings (we always do big bus tours upon our arrival in any big city). You can buy your tickets from the driver (cash only) or you can usually buy from your hotel's front desk using a credit card. While you can get a pass for 1 or 2 days, I think the 1-day pass is more than sufficient! Make sure to do the entire tour once, then you are set! They offer guided or pre-recorded bus tours ... guided tours are English-speaking only but well worth it for the added personal touch and lively commentary! We saw all of the major sights and then knew where we wanted to go back to later on during our stay (and more or less how to get there).

The big bus tours have great guides who all are very knowledgeable and seem to enjoy the job. There are 27 pick up points where you can just hop on and hop off. The traffic can be difficult particularly around regent Street. The red tour have "live" guides the blue tour headphones with different languages. Take the Thames boat trip from Westminster pier included in the price. Also included is a night tour which we didn't get chance to try.

I've used big bus tours before and it was great so booked again this time I visited London. We always waited ages for a bus, took random routes without any information so didn't have a clue where we were going. Poor audio quality on red and blue routes. Ended up getting off and just walking around instead.

Went on the red bus, was really lucky managing to time it perfectly so no waiting time until the bus' departure. I paid online and just showed my ticket, very easy. Our tour guide Dave was really chatty but in a good way, gave me a chuckle more than once. Makes me hope and believe that not every tour is exactly the same. Got lucky with the weather and the breeze was absolutely lovely. Got to see a big part of London without much work.

Buying tickets online will save you money. Once you arrive at your desired bus stop they can also give you discounts to London Attractions, we got a discount on the London Eye, it was worth it. The kids loved the bus and the eye. kids are 7 and 9. it was a fun way to get to see lots of things with out shelpping tired kids all over the city. If it is raining they offer free ponchos, or you can sit on the bottom, the tour guides were knowledgeable and friendly.

Spent from 12.30 pm doing the big bus tour today including the river cruise up from the Tower of London to Greenwich. The tour Guide on the bus from Tower to Green Park at 3.30 was extremely helpful and gave a really good tour of London. I really recommend this tour company as they have 2 really simple routes. It is well worth the 33.00 spent on the tour.

This is the typical hop-on hop-off bus tour. It really does get you anywhere, almost. The main problem is that traffic in London is pretty chaotic and many streets are just blocked or with very slow-moving traffic. Thus, these tours tend to either get diverted or just stuck in traffic for long periods of time, making it not so nice an experience. If you can, try using the tube to move around or book a river cruise.

hop on and off as you see something to want to visit, or stay on for the whole trip and see London and hear stories, eyephones given and even a poncho if its wet!! good value for ticket for two days, and a thames cruise included, great fun, most of the drivers were pretty cool, and the lads selling the tickets had abit of fun with the clients and were cheeky chappies, great tour

We booked for a family of 6 at a cost of £89, which included the bus, a cruise down the Thames, and a guided walk. The buses were frequent, at least every 20 minutes, with a choice of headphones which you plug into a little box on the back of the seat to listen to a running commentary of what you are seeing, or a live guide on board (no headphones needed!) The buses were well presented and clean, we rode on two where the info unit that you plug the headphones in were broken, but we just moved seat so no great issue, the guided walk was excellent and is either the Horse Guards and Buckingham Palace, or the changing of the Guard at Buckingham Palace, and runs from Trafalgar Square, the guide (Ken in this case) was excellent and a credit to the company, indeed as were all the staff. With the option of 24 hours to hop on and off and explore, a good boat trip, and a leisurely pace this is a great way to sightsee. The negatives, well for me there was only one, and that was the playing of classical music whenever there was a gap in the excellent informative commentary - you really can get sick of 'Land of Hope and Glory', 'Jerusalem' and 'Greensleeves' by the end of the day.

Just bought the tickets today in the hotel and everything went well. When asked to change the tickets, we were told that we can buy tickets cheaper and with no wait for the London Dungeon. At the Dungeon we were told that we have to wait 1,5 hours. Now we go tomorrow, but that screwed the plan for our next day. Asking the money back we got a no. Very disappointed. Entering the bus back to our hotel, the driver told us that the big bus employee changed to the wrong tickets.

Really enjoyed this. Started at Tower Bridge with the boat cruise (you just need to get a ticket first from one of the staff near the buses) which was great. Then onto the red route with a live (not recorded) tour guide- we had Jack who was great! Easy to hop on and off. Never had to wait more than a couple of minutes for a bus. Got caught in traffic, but that is inevitable at rush hour. Really great value and a good way for all the family to see London. All the staff were really helpful and friendly. Would definitely recommend.

A great tour with plenty of options of all the main areas of London. Hop on and off with plenty of stops in the more popular areas. We had a wonderfull tour guide called Karl, look out for him if you can, he made the tour so much more. Very funny with great knowledge of london.

Did a lot of research and selected Big Bus Tours over the other hop on/hop off buses in London. Bad decision. First, it was challenging to locate where to get on the bus. No sign or Big Bus representative on the sidewalk, and the map from the website wasn't very helpful. When we finally found the bus the first two that passed were full and the drivers wouldn't let us on. After waiting another 10 minutes we finally got on a bus and had a great view from the upper deck and live tour guide when was nice. But no one scanned our ticket which I knew this was required before we could get on the Thames cruise which is included with the ticket price. When we got off the bus at the pier we did find a Big Bus agent and asked if he could scan our ticket, but he was distracted in the middle of our conversation and walked away to light the cigarettes to two passing young ladies. Overall customer service was very poor throughout the day. Staff were not helpful and in most cases seemed annoyed when we asked a question about their service. But the highlight of the tour was the river cruise (perhaps because it is run by another company?). Well organized and the tour guide on the boat was super informative with a great sense of humor.

While I haven't experienced the other hop on/hop off tours, I can only hope they are better than Big Bus.

Visited London during the prudential bike riding weekend so roads were closed and disastrous! Big traffic jam which could not be helped. But I found d the drivers seemed to not have any idea and when asked questions lied to us saying we were going somewhere and would go in the other direction. Half the buses didn't stop at the "new" stops. Most were really quite unsupportive. Got more help from the other bus company reps! The trips would have been better if all the buses ran love commentaries that weekend because the recorded ones didn't run because the routes were different.

First trip to Europe: We did the Big Bus HOHO tour 24 hr pass. It is the best way to get a sense of direction in the city. We did a complete round trip before deciding where to get off and back on. There is commentary available with headphones to tell the history. Excellent!!

We were staying in London for only 3 days so this tour was really good for us. We spent a day just getting on and off at all the main attractions. The commentary was great and informative and the free headsets were a plus. Sure the traffic was bad and it took a while but that really cant be helped. Not that hopping in a taxi would change anything with the traffic jam either and the underground doesnt provide any of the historic information, let alone none of the sights. Great tour with helpful staff at most stops. We would recommend for a nice day out.

We researched the various bus tours and selected Big Bus because it 1) offered the best family discount 2) had great reviews and 3) offered the hop on hop off NIGHT tour. As with any new town and transportation system, once you learn it it's pretty easy to navigate.

Every bus stop on its route has a designated bus stop post (as with all the tour companies). They were easy to find. We rode the entire route first thing the first day, which gave us a good lay of the land. Our live guide was hilarious. We never waited more than 10 minutes for a bus and used our 48 hour pass to get us around town several times.

For our family of four this was money and time well spent!

I've done a couple of hop-on, hop-off bus tours in my time, but this has to be one of the best!! The route/s were easy to follow, and unlike others, the stops are right next to the attractions!! We only had a couple of days in London, and this was the perfect way to see it all!

When you first 'check-in' with the staff, they also offer you discount tickets into some of the attractions - we ended up buying tickets into the Tower of London which was cool!

The staff/guides on each bus were also fantastic - very friendly, and very knowledgeable!!

I would definitely recommend this to my family and friends! :)

Just returned yesterday from London. We paid £25 x 2 (£50) for a 24 hour plus ticket on this tour bus. We waited at the bus stop for nearly one hour for the bus to come in which time several of other Tour Bus company buses arrived. When the bus finally arrived the Guide (Peter I think) was very good. It took quite a while due to traffic to Westminster Abbey where we got off the bus but the guide made it very interesting. After visiting Westminster Abbey we waited at the bus stop for another bus but had to wait again over one hour, in blazing heat for the bus to come. Again several of the other Tour Bus company buses passed. When it eventually came and we set off, the guide this time was not very good. After a while we were asked to change buses which we did and got another Guide who was very poor. He just sat in a seat at front with his back to most of the passengers and we could not hear him. We got off the bus at Piccadilly Circus. It was a lot of money to pay for what we got. If I get one of these tour buses again it will be with The Original Tour company.

The idea was to take my friend to visit London in a way she would see London from the top, visiting all sites in a quick way. The tour itself, was good, however, even though we chose the longest route to make sure we would see everything, the bus did not go by the Big Ben.
It crossed a bridge, getting an image from the back of the houses of Parliament. Very disappointed at that moment. One of the biggest points in London, and the bus skipped it. Also, some of the seats on the bus did not have the audio working, so we had to change seats to be able to hear the description of the sites.

The booking proces was very easy and quickly.
in March we visited lovely London and we were traveling with your BigBus blue route.
Everything was OK till when we got off at stop No. 13 we went to see Big Ben and went back to the same place again to take the bus.
But the one who came was only shuttle bus and the driver told us that he was not going any further, he can make us a ride to the next stop where you will change to another bus.So we did, and on York Street was off at stop No. 14, after the passage of your employee on the other side of the street comes your bus which we got but he did not go further in the direction of the bus stop No. 15 only to stop No. 23 Lambeth Palace and so on.
Thus, we lost part of the route or attractions and landmarks stops at 15-22, for us it is all the more sad that it was our trip with our parents (elderly) who were in London for the first time and unfortunately the last, I wish I did not have chance to see Shard, CBD, Tower Bridge etc., especially since the ticket for this bus is quite expensive.I just wanted to know what was the reason that the bus did not go according to the schedule and changed the route.
After coming home I sent email with description about this situation as written above and till today I did not get any substantive response beyond the casual response, they got my message and check circumstances. Even attempt to contact via chat on their fanpage did not produce the effect, so that is why I am very disappointed such treatment the client.

First experience wasn't good. There were a number of people trying to get on the bus and the ticket taker was unhelpful. I guess he has a schedule. You can only get on the bus with a yellow receipt which he gives you when you give him your ticket from the agent. It was confusing as he seemed frustrated that he had to explain it - so getting on the bus felt like we were school kids being told off.
The family in front of me wanted to ask a question and he was not interested in answering - just wanted us all on the bus.
The commentary is good and the stirring English Tunes in between are nostalgic.
The map is a bit confusing and finding the pick up stops isn't easy if you dont refer to your map.
Once you're on the bus unless you strictly follow the map i couldn't see anywhere which bus i was on - hence ended up on the wrong bus and didn't know until i realised we were turning away from where my previous bus had come from. Then to get back to where i needed to go would have meant having to take 2 buses and in London traffic would have taken ages .... easier and quicker to walk to 2nd bus stop which i enjoyed anyway as i strolled past Buckingham Palace.
I got on the wrong bus because i came on from behind the bus - hence not seeing the sign on the front of the bus. And rushing to get on because i sensed the pressure for the drivers to keep to there schedule. Maybe i missed it if it's on the back and i doesn't appear to be showing anywhere inside.
Then to top it off, when my final bus arrived (after my long walk) i hesitated to get on as there were loads of people at the stop before me - so in a flash he had the doors shut and ready to take off. Because the stop was shared with regular buses and other tour companies, its a mess.
On top of that, the commentary advises that you stay seated at all times but they are allowed to have standing passengers! - and so many people stumbled going up stairs because the driver takes off before every one is seated! - go figure... that schedule again.
Apart from all that, its probably the best way to get around London as a tourist and see all the important things - and theres a LOT of them.

I have done this tour a couple of times... I find it great value for money and the best way to see the sites jumping on and off as you please... Great value for money we paid £25.00 each but this is only because there was a fun run and some of the tour wasnt running around Big Ben etc. it normally costs £33.00 plus you get the free boat trip on the river Thames included which is just lovely. Bus drivers are helpful and buses are clean. Some have a tour guide or you listen to the commentary. I would suggest when visiting London you check out the great offers on... You get two attractions for £55.00 and goes up in price of you want to see more you safe so much and you get the tour bus for £13.50 If I hadn't been to London before I would for sure be getting this offer. You can purchase this offer around where the London eye is and shreks tour I really recommend for a cost effective saving ...

This is certainly the way to explore London and understand its history as a taster. I took the red tour which is in English and included boat trip. We caught the bus from Victoria all the way to tower of london. Here we then caught the boat that's included in some tickets along the river Thames back to Westminster where we enjoyed seeing the city from water and then enjoyed parliament.

The bus journey is good, with a human guide but it's noisy with cars and traffic can be so slow. Bring sun cream, and hat.

You do get headphones, and ponchos for free.

Bought this tour after the Original bus tour company staff threatened and abused my family and 10 year old child. Big bus tours were amazing and I wished I'd seen them first before having lost nearly £100 on the Original Bus tour.

We did this at the tail end of our trip to London and it was highly enjoyable. It was convenient, and was helmed by very good tour guides (we experienced 3 different ones as we hopped on and off). It's a great way to get around town because you can never cover that much on foot, and it's easier than using the tube. You may think it's a corny thing to do, but I say surrender.

I would recommend this to anybody. Book online though before you go and book the 48 hour tour. Gives you a whole two days then to make the most of what they have to offer. We went late afternoon which was still good. However i was kicking myself a little wishing we had gone first thing in the morning to make the most of it. There are several different routes which you can go on which are all included in your ticket and also hop on and hop off at any of the stops. It's a must do for anybody coming to London it gives you a great view of both city's.

Our family of four went on three Big Bus tours recently. Two had live narrators - a shout out to Kevin whose knowledge of the city made for an interesting two hours. The other narrator wasn't nearly as good. A few things to know:
--Sit as close to the narrator as possible. Otherwise the bus's engine and the constant city noise will make it very difficult to hear clearly.
-- London traffic is awful, so be prepared for long waits at intersections, frequently taking several traffic light changes to get through.
-- For that reason, avoid tours on Saturday. We swore we could have walked the route faster than the bus! Traffic taxes during weekdays reduce the number of private vehicles significantly.

The tour cost the four of us C$124 for a 24-hour package. Interestingly, we tried to show our vouchers to three different drivers, all of whom just waved us on to the bus without even looking at our voucher or exchanging it for a ticket. Which meant we ended up using the bus over three days. We could have probably used the bus without ever paying, but we're not dishonest people. In any event, think hard before buying the 48-hour pass, given our experience.

Was it worth the cost? In the end, despite the long waits for each bus and the slow traffic, we agreed it was a good way to get to know the city, especially when compared to more expensive alternatives such as black taxi private tours.

I love using Hop On Hop Off tours at the start of my trip to get a feel for the city, and after having a good experience with Big Bus Tours in other countries, decided to give them a go in London. I got on a bus, and then when we got to Trafalgar Square, the tour guide told us the walking tour to see the changing of the guard was about to start. I hadn't thought about doing that, but I jumped off and did the walking tour. Jack, our guide, was super knowledgable and friendly, and he got us to see everything you could want, with great vantage for photos. Highly recommend! When I got back on the bus, our guide was Steve and he was very entertaining and made the 2+ hours we spent going around the first 20 stops feel like no time at all. The free wifi on the bus was extremely fast and very convenient. The whole day was extremely easy, and I learnt so much about London! Definitely give it a go!

We visited London this weekend and purchased Big Bus Tours London tickets online following good reviews. We were so disappointed. We boarded the bus at 1.30 pm on Sunday afternoon. After hours of boredom sat in heavy traffic having seen hardly any famous sights we left the bus at 4.00 pm in frustration. During our whole trip a tour guide did not board the bus and the only information we had on London was Greensleeves being played through headphones. I would advise... do not waste your time and money.. walk to see attractions. You will see more attractions, it will be a lot quicker and far more enjoyable.

OK, Steve Maynard, tour guide extraordinaire ... here's your shoutout!! The best tours are the ones with live guides who expound WAY more than the canned, recorded tripe. So glad we returned to this tour. Definitely recommend the 48-hour pass to get in as much as you can with the hop-on, hop-off. Just sad that we were too tired to also do the night tour, or the riverboat tour. Excellent value for the money!

Bought 24 hour ticket from friendly Regent Street vendor around 2 p.m. on a Saturday. The ticket was valid until end of Sunday, which was great. I prefer the Red bus because of the live commentary that can point out different things and situations that a recorded commentary cannot accommodate.
You get a pair of earbuds to make it easier to hear the commentary. From the upper, open level, you get a great of view beautiful old London buildings. Think about it, is there a better way to see all this? Certainly not from a taxi, and your legs would fall off after walking all of the Big Bus routes. The inclusion of the boat ride down the Thames is a nice break from the bus and a good way to see the city. Enjoy!

Really great day out. The tour guide on our bus was amazing and knew so much about London it put us to shame!! Excellent service and also could do the Walking Tour and the River Tour. Excellent value for money. Would advise anyone visiting London to get a ticket and have an amazing day out.

We took our young Spanish visitor on the Big Bus red route tour today. A practical way to cover a lot of sights but what made it was the live commentary from tour guide Giovanni, who was charming, entertaining and very knowledgeable. A hit with all in our party, inc me and my husband who've lived in London for 27 years! The cheapest orientation family ticket (bus only) is reasonable value at £55 for four people. Worth doing for sure!

Ours was a 2 1/2 hour tour with live tour guide announcing the sights as we passed around the city. The stories told enhanced our appreciation of what we were seeing. THere are other buses that provide the stories in multiple languages but the tourist must listen through ear buds provided. This is a hop on hop off bus so anyone can stop to see what they wish at their leisure and catch the next bus later.

We boarded the Big Bus not knowing what we were in for. It was great especially if you sit on the top. The audio gave you information on main sights and other points of interest and as part of your ticket you get a trip up the Thames on a boat so you see the Houses of Parliament and tower bridge more closely. We took a couple of routes so it covered quite a lot of London and surrounds. Suggest the audio tour rather than commentary

Having kicked off most of our jetlag, the five of us Aussies decided to see London as a family today and as luck would have it, we ended up spending the day with the font of knowledge that was our guide, Big Steve! He had all of us in stitches and was full of useful information and secret tips to make our stay even better. We ended up getting back on the bus after his break to finish what we started. Big Steve is a credit to your company and we greatly enjoyed spending UK Father's Day with him. Would highly recommend! Big Steve was the BEST! We look forward to hopefully seeing you back in Australia some day!

We booked with Big Bus as we were able to get a 2 day ticket. First day we got on a bus about 4pm and it went round its route. We listened to the commentary which was always behind the building/area they were describing. They also missed out several landmarks including Buckingham Palace! Although you don't actually go around the front of the Palace, you see the back and surely it's worth a mention. The bus then came to a stop and a chap came on and said the bus was finished for the day and we had to get off. The driver never said he would be finishing ha,f way round or that this was the final bus of the day. Very disappointing, however me the chap at the stop suggested we wait for another bus coming in and we could get that one which would at least take us closer to our hotel.
The next day we got on one route and again the commentary was poor and half way round the route the bus went on to a different route without any warning! A Big lack of communication on the Big bus. On the positive side the boat trip was great. The chap who did the commentary on the boat trip was great and really made the tour. I would not recommend Big Bus in London which is a pity as we have used them in other cities and found them to be good.
PS. Can we have another song - got a bit fed up with Land of hope and glory?

Wow! Wow! Wow! That should say it all. I loved this Big Bus tour. We took the green, blue and red lines for a full day. Unfortunately, we ran out of time to be able to use the orange line to see Kensington Palace. Will definitely fit that one next time we tour London. We were extremely pleased with the blue and red tours. Kevin was our tour guide on the upper deck of our red tour and he was absolutely charming, funny and amazing. Thanks for your awesome tour Kevin! Highly recommend using Big Bus Tours. We have used them in Madrid and Paris. It's a great way to get around and see all the sights.

We were tired of walking. So when we saw the Big Bus tour outside of Hyde Park, we jumped to buy tickets. Although it was late in the day, they sold us 24 hour access to the bus. We enjoyed riding around the city and hearing the history of places. This helped us plan the next day which we had left open to visit what struck our fancy. The audio tour was fine and it was nice to ride on top to oohh and ahh at London.

Wow. This was very good. A bus tour, a river cruise, a walking tour, all for one fixed price. The buses were frequent and you can hop off and on as many times as you like. We used the red service during the day for the live commentary, and yellow/purple to get back to the hotel at the end of both days. We had a couple of guides on day one who were ok, and then we had two guides on our second day who were out of this world. It was amazing to see both put so much energy, enthusiasm and a real passion for London into it, even when the traffic was a little slow, but it just really shows how good they are. I work in the performing arts/tv and was so impressed by it. So, much thanks to Lianne and Steve (Stevie) for a great experience. The kids loved looking out for things and singing, 'the wheels on the bus with you', Steve, and cheering and laughing at you Lianne. All the staff we met were very friendly at all the stops and the drivers helpful too. We did the river cruise which was great, but thought the walking tour might have been a little too much for little legs. Keep up the good work Big Bus, you really do have some real stars working for you. We've done lots of different tours, here, and in other countries, and have to say, your tour guides are up there with the very best.

After a bit of research we decided to use Big Bus tours and were really happy with both the bus tour and the free river tour. The staff on both tours are very knowledgeable and very friendly adding to the experience. Both the bus and the boat were comfortable and clean and are a great way to see the city. Being able to hop on and off as the mood takes you is the ideal way to spend a day in London and you can spend as much time as you need at any of the attractions. This was our third time in London and wish that we had done the big bus tour first time around but you live and learn.

Thousands of people have already said it, but I will add my version: we loved the convenience of hop on/off privileges, we found a stop only a few blocks from our hotel, the buses were comfortable and clean, and we really enjoyed the service! We toured all over the city and learned much from the guided recordings. We were lucky that the weather was perfect and we could sit on the open 2nd level, enjoying the sights. I absolutely recommend Big Bus Tours, wherever you visit! A+, would ride again!

Our family of four booked a 24-hour ticket online, which was cheaper than buying at the bus stop. We took advantage of the bus tour from Trafalgar Square over to the Tower of London. Make sure you choose a Red Tour (not orange or blue) if you want a live, English-speaking guide. Our guide was funny and kept the information flowing through very heavy London traffic. After we toured the Tour of London, our 24-hr ticket included a cruise up the River Thames. We also took advantage of one of the free walking tours included with our ticket, the Royal Guard Tour. Our guide was informative and entertaining as we walked from Trafalgar Square to Buckingham Palace. He knew the exact places to stand to see the old guard marching towards the palace and the new guard coming in. Well worth the price!

When you have only two or three days to explore a major city, the hop-on hop-off tourist bus is probably the most convenient way to see the sights of that city.
On our recent European tour, we used Big Bus Tours in both London and Paris. Of the two, Big Bus London was much better; more frequency of service, and longer routes.
You can go to their website and purchase online in advance of your trip. You then print your voucher and present it to one of the agents at a pickup point, who will then print your official tickets. The two day plan includes an enjoyable boat ride on the Thames from Westminster to Greenwich, though that service is provided by a second vendor.
You will still need to develop some understanding of the London buses and Underground to get to one of the many convenient pickup points. You will want to obtain an Oyster Card, either in advance or at the Airport to easily ride the London buses or the Underground. One bus ride got us to Baker Street, the closest pickup point to our hotel near Euston Station. One day we returned to Euston via the Underground after various Big Bus rides and the boat tour.
The combination of Big Bus London and public transport resulted in a very enjoyable and time efficient visit to London.

We purchased 2 48-hour passes for the Big Bus Tours in London so that we could maximize the time going to visit all the sites along the routes and do some general sightseeing. Overall, the non-live lines (Orange, Green, Blue) were great but a little generic, and we ended up hearing many things over and over. We hopped on a Red bus route because we wanted to hear the live commentary and were NOT disappointed! Our guide - Big Steve was AMAZING! He was funny and interactive with the guests, gave wonderful recommendations on attractions and restaurants, and had a lot of knowledgeable tidbits to share! In addition - once he found out we were from Texas, he told us to check out the Texas Embassy in London, a hidden gem that a lot of people don't know about. It was awesome to have had that experience to share when we got home too! Big Steve is AWESOME and the best guide you can ask for. Highly recommend this tour and do the live commentary in particular!

There are many Bus Tours options in London and after a lengthy analysis , we have decided to go with Big Bus Tours as they were the best value for our needs ! We bought the 48 hours ticket which we used for 3 days ( from noon on Monday till 13:00 hrs on Wednesday ) . We did the night route and 3 out of the 4 day routes , We took the short cruise on the Thames and the longer one to Greenwich . We started one walking tour but rapidly found out that the group was too big (over 20) , so we got back on the bus . The narration on all tours was excellent and the buses quite comfortable . Overall we have spent more than 11 hours on the different buses and boats and stopped at 13 different locations . A great value !

Myself my adult daughter and my two younger teenage children wanted to take the night bus on a family ticket. 2 adults and 2 children.
We were told by the bus driver that we didn't qualify for a family ticket as we weren't a mum and a dad and 2 children. We argued that we were a family and after much discussion he allowed us to travel.
The route then wasn't as described in the leaflet, a lot of the landmarks were missed out and we didn't even get a front view of Buckingham palace! We went down the side and we're not even told it was there!
I have done the tour in the past by the original bus company and that one was great. If it was my first experience as a tourist, on a tour bus around London, I would have been extremely disappointed with the attitude and service of Big Bus Tours. My advice is avoid this one and use one of the others!

We only had one day to take in all of London so we were really hoping the bus tour would be excellent. The tour guide was a nice, friendly guy, but he just was not good at his job. He rambled and the bus drove too fast past all the major sights. At one point, the bus pulled over for about 10 minutes because a side panel fell off the bus. I usually love the bus tours and will ride them all the way through, but I could not wait to get off. We waited until we got to the river stop and hopped off and never got back on. We got on the free river cruise and it was excellent. The tour guide was funny, friendly, engaging, informative and really knew his stuff. We loved that tour. Too bad the bus tour was not at the same caliber.

What a wonderful service ! Buses every 15 mins and the live tour guides were amazing...We learned so much about the London area both past and present. We hopped on and off when we saw something we wanted to visit ... it was all so easy! These buses are a different colour to all the rest of the London buses and I would highly recommend it for that reason alone....we could always spot ours from the many other tour buses and the regular London transport ones easily and quickly and there were employees at most of the stops in easily recognisable burgundy uniform to help us out. All staff were most helpful. If you carry their map you will be instantly recognisable as one of their customers and they will offer help and assistance. We will definitely do this tour again. We chose the 48hr ticket, which gave us a river boat cruise night tour and 3 guided walking tours all for free.

My sister and I recently visited London and decided the best way to see all the sights was to take a bus tour.
Our Tour Guide, Patrick, was the making of the tour, he made every place of interest so special by giving us detailed and informed information but he did it in such a way that made it even more special. He was also happy to answer any questions we had about any particular sight and his sense of humour was the icing on the cake. Also thanks to Nigel, the driver, who made sure we were kept safe in the madness of the London traffic.

We hopped on at Westminister Bridge and had a 2 hour bus trip with the evening sunset and London in all it's glory. We enjoyed our evening bus ride immensely. We got to see so many places we otherwise did not have time to see. Plus with so many people in London it is great to see things from the top of a double-decker bus. Remember gloves, a hat and a good jacket if there is a chance of slightly cool air, it gets cold up there outside. But worth it, we all braved the chill and enjoyed it all. This trip supplies you with a head set so you are not subjected to having to listen to someone talk all the time.
Great trip.

Thanks Pete for your Red Line tour yesterday. We were going to "hop on and hop off" but you were just too entertaining so decided to stay for the whole trip. Very glad we did! A worthwhile tour to get your bearings and learn a bit about London. My recommendation is to do a tour with live audio rather than a recording.

I booked this for the day after we were arriving in London. The first day was just travel and with 5 hours ahead, it was going to bed at 5:00 AM. Figured an easy tour, which we could join in on anytime was perfect.

It proved to be great. Their were ear plugs for one line, but you could get off and get on a bus with a guide. We did that. We'd rather have a real person then a tape recording and the girl leading the tour gave tons of facts, but she keep making me laugh. She was working hard at her job, but light enough to make it fun.

We had to detour a bit b/c this was the day of the London Marathon. So, some areas we just couldn't get close to. To make up for it they gave us a pass for a second day, very nice.

We did get off the bus for a while for lunch that was pretty good for London standards. They let one waitress work the entire restaurant and they don't barely get tipped.

Anyhow, with 2 days of 2 hrs sleep, I was delighted when we finally decided to jump back on the bus. It did give you a good idea of the layout of London and different areas, especially if you had read up on the city. We saw where Central London and New London divide at the bridge. It's strange, one side has big, modern skyscrapers and the other very old historical building. Saw Piccadilly Circus, Harrods, Hyde Park, Buckingham Palace, Notting Hill, the Flea Markets, and Meat and Cheese Center, we went past South Kensington where the Victoria and Albert Museum, The Science Museum, and The Museum of Natural History were, Covent Gardens with exclusive shops and all the theater shows close by. We saw the 3 bridges that crossed the Thames River. It was a perfect start to get your bearing of the city and each unique neighborhood.

Included in the price 3 walking tours which sounded great, but we just didn't have the time. Also, included was using The Red Thames River Boat. My husband and daughter did use this to get to Greenwich to see the Royal Observatory. I used the bus for a couple of stops to get around as we hadn't purchased the Oyster Pass yet.

Well worth the money. Think £25 per person. I liked our guide and felt I had learned a lot. Got a good feel for London. Definitely Recommend as a start. Between that, walking, using the tube, by the end of the week, you will know the layout of London pretty well.

We brought our passes online which is cheaper and adding the fast track for the London Eye and a boat tour of the Thames. This is an on and off bus. Saw most of London without the use of the tube. Nice tours with earphones on some routes and live guides on others. Tours by earphones available in a various languages. I have difficulty walking so the young men at the various stops helped me by stopping the bus and making sure I was near where I wanted to see. The bus stops are easily identified and located throughout London. Best of all, we caught the a bus right in front of our hotel the Doubletree Hyde Park that morning and another returned us at the end of the day across from our hotel. We had caught the last bus of the day.

After reading several reviews for the major HOHO busses in London we pretty much scratched that off the list before we even got there. I did not want to buy a ticket only to find we could never find a bus to get on.

After checking in at the hotel, the Bellman/Concierge suggested that we do the HOHO bus (okay, we'll take our chances) and he sold us two tickets for Big Bus which also includes a boat ride. We got on the bus with just a voucher which was not stamped with the time (starting our 24 hours) until we got to the Big Bus office which was about 1 ½ hours after we boarded.

The busses were never full and we could always find a seat up top. Please note that there are “stop” buttons behind a few seats so if you want to stop, be sure to press the button as we missed one stop since no one was waiting to get on. We used the earbuds for narration and the quality of the sound is very good although the music got tiresome. Expect to change busses as Madame Tussaud’s as we did twice, drivers must begin and end shifts there. If you have a question, ask the roadside agent in the Big Bus uniform (not the driver) which seemed to be in all the major stops. Some attraction tickets can also be purchased from these agents.

Tip for the boat ride: You will be using “City Cruises” for the boat portion, a bit confusing as "City” is hidden in the signage (see upper left hand side of Big Bus map). Also note the times of the boat rides, we were out early (like 8am), the only people out were the locals going to work.

Another tip: Litter/trash cans are VERY difficult to find in the city so plan on carrying your trash for a while. We walked around with our coffee cups forever until we found a live street sweeper.

Visited london for the first time and decided to buy hop on/off tickets from the big bus company and didn't regret it. Staff was well informed and very entertaining. Got around london without any problems. I'd like to point out one young lady who works there. I hope i remember her name right. Danielle hosted a bus tour on one day and the following day it was a buckingham palace and harry potter walking tour. She was outstanding. Very bubbly and cheerfull. Absolutely happy girl and i was very happy she was my tour guide. Need more of those people like her!

We've been to London several times but this was out first bus tour, our first time being proper tourists 😳 We are 2 adults and 3 kids and our tickets cost £80 all together. I balked at the cost to begin with but then the young man told us that this included a boat trip on the Thames, so we took the plunge. We were given free headphones and headed for the open top. It was a chilly day but we weren't bothered as what a great way to travel around London. The information given through the headphones was great too, did you know that the flag flying on the top of the Houses of Parliament is as big as a tennis court? We thoroughly enjoyed out bus trips and saw lots more than if we had walked. The staff were very good too when it came to helping tourists find the right bus for the different routes. Well worth £80

My wife and I took the big bus tour of London when I was over in England on a business trip. The route that the bus took it all the great landmarks of London. Our English tour guide on the bus, was very informative, humorous, and generally made the two hour tour a lovely experience.

This is a great way to see London. We got a 48 hour pass and made use of blue and red tours and boat. Our first tour was on a red line bus, in my opinion the best, because its live commentary. We had a bus load of children on ours and it was quite noisy when they got on. But, we had a fantastic guide, Steve, or Mr Steve as he got the kids to call him. He was very good with them, asking lots of questions and keeping them amused. Once they got off, it was good to see how knowledgeable and funny he was. Great tour Mr Steve, from your brummy posse. Loved the whole experience. Will be coming back with parents later this summer. Good work, big bus.

Although I enjoyed the tour, it took over 4 hours to do a complete trip (red line) from where I started. The next day I did the part of the blue line that wasn't the same as red line. After an hour and a half traffic was getting worse, I just got off and took a taxi back to my hotel. There is construction everywhere in London and it doesn't make for great sightseeing at times.
We did this bus company last time we were in London and it was great. Easy way to get around and we loved that the bus stopped almost in front of our hotel.
I would recommend Big Bus Tours but just plan on it taking longer due to traffic.

Did a comprehensive tour around London-covered all the landmarks which was fantastic.
Only joined during midday- but managed to finished everything within time.
Bought tickets online- it is £8 cheaper than on site so that was awesome!
Seatings are widely spaced so very comfortable- travelled with two toddlers & one elderly and they all enjoyed it. Although at times i was concerned with my los but Ray the driver handled the big bus quite well- no jerking, abrupt stops or whatsoever :-)
Try to look for buses with live commentary- Leanne the awesome commentator made the whole experience amazingly brilliant!
She was right when she said - by the time you finish this tour, you will get a degree in the history of London lol..

We bought our tickets in conjunction with the London Eye. We were staying in Trafalgar Square. When we went to board the bus there, the rep from Big Bus Tours told us we couldn't board, and had to go to the London Eye to get our tickets (mind you, I had our tickets printed out because we had bought them online). What is the point of buying online if we have to go elsewhere to get actual tickets. Then, when we finally boarded the bus, it took two hours to get from the London Eye to Tower of London due to the traffic. Later, when we tried to get back on the bus after dinner at 6 pm, we were informed we could not because the buses stop at 6pm. Again, what?? So, we paid all that money for a two hour bus ride. Not happy and requesting a refund. Terrible experience.

We were traveling with a toddler ( no stroller) so choose big bus after researching here for our options. I am glad we did and chose the 48 hour tour. But we used a bit of strategy and ended up making the most of it. First thing is we started the tour towards the second half of the day. The following day we started early and did the tour from one end to the other, just to get our bearings of the city and to pick and choose where we actually wanted to go in for some additional sight seeing. From the second half of the day we started to hop and hop off, and didn't have to wait for more than 10 mins in any of the locations. The second day, we did the round trip cruise ( included in the ticket), and also used it as a way to get from westminster pier to the tower bridge and then back to London eye ( huge time saver). And with all of this we also managed to squeeze in a walking tour, which was super fun.
The biggest problem was one of the streets (tooley) was closed due to construction and there was no big bus person ( or any sign) giving clearing instruction on where to wait or what the alternative was. We ended up wasting nearly an hour to start the tour, and not after the clock started ticking. Overall the service was good and there were a lot of big bus guys (with the big bus logo on jackets) ready to offer assistance and help and more importantly be flexible ( we got off at a non-scheduled stop). I would definitely recommend this, especially with young children. London is a massive city and covering it over 48 hours is difficult, so forget about doing the 1 day pass, it doesn't make sense in terms of time and money. We did not do the night tour, it wasn't getting really dark until 8pm, and with our toddler it was difficult to stay past in the city longer than that. The commentary on the bus was very informative and the live commentary was also very effective as they had a couple of really funny engaging people with lot of insightful stories about the city.
The 48 hours pass is the way to go to get your money worth and also with a little bit of planning and strategy you can really make the most of it. Just remember not to use this to get from point a to b, because a lot of time will be lost in the commute, and if you are stuck in traffic, its worse.

We purchased a family ticket which included a boat ride. This cost just over £100 (not sure of the exact figure). The lady we purchased tickets from LIED about the times the services where available until. We where told we could use the bus until 10pm or even take the last boat back which again was up until 10pm.

The LAST bus we could take was 6pm and the LAST boat was 7pm. So either the ticket tout needs some training or this company are lying to people to make sales.

We waited for over 45mins at one stop - The hop on hop off bus really did not meet up to its name. After waiting 45 mins we got took to the next stop and told to exit the bus and this was the last bus. If we needed a bus we would have to walk to another stop....( this was 20 mins away)

We then FINALLY got on a bus but at this point it was rush hour and this journey took us a total of 3 hours to reach the point we wanted. ( covent garden)

I was told to call for a refund- but they also dont answer the phone.

These tours are an excellent way of getting around to see the sights London has to offer, plenty pick up points and you can hop on / off as much as you like. The commentary so you go round is very good and informative. Very easy booking service either by buying ticket or as I did this time by e-ticket, very quick and easy to book.

As I was in London for the London Marathon I didn't want to do a lot of walking, so this was an ideal way to see the sights of London. As our hotel was close to St. Pancras we were able to get on the Green link route to join the other two routes at Covent Garden. We were informed that the Red route had live commentary and the Blue route recorded commentary. We were going to go on the red route, but after a couple of blue buses came we decided to hop on one of those, the commentary was adequate, but from other reviews I'm sure the live commentary would have been better. As I said, I didn't want to a lot of walking so we skipped the walking tours. When you take into consideration you could hop on and off as many times as you like, some walking tours and a river cruise thrown in, it was good value for money

you can see London in a weekend or even a day this way! hop on hop off at frequent stops so you can get out and get a look around. Get the red route for the guide it's the best way to learn things they're so informative and answer your questions. It really is value for money we got the night tour and river tour with out 48 hour ticket and we got discounted tickets for other attractions like the london eye, london dungeon and the aquarium. Brilliant value for money and the best way to get around. All staff are very helpful and friendly and will help as much as they can :)

Spent a full loop on hop on hop off big bus with three jet lagged kids and grandma. Had the best experience with BIG STEVE- he was entertaining, knowledgeable and made the day for us. Kudos to the other staff- all very helpful and kind. Bravo Big Bus!

The bus service comes in two varieties and routes. There is a red tour with English live commentary and a Blue route with different stops and a variety of pre-recorded comments. All buses have an open-air section on top which allows you to take photos with a good perspective and no dirty bus windows. This is less desirable when it is cold and wet. Some guides are more engaging or more specific when pointing out sights than others. Occasionally, buses run late and as a result may skip a stop. Overall, we were very happy- so much so that we booked their Paris tour later in the week. Electronic vouchers may be hard to scan from some phones (turn up the brightness), so print vouchers if you can when buying online. We went through another service to buy a two-day ticket which scanned as the wrong tour. With my confirmation email, the driver set it straight. You can download the Big Bus ap and get tickets and tour maps directly.

We lucked out as our hotel was very close to one of the stops for the Big Bus. We bought a 48 hr pass. Went on both lines that were offered. Be prepared to sit in a it of traffic. This wasn't a problem as one of the lines has a live commentator while the other is recorded. Both were interesting. A boat cruise on the Thames was included but we didn't use it. The weather was very chilly. There is also a night tour included also. Worth of money and like I said, very convenient.

Of all the tours my friend and I completed on our trip across Europe, the big bus tour in London was the best. Danielle was our tour guide for one of our bus tours and a walking tour. She went above and beyond (even after the tours were finished) to truly make us feel like we were getting the best experience and make us feel like locals, which is especially hard to find with a corporate tour company. She was highly knowledgable about the history of ALL of London (which is huge!) and her recommendations were some of the highlights of our trip. She offered to personally accompany us to a few of her favorite pubs and local restaurants that were close by and I truly feel like our trip would not have been as fulfilling if we wouldn't have met her. You can trust that you will learn a lot and have a great time if you have her as your tour guide. Thank you Danielle, we can't wait to return to London! Cheers!

In bigger cities like London and Paris, we tend to use Big Bus as a full day program rather than a Hop on Hop Off.

Since my brother is visiting, we are doing touristy stuff with him and since I loved my Big Bus London experience a couple of years ago, I opted for Big Bus again.

Their website is pretty self explanatory and easy to navigate and buy tickets online (minor discount available for online booking)

The red line is the one with live commentary and only in English. If you need any other of the languages that Big Bus offers, what you want is the blue line (recorded commentary).

The blue line covers all that the red line does and a slightly longer trip around Hyde Park which is very useful if you are staying at a hotel in that area or need to get to Paddington or Victoria stations to catch a train out.

I bought the one day ticket (valid only on that day) rather than the 24 hour one, because we were going to be on the bus by 9 in the morning, so no chance of using it the next day.

The 48 hour ticket is better value for money. Plus you get a night ride around the city. But since we live in London, it didn't make sense for us and my brother had other plans for the next day.

What I really liked when booking tickets was that it didn't restrict you to pre-choosing your date, so you have the option to hold on to your ticket for a slightly sunnier day if you have time flexibility.

Our first guide for the day was Leanne #bigbusleanne who was AMAZING! Such an infectious bundle of energy. she gave us an all singing, dancing, musical experience on the tour. None of the following guides could match up to her energy and enthusiasm levels.

We then stopped for lunch before hopping on to City Cruises (complimentary with big bus) before we completed the circuit.

Big Bus does offer 3 free walking tours. But it won't be possible to attend all 3 of them and complete a circuit. If you take the 48 hour option, you may be able to do 2 of the tours. Then I would recommend the Royal Walk (to take in the changing of the guard) and the evening ghost walk.

You do get a booklet of vouchers, but I don't see myself using any of those any time soon.

Took 5YO and 7YO to London in the school holidays for the first time. Was nervous by the sheer number of operators doing this same trip but in my opinion I picked a perfect one for our needs. We parked up in Ealing Common (£10 all day parking in the secure multi storey shopping centre) and tool the train into Paddington (£12.10) which took about 10 mins. Jumped on the tour bus (less than 5 min wait) and we were off. Saw all the sights and hopped off at Westminster and Buckingham Palace. The boat trip from Westminster London Eye to Tower Pier (Tower of London) was incredible considering it was part of the ticket price. As soon as finished at the Tower of London there was a bus waiting for us.

In summary - does everything it says on the tin for a great price. Speaks volumes when you look at the occupancy levels of the other tour bus companies, Big Bus is filling their capacity far easier.

Buses clean and you can have a free poncho if it rains and you are not prepared like me.

5 stars, well done Big Bus Company.

As this was our first time in London what better way to see it on a bus. We don't see buses like this where we live in Texas so it was an experience.
Sam our guide was so sweet, it was cold and raining, and she looked so cold but she still had us laughing and sounded happy. She was very knowledgeable. We was stuck in traffic for about an hour up to St Paul's cathedral and was friendly towards us asking where we were from etc she even took pictures of me and my partner with the dome in the background as she could see we didn't like our selfies. She is a great guide and even though the traffic was bad that wasn't her fault. We stayed on the whole tour it took about 4 hours. Would definitely use big bus again.

I have decided to leave a review here to see what response I get this time!
I took my very excited 4 yr old on her first trip to London as she loves reading Paddington bear books and she asked to go on a bus tour.
Sadly, the tour was very short lived as we made it round the Tower of London and then sat in traffic with no movement for about an hour!
It seems this was due to the new cycle route way being built and congesting that area.
I accept traffic is to be expected in London but what I am more annoyed about is that I received an email asking me to review big bus tours on trust pilot, which I did so in a perfectly fair manner. This review was responded to with a promise of a full refund plus complimentary tickets so my daughter could experience the tour again properly.
I was chuffed with this response and told her about it.
Sadly, it seems this is just a standard response on any negative reviews your company receives, as despite following the guidance received, big bus tours ignore every email I have sent to try and arrange this promise!
Makes you look good on your negative reviews but is dishonest!!
Come on big bus tours - step up and live up to your promise!!!
Don't mess with 4 yr olds!!!!!

We had an excellent day using the Big Bus tour. Buses were frequent, we did not wait long at any bus stop. Staff were very helpful and friendly. Also enjoyed trip on Thames with City Cruises. Good commentary and an excellent way around the capital.

We took this tour with my parents on their first day to London...we had all been to London before and took this trip to reaquaint ourselves even though we probably didn't need it.

The tour guides in general were not terribly engaging, bordering on rude and condescending in some cases and the routes were slowed down and also disrupted and confusing due to road works...this wasted a lot of time as we waited for buses at places where the map said we should be standing, only to find that due to roadworks we were in the wrong place.

Really, it cost us over $100 Australian dollars for two of us and it literally took us the whole day to get it finished due to all the time wasted waiting around and working out where we had to be to join the right bus.

Look - perhaps we hadn't asked the right questions in the first place nor read the brochure properly, but half way through the day we would have bailed except that we had already paid the money.

I did it for the commentary, but it wasn't really worth it - better to walk around and see the sights on foot.

I really enjoyed my day in London with the Big Bus tour, a ticket for the day is available for 27 Pounds which is a good deal and the busses drive regularly which is very convenient.

Especially the "Mystery and haunted Tour" with Patrick was an amazing experience I wouldn't miss. You walk around London in a small group and the see some things that you normally would never get to see. On top of that you get a guide who is dedicated friendly and just a very cool and nice guy who tells you a lot of information about ghost stories in and about London and you could feel the passion he puts in! And the best of it is that the tour is for FREE when you purchase a Bus ticket!!!
The mystery tour was one of my highlights during my stay in London and I can only recommend it!!!
When I come to London again I will do the tour again any time!

Big Bus tours are well organised and great value for money.

I recommend u buy a 30 pound 48 hours validity on weekends. A day ticket is 26 pounds.

The tour includes a boat ride on River Thames as well. The guides are well trained and have a good sense of British humour.

LOCATION:
Varies through the city - see their map. Only goes in one direction even though it is hop on hop off so you have to wait often

ABOUT THE TOUR:
Head sets are not very good so recommend bringing your own. Info is worth listening too because you will learn a lot about London

Opt for a package with the night tour and river cruise if possible, well worth it. London is beautiful at night and the river is a peaceful trip with a different perspective of the city. You can start at the Emirates Air Cable car and end at the London Eye so it is an ideal trip if you want to see those attractions.

OTHER:
When staying close to Green Park / Piccadilly, the pick up location was not the best. We seemed to wait a lot and there were lots of other Tour Buses going by...we looked at the other bus company and found their routes and times seemed to be better for our location - check out all maps for the 3 main tour buses before deciding...might be worth paying a little more depending on where you are staying because their routes differ

If you want to see London, use these guys. The service is very regular, you can hop on and off the buses at regular, designated stops, the commentary is very informative and interesting.
As you enter the bus, pick up your map and ear phones, get plugged in, and enjoy!

We used golden tours a couple of years ago and they were ok but went with big bus as they were cheaper for a family of 4.
Plenty of buses about so just hopped on as we needed rather than follow a timetable. We didn't get a tour guide so can't really comment but Simon ( I think that was his name) who sorted our ticket out at Westminster Bridge was a great guy and really helpful as were the other guys we encountered over the two days.
I was unsure when choosing as all companies had similar negative reviews but I made the right choice!!

there are so many different companies offering more or less the same product: Getting you around the city
But Big Bus is very different:
They have comfortable and clean buses, they run very often and they have live guided tours. We were so lucky when Nobby (on of those guides) gave us a lot of complimentary and helpful information, we had lots of fun with our guide in the afternoon, all together three different guides, but all of them funny and very friendly.
