(All the other people working were always friendly too and supported as much as they could)

Definitely a recommendation !

First off, I got the tour free as part of the London pass, but I certainly wouldn't buy it after the time we had.

Day One. I didn't know you had to have tickets printed even with your London Pass, many places just scan it. So my son and I run up to a bus where we want to start for the day. I start to ask the guy at the station what to do with the London Pass, but the 2nd bus driver sitting in the bus is pounding on the window hollering at us to get on. Should have been my warning I suppose. So we hop on courtesy yellow line, show our London Pass and sit down. He asks where our first stop is, we tell him Madame Tussauds, he explains yellow turns to orange at such and such stop. We ride a while, he points out some interesting things, they have to change drivers. Isn't easy, see the steering wheel column is stuck and the next driver is rather large and can't get behind the wheel. They call for help, or to figure if the other can keep driving. 30 minutes later they're still doing this, so I ask where the next stop is and start walking. 45 minutes later, no bus has shown up, but several have passed, and my bus is still parked behind us. We give up and start walking. We walked from Marble Arch to Lancaster Gate tube station and grab the tube into town with a new set of plans. Pissed does no even begin to describe my attitude about the whole thing. Luckily my son is 11 and I wasn't carrying him, I looked it up, and it's only a mile, but not the way I wanted to start my day. I guess it's a good thing they didn't print my tickets, because I got another chance the next day.

Day Two. Walk from the hotel back to the yellow line stop. Have our London Pass scanned and got tickets printed, get on the next bus. Am informed that yellow changes to orange at such and such place, but if has to make a circle as yellow first, and am given the option to hop off on a later stop and wait for an orange. After yesterday I say no thanks I'll stay on this one, just in case. We make the circle, change to orange, change drivers without incidence and keep going. We listen to the our audio hop on and off a half dozen times, had a perfectly lovely experience.

Unfortunately I don't know which day is typical for the company.

I'm a big bus fan. What can be better than a bus ride around learning all about places. Positives.... Staff good, buses in great condition and commentary Interesting. The boat ride a nice touch. Negatives... London traffic. It just isn't made for this type of tour or hop on hop off. At times it was so slow that it was easier to use the underground. It was easier to get around New York. No disrespect to what they are trying to do and it could be phenomenal but we had a pass for several days and the traffic was so bad it was hard to use as a hobo. But if you have a day spare take a tour for the views and knowledge as that is where this excursions strength is

We have just returned from a sightseeing visit to London, this was our 4th visit and on previous occasions we have always used the big bus tour but this time was not a success.
On our first day we waited in for 45 mins for a tour bus to turn up, the attendant was very unfriendly and we were £64 for a 2 day pass which would of been ok but as the bus was running so late the driver cut off some of the tour to try and make up some time.
On the second day we waited 55 mins in the cold and rain and when the bus turned up there was no-one on it and when we asked the driver what the delay was he just shrugged and said traffic but several other tour buses were running on a regular basis, we watched them go past every 10-15 mins but has we had spent all that money we didn't want to change.
We feel extremely let down and disappointed with service we were given, given it was the middle of February and the buses were not busy

Always using Big Bus Tours ASAP when arriving to a new city to get a quick overview of the city and locations of different tourist attractions, to then know what to actually visit during my next days. Using maps and tourist guides is one thing, but with the hop-on-hop-off Big Bus Tours it is all much more convenient and it also gives much better idea of actual distances and time required between moving between the attractions. The audio guides also give valuable and interesting information.

I purchased the one day Big Bus ticket with a promotional free extra day. I believe the ticket always includes a river tour. The first day I waited 50 minutes for my first bus ride at Lancaster Station.The employee there made phone calls a couple of times and kept telling me they would be there in a "couple of minutes". I get the idea he waited until I became irritated and started making comments about how many times the other brand of tour buses passed then called and told them to come but I couldn't be sure. At the next stop we waited over 10 minutes so in total I had over an hour of wasted time. I was very tired and not up for walking much due to my overnight flight so I just rode around and viewed the sights from the bus. Since I did not get off I do not know how frequently the buses picked up at the other stops. In my opinion a lot of time was spent on the blue route without seeing much of interest except Harrods which was cool at night because of its lights but would be uneventful during the day if not stopping there. It was a good activity for the situation although the wait was very irritating. When I went to the bus stop the next day I told the attendant that I would be writing a review and mentioning the long wait on the previous day. He made a couple of calls and the bus came after about 10 minutes. I changed to the red route at Marble Arch. It had the same kind of recorded commentary, not live as advertised. I rode to the Saint James park area and viewed nearby sights then walked to the meeting point for the river cruise. I really enjoyed the river cruise. You can get on and off at any of the 4 stops and ride it one way or round trip. I couldnt hear the commentary very well but you can request a recorder with earphones. Afterwards I walked to Buckingham Palace then to the nearest stop which took me back to Lancaster gate so I didn't use the bus much that day. My advice is that you need to plan on a whole day if you want to make even a couple of stops and, for the most efficient use of your time, stick to the routes that are both blue and red. If I went again I would at least investigate the other hop on/off bus company reviews to see if they seem to run more frequently for the same price and number of sites covered. One was called "City SightSeeing" and another was called "The Original".

The bus tour staff were nice and professional, however, the London traffic is so horrendous (with road works). that an indicated 2 hour tour took us more than 4 hours just to get to the Tower and have a short Thames Tour. I the end, it was taking so long to get anywhere (sitting for 30 minutes in a traffic jam is not what you pay for in a tour), that we just cut the tour short and went back to the hotel. Its probably a great tour in total but they should have advised us of the delays before we bought the tickets. Its not like the traffic was unknown.

Booked our tickets in advance £28 for 2 days on the bus and 2 days on the river cruise (taxi).The buses do different tours red and blue with different sights .you can get on and off as you want and some have audio commentry (choice of languages)via earphones (supplied) some have a tour guide whom speaks via microphone and speakers and are not omly informative but alse entertainingly funny.the Thames cruisers travel up and down the Thames and stop at berths all the way up and down either side of the river plenty of seating (all inside) and refreshments are available inc.a bar again with a live commentry via microphone and speaker.

This has to be the bargain way of touring london great value and very enjoyable.

In London with our grandchildren we picked up a Big Bus at Madame Tussauds and, taking the guide's advice, changed at Regent Street to the shorter tour. We had just a few hours so this was a great way of ensuring that the little ones saw the highlights of London. It's so easy to go place to place on the tube but this way we were able to see everything as Ivor the guide pointed the sights out to us. A couple of hours well spent. You really need to be upstairs to see everything so make sure you wrap up well in January.

If you're looking to see all of the most famous parts of London, this is probably the best way to do it. The blue line takes you all around the monuments and most historic parts and it's always interesting to hear the stories whilst seeing the sights. It's worth sitting on the upper level to get some really nice pictures even if it's a bit cold. It seems like the most touristy thing to do, but it's only so popular because it's such a good introduction to the city. You can hop on/hop off at any stop and there is a complimentary river cruise included. I would just suggest making sure you know the schedule and when it ends so that you can end the tour where you want to or where you're staying. It's worth the money, but the best way we found was booking online directly from the big bus website. It was more expensive from hotels and street shops. You can purchase it on your mobile right before getting on and then they'll scan your phone on the bus. It seemed like the most convenient way to do it.

Has a single afternoon in London and wanted to hit the sights. Had been umming and ahhing about a open top bus tour and after a bad flight decided to do it to save time. Talked with the rep and told him what I wanted to see - he said the blue line would take me to everything. What wasn't mentioned was that for a lot of the sights you can't see them from the bus, you have to get off and then get back on. I was very clear that I only had that afternoon and wanted to stay on the bus and just get a glimpse. For the first 1.5 hours the only notable sight seen was Marble Arch - about 5 times. Then finally in the second 1.5 hours saw Trafalgar Square, Westminster Abbey, Houses of Parliament, Big Ben, London Eye, Tower Bridge and Tower of London. It doesn't drive past Buckingham palace, but it stops around the corner. I couldn't get off because by then it was dark and I'd been freezing on the bus for 3 hours. Wasn't worth £32. Other tours like this you've been able to see all the highlights and they're a great way to see a city when you only have a few hours.

We recently took the tour around London. As a family we have taken hop on hop off tours around the world and have to say this was one of the worst we have ever been on. The tour was very disorganised and definitely not worth the money we paid for it. We spent most of the time on the bus stopped as they spent at least 10 minutes at each stop which was just not necessary. Not only that but the recorded commentary was very poor it spent most of the time playing annoying music. We ended up getting off the bus and catching the tube as we just were bored and could not take it anymore. Definitely not the best way to get around London.

We downloaded the big bus tours app, and booked through there managing to get 24 hours free, so had 48 hours access for the price of 24! this was not advertised on the website so glad we downloaded it.

This was a brilliant way to see London, with its hop on hop off deal you can stop on any of the designated stops on the route, explore the area, then get on the next bus, so easy and flexible!

Busses ran every 5 to 15 mins so you never wait long for another one. There are 3 routes, Blue, Red and Green. We didn't use the Green route but the Blue Route has a 12 Language audio tour, in ear headphones supplied, that provide a running commentary at each place you pass of interest, playing classical music in between. I found it interesting and informative, but once I had done the route I didn't bother listening again, I just sat back and enjoyed the view.

The red route for me was by far the best, with the tour guide. We had some great guides who were very enjoyable to listen to and such fun! they were brilliant with both humour and knowledge and made the tour so much fun.

The buses were clean and comfortable, the staff very polite and helpful. It was such a great way to get around and see so much of London for a good price in such a short 2 days. Well worth it I can highly recommend to everyone.

This is the full day VIP tour from Viator, which is available through tripadvisor. The trip is a very good way to get an overview of the highlights of London. Moreover, the guide (Dan) was remarkable. He was informative, entertaining, and just snarky enough (in a benign way) to keep you smiling and glad that you are there. We did the tour on Sunday morning, which was ideal because of the lack of traffic. The payback was that the tour could not go into the cathedrals officially. Individuals could go in on their own, however. The overview was nice because it helped figure out where we wanted to dive deeper into and where we had enough. Again, Dan was wonderfully helpful for this. The other pleasant surprise was the tea and champagne at the end of the tour (an option). As I understand as a silly Yank, we had a traditional teal with all the trimmings. It was not a second rate experience. There were two issues not quite as advertised. The first is that there is no Thames cruise. You are on the Thames via what is essentially a water taxi ride. Pleasant - but not a 'one way tour of the Thames'. The second is that for there is no pick up a some major hotels, which isn't clear when you sign up. Taxis are remarkable in London, so this isn't a big deal once you figure that out - but when you sign up, its almost a wee bit misleading.

My husband and I visited London for the New Year's Eve celebrations, we had a two day ticket and had a fantastic time both on the bus and the river cruise, both tour guides were amazing, good fun and informative.

Great way to get your bearings in London before you start walking around. The tours takes 3 hours and takes in all the main interesting things. There are 3 types I took the yellow was very happy with the experience. Cost seemed a bit high but when you realize your ticket lasts 48 hours includes a river cruise and the on off bus.

I took my husband on the Big Bus tour of London on December 27th, 2015. There is enough shelter to sit outside on the top deck.
The Blue and Red routes were well articulated. The Red route had live commentary with a few jokes on the side.
Select your hot spots in advance so that you can plan your journey well.
Book online.... we ended up with 48 hours for the price of 24 hours. Also, we had a FREE Thames boat cruise included.
We have used the Big Bus in Paris, twice and Athens. Never fails .... Loved it. Thank you Big Bus.

Took the Big Bus Tour with a live guide, not the pretaped head sets..what a way to go. Our guide, Big Steve was entertaining, informative and so much fun. It was a rainy day and we were on the covered top part of the bus...saw a lot, learned a lot..would go again in a minute! Thanks!

The blue route was a good way to get some information about the history of the City and to hop/off as desired. However, hopping back on could take a while in between buses. We hopped onto a red line bus and there was very little historic information given by the human guide. I prefer the headphones on the blue route because it is consistent. It is difficult in January with the rain and cold to appreciate the bus ride completely as we would have liked to be on the topside to get the best view and the best pictures. But if you wait for no rain on London, you won't see much. LOL. Overall we enjoyed our time driving around London on the bus. Ran out of time for the boat ride and it poured the 2nd day so we Saint get to do that

Best way to see London if you don't have a lot of time, I would recommend that you try and buy the 48 hours bus tour this will include a boat trip to Greenwich. The boat trip is also recommended as it is a nice way to see London. Make sure you go on the live guided tours as the audio tours can become a bit boring. The live guides are awesome!

We took the GREEN LINE Big Bus from Kings cross bus stop at almost 9Am. It took us more than 20 mins to wait for the bus to arrive. From there, we were dropped off at ALDWYCH bus stop and waited for the RED OR BLUE BUS for the tour.

The tour was indeed wonderful and convenient as it stops to all landmarks or tourist attractions in London. The tour guides at the Red Bus was wonderful, cheerful and very knowledgable. What I just noticed is, some of the staff at the bus stops and drivers were not that accommodating. We were annoyed by how they sarcastically answer our queries. Because if we have known, we wont ask in the first place. I think thats something they can improve with. But with golden tours, I must say they are very consistent because almost all stops, there are also golden tours agents who looks after their clients really well. It made me think that I should have availed the tour from them instead.

The tour itself is a must at London. I just wont recommend Big bus company.

I have used Hop-On-Hop-Off city sightseeing buses in the past to see other cities and this company was suggested to me by the hotel I was staying at, but I was very disappointed.

We were told that the buses will come past each stop every 10-20 minutes, however at some stops we had to wait up to 40 minutes for a bus to come past which isn't good enough when you are trying to see the sights in a short amount of time like I was.

We even had a bus driver who didn't stop at one of the stations, one that we needed to get off at to get to our hotel and when asking the bus driver about it he rudely told me it did stop and that I should have been paying attention - however there was another couple who also wanted that stop and also didn't get the chance to get off the bus.

Overall, we ended the day frustrated and disappointed - will not be using this company again and will instead be recommending "City Sightseeing" a red double decker bus company that we have used in other cities and that also operate in London.

We visited London last weekend and booked Big Bus Tour tickets online at £26.00 each. Cheaper than buying at the hotel for £32.00 each!

This proved excellent value. It was automatically upgraded from 24 to 48 hours, included a free river cruise (again hop on, hop off), £5.00 each of The Shard and various other money off discounts at eateries and attractions.

All bus drivers and conductors we encountered were helpful and polite. Commentary a bit hit and miss. On one trip we had an excellent commentator on another trip we were just given headphones.

The buses we used were clean and had an open top upstairs, some with partial cover.

Definitely a great stress free way to get around London.

There are three (four?) bus tour companies in London, and I've been on most or all of them - they are pretty interchangeable. Get the best deal that fits your personal needs (number of people, days available, etc). If you are an English Speaker, I strongly recommend a tour with a live guide - they make the trip so much more informative by pointing out little things that the recorded tours miss, and by being available to answer questions about things that catch your eye - especially if you are stuck in traffic. If it is a sunny day, I highly recommend sunscreen if you are on an open top bus - even if it is cool. Up top is best if you're taking pictures - and there are a lot of things to photograph on London bus tour. It's nice to take the tour your first day in the City so you can get a feel for the overall layout and it will help plan how you want to see the main sites.

I've used Big Bus before for a quick 1 day overview of London and DC and 2 days in Shanghai. Good for when you don't have a lot of time. In this case, though, it was taking way too long. From the time we bought the tickets near Bayswater tube station until it arrived at Madam Tussauds (which we weren't getting off for), it had already been like an hour and a half and so while the bus was sitting in front of Tussauds for 10 or 15 minutes while they continued to try to sell tickets to other attractions, we bailed. Hopped on the tube to the Tower of London. The bottom line is with Google maps and a transit oyster card, you can pretty much do what you want to do without being drivin' around slowly and waiting pointlessly at spots you don't care about. The oyster card gives you unlimited bus riding too so you can get your scenic double decker bus ride on the transit buses. I'll think twice before using Big Bus again.

I had not been to London for 30 years and wanted an easy way to reacquaint myself with the city. On the afternoon of my arrival day, while still fighting jet lag, I bought a 48-hour ticket. I used Big Bus (easily accessible close to my hotel) on three different occasions over the next 48 hours. I succeeded in my goal of seeing the city from one end to the other.

Note: There is the red tour with a live narrator and the blue tour with a recorded commentary. In the end, I preferred the blue; the live narrators felt they had to fill the time even when the bus was not moving and I got tired of their efforts to be funny.

We boarded this bus around 11:30 and were told we could make the circuit in two hours. We spent approximately 90 minutes off the bus, eating lunch and seeing the sites; we missed the attractions that we were hoping to see the most, because of the route taken-we saw one stop three times-and the long waits for the next bus to pick us up. Traffic was heavy that day, which was a factor, but the upshot is that I missed seeing the Tower Bridge, Tower of London and St. Paul's Cathedral. We could have saved so much and avoided attractions of which we had no real interest if we had simply taken the tube. That was my only day to tour the city, so disappointing scarcely describes the experience.

In one week I did the Hop On Hop Off on both the Original and the Big Bus tours. I found Big Bus to have far superior guides. The Original guide we had may have been tired, but she seemed rather uninterested in the entire trip.

On the other hand the Big Bus guides (we had two different guides as we hopped on midway) were both excellent, clever, and actually gave interesting and enthusiastic information about what we were seeing. On the Original bus tour we were often sitting at traffic lights next to something interesting (like the Westminster House of Parliament ) and said nothing.

We used The Original first (and it was a nice day) and thought it was fine. A few days later took Big Bus (on a cloudy day) and it was so much better!

I was travelling with 2 foreign friends who had never been to London & I chose Big Bus tours to give them an overview of this great city. Our hotel was very close to the Victoria bus stop from where we could take either the red or blue route - we did both. the commentaries were clear & interesting, the live ones very amusing. Staff were generally very helpful.The short boat trip which is included gave another view of London. The only thing we found disappointing was that the buses stop at the very early time of 5.00 pm. At first we didn't realise this & stood for some time waiting for a bus that never appeared.

Our visit to London was going to be very short, so we decided we would take one of the bus tours which would allow us to see the city without trying to go to every single place. There are 30 or 40 stops along the route which allows you to get on / get off wherever you want but which also lengthens the trip considerably. The stairs to the upper deck were very narrow and steep so not ideal for people with physical challenges. Sadly, it was extremely difficult to take photos from the lower level deck as the windows were highly reflective. It was also very hard to hear the guide from below, despite his use of a microphone.

Good servive but you are loosing a lot of time due to BIG TRAFFIC JAM in London
(same for all the tour companies)

I booked this tour ahead of my arrival in London and at that time, it saved me a few pounds. (I recently checked the site and the price for an open ticket seems to be the same now for a pre-booked ticket).

Customer Service:
The ticket vendor/collector waits at most stops and you can validate your online voucher or buy a ticket there. The bus driver and the tour guide were friendly enough. Free earbuds and maps were available on board.

Tour:
The tour covers a lot of London quickly. Of course like with all bus tours of this kind, you can simply hop-on and hop-off at any major attraction site. The guide was funny informative and spoke clearly.

Value for Money:
At 26 GBP it's quite a lot for a 24 hour ticket, because realistically, if you were going to use this as your mode of transport around London, you might as well use the Tube (it's cheaper and more of a local experience). You copuld potentially get stuck in traffic while on the bus too which may cut down on your sight-seeing time if you're in London only for a short while. But if you want to see a LOT of London in a short while with no particular interest in lingering in one of the major sites then this would be worth it. I was in London for 6 days and I couldn't even see all of it. If it wasn't for this bus tour I would have missed seeing The City of London (the old part of London not to be confused with the larger Metropolitan City of London itself).

I would recommend the Big Bus to anyone visiting London. It is a great value and great way to see the city and learn the layout.

Our tickets included the night tour and a one way boat right on the Thames. The night tour was cancelled due to the season so we were given an extra day on the bus! We road the red and blue lines, and the tour from Westminster to the Tower of London!

Red line - live commentary in English. We hopped on and off several times over two days. Our guides were VERY informative and willing to answer all the random questions that came their way. I know it's not easy to stay entertaining and candid but they were all so very kind and pleasant to listen to. Their random facts were fascinating and helpful. They also gave people a heads up when a stop or attraction was coming up so they knew when to get off the bus.

We were waiting for our tour to start at Green Park and I asked about the changing of the guards. Our driver told me that it was every other day and we should go now or else we would have a hard time getting seats. I thought that was nice information for him to give us. He even gave us directions though the park.

The Blue line is recorded. Cheesy music with fun facts and information about the area you are in. Sometimes it doesn't sink up with what you are looking at but I still learned a ton. They have headphones on the bus for you as well!

This is a great way to see the city and manuever without having to take the Tube or a taxi. It can get crowded but most lines run every 5/10 minutes. If it's raining - they offer rain ponchos.

Highly Recommended!

I really enjoyed the experience on the Big Bus tours, the tour guide had a lot of interesting information to share, and was energetic in his delivery.

I wish I had a better day weather wise, but it was still very much enjoyable.

Tickets for the Big Bus Tours were purchased early in the day at the train station. I boarded and let the speaking guides inform me of all the wonderful sights and highlights of London. I soaked them all in, taking the river boat tour that was included to see things from the water. I was very happy with a full day of sightseeing and the helpful Big Bus guides to inform me to bus schedule times and describing options for walking, riding or taking the boat. All in all an excellent way to see London when it is your first time and you have limited time to see it. Recommend this bus company for sure. Good value.

London is a very large city with a lot of sightseeing to do. This hop-on/hop-off tour is a great way to orient yourself. The tours with live commentary are great, giving loads of information, both historical and trivial.

The buses run often but may not be the best option for transportation around London as they only run in a single direction.

It's best to book online. That is where you find the best deals.

This is a hop-on/hop-off tour. You can ride all day long, stopping whenever you wish at any of the many stops. We chose to stay on a RED bus, which meant we had a live English-speaking tour guide. The BLUE buses have recorded tours in many languages. We felt that we got to see so much of London which otherwise we wouldn't have been able to see or learn about on our own. The top of the open-air bus was great, but chilly. Starting out early in the morning meant we missed the huge crowds. At some stops later on, patrons weren't able to board the bus, because they were already full! We did the whole loop on the red line (3 hours) and enjoyed it all, then stayed on and went partially around again, stopping where we wanted to.

We picked this tour up at the beginning and as it was a beautiful day, we sat on the top and were joined by our tour guide. He was a chatty soul who told us all about the historical bits and bobs on the tour route and then funny quips and irrelevant information that doesn't relate to the tour but we all had a good little giggle at them as they were interesting and funny. I don't know if all the staff are as good as he was but it was well worth the money. It was hop on and hop off so if you wanted to see something you could just get off and get back on but we did the whole lot one the one loop.

I recommend getting the yellow tour from the beginning spot on the map (Piccadilly Circus) as this is the tour with live commentary on. We also go the river cruises tickets with the purchase so got a river tour as well - another funny commentator and nice little cruise along the river

I love the Big Bus company and I tour on them in the major cities I visit. The Big Bus offers several routes (Red, Blue, Green) so you can see different parts of London. I like to ride the entire route non-stop without hopping off/on the first day I visit a city; this way I get a good sense of the city. The Big Bus London's provides a lovely pre-recorded history lesson of the various sites on the Blue tour and live description on the Red tour. London's traffic is very busy and it seems like there is a traffic light every 100 meters, therefore, it takes a really long time to get through the route. But overall, the Big Bus is a great way to tour the city.

For first time visitors in London, Big Bus is a great way to go to see the sights and highlights. Note: when you buy your ticket make sure you get the "yellow" voucher and not just the paper receipt. The driver should give it to you. It is required to take the Thames River Cruise - they'll ask to see the yellow voucher. Overall a very positive experience. Start early in the day for a full day of touring.

Here is why we loved the Big B hop on hop off bus. The 48 hr ticket included: a full ride around London at the top of double decker with headphone description of attractions, A nighttime bus ride around London, walking tours (we took the Royal tour and saw the changing of the guards) and the river cruise (we took it from the Tower back to Westminster as there was a smaller line up from that end) and we took it on the morning of the third day just before our ticket expired to a place we wanted to go that morning and hopped off..... Remember this is a 48 hour ticket not a 2 day ticket. Well worth the money and if you know the days you are going to need it before you leave home, buy it from home before you go and save a bit of money.

Big Steve was my tour guide on the red line, and he was hilarious. He already made the cost of the ticket worthwhile, without including all the awesome sights and ability to hop on and off all day. The tour was FULL of interesting information and Steve was very interactive with all the passengers. He was even chatting with them in their native languages (by the way, his American accent is great).

The Big Bus Tour stops around all the places you want to see. I recommend splurging on the 48 hour ticket.

If you're just in London for a few days Big Bus is great for getting around. We did a lot of walking and hopping on/off. I've been doing big bus tours in several cities already (cape town, sf, barcelona,...) and they are always fun and cover the important tourist-y stuff. The red tour has live commentary and from the 4 tour guides we met three of them were funny and/or very informative. Recommended.

Just returned from a brief first visit in London and wavered between "Big Bus Tour" and the "Original London tour". Both are comparable in price and no doubt you will likely get a similar tour from the other company but Big Bus won me over thanks to the added 'night time tour' which felt great riding on the open roof of the bus on a mild night to take in the colors and sounds. The cost of the 48 hour hop on hop off with free night tour was only a few more $ so well worth the upgrade from the base ticket. Most of the guides directing were pleasant but one guide that is a must and highly recommend is Kevin for the 10:20am changing of the Palace guards walking tour. He was animated, informative, and pleasant. The river cruise included was ok and brief. More time spent waiting to queue the line than to cruise it seemed. Overall I can recommend this tour for incite especially if you are pressed for time in London.

3rd time I have used Big Bus with visitors from out of the country. This was the worst of the 3. Busses did not run as advertised. Many waits of over 35-40 min. for the Red route. Live narration was so so...he sounded bored. Other tour busses were running circles ar9und the Big Bus tours. Staff of the Big Bus, at the stops, are always polite, friendly, and helpful.....but gone from some posts by 4pm! Route points out lots of interesting sites.

This is a mixed review - there were things that were brilliant and things that sucked. If I could give this experience 2.5 I would have chosen it.
Let me start by saying we chose the 48 hour tour at GBP33 per head. I know this is expensive and it's all relative, but where we come from (South Africa) most people live off of less per month, so for us this was really an experience.

1. THE BAD:
We booked online as it was cheaper and we were promised a boat cruise, the buses, walking tours and a booklet with reward vouchers.
On getting to our first bus we scanned our code for our tickets and were given 24 hour bus tickets. We said this wasn't what we booked and the usher/ticket selling man very rudely basically told us that this wasn't his problem. If he'd had a nicer tone, it would have been much better. I realize this might have been his defensive mode, but we were very confused and afraid of losing so much money. Some reassurance would have helped. Added to that the bus driver was being rude to some tourists trying to get onto the bus and was barking at them to wait for others to get off (logistically I get that,, though). Our usher man also told us that the reward voucher booklet would cost 6 pounds and to take up our issues at Victoria station.
We finally got it sorted out after we stopped at another stop and had a more helpful usher. They finally put us through to the office who then helped and rectified the mistake.
This whole experience sucked about 30-45 minutes off our time. Fortunately we aren't just in London for a weekend.
As we got to our boat cruise later the day we were about to ask whether the boat goes to Greenwich (included in price) before the usher just made marks on our ticket (you can only use it once). The boat didn't go to Greenwich and the last one had long since departed. We couldn't hear the guide and in desperation I took a German audio guide (I have limited knowledge of the language). It crackled so much I couldn't hear a thing.
Fortunately we found a nice usher the next day who said we could go on another boat to Greenwich which was brilliant.
The final bad part of the tour - on both Saturday and Sunday we rushed toward Trafalgar Square trying to join the haunted walking tour. On Saturday there were other tourists we didn't know running around with us looking for the group and we couldn't find anything. Granted - we might have missed them in the rush. I guess the tour doesn't operate on Sundays, which I'm hoping accounts for our second rush. It would've been nice if they'd let us know, though. I told a few crew members earlier that day that we were hoping to go on the walking tour and nobody said anything.

THE GOOD:
The live English guides are (mostly) brilliant. Especially Big Steve. I think he needs a raise or could even start his own tour company. Really a great guide - professional, informative, but jokey and fun. We even stayed on our bus, even though we missed our destination, because we wanted to hear the rest of his stories. Our boat guide (couldn't catch his name, but he was older) was also very good. He had a dry sense of humour which made it quite a funny trip. Out of all the live guides we only had one bad-ish guide, who went on about Boris Johnson's cycle lanes and how it was absurd. It may well be, but a bus tour is not the place or the time to air your own views.

So, if everything worked I would've given this tour a 4.5 out of 5. I think they try very hard. It might just be that the company is so big that quality control issues are slipping through.

Prebooked out tickets online for a bit of discount. Print off your confirmation & exchange with vendor for your ticket, hope on a bus & off you go!

The red route is the more central one, Westminster, West Minster Abby, Big Ben, London Bridge, Tower Bridge, St Paul's Cathdral, Buckingham Palace & many more. The blue route covers that & Kensington Palace & the famous Harrods!

I booked the 24hr ticket with free cruise. Having done a bus tour before (Not Big Bus) the river cruise then took you from Big Ben to Greenwich. However this free cruise was only between Big Ben & Tower Bridge. So I was quite disappointed that we didn't get to Greenwich, however if you book a 48hour ticket, Greenwich is included, but if you buy a 24hour ticket, you get 24hours free anyway...... It's a tricky one! Should maybe state this more on website.

Other than that, it's a must do for visiting London as you get to beat the traffic & all the busy pedestrian traffic & take in all the sights & landmarks from the top of a bus! :-)

So a year later we tried the big bus tour again, and by mistake got on a live commentary bus... This wasn't anything like last year though. We had Jack and he was brilliant, so informative, polite, funny. And then we got a lady called Pearl and she was also fantastic.
There were a few diversions but nothing horrendous, and they still managed to provide lots of information. Just a really enjoyable tour.
River cruise was great as always.
Also, customer service last year once I complained was good, apologetic and dealt with the individual appropriately.
Thank you

Meh. I have to admit that seeing cities by open-air bus is one of my least favorite forms of tourism; I far prefer using public transportation, walking, and exploring the city at my own pace. But, we were traveling with some individuals who had never been to London and had some physical limitations that made long days of walking unfeasible, so we decided to buy tickets for the Big Bus, as it gives people in London only a couple of days a good sense of the city.

Upsides: a two-day ticket allows you to break-up the bus tour with some other sightseeing (we did about half of the tour on the first day, and about half on the second day, with tours of Westminster Abbey and the Tower of London to break-up the bus time). Very frequent service; we never waited more than about 10 minutes for a bus to appear. Good coverage of London—between the red and blue route, you can see a great deal of Central London. Additionally, the two-day ticket (at least) includes a boat cruise and a night tour; we did not partake in either of these due to other plans, but it was nice to have the options.

Downsides: the red bus has live guides and the blue bus a multi-language, pre-recorded audio guide. We stuck with the red bus, assuming a live tour might be more interesting. The quality of the guides was extremely variable—one was quite excellent; he was entertaining, full of knowledge, and kept things lively and interesting. One was quite bad; he did not seem to want to be on the bus and repeated himself incessantly, much of it about logistics of upcoming stops, bus transfers, etc., as opposed to sightseeing; instead of filling in the gaps between sights with more detail or history, he would either be silent or offering unhelpful personal opinions about upcoming ruddy matches, etc. A third guide was mediocre—keen, but new to the job and still learning the script and history. Given the price, I would have expected a more consistent experience. Additionally, this is pure sightseeing—i.e., you SEE the places, but that’s about all (unless you very frequently hop on/hop off); I found myself itching for more information about many of the things that we saw. The bus also has to deal with the heavy London traffic (not its fault, but the stop/start/stop nature of the tour leads one to get drowsy pretty quickly).

Overall, a mixed response. If you’re brand new to London and want to quickly scrub into the layout of the city and the major sights, a one-day ticket might be a good use of time and money. If you’re traveling with people who are unable or unwilling to get around via tube/foot, this is also a good option. If you have limited time and want a quick flavor of the city’s sights and sounds, this will work. But, if you are a more sophisticated tourist who desires more local experiences, or already quite familiar with London, I would not recommend the Big Bus.

Even though we've been to London mant times, we still love the hop on hop off tour bus. Use the bus tour to get an overview of Central London and then use it to get to and from the places you want to visit. Multiday passes are very reasonable and it will drop you off and pick you up in front of almost all of the popular attractions in London. If your staying outside Center City, catch the tube to Victoria Station and then climb on the bus.

We had been to London before and tried another bus company but this time saw that Big Bus had better reviews so thought we would try it. Glad we did. The red route has live tour guides and we like that much more than the headset ones. On part of our tour the guide was fantastic giving great information - on another part the guide was just Ok but still better than a recording. On the Blue bus tour you had only recording so we tried to stay more on the red. They have a night route as well that we did. Overall the best bus tour in London from our experience.

At first we thought this would be a good way to tour London.... not really. :(

Spending long time stuck in traffic!! Worse than in LA!

Looking at their map, they do stop at lots tourists attraction spots. However, with the traffic in the city, waste lots time on the bus.

Besides day tour till 6pm, they also have are few night tours. WARNING..... SUPER SUPER CHILLY if you want to sit on upper deck to see better city view. It is very windy at night.

Including the ticket, you can take one river cruise and 3 walking tours. However, you still need to buy another one way ticket to come back to where you start Or else you have to find your way back.

The tours are either 10am or 2pm. In the middle of the day, so you have to plan your day accordingly.

Next time, I will try to use their underground (subway). It is very common public transportation there.

Very disappointed with the linking. We waited almost an hour for next bus to "hop on" while other tour buses came and went regularly. Frustrating and a waste of precious time. Could have gone and done something else if we had been told there was going to be a delay. Would not recommend this crowd.

A trifle overrated as a good way to see London.... bus goes round in circles and it would be advisable to get off after every two stops to see the sites. The night tour is a rip off.... its the same as the day tour with nothing more to see....

Need some innovation here ..... check out Edinburgh and Singapore.....

Sitting for 4 and a half hours on the bus is not exactly the way to go !

We brought 3 Canadians to London and the best way to see London is via the top of a double decker bus!
Gee it was chilly but what a fantastic tour. I live in the UK but learned more about London than ever before!
Nat was the guide and what a fantastic young man he turned out to be!! Witty, clever informative and an excellent clear voice!!
The facts, the figures, the history and a whole lot more besides!!
That young man will go far....gosh his memory was amazing!!!
Hop on hop off was also very useful for a closer look at other attractions !
Excellent and well worth doing!

Will watch out for the unseasonable weather next time and bring a thick coat and scarf!!

Thanks again to Nat and Winston the driver!!!

We choose the Big Bus Tour over the others because of the route that it took and because we could hop on and off. With buses running every 10-15 mins it made getting around the city easy. The guides were informative and funny. Our last day in London was spent on this tour and we had a blast.

The boys loved sitting on top of the bus seeing the sights of London, hubby and I enjoyed the commentary during the ride, very interesting. Loved the fact we could hop and off as we liked. Added bonus with free boat trip included, another big hit with the children. Highly recommend.
the Bus tour gives you ideas and general ideas of where things are located. The benefit of the hop off - hop on is very nice!

We used the Big Bus in London and Paris. It was great to just hop on and see all the highlights,listen to the history, get a feel for the city and then later get on and off to explore. We also did their river cruise in both cities which was fun!

We bought our tickets over the internet and exchanged for paper tickets in the morning. The lady at the Kiosk at Victoria station told us that the last trip of the day would start at 7 PM. So you can assume, departing from stop one at 7 PM.
We had a nice trip to The London Tower, visited and took the boat back. The stops and tour guide on the red bus were great.
We then took the blue bus at stop 13 at 5:15 PM because we wanted to go around the whole circuit of the blue tour. We were inside the bus, that was packed, then on stop 30 one of the guys from the company came in and asked where we wanted to go and we told him we were doing the whole blue tour. He told us to leave the bus because that bus was going to stop and the next one was coming to take us the rest of the way.
We were waiting with all those people who left the same bus then another one came. We asked again one of the tour people where that one was going and he told us that wasn't the one we wanted and wait for the next one. We waited, when the next came we asked again and he said that they not only weren't going to go the rest of the blue circuit but this one was the last trip of the day. It was around 6 PM. We asked them again and the guy then told us he didn't say anything about us finishing the circuit, calling me a liar. We then had to take that bus and go back to the same places we already been in the morning, just we wouldn't be stuck over there.
Next morning we went to the kiosk at Victoria station just to leave a complaint and the guy over there called us liars again, said that couldn't have happened, we didn't pay attention at the time and a bunch of other excuses.
So be really careful, and ask for everything in detail, they should provide a time schedule for the afternoon, because whatever they tell in the bus is not right.
Next time we would try a different bus tour company because this one is not reliable.

We live in London and decided to do this tour as we wanted to experience this in our own city but had used similar bus tours in other parts of the world. We managed to get the tickets far cheaper by booking on line the day before on the website '365 Tickets'. We boarded the 'red route' bus from Green Park which was our meeting point. The guide who did the commentary on the Bus was excellent and pointed out everything along the way as well as some trivial stuff which made it even more enlightening. We hopped off at Tower Hill after 1 hour 30 minutes and joined the River Thames boat trip which also came as part of the deal. We decided to go as far as Greenwich to see the Cutty Sark and then came back to Tower Hill to pick up the bus again for the 'blue bus' route which was the recorded tour - earphones were provided.

All in all a good experience. I would thoroughly recommend this tour as the staff are really friendly, helpful and informative.

If you are a tourist, do this on your first day in London. It will help you know what you want to see and where it is located. The Red Line tour has a live person describing the many sites and key points of interest. The Blue Line tour is a recording. Big Bus supplies very good ear buds, if you don't have your own. And don't forget to grab a map, which are available on each bus. This line was recommended by our hotel, and they didn't receive a commission or payment for the recommendation. Apparently, this line is one of the Best in London.

We took a tour the day we arrived in London. Our family was tired from an eleven hour flight. Nice that you can hop on and hop off to see sights more in depth. We also got the two day pass which included the boat tour. The guides were informative.
We just took our Big Bus Tour and found it a great value for our family. Good routes, easy hop on and hop off, enough buses to keep the wait to a minimum. We were happy.

Bought a 2 day ticket and made full use of it. We were able to take in all the major attractions and a bus was always only a few minutes away. The Big Bus employees were fun and informative. Would absolutely recommend this service if visiting London.

The nice thing about big bus is that your ticket is for 24 hours and includes the cruise on the Thames. Getting on and off and meandering is excellent and the pick up/drop off stops convenient. Tickets were approximately $35.00 USD a piece. You can sit up on top or down below. Great way to get a taste of London and then go back and spend more time where you want later.

I cannot stress enough how absolutely terrible this bus tour was!! Having only endured it for about 15 minutes, I can only imagine the torturous dialogue would have continued once we had left, in disgust!

We were looking forward to showing our two Australian visitors around our wonderful capital, with an informative guide to explain things en route. Imagine our horror then when, once seated on the upper deck of one of the Big Bus Tour buses, the young female guide began to chat away as though she was on her mobile to one of her friends! I could not believe the drivel that spewed from her mouth and the manner in which it was delivered! We could not believe our ears! I was just cringing in embarrassment!

As we passed along Oxford Street she put on this high, falsetto voice, let her wrist go limp and squeaked, 'Oh, this is where all the well-off shop, up this end. Ooh, la de dah. Down the other end are the common people.' We then passed one of the theatres, where she informed us she didn't have a clue who was on at the moment but a while ago, Titanic had shown. She then fluttered her eyelashes, pretended to swoon and sighed, 'Leonardo Di Caprio', just like a young teenager showing off to her friends in a playground. No history about the theatre or anything sensible at all.

The final straw was when she started to go on about the Queen (and no, we're NOT Royalists!). Again, the falsetto voice and the limp wrist, as she warbled and squeaked, in what was supposed to be an upper class voice, 'Ooh, I think I've had enough being Queenie now. Oh, who shall I give my crown to? Should it be Charles or William? I really don't know.' I cannot express, via the written word, how totally awful it was! I work with primary school children and said to my partner, it really was like watching one of their more tedious class plays. Nothing was serious. There was no proper information given about the rich, diverse history of London at all. It was a shocking waste of time and money. She was totally idiotic!

Talking about money - we couldn't believe it when one of the staff approached us for our fares. £64 for two people!!!!!! We could not believe our ears!! My partner said he was not paying to listen to such rubbish and asked if they were having a joke! The member of staff then suggested the fee of £50 instead, to which my partner replied, 'No way! We are getting off!' and, thankfully, we did, swiftly followed by our visitors and a couple who had been sitting nearby, also in disgust!

I have been on many a city tour before now and have a good sense of humour but never have we witnessed such a pantomime as this! It was a total, embarrassing shambles and the joke to top it all? Sixty four pounds!!!! I see the Big Bus Tours have many satisfied customers and don't doubt that many of the guides are extremely knowledgeable about the city of London but this clown either needs sacking immediately or training up to a much higher level! What a bitter disappointment for our Australian friends, who were looking forward to an interesting, fact-packed tour of our great city. What a joke!! Wish we'd had a pre-recorded guides voice through a head-set!

We used the Big Bus tour in July on a lovely sunny day, so waited for a bus that had seating available on the open top deck and were not disappointed. My husband, myself and 2 children (aged 15 & 11) spent the whole 2 hours on the bus and the guide was very informative and funny. I used Tesco vouchers to buy the tickets and it was well worth it, especially as it included a free river cruise which was very good as well.

We purchased the 48 hour ticket which included a nite tour and boat cruise. The day tours were great. It is almost impossible to find the bus stops . Once we found it , the tour was great, the tour guided were very entertaining. The boat cruise was nice. My only problem was the night cruise. We asked 4 employees during the day about the night tour and we were told the same thing. The night tour is a hop on hop off tour. We got on the night tour at our bus stop. The tour took a different route then normal and said it was because of traffic. When we asked when they were going to get to our stop, we were told that they were not stopping there but proceeding to the last stop at Marble arch. We were told that we had to get off there. It was 1030 at nite and we were literally thrown off the bus and told to find our way back. You can imagine that a older women like myself along with a pregnant women , we were extremely upset. We had to walk thru a park at nite passing homeless people to try and get a cab. Needless to say we are not a fan of this company

I'm an American who was visiting my British GF on holiday to propose. On Saturday the 15th of August, we took a Big Bus Tour through London. Big Steve was our tour guide. He was an excellent guide and really made the tour enjoyable. He was chock full of factoids and British humor and anecdotes. He was so enjoyable that after disembarking the tour at Buckingham Palace to enjoy a pub lunch at the English Arms, which he recommended, upon our return to the stop, he was waiting to re-embark from his much deserved spot of tea. We were so delighted to see that he was going to be conducting another tour that we waited to re-embark on the same bus that he was taking on. His knowledge of the history and lore of the city of London made the tour exceed my expectations. A big three thumbs up to Big Steve and a score of 11 on a 1-10 scale. He also did remarkable American accents. Thank you Big Steve for making my tour of London truly memorable.

I took the Big Bus Tour on my third trip to London - my only mistake was not taking it the first time when I first got there. I had avoided it thinking it was just a touristy money trap - I was so surprised. The tour, if you stay on and don't get off, usually takes about 3 hrs total (depending on traffic) and covers every area of London imaginable. This tour group had excellent drivers, and the live voice tours (not the recorded ones where you plug in the headphones) I found extremely enjoyable. I had a wonderful tour guide, an older gentleman, who, if you listed to what he was saying, told you all about the history and how long that building had been there and what had happened before that. He was extremely knowledgeable in the history of London, even quoting Churchill in that Winston Churchill voice as we rode past the War Rooms. On my next trip back, I plan to take the tour again with Big Bus Tours.

I have been to London many times but had never thought to do the Big Bus tour. On a warm sunny day it was a great way to soak up the atmosphere and see the sights whilst avoiding the exhaustion from walking! Even familiar places are viewed from a different perspective.
The top deck is the place to be towards the back - not sure it would have the same appeal on a wet day though.

Fantastic way to see London. You can hop on and off where you want. There are different deals too but we found the 48 hr to be the best as it included a boat cruise on the Thames so we used that to get to Greenwich.

Long wait times. Say it would be 5-20 minutes between buses but waited over half hour for each one. Original Bus Tour had 3 to Big Bus Tours' one at bus stops. One of the bus drivers was rude to another customer when he asked a simple question. Guys at stops were polite but told us many times the bus was only a few minutes a way when it was not. Rained and the buses we were on had no tops on upper deck so bottom deck was over crowded. Bus are clean and look good.

Although I have vacationed a lot, this was my first time taking advantage of a bus tour. It was amazing and I highly recommend Big Bus Tours. We had 48 hours passes which gave us hop on hop off access during the day as well as the night bus. We took the red line which had a live tour guide and the blue line where you plugged in ear buds to listen which are provided. Both were great ways to learn all about London. The bus drivers did a great job considering the amount of traffic and tight corners. I was very impressed. All the staff giving information and drivers were all polite and helpful. The night bus was also a great way to see London all lite up however, all the buses were very full. We took advantage of the complimentary river cruise and loved it as well. There are so many stops and many are located near convenient tube stations. I will definitely be using your company on my upcoming trip to Chicago as well!

A great way to see London in comfort. We decided on a bus tour at the last minute on a August weekday. We didn't have to wait long for the bus, we got on by the London aquarium. We saw many iconic London landmarks on the red tour. Traffic was quite good for London. A informative audio commentary. Well worth a trip on these buses.

To save money book your ticket on line 24hrs before you go. Down load the map. Pick up the bus at any of the bus stops marked "BIG BUS" We only had time to do the red route so if you want to do more start early. I thought I knew London from working and visiting there over the years but the live commentary pointed out interesting facts about many places known and unknown to me. I must say that this was a very interesting day and was a nice way to celebrate my up and coming 87th birthday. This tour would be very useful as a starter for visitors to make planning of site visits to suit ones taste

If you wish to get an excellent overview of London and get excellent guide information then I have no hesitation to recommend this tour bus company. We had a one day pass which included a river cruise and also a choice of walks included in the price of the bus tour. We took both bus routes blue and red, also the river cruise and manage one of the walking tours as well.

Love the Big Bus. Convenient as it hits all the major landmarks and the guides provide information for each sight that'll really open your eyes and enhance your experience. Plus, it's great fun. Always get the 48hr ticket and use it to get around the city. Of course, more expensive than the tube, but way more enjoyable. Best tour company I've found worldwide for hop on hop off buses. Used Big Bus in other cities. This is the way it should be.

My 2 days Big Bus tour with friends would've been a wonderful experience if not spoilt by a member of staff who shouted on me in a very unpleasant way.
I reported this incident to other members of staff who advised me to write to the manager. I emailed the matter to the manager as advised but, after 6 weeks, still waiting for the reply...
I would expect far better customer care from a reputable company!
On my return, no drivers could tell me which big bus tour to take to get back to my hotel. They sent me on a walking wild goose chase. Very disappointed

This is a really useful idea as its a hop on/off bus tour. We decided to do a red tour and this we found to be the best option as it has a real life guide rather than a recorded one. The tickets are valid for 24hrs and you also get a free boat tour.

Brilliant! you must go on the bus tours when in London, if your interested in learning about the city then these are a must. You pay a one off fee and then get an open ticket to hop on and off. well worth the money.

This one of the best things you can do as soon as you get to London. It will really help you get the lay of the land. I suggest the two day pass . You can jump on or off the bus at any stop. Also the tour guides, Connie and Becky were outstanding. They were knowledgable and funny.

A fantastic way to get around London Cheaply, stayed on the bus for Hours in the sunshine catching all the sights. If you are lucky enough to be on the same Bus as NOBBY the tour guide, even better, what he doesn`t know about London isn't worth knowing. FABULOUS.
Big Bus Tours - London was a good experience to see the city. I really enjoyed the architecture and the history. The only downfall of the tour was the traffic.

We booked this bus tour as it had a pick-up near our hotel, offered routes for places we wanted to see and the tubes were on strike on the day we chose. The tour offers two routes. They cover pretty much all the sites you want to visit. The Blue Route has a recorded commentary and the Red Route offers a live commentary. The traffic on the day was terrible and with all the road-works it was slow going. From Kensington to St Paul's took three and a half hours. As such we only got off the bus for a short time and then joined the tour to see the remaining sites. The buses we used were modern and clean. I would recommend checking the traffic news before booking any trips. Particularly if you want to make the most of the hop-on hop-off convenience.

Went on the Big Bus Tour around London today, it was absolutely fantastic! The tour guide was really kind and was super informative, me and the family learnt so much we didn't know before! Granted, they drive a little too fast to take perfect photos, but you have plenty of opportunities and it is educational in a way that isn't boring or droning. For and adult and a child it cost £45, which is pretty standard for a London attraction, and is really worth it! Highly recommended!!

Seems a lot for your money but then there are 3 companies in competition and all wanting to take you for a ride - around London. I cant compare as this is the only one I have used. What I can say is that you must allow a lot of time to complete what's on offer. Its good that they now validate the ticket for 24hrs from when you first get on your first bus as you would not be able to complete your trip.
We started our trip at 2pm and did the 'east' loop from the Strand. We got off at Westminster Pier and got on our river cruise - which is also included in your bus ticket - travelling to Tower Pier. Alighting there we decided to walk back to our hotel along the Embankment.
The next day we did the 'west' loop. That seemed to take much longer as there were a lot of hold ups around Buckingham Palace and very slow moving traffic (so pleased I wasn't a driver as I would have been so frustrated}. The only good thing was that we were able to have a good look round whilst stationary.
The young ladies doing the commentaries were very knowledgeable and informative. Its worth mentioning that you can hop on - hop off at any time. Also there are 3 walks that are also included as part of your package although we didn't have time to do those. Look 'online' to see a map of just how far and where you go. Also look at the combo packages that can be included with your ticket and will save you money.

When I exited Victoria Station, I found the agents of Big bus tours right outside.
They gave me a map & explained about the city tours they run, namely The Blue & Red tours (Duration of tour/tour route is long for The Red tour).

I purchased one day tour ticket for 32 pounds which was not just for the Bus tour, but also included Cruise on Thames river & several walk tours they have organised in the city.
They also had 2 or 3 day tour tickets for tourists who have an extended stay in London.

Then I boarded the Big Bus from a bus stop around 30 seconds walk from the Victoria Station & got my seat in the open 1st floor from where the attractions of the city were clearly visible.
It gave me enough access to click photos or take videos while going around the city & to enjoy the sun.

They provided me with complementary Earphones (Decent built & audio quality) to listen to the audio files that gave information in more than 12 or 15 languages about the various attractions as the bus went through them.

The Hop on & off facility was a real boon for me as I was able to alight the bus wherever I wished to explore/spend more time.

I then boarded another Big bus which had a very knowledgeable guide who shared interesting facts about the places making the travel much exciting!
They took me to all the important places to visit in London & the Cruise experience in Thames was wonderful.

I really enjoyed using Big Bus Tours & I will surely recommend it to any tourist to have a no-nonsense ride around the beautiful city of London & the 32 pound ticket was worth every penny!!!

Keep up the good work Big Bus Tours!

They charged us for the full tour and gave us very little if any. Apparently there were road closures in London due to an event. The drivers were ill prepared to explain the situation. The buses did not have narration as promised. Most of the stops in the City of London were diverted. In summary, they did not deliver what they promised. Tried calling them today and got a recording. They should have either discounted the tickets or made it clear to users that they were not going to deliver what they promised. We waited for half an hour for a Red Route bus and none arrived. The drivers were quite unprofessional and did not address the situation. We were left listenning to music and no explanations of the sites. Terrible experience.

Researched online before visiting London in July to see what the best tour bus operator was and decided on big bus. When we boarded I asked for 2 two day tickets and the driver told me the 48 hour ticket was not available only 24 hour for £32 or 72 hour for £39. I said I could have bought the 48 hour ticket online and he just said "awh well they're not selling them for some reason". I said we would need the 72 hour ticket so and he told us to take a seat and he would have someone come down to us. I went online on my phone and purchased 2 48-hour tickets for £33 each. A ticket seller didn't get on for about 12 stops and his scanner wasn't working to give us physical tickets. We didn't get the physical tickets until the following day and the 48-hour time only started at that point. We took the boat trip down the river to Westminister which was well worth doing. The main problem with the bus is the amount of traffic in London it can take soooo long! We used it as our public transport for the duration of our stay as there was a stop near our hotel. Some of the drivers were very rude. We boarded at the London eye a lot and had to check which direction the bus was going as they don't have it on the front and some drivers just pointed or groaned. One said "East" so maybe I should have been carrying a compass... Still not sure what the problem was with purchasing a 48 hour ticket but would perhaps recommend booking online. Buses very regular never had to wait too long. Also gave out ponchos which unfortunately came in very handy on one of our days.

So many buses in London. So much traffic. Takes 45 min to go somewhere where you could walk in 10 min. I did enjoy the commentary and learning about what you were passing, but it is not an efficient way to get to the sites at all. If you are in no hurry and just want to ride for a long time and get the history than you should do this. Otherwise, just walk. Would be nice if they had a better app that directed you to the nearest stop to hop back on and/or could show you were the closest bus was(like uber) while you were waiting at the stop.

One of the critical consideration point to take a hop on hop off bus tour is the amount of vehicle the company provides, so if you don't want to wait too much, take the tour that is provided by the company that has the most bus.

At first i bought ticket from another competitor, but i was so tired of waiting, meanwhile i already had more than 5 big bus tour buses passed me and my bus hadn't arrived yet! Finally bought big bus tour ticket and i'm very satisfied with it. From the amount of the buses that i saw, i'm 90% sure that big bus tour has most buses compared to other competitor, great job.

We had bought 48 hour London Big Bus ticket with a river cruise and night tour, everything was brilliant and service was excellent until we had to go on our last ride. At first we thought we would highly recomment this trip, but this ruined our impression. We had to wait for our last ride on Green route bus for 20 minutes in the rain and in the middle of our trip it stoppend and the busdriver (in the picture) said that everyone needs to get out withour no explenations with what to do. Get out! No further notice of when the bus is going to start the journey or when the next bus is coming to the stop that we where left at. The busdriver just left the bus unattended and started a concersation with another Big Bus driver. Both had a smoke just infront of all the customers that were thrown out of the bus. After waiting for 10 minutes (the bus driver did not even pay attention to us) we decided to start walking again in a bit of rain.. Thanks for a shower Big Bus tours!

We purchased our 48 hour passes through our hotel in hopes of making travel around London easier for the older family members travelling with us...as well as score a nighttime bus ride and a river cruise.

The nighttime bus ride was alright but nothing too special and the cruise never happened due to timing...the bus stops aren't as easily found as some other competitors and it was overpriced.
Use the competitor if you are thinking about using a hop on hop off tour. This one was a rip off!

If you want to go to more than one place in London so see the sites, then using Big Bus Tours is by far the best value and most fun. You can hop on and hop off as much as you like. There are three main routes which loop round areas of London, coloured green, red and blue, and you jump on any of them.

Each bus route either provides free headphones to plug into the seats or a live guide to listen to information about all the landmarks near by. This was actually really good and informative. The buses take a maximum of 15 minutes to arrive so you don't have to wait long for them. The buses were clean and modern and the open tops were brilliant for taking photos.

In with the price is a free boat cruise on the Thames which was great. The captain gave us funny and helpful information about everything along the journey which we all enjoyed. There are also some walking tours free with the ticket price although we didn't take advantage of these.

Great way to see London good price. But better value if your a family buy famliy and one adult as famliy ticket are only 2 plus 2. Kids loved it great interaction from the tour guide and good knowledge. Only down side when you hop on and hop off other bus companies trying to sell you tickets . Overall good value

I am glad I did not read the reviews before closing the Big Bus Tours in London, as some of them seem very negative. I personally had a wonderful experience! To me, it was a great way to see the city, walk around and hop back on whenever I needed to get to another destination. Additionally, the river bus was included as a part of the paid-fare for this tour, so I got to use that as well. They provide rain-ponchos if you chose to sit on the open space, while there is some drizzle. The information provided was helpful to learn a bit more about the city and their prompt turn-around was great, so I never waited for more than 10 minutes at any of the locations.
I had a great time and I recommend it!

We were advised to book a hop on hop off bus on our first visit to London by friends who grew up here. Sound advice. Gave us good overview of Central London and the commentary from live guides was awesome. We booked a two day pass and day two got a bit frustrating as by then we had mastered public transport. However the plus was this ticket gave us an extended River cruise and that made it worthwhile. Definitely recommend for your first day in London.

We recently took the Big Bus hop on hop off for one day and it was an excellent way to see the highlights in London. We did get off in Trafalgar square to take the walking tour included and it was an amazing experience to see the change of the guard without the crowds in Buckingham palace. Kevin our guide explained us all the process and we went behind St. James castle where the ceremony really begins, and took us all the way to the path where the new guard arrives to the palace. It was very educational for my family and me. He is such an amazing guide. Thanks Kevin!

spent a full day on and off the Red Map Big Bus. Bus was comfortable although no aircon and it was extreme,lay hot. The tour guides we had were all English speaking and all were humorous and gave great commentary. A lighthearted approach providing some interesting history about the city and anecdotes from the past. Easy to get on and off with various crossovers with other tours. Boat trip included. All up good value and a must do.
Included with big bus tour: Big Steve gave a great walking tour of the changing of the guard highlights. It was AWESOME AND SMASHING!! We even caught a glimpse of the QUEEN!!

I did the Big Bus Hop on / Hop off tour of the City. It is a great way to get an overview of what is where and allow you to get off to see some specific attractions. Some of the routes have live tour guides and others recorded guides. Save the maps as there is no way to see everything in one day and use them to go back to areas of intrest

Stops at great attractions; has headphones or personal guide. Buses come every few minutes - did not have to wait long to catch another bus. Ticket valid for 24 hours. Once you buy tickets (vendors are located throughout the route or you can purchase online) you hop on at any pick up spot which is marked (like a bus stop).

First time visit in London. Jumped on blue tour at Baker Street. Narration on earphones was overall good but a bit short sometimes. The "pause"music was mostly annoying. Traffic delays was expected but not so bad. Hop on hop off worked great for us.

My partner and I decided we would like to do a London by night bus tour with Big Bus Tours on the 8/7/15. We visited a web page where we downloaded a PDF containing a bus time table of stops. Due to tube strikes, we attempted to get on at Covent garden. The first driver pulled up for the 21:05 slot at 21:15, already ten minutes late. A foreign family who could speak some English tried to board and after a little confusion the driver became angry. He shut the doors and drove away in a fit of rage. Considering they weren't the only people waiting for the bus we found this disgusting and grossly unprofessional. Against our better judgement we waited for the 21:35 scheduled bus, this one was on time. The foreign family boarded with little trouble this time round. We asked if we could pay to get on and the driver gave what can only be described as an abrupt answer. We were only enquiring as to wether or not we could join at this stop. This was due to the fact the timetable did not state if it came back to that stop. I have visited the web page and seen that some information is provided, although I would suggest that this information should be included on all formats to stop confusion. We will not be using this service again due to the attitudes of both drivers.

We took the red tour which is supposed to take around 3 hours in total if you stay on the bus, however we took 4 hours due to rush hour and tube strikes the traffic was horrendous. That being said it was comfortable and informative and a great afternoon in the sun upstairs in the outside seating. I would suggest if you are up top you may want to sit a little closer to the front rather than the back as the commentary can be hard to hear with traffic noise etc. This is a hop on hop off tour and our tickets were good for a full 24 hours so you can take your time and really discover some of the places the bus stops during the tour.

When purchasing the tickets we were informed that this tour would last us 2 hours 30 minutes to 3 hours max! We hopped on the bus at Harrods and three hours later we hadn't seen half of the bus tour, and had just about made it to the big London sights. We had to abandon the tour out of sheer boredom and fear of missing our flight. We just about made it to Tower Bridge. We were misinformed of how long the tour would take and quite frankly it was a waste of money! Advice to anyone going to London, buy an Oyster card, plan what sites you want to see and take the underground!!

I thought the Big Bus would be an efficient and effective way to introduce a couple of members of our group who had never been in England to London. Unfortunately, the traffic was so heavy that the circuit (without hopping off) took the better part of a day--though we had been told it would take approximately two and a half hours.. We finally departed the bus and took the tube back to our hotel in order to have time for other scheduled activities. The audio guide was not as helpful as it could have been.
