Website made it sound that you could pick up the London by Night Tour at any one of 10 stops, hop off and back on to finally return to our 1st stop. NOT TRUE!!! Stop #6 was Trafalgar Square near our hotel so we planned to take the first of three available buses, which would get to Trafalgar at 8:30 pm. Since I am handicapped with a walker I move slowly. At 8:20 we were around the corner from stop #6 when the (early) bus sped past. We flagged him down and asked where we should board. He indicted "back there" and sped on. The next bus was due at 9:00 pm. He arrived ten minutes early and we boarded. Bus #3 was due to arrive at 9:30 pm and stated that it would not do the full loop so we were glad to be on bus #2. Our driver raced through stops and few people got off or on although we met up with another bus a couple times (bus #1? Bus #3?) We were really looking forward to seeing Picadilly Circus lit at night, the last stop before we returned to Trafalgar Square. We got to Marble Arch (the stop before Picadilly) and the driver informed us we would have to get off as he was taking the rest of the passengers back to their hotels and then back to the garage (the route for bus #3)!! So here are two senior citizens, one with a walker, flagging down a taxi in an unfamiliar neighbourhood for an unexpected £20 cab back to our hotel at 10:30 at night! Bad! Bad! Bad!

As bus tours go this was a disappointment. Whilst The buses were clean and comfortable and the commentary was good however due to congestion took an eternity to get anywhere, we were looking for something to do on our last day in London and it certainly used up our last day, so much so we abandoned the bus and hit the tube to get around the remaining sites we wished to see. Don't waste your time and money, plan what you want to see and get around quickly and easily using the tube.

I took friends from Australia on two Big Bus tours. On the red route we had commentary from a well-informed young lady. We paused for refreshment near the Green Park stop then joined the blue route with automated commentary via earphones. For the majority of the blue tour we were treated to music and frequent plugs for the services of Big Bus Tours. There were very few descriptions of the interesting sites that we passed and the few comments along the way were delivered after we had passed the sites (usually a block too late). Bus stops were advised after the bus had stopped and not as it was approaching. We were keen to leave the bus to connect with the Tube at Oxford Circus and nearly missed our stop as the announcement of the stop came long after the bus had actually pulled up at a set of red traffic lights. All in all, a very disappointing experience.

We stayed in London for a long weekend and commenced our break with a whistle stop tour of London on the 'Big Bus'. Our guide was brilliant, she thoroughly entertained us throughout with the perfect mix of information and humour. The tour was over two hours but it seemed to fly in, it was so good. I'd recommend this to anyone who wants to see the sights of London and learn a little bit of history on the way.

These double-decker buses run a circular route through London, hitting the major tourist destinations. You can "hop on" and "hop off" at any of the stops. The red line has live commentary in English, while the blue line has recorded commentary in your choice of several languages (you listen via earphones that plug in at your seat). It is the perfect way to get to the top sites without hassle and to spend your time at the places that are of interest to you. Be sure to include the river cruise in your ticket. There is no extra charge, but you have to ask for it when you buy your ticket.

As someone that works in the city of London i found this a great way to see things that i walk past every day without realising. Very informative and a nice way to spend a day hopping on and off. for people that don't know their way around this is great way to find your feet in a new city.

London Pass would be better if you have been to London before. This was our first visit and Big Bus Hop on/off buses worked for us. We went to Greenwich but got charged extra for return boat trip despite getting round trip ticket for it with our 3 day purchase.

If you need to get around London unfortunately the cheapest way is taking one of these hop-on/hop-off tours. But this company is not worth the price. The buses don't run late enough. It takes forever to get from one point to another. The drivers are rude and have no clue about the schedule. We couldn't get a straight answer out of anyone. They advertise the night tour as being a hop-on/hop-off, but if you hop-off there is no way to hop back on, you will be stranded and will have to take a city bus or the Underground.

Their saving grace is their guides. We took a walking tour of the changing of the guards and the guide was FABULOUS. The same is true of the guides on the bus on the red route.

Fortunately the weather was good so we sat upstairs in the open top bus which gave a good view of all the beautiful old buildings dotted around London. Normally you only look at the shop windows, not upwards at the detail.

The guides are fairly informative and it's handy being able to hop on and off as you choose so you can spend as much time (or as little) as you like at various attractions.

We also took the river cruise which was included in the ticket and that was a great way to see everything along the Thames.

Perfect way to see london and that is high praise as we are not a bus family! Buses ran all the time, easy to change and site see at our own pace.

Tour guides were very informative and fun on the red line and the blue line audio tour worked great as well. Only had time for one day on bus but second day was free and two days would have been perfect.

Highly recommend, especially if you are on a tight schedule, everyone was extremely helpful and even had a driver help us out with a lift after the tours had stopped running....above and beyond!

Convenient stops, friendly helpful staff, brilliant day out.
Love the hop on hop off, never waited too long for a pick up, river tour a bonus and must do.

The tour of London using the facility of the hop on hop off bus is really interesting.
It is important to pay attention to your tour guide or else what you see will be mere monuments/attraction
Our tour guide Joao Nunes was particularly nice and humorous, I hardly wanted to get off the bus.
Sadly people are generally in a hurry so as to finish the tour... one must spend time listening to facts and myths about attraction to this place to enjoy
On our way back, we were close to the finish time of the bus schedule, however a kind tour guide dropped us off to the closest destination.
I went with my year from Ireland. The bus was descriptive and was great because its a hop on and hop off bus. The bus' were frequent and I would recommend them.

Yes, this is a perfect way to see London fast ! As needed just Hop On & Off this Open Top Bus to see various sights. The buses were clean earlier in the day. There were ear buds to hear about the areas. They offer 1 & 2 day passes.

We had limited time in London, but wanted to see all key sites, and Big Bus Tours did that for us.
The commentators were excellent, providing a wide selection of information about London.
The convenience of hopping on and off was very useful, and if we went back we would use this capability more extensively; much easier than jumping on and off tube trains.

Get on a bus with a tour guide. You will get a real insiders view of London.You can hop on and off as often as you want. Great way to see all the sights of London especially if you don't have a lot of time

I did the tour early June with a friend. Our bus driver Jim was so friendly and helpful, he made our day! We only had a day so it was the perfect whistlestop tour of Londons landmarks. The pass lasts for 24 hours which is handy

Changing from blue route to red route at the Lundon Dungeons was confusing. Bus drivers were disinterested or perhaps rude. Ride itself no more than just a bus ride around the attractions. Worst thing was that they just dropped us off at some location when they decided that it was time to clock off and the buses wouldn't run anymore to further locations in the evening. Perhaps it was part of the schedule but they should have highlighted by it better in the brochure. So not worth the money I paid. You'd be better off taking the tube. However, if you just wanted a ride around the city to see all the attractions especially if it is your first time to London, then just take one day's tour. That would be enough.

We had 3 day passes and really used them! We always seemed to be on the Blue line (with the recordings), but that wasn't a problem. There was a big race the weekend we were there, so some of the routes were changed, but not really a big deal. We were always able to get on a bus, not always on top, but most of the time we could.

Never too long of a wait for the next one.

The Night tour was good, but pretty crowded. We got on at the Marriott County Hall which was the first stop on the route, so we didn't have a problem getting seats upstairs.

They seemed very organized and we really enjoyed the Big Bus in London. (not so much in Paris, however)

I've done this tour several times with American friends and it really is the best way to get as much as possible of London seen in one go. The hop on hop off idea means u can stop to see some attractions in depth and then carry on with the tour. The buses with the live guides are best (if you speak English!) as some of the guides are very entertaining.

The only downside is the price, always cheaper to book online than to buy on the day.

My experience is already going down with big bus tours even before taking the actual trip. I took the 3 day + night tour with them and wanted to know if I can use the night tour on the evening before the three day booking. No response at all since 2 days now. not even an acknowledgement of email receipt.

Just like the tours in previous cities we have used this service does not disappoint. You can listen I think in 12 different languages with headphones and there are numerous points to hop on and off. Don't take a cab it's so pricy...just use the Big bus service!

We chose a couple of optional walking tours that went with our Big Bus pass. We met Kevin at stop #10 for both. The first walking tour we took was the Royal Tour where we went to see the Changing of the Guard. Kevin was fantastic. He explained many things about the royal family and also took us to the right spots at the right times to get the best experience for the changing of the guard.

Later that day we went to stop #10 for the walking Ghost Tour. We were happy to see that Kevin was the guide again since he did such a nice job in the morning. Although Kevin did the best anyone could do for this tour, for a couple of people who don't believe in ghosts, it was a tough sell. Kevin was a great guide and very personable.

For the morning tour Kevin did a great job of making sure that everyone in the group was able to stick together. It was tough with traffic lights and a fairly large group - maybe 40 people. In the evening tour I was surprised that he wasn't as attentive to keeping the much smaller group together (maybe 15 of us). There were a lot of people standing outside bars on the sidewalks and I'm pretty sure we lost one family.

The most convenient and affordable way to visit the main sightseeing places in London. You can hop-on and hop-off at any time and you will not have to use any other means of transportation.
A live or recorded tour guide will tell you all the important things during your daily tour.
Careful, since the routes usually end at 18:00, so try to be around your destination until then or you will have to take other means of transportation to take you there!

If you are only here for a short time this is a great way to see all sights of the city. The red tour has a live guide on who tells you all the stories of the city and points all the important bits. We also did the green tour as well. It's great how you can just hop on hop off as many times as you like.

My 2 daughters and I went to London and we were lucky to get Red a Haired Stephen as our commentor for our live bus tour. He was informative, lots of inside information about where certain people used to live, etc. Stephen was funny, and so great, instead of getting off at the Tower of London, we contined the your until the end. He even helped us fund a great place for lunch. I would definetly, if ever back in London, take this tour again. The only way to get an overview of this fabulous city. Thank you Stephen.
Dawn
Vancouver, BC
Canada

Used the bus as part of a short family break in half term holiday. Plenty of buses and staff who went out of their way to help us.We saw loads of great sites without having to walk miles or be constantly on and off the tube. River tour was a big hit although be prepared to queue at busy times. Happened to be on day of state opening of parliament so road closures, diversions and rush hour gridlock meant we were on one bus on a diversion route for a long time.Interesting recorded commentary but please could we have a bigger selection of music clips as it gets very repetitive after a while.

I went on this tour when visiting London with a family member visiting from outside of England. What a waste of money. If you have mobility issues, and can't walk much, this could be an OK tour, but I can't see any other reason to go on it. (even then, you'll probably do better on your own.) Especially as city buses and the underground will get you wherever you want to go, only more efficiently and more quickly. Tour guides are unregulated, and while one we had was somewhat interesting, one just went on, and on, and on about the upcoming royal birth, and ignored what we were passing.

We spent a lot of time waiting for buses, and twice everyone was told to get off the bus and have a nice long wait for another bus. Time I would have rather spent actually seeing London. In a full day in London, we saw impressively little. Though we did pass a few of the same things multiple times....

If you can read a map, you'll see a lot more by walking. Choose a few destinations you want to see, and either walk or take a regular double decker bus to see them. Or sign up for a walking tour of the city. It's what I wish we had done!!

We prefer to explore new cities using a hop on hop off bus system. This is something we have done routinely in the U.S. On our first trip to London, we decided to give it a try and selected the Big Bus. We bought the 3 day ticket and had a marvelous experience. The buses arrived frequently, took us to all the major sites, drivers were courteous and buses were clean. On your trip to London, Big Bus is the Way To Go.

There are lot of hop-on-hop-off tours in London. Big Bus offers live speakers which can be great, but can also be rather boring (I had the experience with two very different speakers). The live tour (red tour) seems to run not as often as the blue tour, so I had to wait for 30 minutes twice before the next bus came. (While at least two blue tour busses passed.) The guides at the bus stops were not very helpful, they told me that it would only take a minute before the next bus arrives - apparently, they had no idea of when the next bus should be due as well. The company advertises a book with discount coupons for some attractions in London, however, when I asked the bus driver for one, he did not have it available. So all in all a tour with a good live speaker can be great fun, but the rest was a little disappointing.

Can certainly recommend using big bus tours whilst in London. We've seen such a lot of sights during our short break in the capital and used both the blue with recorded audio and red with a guide. All the staff were friendly and helpful keen to share their local knowledge and tips but we wanted to mention our first guide, Elizabeth who quite simply was a fountain of local knowledge and made the trip all the more interesting. With the addition of a boat trip on the Thames, walking tours and reduced admission offers its great value way to see London and

Wonderful way to see London and hop on and hop off as you wish. This is the second time we've used The Big Bus Tour and would highly recommend it. Kudos to all the staff who are located at each and every bus stop and always willing to answer questions and point you in the right direction. A great value!

We had a great tour of London on top of the bus with tour guide Nobby who was very informative and jovial with a good sense of humour and our driver who did a good job too around the busy streets of the city. The best way to see all the major attractions and learn all about them.

First time in London & I had no idea, so I got the Big Bus (BB) tour. With the additional walking tours and cruises it is impossible to get it all done in a day. Go for multi-day passes and keep an eye out for additional days for next to nothing. Really sit down and plan how to best use the tour pass. With multiple lines and connections, know what you must see then what you also want to see. The walking tours are excellent but time consuming. I always used the top of the bus, although it can get cold, because I didn't want to miss looking left and right and be just a passenger.
Best way to see beautiful London! We had Big Steve as our tour guide - he was brilliant and very entertaining! Big bus tours gets a thumbs up from me.

Combat jet lag by staying awake with this exciting tour!

My husband and I bought tickets in advance and went straight from the airport to a BigBus tour stop (Gatwick Airport to Victoria Station to Tower Hill Station, since that was the closest stop to our hotel, and we wanted to ride the entire circuit), first thing after our arrival in London (after 8 hours on a plane). Honestly, it was the perfect way to get familiarized with the city without having to do much thinking! I emailed asking them to mail me a map/brochure (to the U.S.) before my trip, and they were happy to comply. Super helpful trip-planning tool!

We bought the 1-day pass, and it was a really fun way to begin our trip. The whole system is very user-friendly and easy to figure out even after just arriving, and there are BigBus employees at every stop to help if needed. The entire circuit takes a little over 2 hours (with no delays, traffic, or hopping off), so it's a great way to kill time before hotel check-in, too. We only hopped off at Buckingham Palace and didn't utilize any of the extras, like the river cruise or walking tours, but still felt it was well worth the money.

Opt for the live "red" tour line--the free headphones on the "blue" audio tour are pretty uncomfortable and the commentary isn't very informative/exciting; lots of "elevator music" in between sights. Sit on the top deck for the best view!

We know London well, but had a friend from South Africa staying, so decided to take her on the Big Bus tour. It is not cheap, but you see so much of London and overall, we thought it was worth the cost. The ability to get on and off, plus the routes take in so much history, made it a great trip. The audio tour (blue) bus was good, but we liked the guided (red) tour better. Some of the guides could have been a little more enthusiastic, but we were spoilt by Pete (who mostly works in the office) who was amazing and such fun. Overall, thus a great way to see a great city.

We were in London for two days and this is the best purchase that I made. The buses were convenient and easy to find. They came in every 5 mins or less. The waiting time was never too long. The drivers were super friendly and willing to help. We got a headphone and a rain poncho in every bus. We were not disappointed. It stops in all major locations. the bus routes are great! I will definitely recommend to any tourists or first time travelers to London. We even took the boat bus and its all included in the price. Worth the money you pay!! Unfortunately we didn't do the night tour as we were too tired and it was a cold night. But I would think it would be great.

Visited London for 3 weeks in May with my girlfriend. We bought tickets for the big is tour and sat at the top of the bus. Very nice even though it was a bit rainy. Big Steve was our commentator and he did an excellent job with his witty and educative commentary. Was quite impressed with his enjoyment of his job. He was so friendly he even offered to help take pictures of us in front of certain landmarks. The bus tour encompasses all that's worth seeing in London and they even give you a complimentary boat ride on the Thames. Will definitely use again.

We only had two days in London, and the Big Bus 48-hour ticket was the perfect way to see as much as possible in a short time. We loved the personal narration of the guides on the red bus, and the Thames river cruise was such a great value. My husband and I are very glad we booked Big Bus. The only trouble we had was nearing the end of the day. We found that they try to consolidate buses that aren't full as drivers are ending their shifts. This wasted almost 40 minutes of our day because we had to get off our bus and onto another one and then wait for other buses to consolidate onto ours. Aside from that, we were very pleased.

Booked a 2 day pass on big Bus Tours. We got a couple of really good commentaries by good guides and the stops are good. The only thing that spoiled it for me was a couple of aggressive ticket guys, one was at Victoria station and he got onto the bus and basically yelled at everyone to move to the back, and i mean yell!! The second issue was that they often have what they call "diversions" where they don't take their advertised route. That's fine if you're on the bus and you know you've been diverted, however if you are at the stop waiting like we were and it's been diverted then it's stiff cheddar for you. This happened on both days. We also found that they scaled down the service in the afternoon. We waited at stop 26 for 45 mins at 4.30pm and no busses came. We rang the office and were told the bus was only 5 mins away but another 15 mins passed and we ended up getting a cab. When you book via your mobile (which is what I did) they should have an sms alert to let you know of any diversions so that you're not sitting there waiting for a non existent bus.

The Big Bus took you round all the usual sights. I would have liked more commentary but a good way to see the main London attractions.

We were quoted a price in the morning, which changed by the time we took the tour a few hours later but they agreed to the original quote so might be worth not accepting their first price!

We went on the blue tour with the Big Bus company we were on the bus for five hours ( you are not told you are on that long) while waiting initially the guy at the bus stop said a blue tour would only be a few minutes he reappeared about thirty minutes later and told us to get a red tour and change at Victoria but then a blue tour arrived not as nice buses as the red tour. We had to change buses half way round ( you are not told that you will have to change) at a cost of £64 for two tickets I feel that those who choose the blue tour do not get the same service as those that choose the red.

Myself and colleague were in London and had some spare time after a business meeting and decided to kill some time by taking an open top bus around London.

The tour itself was fabulous, we got to see all the sights of the City, Big Ben, Buckingham Palace even where the Queen buys her underwear.

Once we had done the full circuit we left the bus at our starting point at Hyde Park. We were then put onto another bus operated by the same Company to deliver us back to our Hotel - the "Home James" bus.

All staff that we encountered were friendly and welcoming and a credit to Big Bus Tours.

I an 1000% recommend this particular Company for anyone visiting London
The best part of it for me, was our Tour Guide - Neil. What a lovely man he is, full of knowledge and on hand with interesting facts and very funny as well.

We chose this tour to make our way from Buckingham Palace to Big Ben. We found the tour information had no consistency as some buses were people talking and some were recording. The recording meant fooling around with headphones and carrying them with you to next bus or get a new pair which is such a waste. The bus maps were not exactly easy to figure out and we ended up getting on the wrong bus and had to get off and cross the bridge again at Big Ben to get on the right bus.
We got off to grab dinner and found that when we went to get back on at St. Paul's Cathedral stop, the bus line had stopped running. It was Sunday evening and we still had the rest of the night to see the city. The guy who sold us the tour did not inform us of the that and we were very far from our hotel.

This has to be one of the best ways to see London. I write this not as a tourist, but as someone who has lived in the capital for many years and never taken an open-top bus tour before.
Not having tried other tours I can't compare this to other companies offering similar experiences, but I would thoroughly recommend Big Bus Tours. The routes chosen are fantastic and take you close to every single major attraction you could wish to see, the buses are clean and convenient (they run every 15 minutes) and the staff friendly and extremely helpful.
It's not cheap - £32 for an adult and £13 for children, but maybe other bus tours are similar prices? And you certainly get a lot from it. You can hop and off throughout the day at various major landmarks, so its a great way to see the entire city and it also includes a free river tour from Tower Pier to Westminster - well worth taking.
On the Blue Route, you are supplied with headphones on the bus and can choose to hear the commentary in a variety of languages, or simply just enjoy the journey in peace if you prefer. (I think the Red Route has a live commentary in English).
On a sunny day there is no better way to see the beauty of London than from the top deck of an open-topped bus!

Having taken these tours in many major cities, I knew what to expect. But Big Bus Tours had very poorly written, recorded commentary, which long stretches of over-the-top classical music. Oftentimes we were passing interesting buildings and sights of note, and the music just carried on. Not a single bus had a live guide, which is unfortunate, because those offer an opportunity for interaction, questions and engagement. Buses also were infrequent, and once the rain came – as it often will in London - not a single bus had any cover available. Extremely disappointing.

We had a great time taking the two day tour. Highly recommended for a first time London visitor to get the lay of the land in a fun and entertaining way. We booked the two day package that included the river cruise and enjoyed the cruise as well. We had a number of guides but the best one by far was Big Steve!

I took my parents on the bus tour of London. This was poor and not good value for money. The tour only lasted as long as it did because of the amount of hop on hop off stops there were. The commentary was too quiet even when on full volume and was sporadic comments rather than a commentary. Very little information. Overall poor and disappointing

We purchased a 2 day ticket from Green Park stop (By the Ritz hotel) Went on red bus with live commentary but if no live talk there is audio head sets for you. This is amazing value for money as the hop on and off means you can use it as your mode of transport thus avoiding the dreaded tube stations. They also offer a hotel shuttle bus after tour hours up until about 9 pm. Highly recommend this
What a great way to sight see round London with no hassle, jump off and on the bus as you please, reasonable prices and helpful staff to give advice, recommend this tour

They had a lot buses going around London. It a good way to get a lay of the land. Suggestion is to get a day pass go to all the sites then decide later which ones you'll want to go back to and visit in depth. There are two buses the blue bus has a pre-recorded guide tied to a GPS locator. The red bus has a live but only english speaking commentator. I suggest you get on the red bus. The routes of the red and blu bus are basically the same and you can hop on and off from one to the other.

We always try to do the open-top bus tour when we visit a city as it helps orientation and to pick out sights worth a closer inspection. The bus tour of London was a massive waste of time though, mostly because the traffic in the city mans you make very little progress. The commentary was pretty poor for a great city like London too - not enough historic detail or interesting facts provided. Listing one or two big shops on Oxford Street seems a little pointless on a sightseeing tour.

Our second trip to London in less than a year. We were there for two full days. Bought a one day ticket on-line and got the second day for free. We were able to use the Big Bus for 80% of our travel. Better than schlepping up and down into the Tube.

Taking this Hop On / Hop Off bus tour was a great way to see London. You ride the bus and you can hop off to go explore an area of London - then you hop on the next bus to move on. Fees are reasonable, although unlike Paris, in London you cannot purchase tickets directly from the driver - you have to purchase tickets from a kiosk. The upside is the unobstructed view from the top of the bus is spectacular!

I'm a bit of a reluctant tourist but my wife pressed for us to go on one of the bus tours and I'm glad she did. For years I have just bought a tube day ticket and explored in my own but if you do that you just don't get the full picture. The routes cover all the sights and the tour guides are humorous and knowledgable.

Top tips.
1. Search the Internet for codes - you'll always find some reduction and booking online in advance saves more cash.
2. We went with big bus as you can present your smart phone or ticket at the bus stop, I think you have to go to an office with the other firms.
3. Get off at the Tower of London (and see it - it's great too) then get the included Thames cruise down to Westminster - it all fits together nicely and the cruise is also superb.

Just spent a morning on the red line big bus tour with Nick as our guide. Joined the bus at green park and left at Westminster. 2 hours of information from an interesting and informative guide. Worth the money but couldn't find the tip jar when leaving the bus to thank them

I bought a ticket online for Big Bus Tours for my first trip to London. I found it a great way to see all of the sights and the hop on hop off facility is excellent. We were able to do the full tour then decide where to go back to and get on and off where we wanted. We also went on the river cruise to Greenwich which was included in the price of our ticket. I would recommend Big Bus Tours to anyone going to London, especially for the first time. It really helped us get our bearings. The buses came around frequently and all of the staff were very friendly and helpful.

We used the Big Bus tours because they had the open topped bus and used the live commentary bus (red line). The commentary was pretty good, we had one older gentleman that was pretty funny and easy to talk to. A couple of the other narrators weren't as personable was were full of information.

This was a great way to see lots of the sites and get around the city. we ended up on and off the bus all day. I was able to get some great photos right on the bus.

The buses came on a frequent pattern. The biggest challenge was trying to figure out where to pick them up, the signs are small at the bus stops. I assume this is a challenge for all the tour groups.

we spent the best part of the day viewing London from the top deck. Earphones for commentary and rain coats provided. Ver interesting, well organised and run. Clean busses frequent timetable. no hanging around. we only hopped off once for lunch. Had a great day

I was in London with my family and after our good experience in Budapest we booked a City Tour with the Big Bus Company. From the very beginning we felt a bit weird with the staff they had around: all of them trying to sell tickets for further attractions as they were almost beggers, they were trying to be funny (First approach at Marble Arch, as an example: "- Sorry, I have a question... - Perfect, then keep it for yourself") and although it may be funny among friends, I don't think this is the way to approach your customers. I felt as many of them were completely fed up of their jobs (and customers) and certainly unpolite.
Apart from that, concerning the routes marked on their maps, you can forget about following them properly. We took 5 times the buses and they changed 3 times the route the had marked in the map (we were really aware of what colour we were taking, yes). Not only this, we tried 2 times in 2 different days to pass by Harrods by afteenoon/evening and although it was NOT the last bus, in both cases the answer was similar: "- Oh, just go to the hotel, relax and you'll visit it tomorrow (??!?!?) / - There's no bus passing by Harrods today (hhuhh???) you can get off in Gloucester Square and walk if you want".
I could keep writing and writing, but I guess it'll be more productive if I just recommend the guys of the Big Bus to be more friendly/polite and keep some kind of schedule for their buses.
In any case, I think next time I'd rather book the tour with the guys of "The Original Tour".

The Big Bus Tour in London is the best way to get around the city. For one low price you can get to many museums and all of the major attractions. The bus took me to Buckingham Palace, the London Eye, and the British Museum. It stopped within three blocks of my hotel, and keep me warm during my travels.

I booked a Big Bus tour today because I wanted to get to Kensington palace and didn't think I'd navigate the tube that well.

I enjoyed the audio-recorded commentary as we drove through streets of London that I'd walked earlier this week. I learned a lot about the city and various areas that I wouldn't have learned if I hadn't taken the tour.

I appreciated the hop on hop off nature of the tour, and definitely liked that they had designated stops, and Big Bus staff at various stops to answer questions or guide you as needed.

Next time I'm in London I may venture to take public transportation, but this is a definite recommendation of first timers to the city.

Hopelessly under staffed and complete lack of buses. Every time we tried to get a bus we waited well over 20 minutes and just gave up. Whole day was wasted just hanging around for the buses. The staff(when we could find someone) just said it would be 10 mins. Definitely not worth the money. Get a Oyster card and use the underground or the other hop on bus company ( loads of their buses kept passing us at the stop waiting.
Tried to complain and have just been ignored.

I have been to London a few times in the past, and I was always with a group fo friends, hence never thought of going for the tour bus. We always walked ( and walked and walked )
However, this time, I was with a friend who visits places mainly thru tour buses. It was really one of the best decisions I have made. I paid around £27 for 2 days ( the deal was only for winter) on the bus, plus a river cruise.
On the first day, we had a tour of London after 5pm, so we got to see London at night. Then the next day, we hopped in and out of the bus whenever we wanted to get down, grab some lunch etc. It didnt matter that we waited, or missed a bus, as there is always something to look at/do in London, like taking photos around while waiting for the next bus.
We had the river cruise which allowed us to see London from another angle. Also, we did get stuck in traffic a lot, which was fine, because I rather be sitting in the bus than walking around. I got to see a lot more than the few times I have been to London before.
Well worth the money ( as ticket on tube/train is quite expensive). I am now planning to take my two young children on it in the summer.

I am a big fan of hop on hop off tours, as we are frequent travellers, that look for bargains. Hands down hop on hop off tours is a norm for us. Not so with Big Bus Tours of London. The staff was not terribly friendly when waiting for busses. Expect wait times to be no where near as advertised. Wait times exceeded 45-60 minutes not the 15-30 as advertised. We had an on duty bus driver pass us by twice, even though we were at a designated stop on their route. I guess we were supposed to enjoy their jaunty wave as they drove by. Avoid this tour offering at all costs.

I am almost 62 and used big bus tours this week on a day trip to London whilst hubby went to an exhibition. I cannot praise the service enough. At every stop the staff were there asking if I needed help or advice on where to go, the river cruise was fab, I have only been to London twice before so just wanted to see the sights wasn't bothered about shopping, it was fab cannot recommend highly enough. Great service, thank you to all.

If you go on the walking tours that are provided with Big Bus you need to go with Kevin! He is a funny guy who is very knowledgeable about London. Also, take the red line to get live commentary but make sure you get Nick (very funny also) or someone else who is engaging to make it more fun and so you learn more! :)
Well spent day with Big Bus Tours. Comfortable buses, lots of stops. Good sound system. Would like to have more detailed timetable for the future trips.
Visited London and pre paid the Big bus tickets.Its the only way to see all the sights, shame about the good old British weather.Only gripe would be having to wait 30 minutes to get on!!

Visited London for a couple of days during half term and decided to take a hop on hop off bus trip on the second day as we thought it was the best way to see the sights. The first bus we boarded had audio commentary in 12 languages with free headphones, a map and rain wear!! Very handy! We had to change bus at some point as we needed a different route (Red. We were previously on Blue). This bus had an English guide, called Chris. He was very informative and included plenty of dry humour in his talks. He obviously knew his stuff. Very impressed. The driver was called Al and was also very good. There was also a free river cruise with our ticket, but we didn't use this. Maybe next time. The buses were new and clean. A very enjoyable experience apart from the weather.

I have been to London many times but this is the first time I can actually say I "know" London. Previously I always took the tube from point to point which wasn't helpful in learning placement within the city. The Big Bus Tour did that for me. We had the Winter Rate which include 48 hours of touring on the bus and a very special Thames boat tour to Greenwich. It was truly a great value for $50. Highly recommend first timers and all others that always tubed it.

A really reasonable, fun and informative way to see London. Because of friends coming to visit, I have used the tour bus on numerous occasions, and it is always a guaranteed good time.Staff always friendly and we got the 2 days for I offer plus a river cruise and walking tour , all for £25 per adult as we booked online, just slightly more if you buy at the stops.

I've been to London a few times and seen the buses and thought, I must do that next time... well yesterday was that day. I'm in London for a couple of days so for £31 (if bought at any of the stands/bus stops) from the very friendly staff. I'm only sorry I did't get his name, I joined at Buckingham Palace and spoke to the nicest Millwall football fan - great guy very knowledgable about the route - where to get off have a wander and hop back on.

There are different cost depending on which tour you want to do. For the money you can just go round & round. 3 routes (Red - Live tour Blue - Prerecorded guide & the Green for the north tour & a river boat tour - excellent value for money. and you could fill a whole 2 days seeing all of London & most of the big sites.

Our Tour guide was Chris & the driver was Al - hats off to you gents. Great 2.5 hour doing the whole Red Tour (20.02.2015) Chris's jokes are relatively funny and on topic, but great welcoming manner & knowledge of his surroundings. Al - great driving.

To anyone thinking about doing the tour - if your thinking of going top deck - wrap up warm, I stayed on and did the whole thing without moving and I was really cold by the end of it, obviously its February so that was to be expected.

Just do it! - You won't regret it. :)

As anyone who has been to London knows, driving and parking in the city is challenging. Big Bus has two routes and a link from the Euston Road area to a stop common to both routes making touring the main attractions easy and carefree. Tickets may be used on both routes. Each bus has a very knowledgeable and entertaining tour guide pointing out all the major attractions and many that we would have missed had we been on our own. Riders may get on and off the bus as often as desired at the many stops throughout the city. I found this means of seeing the city from above ground preferable to the tube, which, however, is the quickest way to get from one point to another, but with no scenery or commentary. We chose the more economical three day pass, using them on both routes.

The bus tours are very useful because they give you an overview of the town. That's the up side. The down side is that they don't stop everywhere you are, the guides are very hard to understand if you are not from London and don't use the Red bus with the headphones, and the drivers can be testy! One of them basically told me how stupid I was for asking if we were going to get closer to St. Paul's Cathedral. I think he got up on the wrong side of the bed. If I were going to do it again, I would use the same buses that the locals use -- the city busses. You need to purchase a card for them, but they stop everywhere and with a map you can figure out where you are. It is also cheaper.

Big Bus tours are great for first timers to London. You will get an idea of how large the city is and how far apart the famous sights are. To get maximum value out of the £25 make sure you do the River Cruise included in your ticket price. They go between Westminster Pier and Tower Pier, with a stop at the London Eye. Last boat is 5.30pm at either end.
The open top buses do two routes, red and blue. They are both the same except the blue route does a larger western loop to include Harrods, Kensington Palace and Hyde Park. The only reason to do the blue route is if your hotel is in that area, particularly around Lancaster Gate.
Live guides are far better than the taped commentary, but you can't always choose what you will get. There are change over points at Green Park and Marble Arch where the bus stops for a good few minutes.
A full circuit on either route takes a long time. Two hours for the red route and three hours for the blue.
You will see nearly all the famous attractions in London. Big Ben, Trafalgar Square, St Pauls and the Tower of London. One exception is Buckingham Palace, the bus doesn't go anywhere near here. You cross the River Thames five times and the highlight of the whole trip is when you cross Tower Bridge. From the top deck you have a perfect view as you drive under its arches.

We made the mistake of hopping on the tour late in the afternoon on a rainy Friday. There were six of us on the tour and after the first hour, we were more than ready to get off. Problem was we were far from our hotel and it was very cold and rainy. Had to wait another hour and a half before bus could slog its way through traffic and get us back in striking distance to hotel. Driver had us get off bus and hop on another which took us closer to our hotel. Seeing sights at night was okay, but by the time we were near Buckingham Palace and National Gallery it was too dark to see much. We never used the second day "free" for river boat down the Thames because we didn't want to be stuck for hours. I realize it's a hop on, hop off tour, but if you get on too late, you won't find another bus to ever "hop back on" so you'd really be stuck. The recorded tour was okay, but at some points it seemed they were desperate to fill the air. The music was annoying after first hour. When they started talking about someone who liked cheese and the parrot that died we knew they were looking for filler. It's an expensive tour and you figure "oh it's London I've got to go on a red double decker bus"...but there are better ways to spend your time. All that being said, if it was a lovely 70 degree day, I'm sure I would've felt better about the trip. As another reviewer noted, they had to detour several times due to "police activity". Bummer because who knows if the normal route was more interesting?
Enjoyed a 48 pass on the bus tour and used it regularly over the weekend. Hopped on and off to get to and from places. Helpful drivers with good tips

This is a great way to see London for the first time. The bus takes you all through London and Westminster to the highlights. You are able to get off & on where it makes specific stops. It is a 2 day pass which allows you to return places you wish to focus on. There are headphones with a running commentary of what you are viewing. Sometimes there is a tour guide on the bus which is a lovely touch.
One disadvantage is they only stop at prescribed stops & aren't always flexible in cases of personal distress.

This bus tour was one of the best I,ve been on, wearing the headphones provided helps you enjoy the tour even more, the good thing about it is you can hop on and off as many times as you want, full of wonderful facts about London that you never knew, we did the two day ticket and booked on-line, saving us more money.

If you only have a few days to see London, this tour is amazing. You don't need to worry about transportation since they go all over the city and include all the important attractions.Also, transportation, like taxis & the underground are very expensive in London so you will actually save money with this tour. The tickets are good for 24 hours. Or you can buy a pass for two days which saves you money. You can get off and on along the way and there are buses that pass every 15 mins. These tours also include walking tours and a 30 min tour on the River Thames. There are two different routes, colour coded, red & blue. Most of the larger, important sites are on the red line. You can also buy tickets for the attractions from the guides at the bus stops so you can avoid the lines for that when you get there. Just be careful, for example we went to visit St. Paul's Cathedral on a Sunday and we had been sold tickets to this site but we found out later that it is free on Sundays. We called the bus company when we got back to our hotel and they refunded us the amount. The bus included earphones to listen to what site you are passing by and a brief history as well. They also included parkas in case of rain but we were very lucky, the four days we were there it didn't rain at all. They are double decker buses with the top area open. The bus drivers are courteous and very helpful if you have any questions. The river tour is worth it as well, very nice and informative. It's a good idea to leave a tip to the guide before getting off the boat.

I went on a Big Bus Tour Sunday Jan. 18th with my girlfriend. We were flying home in the evening. We had plans for visiting London Eye, St Paul’s and Tower. Unfortunately, when we got to St Paul's around 3 pm, time was flying and we had to cut short. We told the Big Bus representative at the bus stop at St. Paul’s that we had to cut short our trip and head back to the hotel without visiting The Tower, of which we had purchased tickets already. She said "just a moment", made a call and all of a sudden she gave us 40 £ back as a refund for our tickets! GREAT SERVICE – THANK YOU! Eileen & Ina

This was ultimately the best and most economical way to see London. My mom and I went on a trip in December and although a little chilly up top, it was a great way to hop on and off the bus anywhere we wanted and less expensive than taxis or the tube. Some guys are better than others, we had some that were hilarious and others a little boring, but overall friendly and helpful and informative and we were glad that we spend the money on the first day so we could use it the entire time. They had a buy one day get the 2nd day free deal which was great. Highly recommend.

Also, it was less expensive to buy tickets to other attractions from their people at each bus stop then it was to buy the attraction tickets when you get there. We bought tickets to the London Eye and Tower of London from them and saved some money.

We had one day in town and decided to start it with a bus tour of the sites. I guess we caught the best guide Big Bus hade to offer as noted by the person just before this review. Nick brought the city and sites alive and entertained us with his wit and wisdom. What a great way to start the day. Thanks Nick!

Our tour guide Big Steve was awesome!! He knew so much about London and really knew the history, not only of the main attractions but little things like how a certain common day saying started. We circled the tour twice with big Steve and he definitely made our day in London! He is so interactive with the passengers on the bus and really makes the tour that much more. I love taking big bus tours but this was definitely my husband and I's best experience with Big Bus Tours. I hope everyone gets the chance to have big Steve as your guide, he will definitely make your tour a fun, learning experience.

Simply SMASHING Steve ! From your Floridian friends :)

We mostly took the Red line that has a guide on board, and were able to see many of London's landmarks with a two-day ticket. On the Blue line they have earbuds if you want to listen in another language or English as you drive around. Anything that interests you I would get off because it takes a long time for the bus to circle around. Or if you don't like walking you can just drive around and take pictures from the bus. If you aren't good at navigating a new place the Big Bus Tour is perfect for getting around.

I always find these types of tours an easy way to see a city. This one didn't disappoint. Saw plenty of London from the comfort of the top deck (yes, in winter).
The included river cruise was excellent but I would recommend getting on the boat at Big Ben and cruising back to the Tower. It is easy to get back on the bus again and even though you repeat part of the journey, the views of a Tower Bridge are worth it.
Only concern was the number of times I had to change buses to the one in front. Being a little mobility challenged made this hard.

The Big Bus was our first choice as the bus offers 2 different routes one being a tad longer then the other. The red line also offered a tour guide on board which was excellent whereas the blue bus used headphones which still was great commentary. Takes you to the main landmarks in London which was great!

My friend and I bought tickets because it was suggested to us as a good way to see the city. This is true. It was very cold when we visited London and so a warm bus to ride around in was very welcome. We ended up sitting on the red line bus for almost the entire time. We didn't have time to hop on and off at each stop, which would've maximized the money we spent on tickets. We basically spent the money in order to listen to the pre-recorded city commentary and look out the window. It was enjoyable and comfortable. Because we purchased tickets in the off season, we got a 48 hour pass to ride instead of the usual 24 hours. This was a nice perk although we didn't end up using the passes for the second day. I'd say the cost is more worth it if you're going to use the bus as it's meant to be used: to ride around the lines and hop on and off at certain points in the city where you want to explore more. Sometimes there is a wait of up to 15 minutes for a bus, which sucks in the cold but it was doable. Also busses sometimes get crowded so keep that in mind. Also busses stop running at 6pm. So start early or make sure you can navigate the tube to get home.

We weren't sure what to do one day so we decided to take a bus tour of the city. The guide was very good telling lots of information about the sights and the buildings we passed along the way.
The price of the ticket was excellent value for money, we had a 2 1/2 hour bus tour and then we went to Westminster bridge to get the boat for the cruise up the Thames. Although we could have done this over 2 days we did it in 1. Both my husband and myself really enjoyed it, I would recommend it to anyone, its one way of seeing lots of the sights of London.

What an excellent tour I wish could remember the name of the guide a big jolly guy, a real cockney very informative. I learnt a lot about London. It seemed experience but it was great value for money considering everything that you could do

For 2days we were able to roam around london at a less cost.. enjoying the hop on hop off facility of the big bus tour london
You can book online as they have 48 hrs where 24hrs is free for a rate of 24hrs
but take note that the timing ends at 430pm..so u can plan ur transpo once the big bus is not available
this Big Bus goes to major n minor attractions of the city

Friendly and accommodating staff

I've bought the offer £25 for 48 hours which includes free river cruise and walking tours. The "hop-in-and-out" bus rides (especially its roofless top) were excellent since it was sunny and well-equipped with audio tour guide, we went for the longest river cruise ride from Greenwich to Westminster Pier on day 1 and picked the royal London walk on day 2. Certainly worth more the value that I've paid for. Thank you for the good and memorable service.

The trip costs more than 30 pounds. Yet it is a good introduction to the city. I took the ride on my first day of arrival, to get an overview of the city. If you are not afraid of the cold during winter, you can go to the second level of the bus and enjoy the pretty scenery, and the audio guide (they provide you with a free earphone and you can just plug it into the back of the chair). After my ride, I had a rough idea on the famous tourist spots in London and I can plan my itinerary in the following days. You can get off the bus at any stop you like, and get on at any stops, just find the stops in the map.
Apart from the bus tour, it also includes free walking tours and a river cruise. It was marvelous, esp. the walking tour! The tour guide brought us to a perfect spot to watch the changing of guards, and he is pretty experienced. I missed the Harry Potter tour, for HP fans, don't miss it like I did >Overall the price is expensive, but service is good and I think it worths.

Good value and one of the best way to see London. The open top Red Big Bus takes you to all of London's top tourist attractions & iconic landmarks. Famous stops include Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, Westminster Abbey and the London Eye. There are more than 50 locations where you can hop-off the bus to visit attractions or explore places of interest. This facility gives you the freedom to plan your own itinerary and explore the city's magnificent landmarks and exciting attractions for as little or as long as you like. You can hop-off and hop-on the open-top buses as many times as you want within the validity of your ticket. The Blue Tour offers you a choice of a multi-lingual recorded commentary, or a live English commentary by entertaining & friendly guides on the Red Route. The free River Thames Cruise is included in the Big Bus Tour. Our family truly enjoyed the Big Bus Tour of London.

I went to London in March 2013 with my sister from Dubai I decided to buy her the London bus tour it's fantastic amazing effortless way to visit and see historical and attractive places attractions in the city of London she enjoyed as much as my 9 year old daughter and we saw the changing of guards at the Buckingham. Palace so organised and serene it was a fun day

We were able to get a good deal on a family ticket on the internet so we chose this way of taking our two children to see the sights. The Big Bus stand was right outside the train station and we were directed to a bus stop around the corner. The buses ran regularly and we experienced both those with a tour guide and those where you could use headphones. My children preferred the headphones as it was easier to hear and there was much more information.

We found the staff to be very helpful as they checked we were catching the right bus to where we wanted to go. You can hop on and off as many times as you like and never have to wait more than a few minutes. We saw all of the main sights and were able to enjoy a leisurely tour despite the city being very busy with those wanting to see the poppy display and 50,000 arriving for the American football. I would recommend.

fun, me and my family took the bus to big ben and the buckingham palace and to the london towers then the last stop was picadilly circus i believe they gave us 45 mins. for every stop?? well it was fun but my son had a little camara and he was taking pictures of a car ( he loves cars) so he took the picture then he dropped it and it landed on the road and then the car behind us ran over it ! :( i am trying to say it goes a little to fast but all drivers are different! it was really fun great for kids!

On our first day of a London trip we decided to use the Big Bus Tour as a way of scouting out the place. They certainly covered most of the big attractions and were very handy. I would highly recommend this as a good way of orientating yourself to London. My only reservation was that some of the staff could have been more helpful. We received inconsistent advice about the available packages. I would use them for a day and then get around in the Tube once you have mastered it.

My wife and I came up to London on Remembrance Sunday and visited the Tower of London on the Sunday (which I have reviewed separately) and then took the Big Bus Tour on the Monday. Although I've visited London many times and know a little of it's history, we both found the tour fascinating. It cost us £20 each (which included a one way trip on a river cruise boat) and lasted about 4 hours. The weather was fine so we stayed upstairs on the open top bus which is fine if you are wrapped up, especially at this time of the year. The audio tour was really informative and we had the option to get on/off whenever we wanted and saw all the main highlights of London. When we got back to Westminster we got off and got the river cruise back to the Tower of London and had a pleasurable trip back, again with a guided tour of the sights. Drinks and snacks were available. Highly recommended for those of you that have never done this before or even if you have a bit of knowledge of London. I hope you find this review helpful.

I had one day trip to London and taking a hip on hip off buss is the best choice ever. Big bus has plenty of busses through all London. You can see in few hours the main turistic attractions. And can take great pictures. I dropped off when I wanted to take a better look to the atractions and after 10 min another buss would pick me up.

If you have never been to London sightseeing before, a bus tour is a must. It takes in all the major sights within a few hours, and you can hop-on and off wherever you fancy. We managed to fit in changing of the guards at Buckingham Palace, shopping at Harrods and a brief visit to the Natural History Museum (where they currently have an open-air ice rink). We wanted to finish our tour at Hamleys toy shop but due to road closures the bus couldn't get near and took a big detour which took ages through traffic. It would have been nice to have been told beforehand as my 8yr old daughter was very tired by the time we walked from Trafalgar Square. If it wasn't for this I would have scored higher. Oh, and wrap up warm if you want to sit in the open-air part of the bus, which is the best way to see London.

The boyf. and I decided to do a bus tour as we only had two days in London and thought it would be the best way see all the major sites in a short period of time.

The bus itself looked clean, friendly staff and we only had to wait 10min for a bus to arrive. The red tour also covered all the major sites and was around 2h 30min. However, we did not learn anything from the tour. The tour guide never spoke about any historical events or interesting facts. The only comments given were e.g. "this is stop no. 7 now", "we will not stop at the next one due to road work" or "to your right you will see the houses of parliament" but he would never give us any information about it. It was quite a shame as the bus tickets were not very cheap. It was very disappointing.

We paid for a day pass with Big Bus Tours that started from near Paddington Station and got off at various places of interest in the city. One of the buses we went on had a local Londoner tour guide who told jokes and kept everyone amused. The tickets also included a Thames River boat ride which was great to se London and the bridges from a different perspective. This is the best way to view London and get very comprehensive information of the various places we pass by. Highly recommended to any visitor to London.

Just returned from a weekend trip to London and paid big bus tours £52 for what was a terrible service. We were unexpectedly asked to leave the bus, at a stop that was miles away from where we had got on and in torrential rain. We were told to stand in the red phone boxes , which could have doubled as men's urinals. We were told another bus would be along to take us further, but this never happened. The staff were unhelpful and the whole thing was a shambles. The result was that it costs us a further £10 for a taxi . Beware!!!!!!

We needed to get a feel for the city and see some important places. We picked the wrong bus. The bus took us all over the city and we went over the river FIVE times. The sound system is the kind you plug your earbuds into which they kindly provide, however, you could understand what you were supposed to be looking at. The ticket was good for 48hrs, so the next day we waited for a live tourguide. It was much better, but other buses I have ridden on have been better. We never got close to Westminsters or Buckingham. The ticket also came with a river tour which I think most tours offer. Use you money on a better bus like the Original London tours bus.

A brilliant way to show some one special London for the first time.
With three routes to choose, there is ample choice to plan a super trip around my favourite city.
Big ben , Houses of Parliament , Trafalgar Square, Piccadilliy Circus, Downing Street, Harrods are just the tip of the iceberg. Jumping on and off the bus gives you the flexibility to change your plans whenever you want, that is what makes this bus experience so much fun.
Take the upper deck and enjoy all the sounds and smells emulating from the city streets, it can be a bit chilli up top so pack a hat and have a great time.

2 kids and 2 adults went on the Big Bus Tour last week - over the 2 days we enjoyed the personalised commentary especially by Robert who was really funny and gave us all a memorable tour. We went to the Tower of London and again had a great and highly amusing commentary with Barry the Beefeater - British humour is excellent and definitely worth experiencing on the tourist circuit. Finally the linked boat trip up the Thames was a great way to see London on a wet afternoon with again witty commentary. It seemed a lot of money when we initially bought the tickets but the flexibility of the ticket and the variety and quality of the tours and modes of transport made it really good value for money.
This bus had the most buses and we were not waiting around for the next bus long, if at all. It also has other package deals you can put with the bus like the river tour and London Eye!

At half term, the buses were bound to be busy and filled with people but as you can easily hop on and off we easily got a seat on the upper deck in the sun two stops in. The commentary is available in many languages on the blue route and you get map and headphones included. Despite visiting London many times before, we saw different parts of London and were able to get a good look at all the sights at height! It is ideal if you want to see the main sights with a limited budget and / or time. Some stops were particularly busy, which is to be expected, and some diversions in the city ensured the journey time was lengthened but we certainly got our money's worth (although we booked online before hand which gave us a good saving)! At the bigger stops there are BB rep's and the one at the Shard was particularly entertaining. The busses seemed to finish at about 5 (ish) and it would be helpful if they went on a bit later. Helped make a lovely day really fun.

We went on big bus on the busiest day in October when school was on holidays. Buses were crowded and it was difficult to get seats on upper deck especially on the red routes. But we were lucky and we sat thru almost the entire route without hopping off. We saw not all big buses were packed - if you don't mind the blue routes then upper seats are always available. We find the guide quite funny and we enjoyed the stories he told about the buildings and landmarks. It was an easy way for us to quickly explore the city and to take a quick look at the london monuments. As mentioned we did the whole route on the bus the first day and on a busy day it took almost 3-4 hrs! And on the second day we hop off at Big Ben and tower bridge to take pictures and walk around. So apparently big bus is only good for tourists like us, not planning to spend more than an hour on a spot and not planning to hop off at all spots. We didn't mind visiting briefly. So if you plan to thoroughly look at all monuments and would spend a few hours at a place for example line up the museums then big bus is not for you. It would cost you a lot of time since the traffic in London is always busy and it really need a few hours to finish all stops. It's not a means of traffic it really is a tour I think.

We have recenty come back from London on a site seeing weekend. We bought a family ticket for the big bus tour which was really good value, as we got the 2nd day free. We went of the walking tour for changing of the guards and went on the river boat experience. In addition you get to see all landmarks of london without having to walk and fight to get on tubes with the kids. You can also hop on hop off at any of the stops which was great. I would highly recommend anyone visiting London to get the bus. The commentary staff are so helpful and work till the last bus (around 7.30pm) In particular We would like to thank Ali (AKA Jackie Chan) what a lovely guy. Would also like to thank all the other staff who helped us get our daughters bag which she left on one of the buses, they all went out of their way to get it back for us which we thankfully got back later that afternoon.

Having been told by all of my friends who have visited London that the hop-on/hop-off buses were an absolute must, we booked our tickets as soon as stepped off the Eurostar. Instead of listening to the entertaining guides that had been advertised and seeing all of the major sights, we spent most of our time waiting for driver shifts to change or sitting in traffic staring at non-descript office buildings while listening to the same set of cliche instrumental music on the headsets. Frankly, I was tempted to jump from the top of the double decker if I heard "Pomp and Circumstance" one more time. Only the red route has the live commentary -- everything else is pre-recorded. The routes make it very difficult to get from the Kensington area back to the central London area without having to inch your way through areas with little or no highlights. In hindsight, we would have been better off taking the Tube and spending more time at our destination.

We took on this tour as it offered a free second day. The tour was long and slow. It is hop on hop off however not many people were doing that. The prerecorded voice track was a bit off of the actual sights. They also offered a live voice tour, we tried the second day but were unsuccessful in finding a red line live tour. Ask prior to booking how frequent the red line is offered. The second day we were lucky enough to get on one of the last buses leaving for the day. We went one stop and were told to get onto a different bus as the one we were one was terminating for the day. We got to stop 5 on the list and were told the tour was over. We were forced off the bus and that was it. No more buses for the day. No one bothered to tell us when we got on the last bus or when we were made to switch that this tour would be cut short. Another patron just bought a ticket for 32 pounds at stop #1 and only got to stop #5 with us when he was told that's it for the day. He was highly upset. We had travel cards and can navigate the tube system so getting back wasn't a problem for us but if we didn't have them at our disposal it would have been a huge problem and a huge cab fare to get back to the starting point. I personally wouldn't recommend this company due to our bad experience. There are other open top tour companies maybe try a competitor.

Was stuck in London for 20hrs on a layover at Heathrow. The Big Bus Tour was the perfect time killer... Hopped on and off a few times, spent three hours at the Tower of London, took the included boat tour ride on the Thames, had fish and chips and a couple of beers and made it back to the airport with three hours to spare. Saw most of the major sights, guides were great, I would do it again!

When your plane lands early in the a.m.from an overnight flight just leave your luggage at the hotel and hop on the bus to get a over all feeling for the city. Fortunately we were in time for the Buckingham Palace changing of the guard walking tour. The guides know the places to go, what to see , where to stand and very knowledgeable about London's history. This tour was excellent We hopped back on the bus to continue the tour of the city before checking in.
The audio from the headphones about various attractions on the bus were infrequent and not comprehensive.
A live speaking guide would be more beneficial

We travelled today on the Big Bus Tour red route in London.
There was a member of staff making the live commentaries that stood out from the rest-it's Robert who was on the route from around 13:00 till 15:00.
Robert took the time to introduce himself to everybody which the previous staff did not do.What stood out was his level of professionalism and knowledge about London which he was passionate to transmit.He came across as calm and approachable.Out of the 3 staff we came across doing the live commentaries he was the most enthusiastic about his job.
We have learned a lot about London today and it's all thanks to him-I have lived in London for over 20 years and felt all his recommendations of attractions to visit were genuine.

In July 2014 we visited Budapest, where were really surprised from very good Big Bus service. Therefore being in London in September 2014, we expected to get such a good quality from London Big Bus service. However, we were very disappointed: 1) Overpriced. 2) There is only one-way direction of this bus , and you can return back to your hotel by this bus only making whole trip. 3) London Big Bus route runs through the center of the city, the streets are narrow, we got stuck in a traffic jam and moved like a turtle more than 3 hours from city center till the Tower . 4) And the last but the most important - almost all the time we have listened to light music in our headphones instead of audio guide explanations. The only one thing we liked - the Big Bus tour price includes river cruise, however you can buy this cruise directly on the boat station.
Probably the best hop on hop off operating in London, great value and great staff, recommend taking the red tour with running commentary.

Our daughter loves Harry Potter and our tour guide, Kevin, was fantastic. He was engaging with all of us, he was entertaining and was very knowlegable! If you get the hop on hop off tour, don't miss the Harry Potter walking tour and ask for Kevin!

I can't believe I'm saying this but I wish we would have done the 2 day ticket instead of one. My son loved this. He's not a big underground fan and prefers to be above ground. What a good way to see the city and the route is great but it's London...it's a big city. One day on a tour like this in Barcelona is fine but we really would have done well with the 2 days ticket to get off and on more. Definitely do take the tour, you will see so much more than being on the tube all day or walking. Nice plus is the guided boat ride from the Tower to Big Ben. Our guide was funny and views were great. My son wanted to do it again. I think this is the best way to go if you have kids.

London double decker busses are famous and a good way to get around, whether a “tour” hop-on-hop-off or public transit bus. There are about four “tour” double decker bus lines that ply about the same routes and show off most London attractions. Taking one early on in your visit is a good way to get the lay of the land and you can always hop off and back onto the next. Most bus stops are within walking distance of major attractions. They cost about 24-30GBP each for a 24 hour pass. Public buses are cheaper on a per trip basis, but you’d better know where you are, where you want to go, and how to get back! The Tube Oyster card is honored on public buses. On the recommendation of our concierge, we chose the Big Bus. You can buy tickets at most major stops since they have guys there with credit card machines hawking their line and bad mouthing the others. It was kinda fun since we had a Big Bus guy and an Original Bus guy trying to dicker to woo us. (Saved 4GBP!) Went with Big Bus which has Red and Blue lines that are common for most of the route and you can switch between . The Blue goes further in two longer loops and you must take it to get to Kenningston or Harrod’s. The Red Line has live English only guides and the Blue Line has audio recordings in numerous languages with ear buds. A good way to sit on top and take some pix and figure out what you might want to do next. But be forewarned. Buses are subject to the HORRIBLE traffic in London. If you want to get somewhere faster, take The Tube and Mind The Gap!!

If you're in London for only a few days, these buses provide an excellent way to see the whole city. The bus tour takes about 4 hours or so and does a huge circuit of the city, with interesting and informative commentary pointing out the city's sites and providing the city's history. One can also hop on or off at the numerous stops around the city, which are conveniently located near most major attractions.

The tour is a little pricey (it was 30 Pounds per person for the 1 day pass), but my wife and I feel that it was well worth the cost and highly recommend it.
My wife and her friend did a bus tour of London. They thought it was very entertaining . It showed them everywhere around London . They said it it was well worth the money.

We took the Big Bus tour on our first day in London, and it was magnificent! We got to see everything we wanted to see (and more!) during the tour. It was very exciting, educational yet also relaxing and enjoyable. Make sure to grab a spot on the upper level of the bus to get a prime view of the city sights. One of my favourite parts of the trip. Friendly service, I would definitely do it again!!

This was the 2 nd visit to London and I did the Big Bus Tour both times. A great and easy way to see the city! And Big Steve was absolutely wonderful and helpful. If you have the chance to have an actual guide (versus the headphones), choose that. We liked it so much, we did the BBT a week later in Paris too!

I know a lot of the larger cities that draw tourists have these. This is the first time I've done one. I think it's a great way to see the city. I think the hop on/hop off feature is fantastic. We covered a lot of ground using the bus and, sitting on the open top part, I was able to get a lot of great photos. The ground staff members we encountered were very friendly and willing to give tips and advice. The bus drivers were all very friendly, also willing to give directions and tips. In a city as big as London, with so much ground to cover, I definitely recommend Big Bus Tours. The buses were all clean and well maintained. I found the price to be tolerable. I thought, for the amount of money spent, the return was high. Again, remember how large London is and how much there is to take in. Also, with your ticket to the bus, they give a voucher for a free river cruise. We did not use this as the week we were there, it was unseasonably chilly.

Our family of four visited London for three days. We started out by trying to see all of the sights on our own but everything is so spread out, we quickly realized that this wasn't going to work! We happened along the Big Bus Tours at one of the tourist sites and hopped on! Our tour guide, Nick, was absolutely the BEST! He was full of information, fun facts and lots of great jokes! He really made the tour a blast! We also went on the route with the taped guide and while that was informative, it lacked the upbeat and friendly feeling that a Nick provided! I would recommend the Big Bus Tour.........just try to get Nick as your guide and you'll definitely have a great time!

A wonderful way to see London. Buy a 24 hr ticket or specify which district. All colour coded so just hop on off on red/blue/purple/green. Don't forget to ask the driver where to pick up the next colour bus you have choosen.

There two other London hop on hop offs by Gray line and Original Tour.The Original tour is 3 pounds less.They are more frequent.They all stop at the same bus stop.When you are waiting for the bus only you know whos more frequent.

The Big Bus provides a comprehensive tour of London ... take advantage of the "on and off" opportunities and the river cruise included in the tour ticket. Also, take the guided tour (instead of the taped tour).

The tor was excellent and the tour guide was highly knowledgeable. Enjoyed the red tour best. Took another bus tour, but didn't enjoy it as much as there was no guide. Tickets are good for 24 hours, so you can go on more than one tour. You can also hop on and off the bus along the path, so you can spend the time you want at each stop and just pick up another bus when you're ready. The riverboat tour that came with the ticket was an added bonus.

Our hotel was on blue bus route but we changed after hopping off for a museum. The Red bus was much better commentary but was only in English. Still thought the blue was good and you need to get it for some places.
