What a great way to see London, we saw all the sights and hopped off and on whenever we wanted to see the places of interest for us. An added bonus was that it included a Thames river boat cruise which was most enjoyable.

Bought a two day travel pass for the Hop Hop Off service, this proved excellent value for Money as it included a thames river trip to Greenwich and also three walking tours. Joined the main tours from a shuttle bus (Green Route) from the St Pancras area. Found the main boarding points well staffed with helpful staff. On the Red Route found a live tour commentary excellent and entertaining. Took the Ghosts by Gaslight tour in the evening, and this was very good. The guide being one of the guides on the Red Route, I thought I knew London having worked there for a number of years, yet he showed me places which I never knew existed. Very good value for Money
Liked the live tour. We could hop on and off at sites round London using this and getting clued up on site info.

We did the hop on hop off with Big Bus yesterday and it was excellent. Very good service and such an excellent way to get one 's bearings. My wife and I are now of the view that any trip to a city should start this way. After a lot if hiking around it becomes a nice sanctuary where you can just relax and absorb the sights.

I joined your bus on the 7 August 2014 we picked up the bus from the eye the guide was informative but not a lot of personality we rejoined the bus at Buckingham place and what a treat we had Nick is very informative great personality and really funny we hopped off and rejoined at convent garden who ever the guide was he was uninformative and extremely boring we were going to get off but instead just switched off if they were all like Nick u would not have a problem

We did part of the bus tour in London but found that the audio and the bus were not in sync so the recording would say look to your right but we had already passed the sight.
We were looking forward to doing the boat tour but when we got to the boat we were told we had to go back to the main Big Bus office to get a different ticket. No one had mentioned this before and we had scheduled our day so we would make the boat tour. Going back to the office at that point wasn't an option. We were also scheduled to do the tour in Paris, I asked to cancel a few days before based on our experience in London but the company refused.

This was a last minute decision to have a day in London, with travelling to st Pancras by train, I had never seen any bus tours departing from there before so I was pleased to stumble upon big bus tours, the guy was very helpful and good with the kids as I was with them on my own. The bus turned up within 10 mins and the driver was cheerful too. We had great seats up on top deck and when we had a shower part of the top deck was covered so we stayed dry. The sites covered in this tour are exactly what you want. having lived in Britain all my life and never done this, I couldn't recommend this highly enough. The drivers and guys at the stops were extremely cheerful and helpful. Well worth the money.

Bought a 2 day ticket...was cheaper than I expected...Nice....cannot fault this service...got us around to the sites we wanted to see and filled the between times on the Bus when we needed a break to relax and re-charge...the on-board commentary on the Red route was good and amusing ....Plan your day and use the Big Bus Tour...real value for money....plus a river trip included...

We visited London last week and bougth a 2 day ticket for the big bus, and included a river cruise.
It was quite nice, friendly staff, most of them.
One negative note was the overcrowding and the waiting times.

We have just spent a week in London, and we couldn't recommend this bus company high enough. Thanks to a very informative ' Neil Tyler ' he was so friendly and helpful. He is a real asset to Big Bus Tours. All of the staff were so helpful. Hope to see you all next visit.

We shopped around for a hop on, hop off sightseeing tour of London and chose this company as it offered two days for the price of one and as a bonus was slightly cheaper than the others. We were taken to all the main attractions and the commentary was very informative and was available in many languages. The buses came frequently and the staff and drivers were friendly and helpful. Would highly recommend.

Having been on a bus tour in the 1990's it was a surprise to see how much the tours have expanded now.
The tour we took ran for well over two hours and was great chance to see more of London outside of the main city area.
Well worth the money.

This was our third big bus tour (Abu Dhabi and Dubai previously), it was a great way to see the city and learn about the sites. The drivers and staff were friendly and patient. The only negative was the weather...
Would recommend to anyone who lives in or visits London.

Most of what you want to see in London can be seen from this tour. Especially since most of you JUST want to see. I would not have seen a lot of what we did if we weren't on the Big Bus tour. There is no way I would've gone to see The Ritz Hotel or Harrods even if it weren't for this tour. There are two lines, and the Red is much better! The live commentary makes all the difference. We had 3 different narrators over the day of hopping on and off, and each was hilarious and interesting. We did take the Blue Line as we went out the Kensington Gardens (not worth it might I add). Learnt so much on this tour, but it also comes with some perks. All the workers will sell you tickets to other attractions, HOWEVER DO NOT BE FOOLED. If you buy a ticket for The London Eye - it is not a fast-track ticket, and you have to exchange their ticket for real tickets at the attraction!! We were not informed of this, but it didn't end up being an inconvenience. The tickets are also good for a lengthy amount of time, for example Eye tickets last 2 weeks and St. Paul's tickets last 3 month so don't worry about not being able to go on an attraction that day. We rode the bus for 2 days, which was plenty of time to see everything and get the whole picture of London.

We took the Big Bus Tour on our second day in London. This was a great way for us to get our bearings and the kids loved sitting up top. Both tour guides were informative and gave great tips and insights on the city. We also enjoyed the boat tour on the Thames that was included in the price. The stops were well located and close to major attractions.

Went on the bus tour with my 3 children and it was a perfect way to see London . The stops are so convenient for visiting all of the iconic places and the commentary was fab .
My only thing that I would advise is find out the last bus time and colour to where you want to finish , as we almost got left stranded at Victoria when the tour ended , but the lovely driver told us to stay on and he took us back to Kensington .
A perfect day out especially when the sun is shining for all of the family .

We thoroughly enjoyed the experience. We bought a one day tour but when we went to claim the tickets we were told there was a "bonus 2nd day plus a boat cruise on the Thames". It suit us just fine. We didn't have to rush and we didn't. The grounds people were friendly and helpful and there were plenty of them at each stop. So instead of asking the drivers your questions and holding up the tour, the staff at each stop was there to assist with any queries you might have before you board. We only did the recorded tour and the commentary was informative. It was the first day of summer holidays and despite the massive traffic jams the trip was handled with minimal delay. Some of the the buses have a partial enclosure in the upper deck so for those of us that didn't want to bake in the hot sun but also wanted to have a better view of the city than the lower deck, it was a nice option. Would definitely recommend Big Bus Tour London.

Although we've been to London many times before, we decided to give an open top bus tour a try. We booked online which cost £60 for a family of 4 and included a 30 minute trip down the Thames with City Cruises, which I didn't think was too bad price wise.
Our trip started quite well, we managed eventually to get seats together on the top deck of blue route bus and spent an hour listening to the commentary through the headphone provided and enjoying the sights. We then got off at the Tower of London and joined the queue for the City Cruises trip down the Thames. This actually turned out to be the highlight of the day, viewing the sights from the water was excellent and the commentary by the crew was informative, clever and funny.
Unfortunately when we tried to re-board a bus to continue our tour it was a nightmare. Every bus that came along was packed on both floors. Eventually, we managed to get seats downstairs on a bus hoping that eventually some people upstairs would use the hop on, hop off facility and we could move upstairs. Sadly, this didn't happen, instead our driver decided to allow an extra 30+ people to cram onto the bus, resulting in people sitting on the FLOOR on the top deck, and the rest standing up downstairs. A few people complained to the driver that surely this was dangerous, but he just shrugged his shoulders and continued! We exited the bus a couple of stops later as it was ridiculously overcrowded and the temperature inside was really uncomfortable.
A very hit and miss experience all round. Couldn't fault the first part of our tour and the boat trip was great, but the second part was truly horrible!

This was so fun. We loved these tours. They take you everywhere, so you can get your lay of the land and since it's a hop on hop off you get to see all of the different areas of the city. Take the tour buses that have the live tour guides, they are very fun and interesting.

We were earlier confused as which tour to take,but the Big bus tour brochure was the least complicated.They also gave us tickets which were valid for more than 24 hours though we paid only for day.
Also this company had the maximum services ..their buses hardly had us waiting at any stop.So this is definitely the most recommended bus tour company.

Great overview of London. Includes a river cruise. You can identify places you want to spend more time at. You can hop on and off the bus with ease and your ticket is good for 24 hours from the time you purchase it. I preferred the live narrated tours but recorded tours are available. Not every bus has a live tour guide. The benefit of the recorded tour is that with the headphones on, you are not bothered by the ambient noise especially if sitting in the upper open deck. If you have your own big headphones take them with you. They also offer a special track on the recorded tour buses for kids that are tailored to them.

This was my first time traveling by hop on hop off bus, and I can't say that I overly loved the experience. We booked the bus tour because we had a group of 15 students and thought it would be a great way to see the city. While the guides one 1/2 buses were great (and the other super super dull), we found it hard to actually Hop on and Hop off and make best use of our £21 tickets. It was hard to incorporate this into our schedule well, and with limited hours (everything finishing up by 5pm), it was difficult to feel like we got our money's worth. We chose this tour because it had a Royal Guards Walking Tour included, which we did - but also ate up a large portion of time. We did get to see some of the music at the beginning of the changing of the guard ceremony up by St. James Palace, and then rushed through the Park to get to the actual changing at Buckingham - which we were told was the boring part. Some of our students almost got lost because the group was so big - and were thankful the guide had a flag to helot hem find their way. We were left at Buckingham - which wasn't really near where we wanted to get on the bus to make the most of the tour - so we walked 25 minutes to a better start point. It was very cold and windy, so sitting on top wasn't fun - though some of us braved it for the better pictures. We didn't have time for the other walking tours (Harry Potter for example) or the Boat - because if we did them we would have missed the bus. Maybe on a 2 day pass this would have been easier, or with a smaller group, but with a large group in London for 10 days, this wasn't necessary.

The following day we had a private guide from walks.com who toured us around Westminster Abbey and the Tower of London and we learned WAY more and saw WAY more through a walking tour then the bus. If was to go again I wouldn't go a hop-on hop-off tour as much as a 2 hour into sightseeing tour, and then walking tours after that. The bus and tube system is so good in the city that this type of transportation isn't really needed, and is way less authentic. Our students enjoyed the tube much more as well as our walking tours.

We also had problems with our reservations and no one would email me back with answers. I ended up using a Facebook page to ask questions, and even then got super vague answers, so we didn't quite know how to redeem our online tickets for the buses when we got there. Customer service and website organization could both use a boost. If I were to consider a bus tour again in any city, I would probably consider the competition first - didn't find myself impressed with what they had to offer.

Overall the tour in itself is fine. It is a very long day so be prepared. The bus drivers are amazing navigating their buses. You receive lots of information which makes it interesting. All the lines except the red line are pre-recorded commentary which you listen to with ear phones. This works great as you hear everything. The red line has an actual person giving commentary. This is where we ran into issues. Soon after we started on the red line portion of the tour, I put up my hand to get the host's attention. He ignored me for a bit then finally he asked what I wanted. I told him that we could not hear what he was saying (and I do not have a hearing problem). Well, he was very rude and told me that the sound was as loud as it would go and answered me in a way which indicated that I had offended him in some way. Someone else asked him a question and was ignored because the host could not hear him. No effort was made to get out of his seat to address the question. It was obvious he was going to do his commentary, get paid for it and he was done. This ruined our time on this portion of the tour. So, as soon as we could, we switched to the blue line with pre-recorded messages. We have done several Big Bus Tours and this one, the red line, gave us an ugly taste of British hospitality. Do the tour and you will enjoy it, but stay off the red line portion to enjoy your day.

You can get on the bus at one of their stops and then pay for it later on. Someone will come on board to collect payment

If it is a nice day, sit up top but be sure you have sunscreen on.

If you plan on going to the Tower if London, a Big Bus tour representative will sell you tickets at a better price than at ticket counter. The price also includes a cruise on Thames River which is very good.

All in all we liked the tour except for the red line portion. There were several upset people on that bus.

Hop on, Hop off bus tours in large cities are often slow paced due to traffic congestion. London Big Bus is no exception. We spent far too long on the bus to do the entire circuit. Save time and money by taking the Underground directly to where you want to visit. Both our buses had prerecorded audio guides which were nothing special either.

We thought a 2 day pass would be great just to use the bus for transportation. Not worth it. Get the one day pass and do the whole tour. Great way to see the city in a relaxing way. Good tour guides. Hop on hop off allows you to pick and choose what to see. There seemed to be times when only blue route bus ran and we wanted to catch a red route to get to another destination quicker. Also had to wait a bit before a red or blue route bus showed up depending on which direction you were looking to go.

After a very bad experience with Big Bus in Paris, The London Big Bus experience was a refreshing change. It is an excellent way of visiting all the attractions in a short time. The guides, drivers and the ticket officers at stops were very helpful and courteous. Totally recommend it.

For anyone visiting London then this trip is a must. We were travelling with two young children and booked direct online through their site - cheapest way. We were presently surprised to find that when we went to board the bus that they'd thrown an extra days travel in free of charge, unfortunately for us we were coming home the next day so couldn't take advantage of it.

The trip was made even more enjoyable by our tour guide Elliot Falkner whose wit and knowledge ensured that we knew everything we needed to know about London and a bit more. Cheers Elliot.

My family of four (includes 2 children) enjoyed the hop on, hop off tour. We especially liked the buses that had live commentary, which we thought was much more interesting & entertaining than listening w/headphones. We also participated in the royal walk which we highly recommend! Our guide Kevin was excellent! We saw the whole changing of the guards and he was amusing as well as informative about what we were seeing. Very good experience overall!

Many years since we had an open top tour around London but glad that we took this hop on hop off. Included was a river trip to Greenwich.
There is only one problem with these tours and that is that there are only 24 hours in a day.
Brilliant tours

Hi firstly it is worth saying it was the Pride parade when we were on the tour. We rang before booking and they assured us the tour would be back to normal after 3pm. We arrived on the bus for 245pm. No communication really from the driver. The commentary half the time didn't liaise with the sights. You would have been looking for the building or place on the left or the right and either you had passed it or we hadn't reached it yet. It took us over an hour to get through Trafalgar square. We have done the Paris bus tours twice and really enjoyed them. But have to say the London bus tour was a let down.

If you are looking for a simple drive around London take bus#15 ( buy Oyster card and you can save at least 60%) it goes practically the same rout. I wish Big Bus had better commentaries and very few facts There was mostly classical music over headphones.

Once bought the ticket lasts 24hrs, new ear phones given when you get on, recorded information as you go round was fantastic, goes to all the major attractions and nice areas of London, just hop on and off, very frequent service, staff very helpful too.
We didn't use it, but the ticket also gives you a discounted price at various places eg Madame Tussaud's.

Whether you are in London for a few days or weeks, the best way to see all the major attractions and get a great feel for the place is with Big Bus. The buses come frequently and you can hop on and off where you like. It even includes a cruise down the Thames. There are two routes, the red and blue. We did both. Loved the fully guided walking tour we did of Royal London and wish we had more time to do the other walking tours. There are other bus companies offering the same service but Big Bus is the biggest from what we were told. The commentary was great on the red route with a digital recorded tours on the blue route. Book online and save 23 pounds for one day or pay when you arrive 27 pounds.
Highly recommend!

We decided to take the Big Bus tours and stay on it for the entire round-trip so see everything along the route. The bus is a hop-on/hop-off type and your ticket is good for 24 hours, but we chose to stay on (many others did too). The entire trip took about 3 hours because there was lots of traffic, but that was ok. Good overview of London and would recommend.

The Big Bus tour of London (red line version) was a lot of fun for my two teenagers and me. Our guide, Eliot, had a dry wit and still had energy after ten hours of narrating London's history to tourists. It was very helpful to be able to ride the Big Bus in to central London from St. Pancras station, I recommend this company.

Big Bus Tours are the best way to take in all the sightseeing places in London. Within a two-day period you can cover almost all the famous places in London and the best part is that you can hop off at any point and then get on again on the following bus at your will. The staff is courteous and helpful and the recorded commentary makes good sense. The frequency of service at each hop off point is the best amongst all the hop on hop off Buses and I would surely recommend this Big Bus over any other competitor. The people managing the Buses are professional and always courteous and smiling.

The London tour was on the day of the Tour De France so it was an extremely disorganized tour. First, we could not find the guy selling tickets at the bus stop. He appeared after the bus came. The drivers were not helpful or informative. We kept being asked to change buses for reasons we were not told and then once on the bus, the route changed with no communication upfront. We would not go with this company again. There are at least 3 other tour companies doing these tours. Check into those.

This bus tour has several routes. I suggest you take the red tour first, since it takes you to the best highlights of the city, but the other tour routes are amazing as well. You can hop off at any of the stops, and hop back on to the next bus (just show your receipt). Really great!

We have enjoyed the a Big Bus Tours in the past. In the past. Three out of four guides were so monotone and bored with their jobs, passing out conflicting information, it was quite frustrating.

Today's traffic added to the unpleasantness, but honestly the guides need some help. The only decent one was unfortunately with us for only two stops. Guides need to have some enthusiasm and pep in their talks, not sounds like they have been forced to ride this while being flogged.

I'm out a good deal of money for a miserable experience. I'm not sure that I will ever go again.

We took the blue line in London today. Over three hours and we didn't get through the entire loop. It was excruciatingly long with very very long periods of music playing with no commentary. At one point, we went 45 minutes without hearing anything but the same four songs played over and over. We took one red line and the commentator fixated on the bad driving of another bus driver and gave hurried commentary on the sights we were going by. The boat tour had a recorded tour, which was very disappointing. The windows in the lower level wouldn't lower and the top seats were ridiculously uncomfortable. The only good tour guide was at the very end for one stop along the Thames. I wish we'd found him earlier. He said he'd only been working there seven days!

For the huge price paid, we were mostly bored and saw the Marble arch three times and not much else. Oh, look quick through those trees at the house of Windsor! Or it told us to look for something that had already gone by. It was a huge waste of a day, we were hoping for a good orientation to London.

What a fantastic experience we had with this company from start to finish! All the representatives were helpful, all the drivers were welcoming(watch their expert driving in London traffic and narrow streets!) and all the guides were great! The company offers great value tix for some of the attractions - we used it for our visit to the Tower - saved lots of time not waiting in line.
For the price of one day they let us ride the bus for two consecutive days +river cruise and a walking tour - unbeatable package! We bought our tix at the airport - they were good for any day in within a week for the price of $29, which was a little cheaper than at the stops, All the stops are clearly marked, maps are easy to navigate, rain ponchos are included.
Highly recommended!!

We bought a 24 hour ticket and stopped at several places by hopping on and off. We never had to wait for a bus at any of the stops! A trip up the river is also included free of charge, the boat was quite full and we didn't get a seat which was a bit of a let down as I was travelling with my mum who is 70 years old. All of the staff were polite apart from the initial ticket seller at Paddington who was quite rude. Over all a good experience

It is indeed convenient and covers all of the main touristy spots in London, but I would have to agree with another reviewer that you can do all of these locations on your own on the tube in half the time. Oxford Circus and Fleet Street are traffic nightmares and we found that while we expected to be on the bus for an hour or so, it took the better part of the day to do the entire route. The guide was informative and interesting, but even he was running out of things to say when we only moved a city block in fifteen minutes. It includes a 'free' boat tour on the Thames, but we never had time to do it.

We had a fantastic experience on the Big Bus! We planned to get off & on, but had such good seats on the Upper Deck & the Best Tour Guide in London - Big Steve was friendly, funny, & extremely knowledgeable & made our trip even more special than we expected!

We bought the tickets for this the last day we were in London. The original idea was to get tickets to the hop on hop off big bus instead of the two tickets but we didn't getting both anyway. I think they were about $150 or so for family of four. Once we figured out where to get on the damn bus everything was fine. However, there was a construction project going on downtown which kind of screwed up the routes. We did both the live tour bus and the one with the headphones. It was a great way to see Piccadilly Circus etc. and get some fundamental understanding of the history of the city. Obviously very very tour street but we enjoyed it and I would recommend it. Would probably be good on the first day you get there so you don't have to waste one of your London past days or something. I really wish this was included in the London pass like it is the Paris pass but unfortunately it is not .

We used the Big Bus Tour in London. At the end of the day we were trying to get back to our hotel near Paddington Station. We were on the bus with another small group of people. They asked us where we were going and we told them Paddington Station. The stop we had got on never came up, he was not using the regular tour route. Finally the man in the other group went down and asked him where the Paddington Station stop was. He told him that is was a long ways back and told them to get off and find a cab. He came up to us and told us that we had missed our stop and we would need to get a cab. Very poor service!!!!!

After using L'Open top busses in Paris, we were looking forward to seeing the sights of London on Big Bus Tours London. Compared to Paris, the value was very poor for a 2 day pass and the regularity of the services and a bus coming along was not as advertised. We spent more time waiting at bus stops (for 20 minute periods at a time) and being moved from one bus to another! than we did seeing the sights. We only had live commentary on 2 busses rather than all busses as advertised. I would not recommend this company at all. The cost is not worth it and the service level was quite poor.

The big bus tour (open top double decker bus) is a good way to get your bearings and identify which areas you may want to return to. There are a number of different routes - red and the longer blue route which covers all the main sights. There is also a purple route which will drop you at you hotel - very handy! The blue route has audio commentary, but the red route has a real person detailing the sight as you go. I experienced Mike, and he was brilliant. Service with a sense of humour.

If you planning ahead, have a look on the web as advanced purchase may give you a cheaper price. I also added the boat cruise and London Tower into the price, which is very worth while.

We only had one day for sight seeing and decided a HOHO bus would be the best way to do this. I found the Big Bus Tours to be easy to use. There were staff at each stop and they helped us get on the right bus (red line). Then we took advantage of the boat tour. I would do this again in a heart beat.

There are two lines on the big bus tour, the blue line with an audio tour in different languages and the red line with live guides. We got on the blue line first as it was right outside our hotel and then changed to the red line at marble arch. Our guide Jade was absolutely fabulous!! She was so helpful and gave an informative tour whilst also being very funny! She greeted everybody on the bus and was very sweet and bubbly! We took the river cruise (included free) which was wonderful and then jumped back on the red line bus with a different guide who was also brilliant (though I didn't catch his name!) All in all, it's a great way to see the city and worth the £32 price! Make sure you use the guided busses as our guides really made our day!

Took the Big Bus tour today with a wonderful chap at the microphone by the name of Nick. He was so delightfully entertaining that I gave him a very nice tip. We rode along for a good 30 minutes on the bus and he had some very funny observations....especially about where the Queen Mother "buys her knickers". If you can find Nick, he needs to be on a talent show.

The entire Big Bus operation is extremely well run and well worth the money you will pay for a one, two or three day pass. Best way to get around London.

The hop-on hop-off Big Bus Tour was a terrific and leisurely way to see the city. We were in London for two days with prepurchased travel passes but we preferred the BBT to the Tube. Of course the weather during our stay was wonderful. Had it been raining, we might have relied more on other forms of transport. At one point on the first day, there was a cab strike and we were stuck at a bus stop for more than an hour until we just gave up and walked back to the hotel. BBT gave us our second day for free to make up for the inconvenience. The BBT also gave us free access to the Thames River Cruise to Greenwich. BBT is a great option for seeing the city. Buy online to save money.

My family of 4 had the 48 hour pass and had no troubles at all. The bus took us to everywhere we needed to go, from the Tower of London...to the Beatles/Rock-n-Roll store and everywhere in between. Somehow we (and another family) ended up out on the route and did not realize the buses had stopped running. When we inquired on how to catch a bus back to the London Eye, we were told that the last bus had already passed this stop. The company had a bus right there and they took us back to Victoria Station, where we could catch the tube or just walk back to the hotel. Something that went above and beyond anything they had to do, but it was very much appreciated.
We took 2 of the walking tours and they were one of the highlights of our visit.
Harry Potter Walking Tour - Our guide Nuri was the perfect guide for this tour. She made sure the kids were an integral part of the tour and often had them participating in different activities.
Changing of the Guard Walking Tour - Our guide was Kevin and he was awesome as well. He made sure that we saw more pieces of the changing, than what happens at Buckingham Palace. The history of the changing that he explained was very interesting. His sense of humor made the tour very enjoyable for the whole family.

The big bus tour has two variations: recorded tours and live tour guides. Assuming you don't need language translation, try to get the live guides. We hopped on with three different guides and each of them made for a lively look at history.

Very good tours. I would recommend starting your trip with this tour to get a feel for the city and see which attractions you would like to further investigate.

Our tour guide was big Steve and he was excellent. If you can catch one of his tours, it will definitely make you excited for the rest of your trip to London.

The bus tour is well organised and I would recommend to anyone wishing to visit London city centre over a short period of time, it gives you an idea of the main tourist attractions available to visit, the ticket also includes a short cruise of the Thames. Best value for money is the two days tour prepaid over the internet.

We would highly recommend the big bus - it gives a great overview of the City and the opportunity to hop on and off. We only had a short time in London and we found this to be a great way to take a lot in with really good access to the 'things to do'. The commentary on the way was really helpful. Even when cold I'd suggest sitting up top as the 360 degree view is unmissable.

We have taken hop-on, hop-off tours in several cities and opted for the Big Bus as it had live commentary on the red route. We signed on at Victoria station but had to take the Blue bus to just below Marble Arch to catch the red.....even though they followed the same routes but not as frequently as the bus on the blue route. Anyway, after a 30 minute wait the red route was excellent as we had a very knowledgable and humerous guide who pointed out all the sites with lots of extra details filled in. An added bonus was a guided tour down the Mall the next morning to watch the changing of the guard, and we had a special bonus of the Queen and Prince Phillip's limo passing us during the walk and we all got a good view of the royal couple. The guide explained the ceremony and led us to a good vantage point to see the parade.

Hello from Canada! We were ending our African Safari with a few days in London. Booking the Big Bus Tour was a great idea! 48 hour with a river cruise helped us to see much of London. And our tour guide Nick was fantastic! Funny, witty and informative! You will sit in traffic and not move for parts of it, but if you are only in London for a short time, this is great!

We always do a "hop-on hop-off" bus tour in any new city. It's a good way to "get your bearings" and good transportation to the places you want to visit. We had a grand experience with Big Bus in New York, so we decided to choose that line over the competition in London. We bought a 24 hour pass for 32 pounds each and extended that to 48 hours for another 6 pounds per person. We were on the bus to get where we wanted to be/return from for 2 hours each way--which might have been necessary. My real complaint, though, is the return trip on the blue line in the afternoon. Attendants were rude and did not tell us about the switch to the purple hotel line. We were dropped off at a stop different from the one from which we were picked up--thus we had no idea where we were! Blue line Big Buses passed our hotel long after we were sent on the purple buses. Be advised!

We were very lucky to have a sunny weekend in London, so the open bus was a must for us. There is a lot of competition from tour companies and it's worth checking with ground staff what offers they have, especially when you have two or three different companies standing around. The leaflet said £32 / day but in the end we got a 48 hour ticket for £30 each. The price includes the bus, boat tour on the Thames and three guided tours. We opted for the bus without live commentary so we could get the tour in German (you can select from 8 or 9 different languages) some of which was very funny without intending to be so. We never had to wait long for a bus to arrive at any given station.
We also did the guided "Royal Walk" which includes the Changing of the Guards. They don't actually take you to Buckingham Palace to start with because they know exactly what is happening where and how you will get the best possible view (and of course the best possible pictures to take home). Our guide was Phil and he was hillarious as well as enthusiastic and knowledgeable, really made our day.

Just arrived in London? I recommend taking the Big Bus Tours. This is a hop on hop off tour and can choose from a live guide (red line) or an audio guide (blue line). We purchased out tickets at a kiosk located at one of the tours stops and were given a map of all stops, etc. We opted to take the blue line (audio guide). When boarding the bus, we were given headsets/pods, selected our own seats (try to get in the front - we sat on the upper level for great photo ops), plug in your headsets/pods, and select the language you wish to hear the tour. Wonderful way to be introduced to the city and provided with a high level overview of historical events/buildings, and places. I found this tour very informable, reasonably priced (for 24 hours to hop on and off around the route), route was along at least the top 10 sights to see in London if not more. My only issue with this tour is that the seats are a little narrow even for me and I am 5'2'. Plus, some people on the bus may not be as considerate as others. A few people might stand or keep their arm up the entire trip videoing/taking pictures so if you are behind one of these inconsiderate tourists, be prepared to stand up to take your picture or move to a seat in the front of the bus.

I used Big Bus Tours to get around central London and see the sights for 2 days. The second day extension is very reasonably priced. The ticket included a river cruise - which I took from the Tower to Westminster, and was added value. I found the commentary informative, the routes took in a good range of attractions, the hop-on hop off worked well, and the buses were frequent, so there wasn't too much waiting. At each stop they had staff who were friendly and helpful. All up, great service and really good value for money

This was a great tour it covered all of the most interesting sites in London. It rained the only day that we had to take the tour and we really did not get to get off at a lot of stops, but still got good pictures from the bus. I suggest taking the tour over at least 2 days and starting when they open and touring all day. Pick where you would like to stop and hope that it does not rain. Having the headphones can be confusing at times as to what area they are talking about but you still get the history of the area. I highly recommend this tour for everyone who visits London.

We booked this bus tour for our first full day in London. There was a stop just outside of our hotel, so we were able to just get on and see all the sights in one day! We got off at a few different stops to look around and go to different museums. They had lovely music playing in the blue and purple tours (Holst's Planets!! :) ) and interesting information about your surroundings. Worth the price!

A great way to see London. We got a 24hour pass which included a boat cruise. The red line route came with an English speaking guide. Each new bus we hopped on we found the guide very informative. The blue line route only has plug in audio. We found the buses came every 10 to 15 minutes as advertised. I would certainly recommend this tour company. In fact we have just used the same company in Paris because of how good the London tour was.
Good way to see London. We were in London for 5 days and had a 48 hour pass with Big Bus. Was great to get your bearings and have a good look around. Plenty of buses, never had to wait long.

My wife and I wanted to visit all the sites in London and weren't sure where to start.
For £32 each we went around the beautiful city and we're able to hop off where we chose. On one of the buses we were very happy with our guide whose name was Gareth. He was funny, helpful and very accommodating to our requests. Thanks!!

The Big Bus HOP ON HOP OFF bus was the BEST thing we did in London. It immediately oriented us to the city - so much better than being in the tube and missing out on all the sites. The bus gave us an overall sightseeing tour (they have audio narratives on some lines and live narratives on others). The drivers are very helpful. You can hop on and hop off all day. Never had to wait more than 10 minutes for a bus. I highly recommend it.

We came to London with a French family, and thought this tour would be the way to give them an introduction to the city, particularly given a very uncertain weather forecast.
We got on at Marble Arch, "hopped off" at Trafalgar Square and walked to Covent Garden for lunch, hopped back on at Trafalgar Square until the Tower of London when we took the inclusive Boat Trip to Westminster Pier, then back on the bus to Buckhingham Palace, then home.
At £27 per adult, it was very good value and a first rate introduction to London.

The Big Bus tours allow flexibility with the hop-on/hop-off option as well as the option to have a live commentary or a recording to listen to. The tour hits all the main spots in London and provides free walking tours (I recommend the Harry Potter walking tour-very entertaining and informative!) and a city cruise for free.

Wednesday 23rd April 2014 - a great guide on board the Big Bus which we took around the sites of London, his name was Steve and he was from London. I really recommend this tour and try to get on the Red tour with Steve.

I come home each year in March and always spend 3 nights in London. I use big bus tours now. Been riding with them the last 3 years. I tried one of the others once but didn't enjoy it so much. What i also like is when i travel they always have the BOGOF tickets so you get 2 days for the price of 1. Excellent value for money! Plenty of stops to hop on and off. Excellent walking tours and boat cruises inc in the price (one tip) if you go on the boat cruise, buy any snacks before you get on the boat. I know i've been out of the UK a few years now but a bar of choc, bag of crisps and a can of pop were almost 4quid.. ridiculous! although the boat trip was excellent all the way from Westminster to Greenwich and back. Yeah i know the boat cruise is inc in the cost of the bus ticket and i kept telling myself that eating the chocolate LOL.. they got to a make a pound or 2 as well.

One thing i'm annoyed with myself on, is that i didn't get the name of one of their drivers who was amazingly helpful in the evening going out of his way to get us up close to the top of Baker St by the Tube station when we were the only ones left on the bus at their stop by Marble Arch. I'm not sure if he was allowed to do what he did but i appreciate it greatly. Excellent customer service. We did have a driver the next day that wasn't quite as helpful. If i'm asking questions about places, one word answers aren't really what i'm looking for but the driver before was perfection and he made up for the other driver.

Took blue tour of London, interesting factual commentary in 12 languages, headphones provided. Open top bus takes in all major sights with hop on hop off option and plenty of bus stops in nearby locations. Great river cruise included with brilliant commentary from Dean our Crew member... option of 3 walking tours but we did not partake as we wdnt on London Eye instead. Ticket for tour allows you bypass the queue to purchase your ticket at booking desk but you do still havef to queue for attraction. It was fairly busy on the day, however we only waited about 15 mins to get into the capsule and believe me it is well worth it!!!!
We spent all day on the tour from 10am and we were dropped off in the Mall at 8pm. Well worth the money if you want to see London in all it's Glory and you get amazing views from bus.

We decided on Big Bus Tours on our final day in London near Russell Square. We went to the Green pick point having already purchased our tickets at our Hotel. The attendant told us to board and we spent an hour to pick up other people via such places as King Cross Station and passing Russell Square to our starting point in Leicester Square. On boarding our bus we were not informed to pick up some earphones and it was only when we saw people wearing them whilst on our journey I went down and picked up some earphones for my wife and myself, sadly having missed many of the attractions detailed. What a difference the earphones made. The commentator was excellent, detailed and we enjoyed the journey from then on. Overall it is an excellent way of seeing the sights and the ability to get on off if wished is well explained. If only we had been advised to wait walk to a pick up point for our journey and told to pick up some earphones it would have been excellent and worthy of 5 stars, sadly we were disappointed at the beginning, it spoiled a wonderful few hours. John H

The Big Bus tour in London is the best deal around. Be sure to get a two day pass. They have guided and audio only busses. The ticket includes a boat rude on the thames river. You can hop on and off all day. I suggest you get on the red line (guided tour) first and take it all the way around marking what you want to see and do. Then simply take the bus to each destination and hop off. Best ever way to get the lay of the land. Oh, and they have uniformed attendants at most stops to help with directions and answer questions. They are so nice and helpful. Highly recommend!

What better way to see the city than pay a flat rate for 48 hours of unlimited use on a open air bus tour with real tour guides who add their own flavour to the tour? It was a perfect way to see a large amount of the city especially because my mum isn't able to walk the city quickly. Plus, if you are always in the underground do you really see the city? With this bus tour you not only see the city but learn so much about everything. What is also cool is this company has 3-4 different lines to catch so you can get to further away places, as well as a broad range of locations to stop at. The guides were also incredibly helpful, and it was fantastic that there were employees of the company at every stop able to further help us to attractions and they had discounts on tickets for museums and attractions in london. The best way to see london by far!

Much of our first day in London, after a nighttime flight and little sleep, was spent on the Big Bus. For whatever reason, we were always on the Blue Bus which had recorded commentary and musical interludes between points of interest. Unfortunately we got stuck in quite a bit of traffic and sat for a good chunk of time listening to that music in the chilly upper open area of the bus. That was a little frustrating, but I don't know hat could have been done about the traffic - we took the tour on a Thursday so perhaps weekends are better. I did find myself wondering if the people on the Original Bus Tour were having a better time so next time I might try that option. I had read in a travel guide that they were virtually the same and made a decision based on price - at the time the Big Bus Tour was a little less expensive.

I was doing this Big Bus tour with my 5year old niece. I found it extremely refreshing as I have been to london so many times. This was so different and engaging. I would recommend this as a must activity if you are visiting London

This is a great way to get around London & see a lot in a short time. My husband & I had a 2 day pass. It also included walking tours & river cruise. We rode the full circle & then started the hop on, hop off to spend more time in specific areas. The blue line used ear buds for commentary & the red line had a guide. Both were good, just different. We went on the river cruise & one walking tour. I recommend them all.

The hop on / hop off bus tour offers a good value but the overall experience depends in large degree on the guide working at the time. One of the guides was very informative, funny, and friendly. He provided information as well as entertainment. A guide on another bus found it necessary to announce (in the absence of any such request) that "he spoke the Queen's English and would have to slow down for the Americans" as soon as we and some other folks walked up to second deck of the bus near the Trafalgar Square. It is rather surprising to find such an unfriendly person who chooses to work in the tourism industry.

Excellent way to see major sites in London. We rode the bus for the entire route to get oriented to the sites, then started our hop on-hop off option at the sites we wanted to visit. Take the red loop first with live commentator. Blue tours are recorded but are interesting too as different facts are always presented. Cheap transportation around London. Big Bus staff at most major bus stops....get up and on the early bus so you can sit up top - much better view and it's fun too!!!

the big bus tours in London were amazing. I went on these on the 14th march and 15th march 2014 -- Ali who was at the London Eye stop 14 was very very helpful an excellent employee telling me what stops to get off and how to get about London at night. The tours all moved very quickly... would use your tour company again

The bus driver forced us off the bus at 4:30 (when the tour is supposed to end at 5:30). We had to wait for another bus for half an hour. Take the Original Tour instead. Not only is it cheaper, it is run for 24 hours and basically makes the same stops as the Big Bus tour if not more. I repeat, do not choose this tour. You will just waste a lot of time on the pavement waiting for buses that never show up.

I'm a teacher came to London with 35 students last year.Walked into the Big Bus shop in the morning hopping to enquirer about the tour, there were loads of staffs in there on what looked like a meeting or something, when I started to talk this woman that I believe was a manager (she was the only one not wearing uniform) very rude and with no costumers service skills at all, literally kicked me out of the shop.Shame, you would think the managers should be an example to be fallowed.Well, just round the corner I found another company with better price and staff with proper manners offering the same tour.So next time I know where to go.

I met a fellow Australian in the lobby of the hotel I was staying in and we decided to do a bus tour on my first full day in London. She had been touring for weeks, so she was a bit more familiar in how to get tickets and where the bus went from. So, we spent a day together... and what a fantastic introduction to London I had. We spent most of the day on the actual bus because there is so much to get through, but that was not the least bit disappointing... It gave me a wonderful perspective of the city on my first visit.

Found Big Bus after web search and checking on Trip Advisor and glad we did. Excellent value two days for price of one in March. Best to buy ticket on website beforehand. Bus stopped right outside St Pancras (green route)so can use for journey to hotel, enabling us to see a lot of London sights on trip to our Kensington Hotel. We weren't in any hurry and after one change with short wait for blue route at Strand this took us a couple of hours. Bus was comfortable, clean and modern with very good commentary. Big Bus appear to have reps at each of the bus stops to sell tickets and offer advice /guidance. Didn't have time to sample river and walking tours but even so found the service very good value. Recommended if you want to pack a lot of the sites in a short stay.

The routes are great and especially the red route. The fact that they have a live English commentator makes the tour even more joyful.
You can also buy tkts for other attractions from the big bus people and skip the queues! Excellent.
The ONLY downside is the frequency of the buses. I don't know if it was just on the day we used it but on the said day you might have waited for the bus for more than 45 minutes and then 2 or even 3 buses appear one after the other!

This is a great way to see London, and as we have a young family we thought it would allow our five year old the best view of the sights. However, be warned that the buses get extremely busy and we found it difficult to get seats on the top deck which was really disappointing. Some buses came and went because they were already full so best to plan your hop off stops carefully! In addition, when our toddler started crying (and we desperately just wanted to get off..) the tour guide was not at all helpful. Again, slightly disappointing for something which is marketed as a family friendly hop on hop off service. However the river cruise was a breath of fresh air (literally!) and definitely worth doing. No queue and with 400 seats it was not over crowded, excellent commentary and for us, the highlight of the day.

Took my mother in law on this bus tour for her first time in London. Went on the blue line so that she could see all the main sights- didn't anticipate that it would take quite so long so we felt we got our money's worth. Was definitely worth buying tickets online in advance as it saved us a small fortune. We also used the bus on the second day and we didn't have to wait more than 5 minutes for a bus to turn up which we were pleased about. The staff were friendly and helpful, especially in suggesting how to get to certain places.
The thing I felt let this tour down was the recorded commentary which was very scarce and seemed to miss out a lot of the main attractions. At one point we found ourselves next to the Tower of London whilst the commentary was about the Olympic Games. I understand that due to traffic that the timings must be tricky but to miss major sites out altogether was baffling. The majority of the time was spent listening to classical music which was pleasant but not very informative.
It certainly served its purpose in order for my mother in law to see London, however for someone who has been many times before I would have liked to hear more history and stories. If I used this bus again I would certainly like to go on the red line with the live commentary as this seems to be worthwhile.
Overall a good experience but expected a bit more.

Yes, we enjoyed it! We were on the blue line (there are several options) starting at Bond Street. After a little over 3 hours (we did want to see lots and this route sure did that) we got off before the round-trip was finished. First a few problems - we were the first group (3 of us) to get on the bus - straight to the front row of the upper deck. Only problem - one of the plug-ins would not permit the plug to have the speaker cable to go into the housing (so not a good option), second problem another one would not permit any changing the channel and it was on no language, We made it work by sharing the cable - each person (yes someone sat with us and we shared with them) got to listen through 1 ear. The bus driver laughed it off (we did not). The trip went passed many sights - the information provided was quite interesting. Although I've been to London over a dozen times I always see and learn new things. Some of the upscale neighborhoods we once I'd not seen before. If you are looking for a good way to see the area - take this tour. One big option book on-line, it saves quite a bit over the walk-up price. One other if you take the red line there is a person presenting the information. Oh yes, just as with other companies you can get on and off as often as you like for the time set for your ticket.

I booked a fixed-date 48-hrs tour, which happened to be a stormy day in December in London. The buses did not arrive as frequently as advertised. As a result, the buses were quite full when they finally came. The stop where we first got on was not manned by a staff. Where stops were manned by staff, you'll find the staff polite and helpful. The quality of the audio recording was very good, if you can get a seat and listen. As it was a rainy day, most people were inside the bus. For most of the time we were onboard, we were standing up. On our first day, we hopped on and off twice only. On our second day, after waiting for the bus for 30 minutes, a fully-packed one came. Then we decided to give up on Big Bus. Overall, expectations were not met. If I'll ever do this again, I don't think I will book for a fix date. I'll just buy the tickets on a good day on the spot.

I would like to thank BIG STEVE who made our experience fantastic he provided great commentary

Thanks BIG STEVE and the Big Bus Tour

Damien and Lisa

Just got back from a weekend in London and this bus tour with river cruise was one of the highlights for my 11yr old daughter. £62 for 24hrs (family of 4) with extra day free was a bargain in my opinion. Ian the tour guide was spot on, full of interesting facts, very knowlegable & fun. Would recommend to anyone.

What a great decision it was to get the Big bus tour of London. The tickets for myself and my wife lasted for two days and we hopped off and on at any of their stops too see any of the sites .
All the drivers we came across we're brilliant and funny which made the tour good fun. You also get a pair of free ear phones which you plug into the seat in front of you where you can listen to a pre-recorded commentary which is very informative. The tour takes you to all the sights and attractions and is much cheaper than the underground as we found out. You can also get your tickets for the Tower of London at the main big bus stops at a good discount than at the actual ticket office at the tower.

We booked this company to show our grandchildren the site we wouldn't have time to see on our flying visit to London. As a Londoner born and bred I am very proud of our capital city and its history, unfortunately the guides we experienced on these bus tours were not. We travelled on three buses in total, the first had recorded commentary which was OK, but the other two had actual guides and they were bad! The first held the mike on his lips which made his speech difficult to understand and he seemed to be more interested in where passengers came from assuring them he had visited their town/city/country.The second seemed to be only interested in the sports car showrooms and the fact that the buses were only running for another hour and twenty minutes! He actually said that Marble Arch was place in its present location as the royal family wanted it moved, no mention at all of Tyburn or the gallows site it stands on. I found the whole experience very disappointing and not showing our Capital off as it should be. I think it is probably pot luck when you book these tickets but surely there should be a standard in training for guides.

Bought the 48 hour ticket when in London in September 2013. Bus stop was just near our hotel. Didn't expect actual helpful employees to be at the stop selling tickets prior to us boarding the bus. Is a great way to get an overview of London. We did the Blue Line to start with and it took us past so many sights ! Commentary was very good. Snippets of rousing British tunes in between - although being stuck in midday traffic means the tunes get repeated too much. (Never thought I'd be immune to 'Land of Hope and Glory' ! ) We were on the first trip of the day and it took 4 1/2 hours for the round trip. Probably too long - but we didn't have to stay on - we just chose too. The London traffic was truly horrendous for the last 1 1/2 hours of the trip.
Because we bought the 48 hour pass - we got a free river cruise. Used this to go to Tower Bridge stop. Boat was very crowded and not many of the seats had a decent view. You could only see one side of the river from a lot of the seats. Also it was very hot on board.
We did use the Big Bus again on the second day - it came in handy to get us back to the hotel when we were tired of walking. Loads of stops to get on or off at. Well worth the money.

My husband, daughter and myself have just visited London and we decided to book a 48 hour bus tour which conveniently left from outside our hotel in Russell square. Thanks to this bus tour we saw London properly for the first time and in 2 days we managed all the famous sights. There was a member of staff at every stop and they were all so helpful and very friendly. i really recommend this Bus company to all.

The buses are clean and new, the circuits are well studied, the staff is really nice, mostly the guides who were funny but still serious in their job...
London is worth a visit, and the Big Bus Tours makes it super easy and efficient. Just perfect.

So many people will scoff at people going on these big buses, but if you have never been to the city...take it. It provides a hop on hop off pass that will get you to ALL the big attractions across the city. The drivers are knowledgeable and trust me, there is so much to see.

I went on the Big Bus Tour and was disappointed. I did have a buy one day/ get the next day free offer. I mistakenly thought that this would be a good, relaxing first day in London activity....it was not at all. The first day it was rainy and quite cool. There were not enough seats under cover for everyone and rode on the upper deck and it was miserable. They did give us light weight rain ponchos but it still was very uncomfortable. We also had to get off the bus and switch several times. I was on the "blue" route with a taped tour and must have heard the same two background songs a hundred times! When I finally got a seat "under cover", I didn't want to get off because I was afraid that I would be stuck sitting out in the rain again. The second day was better but still a lot of waiting around. On the second day I went on the "red route" and there was a live tour guide. He was very personable, knowledgeable, and entertaining.
I had gone on a Big Bus tour about 20 years ago and it was wonderful. It is disappointing to see that the tours have gone downhill.

I went with a friend on the big bus tours yesterday (a monday), and we got 24 hour tickets. It was a reasonably good way to see many of the major monuments of the city in a day, but be prepared not to have time to stop at any of them. i think you could get off twice, maybe, to take pictures and look around, but if you want to go on the whole route, you could only maybe stop for an hour at two locations, and once for a quick lunch. A good way to familiarize yourself with the city, and then be able to take the tube the next day (most of the attractions are located near a tube station) and spend time at the attraction you really want to.

the audio guide was pretty good, but not a patch on the one live guide we had during the day. the discounts offered to each attration are minimal, but better than nothing.

if you're going to sit in the covered portion at the top of the bus, sit at the very very front, otherwise it will be hard to see the attractions except when the bus passes it and you can see it out the back. (you can also get some really good photos if you press up against the glass) if its a fine day, the uncovered portion is definitely much better.

cant fault the price, but the maps are a bit pointless-cant tell where the bus stops are, except very generally.

all staff were really friendly.

word of advice: BRING YOUR OWN HEADPHONES! the disposable ones they provide are sooo uncomfortable and wont sit properly in your ears. the headphone jack is the regular one, so any ipod headphone will do.

First time in London, so this was a great way to see a lot of London with all the big sights. The good thing about this tour is you get to jump of the bus when you like, then jump back on when you like as the buses come every 10 min. They have a red bus and a blue, one has person telling you all about London and it's sights as you drive around, the other has a recorded voice telling you. The ticket lasts for 48 hours so it is a must for people wanting to see London.

I travel extensively to London on business but never on pleasure. Taking the opportunity to take the wife to London we opted for a Big Bus Tour from London Bridge. The operator at the bus stop ( who we discovered was Italian) could not do enough for us. He gave us the maps and explained how the tours worked. We took the Blue bus tour and enjoyed the commentary passing all the sights and many of the sounds of the capital. We got off at the Victoria and Albert and went for a visit. It was so easy to then catch the next bus along and continue our journey. We travelled the whole trip, returning to London Bridge. It did seem expensive but when you consider that the tickets cover you for two days PLUS we had the option of a river trip all included it was good value. Next time I am on business and see the buses going past I will know what they are listening to!

We went to London in August 2011 and took Original Bus with no problems at all. We thought it would be good to try Big Bus this time. No reason but just to see how they are. Big mistake! Our hotel was near St Pancras station. We arrived at Pancras Rd to take the green line not knowing where to go. We saw a lady with the Big Bus shirt so we thought we can ask her where exactly should we wait for the bus. She was on the phone and speaking in Spanish. I tried not to disturb her so I just waited for her to finish. I made sure that she saw me. After 5 minutes, she was still on the phone and walked away from me even though I knew that she saw me. Another 5 minutes has passed and she was still on the phone. So I motioned to her that I wanted to ask her a question. She never let go of the phone, but instead, she handed me a map. I said I don't need a map as I have downloaded the Big Bus app. Nevertheless, we saw the bus arriving and it stopped close to where we were.

No problem for the rest of the day, until we took the red line bus at Marble Arch. After three buses for blue line came by, we knew where to stand to be the first in line when the red line bus would come we would be first in line. We stood there for about 25 minutes. When the bus came, a dispatcher came aboard the bus and shouted that this would be the last bus for the day. I tried to show our board receipt to get on the bus, but instead the dispatcher stopeed us with his right hand and asked us in a very condescending voice "Where do you think you're going?" and let other passengers board the bus first. I thought that was unfair, so I tried to get in the bus as well and asked him what did he mean by his question? He got angry and started shouting threatening us to throw us out of the bus! We just continued on to take our seats, but he was still shouting at us!.

Never again would I take the bus from this company. Avoid if necessary.

I should have stayed with Original Bus.

I have been to London about 7 times and have had a great time sightseeing but have never taken the bus around. With a shorth amount of time and a 7 and 11 year old with me this was a no-brainer. We got on at the London Eye and off we went. The headphones saved me fro trying to explain what we were seeing and the sights were plentiful. We were on for about two hours when the weather started to turn bad. Luckily we were at Harrods were we got off and had lunch at the Disney Cafe. We could have gotten back on a bus, but in a time crunch we took the Tube. I would certainly suggest if you don't have a week to try to see London do The Big Bus Tour. You will be happy and get great photos while not getting your feet tired!

We had three guides on our tour around town today, each with a completely different style, but all fuelled with a knowledge of the town combined with an enthusiasm for sharing this with us. Hearing about the districts we passed through, the people who had lived or worked here in the past, the buildings, monuments and parks was a great way to get a feel for the cities of London and Westminster.

I heard lots of things which I'd learned at school many years ago but much more that I'd no knowledge of before, so this was a really enjoyable way to take on board some of the history of the place. The hop on/hop off deal over 48 hours represents great value for money and a full circuit of each route followed by a drop off would, I reckon, be the ideal way to make the most of this facility.

We thought it would be a good idea to check out London before deciding where to go and bought a Big Bus ticket at Euston Station. It was valid for 48 hours and included a river cruise and discounted admission to various attractions. It was well worth the money and gave us a great overview of the city!

Don't know London at all and wanted to see the City from street level and not the underground. Public bus service would have been complicated so it was much easier to hop-on and off these buses and see famous landmarks. Bought tickets on-line and they were valid for 48 hours, took green and red line bus on day 1 and blue line bus on day 2. Couldn't have been easier and great value for money. All staff very helpful.

Last week we had a short 3 day stay in London and thoroughly enjoyed the Big Bus Tours! We purchased tickets online prior to going to save time and it gave us a great overview of the city. We were able to hop on and off as we chose for the course of 2 consecutive days. I would highly recommend planning on doing the Royal walking tour which is included and gives wonderful vantage points to viewing the Changing of the Guards at Buckingham Palace as well as a wealth of valuable information. We found both the Red and Blue lines to be great although with the audio earphones on the blue line the information was often more understandable so don't discard the option to go on the Big Bus Blue Line also! Absolutely make time to relax and enjoy the Thames River Cruise also included in the ticket price.

We purchased our tickets in advance online before the trip and found the available information on the website to be slightly misleading as far as the start time of the tour. We only had a few hours to spare as we were on a layover at Gatwick airport. We arrived at 8am for when the website stated the tours started from Victoria Station. We were told different stories by different employees on where we needed to go to catch the bus. Finally an employee walked us down to a stop and told us that the bus would be here at 8:30, but the tour would take 3.5 hours, which we were originally informed would take 2.5. We didn't have an extra hour to spare, so we were very nervous that we had just gotten ourselves into a tight timeline. When we boarded the bus at 8:30 we were instructed to hop on the red line (we were on the blue) at the 4th stop, this way we would have enough time, as the red line only takes 2.5 hours for the entire route.

Everything worked out fine - the tour was the perfect amount of time and gave us the opportunity to see all the sights during our layover.

This is a must tour when in London. Our tour guide was Nick. His knowledge of London was incredible. Taking this tour opens your mind to how historical London really is. You can hop on and off of the bus. Also, your ticket is good for 24 hours from the point that you first use it. Also, your ticket gets you discounts to other popular attractions such as The London Eye. Forget the rest, this tour is the best. Make sure you use the live guided tour buses, not the recorded tour. Guides like Nick make this tour great.

I've been to London many times, and was there again this month to show my parents around. Tried the bus tour and learned so much more about the city. Sit upstairs for a better view and get on as many different places as possible. Do not under estimate how long you will spend at each stop and allow bus wait times as traffic downtown can be unpredictable. Also take advantage of the river cruise which is included in the ticket price, and the fast track discounts they offer to the other landmarks - it beats waiting in long ques!

We had three nights in London and used the Big Bus for two days. This was money well spent. One line had live narration and one audio. We also were able to take a short river cruise and a wonderful Beatles tour with a great enthusiastic guide. The hop on hop off feature was great. This is a great way to see London on a first visit.
Jerry The K in Ct. U.S.A.

Myself, my boyfriend, and two of our friends took this tour September 1 and 2 2013. We thought that this was a great introduction to London, as well as a good (but VERY SLOW - London traffic is bad. If you need to get somewhere - take the underground) form of transportation for us. Our only complaint was that the recorded commentary which is available on the blue line buses is horrible. It doesn't really match up with what you're seeing and it just plays music most of the time. The red line, however, which provides live English commentary, was WONDERFUL! Those buses seem to not come around quite as often as the blue lines, so we found ourselves waiting for a while at times, but it was worth it. Every tour guide was different and had their own personalities, but they were all great and really made the tour enjoyable and informative. We bought our tickets online ahead of time and saved a few pounds. Also, the staff on the bus sells tickets to the major attractions, oftentimes at a discount and makes it where you can skip the line. I recommend doing this during peak travel seasons and for the popular attractions (for example, we did this for the London Eye and saved waiting in the ticket purchase queue). Overall, we had a great experience with the Big Bus Tour in London!

My partner signed us up for the Big Bus Tour...I'm not sure why he did. The service can get you around town. And they do provide a recording about some of the places you pass with the provided headsets. But it's not worth it. It's not even worth using it as a means to get around town. Instead buy an Oyster Card (research it...it's worthwhile!). You never know when the bus is going to be coming by. Their map is hard to decipher as to which way the buses travel their routes. The staff is less than accommodating nor are they friendly (unlike everyone else we seemed to meet). In fact, one employee was on a personal cell phone call at their bus stop; he couldn't be bothered to answer questions. So I say don't bother with them at all.

We went to Tower Bridge to sign up for a tour bus - thinking we could learn a bit about our capital city.
We were given a leaflet by one of the Big Bus company sales reps at Tower of London. We then started speaking to the rep from another company to compare prices etc.
the big bus rep stormed up to us and grabbed the leaflet out of our hands and started shouting!
I have never been spoken to like that - especially as we hadn't decided which company to go with! The sales rep have done the company out of ticket sales! Other people who were also about to buy tickets also chose to go with another company.
Absolutely appalling behaviour!!
I emailed the company too and sent them a photo of their employee.. But no reply!!

We hopped on the Big Bus red line, as according to Rick Steeves those were the busses with live tour guides. We weren't disappointed - Nuri was our guide and she was wonderful! She helped with an upgrade issue we had, and continued providing stories (I quite enjoyed the Thomas Hardy story!). We highly recommend the trip - it was great! So here's to you Nuri - with love, Seattle!

Many thanks to the Big Bus Tours, and especially the wonderful tourguide Chris, and the driver (who I cannot fathom maneuvers that bus around those tiny streets) Patrick.

Not only Chris and Patrick of course, but all of the staff, from the guys selling tickets on the street, to the tour guides and drivers, each were very interesting and accommodating. They were most helpful in pointing out how to get on and off to see various different attractions. I got the 48 hour pass and never had any trouble getting where I needed to go.

The live commentary busses are most recommended. However, if you find yourself on one without, just whip out your headphones, and plug it into the jack in front of each seat. You will hear a recorded commentary that is also very interesting. I admit, I can't quite figure out how the commentary knows exactly where the bus is at that moment. There must be some sort of sensor that triggers the audio commentary pertinent to that particular section of town or monument.

Big Bus Tours is highly recommended.

Recommended to do the big bus company tour in order to get our bearings for London however, we were really disappointed when the bus we caught stopped at Paddington for 30 minutes and then again at for over 30 minutes Baker Street. It was at this point we got off and caught the Tube to see our sights and ditched the Big Bus Tour.
The only positives from our experience with the Big Bus Tours was the map and the pre-purchasing of attraction tickets to avoid waiting in lines at St Paul's Cathedral and the Tower of London. Overall it was a waste of our valuable time and money when we wanted to maximise the number of sites we saw each day.
For all future London tourists, use the Underground! It is fast and reliable and it is much more enjoyable to walk from site to site... get a Big Bus Tour map though.

Having lived in London since 1988 you often think - I really should visit the city I live in. We (wife + 2 kids aged 12/15) spend 1,000's flying the globe going to far flung places....and yet on our doorstep.

The temptation is to say "yeah yeah we should really go visit...." and you don't.

With that in mind one Sunday with no plans and the weather fine we thought "lets do a bus tour". Of course we were the only locals on it. But it was brilliant. We had a couple of great tour guides who told us loads about "our" city we didn't know. Did we see anything we hadn't seen before? No but that didn't matter because we learnt the stories behind the buildings.

Good value for money as there are three main routes, a river ride and discounts on various attractions. The hop on and off works well as you can stop for lunch (or whatever) when you're ready. You never wait long for the next one when you are ready to continue.

So if you are visiting London "just do it", if you live in London "just do it!".

This was a great way to see all the sites of London plus catch some interesting commentary from the knowledgeable tour guides. We had a nice young man by the name of Nick - my kids loved him since he told us many interesting things about the City while keeping it light and funny. It is no small achievement to keep the attention of a 15, 13 and 9 year old during a 2.5 hour bus tour but he did. My kids still talk about him to this day and can recall many of the things they learned 3 months later! Some people think these bus tours are a bit cheesy and perhaps they are...but we liked them just fine.

My grandson and I enjoyed a wonderful day in London yesterday thanks to the Big Bus Tour.

The Friday before the August Bank Holiday weekend --- ( am I really crazy ? .......... no just couldn't do any other date .... )

But despite the crowds and the traffic because we used the "Big Bus" we managed really well.

We came into London via Waterloo Station and caught the bus at the London Eye stop. Very easy to find from the station and 5 - 10 minute walk. ( 5 mins him / little longer for me )

We were hoping that on such a busy day we would still get seats on the top deck ( a must if you are going to get the most from the tour ) ---- and we did on every bus !

As we rounded the corner and crossed over Waterloo Bridge my grandson ( 13 yrs ) said "Wow I didn't think it was going to be like this ! "
