Waterloo Bridge is magnificent any time you cross it - I love it every time, but there was something really magical on that bright sunny morning with London stretched out in front of us. Westminster ... the Houses of Parliament and Big Ben on one side and St Pauls on the other - and everything in between .......... we were hooked ....... so we ended up doing the whole tour !!!!!

We went eastward seeing Fleet St, St Pauls, London Bridge, The Shard, Tower Bridge and the Tower of London along the way ..... then back to Westminster.

Did my grandson want to get off ( we could have done, lots of hop on / hop off opportunities ) - no he was enjoying it all far too much .........

So over the River again into Lambeth and across back again round to Westminster.

We were covering so much ground so easily --- I can't imagine being able to do it as well any other way ......

I managed to persuade him to leave the bus at Buckingham Palace and Harrods. I was happily surprised when each time we returned to the bus stop we waited just a few minutes for another bus to arrive to continue our journey.

So in the end we did the whole route and saw "everything" .... including going to the Tower for a second time and taking the boat trip back along the River Thames to Westminster Pier all included in the price.

What a day !

I had hurt my back and foot the week before - so very happy that walking was minimal ( although still managed some ..... ) and that most of the day was sitting down.
Even got a seat on the train home !!!

I really recommend seeing London this way.

Great value. My husband and I purchased a two day pass at a cost of 36 pounds. And we hopped on and off the bus for the whole two days. We visited the London eye, Big Ben, Westminster Abby, Buckingham palace, the national art gallery, St. Paul's cathedral, crossed london bridge, visited Hyde Park, visited Harrods department store, did a cruise down the river Thames just to name a few. Buses are very regular, so you don,t have to wait to long. You are supplied with headphones for the buses which are interactive this way, yet you have the option of waiting for a bus with live commentary. We had Andy initially give us our first live commentary on our first bus ride. He knew his job well and kept us entertained. On our last trip, we had the privelage of being on a bus with Richard giving the live commentary. We needed to get off at St Paul's. But really, I could have listened to him all day. Thanks Richard.

My 13 year old daughter and I took the Eurostar over from Paris to London for the day -- (2 hours/20 min) so the Big Bus Tour was just the thing as we only had about 6 hours in London -- we always got on the top of the bus as it was a beautiful day -- takes in all the major sights and saves on walking!

Lived in London 30 years ago WC1 never rode on a tour bus...
Brilliant way to see London.. Great way to see the Capital.... Bus driver great man... took us back to park lane hotel in the tour bus...

Used a 24 hour ticket to see every part of London. Buses were extremely efficient and very frequent. After 10am we never waited more than 2 minutes for a bus and we achieved our purpose of seeing all the major sights. We did get on and off and had 3 different guides. Jeff was our 1st guide and he was really helpful and patiently answered lots of questions as well as giving us entertaining information. Our 2nd guide was very grumpy and unhelpful and never learnt his name and our 3rd guide was also great. Would definitely recommend Big Bus tours and use them again. We also did the river cruise. We saw other tour buses and the Big Buses were definitely the most frequent.

We did a two day pass while in London with our 19 and 21 year olds and it was worth the money. We saw all the major attractions, got all the facts and were able to get around the city to where we wanted without having to walk the whole time. Very nice ride and the guides are very knowledgeable. Just be aware that if you are on a time schedule to get somewhere you might not make it. The bus takes the roundabout way and stops several times. You have to be flexible.

The pass included the river tour which we did take advantage of and the ghostly walk in the evening. Jessie was an awesome host for that tour. We saw some sights that we never would have found on our own and his enthusiasm was both entertaining and refreshing. We did a similar tour in Paris, not a Big Bus Tour and it was ok, but not quite the same level as London. I would recommend it for first time visitors to the city.

The tour was great and it was extremely convenient using the bus to see London. We even used it when we needed to go to a boat tour, instead of paying for a train ticket. Our only issue was that there was a time or two when we had to wait awhile for a bus and when one came, there were 2. Also, a tip, when you get to London, our hotel gave us a map of London and in it, there was a discount for the Big Bus Tour, but we had already paid.

As we had walked many miles around London, we decided to take a break and hop on a tour bus. It was £30 each, quite expensive, I thought, but then I was in London! The tour took just over 2 hours and my husband and I certainly enjoyed it, it did help that the sun was shining as we sat upstairs. Our driver was called Winston and the guy on the loud speaker was called Dave. They were a super team and Dave was very knowledgeable and it was obvious he certainly enjoyed his job, along with being very polite and helpful to everyone, he certainly made the whole tour very enjoyable. Later in the day we decided to hop on again, this time we had a different person describing the sites. What a let down, he wasn't in the least interesting, more into trying to be funny and talking about himself, apart from the fact that we couldn't tell half of what he was saying. I do think the big bus tour is a must, but keep your fingers crossed you get a good team on board.

I liked the big bus hop on hop off tour. We arrived in London in the morning, checked into our hotel and hopped on one of these buses. It is nice you can start the tour from any stop. The first bus we were on it was a little hard to hear sitting in the back. For others we sat closer to the guide and it was much more enjoyable. Overall the guides were interesting. We saw a lot more big buses than original buses. The river cruise was great. We paid for 48 hours, but only used a days worth. Maybe if you did a walking tour 48 hours might be good, but only one day is needed for the bus/river. Overall we thought it was money well spent.

We had a fantastic experience on the Big Bus Tour on Monday. The tour was great value, we saw so much but the major highlight was our fabulous guide "Big Steve". His knowledge was extensive but it was his humour that really made it for us. This was the first time my parents had been to London and it is fair to say he really made their trip. We would highly recommend this to everyone!

My boyfriend and I have taken to the tour buses whenever we go to a big city now. As we had limited time in the city, this was perfect for getting around and seeing the sights with many hop on/hop off points. We paid £30 each and this included river cruises and walking tours. The hours the buses and boats ran were later than was advertised and the ticket was valid for the next day also so much better value than when I first looked into this. We went on the red tour which has the 'live' tour guide rather then the audio. We got on near the Southbank Lion and got off at Green Park where we sat and had lunch in the park next to the Ritz. Our tour guide changed here and I must say that both of them were very good, each with their own little stories so you know that they are not just following the script. We did the whole of the red tour and then stayed on until the Tower of London where we got on the River Cruise. There was a beautiful rainbow at the side of Tower Bridge and it was beautiful. Overall a really good tour and would recommend it.

My husbands choice while in London was this bus tour, we were fortunate it was a pleasant day so were able to sit on the open top deck. We did most of what we wanted but our bus suddenly detoured - we were told due to heavy traffic - we then had to switch buses for the blue line to get to Madame Tussaud's - traffic was bad and we didn't get there until 3 pm and with a huge queue outside we decided to give it a miss then hopped onto the next bus and the kids had a great time in Hamleys instead! It was a week day so crowded but we still managed to get lots in! A bit pricey but good commentary!

We opted for the big bus this time because we never had the chance in the past due to the weather. This time the sun was shinning bright and after about 40 minutes into the tour, we moved to a shady spot. We really enjoyed the tour guide.

The busses were nice. You were able to get on and get off whenever you like. Often times they would have a live tour guide which was nice. With the bus ticket you also got access to a few walking tours and a river tour. We did the river tour which was fun but our favorite was the walking tours with Kevin Russell. First we did the ghosts by gaslight tour. Kevin made the tour incredible. He was very knowledgeable, energetic and funny. Near the end of the tour we stopped at a pub. Talking to him over a couple beers made it an even better experience. The next day we wanted to do the Harry Potter tour. As expected it was a rather large group. We got grouped with the other tour guide that day and even though I am sure he is also great, we left with Kevin's group instead. At the end of the tour we had our picture taken with Kevin at one of the locations in one of the movies. I just wish we would have done this at the beginning of our stay in London instead of near the end. Other than that it was great.

Booked the trip online and no problems exchanging booking voucher for tickets. Staff all very jolly, friendly and helpful. Buses got busier as the day progressed, but expected that really. Went with our granddaughter this time and did lots of hopping on and off, but would like to go again on our own and see everything. Lived in London for some years, but learnt lots of new things. A great experience and one that I would highly recommend.

I went to London on the 29th of July 2013. It was brilliant the kids really enjoyed it and we did the blue and red routes and the river bus was included. We had to get stuff done in London so we hopped on and off buses as needed and there was excellent commentary from 3 different guides who were amusing and full of really interesting fact. My girls 9 and 15 sat listening and looking at the sites fully occupied it was crazy I am used to all the bickering and the service made moving round London easy. I heartily recommend the service.

Having been to London many times a friend recommended I try the bus tour.
1st thing I recommend to you is try to get one with a guide on board - they all have recorded commentary, but the live guide added so much - she was very friendly, seriously knowledgeable, funny & welcoming.
you an get on & off as many times as you like, to get photos or spend more time at a certain attraction and then just jump on the next bus.
if you're a 1st time visitor this is an absolute must - it's the best way to see London, even if you just stop on the bus & do the whole tour (about 2hr 40 mins) then jump on another one - 3 in total.
The cost is relatively low (£39.00) for my daughter and myself on a one day ticket, get there early and make the most of it or get a 2 day ticket and plan where you want to get off.

A good selection for touring in the bus for knowing London sight seeing locations and free river cruises by them for the tourists. We have selected a two day validity Big bus tours at a very nominal rate by internet so that we can cover most of the places during the two days. The red bus is for English speaking and other buses are for other languages tourist of 5 other languages viz.spain,french,german,chinese,urdu . An ear phone and a rain cover is given free for the tourists. Occasional Rain will not affect the touring passengers. The buses are plenty and is available in 10 minutes to a maximum of 20 minutes.in any hop stop. Clear and Jovial explanations by the guide is marvelous. The bus goes through all important locations viz., Greenpark station ,Marble Arch ,Oxford Street, to London eye,Tower Bridge .London Bridge, Palace and too many attractions.

Despite visiting London weekly for business, it has been years since I have done "the tourist thing". My fiancee and I had some ideas of where we might visit, so after a stroll through Hyde Park from our Hotel I suggested we try it - having done similar in New York earlier in the year.

We decided to take the 48-hour pass for an extra £6 (therefore £36 each), which gave us a choice of any of the tours and also a river boat ride. The red tour is/was best, as it has a guide who talks you through the sights as you pass.

Despite having walked passed many of the sights over the years, to be able to sit back and get a little more detail - with a much better view - was excellent. As with many of these guides, you can hop on and off throughout the duration of the ticket - making it the only way to see the city. Simple maths; a day pass on the tube = £7.50, 2 days = £15 and you see nothing. Therefore £36 to see the sights is a bargain!

Whether you're from the UK like us - or from overseas, I highly recommend this. Even for a regular (albeit business) London visitor like me, there was plenty to learn.

We just loved our Big Bus Tour, we had warm and sunny weather and it is so nice to have the flexibility of getting on and off of the open air bus at various tourist sites as needed. We bought a 48 hour pass and used it both days and also used the Riverboat up the River Thames to Greenwich which was included in that price. Our guides were lively and interesting. It took us to the places we needed to go. We ran into problems a few times with very crowded buses, we were not always able to get up top, but in time, space usually opened up. We did get left at Oxford Circus one night during rush hour. It was the only time the bus did not show up as scheduled. We waited 45-60 minutes. As we gave up and as we walked away, one finally pulled up, it was full and we could not get on. We had to find an alternative route back to our hotel. Subways were backed up all of the way onto the street. The buses do not run all night.

This is an excellent way to see a big city like London. The ticket is good for 24 hours, and stops a re very convenient. They red bus has a live tour guide, but the recording in the blue line is also great. This is a great way to see all the highlights. Some bus are stroller/wheelchair accesible.

We took the Big Bus tour to help us orient ourselves to London. We couldn't have been happier with the tour and the Service. The materials were clear, the audio augmented the tour well. We also took the free river tour, as well as the Beatles Walking Tour ( a very knowledgeable guide who lived through Beatles London in the 60's.)
We used the hop on hop off quite a bit, getting off at Speakers Corner, Picadilly Square, Westminster and Parliament, and others.
We would definitely take this tour again.

Big Bus Tours Red Tour has live commentary in English. We had a great driver/guide duo: Mike and Nick. They took us around the city, explained the required diversions from the mapped route thoroughly and kept us very entertained! And hey BBC, check it out: my entire party votes that Nick should be the next Doctor!

We bought the 48 hour tickets and used them the first two days we were in London. It was a great way to understand the layout of the city, since it is so spread out. We started with the red route, where we stayed on for about 2 hours initially and listened to our live tour guide. I wish I could remember our first tour guide's name, because she was fantastic. She was not only knowledgeable but funny and seemed to truly love London. She also gave tips on the way on her favorite places to visit, and plays to see. Other guides we had were good too, but not quite the same as the first one we had. The second day we tried to use the bus more as our method of transportation, but in retrospect I think it would have been easier and less time consuming to just take the tube, which ended up being much more simple than the public transportation systems that we're used to. If I were to do it again, I would have booked the 24 hour ticket, and used it for just the first day.

We also did one of the walking tours offered by Big Bus, that was included in our ticket, and that we were allowed to do any day the week of our bus tour. We chose to do the Beatles Walking tour, which started at Trafalgar Square and took us to areas that the Beatles had played at or recorded. The tour guide, Ian was very informative and passionate about music. He had a lot of neat stories to tell us both about the Beatles and other music of the time. It was overall very interesting, though I probably would not have done it if it were not included with the price of the ticket. I would recommend this walking tour if you are a fan of the fab four.

My friend and i went on the Big Bus Tour on Saturday 6th July 2013, as my friend had never been to London before.....the people outside Victoria Station were very friendly and helpful and sent us to the correct bus stop....there was a bit of a wait and gettin on was a bit of a scrum but we managed eventually. The Tour and the guided commentary were brilliant...it took in all the place it should and all the places you want to see in London, the only thing I think they are missing is selling drinks on the buses at the various stops....it was VERY hot on the day we went and we ended up getting off, not because we wanted to but because we were parched....We even went on the River Cruise which again was brilliant, the tour on that one was hilarious and even spotted where we lived from our accents (weird!!). Would recommend this to anyone who wants a general sightseeing tour....loved it

I have been on this tour twice in 6 months and would do it again and again. The trick is - get the LIVE tour guide.
I start at Trafalgar Square and wait for the live tour guide; hop on and don't get off until we are back at square one. I then hop off, grab a coffee from Costa and grab the next bus to get to where ever in the city I am thinking of visiting - it is a relaxing way to travel London.

On our recent trip I had prebooked, online tix for the Big Bus Tour for 48 hours. They give a discount if you do it online and in advance. The bus tour was a great way to see everything and get a lay out of the city. There are 3 routes. Two are 2 1/2 hour routes if you sit from beginning to end and complete the circle. Unfortunately, our first time on the bus there was a water main break and Regent Street and Piccadilly were blocked and the traffic was stopped. We were on a recorded tour. It took us about 4 hours to do the round trip. Someone should've told us to get off and walk to pick up another bus that was not stuck in this traffic. My complaint is not that the route was changed, because that is understandable, but I had thought that this was the usual traffic.

Other than that inconvenience, I found the tour to be a great way to see everything and the live commentary was very interesting and friendly. The tour has a River Thames Cruise included and when you buy the 48 hour ticket, the cruise can be extended to Greenwich, which was lovely.

There is another bus company that was doing the same thing but for a little cheaper. They did not have a 48 hour option online, but they told me that they would've upgraded my prepaid 24 hour ticket. I do not know if they were same, better or worse, I just know that they were cheaper with, what looked like the same route.

First, a caveat: it is packed in London right now. Traffic and tourists are everywhere. So, when we got on the bus at Oxford and Regent, we expected it to be a slow ride, but it took forever to make it just a short ride to Trafalger. We Bought our tickets online in advance. We had a text message sent to my cell phone so that I had an electronic ticket. When we met the bus, we asked them if this was sufficient, and they required us to get a paper ticket so we could ride on and off and do the water tour. They asked us to go to the next stop and get the attendant to print a paper ticket for us there. At the next stop the attendant told us that he could not put a paper ticket either, but a ride to the next stop. When we started going further to Trafalger we were going to stop and get tickets there, but the bus hit a pole and we decided enough was enough. There was an audio guide on the bus system accessible through earphones. However, it was extremely basic about Lindon. We had no live guide on our bus and probably should have gortten off the. Without that guide, the tour is terrible! Much easier to see most sites on foot with a guide book! We ultimately decided, to walk the rest of the day and really experience the culture and sights of the city! In my opinion, unless you are not a good traveler and need to totally rely on someone else, get a do it yourself guide and skip the Big Bus!

We got here in the morning and got off at the Tower Of London. The tour guide was very nice and gave a lot of information about where everything was, and the history. He answered all the questions everyone had and I never would have guessed some of the answers. Such as Buckingham Palace has 78 bathrooms, and the red capsule on The London Eye was to track how many times it goes around. There were some really good picture taking opportunities on the bus too, and I got some really good pictures. The busses almost run nonstop so it is really hard to miss them. It's like one leaves, then another one comes 1 to 2 minutes later. It is fun for basically all ages.

We spent the whole day, hop on, hop off on the Big Bus Tours, we had a whirlwind tour of London, on the red, blue and green routes, and the guide that we had on the red route, Christine, fantastic, friendly, knowledge aplenty, our teen Dutch guest where very impressed, and us too, also good value for money.

This was a great value and we enjoyed the commentary, learned a lot, plenty of busses so the wait was never long when hopping on and off. The drivers were all helpful and courteous! Pleasantly surprised. Especially loved the walking tour and guide Phil, seeing the Changing of the guard.

A great preview of the city & to get a lay of the land. We loved the frequency of pick-ups, the informative talks, the convenient stops, and comfortable buses.

Definitely go to the open top. A great view of the city! I would do a 2 day pass because London is that big that you would do a full blue bus round (2-3hrs) followed by hopping off & on as you wish. If it rains, they have free ponchos.

We loved hopping off at the Tower of London stop & taking the river cruise to Westminster Station stop. The River Cruise was very good.

Definitely worth doing!

We got on the buses at one of the "green link" sights; the bus was packed, and we should have known it was a bad sign. Got off and onto the red line, and, for awhile, things went well, and we enjoyed seeing the Tower of London, St. Paul's, and Buckingham Palace.

We were told we had to get off the bus and get on to another one, as traffic was halted on Regent street due to a water main break and we needed to be diverted. The "diversion" meant backtracking onto the route we had already travelled, not once, but twice, and listening to the same old commentary. Elizabeth was almost impossible to understand; I don't know if it was her sound system or her Scottish accent, but it was most unpleasant.

We alighted to have lunch, and decided to head back for the hotel for a break. We got on a green link bus. Again, about halfway through, we were told we had to get off and change buses, though this time we had to wait. We were also told that we would not be able to access a large part of the tour because of the water main break. However, no compensation was offered for this.

After a break at the hotel, we decided to give the Big Bus one last chance. We got on at the green link and we were dropped off at a stop, where we waited over 20 minutes for a bus. "Original Tour" buses drove by every 2-3 minutes during this interval. When the bus finally arrived, I said to the driver "we have been waiting over 20 minutes" and he replied, "the buses only come every 20 minutes". I said, "That's funny, you advertise every 5 to 15", to which he replied "you caught me. yes, that's right. we are supposed to come every 5 to 15."

We have taken these tours in many large, heavily trafficked cities and have never had such an experience. Being forced to get on and off of buses, long wait times, and having a good chunk of the tour be inaccessible without being refunded a part of the fee was just not professional, courteous, or what was promised when we paid what we paid to ride. STAY AWAY.

We went on the big bus tour as we thought it was probably the best way to see all the sights as we only had a day to fit as much in as possible.
They have two buses - red for live guide and blue for audio in several different languages. We went on the red tour and went the whole way round. Guide was informative and interesting. We also hopped on a blue bus as this covers some of the bits the red one doesnt.
Person who sold tickets said they guaranteed a bus at any stop within 10-15 minutes. In the most part this was the case, however we did have one time where we were waiting for quite a bit longer.
You get a river cruise included in price of ticket, although queue was huge even fairly early in the morning so we didn't manage to take advantage of it. They also give you discounts on some attractions and a book full of coupons to reduce the price of some things. In all I would recommend.

This was our first trip to London and they are everywhere, their tour gave a great overview of the general tourist destinations but we found that for the price it was too expensive.,
, the wait for b uses was long, the other bus companies had more coaches running, At ties the buses were so full that you either couldn't see anything or there were no seats. Back to the basic rule if you do anything in Europe Do IT EARLY. In the end my husband and I found it easier, cheaper and more relaxing to buy an oyster card and a London map and take the subway in our own time and visit sites as the mood took us

Had a rather soggy first morning on the bus tour, cheered up hugely by our fantastic guide Leanne. Went with the recommended 48 hour tickets, which were well worth the extra money!! Did the Thames river cruise both to Greenwich and Westminster (and the London Eye!, perfect for our Pre-booked excursion!) both boats had lovely crew members and I would strongly recommend as a fairly quick way of getting about a bit! We then had a fabulous sunny afternoon, the following day on the bus tour. We hopped on and off at various points and always met very helpful staff, drivers and tour guides, I would highly recommend this as a fantastic way to see the city and it's sights :-)

We purchased a day pass for big bus on June 29th 2013. This coincided with gay pride events so almost a third of the stops were skipped with no price consideration. It still costs 30 pounds a piece to sit for an hour and a half in traffic re routes. When we finally reached a hop off spot the next buses took about twenty minutes and were packed full. It was very difficult to get a seat up top and the views were terrible from the lower level. The guides were boring and flustered except for one who was very good but also very vocal about his expectations for getting tips. We didn't mind this as he had earned it. The river trip was quick but fun however it was jam packed and we had to leave the pier for an hour before we could come back and actually board the vessel. Also guidebooks say this route will take about an hour or two but it took about four without hopping off. With traffic and poor views, you are really much better off plotting your stops on the tube to get around. It is much quicker and much cheaper.

We came on the big bus tours on the 28th June. The weather wasn't great at the beginning of the day, so we were reluctant to go on a FULLY open top bus!! Our tour guide was a young lady called LeAnn, who encouraged us to come sit up the top when we felt ready as we would see more and gave us a free poncho (which she was wearing herself!) LeAnn was absolutely fantastic, she was telling us funny jokes and interesting facts about the city. It was clear that she loved her job and it was so nice to see that the weather clearly hadn't dampened her spirits, at one point she even had us singing along with her!
This was mine and my husbands first trip to London and even though it wasn't what we would call summer (we live in California!) it was one of the best trips we've done. It is a beautiful city, mixed with old and new things to see. Our trip on the big bus made our trip and we will recommend it to everyone! LeAnn it was an absolute pleasure meeting you, thank you for everything maybe see you in California ;)

Kelly and Chris

We have used the hop off hop on bus tours in lots of countries but in London potentially there is too much traffic!! We were on the bus for two hours before getting to a sight after we got on at Knightsbridge. We actually got off and walked ourselves (I must say thanks to their map). We did take advantage of the free Thames cruise and that was great the guide on that tour was fabulous we really enjoyed. We felt overall for the price we paid £30 the map and the tube would be a much better option.

The tour route takes you everywhere in London you could want to go. Use the Red bus as the live commentary is excellent. The boat trip is fantastic and the commentary from the staff is funny and informative. Best value is the 48 hour ticket booked online as this includes longer boat trip all the way to Greenwich

The Big Bus was a great way to get around London. However, it was cold and rainy and to sit outside in the elements atop the bus was challenging. If you want to take lots of photographs though this is better than the buss that is enclosed. It is harder to take pictures through the windows. The red line has a guide telling you about some of the buildings and sights you pass. They were just ok. The blue line has a recorded commentary and you use headphones to listen to that. Overall, it was good. The buses run fairly often, but one particular location we had to wait 15 minutes for a bus. While the other buses came and went.

I thought that these tours were so cheesy. I ended up having a day to myself and London and decided to hop on one of these. It was the best decision I made. I love that they are so informative, the tour guides are friendly and give you little tips on what to do. After taking this tour I started to take them in other cities that I would visit, but none have yet to compare to the one in London.
Bus was untidy, sales people were pushy which we observed on a couple of occasions. Buses are not as often at stop points as other hop on/off buses.

Convienent hop on and hop off if you have the time. I was travelling with friends that have never been to London, and this was a good way for them to see everything. Upper level of the bus is worth the seat assuming the weather cooperates. The good thing about this tour, is that their are many stops and its a continuous 24 hour ticket. Recommend the live guided tour versus the plug in ear buds. River cruise on the Thames was also included, but chose not to part take in it.

I reluctantly bought a ticket for this bus ride thinking it wouldn't really be worth it. For the value I thought it was a great buy after taking the bus for 2 days (I bought a 24 hour pass) and then took the included river cruise. It was a great way to get accustomed to the city and has great picture opportunities. I thoroughly enjoyed the river cruise and could just do that all day. You can buy the tickets online at their website for a discount and I would recommend that. I was in town for a conference and wanted to learn more about London. It stops at a lot of places to explore then you can hop right back on.

After walking around central London, my 86 yr old mom asked if we could do a bus tour for her to see more. I quickly agreed and spent one evening researching 3 companies. I chose this one, based on reviews and area covered. We were on a red bus, with a friendly, funny, English speaking guide. He seemed to read from a script and did not point out anything that wasn't on their map. We went by the BBC, while the Queen was standing out front! St Martin in the Fields, several embassies,etc went by unnoticed by our guide. When we reached Trafalgar Square, someone asked our guide if there was a reason the statue of Admiral Nelson was facing the way he was. The guide had no clue. My friend had just told me the day before he is facing toward the sight of the Battle of Trafalgar! Must have been an important battle for there to be a square and statue in his honor. Now, I understand these are highlights only, however, a great guide would fill the empty time of driving with chatter and stories about the area. London is full of history and I feel we should have been filled in on more of it. This tour was definitely not worth the money I spent on it.

For anyone who wants a day out and around London this is something really fun and relatively cheap to do. My friend and I went on the other day and I have to say apart from it being really fascinating and a great way to look at the amazing city, the tour guide who I believe was called Nuri (?) was absolutely brilliant. She was incredible with knowledge of London but her out going and dynamic personality made the trip that much more brilliant. The driver also contributed in at times. This tour would appeal to all people of all ages. The option to hop on and off is appealing too. Definitely worth doing if you want to see London.

We really enjoyed this hop on hop off tour. There is a blue and red line. Blue line has headphones and the ability to listen to the tour in about 8 different languages. The red tour is a live guide English only. We were on the blue line most of the time and found the day to be very informative. The only down side would be that the buses finished about 6pm when it's not dark until after 8:30.

I always take the hop on and hop off buses when we go places, they usually are a great value. The main stops had buses that weren't packed like sardines, but the ones at the beginning and end were miserable. They have a red line and a blue line (one had the tour in several languages, the other had a live tour guide in English only). The English only buses ( I think the red line) weren't near as packed as the multi language buses (blue line). We would get on the blue line bus near our hotel and then hop off when we got to the Marble Arch stop and hop on the English only bus so we would at least have a seat to sit on. The other buses we saw didn't look that packed, even the city buses weren't packed. Also if traffic was bad, they wouldn't reroute so it took an eternity to get anywhere. They also stopped running fairly early in the evening despite it staying light until after 9. Once I got the hang of the subway it was easy. You would be better off taking city buses or the subway than this tour. Maybe some of the other companies would be better, but I was completely disappointed in this one.

My favourite way of visiting cities is doing this by making a day-long-walk, but a double decker bus tour is a good alternative when you travel with kids.
We took a BigBusTour one with automatic commentary.You get your pair of headphones along with plastic raincoat and a map of tour. We hop on stop no 36 which allowed us to sit othe too level, in other places the bus used to be overcrowded and sometimes it is even hard to get in.
The tour makes a nice circle around city of London giving you an opportunity to see or most frequently hop off to visit most popular places in London. Automatic commentary is provided in most popular languages and is rather simple. It is not boring but also do not expect anything extraordinary. I suppose a bus with live commentary is a better choice.
The whole bus tour is quite long - close to 4 hours. Buy some water and food / snacks, you will probably need it. Concider taking cap / hat on sunny days if you want to take top platform. No ytoilet on board.
After enjoying bus tour do not forget to make a use of your river cruise ticket which should be offered to you after your bus ticked is checked. It is realky worth trying especially if you are with kids.

Ok let me start with the tours I have already experienced. I have been to Chicago, Washington, SF, Boston and even Delhi and took various hop on hop off tours.. N I can't deny that big bus is truly the worst experience ever. The guide was old and dumb and did not tell anything about the history of place. He was cracking some stupid jokes and laughing himself. Moreover, as we had an extra bag, he told us to keep it on my lap and made me sit with a stranger. The big bus guide was too busy in adjusting more and more people to have maximum profit.They made strangers, who did not even want to sit together, sit with each other by forcing them to do so. Overall I would say that big bus tours is total No No! I just sat in bus for 30 minutes and couldn't bear the rudeness of the guide I travelled whole London using the underground train. Doing it this way was far much better than big bus tours..
It was great as you can hop on and off whenever you wanted. It also includes the river tour which kids loved. A must do with kids who may get tired of walking but you have limited time to see it all.

Bus tours aren't just for foreign tourists. We made a trip down and used the Big Bus Tour as part of our trip to London. It covers all the sights and the red route with the live commentary is delivered by an enthusiastic and informed guide. Even after seeing London up close on a few occasions and picking up knowledge from various media sources, I was still able to listen and take in a mass of new information.

The buses are regular, we were fortunate that the blue route (recorded commentary only) passed by our hotel and we switched as soon as we could to the live. The rain tried to dampen our day but failed.

We also took advantage of a walking tour which was included with the ticket and took a boat tour from the Houses of Parliament to Tower Bridge (again included in the price). Its all hop on, hop off as many times as you want.

Book online before coming for a discount.

We took three kids under 9 for the single day tour which cost £54 and was not only a most excellent day but fantastic value. We took the live commentary bus for the full tour which was very informative and cheerfully presented, did the Harry Potter tour (a highlight for the kids) and went on the river cruise twice which was beautiful in the (lucky for us) sunshine. The lads on the boat do a bit of a commentary and REALLY put effort into trying to encourage TIPS as they say they are not paid to do the talk. That was a little cringey but was the only downside. Would highly recommend the tour overall as a way to see a lot of London in one day.

Recently my family visited me and we only have two days to spend in London. My old age dad can't walk much due to health condition and this big bus tour came out as a good option. It give you the brief knowledge about the attractions by the live commentary. Tour guide was funny but not everyone can understand the British humour. I bought two days pass but only manage to use it for one day, make note the bus only run from 9am to 4pm or 6pm during summer. But the whole journey of red line only 2.5hours if you do not hop off. You can stay on and complete the red route before you get off, so you can have the london central overview. Don't forget the city cruise is included in the 24hour ticket and worth to board. Sincerely have staying London for years and first know about London more deeply after the commentary.

Hopping on and off made this an ideal way to get an overview of London proper. Included was a boat ride on the Thames, which we took all the way to Greenwich. We did get hung up in noonday traffic but this was an overview and we could get off and see Buckingham and Big Ben and Apsley House and have lunch. The next bus would be around within 20 minutes for the most part. We preferred the tour buses with live commentary but there were alternative buses that made some of the same stops with commentary recorded to be heard in Spanish, French, German and Russian as well as Polish and one or two other languages. Enjoyable couple of days.

Second time we have used the big bus so this speaks for itself. Ricky *there is no one coming down Neville, there is no one coming down" our guide was fab. Really knew his history and took an interest in every passenger getting on. Great to use to hop on and off but if you can do the whole circuit well worth the history lesson.

Great decision to start our visit to London with a 48 hour Big Bus ticket. Hopping on and off as we discovered the city proved a popular way to go for the whole family. The Tour guides on the Red line varied in quality; some better than others but generally v.good and friendly. River cruise also included.
One attendant at the Speakers corner stop on Tuesday 7th. actually walked us to the other side of Park Lane via the under- road subway in order to catch the blue line bus that we just missed on the Park side. Fantastic service !
We'd recommend the Big bus Tour to anyone who wants to see London.

We liked the live guided loop of this tour best that covers most of the main part of the city. Try to get on top for the best views. We got off at the Tower and took the river boat back to Westminster.This was the best part. Then when we were ready to go back to our hotel we hopped on another route for a tour of another part of the city.

Having lived in central London for 8 years, and London for my whole life I wondered what there was new to see. A friend from the US wanted to do a bus tour and I was surprised how much I saw and learned. Our guide Rob was excellent, funny and got everyone involved, including the whole bus making someone's birthday very special! Recommend highly.

Having a friend over from the United States we travelled to London Gatwick from Inverness on the 7am flight down and caught the Gatwick Express up to Victoria where, at 10.30am we took the first journey of our pre-booked Big Bus Tour. We had several hours to kill before checking into our hotel (St Giles - brill location and comfortable hotel with a breakfast not to be missed) so decided to do a loop of the tour to pass the time. We had opted for the 48 hour pass to give us time for the three walking tours and Thames river trip which was included in the price of £28. At only £7 more than the 24 hour pass this proved to be well worth it as time, when you are enjoying yourself, runs out far too quickly and we would not have enjoyed all that the ticket offered. This is a hop on hop off service but it was useful to do the full loop first. We travelled the main routes during the first day (Monday) and used these same routes on the Tuesday to reach the meeting points for the walking tours. These tours lasted around 2 hours each, were very interesting and included landmarks such as Westminster, St. Pauls and Buckingham Palace (timed to coincide with the Changing of the Guard). One of the walking tours included the Harry Potter theme and we visited many of the filming sites. However I would say that this particular walk was fast paced and anyone not spritely on their feet would find it difficult to keep up. After each walk we used the bus to go on from there as the tours always end in a convenient spot to rejoin the bus. By timing it right we were still able to use our tickets on the Wednesday morning on the Thames River Cruise to Greenwich where we could have left the boat to tour the village before catching a later boat back to Wesminster. However we chose to do a round trip and then still had time to do the route we had left until last which was one which took us around Knightsbridge, Harrods etc. We made our final stop Marble Arch so that we could then walk the length of Oxford Street back to our hotel on the corner of the other end of Oxford Street where it joins Tottenham Court Road. We left Thursday as our free day as we were travelling back to Gatwick for the evening flight home. In real terms, we gently accomplished so much on the big bus tour that, by leaving our shopping time until the evening (shops are open until around 9pm), we could easily have travelled to Gatwick on the Wednesday evening to come home and thus save on our hotel bill for the third and last night. I thoroughly recommend the 48 hour pass with this company. There are other companies operating similar trips and I cannot make any comparison. Certainly we would not have seen half as much (yet would have spent much much more on tube and bus fares) without the BigBusTour and it was hassle free. In between bus rides we chose to walk to places like Covent Garden and Downing Street (as we were in town at the time of Lady Thatcher's funeral) and found that combining all elements we saw and did everything we set out to do, and more.

After a visit to the Tower of London we wanted to catch the first available bus after 3pm. We waited for well over 30 minutes for a bus to arrive and when it finally did it was totally overcrowded. In the meantime, however, at least three or four competitor buses came and went only half full. It is my belief that Big Bus Tours have far too few buses for the booking they take. To make matters even worse, there was either no air conditioning on the bus or it wasn't working and this, combined with the overcrowding meaning that a minimum of at least 20 people were standing in the isles. meant that we and others decided to cut our return journey short and leave the bus at a much earlier stop than as intended. This bus experience was more in keeping with a rush-hour commuter journey than a tour experience and I would not recommend others using this company.

Hi, we had a very poor experience on the blue bus on the Big Bus tours last Friday. We thought it would be a great way to see a lot but we think we jagged a poor day. No one was friendly, there was not enough information. We were ordered off one bus only to be put back on the same bus and then made to sit for 40 minutes before the tour started again. The staff were incredibly rude and put a damper on an otherwise excellent holiday.

Brilliant way to see all the sights if you've never visited London. Regular, convenient buses with helpful imformative guides. You can hop on and off at any stop and a bus will be along every 5 - 10 mins. We bought 48 hr tickets for an extra £2 and it included a free river cruise. We also did the free Harry Potter locations walking tour which was also included. The guide was very funny and he gave a great tour. I would definitely recommend the big buses and would use them again.

We had a super trip with The Big Bus Company. Our driver was Pitch, who took the London (hair-raising) traffic in his stride (cool & calm without a hint of road rage) and our guide was Nobby and what a guide. He was incredibly knowledgeable and a natural comedian. We genuinely enjoyed his commentary and we learnt a huge amount about the area. Nobby's the 'real deal', none of your 'mockney' here! He gave us a good laugh; we're still chuckling about some of the things he said.
We had a good view with Pitch slowing to a crawl when Nobby gave the cue, good teamwork. I must say also that the chap at the sales bus by Victoria was very helpful and walked us around to the relevant stop to make sure we didn't get lost (despite having a sore back!). Really good service and enjoyable trip. London condensed I call it.

We are in London for two weeks and decided to go on the bus tours today as it was such a nice day, as well as going on the london eye which we purchased tickets for, from one of the friendly staff on the ground. We had such a lovely day out, we saw all of the main sites as well as learning fun and interesting facts about London. Our tour guide was a nice young lady called Leanne (with the nice hair!) She was extremely friendly and funny. We decided to stay on the whole way round with her and we're so glad we did. Everyone that we came across today were very kind and helpful, we will remember this and recommend it to anyone who is coming to London.
Sandra. USA

value for money you get to see lots of the landmarks in london and can hop of and get on when you want this was a good idea for me with having walking problems so I was able to sit downstairs and get off for a short time

We read reviews on here before booking a Big Bus Tour on our recent trip to London and have to say we totally disagree with some of them! Book on line before you go and it is cheeper! This is an absolutely fantastic way to see the whole of the city, with stops at EVERY landmark within easy walking distance! The drivers and staff were really helpful and answered any questions we had. We never waiting longer that 15 minutes for a bus and that was using the three routes around the city. Information was very clear and headphones and live comentary excellent. Even better was that there was a stop right outside our hotel at Marble Arch. As we booked when we were away I had the confirmation sent to my mobile phone. When we got on the first bus in the morning, the driver said someone would come on and scan the barcode on my mobile (very clever!). Nobody did and we used the bus hopping on and off & used the boat ride several times throughout the day. By 4pm, my phone battery was getting low so I asked a member of staff to scan it for me. He did, printed our tickets and informed us that because it hadn't been scanned earlier the 24 hours to use the ticket started from then and we basically had a free day to use the buses! Result! Meant we could get all the way round the city from Marble Arch to Euston Station again for free stopping at Hamleys Toy Shop with our son of course!

We booked our tickets online and printed the boarding pass before we departed which saved over £20.

The ticket attendants on the streets aren't all that friendly and some have a stupid sense of humour (ours pretended the printed ticket was fake - not funny).

They tell you the bus you want will only be 5 minutes but it usually arrived in double that time so there is always a longer wait!

The best way to see London is on the top deck, many big bus tour vehicles are fully open at the top however and this can get rather cold (other bus tours for example have a partial enclosed roof on all of their tours but I only saw one big bus like this out of their whole fleet).

The guides are knowledgeable. We always take a very early Sunday tour as it can get very busy and crowded later in the day.

I wish the tours would be more specialised - ie if you wanted to just see 'celebrity homes' in London they would just focus on those streets and telling you about the residents who live there (like they do in LA) or do a 'history' tour. Rather than focussing on one area they cram in everything in a short space of time! Nevertheless it's still a good way if spending time around the city.

I can't say too much bad about the Big Bus tour - but nothing great either. For those who have time and just want to ride around and see the sights its OK. But if you are on limited time there are better ways like the local buses to get where you want to go. The guide was good - the views just ok as it seems we were more near adjacent to attractions than at them. Their stops an droute are not always to the attractions but close to them - a lot of 'over there' you can see... We saw the back of B'ham Palace, the back of the Abby etc. Long stops at some places wasted time.

We are a family of 4 with kids of 8 & 10. We live in London but like most Londoner's we take it for granted. We took the 48 hour option and used it to its full extent. Don't sit on the bus for the whole time and expect to see everything as it doesn't work like this - jump off and jump back on again. This is a great trip and we found all the guides to be humorous, informative and good fun. One of the guides was ex big brother contestant "Shabby". She was brilliant - entertaining and full of interesting facts about London and its history. Would recommend this to anyone looking to get around London, take in the sights and have a laugh at the same time.

If you want to see in 2 hours all London key attractions you have to make the tour with this company.
The buses are clean and the tourist guide was really good, we have taken the red line where in the bus unfortunately where not available the comments in other languages than English and this was a bit of a problem for my wife and son.

Staying at The Grovenor next to Victoria Station, right out the front door was a stop. Very professional. Narrated tours on red bus line, narrated by headphones on blue bus in several languages. Enjoyed both. Offered a great overview of London. 48 hour ticket seemed to be best buy for us, included Thames by boat as well. Will always include on future trips.

Website has a map of routes and they provide a copy as well.

Enjoy this one, seemed to be much more crowded in the afternoon.

If you are new to London or a first timer, its worth a ride to get yourself familiarized with central London, Its a hop on and hop off tour and a great way to spend time and money saver for you...highly recommend it!

24 hours hop on hop off London sighseeing, pre-recorded guide tour, free river Thames cruise, free walking tours(The Ghosts by Gaslight Walk or Harry Potter).Good way to tour London, and to see most of the famous landmarks on the run.

I was visiting London for work and only had one day to check out the tourist locations so my friend and I decided that the hop on hop off tour would allow us to check out all of the major sites and get around the city easily (tickets in the winter are good for 48 hours). Even though it was a really cold day in February we decided to truly be able to see the city we would have to sit on the top open air section of the bus. We were not disappointed, the views from there were great. Most of the time we were on the Blue Bus so the commentary was automated which was fine for us.

There were Big Bus Tour representatives at every stop to help with any questions, recommendations on where to go and to buy tickets if needed. Included in our ticket was the opportunity to take a boat ride down the Thames. We took the boat from the London Tower down to Westminster Pier and Big Ben. It was a lot of fun to see some of the sights from the boat (and didn't have to sit at traffic lights).

Along with the boat tour our tickets came with the opportunity to join free walking tours and we ended up making it to the Ghosts by Gaslight walking tour which was pretty cool to see behind the scenes places of London. (We also stopped along the way to have a beer and warm up at pubs known for ghostly activity).

All in all I recommend taking the Big Bus Tour (even in winter) because it had a bit of everything, from the bus to the boat to the walking tour we felt that it wasn't just a run of the mill tour experience.

I recently went to London with friends for my first time. We all agreed that since it was our first time a "hop on hop off" bus was the way to get our bearings. We bought our tickets outside Paddington Station and were told that we could catch the bus in lots of different places to get back to the same place with the last arrival at Paddington to be 6:00pm. What they didn't tell us was that in order to catch the bus back, you had to be in the correct location (not disclosed at boarding) at 4:00 pm to catch that bus. So we spent a lot of money on a bus that left us in the heart of London in the dark trying to figure out the mass transit system. Really felt ripped off!

We would HIGHLY recommend this to anyone visiting London. The buses run regularly and take you to everything you could possibly want to see. The commentary on the blue tour is recorded and a bit more dry than the red tour which has a live guide to inform and answer questions. The hop on/hop off feature was excellent for allowing further exploration of certain areas of interest. In the Winter, they give your pass a 48hr expiration to sweeten the deal, it is 24hrs during peak season.

Went on a Big Bus Tours open top tour on Feb 19th, in the half term hols. Caught the train up to Charing Cross and paid for the bus outside the station at Trafalgar Square. For 2 adults and 2 kids aged 13 and 10 the cost was £70 which includes a boat trip up the Thames. Before I think March 1st or somewhere around there the ticket lasts for 48 hours so the savvy amongst you will probably go halves with another family and pass the tickets onto them when you get back. Too late for this year now and you do take a gamble on the weather but we oicked probably the best day of the year so far! If its raining then there is an inside part of the upstairs bus and obviously downstaits available. The buses were pretty busy but never totally packed although I expect that would change in summer, especially holidays. Rain poncho things are provided free and also headphones which plug in. Now here was my only problem. The headphones are badly designed in that they will not stay in! Best advice is to take your own. You can hop on and off of the bus at various points and obviously take the boat tour, from Tower of London stop up to Westminster where you can reboard a bus and continue the tour. Some of the buses have guides speaking on a mike, sometimes difficult to hear everything if its a tad windy, I preferred the headphones. One older chaps accent was so ridiculously cut glass posh that my kids were giggling the whole time and I sometimes couldnt quite understand him ha! Overall I thoroughly recommend this tour, first time Ive ever done it at the age of 49 and it was great. Not sure it would have been as good if it was was pouring down but you can check weather before you go. Important point- you can save around £10 off the £70 price by booking online. I took the more expensive option as you never know what can happen with London transport! You couldn't really do many attractions as well as the bus tour as you'd run out of time unless you got there really early. You could maybe do the London Eye and continue on but something like the Tower of London is a day out in itself.

It may cost more, we took a hint from a conductor, 24 hour ticket, did the entire loop late on the first afternoon we arrived, then the next day we already knew where we wanted to go, where to get off, the free walking tours they did, etc. then did another day, there are always buses going around, so hop on and off anytime, close to most hotels. Staff know their product and city and are extremely helpful. Thanks guys and ladies!

Me and my girlfriend used the big bus tours service last weekend, staff were very friendly and the tour guide was brilliant! We found it a very cheap way of getting around London compared to using taxis and got to see the sights along the way! Also you get 48 hours use and a free cruise on the Thames which for the money is great. Soon as we arrived in london we were out of our comfort zone as never been before but due to the staff they have on most stops we felt very comfortable and safe making our way around all the sights hoping on and off the buses as we pleased. We will definatley be using the service on our next trip down. Thanks

I had a hard time deciding which bus company to use and finally just picked the Big Bus Tour, as they both sounded great and our group really wanted to do this (10 of us)
We went in February and they offered us 48 hours and a river cruise. We took the bus tour (the Red one with a live commentary and that was great. As we did this our first day, it helped keep us awake! We got to see where the different areas were and what we wanted to do in the coming days. As we really didn't Hop on or off that first day, I can't say anything about the schedules or amount of buses, other than that there were plenty of them, just not as many late in the day. The next day we took the River Cruise from Westminster to the Tower of London. It was wonderful and we got a great tour person and saw so much. A definite must do for everyone! The view from the river was so pretty and we got to where we were going in a really cool way!

Okay, I'm addicted to this bus tour. I get to London at least once a year, usually twice, and I always go on the tour. Why after all this time? I always like to check out the entire city without paying cab fees or hiking around til I'm exhausted. Especially if I'm having a bit of jetlag, I can still see the city without expending much thought or energy! I can pop off on a whim, and since the ticket is good for more than one day, combined with my oyster card, I really get to see it all without having to be overly selective. Now, if you are going to London for your first or only visit, you ABSOLUTELY MUST go on this tour as soon as you get there! Get a top deck seat towards the back if the weather is decent. A lot of people like the front seats but you will be looking through windows and the small roof will sometimes obscure your view. In drizzly or cold windy weather that is a good idea but generally, enjoy the better open air view from the back seats. Look for staff on the sidewalk selling tickets. Keep the map! It is a really useful tool for getting around town and understanding where everything is in relation to each other. I should mention that this is a guided tour. I've had both excellent and so so guides so I actually prefer the recorded tour at this point in my travels. That is a very subjective thing though.

There were loads of locations all over London to hop on and off these buses so it meant that we never had to walk too far. Initially i had been worried about finding the stops but they were quite easy to find and pretty easily visable. We visited all the attractions and were given all the information on each one courtessy of a handheld instrument that you held to the ear. We got a free Thames boat trip with our tickets and this was actually the highlight of our day..the chap giving out all the info was hilarious and had us all in stitches for the whole trip...definatley recommend the boat tours.....all in all a fun informative day out for all our family.

We bought our tickets online and got and extra day free with a cruise down the river Thames also included in the price. We didn't get our moneys worth on the bus as we only got to do half the blue tour, this wasn't the bus companies fault however, we spent too much time doing other things and didn't get time to get back on the bus. It was very cold while we were there and being on the top deck was tough, we did move downstairs after a while when we got too cold but we missed a lot as you can't see a whole lot when your in traffic and there are other buses and cars beside you, so bring extra warm clothes when going on the bus!
There were plenty of staff dotted along the bus route selling tickets for the bus ride so it wasn't difficult to get help if we needed it. We did ask one of them for the timetable for the cruise but he didn't know. We were able to find this on their website where we found a link to the boat company.
The boat trip was definitely a highlight for us, on our second day we decided we would get the boat from Westminster to The London Tower as we wanted to see the tower and we felt like we hadn't made much use of the bus and wanted to get our moneys worth!! It was absolutely freezing and snowing heavily and if I'm being honest I was dreading the boat ride as I had imagined it was going to be open to the elements! How wrong could I have been, it was a huge and inside it was like a ballroom with glass to the front and sides and the heat when we walked in was so comforting after having walked the streets of London all morning I was so relieved to be inside, they had a little snack bar where they were selling beer, tea, coffee and food.
The tour was brilliant, great seeing everything from a new angle. The staff on the boat were lovely too, very friendly. I would recommend the boat trip to anyone.

We really enjoyed it the only way to see London in a short time frame. Our guide was knowledgable and really funny. Only disappointing thing is that coaches aren't allowed to drive up to Buckingham Palace so unless you get off you just get a side on view not the famous balcony shot! Would defiantly use again as a way to hop off and on. We booked on the Internet and a slight reduction.

We decided to do the hop on hop off tour at the start of our time in London. We had two children 9 and 5, and was great to go around and highlight the main areas of London, then come back the next day or hop off the bus to see the different sites that interested us. The guide was very funny and provided a lot of interesting acts along the way. Highly recommend for those who have limited time or want to get a feel for the city prior to exploring the different sites.

We were only in London for 3 nights, so we didn’t want to waste time on the Tube. We decided to book a double decker tour bus. Honestly, I don’t think there is much of a difference between the Big Bus Tour and the Original Bus Tour. They are both plentiful and around the same price. I liked Big Bus Tours because their customer service dept responded to email questions very promptly.

The tours were interesting and the guides were friendly and informative. Go with the 2-day package to save some money. If you know your exact dates, you can purchase online and save even more money.

Keep in mind if you want to get an early start to your day, you will want to get to one of the first stops. Otherwise, you might be waiting for a while for the bus to pick you up. Also, I recommend bringing your own earbuds to listen to the commentary.

Victoria is an excellent tour guide, funny and informative.

Cheap way to get around as you can hop on and of when you like with your ticket. Sadly didn't have time to do the river cruise that comes in with the ticket price but will do it next time.

I have done the Big Bus Tour before and was thoroughly impressed, so decided to buy a 2 day pass for myself and 2 friends when we visited again this year. Day 1 was fantastic, nice and quick getting between places but a great way to see all the sites as well. However, on Day 2 we were all less than impressed. The driver was terrible... he made the journey uncomfortable with the way he drove the bus for starters, and every time we stopped at a bus station he would spend a good 5-10 minutes chatting with the Big Bus Tour guides that stand at each stop. At one stop he spent 15 minutes talking to a passenger about getting to a certain location, which I was under the impression was the job of the guy standing outside at the stop??? So the previous day took us an hour to do what took us over two the next (and the traffic was even less conjested than the previous day!). I should also note that we were overtaken by two other Big Bus Tour buses, showing just how slow and delayed our bus was. Not impressed, missed going to some of the attractions on the other side of London due to the hour delay.

I'm hoping this was a one off because the previous day and my previous experiences have been great, but this one day ruined my opinion of the Big Bus Tour.

We needed to see the major highlights of London in 3 days and this was a perfect way to do it. Its a great way to tour the city quickly - plus its very informative. The blue and green lines have audio that you can plug into in all languages (they give you free ear buds) or you can get on the red line for live audio in English. I thought it was very affordable, plus you can get on and off all throughout the day. The last bus runs until 6pm. They will give you a route map which is very useful - but make sure you ask the driver if they are operating on any diversions. One afternoon we were stuck in a ton of traffic for hours (off the route) because the regular route was on diversion, causing us to miss our stop. We were not made aware of any changes to the route. We were told that the driver will only tell you about diversions if you ask. Make sure to do this, it will help you plan where you want to stop off at in the event the traffic route is abnormal on a particular day. With all of the special events and holidays in London - I am sure diversions are a regular occasion.

Arrived Friday afternoon and decided to try the Big Bus Tour. We got on at the Marble Arch stop and bought our tickets right at the stop. There is a representative at each stop. Let me explain how this works:

1. Ask about prices first. We got the senior rate 60 or above for 15 pounds for 48 hours.
2. Get on the bus and do the whole route about 21/2 hours and see everthing you might want to visit.
3. The red route has live commentary. The blue route has headphones for different languages. You will get a map with routes and attractions.
4. Do the river cruise. You can get on at The Eye and go right down to the Tower of London.
5. If you have time, they have a stop for walking tours that are included in your ticket price.

This bus did not disappoint. We used it over and over for 2 days. We never waited more than 10 minutes for a bus and there was plenty of room. The stops are very close to the attractions. I would use this service again in another city. Loved it!!
Hop on, hop off with good explanations. I only had 36 hours and this tour conne4cts with the Thames river cruise. I finished my wanderings with an evening of Oxford St shopping and a falafel roll.

We used the blue line and the red lines. The blue line is recorded commentary only. The red line is live commentary in english only. The live commentary was well done with a good blend of comedy and information. Definitely get a seat on the top deck for red line to see what the guide is pointing to -- it helps a lot. Complimentary head phones (respectable quality and sanitary), complimentary ponchos in case of rain, and clean buses round out the good comments. Most drivers were courteous also.

A minor disappointment is that occasionally the driver starts driving while passengers are still finding their seats. This is especially problematic if you are travelling with small children as we were.

I had one significant disappointment - the frequency of the service. On our second day, they underestimated the amount of passengers. Buses were running on blue line with at least 20 minutes in between each bus and they arrived full in the morning. People were standing and there were not enough headphone jacks for everyone to be able to hear. We passed multiple bus stops where passengers were not able to board due to the full bus. At one stop, I saw another operator taking a picture of the bus (from the outside) as if to show his potential customers what they would face if they chose Big Bus Tours.

Overall, I would still take it as it is a good overview of the city, but they need to be careful to increase service so that passengers are not left waiting. If it turns out less people are riding, they can always remove some buses from service -- just hard to add them when they underestimate passengers.

We booked our "24" hour pass for the bus at the stop near our hotel and was told it starts at 9:00, am the bus was 40 minutes late. The traffic was heavy and it stopped frequently at one point for 30 minutes, we were told we could get off and shop if we liked. By the time we made it to the tower of London (the first stop) it was noon. We took a short tour of the tower and then the river cruise (included in price) and grabbed lunch at a pub near the ship Golden Hind. We reboarded the bus at 3:30pm and were ready to tour again. BUT the bus stops at 4:30! and they just pulled over and let everyone off at 4:15...we had no clue where we were and our hotel was across town. It was 2 taxis later to get back to the hotel. So much for the 24 hour ticket....just take a taxi!!!

I found the Big Bus tour to be very disappointing (Oct '12) - long waits at each bus stops, a bus driver change at Marble Arch only to have to change buses at the next stop so that the driver has a break. This meant there were too many people and no seats upstairs on a beautiful day and we were told we'd have to wait 20 mins for the next bus. With these delays and the London traffic you see the city quicker by walking. And being downstairs you'd do better on the regular city buses.

Most of the buses were the blue line with recorded commentary. The one red bus we were on was incredibly disappointing - the commentator had no information to share other than the number of remaining stops, that it was late in the day, most sites were closed already, etc. He was obviously bored and anxious to end the day (at 4pm) and the recording would have been preferred. The river cruise was nice and the commentator was great, but all in all I'm very disappointed with the service received for the money. There is no emphasis on the customers actually seeing the city. Take the tube and city buses instead and save your money.

The Big Bus Tour is a great way to see a lot of London in a short amount of time - perfect if you have a long layover at Heathrow. I was able to see all of the spots that were on my "tourist must see/do" list and still had plenty of time to enjoy the London Eye and sip some tea.

Tickets may be purchased at the airport or kiosks in the city.

They have three different lines. The funniest one is the red one, when you have real people talking about London history and monuments. It does not replace the subway pass, once the bus only covers the main attraction and also because it runs one way in the city, and sometimes you will need to do the entire tour again to reach the place you want to go.

Great way to get brief overview of all major attractions. Hop on - hop off at any stop. Live commentary from very friendly, knowledgeable and extremely helpful tour guide, not standard taped recording. Always willing to answer questions. Travelled on last bus of day and guide checked with each passenger to ensure that they understood where they were going when they disembarked and helped them with information with onward travel if required as they would not be able to get another bus back to their starting point. River cruise from Greenwich to Westminster included in price, which was very good.

The Big Bus Tour company made us able to fit all London attractions into one day. Was convenient to get on a bus pretty much anywhere in the centre of London. The guides were comical, friendly and were very brushed up on their history. You also get a free thames cruise (which I unfortunately didn't have time to use). I'd recommend this to anyone.

I used the guided tours exclusively for the first couple of days just to get a grasp on the lay out of the city and its sites. The guides were each informative, entertaining and helpful when it came to the hopping off/where the heck do I hop back on part. I switched over to the unguided Blue line for a day but could not find the return stop (my fault for not paying attention) and just hailed a cab to get back to the hotel. I found that the headsets on the blue line were informative but not always in sync, maybe the traffic congestion didn't aid that. Still in all, good deal for the money, and an easy way to get to sites in a day.

We only had 3 full days in London, so decided to see London via Big BusTours. There are couple of other bus tour services. Why picked this one? Ultimately boils down to price 20 GBP for 24 hour pass (bought online for specific date) vs regular price 29 GBP. Also, its Blue line covered slightly more areas in London vs competitor (most have same stops). Price includes a free cruise ride along Thames. Blue line has only pre-recorded guide vs Red line -- live person who can point out many more historical info and share funny stories. We started early morning and the traffic was ok. By lunchtime, London traffic lived up to its reputation. Downside? Sitting on the upper deck, ready to Inhale plenty of London air pollution and it can be chilly.
Very good sightseeing experience! Price hopping on at tower of london was 20Â£ and the guide called patrick was amusing and very good at his job! Recommended!

Highly recommend doing the big bus tour in London. It is great that the main line had a real person narrating as there are no boring gaps between sights and it is much more entertaining. The lines for this company are very comprehensive.

I recently spent 10 days in London (3rd trip) and the first thing I did was the Big Bus Tour. Using the Big Bus Tours is great for just riding around and relaxing after a flight to the UK. The bus stops at or near all the main attractions, and points out many attractions you may not be aware of in London.

Excellent value and time well spent. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Plus you can purchase ticktes for other attractions on the Big Bus at a discount and avoid the lines. I did this for St. Paul's Cathedral and avoided a really long line upon arrival.

Highly recommend!

The Big Bus tour is an excellent way to see the city, visit tourist attractions, and just plain old get around. There are so many stops and you are able to easily hop on and off, without much wait time for buses. One bus, I think the Red route has a live tour guide. Our guide was quite personal, funny, and extremely knowledgeable. I liked having the live guide, but the recorded Blue route was good too. The tours are recorded in several languages so it may be a good choice for people that don’t speak English. Each bus we rode on was comfortable and very clean.

We had book a trip to london last minute so we wanted to squeeze as much of London in a possible. We paid £28 each and it was well worth the money as we got 4 routes, a boat tour and 4 walking tours included. ( Walking tours included a Harry Potter tour, a Ghost tour, a Beatles tour and another).
We went on the RED route which had about 30 stops, it sound a lot but the whole tour took just over 2 hours and it flew by. You are encouraged to spot off as many times as you like as the next bus is only 5-10 away.
We had a great tour guide called Kevin, who really helped to show a different side of the city plus his beautiful rendition on Oliver's 'Who will buy' was brilliant. He was your typically cheeky cockney guide.
Thank you Big Bus Tour Company, we had a fantastic time!

Even though we had a heads up it was still very difficult to find the stops to join the bus tour if you were not in central London. The live guide provided a very nice commentary. Buses stop running at 6 pm. Not a great way to go between attractions. Use the subway instead.

Don,t know what happened on the 17th of august with the bus tour?
