We started the trip off well and given headphones to listen to the history of London as we travelled around to see the sights, we got off by the houses of parliment to travel on the free boat ride on the thames which was excellent..... however on coming back to pick the tour bus up at westminister it never arrived and after waiting on near an hour for it to arrive the bus turned up it was fully packed and had to stand by the driver, who insisted on letting more people on as we stopped at pick-up points when there was clerly no room to get on, in the end we had stood for over 45 minutes and people were sitting on the steps of the bus.. We had missed most of the sights coming back not able to use the headphones to listen to the commentry.... we were on the tour bus for over 2 hours coming back and after being out all day was really not exceptable there were no toilet facillities . It was not the trip we had payed for and quite honestly spoilt the day out for us as from the begining it seemed to be going well, so certainly through my experience i could not recommend it and has put me off doing it again..............
Was in London from a layover flight, 8 hours. With this bus tour had the time to actually see ,London' s most important sights.. Worth it if your time is limited or not.

Decided this would be the best way to see London as had a 15 year old with me. Similar experience in Barcelona taught me that it is easier to sit on the whole way round and pick out the places you would really like to see and then if you have time, get off at those particular stops. Found the guided tallks very interesting and swapped over to the blue route on Regent Street where they had a personal guide. The only thing that really spoiled the day was the weather but then who could help that?? Took the cruise down the Thames to Tower Bridge and decided to walk to my departure train station from there rather than travel all the way back to South London to have to get a tube back again. Traffic congestions sometimes but then again it is London!! Nice to sit on the open top bus and enjoy the views, would recommend this as a very informative and comfortable way to see all the sites and hear the history as well. Tour cost £35 for an adult and child, tube would be much cheaper, around £11 but not nearly as enjoyable.

I was in London for 2 night by my self n trust me 2 days I needed to c all of London ..it had a bus every where ,never faced any problem . The staff were great .. I was given a good rate for a 2 day ticket . Worth it . I enjoyed my London trip on big bus tour ....

This is a hard review to write because I thought the hop on hop off bus ride is pretty awful. But, in their defense, I was riding it during rush hour and it was painfully slow. I think it could be a good thing to do on your first day when you are tired and jet lagged if you avoid the busier parts of the day.

Now, on the other hand, their changing of the guard walking tour was excellent. We got views that the other tourists didn't. It was fun, informative, and the guide was great. The free boat tour was excellent as well. I think the price is worth it if you take advantage of these two options.

We travelled today on the big bus. We hopped on at Covent Garden where there was a staff member waiting at the stop. We quickly converted our vouchers for tickets, got our headphones ( it was the blue circuit bus) and were on our way and the only ones on the bus which was unexpected given how busy we were told it would be. The commentary along the way was excellent and in time. Despite warnings of the time it takes to get around we were quick to move along. The bus was clean and easy to catch. There seemed to arrive more regularly than we anticipated. When we got off at the Tower of London someone was waiting to sell tickets. They said they were cheaper and would give us a Yeoman Tour. This was a but misleading as the price was that of the normal entry less the optional donation fee and the Yeoman Warder tours are free anyway. We intended to get the boat back to Westminster however as it was raining there was not enough room underneath (it seemed ridiculous that they had tables I see which took up a lot of room) and the wait for the next boat was another 25 minutes. It was too cold to wait so we were lucky to catch the next Big Bus I stead but standing room only and the guide (red circuit) was only upstairs and could barely be heard. Overall the bus was fun although is a bit expensive.

Really enjoyed this attraction! The staff are very informative, factual, and entertaining! If you've never been to London, it's a great way to get the feel for everything. (I wish I had done this tour the first time I came to London). They recommend good places to eat and shop. Also, by going on the bus tour, you get discounted rates for other things to do in London like the Tower of London and London Eye.

Try and get James as your guide. He's funny and informative!

We spent four lovely days in London and Paris and used this company in both cities after reading various reviews etc.
The positive thing is it is a good way to see everything in one go and take some photo;s whilst sitting down.
We however were not expecting to be told half way though the trip that no matter where the bus is at 6 pm it ends there..and you have to get yourself home or back to where you need to be.
We thought we would be taken back to the original destination we got on at.
We had an hour or more walk home at the end of an exhausting day.
The company needs to make sure people know that the tour ends wherever they are at that time and make it clear...
The host and driver were the only unfriendly people we met in London and we did not even get offered headphones.
Not recommended but if you do..get an early trip and ask for headphones.
Sit upstairs and dont expect it to slow down for pictures
London was lovely..clean friendly and beautiful
We used the same tour in Paris and although we paid upfront on the website before we left they made us wait for the last people to board ...why?
Paris was very unfriendly and rude I am sad to say which is what everyone warns you about.

Bought tickets beforehand for a named date which was cheaper.

We arrived early at Heathrow, got the Connect to Paddington and the stop was just outside. Used the bus as hop on- hop off transportation.
As other posters have said, the traffic can hold things up sometimes, but that's London traffic, all busses will have this.

We also got the boat trip from Tower of London to Westminster and the Captain gave a brilliant commentary, we probably learnt more on that trip than on the bus, but we did get the blue route with the recorded commentary, but it was fine, the headphones are great. Even though it was busy, we managed to get upstairs most of the time.

It was a useful way to get around and good value .

My husband and I bought Big Bus tickets online the night before, which is cheaper than buying the tickets the day you want to use them. Overall, the experience was good. It was raining, and because the bus was full on the lower deck, we had to sit in the open-air upstairs section. Fortunately, the bus provides rain ponchos which made it feasible to sit up there. We enjoyed the experience because we were able to see the scenery go by as we traveled around town. However, the traffic was heavy and it was very slow moving. It took us 2 1/2 hours to go from Paddington to the Tower of London. Following our time at the Tower of London, we hopped on the river cruise to Westminster. The river cruise was very entertaining, basically due to the guy who did the commentary, and I would highly recomnmend doing this as part of your ticket option. It was a much faster way of getting back across town, too, since we skipped the traffic. From the dock we walked up to the National Gallery, and spent a few hours there, before joing a Ghost Tour, one of the walking tours which is also an option that is part of the ticket price. So we felt that by using the bus, the boat, and the walking tour, we maximized our use of the tickets.

However, I don't really see this as truly a "hop on, hop off" service. The traffic is slow and it takes a long time to get around, so by the time you travel from point A to point B and spend a few hours at one or two attractions, the day is gone. The ticket is good for 24 hours, but the buses stop running around 6:00 or 6:30 pm. So, say you start at 8:00 that morning--basically after 6:00 pm, you can't utilize the second half of your 24 hours you paid for (unless you do an evening walking tour). This 24 hour window only works if you begin in the afternoon, and then finish up the next morning. I can't really recommend it as an expedient way of getting around to the various attractions. You might be better off to take the tube around if you really want to pack in as many attractions as possible. But, if you want to see the scenery and aren't too terribly pressed for time, this could be a great option. Overall I give the experience four stars, because it was good for what it can offer, given the constraints of London traffic.

If it's your first time to London, The Big Bus tour is a good way of seeing a bit of everything and learning the main areas and attractions. I did the tour during the Jubilee celebrations which meant they had to re-route one section, but I was impressed at the way they handled it, and the guide still had some information to share about Mayfair even though it wasn't usually part of the tour.

I would suggest staying on for the entire route so that you can see everything the first time and get your bearings, and then hop on and off as you wish. They also include a small boat cruise, which wasn't anything much but you can get some good shots of the London Eye from the river.

I found it to be quite pricey though, especially since they didn't have student/concession prices.

***A word of warning!! DON'T buy your ticket from the street vendors, they don't work for the company and don't know anything about the tour! I bought my ticket from a vendor who said if you buy a 24 hour ticket you can upgrade any time on the bus to 48 hours - WRONG. The bus people didn't know what I was on about. The vendor also said the boat tour went to Greenwich, which was also wrong as this is only for people with a 48 hour ticket.
(In the end the company let me pay the difference to upgrade so I could go to Greenwich, but it's not how they normally do it.)

So in short, buy your ticket at the actual BUS and not from the agent/vendor.

Half the tour was re routed due to a marathon in the City of London. We brougtht our tickets at one of the bus stop. All though the man was friendly everything he said about the tour was a lie, we stopped at about ten stops that were not even on the map, when we asked why the driver said that we had an old map. We planned on riding the whole tour first all three bus line colors, when we were told there was not enough hours from the time they open to close to do it, even if we didn't get off, per the driver. It was so bad we the stops were far from the places we did want to see half of our day of the on and off again was walking. Stay away, find other means to see the city, not worth it one bit, and the other buses are worse. They have no reason to stick to what they advertise, they know they will never see you again and you have no one can careless if you complain. Warning, rip off. SCAM....

While the main attractions were pointed out - sometimes slightly before or after- there are so many other interesting looking places that I have no idea what they are. I guess that's why you need to hop off! Our driver ended his shift halfway through the tour and we were left not back where we started which was inconvenient. Make sure you know where your driver finishes.

The Big Bus tour is very affordable and way fun. We did the upgraded 48 hour tour and loved it. Our Live tour guide James Fuller was really informative and funny he interacted with the people on the bus it really made it fun. He also helped us figure out what tube stop we needed to get off at to get to dinner. I highly recommend this tour.

Did the 24hour ticket tour which I bought on-line before we went. Travelling with my wife and 2 small children and I can't recommend this company enough. We got on the tour at green park with no problems, very friendly and helpful staff. Got the red tour bus with Ashleigh as the live guide - she was brilliant and very entertaining. Got off at Hamleys for the kids and then rejoined the bus and took it to the Tower of London - had Ian as our guide this time and he was brilliant with the kids. Then took the free included boat trip form tower bridge back to Westminster. All in all a brilliant thing to do with the kids on their first trip to London - did encounter a bit of traffic but this was central London so what do you expect.

We came to London for the jubilee weekend - myself my husband and two children. The guide, Ashleigh Wilson was superb, my daughter had asked her to point out the Pankhurst statue and not only did she remember but she even remembered my daughters name too!! She had the right amount of information, banter and humour. We learned loads of interesting historical facts without being preached at. She interacted well with all the passengers on the bus and everyone seemed to enjoy it as much as us. Although I've been to London before but this is the first time I've done the bus tour - I would recommend this to everyone as a must do event in London as my 14 year old said that was like a show !!
Well done Ashleigh for a great day!

Dont waste your time using the big bus tour in London. Paid twenty nine pounds and got kicked off the bus 2 stops before our destination because the driver was going to the pub. Many buses pulling up that we're out of service. Asked staff at stop for assistance but he wasn't any help and was quite rude to other tourist who were also asking for assistance.

Had a call from the bank today to say there had been fraudulent use on the account, someone has been using the account to purchase currency in Chicago! the card is never used to make purchases but being in London we didn't want to carry cash ad was only used when boarding the big bus tour, looking back we thought the guy was being friendly and taking time to chat but the reality is he was keeping us talking while he ripped us off!

Happy birthday hubby our account has been emptied of £600+!!

This was the second time I took the Big Bus Tour in London. The stories, anecdotes and the incredible convenience of being able to get off at any of the stops, do a tour, have lunch etc and get back on without having to wait more than a few minutes for the next bus was invaluable especially as I was there only for 3 days and my son, who had never been to London was visiting. We chose the Big Bus Tours also because they were the only tour bus group who had open air double deckers, and the weather was sunny and warm. Our tickets included a boat ride down the Thames. It was shorter this time than last year but still great. Any tickets we needed were purchased ahead of time and discounted. Great fun!

Having family in the country for the weekend, we thought we would do the whole London sight-seeing experience, plus given that it was a nice day, i.e. the rain had stopped for the first day in six weeks, we thought a nice trip on the duck tours would be perfect. Errrrrrr, that is if I had booked in advance, so we took an alternative substitute with the Big Bus Tours. There were two reps of two different tour companies standing at the same bus stop which was somewhat off-putting and although the other company was cheaper, the rep that sold us this tour was actually interested on what we wanted to do. It was rather disappointing and rather unreasonable however, that they didn't offer OAP concessions, but off we went.

The bus tour was mediocre, not much excitement other than the sights to see, which explains itself. But the cruise down the Thames was a GREAT experience. We had a fantastic tour guide who excelled in charm, wit and was an excellent allround entertainer. He was knowledgeable, informative, hilarious and really accommodated for all ages and cultures of his audience, it's a stage he should be on!

Hello there, hotties

As Ryan and I write this, we are on a Vueling flight from Paris to Rome. It should be mentioned that there are small children sitting directly behind us, and we got some kickers, folks. We will try our best to not have our current mild irritation impair the accuracy of our review.
We had about 4-5 hours to explore London, upon reaching the city, utilizing the Heathrow Express. We wanted to see as many sites as we could in this time frame so the hop on hop off bus, it was. For 29 Euros PP, we were given a pair of ear phones and that's about it. We purchased our tickets through a convenience store outside of Paddington Station, which may have been mistake #1, as he didn't direct us where we should go to board to the bus, any more than pointing a finger to nowhere....after we asked for clarity twice. Ryan is an avid map reader (I suck at directions) and the human mapquest in the states, but even with his natural abilities, we were unable to track down the location to board, with going back and forth a few times. We also had asked for additional information from the seller of the tickets, who appeared to be either uninformed or uninterested.
Anyways, upon entering the bus we were told 'it's a 3 hour and 50 minute round trip [blue route] bus ride without getting off the bus.' This caused a slight bit of hesitation for us, initially, as we had already paid for our tickets (seemingly non-refundable) and had to leave for the airport in 3 hours. When we informed the somewhat pleasant big bus employee of this, he implied we should probably not do the tour. However, we decided to risk it, which ended up working out just fine. It is quite easy to get on at later stops on the bus ride, actually, which is what we needed. The bus loops around the same streets, at different spots/sites.
The guide via headphones provides information in 8 different languages, so that is a nice perk. However, it is not the best quality, sometimes only one ear plug working at a time. All in all, for someone who has limited time and wants to see a great deal of what London has to offer, I would recommend this tour.

K Grade: C+

Ryan: I didn't have any problems with how the tour operated but more direction in buying tickets and finding pick-up locations would be a major improvement. The traffic congestion in London means that you spend the entire tour moving at a snail's pace. So, if you are in a hurry to get to a particular spot, it may be faster to just walk.

R Grade: C

We found the 48-hour ticket to be a good buy. It gave us plenty of time to use the busses and even take the river cruise. Big Bus tours offer quite alot for the price, but you need enough time to take advantage of what you want to see. We tried both the live commentary and the recorded, and found we got more info from the recorded commentary. And they even offered free rain ponches on the bus, which we fortunately didn't have to use once during our visit.

We used the big bus tours for 3 days and it was just great so convienent. The live commentary was awesome! They gave a lot of background information and I learned a lot. The buses are always going by so you don't have to wait that long to hop on and off. The maps are great. I loved the whole concept. I would defiantly take the buses again if I came back to tour London again it's a much cheaper option for getting around without taking the tube. And sit on top of the bus it's just beautiful!

Big Bus tours is a bit expensive 29 pounds for 24 hrs trip, however, if you properly plan the use of this service you can get your money back!!! My recommendations is that you utilize a least one of the walking tours, use a least one trip in the boat and ride a least one time in the bus around the main areas!!! The bus is great shape and constantly passing by, so you do not have to wait for a long time. Be aware of the red and blue line since the blue line has an extensive route while the red line is mainly for popular attractions. If you are staying for a few days, then buy the 48 hrs ticket for a few more pounds. The red has a tour in English while the blue line has a recording in 8 main languages. It is easy to find a stop for hop on hop off bus. It is cheaper than taking taxis and subway troubles:)

We spent over 3 hours and got about a mile on one bus. They had two buses break down over 'audio problems' an excuse we didn't particularly believe as it was working fine. We had to change buses twice.

We switched to the red line and it was no better. It got nowhere due to traffic and long stops. The commentary was terrible with a young man that thought he was a comedian that was very rude to Canadian guests.

Very very rude manager with obviously practiced babble when we complained. We finally got off and got on the tube as we were running out of time to get to a train.

You can see far more and get out cheaper with a daily tube pass and a little walking. A total waste of money and the only rude people we ran into on our 4 day outing of London. Certainly don't let this bunch give you an impression of what London or Londoner's are like. You can be sure I will be filing complaints with other British agencies about this 'tour'.

Their website states "A Child Ticket is valid for children aged between 5 and 15 years inclusive. Children under 5 years of age may travel free of charge". Prior to purchasing our tickets we had also checked with the vendor that our 3 children (all 3 years and under) were entitled to travel for free.
We have waited for over a week for good weather so that our children could experience going on your bus tour. We were extremely disappointed at the rudeness and poor attitude of one member of the staff.
Unfortunately, my experience today at 12.06pm was;
1. After waiting about 20 minutes for a second bus in order to secure ourselves seats the bus was about to embark when we were rudely confronted by a member. This representative directed my husband to travel on first row of the upper deck with 2 children on his lap. I pointed out to the driver that requiring my children to travel in such a manner jeopardised their safety when the bus was in motion. The driver then tried to charge my child 12 pounds and used profanity at our family including the word "bloody".
2. I requested a full refund. This request was at first refused by the driver - who had stormed off in order to load more passengers onto the already overcrowded bus. When a refund was finally granted over 1/2 an hour later he initially also refused to provide us with a receipt.
3. At no point did we receive an apology for the inconveniences. This is even after he falsely accused us of trying to take an additional child on board without permission. The ticket vendor had immediately corrected him - we had declared all three of our children and had been granted a waiver for them.
It is disgraceful that my family's experience of London has been ruined by such poor business practices and customer service.

I don't know if this was an off day or typical, but we did not enjoy this experience. The traffic was absolutely horrendous on the day we went. We were cooped up on this bus for hours and barely even went anywhere. The bus was freezing- even on the bottom of the bus. I don't know if the busses are heated, but if so, they needed to put the heat on. The tour guide barely said a word the entire time. We started at The London Eye and after driving around for a long time, we somehow ended up back in the same place we started, but on the other side of the road. The bus goes around a loop and you get nowhere fast (or slowly). We saw a lot of some areas of London, and didn't see some of the other areas at all! they need to change the route.

On our first day touring London, we had no problems getting on the first bus. But near the Tower of London we spent about an hour or so waiting for a bus that never came. Other tour company buses have already passed by but not The Big Bus. Sadly, I booked them for 48 hours. The second day was the same--our first day touring ended in Harrods. I waited in the Harrods stop for quite a while before the bus came. I really think they should have more buses available.

After reading various reviews we decided to try this company. We bought tickets at the bus stop and hopped on the bus. The first negative was the driver who looked totally disinterested, as if he didn't want to be there, really off-putting. It was a cold day and it started raining. We thought we were lucky getting undercover upstairs seats, 2 from the front for the best view. We didn't have a live commentator but the recorded trip. As we progressed, the windows at the front of the bus began to slide open and it was an unsuccessful battle from there by various people to wedge it shut. The rain and cold wind blowing in on those seated there. We got off and went to see Buckingham Palace. After lunch we thought we'd try another of their buses. After waiting quite a time for a bus one arrived, full. We squeezed on, the driver told the bloke selling the tickets at the stop that it was crazy, the bus was full, the service had been reduced and 'these people shouldn't be allowed on'. It was cold wet and the windows started frosting over. Tourists had no idea where they were, no announcements at stops and so many tourists standing had no idea what was happening as they couldn't plug headphones in. We again got off to look at Harrods, came back to the bus stop after that, along with a number of people, waited a while for a bus which again was way too full. Many hopped on but we gave up and headed for the tube.
Perhaps the tour with live commentary may have worked but our experience was not good. I'd be looking elsewhere next time, couldn't recommend this based on our experience.

We used Big Bus Tours to get familiar with London on our first trip to this awesome city. We had a stop right at our hotel (Thistle Kensington Gardens) and the buses ran frequently. The recorded commentary was very good. The weather was cool, but this tour was worth the money. They even provide free ponchos (which we had to wear a few times - ha ha). From the top of the bus, you get a beatiful view of the city and its sites.

This tour worked well for my husband and I. We had a day and getting to see all the major attractions and hear the history was well worth it. We did hop off and on to delve into a few sites and areas in detail including the National Gallery, Trafalger Square, Westminister Abby, Harrods and Kensignton Palace.

I did like the blue line and hearing the recorded history. For 23 pounds each, we rode from 10 in the morning till 6:15. Made one giant loop and saw London!

I just had to make an account to review my experience with Big Bus Tours.

I came to London with a friend for the day and thought the best way to experience London would be to take a bus tour. I was going to go with a competitor tour company but was persuaded by a very friendly ticket seller to choose Big Bus and I'm very glad I did. I didn't catch his name but he was very nice.

at £29 per ticket, it is quite expensive. However, when you consider that you get a river cruise and optional walking tours it doesn't seem too bad. We didn't have time to do the river cruise or any walking tours so it seems a better idea for those that are in London for a long weekend etc rather than day trippers..

We were on a 'blue route' bus for a while before getting off at Covent Garden, the recorded tour was very good. When we got back to the stop we got on a 'red route' bus with a live guide. I have to say we were both very impressed! Our guide was informative, witty and entertaining. There was only one other family and another couple on the bus when we got on, so the guide simply sat with us and gave us the tour off of the microphone which was nice as it felt more personal. We did the rest of the tour with him before having to get off at Victoria to get on a train home, it's a shame we couldn't use the rest of the stuff on offer.

Overall, although slightly expensive it is worth it. My friend and I defiantly got a feel for London. I would recommend going on the 'red route' and having a live guide as our guide that day was wonderful. I've been trying to think of his name all day, His name was either Jamie, James or Jason. He was young (Mid twenties) and sounded very educated.

We will be back in the Summer!

Emma & Siobhan

We were disappointed with Big Bus tours. We had to wait for over 25 minutes for the first tour bus at the beginning, at one point we were all told we had to walk somewhere else, then they changed their minds. Once we actually got going things improved although of course around Oxford Street the traffic makes for a slow journey. We later had another long wait for a bus, again things seemed to improve as it was the red route with live commentary. However, we had to wait outside a stop near the Ritz for a very long time (having been told to get off the bus and move to the next bus and then moved back to the original bus). What a shambles!

The big bus tour is a great way to get an overview of London - but it could be a whole lot better. We spent three hours in heavy traffic crawling along at snails pace.
Whilst the tour goes near all the great views of London you tended to glimpse them from an awkward angle. For example, we approached Buckingham Palace from the side but rather than going around the roundabout in from of the palace we turned away and thus only saw the end wall!
So with the heavy traffic there was little time to hop on and hop off unless you managed to get a two day ticket.
On board commentary poor and unimaginative - by contrast the included boat trip up the river very enjoyable with an excellent commentary.

I regretted taking the bus tour the entire time I was in London. We spent hours and hours sitting in traffic and listening to the annoying canned commentary and "elevator music". The company advertises two lines, one with live guides, but the live guide buses seemed very few and far between. On my two days on the tour I had to transfer buses multiple times because of issues and each time the bus was completely overcrowded. Almost every time we made a stop we sat on the curb for multiple minutes, even if no one was getting on or off. If you're visiting London and want to see more than the inside of a bus, you'll be much better off getting a day pass for the Underground. I really regret taking this tour because I feel like I missed out on so many things I wanted to do because of sitting on the bus.

Excellent tours, great buses with live or recorded guides.
You get to see things that you won't otherwise and you learn from the guides about the places you see.
Good value for money.
Like the idea of hop-on hop-off at stops/sites.

I was on a recent business trip and my wife came with me and we got her a ticket on the Big Bus Tour to see the sights. She enjoyed riding and listening to the live tour guide and the ability to get off and on when she wanted. She ended up taking the river cruise and decided to take the longer cruise which ate into her time at other sights but she enjoyed. She didnt have any issues waiting for buses. She feels that it would be worth doing a 48 hour pass to have more time, so look for deals on that.

Take this one of the first days you arrive in London. This way you can see what there is that you would like, you can get off and venture inside or just plan the rest of the week by taking the tour. Each bus has earphones and different language for whomever gets on. If you want to sit inside if it's cold you can. If you want to sit up top and outside for better pictures, you can. You can even opt for a 2 days pass, get on and off at different stops. Definitely worth the money!

Interesting tour of London but took more than three hours to complete. Didn't dare hop on and off as no chance of a seat upstairs and queues if you did. We are talking end if Feb bit Summer time Rather expensive at £27 each!!!!!!! Cold unless under cover. Heating at foot level would be a bonus. We did move forward to be under cover but then view is restricted. Operative did try and form a queue for boarding (having had to order an extra bus as there were so many of us but chaos ensued. We were advised that extra bus would be 15 minutes but took at least 40 uncomfortable minutes to come.

With the "selected date" option and the winter 48h bonus, it was only 23 € for two days of traveling and guided tours in London. I saw on tripadvisor that the original bus tour had long waiting times, so I took the Big bus tour. No disappointment here, every 10 to 15 minutes there was a modern bus to take you too the next stop. Nice audio guide, a lot of interesting information and stops at the main attractions in town. So value for money and you see more than taking the subway.

Disappointing was the long trip to get from Harrods back to oxford circus or any other touristic place, more than 1h30 without any interesting stop :( If the big buses just turned around after the Natural history museum and Harrods back to Piccadilly our experience with Big Busses would have been much better. Also at the end of the day it was never clear at what time and where the bus stops and until what time it keeps driving. They just mentioned 4:30 pm. So we were dropped of on place we didn't want to stop at all.

Tip: get up at oxford circus red or blue tour and use it between this stop and buckingham palace, walk by your self past the palace true the park to the stop at piccadilly/ritz and take it towards harrods and natural history, afterwards get of the bus and please do take the subway.

We did the nice river cruise to Greenwich, which is the most efficient if you hop on and hop off at the tower bridge pier. You can take as much as you like within the 48h.

We tried to do one of the walking tours but it was not the day that the guards changed, and the guide wasn't very enthusiastic to show us something else. But I think the changing of the guards with a guide would be better than without.

What better way to see the sights of London than from the top of a double deck bus with a knowledgeable and humerous live guide!
The Red Tour has an English speaking guide and follows a route around all the main attractions and sights of the Cities of London and Westminster whilst the Blue Tour has recorded commentary in 8 languages and additionally takes in other important sights in Kensington and Bayswater.
The ticket is normally valid for 24 hours but we were really fortunate and were given a special offer that extended that to 48 hours at no extra cost and so gave us plenty of time to hop on and off at will to visit some of the attractions we wanted to see close up.
With 4 walking tours and a free river cruise you need to plan your day (or two) wisely if you want to get around to see everything.
Whether a tourist or a local like me who has never got around to following the tourist trail this package is the perfect introduction to London and its fabulous history. Educational, entertaining and very well organised I can heartily recommend The Big Bus as an excellent value day out.

You can get on or off at any of the 25+ stops, though if you want a seat on the top of the bus, you may have to wait a stop or two for people to come down and get off. The Red Tour was live commentary from a guide, who was very knowledgeable and fun to listen to. The tour went all over London, which was a great way to experience numerous attractions London has to offer. It also gave me a better idea of some places I would want to explore on my own. There was a winter special going on, where your ticket was also good for the next day--take advantage of it! Included with your ticket are free walking tours and river cruises; we were only able to do the Harry Potter Walking Tour, which was great! Our guide was so entertaining, and it was a fun experience. Big Bus is a must if you want to see the best London has to offer!

I went on a trip throughout Europe in October 2011. One of our last stops was London. And one of those last stops was The Big Bus Company Walking Ghost Pub Tour. If you buy the site-seeing pass for the bus for the day, the tour is free. Samantha, a super friendly Scotswoman, was our tourguide and I couldn't have asked for a better way to walk through the city! The ghost stories ranged from the scary to the bizzare and she made each stop memorable. Plus the occasional stop at local pubs didn't hurt. What I liked most was going to more "local" pubs than tourist locations. We finished the tour at the Cheshire Cheese which was rebuilt after the great London fire. Tons of history and lot's of good beer.

I recommend everyone to go on this tour!

We were exhausted. We had visited about 10 attractions in the past 48 hours and walked around 15 miles (probably more considering all the walking in the attractions). We were sitting outside Buckingham Palace not wanting to move. The bus tour sounded like a fabulous idea.

We started on the Red Tour which had a live guide. Our guide was very funny and inserted a lot of his commentary, which I appreciated. Some of it was side stories, some were jokes, and some were commentaries on the tour. My favorite line from him was, "Just remember, in London if the sign says it was given to London, that means it was stolen." He was extremely entertaining.

At stop 1 on the red tour, we got off the red bus and got on the blue bus to see the West End. This was an audio guided tour, which was not as good as the guide, but one of the best audio guided tours on a bus I have experienced. I actually really enjoyed this half because we saw a of the city that is not often visited by tourists.

We got off the bus when the blue bus was about the repeat what we did on the red bus. It seems very expensive at first, but afterwards I was extremely satisfied.

Even though we did not take advantage, the ticket includes a river boat tour that will go to Greenwich.

The Big Bus Company tour buses are great for getting around in the touristy areas of London, allowing you to hop off and on any of their numerous buses throughout the day. Lucy is a terrific guide; if you are lucky enough to be on her bus, stay on. She was much better than the two other guides we had. My complaint, however, is with the ticket seller standing on the street in Trafalgar Square. He was a fast talker, jokester, tossing out compliments. After boarding the bus I realized he short-changed me two pounds.

We did the Big Bus "Blue" tour because it covered more area than the "Red" route. We took this tour on our first full day in London. We thought it would be a good way to get our bearings and see as much as possible in one shot. We were very happy with the tour!

It's easy to hop on at any stop, however only a couple of stops sell tickets. The maps that you can pick up in hotel lobbies show you which stops sell tickets.

I'd suggest buying the two day ticket. We ended up using the tour another day to get to the London Eye and wished we had bought the 2 day ticket the first time around.

If it's nice weather I strongly suggest that you sit on the roof top and listen to the audio commentary. ( The Red Tour has live commentary) The audio has just about every language available. We do think that they need to update the audio a bit. The most glaring omission was not mentioning the more recent Royal Wedding when going by Westminster Abbey.

This attraction is well worth the money and was a great way to see a great deal of London in one day.

This was not worth our time, and certianly not the money. Too much time is spent waiting, that once we got on, we didn't want to leave the bus. We grabbed a seat up top on the first bus of the day (on day two). 8AM or so - The stench of urine on the freshly "washed" bus was so strong, that we were eager to move to the open seats on the rear. And in the end it got the better of us, and we only completed the eastern loop.

We purchased a two day pass thinking that we would be using this tour as a way to learn the area of London, and see some sights that maybe just passing by would be enough. It was hard to catch a bus, the ticket agent wanted to get us on one with a guided tour. We settled for a taped narration, which was lackluster.

We did take the included free boat ride from the Tower to Westminster. It had live corny Cockney narration which included a heavy pitch for a tip on disembarking.

Next time I want to mix urine and transportation I'll take the tube, saving time and money.

We did the Big Bus tour in London on our last day, and I wished we had done it on our first. It really does give you a great overall feel for the city and lots of spots to hop on and hop off.
We took the Red tour and liked it just fine. The pretaped commentary was interesting. Sitting on top is very nice, but not necessary to enjoying the tour.
I didn't try to ride the bus past 4:00, so I'm not sure what time the tours stop although marketed as 24 hours I think that is a miscommunication that the buses run 24 hours and I don't believe they do. Good question to ask if you were getting on in the afternoon or hopped off at a stop late in the day. We had previously taken the same boat tour that is included for free with the Big Bus tour and had paid around 12 pounds just for that. We paid 27 pounds each for the bus tour, so with the added boat tour and ability to hop on and off I found the value to be good. I liked it so much that I thought if I brought a group back I would recommend it to them as an introduction to London.

We took the Big Bus tour of London recently. The ticket agent sold us tickets for the London Eye as well. The tour was nice -- a parky and engaging tour guide provided an informative tour of the city, although there were almost as many references to recent movies as there were to historic sites! Nonetheless, it was a comfortable, safe and well-thought out tour.

We had serious problems with the extra attraction tickets. First, the arrangements (preferred access to the London Eye and shorter lineups) did not materialize. We also had to return one of the three tickets we purchased -- something we were told was easily done. What a nightmare followed. Rude and unhelpful employees soured us on the company. Returning the ticket, it turns out, requires a written submission. More to the point, the objectionable conduct by the employees speaks volumes about their commitment to customer service.

You have choices for your London Tours. Based on our experience, I would recommend that you look elsewhere than Big Bus.

I waited for a decent weather forecast and bought a 24 hr ticket on Sunday morning. There was some effort made to up-sell various London attractions but the rep could tell right away I wasn't going to bite.

Managed to get seat on the upper deck with no problems. The first guide (Samatha from Glasgow) was knowledgable and entertaining - a perfect mix. She knew her history well and was able to adapt her spiel on the fly as our bus was redirected because of the the London Half-Marathon which was being held on this same morning.

I decided to take the entire tour non-stop just to get oriented in London. The tour was good for that purpose. Hop-on, hop-off sounds good but there is a real risk you will be stuck on the lower deck when you decide to get back on at one of the more popular.
stops.

There was a change of guide at Green Park and unfortunately we got saddled with a lack lustre gent with a Midlands accent. I should have heeded the advice of others and got off and waited for the next Red Route bus as this guy gave a patchy commentary and was more interested in telling his own schoolyard puns and awful jokes.

The frequency of Big Bus red route buses appeared to be fine - about every 20 minutes. I decided not to take the included Thames River Cruise but I probably should have as I heard it was pretty good.

Overall, did I get my 27 pounds worth? Well, probably not. It certainly is over-priced - but hey, welcome to London. Big Bus was certainly was not a rip-off and passengers seemed a little bit more satisfied than those on the competing Original Bus Tour which was not coping quite so well with the traffic redirections.

Whilst visiting familty, we only had one day sightseeing in (that) London so decided to do the tourist thing and go on an open topped bus tour. I must admit to being nervous about being disappointed for our £60 but the whole thing was excellent. Did all the big sights (only one misssed was the front of Buckingham Palance - must have been restricted access as we saw everything else?) and were on for 2 hours. The highlight was our guide (Malcolm) who was very knowledgable, spoke about a wide range of topics, threw in plenty of literature quotes, pointed out a myriad of sights (both big and small), was full of tips (such as which seats to buy at the theatre) and above all was absolutely hillarious. Highly recommended.

Top tip 1 - your tickets are valid for 24 hours and you can go round as many times as you like on all 3 routes. So, if you set off in the afternoon, you can do another tour in the morning of the next day.
Top tip 2 - you get a free boat trip thrown in

In all fairness you can't expect much from these companies even though they do charge a small fortune :) but I do have to say I think Original tour has to win this one. More buses, better guides and cleaner. Big Bus staff were very nice and helpful though and at the end of the day they both go through the same route and London is so beautiful it all makes up for it. And yes the guides have British accents but... We are in Britain ;) I think it adds to the charm :) I'm not sure if original tours would be that much better but it's personal choice at the end of the day and all I cam do is suggest going with Original.

I initially thought the price for the Big Bus tour was quite high in comparison with similar day tickets to 'hop on, hop off' bus tours in US cities, but I soon realised the Big Bus Company London tour was excellent value for money. London works well for a bus tour like this, attractions are close together and of course are just full of interesting and amusing history for the guides to impart. I did most of the available tour on a Saturday and was surprised that the traffic didn't really hold us up too much.

The few small children I saw didn't seem that impressed, but I would highly recommend this tour to adults who did not have much time to spend in the capital; a quick way to get an idea of where the key attractions are, then decide which ones you want to visit.

The three buses I caught during the day were well maintained and clean. There was always at least one member of staff on the ground at each stop to answer any questions and, unlike day-to-day travel on 'normal' buses, the ride was always smooth!

The bus tour is like a lotto. If the live guide is good, then you are going to learn and enjoy. However, they change guides at some points and there are huge differences in the quality of guide. I would prefer a recorded guide over a boring live (maybe not Alive!) tour.

What I liked most in the Big Bus Tour is that it is very well organized. They have staff in every point. There are three different tours (red, blue or green). Green is useless btw. Most of all, I love the walking tours. Phil, also known as Dobey, was a real Harry Potter superfan so he did the tour with so much enthusiasm. I liked him so much, I did not mind giving a good tip. Kevin, who was our guide in the Beatles wallking tour was so lively. He was able to make us sing, wave, do crazy things with his enthusiasm. These two walking tours are already included in the price of the Big Bus Tour. How good deal is that? For that reason, I think people should at least be willing to hand some tips to the guides. It is a way of showing appreciation for good work.

Phil and Kevin of the Big Bus Walking Tours - thank you and keep up the good work. My son adores both of you and will always remember you with fondness.

Excellent Way to see London, Open top double decker bus. Hop on and off within your timed ticket ( usually 24 to 48 hours ) at any venue you choose. Commentary via head phone ( new in packet ) in various languages. Bring camera , comfy shoes and do not be in a hurry! We found this to be fantastic value for money.

The hop on and off part of the tour is what caught my eye. It is the only tour in London who offers this option and it really makes a difference; I would hop off to see attractions and hop back on and continue the tour route. And there is lots of stops all around the city to catch the buses from. The tour goes through the typical, famous London landmarks as well as many others that a tourist wouldn't have known about. And the drivers are nice enough to even drive by landmarks slow enough to capture nice pictures! The tour guides are full of information and are really friendly. If possible, sit up on the second floor of the bus; it has the best views and you're able to hear the tour guide better from up there.

We did this on our first day in London having just arrived from Australia, it was great way to see London to start our holiday. We got off at the London Eye and saw London from there, we then hoped back on and completed the bus tour back to where we had picked it up. We got to see so much and while we did not get off much, it was a great way to get an idea where thing was and to see things that we had not planned to see. It is worthwhile and I would do it again.

We only had 2 days in London so we decided to see the sights by using the big bus tours. We chose the red line with a live guided English commentary, our guide Jade was absolutely fantastic! She got the whole bus singing and was full of interesting facts!

I would recommend doing the big bus tour if you are only in London for a short amount of time as you see all the sights! Because it is hop on and hop off you can choose places you would like to spend a bit more time. There is a river cruise and walking tours included so it is very good value for money!

Smashing! Great bus tour plus the convenience of getting on and off all over London (and I mean everywhere!). Tour guides are knowledgable and entertaining. Included are a choice of 3 walking tours (loved the Beatles Tour through Soho backstreets) and a boat ride on the Thames.

wow what can one say about the BIG BUS TOUR COMPANY, Brilliant, We were a party of nine, Family, and friends from Australia visiting us, In age we ranged from 7-72 we had four days to show them London, The 7 & 72 year olds found walking from one attraction to another tiring, So we all got on the big bus tour, absoulely 1st rate, A very good comentary throughout, and hopping on and off the bus we were able to see all the attractions and nobody tired and weary.
A big plus was the helpfullness and very friendliness of all the staff, They made you feel very comfortable in their presence, Thank you all.
We shall certainly recommend you to all family and friends visiting London.

I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND THIS TOUR COMPANY TO ANYONE!
I took the Big Bus tour on a Saturday afternoon in January. I took the Blue line with the pre-recorded commentary. I picked up at the Paddington Station stop. First we stopped at Marble Arch for almost ten minutes. Then we stopped at the next stop at Madame Tussad's so they could try to lure more customers. It was below freezing outside and they turned off the bus and left the doors open for almost a half and hour! It was freezing! When I asked how long we'd be waiting they told me 'just a few minutes' and 'this is the only stop because we start from here'. Thankfully we were allowed to get on/off the bus, which we did at Piccadilly. We picked up at 3:30pm close to Trafalgar Square. Unfortunately the bus we got on had the commentary slow, so we didn't know what we saw until after we passed it! I missed The PALACE! We stopped again for 10 minutes at Victoria Station where they told me if I was interested in the palace I should 'go take a walk', but I told them I just wanted to get back to Paddington. The bus returned to Marble Arch where they told us to get off! They didn't say anything about not making the whole bus route (back to Paddington where we started)!!!! NOT ONE ANNOUNCEMENT FOR THE TWO HOURS WE WERE ON THE BUS!
I was quite upset about having to try to find a tube station, pay my SIX GBPs for a tube ticket, and try to find my way back to my hotel in time to get to a show.
I didn't even bother to use the ticket the next day or the other tours, I was so disappointed in their services.

We had a great day on board the 'big bus' the guides are excellant and as well as being informative had a great sense of humour. Included in our tickets was a trip down the Thames, that too was well worth it and the guide was very funny. It is such a great way to see London being able to get off and on the bus as often or as little as you want. Definately recommend and would definately go on board again.

If it wasnt for this bus tour we would not have seen half the attractions, we used the guided tour bus and the personal guides were excellent, the tour included a trip on the Thames which our two children thought was exciting also.The tour guides supplied us with so much imformation it gave us a history of london as well.
Wewould definitely recommend any one coming to London, to use this attraction as you can hop on and off at some many different attractions.
well worth the money spent.

We just got back from London (Dec 1-2) and the first impression of this tour wasn't so great. The first round of stops was very long because everyone had to purchase their tickets before boarding so each stop took about 15-20 minutes. Don't use this as a mode of getting around the city because it will take too much time. We really enjoyed the red bus commentary tours, the guides had lots of information that you probably wouldn't get anywhere else and each guide was different (we ended up repeating parts of the tour and got different, interesting info each time).

We definitely took advantage of the walking tours (changing of the guard and the ghost tour), both were very interesting and well worth it. The guides weren't looking for tips or and weren't bothered when we were the only ones who showed up because the weather was pretty harsh and essentially had a private tour. The guides on the streets were also very helpful. We were there during a student revolt with half the city being shut down and one of the tour guides we met earlier in the day found us on the street and helped us get around and had awesome recommendations.
We also took the free boat tour, twice. We sat on a different side each way which was also a great way of seeing the city and you still could get some great pictures from the boat even from inside :)

I'd definitely recommend going with the Big Bus tour company especially in the winter with the 2 days for the price of 1 offer. But be aware that the Original Bus company probably has a 2:1 bus ratio over the Big Bus company which can be frustrating when sitting at a stop, but the walking tours, boat tours and commentary tour is way more preferable.

We just got back from London (Aug 20, 2010) where we made the mistake of taking the Big Bus tour. Almost no redeeming qualities. We waited long times for the Big Bus busses, I noticed that at least 3 original tour buses would pass us before a Big Bus would arrive. We were on three or four different buses and the commentary on all of them was uniformly stupid and too loud. Apparently designed for people with only a grade school education. The tickets cost 26 pouinds each--way more than it was worth. The only somewhat redeeming feature was that you get a boat cruise on the Thames included--and that was much more entertaining than the bus tour. Don't use this company. There are several other options.

We took the Big Bus Company on a recent trip to London as we were only there for a short time. We were dropped at St. Pauls where we looked around before returning to the drop off point. While there three of the buses passed us and another driver indicated he would not stop for us. We went to the drop off point as indicated on the brochure for St. Pauls. We waited for 45 minutes, during which time we didn't see any buses. After ringing the company we were told that the stop we were at was not being used that day. At no stge before this were we informed of the change in stop. There was no explaination as to why we were dropped at a stop where we could not be picked up. As a 'hop-on, hop-off' service this was madness. We were given complicated directions to where the bus should pick us up but again there was no service.
I e-mailed the company to complain about the service but I have no gotten even an apology in reply. Awful service!

You would think that a hop-on hop-off bus tour would be the ideal way for a visitor with limited mobility to enjoy London. Think again: not unless you just want to ride round and round all day.
One problem is that the stops are not always very near to the attractions.
Tower of London: it's a 200-yard walk from the bus to the entrance. And the same back again, of course.
Apart from their well-practiced patter, staff were not always well-informed, or even helpful. It varied. Burlington Arcade? Not a clue where it was, or which was the best stop. Result? An (incorrect) guess followed by a long and tiring treck.
Change from one loop to another? Same stop for both? Not necessarily! And more information and guidance from staff on this matter would be welcome - especially when routes have been altered owing to circumstances.
The map they provided was rather lacking in detail. Guests would be well-advised to use a more detailed street map as well.
The commentaries were of varying interest and quality, light on facts and heavy on personal opinion. Staff would do well to experience the high-quality commentaries we enjoyed on a similar and much better-organised tour of San Francisco.
At £26 the tour was not cheap, but would have been worth it if everything had been right.
The ticket also included a Thames Cruise. I have to say that the voyage from the Tower of London to Westminster was a delight, with a top-quality informative commentary. Full marks for that, and the staff here were brilliant!

I am a young London professional, and I had my mother and sister in town for a few days. They've never done a sightseeing tour of the city before, so I thought it would be fun to get the Big Bus, as it would be a good way to see all the highlights in one go. Turns out that was a bad decision.

In the beginning of the tour there was no commentary from the earphones, because of a problem with the bus. We had to go down and wait for another bus, which arrived shortly after. Then at some point after Baker Street the tour changed direction because of some engineering works, and we drived to Regent Street from a totally different route than the one on the map. The driver wasn't happy to explain that to me, instead telling me to 'just look at the map', which didn't make sense anyway.

The worst of all came in the afternoon, when we got the bus from Tower Bridge to Victoria. Somewhat confused with the map, as we hopped-in I asked the driver if this bus is the right one to Victoria. The driver's reply was "WHAT? YOUR NAME IS VICTORIA?". I asked him again, and he replied "well, you look funny for someone that goes by the name of Victoria" (I am a male by the way). I asked him again, he pretended he couldn't listen, instead embarking on a half-minute monologue in a Brixton slang, making fun of me while my mother and my sister were looking bemused at the sad incident. He finally told me "yes, this is the one to Victoria" but it was too late.. My day was totally ruined by then.

I don't know if the guy was on crack, nor do I care. If I wanted to experience this kind of behavior I would have taken the night-bus from Elephant and Castle to Brixton. Spending 26 quid and being treated like that is unacceptable. Never again.

My Canadian Cousin came to the UK for the first time in 30 years and we decided to spend a couple of days in London seeing the sights but on a very restricted budget. Initially the £25 ticket price for 24 hours seemed very expensive (£21 is pre-booked on internet) but in retrospect we had excellent value for money and would never have seen all the sights we did, had we not bought these tickets.

We bought the ticket at say 4pm on Friday and so it expired at 4pm the next day. We jumped on an off the bus at different sights on many occasions and the ticket price also included free city boat cruises down the Thames, which really made our day.

One word of advice though, the buses with a red sign on the front come with an English speaking tour guide, the buses with blue signs come with an earphone system with which you can select the automated tour guide info in various languages. Check when you get on the bus, which direction it is going in, as we did get confused by this. Being English speaking, we actually preferred the English tour guide on the mic, as he added a bit of humour but were less impressed with the American tour guide who appeared to think her audience was American and kept cross referrencing and comparing things to the States. On the City Cruises the guides were fantastic, using real British irony and sarcastic humour to brighten up their repartie whilst being very informative at the same time - but then maybe you have to appreciate the British humour to get it - nonetheless a good deal of the audience seemed to enjoy it too.

All in all, if you just sit on the bus as we did the first time, the round trip took about 3 hours, we saw all the major sites and ticked off what we wanted to get off and see the next day - well worth the money and wouldn't hesitate to use it next time I go to London.

My wife and I loved the bus line, and thought that it was a great way to see London. We had both been to London several times before, and were able to learn about things that we were previously not aware of. The live tours are totally worth while as you are able to ask the guide all of the questions that you would like. We also enjoyed taking the boat to Greenwich. The boat ride is included with the bus tour. You can save money if you book in advance with their web site.

I think the Big Bus is great. My wife and I used our tickets to the max, we went on two of the walking tours (guard change and the pub one) used the bus to hop and off and even went on a boat trip. Now I am not saying we did not have any difficulties (like traffic and hard to understand Russian guide) but it was the best £48 I have spent in a long time.

p.s. to all the people who said it was bad, give them a second chance

I’ve only just recently moved to London and am not quite a pro at tourist attractions yet, so when I had family coming to visit for the weekend we decided to do the Big Bus Tour. We chose Big Bus over the Original Tour because they had live commentary instead of the audio headsets. Well, this isn’t true for ALL routes, only the red line. We unknowingly joined the blue line tour at Piccadilly, so we hopped off at the next stop to catch the red.

The first (and only) place we got off at was Covent Garden. When we went back to board the bus, we saw a few other people waiting along with the rep from Big Bus. We waited. And waited. And waited. And more and more people joined the horde. The rep told us that there was apparently some march happening around Trafalgar, and that people were blocking the street and none of the buses could get through. This excuse seemed fair initially, until the Original Tour buses made stops where we were waiting, one right after another... Seeing as how both companies generally follow the same route, it was a bit hard to believe that their buses could manage to get through yet Big Bus couldn’t. I think we ended up waiting for about 45 min. before the bus finally came.

When the bus finally did arrive, naturally there were loads of people waiting to board so we got stuck on the bottom level where you can’t see anything. We managed to get to the upper deck after a few stops, but the guide doing the commentary was awful. She has a very thick accent (not English, not sure what) and felt the need to basically scream into the microphone. I had no idea what she was saying most of the time so I can guarantee that my 7-year old niece was equally clueless.

The bus tours aren’t exactly cheap at 24 GBP for adults and 12 GBP for kids. I’d suggest saving your money and taking a do-it-yourself tour. Figure out which sites you want to see and then just use the Tube instead. I’m sure you’ll have a much better—and cheaper—experience.

Well, let me start off by saying that we bought this bus trip probably more for the walking tours and river trip than the actual bus tour.

We bought our tickets at 6pm on our first night in and joined the Ghost and Gas lamp tour. (Not that it got dark at all - it stays light so late in July.) The gentleman who took us on our walking tour was a proud London native who had a good sense of Humor. It was a great way to get acquainted with the city. The tour lasted about 3 hours if I recall correctly and had a few stops at pubs along the way. The walking tour ends pretty far away from Trafalgar square, but the guide ensures that you know the correct tube routing to get you back to where you need to go. (Tube in London is very expensive compared to Paris Metro!)

The next morning we walked over and participated in the Royal London walk. Our guide was also a slightly older Brit with a rather proper manner. He was a great guide and we really enjoyed this city walking tour. He got us to two different locations to watch the guard. Though we did not see the changing of the guard from the front of Buckingham, we had a front row view of the new and old guards changing that was phenomenal, and much better than sitting with thousands of people in front of Buckingham. Once you see the new guard form, you need to double step to the second viewing area but it was a perfect view. This tour lasted about two hours.

After that we got on the red line tour. We went a few stops with a live commentary guide who was okay, but nothing special. Then we had to get off two stops later because that route ended. Low and behold we got on the bus with who better than - our guide from the night before. He remembered us and welcomed us again. His commentary was jovial, interesting and wonderful. We stayed with him for most of the remainder of the loop, but alas we got off at Tower of London, did that, then the London Eye and the river cruise (which was nice enough). Our 24 hours was up after that, but they still let us on the bus at 6:45pm to finish the last 5 stops without an extra charge...the bus driver did not seem to care. The final guide we had was once again, informative, but her Ukrainian accent made it a bit tough to understand.

All in all this 24 Pound per person tour was packed with value and I think since we ran into great guide, our tours were great.

I did notice that the two bus companies are rather competitive in getting people to buy their competing products. I of course did not really see any of their guides, BUT did overhear the guide for their walking tour at our changing of the guard and he sounded like he was going through the motions, not near the energy of our guide.

I think all in all, you experience will differ depending on the guides you get, on the bus but we really liked the walking tours.

The Big Bus Company is definitely the BEST way to see London. I took the bus tour on March 25th, 2008 expecting it to be just a typical drive with some typical guide, anticipating that he would have the enthusiasm of a two-toed sloth. I was happy to be proven wrong.

It was a cloudy and windy first day in London for my group of four, and the weather was already reinforcing the dreariness the city is known for. Not exactly the ideal day to take a tour, but you can't really blame anyone for that. With limited time to spend in London (5 days), we were ultimately at the mercy of nature's elements. Besides, it was predetermined to take the Big Bus Tour even after reading the reviews about it.

After doing some online research, viewing the online website, and contacting the company via email about minor details, Big Bus made it tremendously easy to find the nearest tour stops with respect to the place I was staying. I stayed at the Strand Palace Hotel and the bus stop was about 1-2 minutes away, walking distance.

Not knowing what to do when we got there, we were quickly greeted and aided by a friendly street representative. She gave us vital information about the Big Bus Company and told us about special offers going on at the time. She was extremely helpful as we would have been completely lost without her. Tickets can be sold at the stops if you're the spontaneous type. The price of a bus ticket was fair given that there was a 24-hr time limit on them. Our special offer was a free river tour for purchasing a ticket, but it may vary depending on the time of year.

So, my group waits anxiously for the "red line" which the friendly street representative highly recommended. This was the live commentary line and comes every 15 minutes. I remember she informed us of a blue and green line, but those were prerecorded guides. Not a really personable way to take a tour, but that's just me. So far, the customer service and personal relations were quite impressive, hopefully the tour could match it.

The tour itself lasts about an hour and a half, maybe a little longer. I suggest sitting on the second level of the bus because that is where the tour guide is, and also there will be tall buildings and structures that are better observed and admired with an open view. On some parts of the tour, the bus driver actually slows down the bus and traffic just so tourists can have brilliant photo ops. Very accommodating.

Our tour guide was remarkably energetic and funny, even on such a gloomy day. She was very informative and she added a few tidbits that one probably wouldn't find in any history books or documentaries. I don't want to spoil this for any would-be tourists, but I like Winston Churchill even more.

Our guide gladly took the time to get familiar with guests and make them feel welcome. I'm from California, and we live and breath tourism. So there are certain characteristics that need to stand out in a guide for an attraction to be not only successful, but enjoyable as well. I personally felt that our guide met and exceeded those characteristics.

Like the street representative, our guide was extremely helpful. There wasn't a question she couldn't answer regarding where we should stop and where we needed to go. But that just tells us that the Big Bus Company trains their personnel very well.

I went on the bus with a mindset that I wouldn't have a good time because the day was so dreary. If you're the daring type, and you deem it necessary to sit on the second level while it's raining, the tour guide will brave the weather with you, and even offer you a complimentary raincoat.

Overall I got to meet wonderful Londoners, toured an absolutely beautiful and historic city, and most important - created everlasting memories I will cherish for as long as I live. And I couldn't have done so without such a fine company and the friendly faces who made it worthwhile.

Thanks for taking the time to read.

There was almost always a guide at one of the stops to help us choose where we were going. Got to know some of the guides who were lively and who were always happy to run into us for a second or third time. Used the bus as our main transportaion in London -and My Mom is 70 years old. we both loved it!!
Thanks Big Bus!!!!

We prebooked tickest for the big Bus before leaving Australia. We joined the bus at Trafalgar Square and it took 45Mins before we were able to get upstairs. The bus was very old and whilst we could finaly see somthing when we got upstairs we could not hear the comentary. In fact we more able to hear the comentary from Original Bus following us. Added to the inability to hear we also had noisy breakes on our bus.

The trip took almost 3 hours to complete and the majority of time was spent idling in a trafic jam. We had to get off the bus at Green Square and change to another bus as the one we were on was stopping for a rest. This all took more time and we lost our top floor seats. We got off at Hamleys toy store and then caught the tube and walked. Don't waste your money on the Big Bus in London!

We loved the hop on hop off Big Bus tours of London. The buses were so frequent and the commentary was so helpful. It's a great thing to do early in your visit to familiarise yourself with all of London's landmarks. Brilliant!

The Big Bus Company Tour was fantastic. I don't know why some people have complained about the service - but we were 12 people on the bus and the quality of tour was A1.

The tour took us through all the important landmarks in the city, the tour guide was good, spoke from experience.

The Thames boat cruise was ok, its not a big deal really. Get down at Hayes Galleria for sure - lovely place to sip some coffee. The H.M.S. Belfast is docked there - so you can quickly take a round of the ship. It fires its cannons at 1 pm - so try and time it so that you can be there while its happening.

We had the option of the Original Sightseeing Tour - but this one was cheaper (we got a group discount) and is most certainly recommended.

Our flight was cancelled so we had to cancel our trip. I notifed Big Bus Tours 2 weeks in advance to see if I could get a refund for 4 tickets but they said no.

Look at your options for bus tours before you book in case you need to cancel.

This hop-on, hop-off sightseeing tour bus is not a sightseeing tour bus at all. We was stuck on the bus for 2 hours and saw nothing in the way of London landmarks or places of interest. There was no tour guide on the bus, but was given a pair of earplugs 1 hour after the trip began, which again was a total waste of time as the only thing i heard was music and no commentary of anything we drove passed. It is more a service bus than a tour bus, and a very expensive £41 each service bus. I would advise anybody thinking of going on the bus to think again and spend their hard earned cash on some other tourist attraction as this one particular attraction is not what is advertised and a very very expensive service bus.
Really fun day out and had a great time exploring London on the bus. Would recommend to anyone visiting London. Helps that it was a nice day!
Loved this. Got to see the most popular sites. Able to get off at any spot see the sites at that location and get back on to go to next. Free headphones for spoken tour free wifi.
walking tour by Julia was excellent at Buckingham palace and city of london tour and we request bus tours to have live tour guide personnel to provide live commentary in buses also .
Naz was so knowledgeable and helpful in us having a great day sightseeing in London. The narration was great and the route very convenient. 💯 great experience!

We booked the bus so we could easily get from tourist destination to tourist destination, while also hearing the tour guide (even if it was a recording). My favorite part was the boat tour on the Thames! We had a real live person as tour guide, and he was excellent!

The commentary was more suitable for children and only 50% of what we could see was even mentioned. Most of the time music was playing with no information. Expected more from a tour that costs £36 each.

Went on the Halloween bus tour tonight at 8pm, Sexy Nick (named by himself not me) was brilliant, had everyone’s attention for the whole journey as well as being very funny was also extremely informative his knowledge on the history of the City was outstanding you could tell he wasn’t reading straight from a script and that he seemed to be enjoying it plus he could sing as well.

Oh and Ted the bus driver was also great.

We purchased the 24 hour bus pass. We saw the entire city of London. It was an easy way to get around the city and see the big London sights! I would suggest getting the app because the bus stop signs were not up to date. We had to run after a bus to catch it because we were just going off of the physical bus signs. Thank goodness there was traffic so we made the sprint to the next stop. The river cruise part of the tour was amazing. We had boat captains who believed in doing live commentary and they were hilarious! They were very knowledgeable about the city. This was a great option to breaking up a long day of walking around. The tweens loved being able to relax on the bus and just listen!

Excellent bus tour.
I did Jack the Ripper tour and Julia our guide was fantastic.
She made it so interesting and her knowledge was very good. It was so informative. I CD an highly recommended this walking tour.

Look no further! This company runs a fantastic tour, they are easy to locate and are very friendly! The guide that took us to the changing of the guards knew all of the tricks for the best experience and photos

1) It is far too expensive
2) Too much music when there was no commentary
3) Some of the commentary was ‘too light’
4) Most of the time we sat in a traffic jam
5) We passed some important buidings but no information given about them
6) The earphone for one of us did not work so we had to share one
Good trip for a familiarisation with the history of London to its present day. Recommend for those who want a short fam-tour.
Our kids loved riding on top of the bus and seeing all the sites. It was so convenient to be able to hop on and off throughout London.
We had a great time with great service!! We would definitely book again if we return. They did a great job!

If the site would allow for a (-1) review of the company this company would qualify. The driver seemed to have gotten lost, circled an entire area 3 times stoped the bus and was told then by his supervisor that all passengers will get off and can wait for the next bus in 30-40 min…when I confronted them them became belligerent seeming to threaten me with physical violence. I’m guessing this is probably a common practice with this company especially towards Americans whom they appear to have issues with as well. When traveling to a foreign country one would expect at least to be treated with common courtesy in the same way I would treat anyone else regardless of their country of origin. I would caution any Americans traveling to London to avoid this tour company. Their lack of professionalism as company and poor business standards will result in their eventual bankruptry…. American‘s be aware of this company…unfortunately these individuals lack any type of manners….poor reflection of the people of the city
The tour visited all the right spots but the audio guide was pretty bad. It was more music and slapstick comedy than actual interesting facts and history
Excellent network of routes and staff super helpful. Narration is good and amusing. If going, try to book the bus and the river cruise. You'll get to see everything.
