What a great experience we had on this tour! Saw all of the sights, easy to navigate, and just a simply smooth ride all along. Thats not the reason for this review. The reason for this review is this.. I was so excited about being in London that I was filming the whole thing on my GoPro. I was at the top and front of the bus, had my GoPro setup for a sick Timelapse and got off at Big Ben... and yes... I left my GoPro on the top still filming... I didn't realize I left it until about 15min later.

I went to the nearest BB stop and asked the person if anyone has found a GoPro on the bus. They said no one had at that point. Now at this moment I'm not very optimistic about getting it back. Being American, I'm thinking that if someone found a $400 dollar camera on a bus in another country they would snag it for themselves. The sweet lady at the BB stop told me I could email in at the end of the day when the drivers come in for the night. So I did, not thinking much would come of it but sure enough I got an email back stating they had it!! Unfortunately, I was going to Paris the next morning and then flying home the day after and wouldn't be able to pick it up.

I was communicating with Marcelo Melo (shout out to this guy he is the best) and he helped me arrange FedEx to come and get the camera. Marcelo boxed it up for me and FedEx picked it up on a Thursday and it was deliver to my house in Texas on that Monday..

I cannot praise BB enough and the employees we dealt with over there. They were simply the best and nicest people we met in London. Thank you so much BB and especially Marcelo!!!

It’s certainly a convenient way to get around and see the sites. In the end however, we ended up doing more walking from site to site. For us it was still worth it to have the audio commentary while we were on the bus.

The bus was dangerously over crowded with people stood throughout the aisle and on the stairs. Every bus stop had at least 40 people trying to board a safety hazard it was crazy and finally decided enough was enough and we got off never to return. Not sure what was going on but the sales team were having a ball selling tickets. It was fraudulent trading taking customers money this way. The sales guy even gave us a deal “ because we were English “ what a joke. Stay well clear !!

The 3 bus routes and a river cruise cover a huge amount of see sights and the ticket works for 24 hours! Loved it!
The tour guide on the radio was poor and rare. Instead of it, it was mostly music, the same few songs over and over.

Give this one a miss! A complete waste of time. The recorded commentary gave very little information. It was like a kid’s show with silly theatrics! Pretending they had a “time machine” to get historical figures to comment was very annoying! Mostly music, the same songs over and over too! The Thames “cruise” was a farce! We passed Downing St and no mention was made of it at all! I regret not checking Tripadvisor for reviews before wasting money for 4 tickets! No comparison to other Hop On Hop Off tours we’re done in various other countries!
It helps to get familiar with the area and do site seeing in a comfortable way, no crowded sidewalks, great for pictures

As a tour guide myself I don't usually do Hop On Hop Off buses but I was travelling with my parents who are a bit older so it made sense to see the city this way. We did the Big Bus Hop on hop off in London 48 hour ticket because it allowed us to do all the buses, the river tour AND the Jack the Ripper walking tour.

The bus option was a nice way to get around the city without too much walking, the river tour was lovely, but the Jack the Ripper tour was what I was really excited for. The canned tour commentary on the bus was mildly useful but I've always preferred a more interactive experience, I was not disappointed with our Jack the Ripper tour guide Nick.

As a true crime fan I know a bit more than the average person, not a Ripperologist but I know a few things. I had just recently enjoyed a podcast called "Bad Women: Ripper Retold" by Hallie Rubenhold, which looks at the Ripper's crimes not focusing on who infamous serial killer was but rather who the victims were. In essence given these women back their identities and their dignity. I was worried that the Ripper tour would focus on the Ripper and paint all the women as simply nameless victims.

Nick and I chatted as the group gathered for the tour and he was very friendly and welcoming. Our tour of 8 was peopled with a variety of folks, including a family with 2 kids under the age of 12, older retired folks, and myself (a slightly expectant tour guide). Once we had everyone gathered we set off to follow in the footsteps of the notorious murderer. I was delighted as Nick let us know that he was not there to glorify or guess who Jolly Jack was, rather he wanted to focus on the conditions of Whitechapel, the society of the time, and the women themselves.

At the tour company I work for I am a trainer for new guides and Nick was so good that if he were to apply I would happily hire him. He is engaging, knowledgable, a masterful storyteller. I was so impressed with him and his ability to navigate delicate subject matter with 2 young kids on the tour. Nick was funny at times but also serious about the subject matter he was dealing with. There was a sincere passion for his craft and a love for Whitechapel both in the past and the present.

Honestly the bus tour was fine, the river tour was lovely but the Jack the Ripper tour was the highlight of my 5 day trip to London.
Great way to experience London for the first time. We liked it so much that we plan on doing it again before we leave in a few days, and doing the Big Bus when we go to Dublin.
Great way to see the city. Really appreciated that there were Big Bus staff in some stops. They helped with information on stops and timings . This was great to ensure that I got value for money.
Poor audio experience. Tried to be humorous vs informative. Announcements were unclear so we missed getting off bus for sight seeing. Walking tour on our own was a better option.

Very poorly organized. No clear directions given for bus stops to hop on at or hop off at along the route. A couple of unfriendly and unhelpful bus drivers which made finding our way around very difficult. Last minute changes at the bus stops, which made it all very confusing, especially considering that the City of London is very busy. We got lost several times and did not know where we were supposed to pick up the bus after we got off. There are no marked bus stops along the route. Do not recommend this for anyone who is depending on a smooth run.

We were on the Red Line Big Bus Tour in London, England on September 24th, and were most pleased with the performance of our live host Steve for our visit.
Steve was extremely knowledgeable on the facts, and his delivery was the best !!!
His performance was far superior to the normal recorded dialogue that you get via head phones, and the ability to ask him questions was terrific !!
I recommend that you add more live guides to your fleet in the future.
Bus is convenient but do not recommend. Bus was dirty and guides were not nice. In London, it is actually easier to get around on the Tube.

We were lucky to be apart of the Jack the Ripper walking tour with the wonderful guide Julia. She was knowledgeable, friendly and engaging.

The experience was approx two hours and offered a unique take; focusing on the stories of the victims and offering a few theories on potential suspects.

As an avid fan of the true crime genre, I came out of this tour with a heap of new information and was blown away by Julia’s knowledge. Her theories made me change my preconceived ideas about Jack the Ripper.

Would give this tour and the entire service 6 stars if i could! Definitely worth the ticket price. A must see for anyone interested in the history of East London and Whitechapel. You will not be disappointed!
Worth every penny! The drivers were great, the routes were perfect and the attendants at the stops were awesome, especially “big Steve”.
A great day out. We did 2 walking tours with Julia including the Jack The Ripper walk. Very informative and fun too. Julia was great and very knowledgeable. Definitely recommend
The bus tour was great, but the best was the Jack the Ripper tour we had from Julia! She was fun and very knowledgeable. We would take another tour from her!
My son and I had a great time with Nick. Lot of information to soak in. Nick is amazing. Very knowledgeable and engaging. Wish we had more time.
Everything went really well. Staff on and off the bus was very helpful and courteous. Great narration too. Busses were clean and the whole experience was well worth it.

This experience was the best way to see London for the first time! The staff were so amazing. I was on four different buses and they were all amazing! One of the buses had faulty audio and they took it out of service, immediately! I'm looking forward to returning and getting back on the "Big Bus"!

Recently rode the Big Bus across two days while in London. I found the sound track informative and useful. Being able to "hop off" and then "hop on" across London was very helpful way to travel and visit sites.

First: If you are interested in the history of the sites in London, give this tour a miss. The narration is flippant, petty and overall most annoying.

AND: We boarded our bus on the day the late Queen was being moved from one location in London to another. We were advised by the tour operator that there would be a couple of diversions but that it would not have a significant impact on our route and that we would still have time for the river portion of our tour. WRONG. We spent four hours on the bus and barely made it half-way through our route, most of which took us down small insignificant streets. The majority of the time we were at a dead-stop in traffic snarls.

The pier access for the river portion of our tour was completely closed so even had there been time we would not have been able to do it.

When we asked for an opportunity to reschedule our tour our request was denied. It was a massive waste of precious vacation time and money.

Excellent tour, nick was the best guide- funny carismatic and with a lot of knowledge and interestinc
facts!!! Really recommended
The walking tours with Julia were the absolute best thing we’ve done in London so far. Super fun, informative, and just a really great time!
the tour not bad but the narration was annoying with the lady irritating and virtual no information at most of the important sites second time in London and will not use this tour again

Visited London for 3 days/2 nights and spent a fair amount of that time on the Big Bus Tours plus the 30 minute river cruise (we did Tower of London to Westminster). We had a 2 day premier family ticket and it worked out well for us.

We did some of the main red route on Thursday although it was a bit of false start as our e-ticket wasn’t scanned at all the first day, despite me offering it up to our first driver, so we didn’t officially start until Friday! We also completely forgot to grab maps and earphones when we first got on so just used that first afternoon as a bit of a sit down and a drive round after having visited the British Museum in the morning.

Friday we set off from Westminster in the morning and we happened to have a live tour guide this time, rather than the pre-recorded audio. This is something the company is experimenting with apparently, re-introducing live guides here and there to see what the feedback is. Our guide was Chris and we thoroughly enjoyed our trip round with him. The pre-recorded audio is ok and we did pick up some interesting facts from it, but we much preferred having Chris on board for our Friday trip. Having a live guide allows for a much more ‘personal’ experience with a mix of information and humour. It’s also more interactive with the opportunity to ask questions, if you’re not sure about where to change routes for instance or get other useful information such as how to get the most from the river cruise (Chris recommended doing Tower of London to Westminster for example, rather than the other way round, so as to get the most from the bus route). He was also careful to announce to the driver when people were coming down to get off. It made for a much more pleasant and useful experience than just having the driver and pre-recorded audio to rely on. You also don’t have to worry about the earphones of course which is easier and certainly worked better for our kids who found the supplied earphones too large and uncomfortable. So, a big thumbs up for Chris and live guides in general from us! Definitively worth doing the 30 minute river cruise by the way (a partnership with City Cruises) as a part of your trip(s) round London. Very funny commentary on board - sorry I didn’t make a note of the chaps name - and it definitely added to our day.

Saturday we decided to try the blue route which meant starting off on the red route again (heading west) and then changing near Apsley House. Back to just the pre-recorded audio again which as I say is ‘ok’ but we missed having a live guide. We also found the red route bus a lot busier on the Saturday and we couldn’t find space up top for the first time during our visit to London. Thankfully it wasn’t too far until our change to the generally quieter blue route. We found this one interesting but to be fair it’s no comparison to the sights you’ll see on the main red route. I’d only bother with the blue, or green, route if you’ve exhausted your time on the red route, or you have somewhere specific you want to see/get off at.

So, overall we’d certainly recommend Big Bus Tours but it’s a ‘lite’ experience without a live guide. Hopefully they’ll have more and more on their buses over time.

We finally gave up, got off, and walked - we really should have done that from the beginning. If you must do this, some tips:

1. Do not buy a ticket from anywhere but online. The sellers at the airport and elsewhere overcharge - as much as 10 pounds more than you pay online. And they lie to you, saying (for example) that it's not possible to buy just a bus ticket, that you must also purchase the river cruise. Not true.

2. DO NOT rely on the maps provided by the bus company. They are woefully inaccurate in reflecting the actual route taken.

3. Do some research about the sights you hop off to see beforehand. You will not receive information from the recording about where to hop off to see this sight - knowing beforehand will keep you on track.

4. Really. Don't waste your money. Just walk. Do the walk along the Thames. That was wonderful.

This should really be divided up into two parts: The Thames River cruise, which was WONDERFUL, and the bus ride, which was not. The river cruise was expertly navigated by the captain and wonderfully narrated by a member of the crew, who was knowledgeable and funny. I'm glad we took the cruise first, because it was truly a highlight!

The cruise let off at the Tower of London, at which point we decided to hop on one of the buses. The on-the-ground crew there at the tower was great -- funny, friendly, helpful, and got us organized in a line to await our next bus. A+ to them! It was when we got on a bus that things went a bit south. We were expecting a live tour guide, as we'd enjoyed in past experiences with Big Bus, but unfortunately all we had was a minimally narrated recording. We had planned on taking the bus throughout the entire route, but got off halfway through and walked around London instead, using our guidebook for information.

In short: We would have been better off buying a cruise ticket standalone and using the Tube for "hop on, hop off" service! It pains me to give a so-so review, but there you have it. The only reason I've given it a three out of five is for the cruise and the grounds crew!

- That they did not know in advance that some of the stops will be closed as the change was made on short notice (also not true -- RideLondon and its plans were not made on short notice. We were not aware of them as tourists, but a London-based vendor absolutely should have been)

I should note that at least one other bus company, TootBus, did not sell tickets for 29 May, with a note on their website stating they were not selling due to road closures. We later picked up the bus tour again with Francesca as the guide - she was excellent - very informative and funny - and readily helping people out with other information - we stayed on at the end of the tour to go round again to stop 6 on Regent Street to get back to our hotel - on the Sunday traffic was pretty chaotic with the marathon so we walked to Westminster and did the river cruise to Greenwich and back - Because we had paid through booking.com we had to go to a specific point to have the e ticket verified - but staff let us on the bus anywya until we arrived there - A good way to see all the major sites - a shout out for Francesca (the guide that took over from her was a bit surly and not very interesting - but we had seen it by then) - Recommended.

We decided to buy a 3 day pass with them as the people who were selling the tickets were friendly and helpful. Well that all changed once we got on the bus, we tried to ask the driver which stop we were told to get off at and he said very rudely "if you were listening on the headphones it would tell you which stop is which" and wouldn't answer anymore questions. The rest of the bus drivers were also rude and unwilling to answer simple questions. Even trying to find out what times the last bus came was ridiculous, they either "didn't know" or gave a completely different answer than someone else. The live commentary people were the best though, Liam was super helpful and friendly and told us a lot of good information. He took the time to talk to us and gave some good suggestions on places to visit, and another lady whose name I didn't get was also friendly and kept us entertained while we were stuck in traffic for half an hour.
There was also a night tour included in the ticket, however what they didn't tell us was that the London marathon was running Sunday and some stops would be closed off on the red line, which was fine but there was no information provided for a change of pick up location for the night tour if the roads were still closed (which they were). We weren't the only ones waiting around for it either, there was another group of people who had been told that morning that the night tour would go ahead as planned from all stops at the normal time because the roads would be open well before then. Which they weren't. Trying to call the phone number on the website was also a joke, we were on hold for 10 minutes before giving up as it kept going around in a circle of ringing and robot. We walked down the road to where a lot of the buses were passing through, and when we tried to ask one who was stopped at the side of the road, he wouldn't open the doors and started making rude hand gestures at my friend which was extremely inappropriate and unnecessary.
We bought the London eye ticket as well, and they told us that it would be quicker and we wouldn't have to wait in line. Wrong. We had to go into the ticket office, wait half an hour to swap the ticket and then go and wait in line to get on the eye. Took about 45 mins all up, which in my opinion is not quicker.
So maybe try a different company if you are considering a hop on hop off bus tour in London.

TL;DR- if you just want to get around the city, don't mind getting yelled at for asking general questions from the bus drivers who aren't willing to help and don't care about the buses coming on time, then this is the company for you!

The day we took our tour there was some work happening in town and so they had to skip a bunch of stops and we weren't notified of this when purchasing our ticket. Also, the staff on the bus didn't give us a printed ticket, so when we got to the ferry, they didn't allow us to get on board and as a result we wasted about half an hour to 45 mins waiting for the big bus to show up again where they dropped us off so we could get a printed ticket. They didn't show up, and after requesting a lot the ferry people, they finally let us on.

Even after contacting them, they didn't issue an apology.

we hopped on today...107 pounds for a afamily of four....buses were overcrowded...people standing up....cant really sight see in these conditions....whilst they accepted over crowded situations i was told off because i was standing over a line near the driver....huge disappointment....people obstructed seats in front with pushchairs and no one corrected this even though we were standing up....very very disappointed
Tours were good, when we were in London there were environment protests so the routes were changed which made it unreliable if you wanted to make plans. But overall it was good.

We hopped on #14 with Alexis as our guide and she was so great that we almost didn't hop off to explore!! However we did eventually hop off to explore the orange and blue lines, specifically tower of London, Westminster Abbey, and Notting hill for lunch at Farmacy(delicious). We wished that there was a tour guide upon every bus, not just the red. We were sad that the marble arches was closed due to protesting but we understand!
Anyways. Definitely recommend and absolutely sit on the top deck!

Having used the Big Bus Tour in Paris in January, which was excellent, we decided to try the same in London with our 6 year kids. What a disappointment, complete opposite of Paris. Little information about the climate protests just the ‘route is being changed’. Packed full buses sat waiting for a driver for over half an hour in hot temperatures. Over £100 for 2 day pass not worth the money as on the headphones most of the time music played rather than commentating on the sights. Money grabbing swindlers with no thought for the customer!

Did the Blue Tour with the Big Bus Tour and a complete waste of time and money. There was no commentary or Tour Guide on the Bus, just the driver who drove around the sights that we had no idea what we were seeing. Never said anything when we boarded the bus and after two stops we got off. We might as well have just gotten a regular Bus. Bad form not to advise us there was no Tour Guide, would not recommend them!

Our recent trip to London unfortunately coincided with the Extinction Rebellion protests and the one day we chose to check out Big Bus, traffic was gridlocked. I am certain Big Bus offers a great experience but we were disappointed that nobody warned us of the delays before selling us the tickets or boarding the bus. We boarded at Edgware Road around 10:30 and by noon had only gone two stops, with no commentary nor explanation of route changes. We abandoned ship in favor of the underground. We have attempted to obtain a refund or voucher but to no avail. I’m sure this is a great service but customer service has been a bust.

We went on the Big Bus hop on hop off today. Due to the protestors near Marble Arch the route has been altered. As an alternative Big Bus offers walking tours from 1 of their stops so you dont miss out on the sights. And don't sit in traffic for hours. We opted for the walking tour with Big Steve and he was great. Very knowledgable and so worth it. Glad we had the opportunity to do the walking tour with him. A really great guide.

Great experience with Big Steve. Big protest near Marble Arch. Streets closed lots of traffic. Big Steve from Big Bus came in on our stop before the protest area and offered a walking tour to the cruise dock. Well worth it. Showed us places we would have never seen on the bus. Thanks Big Steve. Good idea Big Bus Tours. And to think this was only our first day of the three day pass. Cheers.
We took the walk tour with Karen and she explained us every single detail! Very knowledgeable lady! This was in central London by Trafalgar Square. Now I know almost everything about King Charles!

I ve read some bad reviews, but I wouldn't agree. People are just not informed and not prepared to visit size of the city as London is. Guys,inform yourself!! Even there was traffic interruptions today,we had great tour. Hopped on on Trafalgar square on red tour and the guide was great. He gave all info u needed to know. I observed people are not listening and are much into their phones sharing real time on Fb..Insta etc..:) we switched to blue route with no problem and every BB staff we meet were great and helpful. At no city where I ve used BB tours I didn't see so many staff allocated. Great job. We did waited a bit longer orange route,but hey....it was huge traffic plus protests, so...of course it would be late. And we also had to change the bus but I didn't asked why and I didnt care. For all those not knowing about ticket validity....come on...when u book online everywhere is clearly written all about it..just read all of it not just date time and price ;)
We are looking forward to our walking tour and cruise and night tour. I m sure BB will have great review again from me.

Would never use this company again. We booked tickets that included this and the London eye and Madame Tussaud’s.

We had booked the eye for 12.15 so it said to also exchange our printouts for the bus tickets at the eye.
What they don’t tell you is that from the minute the tickets are printed they have a time on and this is when you start using up your 24 hour period. I had assumed you could just exchange your ticket and then the very first bus you got on, that’s when your time would start.

We asked at the eye where we would collect the tickets, they directed us to a collection point which the que was horrendous for. We waited for about 20 minutes before getting out of it. It turns out, we didn’t need to do this, the print outs can be exchanged for tickets at any little box that sells these bus tickets.

Staff at these boxes are not friendly.

The company has about 3-4 different bus routes which is okay, except the buses don’t stick to these routes. We got on the route to go from Notting hill to Kensington, we ended up at Aldwych by Covent Garden.. ridiculous. No information from the company about this.

Only about half of the earphone plugs worked on the bus so that was rubbish. Buses were not clean.

We waited at Notting Hill Gate for at least 45 minutes for a bus. Whilst waiting, 4 other buses from 2 other companies came past. No information provided. I understand that there were some demonstrations on near Mable arch but on 15.4.19 these were not too bad and the other buses made it through.

We were also unable to use the river cruise as the very first one in the morning is not until 10.10 from Tower Hill which is just too late in London when we wanted to get out and get seeing things again. We were at the natural history museum after taking a tube across the city for 9am from our hotel for example.

I’d never use this company again.

Well worth doing, especially if you haven't been to London before but don't get caught out like we did...we booked online but despite what your booking confirmation might say, the operator will NOT accept the confirmation on your phone even with photo ID. They will ONLY accept a physical print out of the actual confirmation. We found out the hard way and then spent quite some time running around London trying to find somewhere to get a print out.

We boarded a bus at 4.50 at Buckingham Palace and drove one bus stop. We were then asked to change buses with no explanation at all. We were then left sitting there for 40 minutes, no driver and no guide on board this bus. We had to exit the tour and take the Tube as it we would have missed our train from Euston.
I have complained and will be looking for a refund as this is the worst customer service ever,

After all the hype and anticipation to go on this bus we were all extremely disappointed.
The bus was so crowded we couldn't see or hear what was happening.
All we did was travel around some streets of London but not see much.
Very disappointing after spending all that money. There were 4 of us, so it mounted up to quite an amount.
We took a ride at St. Paul's and our guide Ema was very kind and helpfull! It was nice to learn some new things about London.

Took my parents (61 and 70) and my two children (10 and 11) and it was a stress free way to view London. I recommend downloading the app and using that, we experienced detours on the route due to an event and with the app it was easy to keep up and know where to go.

We paid £60 for 2 tickets, 24 hour hop on off. Having used Hop on/off in various cities before we expected this to be a great way to see the London sites. Unfortunately we had to wait ages to get on a bus, the first one was full & drove past. Then we were told that due to the demonstrators in London & some road closures, the route was different & there could be hold ups. Wow- this was certainly true. The bus crawled along, with people speeding by on foot. Then when the bus stopped the audio commentary didn't say the stop number nor did the tour guide onboard. There was a great deal of confusion as people were asking where they were, where to go to get to wherever, complete chaos.
We wanted to get off at stop 23, the bus sailed past & then said, oh you can get off at Buckingham Palace!!!!! Not the point when travelling with two young children. Why not announce each stop number & destination. Wouldn't recommend.

Bought tickets for my family and myself in Australia (6 of us) the whole experience from the start was dreadful.walked from Hotel to Regent street to start our journey, was sent to tragalgar square by bus operator to validate our tickets, then sent to green park to validate our tickets, there was hundreds of passengers trying to get on the bus.
So walked to the Palace.
Eventually got on a bus that took us to Green Park, then told we all had to get off and cross the road to get on a different one.
We all managed to get on, no one could sit together, then the worst tour I have ever taken started, the Guide Lionel was the rudest most Bombastic man I have ever come across, he spoke to passengers like they were something he stood in, shouting at them, pointing his finger at them, anyone that wanted to ask a question was shouted down.
We got off at the tower, had a look around, decided to get on another bus and have our tour.
The driver of this bus must have gone to Charm school with Lionel, several people got on looking for a seat, he shouted get off and get on the next one, we had already waited for 25 minutes.
So we got off and finished out sightseeing on the Tube.
I am going to try and get a refund, this is Fraud for taking money and NOT supplying the service advertised
Thoroughly enjoyed our HOHO bus tour around London. Our guide was fabulous. Wish we had time to listen to more.

We had a great host in JoJo! the tour itself was awesome, informative, and easy to use. I just wish the times and the bus tracker were more accurate. Even though I've been to London many times, this trip gave me a whole different perspective.

It's a great choice if you have the 2.5 hours to do the whole loop. We got off at the tower of london and then we jumped on again to our next destination (Westminster). While on it, the live guide was very informative. But very pricey at £89 (us$101) for two adults and a teen.

Great if you like standing around bus stops for 40 minutes. Very unreliable and over crowded. Routes often changed and stops missed out without any notice blamed on traffic problems although several other tour bus operators managed to pick up their customers. Audio commentary did not work on 3 out of the 4 trips we managed to join.
My advice would be to go with any one of the other better organised companies.

I have taken hop on hop off bus tours all over the world and this one is by far the best. Very upbeat, full of energy staff members. From the drivers to the live tour guide was friendly and fun! Clean bus as well! Oh, the staff was friendly even at the bus stops!! Highly recommended!!

Took the Big Bus tour with Courtney as our guide. She was friendly, funny and knowledgable and was able to keep us entertained even though we often had to stop due to traffic. Perfect way to see the city and not tire your feet!!!

London weather is changeable- I would recommend WARM clothes!!

If you are new to London, and want to see where everything is, this is the way to go. It takes you past the majority of major tourist attractions. You get to see them all, and you can hop off, go do something, then hop back on again.

We took my mum to London for her birthday, it was her first visit at 65 and she has trouble walking long distances. She wanted to see the sights with as little walking as possible so the bus tour is perfect! We got to see everything we wanted too, we planned our route in advance so we could get off and on to snake the most of the tour. The day started wet but the sun soon came out and we managed to get a seat up stairs each time we got on a bus. Whilst on the bus tour we experienced 3 different tour guides. The first was a little serious and dry but soon warmed up, the second was interactive and chatting but not much information passed on, the last was the best. I think his name was Joe, he gave us so much information in the short time we were in the bus with him.
Thank you for making our tour enjoyable. :-)

This was an okay experience. It was an easy way to get around. We had one tour guide that was amazing, Joe was entertaining and knowledgeable! However, the rest were pretty dry and lacked enthusiasm. It took quite a while to get from the London Eye to the Tower of London (easily 2 hours). One bus was stopped and all passengers had to get off and wait. For what? Nobody knew. Another bus was evacuated and everyone rushed to the bus and it was filled up. We missed the bus we had just got off due to over crowding. We waiting around for another 20 minutes and we were let on the second bus. No reason or explanation. Just a waste of time.

We paid for 24 hours but nobody checked any tickets throughout the day. We could easily return without having paid for a second day.

The help line responder was in the Philippines, took him a while to find 'the product'. Then, because I don't have access to a printer or smart phone technology, and I can't buy a ticket on the bus, there's no way I can get a ticket. Disappointed.

Let me begin by saying that this tour is a definite must! My friend and I were unsure about doing the Big Red Bus tour in fear of it being a tourist trap. Now, it was one of the most memorable moments from our trip thanks to Big Steve, our tour guide. He made sure he personalized the tour for everyone sitting around him. Big Steve was super nice, a great person to talk to, made us laugh, and shared his America stories with us. We were able to see all the sites in London in a day while being able to hop on and off. Big Steve was very informative and even shared his favorite place to eat in the area. Thank you Big Red Bus tour and Big Steve for the amazing time. Big Steve if you read this, sorry for the late review. You were truly the best! From your Florida friend Justine :)

Would highly recommend this attraction! Ideal for younger children! Very informative! Brilliant staff! Lovely day out!
Could not fault in anyway! 5*

The blue route took about an hour 20 minutes and the red route well over 2 1/2 hours, but we never had a problem finding seats or listening to the audio. London is a busy city and we ended up taking many taxis as well, just to try to see as many sites as we could.

My friend and I purchased the two-day Big Bus tour. The first day was rainy and cold, so we were very happy to be able to explore without being out in the miserable weather. Our first commentator wasn't great, but the others were very entertaining and informative! The second day there were many closed road/diversions from the regular route - my friend and I waited at one stop for almost an hour before we realized the buses were diverting around our stop. Since we were visiting from out of the country, we weren't able to successfully use the app to look for updates! It would have been nice if there was a sign on the stop or some sort of notice saying the Big Bus tours would not be stopping there that day. Other than that minor incident, really great experience! Would definitely recommend for folks new to London!
I had a great time today with Joe as the guide. He was friendly and knowledgeable. I would definitely do this again. Thanks Joe for a memorable trip.

Enjoyed every moment of the tour. Was easy to book through the app on the phone. The tour itself was made very informative by listening to the live commentary made by Valdas, the on tour guide. Highly recommended

It was the first visit to London for our teenage son so we thought the hop on/off bus tour would be a great way to get started. Our hotel recommended the Big Bus tour - for 2 reasons mainly, they liked the frequency of the busses and the live guides. We were blessed with a lovely day weather wise and enjoyed our guide, Valdas. He had a wealth of knowledge and was available for any questions (something you don't get with a recorded tour). Very happy with our experience.

Without taking the top tour and top prices, you can still use the tour to have an overview of the city you're in. We bought a customized version at the airport, with the Shard and the Big Wheel added. You have to calculate how much time you really have and how many attractions you can realistically visit within your time frame (three-day tour in our case). With the sun quickly setting after 4:00 pm, you have to leave out the sit-down tour at the end of the day. We had a really nice guide who sat with us on the upper deck, with the rain and the wind , going around Picadilly Square, giving his insights and knowledge of the history. This is not true on all buses! We spent much time at the Science Centre, waiting to see the IMAX feature, therefore several hrs indoors. The Shard visit was done during low season and that was perfect if you wish to have photos taken by the glass sides; the sun came out and gave us beautiful views of London! We did not buy any of the photos; these tourist shots are overpriced all over London, as in other cities n North America, of course! During the last ride of our package - you can also switch between different colours defining the individual tours as long as you know where you will end-, we used the "Home James" option whereby one bus at the last drop off takes customers who need to be driven closer to their hotels. You may have to walk several blocks, but at least you're not miles away from your starting point. The Website explains it all, just be ready to adjust your timetable according to the weather and the length of each one of your chosen attractions. And if you switch lines, you have to find the proper bus stop for the specific route!

Wonderful tour, bought a 2 day ticket and rode around London checking out all of the sights. All tour guides were great, one critique is that one tour guide kept saying "on the right is XX on the left is XX" and he was referring to HIS left or right about half of the time, this was confusing and I found myself looking the wrong direction sometimes. An easy mistake to make, but when you are driving by and want to take it all in, the little bit of time to look the other way can make the difference if you miss seeing the landmark as you pass it. Again, not a big deal. I was able to do about 2.5 complete red route tours and 1 full route on the orange line.

Each time I went by something, different tour guides had the same major facts (landmarks and dates) but different tour guides had different fun "trivia" type commentary. One tour guide kept joking about being single and wanting to marry Prince Harry or a guy in Mayfair (the posh part of London) she was hilarious. Another tour guide had more to say about Harry Potter trivia, and the black cab protest- and a way to get back at the diversions they were causing- take Uber! Fun, entertaining, informative, and a welcome rest from walking everywhere during my trip. Would definitely do again, and I will search out Big Bus tours in other major cities. Thank you!

It was a nice sunny day but SUPER cold or at least to my friends and I. Wear layers!!
Appreciated the commentary throughout the tour and SOME buses even have live commentary with headphones that they give.

If this is your first time ever in London, I suggest it. (Unless you got something else planned on how to go about your day) Got us around pretty much the whole day but make sure to keep an eye out on the last bus don't wanna get stranded and stand there waiting.

Big bus is always a good choice!
you get to see the whole city hop off to take pictures then hop back on.has a thames river cruise included which you get to take many pictures in a different angle. in this city, they offer a walking tour. I recommend everyone to do it because you get a lot of information from the tour guide ( Henry) was exceptional! very funny, very knowledgeable and always kept the tour interesting.
I recommend downloading the big bus app it has a lot of info you will have handy at all the time.

Very good tour. Lewis ourtour guide was knowledgeable and fun. Made the tour very enjoyable . We did the red tour. A little dissapointed that we wanted to do the blue route but it finished at 16.30 so could not do it

We purchased the 3 day tickets and only managed one journey in the whole time, routes were changed and stops closed but not updated on the page my husband and son were very frustrated at the time it took walking around to find another stop we ended up buying tube tickets and Uber’s. Awful experience and one I will never be repeating

We had a ball Peter H was first class knowledgable interesting and engaging absolutely loved it. We saw everything from the comfort of our open top bus which was well navigated by josh. Well done guys tally ho!!!!

We took the Big Bus tour in NYC and appreciated it, so we did the B.B. tour in London. Not as good, but we did have one excellent guide, John. Was disappointed their wasn’t a live tour guide on Blue line. We were able to see a lot however. Would use it again.

We bought our tickets for the Big Bus tour from Expedia before we travelled and saved massively on the ticket price. In hindsight, this was perhaps not the best idea as Big Bus tours were completely unprepared to compensate me in any way for my complaint and have fobbed me off back to Expedia.
The tour is advertised as hop on hop off, but to be honest, due to the volume of traffic in London you will not have time to get off the bus and see any sights for more than a couple of minutes, especially if you want to go on more then one route. If you have a 1-day pass stick to the red route as that's by far the best and you have the live commentary.
What follows is my copied and pasted complaint that I sent to Big Bus tours via their app whilst I was sitting on the bus.

I have to say I’m a bit disappointed with the communication on the buses. We have had long waits at stops today with absolutely no information from staff. Firstly on the red route this morning after getting on at Tower Hill we stopped at stop 1. We were told to get off the bus and get on the one at the front and then we were told to stay put. We were told the bus would hold for 10 minutes so we had time to get off for a drink or toilet break. The female staff member told us where the toilets were and we quickly visited the station to use the toilet and returned to the bus just in time for it to drive off. The female staff member acknowledged our return but did not say the bus was leaving. There was another bus sitting so we were told to go on this. This sat for 10 minutes more before leaving.

We decided to get the blue bus from stop 5 so changed there. We waited for 10 minutes and I tracked the bus on the app only for the next bus to drive straight past. It stopped at stop 4 so we crossed the road to catch it there. We arrived just as the door shut but they opened the door for us, I said that the bus drove right past us to be told that it doesn’t stop there!

The commentary on the blue bus was next to non-existent where mostly the same music played on repeat. We stopped at Gloucester Road for 15 minutes with no communication from the staff. My son went downstairs to check and the doors were closed and we had no driver. Due to roadworks we then went on a long detour (approx 30mins)- but this is no fault of the tour company.

We got off at Madame Toussads and had a walk to Baker Street and a coffee. We returned to the bus stop and joined the orange tour. This time we got on a sitting bus and waited 25 minutes before it left. When my 9yr old son enquired when we would leave he was told we were waiting on a driver! If we had known the bus was going to sit so long we would have walked to join the red route.

The bus went down Regent Street as advertised and the commentary was a lot better than on the blue route. We then went off route again without any notification from the driver. We came to a stop at Covent Garden and despite the fact that people were getting on the bus, an announcement was made for everyone to get off the bus as it was going back to Baker Street. Everyone on the bus looked confused and the order was barked over the tannoy again to get off the bus! Everyone disembarked and waited for the next bus to come along. It was at this point we realised that we were no longer on the orange route.

Within 10 minutes a Red Route bus appeared and everyone piled on until it was at capacity. A couple of stops in the member of staff doing the commentary made sure to inform everyone that this would be the last bus of the day and no others would be following us. We were fairly surprised at this as it was only 4.15 and the app and map advertised that the buses would be running for at least another hour.

We travelled on the red route until the Tower of London which had been our first stop of the day so that we could take advantage of the boat tour. Again, despite the fact that the boat tour was advertised as running later we managed to catch the last boat of the day at 5.15.

I just feel there was a complete lack of communication between staff and customers on this day. We were left sitting on a bus several times with no indication of when we would be leaving. The app informed of road disruptions to the route, but your staff did not. There are staff at so many points in the route but they mostly seem interested in selling tickets rather than creating a good experience for customers.

On the plus side, I did find that all of the tour guides on the red route to be very knowledgable and they had very interesting commentary. I wish we had never got off the red route as they were by far the best experiences of the day.
Worst hop on tour I have ever had Guidis were unfriendly dident talk allot and if they talked you could barely even hear them.
We had the best time on this tour- our guide Valdas was very knowledgeable and made the tour! Definite must for when visiting London- and try to get Valdas as your guide:)
Great tour with some great tour guides! Takes you all over the city, and there were staff everywhere in case you needed help with anything.

The big bus London is the way to go to see your sights! Our bus driver Steve was the best and our live guided guy Oliver was fantastic! You must see the city with these two guys! Made us some remarkable memories. Thanks guys you're the best! Wish you guys were on all our tours on our next holiday!

The makes see the sites of London an easy thing. But make sure you get on the right bus, particularly at junctions with other lines. I ended up re-looping the red line at Westminister. I wanted to continue on the Eastern route but unknowingly ended up return west and had to redo the entire loop to get back to where I wanted to go. Good live English speaking tour guides.

Best 2.5 hours to see the best of London! Very friendly and knowledgable staff. Highly recommended!

We were able to see the best sites and scenes in London in less than 3 hours. We were able to see the best of London without having to worry about how to get there and No hassle with trying to find parking.

What a sight from the top of the double deck bus!!!

We had a wonderful time, all the guides were great (though Fay was my favorite). There are often staff at the stops who are happy to help. We're on our way to Paris & we've already bought our Big Bus tickets for there.

The only reason this tour is poor is due to the narrow streets and amount of traffic. For those reasons it took FOREVER to get to your next stop.(We used the big bus tour in Paris and it was perfect) As for London we found it best to go on foot and/or take the tube. People are very helpful in pointing you in the right direction!

We booked via VIATOR (BR-675863876) for the BIG BUS LONDON HOP-ON-HOP-OFF TOUR for December 25, 2018 for six (6) adults. We redeemed our voucher at the Gloucester Road Bus Stop & we were given the tickets, only to be told that if we take the River Thames cruise (which by the way is included in the ticket), we should upgrade for an additional 21Euros each (the first bummer). We went to see the sights by hopping-on&off with no problems but when we tried to board the bus at Piccadilly Circus, the Big Bus tour operator who was there refused to board us because he said we need to upgrade our ticket to Christmas Day Special for an additional 9Euros each (the second bummer). December 25 is Christmas Day isnt it? Duh! BIG BUS IS BIG SUCKS!!! VIATOR needs to coordinate well with BIG BUS. We WON'T be taking any BIG BUS tours from now on.
We enjoyed it! It was rather cold on the bus but the comments were great and usefull :) Same concept as Dublin, ok 4 us!

This is definitely a great way to see the city at a reasonable cost, earphone with various language selection available so you can listen to the commentary as you enjoy the tour. Definitely a must for any tourist visiting London

This was our very first time in London and your company was recommended to us by our Hotel, Doubletree at London Tower. We purchased a 2 day pass and started our Journey at stop 16 about 10ish yesterday morning. The tour guide Mick was very good. Obviously very experienced. At one of the stops I witnessed 2 of your employees having a spat at each other in plane sight of passengers. Totally unprofessional. We changed routes a couple of times throughout the day. We had just hoped off the blue route in the afternoon at Marble Arch to join the red route to get back to our hotel and were told the red tour had finished for the day and that we would have to get the underground back to our hotel. We were left stranded, not knowing where the train station was. It took us over an hour to get back to our hotel, having to change trains twice and getting lost. The host at the stop was very rude and totally unhelpful. Today we hopped on the Red tour at check point 15 St Paul's Cathederal at about 11:30, to head back to our hotel. The bus sat for ages at the stop. Once we got going, the bus stopped about 100m up the road. We were up the front and could see that the driver made an unscheduled stop to take a personal call on his mobile phone. He was talking about sending emails and the like. This was totally unprofessional and should not happen. I found the majority of your staff to be rude and unhelpful and only interested in selling tickets. Once you've got us, we are captive to your poor service because of the amount of money we had to falk out. My suggestion to you is to do an audit on all your staff and get rid of the dead wood you are carrying. They are hurting your business and the London city itself. If I ever have the opportunity to visit London again, I will be surprised if you are still in business because word gets around pretty quickly and unless you lift your game, I don't give your company much time before going under.

On 2nd Jan 2019 we completed the red tour in the morning with excellent live guide Mick (is he a radio announcer?!) very pleasant speaking voice and knowledgeable about sites.
Completed blue tour in afternoon and had planned to return to hotel on red route at 4.40pm...only to be told that we had missed the last bus! We were stranded at The Marble Arch! Unsympathetic tour guide vaguely waved us toward the tube. Took three trains and 90 minutes to get home on crowded trains. Disappointed 😢

Rude and grumpy drivers, over crowded buses. We stood up for most of the journey with 3 kids and no access to audio or able to see out the windows. Might as well been on the tube. Buss took 30 minutes to arrive to one stop and it was very cold. At other stops passengers were left in the the cold as they couldn't fit on the buss. Just awful and very expensive.

I took a Big Bus to sight see London downtown, but it was an awful experience... It was a cold rainy day, the bus was over-crowded and there's no heating... result: Couldn't see anything thru the fogged windows!!! My feet were freezing... conclusion: It's a waste of money!!!

Tours are slow, if you have a ok understanding of the underground and already know what you want to see then I would not recommend this tour.

The earphones given on the tour are not great and it can sometimes be hard to hear the live announcer.

On two separate occasions the busses went right past us due to the stop already occupying a city bus. We had already waited 15-20 mins for the bus. We did signal the drivers who did see us.

Did the Big Bus tour with our 7 year old granddaughter. Have to say it was worth every penny. She loved it. Our guide was Caron and Omar the driver. We all felt the experience was greatly enhanced by Carons brilliant commentary on all the wonderful sites around London. Her anecdotes and interesting facts added to what was a thoroughly enjoyable trip. The river cruise was also very enjoyable. Great way to see the famous sites.

We did 3 of the routes, had 5 live and one recorded tour guides - only one of the live tour guides was lacklustre, all the rest were great. We saw a ton of stuff, lots of good information!

We were on the busses both during the day and after it got dark in the late afternoon, do them both if you can, both are interesting and London is a great city!

Sheri was a great tour guide and Pippa drove us around without incident. Brilliant!! Well worth the experience especially on Boxing Day!
Thank you ladies..
It is a great way to get over view of London. Also you can get combined ticket with a boat tour of river Thames a great way to view the bridges. The crowds were huge next time we will go in the Fall.
The inside of the bus I'm on right now smells like cat urine and I have a 5 month old that shouldn't be inhaling this smell but no one is doing anything or cares about this fact

Our experience with the Hop On Hop Off tour with Louis was amazing. He’s a funny guy and he knows his stuff! Very knowledgeable of London and he adds humor to the tour. Great guy and great tour! 100% recommend.

Had a good time on the London Big Bus tour - the red line. Our guide (Lewis I think) was really good and friendly. The lady who gave us our ticket though didn't greet us or respond more than with a mumble to our questions of whether or not we could hop on the bus. Her service really needs to imrpove. But the service of Lewis and the entire experience was good.

My family and my sister’s family are here for vacations. It is the first time I visit London. I strongly recommend first time visitor to hop on to this Big Bus Tour and get to know London! It is really helpful indeed. Special thanks to Kathy and James for the wonderful explanation and ride on 19/12/2018! Bought a 2 days tickets bus tour and will be going on the cruise tomorrow. :)
We visited London for a short visit and was able to cover so many sights with the hop on hop off tour! Tour Guides were great and definitely knowledgeable!

I strongly suggest when you first arrive in London that you take a couple hours and ride the Big Bus to tour the area and find out where you want to visit. The hop on and hop off feature is definitely worth it! The bus fee was included with London Pass - great savings. The bus tour offers either a live tour guide or you can listen to audio recording. Did a little of both. I wish we had spent a little more time on the bus as we got off to eat and I got confused on time of day with it being my first day of new time zone.

As we only really had 1 full day in London we purchased the family ticket to see quite a lot of the sites and hop on and off as we liked. Great way to see London and commentary was really good and informative. Never had to wait long for the next bus and stops where all next to key locations.

I purchased 2 tickets for the Big Bus Hop on Hop off tour. It was raining heavily and therefore the bus as packed as everyone wanted to be sheltered downstairs. The headphones gave information on certain landmarks but the driver gave no information where we were and where we were stopping. According to the confusing leaflet there were options for getting off and going on another bus and even a river boat trip. What happened was we paid over £70 ( for two) ... sat on a crowded bus ..never saw a thing and ended up practically where we started about an hour later. Total nightmare I’m afraid !

Bill was absolutely amazing and would definitely recommend him again!!
Karen was lovely too she has a nice voice and made me feel relaxed!!

Would definitely recommend Big Bus Tours

From the first time I started to travel around the world, I swore of tour buses and the annoying promoters. When I am out traveling I prefer to get around as the locals do. Since the age of our travel group was from 16 - 50, we decided to take this bus around to see as much as possible at a limited time, since we only had two days to go around. The guides were entertaining and had a lot of knowledge of the town, which was nice. Some of the busses had pre-recorded information, but It didn´t matter. The only downside was that there were no busses who took the whole round of the city, so we had to change busses sometimes. And some of the routes took forever because of traffic.

We had a great time on the bus, with a very lovely host. I think her name was Caron.
Also gave us great advice where to go.

The bus-business is still kinda sketchy, you just never know if you made a decent deal price wise or got ripped off. Online, booths, vendors at stops. Plus all the alternative companies. Especially when they never ask you to show your tickets for which you just paid a decent amount of money.
We had a wonderful experience with jo jo, we got to hear lots of history & was very informative. Our 8yr old son said jo jo was the best & he loved it. Thank you Jo jo we will recommend to anyone.
For Maddie’s age, her knowledge of London was unbelievable and enjoyed everything she shared. She made the Bus Tour so enjoyable- great employee to have.

The Hop on Hop Off Bus is a great way to see the city (especially to escape from the cold in December). The live guides give you a lot of tips and recommendations so it’s a good way to start your trip. Although all the guides are lovely and friendly, Louis was my fav; especially in his attempts to keep us entertained with the traffic 😂. And the bus drivers are all top notch and friendly.

The bus makes many spots all over the city (especially with the multiple lines so you can go to whatever part of London you want). Also, the buses are nice and clean. Overall, a good experience !!!

We did this based on recommendations of other people to while away the jet lag. Perhaps because it was November - it was pretty cold so I didn't find it a particularly fun or informative time. Our narrator was not very entertaining and I found him difficult to understand. He too seemed bored and cold.
The stops are easily marked and there is plenty of time allowed to get on and off the bus. In truth, I found this rather boring!

I toiled over picking the best option for the HOHO company. I chose Big Bus because the cost, convenience and reviews were mostly positive. And when they weren't positive, they at least responded to address the customer concerns.

Result: We loved the Big Bus. All the stops we wanted during the times we wanted to go. I found this bus company ran the longest hours per day, had the easiest phone app and the best offer with its 24 hour ticketing policy - for example, we started using our bus pass mid-day Friday and it went to mid-day Sunday. That was so convenient and cut down on our Underground usage. We could get to other tour pick-ups without extra costs. The narration was interesting and educational at a basic level. The handy maps and rain gear was helpful.

There were 2 stops that we a little odd - one was connecting to the Blue line - there was an odd loop. But there were reps there to help people get on the right bus.

Very cool all around.
Karen was very knowledgeable and friendly. The bus was clean and the service intercom/headsets worked.
This tour is great and covers all the attractions of London. My tour guide Tabea is a fabulous storyteller and she was very helpful.
This was a terrific tour. Cathy’s narration and comments added lots of color and fun to the day. This was a nice overview of the city.

This is a great way to get an overview of the city sights. You can decide which areas need a further look, and which just get a cursory glance. All of our guides were hjelpful. The only issue we had was road closing near St. Paul's, so we could not get as close to it as would normally be the case

The trip on big bus started well. The bus reach starting point on time or slight earlier as mentioned in their app as we were took the first one. But the problem started in the afternoon, we waited more than 20 minutes at stop 14, and was told by staff stationed there to wait another 10 to 20 minutes. We decided to take public transport to save our time to St. Paul. The thing was getting worse after we visited St. Paul. We waited more than 30 minutes at stop 15. We used their app to track the buses, have to say that it is really nice feature, the two subsequent buses did not come to stop 15 at all after leaving stop 14. They took the route that was different from the planned path according to their plan mentioned in app and brochure. We decided to take tube instead as there was no way for us to know whether there would be big bus coming.

I am very disappointed with their service. If you just want to visit a few place, taking public transportation like bus a tube could be a better option, of course this require homework.

We have just come back from a fun weekend in London! We took our 3 children for the first time and am so glad we booked with Big Bus tours! They made the experience so much easier and loved having JoJo as our operator, she was very helpful and knowledgeable about the history of London, I loved her Essex accent too! Will definitely book with Big Bus tours again!

Always hesitant with bus tours but this one ticked all the boxes: lots of stops, running all day, option to listen to the prerecorded commentary (that has music in between landmarks so you're not sitting there in silence) or switch up to another channel for the live guide onboard, along with providing earphones to use.

It had been raining when we boarded but the crew had complimentary ponchos for us to use if we still wanted to be upstairs, which was really appreciated.

There were traffic delays on the second bus we took but the guide kept everyone informed of the delays and assisted people with finding the right stops/bus switches for them to make it to where they wished to go, as it was one of the last buses on the run (so shout out to Ricky Quick for going beyond what most guides would!).

In late October we were in London and picked the hop on/off Big Bus for two days, it is possible to see most of London's popular attractions using this Bus, went for the two day pass as this includes a return river cruise and walking tour also.There are four different routes to travel and they use Marble Arch as the change over point. Tickets are available on line and from any uniformed Big Bus staff, they are not cheap however if used fully they are worth it.

We booked the Big Bug London HOHO through london pass. Got on the first bus in our area on the the red route. Cathy was a great tour guide, providing a lot of information while keeping the tour fun! She definitely made the experience a memorable one! We only used the tour bus in the morning because the traffic and rain made it impossible to catch one of the later buses to continue to a different route.

The Big Bus tour was good and great commentary was given. There are 4 tour lines to take and you will need more than one day to do all. The traffic is very heavy but the buses managed to get by quickly. Make sure you hold on to your voucher amongst the excitment for they are very strict. Also, the last bus times are very confusing to make sure you make it back in plenty of time. But overall, very nice tour.
It was very well organised and the mobile app was very helpful. Kathy was amazing guide, really funny and informative!

We brought a two day ticket as we wanted to do the river cruise, shame about the Greenpeace protesters on all the bridges on the Saturday which hampered all the tour buses getting around the city, we enjoyed it never the less JoJo our tour guide made us laugh on the Sunday morning on the Red Route she knew so much and was so chirpy loved her commentary. We would definitely book a Big Bus ticket again when we next come to London.
Tip if you know London has something on that day which may mean road closures just try and think ahead when booking your tickets.

We took this tour on September 27. We were able to sit upstairs where we wanted and ended up sitting right behind our guide, JoJo. She was welcoming and was very easy to hear and understand. We could tell that she liked her job and she that she liked London. We learned a lot about the attractions that we passed and also some of her personal insights into some of the buildings, neighbourhoods and restaurants. We had fun.

Booked this tour and i have to say it started well with the red tour bus fabulous friendly and helpful but when we changed to the blue tour to go to Madame Tussauds went down hill from there. Did not tell us where to get off the driver was rude a few times to customers and as for the staff on the way back they were rude & ignorant not helpful at all. Then threw all the passengers off at Trafalgar square because the bus was not getting over the bridge because of a protest. Was not informed of this at the start of the tour. Just no communication at all. Should have gone with the other tour more buses as well.

Our first time in London, lots to see and sort of overwhelming, but this tour is perfect. The 4 routes hit every area you want and all of the sights you should see. My review could end here, but I have to include the best part...superb customer service. My husband had his wallet lifted at The Tower of London. We lost ID, cash, credit cards and our brand new 2 day bus tour tickets. We went to our hotel (The Rubens at the Palace...see separate review of these heroes) and cancelled the credit cards then started walking to the police station. On our way we passed the Big Bus stop, the representative who sold us our tickets recognized us and asked how our day was...when we explained he got his Manager Dave involved and soon Dave made our day with complimentary tickets for a day....unbelievably kind and very much appreciated. This is customer service at the highest level!
paid full price on 2 tickets the tour was shortened due too the lord mayor show we asked for a refund and was refused tour guide said always something happening in london joke

This tour was amazing and well worth it! If you want to see everything London has to offer, you should book this tour. Our tour guide Joe was the best! He was funny, friendly, and full of information and fun facts on everything we saw. He definitely made the experience even better. Highly recommend especially if you’re not going to be in London for too long but want to see everything.

So this was a great way to see the sights however I have a few gripes. We had 3 different “guides”. One didn’t speak very clear English and was hard to understand. The second one didn’t really do much “guiding” he was basically a passenger with a big bus tour jacket on. Then the third was called Bill from Australia he was totally excellent, funny, engaging, factual, interesting and worth his weight in gold. The tour was a tad disjointed due to road closures, this was to be expected, I do feel we should have been made aware that we would miss 5/6 stops due prior to purchasing our tickets. A massive problem too was that there was NO information on which stops to go to and where they were and there were people on the streets who were big bus employees and yet had no idea where we could find the next bus. One of these such people sent us on a 1.5 mile wild goose chase looking for a bus stop that never appeared, we eventually took a taxi and missed the rest of the bus tour.
Has the potential to be excellent as long as you get a good guide and communication within the company was improved.

You must see the London sites this way! Live English guided or multilingual channels tell you what you are seeing as you pass! Unlimited on and off privileges for the duration of your pass! The guides are friendly knowledgeable and funny! If you’re site-seeing in London this is the way to do it!!

I booked the big bus tour in London for me and my 2 nephews who visited me in London for the day. I and my 2 nephews were sent to the wrong bus stop along with a group of about 30 people and waited for about 2 hours, upon further investigation we discovered we had been sent to the wrong stop. The guide sent someone who had never been to London, who didn't speak English as their native language on their way with some directions and told everyone to 'follow him'. During this time we were passed by multiple buses from competitive operators who next time I shall be using. When I have tried to address this issue directly with the Big Bus Company they 'can't find my booking' and have referred me to chase around after a third party vendor who offered a discounted rate for booking multiple attractions. We never even set foot on the Big Bus for the Tour as after 2 hours I had the take the boys to their next attraction. Thanks for ruining the day guys.
Used the bus all over London. Live tour guide Joann (our little Irish guide) was excellent, funny and informative. Great way to see the city, and get to attractions, etc.
We only had a day in London, and this was a good way to see the sights. We particularly enjoyed the live narration of our tour guide, Caran, who was knowledgeable and entertaining.

The tour was actually quite long, so you could really do this two days. Cheap way to get around London, but it takes so long to get around, that you may have to wait a bit if you're using it for transportation.

When you buy combo ticket of one day from London Eye,it is cheaper but You need to collect from Eye office which opens later (11 AM) than you would like to start bus tour ( Starts operating at 8 AM).This cuts down maximum usage of Big bus.Stops are very close by and staff very cooperative.
Simon was amazing! Added a lot of fun and quality to the tour and had a lot of knowledge around the different buildings and places we passed. Would recommend!
Economical and informational way to get to lots of different attractions around London! We had a great tour guide each time!
Great tour! Spent 3 days on and off. Very convenient. Great guides, especially JoJo and Bill! Very knowledgeable and upbeat

The Big Bus tour was part of our London Pass; did it first day in London because thought it would give an overview of the city, which is big and hard to navigate. The tour lived up to expectation because we would never have made it to all the sights the guide pointed out, so at least we got to drive past them... one disappointment is that it does not drive past Buckingham Palace so you don't really get to see it unless you get off an walk ( not their fault, I think the street is closed to buses) --- we took the tour from Victoria station, got off and toured Tower of London, then took the rest of the red tour back to Victoria.... The pass said it was only good for the day but they never scanned out ticket so we probably could have ridden next day as well. The guides were very good; it was a bit cold up top but you can see better from top deck. It was a fun experience. Bring your hat , gloves and scarf this time of year!!!

We had a great time on this tour, the live commentary on the red route was informative and we managed to see everything we wanted in one day. However, you can't get off at everystop and manage to see everything in one day. The London traffic is too bad and you will not fit everything in. I spent a full day out on this tour and spent a majority of the time on the bus. I still managed to see the main attractions in London don though (tower bridge, buckimgham palace, tralfagar square, etc.) My advice is go early so you have time to get off and see everything you want while also completing the tour.
Kathy was very knowledgeable and very nice as our tour guide. She was very pleasant and receptive to questions.

As it turned out we chose the day to start our tour as tens of thousands of others - to demonstrate against climate change. There was complete standstill that day, but luckily we had a tour guide, Terianne who managed to make the trip quite fun. As we were barely moving she was scraping the barrel for information around the surroundings, but had a good sense of humor and made fitting remarks continuously.
If you are thinking of taking the tour, keep your fingers crossed for her to be your guide.

We purchased the 72 hr. hop on/off package. It was a great deal. Learned a lot of interesting facts about London points of interest that we wouldn't have known otherwise.
Drivers and Tour guides were very friendly.
I would purchase it again.

Ground staff were not as excitable. However, the guides were very helpful. One American lady help us to find a coffee shop. Next, A very attentive guide. Got us to the right stop consider we were with two very young children. It is also very nice to listen to local accent. Brighten up our day when she starts speaking French to the French tourist to calm them down without being rude. Nailed it. Well done JoJo. Definitely hope to get JoJo if we are on the bus tour again.

This was my first time visiting London and everybody I talked to recommended doing one of the bus tours so I would be able to see as many of the sights as possible. My hotel was near the London Eye and Big Ben so I did those on foot and found a bus stop near Big Ben by the river. While I was trying to decide which tour to take I decided that I wanted one with an open roof since the weather was so nice. I noticed a couple of Big Bus employees standing near the bus stop so I approached one named Ralph who was fantastic! I asked him what the tour entailed and he took the time to explain everything to me, gave me suggested routes to take based on what I wanted to see and even recommended inexpensive places to eat! The tour itself was excellent with a live tour guide on several buses but there is always an automated tour guide you can enjoy using complimentary ear buds provided on the tour. I hopped off a few times to enjoy some of the sights and got to see many of the major sights around London in a short amount of time. There was even a boat ride down the river from the Tower of London to Westminster included in the ticket and the live tour guide on the boat was hilarious! All in all this was a fantastic experience that was well worth the money invested!

Went on the tour and had the full intention of hoping off a few times but we loved our tour guide so much we stayed for basically the whole route. Lewis was great! he even made sure to ask us what country we were from to make the tour more personal. AND he was hilarious, my husband and I laughed the whole time. He also told us the best spots to get the best photos. The only bad thing was the weather that day but we had such a great time that it didn't matter.

Did the Big Bus Hop-On Hop-Off tour as part of the London Pass. Was hesitant at first because I figured I could get a similar experience riding on the top of a double decker bus. Sure glad I did it though. Our guide was funny and informative. Well worth the time and money to get a crash course of London history and culture. Our guide, JoJo was great.

Steve
Best way to get around London, Fai our tour guide was amazing , knowledgable , funny, and made our tour fun!
Kathy, our guide, made our open top bus tour one of the best we've ever done. Lots of interesting tid-bits of information you don't get on the offen out of sync recordered commentary. Thanks Kathy.

Be prepared for slow traffic in London! The tour commentators are great and very helpful. The busses run frequently so it's very easy to get off, walk around, sightsee, then get back on a bus to continue the route. There is so much to see in London that you could easily buy a 2 or 3 day ticket to take advantage on the different routes and Thames cruises.
Susan gave great detail information about the city with a bit of humor. Felt safe with Enzo's driving. Both made my stay in London memorable.

We were in London for a short stay and took advantage of the Big Bus Hop on Hop Off tour. We were fortunate to have Faye, as our tour guide. Faye was extremely patient with passengers questions and her knowledge of London's landmarks was very informative. Her diction was clear and audible. Thoroughly enjoyed it as a way to take in as many sights as possible.

Quick trip to London for football game. Decided to do the Big Bus Hop on Hop Off tour.
Enjoyed the experience with JoJo & Norris. Jo Jo's narrative keep a smile on everyone's face,despite the traffic issues. Great tour.
We had a good tour and it gave a nice overview of the city highlights. There are plenty of stops, hence the hop on hop off name. Try to get seats up top.
Big bus tour was fun, entertaining and informative! It's a quick, fairly inexpensive way to see the sights of London

Our guide on the bus was a highlight of our trip!! Funny and knowledgeable, with lots of interesting commentary, she made the chilly and blustery day brighter. We bought a 3-day pass and hope to see her again on another day!

Best part of the tour was my guide advisor “Ahmed Abdullahi”! He was very friendly and informative and told me all the best sites and must sees! I am glad I followed his advice and took the river cruise to boot for free! He was even able to contact his supervisor and grant me a new ticket that I had lost and was able to finish seeing all that the Big Bus tour company promised. If you don’t do anything on your trip to London this is probably the best deal for your money! Two big thumbs up!

Like several others who posted here, we pre-booked for 4 adults.- We were staying in South Kensington. Went to the first stop - near Victoria/Albert museum. No longer a stop.
