Walked to second stop - 10 minutes away, by Harrod's - no longer a stop. Looked on app for 3rd nearby pick up - nope, not a stop.
We finally found a Big Bus going the other way - the driver stopped, got out, and had an angry phone call with someone about traffic problems that he had not been told about.

Our family has done hop on, hop off buses in many cities. We thought they were very good to excellent. This was by far the worst. I see from other recently posted reviews that others have had problems. I am very sorry we selected this company and would suggest others avoid it.
Tour guide Tabea was great tour guide and very helpful to all the passengers to know when to get off the bus.

My wife and I recently spent nine days in London, and decided to go on a 24 hour Big Bus tour on our first day. It was a great way to introduce ourselves to the sights of London. There are four lines to choose, all transferable-Red, Blue, Orange and Green. We spent the majority of our day on the Red Line, and hopped off at the Tower of London, where we enjoyed a two hour tour. Overall the Big Bus tour was a very good experience, with the only jarring note being sitting for twenty five minutes at Victoria Station, waiting for a driver and guide change.

Bought a 2 day hop on hop off tour, was very impressed with the commentary from the tour guides had lots of information regarding the famous landmarks ,and also some general information tinged with a bit of humour.
Would highly recommend.

A few years back we took the bus tour both here and in Paris. That time the London tour went fine. This time, I had three 16-year old girls on the trip, who I sent on the bus to see the city, as I was chasing our lost baggage at Heathrow. When they came back, what I heard was surprising, since my daughter had been on the bus before, and this was nearly off-peak season. The commentator was not that enthusiastic and they actually hopped off one bus and waited for the next one!!!! (The other two girls were in London for the first time). They did like the second bus but said, that the overall trip for the money paid was Meh!!! So I am hoping the service gets better.

We were told by a local to get on a tour bus to see London was the easiest way and Big Bus was no disappointment. Dennis approaches my partner and I professionally giving us the best deal. After hoping off the bus to see the London eye we were a bit lost but saw the bus and hopped right on to be greeted by Jojo and her amazing personality. I wish we would have done this earlier in our trip!

Absolutely wonderful! The bus tour was so efficient and the guide (said he had only worked for the tour for a brief period-- July) was incredible! He knew the sites and history very well. It was clear that he was doing the tour guide thing for a bit of fun because he was a very well educated gentleman. He stood up, spoke to the group, was highly engaged with the tour and controlled the tour in an excellent manner. Really great! London is a gorgeous city that expertly integrates new, futuristic architecture with its rich history and culture.

This bus tour is ideal because not only do you good to learn all about the capital and see the sights but you get to take the weight of your feet for a good 2 and a half hours, if you choose to stay on the bus and take everything in, But if you wish to hop on hop off and visit certain stops you are free to do that as well. This is very imformative trip and for visitors from near or far it is one way to visit London.

You hardly get to see most of the attractions
. The traffic is so bad and the congestion basically from one attraction to the other it takes you an hour to two hours. better off taking the tube to visit the attractions.

I purchased a one day hop on and hop off bus tour ticket because I was very limited in my time in London and thoroughly enjoyed seeing many sites just on this bus. Our guide Jojo was amazing and a true Londoner. Def recommend this company

Booked a one day pass and took Red tour. All the busses were crowded - usually standing room only. The busses have a recorded audio guide. On every bus, some guides didn't work (static, no sound, one of the 3.5mm jacks was plugged up). Waited so long for a bus at Tower of London we gave up and took the tube. On the positive side, busses are clean. Would not do this tour again.

super short break - the highlight after our theatre and dining events the only way to visit was the BIG TOUR BUS HOP ON HOP OFF a great day around London - saw many many sights - and spent time at quite a few HOP OFFS - the only way to tour - using the ordinary buses takes so much time planning and switching routes The inclusive river Thames trip was a great bonus We joined the tour at Russell Square 1 minute from the Hotel and at the end of the trip - drop off at the hotel - at our age this is the way to do it Oh by the way I nearl;y forgot this - GREAT VALUE WORTH EVERY PENNY - staff were very good and helpful - well done
Great way to see London especially with a best bus driver Ray” Ray of Sunshine”He was really helpful and made our day!!! Thank you Ray and Big Bus London!

Had a day to spare so took the red route and sat back for the 2.5 hrs and listened to commentary by Emma, a true Londoner who impressed us by knowing everything about the city and its history. Enjoyed the day in the sun.

Hop on Hop off is generally a good tour for the overview & view of the cities tourist attraction. They even have a live guide on board. Big bus is the most popular and frequent service , but the traffic is london is too slow hence the tour go slow, secondly the tour is unidirectional so if you want to visit the previous stop again you need to wait for another two hours to reach back the same spot.though they were proving poncho it was too cold and wet upstairs. the buses generally get dirty & littered as the day progress .

Absolutley loved this tour! The hop on, hop off tour is the best! We were able to explore when we wanted to at whatever stop and hop back on the next bus that came by! The staff were extremely friendly and knowledgeable about each area of the city. They knew historical data and it was overall an awesome experience.

Ally was our guide and she nailed it. She answered all questions and took pictures for people. We rode all around the city and she knew every area.

Overall, awesome tour that allowed us to see the city without ALL the walking. We were able to walk when we wanted.

First of all hope you get on a bus with Mattie (or Maddie?) as your commentator and Gary as your driver! She was so much fun! and Gary has to be the calmest, most patient and kind driver in all of London! We loved all the Harry Potter references!

Ellie was absolutely fantastic!! We rode the red route with a different guide and when Ellie came on board we had to go around again because she explained so much history. I felt like she really did her research and had great customer service. I wish we could of had her on all the bus we rode.

Wasn't looking forward to the HOHO experience in London last week - We were with my in-laws and it was the best way to see lots of sights without them having to walk.
I was absolutely amazed at the tour....our guide Phillip was so knowledgeable - he went out of his way to tell us historic, current day and personal history of the London sights.
I would recommend this tour to anyone going to London even you've been before (which we had) and if you get Phillip as a guide you'll be doubly pleased.
If you are going to London, this is a must. We traveled all over London first then decided to get off when we wanted to. Must take. Great

I booked 4 tickets to tour London with visitors. We boarded at the Tower of London to find the bus full with many people standing. The traffic was so bad it took over an hour to get to Hyde Park. There was no live guide, only a recording that churned out patriotic music and an occasional comment pointing out parliament, lambeth palace etc but with very limited descriptions. There was no comment about the monument at Hyde Park Corner, Green Park etc.
I abandoned the tour at that point and realised you can take a taxi to visit the sights a lot quicker and cheaper and more comfortably.

Only had one day in London and spent it on the bus going on the different coloured routes. Fantastic commentary throughout and all staff very pleasant and helpful! Would highly recommend if tight for time to see London and get a history lesson!!

At the outset, the Big Bus London Hop-On Hop-Off Tour disappointed us.

While waiting for a bus, we saw Big Bus London driver zip by our St Petersburgh Place bus stop, leaving us behind even though the bus was not quite full of passengers! Was he so much in a hurry that he missed us? Where was the bus stop attendant? In the end, we had to wait another 15 minutes for the next bus to come.

The service staff at various stops were a bit unfriendly in contrast to the other bus attendants around.

Maybe you should try the Golden Tours Hop-On Hop-Off. I haven't tried Golden Tours either but hopefully, they won't just zip by you like Big Bus did to us.

Four of us did this and saw everywhere in London we wanted to see. Saw the London eye, London Bridge and the tower. The guide on board was very informative and told us a bit of the history of the places and buildings we saw. This was definitely the best way to see London and you could get off and explore by yourselves or just enjoy the tour.

At the first time we have a problem with the tickets because we buy it online and we dont receive any confirmation but a nice guy Ahmed Abdullahi help us to get them, excelent service from him! He is the best of big bus

Been on a few different bus tours this is the 1st time with this firm I actually feel like I learnt something this time much happier.

My only complaint if any bus driver didn't wait for us to take our seats up top very very un nerving

The bus was late by an hour and this seems to be standard. The operator is trained to keep you there by saying it won’t be long now, it is just stuck in traffic. The headphones were spotty. The tour itself was nice but the traffic is really bad in London and the bus stopped often and the sights were obscured for people sitting inside the bus. I would not do it again or recommend it.

We arrived on day one later then planned and decided to do the bus tour, as something just to do, to pass time. Since it was a little passed 3pm, the guy selling us our ticket said we had 24 hours to use the ticket and could use them into the next day. That's when we met Jo! We joined her tour mid route and she was awesome!! She had us laughing and made sure she pointed out all the great picture spots. She even had tips on other places to go while in town. We followed her advice and went to watch the Changing of the guard at BP, as well as checked out two of her recommended restaurants. One day two, we decided to start the red tour from the beginning.....and to our surprise....Jo again was our tour guide!! She even recognized us from the day before. She was just as fun and knowledgeable as day one!! She was a real highlight of our trip! Thank you Jo and Adrien (bus driver) for a great time!! Kuddos to Adrian for his excellent skills on maneuvering the big bug through Londons street and traffic.
Emma was wonderful, knowledgeable and helpful on my visit. She even explained which stop to get off to Uber to Harrod’s

This bus service was excellent and convenient, if you had an e ticket you could jump on at the closest stop and get it scanned. We loved the live commentary, especially by our tour guide William - insightful and fun facts!

We arrived to London and had just two days to cover as much as we could. We decided to get an overview on the Big Bus and first one we picked had a guide we loved. Her name is Terianne. She was friendly and had a lot of great information historical and practical about London and sites we were passing. She made the whole experience fun and exciting. The company is well organized. Only problem is the heavy traffic in central London, but there is not much anyone can do about that. Terianne filled the time with fun anecdotes and tips. I would happily recommend the tour. Especially if you take it in the late afternoon when the city glows in the evening sun. Great for photography.

If you have time (2-3 hours) to do this it is great. If you don't have the time, I would not do this. You can hop off at different stops if you want. The bus is driving fast so you can't really get good pictures. JoJo was a great tour guide.

The first bus we went on the guide was completely mumbling, second was an American and she was extremely not knowledgeable about anything but her script. Then the other two lines don’t even have a guide. The busses were dirty ! The boat goes down to one area and stops for 35 minutes and for nothing no one tells you what’s there or that you’re stoping for 35 minutes while your waiting for a group of students to get on.
My take is to get an Oyster card and explore yourself. This is a waste of money and people selling tickets fight over selling them
To people. Skip this

Jo was hilarious! We stayed on the whole loop just to hear her commentary! Especially loved the British humour towards the Americans who had no idea what she was talking about 👌
Nas was a great driver also! Hats off for driving in London, let alone a bus.
Love the aussies 🇦🇺

We have been on Hop on Hop off bus tours in numerous cities in Europe & in New York. The London One was the worst tour we have ever been on. The entire tour was supposed to take 3 hours. We got through 1/2 the tour in 3 1/2 hours. We sat in traffic most of the time & had to detour due to construction. During the detour there was no commentary. The commentary we did hear was 5 minutes behind the point of interest so we missed some of them. The only saving grace was the river tour. There was live commentary & no traffic.

Family of 4 with teenage kids. We got some great insights into the local sights particularly from Joe who once drove a black cab and has a great deal of knowledge delivered in a fun way. Thanks Joe great afternoon
Enjoyed the tour - our guide Irish Jo was good and had sone good stories to tell. Admire the drivers skill in the London traffic. Biggest regret not having time to do the boat trip. Always next time.

We purchased the hop on hop off bus tickets because this was my first ever trip to London in my 31 years of life and I wanted to see everywhere we was very lucky to jump on JoJo's bus she was amazing myself and my partner did the full tour with jojo and she was just the best told us stuff even I didn't know and I'd done my research. If I could give more than 5* I would she was funny, told us everything she knew and made it a brilliant journey that's why we stayed on the bus for the full tour

Great trip on arrival to London. Recommend taking the full tour and then selecting where you want to stop. Took about 2.5 hours to complete. We loved the river cruise and found the top deck and guide very enjoyable. The bus guide was ok and the recorded commentary was just average. We ended up missing the last bus home and had to take the subway.

We were in London to join a cruise out of Southampton and had 24 hours to spare before boarding our ship. I had booked a one day pass on the Big Bus Tour which included a Beat the Line Ride on the London Coca Cola Eye and a boat trip on the Themes. It was the best way to see as much of London in a very short period of time. We first spent 3 and a half hours on the double decker bus taking in the sights of London with live commentary from our onboard guide which was excellent. We then joined the thousands of other tourist at the London Eye and after redeeming our ticket from the ticket office we were on the eye in less than 30 minutes. From there we boarded the Themes tour boat which is moored at the London Eye for a two hour plus river cruise with very informative live commentary again. We saw and did so much in a very short space of time. The Big Bus Tour organised the lot and although it cost 126.00 Pounds or $226.00 Australia dollars for the two of us it was great value

We bought the 48 hour ticket which had some extras including a walking tour and a river cruise. Day one and we thought what amazing value this wa as out guide was very informative with history and anecdotes of the passing sights. Also explained how to switch over to alternate routes. The next two times we used the service was a shambles with tour guides just going thru the motions and stating the abovious sights as we passed them with none of the interesting witticisms of their colleague and one guide hardly knew much at all including some commentary about a haunted house in London and when quizzed by one of the other patrons about some more details on the story had absolutely nothing to back it up. A hop on hop off bus is a great way to get your bearing on the first couple of days in the city but I would suggest using one of the other two providers.

OK London is known for it's rain so on a rainy day you might expect that the open topped bus - which is nice in fine weather, could also be closed when it's throwing down cats & dogs from above. Like the rest of the worlds open topped buses = Madrid, Paris, Seville and even tiny little Bilbao, all have open topped buses that have a closing sliding top roof. But NO not in sunny London. Top deck has 4 seats under cover and the rest our out in the open. Consequently the rain falls on the seats and subsequently flows back ad forward as the bus stops an goes. A nice way to fill your boots with water.
And then when you hop on the bus at St Pancras which is the green route they said and want to change over to the red route by changing as the map said - STOP, surprise surprise the green bus changes into the red bus. Confused, we where and then there was the wonderful red ear buds to hear the infrequent commentary that is very much dependent on finding a socket in a seat location that actually worked. 4 seats found 2 not working which isn't good on the green / red bus then it was a raffle as well on the only two other buses we got on. Quicker to walk in London than sit on a bus (traffic is manic).
And then there was the smooth operator at St Pancras offering 'never to be repeat' only available here 20% discount skip the line tickets for The Tower of London. Which actually turned out to be only 10% discount freely available most spots and NEWS flash, there are NO skip the line advantages to be had at Tower - so nice rip off their lads.
Overall excluding the added issues all faced due to the rain, this company is running a pretty shoddy operation that I'd suggest could easily be avoided by not buying tickets fresh off the train from anywhere - like we did at St Pancras and doing a bit of research as we should have. Appeared to me that 'The Original Big Bus'companies buses that passed us had living commentators, better routes and better equipped buses.

we boarded near hyde park and enjoyed the tour. Our guide with classic wit was able to infuse the history of London with humour. would recommend this for the first day in London tour. It helps plan subsequent days

Took entire Red tour from Green Park with my two 15 year old daughters! Big thanks to Ellie who was a fabulous guide with lots of interesting info about the sights and who was enthusiastic to share her knowledge! We live near London, but have never done an open top bus tour! Who would've thought that one night in a particular hotel would be £28,000!!?? Would recommend this route if you want to see the most famous buildings in London - the two hours went by in a flash! we didn't care about the traffic - London is a busy working city so there are bound to be hold ups, and to be honest, it just meant more time for photos and to watch the city go by! Sit on the upper deck to get the best view and see things you wouldn't normally notice form pavement level!! Loved it! Thank you for a great day out!!

My friend, myself and our 2 kids had a fab day out yesterday. Brilliant and funny commentary from the guides. Staff at stops very helpful and the river cruise was a great bonus. Best way to view London ever.
Wonderful experience, would recommend to others. Nice details of buildings and other important landmarks. Guide Ellie was very nice to listen to. Thanks Ellie!
Our tour guide Phil was excellent. He had a lovely, upbeat manner. He was very interesting and had Lots of fun facts. All his stories were appropriate for all ages. He was very friendly and helpful.
Great experience with Terianne our live commentator and learnt some quaint details and loved her passion and dedication!

We had a wonderful experience on the London Big Bus tour with live commentary from Emma! She was absolutely fantastic! Very knowledgeable on the history of London and plenty of humor added. All six of us ladies enjoyed her so much we stayed on the bus longer then originally planned. She set the standard for the rest of our excursions but no other guide came close! Thanks Emma!

I had a great experience. I never had to wait long for a bus. I never had trouble getting a seat on the top level. The routes were easy to understand and follow. On the red line, there are live tour guides. I didn’t find the bus drivers friendly, but I had little interaction with them luckily. I would recommend this tour.
We did this on our first day and this is a great way to start your vist. Good sightseeing tour but our tour guide was not so friendly and nt so interesting.
It was great, we had a great tour guide. I would highly recommend for people who want to see London's most famous attractions in little time.

Marta did a wonderful job despite difficult technical issues with the sound system. She was very knowledgeable and injected humor throughout her tour. I’m a professional tour guide in NYC and really appreciated her expertise and delivery. Unfortunately the sound system on the bus had a lot of static during the first half of the tour, then cut out completely for the second half. Marta exhibited much less frustration than I would have in that situation and bravely soldiered on. Kudos to Marta!

Great ride on the Big bus today our host Jo Jo was fantastic full of knowledge and great fun
She totally enhanced our experience with her personality and wit
This is a must do tour around London for any new visitor to the UK to get orientated and get a taste of this amazing city
Recommended!!!!

I really enjoyed this bus tour. I took the best pictures from my whole trip from the top level of the bus. Our tour guide - I believe her name was Ellie - was very friendly and gave us lots of information about the sites. I really enjoyed it, and would highly recommend Big Bus London!

The view was breathtaking the service was awesome and they were well informative on all the historical buildings shops and much more. We did the redline tour. Our tour guide was Emma she was so awesome. Will indefinitely be back.

Visiting London with family and decided to buy tickets for the first time ever. It was definitely well worth it.

You could spend the entire day hopping on and off the bus at different landmarks.

We got on the early red route bus trip and found Kathy to be knowledgeable, pleasant and very helpful!

We did the bus on our first fill day in London. Thought it would be a great way to see everything and a way to decide what attractions we would like to see throughout our visit. You can pick up the bus at any of their designated bus stop locations. Downstairs inside the bus, especially in the back, was warm so we opted to sit up top. We enjoyed the live commentary on the red route. We did the entire red route and a little bit of the blue route. Great way to relax and take in everything. Added bonus is there is free wifi on the bus.

We thought we would be getting a live person telling us about the sights we would driving by on the bus, but we had to listen to the pre-recorded tour highlights as we drove by the main sights on the Red Line; we were given earbuds and the narration was adequate, but not live. Perhaps it was because we got on later in the afternoon. Unfortunately it was rainy that day and we had to sit downstairs in the bus and could not go up to the top deck as it was about 75% open to the sky and with little kids, you have to keep them dry and safe. When we got to Green Park, we had to get off the bus we were on and move to another bus as it was a change in shift. The pre-recorded narration on the second bus did not work so we had no commentary on where we were going or where we actually were. Not so great service! Was part of our London Pass included attractions. Perhaps we should have taken the Golden Bus instead.

Barbara the live commentator made this ride amazing! She put an Englishman to shame! This lady knew some of the most diverse facts about London landmarks and other landmarks that are not so well known. I was out with my partner and to family members from Austria, they loved it too. Great tour! :)

voucher ID 531424461 - my ticket number.

Recently did the hop on hop off tour of London. Great way to see the city, a must do in London. A little pricey for a 2 day pass for a family of 4, but still a must do. Buses were frequent and the tour guides were informative. Would definitely recommend.

We took our elderly grandparents on a special London trip, and this was definitely a great option for people in large family trips or elderly people that can’t walk too much. We did an entire loop on the red line, however on our attempt to get home from Westminster our bus driver wouldn’t give any directions so we missed our stop. However I won’t deduct any starts for this because Nick was fantastic - one of the most informative tour guides I’ve ever had personally and really had something to say about every street and make every fact entertaining. Unfortunately I can’t remember the names of the boat guide that we had or the guide on our return bus home that was also so lovely but I have to say what a top notch team!

Had a fantastic tour!
Laura our guide was brilliant! So knowledgable ! And funny
Highly enjoyable day

Used the Big Bus tour in London in August, and had a great experience. I was first a bit skeptical that it would be a convenient way to get around. They have a ton of buses, and the bus guides were great. They have a canned audio for all languages, and some of the buses have live people giving the tours. JoJo was our first bus, and she made the trip! She had great information on the city, and made the trip so worth it!

I did have an issue that I lost my wallet on the bus. later in the day. The next bus helped me catch the original bus, and unfortunately it was not located. The BigBus administration was very helpful, and also replaced my ticket for a day, since I had a three-day pass. The customer service was great, and I was very pleased with the overall experience. The three-day pass includes a night ride and a return trip on the boat tour, which was also worth it. Thank you BigBus for the excellent experience.

Yes, you're stuck in traffic a bit, but our tour guide Emma was super nice and knew really a lot about London, she was the reason why we didn't hop off, we stayed for the whole tour. I used to live in London and she just blew my mind with the knowledge she had. I'd say the guide is at least half of the experience so be sure to try and catch Emma.

My husband and I were visiting London and today we decided to book with the Big Bus Hop On Hop Off. It was amazing and Nick was so knowledgeable and cracked jokes.
I highly recommend this tour and if get Nick you’re lucky.

First, London Bus Co. We think it's the great customer service that your peeps gave us that made this experience so wonderful. Big shout out to Terianne who gave great narratives on the red tour. Great Big Shout Out to Zoltan who escorted us to the boat dock. He went out of his way to make sure we got to the Cit Boat Tour. Finally Captain Jamie, you were the best tour guide. Your jokes were funny, and your info was great. We chose the boat tour combo and are so pleased with what we got out of it. Started at the Palace and from there saw EVERYTHING. We were worried about how to plan ourbtwo days, and the first bus stop guide helped us know how to use this bus tour. In general, don't panic. You will see it all. The two day pass, for us got us to the highlights we really wanted. Palaces, British Museum, Bridges, Parks, Parliament, Thames. Westminster Abby, neighborhoods. We waited on average 10 to 15 minutes for our buses. I had one problem. The app is terrible. NOT at all helpful tracking buses for us. Overall, we really enjoyed our two days using the Big Bus Tour, and we recommend this company.

Got one-day Big Bus Hop-On/Hop-Off from London Pass. We actually rode the Red and Green lines and didn't have time for the Blue line. Highly recommended for people with difficulties walking or just a starting tool to get familiarized with the city.

I continue to use Big Bus Hop-On Hop-Off. Even though I've been to London several times, I was traveling with my teenage son who had never been. Coming in from the US, arriving in the morning after an overnight flight, a bus tour is just the thing to see a lot without walking! We took both the "live tour guide" tour and the recorded tour. If at all possible take the live tour. Our guide was wonderful, very knowledgeable and funny! July was tough as it is high tourist season so both people and car traffic was heavy. The tour at times went very slowly and the bus was often crowded. I highly recommend the two day tour. The first day you can get the lay of the land and enjoy the ride in your jetlagged body, take the included night tour (no hop off) and the second day you can spend going to the places you only saw the day before. Don't miss out on the river cruise to Greenwich, it is a lovely half or full day trip! A great value and super friendly staff.

We did this as part of the London Pass on our first full day. There are a few different routes that you can go on to suite what you want to see best.

I didnt catch her name but our bus had a guide on it who was quirky and very informational!

They also have staff waiting at the pickup spots so that you can see where you need to be. Big Bus is the best way to get a crash course on your first day in any city they operate (we have done it in Dublin, Rome, and now London!)

Great value for the money & Great service!
Carlos De Melo is a great supervisor with excellent communication skills! He was very helpful and offered great assistance!
I highly recommend it

I took the red tour in a Big Bus as a part of the London pass. The first guide Laura was great. She was super funny and her commentary was on point. It was a great way to give “tired legs” some break while still seeing this great city.

appart from having a day out in let's rip off a tourist season. the guy who sold me the ticket was very rude and discriminatory towards me. not only this he sent me in the wrong direction knowing full well I was on crutches. when we arrived at the bus stop the guy who collects the tickets was equally rude and discriminatory. he made me climb stairs on crutches as know one down stairs would give up a seat for me. companies like this should be trained in disabity and deaf awareness

Good sightseeing tour, got to see all the main attractions of London, we used the bus a few times and got a few different tour guides which were all good however Ian (New Zealand accent) was great, very funny and friendly and made the journey on the bus interesting.

I liked the BigBus company. The staff was nice and the guides made me giggle while telling the story. The trip came with the Night Pass and also a Boat Tour. I did the night bus and the driver was fast. It was just a fast, cold cruise. I don’t recommend. However, the day trip to Greenwich was included and I made a day trip from Westminster. It was perfect. I highly recommend the day trip.

All in all. The bus tour is worthy the money. Even 2 days I did not have time to ride all the routes they offer.

I am requesting a refund for this trip. I asked for it via email already but did not get a response. I purchased the ticket online for a specific day, and it turns out that that day was the Ride London day, which means central London was closed for traffic. So not only did I not get to visit many great areas, other areas were even more congested than typically, and I spent hours on the bus in stop and go traffic. Hindsight I should have just gotten off but the tour guide kept on saying that it would get better after the next light. A simple email before the day informing me of the closure of London's center would have been great and I would have taken the tube instead of booking this tour.

I purchased the tickets online on the day but did not receive a text as requested. I had to screenshot the confirmation page to show i had purchased the ticket. Then when downloading the App it kept crashing. Also the App was not updated as we walked to St Paul's for our first pick up and it was closed due to roadworks! Was not happy as we then had to get a taxi to the next stop! Once on the bus the tour guide Ian was very entertaining and knowledgeable. But the previous stress of the tickets and closed stop put a slight damper on the experience.

I had such a great time! You can tell my guide Barbara really cares about showing her riders a good time, she was singing along to every song dancing up and down the deck making sure the energy was always amazing, she honestly made mine and my friends experience unforgettable. I really enjoyed the random facts she told us about the girls as we drove around as well, it was really interesting and insightful!
Our guide Caren was very pleasant, helpful and infomative. Weather was also excellent. The boat cruise had a bunch of new infromation, quite amusing also. The whole experience was stunning.

This was our first day out in London and we got to see so much of the city! Haymitch, our tour guide, was fantastic at giving us detailed information about all the sites and kept the tour fun and upbeat. Would highly recommend this to anyone wanting to see London!
I did the day tour with my nephew and he left his phone on one of the buses. We got it back the next day, thanks to the several great staff members who very, very helpful. Thank you.

It's my mother and sister's first time in London, and I thought what a great way to show them the sights! To begin, a gentleman named Habil (?) I believe was extremely helpful in getting us set up for the proper tour to fit our needs. Once we boarded we were guided by Cassie who was fantastic! She was very knowledgeable and quickly answered questions patrons had on the spot, such as "when was this bridge constructed?" We also enjoyed her sense of humor which went over some people's heads, but we appreciated each quip. Great experience for the family, 5 stars!

I took family who were visiting from the Caribbean on the Hop-on-Hop-off bus at the weekend and they enjoyed it immensely. It was great opportunity to see most of London in a short space of time. I must admit I miss the open mike, as the system kept breaking down so you missed some of the commentary.
Perfect tour guide with a wide knowledge. All the family enjoyed this trip. Very professional and experienced
We had the pleasure of having Barbara act as our tour guide. She is very knowledgeable and refreshing. Her personal anecdotes were greatly appreciated.

We visited Europe this summer and signed up for the hop on hop off tour for both London and Paris, both cities did not disappoint. I read some reviews and I agree it all depends on who the guide is. The lady in Paris was sweet, entertaining, and smiled. The gentleman in London was hilarious with impeccable comedic timing with some of the more gruesome facts. The river cruise was included in our package for the 48 hour family ticket and it was well worth it. We had 6 people in our party aged 13 to 80, everyone had a wonderful time.

We got the Big Bus tour tickets because they were the first to collar us outside Waterloo... Friendly sales guy gave us a really good deal on tickets (£30 cheaper than booking online)... All the tours seem to stop in the same places around London (you're always seeing all the tour buses when you're getting on and off) and the Big Bus ones (which are brownish) are as good as any. We found some of the drivers and live commentators seemed a bit bored but others were great and we were lucky enough with the weather to sit on the open top for the whole time (which is a must - you don't see anything from inside really). The routes were great and they run every 5-10 minutes on the main 'red route' around the central areas. A real bonus was the free boat trip which we took from Tower of London down to Westminster. We learned a lot from the live commentary which you listen to through headphones that plugin on your seat (so you can listen to a pre-rerecorded one instead or different languages). The company has a free app to help you find bus stops (which we found crashed a lot) and we struggled to find the stops sometimes as they don't all seem to be listed on the bus stop signs. All in all though a great value tour bus operator which gave us exactly what we wanted.
This is the second bus tour I have been on. JoJo the tour guide has been exemplary and was a lot of fun and full of information. Made our day!

We visited just about everywhere of any historical interest it was fantastic and our driver gave a constant running commentary, with quite a bit of humour laid on besides! It was a very long trip as we normally like to go right round with the bus first and then we know where we want to go to and do it again, but this time, we basically did the whole trip and were too exhausted to go round again and stop off at points we wanted to spend more time at, but we did manage some of this the following day! I think you need to think about more than one day to do all you want and visit places during the initial drive round. Where-ever we go if there is a hope on hop off bus we take it during the first day or two and that gives us a better knowledge of what we want to do and where we want to spend more time. London's Big Bus is amazing.
I liked it very much. Our tour guide from yesterday Emma, was really great! The descriptions were really good and funny.

I highly recommend the Big Bus Tour Bus in London. We are a family of 6 and it was a great way for us to get to know London at a high level. We enjoyed it and highly recommend it. Also kudos to Lockman. He was the gentleman that helped us purchase this experience and he was highly professional, friendly and very knowledgeable.

We spent an afternoon on the Big Bus tour, hoping to get our money's worth. We weren't in London long, and we knew this was the fastest way to see the sights.

The recorded audio that plays is kind of lame, and when you maybe luck out and have a live guide, the channel they use is static-y and you can barely hear them.

The biggest disappointment was our last driver. There was no room at the top of the bus, so we had to sit "downstairs". The driver was screaming and swearing (including f-bombs) all over the place at other drivers and over the phone. He was AWFUL. He was also a terrible driver, in general. The screaming/swearing fits happened at least a handful of times. He announced that the last stop was at the London Eye, which is where we wanted to be let off. Then he changed his mind and said we were continuing on. He said we'd have to get there from the next stop (don't remember what it was). Then, all of a sudden, were being let off at the London Eye! We had no idea what was happening. We even heard him turning down people at stops (not letting them on), even though there was plenty of room on the bottom level!

Unfortunately, we didn't get his name, as he got off the bus before we did and didn't know where he went.

Very disappointing experience!

We did this our first day in town. 10 of us. We did the 3 hour RED tour. It was fine. Hop on and off. Buses were running about 10 min apart mid day. With the standard ticket you are also able to do a river cruise. We did one back from Tower Bridge to Westminster which was great. Recommended.
Loved the interesting stories from Emma on the red line bus. It was a great way to see the city and learn about the history.

My wife has been to London many times - I had only passed through Heathrow on my way to Africa or some other work location. London was a new experience made more interesting by the "Big Bus" guides. Even my wife learned some new things. We had several guides and enjoyed them all. Even off-duty drivers were friendly and willing to offer advice and answer questions. It was the best money we spent in London. We rode the entire Red and Blue Lines.
The flexibility is great when you don't have a lot of time for long tours. Great way to see London in a short time.

On my family’s first trip to London it was difficult to know what to do or where to go. We read previous reviews of Big Bus tour so decided to give it a go. Once we got on the bus we found we had the greatest guide JOJO and driver Wesley. They made the hot day a great time for our family/friend group of 9. He knowledge mixed in with a health sense of humor made the day super enjoyable. She made sure we knew all the tips and tricks for navigating London, made great suggestions and still kept safety at the forefront of the tour. She was so great we decided not to hop off at some locations because we didn’t want to lose this guide.
If you get a chance, before you hop on- find out if JoJo is working- if she’s working- she’s with the wait!
PS- thanks Wesley for navigating the drive for us- you got skills!
A grateful American family.

My partner and I stayed at the Royal national hotel where there was an office selling Big bus hop on hop off tickets for 30 pounds each with the inclusion of the river cruise.

We both felt that it was an easy way to get around and see many iconic locations.
I feel like it is very suitable for people to do one of these tours at the start of there trip as it is a great way to get your bearings of the city of London.

All our buses had live commentary and I felt they did a great job!
Would definitely recommend to family and friends.
With a live tour guide but you could choose the pre recorded multi lingual version. We got Martha on the Big Bus Red route and she was extremely informative. START early.
This is a great way to tour London. You can 'ride' to various locations and then hop on and off as the mood strikes you.

My travel agent suggested this tour for myself and my daughter to see London. We purchased a 2 day pass. It was very confusing on how to get our tickets from our vouchers. After we figured out where to go and who to speak with we were only given a 1 day Pass. It took forever to get to where we wanted to go and the bus was way to crowded. I told my daughter we were better off with the public transportation. I don’t know how to get a refund. But I would definitely like one. And would not suggest this tour to anyone.

Bought what i thought was a classic ticket 72 pound(2 people) after my 10% online discount. Got given a basic ticket at bus and only realised when I tried to get on the river cruise..."too bad you got wrong ticket". Went to bbt ticket seller "too bad you got wrong ticket". No where on the ticket i purchased does it say what sort of ticket it is...just have to take your word for it but a classic ticket with cruise was 66 pound (2 people)on your website today...I got ripped off.So my advice....

1. DONT BUY A TICKET.

2. DON'T BUY A TICKET online and get ripped off.

3. The headphones are mostly faulty and you don't get any commentary.

4. THE GUIDES ON RED BUS SHOUT AND SPEAK SO FAST INTO MIC YOU HAVE A HARD TIME UNDERSTANDING THEM. If you do manage to get a headphone that works.

5. The buses were overcrowded...after 3.30 traffic is way too busy to use service. Quicker to walk.

6. Bit of road rage happening from bus drivers. Not a good feel.

6. DON'T BUY A TICKET. Go on another tour.

We had one day in London and wasted it on your buses.

I bought tickets from a discount website making them £10 cheaper than they would have been had I paid on the day. All staff were very helpful but the routes (specifically the green one) are not as shown on the map which made things confusing and messed up my plans for the day. Then the bus I got onto had a broken audio system so we had to change buses which meant 2 bus loads crammed into one which in 35 degree weather was far from ideal and a few people had to get off to stop from becoming unwell. There was also one point on the tour that we passed a Korean War memorial where there was clearly some sort of ceremony taking place with uniformed soldiers and people, I assume, of Korean heritage paying their respects but whilst we were stopped at the traffic lights alongside them, the live guide continued to talk loudly into the mic. I felt this was disrespectful.

However, the river cruise that ticket that comes with the price was well worth the money and by far the best part of the day.

We arrined in London on Saturday and bought 72 hour delux ticket everthing was fantastic until Mon when we got off at Lambert to visit Imperial war museum after visit we got back on bus asked driver if this bus took us to tower of london to do river cruise he said it did, so between drivers and guides we were on and off buses for the next 31/2 hours, when we eventually arrived at tower of london were told we were too late for river cruise.Disappointed is an understatment so were making our way back to marble arch tour guide tried to tell us there was no purple line even though we had used it two days previous and we would have to get off bus and go on underground.Please train guides/drivers very disappointed travelling in that heat for nothing

We had a tour today on the red line with Ian as our tour guide, he was brilliant and really made the experience as we had two other journeys on other routes which weren’t half as enjoyable! He was knowledgable and slipped in the odd joke which made the journey all that more fun! Great way to get around London as you can hop on and off as you please. Would definitely recommend!
The information was really good and the tour guide was very funny and interesting. I did both red and blue lines.

We purchased 4 tickets online at a cost of £133.12
Sat for an hour listening to drivel, and when we eventually got off the bus turned to see that we were probably a 15 minute walk from where we started.
Painful waste of money.

We were on a Tour with Faye for about three hours last week and thoroughly enjoyed it. She shared quite a bit about London and the sites we were seeing and also helped answer several of our questions to get around the rest of the weekend. Thanks Faye, it was very nice to meet you!

I only give a 1 because there was not a lesser option. The stops where not clearly marked and the employees were not overly friendly. If there routes maps overlaid with the London site map they might have something, but alas that is not the case.
They also closed routes and stops without letting the customers know which added to the chaos. All in all we would have been better off just using our ticket money on an Oyster Card and a good city map.

Normally enjoy taking 'hop on hop off' tours when travelling as you get to see everything without having to walk all over the city in the heat all day (something you begin to appreciate once you reach my age!) - and Big Bus London did not disappoint. I used the bus service over the course of three days and oh boy did I get my money's worth!

The stand out feature of this tour for me (I must admit I always intend to write reviews but never actually get round to it, which really shows how much of an impression it left on me!) was our tour guide, Cassy. By far the best (they were all good though, some more so than others however) she knew an incredible amount about London, it's history and its culture. I am a lecturer in architecture and I still can't get my head around how much she knew about all the different famous London architects and sculptors - Christopher Wren, Norman Foster and John Nash all made appearances in her presentation! The energy, passion, personal and informative nature of the tour meant that the time flew by - there was even the occasional (painful but grudgingly I must admit funny) joke thrown in! A few chatterboxes on the seats behind me were slightly annoying but after a swift brush of their ankle with my foot they thankfully alighted at the next station.

All of the other staff were courteous and helpful, the bus comfortable and the weather great (a rarity for London I'm told). I look forward to trying out Big Bus in other cities and hope the service is as exemplary!
Charlotte was our guide and she was wonderful. She was very knowledgeable and entertaining. Would definitely recommend this tour!

We needed something that would hit all the key sites in a day and they did just that. The 24hr pass allowed us to get some gift shopping done and sightsee at the same time beating the foot traffic and multiple Ubers or cabs it would have took. We ended up with 4 different guides and all but one were amazing and gave us a ton of info. The added river cruise was a great way to cap off the day and see Tower Bridge in all its glory.

We booked a 3 day ticket for the beginning of June online and it was easy to swap on the 1st day for tickets. We saw such a lot, we were able to hop off and catch another bus later to carry on with the route. It was quite busy but we always got a seat on the top deck. The commentary was excellent and the drivers and other staff were very helpful. The Thames boat trip, part of the ticket price, was also excellent. A great start to our UK trip.

On paper this looks like a good choice. We were there mid-week, getting on and off a few times in the morning so we had several different drivers and guides. Some guides were good and some weren't. The real problem was the traffic. After making it less than halfway around the loop without any issues, the traffic suddenly got bad and we were sitting more than moving. We realized after crossing the Tower Bridge that we wouldn't make it all the way around before they stopped running so we got off and toured Tower Castle then got back on and only made it a few stops until they quit running. We had to use the underground train to get back to where we needed to be.

What was supposed to take 2 1/2 to 3 hours for a loop would have taken over 6 hours based on what the guides and drivers were saying. We would have been better off to use the underground train and just go where we wanted to go. There are so many roundabouts that it feels like you're driving in circles a lot of the time. The guides also didn't do a good job of telling you which stop you were at or what could be seen at that stop. We had to rely on our map and looking at the actual sign (leaning over the side of the bus) to get that information.

If you want to spend almost the entire day just driving around and don't intend to get off, then this is a good option. If you have more than two things you want to get off and do, you're better off getting an underground train pass and using the train to get to just those places. We, unfortunately, never made it all the way around even though we spent almost five hours on the buses.

If you do take the bus and get a bad guide, get off and wait for the next bus and you may get a much better one. Also, get on the bus even if the top is full and sit near the bottom of the stairs because at the next stop or two people are likely to get off opening seats upstairs that you'll be first in line for.

I booked for my family for three days but unless you go early early you won't be able to find seats on top deck "
They try to sell you tickets for other sights telling me it is faster and better to get your tickets from us but when you arrive to sights they tell you to get in long line to get tickets as big bus tickets should be replaced and more over you have to book an appointment for your visit as it is busy now so it is much better to book on line
Big bus company needs to stop telling lies about faster tickets just to increase sales

To avail the services we waited at the Tower of london stop for appox. 2 hrs. with my small kids and then the bus came. We just took a ride but it did not cover the main attractions of city. Also the river cruise was disappointing as after boarding we came to know that the engine was not working fine and we have to disembark and they did not offer us the alternative boat.

All in all, the experience which should have been memorable. It become ordeal for me and my family.

We hopped on a redline (English only/live guide) and the first tour guide was good (not sure of her name- young lady with short, dark hair- otherwise I would mention it).

Then we switched guides and the guide adjusted the sound and it was too loud, so loud it hurt our ears. At every stop she kept repeating her name and the bus driver’s name. Also, it was a very busy day and she kept telling how many seats were available on the top deck, but not counting as people kept coming even after it was full (everyone wanted to sit on top), so there was excessive time spent managing passenger seating instead of touring. (I remember the name of the guide, but I don’t want to call her out, because it wasn’t completely her fault).

We hopped off and had lunch and got back on a blue line (recording which included multiple languages- including English) and enjoyed the rest of the tour.

I was a little disappointed in the recorded audio- was a little sparse and could include some interesting stories.

Would I recommend it? Maybe? Not bad, just not great.

Service is just okay. Initially you enjoy after some time it is boring.
Anyway London traffic and bus operations are smooth which needs appreciation.

I use these types of hop on/hop off tours in major cities I go to in order to get a "lay of the land." I usually just do a one day pass, and then take public transportation the rest of the time. I was impressed with the scope of this tour, as it really covers the entire city pretty well. The narration is appreciated. We never had to wait too long for a bus. I chose this company because it did not require you to first turn in your ticket confirmation for real tickets at a certain location-you can just do it on the bus.

this is one of the best ways to see London ... from the open 2nd deck of the Bus .. one needs to be wary of the direction and be cautious of the traffic jams that can cause delays especially in central London. Overall we enjoyed the tour ... only hiccup on the way back the bus really takes a long time as they combine the tourists from different coaches and this can cause a long wait for other customers ... but the drivers and other staff were quite friendly and provided good information about the city ::)

Stuck in traffic jam from the start. Earbuds to listen to guide didn't work. Then spent 10 minutes inside Victoria Station for some unknown reason. Felt sorry for the tour guide who was running out of things to say. Bus tours of London we're probably fun in the past, but now they are obsolete because of London traffic. A walking tour would be much preferable.

we've been to London many times, walked around to specific sites, however this tour was still very interesting and well presented. We heard loads of interesting facts and were taken to areas of London we hadn't been before. The tour guides on the bus were also very good at presenting the information, a special mention to Maddy who was very good.

The bus stopped all of a sudden at 18:15 in one stop. All the people in our bus was disoriented, no one knew the tour was over. It was the same for other 4 buses from the same company. The said that was the last stop even though in the app and the papers it was said that Sumner period timetable finished at 19:30. According to the coordinator the summer time started instead in the 15th of July. It was ridiculous. Tenths of people was complaining but they simply suggested to "send an email".

Red rote with a real person doing the commentary was very good, as was the bonus of a free return boat trip from either westminster or tower bridge to greenwich. Blue and Green routes with pre recorder commentary much less good. Some overlap between routes. Traffic can mean progress is very slow especially to the east of london.

We used Big Bus Tours last year and this year again just to give them one more chance to redeem themselves. This is not worth it. Both times we had to wait close to 45 mins in blistering cold to hop on a bus. Buses, they tell you, come every 15 mins. That was never my experience. Definitely won't be using Big Bus London ever in life again. Thoroughly disappointed!

firstly don’t buy from agent on street, go to agent at bus stop, its cheaper. We were conned. Paid agent and cost us £5 more. They are very friendly so be careful. Secondly we were told tour would take between 2 1/2 and 3 1/2 hours for full tour. After 4 1/2 hours we asked driver how much longer and was told approx another hour. We had to get off bus and get other transport to our hotel for our bags in order to catch our train. So leave plenty of time for this tour. Have to say traffic was nose to tail for most of the tour so perhaps it was just a bad day. Won’t be doing again though when we go back to London

I have sent complaints to Big Bus for 4 days and they haven't responded at all but this is what happened on July 4th with Big Bus we attempted to get on the 9:20 red bus from the tower of London at 9:45 to get to Trafalgar Square to go on the walking trip ,that started at 11, decided to take the blue bus to London Eye and walked to waterloo and talked to Kooip at 10:16 and the red bus was still not at the tower of London stop we ended up walking to the square from the London eye we asked the person at the square where to catch the green bus when we got there and he said the left hand side of the church and couldn't find the stop ended up walking to the British museum. We walked to Woburn and asked the rep there how to get to the cruise, he had us take the wrong bus not telling us to cross the street the rep at convent garden after asking how to get in the river cruise told us to WALK AGAIN to the pier. In summary the 1st stop at the tower of London at 9:40 the rep told us 20 minutes left us with the belief that the red bus would come soon and showed absolutely no interest in our satisfaction as we were completely ignored because we were not making a purchase. One of Big Bus's reps at least tried to discover why there was an absence of red busses. The Big Bus rep at Trafalgar Square gave us unclear interpretation information on the location of the green bus stop. The rep at Woburn rather than told us where to get the cruise the fasterest, which we told him we were in a hurry to catch, had us go the long way, some of Big Bus's brochures say some cruises stop at 4 while Big Bus's representatives are saying stuff like 7 and 7:30 so we didn't know which to believe also on a blue bus my audio guide box did not work. It was a total disaster, lack of organization, lack of caring,and just the reps lack of knowledge. This was madness we walked 8 miles (around 13 km) from the lack of the red bus and while trying to use the instructions Big Bus's employees gave me today
Unmarked and markings were incorrect. We were told by Big Bus employee that information signing had changed. I would suggest getting a taxi instead of riding around in a bus all confused.

The Big Bus tour takes you around all of London to different landmarks and sites. The bus provides different routes to accommodate different interests and time. Both the live commentary (red line) and the recorded commentary (blue line) provide interesting information about the surrounding buildings while driving. Unfortunately there was no WiFi on any of the buses that we went on, although advertised on both the brochure and the buses. Also the bus takes a while to travel around because of traffic (which is out of their control). So if time is an issue, walking may be more efficient in some cases. If short on time, the bus is great to sit on and look at all the sites from the bus. However, if you've got more time in London, I encourage skipping the bus and walking to all the sites.

Bringing our elderly mother to London for three days, we thought a bus trip would be ideal. She would see the sights and not have to be dashing up and down tubes. She wanted to go to Greenwich, so a cruise to there included seemed the ideal way to travel......WRONG. I bought two day tickets for each of us. We got on the bus as Kensington Palace and having checked the map I planned to get off at Tower Hill to join the cruise to Greenwich. After a couple of stops I realised we weren't following the map at all. This was most confusing as my planned day of a trip down memory lane for my mother didn't happen. We did catch the cruise however a lot later than planned thanks to not knowing where or when we would get near a boarding pier. I then didn't trust the boat times home so we couldn't stay long. Which regrettably was the right decision. The journey back to Kensington Palace was also a disaster. Again I checked the map and asked the young man at The Tower which bus we needed. He confirmed the blue route. Unfortunately yet again we went on some random route and ended up at Marble Arch nowhere near where we expected. At this point the driver got off, so I followed to ask where we were going..... then all chaos broke out. We were on and off buses, no-one knew which bus would get us back and as it was the end of their day no buses were going to Kensington. In the end a driver checked where we wanted to go and they operated a Home James service stopping at or near selected stops. What was supposed to be a relaxing day for my mother turned out to be very stressful. She was tired and ended up having to go to bed which ruined our evening. We had a second day to use and had planned to go on the rest of the trips (red and green routes). Unfortunately we had lost confidence in the Big Bus and decided not to. I had done other tours in London with other companies which had been reliable. We chose Big Bus as they offered what we wanted. Sadly they did not deliver and we were left diappointed.

I am requesting a refund for our tour of Hop On Hop Off tour in London. I printed only 1 page, didn't realize we needed two tickets for our 48 hour excursion. Only one of us would not go without the other. Please, please give us a refund.

Thank you,
Jim and Nancy Davis

We did this on our last day in London. Had we been in London for longer we would have done this first and used it to contribute to our list of places to visit. One of the tour guides we had - Matt - was informative and hilarious. It’s worth the high price for the ticket and I now have a whole list of things to see the next time we visit. It takes 2.5 hours for the whole tour or you can get off and on as you would like. A river cruise is included with the ticket price - we ran out of time and didn’t do that part.

I would like to give a massive shout out to Craig and say thank you for all his help in the past 2 days. He was helpful answering my questions when recieveing my tickets at the kings cross pick up point on the green link. I had a mini bad experience waiting for a bus that didnt show that night at convent garden that night. The next day i spoke to another guy who was at the kings cross pick up and he wasnt vert helpful just aploigised and that was it. By chance i happened to run into Craig again at the waterloo stop off (i believe) i explained to craig what happened he was very very apologetic and tried to fix the problem best he had. He then very kindly walked me over the bridge to another pick up point to make sure i got on the right bus. I did go to say thank you but he was very busy. So i just wanted to say Thank you heaps Craig.
Will definitely recommend Big Bus Tours

We landed at Heathrow and knew we were going to be tired from travelling, so we decided to spend a couple hours of our first day doing a bus tour to see the major sights of the city without having to do a lot of exhausting walking. We did the red route because we thought the idea of live commentary sounded fun. We enjoyed being able to see a lot of the major landmarks, but the tour guide didn't seem interested in being there. Most of his comments were along the lines of "See that building? They're tearing that down to build apartments. Oh, and that one? That's going to be a luxury hotel. Grumble grumble." It wasn't a very informative tour, but for tired travelers just looking to see the city, it was all we really wanted.

This is a perfect way to see everything and decide what you want to go back and visit more in depth. We picked up the bus first thing in the morning in Green Park and had the bus to ourselves for quite awhile! We had a French tour guide and she was very entertaining and helpful with plotting our route. The bus drivers are amazingly talented at navigating such large vehicles through the London streets. Well worth doing on your first trip to London.

We bought tickets for the Big Bus London Hop-On-Hop-Off Tour and enjoyed it so much we ended up also using Big Bus HOHO tour in Paris and Barcelona. If you're looking for an easy way to get around town and see all the important sights this is a great option. All the buses we were on gave out new, free headphones and have recorded tours so that you can listen if you want or just enjoy the ride if you don't. As far as getting off the bus....there are clearly labeled stops on the Big Bus map that is readily available on each bus and at each stop. Also, if you listen to the tour through headphones they announce the next stops. It's very busy in London and way too dangerous for the bus to stop and just let people off wherever so you do have to pay attention to where you're getting on and where you want to go. The tickets are super easy to buy - they are available at each bus stop or online. My 10 year old was entertained the entire time!

It's a Great way to learn the history
of London. All the important places
are narrated and sighted as you travel
throughout London! The fare
is reasonable! You can Hop On & Off
throughout your visit!

We had Angus and Wesley on part 2 of our tour and they were excellent. Angus delivered a lot of information in a easy-to-listen manner, with lighthearted delivery and he was very good with the two small children travelling with us.

Big Shout out to Fay !

Smashing tour guide. Friendly and informative.

I really enjoyed my tour and the cruise at the end was a nice little touch.

Pauline (Ireland)
Our guide, Nobby, was humorous and very knowledgeable about tour sites. We enjoyed our bus tour experience. It's convenient to use a hop on/hop off tour when visiting multiple sites.

I did a bus tour in Barcelona, which I loved, so I thought that a bus tour around London would be a good idea. Unfortunately, the traffic was so busy that it was just like being in a traffic jam. I chose the red bus tour because it had the live commentary, but the traffic noise was so loud that the commentator was drowned out. The red tour was also the shortest tour, which fitted our schedule, but the commentator said "we're just going to have a break for 10 minutes", the bus parked up in an uninteresting location and we could either walk around for a bit or just wait. I knew that the bus would stop for people to hop on and hop off, but I didn't expect it to just stop. Then another red route bus pulled up and all of those passengers joined our bus. After we set off again I studied the map and decided that I couldn't face the whole tour so we jumped off at Covent Garden. Best decision of the day...….we walked and tubed instead. Save your money and do your own tour.
We had great fun getting off and on the bus at stops we wanted to see with out worrying how to get there and the bus always turned up 15 mins to move on again

So we did this our 2nd day. The bus had issues and had to be put on another bus... We got off at Piccadilly. Did our thing.. Went back to catch the bus back.... Waited for like 30 min. Asked when the next bus would be there, only to be informed that the last bus had already run. No information was provided as to when the last bus would be running so we had to catch a cab back to our Hotel. Other than that, good information, provided a good tour of London.

Used the London Pass and downloaded the Big Bus App (very user-friendly and interactive).

Easily found the closest Hop-On-Off stop at Tower of London and did not wait more than 15min for the next bus to arrive. The gentleman processing tickets could have been more helpful and looked like he hated his job (other tour bus company representatives were more friendly). The only reason we chose Big Bus Tours is that of our previous positive experiences in different cities.

Didn't mind the typical London traffic due to our knowledgeable and entertaining guide--Angus. He incorporated humor and fun facts along the entire route, offered to take photos of guests, and added personal recommendations and stories to keep us entertained.

Overall, happy with our experience and would recommend.

Hello! I was visiting from NY with 2 friends (from Dallas and Chicago). We had the pleasure of having Chris as our guide and Leon as the driver. Chris was incredibly engaging and knowledgeable. He also made some funny American quips. Leon drove well and I felt safe. It was a blast!
Get the 3 day pass, spend the first day just riding the loops and use that time to plan where you want to hop off over the next 2 days. Very easy to use, with good commentary.
On a recent Hop on Hop Off in London, Fai was our guide....can’t say enough about how knowledgeable and pleasant she was. She made our first day a most pleasant one.

The hop on hop off feature is awesome. We stayed on to do the loop and then decided where we wanted to go. Angus was absolutely fabulous! He was just colorful enough and a wealth of information. I cant recall the bus drivers name but kudos to him as well for navigating the traffic in London city! We really enjoyed and highly recommend this tour.

We counted some steps and platforms down to Underground at 178 steep steps...very fast and crowded. Buy the 72 hr passes on this and it will take you to nearly all the destinations. Good guides. Lovely sunny (or rainy) rooftop views. Clean and comfortable and excellent value for the money. We did NOT do this on our last visit and our legs and feet were sore for days after.....and lots of time lost. DO IT!

Went on the Hop-on-Hop-off Big Bus Tour in London on Saturday May 19th. Our guide Peter was so funny and gave us a great tour of London. So educational and not a boring moment in slow London traffic. We highly recommend it.
We have used the hop on hop off in many cities around the world. This one was impressive. The Thames boat tour is a great way to see London and is included in the fare.

We were in London for a show and decided to take a hop on, hop off bus tour and play tourist for a bit. Took the bus from Marble Arch to Westminster Bridge, then the boat down to Tower Bridge and finally the bus to Trafalgar Square. Went on the red line both times so got the live guide who was alright. There was a protest that day so road closures meant traffic so things were a bit slow but you can't blame the bus company for that. It was also raining for our 2nd trip so we stayed downstairs - audio was harder to hear from down there.

The red line guide named Angus gave good information and was helpful, but the traffic jams kept us from covering much ground. Several of the hop on places were hard to find----we kept crossing back and forth across the street trying to determine where the bus would actually stop. We were told that some of the routes had changed recently and were in the process of being marked more clearly on their maps. Since I was rather tired at this point my trip, I was just happy to be able to sit down and watch the sights go by. If you are able, just walk to all sights in one area and then take a city bus to another location the next day.

We went on a bus tour on hop on hop off Big Bus last Saturday and it was amazing. Our bus driver Patrick and Bus Guide Karen did exelent job, I found so much information about London, we will deffinitely go back to do it again!

This is our first experience of taking the hop-on hop-off tour. We are very happy and satisfied with the service of big bus staff, especially the driver names Philip. He is friendly, informative and helpful. Definitely he is an good asset for the company. I found this is the best way to get around the city. Highly recommended.

We only used the blue route and the problem I have is the wait time between each bus. It says every 15-20 minutes but we waited at one stop for over half an hour. We got fed up of waiting in the rain so ended up getting an Uber.

We also had to stand on another bus. It’s not much of a bus tour when it’s so packed you can’t see out the windows.

The map on the app needs updating as it was difficult to figure out our bus route as all the lines crossover.

I don’t think a finishing time of 6pm is conviniant either. After spending most of the bus rides in traffic it ate up a lot of our time and since our ticket was only valid for 24 hours we didn’t get to use the red or green route.

Apart from these problems the bus tour in itself was fine. It’s gets you from point A to point B. You’re provided with a map and a set of ear phones. The ear phones are connected to little speakers which give some information as we drive along. Speakers have numerous languages available.

We waited at two different stops with young children for half an hour for a bus to arrive. Apparently there was a march going on in London causing traffic delays yet every other bus tour company seemed to arrive. Nearly £70 to ride the bus that never turns up. Don’t waste your time or money.

In fairness they refunded us, however wasted a lot of time on our day out.

My visit to London was short and I knew I wanted to get a lot in. The Hop On Hop Off double-decker bus was the way to go. My companion and I stayed on the bus - up top where it was open (and fortunately sunny.) There was a lot of traffic- but after all it is the City Of London. We did not get the combination river cruise - as the Thames looked very choppy. I was amazed at how many attractions we took in. Incredible! We plugged in the earplugs and toured for over 3 hours.

It took the bus 2 1/2 hours to travel from Gloucester Road stop to Tower of London. Impossible traffic. Gave up and used the Tube. Wrong info on the brochure re City Cruise, so missed that also. A huge waste of money. We have previously used the Hop off and on buses in many countries around the world and have been very happy.

Did the big bus, brings you to alot of the sites but the traffic in London is brutal. I found at times it was faster to walk or take the tube to places. If you on a time crunch not sure I would recommend it but definately brings you to all the hot spots.

Purchased the 3 day pass and it was worth the price. The bus picked up right by our hotel and stopped at all the major attractions in London. The staff were friendly and very helpful to answer questions about the routes, times and general info.

Purchased 48 hour tickets and used them to go to our hotel then around to see the sights on our first day. That gave us ideas of where we wished to go the following day. Found the stops easy to find and use and the staff were very helpful. The buses weren't busy but it did rain so the top deck wasn't used as it was open top. As we had started in the afternoon this effectively gave us 3 days travel so caught the buses back to the station when coming home. Great value and a great way to see and hear about London especially Maddie on the live commentary tours (Red route). The other routes you use headphones which were provided.

What a great way to see London and learn about it. I booked it as a birthday treat for my husband and my mum whose birthday was on Saturday 21st April (same day as the Queen) and we had the pleasure of being looked after by The Dream Team which is Mike the driver and Kevin the tour guide. Kevin is full of many interesting facts and interacts with his passengers and made the tour relevant to lots of the passengers when he had found out where they were from. He made a great fuss of mum which made her day to be the centre of attention.
We would all recommend using Big Bus and i will join them again. We had an Open Day Ticket which meant we could Hop On and Off the bus as and when we wanted and this also included a one way trip on a City Cruiser where there was also a commentary.
This is an ideal way to see London and if you want you can just stay on the bus, which is great if you are with people that are not able to walk far.

We went on the bigbus for a day...our guide was phil.he was awesome and funny and entertain us with even minute details of the places we saw.was a good experience for us.
Arun and shalu

I would really recommend this way to see the London sights. The hop on hop off is such a fun way to do this, they are around every 15 minutes approximately. The staff are helpful and knowledgeable. We bought our tickets ahead of time, on line through trip advisor and saved quite a bit of money. We did the 48 hour package and it was perfect for our time here.
There seemed to be more of the Big Bus than the other tours so more frequent pick ups. I have great admiration for these drivers, London is not an easy city to maneuver around in!

I enjoyed it very much of course, but I didn't like the fact that once you buy it, the timing starts from there. I'd of liked to save it for later instead of having to hurry up and start the bus tour right away. The ticket is so small, I lost it before I could even do the river cruise. It made me really mad cause I payed so much and I couldn't enjoy it as much as I wanted.
But besides all of that, it was a great experience, we've been everywhere around london and seen all of it!
Really enjoyed the trip around London on the bus. The guide Faye was very friendly and knowledgeable, helping passengers with any questions they had.

Kevin and Barry were the best! We laughed all the way through London. They have great maps and helpful people to get you onto the route you want. The information shared changed our plans for a positive allowing us to see things we would have otherwise skipped. Thanks Kevin.

We found the Big Bus not only a great introduction to the Cit but also a very useful means of transport around the main attractions. Commentary styles varied from bus to bus as would be expected. Well worth using the Big Bus Tour if you're a first time visitor like us.

We recently took a family vacation and really enjoyed the Big Bus London. Nobby was our guide on the red loop and was very entertaining. We liked the ability to see everything from up top, which allowed us to see parts of London most don't normally see.
