I would highly recommend this for families who aren't quite sure what they want to do, so endless hours wandering around from attraction to attraction.

The best way to see the city, without a doubt. So easy, stress free, good commentary, comfortable, reasonably priced, and you see everything worth seeing. I'll never visit another big city without doing one of these tours.

I only had a day in London and this was a wonderful way to see the city. I could hop off at the two locations I wanted to see - Tyburn Convent by Marble Arch and the Tower of London. The bus ran fairly regularly and I never had to wait long. If you only have a day, it is a great way to see the sights. My ticket also included a river cruise along the Thames and I really enjoyed that as well! It is better to get live commentary rather than recorded so you really get the commentary at the right time.

We enjoyed the big bus. Found it a great way to see the streets and get a feel for what we wanted to see and not see. The commentary was great and recommend it to first timers in London. we learnt facts that even Londoners didn't know.

We spent St Patrick’s day weekend in London and decided to do the two day pass. I’ve done many of these tours in other cities (including London years ago) and I found this one not as informative and lacking in organization. We made a plan based on the map and figured the stops went in order however on the blue route we seemed to skip the area we had intended to get off at. Not sure if this was due to events going on in the city but we wasted an hour touring a part of the route we hadn’t intended on seeing.
We also waited 45 minutes at a stop near trafalgar and a bus never showed up. We ended just giving up and getting a taxi back to the hotel. There were quite a few people also waiting at the stop that waited and ended up leaving as well.
Net net. Definitely not the best one I’ve done and would likely try a different company next time.

The tour routes were great, tons of information via the audio guides on the blue route and the live tour guide on the red route. Much easier and relaxing than driving, or walking all over town. Saved a lot of time by taking the tour. It was also nice to be able to get off wherever we wanted to and actually experience some of the major attractions.
Raju is a great guy. Very helpful. Don't bother with Sharjah trip. Raju did advise it was ok but he is an employee

We missed our connecting flight so had a day to explore. On very little sleep, we wanted to maximize the time we had. The tube cashier recommended this as we could get on and off if we wanted to spend more time at one of the stops. It was cold and raw, so other than taking a quick walk to see Buckingham Palace before the bus left, we mostly stayed on the bus until getting off for the river cruise on the Thames. Karen, the guide was knowledgeable and kept things interesting with historical anecdotes. Tarek (sp?) our driver was amazing, maneuvering through traffic. (It was our first time driving on the left, so a bit unnerving at times!) The river cruise provided us a view from a different vantage point. By doing this tour we were able to cram a great amount of sightseeing, actually knowing what we were seeing, into a small amount of time.

This was our third experience with Big Bus tours and our second in London and for a great way to both see the sights and get around the town, I'm not sure this can be beat. We've used it as a very slow, indirect mode of transportation to get to various sights and it works wonderfully for just that.

As it was my first time in London, having the opportunity to enjoy London on Big Bus was certainly the best decision I made. I enjoyed the sight seeing and hopped off the bus to visit some places, shopping and taking pictures. I will repeat again in future!

We are BIG fans of the Big Bus Tours. We landed in London and had already purchased our Three Day Hop-On-Hop-Off Tour. We loaded up and was able to see all the main sites and the tourist attractions without having to worry about parking or traffic. The guides were fun and very informative. Would highly recommend this tour for families or literally anyone! Have fun but purchase it online to get a discount and not to waste time when you arrive!

Due to the awful weather my friend and I spontaneously decided to go on a hop on hop off tour of London. We got on the red tour with the live commentary and we were not disappointed: our guide Ricky was knowledgeable and totally charming. We had a great time and got fantastic insights to this lovely place. Thank you Ricky!!

This was a thorough bus tour that seemed to take us everyplace. We always find this is a good way to get the lay of the land when we arrive in an unfamiliar city. Our chief complaint about this trip is that the view was very poor. Because of the cold weather, we sat downstairs on the bus. My husband who is about 6 feet tall couldn’t see much without bending way down -almost in my lap. He said he saw a lot of sidewalk. If the windows were higher, this wouldn’t have been a problem. Otherwise, the recorded narration was clear and informative.

Would recommend the tour for anyone who'd like to see the main London sites in one day. We spent a few hours on the Red route which visiting most of the main attractions, and the ticket also included a great ride in a boat along the Thames.

We had a few live commentators as we hopped on and off, but a special mention to Matthew Perry (no, not that one!) who was absolutely brilliant!

I spent over 3 hours on one bus, that i wasnt sure where it was going to end up! Map wasnt clear for me. Make sure you know where to get back on and off as this can get confusing if you go off the beaten track ended up walking back to hotel a few evenings due to the bus finishing around 4. This service should run until 8pm in the week

what a fantastic tour we had today.
Excellent guide steve and his driver showing us around as roads were being closed and detours made.
Today was my unusual turn to be a tourist. And I must say. Big bus tours LONDON have got it right.
Red or blue Tour you can’t go wrong.
So sit back and enjoy the real LONDON

We were able to sit upstairs on the front row with a splendid view of the city as we went through it. Karon was our guide and Russell was our driver. She was friendly, knowledgeable, and provided a lot of background information about the sites we were seeing, which was exceedingly interesting. She fielded questions, and managed the tour bus so efficiently as people were hopping on and hopping off. The bus driver did an amazing job of navigating us through some of the smaller streets. It was a thoroughly enjoyable activity, and I'd highly recommend it to get a bird's eye view of London in a short amount of time.

If you're going to see London, make sure you Terry the Big Bus Tour hop on hop off bus.
Excellent way to see and learn about London and if you happen to have Garath as your tour guide, you're in great hands.
His knowledge and friendly delivery of his knowledge is worth every penny.
Give them a go. You won't regret it.

Big bus ride was excellent we taken London eye fast track , shrek adventure and aqua life .
Bus stops at interesting spots .
It’s must , my whole family loved it

We took the open top bus tour on Saturday. We chose the red route as it has a live guide and we were definitely not disappointed! Kevin was our tour guide (with Frank driving) and he made it so fun and really inclusive. We laughed loads and had a great time, even when the rain started pouring!

I lived in London for five years but the tour gave me a whole new insight! I will definitely take my daughter when she is a little bit older and fingers crossed we get Kevin as our guide again.

Always book Big Bus Tours in every city break and they are always fantastic!.. staff are so helpful, the buses are spotless and the routes cover all you could want to see. We pre-booked tickets and presented barcode on phone to collect. Easy enough to just purchase on day though from staff. Can't fault this company - yes the tour can take a while as like any city traffic is congested but walk if you want faster pace. If you want to get a feel for city and layout these bus tours are a fab relaxing way to get around!

Our hotel recommended the tour so we booked it as our first activity in London. Although the concierge told us where to pick up the bus, we had a hard time finding the “Z” sign on the bus stop. Once we did it was easy. It took at least 20 to 30 minutes for the buses to arrive. The first part of the tour we had head phones which were ok but they only gave basic info on the attractions. However when we picked up the next bus from Tower of London we had a live tour guide and he made all the difference. He was funny, witty and insightful! If it hadn’t been for him this review would have been less enthusiastic and more negative.

A great means of transportation for us as we explored London via the hop on / off tour bus near our hotel. There was a complimentary city cruise included in our 4-day tickets. Ticketing staff stationed at our regular bus stop was very kind; he even informed us of the estimated arrival of the next bus so that we could have a rest in the nearby cafe given the limited accessibility.

Used the Hop on hop off bus for 48 hours when in London, purchased with the London Pass.
Some of the bus stops are really hard to find, and most of the buses we used didn't have the commentary working, and had to keep rebooting.
Ended up using the transport as a way to get around London rather than walking, but most of the time walking would have been faster as the traffic is awful.
Overall an ok way to get your bearings in London, but the tube is far superior if you are confident.

Really do not understand how this disaster of a tour got good reviews. This is the first hop on hop off when I got off without finishing the loop. Travelers can buy 24- or 48- hours. This includes 3 loops (blue, red and green) + walking tour + boat ride - of course all in the hope that people won't be able to make it for all tours offered. Blue and red are pretty much identical with blue having pre-recorded audio guide and red having a live guide on board. I took blue tour. It took 4 hours and when I asked the driver how much longer, before I will finish the loop, he told me it will take another hour to get back to where I started. At this point, I gave up and got off. The tour is so long not because there is much to see, but because most of the time you spend sitting and waiting in traffic. While I understand that Big Bus cannot resolve traffic in London, the least they could do is to make the audio guide informative and entertaining - so that people on board of the bus could at least learn something new, while waiting. This could not have been further from the truth. Audio guide is absolutely horrendous. For example, it did not bother to include any content about Tower of London - which is supposed to be one of the main attractions in London. I mean none. It is a good thing I already knew what it was, when we both drove by and stopped there. Out of total 4 hours spent on the bus, audio guide was talking maybe for half an hour; the other 3.5 hours I was listening to pre-recorded music, to which I have developed a strong allergy after that. Overall - don't waist your time. Just use subway to get where you need to get. If you really want to be on a bus tour take a night tour bus with Golden Line - which I took it a night before the Big Bus tour - I thought that it is somewhat mediocre, but it is amazing how standards fall after horrible experience I had with Big B.

We bought the 2 days Hop on Hop Off ticket. Good if you only plan to do a complete loop. Impossible to do a trip to selected places otherwise.
We got off the blue bus to catch the red. And it just departed without waiting if people from the blue bus will trasfer. We missed it by seconds. And oh well another bus due in 20 mins they said.
But we waited for the first bus for over 15 mins because it came late!!!!
Avoid this company at all cost.

My husband had a 21 hr layover in London and wanted the chance to see as much of London as we could in the time we had. He found this bus tour and it was perfect! Our tour guide Joanne was very knowledgeable and gave lots of fun stories behind many of the locations, she even gave recommendations on where to eat and helped passengers find the best spots and times to see certain attractions like the changing of the guard. If we go back to London I would take the tour again in a heartbeat!

We have never traveled outside the US before and so were so excited to see London. We decided to use Big Bus and so glad we did. We used the Red Line and we had an amazing guide called Georgie and the driver Julian. So knowledgeable and funny and so polite. Very English!! We loved her. If you do the Red Route we hope you have Georgie as your guide.

Covers major attractions, also includes a 30-minutes river cruise.
Picked Big Bus out from the 3 Hop on/off bus companies for 2 reasons: 1. Big bus has mobile app offers live bus tracking 2. Got a discount coupon from Booking.com. It’s 15% off the £35 on-street price, no need to pre-book.
1. The mobile app is confusing to use, the pick up stops are not easy to locate. We ended up walking from Trafalgar Sq to Leicester Sq., another time using the subway.
2. Took subway to the first of the 5 assigned stops for the tickets, at green Park Station, Big bus rep said the machine can’t scan the Booking.com bar code, sent us to Marble Arch station. Arived at Mable Arch the machine can’t scan again & told to go to Baker St Station. It’s totally wasting time. Thanks to one of the staff was kind enough to offer a different type of discounted ticket at £30 each. Most staff are helpful and friendly, a couple couldn’t care less.
River cruise was quite pleasant.

My son and myself visited London and paid to go on a Bus Tour with this company.

We were on the bus for 4 hours at least and literally saw the whole of London and the sights.

Absolutely well worth the money paid

We started at our hotel near Waterloo and headed from stop 24 to Buckingham Palace to see the Changing of the Guard. From there we had to wait quite a while for a bus, which did seem to be the norm... they could do a better job of timing it seems. The drivers and staffers were really nice and helpful, as was the app that showed us where the buses are en route. I’m not sure the stops were accurate as it was hard to understand which directions buses were headed and where they were headed next. The blue line is what we rode for the day, and after hopping off at Harrods we had to switch again when our bus went out of service. All in all was a good tour, audio was helpful but same 2 songs (green sleeves and pomp and circumstance) got a bit redundant...) got a bit annoying.

A great way to get around London and see all the important landmarks before setting off on your own to explore. There is an audio guide in several languages, you can always hop on/hop off during the day if you see somewhere of particular interest, good value for money, buses run frequently and the tour took about 2 hours

Like bus tours in all cities, this is the best way to get an overview of the highlights of a place and to isolate what spots you want to follow up on. The big bonus is if you get an enthusiastic quide...which Matt certainly was. With his thick Scottish brogue offering sometimes witty but mostly corny commentary, the 2 hours flew past and some of the historical insights were interesting. Definitely the way to go. If you get Matt, all the better.

Enjoyed the city cruise. Commentary is done by the crew. Very informative and amusing. We took the 2 hour cruise to Greenwich on the 1st day of our 48 hour ticket. The 2nd day we did the Big Bus tour. Hop on hop off. Toured the city taking in Houses of Parliament, Trafalgar Square Westminster Bridge, Piccadilly and much more. Again the commentary was done by a person rather than a standard recording & headphones. Again very informative and interesting.

We had a 4 hour window in which to see London - and were travelling with little children and much baggage. Big Bus tours really stepped in! Firstly, their staff are all friendly and helpful and made the confusion of travelling around London with little children a breeze. The commentary is synced well and is easy to understand and you really get to see London. The only reason I feel that they lose a star is due to the fact that they do not have chargers on board - whilst competing tour companies do. Travelling in London is very heavy on your batteries and a charger would have been really helpful. Also, the printed map and the app were a bit out of sync which caused a little bit of confusion.

Fantastic story telling about the streets and attractions of London. Never seen such an enthusiastic and fun guide like Matt who kept us glued with his unique oratory skills. Buses are at frequent intervals. Great value for money.

We had purchased a 48 hour premium tour. We enjoyed the first day of the tour and the cruise was wonderful with staff being very informative and letting us know the complete tour trip would take 2 hours, time we didn’t have. However, disappointingly the same cant be said for the Bus staff. We caught the bus with our 2 and 4 year olds to Kensington Gardens as we wanted to visit the Princess Diana playground (which we learnt about on your tour 👌). When disembarking we asked the driver what time the last bus would be to allow us to get home. We had caught the last bus home the night before which got us back to our accommodation at approx 7pm (near the Tower of London) we luckily got on the last bus however unfortunately when the bus got back to Marble Arch we were unceremoniously told to get off the bus as it was changing Colour and would not be continuing to where we needed to go. Asked which bus we could get on (it was 5pm) we were told there were no more buses going to Tower of London. We had been in that same spot with our bus going to Tower of London the night before! So we were left at the beginning of rush hour (we’d already made the mistake of going on the tube during rush hour) to make our own way home. Totally disgraceful. There was no Concern or apology given. Your street vendors are extremely unprofessional. We will choose another company next time.

The regular price was $48.00£ per adult for one day but because it was a slow day and there were two companies competing against each other, the Big Bus gave us 48 hours for $25.00£ each. There are two tours (blue and red which cover the main sites downtown). Tons of traffic in the downtown core making it very slow to get around. All companies operate two main routes, two smaller routes and a free boat cruise down the Thames River plus free walking tours. The smaller green line leaves right from St Pancras Train Station so it was very convenient to us. The entire trip takes about 3-4 hours depending on traffic. This is a great way to get your bearings if you are new to the city.

The main pick-up location was walking distance from our hotel, the J.W. Marriott Grosvenor House. It took us to our intended destinations (Trafalgar, Tower of London etc.) , but when we needed to reboard at one official pick-up locations (don't remember exactly where), the sign at the stop said they no longer pick up at that location. Other folks we met had the same problem too. We had to use Uber to get back to our hotel.

I bought a 3 days tour on this Hop off Hop on Bus! First of all, when you purchase the ticket no explains to you how the trip works! But I did ask the man if this bus will bring me back here after the tour and he said YES! He did not say I would need to change bus! So I sat on the bus for 7 hours waiting to get back to Kensington Palace! After speaking several times to the driver who keep saying he will drop me off there for about 2 hours and never did! I got off only to be told that the bus will not be going to my Stop and I would have to wait another half hour which turned into 1 hour for a bus going westbound! After about 50 mins I finally give up and got a taxi back to my Hotel! Yesterday my husband and I went again now I knew that I had to change to west bound when I’m ready to come back to Kensington Palace! We went on the cruise which was really enjoyable after we asked the Big Bus tour guy where do we get the WestBound back the Kensington Palace! He assured us and lots of other folks that was waiting that it would arrived exactly where we were standing! It was winding and cold! He said 20 mins to Half hour! And so we waited and waited! Every bus that came along was Eastbound! So everyone kept asking him where is the WestBound....he said it coming and walk away to smoke his cigarettes! That’s all you see these guys doing smoking and arguing with customers! Very nasty to people having questions! We again had to wait over 1 and half hour for a WestBound! They said it was traffic! But all the other tours west and east from London tour and Circle line tour had buses running back and forth that says Eastbound and WestBound alternatively! All the buses for big bus tours were Eastbound my husband and the other folks counted 7 Eastbound! And 1 hour and 30 mins 1 WestBound! I will never use this tour ever again! The all fight with each other and also with the customers! It’s just been a disaster for us so far! Not happy!

It doesn’t take you long to realise that there are much better ways to visit London than this.
The ‘commentary’ is lousy. Sparse in information and out of synch with he route.
If you’re going to choose a bus tour, pick pone with a real person providing the commentary. You’ll get a much more interesting insight and some humour.
Big bus tours have all of the fun of sitting in a bus in traffic.

Lots of locations to hop on the bus tour. Tour guides were super friendly and knowledgeable. The employees at each of the stops were also friendly and gave me lots of good tips for the attractions I wanted to see. Also - highly recommend doing the river tour - I was a great way to see the city from the Thames !

We had taken a Big Bus Tour in Paris and loved it so decided to do it here in London. There are three different routes and we got on the Red Route and were happy to realize that there is a live guide rather than a taped one that you listen to through headphones! That was great too in Paris but this was a nice change!

Our guide was Matt and he was AWESOME! Full of info, hilarious and witty. We have laughed over and over thinking about some of his commentary. The best.

Big Bus Tour is a great way to see the highlights and get information about the various sights.

Highly highly recommend. And I hope you get Matt!

It is a good way to explore London, but given the waiting time it needs to be planned well. They provide a head phone, which enables the travelers to learn a bit of history. We traveled in roof top and it was bit windy and we luckily had appropriate clothing.
This is by far one of the best ways to see and experience London. You can hop on and hop off at any of the stops....There are 3 routes to choose from and a river cruise...worth doing

We bought a two day bus pass via trip advisor. It was good for 48 hours and they added a free day so we had 72 hour passes (Oct 2017). It also included a Thames River tour.

We found the tour bus was a good way to get an overview of everything and the ability to get on and off was good for places to see in depth. We took the river cruise from the Tower of London back up to the Westminster bridge. We were entitled to use the bus tickets for additional legs but decided not to. Make sure to separate the bus tickets from the boat tickets or you'll lose the bus tickets to inattentive boat tour collectors who are not affiliated with the bus crew.

The base tour was about two hours if we stayed on the bus and there were additional routes to other points in the city if we switched at particular stops.

A downside was that the tours ended fairly early (545 or 6pm I think) and that was a disappointment for us who wanted to be able to ride around through the night hours.

Preferred the bus to the London underground for getting about.

As an excellent way to get an overall impression of this great city the Big Bus tour allows you to see places from the road as well as the river,because a river cruise is included. First BUY your ticket which may sound expensive,especially if you are a group of friends travelling together but it is really good value. Second,find out where your nearest HOP ON point is. If you start at Victoria station you need to wait outside the Grosvenor Hotel,for example. Be patient!- it could be that you have to wait a while before a bus appears because of London traffic conditions. If possible start as early in the day as you can and HOP OFF as often as possible. The commentary,in a number of languages,is quite up to date and informative.Good luck getting a seat on the top deck!

The Big Bus was advertised as a 24/7 tour but since we were here after Oct 1st, hours ended at 5:00 o'clock. This was NOT publicized so without warning, we were basically kicked off the bus at 5pm and left to our own devices to find our way across town to our hotel. We bought the tour that included the Thames cruise but had so much trouble finding the right pier that we ran out of time and couldn't do it. If we had planned the cruise while we were riding the bus it would have worked out as the pier is one of the bus stops. The basic bus tour was enjoyable except for these inconveniences.

We rode the Big Bus while in Paris & enjoyed it, so we decided to give it a whirl in London. The tour guides are out of this world. They are both informative & entertaining. We really liked that you could hop off & explore an area of town, then hop on another bus to continue your journey. This gives you the freedom to see the sights at your own pace.

there are many hop on hop off services in London. Go for city sightseeing or any other. Big Bus staff & drivers are unfriendly. The tickets are same for all hop on hop off buses choose any other bus than "BIG BUS". I had sent an email about the bad experience I had ... no responce from Big Bus company. I had taken Big Bus in Dubai which had very friendly staff & theerfore decided to go for the same in Londoon...however bad experience

Took a tour on the Big Red Bus as our time is London was limited. We jumped onto the Blue Line tour, which gave us a fantastic overview of the sights of London. If you stay on board and do the whole tour without hopping on and off it will take around 4 hours, allowing from traffic, but it does cover most of the more well known sights. Great sound system on board the bus which guided us through the whole tour. I would definitely recommend this tour, we paid £35.

I was charged with the job of showing two Australians London in a day! The Big Bus Tour (blue route) was fantastic and they were able to say that they had seen all the sights and then got off to visit Harrods. The audio commentary was very interesting even for someone who has lived near London all her life! Would recommend. Shame we did not have time for the other routes, the free walking tour and the free Thames ride.

Big Bus is the best way to explore London whether you are visiting from overseas or just want to explore our great city! We selected Big Bus for our team outing and we weren't disappointed. We were impressed by the 2 routes available and the areas covered. The fact they support 12 languages! The information provide at each stop about the facilities available and finally the information provided via the tour commentary on the blue route and the level of knowledge imparted by our guide Nobby on the red route. All in all a great experience and would recommend it to anybody.

Three day ticket. The bus tour and the three routes are ok. I assume you get the same with all the bus tour companies in London.
Why did I rate only two out of 5:
During the three days we had six occasions where we had a question and spoke to the next company employee. Two times the person we spoke to was very helpful and friendly. Four times the person was just rude, unfriendly and not helping at all. That is bad service and not just a coincidence.

This is another thing we always do when we visit london. We always buy a 2 day pass which includes a return trip on City Cruises from Westminster to Greenwich.

The blue route is a recorded commentary that you listen to through supplied earphones. The red route has a guide givivng live commentary.

The buses often run late, usually down to the shear volume of traffic in the city, plus at the moment there's quite a lot of road works.

we use the second day to re-visit sites passed on the first day. And we use it sometimes instead of the underground.

Discounted tickets can be bought online from the Big Bus website. There's also an app so you can see where the closest bus/stop/point of interest is.

We loved the red line tour. The commentary from the tour guide was very informative. We only purchased a one day ticket and in hind sight should have purchased a two day to do the tour justice. Because it was a one day fare we did not hop on/hop off as often as we wanted (we wouldn't have had enough time to go through the whole red line circuit).

The first half of our London bus tour was enjoyable after we moved seats many times because the audio did not work at many of the seats. This is something that should be checked daily before the bus begins the tours because these buses get FILLED so if you happen to be in a seat with no audio and there are no empty seats, you won't be able to hear the tour.
We got off of the bus at the Tower Hill stop to take our free Thames River cruise to Westminster. This part of the tour was 100% fabulous because if was informative and fun for all on the boat cruise thanks to the guide on the boat.
The problem was returning to the Hop-On bus after the cruise ...
The map showing where to reconnect with a bus does NOT show the bus stop as being over the bridge. Rather, it shows being just around the corner from the Westminster Underground stop. We walked around for 30 minutes until we saw a bus stopped at a traffic light and the driver told us we had to cross over the bridge, which we did. However, once we arrived at the stop the next problem happened ... we wanted to continue on with the tour from that point and there were two Hop-On employees at the stop who told us which bus to reboard in order to do this. UNFORTUNATELY FOR US, it was the WRONG bus and we ended up having to take the same duplicate tour for the next 1 1/2+ hours in very slow moving traffic. By this time, we were so disgusted, we again got off at the Westminster bus stop where that same employee was there. We told him that he gave us wrong information, which wasted alot of our time and he apologized and then told us the right bus to get on. We just wanted to get into a taxi and go back to our hotel because we were so weary from this wasted time so that's exactly what we did.

We used Big Bus tours in London and were happy overall with the experience. The tour routes were great, the wait times weren't bad at all. The live commentary on the red route was the best! Chris was funny and informative!
Bit of a struggle at night figuring out when the bus stopped... I wish they ran later at night, but this is the bus tour to take.

We really enjoyed our tour on the big bus, we much preferred the tour with the live commentary, all staff were great but a special mention for Big Steve who was very knowledgeable, helpful and funny. We also enjoyed the river cruise that was included in the ticket.

Booked this bus tour for me and the missus.
Staff friendly , informative and keen to assist.
Bus clean.
Maps were good and easy to follow, staff good at recommending routes and how to get to places.
The tour lets you find your feet in London very quickly and the included river tour was good as well.
Would do it again.

With numerous options for tours, how do you begin to decide? Our concierge recommended the Big Bus tour. We hopped on for two days in our 24-hour window. Our first guide wasn't bad, but on the second day we had Karen. We thought she was a great tour guide. Fun facts interspersed with historical facts made it a delightful experience. Always nice to do a bus tour, and then we can choose whatever we want to see again.
London can we quite overwhelming as far as sightseeing. The hop on hop off ended up being a great way to tick the boxes. Commentary was informative but not annoying like others we have been on.

It is not practical, the bus stations are far, the buses are very late. I dont recommend it!! Once you buy the ticket the staff is not welcoming anymore. Buy the London pass and use the golden tour instead. Or just use the orginial tour. Or even pay 1.50 pound with an oyster card for each bus (no tour) : flexible time, frequent buses, every station.

The first day in London we were jet lagged so took one of the routes to get the lay of the land. It was very interesting and helpful. It was raining but that is not unusual. They do offer free rain ponchos. The next day we took the river cruise that came with the package, We got there a half hour before the first boat left. That was worthwhile since we had no trouble getting on. The tour guide did a great job letting us know what to look and what we should know about everything we saw. He was also witty which made the trip even better. Later we took another bus tour with a real guide instead of a recorded tour. I wish I could remember her name. She made the bus ride worthwhile because she knew what she was talking about and put a personal touch to her job. I can imagine it would be tough to get on in the busiest tour season but we had no problem. And anyone associated with the company was very helpful.

I've been on hop on hop off bus systems in 8 European countries . This is the only bus tour I didn't thoroughly enjoy.

The drivers were absolutely rude! Don't dare think about asking them a question. One in particular actually raised his voice when we asked a question. Another when asked if the bus went to marble arch said sure and neglected to tell us if we took the redline we were a few stops away. The blue line that was this bus was a 1 1/2 hour trip . In disgust we got off and took a taxi back to our hotel.

Another driver took off while we were trying to get off and sent us flying trying to grasp a support bar.

We had a 2 day pass and saw the same drivers repeatedly . The behavior I described we saw again and again .

I will use hop on hop off again but not this service .

There is no quality control with this group. Last stop of the day the drivers and others gather and tell passenger stories . They seem to have lost site of the fact that people can over hear them.

Do yourself a favor and use another line.

Selected two days tour. It's good and covers all major central London attractions. Good if you have elderly people or children with you otherwise most of attractions are at a walking distance. Better to combine it with river cruise to get discount.
Also do remember to book for bus tour first as you can get discount on London attractions (Madame Tassaude, London eye eye etc) after booking bus tour. Weather plays a critical role too.
They were unfortunately less organised as the route amended due to protest and no one was there to guide.

My wife and I had one day in London last week and we used the Big Bus to get, see sights, and learn. The experience was tremendous, and it was particularly awesome because of the tour guide we had. Steve was awesome. He was personable, knowledgeable, and genuinely interested in helping us have the best possible experience in London. I'd recommend Big Bus Tours to anyone who asked how to see London. Thank you for a great experience!

We spent 4 hours traveling on a Hop on Hop Off Big Bus touring most of the downtown neighborhoods of London, which gave us a terrific overview of the city, and gave us ideas for which sections of the city and which tourist sites we wanted to visit. Comfortable seating. The map provided gave us a sense of which neighborhoods we were going to see. The driver was very helpful.

So...i'm actually not the sightseeing bus tour kind of travel person...AT ALL. Therefore it's likely that i suffered more during this thing than others might.
We did this, because one of the kids REALLY REALLY wanted to...it was my first and definitely last time.

On the plus side, the bus was comfy and we had a seat every time we ''hopped on''. They ride on a regular basis, so there's no long waiting for a bus when you decide to continue the tour.

However, the waiting whilst on the bus, at least in our case, was nearly unbearable. At times we stood for over 20 mins! Or were driving at about 10 mph for half an hour....

I guess this is partly due to us doing this during perfect tourist high season...but then London doesn't really do off-season does it...

We went on a 12 day 4 country vacation and the Hop on Hop Off Tours are a great way to see a lot of the main attractions in a short time and gain a lot of knowledge, let alone just getting to and from places. We had several tour guides in London but Joanne was by far our favorite! She knew everything about everything we saw and has a great sense of humor. We have been back in the states for a few weeks now and we still talk about her everyday!!

We went with the Big Bus per recommend of the hotel. On several stops we waited while several of the other tour buses came and left. When we asked the ticket sellers for the Big Bus at the stops they always said 5 minutes without checking the time. There are 3 colored routes, Green, Blue and Red. The Blue and Green are recorded tours the Red have people on the bus to give out interesting information. Both the tour we had were very good.

We picked this ip at Victoria Station. There was live commentary and it was excellent. We then stopped stopped at Westminster where we picked up the thames river tour and that likewise was excellent. From there it was downhill. After walking back and forth multiple times over London Bridge we spotted a bus and tried to wave him down. He pointed ahead and then picked us up. The actual stop was at the Monument but it looked only like a plain red city bus stop. Due to construction there were many detours. The driver was unfriendly and unhelpful. I got frustrated and finally got off near Trafalgar Square and walked back to our hotel.

Looked forward to our day out on the Big Bus, that showed great promise. Unfortunately our expectations were not met and the overall experience was underwhelming.
I recognise that London traffic is a nightmare but when a company promises regular buses, they should deliver.
Our shortest wait time was 30 minutes, stretching to one hour. This meant there was no time to actually visit venues. Recorded commentary was quite poor. It didn't match our location - either a few minutes before or after, thus we missed knowledge on many landmarks. First bus had no commentary working so wasted 30 minutes changing buses. Many headphone ports didn't work on any buses.
Tried calling the company to see if we were actually going to get a bus near the end of the day. No answer - just put on hold. After over an hour standing in the rain, an over crowded bus finally arrived.
I would NOT recommend this company. Have contacted them to request a refund. No response.
We took the Big Bus tour on 9/5/17 and our guide was Kevin and the driver was Isaac. It was an enjoyable and entertaining tour. Learned a lot about the different sites. I would recommend it.

We took the red route with very good narrated tour guide. Other buses with recordings don't have enough to say while you sit in traffic. Our guide (Steve) kept talking, and singing, and telling poems. We have been on hop-on hop-off buses before and decided it was a good way to tour London with no particular destination in mind.

Visited London again, as my mother has an apartment in Mayfair. So decided to do the big bus tour, on the open top, double decker bus. This tour also has a live tour guide, telling you about the key features in London, various facts, and the odd joke or two.
The full tour from start to finish can apparently take just over 2 hours depending on traffic. But you can also hop on and off at the key tourist sites in London.
You MUST keep your travel ticket, as they will check this to allow you on the tour bus.
It was £35 per ticket, but this also included a Thames river tour within the price, using the same ticket. So really, for live tour guides, as well as the bus tour and river tour, it's not too much of a bad price.
Great on a sunny day, but if it's raining, the tour bus does provide disposable rain ponchos, at no extra cost if you choose to go upstairs to the open top- which i recommend for the best photos.
Overall, nothing to complain about and job well done.

After using the Big Bus Tours on a trip to Paris earlier this year, we decided to book the London version for a 3 day family trip. As long as the tour bus route stops near to the location that you are staying then I would certainly recommend this way of traveling around the city. We would usually spend a lot of our time going up and down stairs and escalators on the underground , however, hopping on and off the bus at sites that we were keen to visit was so much more relaxing and having the added bonus of the commentary was fab. We all learnt so much about the city that we have visited many times before. The only suggestion I would have is that on the website it states that a ticket is per day, but the first day does not begin until you step onboard the bus and then runs for 72 hours as I purchased a 3 day ticket to cover Tuesday noon until Thursday noon. It was not until I asked I was told that I only needed a 2 day pass. The other sightseeing busses that tour around London all state 24 hour, 48 hour etc tickets, maybe Big Bus Tours could save people overpaying and there fore using them again by changing their ticket details?

We promised our boys we would take them on a sight seeing tour of London but with so much walking we felt it best to pay out for this and we were glad we did! There are three routes that you can hop on or off as necessary, two have an audio tour and one has a live tour all are interesting and very informative. The price also includes a river cruise to Westminster which was also very informative and scenic. I think this is the best way to see London if you have small children and you're not able to walk very far.

We did the Big Bus tour we did the Red line where Grace was our tour guide. She is fantastic has great knowledge great personality and fun to listen to. We also did the Blue line which had more stops and was worth every penny. They even gave us a river tour as well with the purchase. First time in London so it was perfect for us

Whilst in London celebrating our daughters 6th birthday, we took this open top bus tour.
I booked it online beforehand, very easy to book with various add ons you can choose, we added fast track tickets for the London eye and got a boat cruise throw in as a bonus.
There is a great app to put on your phone, that shows you a map and where all the stops are and what you can do around each stop. The staff are really friendly and helpful and you can hop on and off as many buses as you like.
The first one we got in was a red route bus, we had a live commentary from a lovely blond haired lady, she was so knowledgeable and really good fun. We know London quite well but I really learnt so much whilst on this tour. For non english speaking customers there are routes with pre recorded tours in many languages. In the afternoon, we hoped on another bus and just enjoyed seeing London from an open top bus, until we got to where we were heading.
Definitely worth doing whilst visiting London!!!

Have used this for the past 2 days and it's been one of the best decisions we've made. Pete A. and Julian were so helpful and kind. I definitely recommend this if you only have a couple days in London and want to hit all the big tourist attractions. They also have discounted tickets to some of the places (london eye, shrek, tower of lo don, etc.) so make sure to ask one if the tour guides before you purchase at the attraction to save some money.

Found the bus tour to be very good. You have a choice of routes, one has a tour guide and the others have pre-recorded guides. Easy to hop on and op off at the various attractions en route and we never had to wait too long for a bus. There are good saver packages too, we used one to give us a discount on the London Eye for instance. The main problem with the tour is the slow London traffic but obviously there's nothing that can be done about that. The day we went it was overcast in the morning and in the afternoon it was very wet. Plastic ponchos are provided for the hardier passengers who want to sit upstairs but it does take the edge off the experience. Again, not much can be done about that and it's a question of picking the right day.

Paid £35 for 24 hour tour around London. The service allows you to use the bus within 24 hours, so you can sight see one part of London and continues the next day as long as your 24 has not expired. So make sure you board the bus before the time you pay for the ticket. Free maps, raincoats and headphones are given as part of the package. Great way to tour London

This tour was the best way to see London and decide where you want to make a return visit to. Complimentary headphones, maps, rain cape make the trip easier. Choose what language you want to listen to. Very regular service, we were never waiting more than 10 minutes once we hopped off to hop back on again. All the best attractions included. Valid for 24hrs from when you start the tour. Highly recommended.

A really valuable few hours going around London on the Big Bus. The commentary is via ear plugs and they have several languages so yours is bound to be included. A worthwhile trip - you can purchase a ticket for 1 or 2 days and it will include a river boat cruise. You can hop on and hop off the buses for either 1 or 2 days depending on the ticket you purchse

We booked a 2 day hop on hop off bus tour and it was very nice! We took both red and blue routes. Red route had a live guide which was nice. We learned many things from both tours about the city of London! It was a great way to cover a lot of ground! Also it was nice to be able to select things to see based upon your own interests vs. being on a proper tour. The upper decks were often crowded, but otherwise it was very nice. I would highly recommend this especially if it is your first trip to London. I have been here many times before, but it was the first time for my kids. It really provided them with a lot of information. We also did the one way Thames river cruise which was good. That too had a live commentator- he was pretty funny!! Love the British humor!! Thanks for a good 2 days!!

We choose this tour bus as it was recommended to us and we can see why!! We saw many of London's iconic buildings, land marks and statues in the two and a half hours we were on the tour and it was the commentary from our highly entertaining, informed tour guide Peter Harry (could be Harrington?) who really made the trip that extra special!! He was funny whilst incredibly knowledgeable and we all learnt so much! Our two young boys (7 and 4) are still talking about the trip and what they learnt! The bus itself was comfy with plenty of room and our tour- red route- included a one way city boat cruise from Westminster to Tower bridge which was equally informative and entertaining and a real bonus to what was already a great day. We think it was well worth paying for and exceptionally good value for money. We cannot recommend the Big Bus enough! Thank you to Peter, our tour guide, for making our day!!
Third time using this company and never fails to impress. Always good commentary and pleasant staff. Useful insight to the history of London and regular hop on hop off service.

The Sunday of our visit just happened to be the London triathlon with heightened security and lots of traffic diversions resulting in heavier traffic on the other roads.
The four of us had visited the London Eye early on and had inclusive tickets for the bus tour. Because of the event taking place our figure of eight red tour, with guide Karen (very good) and driver Matt, to the Tower of London was diverted to the other side of the river and back to the start, so we got off and had lunch at a dingy little cafe, right at the bus stop, because we were starving.
Got back on a different bus and ended up back on the proper route to the Tower but with a different guide, nowhere near as good as Karen, couldn't make out what she was saying because she had such a thick accent and held the microphone right up to her mouth so very distorted. This part of the tour was a second loop of the figure eight which took us towards Green Park where there was a change over of guides and drivers, hello again to Karen and Matt. Yey!
We stayed on the bus as it went past Green Park, Hyde Park, Buckingham palace, and on towards the Tower of London in the first loop, we finally got there.
The return journey we decided to do on the river cruise back to the London Eye. We had a little bit of a wait but it was very enjoyable with some tremendous photo opportunities, unfortunately, being on the upper deck we couldn't hear the commentary very well. It was great going under the bridges because the captain would sound his hooter and people on the bridges would wave and we waved back. JUST WATCH OUT FOR THE IDIOTS WHO THINK IT'S FUNNY TO POUR WATER (?) ON YOU AS THE BOAT GOES BENEATH THEM. In all we had a very good day.
We decided to stay on the bus initially because we had been to London before but never done a guided tour. We were going to go into the Tower of London if we had got there early as originally planned, however by the time we got there, late afternoon, the queues were enormous with not much time before last admittance so we gave it a pass this time.
Tip: if you are going to do a bus tour check to see what events are on that day. There will be very much heightened security, traffic diversions and heavier traffic than normal on the regular routes.

Was led to believe the busses run every 5-15 minutes in the summer. Had to wait over an hour while three big busses Sat 50 yards away not taking passengers and two westbound busses we were waiting to board drove by without stopping. We were definately at the correct stop....and were waiting with 20-30 other angry customers. The blue line plays more music than recorded commentary.....and our English speaking tour guide on the red line was obviously not a native English speaker (quite difficult to understand). I would recommend greyline or original tours over big bus......definately not worth the money.

We were looking forward to this tour with our 3 & 4 year old to see the sights. Unfortunately the weather was poor heavy rain which meant you couldn't use the upper deck and therefore meant viewing capability was poor on the lower deck. The driver was rude and unengaging when asking questions about directions. They didn't stop so you could take pictures of the landmarks you could see.Whilst the weather wasn't down to the company it wasn't ideal when we decided to hop off to do a few landmark sightings that when we tried to rejoin the bus about half a dozen were closed and this wasn't visible on the map online or hard copy which meant a very long wet walk with two small kids. We found this tour a waste of money best reserved for dry weather so if stops are shut able to walk in dry. I don't think be using it again.

We had some American relations and their friends to stay over the weekend of the 29th & 30th July. We booked a full day's activities on Sunday the 30th including a visit to Buckingham Palace followed by a Big Bus Tour. Unfortunately this visit coincided with the Ride London Bicycle race through London, although we weren't aware of that until we actually arrived in town and were not made aware of it when we booked the tickets around three weeks earlier. After the Palace visit we went to catch the Big Bus to Covent Garden, however, because of the race a lot of the roads were closed and inaccessible to the Bus so we were advised to catch the tube instead. Later on we again attempted to utilise the Bus Tour but a lot of the roads were still closed. Although the Big Bust Tour staff were extremely helpful and offered to extend our tickets for another 24 hours this was not an option as our visitors were due to fly home the next day. We were quite disappointed we were not able to show them the sights as we had planned and duly put in a complaint to the Big Bus Company. And this is where full credit and praise must be given to the Company and its staff at Customer Services. With very good grace they apologised for our disappointing time and refunded our tickets in full. With service like this I would not hesitate to recommend a trip on the Big Bus Tour and will certainly look to be using them again the next time we are taking visitors on a sightseeing trip of London.

Love the Hop On Hop Off in both London and Paris. The free headphones work okay but not all of the jacks (at each seat) work great. We had to move seats on a few trips to find one that the narrated tour sounded clear. They play in different languages and sometimes it would say English was #2 and it was #1 instead so try all numbers if you plug into one with an unfamiliar language. Great information and if you sit on top you can get some great photographs and figure out where you want to get off and visit longer. Highly recommend in all cities for a great overview of the area and tips and history you wouldn't hear otherwise.

DO NOT USE THIS SERVICE. Good narrators on the bus and on the Thames boat ride. HOWEVER, several hop-on bus stops are not marked in any way. Using their (poorly drawn) map, we guessed where the stop was, but were off by a bit. When the bus stopped, we ran over to it. The driver pearly saw us coming and waving, but literally closed the door in our face, looked at us and shrugged as he drove away with a half-empty bus. We had to wait 30 minutes for the next bus. Later that day, the exact same thing happened at another stop with a different driver. It seems that their drivers don't like their customers and prefer to drive off and leave you behind. This is inexcusable behavior. Their tickets are very expensive and of questionable value. You have a reason get to expect courtesy and respect. Big Bus Tours is the OPPOSITE of that. DO NOT USE THIS SERVICE.

Booked the two-day hop on hop off tour online while vacationing for three days in London. When we redeemed our vouchers, the attendant gave us a great deal for 4 attractions in London packaged together. The hop-on-hop-off tour itself is good. Some lines have pre-recorded commentary while some have live commentary. The live commentary was very funny and interesting. The lines covered a lot of London, and we got the river tour included which was also nice. Complimentary rain ponchos and headphones are supplied on board of the bus which is also a plus. The only thing keeping me from giving this a perfect score is that both the instructions leaflet and the attendant information about destinations and times was not accurate. Other than that, you can't miss with this one.

For information,Today just completed Big Bus tour, but unfortunately very poor service. Waited over 40 mins at Tower of London (around 3pm) to get on boat to Westminster. Other boat services came and went several times but Big Bus boat service long wait and huge line of people waiting. Then tried to go on "Blue route" to west London but our bus stopped at Marble Arch and all told to get off it did not go further. Driver said get next bus. This we did but it went straight from Marble Arch to Baker St. and did not do the advertised tour route. At Baker St. official said we got on wrong bus, should have waited longer for a different one, so we walked back to Marble Arch and waited again. Many Big Bus pass us saying "No Service". Many people waiting and after around 35 minutes a bus showed up to do the west London section of Blue route. Bus was full with so many waiting !!!. Tour itinerary is good but customer service awful and very confusing especially for foreign visitors. Will not bother with this company again.

We picked Big Bus Tours because of the amount of stops they offered and because there were so many of them which meant no long wait times at stops. The other competitor was "The Original Tour Bus" as these two were pretty much the only tour buses we saw on a regular basis. The other tour companies had very few buses and would most likely result in time wasted waiting at bus stops.
I don't think we ever had to wait more than 10 minutes for the next one to arrive which allowed us to do a lot of sightseeing in one day. My only complaint is that the Wi-Fi didn't work on most of the buses. The Big Bus Tour is a little bit pricer than The Original Tour however it offers more stops so it was worth the extra money to us. One ticket allows you on any of their three routes (red, blue and green). Free headphones are available on each bus and they even give you a poncho if it starts raining!
I met a couple who live in London and have tried every tour bus and they told us that Big Bus was by far the best way to tour the city.
Be warned if you buy your ticket at a bus stop the other tour companies will try to haggle you into buying theirs. No big deal, just a bit annoying and overwhelming.

The Big Bus Tour was a great overview of the highlights of London. It is a must for first time visitors. We especially liked Kevin, the live guide on the Red Line. He was informative and humorous, a great combination.

I used Big Bus in New York and it was fantastic!
I was excited about using them in London and it was a nightmare. I understand the traffic is not this companies problem but it took forever to get anywhere and the two lines overlap so you see 90% of the same spots. Also one day we were using it there was a parade that the driver and guide didn't know about (not their fault) but we got rerouted back around past everything we had just seen.
To be honest I would suggest a city map and a tube map and travel around yourself. The tube was fantastic...I figured it out day 1 and wish now that I never wasted my money on the Big Bus.

We purchased the 2 day option. While it was a nice way to see the city, we were disappointed in the inaccuracy of the paper map provided and the app, as well as the lack of knowledge of the tour guides about the name of the stop so that we could plan our route. Stops did not go in the number order on either. Route changes are understandable, but need to be communicated clearly. This caused us to spend significantly more time on the bus and miss attractions on our agenda. At several points, routes seemed to go in circles, and we found ourselves sitting in the same traffic jams looking at the same sights. While there are benefits to travelling London from above-ground, we found the tube a much more efficient way to get around.

We had a very nice day and gained insight into London. We especially liked that you get to know about the history of the City during the tour. The only drawback was that the map we got was sometimes a bit difficult to read because it didn't show where the north or east bound tours were going to but luckily the staff was very friendly and told us which bus we had to take.

Bought a two day ticket initially as a means of getting around London, but after being on the bus for a few stops, we realised that the guides were not only very knowledgeable, but great fun as well.

Stops near all the main sites to visit, and guides were great at advising what was worth visiting and what to avoid.

If you're there on a day there's a major event on, and being London there are a few, then chances are there may be road closures. These are all very well advertised and shouldn't be surprise when the bus tour is affected.

Simple search on Google or looking at signage should keep you right.

Earlier today we paid £60 for two of us to go on the Big Bus Tour. Only after we paid were we told that there was an event on and that some of the stops might not be available. We took the a Blue bus tour starting at the Aldwych - an hour and a half later we were back having visited Oxford Road, Regent Street and Marble Arch - approximately 20%of the advertised tour.
My advice is to make sure that you find out if there are any planned alterations to the route before you pay for your ticket

We bought a two day ticket, hoping to a have the same easy, go where you want to go with commentary of the city, that we had in New York with a similar type of bus company. It was a waste of money.
We were there the day of the pride parade and obviously roads were closed. This of course is not the company's fault, but maybe inform the customers that the tour is not going where they think it is.
We were on a blue bus and I know there's no live commentary but it would have been nice if the driver had made an announcement that the bus was taking a detour. We finally got of the bus and just decided to walk, which was actually nice since we got see the parade and it was rad.
The next day we tried to catch the red bus from Hyde Park. It took so long we just decided to walk and take a bus from a different stop later. So later, we were on a stop at Regency Street and waited and waited until giving up and (ONCE AGAIN) just walked. We found out soon that Regency Street is apparently closed for cars on Sundays in July, which again, not the company's fault but INFORM THE CUSTOMERS. There was no sign at the bus stop, no information where to go.
All that walking is not really a problem since we like walking and had a great time, but it sucks to pay for something and not getting any. The next day we complained about it to a Big Bus worker and he just shrugged it off, like "yeah, that street is closed on Sundays" WE KNOW. TELL PEOPLE. THAT'S THE ISSUE HERE.
I give this experience a couple of points because the rare red busses we managed to get on, the guides were lovely and great.

Had a great day at the big bus tour.
Saw areas haven't really bothered to see before and was enjoyable to all the family.

Took the tour starting at Marble Arch. Previous reviewers were right on...red tour, in English, with Joanne is best for English speakers. She knows the city's history, is very friendly and has a sense of humor. We hopped off once in Picadilly circus and were assured there would be busses every 20 minutes. Well we walked around for an hour and began waiting for the next bus...after 40 minutes we gave up and grabbed a Uber. Rip off.

Most London visitors have limited time and don't really know their way around. This is one of the best and most sensible way of seeing the sights and choosing what to see more. The service offers travel in clockwise or anti clockwise, one can get on and off en route.... pick up another bus later, have a break, One of the better options is doing the tour over two days and you will see almost everything. Tickets are available at most main line stations and prices vary depending on the season, but are worth every penny. include an inclusive boat ride up the Thames.

We chose the blue tour because it covered more area. The weather today was sunny and rainy and we loved it all. When the traffic lagged, it just gave us better opportunity to take well framed photos and video. All-in-all, it was the best way to see London-- our kids were thrilled! Thanks, Big Bus Tours!

I like quite a lot to get on the bus and be abe to easily get around to the touristic places. But in london was insane because of the traffic. The regular london buses do have AC, but no the Big Bus...so on a hot day as we had and traffic jam was a nightmare.

We had a bad experience on this tour and found it very expensive.
Unfortunately we used the Big Bus Tour the day of the grand prix in central London. The only positive experience was the boat trip from the Tower of London to Westminster which was relaxing.
In the morning we took the bus from the stop at Westminster Bridge to the Tower of London this wasn't pleasant as we were stuck in traffic through the city of London.

The worst part of the day was the bus in the afternoon, we were at Westminster Bridge but had to walk to Waterloo. Again we were stuck in traffic jams. The worst part of this was that we couldn't get off from Marble Arch until Waterloo train Station. They didn't go on the route that we were promised, we missed at lot of the sights in Central London.

The bus tour is pretty expensive and they should have given refunds for the disruption.

There are many bus tour choices for London. We opted for the Big Bus tour as it appeared they were were in abundance. They did not disappoint. Hardly had to wait for a bus at any time. Only drawback is that you have a real tour guide on redline buses only. If you are on a green or blue line you must wear your earbuds and listen to the recording. It's a good way to see the sights on a surface level and decide what you'd like to see more in depth.

My family and I purchased the 3-day big bus tour which included a free night tour. We were very disappointed in the whole experience. The buses are dirty, the audio is horrible, the WiFi never worked on any of the buses, the staff were rude and very unhelpful and the wait time was awful. You would be better off working across London than taking the Big Bus hop on/hop off tour bus!! We would never recommend this one to anyone. We heard from several of our friends that the other tour bus operators in London are much better and that the Big Bus Tour company is pretty much "bottom of the barrel".... Save yourself time, money and frustration and choose a different provider!!

We really enjoyed our Bus Tour in London! Was an excellent way to see the city vs. dealing with a crowd of people and each site. You are able to hop on and hop off at any point, so it's a great way to figure out where to spend more time.

It was a bit pricey, but we loved our tour guide, Big Steve! His commentary was definitely worth it - quite entertaining! He also showed us to an excellent pub nearby and we were able to hop off and grab lunch in a great spot.

It was a little confusing to figure out where each stop was, but once we found the first few, it got easier.

Thanks so much for a great tour!

The weather was nice so what better way to see London than by open top bus. The tour lasted around three and a half hours and was quite extensive. If you have a weak bladder you need to know their is neither toilet on board or toilet stop. Don't let that put you off though. My only grumble is the cost of the tour albeit with a 24 hour ticket. I thought that £35 per adult is a bit steep even for London.

The best bus tour I have done so far was in London (as compared to the ones in Paris and Dubai) with Kevin and Richard (The dream team) on the Red line route of the Big Bus Tour London. The running commentary was very informative and entertaining at the same time. Good on you guys!!

We purchased the 2 day ticket, which came with the free River Cruise Ticket. The River Cruise is a must do as its a Brilliant way to see London and well there is no traffic.

The bus company were good, providing earphone and ponchos should it rain and the live commentary route was also very good.

However the London Traffic was a nightmare. This made the tour very slow so if time is limited the underground would probably be the best way to get about.

We have used "hop hop off" bus tours in several large European cities---its an excellent way to spend your first day getting to know the lay out of the city. In most cases you get a steep discount if you purchase 2 days, which was the case with Big Bus (and included a one way river boat cruise on the Thames). The 'red' line offeres a live commentary, the others use an excellent head phone commentary. Of course, you can get off & on as you please. Fantastic!

We spent money for a two day pass on the hop on, hop off big bus tours. The bus came to the stop in a hurry but once on in took far too long between stops....so long in the traffic that mostly we would get off and walk. It was disappointing as we hoped to get an overview of the city this way but it was near impossible. London Traffic does not allow for this kind of tourism. It is a waste of money in my estimation.

Firstly book online save money
Tour guide was great picked us up outside hotel and we took Red route and were impromptu transferred to another bus where the live commentary continued. We decided to take red route full circle and we enjoyed this, it was long so take food and water. You can hop on or off if you wish.
We arrived back at Westminster Pier where we hopped on the City Cruises boat trip up the Thames again we stayed on all the way to Greenwich and then returned.

We sat outside and got wet a few times with tidal splashes all added to to fun of our trip.

Toilets are well...interesting

Remember the Sunscreen if you do to want to burn

The audio commentary is provided by the company and its boring. The live audio commentary is nice and the crew don't get paid for providing commentary so throw some money in the bucket at the end of your journey.

Views are stunning if weather conditions are nice

An enjoyable afternoon however, due to the London traffic (which is inevitable in any big city), there was a lot of time wasted sitting at a stand still. It would be more effective to visit all the attractions by the underground or even using Santander cycles. The perk of the bus tour was that it took you to some places, such as Grosvenor Square, that would most likely be missed off an average itinerary but are actually very interesting and good to see - the commentary definitely made it better with interesting information.

After reading reviews of the three major double decker bus tours in England (Original Tour, Golden Tour, Big Bus) we decided to go with Big Bus. The reviews were significantly more positive but it did not correspond at all with our experience, sadly.

We picked up our first bus around 10:30 along Queensway then had to transfer at Marble Arch. No guidance was given regarding the availability of the three separate tour routes, though we had hoped to get on a red tour with live commentary. Anyway, we'd gotten a late start and our goal was to get to the Tower by the afternoon so we took the first bus we got - blue.

Then it took what felt like forever to make our way across the city. The traffic was miserable (I guess that's beyond their control) but in the meantime it would have been nice to get more information about the sites. As it was the kids (8 and 10) gave up on the recorded commentary because it was quite dull and not very expansive. Around 1pm we had made it as far as St. Paul's so we decided to hop off for a quick lunch. It was a busy stop so we figured it would be easy to catch another bus and there was a guide on site to keep us informed.

Well, when we finished eating we headed out to the stop. Several other bus companies passed by and then we saw the Big Bus, but it was another blue (the longer, recorded route). We asked the guide if there was a red on the way and whether we should wait. He radioed in and they assured him the next bus was a red and coming soon after. So, we waited and another blue passed. Then nothing, for almost 40 minutes. We watched bus after bus pass by from the other companies and NO BIG BUS.

Finally, a bus was on its way, now almost 3pm. We asked if it was a red or blue, no intel since apparently our guide was now receiving radio silence... At this point we were about to use our Oyster cards to just hop on public transit but we saw the bus in the distance. We waited and got on, alas another blue bus but at this point we just wanted to get somewhere.

One positive, the River Boat (City Cruises, I think?) cruise that comes with the ticket was absolutely worth it though incredibly crowded. The crew on board are not tour guides but they humored us with live commentary. It was funny and engaging. We tipped and so should you!

At this point we just wanted to catch a bus back to our flat, any bus, so we waited at the stop outside Westminster (If you want to see the Abbey make sure you check the times because if you use the bus route you likely won't make it before they close. We went a different day). We waited and waited and waited - about 30 minutes. We gave up and started walking toward Buckingham Palace, we might just squeeze in one more sight.

After walking past the palace, the kids were exhausted at this point and begging to just get on the tube, so we relented and headed toward Victoria station. On our way, what should we encounter but a Big Bus, seemingly at random, so we started running toward it along with a handful of other wandering travelers! Thankfully, we caught that ride and it took us back to Bayswater after a short stop at Marble Arch to kick off anyone not headed that way.

Overall, I think it would have been smarter, cheaper, and more efficient to just use our Oyster Cards for tube and bus. The commentary via audio was less engaging than a wikipedia page and we never did see a RED tour with live commentary. Maybe if we had experienced that, the time spent waiting would have felt worth it.
I really enjoyed sight-seeing on the big bus tours. It was insightful, and the guide had good knowledge of the surroundings. It was relaxing and enjoyed seeing the sights.

The Hop-on, Hop-off tour by Big Bus Tours was an ideal intro to the sites of London. Some of the buses have live commentators but even the taped version was informative and on topic. They have three routes and the ticket includes a most enjoyable boat tour on the Thames. We pre-purchased the tickets and on check in we found we could also purchase discounted tickets to other venues which was quite helpful. We hopped off to catch the 11AM weekday Changing of the Horse Guards and had no difficulty hopping back on to continue our adventure. Definitely a way to start a London experience!

Bought a (not inexpensive) 2-day hop-on/hop-off ticket which includes boat on Thames. Boat trips were nice and somewhat made up for our disappointment in the bus service. 3/4's of the time we went to catch a bus, we had waits of 30 minutes or more before one came. We watched as multiple buses from the other tour companies came and went before Big Bus would arrive. Toward the end of day 1, we waited 45 mins for a bus so missed a connection to the bus that would have gone near our hotel...we were thrown off the bus at quitting time and had to walk a half mile to our hotel. The music between narrations was really great but the waiting times for buses made it bad value for money.

So after spending £35 each for a day ticket and then waiting half an hour we started to wonder if we made the right choice. We knew when we did finally get on and have to stand that this was not a good idea. No aircon and squashed in was not how I wanted to see the sights. Then we were told at the next stop there were going to be more buses, we hopped off eagerly only to find ourselves again waiting and although this time we were sitting, but cramped in the bus. We decided to get off and get a black cab which took us to The Shard (and Borough markets) then to Harrods while passing all the sights including Buckingham Palace (the buses can't actually go there so this was a bonus). This journey including a trip hone cost us the price of one ticket. I can't talk for other hop on off companies but The Big Bus Tour London is useless and not worth your coin.

I only had two days in London and decided the best way to see it would be a hop on/off tour. I researched and decided on Big Bus. I'm really happy with my choice. I rode two tours; the Red and Green line. They went to all the key sights and had a stop near the British Museum. I was also really wanting to get a guided look at the city and its sites.
I have to say my first experience with the live commentary was nothing special. She appeared bored and commented like it was a script. We did see some key sites but didn't get any information that would have made it worth the money.
HOWEVER I was pleasantly surprised with my other two rides. We took the same line the next day as we didn't see everything and stayed for the entire route. We changed guides after a few stops and both were exceptional. Both gave great insight into the sights and really engaged well with all of us. This was really important as London being London, there were some long waits in traffic. With this in mind, if you are able buy at least a two day ticket.
If you buy through the Big Bus website, you can also add other major attractions for a discounted price. It also includes a river cruise and walking tour so take advantage!

Decided to take the London tour with Big bus tours. Glad we did. Excellent, friendly, funny & informative tour guides & staff. This is by far the best way to see London. We hopped off at Covent Garden for lunch & hopped back on again to go to Tower of London to get the boat up to Westminster bridge. (Boat trip included in price £35 per person). Will definitely be using this company again. Highly recommended.

This is maybe the best hop on hop off service of London. It includes 41 stops, and covers all the main landmarks of London. It has 3 lines, green, red and blue. We always used blue line, and it satisfied us. Also I would advise to buy deluxe tickets for 3 days, because it includes free boat tour and free night tour.

We did big bus in London and wish we had in Paris. There were plenty, lots of staff at many of the stop locations. This is an excellent company. And their add on cruise was good. Right at the Tower Bridge which was a nice thing after doing the Tower bridge tour.

Spent 2 days on the big bus, the guides where fantastic with the exception of one our first was a wonderful lady called Aude who made our tour really pleasant, then we had Peter who really knew his history only downside we joined the tour and shortly after he was finishing. Georgie was very good and witty and full of knowledge and lastly apolgies but couldn’t remember if it was sienna a lovely Italian lady who was very funny and made our last trip on the big bus very memorable. 4 out of 5 guide where all fantastic thank you all so much and I look forward to going back in the Big Bus when I visit again in October,

We have waited and waited for this bus
Bad service bad attitude avoid at all costs
Use the big brown bus it passed us by many times while waiting for this useless service. There excuse London traffic
Just flew in from NY ??? Heaps of buses
And excellent service

What a dour tour bus, we weren't given earphones so missed the 1st 10 minutes guide, on receiving we heard many long bursts of boring dialogue. We were told this was the best tour! We have travelled extensively and always hop on these for a whistle-stop view of the sites.
