I was expecting a local person with a microphone to tell me of the less famous places we were passing, little snips of local knowledge that we have got from other bus tours, (different countries) but no, all we got was music piped in our ears for a majority of the trip, I'm not sure why the trip took interest in showing passengers 'social housing' and went into detail of the housing crisis after the war, the area was grim, i would recommend buying an Oyster card and finding places of interest on foot, this was £35pp it was an expensive bus ride to the boat. The 'free' boat ride (one way) was a treat, the guide was knowledgable and amusing with local snippets and interesting facts, if the bus guides took the 'sailors' onto the buses, then you would have a trip to remember. Ditch the headphones or improve what's piped into our ears.

We had a fantastic tour guide on the Red line big bus tour !
Thanks Matt ! Matt was enthusiastic, funny , and very knowledgeable! We hope to catch up with him again to listen to more stories .

Review by Dr Sim. Tourist should take at least 1 round ride to get a feel of London. I bought the hop on hop off cruise as well with the bus ticket. The route is a bit long. Sometimes you have to take the underground to a specific place if the bus route is too long. Overall a good experience. Regards Dr Sim

I jumped on a 'Big Bus' without a ticket and bought one on the bus. Very easy and you can jump on and off at any of the 40+ stops along the way. There are complimentary earphones to use and you can take them with you.

I loved the tour and highly recommend doing it your first or second day because along the way you will see things you never would have thought of doing and you can then go do them later in your trip.

Fair warning: you WILL sit in traffic and to do the whole tour will take several hours. The beauty of it is that you'll touch on all of the big landmarks and can get off anywhere is you want to spend more time and then walk, cab, uber, subway it back. Or you can jump back on one if their many busses and continue the tour.

My FAVORITE thing about the BIG BUS tour was that a boat tour was also included in the price. I jumped on the boat near Tower Bridge and rode it back down to the eye. The tour guide was hilarious and had just the right personality mixing history with humor.

I highly recommend the tour!

Prior to visiting London I researched the on-off bus companies and chose Big Bus for the walking tours that were included in the price. They listed a Changing of the Guard history tour, a Harry Potter tour, and a Ghost Tour. After getting on the bus in the morning we found out from our tour guide that the website hadn't been updated and that these tours had been discontinued. Now they only offered a single history tour that we had already missed.

They operate three lines:

1) The Red Line has live commentary in English. Our first guide was an informative and funny gentlemen. Our second guide we couldn't understand a word she was saying. The Red Line is great for getting the "lay of the land" but as we found out, with traffic this is not a great way to travel -- it's slow to say the least.

2) The Blue Line had recorded commentary -- we never got to use it.

3) The Green Line went up to the British Museum and Eurostar station. We did use this line, but once again with traffic it took us forever to get to our destination (the stop a few blocks from the British Museum). We got on the bus around Trafalgar Square, but the stop was not properly marked so we walked right by it at first. Also watch for low, untrimmed trees if you are on the top.

The cruise with City Cruises that was included in the price of your ticket was nice. We got on at the Tower of London and rode back down to the Westminster area. You really do get to see a lot from the boat. Plus there is no traffic or traffic lights, and the crew is pretty funny with their commentary.

Don't take these buses thinking you are going to see all of the city or all of the sights in one day. It just doesn't work. You can, however, have a pleasant ride around town.
Are really big buses travelling around the main tourists attractions in London. The tour guide was very informative.

We bought a 2 day hop on hop off pass with Big Bus and were so happy we did. This was our last 2 days in London so we followed the red line one day, the blue line the next and we were able to see the rest of the sites we wanted to see. It was such a great way to get to the different areas & also a fantastic way to just see London driving around. We never had any problems with there not being a bus to get on and the drivers of those buses deserve a lot of respect and praise because it takes some serious skill to drive one of those on London streets! They have rain ponchos on board, one line had a live tour guide, the other gave you a headset to listen to an audio guide. There are also employees at the bus stops to help you and answer any questions. We also bought some of tickets from them to the sites we were going to see - saved us time at the places as we were able to skip the ticket line and go right in. I would highly recommend Big Bus - they provide fantastic service!

I always find the hop on buses the best way to see everything in cities..I don't know if it was just our luck but the traffic in London made this trip not really worth it as it took too long to get around...eg...it took us 2 and half hrs to go from the Tower of London stop back to our hotel, and we seemed to go around in circles quite a few times taking more time. We had a two day pass but only used one day as we weren't sure we'd get back in time to catch our flight..

This was my second Big Bus Tour - first in Vienna last year and now London. As a business traveler, I always like to carve out a day to explore the city. The one challenge is that I am a woman traveling alone. Big Bus Tours allows me to see the entire city in a safe environment. Joining the tour is always in a convenient location - easy to find signage. Enjoy the city narrative and humor storytelling.

We brought tickets for £35 each seemed a tad expensive at first but once you have finished the tour which took over three hours it was money well spent. We did not hop on/off we just sat at the top of the bus and enjoyed the views etc. They have the tours in several languages, handsets are free.

My husband & I spent 4 days in London last year, and I wanted to return with my 16 yr old daughter this year because I loved so much of it. When we arrived I purchased 2 hop on-hop off tickets from Big Bus (last year we bought from another company). We hopped in and off most of one day but audios only worked on ONE bus. On another bus there was a very old man talking into a microphone but he was barely audible. When I mentioned to him that the audio wasn't working, he shrugged and didn't care. It would have been preferable if he would've turned around so his voice projected TOWARD us but he remained in the very first seat in the top of the bus. I suggest you purchase tickets from another tour bus company to maximize your enjoyment.

During our trip to England we took a bus into London for the day on Jun 5th. We decided to buy a 1 day pass on the Big Bus Tour Hop on Hop Off. This was a great way to see as much of London as we could. In the early 70's I lived in London, but my wife had never been to England. The next time we travel to the U.K. I want to spend more time showing her around and this is the best way.

I was in London with work friends for the day and we decided to be tourists. We jumped on the green line and changed on to the red line, it's on this bus we found reid. What a great tour guid he was, very informative and hilarious, we wanted to get off and see the sites but we where enjoying this tour guides great presentation we stayed on until he left us. It's such a shame as he had mentioned that this was his last day with the company, I hope the rest of your guides can live up to his standard the next time I'm in London.

if you want to get from point A to B fast do not use this system.
this is cruise control all the way. lots of great stops...
staff and drivers were very nice and accommodating..
can get very crowdy and pushy
no AC inside the bus- window do not open-full sun outside. seat can get sticky and uncomfortable after a while.
blue route has too many stops- some stops are not marked properly (1.5 hours from Hyde park to London tower)
service stop at 6 pm
the night tour start at 630 pm- I would not call that night tour in June as the sun does not set but at 10 pm- the route is the same a blue line-
Red line is perfect - live guide and a few stop only..friendly guide...
The round trip ticket cruise included in premium ticket is not worth. lots of people-long line from the main dock across from Big Ben. and not much to see but what on the bus route- once inside the boat just cross over to the eye to get the second group of travellers??!! there is another entry point under the Eye ( did not know), less crowd- you get second choice on seating. we did one way to London Tower and that is enough for the boat for me....took the red bus on the way back...

Would I recommend.. yes but only if the weather is cool and partly cloudy

We had a 2 day pass with a cruise to Grenwich. We took the blue route, which stopped outside our hotel. London has a lot to see & 2 days is needed on this bus. The cruise was lovely with great commentary. The buses kept to their timetable. Only 1 complaint, when u get to Sherlock Holmes stop, you are asked to leave the bus & transfer to the one in front. Dont know why this is done & we cant contiue on same bus. This was done on both days. Otherwise good tour.

I've done hop on/off bus tours all over the place, but this one was probably one of the worst. There were far too many stops and circle backs on the route, which meant that trying to complete one entire loop took FOREVER. We only completed half of the blue route in 4 hours. The buses are not air conditioned, which doesn't matter outside of the peak summer temperatures, but during that time it gets quite warm inside and up top in the sun. They were also pretty crowded from about 11am onward, despite the number of buses available. The commentary was good, but there wasn't enough variety to the classical music played between sights when you factor in the amount of time stuck in traffic. So you end up hearing the same 4-5 songs over and over.

If you have only one day in London and don't want to walk or take the tube everywhere, the bus is a good way to go, but if you have more than a day, I'd recommend different options. Maybe mix it up with a walking tour of one neighborhood, tube hopping in another and the bus for just a small section of one loop?

I think the Big Bus tour is a fantastic way to see all the highlights of London for a first time visitor and is also a convenient way to get around town. The Red Tour offers live commentary and other tours offer recorded info on all the sights along the way. We've used other hop-on hop- off companies in the past but like Big Bus the best.

There are several hop on hop off bus tours offered in London. Our concierge suggested Big Bus as the one favored by previous guests. Base price was higher than others but included some additional activities such as a boat tour on the Thames and a walking tour that were separate charges on other bus companies. If any of the additional activities are used, Big Bus becomes the less expensive tour. We took the boat tour, saw sights we would not have seen from a bus and really enjoyed it.
One ticket includes three routes. Primary route is in English with a live commentator. The other two have recorded commentaries in multiple languages via headsets.

I think this is a great way to get a quick tour of the city. You will go all over and see almost all the major attractions, and if you feel like hoping off, you do! I enjoyed our tour guide as well. My only complaint is that they changed the route up a bit from what was on the map on the website, so it screwed up my planning. But if you don't have your entire day planned down to the minute, it shouldn't be too big a deal to just roll with the adjustment. Be warned, however; London traffic is absolutely horrendous, and unpredictable. If you are planning on using the bus to get you to a destination for a specific time, you must realize that it can take over 3 hours for the Red line to go all the way around. I don't know about the other lines, that's just what our guide told us it would take for the Red line. I wouldn't bother with the river cruise, even though it's included for free. You can only see certain things from the river, and you're much farther away from them. Just stick with the buses, in my opinion.

We have used the Big Bus many times in the states so we felt this was our best option for getting around London without fuss. We were not disappointed! Whether you just want transportation from point A to point B or you want to ride the circuit, you can't go wrong with Big Bus and the additional history lessons in route

Thank you Big Bus London and our guide Pete A... just amazing.

If you have limited time this is the best way to see the sites of the city.

We also hopped on the river cruise and did the London eye .. so make sure you buy the package deal they offered when you first get on.. such great value.

Start early as it's gets crowded.

Highly recommended.

We loved this experience -we couldn't believe we had the same bus driver PAUL
as we had in 2014 - it was great to see him - we also had KEVIN as our commentator on the bus - we just loved his humour and made it a lot of fun as we learnt the history of London - i videoed some of Kevin's humourous commentary to take back to Australia to show family - Kevin and Paul work so well as a team,friendly
funny, and so informative, and really make the trip worth while and are truly an asset to this company - The Tour was great - get on and off were you like - we were just hoping we would get the same bus and team when we got back on the red tour -

There are plenty of pick up points around London. The weather was too good not to take advantage of sitting on the open aired top deck. The commentary was good and quite entertaining. The bus goes all around London to all the top tourist areas. There is a blue service and red service, these go to different locations around London. You can get off at any tour bus stop and pick it up again elsewhere. You can also get off the bus and take a boat ride up the Thames as part of the deal. The ticket lasts for 24hrs. It really is a great way to get around and see all the sights of such a beautiful city.

We just got the bill for $45 per person for this. In New York City the hop on hop off is $17. We got on near our hotel near Kensington Palace. In a very short while we stopped at the wax museum and everybody got off including the driver who joined other drivers of parked busses to kibitz. When I asked what was going on, our driver yelled up at the top where we were sitting all alone that I don't listen. He said that We are go climb down from the top and get on another bus. I don't like being yelled at. We had just arrived in London that morning and the plan was to sit on the bus and ride around until we would get into our hotel. It was a very un satisfying experience. The employees are Rude and contemptuous of customers. Don't do this.

On a big part of the tour where only the bus with the recorded commentary is going there was only music playing and nothing was said. This was especially disappointing because we were stuck in traffic most of the time. I did not book the tour just so I can listen to the same music over and over again. I wanted to learn something about London. For that part we could have taken the underground and been cheaper.

Also when I booked the tour online the night tour was still included in the 48 hour tour. Turns out it is not anymore and they didn't feel it necessary to send an email informing people!

We had used Hop On Hop Off bus tours many times internationally as well as in the USA. No problem; however, in London, we had trouble getting busses after we hopped off. Twice we waited 45 and 50 minutes for a bus when they state every 20 minutes and, unfortunately, once we had to walk back to our destination because no bus ever appeared. Several individuals have relayed to me that this happened to them as well. I would not recommend using this service (or non-service)!
We had the wittiest, sweetest and most intelligent tour guide in Matthew! I hope everyone is lucky enough to get him because he made the tour so enjoyable we didn't want to hop off on any sites!

I love these buses especially if you're only visiting London for a short amount of time. This may, was my fourth time on the buses since I've always traveld with a person who's never been to London.
You get vouchers, great staff, really god live torus and recorded tours. You get to see every important "must see" thing in London. It's nice to just sit back and enjoy the ride upstairs, you learn a lot. It's hop on hop of so you can get of and take your time with the attractions, you get earphones, rain poncho, vouchers and a map. It also includes a themes river boat ride.

Disappointing experience. We got tickets for this tour. There were a number of concerns we had. The tour commentary was pre recorded and the commentary did not always match up with the geographic location and in between there was unpleasant music, we wanted to hear the city. We were also unsure of when to get off. When we hopped of the bus and went to get on there were very long waits. Many other big buses from other companies passed by. The map was not helpful. When we did get back on they kept on terminating and we had to reboard. We have done the same sort of tour in New York, far superior. The whole thing was most disappointing, tourism here is huge and this should have been much better.

We thought the Big Bus Tours would be a great way to get an overview of London, and it started out ok. We got a 2 day pass. The second day we went to one bus stop and were informed that they are not using this stop anymore and were instructed where to go. At that spot we were informed that the route had been changed. We were following the route map that had been given to us the day before. After workers decided which bus we should be on, we were so disappointed to be stuck on a long route with bumper to bumper traffic. We should have walked! Granted, the traffic is not the employees nor company's fault. Would not recommend this in London.

The London experience came alive with Pete A and Paul aboard the London Big Bus tour. The live commentary sprinkled with the famous British humour, the convenience and the frequency of buses makes this tour better than the others on offer at the same price.

The boat ride on the Thames was excellent as well. Most people take the Tower pier to Embankment - and miss out the downriver experience till Greenwich.

We have used the Bigbus Hop On-Hop Off tour on two occasions when we have visited London,the last time being 20/21st May.We bought a two day ticket , after arriving in London from New Zealand at 6.15am and finding we couldn't get into our accomodation until 2pm.We caught the Blue route from a stop close to our hotel near Paddington Station and spent the morning being driven around London looking at the sights and thinking about were we would come back to later.The bus was very clean and all the guides and drivers were really helpful.We used the Red line as well and the commentary was fabulous.I would have no hesitation in recommending this tour company and would use them again when in London.

We were in London for a few days after taking a cruise to Southampton. I had read good things about Big Bus before our trip and when I found out it had a stop right in front of our hotel (Doubletree Hyde Park) it cinched it for me.

I bought a two day pass online the night before. We ended up on the first bus in the morning. Since our hotel was on the Blue Route we always had the recorded tour vs. a 'live guide'. While initially I thought it would be better to have an actual guide and we could have switched along the way to the Red route to have one, we never ended up doing that. I found that I did like the recorded one too - it was very interesting and came on right when you were nearby the location it was describing.

We weren't sure which attractions we wanted to go to so we stayed on for the whole Blue route the first time. It became a bit drizzly but thankfully Big Bus had already provided rain ponchos since we still wanted to sit up on the top level.

We got off at Marble Arch once and did some shopping on Oxford Street. Our hotel concierge had told us about the store Primark which was outstanding for its variety of merchandise and mainly for it's low prices. It was also packed though.

We interacted with the drivers and staff and all were very pleasant and professional.

The second day we took the free river cruise - that was also great so I suggest you make time for it and don't miss it.

I had a discount code so received 10% off the price and I really felt it was a good value. I would definitely recommend this to others. So much better than trying to get around by yourselves and so much less expensive than paying taxis to go everywhere.
This was a great way too see all the sights. If something seemed interesting we just hopped off. We enjoyed both the live and audio tours.

I would suggest not to go with this Big Bus. I took there service in shanghai and it was really very good but in london it was very very horriable. Drive and agents at the stop are very unprofessional. They are least bother about the customer who has bought the ticket. They are just busy in grabing new customer. They dont even have info or give any info.Bus are not on time and there frequency is also low on each route. It would rather suggest use tfl service for each attraction that is the most cheap and fastest way to reach every attraction.

There are so many different Hop on Hop Off tours in London, but we were glad we chose The Big Bus. Whether you take the Blue Route with pre recorded narration or Red Route with live narration one gets an excellent learning experience. The only problem was on one of the Red Route busses we were inside the bus and the sound system was terrible and we were unable to hear the guide. We got off and transferred to another bus.
I enjoy these hop on, hop off busses to acquaint myself with a new city. This tour didn't disappoint, but be prepared to bundle up!

A extremely relax & enjoyable ride. Big Bus hop on hop off come with different route & also with different price / package. You can opt for 1 day tour or 2 days tour with free boat ride & other free entry package. You may choose the bus with or without English Tour guide. The English Tour guide name Steve Lovell was so helpful.

We booked 2-days (48 hours) hop on hop off tour in London, it also include cruise tour 😊👍🏻 It was worth every penny and a great way to explore London. Red line has a live commentary and the guide (forgot his name) was fun and had vast information to share :)

Tour guide was a wealth of information and had a great sense of humor. He was a retired school teacher who loved telling others about the history of London. The bus was right on time, easy to find, and the length of the bus tour was just right. Take the Red Route and you will not be disappointed.

I highly reccomend walking tours. We took first one (Royal London) in the morning wondering what it´s gonna be like. We (me and my teens) enjoyed it with Kevin so much that we immediately decided to took rest two (Harry Potter and Haunting Mysteries) walking tours. We also took river cruise and part of a bus tours and spent a perfect day in London.

Booked a ticket for 2 days online, and was offered additional 24 hours for free. The webpage explains all the routes and various tickets, you can also print out the map in advance. There are 3 different routes, the red line is the main one with a live guide. We took the bus on Baker Street, and got to see all the well-known London attractions. The hop off-hop on system is really convenient, just make sure to check when the next bus is coming. You can switch for another line at Victoria Station. The blue line goes through Paddington and stops at many parks. Our ticket also included a river boat cruise, which lasts for about 40 minutes and was really nice. No need to get a new ticket, you just show yours at the Tower Bridge. I recommend buying the tickets online and planning the trip in advance. I think it's a super easy way to get to know London without getting lost.

It doesn't matter if you live here or visiting London. This is a must. London is so beautiful and you see it all from the hop on and hop off. I love this on a sunny day. I tell all my guests to take this tour. Everyone loves it.

We have had Big Bus tour in other city and felt confident this would deliver, not so, first bus late by 20 minutes at the st pauls stop. No commentry this is the reason for choosing this co. Next bus the commentry was all about what the guy with mike liked. Last bus of the day had the best commentry wish I had of caught his name to give him a shout at.

My family and I visited London in April and were looking for a way to see all the major sites without having to walk or commute all over this city. We found the Big Bus Tours to be very convenient as all the major sites were part of the tour.

We did find the pricing a little expensive but did like the fact that you could hop on and hop off at any time. Buses ran every 10-20 minutes. Please note there are 3 different tours (colors) offered; however we purchased the red line and found that we could go on the other tours without paying extra. This could be because it was an off-peak time.

Purchasing tickets are quite easy through the website and bus stops are clearly marked, but not always easy to find. There are representatives at the larger stops who are able to assist. We misplaced our ticket and the rep was able to provide us a hot spot using his phone so that I could log onto my email and have the tickets printed. He definitely went above and beyond the call of duty to assist us!

The tour guide was very knowledgeable and made the tour enjoyable. Her name way Hillaria and she was from Italy. The vehicle is a double decker bus and there are open area (rear) as well as a covered area (front) on the second deck. The bus does offer free rain ponchos and ear buds. Tours are available in many languages as well. Our tour also came with a river ride on the Thames, but we were not able to take advantage of this with our infant son.

Overall a great experience, just a little higher priced than expected. I would recommend taking this tour!

Having used hop on hop off type tours in the USA we felt it would be a great way to get around and see some of the major sites (of which some we re happy to just look at ) .

We chose big bus tours as it has an office situated at Euston station and I felt this was fairly reassuring .

We bought the 24 hour ticket - unsure if we would utilise fully but for such a small difference in fee it made sense .

We were advised that the ticket would be activated when we first got on a bus or the river cruise boat, with this in mind we actually used the tube to get to our first destination ( Oxford Circus ) and then after a light lunch and shopping got on a bus around 4pm.

The tour we got on ( blue route ) does not have a live guide , but instead a recorded commentary - to be fair it was quite good and had some interesting facts .

This brought us fairly close to where we were staying so we got off once at Tower Hill.

The next day we went on the red route which is the most comprehensive and has a live guide - we had a young man who I believe to be called Reid , but my husband said he is called lee ( apologies ) - he was a mine of information and has a rather dry wit - which we loved .

It was strange actually as in the USA the guides rely heavily on tips and let you know this throughout the tour - in the UK this is not discussed and the guide had to end his shift and leave so we didn't even get a chance to give him anything .

I've visited London dozens of time in a work capacity but never done the tourist trail as such - I thoroughly enjoyed the tours and can recommend - sadly we didn't take advantage of the river cruise included on our ticket due to it being rather cold !

We took the Big Bus Tours for 2 consecutive days and it was awsome. We got to visit all the main attractions and sites. We really enjoyed our tour and a special thanks to the wonderful guide "Kevin" who did a great job!

We took a london day trip from paris and it included a bus tour. Unfortunately there eas a marathon happening in london on this day and the rout was a little different. Still u get to see the attractions from london

Bought a two day pass since only it was only @ six pounds more than the one day. The pass includes a Thames River boat ride and a couple of walking tours. The pass is good for several routes. We chose the red line as it has a live guide so you can ask questions. Red route guides commentary is in English only. The blue route buses give you headphones so you can listen to a taped commentary with choice of twelve languages. We had two different guides and they were both good. The commentator on the Thames River cruise was very good - very humorous. Recommand the Big Bus tour as a good way to get familiar with central London.

I recently took my family to London and we spent a couple of days in central London doing the Tourist thing. We bought a ticket for a day and got an extra day for free. This also included a cruise down the Thames. The commentary was good, the buses were clean and whilst slightly on the expensive side it was really worth it.

Takes about 90 minutes to do the complete loop.

Oh and my daughter loved the fact that there was free Wifi on every bus.

Highly recommended. We actually did a Big Bus Tour in Dubai on the way to London and in Paris on the way home.

Booked the classic tour online and it's worth every penny! Went on the tour on 14Apr Easter Day and despite being a busy tourist day, operation was smooth. I hop on the Green line from Holborn and went on Blue line at Westminster bridge. While at Harrods stop I asked for suggestions to have Fish and Chips and had a nice chat with the staff. Eventually hop on Red line again near the London Eye and enjoyed the live commentary by the tour guide, Pete A. He was funny and attentive to all passengers, helping everyone figure out their route and giving suggestions.
Ticket is valid for 24 hours so I hop on a river cruise and had a fantastic time. Didn't get the bloke's name but he had fantastic humour. Tour ended with the chime of Big Ben at 2pm 15Apr. Can't ask for a better experience.

If you're looking to do a hop on-hop off bus tour I highly suggest you use Big Bus tours! Even if you are not interested in the hop on-hop off their guides have tickets for everything!! The guides on the street were so helpful telling us which bus lines to get on and things to do at each stop. The guys on the street really know the city. Once we hopped on the bus we never wanted to hop off because of the tour guide on the bus!! Different tour guides bring you different points of view, of course, but every tour guide did a great job blending history and humor! 10+ stars! Great way to see the city

A few days earlier we did the big bus tour in Paris, which was excellent. In comparison we found this a bit of a disappointment. Route has a major diversion at the moment, which really disjoint the tour and the commentary. The blue route is long and probably unnecessary. London isn't so well suited to bus tours. We abandoned it after a few hours and took the tube. If you know where you want to go and plan a route it's cheaper to get a day travel card and use the bus and tube.

Had a really great day using the big bus today! Never waited more than 10 mins for a bus and there was one route that had a live guide giving commentary and he was just outstanding. He gave lots of interesting trivia along with the information about the major sights that made the ride extremely enjoyable. I asked his name so I could give him a shout out but unfortunately it was such a busy day I've forgotten it. We also did the river cruise that was included and loved that as well. Thank you big bus for a great London experience!

I have been on a few bus tours now, I have been lucky those few times, mainly because of the radio.
These bus tours have two different types, one is the Live Tour - a speaker is telling you about the sites in English - and the radio tour, a pre-recorded voice(s) that tell you about the history of London, the buildings and what tourist attractions are coming up next. The only problem with the pre-recorded one's is that some seats don't have working radios, so the passengers have spent £35 - or more if they are getting a few days of travel - to hearing nothing about London at all, instead they get to look at the sights that they could have seen on a regular bus.
It should also be warned that the full tour, if you are going from where you depart and you want to do a full loop round the city on the Radio tour, will take about 4 hours give or take traffic.
I also kind of wish that the tour had a famous voice doing the talking - not insanely famous, like Hugh Grant - but someone who is a Londoner, and maybe cameo's of people who know about certain histories of certain buildings to take over a section to liven it up a bit since it is a long tour. Although maybe most people do get off and go to other attractions? I tend to just stay on and get all the knowledge that I can in one sitting.

My daughter and I used the Hop On Hop Off bus during our visit to London. It has two primary routes through the heart of the city, one plays a recording of city hi lites (Blue Line) and the Red Line has an live person to describe City Hi-lites. We were able to purchase tickets for Tower of London from this vendor as well as transportation, but since the bus only follows two routes it is not the most direct route to the final destination, so in my opinion a little misleading. When we purchased the tickets the sales vendor made a point of saying we could use the tickets for the bus on two days when in fact the tickets were only good for 24 hours, which again was misleading. After visiting our final destination we had to run to catch a bus as we were at the wrong stop and tried to flag the drivers attention, only at the last minute did he ackowledge us but refused to open the doors and drove off without letting us on. Very disappointing Customer service. My advice is learn the Tube, and invest in a good travel book instead.

The company run a number of routes - some live narration and some prerecorded. The prerecorded are ok and informative but the live tour guides are excellent and really know their stuff and the extra stories they have in the inevitable slow traffic are hilarious. Very easy way to see a lot of the city in a relatively short time. We combined the bus tour with the river cruise which travels from London Bridge to Tower bridge. Well worth it if you only have a short time in London.

We used the Big Bus Tour to get an overview of the city and found it very worthwhile! The staff was helpful and we especially enjoyed our guide - Matt. His humor and information was entertaining. We continued to use the bus the remainder of the day to see and enjoy the sites.

My 9 year old son and I did the Harry Potter walking tour through the Big Bus tours. The walk was longer than we expected but Patrick, our guide, kept my son interested the entire time. The actual bus tour was good and enabled us to see much of the city for the short time period we were in London, but the Harry Potter tour was definitely a highlight.

I purchased my Big Bus tour tickets at Victoria Station, he offered us attractions for a discounted price. We had been planning to go to London Sky so we bought tickets. We had planned to go early but the blue bus took 2.5 hrs just to get to the London Sky so we had lunch and went on the Harry Potter walking tour. The guide (who was also trying to sell everyone attraction tickets) assured us London Eye was open until 8. We got there at 5pm and was told our tickets couldn't be used that they have limited available for 3rd part sellers. We took the tube to Victoria Station to find the guy who sold us the tickets and they had closed up for the night. I am very disappointed, I wasted £46 and missed out on the one attraction I wanted to do. I would never had bought tickets from Big Bus if I had known I was just throwing away my hard earned cash.

My advice is to pay the extra and buy direct from the attraction. The agents must know the tickets are limited.

The Harry Potter tour was really good but since I was ripped off on my London Eye tickets I can't give them a good rating.

Had a great tour with big bus over two days. Steve Lovell the tour guide on the red bus was a highlight with his insight and signature English wit. The tour buses are a great way of getting oriented to a new city so you can go back and visit areas of interest in more detail and at your leisure.

I wanted to do this because I wanted to orient myself to the city. The drivers and helpers make it very easy and can answer most questions. We sat on top, which was the best way to see everything. You want to make sure you dress warmly as it can get very chilly. The best part of our experience was the walking tour we took with Steve. I cannot stress enough how wonderful he was. Truly an ambassador for the city. He was friendly, knowledgeable, funny and told us great stories of all kinds. I would have never discovered all the lovely areas he showed us. Not only was he a great tour guide but personally escorted us the the tube, got us a map, showed us where to go, took us down to the stop and waited until our train came. We were blessed by his generosity of spirit. The Big Bus is very lucky to have such a gentleman working for them. Thank you so much Steve. We will be telling that story for a long time!

Bought a three day ticket ,included 3walking trips unlimited use of the the bus tour hop on hop off and a return trip down the Thames to Greenwich .Had three different tour guides all with very different humours and knowledge ,the first one on Friday was James pleasant knowledgeable and was really helpful .The second tour guide and Saturday missed the bus at Green park and ran to the next stop Serena from Italy well Big bus her English was well below the required standard but she will improve if the tour commentary is in Italian,but as they say could do better .The third tour guide today Easter Sunday was Matt from Manchester ,very knowledgeable added a bit of humour and was fun ,Big bus tours are worth the money and I would recommend them to anyone who wants to learn about the great city of London .

I will be visiting London in September for the New Orleans Saints game. We will only have two days to visit the city. We are staying on Strand Avenue and will spend the first day walking to the National Gallery, St. James Park, Buckingham Palace and then to Harrods for dinner. The second day we would like to do Tower of London and St. Pauls Cathedral and the British Museum. The first two have entrance fees. So, we are trying to decide if we want to buy the London Pass and use the Hop On Hop Off bus to get to our destinations since it does cover the entrance fees. The couple traveling with us has not been to London before and we thought the bus might also be a nice way to see a lot of the city. We plan to dine in China Town that night. I would greatly appreciate any advice.

Loved this company. Great way to see lots of london. Only suggestion would be to do this hop on hop off bus for 1 day. It takes too long to get to all the attractions due to traffic so it takes up a lot of valuable time. I would use the tube the rest of the time as it is easy and quick. Sitting in the top deck is fun and the audio commentary is interesting !

This is a nice and fun way to tour around London. We did only the red tour, and it was very nice, we learned a good deal of history and helped us to choose what we would visit next. Recommend to buy the combo Big Bus + London Eye online, in advance (you'll pay less).

We had only one day in London and the Big Bus was the easiest way for us to take in all of the major sights and landmarks without the hassle of figuring out how to get from one location to the next. We never waited more than a few minutes for the next bus to pick us up. The commentary (live and recorded) was entertaining and the free wifi was a big plus.

We did not expect to have a 'free' guided tour around the Central London, which was included in the Big Bus ticket. We walked with our tour guide, Steve Lovell, and he explained all the shooting scenes around Central London with a sense of humour. It was really an interesting guided tour indeed, and we highly recommend others to join the walking tour, especially those Harry Potter fans ...

By far the easiest way to tour London. With many conveniently located stops, and the ability to hop off and on as you need, you can see the majority of Londons tourist sites in comfort. Our 9 year old daughter loved sitting upstairs!

The tour was fun, very informative, full of funny stories and tales of the old city! Our kids loved to ride the doubled-decked open bus, as they also could chill out a bit after all the walking. After seeing the main landmarks throughout London, we could pick up the ones we'll definitely spend more time visiting.
I highly commend Sarah, our guide, for the excellent and lively tour!

I wanted to see London with my 7 year old daughter in a relatively short time and without a lot of walking. We chose Big Bus line blue. The color is of importance because in the blue line you get earphones and can chose one of twelve languages. Easy, convenient and interesting. Hop off hope on allows to take flexible decisions. An add on us the river cruise. Good job.

My family and I were so excited. We waited an hour and 15 minutes this morning and no bus. The other two companies, golden tour and the original bus tours had 10-12 buses come through during our wait. The two employees had no information and stayed as far as they could from their customers to not have to answer questions. All they would do was lie that a bus was ten minutes away then it was five minutes away. After an hour and a half of waiting there was still no bus. There was a funeral that closed some streets but the other companies seemed to prepare for this. We are finally on a boat as we gave up waiting for the bus. I will be sure to tell everyone I know not to book big red bus.

My husband and I bought two 48-hours tickets for the HOP-ON HOP-OFF Big Bus London tours and were not disappointed. There are different routes taking you to slightly different parts of town. You can ride on a live commentary bus or take the one with headphones and choose which language is best for you.

We rode on a few of the live commentary buses and I have to say, it wasn't always easy to hear to guy or gal tell us facts and stories about where we were. Most of the girls were harder to hear and some of the commentators with strong accents were hard to understand. Go with the headphones!!

These buses take you almost everywhere you want to go especially when you are only in town for a few days and want to see the highlights. Get on an get off wherever you want. The next bus is usually only about 25 minutes away. At most stops, there is a Big Bus employee that an answer questions. That's how we found them in the first place - we were walking near Victoria Station and there was a Big Bus employee (they wear burgundy jackets/shirts) and can sell you a ticket on the spot.

Once you're on the bus you can choose to stay on the lower level or go on top. Most of the top level is open air, but there are some covered seats at the front.

We highly recommend this tour service in London (we used them in Amsterdam too).

It is my first time in London and we decided to do the bug bus tour. Our tour guide was Dani and she was so funny and really well informed. She was an amazing tour guide telling us little anecdotes as we went along, and when the bus had to take a couple of unexpected detours off her route she still did her best to continue her guide, very professionally done! I would recommend this tour to anyone

After a chaotic experience in an American city, we were reluctant to do a sightseeing tour but our experience in London was fantastic! We are now converts.

As a group of 8 people, it was a much more convenient way to see London. We took advantage of the free additional 24 hour offer and made extensive use of the routes over 2 days. We even squeezed in the river boat trip to Greenwich. On the way home, we used the bus to take us back to Euston saving the use of our oyster cards. The buses were regular, the drivers helpful and the complimentary ponchos were very welcome when it rained!

Big Bus is touristy, but if you want to see the sights without spending ages navigating the underground, it is perfect.

It's my first time in London, and after receiving some advice from the concierge desk at my hotel to try this service, I decided to go for it. At £35 for a day's pass, I found this an excellent way to not only travel London, but get off and see sights, then get right back on and keep going. So it's really several services in one: cab, tour guide, bus ride. The guides were all very knowledgeable and pleasant, there were plenty of busses to catch after seeing sights on given stops, and the destinations were are excellent. Highly recommended way to travel London for first or second timers.

This was by far and away the worst sightseeing/tour experience I've ever had in any city or country. We utilized the Red Line initially and the guide was disinterested at best, but we perservered on! When the bus departed from the mapped route, however it set our plans into a little chaos. Not to be deterred, we opted to switch to the Green Line and make our way back to our original plan.
NOPE! We waited at the stop for 55 minutes (the Green line is supposed to stop every 20 minutes).
We saw plenty of The Original Bus and City Tour buses during our interminable wait at Dante's 9th Plane of Hell (aka the Big Bus Bus Stop), and even a few Big Bus Tours from about 1/2 mile away on a cross street, but not one flaming, light cursed Big Bus Green line at its scheduled stop.
We gave up an took a Black Taxi. Not only was the driver way more informative than Big Bus, but we got there in a reasonable time at a fair price.
If you MUST go on a bus, PLEASE, I implore you in the name of all that is holy, pick another company. For your sanity. For the safety of your travelling companions. Hell, even for the poor pigeons that come into kicking range!
Based on my observations from our mind-numbing wait, the other companies I mentioned above appear to run regularly and according to their schedules, but I wish you well.
If I could give 0 stars, I would.

Have been on the London Bus Tour on a few occasions. We were on this tour on a lovely sunny day this week and enjoyed the information given by our guide, Nobby (language is your history!). He spoke passionately about his city and gave us loads of interesting facts. A real asset to the company.

We recently visited London and through the advice from a well-renowned travel book, we bought tickets for the Big Bus Tours. I'm not sure why this was mentioned as one of the best, maybe if you don't mind waiting an hour for a bus to come by, it would be right up your alley. They have two different types of buses, the red which is live English narrative and the blue buses which are just audio recorded. We got on at Marble Arch and the tour through the city was pretty cool. However, the main draw for the buses is that they state you can get off at all of the historical sites and attractions, take a look around, and then just hop back on another bus. What a joke. We got off at the Tower of London and spent a few hours around there and headed back to the bus pick up stop at 3:30 pm - at 4:45 pm - we finally got on a big bus tour bus. Now let's be clear, it's not like we waited because we only wanted to get on a red bus with the live narrative, it was because no other big bus tour bus stopped by there for an hour. During that time there were multiple, at least 4 or 5, other tour buses that stopped, (Original Tours is one that comes to mind). In that time we could have walked back to our hotel. The fact that they claim the buses come by every 10-15 minutes is a joke. The live narrative was great, but the service is lacking and the proof is that all the other bus tours did have buses that came by every 10-15 minutes - just not Big Bus Tours - and for the price they charge I would go somewhere else.

As a multi-time business traveler I would highly recommend the Big Red Bus as a great way to get a quick tour of the major historical sights of London. They do have several routes but it is a "hop on - hope off" service so your day pass entitles you to hop off and spend a few minutes at a site of interest and the "hop on" the next one coming (about every 15 minutes) so you can continue your tour. Then figure out which spots are your favorites and take "The Tube" back to those the next day.

We wanted to see London and noticed the big bus tours well this was a great way to enjoy London and see most of the sites it does take a bit of your time up and the cruise is well worth it too.The staff are wonderful and very helpful.One thing I would do if I returned to London .Thank you big bus company.

Even though these types of things tend to be overrated, we actually really enjoyed our tour! We had an excellent guide and learned a ton from her. She was very engaging in the way she spoke and really brought history to life. The route we took was great since we got to see all the major sights. At this point we were tired anyway, and it was nice to sit for a while. It was great to have the convenience of hopping on and off. However, I would say you probably won't do hop on and off like you would think, so don't pay for a ticket that gives you extra time to do so. We liked riding the tube everywhere and found it easier than figuring out the bus.

Big Bus was recommend by my brother-in-law. Amazing experience, all the staff were fabulous. Our Guide Julian - what a wonderful character. His talk was so interesting, we stayed on the bus for the whole trip before we decided to start hopping on and off! Would do it all again!

We visited London during the week 1-3 March and bought 4 x adult tickets for the Big Red Bus.

It was great value as we got 48 hours for the price of 24 giving us lots of time to get on and off where we wanted to visit over 2 days. (I think this offer is only on until the end of March so best if you check first)

There are 4 routes (all coloured) and the map provided shows clearly the attractions it covers, where the bus stops are etc.You get earphones to listen to an electronic guide if there is no live commentary on the bus. You can also get a poncho if its raining.

On our last journey we had a live guide, his name was Steve Lovell and he was great. Steve pointed out places of interest, not on the map and was very informative about these. It made the journey more enjoyable.

As this was the last route of the day for the bus, Steve not only told everyone what the last few stops involved but he also took the time to go around all the people on the bus to ensure that they knew where to get off and how to get ongoing connections with tubes, trains and other buses etc. This is a guy who knows London and Is happy to help customers. He also had good banter with the driver who was happy to accommodate the customers also. We terminated at Picadilly and took in a few more landmarks while walking up to Shaftsbury Avenue and onto Soho etc.

Great value for money and would definitely recommend.

The tour routes are well planned out to allow you to see all of London's best sites. But one of the best bits is the staff and the service they provide. At each bus stop there is a member of staff there to look after you and advise you on what the next stop is.

On my tour, the driver was Richard and tour guide was Phil. And I must say Phil was fantastic. For every single passenger to board the bus and make their way to the upstairs deck, he greeted them with a friendly smile and asked where they were from. He kept this info in mind when a building or attraction had a relation to the passenger's nationality, always saying "For my German/Spanish/Scottish/etc friends, on the left ....", which made the tour feel a bit more personal. Plus he is clearly very knowledgeable on London's history as he could tell the story of the city throughout the route. Phil is definitely an asset to Big Bus Tours.

We used Big Bus Tours as our mode of transport when in London for three days. We bought the 2-day ticket and got the 3rd day free - excellent value.

The buses usually have audio commentary but we were lucky enough to have a young guy on board on the Sunday to do the commentary. He was funny, knowledgeable and helpful.

We seen most of central London on these buses, getting us to our preferred destinations with ease. We used both the eastbound and westbound buses which covered all the major attractions.The buses are comfortable but getting an upstairs seat under cover is like hen's teeth!

Unfortunately these buses do not run in the evenings but I have to mention one incident which went above and beyond. We were on the last bus of the day which dropped us at Marble Arch about 5pm. We needed to get back to Victoria Station in a hurry so we decided to get a taxi. However, when the bus driver realised this he offered to drive us to Victoria Station, past his clock-off time, free of charge! We were overwhelmed by this! So, thank you so much!

I'd totally recommend this company of seeing everything you need to see in London.

Booked at Victoria Station, took the 2 day pass hop on/ hop off (not much more than the 1 day) plus 1 attraction visit (M Taussauds), worked out much cheaper & fast entry tickets. You also get a free river cruise & a Harry Potter walking tour.
Buses were clean, Tour Guide excellent, takes in all the sights.

I was in London for the first time on a business trip and was lucky enough to get a sight seeing day in and decided to take a Big Bus Tour even though it was cold and rainy. In the end I was so glad I did! Steve was informative and funny. He held my attention and made me forget about the weather. He said lots of interesting facts and even took pictures of me in front of Big Ben and The Tower Bridge. Great tour guide and a great experience! Would recommend because it was fun and a great value too!

This is the way to go for a complete guided tour around London. I've done this several times but I actually enjoyed it this time with my cousin and we had a ball. I would definitely recommend doing the Big Bus tour for a inexpensive way to tour the entire city in one shot. U have the red, blue and green line which takes you to every corner of London.
Very informative tour all around the sights of London. Def recommend getting a seat at the top, ideally in the front too. This bus tour saved my feet from a lot of pain!

I visited the city of London in April 2015 during the Easter Holidays. We pre-booked the bus tour after friends recommended it. This was one of the highlights of the visit. It is a great way to see this beautiful city if you have a limited stay. we saw westminister abbey, big ben, hyde park, st.Paus cathedral to name a few. This is a great option if you have young kids as it reduces the amount of walking needed to be done. The only bad part of this was we got caught in traffic multiple times on a very hot day but of course that is understandable

The best thing we did was book this tour. Big Bus were brilliant from start to finish. Two days for the price of one, fantastic value including a walking tour from Trafalgar Square to Buckingham Palace, Fast track London Eye and City Cruise up the Thames to Greenwich, all this plus unlimited hop on / hop off at all major places of interest. Special mention for the guides, Leo on the walking tour, Steve Lovell on the bus and the guide on the cruise whose name I didn't get. All very informative, humorous and made the tour. I would highly recommend Big Bus to anyone.

we ended up buying a Hop on Hop off (HOHO) instead of an oyster card and certainly had some issues with it. We had a hard time figuring out where the stops were to get picked up..and the first day in London by the time we went on the London eye and took the River cruise for 30 minutes once we got to the HOHO bus and actually found the stop for it cause again it is not clear where the stops are, we ended up only getting to do a small fraction of a tour because the bus only runs till 430 thats it !! we were not the only tourists who had that experience of getting on the HOHO around 4 PM to be told the bus would be stopping for the day.....on the second day on our trip back through London we tried the HoHo again and noticed we waited a long time between stops. One time we were at the wrong stop again but one of the drivers of the HoHo bus pulled over and picked us up out of mercy in the rain. WE liked this HoHO bus cause there was a nice older man doing live explanations. but in order to do the second part of the tour we had to change to another bus which ran longer so we got to see quite a bit of the city where it was just earphones. I made it clear several times to this driver and assistant we wanted off at Westminster abby but by the time the ear phones said that the bus had made the stop for that location the bus had already passed the stop and we did not know where to get off. we had to go a long ways and walk all the way back ...we were not impressed cause we are older and had sore feet and driver was very unapologetic ....on the previous HOHO the driver made sure everyone knew what the stop off but not on this one... In order to use this service you must arrive in the city early enough to take the time to figure out and use the HoHO and be able to see the whole tour. Try to get on one with the live commentary that was the best. They did provide rain jackets to sit up top which was a nice touch ...sometimes the ear phones were off sync

This tour felt very rushed. Our tour guide started to talk about the historic landmarks while the bus was driving but it felt rush. Like look to the left now look to the right. The bus was driving to fast to get all the facts in. Once we stopped to see certain major landmarks he explains the historic background. But once he's done he's like straight to the bus. Doesn't even say take 2-3 min for people to take pics. He did that for every landmarks so we decided to take pics while he was talking. I suggest to try to find another tour for London.

We have been on the Bus Tours before but always used them to 'hop on and hop off'. This time we stayed on to really take in the sights. I cannot recommend this enough. Having Merlin Passes we were able to get tickets at a reduced rate. Our guide Garrath was very knowledgeable and gave us some very interesting historical facts. He took time to answer passenger queries and remembered where they wanted to get off for particular landmarks. The driver (Anwa?) was excellent and I have great respect for anyone who drives so well in London.

We would like to share our extraordinary experience in London with BIG BUS Tours LONDON. We embarked on the Red line bus at stop #1 and were cheerfully greeted by Leo, who was supposed to be our guide during the tour. Ok, we’ve been traveling in Europe extensively with the kids and usually we take the hop on/hop off buses on a regular basis in an effort to get the best of the city we are visiting. Our London experience was BY FAR the best and most enjoyable experience so far both in Europe and worldwide.

Let me tell you something, this guy Leo is totally in love with London and knows a great deal of things and curious facts about historical and modern sights we’ve been driving by. Mind you, that was his THIRD tour of the day and normally you would expect that person to be tired and bored, but that was not the case with Leo. He was very engaged, knowledgeable, and was making tons of jokes cheering everyone on the bus up. Leo was literally greeting every single passenger entering the bus and saying good by to people leaving the bus, notifying everyone about next station and about curious things one might explore on that particular sight. In addition, Leo was encouraging everyone on the bus to ask questions, if any, and was happy to come up with an answer right away. All in all, an awesome trip provided by Big Bus Tours in London with Leo! If you happen to be around and in a mood for a ride, do take the red line bus operated by BIG BUS LONDON and enjoy it! And Leo, keep up the great job you are doing and all the best to you! Nicolaescu family :)

We had a great time in London, and a lot was due to Big Bus Tours. The buses hit all the main locations throughout London. The guides were great - Ricky was our favorite. He was very knowledgeable. The free walking tours they offer were also fantastic. Kevin was our walking tour guide and he was fantastic as well.
Thanks for making our trip memorable.
The Flemings

Excellent tour. We came to London February 2017 and we had a very good experience with Big Bus tour. Highly recommend to anyone visiting London, Mr. Garrett who was an Excellent tour guide gave us good advice on many places to visit.

A fantastic trip round London today on Big Bus Tours. The tours were all on time, the gentlemen directing the tours were brilliant and the busses were clean and comfortable. My main positive though, My young daughter managed to leave her favourite bag on one of the busses, a quick phone call and an incredibly kind and helpful lady called Sharon managed to locate the bus with her bag and left it at our next stop to collect. Thankyou so very very much, you saved the day and made a 5yr old very happy. A really lovely day out for a family and a very memorable first trip to London for 3 young children! Thankyou
Decided to take the night bus for a tour of London in December. It was well worth it as the festive lights made the whole place look beautiful and added to the festive atmosphere.

I wanted to use a Christmas trip to London to show my children some of the main sights of London which they hadn't seen in previous trips.
The guides talk was dull and there were no interesting anecdotes to catch the children's interest. We didn't even complete our tour it was that poor.
I bus tours did respond d to a complaint I made and I received a refund for some of my outlay

Only had few hours in London so we took the Big Bus Tour right outside the train station. It was easy and hop on and off. The red line had a great fun guide that explained the sites and all the shopping area. If you only have a day or two in a major touristy city, hop on off is the way to go

I had a decent time with the big bus tours and saw most of the sites I wanted to see but I feel like it was too long and by cutting out the side streets and high traffic zones they could make it more compact, cheaper and better for the environment with less idle time

I really want to give this 4 stars. Just for the (mostly) great drivers and tour guides we encountered while on our 24 hr (plus 24) trip, but I can't. It wasn't their fault that the day we booked for the tour was the day the tube actually went on strike. Traffic was a mess. It started off fine (even with the traffic). It was a rainy day and we enjoyed the morning with a redline tour guide who pushed that we really should take the thames river tour back if we can (because traffic). We took his suggestion after spending time at Tower of London. He was right, the boat ride was def the way to go. Then it just went downhill the rest of the day with them. After spending time in parliament square, we needed to take the blue line to get to Kensington. We had reservations at The Orangery and gave us an hour and 15 min to get there (we couldve walked it about 30 min), but we had tickets for the bus, so why not wait. Big mistake. After 2 red lines and no more buses at all for an hour (i know, we shouldn't have waited that long), we came to the realization that the blue line was not coming and we'd miss our reservation. While waiting in the rain and about to give up, 3rd red line comes (where the heck is the blue line?!?). We are told the blue line is stuck in traffic and we hop on the red line because we can't wait any longer in the rain. I should say while waiting in the rain for an hour, The Original Tour Bus of all lines have no shortage of coming by us. There's nothing more frustrating than waiting for a bus that will never come and see another company's buses come so frequently. Again, sure it was a horrible day to catch the Big Bus ("sorry, the tube strike!"), but that just put a damper on our day. The next day, I just hoped the one trip we needed to go on went as planned. All I needed was for the green line to serve its purpose, and thankfully it did.

It was my first time in London and I visited with my mum. I was really excited to finally visit London! We arrived at St Pancras international and immediately got two tickets for the Big Bus Tour.
We had to wait a long time before the bus arrived at the stop, this was one of the less frequent routes, but still, waiting in the cold for a half an hour wasn't really fun... We finally got on, went up the steps and sat in the cold (voluntarily) to get a nicer view. They gave us earphones, unfortunately there wasn't a live guide on this route, so the earphones were quite uncomfortable but still nice to know all about the city!
We switched routes near Big Ben and got on an other, bigger route afterwards.

PS: The Buckingham Palace stop was next to the actual Buckingham Palace, so the people who stay on the bus don't get to see the front...

In the end, we enjoyed the tours and both thought it was well worth the price!

We used this tour recently to see a bit more as we wandered around London. Good value tour, allows hop on/off all around the Capital.
The downside came in late afternoon as we tried to get back to Marylebone. It seems that even though tours are being sold, as the last 'tour' approaches, the company finish drivers shifts at the expense of the customers who are left in the cold & rain for a bus with space in order to complete their trip. And in winter, when the bus is rammed, you can't see anything anyway, so the commentary is a bit superfluous.

It is convenient to take a city tour for a day with free river Thames cruise for 24 hours. It is a great way to see the city at a glance. Once I did the hop in, hop off ride in my own pace, I was able to appreciate the beauty, the history, and the culture of the city.

This was a wonderful bus tour with excellent staff driver and on board staff
My only problem was the extra tickets I bought from the street seller for the bus company to see attractions like Madame tausauds and London eye
When you reach the London eye the queue can be long but you need to queue in a separate queue to exchange what I thought were my entry tickets for new entry tickets and these queues are very big on peak times
My advice is buy your ticket at the attraction if you feel the queue isn't too long for you. Do not pre purchase as you may not use it as was our case
These queues are not the fault of the bus tour people as it was a busy period but the illusion when you purchase is you gave a ticket to enter

Big Steve was our conductor today on the bus tour and he was fantastic. He chatted away, answered all our questions, gave us insightful tips and recommendations and had us laughing for a lot of the journey. Really impressed and enjoyed the tour

It was my first time in London and wasn't really familiar with where everything was in the city so I booked the bus tour. You get unlimited hop on hop off access all day with commentary telling you what everything was. Took the first loop around sitting on the upper deck just taking pictures and learning about some of the sights and attractions. Then took a 2nd loop around getting on and off at some of the attractions. Used it all day and I highly recommend it!

Good way to see things quickly without walking too much while still being able to hop on and off the bus
Not many buses
Some irrelevant too short commentary depending on the guide
Too cold for December outside and too crowded inside
Not so many blue lines

Very disappointed, we had hoped to be able to sit on the one bus and experience the whole tour. Only 5 minutes into the tour we were asked to change buses onto a packed bus where we could not get a good view. It was not easy to get to the locations we specifically wanted to see and we were often left waiting at out of the way stops for other buses or passengers. Consequently we missed many of the sights we wanted to see as we ran out of time. The commentary was good in most places although in others it was not relevant, specifically on the approach to Tower Bridge. My son specifically asked me to mention the music as it was very repetitive! We had hoped it would be a relaxing easy way to experience London and it was quite the opposite and definitely not worth the 90 pounds we paid for 3 of us.

In a warm and humid fall day we decided to go for the big bus tour around the London worthseeing museums. palaces. castles. bridges medieval but not only places.
Buses were running smoothly from bus station to bus station along Thames banks crossing bridges and giving you the opportunity to hop on / hop off at convinient stations along the bus route to visit nearby monuments, spectacular views. cafes.
Depending on how quickly you move the tour can take from a couple of hours to a whole morning and even more.
It is an experience no one should miss

Compared to their reputation and recommendation by Rick Steves, we were markedly disappointed by Big Bus. The main, narrated Big Bus line (red) had intervals of about a half-hour between buses. The street attendants were unwilling or unable to tell us how long it would be until the next bus, beyond a meaningless "soon". Each time we waited, a number of the competing bus lines passed through. We also became jealous of the other lines' WiFi service, which is not provided by Big Bus. We did much better the latter part of our trip putting them money on Oyster cards and use Transport for London (double-decker buses and Underground).

On the positive side, the live narrators were excellent, providing wit and knowledge about the areas as we drove through them.

Had a wonderful day on the bus. Nobby the tour guide was really entertaining and interesting with facts and stories as we drove through london. Lived in london for 2 years and found out things i had never known before from nobby the tour guide.

Normally I love hop on hop off buses, but this one was a disaster!
There was a live guide onboard with us, but he made it a one man show only for him!
Hardly any sights were to be seen as they took roads were none were to be seen.
Also they kept driving the same circle coming from different sides. We saw the same building numerous times, with different explanations !!! Do they think their passengers are crazy?
The guide told so much nonsense and for this they charged us £81 for three days! After an hour of this, all we wanted was to get off the bus!!!

Having not been to London as a tourist for many years, and having only a few days to see the sights, a tour bus seemed the best way of fitting everything in during the available time.

I much prefer tours with live tour guides as opposed to pre-recorded commentaries, so when I saw that Big Bus Tour's "red route" had a "guaranteed live guide on every bus or your money back" I decided it was just what I was looking for. The tour covered all the key landmarks and so meant we could see everything and "hop off and hop on" at the places of particular interest to see a bit more.

Having purchased our tickets we headed down to the nearest stop. As we did so, a "blue route" bus drove past. No problem, we didn't want the blue route. We wanted the red route with the live commentary. We waited a while and along came another bus - bad news, this was "blue route" too. When the next bus came along and this was "blue route" too I began to get the picture - it's all very well having a "guaranteed live guide", but it's completely worthless as Big Bus Tours seems to just label all the busses without live guides (ie most of them) as "blue route".

Deciding that seeing the sights with a pre-recorded commentary was better than nothing (having paid over £60 for two tickets!) we reluctantly got on the bus. When we plugged the headphones in expecting commentary though, all we heard was music. We checked the channel to see if we'd made a mistake, but we hadn't.

For the next fifteen minutes or so we were driven round central London past many important sights listening to Pomp & Circumstance, Greensleeves etc. I think during the whole time perhaps four sentences were spoken on the commentary, two of which were to tell us which stop number we were at. Perhaps not surprisingly the bus was almost empty, although when one other couple got on they also thought there was something wrong with the audio commentary.

Eventually, annoyed and feeling ripped off, we decided to give up. We disembarked and, as we stood there trying to re-plan our day, watched as more "blue route" busses arrived. Then, just as we were about to leave, a bus rolled in that was absolutely packed. A "red route" bus! So they did exist! We rushed towards the bus, as did a number of other people who had been standing around at the stop. Fortunately we were able to get one of the few remaining seats.

To be fair, that bus did have a live guide and his commentary was reasonably good. The experience was significantly diminished for us though because having seen how rare the "red route" busses were and how poor the "blue route" busses were we decided not to get off the bus at various points as we had planned but instead to stay on for the majority of the tour and just to skip the rest of it. We therefore missed out on various things that we'd planned for our day. During the rest of our time in London, I never did see another "red route" bus.

Overall I was left with a very poor impression of Big Bus Tours (one which wasn't helped by the fact that when I'd originally tried to book tickets online a fault on the company's website had led to my credit card being charged but no tickets being issued, an issue compounded when my call to their helpline went unanswered). I certainly won't be taking any more of their tours on my future travels. Fortunately however it was one poor experience on an otherwise very enjoyable holiday.

Easily accessible, knowledgeable English speaking tour guides, great way to quickly see London. They also offer discounts to several attractions. We booked the tour that included a Thames River Cruise. Worth the extra $. We loved the flexibility to hop off and stay longer at the places that appealed to us.

We thought Big Bus would be a great way to see the city. However traffic is so bad in London one is better off walking. A couple times we got off the bus to walk sections where traffic was dense and we knew we'd get trapped if we stayed on the bus.
Add to that that the bus waited at each stop while th
We've used Big Bus tours in other cities so we aren't biased against these bus tours. But this tour did its best to make the ride slower. The bus (which is supposed to be followed at a stop by another Big Bus every 10-20 minutes, stopped and waited while streetside vendors filled out the paperwork and payment for new riders. Add those delays to bad London traffic and the tour ended up being almost not worth it. I would not take friends on this company's tour.

Not really good idea to do this in winter time as the bus are open and can be very cold.

Not really see point to do this as you could go to center London take a bus and you will be see the same things which you would see on the London Bus Tour without all information which you can hear on the headphones.

However it could be a some idea for spending time out but only in summer.

We got on the bus and were happily surprised with live commentary instead of a boring recording. Our tourguide Kevin and his bus driver Everton made it sich a fun trip that we didn't want to get off. It was engaging, entertaining and tailored to the crowd on the bus. The halfway stop also conveniently stops at the Tower of London where we had a tour and then you take the boat back along the Thames at no extra charge with your big bus ticket. That's also such a special ride back. We dis note that later in the day mear emd time the other bus we got on that tourguide was quite tired and gave a basic version of the trip. They do also give trips back to certain hotels if you ask later in the evening.

Highly recommend, we got the 48 hour ticket which includes the river cruise.
We bought this tour to do with friends visiting us in London. As non tourists I loved this tour. The bus routes are great, I saw more of London in one day than I have in my 5 years here.
The river cruise is great such relaxing way to spend a few hours.
We went in November so had to wrap up against the chill but with a hot drink and a warm coat this tour is really made for sitting upstairs on the bus taking in all the sights.
Perfect way to see as much of London in two days.

We went on the Big Bus tour in London last weekend. Great thing to do when you want to explore the city, but have a limited amount of time. Overall, great tour and festive guides.
We wanted to go on the mystery tour around London by foot. Sadly, we were only 2 so the guide didn't want to do that tour. He offered us to take a walk around with him and get a personal guiding tour, because he felt sorry for us. The tour was AMAZING, he was truly great and we had a really fun walk around London. We got to see places we wouldn't have seen without his London-expertise. Big Steve, you were the greatest guide ever and the customer service you delivered was top notch. Thank you!

Thanks to Patrick (and our driver) for an awesome tour. Patrick was funny while being incredibly knowledgeable about the history of London. He even had a range of Harry Potter facts for our daughter. We were sceptical of doing a bus tour but we were pleasantly surprised ... not a recorded tour which made it it that much more interesting and feel tailor made to us as we could ask questions. Well done A++++. Remember... ask for Patrick :)

Two of the four guides we we were with during our live-guided (red tour) hop-on hop-off experience were not only knowledgeable but also witty and hilarious. The third guide was very informative but didn't add the touch of humor that was so impressive with the first two.
