The fourth guide did share good information but she had a strong accent that made her a bit hard to understand, and she lacked enthusiasm. The commentary on our four bus rides was nearly continuous.

We also did the City Cruises boat ride from the Tower of London to the Westminster stop. That guide was also informative and witty.

The Big Bus Tour is an excellent way to not only learn about London but also to get convenient transportation to several sites of interest. Just make sure you are aware of the "last run of the day" times. We were somewhat surprised that the buses appeared to stop running at 16:30 (winter season) rather than having their "last departure time" at 16:30. Luckily we were already on the bus during the last run (twice) so it worked out OK but if we had been looking for a ride half an hour later in the day we would have been out of luck. All in all I would definitely do the Big Bus Tour in any of the cities where it's offered.

I experienced both the live English commentary (the quality and humor of which varied by the commentator - but all generally fun and knowledgeable) and the pre-recorded commentary (informative but less rib-tickling). Great to be able to hop off the bus and walk around a monument of interest. Included a boat trip, which I did and which provided a different perspective on London. Only problem is later in the day traffic can cause bus trips to be quite lengthy.

We can recommend this hop on hop off day tour if you want to see the best of London without spending time commuting. You just sit down, put on the earbuds and relax and the guide gives you lots of interesting facts, mostly historical. We hopped off at Trafalgar Square and joined the Harry Potter guided walk which was included in the pass. The walk was a great one and the guide, Tom, was a great guide.

One thing we reflected on was the prerecorded guide on the bus. Maybe it could've been a little more updated. Though it's interesting with facts about where the Beatles used to live it would be cool to have some fun facts from celebs later than the 60's - 70's.

But all in all a great day on the bus.

We were tired when we arrive but eager to get out. The Big Bus tour is a great place to start to get a feel for the City. Guides were informative and witty, as it helped us plan thereafter the places we wanted to go.

After walking around for 2 1/2 days we needed a rest, what better way than on top of a bus. Had used Big Bus whilst in Paris the day before so decided to go with them instead of the traditional "red buses". The commentary is very good, although dependent on the traffic it can be too far ahead.

Diversions are in place near Tower Bridge so not a lot to see while diverting.

We caught the bus in the afternoon, hoping to see things and end up in Covent Garden for dinner time. Unfortunately we got half way and were told that the bus didn't go any further and to change buses. All good except the buses had finished for the day and we were left stranded on the other side of town. I realise that everyone has an opening and closing time, but London doesn't sleep at 5pm! I think the tours could easily go for longer in winter, there would still be plenty of custom.

That said we again used the service (buy 1 day and get another day free) the following day, however had a similar issue in the afternoon when buses did not arrive to collect people from The Tower of London. I will say that the "live" commentary provided on this service in the afternoon was excellent however, the guy knew is stuff and his jokes.

That said - a great way to get around London and see everything while deciding what you want to see and where to get off.
Good bus tour. We had the pleasure of having Grace on board, she was very funny and gave us the information about London in a very good and fun manner.

Used another of these tours in Bath a month earlier and was sorely disappointed, we were however recommended these guys by friends so took the plunge yet again. Didn't expect much after the disappointment of Bath, but this was a different company, city, and story. Great value it must be said, got 3 days for the price of 2 plus 10% off for booking online (just do it). 3 extensive routes covering just about everything London has to see, the hop on hop off scheme ensures you miss nothing and dont wait around ro long for another bus, use this instead of the Tube, you dont see much underground after all !! Guides ranging from the sublime to ridiculous, but mostly entertaining, this was a great way of seeing London during our 3 day stay. Great value too !

Excellent way to get around London. Got on at Victoria and did the blue tour which is recorded included Harrods etc. Hopped off at Oxford St and walked to see the lights.

Had an extra 24 hours free through online booking and next day did the red tour up the Thames and parts of London I hadn't seen like fleet street. Excellent live commentary. Helpful service. Clean buses and frequent service.

In all we probably travelled for 4 hours over the two days. Good value as we didn't use the tube etc at all.

Worst hop on/hop off experience I've ever had! It took more than an hour to go from stop 7 to 12. We waited more than 30 minutes before a Big Bus came to the stop we were waiting at. Plus, it wasn't even the Bus we wanted (there are 2 routes, a blue and red route). We wanted the blue route and when we called the help center to see how much longer the wait was, she said it would be 20-25 minutes. That's an hour waiting at a bus stop. We could have walked! We wasted so much time waiting for a bus. We were forced to take the red route because we didn't want to wait any longer and waste the rest of our evening. Plus, the last full tour is at 430PM. I've done Big Bus in Paris, Singapore and SAN Francisco and they were fine. I don't recommend the London tour. Do the Original London tour or another hop on/ hop off. I've done the Original London Tour and do not remember having to waiting more than 20 minutes. Plus, they had more routes. I also payed less for that hop on/hop off. The guides were also much more helpful.

We enjoyed a family visit to London and booked The Big Bus Tour!
Our commentator for a good part of the journey was Kevin. What a great experience! He is a gem and made our journey delightful with his vast amount of information delivered with a good sprinkling of humor! We need more Kevins!

Hi folks. On Saturday 26th November, I spent the day in London. I went on the Big Bus Tours (red route) around the City. I saw all the sights, and jumped off at Tower of London for a few hours. Then hopped back on the bus to Green Park where I started. It's given me the chance to see places I would like to visit in the future, like the National Gallery. The weather was bright but cold, that didn't stop me sitting on the top deck in the open. The guide on the first leg of my journey, Green Park to Tower of a London, was Leo. If I hadn't bought my ticket to the Tower in advance, I would have stayed on until Green Park and listened to all the commentary, because Leo was so knowledgeable and funny. I learnt so much and loved his little stories. Well done Leo, I am a big fan.

First of all, we were overcharged--$177 for 2 adults, 2 seniors, and one child. The guide sat at the top where there are maybe a dozen seats under roof and it was raining. No one downstairs could hear the guide. We saw NO major landmarks like Big Ben. The guide talked almost totally about places to shop. When we got to Tower Hill, he suggested we get off because nothing else was "interesting" on the tour. The Tower Hill tubes were closed and we had to figure out how to get a bus back. This was the "low point" of our week in London.

We took a tour with Big Bus Tours in London on 11-20-16 and were excited about it. We paid for the 24 hour tour but after about 40 minutes we got off because the tour guide was so difficult to understand and unenthused about what she was doing that it spoiled the tour. It felt like a very expensive public transport bus ride and it was cold at that up on the second level. We tried to moving to the lower level to get warm only to find we were unable to hear the guide. I don't know if she was having a bad day or if she always acts this way but we did not want to get back on and we didn't. We didn't get to take the Thames River bonus cruise because my husband forgot the tickets the next day. I realize missing the cruise was our fault but all in all very disappointing.

We have used Big Bus Tours previously in Paris and thought it was great. We were not disappointed with the London bus. Booked in advance for a one day pass with an extra 24 hours free which we made use of, and also included a short cruise on the Thames. The guides on the bus were very informative and amusing and the same for the young male guide on the River Cruise. We caught the bus from outside the Tower of London and did as many of the London landmarks as possible, hopping on and off at Trafalgar Square, Covent Garden, Westminster etc. The buses ran frequently and we were always able to get a seat upstairs. The River Cruise is also fun and you can travel both ways if you wish, with refreshments and toilets on board. A really good way to see and hear about London and so much better than catching the tube!

I am from England and love London but wanted to see it's sights .The big bus tour price was reasonable for the prices of other companies of bus tours .We went on open tour was great and tour guide was informative and friendly .Bus kept stopping in traffic a lot which was annoying .There is two different routes I'm aware of Red and blue it we went on red but we had to wait a while for the right bus .The river tour was great slight wait for the boat and it was great and the sights the photography factor was outstanding and their is a stop right near Westminster tube station .Well worth and a different way to see London

The tour was very good on the first day but the bus kept taking different diversions which was very irritating. You got to see lots of London which was very good but it kept repeating itself. You had to get off at different places but it was not clear where or what bus route to get. It was also very hard to find a big bus tour bus stop.

Easy to find..with staff waiting at each stop. Even got an extra 24 hours added to my 48 hour ticket. Only used a couple times, but when back in London will definately buy another ticket. The live commentary was excellent...one guy was really funny..i wish I didn't have to 'hop off' so soon!

This was a great day out and a great way to see London, very pleased we did this, you can hop off and hop back on anytime throughout the day and so it's a nice easy way to see so much, it also includes a boat ride down the river Thames if you wish to do that as well, highly recommended and was a great day spent.

This is the perfect hop-on hop-off tour! Many convenient pick-up areas, interesting informative narative while traveling and an open top bus for the best London experience! We loved the extras- the walking tours and the river cruise make our experience even better.

Visited in November. One of the most popular buses, so its easy to find almost anywhere you go. Right outside each stop, there is a Big Bus Employee there to print your ticket when you first arrive. I had my email ticket from booking in advance, but I am sure you can buy one on the spot too. We arrived in London Stansted and then took the Stansted Express into London Liverpool, I had already scoped the Big Bus map before hand. So we walked from the station to the London Bridge and the Tower of London. On the opposite side of the tower, you can board the city cruise for the boat tour on the river. That was great too, the guide was informative and funny. We took it all the way to the Westminster Bridge and then continued on with the touring. You will get a free map and the red tours they will talk about the history and sites as you drive by. They will also let you what number stop you approach. In the winter time, the bus only goes until 1600 or 1630..not sure the exact time, but it does say it on the map/brochure. The stop for the big bus by the tower of London is on the road and to the right. There should be a sign that directs you to the buses.

I bought the ticket with Big Bus Tour through my travel agency. On the first day I came to London, I didn't know so my husband and I got on board a wrong bus (with a different company). The driver and the tour lady was very nice and showed us how to get on the right one. However, when we got on Big Bus Tour, we all encountered low level of customer service. On the map, it shows this bus tour takes travelers to most destinations around London. However, on the reality, we could not go to the points we wanted to. For example, we wanted to visit Tower Bridge but the buses never went there. We wasted the whole afternoon but could not go any further, then we had to go back to hotel because it was dark (we started at noon time, and it usually takes 30 minutes maximum to get there; and it took us less than 10 minutes by taxi). There were two other girls on the bus got upset with the bus; they frustratedly said that they had passed the same points/area for 4 times but could not get to the destination they wanted because the bus never went there. One day we went to the British Museum, on the way back we could not get on any Big Bus Tour bus. We finally had to take a taxi back to the hotel. Many other tours have more buses going around, only Big Bus Tour had limited.

We used the big bus tours in three cities on our vacation. It was very easy to hop on and off, the buses are clean and the customer service is excellent. Save your receipt from one city and use it for a discount on your next vacation.

If you looking for Hop on hop off Big Bus Tour, you must try the original one in London.

They have lots of buses on the move compared to other competitors. Buy from their website directly will get one day free so it is a very good deal compared to others. I did lots of comparison so I believe this is the best deal.

They have green, red and blue lines. Each line covers different routes and attractions , due to it might need to change to other line which need to go through all the stops, it is advisable to plan your destinations so that you can where to hop on hop off.

It is good to join the original tour with live guide rather than audio help as it is always better to have a live person to talk and using audio the earphone might fall from ear time to time which is inconvenient.

You will save a lot of walking and you can maximize your value if you select some combo deal . For e.g. with cruise and etc. You can skip the line because there is always a fast track counter for Big Bus Tour customers.

The Hop on hop off bus is the best way to see any city - London is no exception! The stops are in good spots so you don't have to walk too far between and the buses come often enough that you don't have to wait too long. There is a commentary if you want to listen to it expailning the points of interest. They provide rain coats too

We bought advance tickets from online for the Big Bus Tour. Alas, our train run very late and we arrived to London two hours later than expected and to a different railway station (Waterloo while we had planned on arriving at Paddington). The bus stop was difficult to find and some of the staff was quite unpleasant. Naturally, our planned route didn't work because we were in completely wrong side of the city. Well, the tour guide on the red bus was nice as was the recorded audio. On the afternoon, the traffic was awfully slow.

I don't know why, but I expected that 24 hour tour would run a bit later than 17:00. We were at the natural history museum when we noticed that the last round left at 5 p.m. Somehow I had missed the small print stating this fact. We were only able to ride 3/4 of one route during our day (which was partly due to our train's late arrival) and we got very little for our money. I would definitely recommend investing your money on a guide book and using the underground and local buses instead.

Another minus is the web-page. It was very difficult for me to find the information I was looking for from the internet site (e.g. when does the last tour for the day leave) and where exactly are the bus stops.

We had a a couple of different experiences utilizing the big bus tours. The first day we went on the blue route with recorded audio. It was a disappointing experience with a driver who was at many times scary( driving up onto the pavement/ zooming when other cars were in the way then crawling when there was little traffic). The second day we went on the red route which has a live commentary guide. Our guide Karl was amazing. He was lively and energetic. He made it worth using the big bus tours. We also had a great experience with another guide later that same day.

Just don't bother. For £32 (€38) EACH it was a waste of money. Their staff in Victoria Station was almost bullying. We were told it includes a cruise even though we explained we had already booked a cruise on our London Eye ticket. The guide was rubbish, everything was behind the building, just in the distance or close by or normally we can see it but not today. As someone who works as a bus tour guide this fell way short of any mark. One star is one too many

We enjoyed this and actually while it may seem expensive it is fine as you pay for 24 hours and get 24 free. We used it over the two days hopping on and off as needed. Was great as we are not Londoners and it took a day or two to get the hang of the tube. So the bus was idea. There are two types of tours, one with recording and one with a live guide. Can I mention the Irish girl who was doing the commentary on one of the busses, great fun and very informative. Would love to go back and do it all again.

The live xommentaring with a real person is great
Joanne was our tour guide she gave history with comedy and charm she was so amazing . She made me fall in love with city of London . She didnt miss a beat . Mext time in london do a Big Bus Tour guarantee will change the way you see london and go on top for an amazing view. They have wifi.

Went with a friend and saw London as never.before. The hop on hop off option was great for shopping. The guys so helpful and were full of info. Even about stuff not relating to their company. One small complaint no mentioned of the Cenotaph even as we drove passed it. Mentioned the Beatles several times!!! Guess the quality of the tour info is dependant on the interests of the guy on the mike.

Our guide was fantastic. I am sorry we didn't take her name but she was great. Very knowledgable and made it fun for all ages.

The driver was great and all the Big Bus staff were very amenable.

I felt confident from the time boarded the bus at Green Park that we would have a great guide.

We used the red route which was an English speaking tour. Our guide was very patient and explained frequently for newcomers that they could get a blue route bus if they wanted to use earphones for commentary in a different language.

Clear instructions on stop off points and where to go for the best restaurants, shops etc.

Although we only used our 2 day tickets once and were on the bus for about 2 hours it was well worth it.

The best way to show our daughters all the best loved sights and landmarks without all the legwork. It was their first time to London and they really enjoyed the bus tour. Would definitely recommend.

Top tip - take eats and drinks for little ones to keep them going if on the bus a while.

My wife and I rode the Big Bus many years ago so when my daughter and my sister-in-law wanted a hop on/hop off bus for their short any in London, I pointed them to the Big Bus. Yes, I read many TripAdvisor reviews but didn't put much weight on the negative ones. I should have! A recurring theme in the negative reviews was unexpected wait times at stops coupled with inattentive Big Bus employees. How about a 75 minute wait at one stop with no updates from the ticket seller. When my daughter inquired as to the problem, she was informed that a demonstration is some kind caused buses to change routes. It was suggested that they walk to another stop. Advice taken and then they endured another hour before giving up on the Big Bus. They washed 27 pounds each down the drain? Something is desperately wrong with this organization yet as the largest and most well known bus tour, it continues to earn undeserved revenue. Be careful and heed the critics.

Did the hop on hop off bus tour of London while there for Redskins-Bengals football game. Was interesting and gave a good overview of things to see and do in London. Also included boat ride on Thames River. Very enjoyable. Would do again.

When on the tour bus with my .family and have to say what a great day .London is a lovely place we are so lucky to have this on are doorstep.and to make it more of a great day was are tour guide big Steve he was very entertaining.

I did this tour on my first visit to London to acquaint myself with the area first and then every few years to do the same. It's never dull and I enjoy getting on, then back on when I need to. Try to linger where you're at during rush hour or you may be stuck for awhile in traffic. Otherwise, there's no real cons to this. Don't like the crowded feeling on the bus, go for a Private Black taxi tour of London. I love them both for getting to know London even though I spend my time here every year. I like the fact that I can buy my ticket on-line and have it for when I arrive. No hassle.

We thought it would be a good idea to try one of these bus trips to see the sights. Jumped on at Kings Cross and alighted at Covent Garden for a client meeting. We had lunch by St Pauls and waited for a bus. And waited, and waited. Finally a bus came which was full so we had to wait again, and wait again. When the next bus arrived, there were only seats available downstairs which was totally pointless. Saw absolutely nothing.
We were now so late due to traffic and queuing that we had to jump off the bus near Big Ben and flag a taxi down to get us to Kings Cross. This cost £22 which added to the bus charge of £50 was a very expensive visit to London. If you are tempted to take a tour, make sure you have the time to get around.

I was in London with my husband who was on a business trip. I had an entire day alone as he was on a business meeting so I decided to take the Big Bus Tour. It seemed a wee bit more than the Classic Tour or the City Tour, but the reviews were better. It was nice but as the day wore on the hop on hop off had me and a couple women waiting 20 minutes at one particular stop. We started doubting the bus would ever come. Several other tour companies passed us( one tour had 3 buses pass us in that time) by so the traffic wasn't that bad. When the bus did arrive we asked if a bus broke down and the driver said, "No".
On one of the live narration buses I hopped on the narrator asked me to move to a different seat as I was sitting down. I found out why, as he was playing to the two women from North Carolina the entire time and I would have been in the way sitting right in front of them. With 2 rows of seats before the narrator I was surprised he asked me not to sit there but I found out as the bus rolled on. I was sick of him trying to pick up the women as other passengers were as well so after a few stops I along with a party of 5 got off. we all waited for the next bus, and I hoped it wasn't a live narrator. Your job shouldn't be to pick up the customers and ignore the sights you should be talking about.
I was a bit disappointed in the wait times and live narrator and saw way more blue buses and City Tour and Classic Tour buses, along the way. It seems like I choose the wrong bus tour for my 1 solo day in London :(

The Original Big Bus Tour provided a glimpse into the history and extravagance of London. The bus tour guide was very knowledgeable and sociable.The majority of the famous London sites were seen on this tour and complimented by the Thames river boat excursion with champagne and crumpets. I recommend this tour(4hrs) to all who come to London for the first time.

I'm from NY and London has a similar layout & culture. The major problem with the hop on hop off bus is the traffic in London. If you just want to sit on the bus and travel around the city without getting off then it's fine....but if you want to get off to see sights then DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY. It takes almost 2 hours to loop around so if you get off to see one sight then that's all there would be time for. If you come into the city with jet lag and just want to sit then it's fine. There is so much to see in London that you would be much better off getting a full day tube pass for 24 pounds and go to the sights yourself. Once you see the sights you don't needs the narration the bus offers

We randomly picked this tour company but quickly regretted it. We booked for a large group of us to travel (3 small children and 6 adults) so had to hop off frequently. We seemed to spend most of our time waiting for buses and getting incredibly frustrated when we kept spotting buses from The Original Tour company pulling in to the bus stop spot.

We waited so long (over half an hour) that we were in danger of missing a matinee for a show so we had to jump in taxis even though we had allowed enough time to get to Kings Cross.

The on bus commentary was a little dull (could you have a special version for children?) with lots more music than talking. In sum, we will avoid Big Bus next time we visit London.
loved this journey by big bus tours, i can see around all over London such a famous iconic and lots of amazing places.

My husband & sons used a different company in August & it made their visit to London a very interesting one, so much so that he wanted my daughter and I to enjoy the experience too, especially as it was our first visit. London itself was fabulous, sadly Big Bus Tours left a very sour, expensive taste in our mouths.

We purchased tickets for Big Bus Tours via the Coca Cola London Eye link at a cost of roughly £95.00 for a 48hr ticket & we were sorely disappointed with the service provided.

We are a family of 2 adults & 3 children aged 14, 12 & 9 & we boarded the Eastbound Blue at Lonon Eye. It would have been nice if the driver had waited until we were seated before driving off & if he had pointed out the earphones to us but we realised the following day that the commentary wasn't worth listening to anyway as it was a mixture of repeated or after the attraction had passed information.

Friday 21st October service was abysmal. We boarded a bus outside Madame Tussaud's & took it to the London Eye stop as we were advised this was the best stop to board a bus for passing Harrods, Buckingham Palace etc. This bus is a Westbound Blue. We waited 40 minutes for the bus to turn up which seems like 40 hours when you have children complaining about waiting & not understanding why they can't board one of the tens of other tour buses which drew up in this time, including a good number of Eastbound Blue! Anyway on the bus we go & straight away we should have known it wasn't going to end well when the driver queried the type of ticket we had. Apparently we should have shown our tickets issued by the London Eye to one of the reps so he could issue a paper ticket, this despite having already used the bus company twice. Ticket issued we got on the bus & it was heaving with people, far more than was permitted to be on it so having little option but to stand we put up with it until we approached the Buckingham Palace stop. The stop was mobbed & I felt the driver should have driven passed for safety reasons but no, he stopped so we got off as the bus was already dangerously overcrowded & we couldn't actually see anything. First time I have gotten off a bus without thanking the driver but he was rather rude. We are all in a pretty foul mood by this point at the money and, more so, the precious time wasted when we look up and there's another Westbound Blue pulling in right behind the bus we had disembarked. Now I would have thought that a company such as Big Bus Tours would have had the technology for the drivers to communicate with one another & one could have told the other his bus was full but seemingly not as we were the only people to board at this stop whilst people stood on
the stairwell & upper deck of the first bus.

This time we had our earphones & listened to the commentary as well you can when you have someone singing Frere Jacques, London Bridge or just making annoying,unnecessary noises throughout. It was almost like having two radio stations interfering with one another.

All in all, the tube would be a much more cost-effective way of touring London rather than Big Bus Tours.

We were waiting for more than one hour just to get on the first bus. Later in the day we were waiting for 45 minutes, and they say that a bus will arrive at every stop every 10-20 minutes. You cannot do a lot of hop offs and hop ons during one day with that much waiting time.... This bus tour was the only disappointing thing about London.

My husband and I purchased tickets for this service when we visited London in Sep 2016. Having previously had really good experiences with hop on hop off services we expected this to be no different. We plugged in the audio and were horrified to find that while there was commentry, it chopped and changed regularly (I imagine that the recordings are based on a GPS system?). The recording would often repeat informatiom that was just broadcast or would not fininish on a point and move on to the next point obviously leaving you with incomplete information about the landmark. We talked to the driver about it and he said (and I quote)..."yeah, it's really cheap" while chuckling. I didn't really find it humorous as you can imagine and the tickrts weren't particularly cheap. We thought all of the hop on hop off operations were pretty much the same but apparently not!

Took kids aged 4 & 6 on this tour. Total disaster of a day (in part due to congestion created by Olympians parade at Trafalgar Square).
My main issues....
1. Poor customer service when purchasing tickets to not inform us of extent of delays and fact that 10 stops would be missed due to events in London that day.
2. Big bus tours clearly had less than half the busses operating compared to other tour operators - at every hop-on location while waiting for our bus there were always 2-3 buses passing us by from the other companies. Felt like we wasted half our time waiting for busses - not great with young kids.

We ended up abandoning tour at the Tower of London when it became apparent that about 50 people were waiting on the bus - little chance of us getting seats with the kids!

Maybe just a function of our Olympic heroes being celebrated and causing traffic chaos but would still look at another operator based on service experience.

Really enjoyed our Big Bus Tour of London last weekend. An informative commentary with interesting facts and stories about well known streets and sights. Hop on hop off was convenient and on time. Staff were friendly and very smartly dressed. Would use the bus again, a great day out for all ages.
Its not magic but if you haven't been in London for a while or even if you just want to sit and enjoy the sites, the Big Bus Tour is a great way to spend a few hours.

We spent six days in London and used the Big Bus during the first two days, as a means of relaxing and orienting ourselves. We did not expect much, as the city is crowded and the buses are at the mercy of traffic. We were SO LUCKY to have have JOANNE as our Red tour guide. She is a delightful, with a wonderful personality. Our driver, WINSTON was incredible. He navigated through awful traffic with ease. We did use the other lines (Blue and Green) and found the recorded audio tour to be informative with relaxing music. Others are correct to comment that the bus is slow, but one cannot rely on this as a means of transportation. For transport, use the Underground. We did use the our hotel computer to print the Big Bus fliers, which gave us two days for the price of one. We greatly appreciate that one "day" is actually 24 hours. We took a short boat ride, which was amusing and a nice respite. We also returned to the Big Bus vendors with our tickets a few days later and purchased discounted entry to the Tower and St. Pauls.

We travelled for 2 days around London with big bus excellent service and very pleasant members of staff which were very informative special thanks to zee which is a credit to your company as we had waited at Westminster bridge to get back to Covent Garden after waiting for approx 45- 50 minutes zee came and asked us where we were going to and as time was getting on it was 5.15 and as buses stop around 5.30 we were getting worried but zee stayed with us getting on every big bus and asking for us after 6 buses came and went zee found out there had been and accident stopping the buses getting though to us, then he seen a green line buses flagging it down and asking driver to take us to Covent Garden which he did the time was now 6.30 ish but he stayed with us although he should have finished at 6.00 WHAT A CREDIT TO HIMSELF AND BIG BUS WELL DONE ZEE AND SPECIAL THANK YOU.

We wish we could have used the service all day. The tour was excellent, allowing you to hop on and off at any time. The boat trip on the Thames was included and the commentary superb. A great day out.

Although I live quite near to London, I wanted to take my 9 & 13 year old children to see the sights and learn a bit about our capital city. I chose to do an open top bus tour as I thought this might be the best way. Well, I wasn't disappointed. The tour took us all around the London sights and attractions and we got to see everything that we wanted to and much more besides.

The best part of the tour however was the informative live commentary from the tour guide Joanne. Even with road diversions in place, detours and even a rain shower, her commentary continued with ease. Not only did the kids learn lots of interesting facts, so did I! She was knowledgeable, & interesting but also very funny. She made lots of potentially boring historic facts very entertaining so the kids were gripped throughout. Thank you so much for a great day. Cannot recommend enough. A star!

We always go on the sightseeing tour buses whenever we go away. Its a fantastic way to see the city and where all the attractions are. You are given headphones and chose your language for a commentary throughout. You also have a map so you can see the routes. There was a bit of a wait for the bus but well worth it. We sat up top to enable us to see the attractions better. You can hop on and off as often as you like.

With our ticket we also got a boat tour. We had a guide on the boat who was really funny and pointed out various landmarks. A different way to see the city and to get to some other places.

Would defo recommend and use again. Well worth the money.

For the most efficient way to get around London it's best to use the city buses. Waiting on the Big Red Bus waste a lot of valuable sightseeing time. Employees selling tickets while we wait on the bus. You are also able to walk a lot of places within 15-20 mins.

My husband and I were in London for a business trip, we used to live there. However, we never toured the city, or enjoyed it from a tourists view. So we decided to do The Big Bus Tour. The problem started immediately, and we didn't even realise it. Our ticket seller sold us tickets for a 2 day tour, even though we told him we were only in London one day. The cost difference was £10 each ticket. A Substantial amount. We discovered this later, after the other fiascos. Our first bus broke down before we could even start the tour, we had to wait "10 minutes" that turned into 35 minutes. Finally our bus came, we grabbed our seats and plugged in our earphones to listen to the history of London. They didn't work, the entire left side of the bus didn't work. We eventually were able to switch sides, after missing many interesting sites. Then the right side stopped working. Within a short period we were all escorted off the bus, because the drivers route was finished. (We had also realised that many of the stops on our tour were skipped, and we'd done a loop without seeing The Palace) At first we were told the bus broke down. We trekked to the next bus stop, which wasn't great as my husband had just had a major knee operation, where we waited yet again for another bus which took another 20 minutes. We climbed on this bus thinking we'd see the missed tourist locations. Not going to happen. It turned out to be a different route, and was the last tour of the day. The recorded device was broken on this tour as well, so we were unable to hear any historical facts. As we boarded the last bus the driver shouted at us to come back as we didn't even have proper tickets, we had vouchers that we had to transfer at our hotel for tickets? Which made zero sense to us, then another employee explained that these were just vouchers, and apparently the driver keeps them and gives us tickets? I honestly don't even know, and no longer cared. We met an entire bus full of tourists who experienced the same problems as we had, it was a joke to say the least. Nearly £70 for 2 tickets, we could've taken an uber without the drama
Use any other bus tour than this one. Their employees are rude, their ticket sellers are scammers, who also argued with us that England had already left the EU with his very heavy Southern European accent.... which we found comical. Never, ever again will I use this tour anywhere in the world. What a scam
we booked this bus tour and it will be a long day out going around the whole of london loads loads of traffic so 2/3 hrs become 6/7 hrs to do most of the tour good thing you can hop on and hop off

If you go on this ride and speak english i absolutely recommend the Red line because they have a real person guiding the tour. They are located on the upper floor and they are so professional. Their knowledge about London is outstanding and they talk with a voice that make you interrested. Don't get scared about the price, 32 GBP / person, because the ticket is valid for 48 hours and it also includes boat trips on the Thames. Those guides are also super entertaining. Five stars from me and I think it's worth the price.
By the way, the Blue Line do a different route and here you get headphones and can choose from different languages in the bus.
With only a stop-over to get a taste of London , we used this company's bus tour and saw a lot of the city . Use this to see the Town .

We waited a long time for busses to arrive. We waited 45 minutes at a stop to move to the green line. 2 green line busses came by but told us the next bus to come would take us back to the Eurostar station. We ended up having to get a taxi to make it to the train on time. Other bus lines had more busses coming thru the stops. I would skip big bus London if I were you! Loved Big Bus Paris though. Def recommend them!

The big bus tour is a great way to see the city and become more informed of the history of London. It is a hop on - hop off tour so you can get off at an attraction and once finished you can get the next bus ( they go by approx every half hour ) We had a a very friendly and informative guide, Ollie.

During my recent trip to London I travelled on your bus and it was a wonderful way to see the sights. Peter the guide was very knowledgeable and entertaining - he made history fun! I will make sure to include one of your bus tours when I come to London with my family.

Firstly you pay between $25-$35 per ticket, depending on who you purchase tickets from. That's shonky! First tour brilliant; Michael driving & Sharon tourguide. Very informative & entertaining,great knowledge & presentation thankyou. Second day terrible service. Stop 22 at Westminster Abbey closed - not advised by salesperson. Waited 30 mins at bus stop then noticed a photocopied small sheet of paper informing of stop closure on the pole. Walked to stop 23, waited an hour and 15 mins or more, no bus, even though it is supposed to come every 10-15mins. Called the phone number -no response -that is poor service. Midday on Friday 30 September. FINALLY someone went & found a salesman who had no knowledge & no idea - he was polite enough but didn't appreciate our (over 20 people's) frustration. He also denied being able to contact head office or any drivers - yet he had a walkie talkie & a mobile phone! Ridiculous! I think head office needs to implement a better information system between ticket sellers & keep them informed of stop closures. Letting their staff & customers down. When we finally got on a bus the guide was again informative but we lost maybe 3hrs of our limited time in London. Disappointing.

The bus tour ticket comes with walking tour tickets, as well. We enjoyed doing both walking tours (the palace tour and the Harry Potter). Steve was an incredible tour guide, and we were able to go on both walking tours with him. He was very personable and we learned a lot about the streets of London! The bus tour was also very good. We sat on the bus for 3 hours on the first day, seeing the sights and relaxing before checking into our hotel.

1st time urser of a bus tour so I was a bit concerned but I had no need ,we opted for the hop on hop off ticket which suited us as we wanted to still be able to see things up close as well as get around London traffic safely and quickly and I don't think anyone but a bus driver can do this lol, we'll informed and redirected when needed to be all the staff from the big bus company which I spoke to were all very nice and helpful

A fantastic way to see London from a local perspective on a budget.
The tour is comprehensive and takes in most of the "must see" sights of London.
The ticket is good for 24 hours and you can get on and off as many times as you like.
They are independent tour operators - so entry fees to local venues etc are an extra cost.
A set route takes you through the business, historical and tourist sites at a pace that is suitable for all ages and tastes.
Onboard fully informed local guides provide a commentary that is locally flavoured with typical British humour and banter and seeded with local history and folk lore.
Free headphones are provided on some buses with live commentators - others have a recorded monologue - look left - look right - You need to do a few laps of the Bus Tour or a mix and match of different routes .. the Blue Tour .. The Red Tour .. to get the full advantage - well worth it.
Most Hotels have brochures to make bookings - or you can hail the Bus on the route - ticket sellers are everywhere in the street.
Good tip is to ride on the top deck to get the most of the view .. wear appropriate clothing for the current weather, hat, sun glasses, be aware of windburn to exposed areas of the body. Enjoy.

We got 24 hour ticket for the Big Bus Tour picked up at Green Park at the first stop. The guy that sold us the tickets was a joke as he said he would give us £3 discount each if we paid for 4 adults and 1 child all together in one transaction rather than individually. He charged us £29 each £15 for a child which we didn't realise until we got back to apartment that it was the normal ticket price. Very enjoyable tour though and a great way to see Londons attractions hopping on and off when we wanted over two days.It was my wee sons first time in London so he really enjoyed the open top bus and seeing the sights. They supply Ponchos if it rains and your on the open top bus. Drivers very friendly and some commentary was good too. Would reccommend

Initial impressions incredibly poor, after our family with 2 young kids (6 and 5) were unceremoniously dumped at Marble Arch just minutes after leaving Paddington Station in what appeared to be a departure from the normal route. Told to move to the bus in front which either didn't exist or had departed by the time we were supposed to have taken it.
Guide not interested in looking after customers, just in selling tickets and joking around with other rival company spruikers. Gave up and left after 45-60 mins waiting for a bus that would never have arrived (should have been told to walk to other side of Park Lane?) - I speak English and lived in London for 7 years, good luck if you don't have this experience. Wasted the best part of 25% of our weekend away.
The following day, walked to Baker Street as a way of avoiding previous mistakes and had a reasonable tour on the blue, recorded commentary, route.

We bought a Big Bus 24 hours Plus adult ticket for £27. Which over our 2 day stay in London we used well.
Our ticket also allowed us to cruise the Thames between Westminster, London Eye and Tower Piers and allowed us to use either the audio guided tour or the rep guided tour.
On day one we opted for the audio guided tour which we were on for over 3.5 hours taking in the wonderful sights of London. We would have stayed on longer except we were hungary, so we left the tour at Westminster and got a bite to eat. Later on we used the cruise option to Tower as our hotel was near by.
The next day we opted to do the other route and again was on the bus for more than 3 hours taking in the sights once againm However, this time we broke up the journey by stopping at Harrods and the Oxford Street to do some shopping.
The tours along with the cruise are excellent value for money and as you are allowed to hop on and off are an excellent way to get around the city and take in all that London hs to offer.
Th audio commentary is very informative and accompanies the journey really well.
Another nice touch is the availability of ponchos so that you can sit in the open top part of the bus should if start to rain.

We have Big Bus in NY, so we thought it would be a nice way to see London.
Our only mistake was to take the one that didn't have the live tour guide. Well worth doing! We also got the night tour and Walking tour part of the deal!

We Booked & Paid For This Tour On line Unfortunately Our Confirmation Email Did Not Include A Bar code.When We Went To Get On The Bus In The City We Showed The staff Our Email and was Advised Unless we Had A Bar code We would Have To Go To there Office At The London Eye,I Asked To Speak to A Manager About This As We Had No Idea On How To Get To The London Eye The Staff We Asked Where Very Rude Except For One Chap Who Said His Bus Was Leaving Soon And We Could Get On His Bus To The Eye And Obtain Our Tickets, Sad One Person With Some Common Sense In A group Of 6 How Sad For This Company

We bought our tickets by the Green Line underground entrance. We bought the 24 hour hop on and off tour and London eye combo! What a great deal :) it is also the fast track for the London that is good for 14 days. SO you aren't rushed to use it! It's September so I recommend taking a light sweater and then enjoy the whole trip. I also recommend the guided tour they are so great on the mic.

After planning a few days in London with my young son, I spent ages trying to decide on which hop on hop off bus service to use. Personally, the deciding factor for me was the free night tour and Thames river cruise that came with the purchase of a 48 hour ticket. I am pleased to say that I made the right decision. The Big Bus Tour staff were always very helpful and informative, the bus stops were clearly marked and we never had to wait long for another bus and the maps provided clearly showed all the routes so that you could plan your route/day around the attractions. The only downside is that I wish they could run just a little later as some tourists want to make the most of the attractions when only spending a few days there. We are returning next year and will have no hesitation in booking the Big Bus Company again.

Bought tickets from a vendor on the street and jumped on a bus. Good commentary and able to jump off and on as often as we liked. The ticket included a river Thames tour which we didn't have time for unfortunately. 2 different bus routes around London visiting all the major attractions. Recommended

Got dropped off early in London on Park Lane. Mum and I didn't want to wonder the shops for a few hours. So we decided to do a bus tour. Big Bus was situated across the road by Hyde park. £25 each for the Red tour which was for 24 hours and a boat tour on the Thames. Live English speaking commentary. We stayed on the bus for the whole two and a half hours. Plenty of stops along the way if you wanted to get off. Great way to see the sights way from the crowds. Didn't do the boat tour.

We did the Big Bus Tour again and I cannot recommend it enough. We do it every few years and it is slightly different every time and you learn something new with each trip. It is the perfect start to London if you are a novice. I recommend you do this on the 1st day of your trip and see what you want to do and what you do not want to do as there are many things to do in London and unless you are staying for a month you will not fit everything in if you are doing the sights thoroughly. Do all the stages... Red especially then the blue and the green. The ticket can last 24 hours so if you are late starting on the 1st day you have until that time the next day to use it up.
It's very important to get a good Guide. We started off with Alexandra and she is lovely but very difficult to understand at times and english is my first language! We then changed over to Joanne. She is a lovely woman. Full of personality but do not get on the wrong side of her. She corrected many Customers for bumping into her ( by accident) and shouted at one Lady for being on the phone. It made us all feel a little uncomfortable but maybe she was having a bad day cause she could bounce back straight into Guide mode in a second. She is full of knowledge though and has a delightful way of delivering a story.

Yesterday my wife and I were disappointed and hugely frustrated. We chose Big Bus because of on-line and travel guide ratings. We wanted a relatively comprehensive orientation to the city the early part of our first full day in London. We purchased our 24-hour tickets on line and arrived at the nearest stop - London Tower - shortly after 9 AM. We wanted to ride the Red Line with a "live English speaking" tour guide. We never heard or saw one! We waited one and one.half hours after turning the first Blue Line down having been told by one of their staff that the Red Line would arrive about 10 minutes later - subsequently we were told repeatedly told "just ten more minutes!" Resigned 90 minutes later, after watching competitor buses come and go, we boarded a Blue Line. We did see a lot and learned a fair amount through our ear phones and the Blue Line did make a wider circle than the Red Line. We hoped off at Hyde Park to stroll the park and eat lunch hoping we could hop on a Red Line later in the day to complete the tour. After waiting at the Hyde Stop for a half-hour a Red Line arrived sans tour guide. The driver had the door closed and seemed to purposely keep his back to me while I sought to get his attention to determine if further waiting was warranted. We then decided to take the underground back to London Tower and finish the day on the Thames boat ride for which we had paid extra. We arrived at the dock at 6:15 PM and were informed that last boat for the day had departed even though we were informed by the staff at the beginning of this by now infuriating journey that the last boat would depart at 7:00 PM. One does not spend the time and money necessary to cross the Atlantic to wait helplessly at bus stops and docks! I plan to ask for a refund and will file a sequel if we a granted relief.

Just re-checked Big Bus Tours website – I got on the Blue Tour with a choice of recorded multiple languages. The commentary were off in so many places, not very descriptive, often would describe the monument we already passed. In addition the bus moves with the traffic flow, never stops for a chance to see the site. Could be different experience on the Red Tour with the live guide.
We transferred to the Green line to get to the British Museum. The driver was rude, commanded us off the bus (we didn’t see other passengers dissenting from the top level), and moved the bus the second we got in, so my 70+yo Mom had to climb to the top deck on the moving bus.
If your time is short find the good bus tour; or better explore area by area on foot.

We visited London yesterday,went to Buckingham Palace in the morning then took Red Bus route in the afternoon so that we could see all the sites,although we had seen most of them before wanted to see them all again

Trip was excellent where Steve the guide was excellent with his knowledge and wit.Bus driver was an expert in maneouvoring the bus in tight spaces

We had a brilliant time and tour is highly recommended and there are lots of buses so no waiting around

We booked on line which was very easy

We caught the Big Bus London close to Madame Tussaud's. We wanted the Live English commentary. We loved it! Our guide was friendly and entertaining. We hopped off at the Tower of London and that's where it all fell apart.

Getting back on was a total nightmare!

We stood around for 50 minutes waiting for a bus. None!! Not one came past for 40 mins.

Ridiculously irritating as during this period while we waited, there were at least 4 busses from each of the other bus companies stopping to collect their passengers.

After asking the staff on duty twice what the hold up was, all he could say was 'one is coming'. He had no people skills, not apologetic in the least, more interested in hanging out talking to his colleagues.

Obviously there was a growing crowd after 40 minutes so when a bus did come, it was a bun fight and chaos to get on! Pushing, shoving and no order at all. There is no system is place for queuing. We missed that one!

My husband approached a member of staff . He tapped him on the shoulder to get his attention and explained that we had been waiting with 2 children for this length of time and he should do something, he was so arrogant and kept on saying 'don't you touch me don't you touch me, who gives you the right to touch me'. Not sure what he thought but we just wanted clarification on when the next bus would come, why there were no buses and possibly to assist us with a queuing system. We walked away rather than deal with this kind of personality. Eventually a blue bus came, which we fought to get on once again.... Not fun getting elbowed and shoved while holding onto 2 children! The staff could not have cared less!! And the blue bus without live commentary is not worth the effort.

Chose the original bus company or another company rather. Way more busses at regular intervals, saw that for sure while waiting 50 mins for Big bus tours!

We did a Big Bus Tour for part of a day. We had a decent guide and it does take you around the City and give you a decent amount of history. It was an average tour. If you want an interactive English guide you need to be on the Red Line. It took us about 45 minutes to get a red line bus and before that we were on a blue bus line which was basically just like being on a bus with no interactive guide (they did have headsets). A cruise on the River Thames was included in the price and the cruise was great.

We were in London for a very short time and rode the Big Bus to get the highlight tour. A good way to cover a lot of ground in a short time. The buses we rode were comfortable and clean. We sat in the open top seats even when the drizzle began to fall - what's a visit to London without rain? The top provided a great vantage point for snapping photos and enjoying the sights - and the tight traffic situations the giant bus navigates with ease. The tour was definitely made more enjoyable by a good guide. Our first guide more or less rattled off the buildings as they went by. We hopped off and then back on and had a far better guide - very entertaining and well informed guy. What a difference! Our ticket came with a Thames boat ride which was a bonus - an easy and scenic way to take in the sights. Decent value for money. I would recommend.

We enjoyed a relaxing ride around London as the guide provided a ton of information on the areas we passed through. It started raining mid tour and they provided rain ponchos for everyone on the top deck. We did have to wait longer at the stop to get on the bus than the other tour bus companies, but we felt it was worth it.
Thanks big bus tours my wife and I thoroughly enjoyed the tour. Great live commentary from the guides.

This tour worked out expensive for two adults plus two kids but it was a great way to see London. You can hop on and hop off the bus throughout the day as often as you like. Headphones are provided to listen to the tour guide in a variety of different languages. On a sunny day it's difficult to get a seat up top in the open air.

We had a limited time to take some friends around London. WE took the Big Bus tour thinking we could see most of the sights. We were charge £32 per head, granted it was valid for 2 days, but no one explained we could get a cheaper one day ticket. Our bus took us past Buckingham Palace. Yes - PAST - down the side. We did not see the front! If you want to sit in a traffic jam for 2 hours and not see much - this it the trip for you. We went near some other attractions, like Albert Hall, but did not see it. We had to change bus for some reason, not explained. For a lot less money I could have taken our visitors to more attractions using the underground at a lot less money. Next day my throat had reacted to the fumes and pollution on the top of the bus. Never again!

We did the tour "with the comedian" omg it was amazing. The guy was very funny while being full to the brim with information about the sights and history of London. The tour was amazing. I am highly recommending it to everyone.
The next time we go to London I intended to take the children on the "ghost bus"

Big mistake taking this bus tour. We were waiting at Victoria Station, the hub, for about 45 mins for the Red line bus with **live** narrated guide and none ever showed up; about 3 other competitor buses stopped and picked up other groups and left. Finally we boarded a Blue Line which takes an extremely winding and 90 min tour of London; audio guides didn't work so we were left wondering what we were looking at, good thing we had a guide book. We hopped off to connect to the Green Line to get to the British museum, again another 45 min wait. One bus only for the Green Line, same driver goes to and fro. We found him again 2 hours later and we got off at Tower of London to get on the Thames riverboat --best part, included in ticket--but all buses stop running at about 6-7 pm so don't have expectations of taking it for 24 hr or for a night tour. I would recommend the Golden Bus competitor, saw their buses allover and much more comfortable in appearance. Could save money just taking taxicabs and seeing things your self. Lesson learned.

Hardly any Red line buses with live guides. Blue bus recorded commentary is terrible. We passed tons of interesting looking stuff and all I heard was classical music. We were determined to get on a red bus with a live guide and waited ages and ages. When we finally got one he was great. Very knowledgable. But we had already wasted much of the day and couldn't stay with him as long as we would have liked.

Traffic is too busy to do a hop on hop off in London. Honest to god I always do them and usually its manageable (even in NYC), traffic is to be expected...but this was crazy. Gridlock for ages.

I would never, ever do another hop on hop off in London. We didn't even make it to half of the stops we wanted to (London eye, tower bridge) because once we got off the bus that ended up being a huge commitment of time to find another bus to get back on. Any bus at all, never mind a live guide bus.

Waste of money. Do yourself a favour and get an Oyster card and take the tube everywhere. I wish we had.

London is great though! So enjoy it at your own pace.

Very disappointed! Only once we had paid our money we were told there would be a slight deviation due to an event in London. However we did not anticipate being taken on a totally new route for 3 hours stuck mainly in traffic on back streets only seeing St Pauls and Tower Bridge from the official route. There was a very limited commentary on the headphones, mainly music, because of the deviations. Later in the day the green route was still not open even though other bus tours managed for their customers. We were told to get a tube! The only good thing about the whole experience was the river cruise which was excellent. Would I use The Big Bus Tours when I next visit London - no. Customers should have been told about the extensive disruption .... in fact the tours should have been cancelled yesterday. I do not normally give such bad reviews but I feel very strongly about the fact that so many people paid such a lot of money for such a poor service.

We purchased our passes directly from our hotel. We got two days for the price of one and a river cruise included. I would highly recommend starting your holiday with the hop n go buses. It is a great way to see a lot of attractions. I would recommend you take the red line buses as they have a tour guide on them speaking to you rather than audio recordings. Highly recommend this as a means to see your attractions ...free wifi in the buses, did not work very well. On one bus we were on the audio only worked on top of the bus but not down below.

We chose the 2 day (48 hour) option that included a free night tour plus a round trip Thames River cruise. We were so lucky to have Leo as our live commentary tour guide on the Red Line tour . He was hilarious while also being informative about London and all the sights. We did as others recommended --staying on the bus for one full circuit to get one complete tour before deciding to hop on and off. During our 2 days of hopping on and off, we heard other guides who were not funny at all , nor did they provide any of the interesting historical facts that Leo had. Plus side: Leo ,clean busses, good route, nice night tour, nice river cruise. Negative side: not enough busses , no/insufficient A/C on the lower enclosed bus level. We had to wait 30 minutes one morning for a Big Bus to come by, while seeing many other bus companies (Original Tour) busses stop and pick up their people. The agents told us one of their busses broke down and traffic was also very heavy. Overall , I would recommend taking the Big Bus. We felt it was good value for all the tours included. We enjoyed the open air upper level for picture taking and the fresh air. Occasionally , the top level was full and the lower level was stuffy and not fun. But as people hopped off, we were able to get a seat at the top level .

Brilliant way to get around London, but if you want to do the whole sightseeing trip then stay on the bus...it took over 2 hours, but we saw places we had never been to and learnt loads about our really beautiful capitol. well worth the money. After we did the tour we hopped on and off the bus at certain destinations - far better than going on the tube.

Not too expensive to go on Big Bus Tour: if you'd want to actually see some historical places with less payment and save you time . Big Bus Tours is highly recommended for all. You can never be bored if you go on this bus with the tour guard

Just returned from a weekend in London and we used the big bus to get around which was great and if you used the red route there was a guide on it giving you a lot of information and history about each of the land marks, the other two routes used earphones which was good as well.

Big thanks to Dave our tour guide for making our tour a brilliant experience. We are completely new to London and didn't really know what bus route was best but all the staff were fantastic. We got on the green route then changed for the red route. Dave was very knowledgable and has a great sense of humour! He does his research which was impressive as there was a yaught on the Thames and he knew all bout it. We were on the second last bus and at staff changeover we got a lovely lady who advised us that this was the second last bus and she checked we were all aware and knew what stop we wanted to get off at and genuinely she just wanted to make sure we were all ok. Would recommend big bus tours and we will certainly use them again. Thank you. Oh and the sites were ace too!

We recently visited London and were wondering what to do as we have fairly young children but have done the museums and other attractions before. We were unsure whether the bus tour would be worth it, however we were really pleased, we bought a family ticket for £60 , this included a river cruise and hop on off for 2 days. It was a brilliant day for the kids, the tour guides we very good, it's well worth a try, we even said we would probe lay use this instead of using the tube next time as its easier for children.

Would not normally review a city bus tour but my wife and I had such a good time on Big Bus Tours in London that I had to comment. After a frustrating mix up at Green Park we eventually got underway for the second time on our third bus. The first more modern bus we had come off had earphone commentary which was bog standard information. After changing at Green Park we travelled on an older bus with Carl as our compere. He gave us his take on London which had us in stitches. He knew his history but filled the commentary with personal stories and insights. We meant to hop on and off more frequently but stayed on until the Tower of London and had a great afternoon’s entertainment. Goodness knows what the American and Canadian tourists thought. Because of Carl I am giving this Big Bus tour 5 stars. Great way to see London and all the things visitors might want to see. We also took advantage of and enjoyed the river cruise from the Tower of London to Westminster as part of the trip.

An awesome team on the Big Bus Tour in London on 4th September 2016, when London, around the Thames, became totally gridlocked as a result of the 350 year commeration of The Great Fire of London {1666}.The Thames River was the centre of attraction to thousands who gathered to observe "Out of The Fire".

Patrick, the driver {originally from Jamica, many years ago} and Neil the tour guide, made the epic journey of ensuring the passengers were entertained and warm.

The Big Bus made sure my mom, sister Viv and I were safely dropped off at our doorstep at our hotel, The Old Baley's in Kensington, London.

Well done Patrick, the driver and Neil, the tour guide.You made it an adventure not a nightmare. Four hours of fun instead of 4 hours of stress.

Amazing service and exceptionally great attitude under trying circumstances.

A great experience; very professional and knowledable.

Especially the red route, as there is a real live very knowledgable and entertaining guides.

Highly recommend.

Great way to see the city! Hop on, hop off, and the narratives are quite interesting. Great way to meet new people while seeing the sites as well. The facilitator was great the bus driver was friendly and the ride and connecting different colored buses made for a great way to see most all parts of the city tourists would like to see. Quite enjoyable.

This is a great way to see London - very educational for the kids and even worth it if you know London as you learn plenty going around. Take the "red" routes rather than the "blue", so you get live commentary, which on the two buses we took were absolutely excellent. We got a day ticket enabling us to hop on & off whichever buses we fancies (expect at 15 minute wait for red ones) and included a river cruise too, which again had a very informative and entertaining live commentary. It's not cheap, but a fantastic way to get around town if you're having a touristy day out.

We rode around for a few hours with Leo as our guide. He was just great - informative, amusing, engaging with our kids. I know London very well, but still learned more from him. On a sunny afternoon with tired feet from walking all morning, our Big Bus Tour was a welcome respite and very enjoyable.

We like to use Hop On Hop Off in every large city we visit. It is a tour and a mode of transportation. The River Thames cruise is an added bonus. You can see almost all of the landmarks and skyscrapers from the two modes.

Excellent value for money, the man done us a deal which was two days or bus tours, free river trip and two dungeons tickets for £50 each!
Tour guides upon the buses are full of knowledge and very helpful, will use this service again to sight see around London! :)

I have just returned from a London visit where we used Big Bus Tours.

The day tours were wonderful, but the night tour spoiled everything; you are very much left alone with a bus driver who has no care for the clients, I can only suggest that there should also be a tour guide on the bus too.

We were left miles away from our designated stop, cold and late at night. It turned out to be a 45 minute walk back and the whole experience spoiled everything, due to the blisters and the response from the rude/uncaring driver.

We booked this trip through Wowcher, to make the tour a bit cheaper. My parents & I wanted my 9 year old daughter to be a sightseer around London. The bus driver made us laugh & looked after us when we weren't sure where to get off to see Buckingham Palace. He was brilliant but can't remember his name. Lovely tour & the headsets & information/narration were great. Thank you.

a friend took this tour on a visit to London and recommended it to me, after two failed attempts, due to various circumstances, nothing to do with Big Bus Tours I hasten to add, we decided to partake while on a visit to the big smoke. Despite the cool and sometimes showery weather, we decided to sit on the top deck, out in the open, thankfully the showers held off, and were treated to a very interesting and highly educational narrative by our very knowledgeable and witty tour guide Sharon, she held our interest for the entire tour, which is a good couple of hours with little stories and facts. You're able to hop on and off as you wish, or do as we did and stay on board for the duration, In my experience, l can highly recommend this tour, there are two or three routes to choose from and experience is well worth the fare, excellent couple of hours.
Great tour bus and beautiful of london view... I traveled with my friends and had an amazing day through the beautiful london

Booked 24 hr hop on hop off tour
2 adults 3 kids .... age 16,13 and 7 yrs ... £77 included Thames cruise... booked on phone app very easy and easy to pay.
Caught bus at Marble Arch and guide there very helpful thanks to Simon we think was his name .... as I couldn't get internet up on my phone for code for him to print tickets ....thanks mate !
Guide on the bus Patrick very dry sense of humour and lots of info.
They tell you when bus is going to stop and what number stop it is etc and which attractions are close by very useful.
Thames cruise easy hop off at Westminster walk over bridge to pier, plenty of guides telling you were to go queue etc ... we hardly waited 5 mins if that.
Cruise brilliant again boat crew give informative funny info !
Saw loads of landmarks and when we hopped off we were right at Tower of London ! Great day and very simple journey.

This is an overall review. Some thing have been very bad and other things have been excellent. The drivers have all been happy and courteous. We found the street vendors at the stops were not very helpful and somewhat rude. Did not seem to have knowledge of the product and costs etc. They just wanted our money, quickly dismiss and said "yes" to all questions asked.
We purchased a multi day ticket and this seemed to cause huge issues.
The agent we originally purchased the ticket from had different and conflicting information to the Big bus rep at the stops.
We went on the city cruise and again we were giving conflicting information. It says unlimited cruise on Thames on flyer. But this is not so. It costs extra. The City Cruise company are separate to Big Bus, so I don't know how this works.

At every turn we came up against a problem with our ticket. We heard negative comments about the company from others too. There are plenty of other companies that do this type of tour, so do your research first.

The Blue route has a recorded commentary which is very boring. The red has a live commentary. The commentary was not in sync with the attractions.

Night time tour is a waste of time unless you haven't done it through the day. Expected something a little different at night.

We used the bus as a form of transport and didn't use the commentary.

We did this tour as we needed split days for our time in London. This was the only company that advertised this - we thought.

Spent a lot of time stuck in traffic between London Eye and Tower of London. There seems to.be a lot more blue buses than red, and live commentary is hit-and-miss. On one that we rode, we enjoyed the guide - he cracked jokes and seemed to really enjoy the job. On the other, she only.pointed out the building but didnt't give any further information - she does not seem.to like her job. Like one other reviewer, there seemed to be more "the original" buses than Big Bus.

We had a great few hours with the Big Bus Tours today. The red route has a guide onboard and our guide for the majority of our time aboard was Kevin who was fantastic. He really knows how to engage with the passengers and provide an interesting and highly entertaining experience.

We booked the 24 HOHO with extra 24 hours plus river cruise from Tower Bridge to Westminster. We just did a walk up and the price was very good.

We didn't wait very long at any stop. Yes traffic was a bit slow in parts where there were road works or road closures but everyone is in the same traffic and our guide had plenty to regale during this part so kept us entertained.

We would definitely recommend a real life guide to really give the true flavour of a great City.

The river cruise was good and we definitely thought one way is all you need to see the main attractions from the water.

Highly recommend.

My friend and I booked the Big Bus Tour for my birthday and really enjoyed our day. It's a great way to see some of London's best bits. My advice is to use the bus to get around but make sure you get off and walk around as well.
The only disappointment for me was not getting a live guide on any of the buses despite being on the correct route.
It's great value but only if you take full advantage of the entire day pass, so set out early. Also, you need to sit on the top deck to really enjoy the views so its best to do the tour on a dry day.

Well were do i staff bought our tickets at ticket off at the london eye dont the dont no what there on about
Me n my friends r carers with a boy each one in wheel chair other has specail needs.
The girl sold us ticket for just one child as she said us career were free not right at all and she didnt no what to charge the child in wheel chair to speak to the driver and get one there u cant buy them on bus only the guys on who work forvthe buses that stand at the bus stops.
She charge us 13.50 for one child 🤔.
We got to the bus stop then the guy selling ticket said no it not right we need a family ticket at 40 quid wow alot of money we thought but it a 24 hour bus hop on n off where ever.
Told the guy where we was off he put us on the red line this is just a drive round london n goes round again .
The blue line take u places ie madum tussauds . We wanted there got told to get off bus n go get another bus . Stuck in middle of london we decided google map it we walk half hour to the place .
We got the bus back after waiting ages every 10 min 25 min more like at 6pm.
Never used the bus again after that .waste if money

We had pre booked the 48 hour pass online which was considerably cheaper. We only got one live guide the majority of buses have headphones tours. We seemed to wait a long time for the live commentary bus and we noticed that there were many more Original London tour buses stopping than Big Bus.
The guide Jasmine was very good. She was both funny and informative although the route was long due to the expected London traffic

It's a great way to get an introduction to the city. Did a tour during the summer with Big Bus Tours' tour guide, Big Steve, who is super friendly, engaging, and whose accents are on point! Highly recommend if it's your first time in the city and you want a glimpse of what the city has to offer in terms of main attractions.

We purchased a 48 hour ticket and included a river cruise.
The Big Bus tour was excellent - the buses came regularly, stops were located in convenient locations and the guides at the stops were very friendly and helpful.

Both the audio and live commentary were informative but the live commentary was an even nicer touch as it was more personal.

We also purchased a ticket on the bus to the Tower of London and we were so grateful that we had done that as we bypassed the many people waiting in queues.

We joined a walking tour which left from Trafalgar Square to Buckingham and that was also excellent.

We would highly recommend this tour.

Having pre booked an online 24hr plus 24hr for a separate day within a week ..we thought we was well prepared. .WRONG ! We printed the ticket thinking a member of staff would want to see it and validate it ...NOPE WE USED 24 HRS WORTH BEFORE THEY ACTIVATED IT effectively getting an extra day free.dont get me wrong I can't moan BUT please be aware we sat at stop 16 for 20 mins and saw 30 busses for other tours ..NOT ONE BIG BUS TOUR BUS THOUGH ..WHEN IT DID ARRIVE the driver just pulled us on to where it was more than permitted ..happened TWICE !! ALSO ONCE DIDN'T WAIT for us to get of before leaving ...go with another tour company ..Rude staff ..unhelpful and ruined what should if been two days of enjoyment for our 4 children 😰

Heatwave/Spanish plume in late August in London - a young Egyptian friend and I decided to take the open top bus tour at 2.30 on a sweltering afternoon. She was visiting her brother for a few weeks and had never been in London in the summer before or done this kind of trip. I hadn't 'taken the tour' for 25 years. Expectations were high. We bought tickets enabling us to tour for the rest of the day and all of the following day. Sunshine, open air bus, thronged with tourists eager to look and learn. That's where the fun stopped. Having elected a live commentary tour rather than a recorded one I was anticipating interaction, fun, quirkiness. What we got was a tour guide who clearly was unwell and should have gone home. He complained repeatedly about the heat, customers talking and distracting him, noisy traffic, that he had to stand under the partial roof because of the length of the microphone cord and was therefore very hot - and so on.
