He frequently started to give us interesting facts, broke off and said he would tell us more later - and didn't, and disturbingly frequently banged the mike against his forehead. 45 minutes in and we were longing to get off, and a concerned Swedish customer had gone up to him to tell him he needed to rest and that we were all worried about him. By that point, with my friend on probably her only chance of this experience and various other tourists in the same situation, my compassion and patience had worn very thin. The views were great, the commentary and behaviour of the guide was dismal, so we left the bus at Tower Hill. We then took the boat tour from Tower Pier to Westminster Pier - with Thames Watermen navigating and commentating with all the wit, flair and enthusiasm we had hoped for. Thanks guys for making our day worthwhile! They are not paid for the commentary yet entertained us with panache. My friend can go back and continue the bus tour with her brother tomorrow and will probably get a guide who can cope with the demands of the job. If you do the tour (lots of other perks included) and you get a rubbish guide - do the smart thing and get off the bus as soon as you can and get another one with a guide who enjoys their job and can give you a good time. You deserve it!

My husband and I were in London for just a few days and this was great to see the city. The weather was glorious, a bit hot for London (30 degrees Celsius!) and there are a few routes available to let you cater your day and when you want to hop on and off.
We chose the blue line, the long one, and it was very long but that was due to all the construction and regular city traffic so be careful if you make any other plans with a tight time requirement.
The wind in your hair and seeing the sights on a warm summer day, can't get better than that!

We bought a 2 day pass for the hop-on-hop off bus in August, 2016. We found the service acceptable when we actually rode the bus, but finding where the bus stopped was difficult. Yes, we used the maps and found the landmarks noted on the maps, but still could not find the bus stop. This happened near Trafalgar Square and Covent Garden. If you stay on the bus for the entire circuit, it worked well, but using it as a hop on, hop off was useless for us. We were not able to use the bus at all on Day 2 of our ticket due to our inability to find the bus stop. The London city bus turned out to be much more workable. And, we've used a hop on, hop off bus before in other cities with great success.

By the way, the maps are not to scale and don't include much detail, requiring the use of another map or a phone app when using the bus to hop on, hop off.

To add insult to injury, we were riding the blue line and it suddenly became an orange line coach without notice near the Marble Arch. If it hadn't been for the announcement of the next stop, we would not have known that we wouldn't be heading to the stop we intended. I found another review that mentioned the same issue. The Big Bus employee at the stop with the change from blue to orange lines could have been a little more friendly and helpful.

We have just returned from our first visit to London with our daughters 12&9 years old. As we were there for a short time, we wanted to try cram in as much as possible.
When arriving I to Euston station we went to the visitor centre to get advice about tube tickets, and mentioned going on an open top bus, as my brother had visited with his family a few weeks previously and used city sightseeing. The guy in the visitor centre encouraged to buy the ticket there, which was £73 which I think is extremely expensive when we ended up not using it hardly.
We boarded our first bus outside Aldwych theatre. After being approached by other bus company staff, we showed our ticket and was told to see the guy who had big bus on his coat, he was unfriendly and not at all helpful. Was our first visit to London, and was asking questions but he was useless. He issues us with a receipt, which was so thin, it got wrecked in the rain! Then had to wait half an hour for a bus to come, this was full, so decided to wait, and asked how frequent and was told 15 minutes. Was told when I booked the ticket that this company was as good as city sightseeing, but I don't agree, other bus companies seemed to be having buses arrive a lot more frequently.
Eventually got on a blue tour, and went to the top deck, it was a wet day, but we had not been told you could get ponchos and earphones for the journey, thankfully another passenger advised.
Had to get off at Westminster as my youngest daughter was desperate for the loo, again not happy with the staff on the ground, hounding us to buy tickets for attractions, as did the previous guy at the first stop, and seemed unhelpful when we said we weren't interested.
The next bus was a red one, and the guide seemed OK, however some innuendo used was not appropriate with kids on board and some things he said were not required! Told that road closures were in place so if we wanted to see Buckingham palace had to get off, which we did.
We never went back on the bus, found stops hard to find, and hardly saw a big bus pass us, although other companies did.
We had planned to hop on a bus again at Trafalgar Square but after waiting what seemed forever, decided to walk after another company associate gave us some advice.
Feel let down, and annoyed as we could have spent that £73 on something a lot more useful.
We did t have enough time to use the river cruise as we had used our ticket at 11am and was only valid for 24 hours.

In view of the cost of some attractions we decided on the big bus tour to get around and see some of the sights. Being very lucky with weather we benefitted from seats on top deck. Hopped on and off to see what we wanted and tried both red and blue tour. Very good price for the 5 of us. Even used a 10% discount code I found online. Well worth 81.25 I paid and even got the chance to do the Thames cruise which was offered free as part of 24hr ticket. Go on try it... you won't be disappointed. TIP..Very beneficial to download the app onto your mobile.

I arrived in London on Fri 19th Aug with 4 teenagers, for a short stay, heading home on 21st & thought I'd treat them to the sights on the bus. Too expensive! £180 for a family of 6, spent 2 hours of the afternoon on the outskirts of London due to detours & instrumental music blasting from headset!!! We should have been informed when we bought the tickets there would be lots of detours!!! Don't waste your money travel by tube & you'll get around all the sights much quicker!!Our backsides were sore from sitting & a vast number of the passengers fell asleep, I'm writing this review as we tour round so bored, no sights to see on the outskirts!!! By the time we arrived at tower bridge 5.40, it was closed!!! Unknown to me the ticket seller has changed me for a 2 day pass & river cruise, which I didn't request or use as the teenagers refused to get on the bus again on Saturday morning! An expensive lesson:((((

Arriving at Euston in rain with elderly parents we struggled to find a bus stop after walking to Kings Cross at 11am, which with my father in law found quite far we fortunately spoke to a big bus employee. Bought 4 tickets which allowed us to use the tickets until the end of the next day. This is is a feeder bus which was packed but meant that we were directed to where we could get off and board a red bus . We travelled on a very busy route but heavily traffic which was quite slow at times. Our tour guide Sharon was very funny and entertaining, we really enjoyed the ride. All the staff we encountered were pleasant and helpful.
As we had already planned a busy 2 days going to Clarence House and Bucking Palace we didn't manage to use the tickets again.
It is important to look at the routes as if you want to hop off and on the routes might not suit you., in the direction you need to travel. If you plan to stay on a full route would take a couple of hours and you would be best to have drinks with you. Our hotel was at Victoria and due to road closures not all the stops are in use. There appears to be no information when you buy your tickets or at bus stops. We were told on the bus

We spent a lovely day travelling round London seeing the sights. We started off at Trafalgar Square on the Bus Tour, We had a great guide who was knowledgeable and funny, we went as far as The Tower of London and then got the boat back down the River. This was a little disappointing as we couldn't hear the commentary but still a great way to see London from a different view point. We then headed back onto the Buses again completing most of the Red Route before we transferred onto the Blue Route. We were unaware at first that this was only a audio tour but still took in the sites. We had to change buses a couple of times presumably to change drivers which was a bit frustrating, it would of been better if drivers changed rather then buses. We booked our tickets on line which was a bit confusing, as we ended up with too many tickets, then having to try and get these cancelled then having to rebook more tickets, and wait for a refund. Our mistake but be aware website can be confusing.

This was a great way to see London. It would of been better if the roads weren't closed as it totally messed up our itinerary for that day as we had planned to hop on and Hop off at different sites. There were a lot of demonstrations going on so streets were closed. I'd have to say no fault of the bus company, but if they knew this would happen it would of been nice to know. Then afterwards we caught a bus to end our day, asked if it was still running, he said yes... And then a few stops later said ok.. This is the last stop. Again it would of been nice to know that they were gonna totally end a few stops away. We've used the bus in other countries and we were very happy. Sad to say we were a little disappointed!

I accompanied my 12-year old son for his first visit to London. The first thing we did was to hop on to a red bus. Luckily we were able to purchase a ticket from the concierge of our hotel, but it is also available when one gets on. The buses are clean, mostly on time (depending on the traffic) and it takes one around all the main attractions, with great commentary. Some buses have guides, while others just have commentary which one listens to through the earphones. The traffic was quite busy in peak-time holiday season, August, but if one hops on and off enough, it doesn't matter. It is a must-do for tourists to London!

After reviewing the 3 mail HOHO buses in London we went with Big Bus and we so glad we did. The drivers on each bus were great and the couple of live guides we had were very entertaining. Our 2 year old loved to be in the open top bus and it was a great way to see the city and decide what we wanted to do. All the staff was great and easy to get tickets on line. Great experience. Thanks Big Bus!

We booked this bus tour for my first trip to London and I cannot recommend them enough. You have a choice of routes you can go and you can hop on and off at all the major attractions. Not only does the Red route buses have live commentary, the lady on our bus was excellent and was very funny, but they also supply you with maps, rain macs incase of rain and earphones for the blue and green tours to listen to the recorded commentary. I would highly recommend this to anyone visiting London.

We got a 48 hour hop on hop off tour. £33 per adult but not cheap, but this transported us to all attractions we wanted, and gave a great value city cruise up to Greenwich and back to London eye.
Best to go for red route as the 'live' commentary is better

The Big Bus Tour in London provided the perfect platform for a visit to all of London's key attractions. As a family of five, we opted for the Big Bus Tour due to the competitive price offered by the representative. Our starting point was at the London County Hall as we were staying at the Premier Inn.
It's advisable to research which bus tour would best suit your requirements prior to your arrival. We were lucky enough to enjoy the tour on a rare sunny day in London, accompanied by an informative tour-guide who was both humorous and entertaining.
The tour literally lasts as long as you would like it to. There are various options available from one-day tours, to 48 hour passes which also include a river tour along the Thames. It's advisable to view the city on a clear day with a full-charged smartphone or camera. The tour is worth every penny and allows one to view London from a different perspective.

After 2 days of walking our legs off, we gave in and hopped on one of these tour buses. This company runs a number of routes, taking in all of London's top tourist sites It was a fabulous way to see London. The tour commentary was available in many languages and between commentaries beautiful classical music was played. We stayed on the Red bus line for pretty much the whole tour and all members of our family really enjoyed the experience.

Am on family vacation in London have preferred big bus in midst cities I visited but in London they are too big so lack customer service and would recommend any other which are much better organised and easily accessible

We found the Big Bus Tours company made the day.

Convenient, frequent and knowledgeable staff.

From the drivers to the staff at the stops and also those in the office (Thanks to Sandra ans Paige) who responded reassuringly with great advice.

Money well spent. Thank you Big Bus London 10/10

So we did the tour and we enjoyed it. We hopped on/off the bus for taking pictures or to visit some side seeing area. Did two days with one ticket, so use it, to take your time and see everything you want to see!

My family thought that the bus tour would be a great way to see things on our way from Kensington to the Tower of London. However, these buses move extremely slow. It took us over 3 hours. During that time we spent lots of time parked at bus stops and in traffic jams. We passed a number of sights, but if we had hopped on and off as advertised we would have spent more than a day trying to get back to our hotel. The dialogue on the bus audio system is dreadful. You get maybe one fact and then you have long periods with royal marching music that drives you crazy. Why they can't fill that time with more history of London I have no idea. I probably would have been happier if I had been learning the whole time, but it was an extremely long ride that would have been immensely faster and cheaper on the tube.

Took the Big Bus tour - needed a break from all the walking we had been doing. Picked a perfect day for it and sat on the top of the double-decker bus - wasn't too crowded. Lots of interesting info on the recorded tour, but sometimes the info came after we already passed the location. Blue line tour didn't seem to cover everything it should have. Learned some interesting facts and saw some points of interest that I hadn't seen before.

The big bus tour company do an excellent job! Bought 2 day tickets for a trip around London. The commentary on the red route was excellent and we were able to see all the main sights around London. Also went on another route which was labelled as orange, this route doesn't exist anymore and we were waiting over an hour for it! Other than this glitch, would highly recommend the big bus tour around London!

Well worth the money as you can hop on and off the bus or get your bearings and go back for a more detailed look at what interests you. The included boat trip on the Thames with the additional photo opportunities makes it very good value for money.

The online price for family (2adults 2children) was £64.50 but as I wasn't sure which service we would use - didn't buy online and had to pay £79.00 on the bus! They never advertise on the bus fares and you have no way of comparing.

We got on from Green Park and in about 15min the bus started its journey. We were on red tour and the live commentary was good. However, 6y olds did not enjoy being on the bus listening to commentary and in the end we only went upto Tower Bridge. River cruise was good but you can take it only one way (not round trip). I remember last time I took hop on off London bus tour with another company we could take the round trip and get on the bus without missing part of the journey. All in all for us it was wasted money as we wanted the children who learned about London in school to enjoy seeing all they learn in real life but it wasn't the case.

The beauty of the big bus torus is the hopping on and off as you see something to tour. We take the full ride and then list the places we want to get of and see as we go around. If you've never done this I encourage you do do that , learn and then go. Thank you Phil Harris, your staff in London were absolutely great.

Just back from London and felt let down by the tour buses (not the staff), we used two buses and each bus we had problems with the audio units,and as the buses are busy we couldnt swap seats to try other units. Also there where no small ear earphones for children and the ones provided where to big for my daugters ears so she missed out all together which was sad as she was the reason we did the tour in the first place. The tour itself was ok althugh disappointing you dont actually get to see Buckingham Palace. As we didnt have much time in London we couldnt swap for the red tour which would have been better due to the live commentary. Disappointed overall

I bought tickets with the group of four I was with from the booth at Baker St. at about 3pm and just about made it to Tower Bridge for the last boat trip back to Westminster/ London eye, from where we hopped on another bus wanting to finish back at Baker St. However, the late bus (probably last one) terminated at Marble Arch, and the helpful lady-operator asked another staff - someone who was co-ordinating buses at Marble and who may have been the supervisor, if one group of people can be dropped of at Paddington, and us at Baker st, to which his responses were very helpful. He managed to get the other group on an empty bus, and after fifteen minutes or so, told us to follow his fellow driver who led us to a night bus tour bus - informing the driver to drop us off at Baker Street to which the driver started grimacing. I had my doubts, especially after the mystery solving experience of Sherlock Holmes at Madam Tussauds, that this bus wasn't going to Baker St, because the bus was already half full and passengers had already plugged in their earpiece for commentary, and when the Bus got to piccadilly circus I questioned the driver if he was going to Baker Steet?? to which he replied that this was a night tour bus and it doesn't go to Baker Street. So, why do they mislead people like this?? We got off at Piccadilly Circus to make our own journey back to Baker St after a long tiring day.
Although this company tries to be helpful, they have no substance, and if I was a tourist in London I would be wary of this company.

Having done previous tours with other companies as treats for our children when they have been old enough to appreciate the sites of London and recognise them I was zoo disappointed with this one.

They were filling every seat but not mindful of those with children, larger people and then on top of this the weather and any potential issues on the roads.

This company has Zero customer service on board these buses either than seats being filled and a comedy routine that is not funny and lasts the whole journey which makes you want to keep hopping off to find a bus where the guide doesn't keep up a comedy routine..

we were stuck around St Paul's for so long, it was hot, we had children and yet the routine continued without anyone checking to see how people were.

They could learn a lot from other tour companies….

Not great for the money you pay!!! Hardly saw a big bus to "hop on and hop off"!!! Waited ages at Buckingham Palace red/blue stop, not a bus in sight as we watched several other company buses go past!! Very disappointing for my little girl who was looking forward to a open top roof experience; ended up getting to tube to our destination and given having to miss a boat cruise as had waited so long for no bus to arrive at Buckingham Palace!!
Also no one around to ask advice regarding bus routes etc, was very rudely told by a man from another bus company when I asked if he could tell me if there is a bus that stops here? "Not my company!!"
Would not recommend!!! A £32 rip off!!!
I have been on 3 hop on, hop off bus tours and this is by far the best. A real live commentary by the brilliant Kevin kept us entertained and informed. Thoroughly recommended.

I took Big Bus when I went to Turkey and was expecting the same good service here in London.  OMG, what a nightmare! I traveled with my parents and most of the bus drivers were very rude, they don't even greeted us when we got in the bus and they seemed upset all the time specially when I asked them something.  The worst happened last Monday when we were waiting for the blue bus in the london eye stop. It was 6.55pm, and we waited soooo long for the next bus. There were no staff there, sooo when the next bus arrived it wasn't on service, so I asked to the RUDE driver for the blue bus, and he answered with another question,  asking me what company I was looking for,  then I pointed to the BB logo and he said (I get mad when I recall this) so what? What's that? What do you want to say? Do you speak English? Oh gosh! What a horrible person, how come this guy is an employee for a TOURISTIC company? Literally they don't know how to treat people in a polite way. Luckily a staff member arrived afterwards and he kindly told me what bus I should take to get to the Marble Arch. I'm glad he just appeared in that bus stop.... In addition,  after 7pm the buses were driving in high Speed like they were in super rush to finish their shift,  I thought for a moment I was in a normal bus not a Touristic bus.  Furthermore,  they also take random routes without previous notice.... What a bad experience. I'm planning to go back to London soon and definitely will opt for another company.

Lots of interesting stops. Good commentary. It was a sunny day, so we sat up top. The Big Bus is a great way to see the sights, especially if you are only in London for only a short time. You can hop off and on at any of stops as many times as you want..but we stayed on and enjoyed the commentary for most of the circuit. Buses come regularly (about every 10-15 mins).

Tip - ticket price on the official Big Bus website is £22 for a day pass. At the bus stop they ask £32. All you need to do is mention the Internet price, and the bus stop guy will drop the price considerably - he ended selling us the 24 hour pass (with boat trip) for £25 each. Nice!

My husband and I have never been to London, so our first day, we got on the bus, and did the entire circuit. It took about 5 hours, and went all over London. Well worth the time. You can listen to a recorded tour via headphones, but I found the music disrupted my experience of the trip. We had perfect weather, and the open top of the bus was fantastic.
Went with family in London on big bus it was really good way to see whole London. The river cruise ride was included in the package. Was amazing.

Hop on off buses are a great way to get your bearings in a new city, and Big Bus London goes to all the major attractions. Although it is really easy to get around London on the tube, you miss a lot too. The Big Bus guides were all knowledgable and helpful, despite the chaos caused by road closures due to the RideLondon cycling event the weekend I was there. Really, the company should have had half price tickets that day or just not operated, since the bus couldn't go to a number of the stops, making it really hard to hop back on. Drivers and guides all did an admirable job of trying to make sure everyone got where they wanted to go.
The inclusion of the boat tour was good value and I was glad I bought my ticket for the Tower from the bus company as it saved me a very long queue.

I was very happy with my day until about 3.30pm. I got off the bus at the Buckingham Palace stop, came back to catch the bus at 4pm and along with many others waited until 5.15pm for a bus. Not a Big Bus team member in sight. Several buses of the other tour companies came and went during this time. By the time we got to Marble Arch to change buses to get back to our respective hotels total chaos reigned. Some very hassled staff were trying very hard to help people but 1 in particular who I had the misfortune to deal with until I realized he had no idea what he was talking about was rude,disinterested, and giving out incorrect information. He couldn't have cared less and just sat on the fence and laughed. The staff seemed to think the tours were all finished and yet it wasn't the end of the day as stated on their Brochure! Then I found I had been given an out of date tour map by staff at the stop I started my tour on that morning which didn't help. All in all just not good enough. It meant rhat I missed several places I should have had time to visit. I would definitely not recommend this company to anyone. If you are looking at purchasing a hop on hop off bus tour book with one of the other companies.

We were heavily disappointed in the route. The two main places we wanted to see were skipped due to "police advised diversions" although the other bus companies seemed to have no problem getting to those attractions. We had to walk with a four year old for 15 mins to see Buckingham palace from the nearest stop available after working out how to get there from the stop. And then we ended up taking the tube to see tower bridge when we realised we were not going to go over it and missed the closest stop. Yet every other bus company seemed to be able to go over the bridge. So disappointed in the route as nothing was advertised or advised of route closures - but I guess that was intentional otherwise they would loose customers to their competitors that were still travelling those routes!
However It is a great way to see the sights from an open top bus and the commentary wasn't too bad. It's an excellent way to get your bearings in a new city. There were heaps of big bus tour busses although most had a full top deck most of the time. We had one particular bus driver who was very good and others that were not as good, luck of the draw I guess.

We took the Eurostar from Paris for a one day trip. The Big Bus Tours was hard to locate outside Pancras station, but once we located it, we were on our way. It took us about 30 minutes to arrive at Westminster. We walked from this area to Buckingham Palace and arrived just in time to see the end of the changing of the guard.

My biggest complaint about the bus was the lines of people trying to hop on board at the stops.

We needed to be back to Pancras for our train back to Paris. We took the blue/red line around towards the Tower of London. The traffic in the afternoon was horrendous. Thank God for the bus driver who understood our plight and helped us to hail a taxi so we could make our train.

I suggest you do the Tower of London part of the tour in the morning in order to avoid the traffic jams.

We visited London in June 2016 & I must admit London wasn't really on one of my top ten places to visit. However I was totally wrong! I loved London it's such a fantastic city, one of our many highlights were the Big Bus Tours. It's a fantastic way to see the city & work out where you want to visit, the staff were all extremely helpful as we found most Londoners were. The Bus tours are very informative & great value for money. Well worth hoping on board 😊

Wherever we go on holiday we try and do a bus tour to see the major sites and get an overview of the city. I have lived in London most of my life but decided to do a bus tour as my two young kids (6 and 3 year old) wanted to see London's major sights.

It was a great experience and for English speakers I would recommend the red route that has a live English speaking guide.

Well after much deliberation, I decided that this company were the one for me. For £27 per adult you got hop on, hop off access to 3 routes around almost all of the main tourist spots and a river cruise, the ticket lasted 24 hours but you could get a 48 hour ticket at a higher price. Now I am familiar with London, and found them very entertaining, I only used the red route with the live tour guides but they give you so much info, it would be wrong not to. The river cruise took us from Westminster pier to tower bridge pier, then on to Greenwich. Greenwich was buzzing with a weekend market as well as the Cutty Sark.

We loved taking the Big Bus tour to get the "Lay of the Land" during our first visit to London. Traffic was terrible throughout our visit, so the routes took much longer than anticipated. We did have difficulty with a driver who was very nasty with us when we asked to leave the bus after we hadn't moved for 25 minutes to make a reservation. While all other employees were outstanding, that left interaction was uncomfortable and left a less than stellar impression.

What an absolute waste of money and a waste of a day today in London with this company. After arriving at Euston station we waited for over 45mins for the bus before we had to catch a cab to the London Eye to make our booking on time. We then waited another 45mins for the bus which was supposed to take us to Buckingham Palace. Bus driver informed us that that stop wasn't available due to road wrks...so we had to walk the route ourselves. Funny how Golden Tours managed to find their way to Buckingham Palace. After that we waited another 35mins for the bus on the Harrods route but eventually walked it ourselves. Bear in mind when they sold us the tickets we were told the bus' ran between 5min and 20mins. After our visit to Harrods we waited an hr before the bus turned up. Missed most of the sights we wanted to see. I will never waste my money on this company ever again nor will I let anyone else I know use them. My advise...use Golden Tours...they seemed to have bus' every 15mins pass by while we waited like complete idiots in the rain. As for the customer service on the phone (after 3 separate calls)...no apology what so ever, we were just told to reply to our email confirmation to see about a refund. Not an enjoyable experience at all....

Big bus tour is economical & fun! It's saves so much money compared to using taxis. Also, you can see the city & the people compared to being underground on the Tube. Your can hop on & off throughout the city with ease. Be sure to carry a map with you to locate the stops. Using the Tube is probably quicker because the bus comes to stops every 15-30 min. Guides on bus are fun & helpful. Some have live guides & others have headphones for a guided touring.

Very disappointed , there was no commentator on the tour, only headphones, which played Rule Britannia over and over again, in between landmarks, I had to take them of which meant , when I did get to a landmark I'd missed half the information . The bus also stopped at pick up points which is fair enough but it sat and waited 10mins. The landmarks are quiet far apart from each other, most of the journey is driving through London traffic, I felt I'd wasted my money when I got off 🙁

We travelled on the big bus with 4 kids aged 17 12 10 and 9 with the guide steve.
We boarded at green park where we were greeted by helpful staff and we boarded quickly.
Steve was very knowlegable about london and it was clear that he was enjoying doing the job. He interacted well with the 2 younger kids (though he didnt know how many windows in buckingham palace) but struggled to engage with the 12 year old who is very hard to please.
He gave us plently of notice when a photographic oppourtunity was coming up.
I wouldnt hestitate in recommending the big bus company to any of my family or friends
Sue

If you have never visited London before Hop-on Hop-off is a must. It takes you by all of the popular tourist sights and you also get a commentary as you go. I recommend the "red" line which has a live guide, as opposed to the "blue" line which is recorded. They both take the same route. I also recommend getting the two-day ticked which, in addition to giving you ample time to visit the sights, also includes a short river tour. As I took the tour I made notes of places I wanted to spend more time at and used the tube to get there during the rest of my trip.

I use to take the tour every time in London and it will never be boring . The bus will take you though the city and too see most of the attraction . You can stop any where and take the next bus .
Wifi has been added to the trip and is free .

Had a 24 hour ticket in the Big Bus Tour on our recent visit to London. All staff were brilliant - Robert the guide kept us amused on the red tour. Traffic was particularly bad that day but his banter and knowledge kept us entertained. Great way of seeing London. Then when we got to The Tower of London we got off and hopped on the Thames boat trip which was also included in the ticket, which was far better than we expected. Really enjoyed this (apart from the rain shower) and again the boat crew were all absolutely excellent. We also went on the Orange tour around Knightsbridge and Kensington so definitely had our money's worth. Would highly recommend to anyone. Couldn't fault it, waited for a couple of minutes before jumping on the next bus, no long time waits and the kids were delighted as they got to sit in the front twice. Highly recommend.

Excellent! If you want to see the city's all tourist places I recommend take this bus. This is hop on hop off bus. Tips to new travelers, buy the ticket from your hotel (hot gets discount and they will that to you) and ask for one day + (plus) ticket not 2 days ticket. You will save bundle. Below 15 yrs old pay half.

And for other days we purchased London metro passes for 20 pounds. This Metro Pass is good for train as well as metro buses. Day before we left we went to a Metro station and they gave us back cash our unused portion of the fare.

I've been to London a number of times and never done a bus tour as thought expensive and could cover places by foot/tube. This time I visited with my young son who wanted to go on the open top tour buses! It cost £47 for us both but this included river cruise on Thames and 24 hrs bus tours plus free 24hrs. I was pleasantly surprised at how much you could see of London on the tours and the tour guides were great! We managed to cram so much into our two days and also the river cruise which was brilliant. We thoroughly enjoyed the bus tour and saw so much of London that would have missed otherwise. Would definitely use them again.

Great big bus tour ride.
All age children to senior person everyone enjoyed
this ride.
Good décor of bus+ colourful bus attracts everyone.
Don't miss this joyful ride,sitting on upper open deck
of bus & capture highlight of London in your eye is
great opportunity.
Click As many as pictures for memory.

These bus tours are a fantastic way to see and get around London. The tickets are good for 24 hours after purchase, so you can use them one afternoon into the following morning. The guides are hilarious and give great tidbits of information. Plus the fact that you can hop on and off is excellent, If you see an attraction you want to do, you don't have to wait for the end of the tour. Just hop off the bus, and go do it!

Enjoy the view took us around London observed all sight seeing places. Kids were excited and took photos from close up as moving around the tour bus attendant was very helpful answer all our questions had good history knowledge of the place

I called Big Bus Tours on 3 separate occasions to get information to help me as I was bringing a visually impaired man to London. They didn't answer the phone once. The last time I was on hold after the automated message for 10 minutes and then gave up. I drove to London in the end and saw 2 Big Bus tour buses and both were virtually empty. I wonder why.

My daughter and I did this bus tour last week. It was very good and informative and even though I live here I learned a lot of new facts as we drove around. The only negative was the traffic which can't be avoided so prepare to be on it for a few hours. I thoroughly recommend you do this on arriving to London.

Participated in the bus tour this morning. Was advised by a member of staff to take the red line so we did and paid £33 (3 of us, my mum and sister and I) I had done a bus tour last year in NY so was expecting something great from this too. We were told at 8.15am that the next bus would be leaving at 8.40am. We waited until 9.15 am for our bus to arrive which was a blue tour bus not red that we had booked and had to get off at another stop to get on a red. I was told to have patience by a member of staff after having to wait 1 hour for the bus!! It took 4 hours to complete the tour. We paid extra money to have a "guided" tour however I learned very little as our tour guide did not tell us much information!! The highlights of the tour were Big Ben, the London eye and Westminster Abbey, which we were only staying 2km from so we could have got the tube/bus to see. The rest of the tour was boring. Was very disappointed as it is our last day in London and it was a waste of money. Would not recommend.

This is an excellent way to see the major attractions in London. London is busy, lots of people, driving is a nightmare and has so much to see. The Big Bus, hop on and off , covers all of London. The red line has a live tour guide. Your ticket also lets you cruise one way on the river Thames. This all for 32 pounds a couple. Depending on how long your stay is Big Bus can help guide you to those sights that interest you. Easy to access Big Bus anywhere in London. Big Bus helped to organize what we wanted to see in nore detail. If only spending a couple of days in London, Big Bus is a great way to see the major sites.

If it is your first time to London you must do an open bus tour. It is easy, informative and gives you a great over view of London very quickly. I would say plan for one day and then use the day pass for tubes and buses for the rest of your time in London. The reason for the jury still out is I am not sure if Big Bus is better than The Original Bus Tours. The original looks to have a live commentary as opposed to the Big Bus that has ear phones. I would recommend not getting off the bus to do Madam Toussads as it takes a long time to do so use as much bus time to see all of London. I would also recommend seeing Tower of London and then catching the river ferry back to Big Ben. The conductor is very funny and well worth the listen. I would also recommend buying the bus tour and Madam Toussads on-line as a package as it is way cheaper. this is on the proviso that you can do madam Tousauds on a different day. We bought our ticket from a conductor on the side of the road. It appears to be slightly more expensive than buying on-line. The price started higher and then dropped with some haggling.

I booked a 48 hour ticket with them which had a free night tour which starts at the shrek or Westminster Bridge. Buses were good and offered free earphones. Commentary was available in many languages. A live guide was there at the red route which sounded boring all the time. This is a good way to explore london. The frequency of the original tours was much better than big bus. Staff were also less in number at stops compared to the original tours. Night tour was pretty good which made it worth the money. I would recommend original tours though or if you want to travel faster tubes are the best mode of transportation for you.

Before our trip to London we had downloaded the app for the big bus tours, seemed they ticked all of the boxes and we thought if it's good we will go with them on our holiday in December to NYC. What a shambles, we boarded the bus at 08.50 went to Buckingham Palace, hopped off then hopped back on to Harrods. We left Harrods at 1 pm..... Note the time. As advised by the tour guide go to a Tower of London and do the free river cruise up the Thames. We arrived at the Tower of London at 4.20 pm !!! I could have flown to Palma in less time. There were diversions in place which the driver MUST have known about as whilst waiting for the bus at Harrods I overheard them talking on the the Walkie talkie that a driver was running 3 hours behind. I thought I had miss heard. So there we were on an open top bus with temperatures hitting nearly 30c with only half a bottle of water, of course I am too stupid to think to pack a picnic when doing a hop on hop off bus !!!!!!! We paid a grand total of £64 for this exciting day in London. Shame on you, we should have been informed of what was ahead of us, allowing elderly and children to sit there and unable to get off. You are not setting a good example. When we go to NYC in December will we use you again ? Sorry no, so you have lost the potential of 4 paying adults to use your service. I felt as though it was a case of we've got the money sod them. Really disappointed. We have travelled all over the world and yes this was our first time to London, we have had some fantastic times and feel over the years the only other time we were ripped off was in Tunisia. I feel ashamed and so should you.

We chose the hop on hop off option to use the Big Bus and enjoyed the opportunity to see some of the downtown areas in London while receiving a tour guide description for many of the sights. We chose to use it during a busy time in London with Cricket matches taking place while we were there, and we found some wait times to catch next stop options so this might not be for you if you are crunched for time. If you are flexible with your time, the double decker bus is a great way to visit a lot of the attractions and enjoy the option of coming and going to fit your schedule. Fun to do if you haven't tried it before.

Hop on and off, see the sights and hear the sounds of London. Great time was had and topped up my tan sitting on the top deck. We waved like saddos at other buses and they waved back. What a great way to see our beautiful London.

This review is a little tough to write since I have to make the distinction between the tour itself and the experience one has while on the tour. That said, if a company is going to decided to do business roaming the streets or a sprawling metropolis like London in very large buses, then they have to assume responsibility for the experience.

The concept of having regular buses which you can board with flexibility is a great idea. They have pre-recorded messages informing riders of the attractions which are being passed. All of that is good.

That said, don't anticipate that this bus while get you anywhere in London in a reasonable length of time. Traffic is absolutely unbelievable and we eventually got off the bus to take a taxi where we needed to go given all of the street congestion. If you are going to take this tour, make sure you have no where else to be. You may want to consider just using the extensive Underground system in London as an alternative and educating yourself with a tour book along the way.

We will not take this tour again in London.

Bought a 24 hour pass. Wanted to fit in.as much as we could whilst in london.after getting on bus blue line.ending up going past same statues three times.driver came upstairs and asked us where we were going.got us onto bus to take us to London eye.eventualy got there to Buckingham palace.on return told outside Harrods by big bus personal.this is the to Tower of London.how long .his worlds eventualy.nearly three hours latter.arrived.heat wave no water.never ever will we go with big bus.avoid at all costs.

Fantastic tour. Ask for a deal for 48 hrs. Worth every cent. Even did a cruise up to Greenwich which is included in the ticket price. Excellent service and best way to see london city. Hop on hop off any stop. Walk the streets of london too.

We bought a two day pass to go alongside visiting the main attractions in London. We were in no rush which was good because you don't get anywhere in London quickly! Hop on and off... If you want to see the sights or have simply got sick of the tour guide (which I'm sure won't be the case...)
The river cruise was good as it showed you sights that were missed out of the bus route so worth going on! (And no traffic so fairly quick!)
Even if you do end up going around the same sights a few times there will always be something you've missed (like that photo you were too slow for the first time) or the guides will point out something different.
Every member of staff we encountered was very helpful and friendly. A special mention for Winston (Our driver on the night tour) as we unfortunately encountered an accident so had to make a detour. He made sure everyone got off where they needed to even making some unscheduled stops as we had missed them on the other side of the river. We were running so late that the hotel bus had finished, it had been a long day on our feet and Winston kindly offered to drop us off on his way back to the garage at the stop for our hotel. So a big thank you to him!
We only saw some of the London sights at night because of the detour but whether you do it on the bus or by foot, it is worth it for the illuminated skyline.
Recommend this tour if you want to get some good snaps of the city and move around between places after a long time on your feet. And if nothing else my general knowledge has improved greatly!
☺

We used the hop on hop off bus to get around the tourist areas around London real quick and easy! Every time we took the bus we had a new speaker and they always had new information to share so it was a great learning experience every time!

Sight seeing is easy by big bus. They offer also one way ferry trip at river Thames which I recommend to take from the nro 18 stop at Tower bridge. Reserve time as traffic in London is awfull. Not nice if it is raining.

I went on a tour with a friend. We wanted to try the "real turist" thing and decided to jump on a bus tour. It was great and relaxing. Even though we didn't listen to the guide (you were given headphones to listen through) we had a great time and got to see London from another perspective. Unfortunately we chose to go at rush hour so the bus spend quite some time being stuck in the traffic. Other then that it's a tour i would recommend as you get to see a lot of London without the walking. Perfect if you only have a short time to spend sightseeing.

We booked the tickets for our family which came to visit us from USA. Had terrible experience with Big Bus tour first of all they didn't know that there is parade going to happened on Sunday because of that bus service got delay upto 4 hours. No apologies by staff plus we didn't travel wasted all our money. Very disappointed.

I had never stayed in London before and my wife wanted to travel on an open topped bus. Got on near Hyde Park Corner, we paid on the bus when the ticket collector arrived. £32 each. We were on the bus for over 4 hours, which was our choice, changing at the stop outside the wax works extending the tour. Unluckily we were sat in traffic for over half an hour at one point. We were lucky not to go around again as we didn't return to our original stop but disembarked at another stop close by. No big issue. There are discounts for some attractions which come with your ticket and given more time there is an inclusive boat ride on the Thames. I will definitely use this service again as it would be a great way to get about if its dry. The only downside is you can't choose your fellow passengers. There was a French chap in his fifties trying to eat his fifty plus companion's face who, pretty obviously the wife of someone else, sat in front of us. We were okay though as we hadn't eaten.

What began as a calm and typical hop-on/hop-off tour of London jolted to a pre-mature halt at the Marble Arch stop. My husband and I had prime upper deck seats that we scored early in the day at Piccadilly Circus. We nearly made it 3/4 around the Blue/Red loop when everyone was told we needed to get off and get on another bus for no apparent reason. As we made it to the next bus, we were halted by a Big Bus ticked agent who wanted to look at our tickets. She scooted us aside and proceeded to review another couple's voucher. We stood aside watching the entire group of folks who were on our last bus get on the different bus while we waited and waited until that bus was completely full. The ticket agent walked away, leaving us standing there. We waited 20 minutes for another bus to come, but it was full. Finally, we decided to leave and just take the Tube back to our hotel. What a total crock!

My sister and I had a bad experience on this tour today. We got on at stop 1 and were not told that many stops would be skipped due to road closures. Our driver drove us back and forth on Oxford Street until we finally decided to get off of the bus.

Later, when trying to get on at another stop, a tour guide from a different company approached us to tell us a bus probably wasn't coming. The Big Bus staff member standing nearby did not try to talk to us.

When we finally got on a bus 40 minutes later, the driver skipped some stops we were excited about. Not only that, but we never saw a "red line" bus again - which was unfortunate because we paid extra for a live tour guide. We had to listen to the recording.

We understand that road closures are not the fault of the tour bus company - but we would have gone on the tour on a different day had we known half the stops would be skipped. This wasted an entire day of our vacation, which is really a shame.

We decided to go with the big bus and weren't disappointed! The live tours were great; very entertaining - learned new things on the same routes with different drivers. It was very convenient with 2 kids under 8. We were also there for the Brexit demonstrations and our 24 how pass was honored for 2 days due to roads closed and slower service! It was also cool to see things off the normal tour and the live tour guide and great at trying to tell us stuff. We also took advantage of the boat from the Tower to West Minister, which provided new info and the kids enjoyed but crew asked for tips, which was a bit of a bummer - bus ones never did and really appreciated!

We waited and waited and waited ( you get the jist) for the bus to arrive next to Buckingham palace but it didn't turn up. All the other buses and tours turned up but our business must of got lost. I know there were protesters marching around London but all the other companies came by. We paid £27.00 each for our tickets. This is a total joke
We asked the chap at the bus stop and he just kept saying 5 mins. We quit are almost 40 mins of waiting and got a taxi. Come on shape up BIG BUS TOURS..

We took the tube to Victoria Station and bought a one-day pass for Big Bus Tours that cost £28 each. It would have been cheaper to buy it online, but we weren't traveling with a printer, so we couldn't do that.
They promised that these buses come every 5-15 minutes and off we went to the bus stop. We waited and waited and after about 25 minutes, got talking to a man who had been waiting for almost an hour. He said if he could do it over he would go with another hop on/hop off company. We went back to the kiosk and switched our tickets for another company. When we got back to the main bus stop, a Big Bus was just leaving, so we estimate that it about an hour's wait there. This is not a worthwhile thing to spend your money on.

We ordered this ahead of time thinking it would be the perfect way to see the city.

The good: When on a red tour the guide provided interesting commentary.

The bad: Blue tours only have canned commentary, which is not always timed with the location and repeated.
Also, even though the ticket is for 24 hrs. You can't ride past 6pm ... seemed like you had to take the night bus, which was not the same route.
Plus, the red tours cut off early so you really don't get the good commentary except earlier in the day.
Lastly, the top level was usually full so you were stuck riding on the lower level which didn't give you a good view of the sights.

My recommendation is to buy a visitor Oyster card ahead of time and ride the public transportation. The Underground in London is very easy to use and is very safe as the cameras are always monitoring the underground for vagrants and pick pocketers.

Verdict: Under normal circumstances, their service should be identical with other companies. However, if unexpected disruptions happen (in our case, Black Lives Matter protest), the two major competitors are miles ahead at keeping their buses running. So please only buy the tickets after you've made sure that there's nothing unusual happening for the rest of the day.

Time of travel: Sunday 10 July 2016
There was a marathon, so some closure was expected. (The Green Park stop was, however, also closed although this was not included on the list of stops to be closed on the day on the Big Bus website.) We were redirected by a very nice employee to the Queen Mother's Gate (apologies if I get the name wrong). We waited for half an hour with at least five buses from the Golden Tour and three or four from the Original Tour passing by. The answer I got from asking the staff re: the estimated waiting time was, in verbatim, "Five minutes." I can't tell where he got the information to support his claim but he was rather visibly abrupt and flippant, perhaps from all the complaints he'd got so far. He blamed the road closure and seemed unfazed when I pointed out that other companies also followed similar routes.

The situation got worse as we were on the same roads also being used by Black Lives Matter protesters. There is nothing else the driver could have done so I did not mind that.

The most appalling appoint of comparison was when we were waiting to "hop on" again after hopping off for late lunch. We also waited at Aldwych for half an hour, and were unable to find a seat on the first bus that arrived due to a huge number of customers that accumulated. As you'd expect at this point, we saw at least five buses from each competitors (Golden and Original) stopping there and collecting all their customers smoothly.

The next day, however, we saw very many Big Buses around London as the situation returned to normal. Therefore the problem was not the disruption in service itself, but the relative lack of competence on Big Bus's part to manage unexpected situations.

We took the Red Route tour this morning and had a lovely time, all the way from Marble Arch to Westminster Pier. The commentary was lively and humorous, and the traffic was pretty good (until we got to Fleet Street). We left the tour at Westminster to explore the area on foot, then tried to rejoin the tour at stop 22 (between Westminster Abbey and the Houses of Parliament). A sign at the bus stop indicated that Big Bus was no longer serving that bus stop. So we walked to stop 23 (near the St James Park tube station), where we found another sign indicating that Big Bus wasn't serving that bus stop either. So we had to walk all the way to Buckingham Palace to find a bus stop that the company was actually serving. Yet, we had talked to three different Big Bus employees about the route, and none of them indicated that there were any bus stops that weren't served, nor did their map say so.

When we rejoined the bus, we were on a Blue Route bus (the route without a live commentary). The bus was supposed to provide a recorded commentary, but the system wasn't working properly. The soundtrack crackled annoyingly until it died completely before we even reaching the very first stop. By that point, the bus trip was like any ordinary bus trip, only at a greatly inflated price.

Also, their pricing plan isn't very transparent. I looked up the price online the night before, and it quoted a price for a family (2adults, 2 children) would cost £64.50. But when we bought the tickets this morning, the cost was £79. The Big Bus employee explained that there was a difference between the online price and the walk-up price, but that was never mentioned on the website.

We really enjoyed the first part of our tour, but the misleading pricing and the curtailing of service (with no forewarning) left a bad taste in my mouth. I wouldn't feel comfortable recommending this service to other visitors.

I bought two tickets that included London Eye and River Cruise for Two days cost around £65 per person
The bus tours are ok, you get to see all the sights and can hop on and off as often as you like, but beware some buses the ones that have a person telling you about london (as opposed to the tape playing where you use earplugs) this I think is called the red route - the buses were packed with people - often no seats available, but the other buses were all fine! the highlight was London Eye and the River Cruise, the bus tour well... if you don't have too much time its the best way to see all the highlights (as in many other cities around the world) so I guess one shouldn't moan.
Basically covered all the main highlights of London over the two days and so was well worth it

Many reviews have noted that the delays in London traffic contribute to a poor experience. I will say that this is true for all similar tours in London - there is simply no way around that.

However, I will also suggest that Buyers Beware when buying tickets from this company. They post a reasonable price (22£) for an "Orientation Tour" on their website. However, they do not post any prices on the brochures they give out on the street. Once we were on the bus and the bus started moving, we were told that price would be 32£. I later contacted the Customer Service Rep and was told that the Orientation Tour is only available via the website, and that the cheapest "street ticket" is a 24 hour ticket that is 10£ more expensive. This is a classic Bait and Switch scheme.

Beyond that, the recorded commentary was perhaps the worst I have ever heard on a Hop-On Hop-Off Bus Tour - it provided very little in the way of interesting information about this great city that has so much history. Most of time was spent listening to filler music, rather than actual commentary.

We have had the pleasure of going on many Hop-On Hop-Off tours in cities around the world, and never had a bad experience until now. This was our first (and last) tour on a Big Bus Tour. I would encourage readers to consider any of the other major tour providers.

Jeff S.

This was an awesome experience! We bought a 24-hour hop on hop off pass. HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS COMPANY! Very friendly staff. There are 4 different tour routes. We spent the majority of our time on the Red Tour, which has a live tour guide the entire route. Steven was our guide and he was great! Learned so many cool, quirky things about the city that you might not have known from reading a guidebook. Anytime we saw a monument we wanted to see, a picture worth taking, or a restaurant to grab a bite, we hopped off the bus and it was only ever a 15 min wait max to catch the next one! For only having 48 hours in London (as we were just passing through), Big Bus Tours is a great way to experience the city for the first time, especially from a rooftop seat. :)

The tour started out with LOTS of people-- too many for the bus we had all been waiting for. It was a VERY long wait. We were told that we could get the same route a short way down and it wouldn't be so crowded. Hop on and hop off and hop on another bus. Sounds easy, right? Wrong. We got on OK, us and lots of others but the bus tour was changed midstream and to see what we had wanted to see took over 4 1/2 hours! BE SURE YOU KNOW THE BUS IS THE ONE YOU WANT AND THE ROUTE WON'T CHANGE. AND MIND YOUR COLORS! BLUE RED ORANGE? If your Big Bus guy who is collecting your money is Rashid Saleem- find another bus!
Like a dummy, I took another tour on the Big Bus the next day- thinking that it had to just be that one- how could this company be so lousy at what they do? And, yup, you guessed it, it was the same thing! I asked if this bus would return to where I got on with no midstream changes and I was told yes. Nope. Fool me once shame on them, fool me twice shame on me. I will NEVER take a Big Bus tour again. It really is a Big Bus(t)!

This was really very very good. Tour guides on the red buses were mostly funny and knowledgeable and that is where this service seems to be better than most others. Must give a huge mention to Steve, who has just so much knowledge and is very amusing with it too. Said he was only in his first season as well. How do you guys store all the facts. Did the river cruise from Tower of London, but I did feel a little upset that you felt almost obliged to give tips on the boat. Steve got a tip on the bus because he was good and deserved it, although even on the buses, some guides were asking for tips. It was a great day out and we saw all the main sites that we wanted too.

Loved the hop on hop off bus as time was limited but we wanted to see as much as possible of London.The Big bus has red and blue buses travelling almost the same routes The blue has taped commentary the red has live commentary .We boarded at Baker Street on the blue bus and loved the taped commentary..All the staff we met were helpful and knowledgeable and we got off in Trafalgar square.We were recommended to try the red bus as they have live commentary but we didn't enjoy the lady as her delivery was way too loud as we were close to her on the upper deck and not very spontaneous .Luckily we were only going one stop so chose to wait for the blue buses for the rest of the tour We chose to do the boat trip on the Thames and this was superb.We had a great river man doing a commentary and he brought the river alive was well informed with a fab sense of humour.We booked on the day so it was slightly more expensive than if you had booked on line working out at £32 a person ..entry into most attractions is extra so it was quite an expensive day .Recommended you buy a package if you think you will want to visit sevearal attractions .
We really enjoyed the day..

We had a great day in London. The Big Bus Tour was great fun. The red tour is a very reliable route served by many buses and lots of staff. Towards the end of the day, we had planned to get a Green Route bus back to St Pancras. Unfortunately, after waiting more than 30 mins in the cold we hailed a taxi to return us back to the station. This was the only disappointment and did slightly ruin the day, as we had anticipated returning back on the Green Route to make our travel arrangements easier!

Our group of six found the hop-on-hop-off Big Bus tour to be an efficient and informative way to see the major sites of London and get to know the area. The boat ride down the Thames provided an interesting perspective of the city. Much better views from the top deck. Worth the cost of the ticket, and easy to figure out the schedule.

We were a big group and it was cold and rainy but we still sat upstairs. The bus provided those rain ponchos. The tour guide gives a lot of info which was wonderful to hear, on the next bus though we listened to a recorder for the info.
There was a place to park our push chairs. It really needs a full day ,sadly the places we wanted to check out closed at 5 , the same time we arrived there.
The whole group enjoyed it. Some of us got tired and went back in a cab the rest went on the boat ride and continued the whole route.

This is by far one of the best things we did in London. Many thanks to our terrific tour guide Big Steve for making this such a fun two hours. Steve mixed the historical with the contemporary as he guided us through the London streets. From a 60 ad Roman wall to James Bond movie sites , Steve kept us informed and entertained . The bus was clean and the tour was delightful . There are so many photo opportunities on the route. If you can only do one this while in London pick this Big Bus Tour. We hopped on at 8:30 in the morning when the crowds were light and the tour dropped us off near the palace in time for the changing of the guards. Big Steve even gave us some practical advice on where to stand to avoid some of the crowds. Do not miss the Big Bus Tour ... Ask for Big Steve!

I was really looking forward to touring on the bus with my family visiting from New York City. Buses were meant to come every 15 minutes, but were frequently delayed and at one point took 45 minutes between buses. And when they came, most were jammed with people and there we no seats upstairs (and even sometimes downstairs), so we had to stand at times.

The Red tour is the most popular, hence being packed, whereas the Yellow tour seemed less packed, but offered lesser known attractions to see and no live commentary. Given what we spent for eight of us, this was a bitterly disappointing experience, and we ultimately wasted hours seeing very little in our one day in London, when we could have seen far more via our own efforts of another potential tour.

I love these tours. I want to see as much as I can and in as little time as possible. With the bus tours you get art, history, architecture and a way around the city. I bought a week long pass and I used it as transport. There are so many different lines it can take you just about anywhere you want to go be it shopping or Big Ben and a show.

I have been in many cities, always have been riding with Big Bus tours for our sightseeings.

This time it was really disappointing!

First...we expected to get as much information as possible, as happened before. Not this time. There were dozens and dozens of unaswered questions and missing stories. There were only basic informations. Most of the time the music was playing and really not a lot of stories and facts were told!

Secondly...about the music...if it would have been just a few minutes of music - ok... But when you are in a bus riding for 2 hours and about 90 minutes you have to listen to the music....please dont play march music. Your customers will go nuts.

Thirdly...the music was much louder than the voice, so I permamently had to fiddle around with the volume.

In one bus the channels could not be changed, in another one the volume could not be changed.

But the straw to break the camel's back was, that one driver drove off without opening the doors and and did not let us in (bus was almost empty).
We were in front of the bus and the bus driver managed to get off without us.

None of this you expect from Big Bus Tours.

The initial interaction of buying the tickets was easy. The only mishap was that the salesman told us the bus we were getting on had a live tour guide but it didn't (this happened a couple more times with other similar companies within the UK, so there may be some miscommunication between the bus coming in and the sales people...so double check to make sure you get the narration you'd like - whether it's live or audio). That being said, the driver was very clear about where to get off if we did want to switch to a bus with a live tour guide and we did. It was just a stop or two and we didn't miss much.

So, that's when we met Ollie! He was amazing. We really had every intention of getting off the bus, exploring some of the touristy locations and then jumping back on a different Big Bus to continue our day, but we just didn't want to leave Ollie's bus! He was very clear and concise and his history lessons were super interesting and engaging. In addition, he was very helpful to the passengers coming off and on, helping them answer any questions they may have had regarding logistics of where they're going and the quickest way to get there (whether it was part of the tour or not). My sister and I kept saying "ok, next stop we'll get off..." and ended up spending the whole 3 hours on there! We couldn't believe how fast the time flew by. We got off our original pick up location and just walked to some of the locations Ollie talked about. I would he could travel with us and show the rest of Europe!

We purchased the 48 hour pass for our stay in London and must say it was well worth it. The buses stop everywhere you would expect showing you all of the main tourist attractions. The 48 hour pass allows you onto the night tour and also a return boat ride to Greenwich! Well worth the money to get your bearings and allow you to see everything during your stay. Make sure you sign up for Big Bus as there are many similar services in the area.

This tour definitely had potential to be wonderful. The plan was to get a lift around London, see the sights, get off and on, and save walking everywhere. The disappointment was they crammed the buses as full as possible preventing the majority of patrons to see the sights. They should limit each bus and not allow people standing. The positive, however is the tour guides were perfection. Very knowledgeable, especially the river portion.

We had used Big Bus in Rome earlier on the same trip, and were hesitant to try them in London, however the concierge at our hotel recommended them. The first night we had a great time on the night tour, with wonderful staff both at the bus stop and on the bus.
There seemed to be enough buses, but service ended at 6pm, leaving us stranded across town from our hotel, when the driver refused to pick us up at 6:05 (we had been waiting at the bus stop since 5:40pm). There were other customers at the same stop with us, where were also left stranded.
Overall, we were pleased with the very friendly staff and there were plenty of buses mid-day, but it was frustrating that service ended at 6pm despite daylight lasting until 10pm, and "nighttime" buses roaming the city (no hop on/hop off at night).

Absolutely terrible - I recommend you use one of the many other hop on hop off bus operators that are available and who run much more frequently.

Poor customer service and poor attitudes by the ticket sellers and drivers was the biggest negative. One actually swore at me in the presence of my children when I expressed my disappointment at the lateness of the bus (20 minutes for the FIRST pick up of the day).Overall the staff don't seem interested. The bus maps are outdated and do not clearly show where the actual stop is. Most buses don't have live commentary which is OK, but the drivers don't even announce the stops over the speaker. Not once was the wait time at any stop less than 15 minutes

I chose Big Bus tours based on previously good experiences in other cities but I won't be making the same mistake again.

Although it would have been a great deal if it had worked out correctly... it didn't so it wasn't.. I bought on line and they text me my code. In order to get your free boat ride and your London Eye fast track pass you HAVE to have a Big Bus worker print them out. There wasn't one on our green line bus so that complicated things. The bus driver was not helpful. I'd recommend the red line because at least there's live commentary with someone to ask questions of. The red line only has ear phone to plug in a listen but it does have multiple languages. Better yet. take the subway to Westminster and forget the bus.. too much traffic... too forever to get to where you were going...

So much time wasted, after buying our tickets, we waited on the bus for about 20 ,minutes before the tour actually started, many roads closed due to a parade so some of the stops were closed which we were not made aware of before we purchased our tickets. Not very easy to hop back on, we were on our way back to our hotel when they asked us to get off the bus and wait for another one as they were changing the route from red to blue so they wouldn't be going to our stop anymore. We had to stand in the rain and wait on another bus for another 20mins or so which meant we missed our dinner reservations. Wouldn't do it again, very disappointing.

The bus tour is ok as you can hop on and off at various sites to go explore further. I did not like the fact that you have to go to another station to catch the bus. But all in all it is a magnificent ride

Today we used the big bus London. We have used them before in Las Vegas. Booking was easy bus was clean and tidy staff were very helpful and knowledgeable. Lots of stops to choice from. Booklets and leaflets a very good as well. Well worth doing.

A great way to see all the sights. Even managed to work it in with our trip home so we didn't have to catch the underground to our international train trip. The staff at each stop are really helpful they are pretty much at every stop and ready to help.
Did the big bus tour in Paris and the stops were not as frequent as those in London and staff not as readily available. So highly recommend the London big bus. Way better value for money than the underground.

We had only a day to see London. We decided on using the Big Bus company on recommendation from our concierge. We started at 9 a.m. The weather was cold and rainy at times. We were able to go on all the routes plus use the boat ticket. The boat ticket allowed us to take a ride on the Thames. Definitely worth seeing London from the water. We stayed on the bus and listened to the English audio. You are given nice ear buds to use. We got off at several locations and shopped then got off near London Bridge and had a traditional Sunday Roast. The took a nice walk along the Thames to get to the boat dock. We took the boat to Wesminister Pier. Afterward, we got on the green line and took the last bus which dropped us off at our hotel. The buses ran on this Sunday from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. Great way to see London and get to the sites whether you have a short amount of time or are here longer. Best 30 pounds we spent. The tube cost us 5 pounds for one way in one zone.

A very good (though not the cheapest) way to see London is making use of Big Buses hop-on-off tours. Commentation available either live (in English) or in 12 different languages. Try to avoid though summer Saturdays as usually public festivities will block Trafaklgar Sqaure are (we did hit Pride) and disrupt normal operations.

I've been to London before, but this was the first time I've taken a bus tour. It allowed us to see so much more than we could on foot, and the vantage position of being up high gave us better visibility than one has on foot.

We also took the cruise from Westminster to The Tower. It's only 30 minutes, but informative and enjoyable, due to the live guide.

Buyer beware: only the red line has a live guide. The other lines use earbuds which are commonly out of sync with the bus position, due to traffic.

Also, we bought our tickets at the St. Paul's information center. Seemed reputable. We paid for tickets that were 24 hour, but to the end of the 2nd day. When we got to the bus stop, the employee said they would only honor them for 24 hours.

We got on one of these buses when we come out of kings cross station to get into London. We were told 3 different prices from 2 of there workers but ended up getting it cheaper than first told !! We didn't really use the buses as much as we should have but when we was on the bus it was very good especially sat on top as we saw more of London than we have before. You also get a Thames river boat ride as part of the ticket which we used and was very interesting. We didn't know it was gay pride parade the day we used the buses so some roads were closed so it didn't go where it should have but you can hop on and off all day on different buses and routes so can get almost anyway.

When in London there is no better way to get an overview of this vast city than to Hop on Hop Off with these guys. The routes are clearly marked, each stop has good friendly people to help you. The only negative would be the river cruise aspect. Make sure you check the fine print if going to Greenwich. Otherwise a really good value purchase on transport in London!

This was our first family trip to London and we were advised to take a Big Bus Tour to orient ourselves and see some of the major attractions. We took the red line route almost in its entirety without getting off. We intended to use the bus as an attraction in and of itself, so this suited us well. As far as actual transportation, this is a poor choice. If we truly wanted to visit a few attractions in one day, we'd have been better served using public transit. Also, the route seemed to double back on itself three times, so it's didn't exactly offer the best overview of the city either. Overall, it was pleasant, but I would not say it's a must.

This is a great way to learn about a city and to learn where things are. We hopped off in several places and never had a problem catching a bus when we wanted to. We were quite amazed at how efficient they were and this was on a bank holiday weekend when London was FULL of people. They even did a good job on Sunday when many of the roads they use were closed down in the morning because of a 10K run. The river tour was quite nice as well. It gave a different perspective on things and was great for picture taking. Highly recommend this.

We bought the 2 days tickets at our hotel after the promise of a good way to experience the city and even use as means of transport during our stay.

What we experienced was delays, instead of promised 10-20 min between the busses the norm was more likely 30-45 min in between.

In addition we experienced poor information, non advised stops for up to 20 min.

We have tried bus tours around the major cities in Europe. This is by far the worst experience of them all.
Strongly suggest you choose one of the other companies that offers tours in London.

June 2016

Staff service levels are patchy. At our first pick up point, the driver we spoke to was very helpful and directed us to the route we wanted (the bus behind him). That second bus driver was grumpy, monosyllabic and unhelpful - I said 'great start!' to my friends and the bus driver overheard and had a go at us?! Though the guide was funny and helpful which made up for it. The quality of commentary was very mixed from bus to bus however. The River Cruise (which is why we upgraded to the 24 hour tour rather than the orientation tour, as we were told the river was included in the 24 hr version) was actually only between Tower Bridge and Embankment rather than the full river run to greenwich, for which we would have had to pay extra. The marketing for this is therefore misleading. Also the staff (and ticket info) claimed it was a 'free bonus' trip but paying £4 for access to this river section on the '24 hour ticket' is not a free bonus really is it. In addition, we were encouraged to tip the guy who gave the river commentary as he said it was voluntary. The only reason we went on the river trip rather than going on a normal commercial clipper was to get the commentary. So again, misleading and somewhat disappointing to hear that this is not officially part of the tour and we're expected to pay extra for the commentary. Finally, there were parts of the tours where the buses absolutely rushed past places of interest, with no commentary and no chance to really look at the locations. Why the rush? N.B.
