Don't expect to see views of Buckingham Palace from the Blue Route. You get driven down a back road nearby so unless you hop off, you won't see it. Quite disappointing over all.

We used the big bus tours today as thought it would be a nice way to see some of the other sights that we hadn't got time to visit properly. We were sold a family ticket and a few individual tickets at a cost of £85 which to be honest is a lot of money. What we were not told is that half of the red and blue line routes had been cut out because of the queens 90th birthday celebrations so apart from the tower bridge/tower of London and Westminster abbey we barely saw anything. To be honest it felt like being on a double decker bus at home stuck in traffic for some of it. I wouldn't pay for it again

we took this bus because we had a very short stay in London and figured this was the best way to get a glimpse of the city's highlights. and to that end we were not disappointed. the big problem we had was the guide. he was hard to understand because the acoustics were so poor. making a microphone louder is not always the best way to make the speaker easier to understand. as it turned out, I had a very hard time making out much of what he was saying so that diminished my experience. the sights are very nice - London Tower, London Eye, not to mention the serious amount of construction going on in the city. there were cranes everywhere. bottom line: great to use this service to get a great glimpse of the city in a relatively short period of time.

My husband and I made a quick day trip to London to see all the major attractions. We took the bus big tours and are glad we did. It literally stops at all the major spots and let's you hop on or hop off wherever you wish. You catch the next bus when you're finished walking around and taking pics. The open top is a nice feature and allows you to enjoy the sun while touring. Only on the red route do you have English commentary from a live person otherwise you use headphones on all the other routes and can select from several languages.

My 17 year old son and I went to London last Thursday and bought two tickets for the big bus costing us £56. Starting at Covent gardens we just hopped on and off, if the roads were busy we got off and then walked a bit then got back on. We had bought tickets for the London eye and got off at the bus stop very close by. The commentary was very good, not too much but enough to keep you interested. The drivers And ticket sellers at the bus stops were very informative and at 1600hours we were able to get back to kings cross. We would definitely use big bus again and would recommend it to see all the major sights in London.

We only had an overnight in London, so we decided to take this bus tour to get an overview of the city (and to help plan our return trip!) We had Joanna as a tour guide, and she was awesome. She was funny and informative, and she was a complete pro. We are so glad we got on the bus with Joanna!

Big bus tour was the choice after many research comparing other tours. Bought the 48H tickets online and showed to the staff at the bus stop. He scanned the QR code and gave me a physical ticket. There were traffic conjestion at a few places like after the Tower Bridge stop, to note. Boarded the wrong bus at the london eye stop in front of Marriot. Went round the Tower Bridge again, wasted time. There wasn't west bound or east bound written on the map so we didn't know. There were ear pieces and poncho provided in the bus. The night tour went by pretty fast. Didn't manage to go for the cruise.

We had a terrible experience with big bus. The traffic was so bad we could barely see anything. They communicated very poorly and once we got to London it took is 3 hours to get out tickets. The staff of big bus was also very rude and unhelpful.

Having only two days in London (Sunday and Monday in early June), we decided on the Big Bus Hop on, Hop off tour as the best way to see the sights. Highlites - on Sunday when the traffic was relatively light, the tour was OK, we got to see the sights from the bus and get oriented in the city. The Multi-language earbud narration was a bit out of sync with the bus location but travel from point A to B was good enough. Much of the recorded narration is music without comments anyway. The Thames River Cruise was the best part of the day despite being only 20 or so minutes long. Lowlites - then came Monday when 14 of 45 headphone narration connection points on the top floor of the bus were inoperable, picture elderly travelers moving around while to bus was in motion trying to find a successful narration connection, the sync was much further off, traffic was horrendous (>50 minutes to travel the couple miles from St Paul's to Big Ben), the driver cut off a portion of the trip - perhaps to catch up on the schedule and rearranged another section causing confusion about when to get off for a number of people, 5-10 minutes wait times were stretched as three of the competitor's buses came by at the St Paul's stop) and best of all the ticket sales guys from Big Bus and another company got into an argument at the stop. Five minutes later both were trying to strong arm a sale from a family who stopped to inquire about cost. Their behavior caused the family to walk away.
Our suggestion is to find another way as the Big Bus clearly has no interest in providing a quality experience despite taking ~$90 for two tickets.

We've travelled with big bus tours for a couple of hourd during a business conference.
Our tour was made unforgettable by our tour guide daniel who was funny and instructive. We learned a lot!!! Its been great.

Go on this tour. You get to see all the best bits of London. And, you get a really good guide. Ours was Steve, and my husband set out to test him from the start. Sorry mate. But, he answered everything with good humor and was very funny, even suggesting that if i needed a good lawyer, in my marriage, he could help me out. Met him on 2nd day too and he remembered us, even convincing me to do this trip review. Drivers fantastic, especially Paul. Sales staff at Hyde Park really good too and saved money on tickets. Overall, great fun. Loved it. Thought kids would be bored, but even they managed to stay off mobiles whilst on the bus. Bad jokes though...:)

The whole family enjoyed the live commentary...our guide Leo was outstanding! He had a great knowledge of the city, lots of fun facts and enjoyed interacting with the passengers. I've done severs hop on hop off bus tours in London and Big Bus is consistently the best.

This bus tour was recommended to me by the clerk at my hotel. I usual do hop on hop off tours my first time in a city...but I question that strategy in London. London traffic is heavy so my experience amounted to a very slow, dull, expensive bus trip. Live commentary was advertised but not available most of my time, Usually just very limited multilingual taped guide heard through plug in airline head phones Drivers were not unfriendly but certainly not enthusiastic hosts. There are a number of intersecting bus routes so planning and time management are essential. At end of day ended up waiting at bus stop in rain for 30 or 40 minutes for pick up as many other bus tour buses came and went. The other bus tour companies may deliver a vibrant experience: my recommendation is to skip the Big Bus.The tube (subway)is by far the quickest way to traveling London Much easier, time and cost efficient to do a little research up front and take the tube and walk to sites.

I was with family from overseas and wasn't keen to do the bus tour. I've been to London many times, on business, so I really didn't expect to enjoy it. It was a revelation, a great way to see a lot f the city quickly, but sitting on the top deck, I could see all the things I missed walking around. The tour guides were great and made a real effort to engage people. We did the tour on a Saturday so the roads were busy, meaning the tour guides had to work hard to fill the gas between stops. The boat tour was a nice little extra. Heading to Paris next and I'll do the same again, but spread it over two days.

I have just spent 4 days in London. It is a fabulous city. What made my experience the BEST it could be was THE BIG BUS TOUR. It was fun and informative. Seriously, I learned more than I ever did from my history books. It is a double deck bus so your viewing ability is great. You can get off at any stop, look around for awhile, and get on again at any given stop. It is VERY convenient. You will see ALL of the wonderful landmarks ...AND MORE. The guides are entertaining as well, to add to the experience, and THE DRIVERS....OH MY GOSH, THE DRIVERS....ARE THE BEST I HAVE EVER SEEN. ( I am 68 years old and have seen a lot of driving ) But these drivers are skilled beyond belief. If you want the best possible experience, I promise you, THE BIG BUS TOURS is the best choice if you really want to get the most for your vacation......Linda Jackson....Atlanta, U.S.A.

This was one of the less expensive bus tours in London. I noticed their stops were a little further from the attractions so I'm guessing that is way their fees were a little cheaper. Their blue and red line system is confusing because they travel the same routes. They claim the only difference is live audio and recorded yet when we got on the red line there was no live narrator despite their "guarantee." I would do it again but this time I would select the free river cruise (30 mins one way) because you can access the boat from the tower of london.

Big Bus tour is very reliable in terms of service and they always cover great landmarks. But I feel London is too big and if you have less than a week stay, it's more convenient to visit attraction directly using underground or taxi. That way we can explore and cover more attraction, bearing in mind that all tourist attraction will be closed at 5 pm.

We only had one full day in London and it poured almost the whole day. The concierge at our hotel suggested we did a hop on hop off tour as a way to see the city with a limited amount of time and weather not cooperating. We are so glad we did! Even if the weather was perfect this still would have been a great way to see the city. We eventually ended up on a bus with Leo as the tour guide and he was so knowledgable and a joy to talk with, we decided to stay on with him to the very end of the tour route. All the guides were great but if you find yourself on a red line bus with Leo you won't be disappointed! The bus was clean, and free wifi which came in handy for those of us without international plans! The only downfall I would say was there didn't seem to be a lot of red line buses running, for every one red line bus that came there seem to be 3 or 4 of another tour bus company, but it may have been because of the weather. Still 5 stars, great tour, clean, wonderful tour guides, really enjoyed!!

All the main bus tours seem to cover roughly the same routes / sights so we picked Big Bus Tours on the strength of pleasant salesman at Victoria Station (he wasn't at all pushy) and the promise of a live guide on the red routes.
Visited over the May bank holiday weekend, the buses were very busy on Saturday afternoon and we had to wait for a couple of full ones to pass before getting seats on the open top deck. Sunday morning was much more quieter with plenty of space.
A complete circuit of the red route, which covered all the main sights took about 2 1/2 hours. All the live guides were very informative, humorous and happy to answer questions.

Bought a 24h ticket from a salesman by the aquarium. I think We paid 33£ p.p. I thought it was way too expencive for a tour, but the salesman guaranteed that we could use it also for a boat ride down to the O2 stadium the same night. We were going to see Adele, so told when it started and he said we then could take the boat leaving London eye at XX:XX pm. But when it came to it, the boat schedule was hard to read, and there was no boat leaving at the promised time. I don't know if the guy lied to make us buy or was mistaken. Anyways not pleasant.

But the tour it self was nice! Should spend the day touring, and having the time to actually "hop on and off". Plenty of museums and shopping. We got earphones to plug in for a "guide" in a chosen language, it was interesting. Sat up on 2nd floor, great view. Best on a sunny day, at least not rainy.

I got a 2 day pass for the BIg Bus. This included a boat ride and 3 walking tours.It was a great value. We were able to get on and off and saved time as well as money. Our guide for the tour for the Changing of the Guard was Kevin. He knew exactly where to take us so we could see.There are other companies and I wold thin they are pretty much the same.

We only had a weekend in London. I'd been many times but my wife had only been as a child and it was my son's first trip, so we decided to take a tour on the Big Bus. It was very comprehensive and well done. Plenty of stops. Plenty of busses to hop onto. Great itinerary. The audio was useful (only problem was poor headphone jacks on one of the busses). Price was reasonable. I am not typically a big fan of the packed in bus tour but we all really enjoyed this one.

We bought the 2 day pass (buy 1 day and get 1 day free) and were able to see all the great sites London has to offer. Buy your pass online before you go to London - it is cheaper and you get better discounts. Don't buy their extra tours - not worth it. Also if you can get on the bus with the Tour Guide named Danielle then go for it. She was the best. The other tour guides weren't very good. The bus did come on regular intervals - we only had to wait one time at the stop near the Big Ben - then the bus took 30 minutes to come. So I would say shop around and see if the other companies are better. Take the red line which has a live tour guide, the other two lines have a recording and that wasn't very good.
We also took 1 of their walking tours - which was pretty good. The Harry Potter one - it was led by a tour guide named Ken. They showed us all the sites where the movie was filmed. We didn't have time to take their night tour or their other walking tours. They had all these included in the price. So if you are staying for 3 days or less then you don't get the bang for your buck. Don't buy the hop on/hop off if staying 3 or less days.

If you are wanting to see the sights of London with or without kids you need this pass there are stops literally everywhere, usually with BigBus tours tour guides which are incredibly helpful, not just trying to pushy sell but advise you and then tell the (friendly) bus drivers were you are heading who then shout out to let you know its your stop. kids thought it was amazing on an open top bus and at 3 and 5 seemed happy enough to go all the way around, they also have a stop outside kingscross station so actually saved us the fare/stress of the tube so all around fantastic

Bad company compared to the other 5 top off bus tour in london
They do not respect clients
Urge of mony
On 30 may ther was am event in London so some streets where closed
Other companies diverted there routs but continued
Big bus gett an off day
Very few buses
You need to wait for triple time
Green line closed though has nothing with event
Even after event finished they continued same
Eventually i left them and used taxi instead
I don't recommend them in london

We had two choices for the hop on-hop off experience. We choose this one. Hawkers are in front of the buses as they arrive and depart selling tickets. That made buying a ticket easy. Good way to see much of London in a few hours. Once you get to something you want to see, you merely hop off. When you are finished you go back to the bus stop and hop back on. Day was very hot so there is an inside seating option if you wish.

Two of the drivers were less than helpful; one down right rude and the other one obviously had some mental health issues. We have counseling degrees although that was necessary to figure out that there was something very odd about this one driver. His comments were inappropriate and he became enraged at times. His behavior was erratic to say the least. It was a bit disconcerting.

Brochure was semi-helpful. Could have been better written.

Last driver outside of Harrods was quite nice. He helped us get to our hotel despite the fact that we were on the last bus for the day. He gets the Gold Star for this company.

Loved the big bus tour for our first day to get a full view of the city. Our first tour guide was a dud. Midway through his shift ended and Gavin came on board as our guide and was terrific. The rest of the ride was great, scenic, informative and good humor.

Plenty of stops along the way to hop on or off at.

If you're looking for a good overview of the city from west to east you'll enjoy the Big Bus Tour.

Had to write to say what a wonderful experience we had taking a big bus tour of London, the tour guide Patrick was excellent obviously knew his stuff, clear and concise very approachable, funny. He and the driver Nigel kept us well informed of changes to the route due to a demonstration, he made it a funny and new experience! Well done both and thanks.

My wife and I had the luxury of riding on the bus tour of London with our guide, Danielle, who was most gracious, educational and comical. I was wheelchair bound and found her to be very helpful. Danielle was an absolute delight and has previously won the award as guide of the year. I couldn't recommend a better guide.

We spent most of the day yesterday hopping on and off this bus. Every single person we were in contact with from this company were so nice and helpful. Extra shout out to Rich at the marble arch bus stop and to Steve on the bus doing the information- I have never know someone to have soooo much knowledge stored in there head. Amazing experience. Thank you.

We use the sight seeing buses in most places that we visit, so decide to book on to the bus tour. The first part of the journey we had live commentary, we all agreed that this was much better than the recorded journeys.
If english is your first language then try and join a live commentary, they are a little more lighthearted with an injection of humour as well.
You can also ask questions so it is more interactive, it's a great way to get around as it covers a large area and you can hop on and off as often as you like, great way to learn about the history of this amazing place

I was very disappointed by so many rude bus drivers. We spoke to one of the staff selling tickets near our Paddington hotel and because we wanted a 24 hour ticket from late in the afternoon he advised us that he wouldn't be selling tickets late in the afternoon but he said we could hop on the bus and the driver would be able sell us a ticket. However later that afternoon when we got on the bus and said we wanted to buy our tickets the driver told us to get off and we had to get off and go and purchase a ticket at our hotel. By the time we bought our ticket it made us late for where we wanted to go. The next day we also experienced some very rude bus drivers. The route that the buses went was really good and suited us for what we wanted to see and it was a bonus that we got a river cruise included for the price. The only staff member we found helpful was a guy called Charlie who was friendly and he really looked after us and gave us good advice while waiting for a bus on Westminster Bridge.

The sign at the bus stop said talk to bus driver for tickets, as we stepped onto the bus and asked for 6 tickets the driver said we could not buy them from him. Then continued to be quite rude when we told him that's what the Big Bus sign told us to do. We will not be using this line ever and used another great line called The Original who were very helpful and did a great tour.

Yet another successful and enjoyable tour of London and short cruise with new visitors to this city who weren't disappointed by the wonderful sites and particularly helpful staff! Extra time on the bus and a bonus with new sites as a result of a diversion on that particular day.
Highly recommended!

We took the Big Bus around London and it was well worth it. I did not have a pleasant experience with the live tour, though, since the lady spoke too fast and did not seem to care whether we can see the sights or not. What was very entertaining was the ferry ride, which was included in the tour if one so wishes. One of the crew gave a very entertaining tour, although he said he was not a professional tour guide. I recommend going through hop on hop off via big bus, and take the short cruise along the river thames.

With jet lag and big city confusion, we travelled on another hop-on-hop-off line for a day and a half before realizing our mistake. Our first tour with Big Bus had live commentary by Leo, with comments by the driver Josh, and we had more fun and learned more in 10 minutes than we did the whole day on the other bus ( Golden Tours). Pay attention. Leo's comments are quick and intelligent and very entertaining. The tours with the audio are good as long as it keeps up with your location. There in noticeably more leg room. I feel the drivers of these buses deserve huge medals! Big buses in heavy traffic on twisty roads and narrow lanes, and yet it all seems to work. Top deck in the open air is great, ponchos provided if it gets wet. The 24 hour ticket is not enough to see everything, get the two day ticket with bonus tours if you have the time.

In the hotel we have purchased by internet two tickets for Big Bus.
We have paid with credit card. You have a payment copy. We tried to get the bus a the Shard. Since the construction in that area the bus does not stop there anymore.
We should have walked to the Tower. @#$%#.We went to the Big Ben and got on the bus. The bus driver told us we had the old bus routes map. Finally. With your payment receipt you get a 24 hour bus pas. if you enter the bus at 13:00, it is valid untill 13:00 the following day.
We have make the three different routes. You can get in and get out not only at the tourist places but als at the non places. Here you can enjoy the real common London.
Nice and welcoming people.

First and foremost London is expensive. During summer season big bus tickets for 48 hours, that include the river cruise and a couple other perks costs 39 GBP. Not really overly expensive but not cheap either. If you are staying outside of the tour area, an underground day pass is a good compliment. 12 GBP. We rode the red and blue line twice, jumped off at the attractions that we liked and really got a good feel of the city. Our guides on the live English speaking tour were very good. Dress for the weather so you can sit on the top deck. The view from the lower deck is pretty limited and the speakers aren't really great. However you will be out of the rain. The blue, orange and green lines come with headsets and multi language audio tour. I really enjoyed the river cruise. We went from the Westminster pier and rode all the way to Greenwich. Had a self tour there, lunch and then rode the underground back to the big bus at Green Park.

Our hotel concierge recommended the big bus over the other hop on hop off operators. I really didn't see any big difference in the routes or the benefits either way. Do your homework. Cheers, Mates

We bought a two day ticket. The audio guides are OK, but it can be difficult to see the building they are describing, and be warned there is very repetitive music in between the audio segments.

We waited 20 mins for a green route bus from Easton Station and, once that had arrived, stayed with it until we hit a connecting stop with blue and red routes, intending to get the live guide red route tour. Well, after almost forty minutes and watching two blue and two green route buses go past we finally gave in and caught the next blue bus - the third to come by with no sight of a red route bus. The poor Big Bus rep at the stop was most embarrased. Just be aware that the promise of 10-20 mins between buses is unrealistic when it comes to the red route at least.

So we rode the blue bus to St Pauls then after that finally got a red one. The guide was not too bad, however the bus did not actually take the route on the map, which is a little irritating when trying to plan.

In my opinion the tour works best when you stay on it and get the general overview...not when you try to get off and on - that just sucks up too much of your time waiting. If you have places to go you'll get a better deal catching the tube....it's not hard once you've done it a couple of times. Overall the £40 each for 48 hours of rides was not worth it.

Oh...walking back to Euston Station at about 5:45pm tonight with very sore feet we saw a green route bus stopped and tried to get on...but the driver was completely uninterested and said first he wasn't going anywhere, then second that he wasn't leaving for 12 minutes, and that Euston was within walking distance and we would get there faster to walk. It was obvious he just didn't want passengers so close to knockoff time. Sure enough 2-3 minutes later he sped past us. We caught him at the lights...he just shrugged and refused to open the doors. Not great.

I have done hop on and hop off tours many places. This was the least appreciated. Too long wait times between stops, main problem. Several companies do this sort of thing and the others seemed to have more busses available . . would see several of them come by whilst waiting for Big Bus. Part of the problem is just London, massive traffic jams on all main streets. But part of the problem seemed to be just not enough Big Busses available. If one knows London, much better off just using tube. If don't know London, will waste a full day just riding one circuit. Better than nothing, I suppose, but not by much.

Every time in London I always do the open top bus tour. I enjoyed this your better than ever thanks to the live guide, Leo. He was such a friendly helpful young man and his commentary was very informative as well as humorous. Thank you Leo.
Loved every minute of both the open top bus tour and river cruise 🎡⛴🚌🖒 well worth the money having to be able to see all the attractions in and around london 🖒🖒

Pre booked 48 hour tickets on line and printed ticket voucher at home, presented to Rep at Gloucester Rd Stop whose data terminal promptly crashed and wouldnt issue tickets, got us onto the bus without fuss but we then had to convince the rep at Marble arch to issue us with tickets caused us a bit of stress but was sorted withour drama and we got our tickets for the bus, night tour and river cruise. free rain poncho's (yes it did rain) and earphones for the recorded commentary. The commentary is reasonable but due to the very heavy traffic you get a lot of fill in music all very pleasant to start with but its a bit like being on hold on the phone, sometimes the commentary was telling you about sights you past a few minutes previously, I know London quite well but my partner was gettting frustrated looking for places that we had already passed. The hop on hop off system is great but allow loads of time as in high season particularly around westminster and the city is horendous. Be aware thatStop 19 at Westminster Pier is not at the big post marked 'Big Bus Tour stop 19' but is almost at the bridge (there is no marker so just how they expect people to know about it beats me), we were told quite bluntly "that he dont stop here its for our rest" We didnt do the night tour (couldnt face being on a bus for another couple of hours) and missed the walking tour due to being stuck in the traffic which was disappointing.
It was a very good experience. I was very short on time and Big Bus tours was an excellent option to see the important part of London. The guides were toooo good...!! The journey was very enjoyable.

Yes London is busy but this tour is painfully slow!! We seem double back all the time, often the audio is not in sync with the location of the bus which causes some confusion.

Disappointed with the route that this company take. We were given an out dated map from the sales guy which caused us to head towards a stop that was no longer used. This wasted over 90min of our valuable time!! On catching up with the bus again we complained to the staff who asked were we got the map from, I took a "new" map from the bus which still listed stop 18 - London bridge outside no. 29 Tooley street. It's not a good marketing tool to falsely advertise your route with outdated information. Pick your game up!!
Patrick from big bus was enthusiastic and informative And made everything come alive on the walking tour.

My best friend and I saw London with the Big Bus tour and absolutely fell in love with the city and our tour guide! Danielle was so helpful and knowledgable about all things London and made us tourists feel very welcome and comfortable. We stayed on the bus longer than we planned just to hear Danielle's commentary on the local history and we even looked for her the next day to have her again. I would highly recommend this company to any of my friends and family!

Book a 48hr tickett, best way to see London. We had a great time, weather was nice and the different bus routes were well thought. This said, next time we would take a different bus company such as Golden Tour or The Original Bus Tour. There seem to be more of them and run much later than Big Bus Tour. We waited at 17.20hrs by Victoria Big Bus stop with a couple of other people. By 18hrs none had come, however Golden Tour and The Oringinal Bus Tour stopped there twice whilst we waited. We had to catch a normal bus to get back to our hotel. 😡😡

I purchased 2 48hr tickets on sat 30th April, as I have done the bus tour 5 times in the last 18 months with my son and loved it, I took my sister who has mild special needs and it was a disaster from start to finish so I didn't even use the second day, the bus was diverted and we wasn't told the driver went the wrong way twice and had to reverse down narrow streets and over pavements to the sound of a lot of beeping traffic, he then proceeded to drive like a mad man to make up time I presume, I informed a staff member when we got off at the Tower of London and was told that's London for ya, my sister was too distressed to get on the 2nd day, £78 wasted, will be trying another company when we return at the end of May.

Unfortunately we used Big Bus Tours, and ended up doing a formal complaint about a driver named Simon (so he said) driving the London bus.
I was travelling with my mother in-law who has mobility problems. We rang the stop for London Waterloo, and we found it weird the driver hadn't stopped yet once we got to Waterloo bridge. I asked Simon if there was a stop at Waterloo, and his reply was straight away rude in both tone and form: "I asked if anyone wanted to leave, you didn't get up". He continued with a rude attitude throughout the conversation, when i asked "but did you open the doors?" He said clearly he had not, and if I wanted to get out, I should've gotten up.

His attitude was of "I can't care less about you, you go and sort yourself out"...

This is not acceptable. I did not get up because a moving bus is a dangerous environment for people standing, even more with the type of driving Simon was doing. My mother in-law would never get up before the bus fully stopped, and doors would open. Even if not all the above, Simon has clearly no place talking to me like the way he did.

The consequence was we had to leave next stop,and then spend money taking a London bus back to Waterloo, because my mother in-law could not walk that far.

If this is what you want for your holiday, go ahead...
Taking a hop on hop off bus is a good method to cover up all the main attraction of the city. It takes you to all the main attraction points in london.

So glad we booked the Big Bus Tours. We booked a 24 hr ticket along with the Millennium Eye and River Boat Cruise. What a great choice and easy way to see London. The guides on the boat and bus were great and very informative.
Could of done with prior warning about how to activate the ticket for boat trip and the Millennium Eye. We went straight to boat to start our 24hr period and was sent away to get the ticket activated, and again at the eye was sent away to get a ticket. But no major problem and easily resolved. The reps at the bus stops were very helpful.

We had a 48 hour ticket for The Big Bus and enjoyed every minute of it. The ticket also includes a short trip along the River Thames on a boat. The tour buses are a great way of seeing all the major attractions but also allow you to get on and off whenever, and where ever you want, so that you can spend time at the places you want to see in more detail. The Big Bus Blue route is the most comprehensive with the Red route going to the same places but is a shortened version. Unlike some tour buses we have been on the headsets were comfortable and worked perfectly.

I have been to London dozens of times but never done the bus tour before. The whole family went and really enjoyed it. The commentary (of the two different people giving it on our buses) was informative but also funny and entertaining. I thought that the price, at GBP 27 per person, was quite expensive, but then this is London. I did get to see quite a few things that I haven't seen before and the 30 minute river cruise from the Tower of London to Westminster was a nice included side trip.

You get all the highlights of London. The opportunity to get on and off, and the frequency of the busses makes this tour a great idea. On the red route you get a live tour guide which is great. I was on and off three different times and each time the tour guide was funny, informative and friendly. Shout out to Big Steve. Conversely you can go on the blue route and have a recorded tour. Many of the highlights overlap but each route does go into different parts of the city. Great bargain.

I did the pay for 2 days get the 3rd free and it was totally worth it. On a typical rainy London morning, I did the entire Blue Route in about 3 hours (traffic is crazy!) It is so easy to appreciate the city from the top of the buses, the blue bus offers an audio tour in multiple languages and the red line offers a live english commentary. The best part of the big bus tours though is the inclusion of 3 different walking tours and the river tour. Definitely the best bang for your buck and an awesome way to make the most of your time in London!

Having used the Big Bus company in the US we made the choice to use them for our one day in London. We were able to walk from our hotel to Victoria Station to buy tickets and then another short walk to catch the bus. We took the Red Line so we could get live narration and ask questions. It was a bit chilly up top but I wasn't going to miss the beautiful views from up there. We only got off to take the free river cruise (which we took roundtrip) and have some snacks. We then finished off the red line loop.

A great way for those of us with limited mobility - and limited time - to see all the sights. Would definitely do it again.

Had been to london a few times but never been on a tour so we decided to as a family of four, loves every second of it its fair to say not like other bus tours that the kids got bored half way through Danielle kept it entertaining

We enjoyed the Big Bus Tour. It's a great way to see the major attractions of the city. You can hop-on/hop-off and the Red Line has live tour narration from a tour guide, which makes it more interesting than hearing from a recording. We also took the river cruise and the Changing of the Guard walking tour...which is amazing! The walking tour guide Steve was great!

Even though it was cold and sometimes rainy the day we chose for the Big Bus Tour, we still had a great time. Leane #bigbusleane - was great as our singing tourguide! Only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was that because of President Obama's visit on the same day, some of the routes were closed or delayed. Still a great way to see London.

Really enjoyed the Big Bus in London . Everyone was very nice including Jackie working out of her "office" ( stationary bus) by the Marble Arch. We were able to see so much and really enjoyed the walking tour as well as the river boat . Only downside was the map is very deceiving as to distances ....I realize it's only to point out the places of interest but a more accurate map would have been very helpful .

The tour advertises a 10-20 wait for buses. Initially, we waited 30 minutes. No wait was less than 30 minutes. After a hop off, and expecting to hop back on at 6:45, we waited 1 hour, with several other people also waiting at the stop. All of us (3 different families who got their tickets at 3 different places) were all told the buses ran to at least 8, we were told to at least 7. All of us had to take taxis back to our respective hotels, at an additional cost to us of £15. Competing tour buses were passing us bye (so clearly the competitors were running). 2 of the other people said they waited 35 and 40 minutes earlier in the day. Conclusion: lies from Big Bus. Try a different company.

My wife and I did the Big Bus Tour and were well pleased. It includes a walking Riyal Tour which I highly recommend. Tony takes you for the changing of the guard and gets you to theorize locations to see the guards with an excellent explanation of what is going on. We were there on the Queen's birthday so it was quite crowded but the guards walked right by us.

We took the Big Bus tour today with our young children after choosing between a few different services. This one was slightly more expensive but we liked the fact that one bus route covered a broad area wiht out having to switch between 3 buses.
I was however quite disappointed by the commentary. I have travelled to London quite a few times and was looking forward to my family learning about many of the spots we passed. Instead, it just mentioned very obvious spots (ie we're now outside Westminster Abbey.) with no additional commentary and the sound was 70+% music! My daughter was bored and cold and disappointed after having been in New York two weeks prior and having a great time on a similar service where the commentary was continuous, running and informative.
Overall, I wouldn't recommend this service.

Our tour was guided by a guy called Peter (I think) and it was great! Full of really interesting facts and funny little stories and jokes. I learned a lot about London and its sights and people. The route was really great, allowing us a chance to see many different areas of the city, and different styles of architecture. We were perfectly happy to just sit on the bus for ages because the tour was so enjoyable.

I loved the actual BUS tour! London traffic can be terrible. I would recommend NOT buying too many attraction tickets through BIG BUS. The busses and people are very nice! The busses are easy to catch, the recordings are great ! Very informative.

Would recommend Big Bus Tours to anyone going to London. We had a brilliant day seeing all of the sights, we wouldn't have seen so much if we hadn't been on the tour. I love how you can get on and off when ever you please and there are 4 different routes that you can go on. I'd suggest going on a red route as they have a live commentary from a member of staff. The best one we had was called Peter, he was brilliant and made the tour really fun for everyone. You get a free set of headphones so you can listen to the recorded commentary. We did the river cruise as well which lasted about 20 minutes but it was nice to see some of the sights from the river. Book your tickets online as it is cheaper than buying at the bus stop. You can also buy attraction tickets from the staff at the stops to save some time and you get a discount. The staff all know everything there is to know about London so if you haven't questions, they will know the answers.

This double decker bus tour of London serves a purpose. You get to see lots of things and get the lay of the land. The commentary varies in quality. We had one pretty good commentator, and one whose monotone voice was too easy to tune out. The biggest problem with this tour is that it is a slave to traffic. If there is lots of traffic, you're going to be sitting on that bus for HOURS. We gave it about two hours and had only gone about halfway around the loop. But, we'd seen the highlights that we wanted to see. So, we hopped off and took the tube the rest of the way! It's probably still a good idea to give it a go, though.

While I've been to London several times I hadn't experienced it though the "eyes of a tourist" on the big red bus. I planned on staying on the bus for the two hours and just listen to the stories. Unfortunately the guide was horrible. He would tell you what was on the left and then the right and sit silent until we passed the next highlight. I could get more just walking with a map. So I got off at the next stop and waited for another bus. Only to be disappointed again. The sound was horrible and I couldn't hear most of what the guide had to say. What I did hear was very boring. I asked the bus driver where I could get my money back. He said the next stop would have someone I could talk to. The man at the next stop was extremely apologetic and helpful. He asked that I wait for the next bus so he could see who was giving the tour before giving me my money back. Once it arrived he determined who was giving the tour and thought I would like his style better. He was absolutely correct. David was a pleasure. Even though it was one of the last red tours of the day, he was energetic and full of great stories about the city and its history. He interacted with people around him and seemed to have good rapport with everyone. In the end, it was a great experience.

While visiting London we did the big bus tour for 2 days. The red route is better due to the live commentary. We also did 3 of the walking tours in 1 day, our guide's name Dannielle Harte was the best. She gave so much information that I would not have gotten by just walking London by ourselves. If you have never seen the changing of the guards I recommend doing the tour!!

We had a great time on the open top big bus tour, lots of choices, ie; blue, red and green routes, with plenty of stops. The additional river cruise was really good. Don't miss the crews commentary informative and funny. Must say the drivers and guides were very good, very friendly and helpful even helping people who were not on the tour. :-).

We have visited London manny times and in a former life I even lived there but we had never taken on e of the open top bus tours before. We negotiated the tickets from an affable and friendly Brazilian and eventually got a 25% discount, I bet we could have got more with more time! We boarded the red route bus and for the next two hours enjoyed sights and sounds of London from the upper deck to an excellent commentary by Dave who was a mine of information coupled with humour observation. We changed buses to the blue route at Victoria station, after a 50p toilet break!, and continued our tour around the Kensington, Chelsea and Hyde areas of London.
All in all good value for money, multiple opportunities to get off and explore attractions and a frequent comfortable service.
Well done.

I took my 3 year old on the Red Route of the Big Bus tour today and we had a fantastic time!! I chose the red route as I didn't want to be fussing around with headphones on a toddler. We got seats on the top deck every time - the guides were entertaining and I learnt absolutely loads despite living just a stone's throw from London! Excellent views of Big Ben, Westminster, London Eye, frequent crossing of the Thames. We got off at Tower of London and took the boat back to Westminster Pier (included in ticket price) which was very nice for a change. Then we walked past Big Ben up through St James Park to Buckingham Palace before hopping on again.
The actual speed of the tour was slower than I'd imagined due to the slow moving traffic everywhere but hey this is London. It is pricey but we saved a few pounds by buying the ticket in advance online. The guides are helpful and there are often Big Bus reps at the bus stops to help too. A great way to spend a day in London(especially a sunny one like today!)

This is a must do for your trip. I loved the Big Bus Tour because it allowed us to see all of the major sites and get off and tour the ones that we wanted to and later get back on to go see more sites. We also had THE BEST tour guide, she was hilarious (I wish I could remember her name). Definitely worth the money to get to see the whole city and listen to the knowledge that they can share that you most likely wouldn't get if touring all of these sites on your own.

We wanted to do a tour of the city before we set out to certain destinations. We enjoyed the Big Bus Tour. It is a hop on hop off tour. The blue line has head sets for you to listen to in many different languages. The red line has a live tour guide speaking and pointing out various points of interest. I would recommend the red line with the live tour guide. Ours was quite knowledgeable and entertaining!

Big double decker hop on/hop off bus travels all over London and includes a river cruise.
This is a very good deal, especially if you are unfamiliar with the city. You'll see most of the city sites and you can get off and visit for a while and get back on later in the day. Wonderful guide on our bus. Highly recommended.

My husband and I took our two little boys on a hop on hop off tour for their first time in London. It was a great way for them to see alot of the big London sites. There were lots of opportunities to get on and off the bus with stops close to alot of the major landmarks and places of interest. When we got off we never waited more than 15 minutes for another bus to come along.
They offer free headphones to listen to the tour commentary and free waterproof ponchos when it rains. I didn't listen to much of the commentary but what I did listen too was very informative.
My only complaint is that I didn't find the seats that comfortable.
Overall it is a good way to see London and to get to the major attractions.

We were in London for 3 days and I invested in a 48 hour big bus ticket - it was the the best thing we did!
The benefit of the big bus brand is their blue route buses go past Bayswater and Notting hill - which was handily where we were staying.
We got to see all the sights, architecture and really felt wed learnt about the city.

The audio on the blue line was quite stilted, but the live guide on the red route was worth every penny!

I found these bus tours to be fantastic!
very good value for money and kept the kids entertained.

I also loved London. The buses were frequent and driver/staff were friendly and helpful

This is a great tour to go on with friends or solo. The bus has two different tours, a recorded guide in 12 different languages or a live tour in English. The recorded tour takes you around Hyde park and past Kensington palace and gardens. They offer free ponchos incase of rain. The staff are all very pleasant and helpful as well. Check out Big Bus Tours next time you're in London, you will not be disappointed.

Maybe it was just bad luck for us- terrible traffic, bad weather, terrible guide. We chose this tour for a morning overview of the city- we have been here for over a week already and have visited before. An important meeting scheduled in early afternoon so planned to be on one of the first buses. We were told by our concierge this was the best tour bus line and we could easily complete the red line within 2-2-1/2 hours. Also told to wait for the red line with the live guide. We left our hotel at 8:40am grabbed coffee to go and waited for the green line shuttle-came quickly. Audio info along way to main Aldwich stop for main tour was informative. Got to Aldwich around 9:40-cold and rainy wait. Multiple buses for other tour companies came and went. After 30 minutes, blue line big bus appeared. Rest of people waiting for your chose to go on that. We waited. Asked the Big Bus representative selling tickets how much longer- he shrugged and said " rush hour traffic". Then manage expectations- don't promise a bus every 10 to 20 minutes! He assured us we would " easily finish the red line in time." When bus finally came, traffic was terrible- took 20 minutes to go about 2 blocks. Our tour guide seemed to have a standard script- which she often forgot, saying things like "I forgot to mention, if you remember that cream building of the left - I mean the right..." Lots of quiet dead air due to traffic- no tidbits or funny stories about London to fill the time, when someone asked a question, her response was " I am not from London"- that from a LONDON TOUR GUIDE! She did sing London Bridge to us. We have visited many countries and even done a few other bus tours from London this week. Could not believe she thought that was an acceptable answer. Surprising the company does not provide other talking points for traffic like other guides on other tours have done. Others on our tour were actually plugging in their headphones rather than listening to her- even English speaking. The bus was extremely cold. The driver's radio competed with hearing the guide's brief commentary. At 12:30, we were not even halfway through the red line tour. We asked the driver to point us to the nearest underground train station so we could rush back for our meeting. If time had not been a concern; if we had been hopping on and off to see sights; if the weather had been nice enough for us to try the inclusive walking tours and boat tour which hopefully had better guides, perhaps we would be giving this a better rating. Instead it was a waste of our time and money.

We took a hop on and hop off big bus tour in London. The ticket costs 30 pounds and is valid for 24 hours. You also get a free river cruise on river thames with a guide on bus as well as on the cruise which was an awesome experience. The bus provides free ear phones and you can listen to the guide while the bus keeps moving and it takes you to almost all major attractions. Worth a ride!

Took this bus tour as I had limited time in London plus I was travelling with relies with young kids. We took the red line. The commentaries were very helpful. Then we took the river cruise the next day, that was rather short though, but on a sunny day it didn't teally matter. It does get cold and windy so just be prepared. The day we took the river cruise we rode on the blue line...not as good as the one with a good guide.

I have tried the bus tour in San Francisco. And as with that, these tours only become as interesting as the guides they have. The more enthusiastic and friendly the guides are, the better for tourists and for business.

Live Commentary on the Red Line gives great insight on not only the main attractions but everything in between too. Great way to see all the main sites in one day. Hopping on and off the bus is very convenient to take pictures and see the sites. Spent one day hopping on and off the bus. The best live commentator of the day was Sharon, she is easy to understand, her voice projects, very friendly and knows her London inside and out. Highly recommend Sharon for a tour guide.

Took this bus and completed the whole circuit in slightly over 2 hours...well worth the money. Its great that you can hop on and off wherever you want to. Good service/access for wheelchair users too and staff were very helpful and obliging

We have been on Big Bus Tours in Washington DC, LA and San Francisco and this one didn't disappoint. The live commentary was good and kept us entertained. Boris has made a bit of a mess with the traffic but luckily the tour guide could point out stuff to keep us from being bored.

I dropped a star because by comparison this tour was probably the dearest we've been on...

This was our first time visiting London and we picked the big bus because they seemed to be a lot on the road so it meant we wouldn't be hanging about at each stop, the drivers were very helpful but I would say I think the stops should have the numbers on them (same as the map)as we tried to get off a few times only to ask the driver if this was our stop,as if the number was on the stop we wouldn't hold the driver up but would highly recommended this company.

my photography day on the Big Bus.... l have the most awesome views of the historical place in London ..... wonderful on a beautiful sunny day.... and got to see places which l otherwise missed every time l used to visit London

Make sure you get on the red route with Super Steve. Wow did this guy know his stuff, even pointed out the island used in the filming of The Griswolds European Vacation!! It made my day, sorry Steve for shouting the answer, I got a little over excited!. It rained most of the day, but with our free ponchos, the trip certainly brought out the sunny side in us all with Steve's amazing facts. Seriously though, Steve you are something else with your head full of knowledge and very interesting to listen to - note to Big Bus Company - value what you have here!!! Excellent driver too with a great sense of humour.

Worth knowing there are three coloured tours in totally (red best by far) so lots to see and do including a river boat tour. I would recommend you plan out your route first to make the most of your day. We didn't so will be returned to complete our visit and will most definitely be going on the red tour again!

Thank you for a lovely day :)

The tour is a good way to see a lot of London - since it is so spread out, the bus covers most of the touristy attractions. One thing to keep in mind is the traffic - London traffic can really eat in to your tour time, especially if you are waiting on a particular bus. We had to wait 25 minutes for the bus we wanted because of traffic jams. Unfortunately, we were standing around for 25 minutes clueless as to what was going on because the staff either didn't know or just didn't tell us it was because of traffic. That was upsetting. They were more focused on getting more people to pay for a tour than informing those of us who had already paid what was going on. So, bus tour - YES! Staff - not such a fan.

There is not a big difference between the companies that offers this service. This is a good option for rainy days (and in London this happen frequently) because you can visit the city in a comfortable way and also if you have young children that they don't want to walk.
I think it's the only one that has an app, but not a big deal since you manage to ear everything with the headphones on the bus.

I decided to choose the Big Bus tour in London because my traveling companion had trouble walking long distances. I prefer walking or biking tours personally, and I also remember a previous visit to London where I used a bus tour (can't remember which one) and felt very sleepy listening to the pre-recorded guide (to be fair, I had jet lag too). However, I thought this would be best for my companion. The tour seemed wonderful--free transportation plus walking tours and also the river cruise included. In fact, when we hopped on, with a tour that had a live guide, we thought we could make it to the stop for a walking tour to the changing of the guard starting around 10. However, the traffic was terrible and we weren't even sure we could make it to the changing of the guard (11:30) before we got off, much less make the walking tour! But the worst part was the live guide. We started at a point with an arch, and he literally said, "There's the X arch. There's a horse statue. There's a fountain." Literally things we could see ourselves, but no background at all. When he ran out of things to say (because of the heavy traffic) he started reading an entertainment guide to us. This is a guy who either has no in-depth knowledge of history and his city, or who has just run out of steam for being a tour guide (he mentioned he'd been doing it for 16 years). While I am sympathetic to the demands of repeating information for travelers over and over again, it was my experience and I really choose this company for their live guide and the guide was terrible. I also think that traffic has just become too heavy in London and so a bus is not a good mode of travel. We took the bus again after visiting M&M world, and waited probably an hour for a live guide again (to be fair, a couple buses passed while I was trying to find a bathroom--they are quite scarce in this city, I found!). To our utter dismay, the guide on this bus was the same as the first! I did think the service people who were available at all the stops were very helpful and we chatted with one at the stop where we waited for an hour, who was very nice. Since we had paid for two days of tours and we were not about to get on the bus again, we did take the Thames River Cruise portion the next day but for the price I do not think this was a good way to see London. Next time I would do the walking tours available from London Walks (walks.com), which sound like they have enthusiastic guides, and would let me see more of the city.

Really enjoyed going round the red tour route. Big Steve was very informative amusing and entertaining. He even fed the kids when he heard them say they were hungry. Great way to see and learn about the city, especially if your in london for a couple of days and want to plan your activities.

We Had a great bus tour with "big Steve"
A lovely Guy With a big Heart not only made us laugh alot we got to Learn alot about Londons history to
Big thanks
The swedish couple 🇸🇪❤️

When going to London do this first as it will help you see all the city and get a lot of information early on in your stay. It can be expensive if you purchase additional items but totally worth it to pick up other tickets to areas like the London Eye, London Tower, etc.

We sat on the upper deck for the majority of the tour and really enjoyed it. We only went downstairs once it got really cold and most of the sites had been seen. We had two things I was not happy with:
1) We took the Red Tour and our tour guide kept messing up the right and left hand side so you ended up not quite knowing what you were looking at sometimes for the lesser known items
2) We were rushed off of the red tour and then on to a blue tour with no explanation from the driver. Turns out he was running late and was not going to go back to Marble Arch where we picked up the bus. I didn't appreciate that as a lot of us had no idea what we were doing.

The bus is such a great way to get around plus see the sights! Unfortunately, we didn't realise only the red route bus has a guide we had been hopping on the blue line gutted as the little time we spent on the red line was very informative!!! Worth the money!

Had the opportunity to spend 1 full day in London and used Big Bus to see as much as possible. We saw a whole lot in just one day. If I were staying for a longer period of time I probably would not purchase a multiple day pass though.

With only a few hours to spare on the final day of a very short break in London, we decided to take the Big Bus Tour (Blue Route). It's a good, if expensive (£27 per adult) way to see the city's main attractions, especially if your time is limited. We didn't hop-on or hop-off but stayed on the bus for the duration of the journey - which lasted almost three and a half hours, thanks to the frustrating tailbacks and traffic lights of London's congested transport system. So if you are taking this, or any other sightseeing bus tour and have limited time to spare, please make sure that you build in enough time to allow for the many, many delays in getting around.

There is no live tour guide on the Blue Route, only the usual multi-lingual narration via earphones. We ditched this option and just followed the route map. I would like to suggest that there is a recorded announcement before each stop, for anyone either not following the route map or listening through the earphones - otherwise there is a risk of missing a particular stop.

The tour did a good job though in familiarising us with the main attractions, ideal for a first-time visitor to London - although next time we'll take the Tube which will be a much quicker way to get to any planned destinations.

We spent a beautiful weekend in London and used the Big Bus tours to get around. Traffic made the buses go slower, but that's not their fault. The highlight was the walking tour with Big Steve! He told many good stories about the history of London and showed some cool sites where they shot movies like James Bond and Harry Potter.

We just spent the weekend in London and whilst we were there we used the Big Bus Tour. It was a brilliant way to see all the main sights of the town. Robert the guide on our bus was knowledgeable and funny too. It was great being able to hop on and off at any of the stops and we did this to visit the palace and to take a river cruise which was included in the price of the ticket. I would recommend this to everybody.

There is so many places you need to pass by on a trip to London. This a good way to do it. We bought the tickets directly on Big Bus' own site and saved by picking a fixed date. Cruise on Themes is included.

For ease of this review, I'll tell you about the good things and then the bad things.

Firstly, the bus driver was really nice and we had a good laugh when I first got on. He waited for me as I had to run to take the bus.

The live tour guide was good too and told us lots of interesting facts and engaged everyone in conversation and we had some good laughs.

The bus was conformable and wasn't overcrowded so I got a seat on the top undercover, which was great as it was rainy that day.

On the negative side (and some of these aren't the fault of the Big Bus, it's just the way things are), we often got stuck at stops for a long time waiting for people to buy tickets, not only to the bus but for other attractions. We probably spent half an hour sitting at stops waiting for these people.

The traffic was horrendous so we spent most of the trip crawling at a snails pace. I'd got off the blue bus and waited 15 min for a red bus so I could go on the live tour and go the short route, but the red bus went out of the way and followed the blue bus route anyway!

I spent about an hour and a half on the bus, and then got off at the tower of london. When I went to get back on the bus, there was one stuck in traffic a little further up the road from the stop, so I knocked on the door but the driver wouldn't let me on. I do understand this, but inevitably as I couldn't get on this bus I ended up waiting over an hour to get back on the red bus at the tower of london. I believe the man at the stop said there was a taxi strike and the bus was stuck in traffic, However, he kept saying it would only be 5 minutes...In the end at about 2.30pm with the day quickly escaping me I gave up and took the tube to the remainder of the locations I wanted to go to. The Big Bus guide at the station also disappeared into the shadows after people kept questioning him about what was taking so long.

So overall, I had a terrible day because of the traffic and how much waiting I had to do, but the actual time on the bus with the live tour guide was enjoyable.

My two suggestions would be that the drivers need to better communicate with their staff on the ground at the stops so they have accurate information to give to passengers, and they need to make sure people buy tickets in advance and don't try to upsell while the bus is stopped, as if this happens at most stops you could be waiting a really long time just for those people.

The Original Tour buses also came a lot more frequently than the Big Buses.

If I could only use one word to describe this tour it would be AMAZING!

I took the Big Bus Tour around London as I was only here for a day & wanted to see as many of the city's attractions as I possibly could.

Our guide Danielle along with her ad river Allen were full of enthusiasm and fantastic knowledge - the history of the city was told in a very entertaining way (how Danielle can remember all those dates is nothing short of amazing). She has us laughing, as did Allen when he did his Chevy Chase impression getting stuck going around a round-about - we must have gone around it 4 or 5 times, it was hilarious!

If you do one tour, do this one & be sure to get on Danielle & Allens bus!

I approached the Big Bus tour vendor at the end of Edge Ware road. Asked the price which I was told was £27 for and £13 for my daughter. I offered to pay where he told he told me he could only take payment or the adult ticket. As he didn't have change for 2 twenties so walked me over to another kiosk near Marble Arch. I noticed the leaflet said 2 days for the price of 1. When I asked he told me this would cost another £5 (so this offer of 2 days for the price of 1 was a lie) as my daughter was excited I continued on reluctantly. I emailed the Big Bus tour company about my compliant and received no response.As we had one more day of our holiday it would of been nice to of had that extra day should we of had the option! So I would advise people that although the tour was ok there are probably better more honest deals to be had!

The bus sight seeing tours are a great thing to do in all / most cities as u know .

Great to sit on open top deck if uk weather allows ! So summer is best for sitting on the open top top floor of the bus ( song buses don't have an open top upstairs)

If it rains you can sit downstairs under cover ( English summer is up and down as you know ) BBC get weather wrong too

I first went age 30 .. My birthday , for a laugh. .. As I am a Londoner and know London quite well

But quiet a few little interesting things about central London I didn't know ! So I felt
like an American or Chinsese tourist at times lol

I loved it . There are 3 diff routes around central London .

I would not recommend Paddington ( too far west part of London , as nothing nice to see in Paddington to the west of central London)

Hop on and hop off the buses at your leisure . You will either get a tour guide person live on a microphone or a head set in all different Languages for you to pick your language of choice .

Cheap too
.

Have fun !

From
London Lady

We had mixed experience with the Big Bus as they were really friendly and we had some driver who is not at all. Basically he left us middle of the road when I was asking a question from him. But if you are visiting London we recommend you to get on one of these buses. Always buy online it is much cheaper.

Had a great experience with with Big Bus Tour. Hop on and off is a great way to see the entire city of London. Guides were very informative and friendly. We also did the Movie Tour with Big Jim who was excellent!! Very nice and knowledgeable!

Staff on the Big Bus Tours could not be more helpful, polite and efficient; you all made our trip to London all the more enjoyable.
The Red Tour is ace with live guide in English, the Blue Tour also very good.
Drivers willing to advise on how to construct your day to get round where you want to go, that little extra help makes all the difference, thank you all.
You can take as much or little from the tours, and spend as long as you want on the buses, we tended to do an hour at a time, for children of 9 and 8 this was perfect.
Traffic can be busy, at certain times, so being able to jump on the river boat back down the Thames was an excellent option.
Even if you know London these tours are superb, will be part of my next trip for sure.
Great when touring by yourself. Hubby on business. Spent two days hopping on and off. Saw more of sights I was interested in.

We had the best time riding the big bus in the rain see the sights and listening to the guide. The map was helpful. But when hop off for bathroom, then wanted to hop on, we had to wait a very long time. Counted other buses passing by and realized this one was the most infrequent line. Waiting in the cold rain wasn't fun.

I found this hop on hop off bus tour to be just the thing to see the sights around the city. It was well set out and there are 2 routes to chose from and you can cross over the routes. A good time was had whilst visiting the sights

After reading some of the reviews I was a little worried about taking this tour. But I shouldn't have worried at all.

Firstly I wasn't sure where to catch the Green Link bus from Kings Cross Railway Station so I emailed the Big Bus Tours. They replied almost immediately with the details. We found the bus stop easily. Very conveniently placed between Kings Cross and St Pancreas. We waited about 5 / 10 minutes. The driver was lovely and polite and told us (my daughter and myself) what to expect. We got off at the Link bus stop and had decided to take the Blue Tour as that would drop us off very near our hotel in South Kensington. (right outside the museums) Again we waited 5 / 10 minutes.

The tour commentary was very informative. We would have missed so much if we didn't have someone telling us to look, left look right etc. We didn't have a live commentary but in February I didn't really expect one. We sat upstairs to get the best view and as people hopped off we moved up to the very front.

The traffic was terrible, but this IS London. You CAN'T blame the bus company or the driver for the road works and level of traffic. They get you all around London and you get to see everything. We were on limited time so used the tour as transport from the train station, a quick look at just about everything in London and then back to the train station the next day.

All drivers were polite and helpful. There were Big Bus Tours Representatives at most of the stops again polite and helpful. The rude people we encountered were the people taking the tour. I didn't want to hear someone near me talking to their son at the back of the bus about dinner reservations, I wanted to hear the commentary. And for the numerous people with children running up and down the bus..... if they fall who are you going to blame?

All in all good value for money and a well run tour. Glad we did it, and would definitely do it again. Perhaps next time making sure we have time for the river cruise.

If you are short on time in London, the Big Red Bus Tour is a great way to see the area.
You can get off the tour bus visit the sight and get back on the next bus that comes around approximately every 30 minutes.

We did the Big Bus Tour for London and found that it just was not worth the money. You can ride the public busses for much less and see everything- I guess the guide (live guide on one and recorded on the other) is interesting, but honestly, unless you are really conscious of your time, you hop off and then don't hop back on for a while and you just don't use it all.

The buses are not frequent like they advertise.We took a 48 hr ticket
(plus one day free)and on all three days we had to wait 30-45 mts for a bus to come.the staff are helpful and night drop off service is also gud.but there are lots of hop on hop off buses in London and all the other buses arrive in abt 5-10 mts intervals..dnt waste time and money taking a big bus ticket.

We ender up buying a 24 hour. (+ 1 day free) ticket on the hop on hop off bigbus. It stopped by the gasstation near our hotel, so it was easy to start our day with a guided tour. There are three different bus routes, but we got a bit confused by it, as they did not seem to always follow the route depicted on the map. We took the blue route from our hotel, and in contrast to the red route wich had a live guide, the Blue route had a recorded guide that you got earplugs to listen to. I found it interesting, and a great way to sit back and relax, while sightseeing - as sightseeing can be exhausting. I would not reccomend using it as transportation, if you want to get somewhere fast.

The Big Red Bus is a good way to get a high level overview of the city and attractions you can go back and visit with more time...or use it to hop on and hop off. The tour had many stops at many of the major tourist attractions. I rode it in December so the weather was not the best(to be expected). I think it would be great on warmer days where you can ride up on top without being cold. At times, I found some of the guides to speak more about entertaining things then historical things...so this depends on what you are looking for. Be aware, the bus is subject to traffic so anytime around rush hour it won't move any faster than the traffic. I caught the bus at Marble Arch stop close to my hotel. I got off a couple times so I experienced several different guides. One was quite entertaining and funny.

The bus route was changed due the London New Year's Day Parade but we were not told when we purchased the tickets. That in itself was unlucky but it would have been nice to be warned.
The problem came when listening to the commentary in French. It kept being cut off so we didn't get any complete information at all. The English tour did get cut off as well but not all the time.
It was a complete was of money as we could have done a bus tour with our travel cards and have the same amount of information.

Big Bus is one of the best Touristic Buses in London. We travel during 2 days with Big Bus and it is very easy to visit the city. Many places and touristic things are on the road of this buses.
Every 10-20 you have a bus. You can use 2 roads (red or blue) and have access to many languages for the comments. The paper plan is very detailled and clear.

During a 3 day trip, we knew we couldn't see everything in London, but BIG BUS is a good way to see a lot of things in a little time. It is a hop-on and hop-off buses company, so you can stop and leave the bus at every place you want (on the defined road) and when you are finished to visit, you can take a new bus to carry on your tour.

Around 30 pounds per person for 2 days of Big Bus + the City Cruise on La Tamise (Thames) which is very nice to do.

During short 2 day stay for New Year's celebration, hopped on the Big Bus tour and it fit our time and expectations perfectly. We were able to see the highlights of London with two fantastic guides who brought great insight and humour to the tour. With more time would delve into the city much deeper.

This was a great way to see london quickly. We had a 2 day pass. It was convenient to our location near victoria station. The tour guides are mixed, we had 1 that was great, 1 that just sounded bored and another with a smelly fart problem. But that said, the stops are good and there is constant dialog about what you are passing by, very informative. We never waited more than 15 mins for a bus.

We decided to go on a Big Bus Tour because it would give us a quick overview of London sights apart from the obvious ones and then decide where we wanted to go for the next few days. The speaking guide we got was warm, funny and informative which made the tour all the better. We didn't realise until later that a boat cruise was also included in ticket, we went from dusk into evening which was beautiful with all the lights coming on especially nice just before Christmas, highly recommend doing these two tours.

Found this purely by chance as we had a few hours to kill. Went around with the two grandkids (31/2and 21/2) and absolutely loved it!
The tour was easy, panoramic and comfortable, made especially memorable by the wonderful Patrick who had a gentle line of self-deprecating humour and proved to be a superb mimic. The driver, Josh, was a cheerful and extremely capable driver, at one very sharp turn, with several bady-parked cars, the passengers clapped as he executed the smoothest turn I've ever seen.
Really enjoyed this, the children were free and there are several other offers included.
The other passengers were sweet, especially the Americans ( "er, where does the Prime Minister live?") it says something that two young boys were enthralled and want to go back on the big Red Bus.
Unpretentious and an opportunity to see a different perspective for photographs.

I chose Big Bus because of the positive reviews. Im glad I did since they were easy to find and very frequent. At the first stop we found to get on had a staff member standing there to validate our pre-bought tickets, he was very friendly and made us laugh a lot. We got discounted tickets online but when we got to the salesperson he said he could given us even more of a discount. So maybe it's best to buy them in person. The first circuit we did was a pre-recorded tour. It was informative and interesting. It is lengthy due to traffic but I didn't mind so much as I was still getting familiar with the layout of London on our first sightseeing day. I really enjoyed the other circuit we did where there was a live speaker on board. The guy was lively and had lots of info the pre-recording didn't have. The bonus of opting for this during winter they give u an extra 24 hours of riding the bus for free! All in all had a positive experience and very happy I went on the bus.

A great way to visit around London & have good overview. I highly recommend this tour to anyone as a starting point to begin the tour of London & get oriented to explore more.
Options in Big Bus: top open double decker tour (covered lower deck, useful in rains & open top upper deck to get unobstructed views). Red route about 30 stops, Blue Route about 40+ Stops. They have 1,2,3 days passes to benefit fully! In different routes they have Guided Tour as well as self guided Audio tour that gives very useful info of sights & London. We chose the Blue route.
Tickets: Can be purchased from any Big Bus staff at the stops in the route/ website/or from Concierge of London hotels. One can choose a route / option based on coverage & ones interest.
We started our tour from Paddington station stop, while one has flexibility to hop-on , hop-off in any of the Big Bus stops in its route. Interestingly use & throw rain coats available on board the bus are very handy in rains ( used them for good part of our journey as it was a rainy day in London). The traffic is crazy at times, so take Big Bus staff / guides advice & get off to explore a place if he/she says so! With company best friends it's more enjoyable on tour, as we did ! City has lots to see & this tour gives plentiful to satisfy from this journey + very useful info from guides to help with our elaborate plan for London. Hop-off for entitled walking tours, River Thames cruise or for discount offers. Take the tour of River Thames cruise to enjoy beautiful sight, through a 30 minute cruise of London sites around Thames. There is also Night tour ( only operated by Big Bus London), supposed to be exciting. We may try in our next trip to London. The staff on Big Bus tours are very friendly & helpful.

We decided to go on the Big Bus Tour around London to see more of the main sights & learn some more history. Initially, we thought it was a little prices, but I can honestly say, it turned out to be worth every penny. The young guide was fantastic. He made the tour not only informative, but fun. He had lots of historical info & fun facts about London. When it rained he even provided us all on the top of the bus with rain macs, lol. He made it enjoyable for all ages.
