They even held the bus a few extra minutes when I desperately needed to use the bathroom. Half way through, the tour guide swapped with another young man & he was just as funny & informative as the first. We even learned a few extra facts along the way that the first guide hadn't told us (yes, we went round a second time to get back to our destination) lol. I'd recommend this tour for anyone wanting to learn more about London & have fun at the same time. The guides interacted with the passengers & made them feel a part of the tour, rather than just sat listening to someone drone on. Thanks guys. Nice work :)
Great hop on hop off service,even the miserable weather did not dampen our trip,did the full Red route,excellent tour guides on board

In order to see the main tourist sites in London you should take the big bus tour. It will take you to all the well-known sites and give you a narrative in your language so you understand the significance and history of what you are seeing.

While expensive (approximately 35 pounds per person, the tour is good for two days as a hop-on-hop-off tour. One round without getting off the bus is about 2.5- 3 hours. Good audio commentary, although it does not sinc with the bus location, so the information comes earlier than the site. Traffic in London is awful. The tour hits all the major tourist sites and you will need the full two days to see most of them.

Had family here from India. We opted for this bus tour because of the Hindi audio guide. It was great, and took the pressure off me. You need to make sure you're on the right bus however, as one route has live commentary and the other is an audio guide. The first bus driver we had wasn't that helpful and failed to tell us this. Once the ticket inspector got on, the explained how it worked.

Great route round London. Busses run really frequently, but not too late into the evening, so watch out for that.

A little expensive, so make sure you use it for the day!

STRONG ADVICE,THIS TIME OF THE YEAR WRAP UP WELL, IT WILL BE COLD. Wait for a bus that is partly covered, some have cover a third down from the front, it is worth the wait. Before you get on the bus make sure you look at the map, there are different tours available. For your first time visit to London you need the City Tour.
Every time I am in London I tour on the bus to while away the time, even in traffic you see different things. Last time it was summer, but often travel in the winter. this company will give value for money complete with guide. No extra cost, you also receive a ticket for a trip on the river Thames. That is worth is worth doing if you have the time. The City tour lasts at least two hours. All the important sites are there to see; but in today's traffic expect delays. At every important site there are get on-get off stops.
Peter M.

This is a great way to see London.
We went on a live cometary tour and the guide was fantastic funny and made the tour.
We jumped on and off the bus and found it easy to use.
Even used the boat to go down the river which again had a very funny guide on it.
Been on many tours but this was one of the best value for money.

This is the first thing we do when we visit any new country..... Get the tour bus, they will show you the important areas to see and you will get an idea of the town . The big bus tours is one of the best. So please get on one and explore the town .

If there is one thing you must do when you visit London it's go on the Big Bus Tour, in my opinion its the best and very good value for money, you don't only get the bus tour you also get a cruise on the Thames up to Greenwich. We were lucky we got Leo as our guide he was brilliant very funny and he gave us a lot of very good facts about the places on the tour. I must admit I learnt things I didn't know. The driver I think his name was Mike was great how he had the patients to drive on the London streets I don't know. Well done to the both of them for such a enjoyable time.

Tour bus was a great way to see Londons attractions.Steve on the red rout was our guide and he was excellent adding a little humour to the informative information as we went round. There was also a free thames cruise which was also a nice way to see some sights

Although I requested, the original tour bus once I'd paid they insisted it was the same company, but big bus had the better routes. Also don't always believe the staff, although we knew the changing of the guards was scheduled, the driver advised, it's had been cancelled due to the weather, plus stating it started earlier than advertised. As we'd done the homework, we travelled down to the palace, and watched the parade, which we wouldn't had on the drivers advice. Other than that, excellent, friendly staff. Take the boat ride which was excellent, good informative live tour guide on the Sunday bus. Great way to see the City.

I really don't see the purpose of these Bus Tours around central London, unless of course you have difficulty walking. On many days traffic can be horrendous and you can walk faster. Like any other European city, London is best seen on foot if you really want to get the feel of the place. An oyster card will allow you to use the regular red buses or tube if you get tired and need to get to somewhere a bit far off and will cost you a hell of a lot less. Also you won't be assailed by the corny commentary. Any decent guide book will tell you what you need to know.

Many of the drivers and assistants provided me with helpful travel information. One or two were not especially knowledgeable or willing to provide that information. Steve, who presented the Big Bus tour of movie locations was clearly the highlight -- a warm and friendly gent, willing to stop whenever you wanted, take a photograph and share bits of himself and the city. Great guy!!!

Though it was a rainy day the boat ride was a great experience for me & my wife. Was awesome to see the icons of London like Big Ben London Bridge etc. Bus ride staff was very friendly as it was raining & one of the staff members gave my wife something to keep her dry. Though the rain hampered things a bit otherwise a good experience.

We did the blue tour and got the green link from outside our hotel to catch the tour at Covent Garden. I booked the tickets online and got here ticket sent to my phone, a great easy way to pay. The tour was great and got in all the sights, you can hop on and off to explore further and you got headphones to listen to the tour. Friendly drivers and never had to wait more than 20 minutes for a bus. Great value for money as you also got walking tours and a river Thames cruise, inwouldndefinTly recommend as one of the best ways to see London.

A great way to see London. This easy to use hop on hop off bus takes you to the best attractions in London. Collect your headphones when you get on the bus and plug in to listen to the commentary as you are taken around London. Want to see something for longer, just get off at the nearest stop and get on another when bus when you have finished.

It was rainy and we couldn't walk around London. So thanks to Big Bus we had a tour of London exactly as we wanted. The guide described nicely all sites and he did not miss a little humour in his presentation...so we had also some good laughs. We did the big tour in over 3 hours but with all attractions around time just flew. We had to reach an address and the tour guide gave us instruction, so don't hesitate to ask them if needed, we found them very courteous.

My self visiting London and it took a 1-2 hour tour of London on the Big Red double decker bus in late ougust the second day after arriving in London. The weather was pleasant and it was an excellent way to see the top attractions, Big Ben, Buckingham Palace,Westminister Abbey and other highlights of the City in a couple of hour timeframe. The touring bus was completely full for the most part. I got on the bus very close to the flat where I were staying, The ticket price was roughly 28GBP which you could use/re-use in a 24 hour period. We would recommend.London is a brilliant place to visit.

The Red Line which we took had a live commentator talk about all the sights. No commercial vehicles are allowed to go in front of Buckingham Palace, so you will have to get off the bus to actually go around to the front of the palace. We saw the London Tower, London Bridge, The Elizabeth Tower (a.k.a. Big Ben), St. Paul’s Church, Westminster Abbey, and a bunch of other places. You can get off at any stop along the way and then hop back on another bus. The ride was about 3 hours due to traffic (normal time is about 2.5 hours). After grabbing a bite to eat, we boarded the next bus, we took the Blue Line, hoping to see Kensington Palace, not knowing that only certain Blue Line buses went west and the rest just did pretty much the same circle as the Red Line. We just opted not to go west and headed back east. It took us forever to get a green line back to St. Pancras

Our group of four visiting from Canada took a 1-2 hour tour of London on the Big Red double decker bus in late September the second day after arriving in London. The weather was pleasant and it was an excellent way to see the top attractions, Big Ben, Buckingham Palace,Westminister Abbey and other highlights of the City in a couple of hour timeframe. The touring bus was completely full for the most part. We got on the bus very close to the hotel where we were staying, One Aldwych Place.The ticket price was roughly 26GBP which you could use/re-use in a 24 hour period. We would recommend.

Here are some tips from our tour:

- we used the Big Bus Tour to get an overview of London on the first day we arrived and we found this to be very beneficial

- We did the audio tape guide first but I honestly found it boring at times, such as when we were sitting in traffic and just listening to music on the headphones

- I would recommend the live audio tour with a tour guide who is speaking to everyone. I found this to be much more interesting and engaging and the guides gave much more of a personal touch to the tour (and they were delightfully amusing too!)

- We did include the boat tour in our purchase and we were glad we did. The tour on the river Thames was great!

- From the boat tour we got off at the Tower of London and then took a train back to the London Eye area (you can take the Big Bus back but we thought the train would be faster)

- We bought our Big Bus tour tickets at the London Eye area, right by the bridge and this worked out fine as our tickets became activated for 24 hours so we got to use the Big Bus for part of the next day also.

- I can see how the audio tape bus tour could be beneficial for someone who does not speak English, but again, if you can get a "live tour guide" then I would recommend that instead

- NOTE: If you hop on a Big Bus later in the evening make sure it will take you BACK to where you want to go, as we got booted off a bus that was at its last stop! This was a surprise to us.

I hope this helps!
If you need to see London , use the big bus ,it is good and efficient and take the one which give live tour , it is enjoyable with British humour

The bus tour was a great way to get around the city and see everything. I enjoyed being able to get off and do what I felt like doing for the day. It was great that they also had the river cruise and walking tour. We did the walking tour for the changing of the guard with big Steve he was smashing!! He was very knowledgeable, he had perfect timing we got to see so much more than we even expected and thought possible. I strongly recommend you do the tour with Steve!!
The best way to get an impression of the city and hop on and hop off where ever you fancy. The red tour is the best.

If you only have a short amount of time in London or if this is the starting point of your holiday (you may be suffering jet lag) then a big bus tour is the way to go. There are a couple of different routes to choose from and these will capture most of the major sights. It's a hop-on hop-off bus so when you come to an attraction you wish to explore just jump off and enjoy yourself. There are attendants at most of the stops, especially during peak and shoulder seasons. These people are super friendly and very helpful. The audio guide is helpful and provides useful information. Its a great way to see London. If you are heading off to another city/country that operate the Big Bus Tours show them your ticket from London to receive a discount on your tour.

If you only have a short time to explore London, this is simply the best choice. We had Big Bus when we visited Hongkong, and we were really satisfied so when we visited London, there was no doubt to choose Big Bus. We really enjoyed the experience given!

Spent an afternoon doing the full Blue Circuit tour of London. We joined near to Waterloo Station and paid £27 each for 2 adults and £13 for a 5 year old which we thought a bit pricey but having stayed on the tour all the way around getting off at Baker Street Station 3 hours later and seeing a great selection of all the sights of London with a Multi Lingual commentary as the bus went around using your complimentary headsets which you can keep if you wish. It is a hop on and off service and the ticket lasts for 24 hours. You can get on and off as many times as you want at pick up points around London Great opportunity for photo shots and an excellent view from the open top which can be a bit breezy.
Overall excellent tour and staff.

We bought the two day pass and I was shocked on the first day when we rode the entire loop to get an idea of the area; it was three and a half hours long and had 43 stops (Paris Big Bus Tour has 18). You will see everything in London and some.
In my opinion, the route would benefit by shortening it by an hour. It is still a good way to see London and I would still recommend it to others, just take the Red tour as it is the shorter of the two. They also have a Green (connecting line) that services area hotels near St.nPancras train station and the Euston Square area.

We weren't sure about taking the Big Bus tour. But glad that we did! It was a nice way to see the city sights to help decide which ones to go back and see. It was very hot, so it also saved us a lot of walking! The kids consider this a highlight of what they did in London. The guides were good, though sometimes a bit difficult to hear.

We bought our tickets outside Victoria Station from an Official Big Bus Tour rep who was a really lovely chap, who was very funny, friendly and full of knowledge.

We found the guides to be cheerful, knowledgable and approachable. There was a protest in central London during the weekend we were there, so the traffic was a nightmare. We found many buses available to us and did not have to wait to long to catch a ride.

If you buy a one day ticket you received another day for free! Great! Also we had a river cruise in the cost of the ticket - which we took full advantage of and visited Greenwich. We also had a walking tour included in the price, but we overslept and missed it.

Very good value for money. It was a great way to get to know the city. I recommend this tour to anyone who is thinking of booking - go for it! You won't be disappointed.

In the end, do it. It's a quality tour and you get to see a lot of London. If you're in a smaller group and savy with trains, then perhaps just use the subway system to get around. It can take longer then expected to find a bus and then have that bus go in the right direction. But the tour was informative and interesting. Make sure to grab the yellow bus with a live guide.

Only had a few hours to show my friend from Ireland around London! So we jumped on this bus for £27 and 2 hours later we had seen all the main sights!!
Our tour guide on the bus Oliver was great, very knowledge, friendly and cracking the jokes! Was answering lots of questions that some tourists had and had a smile on his face throughout!!
Highly recommend!!

HOHO buses are generally an efficient way to see so much of a city without the effort of travelling or walking for long distances.
I liked the Big Bus tour and in particular the red tour as it covers a lot and you have a live commentary where you can ask questions.
I love to sit and go around the city for a couple of hours rather than hopping on and off. The green line is the only line that goes to British museum but it is dearer than the red ad blue lines. The service is good and there are staff members at most of the stations.
The Big Bus is the only one that offers a night tour for 48 hours bookings plus the river cruise which was quite nice as well but the lines were a bit long.

Best way to see London even though you have to wait for the bus at the stops and sometimes the wait was long. There were friendly staff at every stop who helped you maintain your patience. What you hop off and see is up to you, and if you want it includes a tour of the Thames by boat- but only for those patient enough to join the long queue.

The earphones are great also. You get a 24 hour pass which you can use for part of the next day, so use it as there is so much to see and you cannot do it all in one half day. Go back to the hotel, rest a bit and then get on again.

You will walk your feet off so take comfortable shoes, a raincoat in case in gets cold and rains, a small backpack, and a camera/iphone are all a must!!

Big Bus Tours had more stops then the other bus companies, but also had longer wait times between buses. It took us over 2 hours to get from the Victoria Station stop to the Baker Street Stop. Then when leaving Baker Street we had to wait 20 minutes for the next bus. At most stops while we waited for our bus, we would see at least 2 or 3 buses from the other lines pull up at the stop.

We were visiting London for a short 4 night break during October and didn't realise the sheer size of e city centre. We had walked the length of London but realised we had better find a bus to jump on and off at our pleasure. We weren't intending getting this company but it was the first one that came along. I'm glad we did get this one though as the live commentary guy was great and had a great depth of knowledge about London. We were taken back by the price at first (£32) but when we broke it down it was great value for money. This was a 48 hour hop on hop off ticket and included a free city tours cruise up the river. We used the map to plan our days out around what we wanted to go see and do.. Recommend natural history museum and science museum at Kensington stop and Oxford street stop for the shopping area. Overall was a great tour company and all the staff and bus drivers were good.
A great way to get familiar with the wonderful city. Do this your first day here. Our guide was Big Steve and he was so funny and knowledgeable that we stayed on the bus the entire tour!!

We have done this a couple of times over the years in London. This time it seemed like the vehicles had been brought up to date and it seemed clear that the Big Bus Company was winning the war of tour buses around London. Its good value to get around London. The live tour guides are very knowledgeable and interactive. Most of all the hop on, hop off service is great as you can get off at attractions, shops etc to do other stuff and then get back on when you are ready to move on. Buses come along every 10 minutes or so. Would definitely recommend to see the sights.

We did one of these tours in Budapest a couple years back and got a great overview of the city, so we decided to try it in London. The traffic was the worst I've ever seen! It took us half a day to see 1/4 of the stops ... Hoping it was the rain, we tried it again the next day and it was worse! For the rest of our visit we walked and took the tube. It's very easy and quick!

I must say that all the staff on the Big Bus were fantastic! But the traffic was too much of a time killer when there underground is easy, quick and cheap.

The 27 pound advanced price for a 24 hour Big Bus ticket made for a rather economical way to see the sights of London. It is also a good way to get a feel for the city. And, the River Thames cruise, albeit cool and windy (go figure, it's London), was a nice added touch. Seeing the city from the river gives the visitor a different perspective. If you are getting on and off the bus at same stop, the system works fairly well. But, if you get off the bus and plan to get back on at a different stop, you may have difficulty finding the stop. Not all the stops are well marked. My primary complaint about the Big Bus service comes from the fact we waited over 45 minutes for a blue bus that never arrived. We later found out traffic was snarled a few blocks away due to a protest. Living across the river from Washington, DC, I realize these sort of things happen quite often in capital cities. What I did not appreciate is the fact the Big Bus employees we encountered just prior to the wait made no mention of the delays. After giving up on the bus, we decided to finish out our sightseeing day on foot.

What I really liked about the tour that your ticket is valid for all day. You can get out from the bus, go for a walk and catch the next one in a little while. It was a chilly day, however we went to sit on the second floor for the best pictures! We had no time to listen information about the London as we were busy to look around. It's hard to believe, but to have a ride on the red bus in London was one of my dreams when I was a kid! I liked it, so did my wife!

The bus tour is a great way to get around and see the main attractions. Loved the boat ride on the Thames. We also enjoyed the walking tour of the Scary Sights of London at 6:00. Well worth the ticket price -

Big Bus should be sued for false advertising. The Blue Bus--with recorded narration--was terrible. Narration was not in sync with sights being passed and even if it was the information provided was disappointing. Took a Red Bus tour the next day in hopes of getting better information about London sites, narrator was more interested in telling jokes than providing information. Worst aspect by far, however, was the walking tour of the Changing of the Guard. The Big Bus website advertises it as a "relaxed walking tour" that "puts you in prime position for the Changing of the Guard Ceremony". This couldn't be further from the truth. We speed-walked for the entire tour, there was no relaxed walking involved. First we speed-walked from Trafalgar Square to St James Palace where we watched the beginning of the ceremony. Then we speed-walked down the street to the Mall leading to Buckingham palace to stake out a spot to see the same guards we saw at St James Palace parade up the street. I'm in good shape and had trouble keeping up. As soon as the parade got to us, however, our guide Kevin told us to get moving... we then speed-walked up to a side street leading to Buckingham Palace where we watched another group of guards march toward the castle. The Tour was not "relaxed" and we were not anywhere close to the "prime position for the changing of the guard" promised on the website. We were so far away we couldn't even hear it. To add insult to injury, in an apparent attempt to make up for this Kevin proceeded to demonstrate the changing of the guard ceremony using an umbrella to represent the group of guards leaving and a backpack to represent the new guards taking over. I'm not kidding or exaggerating, this is exactly what happened. Don't waste your money.

A great way to see and get a feeling for the attractions in London. The narration was wonderful, you can get ear buds, and rain coats on the bus.
We went once around on the red line, back to victoria station and had lunch.
Included in the price was a river cruise from across from the London Eye to the Tower of London, while on the river the London Bridge opened for a sail boat.
Traveled back to Victoria station on Big Bus..

We stopped by every important your side in London and there was a headphone to hear explanation and stops and you can hop in hop off to check the other areas it's very excellent enjoyed it very much and it's stops to the major sights was just excellent 👍🏼

We used this to get a look round London so that we could plan our day. And then we hopped on and off all through out the day. Commentary all round the tour. Was really good and the kids really enjoyed it to

Being in London at the beginning of August we booked the 2 day tour with cruise. It was a great experience and enjoyable. Would do it again, EXCEPT be sure to buy from an agent. We did it on a mobile as we had not met any agent, but saw the buses, while at Buckingham palace. We finally saw an agent when we embarked on the bus, he was very friendly and helpful. Long story short...it has been a month that I am trying to correct a billing error on our credit card that timed out during a transaction.

We took the Big Bus Tour around London which gave some interesting information about the sites as you drove by. We sat up top which was fun and allowed for some good pictures to be taken. We also did the boat ride up the Thames towards Parliament which was a fun/different way to see the city!
Enjoyed the tour around London and we had a river trip as well, the information on the tour was interesting and informative, would recommend cause you can hop on and off at any time.

Having just arrived in London from Australia for the first time we had 3 day hop on hop off tickets which was fantastic at getting our bearings and seeing the sights. The ticket also included a cruise on the River Thames which was great to see London from a different perspective, and also a night tour.

You do need to not be in a hurry though as it can be a slow way of getting around due to traffic however the red route is somewhat quicker with less stops and a guide doing live commentary which was quite amusing and informative. The blue route has an audio recording.

The staff were mostly very helpful.

Did a big bus tour Saturday 26th September, starting at Green Park, tour guide was Pearl, she was absolutely brilliant and kept my 7yr old son very amused all the way to the Tower of London. She did a brilliant job and her commentary didn't sound at all scripted which many tours can do. Had a great time.

what a great way to see all the sights up close and without all the walking, i spent 4 hours on this tour and got some great photos to remember this trip by the sight from westminster bridge was fantastic thank you to big bus

We had a big choice of hop-on hop-off buses and we chose the Big Bus tour. Generally we were glad that we did, although the traffic made the trip a bit hectic. The tour was a great introduction to the city. One word of warning, though. DON'T TAKE THE NIGHT TOUR! It's the same as the day tour, except that it's dark and London does NOT light up like Paris does!

Visited Lonon centre for just 2 days and the Big Bus was one of the best calls we made! There are three different routes you can take, we went for the Red route that takes you around the major must - see places in approximately 2 - 2.5hrs, depending on the traffic. The ticket also includes boat cruise - approx 40 minutes, nice views from a different perspective.
It´s best to buy the tickets (voucher) online, just mind that you´ll need to present your credit card to reclaim the real tickets.
The only issue was the tour guides - all depends on your luck. On our first round there was a very energetic young gentleman blasting information and interesting facts non stop - excellent! The next bus was one of the last ones that day - the guide seemed to be half asleep and completely uninterested, not even bothering to point out anything. And the third one the following day isn´t even worth mentioning.
Over all I´d recommend taking the tour, it´s really not possible to walk everywhere in London centre and this way you can see most of it without having to hail a cab or take metro. Grab your own guide book of interesting facts just in case..
For a short stay with little time to visit all the venues, do the Big Bus Tours to see all the sites in one day.

My sister and I purchased a one day Big Bus London ticket, which included all the routes and water cruise. The price was a great deal! We were so impressed by everyone who worked at Big Bus! Alex was very helpful in picking out the right option and attractions for us! Leo did live commentary on the bus and was funny, relevant, really knew his London information, and answered all the questions the riders came up with! It was a great introduction to London and my sister and I were able to go back to the different locations (hop on/hop off) and get more in-depth information if we wanted it!

My only criticism was that it was hard to find the Big Bus stops because they were located on the normal bus signs. Other Big Bus locations have a specified sign/post/stop. This wouldn't stop me from going back though!

Fun, different way to see London.
Went around twice, was no problem.
Lots to see , interesting.
Wouldnt hesitate to do again.
Did feel 28 pound was alot of money, but seems all bus tours are about same price.
Easy to connect and find bust stops.
Booking very easy online , just produced details on mobile.
All very simple to use.

Hardly have I had a better experience in London. Very enjoyable and relaxing after a long shopping day. A bit fast maybe but it covers a great lot and music is good while the speech is not worth.
When you get out from Westminster tube station go across the bridge to find the start. First departure of 7.30 is essential but you won't hop off as the City is desert and bring a scarf along as it is very windy. The tour is well worth the reasonable price and help yourself with the map and the earphones. Enjoy!!

Great way to see the city. Tour guide was live, funny and very historically informational. The traffic in the city is bad but he made the tour good even in bad traffic. Went all over the city and the hop on was difficult because everyone was hoping on at popular locations.

good way to see london especially if you like taking pictures as there is plenty to capture from the bus tour, went with family enjoyed the day but i did find it a little boring but would recommend and great way of seeing london
Really enjoyed the big bus. Great way to see London. Would highly recommend the walking tour with Kevin for the changing of the guards.

I love that you can hop on and off bus as desired (@ bus stops) the bus either goes right by most attractions or within a short walk! The drivers and sales staff are so helpful. And I love that they have raincoats and maps to grab (free) if you need them. I look for Big Bus Tours wherever I travel. It is a great way to see a place and learn history and interesting facts!

took the big bus hop on hop off tour while in london september 2015, arrived at euston station via train and couldn't find any stops for the bus, grabbed a black cab that took us to Marble Arch ($14) where the buses converge. Fantastic way to see the city, beautiful sunny day so sat on top level. Got to see everything we wanted and jumped off at the places we wanted to spend more time at...easy and frequent. Live tour guide Grace was awesome and told us everything we wanted to know, if you let her know you are a Doctor Who or Harry Potter fan she will point out relevant sites and be your best friend forever LOL .... highly recommend, the only way to see London

This bus trip can be a long day. The BLUE BUS can take four hours. The RED BUS covers some of the same journey. Then you have the free boat trip and if you want the Walking Tour. SO be prepared for a long day. But it does take you to all the major sites and sounds of London without Hop On Hop Off. If you do stop off it could take you even longer. It is a bit expensive at £32 but can be used all day for general travel. The tour includes lots of information with headphones in various languages on the blue bus and a personnel tour in English on the red bus.You can pick up a free map of the tour which is also great as a frebby for touring London. If you have the time buy the 48 hour tour for a couple of extra pounds. It gives you more time and stops you cramming it all into one day.

Bought tickets to travel around London and as advised we could 'hop on/hop off' as we desired. How ever once you hop off it's anyone's guess as to when the next one will appear - be preapred to wait 30 minutes even in mid September. Not impressed for the prices charged.

Brilliant value for money! The bus takes you all around London and can drop you off at all the best site seeing places you want to visit. The bus driver was very friendly and gave us headphones so we could listen to the voice that tells you lots of information about the history of London ect. Been to London twice now and we've used the big bus tours both times!

We pondered taking a sight seeing bus and there are a few to choose from. The fellows selling our tickets were low key,no pressure, but very helpful. If you want to sit on the bus, which we did for 3 hours we got the grand view of the city....try on top if weather is good. Headphones are provided and good info. They colour code the buses so if you want a live commentary check the colours....we tried the live one and found it to be Excellent.
Also included is a boat ride which we availed ourselves of....after doing the Tower of London hop on a boat...very little wait...and exit at Westminster....great trip.

I can't recommend this enough, it gives you a great opportunity to travel around the city at your own pace and tailor your time to suit your own interests.

The taped commentary is excellent I don't know how they do it but the commentary never gets out of kilter with the driving regardless of traffic flow. On the weekend they had live guides on board and the one on our bus was fantastic.

I recommend buying tickets to the attractions from Big Bus it is both cheaper and also you can get the fast track option which saves a lot of time and for visitors time is very important. We had prepurchased entry to Madame Tussard's from Big Bus we walked straight in whereas those waiting to buy tickets were lined up for over 50 metres down the road.

The night tour was also enjoyable as the city looks different at night.

I would like to particularly note that without exception every staff member was helpful and friendly, they are a great team.

Thank you Big Bus for 2 amazing days.

We bought a two day pass on the Big Bus Tours.

We had a wonderful day couple of days exploring London. It took us everywhere, we really enjoyed the onboard commentary and the opportunity to hop off and hop back on again. We took advantage of the free cruise on the Thames and enjoyed that too. Excellent.

It was fantastic that they had staff at most stops and they were all very helpful.

My girlfriend and I decided to spend the day on a bus tour so bought 2 tickets at the eye watering price of £32 each. We boarded the bus and were given headphones which we plugged in to a reasonably adequate sound system. The tour started and was quite slow as was to be expected given the London traffic. The headphones played the same 3 or 4 pieces of music again and again and again (Greensleeves and Land of Hope and Glory being amongst them). The actual commentary was very sporadic and the music became so repetitive that my girlfriend took out her headphones thereby missing what little commentary there was.

We got off at the Tower of London and had a drink and then boarded another bus back to the city. This time we had a live guide and the trip was excellent and he spoke almost continually with nuggets of local information and some groan-worthy jokes. We almost stayed on for longer than we needed just to do the tour again with him.

I don't know if they only have guides at certain hours or whether it's luck of the draw but it's a 1 star with the recordings and 4 star with the guide.

This is one if my favourite activities when I visit London and after a disastrous experience back in February I received some complimentary tickets which I saved for my son's 10th birthday treat. On this occasion we had 3 guides during 2 trips due to a shift change during our second trip. It appears that the guides get happier as the day goes on! While informative the first guide obviously had strong personal opinions about the refugee protest march taking place that day and was very vocal about how that impacted the tour and told us that one day when he worked during such an event the tour took over 5 hours to complete - the bus virtually emptied at the next stop! He didn't appear to want to be there - his delivery of the facts was dull and lifeless. The second guide was much livelier and happy to chat and give 'bonus' information about what we were seeing but wasn't on long. Our final guide appeared to be fuelled by a coffee and red bull combo and was great! Lively, informative, friendly - even my 13 yo son was impressed! She needs to be involved in the training of the other guides!!!

Going back to my previous experience - the office staff at this company are amazing and so helpful. They get 5* rating every time!

A fantastic way to see the sites, the blue route will 4-5 hours, the red route has live English commentary, book the two day ticket, see the site on day one, and on day two hope on and off at the site you want to visit, please note the last green bus in not reliable, 7.15 on the Friday night, and 6:00 on the Saturday, not a problem if you are able to walk back to your hotel, but some of the older people needed hail a black cab,
Shame on you big bus tours, as some of these people were dropped by the last blue route bus, and were told that the green route bus was due.
I took the three days pass, and never regret it !!! It's a "hop on, hop off" bus tour, so for three days, I visited a lot and saw lot of the best in London.
Visited London with family and booked London big bus tour which made our trip very memorable saving our time and hazel free.Had enough time to visit without any rush.

Our favourite thing about the London Big Bus tour was actually the free 'Haunting Mysteries' tour with Big Steve (although the service as a whole is great and very convenient).

Steve was friendly, entertaining and extremely knowledgeable about the history of London. He was full of interesting anecdotes at every stop along the walking tour and my friend and I learned a lot and had a great time. Highly recommended.

My husband and I were exploring London by foot when we came upon the Big Bus ticket seller along the river. We bought a ticket right there with our credit card and hopped on the next bus. The audio guide was pleasant, but the bus lines with a live guide are more fun - I think you just have to ask when you pop on or one is blue and the other the red line. The ticket seller will let you know. The bus weaves its way through the heart of London. We spent one tour riding the entire loop, then plotted on our map all of the stops that we cared to hop off on and went around again, this time jumping off at our chosen points of interest. The ticket lasted 2 days so we finished our loop tour the next morning. It's always a good idea to get the lay of the land before you go off on foot - it saves blisters and time!

Wonderful way to explore London from the comfort of a seat.The bus takes to all the best sights in London and you can hop off and explore and when you have finished exploring one part of the tour. Hop back on the next bus to anotherdestination.

Having won some tickets in a charity raffle, I spent a day in London with my wife and 2 grand daughters travelling on big bus tickets. I had expected that I would need to explain a lot before being able to use these comp tickets however to my surprise the. Ole tor accepted them immediately and issued all the tickets. He explained they were valid for 24 hours (I think normally purchased ones are valid for 48). He also said we can get on and off where ever we wanted and could also use them on the Thames cruise boats. We spent the whole day travelling around the capital being given interesting facts about everything we passed. The boat trip between the tower and Westminster was a highlight as the crew were fantastic hosts. I imagined the busses would be stuck in traffic most of the time however, with the drivers skills and the use of bus lanes we got around surprisingly quickly. I can't recommend these tours too highly get day out.

Had to wait ages for each bus, not enough in their fleet. Had to wait an hour in cold for the night tour as the first bus was full. It is stated on the website that you are collected and dropped at stops. We were collected at Trafalgar Square and then dumped in Marble Arch and told to find our own way back! So after paying for a very expensive bus tour we waited an hour, didn't see the full list of spots advertised and had to pay even more on top to get the Tube back. So two women unfamiliar with London were just left to get the Tube back at 11pm at night! I will never use them again. Plus for people information most of the attractions are within walking distance.Big Ben, London Eye, Westminster, Downing Street, Buckingham Palace, Piccadilly Circus and Trafalgar Square are all a maximum 10-15 minute walk away from each other. You do not need to do a bus tour in London, its a waste of money.

We might have hopped on on a very busy day but it seemed there weren't enough buses and too many people trying to get on and due to a lot of unhappiness from people who could not get on, the bus was delayed. We were on the top deck and were baking like potatoes in the heat for what felt like an eternity. Total journey on the non-live guide probably took us more than 4 hours.

As a solo traveler, I was so happy with this tour! I bought a two-day pass at the booth on the street and found it was much cheaper than purchasing it at my hotel. With just a couple of weekends to sightsee, this tour was perfect. It had several bus lines that took me all around London to get a good overview of the city and included a boat trip on the river and several walking tours led by enthusiastic and friendly guides. With the hop on, hop off feature, I was able to explore several sites conveniently. The smartphone app added even more detail to the tour guides' narration. Customer service was super. Highly recommended.

You can see london by yourself without knowing the stories and histories. But if you sit on this bus, you will know so much about london! The best part is the walking tour to see the changing of the guards. We saw the whole process: gathering of the old guards at st. James palace, we even marched with them, coming out of the new guards with the music band, and the queen's guard too. Had we not going with the tour, we would have done like most of the tourists, standing right in front of the buckingham palace watching the back of the guards staring at each other, for 20 minutes! We used our two day ticket to go everywhere we needed, did not even need to use other means of transportation. Well worth it!

I have done this bus company in San Francisco and I compared the pamplets for all the London companies. This is the best company. I now only look for Big Bus. Friendly, extensive routes, London even included a river cruise which we didn't ave time to take. Worth it!!!
Great bus tour does everywhere in London and greatphotos etc. Worth pairing with the river cruise ..
Very good bus tour, extremely knowledgeable and very pleasant courier, great way to see lot's of London and save your feet!

Spent a wonderful day sightseeing in London on August 16th. My daughter, son-in-law and two granddaughters were visiting me from Dorset. We decided to go to London and take a bus tour in order to see as much of the sights as possible. We took the red line live commentary. The weather was wonderful and we were able to sit on the open top deck. We had a wonderful guide who was very informative and humorous. I believe there were 32 stops in all and we were lucky in that there were no with traffic issues. Fairly expensive at £101 for three adults and two children but we felt it was fully worth it. We saw all of the main attractions and we saw parts of London we probably would never have visited on foot. My daughter has since recommended this to one of her friends who has since taken the tour. She could not stop talking about the wonderful time she had with her family. She thanked my daughter for having given her such good information. We all said that we would love to do the trip again. I am sure having good weather makes a big difference.

The Big Bus Tours has a lot of stops where you can hop on and hop off. Prices are quite reasonable. Better to book extra tickets for Madam Tussaud (and others) with them, so you can get a discount and the waiting line is shorter then.

Picked up bus at Victoria Station. Got a 48 hour ticket which included a boat trip to Greenwich. Friemdy staff amd convenient hop on hop points around the city. Have used this company in Paris and would recommend.

My first visit to London and so pleased I decided to take the tour. Our driver was brilliant we were hoping to catch an evening tour and he took us on board and took us to marble arch and told us where to go to get tickets for the evening. We ended up on the last day tour for the day so it was pricey at £32 but was a great way to see London without the chaos of being on the pavement. We only used our tickets for this one tour which is why it felt expensive as my partner is scared of water the boat tour wasn't an option. Our tour guy was a lovely and friendly ypung man with curly hair and glasses. He knew his audience and i think adapted his commentary to suit the crowd. He was great at telling people the best place to get off the bus to get them back to there hotels. If we are ever Crazy enough to visit our ridiculously manic capitol again we would take the tour again

Found this tour to be a great way of seeing the sights and also getting around London. We were especially impressed with the driver sat on the bus outside charing cross station, who gave us all the info we needed in such a comedic way we are still mimicking him now and is one of our favourite memories of our trip. Just one recommendation would be to try and do the red tour, as this has a live guide with more info and humour than the pre recorded tour in the blue route.

As a first-time visitor to London, I was worried I wouldn't get to see the best of London simply by walking (and possibly getting horribly lost!). Not only was the Big Bus so incredibly convenient and easy to use, but the Red Tour, under the direction of Peter the Tour Guide was just phenomenal. He was warm and welcoming (he said hello to and welcomed every person that got on the bus). He was charming and witty, and so knowledgeable from the earliest history, to the newest attractions (including the Shrek Experience - "We're told it's interactive, but we're not entirely sure what that entails"). There's no rush, and it's a great value. The river cruise is the cherry on top. Thank you Big Bus!

Excellent value for money too. Not only are you seeing London from the comfort of the seat you're sat on and getting great photo opportunities and getting to appreciate the architecture a bit more as you're not on ground level (if you're on top of bus) you're beating the crammed, hot, unpleasant conditions of the tubes.

Day or two day tickets are purchased. free map, ear phones and ponchos are provided and you can hop on or off the bus as many times as you like. Definitely the best way to see London!

Spent a day tripping around London on Big Bus. Thoroughly enjoyed the live commentary on the red-route. The blue-route only had recorded commentary, which stifled conversation. Distances around the route are quite long and it takes hours to go right around the route. Found ourselves kicked-off the bus a long way from our hotel because it was 6pm and that bus was going back to the depot. Another bus was apparently coming for us, but there were insufficient staff around to tell us what was going on. Some alternatives on the routes, so make sure you know where the bus is going or you could spend two hours going somewhere you don't want to go. Saw awesome sights with great photo opportunities, but a day wasn't long enough to hop-off frequently to check out the sights.

You'll need a whole day at least to take full advantage of this tour mainly because of the traffic jams in central London and the time you spend waiting for the bus to arrive when you want to hop back on. The recorded commentary is informative (ear phones are included) but the music gets a bit repetitive after a while. The human commentary is also informative and entertaining (thanks to the cheesy jokes) and you can ask as many questions as you like.The ticket also included a boat trip up the River Thames and back. The big surprise came in the evening when we were asked to get off the bus as the tour had ended and we were miles away from where we first got on. Thank goodness for the London underground. Make sure you wear a hat or sun screen if you sit upstairs on the bus - you will still get sun burnt even on a cloudy day.

Our family has taken numerous Big Bus tours all over Europe & US. If you get on the bus with Peter, the commentator, you hit jackpot! He is absolutely the best and doesn't miss a beat...Peter the Great.

Big bus tours is a nice way to see London in two to three hours. It is a tour guide and also a hop on hope off bus. The tour guides are nice and funny. The ticket is for 24 hours and also gives you a free 40 minutes tour guide on a boat.

I used the Big bus tours 5 days when in London as I found after first day that it was the best way to get around in such a big place. I used the blue tour bus four times and the red bus once. The red bus you get a live commentary and a lot more information. The blue bus you have a recorded tour, but in comes in different languages. The only downside...it takes ages to get from one place to the other...but I guess that's London...it's a busy busy place

A great way to see London! We rode on the blue tour and so we had there was no live commentary but the blue tour is more comprehensive and includes more sites. We took our tour on a Friday so the tour took a bit longer than the literature states but that was due to traffic, which is to be expected in London. We would recommend trying for a weekend so as to possibly have less traffic.
There are stops around nearly every corner so getting off and back on is really easy and convenient.
We booked the 48 hour ticket and the plan was to ride the whole tour on the first day and select attractions we would visit. Then, on the second day, use the bus to get to those attractions we selected. That was the plan anyway. We rode the whole tour the first day but concluded that the tube was much faster to get from A to B so we didn't actually use the second day of the ticket. Not too much of an issue since there was very little price difference between 24 hour and 48 hour tickets.
However you decide to do it, a this is a worthwhile way to see London.

We were told the tour from Kensington to the tower took 3 hours and costs £32 pp hop on and off ,it was the hottest day of the year and in London for the day [ our coach left at 4.45 pm]The bus was packed and we couldn't see much for bodies ,we had 2 small children with us, the 1st hour was ok we stayed on the red route,but as time was getting on we asked a guide if we could get back to kensington quick because of our coach, he advised us to get off and get on blue route,at the tower. We had 2 hours before coach left ,waited 45 mins for blue bus which went back were we came from ? driver advised we were ok ,but roads were closed by police so 2, hours and 2 very fed up kids later we hadn't moved??and it was scorching ,we had to phone coach company who waited for us ,even though we were an hour late .Do not ask the big bus, s staff for advise because they do not know the anserw and will tell you anything we had to get off and get a taxi in the end a very stressfull 5 hours, never again.

We waited to do the live commentary tour, well worth the wait. Great views from the open top deck. Best think to do is do the full tour and decide where you want to hop off. Great value . Highly recommend!

Truely wondeful. All of us enjoyed the Bigbus tour. I think it is the best bus tour we have taken. So far we have had 4 bus tours in 4 different cities and found that the London one was best. Will do again next time in London.
The tour guides were fantastic and it was easy to hop on and off. You also get a river tour on the Thames and that was really cool as well. I would recommend it to a friend.

My wife and I took our two young daugthers on a Big Bus Tour last Saturday and had Connie as our tour guide. Connie's knowledge of London was second to none and made the experience fantastic. Well done Connie and thank you.

Taking the BIGBUS double-decker bus tour in London was a very efficient way for a first time traveler with limited time to experience the city. Loved the "Hop-Off, Hop-On" feature of the reasonable 24-hour fare. Wish I'd had the full 24-hours to spend. Now I can say "yes, I saw that" to just about every landmark in London and have made a list of all the areas to spend more time when I return. Recorded narrations were available via headphones from any seat on the bus and well timed to let one know what was ahead. Don't know if or when I'll get a chance to visit London again but know wherever I stay will be within walking distance of a Big Bus stop.

We spent the weekend in London and wanted to show our children the sights so booked a tour with the Big bus company. We decided on a red bus tour and we had a guide called Gavin, he was brilliant, informative and very funny! We got off half way round , went to see a show them got a bus back. This was a different bus and driver but it was Gavin again, we were all happy :) he's a credit to the company!

Best way to ride the london city. You can get a 24 hour pass for 25 pounds. You can start your tour in the afternoon and continuue it till next day noon. These are just hop on and hop off buses with very good frequency of 10 to 15 min. Just tide at the top of the bus and enjoy your day. Much better than Oyester card payment for buses. Hassle free!! Just one more thing..... only way to ride in london is take these busses or Oyester cards since they do not accpet cash

A must do trip when in London surely?!?
See all the main landmarks, hop on and off when you want, free headphones to listen to the commentary, multiple languages available....
Shop around and ask a few of the people hanging around central bus stops. We didn't do the boat trip. Mostly because there's always a queue there with thousands of people and secondly cause it looks like cattle herded into a boat that, if it ever sank, you'd get killed in the crush. It doesn't look my idea of fun at all.
There was 8 in my group. We skipped the boat trip and paid £20 each. £10 for a child.
Some cheeky wee redhead working for the same company tried to charge us £28 each for the same deal and assured us that was the best it can be. Luckily I knew better.
So shop around a bit, get off at number 10 Downing Street and walk 100yrds away from No10 in the same direction the bus is going and you'll find a nice pub that does good food or even just to use the nice clean toilet for free.
You can walk around the corner to Big Ben from there too.

I often take bus tours of new cities, finding it a good way to get a general sense of the place. This one did exactly that, and all of the drivers and other personnel we encountered were friendly and knowledgeable. What I had not anticipated was how LONG it would take for the bus to wend its way through London traffic, turning what had seemed to be a good way to get around town (hopping on and off) into a fairly tedious day. I don't think any other bus tour would have been able to be any quicker -- just want to warn people of the downside of London bus tours mid-summer.

Had walked many miles on our trip to London. We decided that on our last day we would do this tour, but probably not get off of bus! We saw things that we had already seen, but went to parts of London that we had seen before. Enjoyed! Would recommend that you do this!

Love London, very long day..........so much to do. We had a day out for my husbands birthday. We got the train (same day return) and it was truly exhausting. Pace yourself. We didn't and WALKED everywhere despite getting an underground pass. The Bus tours are 100% worth doing especially if you are only there for the day.

If you can afford too, try and do a few days there (at least an overnight) to chill. It's a very tiring day when you have so much to do with so little time.

The Bus tour also does a free boat trip along the Thames, lovely, plus a nice little bonus. Be sure to get yourself a little map, note what you want to see and where abouts it is. Trust me at the end of the day it will help as I swear every time we go I think awww we should have seen this or done that.

Enjoy ...........and get some comfy shoes : D

Recently in London and picked the Big Bus for an orientation tour. What we discovered was that they seemed to have fewer buses on their routes thus we had to wait and wait to get the bus we wanted for the route we were interested in. In one case we just walked. Also in one case they had a stop at some so-called change over point, not sure what it was as the driver did not change- but the bus sat there for almost 30 minutes while the drivers talked and smoked and just hung out. Pretty frustrating.

We went on the blue line of The Big Bus Tour, where you have commentary via headphones. This was very informative and gave you plenty of time to know when the stops were coming up if you wished to get off. We got off at The Tower of London, and went on the River Cruise, which is included in the price. We also got off at Trafalgar Square, and at Buckingham Palace. I would highly recommend The Big Bus Tour, especially if you are on a short break as we were, as it does give you a full day to take in all the sights.

We went to London on a medical appointment, we decided to treat the kids and give them a experience of London brought one day ticket and got the next day free we hopped on and off all day sight seeing, the tour guides were very informative and the river curse were great and informative the kids remembered the saying " when the loin drinks London sinks" great value for money

In London for a few days with my mum and the kids. Been to London many times but never had a bus tour. We enjoyed the Red tour as it had live commentary. This was so much better than the recordings. Our guide was full of interesting facts and kept us entertained despite heavy traffic. The boat was also good. We prefered going from the Tower to Westminster to the other way round. Again this was due to a funny and knowledgeable live guide.

Went on this on Friday During our long weekend in London. It's a great way to see all the landmarks esp as my teens had never been to london before. The ticket is valid for 24 hours so can be used as much as you want within that time frame. We also did the Thames river cruise on the sat morn which is included which was also enjoyable with a tour guide explaining the buildings along the way. Well worth the money as you get the bus and cruise!

I loved that lazy way of visiting. The all lines are heading and hop on and hop off at the right places. A day fee allow you to go all London highlights as the ways are clear for buses contrary to Istanbul where you lose your time in traffic jam. The drivers are nice.

The Big Bus Tours are one of the Hop On-Hop Off buses that operate in London (and other cities). I am convinced that "Ho-Ho" bus systems are an efficient way to get familiar with any city where they are available. We usually get a two-day ticket, then get on one and ride all the way around the circuit so we get a feel for the layout of the city and decide what we want to visit and where we really want to get off the rest of the time we are there. The live guides that are on some of the buses are helpful and will answer questions to the best of their ability. Buses without a live guide (just a driver) have a canned, recorded narrator that explains what is around you. We prefer the live guides because we like to ask them questions about things off the tour route.

The big bus tours are a great way to see London the first time you come to visit. It drops you off right by lots of must see sites in london and picks you up when your done. The buses are frequent, we didnt seem to wait longer then 5 mins for a bus at each stop.
It was a very informative tour, learn some new things.
This ticket also included a thames river cruise which was great. It had a live english speaking guide who was really good.

Unfortunately it was raining the day we had the bus tour booked, therefore could not sit on the upper deck, excellent audio tour, maps, earphones and rain poncho's provided.... the entire tour took approx. 5+hours due to traffic in and around London, however it is best to start early and hop off/hop on at various attractions that you wish to visit, would recommend this as you see all of the main attractions of London for a good price

Purchased the ticket for 24 hours trip at Baker's Street and boarded the bus. Buses were quite clean, drivers pleasant and journey enjoyable. The audio guide in multiple language helps to understand the various locations and is quite accurate. Quite good frequency. Hence get down where ever you feel to. Overall journey takes approx. 3 hours - so have plenty of time to hop on and hop off

We have done a ton of hop on hop off bus tours but this was definitely below par. First of all we bought tickets in advance that were supposed to be for the 48hour (2 day) tour and when we turned in our vouchers the Big Bus tour employee advised us that it was only a 24 hour pass and that it would be extra money to upgrade to 2 days, ok so we paid the extra 14£ to do the tour both days of the weekend to avoid having to use the underground rails. We are traveling with an infant so we would rather the bus then up and down the stairs and escalators...so ok whatever. Then we go to get on the first bus after getting our tickets and they deny us because they already have 2 strollers on board and won't allow a 3rd. Again, I get it whatever so we wait for the next bus which was maybe 2 minutes and hop on. We get off to grab lunch but when we tried to get on the next bus we waited for like 30 minutes and then decided to take a walk towards the next bus stop...we walk and walk and finally find another place to get on and we wait again for like 30 minutes, we see like 10 other tour busses (for the original tour) come and go before we finally see our bus. We were so tired from walking that we all fell asleep on the bus trying to get back to where we started. We get off the blue line to jump on a red line because the red line goes closer to our hotel so we jump off and wait again for about 20 minutes never seeing a red line and we finally go find an underground rail and do that instead. I was not very happy at all. The bus did have some good commentary but I felt it was lacking some information too. All in all not very happy and feet are sore from walking all day.

If there were only one thing I could recommend in London, It'd have to be the Big Red Bus. Nothing will inform you more, or give you a better knowledge and overview of the city. We went around the whole thing at least 4 times over 2 days. It is a must do, so much knowledge!

48 Hours Trip on Big Bus Tours London - The best way to go around London and get to know about the History of the places visited. Tip - The Red Route buses which have live commentary (Only English) are more interesting with a personal touch and humour. But their Agents on the Bus Stops are not very helpful. If you do an online booking, do get a printout of the booking. Copies on the mobile do not work properly

This tour is something that can be enjoyed by all ages! Me and a friend who are both in our 20s thoroughly enjoyed this experience and hopped on and off the bus three times. The tour is available through headphones with different translations or there are other buses with a guide. In addition, the tour includes a ride on a boat on the Thames. Definitely worth a ride on a sunny day!

The drivers are friendly and there are numerous stops and routes. The entire circuit takes about 3 hours(more if you hop on and off, and also if there is traffic). You get a free ticket for a boat tour which we also really enjoyed. I would have preferred a live guide which they had on the red route but not on the blue route that we were on. Overall very good value for the money.

Having taken a similar tour several years ago we were again keen to take in the sights specifically for our son who was travelling to London for the first time . I encountered an issue using my iPad and the online ordering system (my error not the BBC). I emailed , received a reply , quoted the ref to one of the street sellers and .... I coundnt have been more impressed with the service and assistance that I received to resolve ... TOP MARKS Big Bus Company !! Everyone of your team that we encountered is very much customer focused and a credit to you
The tour itself takes a lot in and covers a lot of ground as one would expect, and whilst you can cover this much ground by yourself you miss out on the background information that is aveiled to you on the trip .A tip we used again was to ring fence where we wanted to get off mark in on the planner and hit some of these spots the next day using the tube .
The only flat spot was the guide in the changing of the guards walking tour who unfortunately whilst a pleasant young individual simply didn't do this aspect of the experience much justice , but to balance this the last time we did the same tour the guide was simply the highlight of our visit , so you take pot luck as to who is on .
All in all well worth the charge and can recommend

Our family loves to do a open top bus tour in new cities. You get the general gist of what there is to offer and if you want to explore a location, you hop off the bus. Buying tickets at the bus can be expensive. If you think you will take the tour, look into coupons and deals prior to your trip. We got a great family deal on our tour last summer, by purchasing tickets online a month in advance.

To explore the central Historic Places in London, with the best Views and Fun Live Commentary, Hop on to BigBus! We hopped off for a break with Family at Green Park next to Buckingham Palace for Picnic Lunch and then on again for rest of the trip.

We opted for a 24 hour ticket for me and my two young teenagers. 24hr and 48hr tickets are available but I think 1 day on the bus and an all day ticket on the tube is better value. It was great to rest our weary legs and hop on and off across a 24 hour period. It's not cheap but very informative.

With the tour they offer a free river cruise that has to be used on the same day as the ticket. We've never been able to use this (including previous trips where we have also used Big Bus) as we didn't want to waste the time. The queues for the cruise were long. I think the cruise should be a 48 hr ticket Making the package much better value for money.

Didn't do much research with regard to a London bus tour so probably could of got it cheaper but on the day it was £30 each for a 24hr ticket. This ticket allowed you too hop on and off at any of the stops and any of the buses.

We did the red tour first first gave a great over of the city. Covered St. Paul's, Tower of London, tower bridge, London Bridge, Westminster etc etc lasted a couple of hours and completely worth it. Can't recommend it enough. Especially sat on the open top bus in the sun...perfect.

We did the blue tour the following day before our ticket ran out. It was ok saw parts of London which I never knew existed. But the red tour was far mine and my families favouriate.
Thanks to Ollie on our red tour this morning. You were an excellent tour guide and the whole bus tour on and off was excellent for a one day tour of London. To be recommended.

We booked this for two days, which I recommend. Its worth the few extra dollars. You get on and off bus access plus passage on a Thames cruise boat. I also recommend you take the RED LINE if you can with the live narrator. They are more informative and can answer questions as you move through the city. The nice part about this tour bus is the convenience and ability to hop off and on the bus as you wish. They stop at all the big attractions in London and your ticket enables you to buy discount tickets to other attractions in the city. If you want to see London this is a good way to get an introduction.

Its good to go on these bus tours as they take you to mostly all the sightseeing near you and also it give you the history of the places we visit .. in London they have red tour which gives running commentary by one guide in English and they have a blue tour whcih you have to use the headsets and select you language and this blue tour takes you to madame Tussaud and the red take you to Buckingham palace and other areas you must do the tour if you have shortage of time

I love taking city sightseeing bus tours anywhere I go. This Summer, my family and I bought tickets while in London, however, of our 4 days in London, we only rode the bus once and never again, as traffic was so bad, it took us more than one hour to get to Trafalgar Square, as we got stuck in traffic all the way. Surely, it's not Big Bus' fault, as heavy traffic is out and beyond their control, but our experience in this case, specifically for this Summer was not a good one, so we decided to use the tube the rest of our stay, ad it definitely worked for the best.

Though I'm willing to give it a try if I go back to London.

I recently went to london on Wednesday 5th August with my partner and following advice from family I decided to buy tickets for the bus tour. Our first bus left from Victoria station and the commentary was pretty pathetic., monotone and frankly I could have done a better job myself! We were then switched to another bus after three stops and thank god for that as the next tour guide was fantastic, (a bald headed 40 something yr old) and I really enjoyed being on the tour. We spent the day on the bus and I was really impressed with the knowledge of that employee and his general demeanour. Around 3pm we switched to another bus following the river cruise and a lady named Danielle was taking the tour, Steve was driving. The tour was fine for the first hour despite some tasteless jokes and many negative comments regarding tube drivers and their strike (don't know why this was being discussed on a tour). However, knowing the strikes were starting at 6.30pm my partner and I needed to be close to euston station for our train home and were anxious to disembark at Victoria. So, as no mention of Victoria station was made when the bus stopped in traffic nearby we decided to get up and walk downstairs to show that we wanted off. We were then met by Danielle, guarding the stairs who asked in a rather sarcastic tone, 'where are you going', I replied that it was my first time here and wanted to get off at Victoria. Danielle began sniggering and pulling odd faces and replied, ' well it doesn't look like a stop, does it? It's a red light. So after a few minutes of absolute embarrassment in front of a coach full of people, I walked down the stairs. Following this Danielle grabbed the microphone and started singing circus music loudly in a mocking tone towards myself and the customers who had got up, taunting us saying, 'it's like a little game of musical chairs'. This was not done in jest, but rather a controlling and unprofessional attitude that reflected her irritation at myself and other customers and to be honest left a sour taste in my mouth for the company and my day in London, considering I and paid a lot of money for the tour. Safe to say I won't be using the service again, or recommending. This is a shame considering the other employee was fabulous.

We have used the Big Bus Company several times going around London. If your not into the tube this is a good way to get around central London and take in the sights on the way, and learn some interesting things. There are several busses, but the red tour is the best with live English commentary, which depending on the guide, can be a good laugh as well. There are stops all over the place.
Fun and informative. It gives you a great overview of the historic sites in London. Convenient hop on hop off spots throughout the city!

The hop on hop off bus is a great way to see the city. The bus takes you all around the city to all the attractions. You can get off and on the bus on your schedule. Make sure you get the hop off hop on bus that is narrated so you know what you are looking at when you driving. If you don't want to get off the bus at least you have driven around the city and saw everything.

We used the Big Bus as for some unknown reason we could not get the London pass (see different review) and we loved using the 2-day pass including the river cruise option. The bus took us to all the sites we wanted to see and the service was available every few mins.

You will definitely get your money's worth on this tour. Make sure you go on the Red Line live guided tour as opposed to the blue line pre recorded tour. You just won't get the same feel for the city. The hop on and hop off feature is great tho there is no wifi on the busses and sometimes they are slow in showing up on time. I definitely got to see more of the city than I would've on foot and also took Advantage of the river cruise which was a nice change of pace but very basic in the amount of information that they gave

We spent a few days in London prior to our transfer to Southampton for a cruise. We purchased our tickets for the Big Bus tours prior to leaving the US. This tour bus company met out needs perfectly. We were able to have a good tour of London the first afternoon before the hectic "two days" in London itinerary we had planned. The personnel at each stop could not have been more helpful and friendly. We opted for the blue bus line with a live commentator- the red bus line has pre-recorded information. Tickets can be purchased for 1, 2, or 3 day passes. Our three day pass also included a short boat ride on the Thames! A plus in our book!

What a tour. Took the blue route, and it is absolutely huge. You can get on and off the buses throughout the tour, and easily see all the main attractions in London. Well worth the money charged. Would recommend you use the whole day, in order to see it all, and get off the bus at selected points before continuing.

We were very short on time. Stayed on the bus for the entire red route and saw everything we wanted to see. My only disappointment was Buckingham Palace, we only got a glimpse of the gates. If we had more time and could have gotten off the bus, it would have been much better. The traffic in London is horrendous, spent alot of time sitting still, not the tour company's fault. Seemed to more Big Bus busses than any other company. Our guide, Gavin (I think that was his name) was great!

The Big bus tours cover many of the must visits in London. The bus route is long and extensive. It is adviseable to plan one's ride in advance. This way the visitor can really make use of the hop on hop off facility. Do not forget to take the weather into account. The upper deck is great if you can use it.

Highly recommend taking the tour as soon as you get to the city. We were in London on a short break from New Zealand and took the Red Route on the first day. Great enthusiastic commentator who knew everything and pointed out so many interesting things we wouldn't have known otherwise.
Hopped on and hopped off twice over the next 24 hours. Accidentally got back onto a red route with a commentator who seemed bored but luckily could quickly get off. Hopped onto a blue route and didn't realise until we were on that the commentary was through headphones. Unfortunately commentary only pointed out basics and felt like we were missing out a lot of quirky, small points.
Overall great tour but would be perfect if the Blue Route also had a commentator.

Just wanted to say thanks to the big bus tours...especially nobby the commentator on one of our buses. .really funny and informative..he was excellent. Great service and staff. Well done big bus tours

Big bus tours drove me crazy the maps are not clear, to initially find the first stop was hard you sort of have to guess where the stop might be on the cartoonish map. There are blue buses heading east and west but you don't which ones they are, you have to get off and transfer. It takes forever to get somewhere but that's mostly London traffic. Do yourself a favour and use the tube.

This is a great way to see the city. Your ticket includes complimentary earphones which allows you to listen to commentary in 12 different languages. There are many companies that offer this 'hop on hop off' tour and Big Bus is certainly value for money. The reason for only 3 stars is that we had to change to another bus half way through the tour which was overcrowded. As a result we had to stand and could not listen to the commentary. The other reason for losing a star is that you can only listen to 'Land of Hope and Glory' that many times....
Just in London for a show and overnight stay. We had a morning to spare.The Big Bus ticket took us all round the sights,we would recommend this highly

We only had 3 days in London, so in order to make sure we at least caught a glimpse of all the main attractions, we decided to do a Big Bus Tour. We have 3 teenagers, and this is a good way to see everything and also have the option to hop off and check things out a little closer if you wanted to. The tour guides were informative and friendly. We have done big bus tours in New York and Paris as well, so it is a company we know provides tours that are worth the money.
I did the hop on hop off tour of London. I appreciated the guides explanation of London. It started to rain so the guide provided rain ponchos. I thought that was impressive.

Paid £32 this was for 24hrs (from time of purchase) plus river cruise included. We were able to hop on and off at different locations throughout London and pick up was very frequent. Headphones were supplied on board and we stayed on for full tour. Very interesting and cheaper way to explore London. Don't think we would have seen 1/2 of London otherwise.

One of several bus tours in London. You can listen via headphones on one option or a live commentator who can answer questions. Hop on or off at many of the sites around town. They also have some feeder lines coming into London. Sell tickets at multiple locations/stops.

Enjoyed
The best tour for London tourists, hop on hop off to see the maximum sights in London- with good commentary & open roof top space for a great view of city monuments

Went with Big Bus after reading the reviews and having a horrible experience with a Golden Tours ticket salesman. Big Bus team is very professional and there are lots of buses with little wait time.
