It was convenient that we could buy tickets at any bus stop and didn't have to go to the office, we also got our Eye and Tower tickets from the same Big Bus representative. London traffic is a mess so it does take time to get around, I'd recommend Big Bus and using the Underground to get around if you are pressed for time.

Pros: reasonable prices, they offer a free bus that connects you to the start of the 2 bus loops, buses come fairly regularly. Cons: there is little to no commentary on the buses - the majority of the buses have an audio guide/recorded commentary that gives limited information so we decided to hop off and switch to one of the few buses that has a "live" guide and it was no better! You couldn't hear the guide easily - even though we moved up several times to try and hear him - and then we were able to hear him he didn't say much. We have done lots of hop on hop off tours in various cities and always find them a great way to get a quick lay of the land - and in a city like London where there are so many landmarks and history you could touch on it seemed so strange that so little information was provided.

We booked the Big Bus tour online (We took the 24 hours tickets) and started from Point 1. It took about 2.5 hours for the whole tour and it was much worth it. We learned so much in so little time. We were sitting on the upper deck and enjoyed the sun and nice weather. Bring water with you in case you get thursty. The guide was well aware of everything (We asked him couple of questions and he was able to answer everything). You can use your ticket to hop off hop on at different stations (In case you don't want to do the whole tour in one shot). We didn't take the free Boat cruise as it was a little crowded. Would definitely recommend this tour.

We went all over London, getting on and off the bus, thorougly enjoying London. We took the cruise from Westminster to the Tower and also took the Haunting Walking Tour that leaves from Trafalgar Square. We didn't have to wait for a bus for more than 10 minutes, and we always got a daytime seat up top. On the night bus it was super crowded because it was the last one from Trafalgar, so avoid that one in July.

We selected the Big Bus on a Saturday and took some friends and family members for a open bus tour of London. After looking at the options, we selected Big Bus because they offered a cruise on the Thames river which looked very compelling. There were 6 of us, including kids and we paid GBP 122 pounds.

Once we got to the cruise point by Westminster Abbey we were asked to wait because of over crowding and we were told that "at this point, the cruise is not operating". We waited for over an hour to get onto the cruise only to be turned down because the service was simply too crowded and they could not handle any more people.

It is not the service we expected and paid for. The promise of a cruise on the Thames was a definitive selling point for Big Bus tour, above the competition.

After writing to them to report the issue, we were told that since the Thames Cruise was free, there was "no monetary" loss for us and therefore nothing they would do.

Watch out for the false promise.

Loved this bus tour. Very easy to find the locations to get on to start. Very good price and you get to learn a lot about the city. Love the option you can get off and get back on for free. They have so many buses running you never have to wait more than 5 min for the next bus to hop on. The guides were funny and added great information.

I would highly recommend this tour and if you want a cheap way for public transportation, purchase a 2 day pass as the 2nd day is only a few dollars more.

Fantastic tour.. knowledgable tour guides great value for money as well. We really enjoyed this tour and found the staff really helpful. Buses clean and plenty of places to hop on hop off. Recommend this tour highly

The big bus experience was very good if you want to see the whole of Londons attractions. It's the best way to get around. As long as your not in a great rush the traffic is so busy ! You get on and off however many times you like. The tour guide is very informative and interesting. Can get very hot, on a hot day on the lower deck of the bus ( no air conditioning ) in all very good.

We were on a visit to London and wanted to do the bus tour. As we were at Gloucester Rd we did the Big Bus Tour as it was right next to the hotel. My wife and daughter enjoyed the first day then my daughter and I did the second. Its rather slow to be honest which I guess is the point. However we got off half way around and jumped on the tube and did not actually hope back on. The tour guide headphone speaking tour is pretty good though.

We regularly use these types of tours to get a bearing on the city, an overview of the history of each landmark and sometimes for easy transfer between sights we wish to see. This tour had both live and recorded guides (up to twelve languages) and it was a different tour on each kind. I really enjoyed the commentary.

I am disappointed in the the travel service located inside of Victoria Station that sold me the Big Bus package. They did not give me the same deal that I would have gotten with my family of 4 from the Big Bus company. We spoke with a Big Bus manager but it was too late. Don't fall for that one. Go directly to Big Bus.

My husband and I always like to see new cities using the Hop On, Hop Off bus since it allows you to see everything in one ride, then we can choose where we want to go from there. Because of traffic in London, one circuit on the Blue Line is several hours long, but we really enjoyed seeing everything there was to see in London without having to drive in that crazy traffic ourselves! Kudos to those drivers for their patience in all that chaos every day!

This tour is a great way to see the city and get some background about things you're seeing along the way. We only had the opportunity to catch the Red bus once, but the commentary on the blue line was fine for us. We also checked out the Green Line and were blown away by the St. Pancras Renaissance London Hotel. Wow, that building is fantastic and totally worth taking the Green line to see!
Great for hopping on and off and wait is no longer than ten mins...... Great for a rest between attractions but some of the tour guides were hard to make out otherwise would recomend

The Big Bus Tour in London is the best tour for your first day in the city. It gives you a great sense of the history London has to offer while also giving you a chance to relax and gain your bearings. I got a lot of great ideas of places and pubs to visit while on the loop. It also has many great stops to jump off.

Relocated from UK to US and now back for a family vacation this was a great way to take the family to see all the sights of London. The hop off and hop off feature was really helpful to allow you to explore. Make sure you allocate a whole day to see everything though as with the London traffic it can sometimes take you longer than you think it will to get around. Knowledgeable tour guides on the red tour (english speaking only) however the blue tour has 8 different languages if needed) and gets you the behind the scenes info about London you may not know. Totally enjoyed the day and would definitley do in other cities if visiting

Tick sellers for the Big Bus Tour are easy to find and helpful and informative. The Blue tour commentary available in 12 languages was informative but very disjointed due to the slow progress. We went on a Saturday in July and while the Tour can't do anything about the amount of traffic, I would suggest you use google or apple maps to check the roads for delays before buying a ticket. It took about 4 hours to complete approx 2/3 of the blue route which we thought would take about 2 hours.

With only 3 hours in London I hoped to take the bus.The first advisor said the blue buses were better for a short trip so we spoke to an agent who took £45 and directed us to a stop.Here the driver said we just couldn't do any of the tours in the time we had left.This chap found us an agent who organised a refund directed us to the palace and then got us a lift back to our meeting point.Brilliant!Advice if National Coaches drop you at The Grosvenor just walk 200 yards back towards Marble Arch wait near a ramp and take a blue bus which will bring you back in time

We booked this tour as a way to get around and see the city. The only hard part was trying to figure out where the tour bus first picked us up - it picks up where all the other buses pick up, just look for the Big Bus logo on the pole. There is also an app for your phone that you can download that has the bus routes and stops on it. The red line offers live commentary and the blue line does not. The buses picked up frequently and the stops were easy access to all the area attractions. It is a great way to get around and learn more about the history and sites in London. I would definitely do this again if I am in the London area. It was worth the money, especially if you do the two-day pass.

We only had two days in London before continuing through Europe so wanted to try see as much as possible in the short amount of time we had
This tour was perfect and great value for money

I love that you can skip the things that dont really interest you and hop off and explore where you want. We actually just sat on the bus for a full loop first, taking in the beautiful sights from the top of the open bus (as freezing as it was, it was lovely)

Loop times were great too, didnt seem to have to wait very long to hop back on the next bus and staff were friendly.

Would highly recommend this tour

We had high hopes for this hop on hop off bus tour, but after spending an hour and a half stuck in London traffic with the sun beating down and inhaling diesel exhaust we had enough and after buying a 2 day pass never looked back. It is not necessarily the bus company's fault that traffic is terrible but to tout this as a way to efficiently get around London is a stretch to say the least. I would suggest saving your money and learning to use the Underground.

Went for day trip to London and decided to get a bus tour. The cost was £26.00 for the day and you can get on and off all day. We chose a red tour for the first part and had Danielle as our tour guide, she was great, very informative and funny. The blue bus is audio guide using earphones. It's a brilliant way to see all of London without the sore feet and getting lost in maps.

We enjoyed our day on the hop on and off bus. It is an easy way to see lots of attractions in a relatively small amount of time. Pretty convenient to find and get to what you want. Parts of it are a little boring. Both of my daughters (12 and 16) fell asleep during part of the tour.

I've done this bus before. I enjoy it each time. People come and want to see everything when not enough time. This gives a great overview. Great views up top! And there is cover on half the top so it's ok if it rains. Not all buses have live commentators - just the red line. The gal talked and told stories the whole time! Even when we were stuck in bad traffic.

If you aren't sure where to go as the maps are confusing, ask the big bus workers at the stops. They are easy to spot and well marked in jackets. They are so helpful and friendly.

The free walking tours are fun but you need to keep up and sometimes weave through over foot traffic. Not great with a stroller or older person. The national gallery is right there - leave slower people to gaze about in there.

My mum and I decided on the spur of the moment to get on a bus tour of London from the Tower of London and chose a Big Bus Tour....or rather they chose us! We bought the hop on/hop off ticket and got off at Parliament Square, walked from here to Buckingham Palace then got back on the bus to a Green Park. At Green Park we switched to a red route as we were tight on time (the blue route is much longer) this was the best decision as red routes have live commentary, and our commentator, Big Steve, totally made this tour.

His jokes were hilarious and his knowledge of London and British sayings was fab, we learnt so much on this tour, Big Steve you are a bus tour legend and we applaud you for making this tour a massive highlight of our weekend!

I think a Big Bus Tour is great i any new city. Today we did the red rout also the river cruise from Westminster back to the Tower I would advise to do it other way round as there are a lot of road works

The bus is great as long as you are not in a rush. There are many was to hop off and walk and pick back up. We used this for our 3 day stopover and it was useful. We expected slow travel from it- being in a city from London.
That all being said- not one friendly driver in the 10 we met- sown downright unfriendly. Also- the person who exchanges your voucher for ticket (we prepaid in the u.s. ) was rude. They are all after you to buy a ticket- but the minute you get your ticket and ask a question- he can't be bothered with you. We had to figure a lot out ourselves.

Buy a 1 day pass - then take the subway!

We got a three day pass for the Big Bus Tours which included unlimited trips on the bus, and a FREE river cruise, which was absolutely beautiful. My family and I were looking for things to do and how to get around, and Big Bus did just that. With a wonderful guided audio tour and an amazing outdoor view, Big Bus gave my family a fun and wonderful experience that we will never forget. I highly recommend Big Bus Tours as an eventful and exciting way to get around London.

Took a two day pass so just done the entire circuit on the first day.It was drizzling rain but the bus provides ponchos for those wanting to go upstairs.This sort of added to the experience.The next day we used the hop on hop off function especially due to the fact that the buses are no longer allowed to drive past the front of Buckingham Palace.As stated in previous reports , the red buses with actual tour guides were much better than the pre recorded blue buses.

On the evening of 15th April 2015, we boarded a Big Bus near the Waterloo bridge, and enjoyed seeing one of the world's great cities lit up spectacularly. I heard that our guide (Robert, I think) was in pain with a bad tooth, but he did a fantastic job with his commentary, and his friendliness was second to none. All the sights worth seeing were discussed, and interesting points were highlighted. I had waited since my long-gone childhood to see London, and now I was being shown around by an expert! I would recommend this tour to anybody who wants to see London with its lights on! Shawn and Juliana, Port Macquarie, N.S.W., Australia.

We got a two day pass and used the Big Bus tour to visit multiple sights. There was a stop 15 minutes walking distance from the hotel. The first day we road the bus just to preview where we would spend time on the second day. Must admit it was a great way to see the city. Really enjoyed the live tour on the second day.

From WI, USA, took my parents to London and they wanted to spend a day out in the country and see Stonehenge. Jenny did a wonderful job of livening up the tour without being overbearing or annoying and gave useful information to the attendees. Just enough time at Stonehenge, and plenty of time at Bath. A nice walking map of Bath was provided. Bath is easy to cover in a few hours of walking. Would happily recommend to other folks looking for a tour in the West Country. Bus had a bathroom (W/C) on board..

Only issue I can identify is not really the fault of the tour company. We hit terrible traffic on the return to London, and had to push our table booking by an hour. Also, the wifi on the bus was spotty, even in London on the raised carriageway (highway).

We got on at Victoria and returned to Buckingham Palace after about 2 hours of sightseeing a lot of London, that we would not have neccessarily seen. Well done Big bus! The sights looked even better lit up at night so it was a great alternative to just seeing the 'daytime' architecture.There is a commentary that can be listened to in 8 different languages, but you need either bring your own earplugs or purchase them from the Big Bus on entering. The seats are ok but a little hard by the end of the journey- but worth it. We would recommend but get there early so that you can get a seat on top as this is an open top bus (for a better view)!

We have used big bus tours in a number of major cities around the world. This one in London lived up to our expectations. The audio commentary was clear and timely. Bus drivers were friendly. The London traffic made it difficult for the tour buses to stay on their schedule, I think. At one point we had to wait for over 20 minutes for a bus and then three showed up at one time.

This is a great way to see the city. There is a live commentary o the tour which makes seeing the sites more fun. You get to see everything that tourist want to see. There are many stops along the way allowing you to hop on and hop off. Every tour guide was great.

Visiting a friend who had to work the first day I was there I planned a bus tour. It was really a great experience, they has free audio tour while you drove around, there was wifi on the bus, the tour guides were amazing, and I was able to hop off at the stops I wanted to visit and then get back on since the buses came by every 20 min or so. I really got to see all the main attractions I wanted to see in one day. Which left time for my friend to show me around the less touristy things. Went it December so every storefront and all the main streets were decorated in Christmas lights and it was really enchanting. I would recommend going in December - it wasn't too cold either.

I asked the driver when the next bus will be along if he had any ideas he arrogantly got rude to me and shut the bus Doors and drove of I mean he should have at least some idea of the route he drives this just show big bus tours don't train their staff very well so if your thinking of touring with big bus tours you might want to check other tour services

We choose not to drive while in London and it certainly was the right decision. We used the Big Bus to get around London and see the sights. They provide earbuds to listen to a recorded tour narration while the bus in is motion. We had beautiful weather while there so we always sat up top in the open air section. The workers at the stops were VERY helpful and friendly which helps alot. It is nice to have friendly and knowledgeable people give you advice - Great job Big Bus!

Moving around through hop on and hop off buses was always the first thing to do when reaching a new city. And then I used it in london. It is a night mare to ride a bus that moves most of the time like a turtle. There is traffic stand still in many areas of London or simply to many cars or buses on the streets.
I recommend use the subway instead. You can move around very easily and virtually everywhere.
The big bus staff is attentive and informative but unfortunately the service is compromise by the awful traffic in the city

I had a 24 hr layover in London and I wanted to see the city but didn't have a ton of time for tours or to walk around so this tour worked really well for me. I really liked being able to hop of the bus if I wanted to check something out. The first guide was about as boring as Ferris Buhler's teacher so I hopped off the bus and waited about three minutes for the next bus that ended up having a great guide. You hit all the major landmarks and get a quick history. It's a good way to start off seeing London.

Had a day trip to London and bought a very reasonably priced ticket on the hop on hop off Big Bus Tour. Excellent and very knowledgeable tour guides, great overview of London, includes a trip down the Thames and very conveniently located bus stops. Only criticism would be that we didn't know what to look for when finding the first bus stop. There are no instructions when you book your tickets. We found a couple of very helpful London Bobbies who directed us. Highly recommended

We loved the Big Bus Tour in London. The tour guides are very knowledgeable and funny. Since the tour is Hop on-Hop off, you can basically use it as your transportation for the day. We suggest you take this tour within the first day or two of the trip to help you get familiar with the town and the sites, then you will know what you want to spend more time on for the rest of your trip. I also suggest you sit on top unless it is heavily raining of course.

This is the best way to see the city. The red route brings you to all of the attractions you need to go and has a live person speaking in a microphone. Lots of interesting facts are learned. Buses are clean and comfortable. You can also get a package that includes a river cruise. If you hop off buses come by every 10 minutes. I recommend to see London this way.

Bus tours of this type are a great way to get an overview of a city so you can decide what areas/sights peak your interest and can re-visit later. Be sure to note that there are several different bus routes. I briefly took the blue route to meet up with the red route. The red one has live commentary, the blue one only has pre-canned audio that requires you to bring your own headphones.

Assuming traffic isn't that bad and you can time it right, this is a good way to see London. They seem to run promos where you can get an extra day for free so plan your trip accordingly. The ticket also includes the river cruise, which is a good way to link up form say the Tower of London to the Westminster Abbey area.

Overall a pretty good experience, however the bus without commentary is pretty boring, and it can get pretty hot on the bus so make sure you get an open air seat at the top (which can be difficult as the buses are usually full). The drivers and tour guides are very friendly and helpful, the staff out on the street at the stops... not so much.

We find hop on hop off buses a great way to explore big cities but were very disappointed with the London Big Bus Tour, as the buses were full & the traffic horrendous. Often we could walk faster & as a result did not get all the way around.

Great overview of the city! The Thames cruise included with the tour is so so, but the walking tours were great! There are several tour bus operators to pick from and I'm sure they all have a nearly identical spiel and route, but I enjoyed my experience on Big Bus.

One thing - the live commentary on the Red Route is hard to hear if you're sitting in the open air area - where the good views are -- though you to get funny anecdotes from the tour guides. The blue route, which follows the same path as the red route and then some, offers recorded commentary that can be heard with headphones on any part of the bus. Never have to wait to long between them either.

I love Big Bus and I've taken them in Paris and Hong Kong and find them to be reliable and a truly fun time. You also get to hop on and off at their designated stops. This was no different as they took you to all the main sights in London. They have 3 lines here-red, blue, and a green one. Go on the blue one as it covers the red course as well.

The drivers were friendly and helpful about where to get off. The one thing I have is that for some odd reason on the stop on the Madam Tussards wax museum is that we were there for about 5-10 minutes which i don't understand.

We had heard a lot from friends about Big Bus Tours in London. We took the 3 day package which included Thames cruise and night tour as well.

The circuit is amazing which covers all key London attractions and the staff was very helpful. The bus frequency was good. We especially liked the Thames cruise to Greenwich. Night tour was a bit disappointing as it was still day light for most of the tour. It should ideally start after sunset.

Overall a great way to explore London for first time tourists.

Was looking forward to the big bus tour around London after prior experiences at city sightseeing tours Dublin. Our family of four had a disappointing day.

The busses arrived infrequently, waiting more than half an hour on more than one occasion. There were no live tour guides, just recordings. We simply gave up and took the tube home.

Save you money, buy an oyster pass and a map, and visit the same sights at your leisure.

We were lucky enough to have a Big Bus stop right outside our hotel which made it very convenient. I had purchased ticket vouchers online before our trip but the company has workers at each stop selling tickets for the bus and for attractions. Usually their price for the attraction tickets is a few dollars cheaper than buying tickets directly at the attraction.

Buses came often (about every 10-15 minutes) and they had routes running in "both directions", so depending what stop you wanted to go to you could choose a quicker option than riding the entire route all the way around.

Some bus routes had automated tour guides, which you could listen to with earphones in a variety of languages. However, we preferred the live tour guides (English) who gave commentary as you drove around - and they could answer questions. Very informative!!

Also loved the app for my phone. I could download the city bus route map and could reference it even without using data on my phone for having wifi.

Very efficient way for us to see much of London during a short 2-day trip.

We had to wait some time before we got on the Red Line. Three Original Bus Tour buses went by before any of the Big Buses did. I thought we might have made a mistake picking BBT. Those feelings disappeared once getting on the bus and sitting up top. It was really great to see the sights. Peter was a awesome tour guide! He was very animated and had great tid-bits! I recommend the boat tour, which is included to get a different perspective and photo options of London.
We printed out our reservations and got a discount. Also this tour can get you in one of the sights for a discount cost..and minus the lines!

We're not "tour bus people," but with 3 generations, we took some advice and booked a 2 day, hop on, hop off tour with a river cruise. Bought on line to save money. Totally worth it. Took the Blue bus, so we could listen in multiple languages.

Just down London for 24 hours but the tour bus is a great way to get around London & see all of the sites & London's main attractions. Also you can just hop on & off buses when you like so this is also a great way to get about the city other than using the underground tube whilst taking in the sights. Only have to take into account the time of the tour as if the tour states one or two hours remember that this does not account for traffic delays around the city, so ensure you have enough time for this journey. Well worth the money
This bus tour was a fantastic way to see some key tourist sites in London. Tour guide was very informative as well, and took care to get you on a connecting tour if you wanted to.

Love the Big Bus Tour. It's a great way to get an overview of London and some fun interesting facts as well. It's also great to do on your first day in London to help tired travelers. I've done it twice and have enjoyed it both times
Good value for money gives good view and info to hop on and off when you want to explore and with the good weather boat trip included was lovely way to view london

went to London for the weekend with a friend the bus tour is a must as there is so much to see in London the tours are great with buses running regular and really friendly staff around at most stops to offer advice . already planning to go again

What a wonderful way to learn your way around London. My friend and I did this tour 3 times and loved every minute of it. It helped us to get our bearings and learn to find our way to anywhere we wanted to go. We never got lost. We saw and learned so much about London and its history. We are returning to London next year and will Defnitely do the bus tour again. :)

It was a perfect way to see the major sites during our long London layover! (We had an 8-hour layover but only 2-3 hours actually in London. We took just part of the tour--great to be able to pick and choose!) We really liked having a live guide on the red line as well, and buses came wonderfully often. I saw other companies' buses, too, and can't compare--they all use the same stops. We bought online then exchanged our paper for printed tickets when we saw a staff member at the stop but the bus hadn't yet arrived. In planning, it would have been even more helpful if the map online had been higher resolution, if the stops' locations had been more specifically described (e.g., the Tower Hill stop) and if the stops within a block of Underground stations had been marked with an asterisk (so groups whose members can't walk far would easily plan). But overall wonderful trip!

been to London a few times but never done the bus tour so thought would try it...decided to go on red (shortest) route. Bought tickets from street vendor.£32.00 per person!. Had to wait more than 25 minutes for bus to turn up, this was at 1030am. The guide was very good and informative. We got off at St Paul's cathedral..didn't go in though as that would have put our spending before midday to over £100. Returned to bus stop to continue our tour..7 busses came and went..all full..in the end we walked back from St. Paul's to regent street..very tired and skint.

If you are limited on time and the weather is nice, this bus will take you everywhere in London and give you a ton of info on what you are seeing. What I really liked is it made frequent stops so if something was interesting, you just get off look around and another bus comes along in 15 minutes. You just jump back on and continue your tour where you left off.I loved setting on the top of the open air bus, it was like live interactive guided museum tour. Where all of London was the museum. We bought a two day pass. It was also nice that we could use the bus to just get around to different places we wanted to go in London for a little cheaper than the all day train pass.

The Big Bus Tours was a wonderful experience and it's one that I would highly recommend to everyone! All of the staff were so friendly and they couldn't do enough to help us.
The hop on hop off element was great and made it easy for us to experience all that the city of London had to offer. When we booked the tickets we were given an extra day on the buses for free along with a free River Thames Cruise which was also brilliant!
I would highly recommend booking Big Bus Tours!

London is a massive city to explore with myriad sights for tourists to visit. You really need a full week or more to do it justice. Fortunately, the tube, rail and bus system is incredibly efficient.

Another helpful option is a three-day "Big Bus Tour" ticket that ferries us to all the major sites throughout the city such as The Eye, Tower of London, St. Paul's Cathedral, etc. Of course, we stop at our favourite location in Bloomsbury, the British Museum, wandering about the amazing Egyptian section and the marbles 'liberated' from the Greek Parthenon in Athens. We work in the National Portrait Gallery as well. The Big Bus Tour supplies each passenger with earphones, and their commentary is informative.

This is a great way to see the city!

The tour bus is so enjoyable yet full of knowledge on the history of london...its winter when we went there...lucky for us that its not raining and we can feel a bit of sun...the free river cruise is also great...

however..since its winter..we need to rush before it gets dark around 3pm..but if u stay longer in london...it can be use for 2 days..

Will definitely give another try during summer...

Was in London for the day so decided to do bus tour as we do anywhere we go. Almost had a heart attack when we were told the price even though it did include a "free" river cruise. Much more expensive than anywhere else we have been, including Barcelona! The tour does take you to all the major landmarks although you do only get a brief glimpse of Buckingham Palace. Contrary to most other reviewers I found the recorded commentary gave much more information than the guide. For example we passed the Royal Courts of Justice twice. The first time I had the recorded commentary which told me about them, the second time round the guide seemed to be only interested in the Twinings Tea shop and ignored the Courts completely. He also seemed to think that everyone was obsessed with Harry Potter. Some of us are not!
The best part of the tour was the river cruise. Excellent boats and a witty and informative commentary. The tour was well worth doing but, be warned, you may need to raid your piggy bank before you book.

I chose to take a bus tour because I was only in London for one day and wanted to see as much as possible. The BigBus tour allows you to get on and off at any stop which is a great way to pick and choose what attractions you want to see, and to still see and hear commentary on the sites you don't have time to tour. The radio headset worked great and you could hear the commentary clearly even with city noise and chatty passengers nearby. There is an included cruise on the Thames which was a nice change of pace from being on the bus the entire day. I only wish the bus ran a little later into the evening, as I had to cut short my Buckingham palace visit to make the last bus back to my drop off.

This was very convenient to most anyplace you could need to be in London. We stayed near Kings Cross, and there is a route that takes you from Kings Cross to Covent Garden where you get on "the" bus that takes you through the city. It was an excellent value. At first, we had a little sticker shock at the price, but by the time we finished the 3-hour tour on the red line (the blue line is longer), and understanding that we could use that bus for 48 hours as much as we wanted, we understood that it is an excellent value for the price. There are many stops and you can get off if you like and then back on. The last route starts at 7 pm, so it wouldn't be convenient for taking yourself to dinner and back to your hotel, but well worth the price. Good tour guides gave a lot of history.

Overall, we were pleased with the tours and would do it again. The live commentary on the Red Line is better than the recorded on the Blue. It didn't work out for us to do a walking tour, but we did ride the boat down to Greenwhich and actually enjoyed it more than we expected.

I had one complaint about the tour. It's very hard to determine when the buses stop running. I had read on the website that it was 4:30, but then one BB agent at the Thistle station (Blue Loop) told us that they run until 6:30 (and then Night tour starts a little later). I asked him how they end the tour, for example if we are in the middle of a route when the clock reaches 6:30 what happens. He said they do their best to try to get you back to a stop close to where you need. Fast forward to the next day, we are on the Red route and got on at Buckingham palace. I think it was around 5 pm. The tour guide starts telling everyone that they are ending the tour at marble arch. This was a shock to us, because this isn't the way we were told it would work. The bus driver ended up allowing us to ride the bus with him back to Westminster bridge, where we just barely ran and caught the city cruise back to London Tower (Near our Lodging). I appreciate the driver helping us, but was disappointed that BB put is in a situation where we needed to ask for a favor. To be honest, none of the Employees seem to be very clear on how this works at the end of the day.

Another comment, it appeared that Original Buses came by more frequently than BB. It also seemed that the BB sales guys were more concerned with getting the next sale, than helping customers who had already purchased. I might be tempted to try Original tours if I went again. But with all of that being said, we did enjoy the BB tours.

We just flew from Boston to London.. Ironically we did the Boston Bus tour while there and then because we loved it so much in Boston we decided to do in London. The Boston tour guides had excitement, stories to tell, were giving good vision of what happened. This bus tour was great for the stops but the lack of enthusiasm made it not worth it for us.. Ironically when we got on the London/Thames river Boat tour the Tour Guide was great. So if you can or do this tour MAKE SURE you don't miss the BOAT tour from Tower of London.

My husband and I were in London for about two days. We wanted to see all the sights London is known for (i.e.Big Ben, Westminister Abbey, Tower Bridge, etc.). We decided to take the Big Bus Tour, and we are so glad that we did! They had a deal that allowed us to buy a one-day ticket and use it for two days! Highly recommend!

The Big Bus Tour lets you hop on and off at the different stops, and it offers several stops throughout the city! Included is a river tour that puts you on a boat in the River Thames; my husband and I really enjoyed this!

If possible, take the red bus route. The red route has an actual person explaining the different sights. We heard two different guys, and both were entertaining and made us laugh. The blue route offers audio in several different languages, but you must listen with earbuds (that are provided for you).

Overall, it was a great experience. It seems considerably inexpensive for everything you can do and get to see! I highly recommend it, especially if you are only in London for a short time!

I bought my 2 day Big Bus tour with river cruise along with my vacation package and it was easy to exchange my voucher for a ticket from a Big Bus agent at the stop closest to my hotel (Russell Square).
I loved the live commentary on the red line, the guide was good and hilarious. I wanted to see the shopping areas (such as Harrods) so I had to change to the blue line. The blue bus took at least 40 minutes even though the agent said it was coming in 10 minutes. The green tour/link is just as bad, very infrequent. Plan on bus delays…agents will tell you that certain roads were closed or traffic is bad (you will see this for yourself too) but I think Big Bus should improve how well the buses keep schedule.
The two day tour included a river cruise which was good. I got on at Tower Pier and we had live commentary from another funny guide…hopped off the cruise at Westminster Pier.
I think the people on your tour bus/boat add to the experience. I was lucky that both my red line bus tour and river cruise both had had very upbeat travelers, coupled with funny guides which helped to soothe the sometime lengthy wait times between buses. I did not try the walking tours which were also included in the price.

We had only one day in London. We chose Big Bus Tours as it was only a block from our hotel. It was a good choice! The tour give us a good overview, stories about points of interest and was worth the price and approximately 4 hour time. We had a great guide, which helps. We found out he'd only been on the job a few weeks, so obviously they have a good guide-training program. Although you could 'hop on/hop off', we didn't. We rode out the whole tour.

When I Entered in my hotel Hilton, the staff had told me that please go through the BIG BUS Tours once because we are like 7 peoples and it will cost us very expensive if take any cab for site seeing and defenetely i tell you the Big bus tours is more than the cab and everything else. The bus has so many stops so that i can stop anywhere for one site seeing and then i can pickup another bus of big bus tours thats the beauty of this. so no need of time lapsing and getting late for bus and its not for one day pas its for 3 days tours really awesome trip for us. the big bus tours made our trip to london really amazing. i covered each and every [place of London from Madamm tussade to Tower of london. thanks for wonderful experience
Hop on hop off is a great way to acclimate yourself to,the city. Just make sure you,take the bus with the live tour guide, not the audio. We ended up on both and the live guide was much better.
I thought the Big Bus Tour is a great place to start, they point out a lot of the local landmarks with pretty good descriptions.
Four of us and a small dog enjoyed our Big Bus tour and boat trip on 6th June. The buses were frequent and the staff really helpful. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend this company.

We went on the Big Bus Tour on a sunny Saturday, so London was quite busy but being on the bus was a great way to see the sights and not be caught up in the crowds. We paid around £25 each for one day. There were lots of buses and we never waited more than a few minutes, we also always got 4 seats together. Our first guide, I think was called Elizabeth and was excellent, her knowledge was amazing and really entertaining. She was a credit to the company.
I would have marked the Big Bus Tour London 5 stars but unfortunately the last tour guide was not such a credit and let the company down, he asked far too many times for people to tip him if they wished, and this was said as people had to walk by him to get down the stairs when leaving the bus, which we felt uncomfortable with as after only two stops on his tour bus we did not tip him. We sat near him on the bus and I heard him mutter away from his microphone "nothing" after one group got off without tipping him despite him informing them they could do so if they wished and it would be appreciated. I never like people repeatedly asking for tips, and with this style of tour where you continually hop on and hop off so many buses, its too expensive for us to tip each individual tour guide, though I would be happy to tip good service if we had done a longer tour with a specific guide. I wish we had not done this tour bus last as it left a negative note. However, in fairness to the other excellent and entertaining guides we had who did not mention tips but still got some and well deserved, I would definitely recommend the Big Bus Tour to people and have done so already.

It is by far the fastest and most efficient way of getting to know London, used it as transportation due to its hop on and off service. Very professional employees and very welling to make sure you have a great time!!

Loved the big bus tours, showed you all the top attractions. The free walking tours that comes with your ticket are excellent. The staff are very helpful. I would highly recommend this tour. great value for money.
We did this tour and we had no regrets. The upperside of the bus is good when it is good weather. We were lucky and saw all big points of london in a summer day. It was a real great experience!

I wanted to take my son for a true experience on the Hop-On/Hop-Off Big Bus Tour. I purchased the 2-Day pass, hoping that it would help us achieve our goal in experiencing as much as the city as possible in a limited amount of time. If I would have been aware that there was construction or heavy traffic throughout the day, I certainly would have stayed away completely! When purchasing these two expensive tickets, I was not informed or advised of the construction or incessant traffic (even when it wasn't rush hour!). I'm sure this company is well aware of the status of London roads, and yet they did not think of advising me that the ride would be extremely slow. Thus, what should have been an enjoyable experience was turned into a grueling ride that left me frustrated and annoyed. I do not exaggerate when I say that the bus was literally in the same spot for nearly half an hour. I was told that it would take me two hours to get to where I wanted to go; it took over four. I was also sitting with multiple other dissatisfied customers who were also venting their own exasperation at the tour. In the end, I didn't go to my destination, as I was fed up and decided to take the tube along with other unsatisfied tours after it was clear that we wouldn't be leaving our spot for another half hour. Soon, I'll be taking a flight to Paris to continue my vacation with my son. We had planned to partake in the Big Bus Tour but, after this experience, we are very skeptical to say the least. We will be approaching the managers of Big Bus because we demand that we receive our money back, or at the very least some sort of credit. VERY disappointed and very frustrated.

Big Bus Tours have two different buses, the red bus and the blue bus; they are the same type of bus, same colours and everything, but the red bus gives you the live commentator - they only speak in English - while the blue bus gives you a radio to listen to on your seat, just plus in your headphones, pick your language and learn all about the City of London and Westminster.

The tours are long, so be aware that the blue tour is a good few hours long, however you can get off the bus at particular attractions if you want to and rejoin the tour at a later time. You can also join with certain walking tours for no extra cost and a free river cruise too.

The views from the top deck are a must, however if it gets busy do not stand on the top deck since it is a health and safety hazard.

The complaint I heard from most of the passengers, myself included, was the radios that were meant to give us information about where we were, the history of the place or how it got it's name, weren't working. My one sounded like a tape that was ready to break, the woman in front of me didn't get any sound from her's, and her companions found that got static for most of the time. It's disappointing to not be able to learn much, or anything, because of machines not being fixed and it does make it feel like £32 has just gone down the drain when many people could have just taken the bus to go to certain places and to see the sights of the city for a lot cheaper.

This is a GREAT way to see the sights of London and allow you to get on and off the bus to spend time at the sights that are important to you. I definitely recommend the Red Line which includes love commentary. The guides were brilliant in Classic British humour.

The tour can include the river cruise as well which is a great way to see sights from another perspective. Definitely worth the money!!!

After our first day in London on a private tour with Graham Greenglass of London Cab Tours, my wife and I were prepared for a more extensive tour on our own.

I had done the research with my handy Rick Steves’ travel guide. We opted for a classic double-decker bus tour. However, there were many options to choose from:

(http://www.londontoolkit.com/blog/daytrips/tours/comparing-londons-hop-on-hop-off-sightseeing-buses/).

Based on the reviews, we went with London’s Big Bus Hop-on, Hop-off due to Steve’s recommendation of having the best live narration. We purchased our tickets in advance online, which were easy! We received a discount by purchasing the Tower of London passes too (Bus Tour plus Tower of London Tour for two- £97.98).

The hop-on, hop-off bus tour also included a free cruise along the River Thames and free guided walking tours. For the savvy traveler, there are over 80 stops with plenty of famous London sights, including Tower of London, Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, and Westminster Abbey.

This particular bus tour has two different routes with one live English speaking guides to provide a personal touch (Red line) while the other provide an audio commentary chosen from 12 languages (Blue line).

You get a free map and ear buds for the audio commentary. Make sure your ear jack works near your seat. We found some jacks did not work.

Yet, the audio commentary is not very good because it often is slightly off from the visual we see on the bus. Nevertheless, the environment is good for photo ops in front of famous landmarks (you will see lots of folks taking selfies).

Sadly, we ran out of time and were unable to use the free tours. If possible, plan enough time to maximize your freebies.

Let me say that Hop-on, Hop-off bus transportation is not a very efficient use of your time in general due to the numerous stops and traffic congestions primarily in large cities.

However, I have found Hop-on, Hop-off transportation is an excellent way to get a great overview of an area in a no hassle way (if you have time and are patient).

I highly recommend this tour for anyone who wants a great overview of London without a heavy drain on his or her wallet.

I hopped on one of these buses yesterday after doing no research but just saw it driving by and thought it would be interesting. The tour was absolutely fantastic. It was fully guided in English on the red tour. The tour weaved it's way around london as the guide told us interesting facts about the area including things you could never find out on your own without extensive research. I hopped off at the Tower of London so I could do some exploring there before rejoining another bus and continuing the journey back to where I began. Overall very impressed and would highly recommend to those young and old
Never been London but had to go so I booked a tour and it was brilliant me and a companion we went on the bus tour and enjoyed it and also took advantage of the free boat tour to ty

We had a full day in London before a connecting Eurostar, so decided to take a bus tour rather than ride the Tubes.

Cost was managed via Tesco Clubcard, with a simple visit to the office a short stroll from Trafalgar Square, then we boarded on leaving the Eye.

There are multiple routes, with different buses also covering different languages, although we usually found the English ones quite easily. A lovely bonus to this is the boat down the Thames from the Tower, which afforded alternative angles for those photo ops of the Eye, etc.

I would recommend planning your route in advance as some of the gaps between stops can be lengthy, you can easily hop from Red to Blue line wherever they cross, or like us walk a small distance to cut out a huge swathe you have no interest in.

Recommended for those wanting to see more of London and have the time to do so

Did the big bis tours a few days ago and the live commentary is the way to go. Kevin is the best tour guide for the changing of the guard. Best way to see London is on the Big Bus. I have done it twice now and it was great every time.

Even though been to London may times, hadn't been on the open top bus. Yes there was traffic, but you expect this in a City on a Saturday, however tour guide was very informative and a good way to see London. Would recommend the red tour

We bought a family of 4 ticket for a recent trip to London, £79 total cost. First we were walking from our hotel to the Natural History Museum but the ticket stall holder told us there was a stop right outside the Museum so we could hop on a big bus and be on our way. However, when we left the museum there was NO big bus stop outside, I asked a lady on the entrance gate to the museum and showed her the map we were given and even she was puzzled. Eventually we found it some way further down the road, NOT outside the museum! This got us off to a very frustrating / disappointing start. However, the tour itself is interesting with the headphones you are provided with to plug in and listen to all the points of interest. The first bus we got on was very busy and we couldnt get a seat which meant we couldnt listen to any commentary. If you get a bus with a red light on the front this gives you live commentary from a tour guide on the bus, the blue light signifies its a recording to listen to through your headphones. This sounds great in principal but actually you just end up getting on the first big bus you can find and take pot luck as to whether it is a live commentary or recorded. We were guided through many interesting streets steeped in stories from the olden days and famous people who lived there etc. You wouldnt get this just walking round on your own, in fact we thought we would have missed Downing Street if we had been on foot on our own as it was literally down a main street but not obvious until pointed out to us on the recording system. We got off at Madame Tussauds so we could walk to Regents Park as the weather was glorious. We had a few hours walking in the sunshine then headed down Oxford Street as we noticed there was a big bus stop outside Hamley's Toy Store on the map so we thought we couldnt possibly go wrong. .... Oh yes, the stop IS NOT outside Hamley's, its further down the road outside other shops but actually has a sign on it saying "Hamley's Toy Store Stop" - Again, very frustrating and confusing. Once again when we got on the bus it was overcrowded and we had to stand some of the way waiting for people to get off so we could grab their seats. Eventually we all got seated and continued. You can stop at Westminster Pier and get a ferry boat down the river which was good, a very funny interesting guide giving us various facts and information along the way. It stops near the Tower of London where you can get off so we chose to do this so we could get some good photos of the tower and of Tower Bridge itself which is quite a majestic sight. You can stay on the boat if you wish and simply cruise back, its up to you. However again when we wanted to find the big bus at Tower Hill area we struggled to find it from the map provided. In the end it was pot luck we saw a bus driving along the road and watched which direction it went in. We dashed across the road and luckily for us it had pulled up some time waiting so we hopped on but god knows how long it would have taken us to find another one if we hadnt seen that one. We managed to sit on the top deck as it was getting towards 6.00pm so bus was quieter and I must admit this part of the tour was fantastic as you got a fabulous view of the streets and famous buildings from higher up, seeing them from a different perspective and angle than you would walking. We went past Westminster bridge, Big Ben, through Trafalgar sq and Buckingham Palace etc, all the main sights with good commentary. At about 7.30pm the buses suddenly all pulled up and it seemed as though the drivers were wanting to finish for the day, even though the map details say they run until 8.00pm. they were asking where people wanted to go and asking them to get on another bus basically so that some of the buses could finish for the day. We thought this again very annoying. We wanted to go past Harrods but the driver told us the route we were on did not go that way at that time of day (how convenient for him) so we got off. All in all it was a good tour, but our day was very tiring walking to try and find these bus stops and we got totally frustrated that the stops were not as shown on the map we were given. If you weigh it up for a family of four £20 each to go round London, see most of the sights and get a little ferry cruise as well is not bad at all. Just be prepared for a long tiring day if you want to make the most of these hop on hop off buses (if you can find the stops)

Rising the big bus is the most cost effective way to see the city. The hop on hop off tour gave us a chance to take photos and take in the sights. The route guide was awesome on the Red Route. The Blue Route had an automated tour guide.

Of the hop-on, hop-off options in London, this is apparently the most popular, based on how crowded the buses were. We took the "red line" with the tour guide providing live commentary, vs the blue line which covers more ground but where you are relying on pre-recorded commentary. The buses are very nice, with an open 2nd floor and knowledgeable and entertaining tour guides. The option to also get a Thames river boat ride was also a welcome plus. Downside is that people tend to get on the bus at the same stops in large numbers at different times of the day (so getting on a bus in the hotel district of Piccadily in the morning is crowded, as is getting onto a bus at the Tower of London towards the end of the day), so we had to pass up buses twice during the day as they were too crowded for us to board. So maybe another bus company that isn't as popular would have been more convenient!
Note on seating: 2nd level has better views, the first few rows are covered so are a bit warmer / more protected. If you can get into the first row on the 2nd level, the view with the full glass window in front of you is awesome,
Note on timing: the last bus starts out at 6PM from the originating station. Given that the entire route takes over 2 1/2 hours, that means that there will be buses circling around well past 6PM, especially as you get deeper into the route. But after 6PM, you can't loop around from the final stop (The Marble Arch on the Red line), to one of the earlier stops if that's your intention.

First visit to London and wanted to see a bit of everything. The Big Bus Tour is the way to go. Unfortunately the weather was cold and rainy but soon forgot about that once Ashley got on board. Her live commentary was the highlight of the day. In the end we had to get off to go to the toilet and have lunch but could have stayed on all day. Ashley you are a star!! The whole Big Bus Experience is great, very easy to get on and off, passing all the big attractions, plenty of buses, great way to see London.

These tours are very affordable, convenient and a great way to get around when sightseeing - goes to most places needed allowing you to hop on or off at any point! Different languages are also available for these buses. Wouldn't do it any other way - great staff as well willing to help out

We have tried many of the hop-on-hop-off busses and opportunities in our many trips to London, and this is by far the best on we've found. The crew inside and outside of the bus were unfailingly pleasant, helpful, and seemed to honestly love what they were doing. We will use them again without question: The Big Bus.

I always take a city tour by bus when I am arriving in a new city. It gives a good overview of the city and of the main sites before focusing on what I am interested in seing afterwards.

The Big Bus tour in London provides an interesting tour that lasts several hours; the comments are very interesting. Of course, it is better to stay in the upper deck.

This is the Best & cheapest way to see the sights of London. We bought a family ticket which lasts for 24 hours from the time you first start useing it so if you first get on at 15.00 hours it doesnt run out till 15.00 hours the next day! The buses run every 10 mins roughly from each stop so you can hop on & off till your worn out!!

For the price, this is honestly the best value way to see London. I have now done the big red bus tour twice and taken the Thames river cruise (included in ticket price) once. For sure book your tickets online in advance for a better discount, but really effective way to see as many of the London sites as possibly on a limited timescale and/or if your a bit lazy and can't walk that far in a day. Really great that you can hop on and off as many times as you like, would advise getting the map and planning your stops and hop on/off's in advance so you don't waste time having to double back on yourself.

Getting around London can be expensive so this worked out perfectly for us for both sightseeing and as a mode of transport. They have two routes, one with live English commentary and one with recorded commentary available in 9 languages (they supply earphones). The route covered from Kensington to the Tower Bridge. Although we bought the Night Tour, it was offered for 4£ if you bought a regular day ticket, we wouldn't recommend it. It was a shortened route of the day tour but allowing you to see the buildings illuminated at night. Would recommend this tour to anyone as both a way to see/learn about London and as a transport to get on/off the bus while shopping and or exploring.

The tour is worth every penny. It covers most of London attractions. The tour with the live commentator is very informative and interesting. The ticket includes river cruise and a walking tour which is also good. There are many buses so the Hop - on hop - off idea is good to go into museums and attractions.
Good job guys. Simply amazing.

We went to London for the day with 2 of our children the bus tour was great value for money and allowed us to see all the sights of London. The tour information was pre recorded and full of information. The best way to see London in a short space of time.

We took the Big Bus London tour on 17th March 2015. It was just as we imagined - a fantastic introduction to an outstanding city. Also worth complimenting the staff at the bus stops who provide information on routes and times, they were all very friendly. The tour itself covers everything you expect to see with some really great views of the city and landmarks, and the time you spend on it is up to you. Overall, an bus tour of London!

Was a bit dubious about doing a bus tour but this was a fantastic way to get around everything in a limited time the guides were very informative and made everything come to life even asking me and my partner to get married three times on the trip lol.the best thing is you can hop on and off at various places of interest and see the best of what London has keep up the good work big bus also we had a river cruise which sees the city from the Thames in a different perspective.big shout out to your staff

We started with a Big Bus Tour that was a great way to get a feel for the city. we did the river cruise and got pictures of all the main sights. Between the oyster card we bought at the airport and the big bus tour we had no problem getting everywhere we wanted to go.

We only had a few hours to spare but didn't want to waste it and thought a bus tour of the main attractions would be good. So glad we did it. Rested our aching feet and learnt lots of interesting facts on London into the bargain. The RED big bus tour is the one you need if you want live commentary with funny trivia into the bargain. The blue big bus tour has earphones and a choice of different languages I believe but we loved having Robert and Phil as our commentators/guides, full of fun and interesting facts. Seemed expensive initially but if you buy a ticket first thing in the morning then you can fit a whole lot in ie bus tour, walking tour, river trip etc., we only had time for the bus tour so I cannot comment on the other ones but we will try and do the lot next time we are in London. (Winstone and Pitch the drivers were friendly too, makes a change as we find most bus drivers in most cities are miserable!)

We went on the blue bus with the audio recordings and the red bus with the live tour guide. Jess was fantastic and full of interesting information and facts. What a great atmosphere. He was also very helpful in guiding us off at the right stop so that we could get on the tube. Great two days in London.

While it is helpful to have the on and off option while touring London. We had to wait approximately 20 minutes for a bus at each of our bus stops. There are two bus options red and blue. Red is all languages, blue is english with a live tour guide on the bus describing what you are seeing. We much preferred the personal touch. The drivers of the bus have no idea where things are. When we disembarked at the train station to see platform 9 & 3/4 the driver told us to go across the street when in fact we were right in front of the train station. On another occasion the driver told us the ride to Kensington Palace (a tour we purchased through Big Bus) was the next stop. He then proceeded to drive all around the city which resulted in us having to get off to make a show that evening. All in all I wouldn't recommend this company. The Original Bus tour seemed to have more buses and a friendlier more knowledgable staff.

Thames River Cruise Portion
- unique view of London and its landmarks from the river
- lively, entertaining and easily heard commentary
- the boat crew took time to give good angles for unique pictures of sites along the river
Bus Tour Portion
- caught the highlights of central London with this hop on / hop off tour
- had the live commentary over speakers, but being in the open top, we had trouble hearing all that was said; there is lots of traffic and construction noise in London streets
- the parts that we did hear were informative and entertaining
- the tickets were valid for the remainder of the day of purchase and the next day, allowing flexibility
- this tour is best done on the first day to scout out where to spend time

We absolutely LOVED Big Bus tours! We had no idea of what to expect or where to go in London. Big Bus tour helped us get our bearings in London.

All of the staff were so helpful & friendly!

It made traveling London 100% easier!

Recommend to everyone traveling to an unfamiliar country!
The big bus company was great value . Informative and amazing guides. Price includes river cruise. Loved the ability to hop on and hop off. Stops at all major sights.

We ended up using the Golden Tour company who were complete GARBAGE! I saw these red buses EVERY 5 MINUTES or close to! My sister and I kicked ourselves everytime we saw these guys, wishing we had gone with them.

USE THESE GUYS FOR A TOUR! Using the bus tours, is a great, fast, relatively cheap way to see London quickly.

And make sure to haggle with the salesmen, you can get the price down!

Firstly: I've had to put this in the "family with teenagers" category. I am in my 30's and took my mum for her birthday. So that's as close as I could get it.

We arrived at Euston Station to get the feeder (green link) bus to the main bus tour.

On the downloaded Map it's not Teri blu clear where the feeder bus stops. However after asking the staff via email they were very helpful and we found the stop (directly opposite the front of Euston Station) without issue.

As my mum travels in a wheelchair we stuck to the bottom floor of the bus. It was great weather and I reckon the views from the top deck must of been great. We used the blue tour which has a recorded commentary in a fair few languages available. It was actually really informative!
If you are planning on hopping on and off a few times I'd reccomend getting a 48hr ticket. We went for a ride on the bus after getting back on at the tower of london (see separate review) and we ended up getting off to get our train home. It's a great tour! I'd reccomend allowing a few hours to sit and ride the whole thing though!
Overall the staff were really helpful, buses were new and very comfy with leather seats!
Highly recommended.

I've been to London many times but this last Fall was the first time since having some major hip surgery.I do not like tours /crowds etc but knew I would have trouble walking as much as I had in the past, so I got a bus ticket for the bus tour.
It was great.It stops where ever you'd like to get off and you can walk around/site see and it was fun and comfortable.Almost as good as just being on my own to walk it all.Well priced and not the horrible alternative to just going out on my own that I thought it would be. I would recommend it to anyone with a problem with mobility or time constraints in a certain place.You get to see a lot in a relatively short time.Gives you a good fele for London and it's environs.

This bus tour has the red line and the blue line and you are able to get on and off whenever you want. Also included in the fee is the boat tour from London tower to the river bank across from the London Eye.

The bus service is very good and covers a lot of ground. We started on the blue route, as that was the only route close to our hotel. We got on the red route after our visit to Trafalgar Square and thoroughly enjoyed the live guide and his commentary - much more fun than the recorded audio guide on the blue route. The hop on hop off approach is certainly a good way to get an overview of the City and see glimpses of a lot of areas you might not have time to properly tour.

My husband and I recently traveled to London on our way to Scotland. With only 2 days to see the city, we knew a double-decker bus tour would be the best way. After comparing pricing and specials, we chose the Big Bus Tour company. We found the guides to be friendly, knowledgeable, and even funny. It was hard to see from within the bus, so we braved the cold February air to sit on top, where we had a MUCH better view. Don't take a double-decker without sitting on the top, at least for part of the tour! Unlike other reviews, we found the hop-on, hop-off system easy to use and timely. Finally, bus staff went above and beyond - when we were the last couple on the bus, they offered us three options for final drop-off, and were even willing to accommodate a drop-off closer to our hotel, which they did not have to do. :) Great service, guys!

Traffic in London is congested, as a result the buses take a long time to get through the city. We ended up getting off and walking to the British Museum, the bus ride to that point was already an hour and we were not even close. We did see more from the bus than by taking the Underground, it just wasted so much more time to take the Big Bus.
Biggest complaint is that the last bus starts its tour and leaves Marble Arch at 5pm, supposedly it took a minimum of 90 minutes to make it Westminster Pier. We were at the Pier at 6pm and waited for an hour- no Big Bus, many of the Original Buses. We could find nothing to help on the Big Bus map, waited in the cold, gave up after an hour and walked to the subway and took that back to the hotel.

London has so many sights, and this hop on hop off bus takes in all the sights. But your ticket and get the next day free. We were on it for 3 hours and it still had some stops to make but we decided to get off at Tower pier and get the free river cruise( included in ticket) back to Westminster pier. Definite good value.

Treated my partner to the London bus tour after our meal at The Ritz, the bus picked us up right outside. The evening was absolutely stunning, and the sights we saw were beautiful, I would definitely recommend this experience, especially at night. However, try to avoid going in the winter! We went in early January, and obviously wanted to sit on the open top deck, but we were absolutely freezing!
Went on this bus your yesterday and loved it, the highlight was the tour guide, he was really energetic and informative. The sites we visited in london were wow

Booked for 1 day via online without a problem. Well spent the day with Big Bus Tours. The Themse river cruise was amazing. Buses are quite comfortable, lots of stops and good tour guides in all of them. Had a great time

Booked the 2 days for 1 online without a problem. When we went to get our ticket validated we were told a boat trip was included but did not get the promised voucher book or walking tour.
Information states that buses run every 5 to 10 minutes but at one stop waited an hour for a bus and were told this was due to an accident. I appreciate these things happen but little comfort if you have a booking elsewhere. Guide on bus informed us that the queen would be visiting houses of parliament the next day and told us which entrance she would be using...luckily I researched this myself and discovered it was infact to be at Westminster abbey or we could have had another hour of wasted time. Our guide on last tour of day was very helpful and went around and asked everyone where they were heading and advised them where to get off. The 2 for 1 offer is good value ( if you get all that they advertise !!!) just a shame its only in winter months....maybe a discount on second day all year round as if you are hopping on and off during the tour one day is not enough to cover it all so works out expensive if their are several of you. Returning in august with family but think we will try another company next time.

On this visit to London we chose to do the tourist thing and take the kids on a one day BB tour. We just hopped on and off as we liked in the morning, very helpful and friendly. In the afternoon we headed back towards our final destination and boarded a bus which had guide on....fantastic. Really made the afternoon and the guide (Nick) was entertaining, informative and great fun. Would have done this from first thing if we'd thought about it as the guides make the experience. Would definitely do this again...

It was a wonderful experience. My group and I were in London for just three days and the Big Bus routes gave us the opportunity of getting a very nice opportunity to get a good sense of this wonderful city. All importants monuments, historic places.... Great opportunity... I will take this bus at every city I visit.

After an overnight stay in London we had planned to take a ride on The Eye before our train journey home. Unfortunately the weather was against us and low cloud and a drizzly morning meant it was not worth it. A spur of the moment decision was to take a bus tour and see the sights that way. The next 2hrs were an absolute delight ! We took the RED route which is just over 2 hours long..including Houses of Parliament,Buckingham Palace,St Pauls Cathedral.Tower of London and much more. (BLUE Route longer ) The buses run at 10/20 minute intervals and have many stops. Once you have purchased your ticket you can jump on and off at any of the attractions. We were fortunate enough to have a super guide Dave and driver Patrick. His knowledge was first class and with his little extra snippets of info and a witty sense of humour he made a drab grey morning very entertaining and totally enthralling. We both enjoyed every minute and it was well worth every penny (and that was without the included river cruise as we ran out of time)

I had a 48 hour pass which meant I was able to try out the blue (recorded, multi-lingual) and red (live English guide) lines. I thoroughly enjoyed both, and the opportunity to hop off and on to see what interested me.

I went with the red line today, and had Robert as my guide. He was knowledgeable, funny, and friendly throughout the tour, which is a particular achievement considering the traffic jam that

firstly this Big Bus Tours trip was a birthday present so I don't know how much it cost.
Also I live and work in London.
A great way to spend a few hours either as a tourist or as a Londoner.
Our tour lasted about 90 minutes, we learnt a lot of interesting things about the great capital including how rubbish the traffic is.
Highly recommend

this was by far the best investment for the money.. they take you all over london it was my first time and they suggested the blue loop so i could see it all then i could go with the red or green or both and see the points i really wanted too see.. I only had 1 and a half days to see it so i picked the places that were important and the drivers will help you so much they will tell you when to get off for your stop .. there is a nice view from the top they provide ear phones and a rain poncho because it rains alot i hear. only the one of the loops i think the red one has a live guide that tell you his way of seeing things or all others have non stop naration.. in our tour we bought the 24 hour pass and they offered 48 for bonus and they also let you ride on the river boat for part of the price it is enclosed and heated so that was nice it has two routes and you can do both.. perfect way to see the other side of everything.. under the london bridge great picture opp .they also include 3 walking tours ghost pub. harry potter and one other i didnt have time for but others said it was fun.. good fish and chips stands at the pier also . we took the last bus tour and ended at victoria station to go see a play at the apallo theater they got us there in plenty of time and we got to enjoy london at night see it all light up the tours end at 5-6 so dont forget and get stuck some place cabs pretty pricey.. but our driver paul was so nice and told us how to get to our hotel the safest way and fastest too. told us how to go see kensington station and much more .. no one was rude all were so helpfull.

There were a few choices of tour, The Central London tour and the museums tour were two we decided on. The information given by the guide was interesting and made you feel you knew more when you left the tour.
They were all hop on and off and the stops were well sited for the different landmarks and places to see.
Thanks to big Steve we had the absolute best bus tour ever in London England. Steve was entertaining & very knowledgeable. Thanks for a great experience !

Whilst in London with friends we decided to use the hop on/off bus to take in as much of London as we could over the weekend. Although it is pricey it was well worth it as we had such a great tour commentary off our guide Steve. He was so informative and although we have been to London loads of times before we learnt so many interesting new things. Well done Steve(Essex boy) you obviously enjoy your job! Thanks xx wrap up warm for the free river cruise.

As many have already said, if you're poor on time, this is a fantastic way of catching a good look of London. We were there for 2 days and bought the 48 hour ticket, which included a river and walking tour. That was money and time well spent. We couldn't have seen all the key attractions on our own in such a short time.

Being able to hop off and on again when we wanted to spend more time at a designated location made it easy to continue touring without worrying about transport arrangements. We also had a couple of very knowledgeable and entertaining guides on board which made the trip that much more enjoyable.

Highly recommended, especially for those who are not regular visitors to London.

In London for one full day and never really gone and seen the sights before so decided to do a sightseeing tour. Looked at the reviews for this bus an it looked spot on.

We got the red route tour which comes with live commentary and we had a guy called Phil doing ours and he was great. Spoke with everyone who got on the top floor of the bus and had great banter with everyone. Very knowledgable and extremely passionate about his home city. I would definitely recommend this tour to anyone coming to London. If you are here before the end of feb you get a 48 hr ticket for the price of 24 hr and a free river cruise.

I hate to be attacked by all these guys trying to sell you tours, but we had done our homework and picked them through the barrage of others pitching their tours.
What we liked was that they offered a Hop-on Hop-off tour for an average price: 32 GBP, but your ticket was valid for 2 days AND included a river boat ride.
They have a Blue Tour and a Red tour. Blue goes a little further west and has a driver/narrator in English.( Kensington Garden, Harrods etc Red is more East and has automated narrators in a big number of languages.
Great way to see London!!
Open-top is great, but bring scarves and a good jacket after october

first time visiting London? wanna to explore London the easiest & fullest way? wanna to see / explore as much as possible for yourself & your family with a cheapest budget & with a limited time? wanna feel & breath the London air? ....... I recommend Big Bus Tours - London...!

We have just had the most amazing weekend! We were entertaining 3 visitors from Belarus who had never been to the UK before. We had 48 hour tickets which included a boat ride on the Thames.
