We cannot believe how much we were able to fit into 2 days, thanks to Big Bus Tours. They made it very easy to get around London to see the main sights and attractions, which were clearly depicted on maps of the routes. Getting off and on at particular points of interest, was no problem at all, as the service was very regular, with helpful staff at hand...even on Sunday. Our guests were amazed at the choice of languages on the commentary. As Russian was an option, they were also able to enjoy all the fascinating information and anecdotes, getting so much more out of it. The places we saw and the things we did are just too numerous to list, but a highlight was that after having had a tour of The Tower of London and The Crown Jewels, we found it was very convenient to catch the boat back to Westminster. There were some very amusing and light-hearted details of interest pointed out by the Watermen, which we thoroughly enjoyed. We had beautiful views from the river of The Houses of Parliament and Big Ben and seeing The London Eye up close, inspired us to make that our first visit on Sunday. By Sunday night we were all totally exhausted, our guests were blown away by London and we were very proud to be British!!

Wow it was cold on the bus but fun. We sat on the bus as we wanted to get a feel for London 3 hours round trip from Point A back to Point A. Awesome scenery, but next time I will hop on and hop off a bit more frequently. This is perfect for people like us who have never been to London! Loved it

We're not usually big on tours like this, but a cabbie had recommended the Big Bus Tour of London and we're so glad we listened. We had the chance to see many of the sights we were planning on visiting along with a fun and engaging narrative from a live tour guide. There are also busses that provide a taped narrative, but we found the live commentary to be much more fun.

Over here from Australia, my partner and I decided to do a Big Bus tour to see the major sights and get orientated. This tour was fantastic - gave us the opportunity to see all the popular landmarks that we wanted to as well as go on some great walking tours. The staff are fantastic - guides like James, Jess and Kevin were so nice and highly professional. They were so passionate about what they were doing it made the experience that much enjoyable!
With the help of Big Bus Tours I was able to explore London for one day. Despite the rainy weather I enjoyed it.

We travelled as a family with 4 adults and 4children. The cost would seem expensive at £120, but....
It was wet and foreboding as we got on the bus at the Tower, and 4 of us braved the wet upstairs seats - protective kagools were provided, good touch and we used some spares to put over the seats. It was particularly wet but were British!
The difference was the live guide - he made the difference, Nick was excellent both in information and humour. He made the exact balance of keeping the dreadful conditions at the back of the interesting tour - London a great place with so much to see and hear, I would have loved to have had the tour in the previous days great sunshine it would have been so rewarding.
We got off at for lunch and went to Bill bar (good value and kid friendly).
We used the red tour but had planned to use the blue, which provides a more extensive tour but the number of stops and sites to see was really pleasant for the young children and Nick brought out interesting points for them - this guys a real asset.
We got back on the bus at Piccadily around 3pm and were all able to sit upstairs under cover, a small pod exists at the front providing protection - it was still raining.
The second guide was also very informative and underlines the lengths the company goes to in terms of training I would suggest.
At this stage we understood there was also a free river cruise and walking tour - i should have paid more attention to the information provided.
I think what's provided is a professional service, great buses which operate frequently, recepticals for buggies and good seating both upstairs and down; most of all, the people were competent helpful and provided great and interesting information across our greatest town. The number of stops provides access to all the main landmarks of London.
I understand discounts to numerous events going on in London are also provided - we did not use any due to time and weather unfortunately.
I would recommend the tours and will return. Well done and keep up the service, a staff member
also helped us with further information at Green park stop.

Thanks Alan Long.
Leigh On Sea

We would recommend the hop on and hop off London tour buses as an excellent way to see London with full commentry. There are also some excellent deals you can purchase making this an excellent cheap way to see London and the sights.

We have used this tour in Paris as well so looked forward to seeing London by bus. Red line has a live guide who was so helpful with subway advice as well. The tour covers all the main attractions in old London and using a two day pass is the best deal. Traffic is always a problem and late afternoon is worst. Tour in the morning if possible.Loved sitting up top and "soaking up" the city!

We purchased our tickets as a way to get to all the main attractions without hailing a taxi. Once we were sold our ticket $130USD for 2 days with London Eye, and Tower of London, the girl that sold us pretty much ignored our questions.
Red Route vs Blue Route is confusing. This bus is fine if you want a narrated tour, but it took us over 2 hours to get to the Tower of London, partially due to traffic. On return, we had to wait 20 minutes for a bus to get to Marble Arch, then another 30 to get back to Kensington Palace hotel area.
We noticed the other red bus company, Original Bus Tour always had representatives at each stop to help with inquiries. A nice touch when you're confused as to which direction bus went in.
Today we ended up taking a taxi back to hotel from London Eye and it took 10 minutes vs what looked like another hour waiting.
Next time I'm in London, I'll do more research on bus companies.
We thought about taking the tube, but it smelled horrible underground, and we did not feel safe.

The Big Bus tours winter web site special gave 2 days for less than the one day 32 GBP price...25 GBP for 2 days, including a R/T Greenwich boat bus tour. We boarded the Blue Line at 1:30 PM and it took 4 1/2 hours to make the circuit. It was fine upstairs until the sun started to go down at 3:30PM...then it was cold enough to go downstairs. We had been to London several times before, so the BB tour gave us a different perspective. If your time is short, the one day web ticket was 22.50 GBP, and you could take their purple line which is concentrated on the museums.

I have visited London numerous times before but never did the bus tours as I thought I knew London well enough.
The tickets cost us £24 each but this included a second day free, a boat ride and access to free walking tours.
As we only had half a day we decided to do the entire loop of the bus thinking it would only be an hour or 2. The entire loop took us 4 hours and was well worth it. It took us to all the tourist attractions of London that you would want to see in London and the commentary on the tour is really informative.
On the tour there are over 20 stops. If you wanted to get off at all the stops it would take you more than the 48 hours you get with your ticket but it gives you a good idea of places that you would like to go back and visit.
Although you could just buy a day travel ticket for the tube, for first time visitors or people not confident on the tube this is ideal as the stops are in convenient locations and you haven't got to worry about directions from tube stations.

This is a great way to see london. They drive around to all the main attractions plus more. You can get on or off the bus at any point and walk around. It's a great way of transportation and a tour of london. Especially great to see lots of London in a short amount of time. Also the fact that I got to ride on the iconic double decker red bus was a plus. The stops were well labeled and I could easily find where the pickup and drop off stops were. The tour guide was good. He talked about all the main things around London and threw in a little more interesting random facts here and there which I enjoyed. Typical tour. Overall I enjoyed my purchase of their ticket through them and I would recommend!

My family and I visited London recently for a Christmas family day out.
We used the Big Bus to learn a little more about London and to show the kids. As they hadn't been to London before.
They both loved it and listened using the ear phones provided.
The buses were easy to catch and gave a good deal of info.
Highly recommend.
Good service we enjoyed the tour. But some time the bus comes late & couse some troubles, also it is an easy way to see many places we can not see it without the big buss.

The best way to see London as a beginner It is a Hop on Hop off with either a tour guide or headphones so you could listen to the tour. we were taking Australian youngsters on their first trip to London and they thought it was in their words COOL. I even learnt somethings I didn't know about London.

My wife and like to do a Hop On-Hop Off tour when first visiting a big city because it gives you a good layout of the city and a good impression of what to do next. Big Bus Tours in London definitely delivered with live tour guides and an interactive sense of humor. I would definitely recommend them.

We took the Big Bus Hop on Hop Off. Our guide was informative and funny! There's a physical guide for the RED bus and audio guide for the BLUE bus. Both buses bring you to the major key attractions in London - Convenient indeed and the price we paid for 48 hours of ride was worth it.

This 'hop-on, hop-off' tour of central London takes about 3 hours and has 30 stops (at a guess). London is so diverse that it's hard to know where to start and this tour, with a multi-language guide, takes you through the lot. There are stops for shopping, for visiting the Tower, for watching the changing of the guard or for going up the London Eye. The service has three routes so there is likely to be one near your hotel or B & B. You can take any of the routes and the service goes on into the evening so you can use the bus to get home. We took the trip on the river, at sunset, which was awesome, but missed the guided walking tour which I regret. There are two other competing tours neither of which I have personal experience with; one of them is much the same and the other is cheaper but doesn't have the same coverage of the city.

A friend who had lived in London recommended the Big Bus Tours as the thing should we should do on our first day in London and we were glad we did. It really gave us a good perspective on all the sites and was ideal for helping us narrow down where we wanted to spend our time later. It also helped us get our legs underneath us after the flight from the day be. We also enjoyed the included river cruise as well. Being able to purchase and present the tickets on my mobile phone was an important factor in using Big Bus Tours and saved us some money too. None of the other bus tours had mobile phone buying available.

Have done hop on hop off in many cities but not London, because I know it so well! However, beautiful sunny day decided to try it and we had a great time. The earphones were average, guided ones are better, and despite the chill on top deck (we were well wrapped up and it was worth it), got a Birdseye view of the city. Went on the red route which takes you round main attractions apart from museums area of Kensington (which is blue). Negotiated small discount since valid for two dats and was only using it on one. Wrap up well and take some coffee with you if you are staying on all the way round!

Twenty years ago you wouldn't have caught me dead on a bus tour. Went for the touristy schmaltz on this trip and it's not bad. I advise the live vs the pre recorded trip; I think it's the A line vs the B line but not sure but we did try both. The guide on the live trip added a little extra info and was funny. It's a hop on hop off tour valid for 24 hours.

My impression was that there were more buses available for the competitor's buses, the Original Bus Tour run by RATP (the French!) but I could be wrong.

A good thing to do on your first day in London if you've never been; it gives you a good overview of the centre of town. We did it for my son's benefit and he seemed to like it.

We like taking BigBus when traveling abroad but were a bit skeptic about booking this bus tour after reading some of the reviews here. We also had people tell us that once you get a weekly pass travel card (oyster) you can just take regular city buses everywhere. But its definitely not the same. The tour adds interesting trivia information on some of the attractions and its fun to know. Also, the red line bus has live commentary which is alone well worth the price. We rode with a few funny tour guides that were wonderful, and especially Kevin who was funny and friendly.
A special thanks goes to Lee Fox who helped us when we got off the Marble Arch station and seemed to misplace our tickets. He made a few calls and nagged people to trace them with our credit card receipt even though its against their policy. Thanks Lee! Left a good impression and made us like London even more.

I was initially reluctant to take the Big Bus Tour but with limited time, I'm glad I did! The guides are entertaining, professional and very informative. The flexibility to hop on and off allows ample time to explore the best of London. I highly recommend it!

having been presented with a way of taking my girlfriend to london for the first time to go on the london eye i just needed a way to fill the rest of the day, family and friends recommended big bus as a way of seeing london at our leisure, ticket sellers were polite and knowledgeable, our guide on the bus (chris) was twice as knowledgeable also warm and welcome enough to make you forget the cold as he guided you around london so even my three year old learnt 3 place names.
All round a good experience i will be looking to return to once the summer season returns upon us

we booked our tickets from the newspaper / book stall out side Earls Court tube station we paid £29 each for 4 tickets and i have to say the person who sold them was great to deal with and he knew so much. the ticker lasted 2 days and also included a boat tour on the Thames to two difference locations. we had a ball and i do have to say the bus tour staff were wonderful and we were made so welcome on every bus.the ticket covered the 4 routes and each cross each other many times giving you time to hop on or off, it was oustanding value.

i just had one day from 1pm to 4:30pm and was able to cover a lot of ground thanks to Big Bus Tours. Started at Baker Street station and switched to boat tour at Tower of London. Hopped back on bus at Westminister pier and ended the day back at Backer's street. Great time indeed. Also liked Red tour better (started in blue tour and joined back on red tour after the boat ride) as the live narration was much more helpful. Great experience overall. A must do in my view.

was not sure how to to tour London decided to take the big bus tour which included the Thames cruise
The on board commentary was very enjoyable and fun.
Would recommend

We caught the bus outside Kings Cross Station. The bus stop is situated on Pancras Rd just after the turn left from Euston Rd. The stop is used by all tour buses and there are several representatives busy touting for custom! We had pre-booked our Family Ticket (through Quidco to obtain 7% Cashback). This bus is the Green Route and goes to Aldwych where the Red and Blue Routes can be caught. We used both of the routes to see all of the sights, which was all we wanted to do with our two Grandchildren making their first trip to London. We got off and on several times throughout the day with no bother at all. There is a free headphone system in a variety of languages, so most nationalities are catered for. The commentary is there or thereabouts when describing the places of interest. At some points on the tour the bus slows down in order that photos can be taken.

We travelled very early from Newcastle by train to get to London by 8am - started by buying a multi tube ticket (£8) well worth it for the day ahead. Went to Tower bridge to check the times for the bus tours - Big Bus co very competitive and friendly staff. Decided to do this at 9am as it was abit cloudy for the London eye. On for the whole red trip for over 2 hours but it was worth it - we were lucky enough to have Rick commentating - witty, full of interesting facts ; historic and modern, ad libbed in traffic and made our day! you can hop on and off all day and buses are regular throughout the day - unfortunately commentator and driver changed after last stop so we did, lost our upstairs seats then had trouble hearing 2nd commentator downstairs near driver - however hadnt noticed how good our 1st driver Richard was until sitting watching this 2nd one - seemed he didnt like other traffic! we jerked throughout the journey and he checked his phone constantly! 2nd commentator didnt engage us as 1st had. Pity the rain dampened the last half hour but we got to see London through a driver's eyes - do not drive there for anything!
Best way to see majority of London and we would definitely do again, wait for Ricks bus - he is hilarious - thanks alot! Oh and ask about other tickets - we got our London eye tickets for £19 when we got our bus tickets.- Not much cheaper but we didnt need to queue with 200 people so saved us hours in touristing! ....and we got a free cruise with bus ticket too which we also did afterwards - saw some same buildings but from sea and lots of interesting commentary from a captain with a ginger beard. PS listen to him or he'll tell you off ha! Anyway proper English captains are always gentlemen to women which makes a lovely change in this busy capital!! loved London thank you so much Big Bus tours.

We used Big Bus Tours when we visited Budapest and the service was fab. When visiting London yesterday we booked Big Bus tour in advance. We were not disappointed again. We met the 'green line bus' just 5 minutes walk away from Euston Station. Got on and then were taken to the next bus to start the tour. The bus provide headphones and ponchos (if raining) and a really clear map of the route. The buses are clean and very reliable. Would always use Big Bus tours even if abroad on city breaks etc.

The boat tour down the Thames was also included in the tour bus price. Once again very enjoyable and worth doing.

Fantastic service and reasonable prices compared to other tour bus companies.

We turned up and bought tickets on the day for 2 of us plus our 4 year old and managed to get the price down to £29 per person. Should book in advance as its definitely cheaper. We went from Trafalgar Square to the tower and hopped off to see the poppies. The tour guide was really good and informative and it was a good trip. We got the boat back from the tower to Westminster and again this was a good trip with an informative commentary. The only down side was when we were back in Westminster we had to wait for an hour to get the bus back as the traffic was busy because of the poppies. Basically every bus that went past us was the blue one and not the red tour. It was a good trip back though but its expensive for just one day.

This is a Hop On Hop Off bus trip that covers all of London's sites. There are 2 choices Red or Blue.

Red: Has onboard commentary by a staff member who was very informative (English only), and easy to understand. Overall about 30 stops.

Blue: Similar to Red but with audio via headphones in around 11 languages. These are easy to use and there were many ear buds available for every passenger. We preferred the Red trip due to the personal touches that the staff member provided.

Red, every 20 minutes approx and Blue every 10 minutes.

London was so big that this proved to be a terrific option to use for seeing the sites. About GBP31 pp but this gave 2 full days. For around GBP7 more you can get a third day but this needs to be done upfront, you can't add it on after the first 2 days.

I have seen so many bad reviews of the Big Bus Tours, and its competitors that have nothing to do with the value of their tour, but everything to do with the weather or traffic. They shouldn't be blamed for that. It's just bad luck that almost everyone is bound to experience on vacation. I say almost everyone because we were lucky. Our tour was great! Our whole European trip was thoroughly researched and planned out, so we knew not to bother to go in summer, so we went to London in September. I know the average person vacations in the summer, school is out, etc. But if this is a once in a life time trip, avoid summer at all costs. We also checked the monthly forecast to determine when it might rain (longer than a quick shower) and based on lots of reviews of the bus tours, we ultimately decided on a 48 hour tour during the weekend. This turned out to be perfect. We had perfect weather and only one small hold up in traffic when there was some unplanned road work on one of the red line's streets. We also avoided riding it during breakfast, lunch or dinner times, which seemed to be busy times in the tour for the street traffic.

We hopped on and off frequently and never had to wait too long for a bus to come along. To make the tour even better, our guides were hilarious and filled with interesting facts as well as comic stories about the sights and political figures of London. The Big Bus tour also includes walking tours. We did the Buckingham Palace "changing of the guards" and were very pleased with our tour guide and the route he took us on. We had the opportunity to march along side the guard as it marched to the palace to relieve the old guard.

Even if the weather is bad, the buses are prepared with ponchos for rain, and maps so you can hop off and go inside somewhere until the rain stops, or covered seating on the lower part, which is a pretty good way to see the sights. We did the blue line during a rain shower and it was lovely.

We highly recommend the Big Bus Tour. It's a great way to see London, on both the red and blue lines and the tour guides are warm, friendly and funny!

We bought the two day pass that included the river cruise which I highly recommend. We took the cruise up to Greenwich village which is beautiful and the home of the prime meridian a bit of a walk but worth it.
The bus and the boat are both easy to hop on and hop and the atf is excellent and helpful. Best way to see as much as you can as an overview and gt off to explores those special places that peak your interest.

It is cheap using these buses in the long run, plus you get a tour of London city, you just hop on and off at sites you want to see, the Red Tour has a guide English, the Blue has a recorder in various languages which they give you headphones. Phil the guide on our bus was so informative and such a laugh.I would say dress warm if not summer.

See all the sights.....and then go back and explore the ones that interest you.....at your own pace. Big Bus allows you to do this. Hop on hop off was excellent and we never had to wait long for the next bus. We had a live guide on board whose commentary included a great sense of humour. Two inclusions in our ticket were a river cruise on the Thames and a guided Royal walking tour which took in the changing of the guard at Buckingham Palace.....now that's value for money. This is MUST DO if you're visiting London for only a few days.

We visited london in November and thoroughly enjoyed this tour. You get 2 days for the price of 1 in aurumn/winter. Get the red tour and do hop on and off. Our tour guides were great and the flexibility allows you to shop or sightsee before you continue. I learnt lots and the kids loved it too.

Visiting London for only a few days so were a little overwhelmed trying to figure out what to see and how. Having done the Big Bus tour we feel like we saw everything and more. The guides, (we hopped off and hopped on again) 'Joe' and later 'Nick' were extremely informative and entertaining which made the tour come alive - thank you guys.
The River Thames tour was beautiful and more than expected - I do caution those who see a load of school children boarding ... wait for the next one!
All in all we're very satisfied and recommend Big Bus Tours worth the price.

We took the Big Bus Red tour and enjoyed it very much. A special shout out to Chris the tour guide. Chris shared detailed information about so many points and buildings along the route. Chris's delivery included just enough humorous anecdotes, which were delivered timely. The route was comprehensive, the timing of the buses was punctual and the price fair. The added bonus of accessing the boat tour is a big plus.

Absolutely delighted with Big bus company from the beginning. Had bought ticket dated 8/11 but couldn't use it as couldn't get into city due to Lord Mayors show. Thought I would have to pay again but they let me use it no problem!

Got on the red tour and ended up going the whole way around it was so interesting. Had a local guide chris and driver Patrick who clearly knew their stuff. We got diverted off the normal route and Chris was still very knowledgable which was impressive and proves he is not just reading facts from a book! Totally fabulous time and really recommend it for anyone!!

We decided to use Big Bus as we only had one day available to sightsee in London.
It is almost £70 for two people but the tickets are valid for 2 days. You can get off and on at various places around the tour and the price also includes a cruise on the Thames.

There is obviously a lot of traffic in the city so you have to allow 5 hours to complete the whole tour. You see all the major tourist attractions.

Things tend to get a bit chaotic if it rains and everyone from upstairs wants to get out of the rain.

We would choose the red tour next time with the tour guide rather than the blue tour that has headphones….the music can become a bit wearing.

All in all, recommended.

We have ben to London 10+ times and have seen all. The bus tour gave us a review. In a 8 hour day we saw London and cruised up the Thames to Greenwich. We had only 30 minutes at Greenwich and by past experence needs 2 hours. If you are need to London, you need two days at min to see the attracions.

Though we bought the tickets during their 48 hour special (buy a single day ticket get a second one for free) we only did the one day - it was all we had budgeted for.

We rode the Red Line, except at the end of the day to get back to Victoria Station when we hopped on a Blue Line. The Red Line has live commentary and the Blue is pre-recorded but is available in several languages.

It is what would be expected, a bus that stops at our near all the major sites. The stops were close to where we wanted to go and the guides were always willing to help with walking directions and suggestions. There were a few people on one of our bus complaining about the bus not going as quickly as they would have liked, London traffic is what it is. Depending on the time of day, count on spending some time sitting in traffic, and think of some great questions to ask your guide.

We did go for the boat ride, from the London Eye to the Tower of London, after the sun had set. It was a beautiful ride, the pre-recorded commentary was only so-so, but the views from the water more than made up for it.

The only negative I can say is that the ticket for two days isn't cheap and I was shocked to find it cost over £90 for two adults and a OAP in a wheelchair.
However its a fantastic way to get around London whilst finding out the History of the place.
The Blue tour goes a little further out to Knitghtsbridge, Kensington, Paddington, but has a headphone delivered tour which often gets out of sync with the sights.(something like)
"Please get your camera's ready as we turn the corner, you will see the Houses of Parliament and the Queens clock tower" at that point we were already passing Boudicca on Westminster Bridge.
The Red tour soon became our favourite as it was nice to have a tour guide on board. The tour guides are all very different in their approach one was great with the info and thoughtful with Mum, but quite serious. Another was quite jokey, Our favourite by far was a blonde chap James he had studied at Oxford and had been in the Army....he had us laughing the whole journey, so funny and sarcastic...have a feeling the American lady behind us didn't quite get all of the sarcasm, those lots of folk from the US were giggling away like us. It was appreciated by us, keep it up.
James you are exceptional at delivering the tour keep the sarcasm coming!

Just a little topical information...when we passed the Tower of London, the queue for seeing the Remembrance the poppies had become a mass of people, however from the top of the bus we had a fantastic view over the crowd. Best spot on the bus to see the poppies. Up top on the passenger/pavement side (not the driver/ road side)

We were in london for 5 days and haven't been for many years, so decided the best way to see the sights was on one of these guide tour buses. We asked in the Hotel and they recommended THE BIG BUS company. We paid more then £60 for the 2 tickets for 2 days, the 2nd day is included in the price, no option. Which was ok, as we were going to the National history museum for the day, the next day and could use the service which we thought was great.

We got on the bus and were able to get a sit together upstairs, although it was full. So we were happy. We started the trip everything was going well, we got a great view of the poppies, until we got to Marble Arch, we went round there 6 times with the same commentary every time. I really know now where the beatles lived together in London.

Then we got eventually to Madame tussard's, were we had to change bus, not good as it was full and no seats, so we had to stand. We decided to get of the bus earlier then we were intending because of the lack of seats and were really pissed off about the route. There was things on the map that we didn't get to see.

We also saw it took 2 hours to get to National History Museum and because we were still disappointed with the service we decided not to use the bus again and used the tube to get to the museum.

There was only a pre-recorded tape of the tour

I would strongly NOT recommend this company.

This is the best way to see London, stops at all the main attractions. Just hop on and of when you like. There is always someone from big bus at all the stops to help you and so very friendly, I was in a wheelchair and really no problem, could get on all the buses with ease. Thought I would not be able to get around as can't do the underground was so pleased to of found the big bus tour.

After looking at the poppies 3 friends and myself boarded an open top bus last Saturday . As we did the sun came out , perfect ! We had a really good guide informative and very funny!
I saw more in 3 hours than we could ever have done on our own .on to the Thames cruise another very good guide .a lovely day and Big Bus Tours extremely good value for money ( it also included guided walks but we just didn't have time) will come back next summer !!

An absolute must to see all the sights in London, on top of an open top bus, pick your route ( diff bus for diff route) and off you go, hop on and off when you like, ticket lasts 24 hours, free Thames river tour included, we didn't do this though as we ran out of time, fantastic photo opportunity, one thing I'd say if I did it again I would dress a little warmer, we weren't prepared for how chilly it was up top and it was only October, maybe take a hot coffee and and wee throw but that's just me, highly recommended and I'll do it again but choose the other route next time. Cost was £86 for two adults 2 kids.

What a great way to see the sights ! Hopped on and off all weekend really got our £32 worth plus included in ticket price river boat on the Thames ! Lovely helpful drivers who get asked a million questions a day and they always have a smile of their faces and have s great knowledge of London. Couldn't figure out the night bus though from Marble Arch , we just jumped in a taxi instead. River Thames boat cruise was a really lovely finish to our weekend on a sunny Sunday morning. Would I use again ? You bet I would !! 😃
30 quid and all of London is yours for the taking. Go anywhere go everywhere see everything how fun hop off , hop on.

On a two day stay in London with two friends. On a sunny unseasonably warm October day we decided to try the 'Original' Big Bus Tour. There are other tours but try to take the 'Original' tour.
On the Yellow route there is an English speaking guide who is very knowledgeable about London.
The Red and Blue routes have the option of multilingual commentary.

The Hop On Hop Off option is perfect to introduce anyone to the many attractions and the history of London. Obviously the top deck is the best place to get and unrivalled view of the scenery.

We had 1 day in London and decided to tour the city by taking a Big Bus tour. We paid about 29 pounds (about $47 US dollars) for a 48 hour hop on/hop off ticket. I wish they offered a one day price package if you will be only using the bus service for 1 day.
We sat on the top of the open air double decker bus. It was a great way to see the famous sights (I have been to London before, but for my colleague, it was his first), but will say that it got very crowded at many of the bus stops.
We visited the main London must-do sights (St. Paul's Cathedral, Trafalgar Square, London Eye, Big Ben/Parliament, Convent Garden, West End, Tower of London, etc.) and decided to stay on the bus for over an hour since we were enjoying the ride.
We had a lovely tour guide who explained the sights as we drove by them (although will say that at times it was difficult to hear her with London traffic all around us.
I would probably take this tour again if A)it was cheaper, B)they offered a 1 day package.

I highly recommended seeing London on the Big Bus tour! What a great way to get an overview and hit all the major sights. If you can, buy the 48 hour pass. We went back the next day and stopped at the attractions we wanted to see and used the bus to get us to each sight. They run very frequently and you can have a live narrator or use headphones for pre-recorded audio. Nick, our tour guide, was incredible! He gave lots of facts, stories and humorous antidotes.

We did the full circuit with a hop off / on at Baker Street (to visit Regents Park)
You get to see so much and the commentary is worth listening to as you can learn about different areas of London.
Great idea.

The red line bus, you can wear a headset and select your language. We rode both and the live commentary is the best hands down. You will have to switch buses at some point to see the entire London area. Too bad it rained most of the time, because the view from the top deck was great. Lots of bus tours to pick from. We bought the 24 hour pass, with the free 24 hours to make it a 48 hour pass. Would recommend this bus.

Went on a tour with family. Not easy to find right bus stops, when we asked a member of the staff which direction the bus went he just round,
We did not get to see much as we got on the wrong bus (Not knowing) and saw Marble Arch from different directions.
So feel they should make it easier to find out which but stop to get to go and see different sightseeing points in London.
We felt the price was a lot £32 per person, ok was including a boat tour, which we did not get to do and a second day ( but family was leaving the next day)
Due to road closures bus was also diverted and guess what we drove past yet again, and did not stop at some points due to this.

After visiting London several times, this time we decided to take the hop on hop off bus tours. We always went straight for one particular attraction, whereas this time, we managed to see most of the attractions by bus (on land) and could go down anytime we liked.

Our tour guide for most of the day was Rob, he was very informative and had a good sense of humour. He allowed us four to communicate or intervene during his comments.

We also got a free thames boat tour up to Greenwich, which we found really interesting too. We paid 31Sterling and if I am not mistaken could have had the second day free, but we only had one day to spare as we were leaving the following morning.
30 GBP and all of London is yours. Many many stops many of London's best attractions, Thames boat ride, hop on, hop off, bus every 10 minutes.

big thank you to all the staff at big bus tours London I travelled all over the UK and Ireland and hoped on many bus tours and as im back home now im writing my reviews on all of the tours that I took, I have to say one thing before coming across the POND as I heard some people say the is much more to see and do with other companies other that city sightseeing, I truly enjoyed my quick sightseeing tour around London on-board one of your buses the guides were helpful in every way possible and so to were the drivers.

We only had two days in London so opted for the Big Bus Tour so we'd see as many sights as possible on our short stay. We weren't disappointed as we went round a couple of times during our two days and had the 48 hour ticket for the price of a 24 hours. We went on the cruise also on the 1st day and it was brilliant. We took the morning walking tour on our second day and saw the Changing of the Guard with the very informative guide helping to make it a great tour. We found all the staff helpful, a few more than others, but we have to give a special mention to the gentleman outside Victoria Station on Sun.19th & Mon. 20th Oct for being so polite and helpful to us on both days. We called by to thank him before we left on Tues. morning but unfortunately he wasn't there. He is a great Ambassador for the company and we wish him well.
The only negative thing we found was the morning of the walking tour we and a lot of other people had to wait a long time for the bus at Marble Arch and therefor a lot of people missed the tour. We felt an extra bus could have been put on the route to accommodate the tourists.
We had a splendid time and saw so many famous places and beautiful buildings in London thanks to the Big Bus Company.

We took a group of 8 friends on their first visit to london on the Big Bus Tour.
We started at Trafalgar Square with the Royal palace tour , A great way to see the changing of he guard .Then back to take the tour ,unfortunately a protest march had shut down the center of London so we had to walk an extra ten minutes to Aldwich to get the bus .Then taking the guides recommendation we stopped at Borough Market for some great street stall food After that we got off at the Embankment to take the River Cruise to Westminster Pier .Finally rounding off our day with another session on the bus tour. The red bus with english speaking guide is better than the blue bus with language recordings if people have a good grasp of english

The Big Bus Tour is a very good way to learn all interesting sites of London. The translation is very good (German) but sometimes comes a little late at the sites. Also some big buildings in Westminster should be mentioned additionally. And the music could be a but more varying.

The Service was perfect and very friendly. The hop-on-hop-off Ticket is valid two days. The invalides ship tour must be included strategically depending in the amount of Tourists near the departing station. Otherwise Wartung can be very long and alternative actions are hard to start due to the masses.

One of the smartest things I did when visiting London was using Big Bus Tours. In my opinion, the best value comes from going the whole circuit on day number one and using that as a reference for deciding which attractions to see in depth on days two and three.

Starting out at Kings Cross, the BBT representative there was a wealth of information and an overall nice guy. I was pleasantly surprised when he informed me that my one-day ticket was valid for use until the end of the following day! He also helped choose between a variety of add-on attractions and his recommendations were spot-on!!

The first day was spent doing the circuit and hoping off for brunch and then a late lunch as well as the river cruise. I also hopped off at a few sites to investigate whether they were worth seeing in depth on the second day. The next day I used BBT to get from Kings Cross to the three landmarks identified the previous day as well as an early dinner at Hard Rock Cafe prior to going back on BBT to Kings Cross.

I had zero problems with the bus being crowded. All BBT staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful. Overall it was a great experience and well worth the money.

We purchased this tour so our kids could get an overview of London before we ventured out for our holiday. We waited for the Big Bus for at least 15 min - We saw 4 buses for Original Tour (the competitor) stop within that time - When we finally got on the bus we settled in for what became the pub crawl. Our guide, while nice and friendly, told us about EVERY stinking pub we passed for the tour - nothing was noted about the historic sites, just her adventures at each pub. The Tour was useless - we landed up pointing out landmarks to our children! It made for great laughs afterward, but sorely disappointed in the lack of professionalism. We will use the Original Tour Bus next time

Big bus was great. The red tour was very informative and we had a few great guides on it.

The other companies did seem to have a lot more busses come past while we wye waiting.
One night we were on the last bus that unexpectedly ended at marble arch and left us in the rain and dark without any explanation as to why.

Hop on hop off tours in London are definitely wroth it but I'd probably go with another company with more busses.

Not only did Danny tell us about all the excellent attractions the big bus tour offered, he helped us find several affordable phone repair locations. Excellent customer service from all the big bus tour staff we met, but particularly Danny who went way above the call of duty. Thanks guys!

- Thevindu and Claire, Cambridge UK

We pre-booked the 2 day and cruise tickets for the first 2 days of our trip to London and were very happy with our choice. There was a stop right outside our hotel which was a bonus. The first day it was overcast and rainy, so we sat inside (although we were given rain slickers so we could sit outside/upstairs). From the first level, we missed being able to see some of the sights, but were happy to go along and get a feel for the city. As the weather cleared, we sat up top and got a better view of London. Also on the first day, there was a taxi strike which meant there was a critical mass of taxis gridlocking the area around Parliament. We were happy to take a break from the bus and use this time to take the free river cruise and have lunch. We then were able to catch the bus at 4pm and finish the tour. On the second day, we had our bearings and a better idea of where we wanted to use the hop on, hop off option and did that the second day. All in all, we enjoyed the convenience of the Big Bus Tour. The staff were all professional and helpful - making sure we had our headsets and maps at all points of rejoining the tour.

There are three companies offering hop on hop off sightseeing tours of London.We chose Big Bus for our two day pass and were totally disappointed by the service.They advertise that they pick up from each point every 15-20 mins,but some of the wait times were up to 55 mins.We realise that London traffic is bedlam,but speaking to other passengers,these extended waiting times seem to be the norm.As frustrating as it is waiting for extended periods,the total insult was when we asked a BigB bus employee at one of the stops how long the next bus would be,he became quite aggressive,which was witnessed by all at the stop.Another two drivers we had contact with ,also seemed to have serious bad attitude.In fairness we also struck a couple of pleasant,helpful drivers.Obviously we can't compare the service and staff attitude of the other two companies,but one thing is for certain it couldn't be worse.

Riding for 3 hours in the tour bus allowed us to get a picture of the fabulous city. The only minus was that we saw Big Ben from 5 different angles i.e. the bus seemed to be going in circles towards the end of the tour.

We flew in and jumped on the bus at 12. It would just sit at each stop so long it just ate up the time. We jumped off at the tower of London to ride the boat towards Big Ben but the line was so long they said it would take over an hour. We rode to to Greenwich and did the circle and swept through the Maritime museum which was nice and rushed back to the boat ramp and they claimed the boat was broken and we were stuck til 5pm hence we were done because unlike other bus lines Big Bus shuts down as the fun starts. The Original Bus was still going into the evening. If you are a grampa who goes to bed at 6 pick another line. We paid for two days so we will try again tomorrow, only because we are stuck.
Great open top bus tour of London. Very frequent buses and comfortable seats. Route was fantastic. We hopped off at the V&A stop as the stop was directly opposite the museum. Really great price.

As a first-time visitor, this was the best way to see everything and get a feel for the city. Also, great way to get your bearings. This tour company offers 2 options: the blue tour is about 4 hrs and the red tour is about 2.5 to 3 hours in my experience. Of course, traffic depending, the bus will move faster/slower. The 2 tours: the blue tour has a recorded audio that you listen through headphones and the blue tour has a live tour guide commenting as you see the sites. Also, the blue tour covers a larger area of London. I did both plus the water boat tour in one day, taking full advantage of everything. The water boat tour went from the Tower of London to Westminster area and I am not sure if there are other routes. Highly recommended.

I took the hop on/off Big Bus tour on September 27th. The weather was a bit windy, but sunny so I sat up top and enjoyed the breeze. The first bus had a actual tour guide that was pretty guide and interactive. I got off, did the cruise tour to Greenwich which is a very pretty town. When I returned on the tour, there was no tour guide. We were given headphones to listen to a recording of the sites. That was disappointing since the tour documentation mentioned always having a live tour guide. Other than that, it was good.

We decided to have a kind of lazy day in London as we were going to the theatre at night and didn't want to be too tired after doing the sights in London.

We decided the bus tour was the best way to see the magical sights and sounds of London without it being strenuous in any way.

Our tour guide was fabulous making us sing London bridge is falling down as we drove over the bridge. The only unfortunate thing on the day was that the sound system on the bus failed and we had to transfer buses but that wasn't a massive issue.

All in all a fabulous way to see the sights and so much more relaxing than walking around especially when you have a time limit.

I want to sincerely thank everyone who I encountered with my Big Bus experience. The complementary boat cruise on the Thames was an added bonus. I thoroughly enjoyed exploring London using the bus routes to plan my excursions. It was extremely helpful and convenient, plus it made exploring London soooo much easier. I would like to thank Cathy McCarthy, Moushumi Kallee and Felipe Gonzalez for setting this up, I want to also acknowledge Mouhamed Lounici at your Kings Cross station, he was extremely helpful and quite pleasant to talk to. A few previous reviewers seem to have bad experiences with this service, mine was amazing.
You have a great service and this is well organized and well run, would definitely use it again in other cities and recommend it to others.

Wasn't the best open bus tour I've been on but felt it was ok value for money and a great way to see the main sights of London. We did the short tour first then did the river cruise up to The Tower of London. We then jumped onto the longer tour bus which went on forever and we just seemed to get constantly stuck in traffic. Definitely something to do whilst in London.

Visited on the day of the London climate change protest and although we were warned by the ticket conductor at the start of the journey of 'slight' delays to the service this turned out to be major delays which prevented us from seeing much of London's sights at all. We got on at the first stop, Green Park, and chose the shorter Red Route at only 2.15 hours long as we had planned to do other things with our day. The top of the bus filled up pretty quickly making it hard for some people to get a seat. The start of the tour stared off well with the great tour guide giving off a lot of good info but as the tour continued and the delays and traffic became more obvious and the sightseeing tour became a tour of the London grid lock more than anything else. The sights of London became quick glimpses from a distance (we didn't even get to see the front of Buckingham Palace) and by the end even the tour guide had given up and started talking about the daily football scores. Maybe this was a one off due to the protests however a professional company who provide this service ever day in the city should not have such a clueless attitude to these types of events and how they affect the traffic on the route.

I had heard of original tours/big bus/ etc for hop on hop off in London. We booked big bus and our experience was awesome. Our driver Mike on the blue line bus no 220 on 20th September 2014 was extremely helpful and knowledgeable person. Keep it up big bus .then it was mike for the harry potter tour on 21 St and fantastic guide he was.what a lovely representation of facts.
On 22 and it was In for Buckingham palace walk and ghost by gaslights___ really a lovely guide he was ______ I am sorry I don't recollect his name. But all these people make big bus the best.

Used big bus tours and found them very handy in getting to know way around.London traffic was very slow and there was buses everywhere,would not want to have tight deadlines.The red route bus had tour guides and they would change at intervals,over 2 days travel you find difference in presenters,some I found difficult to understand.So was happy enough on blue bus that has no live presenter but found set recordings good.

Our family - 5 of us - 2 kids + my Mum recently enjoyed a lovely day out in London on the Big Bus Hop On Hop Off tour of London. A great and funny guide and lots of buses so you can stop and get on and off really easily... BIG TIP - get on at Tower of London as there was competition with another bus company and we were able to negotiate on price - making it even better value for money!

We purchased a specific date in advance using the internet and saved $6.00. The green link picked us up at St. Pancras International and took us to Stop 15 on the Blue and Red lines (Covent Gardens). Upon arrival at Covent Gardens, we were greeted by a pleasant woman who exchanged our printed ticket for the official ticket we needed for the hop on and off. We were also given a nice map. I would recommend the Red tour (real narration, not recorded). We had two different tour guides, one better than the other. The ticket included a nice 30 minute cruise on the Thames river, again with live narration, so we knew what we were looking at. I would recommend this tour to others.

The busses are well taken care of and comfortable and hit the highlights of London. The one thing we did not like was the limited number of stops (as compared to similar bus tours in other cities) and the drivers being unwilling to pickup/drop-off riders anywhere other than the marked bus stops.

Hint - if you want a live narrator, make sure to get on the red line, though there are far fewer of those busses. The blue line busses do have pre-recorded narration that you can plug into and in mant languages. They even supply the earphones.

Overall, we would

Took the family (2girls 7&9) on the bus tour on a 48hr family ticket booked on the internet, which was great value. Bus tour guides were at all stops which was really helpful as there were lots of route options. We went on the automated guide which was great as all languages were available and made it easy to switch off if needed. Ticket also included river cruise but we didn't have time to do it which was a shame. Green route was handy a it took us back to the train station. Some buses were busy but they were every 10 mins so frequent. Only disappointment was on our final day there were diversions due to a race so we couldn't go past houses of parliment and Westminster which was a shame, so check for events as this wasn't mentioned when we bought our ticket. Sitting on the open top bus was windy and cold even on a warm day so tasks an extra layer. But the views from the top if a bus are wonderful and the architecture in London is breath taking.
Hop on and off tour great way to see and get round London only thing wrong was recorded commentary not informative enough and padded out with repetitive music

We purchased a 2 day pass. So much cheaper than a taxi. Get off look around different highlight. Loved the Big Ben, changing of the guards, our shopping experience at Harrods, London Eye. Just hop back on bus and go to next attraction. We used the bus in Paris as well.

Our family are not one to sit on a bus and go for a tour but being in London with the kids, they had never seen all of the sights so we took the plunge. We loved Big Bus Tour, a modern fleet with very friendly and funny staff. The Tour (Red route for us) was superb, we got so much out of it and our guide was very funny whilst informative. When we return we will do it again but this time take the Blue tour as we didn't have time this trip. My tip is to make sure you book it before midnight on the day you want to go, it's cheaper online. We are heading to NYC in March '15 and have already looked up Big Bus Tours there, can't wait.

The bus tour is a good way to get the lay of the land, so to speak, and learn a bit more of London than you might otherwise.

However, we experienced a real lack of communication between bus drivers, guides, and the company. Stayed up near King's Cross so we needed to catch the green line each evening to get back to our flat (we bought the 48 hr tickets). Asked various people, including bus drivers, guides, and the employee at the stop (who called the company to ask) about when the last green line bus would leave. Got lots of different answers ranging from 6 to 7:30pm. Couldn't find a published scheduled anywhere. Missed the bus both nights - lots to see in London! It would be helpful if the buses would at least run until dark in September.

Some guides were engaging. Others, not so much. Included river tour was great though!

Took red bus tour of London on a Sunday afternoon. Unfortunately for us, access to Trafalgar Sq that afternoon was blocked due to an ongoing event.
Live English commentary was fantastic with guide being very knowledgeable and keen sense of humour. Was able to take good pictures from top of bus.
Tour ended at Green Park Tube station and we had cool walk back to Picadilly Circus where we were staying.
The tour comes with a Thames Boat ride which was very enjoyable, passing close to the Eye and Tower of London.
Worth every penny but make sure that you pick a sunny day.
Had a fabulous time on the Big Bus Tour in London. Our guide Chris did a great job of providing history and humor on the ride.

Having lived in the London area for a number of years and visiting London many times since, we thought for our last day on this tour it would be nice just to ride around the cities and reminisce. We took the blue route and thought it was very good, we saw a lot of the city bringing back many wonderful memories. I don't think we saw any place we have not visited/toured. The driver was very courteous and the descriptions provided were excellent. Only issue we had was the continuous advertisement for the bus tours after all we had already bought our tickets. One should take the boat cruise also provided.

If time is limited in London, start with the Big Bus tour. Your ticket is good for 24 hours from first entry. Either start early or late in the day to maximize time. Take advantage of the included river tour and get off for lunch at one of the two stops.

On our first day we decided to "do" the Big Bus tour and we were fortunate to have gorgeous autumn day and were not disappointed. Both the commentary on the Red Route and awesome Elgar were excellent. As a bonus we were also able to enjoy the River Cruise just before a high tide suspended the cruises. While the personal tour guides were very entertaining and well informed, the London dialect obviously confused many of the tourists.
Aivars T

We bought the 2 day pass, which cost us about 64pounds. We enjoyed the hop on hop off concept, as it gave us an excellent overview of London.
The highlight of the tour was the boat cruise down the Thames, as the heavens burst to make a sparkling summers day into a wet day. All in all the bus tour is well worth it, as from here you can plan where and what you want to visit at your own pace

We did the Big Bus tour on our 1st day in London. It was easy to find from London Victoria and we sat on the upper level for a better view. We actually experienced 2 different guides, 1 much easier to understand than the other. London had so many different dialects so coming from the US it was somewhat of a challenge to understand them. The Big Bus was convenient and made it easy to see some sites we would have missed otherwise and it enabled us to get our bearings of the layout of London to help with our walks later. Would recommend a bus tour for new comers.

Booked a Big Bus Tour after walking around London for 2 days with our 5 year old made us all tired and weary.

Good value for money compared to other London attractions i.e. London Eye.

We have been to London many times but have never thought to do this type of tour, however, we all really enjoyed the experience, the hop on - hop off is an excellent way to see the sights as well as get around town.

The tour guides were very well informed and we all learnt new facts as well as being thoroughly entertained!

The River Cruise was an added bonus which was thoroughly enjoyable.

Would definitely do this again and would recommend to anyone.

Booking was really easy. Booked on the day before leaving our hotel and just presented the code sent to my smart phone when we arrived at a bus stop.

There are a few different companies offering similar hop on hop off style bus tours. Be sure which one you want before purchasing your tickets. There are a couple of Big Bus shops where you can purchase your tickets and receive information on London and it's sights, as well as Newspaper type stands around London, and also Big Bus employees at the major stops that will sell you a ticket prior to getting on. We were originally going to go on a different bus tour, but they only offered a 24hr ticket for £29 and we paid £32 for a 48hr ticket. They go on very similar routes as the other company, but they also have another extended route that the other company doesn't take. The Big Bus Red route is for English speaking people and has a person with a microphone giving history and stories about the sights you go to and past. The Blue line is multi lingual and has a pre recorded commentary about the sights, which you use headphones to listen to it and dial in your language preference. If you have a voucher or buy your ticket at a stand you then have to have it scanned by one of the guys at a stop and they print out tickets with a date and time so you knew how long you can use it for. The employees are all knowledgeable about London and willing to help with directions and the best stops to get off for the place you want to go. Definitely a great way to see London.

With a family of 6 & 2 OAPS this was a really expensive trip (£146 for a 24 ticket) - but it was a really great way to see all the sights, put them in context of where they are in relation to each other, and have a rest whilst doing so. There are other bus tours, and they do seem to have more buses than this company, but the buses were clean and comfortable with free weather ponchos!

The route was good, and allowed us to see Trafalgar Square, Admiralty Arch, Buckingham Palace, Covent Garden, Tower Bridge etc etc. Buying a 24 ticket also gave us a free River Cruise, which was really enjoyable!

We'd gone to London thinking that the Tube would be a cheap way to travel but with a family as big as ours, the cheapest way was by far in a Black Cab!

Made the fatal mistake off booking online at 10 mins to midnight (would have saved £12!) the night before and then distracted myself checking no engineering works on the trains in from Essex the next day and missed the midnight completion by seconds .... discount lost as now technically the day of travel! Grrrr. Continued with booking anyway still as been promising myself a guided London open bus tour on a dry summer sunday since year dot and looking like I'd miss another year if I didn't get more pro-active on a football free sunday with the weather forecast looking rain free. Having worked in the city since the 80's, the one thing I knew I didn't want to do was sit or crawl in the sort of London traffic I've always seen midweek, congestion charge or not! And if nowhere else, the city area is quiet on a Sunday!

Went on a RED (guided) bus from Tower Hill/Tower bridge stop nice and early (10ish) which is pretty near London Fenchurch St which is where I arrived with my partner and 9 year old. Very interesting informative guide with a dry sense of humour on the first leg taking me around the bits of the city I'd worked around and just walked past in blissful ignorance for years. Soon hit central London which was a bit more interesting for my son (Embankment, Eye, Big Ben, MI6, etc) and the usual photo opportunities. Driver and Guide changed at Green park (one stop short of our first hop off) where our new guide gave an alternative reason as to why Green Park was so called. We hopped off at the Hard Rock Cafe about noon and treated ourselves to pretty excellent burgers, chicken and drinks.

Had a bit of a wait for another RED bus (quite a few blue ones came mind) amongst various rival arrivals too (Golden, the original... ) but we were soon on our way for the second leg with Robert and Paul driving. Robert very amusing. Son not impressed we didn't 'hop off' at Hamleys; partner ditto Oxford Street/Bond Street area. Second drive past the Houses of Parliament and back around to Tower Bridge the other way to where we started from. Felt the guide had earned his tip but got the impression tipping was the exception rather than the norm.

All in all a very good tour and well worth the discounted online price if you remember to get it in time. The hop on hop off seemed very viable although we only used it once ... all stops logically placed and no real rush on or off at any one of them. Ticket would have included walking tours and a river boat trip so all together quite a good deal. Quick enough to see the city in 2-3 hours drive by mode for those pressed for time but 48 ticket prob quite good idea as well as well for those with more time. No idea what it's like in heavy or slow moving traffic but I guess that's where the guided RED tour guide earns his tip to keep things interesting. The speedier traffic free (and rain free) tour on the Sunday was ideal for us.

My husband, young daughter and I jumped on a big bus tour at marble arch and were not disappointed. The tour takes you past all the big sites of London with plenty of stops along the way. We purchased a day ticket and received the second day free which was fantastic as it took us 2 days to see everything. I would highly reccomend getting on the buses with live commentators (red line) although the blue lines are very informative we found the live commentry better. A must for anyone who wants to see what London has to offer!

The Big Bus tour in NYC has always been something I've walked by as a ny'er. In London it was the best decision I made after walking for what seemed like a gazillion miles. My feet were so very happy to get on the bus at the Tower Hill stop and jump on & off as needed. I stopped at Westminster Abbey...Then took red line to Green Gardens where "Big Steve" sent me to Shepard's Market for lunch. (YAY). Local pub with an amazing atmosphere and MEAT pie. (the king's arms). The blue tour took me to the parts of London that were far-ish to walk. The river tour was the perfect way to end the day!
The weather was awful but the tour was great. I was able to hop off and on at various stops and truly take in the sites in spite of the cold and rain.

I booked a 24 hr tour for me and family...

I would recommend the 48 hr tour because there is no way you will visit everything in one day!!!

They give you earphones, ponchos for the rain, you can hop on hop off anytime and anywhere...

If there is a place you want to visit just stop, go to that place and then get another bus... They go every 10-15 mins...

There is a route where you have live explanation and the staff is really welcoming, helpful and cheerful...

Also, you get a boat trip and a walking tour...

Remember: book online and with anticipation, you will save some pounds!

We all enjoyed the convenience of big bus tour, especially in London, there are a few routes, some with live guide. We prefer to the blue line, there are 8 language to choose from. it have a few free walk tours + river cruise. the best is you have actual 48 hours with 1 day pass which is extremely helpful, and much better than Paris Big Bus. They prepare Umbrella for you at rainy day, what a great service.

London is an amazing city and unless you are Charles Dickens with a lifetime to spare you won't be seeing it by foot so a bus tour is a good idea.

However, be warned that £72 for a family of four is what it'll set you back.

Points off for a website that struggles with mobile phone and a missed opportunity of an app that promises much but delivers very little other than a poor map you can't zoom in on with little information.

We booked a 24+24 hrs HOHO service. The staff were very helpful barring 1 at westminster bridge. bus frequency was excellent. Special mention of our THE ROYAL WALK tour guide KELVIN RUSSEL who i think is an asset to your company. he was far better than any tour guides in that area, excellent sense oh humour. he kept the group together even when there were hundreds of other groups around. the free thames boat ride was nice.
the bus routes covered the entire london beautifully.

Purchased a two day pass and loved it. Convenient with stops to get on and off close to all the major places to visit in London. Always helpful staff at the bus stops and the recorded commentary on the bus in multiple languages was informative and humorous. We loved our Big Bus Adventure and would recommend it to those new to the city who want to see a lot and let someone else do the driving!

This is the second time in a year that we have taken the Big Bus tour.
-excellent tour
-many buses (little or no waiting
-received the second day free
-able to start tour at any stop (This was not the case with The Original Bus tour we took a couple of years ago.)

Our family of 5 flew from Denver via DC and landed in Heathrow around 10am local time. We were meeting my wife's parents at the airport. After taking the subway to London my mother-in-law had the GREAT idea to book the Big Bus for a tour around London. This is a wonderful thing to do and I would highly recommend it to others. First, it is advised to try to stay up until 8pm the evening you land to reduce jet lag. The ability to sit on the upper deck of the bus for a 2-3 hour tour (you pick how long you want to stay on the bus) was wonderful. It filled the day and gave us a "second wind" until dinner. It is also a perfect way to see this tremendous city. There are other bus tours and i am not sure if Big Bus is the best. The prerecorded tour information is ok. A couple of the audio devices did not work. We had to move seats a couple of times. However, the idea of a bus tour the day you land in London is superb.

There is a Green Bus which was fine. There is a Red Bus tour which has a guide who describes the attractions. Our Guide was Nick and he was absolutely fantastic, he was personable, entertaining and knowledgeable. The company should clone him. The idea is that you can hop on and off, this is a risk, I hopped off the Red bus and onto the Blue bus. Awful, there was no guide and people making a nuisance all over the bus. Don't get on the Blue Bus !!
i got the 2 dat hop on hop off ticket .worth every penny ,saw every major site in london over the 2 days and the running commentery very good

The red tour with live guide was pretty good and useful if it is your first visit to London. Take care however when using the blue tour to make sure that you know which direction the bus will take - we almost didn't make it to the theatre on time despite getting on the bus at 1810 !! because it took so long to do the 'loop'.

Also be aware of how long the river cruise can take as we almost missed our London eye slot, despite arriving at Tower Bridge quay at 1450 !!

You really need not to be on a tight time schedule if you are going to use this.

I'm not sure that it represents such good value for money either, especially if you are a family. If you can navigate the tube system it is undoubtedly much quicker to get to places of interest, and would give you a pretty healthy cost saving to spend on other attractions.

I honestly didn't think there was a big difference between these hop on - hop off buses so I purchased a 24 hour ticket on this company's bus.

Cons:

1. It was more expensive than the other companies.

2. I stood at the stop by the Hard Rock Cafe for almost 40 minutes without a SINGLE Big Bus stopping for me. I was told to walk down the street (10-15 minutes) to go to another stop and see if a bus was there... reallly????

3. The ticket sellers are VERY aggressive. I saw a ticket seller for this company physically guide customers onto the bus away from another competitor and then get loud and obnoxious with the competitor's vendor WHILE trying to get these poor people to buy his ticket --- which they had no choice as the ticket seller told the driver to drive on so the people were stuck on the bus and 'therefore HAD TO' (his words) buy a ticket....

4. I got on the bus and asked when the last trip was and I was told not for another 2 hours... then 1/2 hour later the guide announced that this was the last trip and he announced there were only 2 remaining stops... I went up to him and said that's not what you told me I'm on the wrong side of the city... his response so jump on the tube or get a taxi

5. The driver Dave (David?) was HORRENDOUS. I honestly thought were going to be in an accident but after waiting 40 minutes to get on the damn bus I was very reluctant to get off. The driver was VERY unsafe and get slamming on his brakes, coming up too close to other cars/buses etc. He knocked a girl on a bike and was yelling at other drivers.

Bottom line don't use this company try another competitor

Rode the Big Bus (Red Tour) several times in London. The tour is as good as the guide....We had an informed, articulate young man at first; unfortunately, he was replaced halfway through by an inarticulate blonde who was trying to be funny, thought she could sing, & seemed to have only a perfunctory knowledge of the city. In hindsight we should have gotten off that bus & waited for another.

I used the big bus tour since they picked up at patting ton station and I didn't want to try to deal with the tube while traveling alone...plus the tube was under some construction while I was in london as well.
Plus I wanted an easy way to view all the major sights, get some good history/background on what I was seeing, and I was excited about the walking tours that are included in the package.

The bus tours offer busses with an audio tour or a live tour guide. I tried both. I was happier with the audio tour. The live tour guides were not united in what they said, and much of the time they said nothing....I was impressed with all the information given in the audio tour and wish I would have been on that bus first because sometimes it gave suggestions on other museums to visit that aren't top on all the lists online.

The big bus tours were really confused. Mother website had times listed, that were completely different then the times listed at each stop and the tour guides stated different times then all th rest too. It was like they didn't know when they were coming and going, and since I was on a tight schedule for a limited amount of time in london I found it frustrating that they ended early, and started late.

Compared to other bus tours, it is more expensive.
I checked out two of the walking tours. One was suppose to be a ghost tour in the evening. Turns out it was nothing more than a pub crawl. They tour guide just brought us to a bunch of pubs where people bought drinks at each one. I ended up leaving the tour because I didn't think any of the places were even truly thought to be haunted, and I wasn't interested in drinking away the little time I had in london.

The other walking tour I took was to do the guard change, and that was a good tour...except that with all the people and craziness at bucking ham palace I ended up losing my tour group...but that was my own fault for being pokey, trying to take pictures and I'm too short to see over the crowd.

Also, the workers seemed very disgruntled. At one stop when there was just a few of us on the bus, the tour guide...who repeatedly told us he was on his lunch break, came over and told us how much he hated the big bus company. I was really surprised at how candidly he spoke and the things he told us about how employees are treated....of course you have to take that with a grain of salt, but it is hard to enjoy yourself when you think you just paid a company to give you a good time and learned how disgruntled the employees are. I ended up getting off that bus because I was spending all my time trying to console the employee instead of enjoy my short trip.

If I had it to do again, I would maybe check out the other bus tour companies...there are a lot...or I would just consider walking the city myself and seeing the eights that way. All of the major iconic places are really within a mile or so of each other, and every few blocks or so are nice, clear city maps. Some of the time it took the bus hours to get through one mile radio us when walking would take 15-20 mins.

Booked a family ticket that was discounted by 25% as we booked in advance, we boarded at Victoria and the day began.
We started on a blue route then transfered to a red route at Marble Arch, We had a very funny and informative guide on the bus, who not only picked out sites but told us about the origin of common sayings why buildings used signs due to illiteracy and much much more!
We hail from Surrey and visit London fairly often but seeing the sites we see more often than i care to mention from a knowledgable view point has broadened our perspective of probably the greatest city in the world!
We also had a ride on the river and the chance of a walking tour (unfortunatley too wet to take advantage)

Well done Big Bus money well spent on a very wet Tuesday.

All the staff were very helpful and provided info for tubes recommended routes ect
The walking tours were great fun and Phil the guide was excellent - thanks Phil for making my sons trip more exciting.
I would definitely recommend using the big bus

Brought the hop on hop off ticket, got 48 hrs for 24hrs , very easy to get around all the sights of london with this service, every team member was very helpful and polite . Would use again when in the city .

This is a great way to see the city. Lots of stops on the way and good commentary. It's easy to hop on and off, didn't have to wait for a bus more than ten minutes. We done the red tour as this is a slightly smaller route and English speaking.

What better way to acclimate yourself in a brand new surrounding then by riding a cozy couch bus all the while being told in your own language what you are looking at! Whatever city we find ourselves in, we jump on a Big Bus tour and get to know the area. Usually we ride the entire route one day then stope in each area of interest. The price is fair and there are plenty of buses and employees to keep the operation moving smoothly. It was a pleasure!

My mom and I had an afternoon to kill after we landed at Heathrow at 2pm. Our connecting flight didn't leave until the next morning. We decided to see as much of London as we could in that afternoon and the Big Bus Tour was a great option for us. We hopped on at Green Park and our guide Stephen was very funny and informative. He was great about telling us when to get our cameras ready for photo opportunities and was a fountain of interesting information. He was very enthusiastic about the great bits of history that are often overlooked in the city and engaged all the tourists he came in contact with, including the ones that didn't speak English.

Also, Stephen escorted my mom and I through the London Underground at the end of the tour and helped us buy tickets and read the map to get back to our hotel. Great tour and great tour guide!

Highly recommend the red route London Big Bus tour. Our guide Chris made it special with an informative commentary covering all the major and lots more less well known sights. It's a real art to deliver a great commentary, not too much information and just a dash of humour. He really made the tour come alive. You can hop on and off at any time and place along the route with buses only 15 minutes apart. If you haven't got long in London and want to get about, this is for you.

I gave this attraction "Very Good" because it was only let down by one of the four guides we had on two of the two bus trips we took. Firstly it was good value for money even though we did not take the free river cruise. One of the tour guides started to quote Churchill on the tour but actually taking on his voice brilliant, one of the other guides I think her name was Jane she was bright bubbly really nice girl credit to the company. One of the other guides spent his time sucking up to the Australians on the tour and then asked somebody where they were from as they walked up the stairs of the bus, when they replied "Liverpool" he looked down and shook his head as they walked down the aisle and made no urther comment, charming.
