I am not from Liverpool although I do no not live far away so maybe he should have been a bit more thoughtful as to whom he had on board. He also then later on was rude to another customer under the guise of health and safety I won't bore you with the deatils . To be honest he should emigrate to Australia well with a bit of luck, even my 12 year old grand daughter thought he was rude.
The amazing thing was he kept on encourgaging people to go on tripadvisor to give their comments.
Anyway back to the Big Bus Tours yes I would use them again, apart from one bad boring guide but everything else was great he didn't put me off.

We used the Big Bus to see the sights in London. The biggest problem with the bus is the London traffic. It took the bus 3 hours to get from Harrods to the Tower of London. I would recommend that you learn the underground (Tube) system and use that. It will be less expensive and quicker.

We loved the Big Bus Tour Bus and the hop-on hop-off concept. We bought our tickets at The Montague On The Gardens, where we were staying, and they had a bus stop only a couple short blocks from the hotel. They are good for 24 hours but the Big Bus staff said it will be good for two days! We used it both days for so many sightseeing places and to just get from point A to point B. You also get a boat tour for the price and we took that three times! The second day we got off at Madame Tussaud's and walked about 15 minutes to see and walk across Abbey Road, walked back and got the next bus and got off at Regent Street and took the couple block walk to see 3 Savile Row where the Beatles had the "Rooftop Concert". So worth while! I seen the competitors hop-on hop-off buses and they were so crowded that I'm glad we chose The Big Bus and happened to have paid a couple bucks more for nice second floor seating. The audio was great as we traveled around and we found it very informative. This is the way to go to see all the important landmarks of London!

First time to London and my partner and I elected for Big Bus due to the fact they offered a Harry Potter walking tour (I'm a diehard fan). The hop on, hop off is great value for money and allowed us to get our bearings in such a big city. The guides on the bus are very knowledgable and humorous and are more than willing to help. We were fortunate enough to get Jess for both our Harry Potter and Changing of the Guard walking tour. He is fantastic. Very knowledgable, passionate and extremely witty, he had us laughing the whole time. He was worth going on the tours for even if you had no interest in the content. Our only regret was not tipping him as we are not used to doing that in Australia. He definitely deserved it though. We enjoyed Big Bus so much that we used them again in other countries and will continue to!

Got on the Big Bus from the London Bridge. Unfortunately we had gotten onto the red bus which offered only the automated audio guide which is not as good as the real guide giving the sights. Especially when your bus gets stuck in traffic and the audio proceeds to the next spot. Look out for the blue bus. Hop On - Hop Off with so many stops is a very good option to join the bus ride whenever you are tired walking around.

After evaluating the HOHO options in London, we were glad to have chosen the Big Bus Tours. We purchased our tickets online (you get a discount if you buy online) and simply presented our tickets to the driver as we boarded. We decided to do this tour late in the afternoon of our first day (we landed at 8:35 am from the states). The timing was great b/c the kids were starting to get tired and it gave them an opportunity to rest while taking in the sights of London. The red line was great b/c there was a live tour guide who kept us entertained. The ride is so relaxing that we did sleep on/off during the ride. There was a lot of traffic on the Friday afternoon when we rode so it might have been better to take the tour when you are not sitting in rush hour traffic. Not sure if I would use it to get around the city as it is much faster to walk or take the underground.

We booked this on the dau we arrived in London. We wanted the live tour guide and were not disappointed. He was very funny and knowledgeable. Our two teenage boys really enjoyed the tour too. We didn't complete it because we hopped off the bus at London Bridge. Want to return and do the other half.

Though the Hop on Hop off Bus Tour gave us an acclimation to the city, it was neither informative or entertaining. I had done a lot of research before booking our Big Bus HoHo tickets online. The first bus, which we waited nearly 40 minutes to get a bus with a live guide, had a guide that didn't say much, and the only humor he gave was saying his name was "Mary". We were not told of sights or history to the city other than things we already knew (ex: "There's the Tower of London"). Being in London for the first time, we were hoping for info we weren't going to get on our own. We sat in traffic for an hour and a half- not the fault of the bus- and finally got off because we were bored (at this point we had completed maybe 30% of the route). We used the bus later in the day for transportation, and got on a bus with a recorded commentary. We both enjoyed this bus much more and found it more informative. Getting on the bus a third time, to get closer to our hotel, we were not told services end at 7:00. We were taken to a destination FATHER from our hotel than we started. The bus was turned off and we were told to get out. Needless to say, the entire bus, approx. 70% full, was stunned. Several expressed their displeasure, and we were told after a time we could all get on one bus (arriving in 20 minutes) and they would complete the route. During this arrangement, we found the employees rude and short. We did eventually get back to the stop we wanted, with a better live guide than the first time. However, if we would have known we were going to be dumped off at exactly 7:00, at a destination unknown to us, we would have never boarded the bus in the first place.

The Cruise Tour (included with the HoHo ticket) was very enjoyable and definitely worth it. I think I would recommend to a friend to skip the HoHo bus, and just purchase a ticket for the cruise tour.

there are many sightseeing bus tours of london and this one is the cheapest, i booked online and if you are in london for more than 1 day then i recommend you get the 48 hour pass as it is no more than the 24 hour pass and it is a great way to get around london with stops frequent and at all the major landmarks which you can just hop on/off to your liking. there are 2 services- the blue line which is mainly for foreign tourists with pre-recorded commentry via hedphones and the red line which has live commentry via a tour guide! i got a 2 day pass so for the first day i took the blue line as it a longer route taking you past kensington and the second day went on the red line which is shorter, and if you are of english speaking then i totally recommend the red line as it is soooooo much better than the blue with its funny,entertaining tour guides and they do really make it an enjoyable experience!!!! the blue line obviously is better for none speaking english but the commentry is soooooo out of time it became impossible to connect the recorded statement to the actual sight of seeing!!!! therefore the blue line for me was a no-go although at least i saw around kensington gardens etc. and also there were more blue buses the 2 days i was there with a ratio of 4 blue line to 1 red which became very frustrating when you are hoping on and off and all you want is the much better red!!!!

Took the big bus london on our first day over the pond. Always a good way to get accustomed to time zone. Water cruise on Thames worthwhile: do it! Service needs to desperately update the English version of the recorded tour. Too many references to Beatles and obscure Hugh Grant films. We could stand a bit more history.

This tour is not cheap but does offer a comprehensive and thorough experience with lots of quirky information along the way. The commentary is available in 13 languages and the controls are simply adjusted for the best listening. I recommend one ear phone in on the traffic side and the other ear cocked to hear what's going omn around you.
The open top deck seats are the prime ones in good weather and the front covered ones when there are showers. The whole ride is effortless and entertaining, the highlight for me was approaching St Paul's Cathedral from Fleet Street- a memorable occasion as this phenomenal building suddenly looms up at the end of the street.
You will have the opportunity to sample some of the major sights of London and to learn some fascinating history along the way. It is a great vantage point and the photo`opportunities are numerous. Flexibility with your ticket means you can hop on and off along the circuit for up to 24 hours, taking your time to explore some of the many attractions en route. Also included in the price is a one way Thames river cruise which adds to the value.
One small cavil is the way the very good earphones are offered to grab like popcorn in plastic bags. Since they are deemed so expendable they can be seen on top of bus shelters, road signs and everywhere around, disposed off like confetti by disaffected passengers. Please stop this stupid and wasteful practice. Otherwise all credit to the bus company for providing a much appreciated and enjoyed guide to the metropolis.

On a nice day take a few hours to ride the circuit and see London. After a morning of visiting attractions, hop on the bus and just relax, listen to the tour, and cruise London. It feels great to rest the back and feet and just see what going on in the city. You will weave back and forth across the Themes and see the city from a few different perspectives. This is the only use for this tour, however. If it's raining or cold, forget about it. It's purely a way to rest and keep the touring alive.

What a fantastic Company. This was the first time we have used the Big Bus and it will not be the last. We had a 48hr ticket. Fantastic helpful staff at all bus stops and the drivers were brilliant. Free river cruise and walking tours with your ticket. Excellent hop on and off service so you can shop and then get back on the bus and relax to your next destination. We used this service while the London Bike Ride was on and it did not effect us at all the staff at all stops directed us to the next bus and where to get on and off. We usually travel by tube so hot, sweaty and stuffy and missing all the sights, this is a much more enjoyable way to see London and you get to see all the sights sat comfortably with a really good commentary. We used, blue, red and green bus routes and all were great for our needs. I would definitely recommend visitors to use this Company. Many thanks Big Bus a fantastic two days seeing things I would not normally have seen.

Get off the bus and take the walking tour. Phil, our tour gude was a blast on the Harry Potter sites tour. The Bus tours were ok, but the walking tour and the river cruise boat from Tower of London to Greenwich with the 48 hour pass were the redeeming value of the Big Bus package.

We traveled to London with our daughter and grandchildren. There were 5 of us traveling together ranging in age from 14 through 69. Our hotel was in the King's Cross area and the Big Bus runs their buses in this area which helped us choose this company. We were very pleased with the different routes and used their services for two full days. Most, but not all of the buses, have efficient handicapped access. If a bus came along that was not accessible we just waited for the next one which came along in 15 minutes or less. The commentary, whether live or recorded was excellent and accurate tuned to what we were seeing. The hop-on hop-off feature worked quite well.

The day we used the Big Bus there were a certain number of roads closed due to a freecycle event in London. However, the drivers and couriers and ticket sellers at the stops were very helpful, pointing us in the right direction to what we wanted to see. You get a free river cruise included with your ticket. All in all a very good day and good value for money.

We took the red route tour because it had a human tour guide, where the blue route has a recording over ear phones. Was fun and convenient to hop on and hop off whenever we wanted. Buses arrived frequently. For best viewing go to the top floor of the bus. Beware of bait-and-switch on also buying entry tickets to certain sites. When we purchased a Big Bus package that included entry to the London Eye Ferris wheel, the Big Bus agent assured us that the ticket included "fast-track" entry, which turned out to be a lie.

A guide instead of earphone on the red line bus was excellent! Later we hop on a blue line, unfortunatelly there was no option to choose the dutch language while there where a lot of Dutch tourist in the bus.

We purchased the 24-hour Big Bus Tours tickets online after consulting here: http://www.londontoolkit.com/whattodo/big_bus_sightseeing.htm and did not regret it! We learned about the cities of Westminster and London, visited museums and landmarks, enjoyed a free cruise on the river Thames with live commentary and got a great lay of the land to set us up for more days of touring and visiting.

This is a great way to see the sights of London. If you do the loops, you will cover all the main sights. We even saw Alan Titchmarsh from the bus!

As you enter the bus, you collect headphones to listen to the commentary. There are Big Bus employees at each stop to assist with any queries. All of our experience with these guides were positive.

The only negative that I would state was that although we did two days and used the buses a lot, we only had our headphones as a guide. When I have previously done these tours in NYC, San Fran etc, there has been a native of the area as a commentator which gives a more informal, better guide to the city.

We used the City Cruise from the Tower of London to Big Ben. This was excellent and the commentary on this, from a cockney, was excellent.

Me and my partner used the big bus tour for one day and we loved it we saw all of the sights and I got some great pictures, it was so easy to use and the people were so informative they are always happy to help, would definitely do it again.

Had reservation about doing this as it wasn't cheap. But have to say what a way to see London. We used the blue tour which has narration rather than a guide, free headphones and even free waterproof ponchos, and we needed them! We purchased our tickets just after lunch and the tickets were valid all the next day as well plus we had a free boat trip. Plan to go again for a day trip and will spend all day hopping on and off.

There are many bus tours but I prefer the Big Bus company. There are three routes from which to choose. You can take the green, red or blue routes. When you purchase your pass you get a nice map showing all the stops. We never had to wait too long for one of the buses to show up. Our travel agent booked us with another open top bus company but we did not use them. I did have trouble purchasing a pass on line from the US but it was a breeze in the UK. Touring a city on an open top bus is the only way to see everything.

My husband and l took the Big Red Bus Tour and had a great day,we were on the red tour and it doesn't matter how much you think you know about London ,the commentators on the bus know so much more, we found all the staff very helpful, and the boat trip to Greenwich was great all in all it was worth every penny ,would highly recommend this Bus tour.

We did the London Big Bus. The buses are reasonably frequent at every 15 to 20 minutes, the route is great and the information that you listen to via the provided headphones is a great way to get an introduction to a city and decide what you want to see.There's even free poncho's, when when the London Weather turns on you !
We also used the free ferry ride, included with the ticket, to get another perspective on the city. Good value.
** If you already know what you want to see in London, just use the underground/tube. It's cheaper and faster - but you don't get to see the rest of the city on your way to things, like you would in the bus :-)
Loved the big bus - good value as we got to use it for 2 days on the 1 ticket.

I must say this is a excellent way to see and get around all the major attraction's I London, and also excellent value for money at only £31 for an adult for 2 days unlimited hop on and hop off as much as you want this is great value, also the staff and drivers are very helpful and friendly, would recommend to anyone!!

I really enjoyed the London Big Bus Tours. I have been in London before but never did the "Hop on Hop Off" tour. The weather was lovely and I thought this would be a new way to see the city. I purchased a 2-day pass at my hotel and used the convenient green extension bus. The buses offer a choice of red and blue lines. The red lines (recommended) have a live guide who can gave us lots of information not generally known about London. The blue lines have taped commentary in numerous languages. The bus stopped at many of the tourist attractions in London. The fare included a one-way boat ride down the Thames, which I took, and purchased the Greenwich extension. Food and beverages were available at reasonable cost. I passed a lovely afternoon sipping Chardonnay while cruising up and down the Thames. The ticket also included several short walking tours at no additional expense--except perhaps a small tip to the guide. I did the Ghosts by Gaslights tour. Learned some interesting facts about London and met some fellow travelers. You can purchase either a one-day or two-day pass. If you have not been to London before and want to see the major sites, I recommend the two-day pass. The top of the bus is open, which is the best way to go. Don't worry if it starts to drizzle. Big Bus provides waterproof hooded ponchos at no additional charge. The one drawback was not being sure which direction I was heading. It would have helped to know this as my extension bus joined the regular bus routes.

We took this tour on the day of our arrival in London and we opted not to get off of the bus for the entire 3-hour tour because our guide, Nick, was so entertaining (and our driver, Barry, was so talented at positioning us for some spectacular photos of major sights.) Nick was extremely knowledgeable and informative about the historical, cultural, and social aspects of London; he was articulate and funny and gave a first-rate performance.

I would assume this is the best way to see London in a short amount of time. If you want to go into the attractions then I probably wouldn't pay for the bus tour because it took us the better part of a day to do the route......and we wound up not finishing it due to time. That said, the information is helpful, the bus was clean and the views were incredible.

I was only going to be in London for a week and as I wanted to cram in as much as possible into this short time i decided to get on a tour bus! a few friends has recommended Big Bus so i decided to go with them (There are a few cheaper options too, but they seemed to have less buses!) I did the blue line first, which has an audio commentary, but i found it very boring and because of the traffic in London a little slow, it felt like there was a lot of time when it would just be music playing.

After grabbing some lunch I hopped on to the red tour. The red tour has a live guide to tell you about the city, My guide was Jade and the driver was Dave(?) and they were fantastic! Jade is a real tribute to the Big Bus company! she was enthusiastic and bubbly! It was a brilliant tour with just the right amount of history and humor mixed in, and I had a fab time! Jade even took a picture of me on the bus to show my friends! I had another guide later that day who was also great but i was only with him for 2 stops so unfortunately never caught his name!

The tickets are valid another day, so i hopped back on the buses and did the river cruise on the Sunday whist checking out a few more of the attractions like the Tower of London and Tower Bridge! The red tour is definitely the best on Big Bus, and if you get a good guide it can really bring the city to life! Thanks Big Bus and especially Jade and Dave for a wonderful couple of days!

We did the Big Bus Tour in both London and Paris and loved it. Good information and highlighting most of the important things that people would want to visit. It was much easier than using public transportation to see multiple sites. I especially liked the fact that there are both the blue and red tours in London, allowing for some different options across multiple days (there is way too much to see for one day).

The double decker red buses were plentiful and seem to be everywhere. We were fortunate and had a lovely sunny day, so the perfect way to see many of the sights in London. Unfortunately, there was an event going on in mid-Westminster, but not one of the bus drivers announced it, or had the detoured routes posted. We jumped off at the Victoria and Albert Museum and the National History Museum. When we returned to the designated bus stop, we waited over an hour. The bus was packed - standing room only, and the bus driver was overwhelmed and terse when asked why the buses were taking so long. She handed me a copy of the printed alert about the event, but then took it back and folded it and put it away. It took us an hour to go less than .5 km, we ended up jumping off and taking the tube home. The next day we took the hop on/off boat. We waited in a long queue for 45 min - 1 hour at the Tower London, finally got on the boat, and were forced off at the next stop Big Ben (10 -15 minutes on the boat). The queue at Big Ben was long as well, we jumped on another Big Bus and went home. The boat trip was worthless and I wish I had known they meant "get off/get in queue", it certainly was not hop on/off. The lack of announcement over the possibility of delay or detour for the buses was ridiculous, especially considering the cost for this attraction. We would have probably still gone, but we would not have been annoyed. We are lucky that we had alternate means of transportation and were able to use it. The sales people will do anything to get you and your money on the bus.

I take this city tour every time I come to London just to see what has changed since the last time. It is fun to hop off wherever you think might interest you, and there are stops at all points of interest. Also important, it allows you to see the layout of the city and make notes on places where you might want to visit later on your own. If you are lucky, you might get a narrator who is a real comedian. Love that British humor.

We recently had 3nights/4 days in London. Before we travelled we decided to prebook the Big Bus hop on hop off bus tour around London. Apart from the savings we were unfamiliar with London and this was a great way to save time without waiting. We just printed up our tickets and followed the downloaded map to find our starting point on the bus tour.
How great the views are even with the crowds and the advantage of this bus company is you get an entertaining English speaking tour guide. Other bus company's need the annoying (sometimes not reliable) disposable head phones to hear your required language.
We sat outside on the top deck! Beware though we had a sudden summer downpour so take your wet weather gear - just in case. Ponchos are supplied if you are caught out. Certainly recommend this Tour!

We went on the big bus on a 48 hour tour. It was great to see all the sights, and was fab that you got a free cruise up the Thames and back.

They give out free ponchos which was a nice touch too.

I would say however, that some of the staff were not so friendly. One bus commentator was particularly unhelpful to people who were asking him questions. There was no eye contact with people when he was speaking directly to them. I felt that as this was one of the last bus tours, all the man wanted to do was go home and have done with it. Not what you want to hear or see when you are a tourist!

Having said that, the bus tour was informative, however, I personally would use another provider if I ever decided to do another tour in the future,

The city of London is beautiful at night. The combination of the monuments and the lighting is really pretty.

Make sure to book with a solid operator the one we used ( http://www.london-by-night.net/london-by-night-sightseeing-bus-tour.htm) only had one other family and we couldn't hear the audio.

Also note that it can be pretty chilly at night in London especially if you are in the outside part of the bus.

Had a great time in seeing London on the big bus tour, particularly enjoyed the river tour last evening, not sure of the guys name, but the trip was informative & fun. Did the royal walking tour today with Kevin "bottle of Water". He was brilliant, told us so much & showed us great viewing points for changing of the guard.

Maybe it was the time of day or the weather, but we didn't really get much out of the Big Bus Tour. It seemed like the bus only stopped at one or two places and drove past a lot of very interesting places. One bus we were on decided to stop service and drop us at another bus stop and that bus was going on a different route so it was take it or leave it. It seemed like we were forever going through Piccadilly Circus. I would try out the Big Bus Tour again to see if it was just us being new to the city or if the Tour itself is flawed.

Fastest way to see London most important attractions. This tour allows you to get an eye on the attractions that you need to witness in London. most importantly is that you can hop off at any site you want to visit or take photos then hop on the next bus whenever you like. They have tickets valid for 24 hrs or 48 hrs. a trip on a cruise into river Thames was included in our tickets (but beware it's not a round trip). You will be accompanied with a recorded guidance in several languages which makes the trip more interesting. I would definitely recommend especially for London first time visitors.

I took a highlighted version of one of the Big Bus Tours London trips and really loved it. The guide was very entertaining and the management of the tour was extremely professional. They were keen to be both informative and make sure everything ran on time. I would highly recommend this tour group to someone who doesn't have much time to explore all the landmarks slowly. They also can customise tours for large groups. My blog Sunny in London features a more detailed review and many, many pictures.

Used the Big Bus Tours in London for the second time in 2 years & the experience was just as good. All of the buses we were on were clean & well kept, plenty of staff at every stop to answer questions.
The weather may not have been very good but it's still a great way to see the sights & to get around the city area.

The tickets seem expensive especially when you add on extensions so as to take the boat ride to Greenwich but they are well worth it because they are valid for 2 days. And you would need the two days. This is a great way to get an overview of London and a bit of gossip about house prices etc. You can hop on and off to walk about and it means you cover a lot of ground in a shortish time. We only had 2 full days in London so the Big Bus tour was perfect for us.

We had a 2 day hop on hop off pass. Took advantage of the river cruise and also the Harry Potter walking tour. The guides were very informative, but Ruth Ellis was not tried and hanged in London, I'm not sure where the Minellium bridge is, or Charion Cross, but we were told they are in London!! James and Dave were great, it was a couple of the others that could do with reviewing their talks.

There are different lines which go all over London. Since there is always a chance of rain, they provide a free poncho so you can ride on the top deck. The tour with headphones is just as good as the tour with an actual guide on board. You get 24 hours with a ticket, but you can actually ride a little longer. Just remember to catch the last bus at 7 pm. Buy tickets to attractions through them to save money and time, and there's a free river cruise to take advantage of.

We have traveled to London for the past 4 years and have utilized the Big Bus Tour HOHO bus each time. I find the price to be the best for what you receive. I also like that that they offer different lines as well as multi lingual and live tour guides. Each time we have taken the FREE Thames cruise and the FREE walking tours. This year we took the Changing of the guard tour with KEVIN. Kevin enjoys his tour and it shows. He knows the ins and outs of the city and the Changing of the Guards. This walking tour is very fast paced and includes stairs and uneven surfaces, so put on your walking shoes and bring a large bottle of water. You will NOT be sanding in front of the palace for this tour. You will be given a quick background on WHY they change daily and WHO actually changes. Then you will see first hand where they BEGIN and then wisk yourself off to where they will be marching. Kevin likes to march ALONG with them and then take a quick shortcut to get IN FRONT of them and see them march on by in front of the palace. I enjoyed seeing it this way and go tthe perfect spot for viewing. I would suggest taking this FREE tour first and then going to see it again at each location for a longer period of time. BTW, Kevin is FABULOUS! We also took the FREE Thames cruise from Tower Bridge to Westminster which was a beautiful way to see London. The wait was a bit longer than I expected, but we were very lucky and were the first to get on the boat. Always sit up top if possible to get the best panoramic views of the city. You will alos receive a small commentary while traveling. This boat ofers inside seating as well as toinlets and a small cafe for drinks and snacks. A great way to get from one place to the next! The HOHO bus itself,some are newer than others, some are a bit worn, but they have the MOST buses out of any of the companies offering HOH service and they come by the stops MORE FREQUENTLY, and that is very important. NOW, about times, these can be tricky, but just remember, the times given for when they FINISH for the day are posted on the map that they offer on all of their buses and it states the time that the LAST BUS LEAVES THEIR FIRST STOP FOR THAT LINE COLOR. Once you figure it out, it works perfect. I have always utilized these buses to get me anywhere in the city, whether it's shopping or nighttime plays. If the BLUE line says 18:00, that would be when they LEAVE THEIR stop number for the LAST TIME of that day. I have seen many people stranded and very upset over this, so please check out these times and PLAN your day accordingly. Otherwise, HAVE FUN! My children LOVE these buses and spend more time enjoying the ride rather than the attractions!

We decided to spend our last day in London visiting the sights on The Big Bus Tour, however we didn't realise how much fun we would actually have on board. James was without a doubt the best tour guide I've ever had the pleasure of meeting. His knowledge about London and his comedic deliverance of this knowledge was second to none. Myself and my boyfriend were almost crying with laughter for the whole time. It was a pleasure to be on board with him. I would actually recommend people ask who their tour guide is before getting on as you won't find a greater one than him. Made our trip complete.

We brought the 48hr big bus tickets which was a bargain.
We were able to go onto the Buses and see so much more than we would walking.
Also your ticket includes free River Cruises as many times as you like.
From Tower Pier to Westminster and with the 48hr one you can go up to Greenwich and look around there.
Staff were so helpful and cheery well worth doing.
Thank you Big Bus for a wonderful time in London

I had the pleasure of taking the big bus tour of London yesterday with my girlfriend. I've been on bus tours of many major cities across Europe. They're always interesting but the guides tend to be a little boring. Yesterday was the complete opposite.

James was the most entertaining tour guide i've ever witnessed, his intricate knowledge of London was unquestionable but his delivery of the info was up there with some great stand up comedians. We had tears in our eyes for most of the journey from laughing.

If you want to do this tour, just hold back on getting on the bus until you know James is the guide.

James, we salute you sir, for putting a fantastic end to a great great weekend in London. Thanks.

Me and the Family went to London in June 2014, it was amazing! they showed us a lot of what we didn't see of London!, it was a fantastic time, would definitely go on there again! they literally take you all the way around London, they show you the shard, Big Ben, Hyde park, St Paul's Cathedral go over the London Bridge, and of course, Oxford street & the London Bridge! The river was amazing! Had the best days of my life in the most visited city in the world, absolutely fabulous!
Thank You Big Bus Tour London for an amazing experience. Would deffo go on it again in the future, For people going to London you should try the Big Bus Tour, they wont let you down, thank you for letting me share my experiences.
We loved our Big Bus Tour of London - we had a great knowledgeable commentator on the bus. Highly recommend - and it's nice that you can hop on and off at various sites and save your feet :)

Had a very informative tour, we found all of the staff to be really friendly and genuinely pleased to help make your trip of london a happy one ! Went on the blue and the red busses, well done to Nick from the red tour bus, it was his 3rd round trip of the day when we hopped on but he was very enthusiastic , funny and knowledgeable ! Would have no hesitation on recommending this company, in fact have already told our friends to book !

First off I have to say "never visit London during Wimbledon"! Was not aware it would be here during our 2 day stay and it made getting around the city horrible. Traffic was awful and it really limited our experience. The Big Bus Tour was fine. We really enjoyed the Harry Potter walking tour and our guide was top notch.

We bought a 24 hour ticket and stopped at several places by hopping on and off. We never had to wait for a bus at any of the stops! A trip up the river is also included free of charge, the boat was quite full and we didn't get a seat which was a bit of a let down as I was travelling with my mum who is 70 years old. All of the staff were polite apart from the initial ticket seller at Paddington who was quite rude. Over all a good experience
Buses are newer since I assume the line is as well. However, the line doesn't go as many places as a the red bus tour hop-on/off buses did.

My daughter & I were in London for 2 days; we purchased the two day hop on-hop off bus pass with the free boat tour. What a bargain! We used the bus as transportation as well as information. They had 2 loops; one with a live commentary, the other with a taped commentary. The boat ride gave a unique perspective, too - up close views of the Tower Bridge, London Eye and the Globe. There were plenty of buses running - never had to wait more than 5 minutes at a stop. SO glad I had read reviews - other tour buses in London had lines of people waiting at their stops.

This is the 2nd time we've used a multi-day pass during our London visits. It is so convenient to move around the city with the ability to hop off & on during the day. Buses are clean and the hosted tour guides bring the history of London alive. Well worth the time to ride the different routes to all the attractions.

A good way to do some site seeing in London. Take some time to understand the routes and timetables and you can use this bus for 80% as public transport if you are not in a hurry.

Good information during the tours.

We hopped on one of these double decker bus tours to get a good feel for sites without having to do a lot of walking. They give you headphones when you get on so you can listen to information on the sites as you were driving past them. Interesting and informative. The location of the stops were convenient and the route covered was perfect for what we wanted. We were able to really see a lot of the London area from just sitting on a bus.

We stayed in London for the weekend and it was one the best days we had experienced, the tour guides are so informative and friendly.
We hopped on and off wherever we pleased, so handy and at £50 for the whole day what a bargain.

We booked a one day bus pass through our hotel during our stay in London. This was both of our first time in London and we wanted to see as many of the major sites as we could before we left. That being said, a hop on hop off bus tour is a great way to do so. It allows you the flexibility to get off at the locations you like and just drive past the ones you aren't interested in. Not only do you get to see many of the top sites in the City but the guide (either recorded or live depending on the bus) provide more in depth history and facts about different landmarks as you go. I have done a hop on hop off bus tour before in a different city and found this one was not nearly as good, primarily in terms of the guide's enthusiasm and knowledge of the city. My mom on the other hand had never been on such a tour before and thoroughly enjoyed this one. My only other complaint is that many of the headphones we received upon entering the bus didn't work well and would only work if held in a certain position which was frustrating because they kept cutting in and out. My tips would be to not book through your hotel as ours charged us more than what we would have paid if we had booked directly through the operator. And also, the best seats (during good weather) are on the second level as they are better for photo taking and sightseeing in general. It was pretty windy and rained a little during the day but we still toughed it out on the upper level since you are provided with a plastic poncho. All in all for the price it is a good way to see the city if you are short on time; however, there is room for improvement in terms of the guides and faulty headphone connection.

We prebooked a 48 hour ticket on the internet and the bus stopped just five minutes from our Hotel. What a great way to see London with either pre recorded commentary (Blue Route) or live commentary (Red Route). You are free to get off wherever you want at stops around the route and then hop back on after you have explored. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience and the staff were very helpful at all times.

We typically do a private car and guide but have found this type of tour bus to also be very informative and helpful. Hop on and off where you like for a 24 hr ticket. The commentary is usually a mix of history and local information. They have all English buses or buses that have taped info in many languages via a headset. We hopped off at The Tower Bridge and took in the Crown Jewels and a quick Tower of London tour. The bus ticket also includes a cruise on the Thames from Westminster pier as far as Greenwich pier if you like. We did this and found it very informative. The weather was a bit windy and misty which made the top deck a little cool but we enjoyed the views from the boat at high tide. There is covered seating below with a few snacks and beverages to purchase. The commentary on the river boat was outstanding. Allow a full portion of your day to be able to take the entire bus line and do the boat cruise. Most hotels sell the pass for the bus. Several companies operate but I recommend the Big Bus Company.

This proved to be a great way to get around London. The price of the tickets was reasonable, and we simply hopped on and off their buses to move around the city. The drivers were courteous (and it's incredible how they maneuver the buses along the narrow roads) and the buses quite clean. It got a little busy at times, meaning no seats on the upper deck of the bus, and the London traffic slows everybody down, however you have to expect crowds and traffic in the city. The 2-day passes included a free cruise up the Thames to Greenwich, which we took advantage of. It was great. Also, I'll note that due to the Taxi Driver Strike that caused some issues one afternoon, they kindly allowed us to use our passes for an additional half-day, which we really appreciated. Combine the bus with walking through the parks and along some of the shopping avenues and you've have an amazing time in this incredible city!

I strongly recommend going on a bus tour of London, especially if you have the pleasure of "nick" and "roody" guiding you through town. I actually learnt things about London on this tour and wasn't bored to death.
Nick kept the stories and jokes flowing whilst roody made sure we were in the optimum position for all the picturesque moments. The only downfall of the tour was the end

These two should be giving lessons.
Bravo fellas.

This was my first ever bus tour and my first time on a bus for several years and I loved it. Our tour guide, Nick was very informative and kept us entertained for the 2 hours we stayed on. I thought I knew a lot about London but Nick told us many things I did not know.
It was a shame about the bad traffic but with Nick on board I did not get bored while waiting for the traffic to move.
Highly recommended.

I was recently in London with friends for their first visit to the UK. In my past visits, I have used other hop on/hop off carriers but this time we used The Big Bus Tour and I found them to be the best by far of any service previously used. The staff at the various stops were all pleasant, informative and very willing to accommodate our needs and queries. We used the blue tour by our choice and found the recorded narration to be great with individual headphones that worked perfectly with exceptional clarity. The timing of the information was spot on, efficiently descriptive, and allowed one to prepare for a photo moment. The location of stops and the frequency of bus pickups was efficient and user friendly, too. The addition of a Thames cruise included in the fee was a real bonus and much enjoyed.

We went to London for the day so decided to go on the tour bus,there were 5 of us so we got a slight discount which was good
The person that we got our tickets firm was friendly helpful and really funny made us all laugh
We sat upstairs on the open top bus with a guide giving us information on the attractions he was funny but informative nothing he didn't know he greeted everyone that go on the bus.
We all really enjoyed the tour round as we went for the day we could not have seen all the attractions only down side we would have to change buses in Piccadilly so we decided to have a walk round went for a cake and walked through Hyde park back to Oxford Street I see the company have not had great reviews but we couldn't fault our experience of it would use it again

One of several different operators doing the same thing in London. We found the ticket seller very helpful, transferred to a bus with a live guide who was entertaining and informative. The commentary included the usual explanations of what we were seeing, as well as some curious trivia about London and insider knowledge that was valuable. The bus did get caught up in traffic, so allow for this when planning your day. We also did the boat tour which was quite enjoyable. A good way to get an overview of the city and learn a bit along the way.

We had a 24 hour pass which gave us a chance to have a trip first then next day could hop on and off at the places we had chosen the day before. One bus had a personal guide explaining the different venues. The other had headphones to listen to the commentary. The buses are interchangeable which is great as they travel different routes and gives a broader view of London. Highly recommend this system

I bought the two-day hop-on//hop-off bus tour for my self and my daughter. We had only two days to see everything...and we did! At the time of tour purchase, the helpful man offered us "extra" tours (on the bus route) at a discounted rate and without the queue. We jumped on the bus, got off when we wanted to see something in particular, i.e. Mmme. Tousaud's Wax Museum, Tower of London, Buckingham Palace, the boat tour that was included in our price and Harrods Dept. Store.

We listened to the commentaries in English, with no sarcasm or editorials (like on other bus tours I've been on.) There were eight languages from which to select.

I believe we got our money's worth: we saw everything, got on and off at our leisure and learned all the history.

The only caveat to my complete satisfaction is that on the first night, the bus didn't go back to our Westminster destination after 5pm, so we had to jump on a local city bus....still fun, but deducted from our original budget.

There are several tour bus companies (you'll see them all over the streets) but for my money, this is the best and I've used them in other cities as well.

Had a little trouble with finding my first bus, but once I did, I was the only person on the tour. The guide sat next to me and pointed out things and gave me the tour. He made me laugh and I really was enjoying it, so I stayed on for about an hour just snapping photos and seeing the sites. He took a great photo of me in front of Big Ben from the bus. Super friendly staff and a lot of sites seen in a small amount of time. I ended up getting off after making the full circuit one time, the next buses the I hopped on were also full of great guides. I definitely recommend.

A great way to see London. Big bus tour enables you to hop on and off to connect to their different bus lines that are going to different parts of the city. Friendly staff, automated or live commentary on the bus gives you a great snap shot of London's great sights.

We purchased the 48 hour pass. This was a good way to go as we did not have to do the full tour in one day. We also took advantage of the river cruise. This provides a different perspective on London as well as some history of the Thames. On the bus tour we preferred the Red line with its live narration. The narrator makes it easier to appreciate what you are seeing. The recorded version on the Blue line sometimes points out items of interest too late to see anything. If this will be your first time in London it will be worth your while to take a tour.

This is fantastic, best way to see London if you have never been before. They have loads of different stops you can hop on and hop off to catch a bus later on if you wish. It takes a good 2-3 hours but the weather was lovely so we managed to sit on the second level of the bus. The only disappointment was we never got to see Buckingham Palace, we just drove straight past it but I do believe their was some kind of event on but overall it's a great experience.

I get to London fairly often for business, but I usually don't have time to be a tourist. When I finally had a free day, I took the recommendation of my British colleague and booked tickets with Big Bus.

I was fortunate to have a beautiful weather day so I was able to sit on the second level of the bus. The hop on, hop off bus route hit all the spots I wanted to see, including a good drop off spot for the London Eye. I imagine some of the other bus companies have similar routes, but this company was reasonably priced, easy to locate the pick up spots, and gave me a glimpse into all the most popular parts of London in one day.

I highly recommend this for tourists.

As I work for a concierge desk in a big hotel, I decided it was time to test the tours I have been sending my guests on. And boy, I wasn't disappointed! Our tour guide was Martin and he was possibly one of the most intelligent people I've ever met. He was very funny and knowledgable about everything we saw. The tour bus itself is great value for money considering you get the free river cruise and walking tours included!!! It's a MUST for any tourist or even Londoner who wants to see the beautiful city at its best. Yes it rained when we were there but we were having so much fun we didn't care! Great thing to do if you have a spare afternoon in London! Well done the whole team. Every Big Bus Tour person I met was incredibly friendly and bubbly and made our day so special!

P.s. - Martin?.....the birthday girl (Swedish girl) was too shy to give you her number ;)

Our Big Bus tour guide, Nobby, deserves his own fan club. He served up London with wit and flair, giving just the right amount of history and lore and his love for the city was infectious. We thoroughly enjoyed the live (red tour) and recorded (blue tour) narration . It's a great way to get an overview of London so you know which sites you want to come back to and get better acquainted with. Three cheers, Big Bus, for a great experience. How soon could you clone Nobby so everyone could have the great experience that we did?

We really loved this tour for our first time through London. Everyone we encountered on the various buses and stops along the way was very professional. We learned our way around the City very quickly with the help of these folks. I would recommend Big Bus to anyone who wants an easy informative tour of London.

I booked the 48 hour hop on/hop off tour for my husband and I online before visiting London in May, 2014. We could not have been more pleased that we chose this company. The drivers and
staff on the sidewalks helping to direct clients were all extremely polite and willing to help - Service With A Smile! The buses were prompt. We would highly recommend the Big Bus Company.

Great service! Hop-on, Hop-off as you wish. Robert was our tourguide for a while and he was excelent! He is very sharp and funny. Lucky if you get him.
Best choice if you want to explore London with limited time.

We came to London as part of a super break deal for 2 nights and decided to book the bus tour on a 48 hour ticket, as recommended by other trip advisor users. I'm so glad that we did! The tours were informative, interesting and the stops were conveniently located and there was always a bus close by, we never had to wait longer than 10 minutes. I would highly recommend this tour as a good introduction to London and even as a cheap mode of transport around the city.

We chose a wet day to get on the big bus tour. Mostly we wanted to just ride around town and listen to the commentary. Unfortunately it seems everyone else chose the same day. It was very crowded and there were times when we didn't get a seat. The headphones they give you to listen to the commentary are good and the commentary was good. I am glad the bus provided ponchos for the rain. Look around for discounts - tickets can be up to 8 pounds cheaper online and from various different outlets

My husband and I took the entire loop of this tour. Every person we dealt with, from ticket seller to "handlers" at every stop (kindly folks who guide tourists to the right bus), to our most EXCELLENT tour guide, KEVIN WAYNE (hello from Chicago, Kevin--you rule!!)...every single aspect made this hop on/hop off the best ticket investment in the city. Excellent overview of neighborhoods and sites. Informative and great fun. Wonderful afternoon! Everyone visiting London should do it.

I stayed at Thistle Kensington Gardens and I was surprisingly delighted when I learned that the Big Bus Tour's blue route stops right in front of the hotel. It was great because the tour had strategic stops and really covers the best of London. My only issue is that after all the tourist spot stops in central London, going back to the hotel took a very long time because there were so many uninteresting stops on the way back to the hotel. Oh well, I think that's the downside of paying for a cheaper hotel in a not-so-central location.

It was a cold, wet day when we boarded the Big Bus. They were on time and gave us some rain ponchos and we ascended to the top of the open bus. It was a bit cold, a bit wet but, the commentary was great. We started on the blue route which was recorded but, it was very well narrated and even through the cold, blowing rain, we had a great time. We hopped off at the London Eye and joined the river tour. The guide was very funny and made the entire trip very fun. While the weather was a bit rubbish, the tour was wonderful. We would book with them agin next time we come to London!

We chose the big bus tour on our quick trip to London. We bought the two day pass. The first day we rode the bus for a tour. The tour was pretty interesting, it definitely helped me get my bearings so I could figure out where I was. The second day we rode it as a hop on hop off to the Tower of London. We got to the tower with no problems, unfortunately on the way back we ran into some problems. We were trying to get to Kensington palace, the representative told us it would take an hour to an hour and 20 to get there. We were on the bus for almost two hours before we decided to get off 9 stops before Kensington. We were really upset because we missed our afternoon tea.
Pros- guides with personality, good way to see the city without walking, tons of buses, lots of stops, hop on hop off, reasonably priced
Cons- traffic can be difficult, no direct routes, blue line drivers don't announce stops

I've never done a bus tour, so I was pleasantly surprised when I went on the classic Red Big Bus tour (with English commentary) with my parents who were visiting from Australia. At £32 per head, it's not cheap, but it's definitely an easy way to see some of the most famous sites around Central London in a relatively short amount of time. The trip took us on a complete loop around Westminster, the old city of London, Southwark and Belgravia in about two and a half hours. Our tour guide, Nick, was jovial, lively and entertaining and had plenty of fun anecdotes to accompany the various sites. Our driver Trevor did an excellent job manoeuvring through London traffic. Overall, we were thoroughly entertained and particularly impressed by Nick's apparently inexhaustible supply of energy and enthusiasm. If you're short on time but want a whirlwind history of the city of London and plenty of opportunities to take photos, this tour comes highly recommended.

Bought the 48 hour ticket which includes the walking tours. Used the hop on hop off bus to orient ourselves and get around the sights. On the last morning we did the Royal Walking Tour. It was brilliant. The guide (I am sorry that I cannot remember name) was awesome. She knew exactly where we had to be at the right time to watch the changing of the guards. We actually walked next to the Royal Fusliers as the marched to Buckingham Palace and caught the old guard marching to meat them. Her timiming was impeccable. One of the highlights of our time in London. My only disappointment was Her Majesty wastn't home.

Loved the hop on hop off feature! Was so easy to get around and see everything. Both blue and red tours were very informative. All drivers and Big Bus employees were extremely helpful!! Definitely recommend if your only in London for a few days and want to see it all! We did the 48hr tickets!

We took our foreign exchange student on a Big Bus Tour on his first day in London. It was an excellent choice. He really saw London at its best, could take fantastic photos on the open top bus and got a great overall impression. Our teenage children also enjoyed it a lot, although they live here.
That was mainly due to our guide Martin who made city come alive. He had an easy and fun way of explaining well known and less obvious attractions and sharing his insight knowledge of London combined with many useful tips. Thank you for an unforgettable tour Martin!
The tour was worth its money as it also includes a River Tour.
You can hop on and off at many different stops, have a live guide (recommended) or an audio guide in different languages.

Absolutely grand tour! We got lucky and had Big Steve as our guide! He made our time on the bus so pleasant we couldn't wait to explore the rest of the city! He had Great knowledge of the city and he was funny too! Wish we could have brought him along for the rest of our days in London!! He is a real master of his craft!

Although it is pricey (62 pounds for 2) it is a great way to get a quick view of the city if you have limited time. The tour guide was excellent; very informative and funny too! It's also a great way to get your bearings around London which was important for me as this was my first time in the city. We saw Big Ben, parliament, London eye, Fleet Street, London tower, across tower bridge and many more. A river cruise on the Thames is also included but we didn't have time for it. Well worth the money.
Big Bus tours was very good! We had one driver named Kevin who was just wonderful! I wold go on this tour bus again. Very informative, too!

Bit of a mixed bag this one but overall still rated as very good. Firstly, haggle on price. At first it was £32 but then we got it down to £27 which seemed more reasonable - but why not be honest and publish your prices? We joined opposite Euston Station and the bus took us to Aldwych where we switched to the red line bus which takes up to 2.5 hours to complete a circuit (traffic permitting). The seats were wet upstairs from a recent shower so we were given plastic ponchos to sit on which was very thoughtful. The first guide was really good and knew lots about London. Halfway round the guide and driver changed, and unfortunately the second guide was less helpful. I know London but still went to places I'd not been before, and learned some new stuff about places I did know. You can hop on and off the bus as you go round and you get a free map with bus stops numbered and highlighted. Break your journey for shopping, visiting an attraction, comfort breaks, drinks, a meal or whatever then get back on and continue the tour.
Our first visit to London! The Big Bus hop on/off service was a good orientation to the area. Nori's walking tour was high energy and very well done.

Buy the ticket ONLINE prior to visit...this will save you almost 50% of the price. London tube is expensive if you are only buying daily fares so if you have 2 days or so in London, this is very recommended route if you want to hit more tourist spots. The bus is not always fast moving (we got stuck in one stop for 20min with no explanation), but it will get you where you go and it comes with reasonable frequency. The walking tours are included...and recommend taking advantage.

It’s been over 20 years since we last visited London, and we wanted to see what’s new. Besides, we had always wanted to ride upstairs in a double-decked bus in London.

So we set aside our dislike of touristy tours and recorded audio guides. And we booked a BigBus tour, starting ours at Oxford Circus.. BigBus is the one tour recommended by Michelin.

We took the longer Big Blue tour with commentary available in 12 languages. It’s a hop on, hop off tour, but we stayed on the bus for a complete 3+ hour circuit. The shorter Classic Red tour takes 2+ hours and has a live English guide. The Classic Tour hits all the top London attractions. You'll see the Tower of London, the Houses of Parliament, Buckingham Palace, Trafalgar Square, Westminster Abbey and Downing Street.

Our Big Blue tour added a Kensington loop -- South Kensington, Kensington Gardens, Kensington Palace, Baker Street -- with a dozen more stops. You can change between the two tours at will.

There is also a Green Link you can switch to from the Red and Blue tours at Covent Garden. Use it for railroad connections -- St. Pancras and Euston Stations -- and for the British Museum and several others.

Our bus was modern, clean and comfortable. The driver was courteous and skillful. We were lucky to secure the front seats on the upper deck. A photographer’s delight!

The recorded audio guide consisted of classical music and jazz punctuated by brief, informative comments. It was helpful, not pretentious or distracting. Museum curators take note!

We can imagine less delightful outcomes. We enjoyed a bright, sparkling Spring day. We had front row topside seats. Although the bus was full to capacity at times, the other passengers were courteous and quiet. Our driver was as good as they come.

The tour was so good, we would have repeated it the next day if the weather held.

When you know nothing about a city a tour is always good to get a fell for the place. The bus does go around a lot of places and it is nice to be able to hop on and hop off. The free river cruise is great. The staff are lovely. However, as someone who lives in London, I didn't feel like I learned much.

Consider getting the 48 hour ticket if you are in London for several days. We got ours at 10 am on day one and were able to board buses on day 2, and more importantly, again on day 3 before 10 am. The red route offers a more interesting narrative because it is by a real person not a recording. The only think I did not like was that the bus waited at stops longer than I've experienced on other hop on-hop off buses in other cities.

Tour guide knew their stuff well
We got to see so much of London on the bus that we would not have seen. Saved our feet a little too with all the walking.
Took you to all key sights that you would want to see when visiting London. Cost £29 PP and included river boat usage. You can hop on and off whenever you like - so gives you a chance to look around

We found the Big bus tours are very convenient and cost effective way to tour London city and at the same time flexible enough to suit our plans by hopping off and on at various places of your choice. There are also many combination tickets available to save cost and plan schedule easily; very good experience and excellent service especially the audio commentary by the staff live and recorded ones.

Excellent bus tour, frequent buses and knowledgeable staff. Would recommend to anyone wanting to really get to know London.

Ticket was £38 each for 48 hours and this included a river cruise. This is on the high side for bus tours, however there is so much free stuff to do in London it's worth the price. Also, the Tube is not cheap for two days travel and you spend all of that underground.

We visited London for a few days for my partner's 30th and wanted to see the sights without too much fuss. Our driver was Paul and guide was Nobby and without doubt we had a great time on the red route of the tour. We planned to get off but enjoyed the commentary so much ended up staying on for the full duration of the red route to hear all Nobby had to say.

Swapped across to the blue route to get up to Knightsbridge/Harrods etc. but it was more for ease of transport than anything else - the bus was full of people listening to the recorded commentary and lacked atmosphere.

All in all a bit pricey but we did have use of the buses the next day as well even though we were leaving early in the morning. Should you be there a few days, I'd suggest getting the ticket on your first day giving you hop on hop off freedom with a few laughs along the way given the right guide.

I've used all of the major open top bus tours in London, and Big Bus is definitely my favorite. They've got live guides (which are really far superior to the audio guides on the other bus tours), and cover more area than the others. They also provide walking tours and discounts to some of the major attractions if you buy the tickets from the driver.

We travelled as a family with kids and got our tickets from a very helpful sales representative which suggested we take the 48 hours ticket and some other attraction, the London eye, madam Tussaud, and the rest. We decided to take the London eye and joined the redline from the Marble arch. We passed through the major landmarks of the city and live commentary was provided, but the traffic meant we could not reach London eye on time, so we stayed and dropped in buckingham palace for some pictures, but the bus gave us nice views of the Big Ben and the bridges. For the second day, we joined the blue line and dropped off at the London eye. Didn't try the boat cruise but overall, some improvements can be made.

We rode the red line tour today and it was such a waste of over 100 pounds (4 of us). We sat in traffic most of the tour, road side streets and saw the back of Buckingham Palace and the top of Westminister Abby in the distance. We did see all the bridges, the London eye and some statues, The tour guides on the street were no help at all queuing up to get on the bus. The narrated part of the tour are ear plugs you out into a prerecorded message, not "live". We really felt duped. Save your money and simply take a taxi to the attractions you want to see.

I have been to London twice and each time we used Big Bus Tours. It is the best way to see the city and enjoy the London sunshine. I have been on the love commentary bus and the headphone bus. Both are great, but I prefer the live commentary. The person often tells secrets or has better knowledge of the city.
I would highly recommend the bus tour to all my traveling friends.
we enjoy bus tour and river cruise , my niece hadnt been to london before so it was a good way to get to sights and get some interesting facts

the hop on bus gives you the opportunity to see london, if gives you 24hrs but finishes at 5.30 at night. this still gives you enough time to see alot.you can get 20% discount with some maps. you get earphones on the bus or a some guys talking through the tour

We did this our first day in London and found it was a great way to start the trip. We got to see all the major sights and then decide where to spend more time from there. We did the entire route and did a lot of hopping off and on at some amazing spots. Found the guides full of funny and interesting information.

Bus stops were difficult to identify and we walked around the city for hours. The saving grace was at stop #1 where we got the best tour and history of London by Big Steve. His knowledge of the city and his enthusiasm and pride for his job and what he does day in and day out are it often found. I give him 5 🌟 for our tour with him on the Big Bus in London.
I enjoyed the three tours that the Big Bus gave me. I really enjoyed the one with the guide on board. He gave a good and funny tour.

Im a londoner and have a week off with my BF. We decided instead of going abroad this week we would do all things London and so we booked the Big Bus tour. ive done a bus tour before a couple of years ago but couldn't remember who with. booked this after looking at reviews.
we couldn't have been more pleased!
it was informative and lots of fun facts learnt by all!
(we often do pub quizzes and are looking forward to getting questions about the things we've learnt)
Our guide was Ken who was great and funny, driver Pitch, also great. Was very pleased with the whole day!
we only did red route ( which is English speaking only) took us about 2 1/2 hours- (we didn't get off at all ) but there were plenty of great places to get off. Ken was good at recommending what was worth seeing and since I know most of London I agreed with the places he recommended!

This tour was a lot better than most, in Germany i was so disappointed because all I got was a audio tour however big bus in London turned that all around they had a cheap rate for 48 hours which included a boat tour and on the bus they had a live english speaking tour guide it is an out standing hop on hop off tour and i would highly recommend it

Fab, had a great time with big bus, big pat on the back for all staff everyone was helpful and made the experience a good one. Live guides were amusing and very informative, definitely learnt more about London than on previous trips. Also thank you to the river cruise commentary , keep the live commentary on board, everyone loves them.

Plenty of hop-on, hop-off opportunites! Take advantage of the included river cruise and walking tours if you have time. The guides are a wealth of knowledge and although I had been to London previously, I learned so much during our day on the Big Bus!!

We have booked online for 48 hours city tour of the city of London. Big bus took us to almost most the places we want to visit in London. the only thing we didn't like is some time takes much time to visit a place which could waste of your time.

I visited London with my friend, and we didn't know where to start. Her family recommended the "Big Bus Tours" and we bought a 2 day pass (it was just a few pounds more) and well worth it. There's a rotation of buses that stop at a lot of popular main spots and you're welcome to get off and walk around at a stop, and hop back on the bus later on to go to your next destination. I definitely recommend this!

So this is basically just a shoutout to our guide on the red line Nick. He was absolutely the most awesome person we met in London - funny, informative, and very kind to all the passengers. My 19 year old daughter and her friend fell completely in love with him (seriously I don't think I've ever seen them so attentive!)... and I think I did a bit too!

His touring was brilliant. At one point we got stuck in traffic and to pass the time he made us all sit in a circle and tell jokes! And then the next evening we saw him out and about in soho and he came and had a drink with us (his girlfriend is beautiful... my girls were heartboken). All in all he's lucky we didn't kidnap him and take him home with us. Thanks Nick, and everyone check out Big Bus!

For your first time in London, we would suggest this type of tour as it gives you a great overview of the city with narration. Plan so you can take advantage of both days of your ticket. This means starting early in the day so you can make the most of each day. Check the weather so it is enjoyable to sit on top and be sure to dress appropriately so you can enjoy without freezing. The bus generates a breeze and so be prepared and you will enjoy it much more. Hop on and hop off when you want. Be sure to be aware of the schedule so you know how late they run. If you use both days effectively, this is a great way to see London. During the week in March crowds were not a major issue however on weekends it will be busy. I can not stress how it is important to plan and start early to make the most of this. Best deal in town and worth it especially for first time London visitors. You can sit inside but the open top area is better for pictures and seeing everything. The boat ride is included so plan on that too.

My family and I really enjoyed this tour. Its a good way to see London and our guide was really nice and very knowledgable. A great way to sightsee with young children. We went to Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, Westminster Abbey and the London Eye and our guide was very informative she really knew her stuff, unfortunately i have forgotten her name, sorry. The river cruise part was a bit of a let down but other than that it was good.

This is THE KEY to a short trip in London. A ticket allows you to get on and off all Big Buses wherever you like over a 24 hour period. The Big Bus tours go to all attractions in the city (37 stops), and a ticket gets you 24hours of service. Best to buy mid-day for that reason. You can use it for sightseeing in itself (ride up top in the open for great views), or as transportation to any attraction. This is the best way to pack in a lot of London for your $$. Ticket also includes a narrated cruise down the River Thames from the Eye to the Tower Bridge. A great op for one-of-a-kind photos in the middle of the river with the bridge behind you. Also ends at the Tower Bridge/Tower of London for further sightseeing.

Having been on bus tours of many cities I thought The Big Bus was good value and well organised. We used it Sat and Sunday and no queues unlike some cities.
We also did the free boat cruise which again was very enjoyable. Great to get the second day free at this time of the year

Took the two day on off tour with Big Bus Red and there was no comparison between John and Dave. John was informative, entertaining and thoughtful whereas Dave gave the briefest of information. I did the entire tour on the second day again as I learned so much more with John. If you get Dave, you're best off taking the Blue Bus and hearing the canned tour -- still WAY better than Dave.

We got our tickets for the Bus through our Hotel but we were very impressed with the knowledge of the commentator as he described everything while we were driving through London. Plus we got to ride the boat from Big Ben to Westminster!!

In non-peak seasons they offer 48 hours for the regular 24 hour price. Very easy to get around the city and see a lot quickly.

Can get on and off and audio tour runs with the bus location.

It does only go one direction, so there is not a lot of flexibility - you won't want to rely on this for transportation.

Pass includes Thames tour, which I would not pay for otherwise, but was a nice perk and a different view of the heart of London.

The great thing about the Big Bus Tour is that it includes your transportation and tour guide. It has guides in all languages and even a live English guide on the red line. The tube & bus system can be a bit confusing for those who have never been to London so the Big Bus Tour makes getting around London much more user friendly. The guides all bring something different, so sometimes it helps to take the ride twice with two different guides. Also, buses and cabs are cash only. SOME cabs accept credit cards but only for longer routes, so if you want to take a cab have cash (in pounds) ready to go. Beautiful country.

Helpful staff, great tour took in all the attractions stops well located and hop on hop off. Well worth the money The weather helped as sat upstairs in the open air and got brilliant views of the iconic sights of London

Be sure to do a bus tour. You get to see so much of London and all the pretty sights. There's far too much to cover on foot. You can hop on and off the buses as and when you like to stop and sight see.

After leaving green park station the first londoner we spoke to was Dave. He basically organised our 48hr trip for us! Tickets for 48hrs on the many buses they run, tickets for the dungeons and london tower...all sorted there and then! we hadnt yet checked into our hotel...Dave pointed us in the right direction for that as well! After check in we hopped on a bus where "big phil" was our guide...his knowledge of the countless gorgeous buildings and landmarks was unrivalled! We had a few different guides as we got on and of the buses at the different stops and all of them were charismatic, funny and helpful. This was my first trip sightseeing in London as an adult, thanks to the big bus co, it was fantastic...many thanks guys!

It was pouring down rain so we hopped onto the bus. We stayed on for over two hours. The guided tour was very informative and funny. The supervisor at stop 13/22 was very helpful. She got us sorted on the right bus, gave helpful hints and told us about the river cruise included in the ticket price. Great way to see London.

London has some terrible drivers, but Big Bus Tours must have some of the worst. If you want a true representation of London driving, use Big Bus Tours. Just don't expect a response should you complain if one of your drivers runs other road users off the road.

We live in London and have never done one of these hop on hop off tours before but we were very pleased recently when my sister visited us from Scotland. We started next to Baker Street station where a Polish girl ( we think Polish) sold us a ticket. She gave us plenty of information and told us there are to lines. The Blue which we got on with audio and red which had a guide. We changed at Hamley toy store, a must if you have kids and waited 10 minutes for another bus this time with a guide. Sorry I cannot remember his name but he was fantastic and we enjoyed his tour and I have to say as local, learnt a lot. You can hop off and on at many stops and it literally goes anywhere you want. I will not hesitate to use the buses again. There is also a Thames cruise included in the price but we did not do this.

I booked online prior to going to London and saved quite a lot. I paid £50 for 2 adults and 2 children. This included bus tours, walking tours, discounted tickets and a Thames cruise. Oh and because it's winter it was valid for 48 hours instead of 12.

I asked how much it would of been if I purchased from London and it would of been £25 each adult and £18 each child!!
These tours offer an economical way of traveling around London whilst getting a commentary of exciting facts. You can hop on at buckingham palace and hop off at Tower of London then head down to the Thames and have a cruise up the Thames.

The bus covers all major attractions ie Coventry garden, Houses of Parliament.

The only downfall I can find is that the buses don't seem to come as regular as others!

I feel it was worth it for me to pay £50 as we spent all our day baring 2 hours hoping on and off the bus at attractions.I also saved around £25 by buying tickets off the agents to the London dungeons. But I don't think it would of been worth £86...

We took a big bus tour with the idea that would give our kids a good lay of the land and an idea of the options for more detailed visits. We ended up getting off after an hour, took the very good associated river boat trip and didn't get back on. So we didn't get value for the hefty 70 pound price. The taped commentary and elevator music was pretty average

If you're looking for an efficient (and informative!) way to get around London, this is a great way to do it. We loved the hop-on, hop-off approach, as it was so convenient for dropping into different places of interest. If you have a finite amount of time and you know exactly where you want to go, however, this would not be a good choice for you. The drivers were very friendly and helpful, even giving advice and directions to travelers. Our guide, Samantha, was funny and informative and made the tour a pleasure. All in all, if you plan on seeing many sites around London and would like to learn a bit more about the city as you get around, this is one of the easiest (though not fastest) ways to do it. Our only criticism is that during hours of high traffic, progress is very slow. If you are on the bus in hot summer weather (as we were), it got uncomfortable at those times, when there was no wind from the drive to stay cool, and the sun just beat down on us all as we were at a standstill. This is a minor point, and no fault of the tour company to be sure.

The full tour can last ~4 hours where you get to see all of London and the in bus commentary through headphones is very informative. The staff was very friendly and helpful. It is also very easy to get on and off the bus to see the stops you're most interested in. The buses come every 20 minutes. This bus tour was on the the highlights of my trip. I highly recommend.
