Buy the 48 hr bus tour so that you can use the bus to get around the city the next day - its well worth the extra cost.

Definitely recommend this hop on hop off bus, we wanted to cram as much as possible into out 2 days. We did the whole of the red route and most of the blue route too. It enabled us to decide what we wanted to see and when. Buses are clean, commentators very knowledgeable, you also get riverboat cruise imcluded in the price of the ticket. £30 for 2 days includes earphones, map and poncho (if you need it) really good value and regular services. We will definitely do this again when we have the children with us.

Bought tickets for this bus tour while in London recently. Bus comes every 15/20minutes which means no standing around for ages waiting. We went on the Blue route which is the bigger route and covers all the big attractions in London plus outer areas like Kensington and Belgravia. We also had a free river cruise included in the price of the ticket and could use the tickets over 2 days which meant we were able to break up our trip with some sightseeing and shopping each day. Would recommend this bus tour however wrap up well if going in winter!

Affordable-you can use the tickets all day, anywhere within the route. Stops at most of all attractions in London. Staffs are friendly, and you are entitled to free tour to few famous attractions. I love my Harry Potter Tour with Mr Russell! He's fun and helpful! (Your open-top bus tour takes you to all of London’s famous landmarks and reveals London’s colourful 2,000-year history. The tour offers you a choice of a recorded commentary or a live commentary delivered by entertaining guides.

The hop-on, hop-off facility will enable you to get on and off the bus at many places of interest. Choose from the 24 or 48 hour ticket to see the city and its sights at your own pace.

Your sightseeing tour of London also includes a free cruise on the River Thames and 3 guided walking tours for you to enjoy; plus Big Bus Reward Vouchers that offer a range of discounts at attractions, shops and restaurants.

The Big Bus sightseeing tour is a safe and relaxed way to experience this great city and it is the perfect introduction to London and a fun day out for all.)

This is a great way to get around London. The passenger is able to hop on and hop off at different sites. There is live or recorded tourist information. They supply a rain poncho with hood...necessary for London's rain.

This tour was a wonderful way to see the big tourist spots in London! They give you the chance to get off and see the sights if you wish or just sit and enjoy the ride. Our tour guide big Steve was incredible! He had heaps of knowledge about the city and answered all our questions, he went well beyond our expectations and went the extra mile! I would recommend to everyone doing this tour to get on his bus!!

We booked a two day tour for sight seeing on our first trip to London. This seemed by far the best way to fit all the sights in at once and proved accurate. You will have plenty of time to see and take photos of all the views and it is best for managing your time rather than hopping the tube or walking to each place. We found that the first trip around the city it was great to ride the full length of the tour and not hop off until we had heard about each stop, especially if you have a fun and entertaining guide. Since we had two days we then took advantage of using the bus as our transportation around the city and being able to "hop on hop off" at various sites later the first day and throughout the second day. Definitely great perks to purchasing the two day pass and would recommend this to first timers in London!

We also purchased the Tower of London tickets from the same vendor and saved time once we toured the Tower later. You do not have to tour this the same day which was handy but managed to get a discount if we purchased our tickets then. You can also get other tickets for other events on request.

Used the company for a 2 day trip around the sites of London which included a river cruise. Friendly staff red tour gives you a live commentary which depends on the style of the guide and the blue route a recording in several languages. Hop on and off where you like the only problem is it finishes at 4.30 so you may have to make other travel arrangements such as tube if you want to continue to explore after that time.

The big bus tour was one of the best days out we had in our stay in London. It was defiantly worth the money as you get knowledgeable staff and tour guides, buses come very frequently so you have more than enough time to get off at each attraction and look around then get back on when you feel ready. I would certainly recommend this to anyone of any age as it was an excellent experience

I used to work for the big bus company and recommended this company when my family came to visit. After not being a guide for many years I figured that the newer guide would be better then me. Unfortunately I got the "shopping" guide who spent most of the tour describing which shops were around. Skipping more important landmarks like tyburn and regent street history for showing unimportant shops. Got off at Fleet Street for lunch and hoping the next red tour guide will be better.

This was a tour I hadn't planned on but because of my limited time I decided to try it to see the sights. I was on the blue line and it was worth every pound I paid. We hit many London highlights and I had the option of getting off or on at numerous stops. I saw so much of London that I wouldn't have seen otherwise, I highly recommend it. The bus even had a basket of disposable ponchos in case the weather turned bad. Good value.

This is the 2nd time my husband & I visited London to celebrate our 25th wedding anniversary.
We did not see much of London 2 years ago & decided to book this Big Bus Tour. It was a decision well made. The tour is valid for 48 hours from the time the tickets are being issued.
We booked our tickets at King Cross Station & boarded the bus just outside the station (green line) We ride on the upper deck; sat at the shelter area & below the bus throughout our journey on separate occasions. We had different feel & different views. Everyone should try this to experience everything. We experienced coldness on the upper deck in December; but great to take photos especially when the bus drove passed the Tower Bridge. We sat in the shelter, at the front row and had a great view if the streets & sights. We sat below the bus when the weather turned too cold.
We went for the free Harry Potter walking tour with our interesting & very enthusiastic guide, Kevin Russel. He brings Harry Potter movie into a very lively journey even for mature tourists like us. The walking tour lasted approx 2-1/2 hours, with an interesting stop to get some cool candies-which we like very much. There are also quiz to test how much we know about the movie, but in a very interesting and fun way. All of us are very captivated by Kevin's way of presenting Harry Potter scenes to us-where some of the scenes were set or filmed.
We bought our tickets for Madam Tussauds Wax Museum & one of the ticket guy at the stop recommended a fantastic fish & chips restaurant to us--we had a real good meal there with nice ambience & great service (inexpensive too)
The guide who gave live commentary onboard the bus is very lively & introduced us to visit the changing of the horse guards which many people do not know & so it was not crowded at all! we had lots of nice photos there with the Guards on the horse!
The next day we hop into the bus again without any problem & went sight-seeing to other spots that we missed-also to board the River cruise that is included!

Great value in winter when you can use two days for the price of one. Unfortunately we could only use for one day, so we didnt get full value.

Also lets you link to a boat tour on Thames on same ticket, which is also adding value. We used the boat tour portion from London Bridge to London Eye, and it worked out well.

We used hop on hop off a couple of times on tour, which also worked out fine.

We spent a full day on the bus, from 10 am to closing at 5 pm, and were very happy with the tour we got of London. Different commentators on different buses had different styles, but that added to the experience by getting variety.

Reading some of the negative reviews, the general answer to all the complaints is you have to pay attention to what is happening in your surroundings, to understand where you are at and where you are going, and this us tour will work out fine. If you expect an individual experience like you get in a taxi, then you can book taxi's for the entire day to go from hither to yon and pay 300 pounds and not get half the commentary on history

I purchased the pass from my hotel and the bus picked me up right outside. I rode the whole route the first day so I could experience the live commentary to find out where I wanted to attend. My suggestion is to make sure you get on the bus with the live commentary because they tell you more information than the recorded one. The free river tour is great also as you get to see London from a different viewpoint. I rode it all the way down to Greenwich and back. I liked the top of the bus when the weather was good. The drivers, guides and bus stop people were all great and very friendly. They were also great about answering questions and giving directions to get the most out of the two days.

Having never been to London we wanted to take a bus tour to get a quick look at a lot in the city and places we were going to see over the next few days. Our hotel concierge recommended Big Bus tours. We took the red line with live commentary, our guide was informative and funny. The buses come frequently and there was always a seat. I personally think that this was a perfect first activity for us.

We highly enjoyed our Big Bus London experience and recommend it. The service is incredibly convenient, with loads of stops and short wait times between buses. The staff is friendly and the tour guides provide a steady stream of interesting and funny facts about the city, it's sites, and history.

We were visiting London with 2 small children and decided to do the "big bus tour". There were convenient stops all over the city near major attractions and sights.

There are 2 lines- the blue with pre recorded audio available in multiple languages -and the red with a live guide.

We found the blue bus experience to be mostly classical music with very little about the neighborhoods or interesting sites around us.

We opted to get on the red line, which had live guides. One was good the other was horrible.

The young lady we had was really interesting and provided a lot of fun and memorable color about the city, it's history and what we saw - or may not have noticed - had we been on our own. Sadly we only spent 20 minutes with her before hopping off the bus at one of the stops.

The second guide we got was incredibly dry. And though he touted several times he "was the most experienced tour guide in the UK, if not all of EUR, with more than 10,000 tours" we found him uninsightful, dry, and, at times, grating.

He was more interested in talking about staying seated, people injured on the big bus tour as a result of not staying seated (something I would think the tour company would not want to lead with), car accidents in London, hospital patients on Harley street, and a recent bike ride he had taken with someone who was Biking around the world, etc. (You may note very little of the afore mentioned is actually about London). We would have loved to learn and hear about insights of the city and it's amazing sights.

If you are looking at choosing the Big Bus tour, it is a good way to get in the sights around the city if you are time constrained. That said, it is worth noting that in our experience it was more of a "big bus" than an informative "tour", as the company's name would imply.

Also, if by chance management happens to read this review, riding along as a tourist with your live operators might be a good way to ensure consistency and quality across your tour guides.

The Big Bus Tour is a very nice way to tour London. There are two lines, the Red and the blue. The red line has live commentary. We had Pitch as a bus driver and Chris gave us the live tour.

Chris was funny and knowledgeable about London as well as the sites. The tour takes a long time. We were on the bus quite awhile and used it to go to the Tower of London.

I recommend that you get on the bus early, take the red bus. The buses stop running a lot earlier than they advertise. I believe the last red and blue bus is around five pm. However, they do have a purple line that will return you to your hotel.

In addition, the ticket to the big bus also gives you a free ride on a boat that will take you to westminster abbey and other stops. We did not utilize the boat as it was freezing, but it's an option.

I recommend this bus but plan to only do two or three things tops per day. We got on the bus on one side of London at about 1pm. Arrived at the Tower of London at 2pm. Participated in the tour at the Tower of London. Got back on the bus at 4pm and only had time to return back to our hotel. This is why you must get on the bus early.

Also, do not buy the bus ticket at your hotel. Buy it from the bus driver. It should cost around 22 pound per day. We paid 30 a person. The hotel up charged.

We bought our tickets for the Big Bus at our hotel, and they charged us more than had we bought them on the bus, so I would definitely buy them from the bus driver. And while you are at it he will offer to sell you tickets to a couple other sight seeing options - so have your credit card ready!
We started our tour by waiting half an hour for a bus - not a good beginning! And that is what earned this tour a low score - lots of lines and waiting around. If you are unable to walk a lot I guess this would be a good way to see the major sights but you really don't get close enough to any of them and end up walking a bit anyway. I liked the ride down the Thames - however we waited over a half an hour for a boat for that part of the tour too. All in all, I would just put on my walking shoes and learn to take the tube - its super easy and a fun way to get around.

My 85 year old Mum and I recently spent a few days in London. Mum was visiting with me from Holland and so desperately wanted to go to Harrods. Being 85 she does not walk to fast or for very long periods. I found the Big Bus hop on hop off tours an excellent way to see the sites with Mum. I also took advantage of the 30 pound per person deal which gave us 48 hours travel on the bus. This was perfect for us.

Had I been on my own I would have enjoyed hopping off a lot more and seeing various sites. The bus does not have a commentator but you can listen through the headphones to see what is happening around you..

The staff were wonderful on the bus and thanks guys. They have several different links you can follow and a great map which shows different areas you may be able to get on and off. They also throw in a free river cruise down the Thames and a walk. We did not do these. Also it may take some time to do the whole circuit because of London traffic. So make sure you start early in the day.

Pretty easy to follow really.

This is the third time we have visited London but the first time we have used The Big Bus Company. Running regularly and on time and driver and commentator very helpful on each bus. Good value for money esp Oct-March when you get 48 hrs travel for the price of 24 hrs. A free river cruise is also included. Now with the addition of the "green" route you can travel all the way from Euston and the other main train stations into the city, saving £'s on taxi fares.

This is a fantastic bus tour of hop on and hop off in an open top bus with great guides giving good and factual infomation on all of london as you travel along. The children were entertained by being able to listen to the highlights as the tour went on. saw more of London than we did with a private guide we had hired and he was fantastic however he was caught in traffic a lot where the bus was much faster to get around.

I thought the price was a bit steep, but i suppose it does take you round London, there are two routes blue and red, we opted for the red as it was already 2pm and it was shorter, as it was october you get 48 hour ticket but we were only in London for the day.
The bus is part covered on the top level which is pretty good help guard against the winds, the tour guide was knowledgeable but when he was speaking on the microphone it was hard to understand could hear him better with no microphone!
would of like to have seen more but time was not on our side.

One of the strange things about this tour is that it's advantage is also its disadvantage. Your ticket enables one to hop on and hop off at a number of stops around the capital. The problem is that the 'hop' term is misleading as at each stop in the hotel areas of. Kensington and Paddington there is quite a delay whilst passengers board the bus.

The tour is highly recommended, but is, like most other attractions in London quite expensive at £30 per person and no concessions.

There are great attractions as part of the ticket - including a river cruise and optional walking tickets within your price.

We loved the big bus tour . At first we thought £30 each was a lot but well worth it, we got 24 hours plus 24 hours free and a boat tour. You can hop on and off at all the sights. There is a running commentary with free earphones, and if it's rainy a free waterproof which is great fun in itself trying to get it on,!!! I would definitely use this company again.

2nd time in London, and if it wasn't for the big bus tour I wouldn't of been able to find my way around! It really is worth the money! Me and my fiancé went on the tour and jumped off and on the bus when we felt like it! Everyone who doesn't really know London or the history should go on the big bus tour! The staff and drivers are all nice and always ready to help you with absolutely everything!
We found the big bus tour very helpful for getting on and getting off as we wanted. The sound made it difficult to hear and everything is so crowded....it was just hard.

When we hopped on he bus it was raining, so we decided to do the first circle and just stay on the bus and see everything from the bus. Once it let off a bit, we joined the "Harry Potter Walking Tour". Ian, our guide, was very knowledgeable and entertained a very mixed group. This tour is a very good value for the money, I just wish we had had more time to do the river cruise and stop at different locations.

This trip into London was from Paris via Eurostar. The 2 hour train trip was unique and allowed my family (4) to quickly decide where we wanted to spend our limited time. This "BigBus Tour" is the perfect means to do the complete city ride tour then spend the next day actually visiting your interest. We arrived early in the AM and left in the early evening and wished we could have spent several days visiting this wonderful city. The "Hop On, Hop Off" is very convenient for rest stops, eating and shopping. The agents at the stops were very helpful and the commentary on each bus was excellent. We will do this again! Al, Kathy, Ashley & Johnathan.

Purchased 2 adult tickets that cost £25 pounds each with our daughter traveling free, in the price of our tickets it covered a 48 hour period that you can use any time hopping on and off the bus when you like, also it included a free river trip. We traveled on the Red route that had an English speaking tour guide, he was friendly and knowledgable, we passed all the main tourist attractions. The bus was clean and comfortable. The following day we traveled on the Blue route that uses headphones and an audio described tour, the headphones are free and new to all passengers that you keep after the journey, we used the tour to get around London. The free river cruse was in a large new boat, it lasted about an hour, it covered a good section of the river and the staff were friendly and professional. the boat had covered and open seats to view the river, toilets and a small bar and snack bar. Worth a visit and we recommend using the Big Bus tour company for 2 days travel and a river cruse it's worth the money.

We booked our tickets online in advance which gives you a discount. Travelling in October meant we got 2 days for the price of 1, and the river cruise is included, so you can get your money's worth if you choose to. The river cruise was by far the best part - the crew member giving the commentary was excellent and it was very informative and relaxing. However on the buses it is a taped commentary, not always timed perfectly with the sights, and with annoying music in between. The tour takes a very long time due to the amount of traffic on the London roads and the number of traffic lights we had to stop at. This meant the pace was very slow and children become bored. On our second day there were two diversions (due to a demonstration I think) which we were not told about in advance and which meant we saw nothing for ages. We eventually gave up, got off the bus and visited the sights we wanted to see by Tube. Disappointing compared to other tours we've taken in other cities.

I chose to take the big bus tour because I stopped over in London for 12 hours and it proved to be the great experience. The service was efficient. the bus took us to the all the attractions in the city. I couldn't visit all the sites but went for the main ones. Good value for the day tour.

We spoke with a gentleman at the Marble Arch station about the tour. He was very nice and knowledgeable and we decided to take the tour. It was a cool day, and it was great until we got off at the Tower of London. we spent three hours at the Tower and we went to get on the bus again, we saw one about 15 feet from the stop and he would was stopped at the curb and refused to let us on. We then went to the stop, with a group of U.S. tourists who were in London for the NFL game. We were told that due to traffic we had to walk across the bridge and catch the bus there. We walked across Tower Bridge and waited. The next bus came and would not pick us up. We had to walk across the bridge again and they had us wait in another spot. Our American friends got and and just took a cab. There were traffic issues so the bus had to double back and we ended up seeing the same things that we saw on the way there. The bus was great and the view from up top was fabulous. Our guides were very witty and made it entertaining. It was nice, but better organizing and taking care of the customer would have been better. Overall, THE way to see London.

The hop on/hop off bus is a great way to see a city. We rode the red bus and the blue bus and in both cases the route took significantly longer than advertised. Partly due to traffic (which is out of the bus' control) and partly to stops to change drivers and buses (annoying since we lost our great seats). We had a good guide at first but when the bus took its break (and made us move to another bus) the guide was lousy. Also, you don't get two full days - you get 24 hours. We took the bus on a Sunday as we'd been told there was less traffic (not correct). When we hopped off, we couldn't always hop back on as the bus was full. We would take the tour again but would plan 4 hours without stops versus the ~2 hours stated in the brochure.

I had only one day to spend in London, and with big bus tours I have actually visited most of the attractions in a single day! You don't have to spend time on transportation between the sights. The river cruise was nice but not the best. I had to wait for the cruise about 45 minutes and it was a bit crowded. Would recommend the big bus tour to all first time visitors to London.

I travelled on the big tour bus for two days in london and i wish to make a number of points. The live guide on our bus was extremely poor. He hsd no interest in his passengers or any of the sights. He only identified places of interest but gave no background or info. The sound quality upstairs is shocking. There are plenty of opportunities to hop on hop off but overall its far too costly for the service provided.

Spent most of the day on the bus - done a full circle first on red line then got off to do river cruise. Well worth it. Nick our guide was fantastic he kept the commentary funny & interesting I was disappointed when he left our bus but when we 'hopped on' again later on there he was again. This is the best way to see London without the fast paced way everyone rushes about. Great views of the city. From the moment we walked out of Victoria Station and met the Big Bus Tour Guide standing right outside. All the staff at the stops were friendly. I priced all the London bus tour companies and this was by far the cheapest but with no compromise on service.

This was not our first time using the Big Bus; however, it will be the last time! The driver at Gloucester Road was impertient to the point of anger when asked a question. He was clearly not happy with his job and extended this to the passengers. The tour representative who stood outside of Harrods refused to talk to my husband when he tried to ask a question and walked away from him. One driver went right past the stop at the Tower and then lied about stopping and opening the doors at the stop. The drivers were impertient, rude, or outright liars . Never again will we tell ours about this abysmal tour company.

As someone who was born and brought up in London, I thought I knew the place well, but returning as a 'tourist' after many years away I decided to take a Bus Tour having experienced them in many other other cities and finding them a useful introduction. I chose Big Bus Tours as it seemed to offer the best choice, price, frequency etc combination, including the free Thames cruise thrown in for good measure. I wasn't disappointed, we started the day at Victoria and exchanged our online booking for a real ticket with no difficulty, very helpful and friendly staff on the streetside. We were planning to hop on and off throughout the day, but in the end we opted to do the complete tour in one go and then use the buses as a means to go back to various spots as we pleased. This gave us the best of both worlds, we saw everything, didn't have to fight for an upstairs seat everytime which is a bonus as the buses do get very busy, and we heard the excellent commentaries of two guides as one changed shortly after we joined. They knew their stuff, were friendly, informative, funny and coped well with the endless coming and going of passengers.

We also took the river cruise, which was fun, but not as well organised. The tannoy system didn't work properly, the staff were not very interested and the boat dumped us off at the Tower of London where we would have had to wait for an hour for the return trip - we didn't wait!

But overall a good experience and one I would recommend to anyone.

I wish I would have read other reviews before hopping on this poor excuse for a tour. The audio information was sparse, and the bus drivers didn't know the answers to my questions about certain stops. One of the bus drivers literally screamed at other drivers. I had to wait 30 minutes for buses. Worst of all, a guide never showed up for a "free walking tour." Seven of us were left stranded at a stop at the end of the day. After waiting 40 minutes, I walked 2 miles alone in the dark back to my hotel. Purchase a guide book and a day pass for the tube which is a faster, cheaper, easier way to the city.

Bus tours are generally a great way to see all the main attractions of a city, especially one the size of London. Big Bus Tours sounds good with it's "hop on, hop off" slogan, but what they don't tell you is that they leave you stranded on the far reaches of the city at 6:00 p.m. If they would simply explain the most effective way to use the bus up front they would avoid irate customers at the end of the day. The tickets are expensive (30 pounds each) as are taxis and metro tickets, if you happen to find yourself far from your hotel at the end of a long day, as we did. Several people on the bus where completely perplexed when the driver stopped and told everyone to get off. Is this any way to run a bus tour? Absolutely not.

I recently booked the big bus hop on hop off bus your while enjoying a quick stop off in London. I came in from Kings Cross station and this tour company had a branch line which picks up right outside. The company we booked from also said that this company would have a greater frequency of pickups although there were a few times where I think we waited longer than original advised. I think we were told that busses are every 20 minutes however at stops with both the red and blue lines (most of them), you are only likely to wait 10 minutes between busses.

The tour has two lines - a red line and a blue line. I think the blue has an additional extended line out towards Kensington palace and the red line had a live guide versus a recording which is much more entertaining and usually provided a better commentary. The entire loop takes quite awhile - 4 hours and we were never able to complete the entire loop in the day we had in London.

One of the best selling points of this tour was the fact that you could get off at the Tower of London stop and jump on the City cruises boat tour for free down to the Parliament and Westminster Abbey. This was one of the top highlights of our entire trip to London.

We booked the 48hrs on Big Bus Tours. It is convenient going around London with many stops to hop on & off. We also took the cruise & went for the Changing of the Guards walk which was very fun. We went round in the Big Bus on our last day while it was raining outside, it rescued us from the rain!

The Big Bus Tour provided a wonderful overview of London but it was the walking tour with Phil that was the highlight of the day!! We got to see the Changing of the Guard up close and personal and take some really spectacular photos without waiting in line everywhere. The tour was fast paced and fun!!

Alas the weather was against us and the wind and rain did not help but this tour was so educational. With so many sights to see this is a necessity for anyone with mobility problems. You can hop on and off the bus along the route so you can see individual places.

At £30 for a 24 hr bus pass it may not appear the cheapest way to see London. However we only had two days and the Big Bus allowed us to hop on and off all the sights we wanted to see. The commentary on the bus was great and informative.

Took my Norwegian student on the tour myself having lived in London for 10 years. I can honestly say it was a disaster from start to finish. The cost was not set and they bargained for our trade over the 'Original Bus Tour'. I should have heard warning bells. We jumped on in Victoria and within 10 minutes in Green Park the bus stopped for 20 minutes as it was the end of one tour and start of another. The new commentator repeated everything we had just heard and then the tour was detoured due to traffic so we missed two stops. We left at Oxford Street and jumped back on at 4pm, the tour was recorded info at peak time on a Saturday.It stopped for approx 10 minutes at each stop. The information was sporadic and mainly just music to fill in time. At stop 17 we stopped for another 20 minutes and I asked the driver if we would make the last river cruise (included in the price). He became agressive and started verbally abusing us for 'hassling'him. He then announced over the tannoy that he would leave when he was 'good and ready and not before'.
Horrific behaviour and what a terrible way for a tourist from outside the UK to view our country, our capital and our people.

Our Big Bus Tour today was excellent, mainly due to our guide, Andrew Grey, who obviously has a passion for London. He not only had all the facts, figures & interesting stories of the landmarks on the route, but proved he knew his subject by being able to answer questions relating to other areas and buildings with great depth.
If you are considering a tour you will be in for a treat if you get the same guide as us.
Thanks Andrew (tell your boss you deserve a raise!)

Used the big bus tours on the blue route in London today. Started off well, the "ground" staff were very helpful, buses very frequent and all going well. On the way back to our hotel they left us stranded for 45 minutes at Hyde Park corner while they sorted out a bus going West. My advice is to watch the time so that you are not going home on the last bus!!

We had an excellent experience with Big Bus Tours. We purchased the tour from our hotel concierge. Buses seemed to be plentiful, so we never had difficulty getting on another bus once we made a stop. We also took the Thames River cruise that was included. I would highly recommend this HOHO tour for those visiting London.
I really enjoyed this bus tour. With a city as crowded as London and so many sites to see, this is the only way to go! You can get on and off when you want to.
Big Bus Tours shows you pretty much all of London. The tour is wonderful and you can get on and off when you like. The only downside is traffic stinks in London, so it's a little slow at times.

I bought the ticket on the day. Luckily I was able get the ticket with some discount (the bus conductor said that it's discounted. i'm not sure it's just a ticket selling tactic). cost per person was around £20 (adult).

This is a 40 to 45 minutes trip. You can hop on and off at places that you would like to spend some more time. I remember that the last trip is at around 6 or 7pm.

Some commentators are easy to understand what they are saying but some are difficult to understand. If you experience any trouble then it might be better to hop off that bus and take another with the hope that you probably get someone whose English you can understand.

For other languages you can use a headphone, I think. I did not use this facility but I remember the commentator mentioned this.

This was my fifth trip to London and second time using the hop on hop off tour. I have always traveled around London using the underground, it will get you places a lot faster, but you really don't see the city. Last year I bought the Original Bus Company tickets and waiting at a bus stop 20 minutes or more. In their defense it was during the Olympics. This year my hotel recommended the Big Bus Tours and told me they have increased the amount of buses they have. I was very happy with their service, and they even extended the tickets for an extra 24 hours due to a Bike Marathon. We were concerned with delays because of street closures, but we were assured by their reps near Hyde Park that there would be plenty of buses running during the bike race. We were not disappointed, there were buses everywhere and we just enjoyed sitting on the bus and seeing the city and getting a different perspective of the city. If you are in a hurry to get somewhere I would suggest you take the underground. We wanted to get to Kensington Palace and Westminster before closing and did not make either one because the route did a loop around Hyde Park and took longer then we thought with traffic. It was nice to take the river cruise which is included. Seeing the sites of Tower Bridge and Big Ben at night by boat or on the upper deck of the bus is very relaxing and enjoyable. Did not realize what I was missing taking the underground. I did this tour for my sister who was visiting for the first time, and would recommend it to anyone who is visiting London for the first time and wants to see the city.

Don't think you can go wrong with a hop on bus in London. Sure it's cheaper to go by tube but the excitement of the top deck cannot be beat. Couple of tips.
I was going to book online but ended up getting cheaper tickets at the stop. There were a few companies looking for business so good deals were to be had.
During the day I didn't have any problems gettings seats, the busses were full but not jam packed and they were very frequent. However by end of the day I noticed they were less frequent and were getting stuck in traffic and there'd sometimes be 2 busses behind each other. As you can imagine this means that one bus is either early or late so at the end of the day I waited over 40 mins and no bus showed. I was in a hurry to get somewhere by 7 so I ended up getting the tube. That was the only downside but everything was great ip until then.

My friend and I did the Big Bus Tours on our recent visit to London. While it did provide a lot of coverage we had constant issues with our earphones including scratchiness and the sound going in and out. I recommend going on the line with a live person talking in English. It was nice to do a free boat cruise though!

Good value for money, a wide-ranging tour that takes in a lot of the sights in Central London, and connects well with main line rail stations and other transport links (Euston, King;s Cross, Waterloo, etc).

Tickets valid for 24 hours, allowing you to take in one part of the route one day, and hop on the following day to complete the rest of it. You can also hop on and off at any time within the 24 hours, and take as many tours or part-tours as you want.

Took the ticket option including the boat cruise, and that gave us a trip from Westminster to Greenwich the following day.

If you prefer to do the trip without guide and commentary, choose the Blue route, otherwise Red.

We checked out all the available hop-on hop-off bus tours of London. We found that the Big Bus Tours was the only company that came as far as Paddington Station (close to our hotel). As we were only just around the corner from a bus stop we decided to use this company.

In the morning we walked to the bus stop and we spoke to a rep and purchased our tickets. We were also able to purchase our tickets to other attractions (which were cheaper than the location ticket office and we were able to walk straight into the attraction instead of waiting in a queue to buy tickets - excellent).

The bus was an easy way to get around London (hop on and off at their set locations near all the tourist/local attractions throughout London). Only downfall is the London Traffic and that cannot be helped.

On the bus we utilised the ear phones as well as the live commentary and they were both great. The live commentary was informative and funny.

Thoroughly enjoyed getting around seeing the sights.

I took this tour in September 2013 and loved it. The ticket price included the river boat tour, and the hop on/hop off ability essentially took away the need for other methods of transportation that day, as my hotel was situated just near the Westminster stop. For the first leg of our journey, we had a live guide. He was great! Very knowledgable and funny as well. Yes, of course you could walk many of the sights yourself, but having the guide explaining in great detail what was on each block was very helpful.

We hopped off at the Tower of London as did most people. When we were done there, we took the river boat cruise back to Westminster, which provided great views along the Thames. There we also had a live guide, very funny and informative. On the final leg of our tour, we hopped back on a bus from Westminster to Marble Arch. On this bus, there were only headphones and a recording of the sights. Still informative, but a bit of a letdown after the funny guides we'd had all day. This is the only reason I knocked the rating down a peg. Oh, and be sure to book online in advance, as it's cheaper than buying a ticket at the green kiosks!

I've been to London countless times but it was my husband's first, so we decided to take a bus tour to get our bearings, see some sights and learn more about the city. I would recommend starting mid day or afternoon, then you can ride and alight at a destination for dinner and still continue the next day and alight at another spot for lunch, etc. The live guide is definitely better than the recorded, but not all guides are interesting - Nick was the most entertaining and informative, if you could know beforehand which bus he's on, I'd wait for that bus! The river cruise was also interesting. My 5 year old didn't always enjoy the journey but being on a bus he was also able to take a short nap.

We decided to get a 24h Big Bus Tour Ticket before our London Pass and Travel Card period started. It was a good way to explore the city and decide where to spend time on, once we get free entrance due to London Pass. In addition: Buses drove very frequently and till late in the evening (think it was till around 7pm).

But there were also some things, I didn't like so much about it:
1. On many seats the audiio guide was not working smoothly. They should think about renovating the buses or at least the players.
2. There were 3 lines: Blue, Red and Green. The Blue and the Red ones have almost the same route, whereas the Green one is just a small line from St Pancras to Aldwych. Would have been nice to have various smaller line instead of one big an one small route.
3. Somehow same point as point two: As the Blue and Red route was very long, it took very long to go for the full circle (I guess it was between 2.5 and 3.5 hours.). And the buses are just driving in one direction. So the Big Bus tour is not a good way to get transported from one to the other attractions, as you may have to make a huge loop and loose some hours to get to your destination.
4. Around 3 times on this day, the bus stopped and we were told to switch to the bus in front of us. After we did, it took a few minutes, till the other bus started, which is not that bad. But I think it is not customer friendly to tell them changing the bus without any good reason.

My family and I (husband, myself, and 14-year-old daughter) booked a 24-hour ticket on our second day in London and found it to be a great, convenient, and enjoyable way to see many of the sights in London. While it is not inexpensive, the fact that it includes the river cruise makes it well worth the money. The staff members are easy to spot on the street in their logo shirts, and were very helpful in explaining how it all works. It is very easy to get off the bus at any of the stops to explore the sights and then just get back on at the same or any other stop. We didn't happen to take the buses with the live commentary, but still enjoyed the informative recorded commentary (they provided earbuds). The day of the tour we visited more places than seems humanly possible - Trafalgar Square, the National Gallery, the Cavalry Museum, Westminster Abbey, Houses of Parliament, Tower of London, the Imperial War Museum, and St. Paul's Cathedral, as well as others I have probably forgotten to list. The cruise on the Thames with City Cruises was great, just get on line early if you want a seat on the upper level. Highly recommended!

Nine of us (4 adults & 5 children) have just returned from a weekend in London where we spent a whole day using the Big Bust tours open top buses.

The cost was £30 per adult and £12 per child (or £77 for a family ticket for 2 adults & 2 children). I thought this was quite expensive at first until I realised that it also included a hop-on and off cruise along the River Thames. When you add up what you would pay for public transport, this is actually great value for money. They even provide disposable ponchos if it starts raining and headsets for those buses that didn't have live commentary.

We managed to cram in almost all of the major sights in London in a day and the open top bus was great for taking photos as you got some really good views. The buses with the live commentary were better too as you could ask questions if you liked and the guides threw in extra titbits of information that you wouldn't normally get. They also made it more fun for our kids by asking them to shout out when they spotted certain things along the way - this really helped to keep them as interested as we were.

My only advice would be to take a jacket/jumper as we had short sleeves on as it started off as a nice sunny day but it gets very breezy on the bus and the citycruise boats.

I will definitely use this service again on my next trip to London - it was brilliant.

This has to be the best way to see London. Our guide was Nick. He was great. His knowledge of London's history was incredible. You will leave off this tour with a fond appreciation for London. Be advised that your ticket is good for 24hrs from the point that you activate it, so you have plenty of time to take full advantage of this tour. Plus, your ticket stub allows you to get discounts at other attractions such as the Eye. Also, take a bus with an actual guide on it. The recorded tour just isn't as interesting.

My wife and I used this service in August 2013 when we were in London. If your looking for a recommendation I would recommend this bus service. I know there are many bus services similar to Big Bus tours in London but all I know is that, the Big Bus Tours busses were clean the staff were very knowledgeable and friendly. There are two busses you can use, there's one with live commentary and the other with a recorded commentary with different languages. Their hop on and off feature is a great way to see the city. All I can say is that this is the best way to get around the city without paying multiple fares for taxis or bus fares!!!

The Tour on the red bus, which is the hop on hop off bus is the ideal way to see the best of london. The english speaking guide was delighful and educational and we were given the history of the famous places around london. The ability to chose the length of time you stay on the bus is great. The tour is the best value for your money. Traveling around london can be a very expensive exercise.

We really enjoyed our Big Bus tour, on the red route. Our guide was Andy Grey, and he was great - funny, informative and really passionate about the city and all it has to offer. We were also lucky to see the Tower Bridge opening, and our bus was right at the front - something our guide said he had never experienced either, so kudos to the driver for that! Tour was quite expensive (36 pound for 48 hours), but it also includes the river cruises and some walking tours. Will definitely return next time, thanks Andy!

My husband and I was on the Big Bus Tour. We sat on the open top decker of the bus. It was delightful. The weather was good, the tour guide was excellent, very knowledgeable as well as friendly and fun. Start early in the morning so that you are "fresh and well rested" as it can get tiring hopping off and on the bus, but it is fun. even the entire day on the bus was not enough to see all the attractions. The cruise on the Thames River was included which was just great. Definitely value for money.
There are more than one company operating these tours, so first scout around (on the web) to get the best deal. We used the "Big Bus Company" and we very satisfied with their service.

This is the second time on the tour, the last time it was pouring and this time it was 27 degrees!!

A good and long journey and I like that you can hop on and off. It got busy at times but we all got sat together. I suppose it depends where you get on.

We booked online which saved us £8.00 each and had our day already planned and the guy who was at the bus stop was very rude because we didn't want to buy any more tickets for other attractions and would have been as well 'riding the bus at home' after 26 years of living in Glasgow, I think it's safe to say I enjoyed the bus in London a tiny bit better!!

The center line has live audio guide,they all have a sense of humor and give tons of good information, you get to see and to know the places that wouldn't know otherwise.
They also sell discounted tickets to most attractions so you save money if you get your tickets through them.
For those of you who'd like to see the change of the guards at Buckingham Palace: it tales place every other days and The Big Bus tour has a free walking tour for that, go with this tour, they know exactly where to stand you to see the guards, change of the guards does NOT take place in front of the place gate,so don't wast your time getting squeezed to the fences, go with this tour.

We did the Big Bus tour on our first day in London as a family. We really enjoyed having the live guide. This was far better than any pre-recorded commentary. We decided to do a full loop and then get on and off, it took so long that we didn't end up getting a chance to go around again but we went to those places over the next few days so it wasn't a problem for us. It was hot on the day we were there and you are mostly exposed to the sun so remember a hat and sunscreen if you burn easily. It was a lot of fun, worth the money and definetely a must do.

We chose to see London first hand by a hop on - hop off bus before seeing specific attractions in detail and the Big Bus turhed out to be a great way to do it. A cruise on the Thames was included in the Big Bus price and was also hop on - hop off. The Big Bus routes cover most everything and they have very helpful attendants located at many of the stops. As with all multi-language tours, you are wise to bring your own ear buds or headphones that fit you so you can more enjoy the tours.

Booked online directly from their website, costing us £27pp which i thought was a bit expensive but decided to book it anyway and glad i did. Got straight on the bus from Waterloo Station (2min walk), very friendly and helpful tour guides, spent all morning on the bus and got off at Buckingham Palace as we had booked seperately a tour here, spent a couple of hours here and then back on the bus for the rest of the afternoon. Seemed to be lots of traffic in the afternoon so took longer than expected and had a 15 min stop half way whilst the bus drivers swapped over! Got on the river cruise at Westminster which was brillaint - funny and entertaining captains who point out all of the landmarks, they really get the crowd involved. Would recommend to every one if you can spare the £27pp price, but it is worth it for the experience and you really do see every thing in London in one day!

We had three full days in London and chose to do the Big Bus Tour on our first day. First of off the day was perfect weather wise. We jumped on the bus at 9.00am (tour starts at 9.00am) right outside the door of our hotel. We then spent most of the day acquainting ourselves with all of the wonderful historic and iconic tourist spots around this beautiful city. The tour also includes a scenic cruise on the river Thames which we jumped on at the Tower Hill hop off. This was a fantastic way for us to get familiar with the city and we really enjoyed the whole experience. The final positive of the tour was I did what we all dread I dropped my wallet on the bus!! I am sure you can imagine what I felt when I realised what I had done. I rushed down to our pick up point and spoke to the lovely young lady (there is a Big Bus Tour staff member at every hop off point...fantastic) She contacted the office who then contacted the driver, he checked with the tour guide and to my absolute share relief my wallet was still sitting on the ground below where we were sitting (I know...note to self...buy a Lotto ticket!). So I would like to give a big shout out to the team at Big Bus Tours especially to Richard (the driver) and the lovely young lady at the Regent St hop off (no 8 I think outside the Café Royal Hotel). You guys are great!
Last mention we did the red tour which is the English speaking tour the guides on the bus were excellent, very knowledgeable and friendly.

Throughly enjoyed our host, Sam, and the bus tour!
First, we purchased our tickets on line.., Though we mis-entered the email address, we were wise enough to take down the reservation number and the staff at the Station (in Trafalga Sq.) were very accommodating and understanding!
We were well advised to take the bus to the Tower of London and to take the Thames cruise up the river to Big Ben (or the Elizabeth II Tower), and then pick up the bus back to Trafalga Sq.
The weather certainly contributed, but the bus tour was really informative and enjoyable!

well worth the money. it was our first time to london and this bus was a really great place to start our visit. we did a 2 day pass and hopped on and off at our convenience. there was a bit of a wait time a couple of times for the next bus, but nothing major. the tour guide was engaging and funny. i would definitely recommend doing this tour.

The Big Bus Tour was conveniently located near our hotel and we purchased tickets on the street as we were waiting for it. Tour was excellent. Only disappointment was that after stopping at Harrod's, the bus did not show up to take us back to our hotel at 7:30 pm. Another passenger had waited for 45 minutes when we arrived and we waited an additional 30 minutes before we finally took public transportation to our hotel. Not a good thing!
The 24 hour buses with the hop on hop off service was appreciated. The price was ok too. Our tour guide was great. Def recommend.

We were recommended this tour by family and so after settling in on our first day we purchased ticket vouchers from our hotel. Tickets are valid for 24 hours so we chose to start at 3.30pm which gave us about 2.5 hours to just sit and take in the city. We would then spend the next day getting on and off exploring more.

Things didnt get off to a great start with the bus driver unable to convert our hotel voucher to a ticket (despite hotel and signs at bus stop telling us to buy ticket from driver). Luckily he let us on and we had to wait for someone to help us at one of the stops.

Once going things were great. We chose seats upstairs in their open top double decker, and got a great view of everything. We werent pointed to headsets (for commentry) so didnt use them on this trip however we were just excited to be seeing London. Part way through however our bus stopped and we were instructed to get off as this bus was finished. We then had to cram onto another bus, getting a seat in the stuffy downstairs with linited view. This was very annoying as we had great seats and now couldnt enjoy ourselves. The bus driver then continued to stop and try and fix his wing mirror at every chance he had, which slowed the trip rigjt down. We gave up, jumped off and boarded a new bus ans found a great seat.

Day two was much better, we travelled around again, this time with the commentary and hopped off and on. We then finished with a free 30 minute river cruise down the Thames, all part of the ticket.

So apart from the grumpy staff and overall poor customer service we found it £30 well spent as you get to see so much of London

We bought a 24 hour ticket each at 30 pounds each. It did not appear to be cheap but we started at about 4:00pm in the afternoon and did the full Blue tour that day to give us a good feel for where things were. The Blue Tour is one for those who do not speak English and you get recorded information through speakers. It was very clear and easy to hear so we enjoyed that part. Using the info we had gleaned from the full tour we sat down with the map that night and decided the order we would use to visit what we wanted to see. The next morning we got the Big Bus again and started our adventure. We hopped on and off all day. The buses come very regularly and the red buses have a tour guide who gives the commentary in English plus they have a great sense of humour. We well and truly got our 60 pound worth and would recommend this to anybody trying to pack in a lot in a short time.

We purchased two 48 hour tickets for £36 each as we boarded the double decker bus in London St., Paddington. It proved to be a good and relatively easy but not cheap way to travel between a number of the major tourist attractions around London. However £36 for a two day ticket was much better value than £30 for one day.
You are able to alight and rejoin a bus at any of the many stops along the route. Whilst the open top deck was much more popular than the enclosed lower deck, we had no difficulty in obtaining a seat on the upper deck on any of the occasions when we re-boarded a bus. On the route we travelled, there was a multilingual audio commentary with earphones provided. We found the bus staff, both drivers and ticket sellers to be polite, efficient and helpful.
Our only criticism of the Big Bus hop on-hop off tour, relates to being on board for the last circuit of the day. The bus we were on, stopped near Marble Arch behind two other buses from the same company. The supervisor then moved passengers from the other two buses on to our bus and then after about a delay of 10 minute our bus proceeded on its journey. The bus soon stopped again, adjacent to the entrance to Kensington Gardens. We were then informed that the bus was going to bypass London St., Paddington ( where we had boarded) and that if we wanted to return there, we would need to walk. As that was the location of our hotel, that's what we had to do. We were told that it was a distance of only about 100 metres. It turned out to be more like 500 metres. Rather a disappointing end to an otherwise good service.

This tour was amazing, well worth the money. I was very impressed and loved each minute. I went with my son for his first time in london, he was eager to see everything in half a day which i thought was impossible. We booked tickets for the Big Bus Tour and sat on the top open air. its a hop on and hop off so you can leave anytime you want to see a certain sight or shop and then hop on to another big bus when u r done, all included in the ticket price. we saw hydepark, buckingham palace, oxford street, st pauls cathedral, the tower, big ben and much more all in 3 hours. it was amazing. they also supply you with ear phones to hear the tour guide speak and u can select many languages. They also supply you with rain panchos incase its rains. we saw everything that day and were fulfilled. Just Wonderful and took loads photos also. Its a must in london if you are a tourist.

Very eager and helpful staff at all of the stops. 30 pounds for the first 24 hours, but you can upgrade to 48 hours for an extra 6 pounds, we were misinformed in that you must pay the extra 6 pounds before you actually get on the bus the first time. Ask about it if you are interested, there are different rates for children. For a beautiful summer day we were surprised that we were able to sit upstairs in the fresh air every time we got on, a credit to the number of buses running. The buses come along approximately every 8 minutes, but we rarely had to wait that long. There are a few different routes that cover all of the London tourist spots. There is also a free river cruise and several walking tours. Rainwear is provided, and headsets give a running commentary. A great way to see London for all ages!

It's been around 15 years since i last visited London, this time was taking the kids and thought a bus tour would be a good option, after doing a lot of research on Tripadvisor and alike i decided to book with Big Bus Tours, i wasnt disappointed. We arrived early morning to a very bright and bubbly driver and assistant -without any hassle gave us a bus ticket having presented my online order form. We went on the red bus route to start with which was brilliant, plenty of space, really lovely funny and informative guide called Phil, he really made the tour a pleasure to be on. We stayed on for most of the route and then changed to the blue route, which to be honest was nice to see different places but really missed having Phil with his live commentary. On the whole lots of brown buses, we didnt wait the 10/20 minutes they stated before another bus came and it was very easy to hop on and off. Would thoroughly recommend Big Bus Tours - a fantastic way to see London. Next time we are in London we will be hopping on!

Hi, me and my daughters decided to go on the big bus your in London yesterday. What a disappointment. As you are taken from street to street the driver who was very nice drives like a racing driver and you only get a quick glance at 80% of the main attractions. Buckingham palace is practically non existing as you dont see it! My suggestion to travelers would be buy a all day tube ticket for £4 and get off at the attractions you want or use a CHEAPER coach company.

This is at least the 4th time we took family around London using the Big Red Bus and didn't disappoint. Despite pool weather, we sat on the open top as they provided raincoats, which was excellent. The commentary was interesting and clearly updated with the ongoing construction history and ever changing skyline of London it kept us entertained for hours. It was easy enough hopping off and back on, we also used it to take us to the hotel and the railway station we departed for.
The only negative comment I would make is that we had to wait around 45 mins for bus for the green route at the end of our visit. Far too long and the brochure states every 15 mins

Finally took the open top bus tour. Must have been to London dozens of times, but in 30 degree weather, sitting on the top deck with a welcoming breeze definitely appealed. Just don't be as dumb as me and forget the sun tan lotion!

We bought a 2 day ticket and paid extra for the extended boat trip as we wanted to enjoy more of the open air on the river and take in Greenwich. Well worth it as it's a lovely place, but once again, in July this year, a bit too hot to enjoy.

All in all I'd recommend the bus tour. You get a cruise thrown in, though as mentioned, if you want to go as far a Greenwich you need to pay a wee bit more.

If you have a sensitive derriere, take a cushion, as the seats are hard, unforgiving plastic.

Not a cheap outing but given you can hop on and off as much as you like, it's a pleasant alternative to the underground.

Bought tickets online which worked out slightly cheaper than on the day purchase. Was a very wet day but was provided with Eco-mac which is just like see thru bin bag to help stay dry. Tour guide was very informative and interesting. You can stay on bus all day or hop off to take in another fascinating route of London. Well worth the cost of £27. You can also take a city cruise along the Thames which was also fun and interesting.

We bought the (not cheap) tickets from our concierge and the bus stop was right outside our hotel on Westminster Bridge so it couldn't have been easier. Loved the hop on/hop off flexibility and the option to take a boat ride. We never had to wait more than 10 minutes for a bus ... We did the same thing in Paris and it was awful. It took 30 minutes of queuing to buy the tickets and once on the bus, the stops took forever. London is much better organized.

Love the Big Bus Tour Company. We were lucky to go on a day when it was dry and so were able to sit outside upstairs and see all the fantastic sites of London, along with listening to a very informative commentary from the tour guide.

What we loved about this was that we could hop and off the bus as many times as we liked and included in the price is a boat trip on the Thames. We got on the bus at the Tower of London after spending the morning there, then went to Piccadilly and had lunch before walking up to and visit Hamleys Toy Shop. We then got back on the bus outside Hamleys, went to Westminster pier where we got off the bus and got onto the boat back down to the Tower of London.

I really good day out !

After using the big bus company twice now, it is safe to say that they are fantastic! Great for families and for for less abled people that can't walk far but want to see lots. Book online for better prices but reasonable with the boat tour too. Only negative is that dependant on your tour guide I'd dependant on how good the commentary is, nick was first, he's was brilliant, lots of info and funny, got you asking questions too, but the second was appalling, boring with a lack of enthusiasm, a crap guide. And the "free" commentary on the boat was good too, very dry "British" humour! ,

Buy only one day ticket for £24 (online). Take the trip in the morning and spend afternoon in the boat between Big Ben, Tower Bridge and Greenwich. The boat ride is free with Big Bus hop on/off. We had a GREAT guide who entertained us for 45 minutes between first two locations mentioned above. Bus ride was almost unnecessary as London center is small enough to get everything seen on foot. If you are staying longer than a day or two, get Oyster Card and use buses (use major line Central London Bus map, download online and print in COLOR). Great way to see all well known locations for pennies. Than you do not need hop on/off at all. In addition, use The Tube to get to the locations further away. Walk, you are a tourist, it is safe if you do not jay walk.
I just wish I learned the boat ride guides name. He deserves 5 stars rating. The way he talked, how funny he was and showed knowledge, keep us interested all the time, just amazing.

Firstly the cost.....absolutely ridiculous how much they charge for this. It's a hard sell with other companies reps trying to get involved and then stating I'd been given a good price - they're all in it together. They were rude and arrogant but as we'd made a special journey to do the tour I bit the bullet and paid up.

The bus itself was okay, hard plastic seats to deal with the weather. The guide though was very poor, I learned nothing interesting and it seemed to be geared towards a tourist who knows absolutely nothing about London - but I'm sure they don't need to be told that the Queen lives in Buckingham Palace !?

The guide mumbled in to his microphone and didn't seem interested, there was no interaction with the anyone on board. Thankfully the weather was nice so we were able to enjoy the sunshine on the top deck but that said we only stayed on board for an hour - money down the drain.

Sorry Big Bus Tours but you failed miserably.

We used this company yesterday and thought they were excellent. The buses, red and blue, came along every few minutes and being able to just hop on and off was brilliant. The tour guides were all excellent, with the exception of one who was had a bit of a "droney" voice but hey, we just hopped off his bus and got on another one at the next stop, where the guide was much more lively. The staff at the bus stops were good too, directing us to Covent Garden, etc and letting us know when the next bus was on its way. The free river cruise was excellent. A couple of other people have commented on how expensive the tour is. Yes, it is expensive but this is London, everything here is expensive and if you take into account the fact that it includes a river cruise and travel around the city for the day, then it's actually very good value for money.

This tour was good. I live in London but had some guests that wanted to do it. I did learn some interesting things from the audio guide but there were also a lot of things it missed. The west half of the tour was a bit boring and a lot of the audio guide references could not even be seen properly from the bus. The hop on hop off is great- cause otherwise its a bit boring after a while.

This tour is £30 to buy a ticket with the driver. Way too much to sit on a bus and listen to audio. You could do half that tour on a £2.40 regular double decker bus with a travel book. Its a great way to go if you only have one or two days in the city. Otherwise get off the bus and actually see the sights on foot. Download an audio guide or get a book and enjoy the city at your own pace!

It was a good tour- just way overpriced. If you buy online it's £23.00 but says nothing about the price hike when buying at the bus. Try to sweet talk the ticket seller- it worked for me and got tickets for £25.

We have used bus tours a lot when we get to a city to get a feel for the place, hear some history and decide what to visit in full detail. We chose this company with its 1st stop right by the Ritz Hotel in Piccadilly. We took the Red line to see the sites in London proper. The tour was well worth the cost. We got off at the Tower of London so we could ride the City Cruise down the Thames to Westminster. It was included in our Big Bus ticket. The cruise was really fun as you get to see some sights from the river you would not otherwise see. When we got off the boat we walked to the London Eye which is just a few blocks away. After riding the Eye, we got back on the bus and took it back to our original stop. Great value.

Absolutely fantastic. We visited London with a 3 & 7 year old. This was a wonderful way of seeing the sites. You can hop off see the " site" and then it won't be long before another bus comes along. We preferred the red route, with the live commentery although the blue was very good too. Tickets typically last 24 hours and include a free river cruise which was great. My one gripe would be the buses could do with just running a little later. Especially in the summer months. But would still give 5* and recommend.

well i have to say i liked the big bus tour so much, that i went for seconds, as this was not my first trip to London.
all the guides were very knowledgeable. every one has a story to tell. all the general guidelines are the same off course, but its fun to hear something new when you enter different buses after some sightseeing. thank you guys, for bringing a piece of Londons history and everyday life to our lives.

The big bus tour of London is the perfect way to get your bearings in London and to see all the major sites. There is a red and blue route although the two routes are common for a large portion of their routes. The red buses however have a guide on them who gives a running commentary in English. On our trip Ian was the guide. He obviously knows London and its history very well and he kept you well informed but he did it in a very entertaining manner which kept everyone on board interested and involved. We used the bus on a Sunday which we understand is a good choice because the traffic in London tends to be quieter and the buses get around without too many long stops in jams. A bonus of booking with this company is that your ticket also includes a river cruise between Westminster and the Tower of London.

We bought a day ticket but to really make the most of everything on offer you need a two day ticket. We hopped on and off and enjoyed the live commentary. We also did the harry potter walk, which for HP nuts is a must as it takes you to film locations you would never find by yourself. We really wanted to do the boat trip but ran out of time and energy in just one day. We used the bus as a way of getting to other places we had tickets for, so saved us using other forms of transport and extra expense.

The Big Bus Tours is a good company and quite a cost effective way to see a lot of London. The price for 48hrs instead of 24hrs is only a few £s more and definitely worth it.

We had pre-booked for fixed dates and were staying out on Bayswater road. This was good as this was early on the route and the buses were not packed. If the weather is good and you can get a seat upstairs then it is brilliant.

The hop-on, hop-off idea is excellent and we saw lots of sights and jumped off at Trafalgar Square and Buckingham Palace for pictures.

The staff are always at each bus stop and very friendly.

On boarding the bus there are boxes of headphones and ponchos, always useful to get a handfull of each!!

If booking on line be careful to check the site on their "Service Information" tab, as if there is an event in London and some roads closed then the whole package comes to a standstill and your experience can be ruined.

Not sure why a company of this size can not work out alternative routes or diversions but they apparently can't.

You get free river cruises as well, which are good.

i booked a trip to London with my daughter and grand-daughter and for my birthday one of my gifts that my daughter and grand-daughter bought me was a 48 hour ticket for the big bus tours. the staff were very friendly and helpful and the buses were very regular and are very good value for money and the tours are very informative and interesting.

Charlotte was the best tour guide I have seen in awhile. Her enthusiasm and knowledge of London made the bus tour really great.We had her for 2 days and she was by far the best of the tour guides that we saw.

This is a great way to see, learn about, and get around London. The guides were very good, we never had to wait too long for a bus. We took advantage of the free Harry Potter tour, which was crowded but well organized, so we were always able to hear the tour guide. Expensive, but worth the money since you can see more of the city in less time.

The routes are well chosen and help you see all the basic sights in one (long) pass. Our "live" guide was great and the recorded tours were informative (though it would be nice if there was a little more variety in the music underscore).

Their website doesn't tell you this, but tour bus stops are marked on the same signs as the transit bus stops. Finding your first hop-on point can be a little tricky.

The 24-hour period of the ticket was quite useful to us. We first did a drive-around late one afternoon to get our bearings, the rush hour traffic giving us plenty of time to look around and take pictures from the bus. We had enough time on our ticket to go back and explore a few places the next day.

I know London very well but had a cousin and her daughter from Canada visiting London only for a day or two so wanted a quick way to give them an overview of the sites of London. This was a good way of doing it and the live commentary was excellent and the staff were friendly! It is considerably cheaper if you book on-line in advance so do that!

My only gripe was the process of getting our tickets on the bus with our previously printed e-tickets. Since we were more than 5 people, the scanner machine of the assistant will not authorise the tickets. We had to get off the bus and she had to phone for authorisation from Head Office. This meant we had to get the next bus which meant we missed The Changing of The Guard at Buckingham Palace. This was disappointing flaw in the Big Bus Tour procedures and ruined what would have been otherwise a perfect trip. So come on Big Bus Tours get this sorted please for future visitors?

We used the Big Bus Tour to see the main tourist attractions of London. The bus is clean and has a lot of frequent arrials to the stops. However the live comentary leaves something to be desired. One of the guides even fell asleep when we were caught up in traffic near London Bridge. Overall it is still a pretty cheap way to see London.

My daughter & I live only 25 minutes train ride from central London and had a few hours to kill whilst waiting to see a matinee show! Since I am awaiting surgery on a torn meniscus in my knee and cant walk very far we decided to jump on board and sit on the top deck in the sunshine! We thoroughly enjoyed our trip!

Our guide Andy was fantastic - very informative and entertaining! I could tell that he was a thespian! We really enjoyed his outbursts of singing! We were so disappointed when the bus changed crew - it wasn't the same without him!

So many interesting facts that I did not know - even my 13 year old daughter was captivated!

Well done Andy! you are a credit to Big Bus Tours! x

We stayed for 2 nights on the Southbank and whilst visited London before never used the tour buses, this time we thought we would give it a go. We booked on-line so getting a saving and purchased a 48hr ticket. For info the ticket starts we booked in first time so plan your days out before to get full value.

We did both the red and blue route and found both to be good in their own right. The live commentary informative and ad lib with funny parts from a very informative and proud Londoner where as the recorded is obviously more scripted, they supply ear buds so no concerns about bringing any.

The weekend we were there lots of roads were closed off due to a cycle ride taking place however this did not spoil the fun and in a way the detours showed us more than expected.

Just hop and and off where you want and you will find helpful staff at all the stops and don,t forget to use your free river cruise as part of the ticket. As we had 48hr ticket we could sail to Greenwich and have to say that this was well worth the 3 hours especially as the timing was right and we came under Tower Bridge that had been raised.

If sightseeing in London this is the only way to see all of the sights without getting lost and is good value for money. Do not hesitate to book, whilst we had sun shining all the time don't worry if its raining as the Big Bus Tour supply you free ponchos to allow you to still enjoy the upper deck.

My friend and I stayed 5 days in London and loved our time there. We booked 2 days on the Big Bus Tour. It was a great (and long) way to get an overview and feel for the city. We stayed in Paddington (near Hyde Park)which was nearest the blue line. If I were to do his tour again, I would only book one day, the second day you hear and see all the same sites and there are other, cheaper, more expedient ways to get around the city. A must do though for one's first time in a new city.

We decided to book the Big Bus Tours as they had a 48 hour option, booked via their website. I had read reviews for all the London bus companies there were good and bad comments about them all.

I would recommend Big Bus tours - they were great, our tour guide was Nick and driver Kev. We found them really funny and informative, they must do this day in day out but made us feel welcome during the journey, we didn't want to get off and stayed on until the buses changed over. The 2nd guide wasn't as interactive. Some routes also offered headphones for pre-recorded commentary.

With young children walking in London can be hard work, we saw all the major attractions without leaving our seats. The boat tour was also good.

While the underground is the quickest and most efficient way to zip across London, the Big Bus allows you to appreciate London above ground. Surely a must do. Throw in the free river cruise and the walking tour which we did not do, its worth the money. You need two days to finish all the routes on offer. Negatives : lots of people on popular sections so no guarantee of roof top seats; weather - it can rain but ponchos are provided; commentary - only offered live on the red line and while it was good on the boat, it was so so on the bus.

The Big Bus tour is a good way to see London. Its especially nice that the buses run so often, but it does get a bit tiring repeating drives when you hop on and off. The cruise that comes with this tour was a great surprise and well worth the cost. Because the staff at every stop and the bus comes so often I give them the highest rating. They work hard at making it easy for the traveler. They are also flexible and come up with alternate routes when traffic or anything else requires detours and changes. We were given a free extra day because some of the stops were not available. This is conjunction with the tube is a great way to see London.
