This is one of the world's best hop on hop off bus operator, with loads of experience not only in London but also several other cities. In London, there are two routes, the Blue, with recorded audio and the Red, with a live guide. Along with the bus tour, our ticket gives you access to some nice walking tours (we took the Harry Potter one) and a boat tour (departing from the Tower of London).

I live in London but had visitors staying with us for just a few days. They wanted to see everything. But of course London is a big place. I suggested a bus top tour and we chose Big Bus Tours. What an excellent choice it was. We got a 24 hour pass (but wish we had got the 48hour one). We started at 2 p.m. on the Friday and were able to use the same ticket until 2 p.m. on the Saturday. We got on at Westminster and took the short route to London Bridge. The Friday was good but there was no guide on the bus to point out the interesting points. We resumed on the Saturday using the same ticket. This time there was a guide in the bus. His name was Nick. He made that journey so interesting that we stayed on the bus all the way round. He was full of interesting and entertaining facts about London and the many sights we passed. We were still able to jump on another bus to take us back round to Buckingham Palace then back on to Tower of London. We then came back to Westminster by boat which was also included in the price of the ticket. Really excellent value. I would highly recommend it.

Best way to see all the must do for London. This company seem to have the most number of buses compare to other companies. But make sure you check what colour service is the bus for. Go for the RED bus for live commentary which covers all the hot spots. BLUE for recorded sommentary that somethimes get out of sync to actual location.
We went on a Monday afternoon, it was raining a little so we got on to one of the buses which had half open & half covered area on the top. We boarded at the no.1 bus stop at Green Park near Buckinghum Palace. Since it was raining, we sat at the lower deck, can hardly see anything. Top covered area was full when we board. When rain stopped, people from upper deck started getting off the bus thats the best time to move up. Punchos were given. We sat of the open which was really refreshing & chilly, we continue the whole route until it finished the entire tour route. With the traffic & rain all in took us about 3½ hours to complete then we hop on to the blue bus for the west side of the tour. This way the best way to see london especially on a rainy day.
Do bring some drinking water though.

We pre booked and picked up our tickets from London Bridge bus stop. We started to be concerned about our choice when the first Big Bus arrived packed to the rafters upstairs and downstairs. We decided to wait. Over the next 10 minutes we were treated to the sight of 3 Original Tour buses passing all with plenty of space on, The next big bus arrived again packed. We got on and stood downstairs. We did get seats upstairs at Tower Bridge but it was a bit of a fight to get spaces and made us unwilling to hop on and off as there just didnt seem to be enough buses.

The recorded commentary was only alright and not a pstch on the one provided on the boat trip.
The boat tour from the Aquarium was the best part of the trip plenty of seats and an informative and witty commentary.

I wouldnt recommend based on our experience

My daughter and I experienced two of the Guided Walking Tours included with our Big Bus Tour ticket. We loved them both and had the same tour guide for both by choice. Kevin Russell was a fabulous guide, welcomed all questions and was amazingly entertaining and informative. He was wonderful at moving everyone through the crowds and never left at the end of the tours until he was certain that everyone knew where they were and how to arrive at their next destination. We found him very kind and personable. We highly recommend his tours!!

I think we had a bad experience. The bus went off route and was stuck in traffic for a long time. The stops between Marble Arch and Westminster Abbey are not worth it. Once we got to Westminster and the Eye and all that it was much better. Fleet Street is really worth seeing!

I guess if you're in London for only a few days go ahead and do it. We were there for six days or so and ended up seeing everything that we saw on the bus tour later in our stay.

Make sure you get on the English bus.

We did this on one of the hottest days of the year and sat on the top, outside; we still enjoyed it.

We did the Blue tour which has pre-recorded commentary. My husband did the Red tour two years ago and said he enjoyed the pre-recorded comments much more as the accent was easier to understand.

We liked that we could get on and off where we liked, though we only actually got off at the Courtauld museum and spent several hours there.

The traffic was terrible, and we sat for almost an hour approaching the National Museum, so we weren't sure how well it would have worked if we'd really wanted to stop and see a lot of places.

We bought an extra ticket for the next day to do the river cruise, which we thoroughly enjoyed. We felt this river cruise at a reduced rate made it worthwhile to have purchased the Big Bus tour. However, because we had been delayed so much the day before we took the tube to the beginning of the river cruise instead of hopping on the Big Bus.

I was only in London for a few days and was looking for a way of seeing a lot in a short time. I selected to do the route with the live comentary as opposed to the pre-recorded and it was a real highlight. Our guide was a local "cockney" and clearly loved talking about London and sharing stories old and new. It was great to see him genuinely excited when we spotted Morris dancers in Trafalgar Square. I didnt use the hop on/hop off opportunity, and rather just sat on the bus for an entire route and was fine with that. It was cold and miserable at the time and it was nice to be able to sit back and enjoy the ride rather than walking long distances between places.

We have just spent a truly fabulous day in London. We used the big red bus company. From the outset when we arrived at green park they were brilliant. Mums in a wheelchair and these guys couldn't do enough for us. Helpingus with chair on the bus.. Due to the bike ride being on across London today, there were detours and some sights were not available from the bus. We were advised to get on the river cruise to see certain sites, which we did. The staff on the boat were amazing, moving us to the front of the queue to aid our trip. Lifted the chair on. And off the boat. Sought out seats for us. Literally treated us like royalty. Bus staff were incredible and so helpful. It made our trip so smooth I definately recommend this company. Absolutely worth every penny. Xx

My family of five caught the bus after watching the changing of the guard at Buckingham Palace. It was a great and informative tour. I was not sure how my children of ages 4, 7 and 10 would cope but they all loved being up high and taking in the sights of London, my 10 year old didn't want to get off when we decided to go for lunch! We went on the Red Tour as it had a live commentary which was funny and informative, I would recommend this tour for English speaking visitors. This is a great way to see the city and learn about some of its history. It is a good way to tour and decide which attractions you would like to go to and spend more time exploring.

Getting on the big bus is a good way to spend a day in London, or any other city for that matter. It's like taking a crash course in the history of the city and its main attractions, and then you get to decide what you want to visit.

Went on the Big Bus Tour Saturday 20th July, just great to hop on & off.
All the staff where very polite, didn't have to wait very long for a bus.
we used the headphones ( FREE ) and you can adjust the volume
plenty to see with good information, would I recommend it YES.

Also if you have time, go for afternoon tea on the Thames, it is just the best ever.
We went with Bateaux London

I go to London on business fairly frequently and anytime that I have a first time visitor with me on the trip, I recommend a Big Bus tour of the city on the first day. Give you a great perspective and understanding of the city and it's history and helps you decide the best places to spend your time on the rest of your visit.

We joined the Big Bus Tour near St. Paul's Cathedral with no intention of getting off until we had completed the total circuit. Very helpful driver and very chatty on board guide made the tour interesting with various historical anecdotes. The area around Trafalgar Square was extremely busy with huge crowds enjoying the sights and beautiful weather. Unfortunately we were unable to drive past Buckingham Palace due to gas/water leaks in the area. For us the tickets were expensive because they included the cost of a Thames River cruise which we had separately undertaken the day before. However, the experience was worthwhile for a couple not very familiar with London.

Got a ticket at 8:30 a.m. I was on a route only served by audio but you can switch to the live commentary at various stops. I had two different live commentators during the day, both knowledgable but odd. Bus timing is haphazard. Three come in a row, then none for half an hour. They are often crowded in the summer. A boat cruise was included and it was well worth the wait to get on to see the city from water. However, the "last bus" is advertised as starting its route at 19:00, which I understand to be 7:00 p.m. I waited outside Harrad's department store from 6:35 until 7:10 to get a bus back to my hotel. There were other passengers already waiting. The 7:10 bus refused to pick us up despite the fact we all, including a family with two small children, needed to get back to Paddington station. The driver's radio was broken so he couldn't report that there had been no bus for 40 minutes and several people were stranded. He refused to give us a ride even though he had passengers on board that he was taking to Paddington station and could offer no useful advice. He did say there would not be any more buses. I spent almost an hour walking back to my hotel and when i was within one block of my hotel saw a Big Bus dropping off passengers at my stop - at 8:00 p.m. Not a great service. There are other companies that offer this hop on hop off type of tour. Perhaps they do a better job.

The many diversions meant that there was no commentary. Driving around London at a snails pace, not knowing or being told what you are seeing is very frustrating!! "The Origional Bus Tour" has live commentary on all buses so that even if diverted you still are told what you are seeing.
With the construction & diversions (detours), chose "The Origional".

We bought a 24 hour ticket - in the end this allowed us to do the red route live guided tour, the blue route pre recorded tour and the boat trip on the Thames. The live guided tour was excellent -Nick our guide was informative, entertaining and had excellent presentation skills. The tour was comprehensive. We did not take advantage of the opportunity to hop on and hop off but this option existed. We were still on the bus at the end of the day and were very impressed with the care they took to arrange to drop us back to a stop that worked for us - this has not always been the case in other cities

If this is your first time seeing London the Big Bus tour is great. The thing I liked about the bus was being able to see the sites of the city while traveling from place to place rather than being stuck seeing (and smelling) the inside of the underground tube stations instead. Being on the top deck was a treat with the nice weather. There was never a wait longer than 10 minutes for a bus to arrive, but depending on where you want to go, you might have to be patient for it can take a considerable amount of time to get to your desired destination between traffic jams and bus drop off/pick ups. The bus always dropped off close to the attractions and sites worth seeing so there was never a long walk to reach them. We definitely got our money's worth using the bus, we saw just about everything we wanted to in the allotted 2 days.

The big bus tour could be a good experience but you should be conscious of walking a little bit.
Be careful, only the blue line has the translator, the red line is only in english.
We went on saturday and there was a traffic jam, so che bus had a very low speed.... That made me crazy :-(
Some drivers are very nice, other less....
Book on internet and in advance, you can save your money!!!

Joined the bus tour at Victoria on red route with commentary, a very irritating young lady for guide but fortunately swapped to lovely Rebecca only 2 stops down. Worth the money just to see all the sights around London without any pushing and crowds, great on the top when moving but very hot when stationary and stuck in traffic. Can easily pop on and off and buses very regular.

The big bus tour was a great way to get around London. We were able to see all the things we wanted and it is great to be able listen to the head phones or live guide to learn about what you are seeing. The buses come often we never had to wait too long, which was nice since the day we were there was a little chilly and rainy. The only thing I would have liked was if the bus stops had the numbers posted on them that were on the map. Every stop is numbered so you're looking for that #stop and it would be much easier if they were posted at the stops.

If you only have a few days in London and it is your first visit, the London Big Bus Hop-On-Hop-Off Tour is a good way to get an introduction to the major attractions of London. Take the full tour without hopping off first and then choose which attraction you want to visit. You cannot possibly go to all the major attractions in a day or two! For longer visits (3 days or more), it is better to use the regular bus or the Metro. Remember that the Big Bus tours run only from 9 am to about 5 pm.

Did this tour on Sun 7th and enjoyed it. Got tickets (prebooked) at around 11am. Had to go hunting for a stop to pick up bus and after 3 separate phone calls to office, eventually got it by Ritz. First 2 guides were excellent (both female) but when we rejoined later in day we got a male one who was poor. Cant remember his name but the driver was Neville. He kept on encouraging people in front of him to ask question after question, most of which we never heard and hence he missed most of the points along the way. Our daughter asked him a question about Buckingham Palace and we are still waiting on the answer. Got the complimentary Boat trip from London Eye to Tower and another one back. The 2nd Boat guide was just brilliant - real local boy with lots of very funny stories. He said he was knew to the game but he sounded like an old pro.
Overall it was good but could have been much better.

Enjoyed our Big Bus tour, both the blue and red line (could not get any info on the green line, does it really even exist?). The red line is certainly more entertaining with a live commentator who will also let you know if seats are available up top. Your ticket is good for 24 hours and since we had already been to a lot of the sights on our own, we enjoyed staying on the bus for the most part and getting off at one or two stops that we wanted. Also appreciated that the next day we were able to use our ticket (not yet expired) to return to the Tower of London. We had to change busses part way through the trip so got "caught" with an expired ticket when reboarding, but the attendant let us get on even though getting to the Tower would be another hour or so past our expiry time (he had a bit of attitude, but still let us get on) Great way to see the city!

Our family of four bought a 3 day pass for the tour and found that overall it was decent but that it took a little too long to get around using the bus as a hop on and off. Most of the attractions we were interested in were along the main line so it did make things a little challenging. We ended up mostly using the cabbies who were so helpful and provided us with a really unique view of London culture. If you're in London for an extended stay than it may make more sense. We were there for 5 nights and 4 days and just found it wasn't quite what we expected. If you ask us... the cabbies are amazing and if you walk and use a cab only when necessary... you're better off. They were all amazingly colorful and knowledgeable chaps!!

I've been to London before but this time decided on taking this tour. Waited a while for the live commentary 'red' line but decided to hop on the next bus regardless, which was blue (recorded) It was still very good! Our group was very impressed with the information and the route of the bus. Sat of course in the open top of an almost empty bus, and saw so much we just could not take it all in! We know now what attractions we will go straight to on a future visit to London, which is the reason you should do this tour first and then decide what to tackle 'on foot'.

I was not on this bus company during my week in London. I picked the "right" priced service, and sure wish I had gone with these guys, or the other big company. Their buses were everywhere, had a great schedule, and great routes. Their staff was very friendly and helpful to me, as I often had a lot of time to talk with them, as my cruddy service's busses hard to find and rarely seen.

This guys look like the second best thing going, but very good.

We had family coming to visit us so we decided the best way to show them London would be to take a bus tour. It definitely was the right decision!
There is no way we would have been able to cover as much ground as the bus tour took us on NOR would we have had the knowledge, interesting or funny stories to share as the tour guide.
Try to get the live commentry tour - our guide was fantastic!
Also, make sure you take advantage of the FREE river cruise included.
A great day out - the best & easiest way to see the whole of London!

Travel around london at a leisurely pace exploring London attractions. Hop off and On. Buses run from 9am until 6pm (end time varies) bear that in mind its a bit confusing with an 24hr ticket (you can catch the buses between 9am and 6pm any time for 24hrs after purchasing your tickets). Buses run frequently 10-15 mins.

This tour is very very very worth going on. The driver and the tour guide were very friendly and had so much knowledge of London. We went on the red tour and sat at the top of the bus. We had a free ticket to ride on the river from the London eye down the the towers which was amazing.
We took in so many sights on the tour and the ticket is valid for 24 hours, so we managed a little time on another one the next day.
You have to go on one of these.

me and my mother got a 24 hr pass was worth the money you can hop on and off at many different big ben, Buckingham palace, houses of parlamant etc stops buses run every 15 mins so your not hanging around long you get a commentary either by person or head phones in many languages which gave good information about London as we went around

I have only 2 days in London there is sooooo much to see so I had heard about these hop on hop off buses so on my train ride from Brighton to London i started reading reviews, there were good an bad ( but then again there is always mixed reviews you need to go with your gut feeling!). When I checked into my hotel I went an spoke to there guy an he also recommended it an told me it was 30 pounds (AUD 50) so I went into my room an googled Big Bus Tours an I was able to get it online for 21 pounds (I know it is only 9 pounds difference BUT when you travel every little bit helps!). The next day I hopped onto this bus at 9am an it took me all around eg Buckingham palace, Westminster, London eye, Big Ben, Harrods etc etc you have this pass for 24 hours (before I hopped on they did ask me if I wanted a 48 hour one for an extra 6 pounds which would of been great but I did not have the time ) you can hop off at any location an then hop on again when you want they come around every 5 to 10 minutes. Also included is the Thames river cruise which I recommend you do it's part of the deal so take advantage of it! The commentary was very good as well. So enjoy x

Have never really believed in bus tours but decided to do this in London to help us get our bearings and learn where the major landmarks were in the city. So glad we did! The commentary was great, helped acclimate us to where everything was and I used their map constantly to help me plot Tube stops and walking. It also helped me get some pictures I would never have gotten otherwise. Well worth the money!

My wife and I rode the Big Bus on our first day in London. We rode the Tube to Green Park. The bus pickup was right across the street from the Tube stop. We rode the entire route to get and overview of the city. The weather was pretty cold, therefore sitting on top of the bus was a bit chilly. The only problem we had was a group of children that sat behind us for some of the tour and talked very loudly, making the guide hard to hear. The guide provided lots of good information about the sites as we passed. I would recommend this as a way to get a view of the city if you're new to town.

The best way to see a lot of London sights on a short visit.

Being able to get on and off anywhere in the 24 hours the tickets are valid for allows the tour to be as versatile as you wish.

The river trip from Westmister Pier down to the Tower of London and then back on the bus was a bonus.

It is more than 40 years since my last trip down the Thames and the big disapointment was how London City have allowed the construction of some horrible ugly building (looks like a low rise multi-storey car park) to obscure most of the view of St. Pauls.

The commentaries, both recored and live, helped to make the purchase price of £30 good value.

This bus tour allows you to hop on and off as you please. Our guide was very knowledgeable and had some wonderful stories to tell in addition to facts. I recommend riding the bus around first (it'll take about 2-3 hours) and make notes about what you'd like to go back and see in detail. The 2-Day pass is a great value and will let you see everything.

The bus itself was comfortable enough, the headphones and audio were of an acceptable quality and I would recommend this tour to help orientate yourself with London.
The traffic wasn't great and the entire tour does take a while.
Very nicely conducted tour. You can get down at any point and hop into bus coming at frequent intervals. Guides in Red Tours are interesting

We only had 3 days in London and wanted to fit in as much as we possibly could. Big Bus Tours was the easiest and most economical way of doing this, hop on and hop off is brilliant and with multiple routes and buses every 15 mins we had a fantastic day of sight seeing.

Would highly recommend if in London.

With only 2 days in London, the Big Bus was a great way to introduce us to the sites and orientate ourselves before we then decided what to explore in more detail. The live commentary was great, the guide seemed quite knowledgeable and appeared to enjoy her job! The staff at the stops were helpful and the buses come frequently so the wait was short.

My husband, 14-year-old son and I visited London about two weeks ago. The first thing we did there was getting on this Big Bus Tours that Rick Steves recommends. This must be the best way to see London! Not only we saw lots of sights, but the guide Andy was phenomenal! We really enjoyed it. Go Andy!

The big bus tour gave us a grwat way to see all of the sights of London and not have to find our way around ourselves. Loved that it also included a river cruise and walking tour. We chose the ghost by gaslight tour and although there were no ghosts the tour guide was very entertaining! He was knowledgeable and made the tour great fun. In fact, we enjoyed him so much we kept him! He ended up meeting us in Germany for a concert a few days later and once again entertained us and made the trip that much more memorable! Cheers Phil if you're reading this! You're certainly Big Bus Tours biggest asset!

We went on the Big Bus Tour round London last week. It cost £30 per person, for the hop on - hop off service, including a boat trip on the Thames. Fortunately, when we boarded at the Ritz we chose a bus with a live commentary. The guide was most entertaining & full of enthusiasm for the sights we were seeing. We stayed on the bus till the Tower of London & then took a boat (included) to Westminster pier. Also with good commentary. We were lucky enough to see Tower Bridge opening to let a sailing boat through.
We then joined another bus, which unfortunately only had the recorded commentary. This seemed to consist mainly of reminders to take your headphones with you when leaving the bus. Very few interesting facts shared on this part of the tour.
Unfortunately, we had to leave the bus before the end of the tour as Marble Arch was closed because of an 'incident'.
This type of tour is an excellent way to orientate yourself in a new city and to decide where you want to visit later.
Thoroughly recommended.

After walking most of central London I bought a 48 hour pass for the bus tour. The can be found all over central London so it came in handy when I wanted to get off and on. The bus ticket also included a river cruise which was amazing! The bus staff were friendly although one of the ticket operators outside of Harrods was pretty rude.

I recommend this to anyone that wants to sit back and enjoy the city sites. The river cruise to greenwich is a must!

The buses are alwYs on time every 10 mins they come, your tickits last for 24hrs so we had nearly 2 days on the bus. With ur tickit you get a free boat ride down the temes it lasts 30 mins. The kids get a free bag and it has a book of london and games in it, if you in london take the big bus its great !!

Found this company to be excellent in May 2011; so went straight back to them in May 2013; recognized 2 super guides --- Robbie and Ricky! Can't wait to learn stacks more, especially from Robbie who is incredibly knowledgeable with a superb wit and relentless enthusiasm ; no desire to explore another tour company; Big Bus Tours are terrific!
Palmer, Ontario

We had a limited amount of time in London and opted for the hop on hop off bus tour. Big Bus tours provided a great overview of London, with the option to get off at any stop, then get back on for 24 hours. A river tour was included. Very enjoyable.
A great way to see London's main attractions. It was so easy to hop off at the places you wanted to see and catch the next bus back.

with only having a couple of days in london we decided to book this in order to see the sights in a short space of time(and save our legs).After an initial glitch getting our e ticket scanned(quickly and efficiently sorted out)we got on the bus, had a bus with a tour guide on.would say that having a guide makes the trip a lot more interesting..Even though it was raining we decided to sit upstairs in the uncovered part of the bus so that we could see the sights better(ponchos are provided free of charge)Had a nice time and the price includes a river cruise and several guided walking tours which we sadly didn't have time for. all in all had a good time and got soaked!

Taking a group of 9 friends from the USA and Australia to see the best bits of England, I decided the Big Bus Tour with live commentary is the best way to see everything you need to see in London in the shortest space of time. It was easy to book in advance, quick to find when we arrived in London and very informative. Perhaps our guide could have had a bit more knowledgeable patter to fill the traffic-induced pauses (as I remember guides from previous years when our children were younger). The river cruise commentary was impossible to hear, but handy to go from the Tower to Westminster, so those two areas got a close up look, and, of course, fun to travel on the river.
And it wasn't Big Bus Tours' fault that the showers on the day we visited London were of the horizontal hurricane variety!
We booked the two day ticket - - was well worth it !! Very good tour of London - -never had to wait long for a bus - -great commentary on board

If you want premier viewing of the changing of the guard then you MUST join Phil from the Big Bus Company on his walking tour! We joined the tour at Trafalgar on Sunday at 11am with some trepidation - was this really something we wanted to do? Did we really want to follow someone with a big group of strangers. Well, let me tell you - if you miss this tour with Phil, you will regret it! Phil's only thought was to get us to the best viewing spot and to get the best pictures! As he says, he has seen this hundreds of times, but he really does know how to get you where you need to be! It was funny, it was informative and best of all, we saw things and found out things about London that we didn't know! Phil was enthusiastic, full of energy and a fantastic example of amazing customer service. Thanks Phil, we enjoyed our walk with you and your group of strangers - if we are in London again we will make a point of walking with you again. The Big Bus Tour is expensive, but you get a trip on the Thames included and a number of walking tours plus guided tours around the city. The guides are knowledgeable and funny - it is money well spent! Very much recommended. Karen and Andrew.

This was my second time to take big bus tour.Like before this tour was also lovely.Took both live commentary and recorded tour.Very funny and helpful guide.Would suggest people to sit above in the bus to get better view of London.Booking online will get anyone a good deal.Missed the walking tours as we had to do london eye and Madame tussarss.Highly recommended.

I would like to recommend the hope on/off big bus tour - London, it was a great way to see all the main attractions in London (we were lucky with a great weather that day..) we took the tour for english speakers, hosting by a great ,cute, funny and knowledgeable instructor named Shabbi (I hope I write her name correctly) It is really worth the money .

Brilliant!
We booked a 48 hour tour and it took us around everywhere we wanted to go. We hopped on and off with ease. The only advice is, if you are in a rush, you may have to use the tube, but use the lift if you get off at Covent Garden station!

we bought the tickets as a spur of the moment thing as we were down in london for the day to see book of mormon. we bought the tickets from the victoria bus stop and got on a headphone bus tour. we were then told that we could only do half the tour as roads were closed and we couldn't even get near the theatre - the reason we bought the ticket. We were angry as the salesman did not tell us.

we then changed for a red bus with a real guide to try to make the most of the 30 quid and we were glad we did. it almost made up for the earlier problems. the guide was fab! we have been to london many times and done a bus tours but this guide told us things i never heard before! her exciting stories and made us laugh and we stayed on much longer than we planned. she showed us the best photos opps and best of all she got us to the theatre. we think her name was charlotte. try and get her as a guide. we also got on a guide called graemes bus who was charming.

overall, we felt a bit conned because of the change of route, but the guides saved the day

Purchased a two day pass and for an initial view of the city it was great. We had a great guide who was very knowledgable. The concept of using the bus for hopping on and off to get around the city is unreasonable due all of the heavy traffic congestion. Best part is that the ticket included the Thames River Cruise. Which is a great way to get from Westminster Abbey to Tower of London. Would take the tour again, but just for one day.

Get the pass and hop on and off when you want. A great way to see London and a lot cheaper than getting cabs. Some will have a real person giving tour info over the loud speaker and others will just be the standard headset with your choice of languages.

WOW! This was an even better experience than anticipated. This company is very well organized and on time. They have several stops all around London. The bus has an audio narration available while traveling from place to place. Once you enter the bus, you have the option to grab a Big Bus Map, much better than the one printed from their website, earphones, and a pancho if it begins raining. The staff was very helpful in explaining which stop would be the best to get off at for various attractions. Since I LOVED London so much, I will CERTAINLY be adding this to my next adventure. It was PERFECT! We got the 48 hour pass. OH, yea! You get a free River Cruise on the Thames River. There is so much embedded into the Big Bus Pass that you JUST CAN'T find a better deal or adventure.

Although I have a couple of grumbles I think this is the best open bus tour of London.

We joined the tour outside Kings Cross/St Pancras after we had dumped our cases at left luggage. The bus that picks you up there is a shuttle bus that takes you down to the pick up point to join the main tour buses. We were a bit limited for time so it was a bit disappointing that we spent 20 minutes parked up whilst a guide spoke to a child who was translating for his parents who spoke no English to get the best ticket deal. We then spent a further 10 minutes parked up because the wifi connection wasn't working for the guide to take payment from them. Neither family or guide seemed to realise that everyone else on the bus were getting a bit fed up at the long wait. Maybe - Big Bus people - ask them to get off the bus to sort it out next time so 40 odd people aren't inconvienced?

Oh and if one of your party is perhaps elderly or infirm you will need to ask the driver to wait until everyone is seated before they set off. My Mum couldn't make it up the stairs fast enough so had to sit downstairs until 3 stops later when loads of people got off/on and the driver couldn't set off so quickly.

Other than than that it was great, very detailed. The Blue Tour is the best and most comprehensive tour.

Did the hop on/hop off bus tour to get acclimated to city. Learned the history which we found interesting. Were able to see where the paces were that we wanted to visit. Guides very helpful and gave good suggestions to make the most of our visit. Buying attractions tickets direct from the bus staff saved time and sometimes money. Glad we did it for a day. You can buy tickets online for the bus ahead of time and in some cases save money. Bus stop map easy to follow.

We are currently in London for our honeymoon and decided to take a tour of the city on one of the tour buses offered around the city.
We are so happy we chose Big Bus Tour and got on the bus when we did. Tour guide Nuri and driver Paul was an awesome team. Nuri was really animated and very knowledgeable about London's history and current events. Paul drove at a good pace so that we could capture the beautiful views of London. Definitely a must do!

I just returned from London, my first trip in years so I wanted an overview of the city. With the Big Bus you get a double-decker bus, open-air on top and a knowledgable and entertaining guide. You can hop and off and a river cruise is included. Our guide was Shabby, she said she was fairly new to the job but you would never know it. She was great, full of historic and local information and humor. Shabby was obviously and justly proud of her city and we thoroughly enjoyed the tour. We stayed on the bus for the whole tour before hopping off. We got a late start so were not able to take advantage of the cruise.

If you only have one day in London, I would HIGHLY recommend this tour. You get to see the whole city I'm a few hours and feel like you haven't missed anything. We hopped on the bus at 9:30 am on a Sunday. We had read the reviews about traffic and congestion and didn't get it initially. Sunday morning is the perfect time to do this tour! I should have recognized this, when walking through Trafalgar at 8:30 on a bright sunny Sunday morning, there was not a person in sight. It was quiet and calm and unbelievable. London on an early Sunday morning had no traffic, no noise, no people. We completed the first half of the tour promptly. By 1pm, the bus slowed to a crawl and it took us over an hour to get from the Marble arch past Regent street. So, I would highly recommend this tour, as it is efficient and the guides excellent. But I would strongly urge travelers to consider an early morning on a weekend to get the most out of the tour without congested traffic. Also, consider wearing sunblock if riding on top of the bus as 3-4 hours in the sun, even with cloud cover, can risk getting burned.

Mpereau@hotmail.com

This is a good way to see the sights of London and then decide what you want to see and what you are just content to drive by. It also gives you an orientation to where the sights are located. Should you get a guide you don't like...problem solved, get off and get on the next bus that comes about 20 minutes later. A wealth of information is given on the tour about the history of London and its sights. If possible, buy your tickets before you go, there is a huge discount if you do so.

Want to make sure that you see all the "necessities" as a tourist in London ? The Big bus tours are not for the experienced traveller, but is is a good choice if you are not too familiar with the city.

I go to London frequently, but I took the tour anyway. The weather was awful (cold and windy and a touch of snow in the air) so a walk was out of the question. And I was positively surprised. OK, the tour passed most of the general "musts" - but also some other sights, for example one or two "new" bridges (from my point of view) and the more peripher parts of Kensington.

The ticket is valid for 24 hours, so you can hop on and hop of as much as you like. For example; if you want to hop off and see St Pauls, do so, or if a visit to Harrods or Victoria and Albert museum´is tempting, take a break and hop on the bus again afterwards.

Not cheap, I payed approximately 50 pounds. But it was convenient and worth the money.

We paid 30 pounds each for the tour. Blue bus includes audio guides for different languages. We thought it was very convenient and easy since we only have a day to tour the city. Hop on and hop off. It covers many major attraction sites.

You can easily buy tickets from the bus conductor at any bus stop designated for the bus tour. There is another competitor call the "original bus tour" which were also on every stop similar to this tour.

We had no problem with this service except that we waited very long at Tower of London Bus Stop. And it gets really crowded when the bus managed to come. It was after 6 in the evening.

Other than that, overall experience was pleasant but felt it was abit pricey.

This bus tour was really good. We were only in London for the day and wanted to see everything, and this did the job perfectly. Would highly recommend it to anyone wanting to see all the sights. Leanne our tour guide was excellent and very funny. Brilliant day out.

Joined the tour at Russell Square and enjoyed the tour round the City of London and surrounds and particularly the boat ride on the Thames. Excellent way of seeing the sights but at £30 a day some might baulk at the price. Things went wrong when we got to the interchange at Marble Arch and had to wait the best part of an hour to continue to Harrods. Staff at Marble Arch seemed as confused as us. We would do it again to see the parts we didn't reach, but probably try another bus company.

My daughter and I spent a couple of days in london to celebrate her birthday-we took the big bus tour so we could see everything.we intended to hop on and off but that was before we were lucky enough to get Ashley as a guide ( a blonde Scottish girl) her commentary was so good, funny and informative we stayed on for the whole tour. People are quick to complain these days so I want to make sure this girl gets the praise she deserves-everyone on the bus (top and bottom) was made to feel included and safety instructions were given without preaching -her tour was the hoghlight of our whole trip and my daughter is still talking about it!! Big bus bosses -give this girl a raise!!

As someone who has and is working in London for many years, this is a trip that I have always promised myself. The weather was sunny and dry, although a Sunday was probably the busiest day. The buses are clean, and the staff really helpful and most importantly there are many buses with this company. When you are waiting for a bus you may be offered other tours by other companies and they can be persistent. My advice, tell them to go away as this company is professional. We took the red tour and saw all of the main sites and as part of the ticket price you are able to use the City River Cruises which leaves from Westminster pier and this is also brilliant.
The commentators on board were both informative and entertaining. The tour really does put London in perspective. London is truly a magical city.

We were a group of 2 adults and 6 children. The headphones were great for the kids and kept them busy and well informed. We were lucky and it was a rain free day and the sights were absolutely beautiful. We live in London but this is by far the best way to see the sights up close and personal. The frequency of the buses was very good and the Big Bus tour was by and far the most popular of the bus tours. The river cruise was great and the guide recited many interesting facts about the local sights.

The staff were very friendly and helpful where needed. It was very easy to hop on and off whenever we wanted to. All in all we had a memorable and fun day out.

We used the Big Bus Tours this past week to visit London. We enjoyed the live audio tour (make sure to take the red line for that!) and all of the neat tidbits that we would never have known without our wonderful guides. The guides were very friendly and eager to help. We also liked that we could purchase tickets for other attractions from the bus - saved us from standing in lines! We would definitely recommend using the buses to our friends.

I booked online for myself and my two teenage daughters and was really pleased with the price I paid. We used the Big Bus Tour as our main transport in Central London and managed to cram loads of famous landmarks into our 2 day visit. Our first tour guide was Shabby who was absolutely fantastic. So friendly, accommodating, knowledgeable and most of all FUN! Her delivery of the facts was hilarious and left us not wanting to get off when we arrived at The Tower.
London is a fantastic city to visit but can be exhausting. I would never have been able to show my children so much of their capital city in our two short days if I had not been on the Big Bus Tour.

Have been on the Big Bus Tours twice now, we see it as a necessity when travelling :-)

Caught the Red Line this visit, and our tour-guide Duncan was lovely, really informative and full of fun interesting facts!

Would consider going a 3rd time to hear a different guide, but overall well worth the price for the 48hr ticket!

Have also enjoyed the free boat tour twice from Tower Pier down to Westminster, it's definitely a trip you'll love :-) even if the weather is a bit iffy like ours has been twice, sit at the top deck/outside as the views are simply too nice to miss :-)

Going on a Big Bus tour is a MUST! It's a great way to see the famous sights of London!! Can sit downstairs or at the front upstairs if it's cold or at the back upstairs if the weather is nice as it is open topped. Our tour guide - Nick - was hilarious and made the experience extremely enjoyable!

Enjoyed the hop on hop off tour. Unfortunately it was freezing when we went and that spoilt it slightly. Tour passes side of buckingham palace and you have to get off if you want to go see it. (we didnt and ended up walking there the next day) we were on the head phone bus and found it all in working order.

There are basically two main companies for open top tours of London and having been on both (Original in 2010 and Big Bus in 2013) I would recommend the Original Tour. The buses seemed far less frequent on the Big Bus Tour and when you're standing around in temperatures barely above freezing (in March!!) and see three buses for the other tour company go by you begin to think you've made the wrong choice. The sections where we got a live guide were good (though I preferred the live guide last time when I got the Original Tour) but the sections with the pre-recorded information was pretty poor and the sound quality was bad.

We got on the live commentator bus and were introduced to Shabby. What a great way to be introduced to a new city. She not only told us about every building and attraction that we passed but she had a bit of twisted humor that we enjoy. A little sarcasm; a lot of personality. Shabby and driver Nick (?) were a good team. At one point in our journey, she had her break and was replaced by an ok person. Later we switched to the blue bus that goes some places we wanted to see. That was a wholly different and impersonal journey. Lots of bad music to fill the ear time. Since it was not a warm day, we switched back to the red tour but sat down inside to warm as bit. The voice we heard, urging and promising people that it was actually warm up top, was Shabby. We went up to share the experience again.
Big Bus was an excellent way to be introduced to a new city and we highly recommend it to everyone visiting London the first time. It is a bonus if you have a commentator like Shabby.

I bought tickets to the bus tour because the bus stop was right outside our hotel. After walking by the bus stop and then buying the tickets online, I discovered that that stop was in fact closed due to the water main break on Regents Street. The stop had already been closed for a week before my purchase, but there was no sign on your bus stop, no warning when purchasing the ticket, etc, that it was the case. I think they should have informed me during the online purchasing process. Also it was difficult to hear the live announcer, but the buses using headphones with a recording were much easier to hear. I would suggest that big bus provide headphones, since traffic is loud in London, even when they have a live announcer.

We signed up for a 2 day Big Bus pass. It's a joke that it's called "hop on/hop off". It should be called "fight your way on to an over crowed bus, wait for it to go, get off, wait for the next bus to arrive while several fairly empty Original bus tour busses drive past". Miserable. It took 40 mins to go from Marble Arch, to the Tower of London. The included boat ride wasn't too bad. We skipped the second day and took the tube instead.

Had a great time with Big Bus Tours. Our guide Ashleigh was funny, engaging and very informative! We really enjoyed our time, despite the rain! They provided us all with rain ponchos that kept us dry. It's a great way to hit the sites of London and would definitely recommend them!

Had a good experience with the big bus tour, I thought Maybe the price was a little steep though.

You can hop on and off freely during the busses operational hours and also get a boat ride down the Thames thrown in! The tour guides were knowledged up well of the city, although some of the information was rather pointless (obviously to fill up a bit if time). Most if the tour guides were funny and enjoyable while lesser others who were a little more serious with rather dry humour. None the less had a good time using the big bus tour!
And they also knock a few bob off attraction tickets too

Definatly great for tourist hoping to see all of the attractions in London although most are within walking distance from each other if you have the time and energy.

My husband and I really enjoyed our trip to London, and the Bug Bus Company was one of the highlights. You can hop on and off at your leisure which suited us. They give you head phones on the blue bus so you can have a more guided tour. The red bus offers a very funny tour guide. It was pouring with rain so the Bug Bus Company left ponchos out for you to take. We looked like walking advertisments, but hey, at least we were dry! This experience exceeded my expectations (to be honest, I didnt expect too much) and provided a much more friendly and easy way to get around London.

When it's snowing outside an open top bus tour isn't the best idea but my family and I decided to tough it. We started on the top (must sit on top could barely see from bottom) with a hilarious tour guide who knew everything about all the sites. Then we had to switch buses as our first bus finished its part of the circle. This guide was just as great as the first but we got too cold and hopped off. We then got on a blue-line bus (red bus has live tour, blue is recorded) and when we tried to listen to it all we got was music. This tour is definitely something I would recommend for early in your trip so you can judge where you want to go as the trip continues.

We wanted to get a good basic overview of the city on our first day there, so we bought Big Bus tickets, and we were so glad that we did! It was such a great way to get our bearings and to see a lot of the major sights and buildings in one go. The live tour guide (I think it was Andrew) was hilarious. He provided interesting information as we went and mixed in plenty of jokes along the way. We learnt a lot in the couple of hours it took to do the full red tour. We hopped on the blue tour the following day and thought it was great that we could just keep hopping on and off at different places around the city over a 48-hour period. We also could have done a free river cruise as part of the same ticket, but we ran out of time. If you are going to London for the first time, this is a must. You won't be disappointed!

We decided to purchase a 2-Day Pass through Big Bus Tours for our Hop On Hop Off London vacation. This was definitely a mistake. We spend so much time waiting on the tour bus when we would see 3-4 The Original London Sightseeing Tour Bus while we waited for our bus. I would definitely not use this tour company next time I am in London.

Started our day at the Royal National Hotel. were met by Gee and his dad, what a double act they are quality yes they sell you the whole package but they tell you the truth. We had a great 2 days out on the bus and at the end they were still making us laugh. The big bus are lucky to have this pair,so funny.The tour is good you see all the major sights and the river cruise is good but Gee and his dad are the best.

We got 2 days for the price of one and the green link was right outside our hotel. Every morning we came out there were two different staff members and all were happy, helpful people. As we hopped on and off we never waited long for another bus. Thanks to the commentator 'Ricky' on the red tour as he made our day. His knowledge and quips were priceless. Our only negative comment was that they didn't run a little later as 4.30 it was still light.Would definately use this service again.

Booked the bus ticket and got 2 days for the price of 1.
The staff you meet at the bus stops agree other friendly's people I have ever met and must really enjoy their jobs as it was freezing the days we were there.
The tour guides on the "Red" tour were very funny and well versed in London history, which is the best combination for that role.
Thanks for making touring London a great time

We wanted a good, family-friendly tour as this was our children's first visit to London. The guides were informative and friendly. Our favourite was Simon, a fellow Liverpudlian, who cracked (bad!) jokes whilst providing interesting details, over and above the standard tour-guide patter. We didn't want to get off his bus. River cruises are included in your ticket and we travelled from the Tower to Westminster. The guide was a Thames boatman, his commentary was fascinating, informative and also sprinkled with jokes. we booked online and got a good deal. I would recommend doing this rather than buying from the many touts from several companies who, literally, pounce on tourists at the bus stops.

For me BigBus Tour was a good offer since I was there in December when they offered one extra day for the same price. Two days give a possibility to use their proposition to the maximum as additionally to their bus trips they offer several walking tours (at fixed time) and a river cruise. Unfortunately I missed walking tours so can't judge their quality. River cruise was alright - you can take it many times if you want as long as your ticket is valid. Though I did not expect a lot from this cruise - just a nice possibility to see the city from the river side. At night it was gorgeous.
As to the bus tour itself: I took both routes - blue (with an audio guide in different languages) and red one (with a live commentary of an English speaking guide). First I took the blue route in Russian - I would say that the recording is a pretty monotonous, up to being boring. Only my huge thirst for information was making me interested in it. But my thirst was not satisfied with that commentary - I really expected to have more informative tour. As for me they have a big room for improvement of their audio guide record (at least in Russian). Well, second day I took the red route - it was much more fun because of cheerful guide and his jokes. If you don't have a lot of side questions this tour may seem very good, if you're the curious one - be ready to stay with not answered questions. I didn't feel that the guide was ready to answer something beside his regular speech. But he always tried - giving a compensation to the information gaps by a good sense of humor.

For me this tour met my needs. I had one day in London to do the tourist thing, so this was brilliant for me. There are two two options, one bus with live commentary (red) and one with a pre recorded commentary (blue). The recorded commentary is provided in quite a few different languages and when you plug in your headset you can choose your prefered language. Where my hotel was located my option for pick up was the recorded commentary but you could swap over at different spots along the tour if you wanted. I bought my ticket from the hotel and just gave it to the Big Bus man at my stop who was helpful and directed me. Infact at the majority of stops I got off at there were Big Bus Staff there to help and direct you which was good. I was there in one of the coldest weeks in January but braved the cold and sat up on the top deck which had no roof which was brilliant for taking pictures! Take your winter woolies if you are going to do that in January! They give you your own headset and if required there were those throw away rain covers available as well plus you get a handy map. The thing I liked about this tour was that you could get on and off as much or as little as you wanted. Unfortunately I ran out of time to do the cruise which was thrown in but feel like I really got to see the sites in one day!

We took this tour following the suggestion of the B&B owner where we stayed. Good points are: the blue tour is in 8 languages and cover quite a big part of the city. It takes about 3 hours, therefore you get a good overview and can decide what to do afterwards, We had a 2-days ticket at the price of one. They also sell discounted tickets for the main attractions and for some of them you can use the fast track, avoiding the long queues and waiting time. But the trip on the Thames till Greenwich was a bit disappointing. They do it with City Tours, which uses very slow boats. The commentary was live but done by a non-professional guide. At the end they also asked for some gratuities. On the way back from Greenwich we started with almost 15 minutes because part of the crew went shopping and did not come back on time. No sandwiches were available on board any more, although it was 1 pm, so we took just some biscuits and chips.
There was no clear information about the first and last available bus at the point of departure (Paddington).
Overall: the blue tour is good, but if you wish to take a boat on the Thames, get another provider.

My friend Haley visited me from Ireland so I wanted to show her around London and Big Bus Tour delivered. Even though it was raining, we had a great time and got good pictures. Our tour guide Big Steve really made it an amazing experience. He was hilarious and really took the time out to talk to us and get to know us. His jokes were appropriate and hilarious. We were entertained the whole bus ride. He knew his information and delivered it in a way where it was not boring! He was so helpful and even at the end, he walked us to a great cozy pub and even had a chat with us there and told us places to visit. If you go on the Big Bus Tour make sure Big Steve is your tour guide!! highly recommend him!

We negotiated a slightly reduced rate for our family tickets directly with the conducters. This tour is superb. Fantastically friendly and informative drivers and tour guides. Free ponchos, maps and ear phones if required. Well done guys, this is well worth the price, hop on and off all day and buses are super regular. This was one of the highlights of our trip to London - many thanks.

I found the tour I was on was great, the staff both on the bus and in the office are extremely helpful. I would definately recomend this company and would use it again on my next visit to London, although hopefully in the better weather.

We had a 2 day pass and it was the best way to see London for the first time. It is an on off bus tour with live commentary. We also did the night walking ghost tour which was part of the pass. It was great! We misplaced our receipt (which is your ticket) and they usually make you buy a new one. We were able to show them the receipt from the purchase at the hotel (we purchased through the hotel conceirge) and they made an exception for us. We were lucky that they were so understanding!

I went to london with some friends for the weekend we wanted to see as much of london as possible and were advised that a bus tour was the best way to do that.we waited at the stop where numerous tour busses stop. There was one man standing there selling tickets he was from the big bus company he was very helpful and talked us through where the best points of the tour were. he also talked us through that our tickets were valid for two days and we could also go on a boat trip for free because it was included. (AMAZING VALUE). Whilst we were in the bus our guide (rikki) was fantastic he was full of knowledge about london he was friendly and interacted with everyone as they got on to the bus he was a brilliant tour guide :-). We went to the big bus tours shop on the second day to ask about the boat tour we were greeted straight away and had all our questions answered by a man called peter who was very helpful and friendly. I have nothing but good things to say about my whole experience with the big bus tours company and would definately recommend it to everyone of all ages :-)

This was a great tour and compares well with any bus tour across the world, the bus driver was very helpful. The guide he gave was brilliant. Price was a little high but the 2nd day was included. The sights of London are fantastic and the bus was a great vantage point to see them.

Whilst on a recent trip to London we decided to do a bus tour. We started early in the morning at Victoria, and we were advised that the whole tour would take approx 2.5 hours. Ours actually took 3hrs due to roadworks, but the guide was fantastic, and kept us entertained the whole time. The tour offers hop on/hop off at various stops and attractions, giving you great access the other sights. We did this a few times, and so ended up with different guides, all of which were great and had a fab knowledge about London. I would recommend starting early so as to not miss other options, such as walking tours etc. The ticket is valid all day, and can even be used the following day, and includes a boat ride. We also purchased Madame Tussauds tickets from the tour office at a discounted rate. As we are English we chose the live tour rather than the recorded tour, which is offered in numerous languages. Really good day, would definitely recommend. Having read other reviews which critise the tour as an ineffienct way of getting around London, please remember that this is a tourist attraction offering a tour of London, not an alternative to public transport!

This is a great way to orientate yourself in London and see key sights. I found the bus stop near Paddington Station easily and one of the Big Bus staff members greeted me and sold me a ticket before the bus arrived. He was very friendly and gave me an overview of the tours.

I did the blue tour and stayed on for the full circuit except for getting off to visit St Paul's Cathedral. I was able to buy a discounted ticket iform the very friendly Big Bus staff member when I got off the bus. I made a mistake getting on a bus doing the red tour but easily tranistioned back to the blue tour at a stop further on.

Overall a good experience and worth the £29.

Bought our tickets from the smiley and funny Tony Ryan outside Victoria Station - that was the first hint at the great staff we'd soon encounter.

Boarded the bus and ran straight upstairs despite the snow to get good seats at the front (glad we did as it got busy).
Our commentator was awesome, had us laughing from the first minute. Commentator changed after 10 mins but the replacement was just as great and knew something about everyone's home countries which is a skill!!

Very informative and little things like where certain scenes of a film were shot was brilliant to see.

Fully recommend them and the hop on, hop off ticket was useful as it also lasted 48 hours and included a river cruise free.

We had a fab but cold day in London in Jan. But the Big Bus Tour Company provide an excellent service. Informative guides, very help staff, they even let my daughter sit in the drivers seat to have pictures taken whilst we were waiting for the tour to start.
The buses run every 20 mins and you can hop on and off whenever you like.
This is by far the best way to see London in a day and then you can select which part you want to tour around.

doing the full tour on day one and the you do the hop on hop off after you know where everything and what you want to go back and see. The live commentary is good although one of the guys I was on a bus with kept saying the same phrase over and over which started to get on my nerves after 30 minutes.

Bought my ticket at Speakers Corner, very friendly staff, though not many of them seemed to be English! My ticket was £26 and valid for two days. Live commentary was very good. Saw all the sights and views from top of bus were great though it was very cold. Obviously that's not their fault...I just wanted the full view. I would recommend this to everyone. My only gripe has nothing to do with the tour but with one of their staff. I was at Gloucester Rd tube station and needed directions to my hotel. A young man with Big Bus (foreign, looked about 12!) was very helpful and looked up the address on his phone. But afterwards he said he was interested in having 'meetings' with me and that he was single. I lied and said I had a boyfriend. So, to recap, I recommend Big Bus tours. But if you're a single girl, not totally unattractive and are lost, run the other way if a wiry blonde East European working for them offers to help!!!

This tour bus is awesome! This is my second trip to London and the second time I've used this bus tour. It's my first time in London with my boyfrend so we took this bus. They have the best routes and their timing is more frequent. Seats are comfortable. Earphones are ok. We enjoyed the ride and the stops we did. The price is reasonable. I highly recommend this bus tour. This is definitely a great way to see the must see places of London in a day or 2.

Big bus tour London is really cool. We have done the red and blue tour twice and that was interesting every time. On the red tour, you have a live comment guide on the bus with you and they're interesting and funny (I can't remember the name of the first guide but the second, Ashley was really really funny and she shared her knowledge with us). Also, with the price (we paid £27/person) we have acces to the boat; So you can see London from the river Thames ! I strongly recommend Big Bus Tour !

The tour covers all the attractions in London and we could also buy tickets to the attractions from the bus company. We joined the Red Bus Tour and we really enjoyed Damian's commentary, he is very knowledgeable, friendly and clear. We missed the river cruise though but we will definitely do this when we visit the next time.

I'd done a bus tour years ago, when I first lived in London, but after 10 years away, thought it would be worth doing again when I had a day to myself.

Given that the Tube makes getting around so easy, doing this kind of tour by bus is a great way to see how all the parts fit together.

Was disappointed that I missed the walking tours, but was my own fault as I'd not planned well!

We only had a whistlestop tour as our time was limited so chose to go on part of the big bus tour.
It was very good and would recommend but for others definitely take your time to hop on and off over the two day ticket and go on the river.
Next time we will do just that :-)

best way to see london great value for money great way to see all the important sights and also included thames river cruise money off vouchers and free guided walks including the jack the ripper walk in the evening get off were you want then hop back on this really is the best way to see london and highly recommended miss it and regret it

This is a great way to get around London and see the major sights of the city. This is a hop on and off tour that provides audio as you tour around the city. They do offer tour guides on the Red route. I would highly recommend taking the Red route. We discovered Simon and Julian on our last day and received some interesting facts and stories from them. They were both very entertaining and learned more in the last 30 minutes of our time in London then we did in the entire weekend.

Need to be aware of the direction of when the buses travel when determining the order of the sights you would like to see. The ticket includes a river boat tour of the Thames River.

Had a better experience in Paris and Valencia, but enjoyed this attraction anyway.

In London, you may hop on/off a blue or red line bus. Red line has a live tour guide, "conductor", who will narrate and answer your questions throughout the trip. Blue line has the recorded tour.

When we first boarded the bus, we had a Great guide, who was very informative and animated. Unfortunately, after a few stops, there was a change in guides, and our second guy was droll and not very informative.

The price was a great. 37 pound per person..for two days and nights .We only wanted a one day tour, but, got a two day tour with an included Thames river cruise. If we had known that in advance, we would have maximized our use of this attraction.

We initially started with the Red Line, which I really liked, because there was the touch of a real person narrating and exchanging with the tourists. Unfortunately for us, we later got on a Blue Line bus, which was tragically littered and we had to contend with loud, obnoxious, and drug induced persons.....in short, the Blue Line had no control over malicious people who had no respect for others.

I found it astounding, that, when I took this same tour in Paris, France , and in Valencia, Spain, that there were no problems with litter and disrepect even though there was no guide to supervise..

Must say, that we Loved the Thames river cruise in the evening. The lights of the city were so beautifull! You may order light snacks and alcoholic beverages, and, depending on time of day, may take a round trip cruise of the Thames.

Definitely a great experience and bargain...just plan on where you want to hop on/off to maximize your time visiting London.

Do this one. It is a great way to see the main areas of London from an open top bus, with a guide commentating as you go.Lasts about 2 and a bit hours and you get a free river cruise thrown in with the price. Hop on hop off at any stop with buses arriving every 10 minutes at the stops. Ticket lasts 48 hours in the winter so you can use it on the tour bus and cruise boat as many times as you like during the 48 hours.

We had a great time in London on the Big Bus! I would have given five stars but just a couple of issues with the tour. A few of the drivers were a bit rude. Some stops go more than one way and they are not friendly when it comes to questions. Some drivers were great, others were beyond rude. I did not ask for the answer to an algebraic equation so I am not sure why they have to be so rude.

Towards the end of the night the buses got so full that it was almost unbearable. I really think they should run past 4:30pm as the last pick up at the Tower of London and other areas.

Having said that we still had a blast and saw a lot of London in one day. Although it may seem expensive, it really is a good value for what you get.

Very informative and excellent views from the top of the Big Red Bus. Good way to see some of London. You can jump off and on as many times as you like during the day so that you can visit different attractions.

We decided to do the tourist thing and take a bus tour when we first got into London and it was a great thing. We were able to get the lay of the land, quickly scope out the sights and then decide what we wanted to come back to see later in the trip. You can get on and off as often as you want. They have audio you can listen to as you drive by sights and get lots of history that way. We had a live guide for part of our tour and that was fun, he really added a great deal of insight to things. Good value for the money we felt, but it is best if you can make use of the full 24 hours. Just be sure you know when the buses quit running too so you don't get off someplace and then not have a bus to get you back to your hotel.

We only had a day and a half to spend in London. We chose to transport via the Big Bus tours because it saved us from having to figure out the subway or bus system. We got a two day pass for the price of one day, and we were off and visiting the most important sites in London. We had purchased tickets onine for the Tower, so we got off there, did the tour, then took the boat trip (included in the price) to Westminster pier, and then hopped back on the bus for Trafalger, Buckingham, and the west end. For our plans, it was a great deal.

And we chose Big Bus over their primary competitor because of the in person commentary afforded on the bus. Transportation and a tour guide; perfect.

The only drawback was that we had to wait about 20 minutes at Buckingham for the next bus. When we were done for the day we got off the green line shuttle by Russell Square and we were home. Very convenient.

It was my first weekend in London and we decided to do a bus tour to get as much sightseeing into the weekend as possible. And we never had to wait any longer than 5 minutes for a bus to arrive.

It was also very handy that we could buy tickets at the bus stops for attractions from members of the Big Bus Tours team, and they were all very helpful. Especially Alex at the London Eye boarding point.

Our guide Nobby and driver Alan were absolutely fantastic, Alan was driving at a perfect speed that we had enough time to take in what was being pointed out and take pictures. And the knowledge that Nobby has is just fantastic. My partner and my self were amazed, and he made it personal by asking where we were all from and adapting the tour as appropriate. When we hopped off the bus we were bursting with knowledge about the history of London. Nobby was a fantastic guide as it was obvious that he had a passion for his job and his home City of London.

I would recommend this bus tour to any Tourist wanting to cram as much into their stay as possible and improve their knowledge of the City!

Alex & James, Manchester.

Having done hop on hop off tours in a few cities, I must say that this one was a little disappointing. At nearly £30 per person, I can't really say it's good value for money. We spent a huge portion of our day either sat in traffic, or waiting for the next bus. We were over half an hour in the freezing cold at one bus stop. I was surprised at how stand-offish, rude and disinterested some of the staff were.
The tour was full of interesting facts about London. Though unfortunately we missed out of some of the information as our headphones kept cutting out.
Overall, a bit of a let down.

A terrific tour around the city ,although took longer than usual, owing to the volumes of traffic.One ticket was valid for 48 hours hop on and off, and also useable on trips to Greenich on the Thames.

What a great way to see the sights of London. Hop on and hop off all day long...well for two daya actually as your ticket is valid for 48 hours. We loved it, the kids loved it. We saw so much more of London than we ever have before, without getting tired and achy feet. A family ticket cost just £70, excellent value when you consider the unlimited travel. The price also includes a river trip which I can highly recommend as you get to see some magnificent buildings along the Thames.

This is one of the best hop on/off tour we did in Europe. We chose the live commentary which was terrific, with a very witty knowledgeable Irish guide. When we did hop on the audio bus, the commentary was in sinc with the route. Another plus was having tickets sold prior to the bus arriving...well organised! Take advantage of the river. Cruises too.. great views

This was my first trip to London and it was for business. I only stayed two nights and most of my time was already committed. However, I decided on the Big Red Bus Tour in order to get a quick overview of the city. I stayed on the bus for the full almost three-hour tour which covered all of the major attractions and provided bits of history along the way. I am already making plans for a vacation trip with my wife and I feel the Big Bus Tour has prepared me well. I would highly recommend Big Red Bus Tour for first time visitors as well as business travelers who want to explore this beautiful and historic city.

You arrive in London and what do you do first? Introduce yourself to the city by way of a Big Bus Tour. Hop on and off for two days, visit the sights, take a trip on the Thames. When the 48 hours is over you can then do as you please as you will have enough of an idea about what you want to see or re-visit to venture forth with confidence on your own.

With only a couple of days in London we prebooked a 48 hour ticket for the Big Bus. To get the most from this attraction you really need to plan ahead as it is difficult to get confused when in the middle of the hustle and bustle of the city. We used the ticket over the two days and experienced both the recorded and live commentary. The recorded commentary was a little out of date although quite informative. The live commentary is great and at least it matches the sights you are actually passing! We also took advantage of the boat trip included in the price of the ticket. This was excellent. The standard of the boat was very high and provided us with great views of London as we travelled down to Greenwich - highly recommended. At the end of our second day we joined one of the walking tours included in the price. The Ghost Tour wasn't at all scary and, although our guide did his best, really didn't capture the eerieness of some parts of the city. However, overall the price for the 48 hour ticket was great value for money.

Arriving on the 1st of nov. at Victoria coach station, not too long before 11am, we thought that having only just a few hours to spend in London, a touristic bus could be a good way to do it, it might be, we'll never know coz this was our first and certainly last time we'd experience London this way... anyway, it might be with another company but NOT NOT NOT NOT WITH THE BIG BUS TOUR!!!
Outside Victoria and after negotiation on the price, we thought it was fixed

We were in London from 23 May ( late arrival) to 25 May 2012( late evening), so lets say we had only the entire 24th and half 25th to see London!!

The Big Bus Hop On Hop Off was such a great choice we had, we were fun on & off at all interesting places we loved to visit. We started approx. 13.00 hrs. of 24th, as the ticket covered 24 hours after ticket activated so the next day we got up a bit early, took another bus and went to the places we missed on the first day. It was really worth to what we paid compare to the time we had.

Recommend to anyone who has limited time like us, this is good option for your London Visit.

This is a great, if expensive, way to spend a day in London and see all the sights it has to offer.

There were plenty of stops (30+), near most of the landmarks we wanted to see. The guides were informative and funny, and definitely made the trip more enjoyable.

Probably the biggest plus: there seem to be enough buses so that when you hop off/on you don't have to wait long for the next one. We waited about five minutes each time.

My only complaint would be that there are a few different routes (blue, red, etc.) and we were never sure exactly which we were on or exactly where our next stop would be. I would recommend confirming your route with the tour operator to ensure that your bus travels on your desired route, if you have one.

We had a short stay in London, it was my first visit, and it was a great way to bring the big picture to light. Dave was our narrator and Nigel our driver, they did a great job together (the young girl at the booth was very nice and helpful as well..unfortunately forgot her name), we had our tour on 9/12/12. I choose the guided tour with the human, not the recorded option, and it was great choice for Dave had a lot energy and made it interesting with his tidbits and style. I believe it is great way to see London, they offered a lot which we could not take advantage of due to our limited time there.

If you are going to do then bus tour I suggest you give yourself two consecutive days to do it to get your money worth. We bought the ticket on Saturday but had plans on Sunday and couldn't use our 48hr ticket for both days. It cost £29 for an adult, I think Original Tours were £26. You can hop on and off all day and see all of London. It was good but cold! They have connection points for earphones but it was better when we had a real tour guide he was called Patrick and very informative!

Go on a tour if in London. Great value for money and fantastic staff to come across, always friendly.
