With a commentry all the way around the routes they are informative and the ticket allows you to hop on and on the buses throughout the day so you can get off to explore and still have a valid ticket. Highly rate this company, it comes with a free river cruise as well. Bargain!!!

We were only in London for two days total so we decided to take a bus tour one afternoon. We were able to buy our tickets at our hotel and easily walked to one of the stops to hop on the bus. Our tour guide was funny and gave interesting information. It was nice to be able to hop on and hop off as we pleased.

The tour itself was very good, taking in all the major London sights, we thought it would be perfect for us as we were limited on time and still had lots to see. We asked the ticket seller on the bus how long the tour takes as we only had a max of 4 hours to spare, she said no problem at all that will give you plenty of time to do the whole tour.
We got on the bus at Harrods, it was pretty empty and we headed straight upstairs and got front seats, plugged the headphones in and off we went. It is a great way to see everything and the commentary was very entertaining and interesting, however when we stopped at Madame Tussauds we were told to get off the bus and join the one in front!
This turned into a fiasco as it was now pouring with rain and as the bus in front was already pretty full and no one wanted to go upstairs and get soaked our only option was to stand downstairs, we were not happy.
There were a couple of staff members at the bus stop who we voiced our concerns to and were met with the answer of "we can't control the weather". No one told us we would have to change buses and now because of the seat shortage we had to stand in the rain and wait for the next bus for 25 mins even though it was advertised that buses ran every 10 to 15 mins. Eventually after lots of bickering they let us onto the next bus so we could wait without getting soaked.
The next part of the journey was good and we enjoyed seeing all the sights but became anxious as it was now getting late and we were nowhere near the end of the tour. We had to get off at Victoria and jump in a taxi to get to our next destination as it was obvious we wouldnt get there within the 4hrs.
Overall the tour is very good but the customer service and organisation leave a lot to be desired. Of course they can't help the weather or the traffic but no one told us we would be thrown off the bus and left to stand for 25mins waiting for the next one and the guide should have been honest in telling us the length of the tour.
If you are thinking of taking the tour on your next trip to London, make sure you have a completely free day and allow lots of time and be prepared for some standing around.

This was our first time visiting London so we opted for a 2day package. Great value and was perfect for people touring around and visiting aimlessly! The staff that were at the stops including the bus drivers were all approachable and friendly. I assumed the staff would be a bit unhelpful since they deal with painstaking questions and probably the same ones over and over on a daily basis, however I was wrong (thankfully!). This was a perfect way to get around the sights and also get some commentary and we also took advantage of the free Thames cruise which was interesting and a beautiful way to see London Bridge. Again the staff were informative, friendly and funny!
This was an easy way to get around - thank you!

Had a great time on the bus! Steve was so informative and funny. We were told the history of London and the history of the London's famous sayings and phrases. I was a bit worried about taking the tour, but with the two days for one and the boat tour included, it was WELL worth it. I highly recommend taking the tour to get an understanding of this great city. So hop on, say what's up to Big Steve, hop off, and Bob's your uncle!

Big bus tours are a great way to get round London and see the sights. £50 for an online ticket for 2 adults and a child which was valid for 2 days and a river cruise. Use the map and plan where you want to hop on and off. Blue tours have headphones for recorded commentaries and red tours have a guide on bus. We did a mixture of both. Go upstairs to the front of the bus if the weather is not great for the best view whilst staying warm and dry. Would thoroughly recommend.

We managed to get a good deal (2 people for £40) as it was raining but we hopped on and grabbed our free poncho anyway. The tour guides were genuine,y funny and interacted with the passangers. We learnt a lot about London and were entertained throughout. We found out about off the beaten track shops and local places to eat which enhanced our London trip beyond the bus tour itself.

The boat trip is fairly short but it is another great way to see our capital city, it was breaks up the bus riding journey. I have used this company for tours a number of times over a number of years and it is not just the same stuff repeated. Each time I learn new facts about London and find hidden gems thanks to the excellent staff. This is by far the leader in open top busses in London.

For £25 we got two days " hop on, hop off" use of the buses, plus use of the ferry to Greenwich. This was excellent value and the staff on all the buses were wonderful, informative and entertaining. We would recommend this service to anyone thinking of seeing the sights of London.

My sister and I got the two day pass for the Big Bus on our first two days in London, and it was extremely helpful. There are two lines - red and blue - one which is recorded and one has a live person. We found the one with the live person much more enjoyable and used the bus to get to and from several stops in the two days we had access. The map provided was helpful, and we never had a problem finding a stop to catch the next one, which was only usually minutes away. They position staff at each bus stop so if you don't have a ticket yet, you can buy one on the spot, or they can help you determine which way the bus is going, since some stops are two different ones combined and go off in two different directions. It was definitely worth the money.

A good tour to do if you would like to see the sites. Nice friendly staff and good buses. Everything is explained well and no problem to do the hop on hop of as it's never a long wait for the next bus.

We did this tour on the last morning of our stay due to the weather being good. £26 seems a bit pricey but for this time of year is valid for 48hours and also inlcudes a Thames river cruise and walking tours. Plus a couple of slightly different tours to do. You can hop on - hop off at any of the stops. We decided to stay on the bus and do the whole tour which was just short of 2 and a half hours. The bus we were on had recorded commentary but on certain buses there is live commentary with a guide. Definately the best way to see all the sights of the city!!

We went on the Big bus tour at the beginning of October 2012, having pre-booked our tickets on line £20 per adult instead of £24 on the day.
You have to print your e-ticket and give to the Big Bus tour agent, he then gives you the proper bus tickets.
The tour we went on was the BLUE route which takes in all the major sights of London , plus some extra ones that I knew about but had never visited.
You get free earphones to plus in which gives you a running commentary as you pass the sights plus history as well.
You can hop on and hop off this bus at any of the stops the bus stops at, then hop back on once you have visited the area you got off at.
You can also get discounts to enter many of the attractions on the route.
Added bonus is you get a free River cruise on the thames giving another view of the city.
When we went the ticket we had bought was for 24 hours but had been up graded to 48 hours so any one wanting to see London but not able to do everything in one day is perfect for them.
Make sure you go upstairs though as you get a much better view, but can be cold so make sure you are prepared for this, plus a umberella, although they do give you a free poncho if it should rain.
We was luck enough to see the Tower bridge open to let a war ship come through just as we started our river cruise

The big bus tours are very famous in london for all the write reasons! These buses give you a tour of the entire city and explain the history of places such as tower bridge! Also with a two day big bus tour you get a thames river cruise free! The thames river cruise is also very good. I combined by 2 day big bus tour with shopping trips, river cruise and the london pass! This saved me the commuting expenditure!! there is no need to take a bus/tube.

Traveled to London with my 19yo son - loved the Big Bus tour! The tour gave us a great overview of the city. The best part of the tour, however, was the walking tours. We took part in the Harry Potter tour, the ghost tour (and pub stop!), and the tour to see the changing of the guard. The walking tours were free with the bus tour -- fantastic!

Took the option of the 24 hour Hop On, Hop Off tour, and split this over two days. Clearly the bus only goes one way round, and accessing the stops we wanted wasn't always convenient, and we ended up seeing some areas twice in order to reach the destination we wanted. One of the live commentators was very good, clear and had a quirky sense of humour, but on the first day our guide was less verbally clear. Overall the information we heard was pretty good. We kept to the Red route, but the Blue route has more stops for those wanting to travel further. We struggled to get our on-line ticket made into a proper ticket as some stops that should have been staffed weren't, so I had to jump off the bus at one point to get a proper ticket, after the driver helpfully let us aboard till such a person could be accessed. Overall useful, and helps with London layout. We didn't bother with the river cruise, as we'd done one separately so can't comment about that inclusive option. Overall O.K. but check out other bus company's routes before booking, as some might suit travellers better than others, e.g. maybe pass nearer your accommodation.

This is the best way to see London. If you can, buy a 2 day ticket so that you have plenty of time to stop off along the way and to take the cruise down the Thames that is included in the ticket. Take the Blue line where there is audio in 8 languages available thru the free headphones. Staff both on the bus and at various stops were terrific. Dress warm because the tour takes a long time. You will see all of what London has to offer and enjoy the view without a worry about traffic or wearing out your shoes. There is a feeder green line that takes you from Euston and Kings Cross to connect with the red and blue lines.

I highly recommend this tour of the highlights of London. Our tour guide, Ashley, was very knowledgeable and entertaining. There were many stops where you could hop off and view the sights in that particular area. This is definitely the way to see London.

Check around first before buying ticket. Â£29 for one day on the bus and tourism services center. Â£25 for two days from London Travel Information (this is different from the tourism services center , please be careful!) I bought my two days ticket from London Travel Information. But I was told that it is only Â£16 from London Tower.
Traffic in London is very bad. Please don't use the big bus as transportation

The hop-on/hop-off bus tours are an excellent way to get a good overview of any city and see where the places are that you want to visit. We rode it for its complete circuit and then did the hop-off/hop-on at the places we wanted to visit.

Although this way of getting around london is rather expensive, it covers all the main tourist sites and offers loads of historical facts, if the bus you get on has a guide. Ours was quite funny and made the trip all that more enjoyable. It was easy to get off when you wanted and then catch another on to the next port of call. The guides are very well informed and welcome questions from tourists (especially americans) although I was a bit puzzled about a few answers, I dont remember being taught those particular things in history. But they lapped it up.
As we didnt have a lot of time we were unable to stop off at all the things we wanted to see, but we will be back next year to see what we missed, and will be using the Big Bus Tour again.

We had a fantastic day out this summer (2012). We had a quick tour round Madame Tussauds and then hopped on the Red tour bus. The commentary was great and we actually learned quite a few things - like, the mileage to London is measured from the statue of King Charles I in Trafalgar Square and that the Swiss flag is square rather than rectangular shape....... We had such good weather and managed to be on the top deck every time we got on. We loved the river cruise too, although the wait was a bit more than the 'every 15 mins' it was billed to be. I think we were in a different queue and it wasn't clear which boat to get on (Greenwich or Westminster?). Anyway it was excellent and again the commentary was entertaining in places (they do tout for tips at the end). We missed a loop of the route so we got back on and completed the north/city loop. We enjoyed the views and the sunshine and being out and about in the wonderful city of London. We definitely took all that was on offer and enjoyed our day out. We started at 10am and got home at 9pm so a long day but really worth it. The booklet of vouchers was very useful too as we got a discount on our food bill. A great day out. Thank you Big Bus Tours.

OK - it may be cheesy and touristy but every time I go to London the Big Bus tour is the first thing I do. Although this was my sixth visit, there's no better way to see the city - or get reacquainted with the city - than atop a double decker bus zooming around the city (hopefully in the sunshine) I learn lots of new facts and details about my favourite city everytime!

My family and i have just come back from spending 4 days in london. My 2 daughters had not been before, so while we were there we thought a good way to see all the sights was with the big bus tour. It cost about £50 for a family ticket for the whole day, you just hop on and off where you like. There are lots of stops at the major attractions and the guides give a great amount of information, they cater for about 8 different languages which i was impressed with.We went 22nd of August and never had to wait in any big ques and the drivers were very helpfull. Al the staff we met from the company were very polite too. When we visit london again we will certainly be booking it again its a great way to see the capitol and hear all the history.Remember if the top deck is full it still works out very reasonable sitting on the lower deck at such a great price to get you around for a day!

You really have three options to get around London. 1) Underground-cheap but you don't see anything 2) Taxi-expensive and only gets you from point A to B 3) Big Bus Tour-which takes you to all the high points with commentary along the way. For a family of 4 it will cost about $120 but you can get on and off the buses at premier locations all day long and while you are on the bus they will provide you all the information of sights you pass along the way. Very Good if you only have a couple of days to see London.

I dont think it really matters what company you use to tour London. The buses are the best way. My only complaint is that the boats they provide need to be sunk. They stink, they are hot and old. Avoid them at all costs! They herd you in like cattle and give you no air, not even working windows. The bus ride is good, better with headphones(blue buses) than with live guides. You will tire of their corny jokes very quickly. (red buses) they do provide free rain ponchos on buses which is great.
over all, I probably would check out a different company because of the condition of their nautical fleet!

The bus tour was a great way to not only see, but learn about the many attractions in London. The tour guides were knowledgeable and funny. It was convenient to get on and off the bus at different stops. Check out the Cheshire Cheese Pub. Great suggestion Brendan, thanks!

This was, by far, the best way to see London. The tour hits all of the major attractions, as well as the hidden spots. The option to get off the bus, explore a little, and then jump on another bus along the route made for a wonderful day in the city. The guides were, of course, very knowledgeable about the history of the city, and quite witty as well.

Whilst having both of my adult children visit me in London recently, I took them each on a bus tour to familiarise themselves of the landmarks of London. We chose the blue route & it was very poor. The commentary was weak on information, with irritating fill in music & it was difficult to find bus stops.
I only good comment is it has comfortable headphones.
Better to go with a more Original bus tour

I meandered over to Marble Arch/Speaker's Corner/Hyde Park and got the bus there...I was cordially met by a Michael Mitchell who was kind , charming and gracious and answered all questions- not only for the people getting on the bus, but other tourists who were asking about bus routes, and the Underground. This gentleman is very much the KING OF HYDE PARK as he helps tourists, gives directions and ample guidance.
The walking tour was done by a slightly rotund young man who put his whole heart and soul into the tour- he was ready to answer questions, help everyone and went out of his way to really provide an entertaining walk around London....I would have liked to have taken more walks with him, but had to catch a plane...you can be sure I will look up both these individuals the next time I am in London ! Wonderful time !

We did an extended loop with "Big Phil". The tour guide definitely makes or breaks the experience. "Big Phil" was terrific and very patient with my tired toddler. Loved that the tour also included a Thames boat tour and that we had access to the Big Bug for 48 hours. Didn't do too much hopping on and off but did enough to know that a good guide gives you your money's worth. Probably wouldn't rate the tour as high based on the other guides we had.
Had a brilliant day today sightseeing in London! The big bus tour allowed us to see so much more than we could have fitted in walking or using the tube! Recommend this to everyone.

For a family of four I think the Big Bus Tour is the best way to see the sights of London when you first get there. We did this and were very happy with the ride. We took the bus with the live guides who were both very funny and approachable. We really liked the hop on/hop off feature as we used this to take our trip on The London Eye and get back on the bus an hour later. There is lots to see and do in London and this tour lets you see the best sights that you can decide to go back to later.
Easy hop on and off. Great when you get a good tour guide!! We were surprised that the service stops at 6. We were let off at the furthest spot from our hotel.Good walk back though!

Congrats , This way around London is well worth the time, plenty of stops throughout the journey, you can just hop on hop off where you like
Highly recommended
A very good way to see London you can hop on and hop off where you like but the seats upstairs are very hard!!

Purchasing tickets online before we visited London was an excellent idea. We were able to catch the bus with no trouble and saved ourselves money by doing this. The hop on hop off tour buses are perfect as tickets are valued for 24 hours and you can visit any attraction and then continue in the tour again. Well worth it.

The buses don't leave frequently, and there is a lot of waiting around at certain stations. There was a protest in London the day we were there. We asked several drivers and station attendents what route we should take to avoid the protest, and each time, they assured us the bus would avoid the protest. However, we were taken in a loop twice to get around the protest. What a waste of time. I realize the protest is not the Big Bus fault, but they need better info to give their customers. We were only in london for 2 days, and spent the better part of one day going in circles because the drivers and station attendents didn't know what they were doing.
Every time I was waiting at a stop, I saw the other companies busses stop by so frequently, comparing to this one. I will not go for big bus tours next time.

Three of us did the Big Bus Tour on 20th June 2012. We used the Blue route buses which have prerecorded audio commentary. We found all staff were helpful with advice on bus times and any route/bus-stop changes due to road works/Olympic preparation. The audio was fairly basic, but covered all main landmarks/places of interest and was certainly good enough for most tourists. If visitors prefer a more detailed guide, the Red route buses with 'live' guide may be better or buy a good guidebook.
Traffic was busy and so progress was slow at times, but there are a number of roadworks /Olympic preparations going on in Central London, so we just sat back and enjoyed the ride.
I think it is unfair to blame the tour bus driver for delays (as in some previous reviews) as he did best possible in traffic and all stops were efficiently done. However, full tour will definitely take longer than two hours at present, so allow plenty of time and relax!
Prices were comparable with other tour bus operators and are cheaper if you buy tickets in advance online.
One the whole a good day out and enjoyable way to get around.

I have been on tour buses in many great cities in the Europe, Big Bus Tour London is the most expensive but inefficient one I have ever come across.

Last year my parents came to visit, I took them around London by foot, I have been to London many times and know quite well of the city, so I showed them the most interesting bits of London. However, after a tour to Edinburgh, we took a sightseeing bus (cost less than £15/pp) which my father found it was quite informative. So he said next time when he come to London, he would like to see London on a tour bus (also by their age, walking around in London for hours is not ideal)

Because none of them speak English, so I could only find the Big Bus Tour that provides the language they understand. I looked up the routes which seem perfect – three routes that go to all the attractions and also include boat travelling on the Thames!

£29 pp x 4 is really not cheap but I thought if we can take the bus for a round and then go on the boat and then take another round, it would be worth it!

For goodness’ sack, the bus was so slow!!!!!

It almost took five hours to get a round, when past the Tower of London, we show a massive queue queuing for the boat, (boat is every 30min, you could wait for hours to get on!), so we didn't bother to queue up.

To be fair, it was a Saturday so maybe the bus would be quick or less people queue for the boat during the weekdays?

But, the part that let down the most was the information it provides, to many places, the audio explanation was just a few simple sentences tells you a name of the street or place or list of people who was buried where... when I see a place I could come up more interesting stories than it does!

The bus was so slow and the information was too little, most time you just sit on the seat staring at a building listening to the same music through the headphone over and over again...

We only managed one round....

I think the reason why it’s expensive may be because it has a red route which provides a live guide, it could be more entertaining than the boring audio tape – but the problems is it’s not every one come to London that speaks English to understand a live guide! They should have two prices and to make the boring audio tour buses (blue route) cheaper!

One good point – it provide rain coat, which quite convenience consider the weather in London...

The Big Bus Tour provided audio commentary through ear buds as we passed each site of note. Unfortunately, my son's ear audio did not work in his seat at the top front of the bus. He plugged his into the audio behind him until other passengers boarded and need them. We shared one set of ear buds after that. Still, it was a wonderful way to get an idea of which sites we wanted to explore while in London. I took the Thames River experience while my son visited the London Aquarium. We learned about the flotilla in honor of Queen Elizabeth's Diamond Jubilee two days before our arrival. The guide did a good job of pointing out sites along the river. Unfortunately, several ladies sitting in the seats behind mine decided it was a good time to visit with one another in loud voices the entire river trip.

This is a great way to get an overall view of London and some history , but THE BEST is the guided tour, with a live person. We took the tour May 11,2012, we sat on top ,the only way to go, and we had Ashleigh- she was a blast, very fun and informative.We were sorry we got off at the Tower of London because the next BB we hopped on was a recording with headphones. This was very boring compared to Ashleigh. So, if you are so lucky as to get someone like Ashleigh narrating, don't get off. Get the 48 hr tour go back next day and hop on and off.

I guess they need to sell tickets even when there is a major event on and many of the roads are full. I bought my ticket from Marble Arch as there was no mention of delay or route changes. However, on the tour, I found out about the "Trooping of the colours" at Buckingham palace which was great. But such an event meant waiting around to see the glimpse of the parade. so it took well over an hour. Then getting back to the stop it was an eternity before another bus came. When one finally was about 40m from the stop, it didn't get to the stop after waiting for 20 minutes becasue of the traffic. so I caught the tube to Waterloo on the other side of the city to meet up with the bus again. The on street guy was very good, but a group of us was waiting for 40 or so minutes, before the poor guy was told they had diverted buses from his stop. So again he was good, and he personally took us to the next stop. These guys are all equipped with radios, but they don't relay the information to those poor guys at the stops.
I found all throughout the day that the BB company buses were very late always. If I did this type of tour again I would go with the Original Bus company. They seem to have 5 buses to one at every stop. It may be a touch more expensive, but it would be worth it. Another thing BB have are walking tours that go from Trafalgar Square, Note to this company. Put the times for these tours on the website. There were in my opinion a lot of very preventable mistakes.
But it is a great way to get an overview of London.
If you don't know what English sense of humor is, a Big Bus tour guide could be a very good start to learning all about British sense of humor, mate!
On your first day in London be sure to do the Big Red Bus tour. It takes several hours and you can jump off for lunch.

We had taken the on/off bus in Dublin and had a fantastic time using it. We pretty much covered the whole city in a day seeing many attractions. Our London experience was a tad less positive. Given London's size and traffic congestion, the big bus lumbers along at a snail's pace while the commentator tries to keep you interested by describing various buildings or historic sites. After sitting in traffic for ~1 hour to reach the Tower of London, the commentator's comments had started to turn into mush. My recommendation is to skip the on/off bus and use the tube. We did that another day and saved a ton of money and time. I put a london tube app on my iphone and that helped a great deal to navigate.

I took my 7 yr old daughter out of school for the day to show her how magical London really is. We live in west London but are always reluctant to go "up town" as it is usually so busy! This was perfect for us.

I chose Big Bus Tours after reading all the reviews and I think they have the most buses. Our guide was Charlotte and she told us lots of interesting and funny things about London that we would never had known if we had done it ourselves. In addition to the usual rubbish tourist fodder of Madame Tussauds etc. she also recommended other simple things to do like pony rides in Regent Park and recreating the Zebra crossing scene on the Beatles' Abbey Road cover (although she did mention this usually upsets the local taxi drivers). The staff we met were all friendly and helpful and the commentary on our bus was well rehearsed, funny and informative and the free boat ride was good too. It certainly gave my daughter of an insight to her fantastic city and left us all wanting to go again.

It was a great day. Even though this was £20 for an adult ticket online it was the best value of the bus tours as it included the boat ride. You can use the buses all day and they are everywhere so if you have £20 to spend it is a much better idea than just going on the London eye for just 30 minutes!!

Good for first timer as we can explore London. Just hop on and hop off wherever & whenever we like to stop. Excellent & funny guide that gives informative explanation.
After riding this bus, we know at least where to go, then we cath buses/tube on our own.

I took a Big Bus Tour and had Ashley as a tour guide and literally she was the best. She was hilarious and really knew her stuff! I wish I had got on sooner so I could have listened to her more! Seriously though I have come to the conclusion that we are the same person. We have the same exact humor and I love her. Go Ashley and Paul as the driver!

Spent a great afternoon on one of the Big Bus tours, covered all the areas and attractions with loads of interesting information from their live English commentary guide. So much to see in London and a great way to see it and learn about it all.
Just loved it all! Hop ins and outs! London bridge, buckingham queens palace, citycruises and london eye!! Name it all

The tour was just great! We booked it for 2 days, and were able to hop on and off with ease. Use the Red Bus, to get a person to tell you what is going on - and the history - while you are on the bus.

Best thing that we booked, on our stay in London

this is a great way to see the city..BUT..the traffic in London makes it a very slow way to see it!
it took us an hour and a half to get from Harrods to Madam Taussads ..we had almost lost the will to live..sorry big bus tour..if you dont have much time to spare and you want to get around quickly..use the underground..hate to think what it will be like during the summer for the Olympics..

A great family experience, to take in all the sights but without incurring sore feet!! Having visited London many times, seeing it by bus enabled me to put all the pieces together (whereas by tube, this feels virtually impossible!). The audio guides were particularly good, offering historical pointers and useful background info - the children loved it! Good value, when you consider that the ticket also includes the river cruise and walks - we didn;t make the most of this, so if you just do the bus tour, it is a pretty expensive way of getting round the City.

I recommend taking the Big Bus Tour when arriving in London. If you can move through the city on Sunday it is the best day rather than Saturday. Saturday might be the worst day to try and take a bus tour due to all the traffic. Sunday was a better day. There are plenty of buses that arrive about every 15 minutes. However, keep in mind once you hop off the bus, it may be difficult to find a good seat when you 'hop on'.

The bus tour is fantastic to get an overview of the city. If you are going to 'hop on/hop off' you should consider extending your ticket for 48 hours.

We used Big Bus Tours two day ticket. Great way to hop on and off to see the sites. Helpful and friendly Guides were at each Big Bus Stop assuring you got on the right bus. This feature was something I had not seen in other big cities (Paris). Ear phones with commentary was informative. Rain ponchos were given on a day that was expected to rain. Would use them again.

We used the Big Bus Tour to get around for the two days we spent in London. It was nice to be able to jump on and off the bus whenever you wished. It was also nice to be able to see many of the major sights (Big Ben, The London Eye, Tower Bridge etc.) on route. The staff was very nice, and you learned much about the history of the city while you were driving. The main problem that we had with the tour was how slowly we moved, and how often we had to sit in traffic. I think that with such a short period of time, next time we might just take the tube to save some time.

You can hop on/hop off these buses at whatever spots you like, and if you stay on, you get quite a view of London's attractions without necessarily having to visit them on their own. We only had a couple of days in London and we wanted to make the best of it, and these buses were worth it. They're narrated quite well, and you feel safe while on board. There are different routes you can take so you aren't stuck with just one.

Brought my mum down to London for her very first time, and because she is bad on her legs thought I would buy tickets for the Big Bus Tour. My mum really enjoyed this bus seeing everything from the top of the bus, without having to get off.
Even though I had been to London many times, and had seen many of the sites, i really enjoyed this too.

We only had 2 days in London and the Big bus was a great bargain. It costed $100 for 2 of us. We took the Thames river cruise and the Beatle walking tour, both or which were included in the price of the bus. It was convenient and entertaining. It was the way to go in London.

We took a Big Bus tour on our first day in London and really enjoyed the service. We joined the red route at Green Park and stayed on that bus until we approached Westminster Bridge the second time. Mike was the commentator and Simon was the driver. We applaud Simon's driving abilities in London traffic. Mick spoke well and kept us entertained though as a first time visitor the facts did begin to blurr after a while. That is London's fault. We had no idea how HUGE it is but the tour enabled us to get our bearings.

We took the river cruise from Westminster Pier and rejoined a different bus heading back to Westminster. We got off a second time, this time joining the masses of tourists walking across the bridge. We got yet another bus as far as Victoria Station and then a 'blue route' bus on to Notting Hill. The commentary on the blue route is good as well but we would recommend the 'red route' if you are able. The included river cruise made the total cost seem more than reasonable.

We were in London over the Easter weekend and before we went we were deliberating over which bus tour to take - we ended up booking Big Bus Tours because they also offer the River Cruise and Walking tours as part of their package - and they offer a discount for booking online! Arriving at the Baker Street stop armed with our printed ticket vouchers we were met by a staff member who issued us our 24 hour tickets for the bus and because we were native English speakers recommended that we get on the Red Line as it had a live commentary. The Red Line buses are slightly more infrequent than the Blue Line buses but we still only had to wait around 6 minutes before one came along. Our first guide of the day was fantastic - very informative and witty, I wish I had caught his name as he would be worth recommending. Our other two guides that day were also good. We got on the bus around midday and thoroughly enjoyed our tour that day - hopping off at the Tower of London and Oxford Circus. The following day as we still had time on our ticket we got up early and got the River Cruise from the Tower of London to Westminster and then got the Blue line bus out to Kensington. The recorded commentary on the Blue line was also very informative and almost as good as the live guides! We absolutely loved our travels on the Big Bus Tours, from the sightseeing to the customer service and frequency of the buses. A brilliant way to explore London and we cannot recommend them enough!

We went to London Easter weekend and just had to do the Big Bus Tour would not have missed it for the world spent 3 hours touring and listening to a well informed and funny tour operator included in the price was a cruise on the Thames which we took from the Tower Bridge got back on at Westminister a full day was very enjoyable got around London quicker than on foot and saw more we even got a little book of vouchers for events and places some were for free entry others were money off could use these througout 2012 great value for money at £29 would highly recommend you can get off and hop back on was valid for a full 24 hours so depending on when you purchased ticket could even use the next day

It was my first time in London and I felt that taking the Big Bus Tour would be a great way to get a feel of the city and I was right. For a reasonable fee we were able to see all of London and if we wanted to get off and visit a certain site then we could. They have either a tour guide or an recording that tells you what you are looking at where you are and the history surrounding it.

We had a day pass for the Big Bus Tour, what can i say, the staff were sooooo friendly. the service recieved was great and every one was so helpful.. the commentary was excellent and without showing my age the younger commentators were knowledgable and very interesting to listen to. the river cruises that were included were will worth going on and again the crew gave an informative and interesting talk. BIG THUMBS UP

I highly recommend you take the Bid Red Bus tour the first day you arrive in London. Not only will you get a great overview of the city but this bus will then serve as a basic form of transportation for the next 24 or 48 hours. You should purchase the 48 hour ticket which gives you 48 hours of transportation from the time you buy the ticket. After we took the tour we used the bus to get to back and forth various tourist sites. Along the way we had different guides and each had a interesting story to tell. On the second day we took the river boat from the London Tower dock to the Parliament dock. This was included in the price of the ticket.

Did the Big Bus Tour on a cold but sunny day in February. It is a fantastic way of seeing most of the great sights of London in a very short time. You can get on and off the bus at any of the many stops to take in your favorite sights in detail. Got to sit on the open upper deck for a great view. Highly recommended.

Although I live in London, my 84 year old father in Yorkshire suggested that we do the bus tour. I booked online and received a decent discount for booking a specific date in advance. Luckily, we were gifted with a sunny warm day for March.
We picked up the tour at Aldwych and chose the Red Tour with English commentary, we were able to hop on and off the buses at will whenever we fancied a break for a drink or food.
The commentary overall was very good, with many places of interest being pointed out to us, some that even I was unaware of.
My father particularly enjoyed it, a good way for him to see London without it being too strenuous.
The tour price also included a river cruise and the options of several guided walks which we did not take up.
Another good point to note is that the ticket is actually valid for 24 hours from the time you first board the bus, so if you only use for an afternoon, you still have the option to continue your tour the following morning.
It's a great way for a visitor to London to get a feel of the place and decide what they would like to see in more depth at a later stage.

We had limited time to see all of the sights in London and couldn't decide what to visit. We opted for the Big Bus Tour and that was perfect. The tour was narrated and brought us by all the main attractions (Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, Westminster Abbey, Tower of London and so much more). You could also hop off and back on another bus if you wanted to spend more time at one particular attraction. Great way to get a little bit of everything.

Being first-timers to London, we were recommended to try Big Bus Tours by our hotel Concierge. He indicated that it takes us to or past all the major attractions in the city and provides either live tour commentary or via earphones (provided by Big Bus), access to 9 different language audio tours. The tour allows you to jump on or off at the various stops to investigate further and found that the buses stopped at approx. 15 - 20 min. intervals. There were 2 kinds of buses - the Blue Bus which had recorded audio tours and the Red Bus which has live commentary tours. The Blue Bus seemed more plentiful but either bus would give you good information.

We originally purchased a 1 day pass but when we turned in our voucher from the hotel for a Big Bus ticket, the Tour company asked if we would want to extend our pass for an additional day for only 5 pounds more - we did that and were glad that we did as there was so much to see in London. The extra day gave us a bit more breathing room to be able to see so much more and thankfully, the weather was pleasant enough to ride atop in the fresh air.

We also used the tour as our transportation around town - the city was getting ready for all the Olympic visitors and had shut down the central tube line, so had we not had easy access to the Big Bus, we would have spent a lot more on taxi transport.

A couple of things - do not lose your voucher because you have to show it to get on. The whole tour takes approx. 3.5 hrs. so make sure you allocate the time if you want to get back to where you started - it is not quick. The last bus leaves the Main Marble Arch area at approx. 4:30 p.m. so pay attention to the time of day if you are counting on the bus to get you back to where you need to be!

We went on the Big Bus Tour in London, as it was still classed as winter, we got 48 hours.
It was very handy as we were able to buy the bus ticket & the London eye tickets at a discounted price from the bus stop at Green Park.
We were able to see a lot of the sights but it was a pity that it ended at 4.30, still we could not complain as we did get is for 48hrs for the price of 24 due to the early closing time.
There are three different routes, Red, Blue & Green. Red & blue are very alike. With the red being a live feed & in English only, the blue & green being recorded in various languages.
The first evening, we happened to get on a red tour with live feed, it was a little hard to hear the chap at time as there were other people running around the bus so the chap had to shout to be heard over them. You couldn’t hear him through he earphones which was a pity, the chap himself was a little snappy with people & rather insulting at times, at one stage I was showing my nieces something out the left window as while the tour guide was showing people something out the right window, he called out over his microphone at me, “No, no, miss your other right ” & then proceeded to say, “It amazes me how many people don’t know their left from their right” I approached him afterward to tell him how he had insulted me, he said he was too busy & take it up with head office !.
Other than him, all the other people we came across were very nice, the bus drivers were very helpful with their directions if you wanted to see something that was not on the map.

With the two days for price of one day, we got a great deal on this hop on, hop off bus. We did both the live person tour guide and the recorded (in eight languages) bus -- both were excellent. The bus stopped running rather early (4:30p) and we got stuck and had to cab back to the hotel.

We have just come back from london for 2 days and we went on the Big Bus Tour as part of the groupon ad
and what a great time we had...The tours,drivers,guides,staff where all Very Good and we will be back again..THANK YOU FOR A GREAT TOUR OF LONDON.

We went on 3 buses in total, 2 blue tours which were accompanied by an informative and entertaining pre-recorded audio, and a red tour with a live guide. We were able to 'hop on - hop off' as often as we wanted and all drivers, guides and staff we spoke to were very friendly and helpful.
The live guide spoke to all passengers individually to find out where we wanted to go, and then gave individual tips on the best places to walk around, different routes, and which stops to get on or off.
There were also additional options of a river boat cruise and 3 guided walking tours which were included in the price.
This tour is an excellent way to make sure that you don't miss any of the sights. You should plan to spend the whole day exploring London.

not long back from a weekend in london while there we decided to go on a bus tour which seemed the best option for seeing all the famous landmarks. we decided to go on the big bus tour they are the maroon coloured buses this turned out to be a great choice the tour guide was fantastic his knowledge about the buildings and their history was fantastic i think his name was tommy ? anyway he was fantastic we could not have made a better choice i would recommend this tour to anyone visiting london. the cost was £27 e4ach but you got discount vouchers for other london attractions.almost forgot ticket includes thames cruise.

I thought the Big Bus tour was great. The tickets were good for 48 hours, and included a free river cruise, map, and audio tour. The buses are hop-on-hop-off, so it's easy to see the sights up close as well. If you go on a rainy day they give out free rain ponchos. I was able to get some excellent photos of London from the upper deck of the bus. However, my one complaint was that the advertised discount for Mme. Tussaud's could not be obtained at the Mme. Tussaud's stop, only at all other stops (and there is no warning about this in any of the pamphlets or their web site). So, we had to choose whether to lose time going to the next bus stop to get the discount for Mme. Tussaud's, or save time and forfeit the discount. (Thought that seemed like a bit of a bait-and-switch).

The bus tour was great and very informative. There were stops all over London. The narration on the bus was filled with interesting city facts. The price was very cheap which included two days unlimited. The best part was the free Harry Potter waking tour. I did not get the guides name but I have never had a guide that was so animated and truly loved his job. By far a great person who has a passion like myself and other "nerds" who love the Potter movies. I would do this tour every time I am in London. Thank you for a great visit to London.

I went on a tour of London last month with my friend Christine. It was our first trip to London and wow - what a way to see it! So many things to see and wouldn't have been able to do this otherwise, in such a short space of time (we were only in London for a week).

It was such a cold day but the knowledge and humour of our tour guide Charlie warmed us up! She really knew a lot and was always making us laugh with lots of funny jokes and stories from around the city. It would've been great anyway but she really made the trip even better. Credit to her and Big Bus for helping show off what a great city London is!

Brilliant - thought we were mad agreeing to sightseeing tour of London from the top of an open bus on the coldest weekend in Jan, but WOW! the tour guides was fab. We saw all the sights we wanted with the added advantage of being able to come and go as we pleased. Would have taken more pictures had my hands not been so cold. The blue line was conducted with headphones in many languages, and the red line with engligh speaking guide. We were not the only fools sat on the top deck, we were joined by funny aussies and americans. The guide and ourselves made it a memorable experience. £27 for 24 hours sightseeing which included a thames book trip and gas lamp ghost walk in the evening. All the big bus tour staff were amazing. Can not wait to go again, perhaps when warmer! Do it, it is great!!!

Either one is good. The audio has a running commentary in multiple languages. The Live tour has commentators that you can query about different aspects. Either way, it is worth it to book through your hotel and use the hop-on/hop-off feature

We bought tickets before we went and they were £5 cheaper at £22 each, in winter you get 2 days for the price of 1, went Friday evening, used THE BIG BUS on and off all day Saturday and Sunday, feel we saw everything, the red bus was by far the most entertaining with well informed, witty, english speaking tour guides, also the ticket sellers at the stops know everything and anything about prices, times and opinions of attractions

We took the bus tour the first day in London, and it was a great way to get oriented to the city. We stopped three times - once to get tickets for Buckingham the next day, once at the Tower of London, and then at the Globe theater. We had a live guide each time, which was quite helpful. If you want to really see, you have to sit on top - which meant, in our case, sitting in a light rain part of the time. So, be prepared with a jacket and umbrella.

What a superb way to spend your day soaking up the history of London with a knowledgeable tour guide with a fantastic sense of humour. As a londoner I hadnt quite appreciated the glorious history and buildings we have and what better a way than to be able to pick your route ,listen intently to the stories myths and legends and hop on and off at your leisure

If you just want to see the major sights of London and only have a day to do it, than the Big Bus is a great way to do it. The only thing preventing me from giving them 5 stars was that the buses were a bit packed at times, but that might have been the fact that we were there on December 24th. Definitely worth the price you pay for the tickets.

I spent one day in London trying to visit as many of the major sites as I could in a short period of time. You can certainly walk London, but as a pregnant business traveler with serious jet lag I knew I would need some respite - especially in the chill of January.

The Big Bus Company has a very comprehensive list of stops and they provide good maps both online and in the bus. Some of the buses had actual tour guides others had just the taped audio available. I found both the live and taped tour information to be very informative and interesting.

During the winter months I was able to get two days for the price of one, which allowed me to take a night tour of London after returning from a meeting. I think the cost is worth having the ability to see more of London in my short visit.

Comfortable buses, friendly staff, excellent tour guides, safe stops, i enjoyed the tours a lot and take lots of wonderful pictures of London. I may say that you have to wait longer than the original London tour buses even thou The Big Bus had staff members guiding, talking and helping you very kindly while you wait. Very important feature if you are alone or traveling with kids or young girls.

This tour is by audio guide (controlled by the driver) or live guide. We hopped-on/off a dozen or more buses over two days and only had one good live guide. The audio guides were NOT turned on very often and instead we had random music to listen to instead of history. When the audio guide was on, it was not very detailed. It would, for example, tell us the statute to our right was ____, but it would not tell us that person was, why he is famous, etc. One guide was funny, but not super historical. There are free tours with the purchase, but they all ended at 4:30, so you don't really have time to take advantage of them. The route itself was good and enabled us to see a lot in a two-day period.

A great way to see London and get an introduction to the different areas of the capital, the big bus tour took us around choice sights with an informative and amusing commentary. I’ve lived in the city for 8 years, but we took guests on the tour and everyone learnt something. Our guests found it incredibly interesting and got a history of places that I don’t look twice at everyday whilst commuting through. It really brings a richness to the city. The river boat tour included with the ticket was a great end, again with a very humorous commentary from a very cockney Thames waterman. Do the red line first as there is live commentary, and if you’ve started early enough (pre10.30) take the other lines. We stayed on the bus from Victoria until London Bridge – on a Saturday Borough market (7 mins walk from stop 19, ask the guy at the stop) is the perfect place to get off and have lunch/afternoon snack from the stalls, before jumping back on and doing the river boat. We bought the tickets on Groupon, but the internet prices are a must – considerably cheaper. We went very much off season and the buses were full, I imagine any busier and they would be rammed – for that reason and the cost of tickets, the tour gets only 3 stars.

I was in London for just a long weekend, so liked the idea of a bus tour to get an overview of the city and to pick out places to see the next and final day I was there. This was great, the commentary at places was excellent, you drive past all the famous places and get information about them at the same time. I started the tour on a bus with a real guide, he was great - then when I resumed it later on a new bus there was an audio tour only. Both were good, it was nice to get the jokes and fun from the real tour guide though. I'd recommend doing this tour starting early in the day, so you've got time to get off if you want, wait for another bus to come around etc. The cruise on the river included in the tour price was fantastic as well.

This is my third trip to London and still believe The Big Bus Company is a very nice indoctrination for both first time and return visitors. You can sit on the bus, become acquainted with the city geography and get on or off if you want to visit particular stops, but I usually use it the first day to adjust from the jet lag and time differences.

As noted by others, during off season you get a two days for the price of one and if you know which day you will start the tour, consider the online option for even greater savings. The nice thing is that you get 48 hours when you decide to jump on the bus, so if you dont start until noon on Monday you have until noon Wednesday during the off season.

I can't comment on the free walking tours offered by The Big Bus Company, but the river tour each of the three times over the years is a nice additon. It's about half an hour and the commentators each time were enjoyable.

The live commentaors as suggested by the others are hit or miss and only the buses on the red line include live commentary. Some are very engaging and knowledgable while others just recite the bare minimum that you can hear on the recorded blue line commentary. Overall at 17 BPS, its a good price for the online option. If its not too cold during off season, try to sit on the top deck toward the front, which is covered. You can definitely see more. You miss out by sitting on the lower main level.

I had obtained a cheaper ticket via Groupon and had to go to the shop to redeem and to purchase a ticket for my God Daughter. The lady in the shop was very helpful and explained what happens and the time scales. we went to the designated bus stop and were asked by a very nice guy if we needed the english only or the mixed language bus as we are english we took the red logo bus and alighted on its arrival. the guide we had was a young lady called Samantha which was on for a couple of stops then she passed over to another guide called Dave he was good in his information we disembarked at Trafalgar Square to see the site and take a few pictures, we alighted another bus to find Samantha the guide on duty, what a wonderful experience on the rest of the tour with her she had the people on the bus interacting with her and was very informative without being boring by adding her personallity to the tour, she was even helpful to us as we wished to visit Buckingham Palace before returning to Kings Cross for the train home giving us time scales and the best way to get there from the Palace. Many thanks to her and I believe she was working her last day, whatever she goes onto do we wish her the best of luck, she was a good ambassador for the company. I would highly recommend the big bus tour as apposed to the London tour as it seemed to attract more travellers which to me says something. Tickets can either be bought at the shop or on route and includes a river cruise as well which we would loved to have done but didnt have the time. Great photo opportunity along the way and if you do the tour and decide which places you want to go back to it is a good way of deciding which you want to spend more time at. there are plastic ponchos given out if the weather turns a little bad, please be aware if you go to the upper deck there are limited numbers of seats under cover so don't complain

We paid around £17 for the tour by booking online and because its out of season we got two days for the price of one.

We found the staff almost universally freindly and helpful.

We enjoyed the tour, the live commentary was a bit hit or miss depending on the commentator with a couple of very knowledgeable guides and a couple who got their facts a bit wrong but it all added to to the fun.

But the best bit of the tour for us was the included river cruise with off the cuff comments from one of the boats licensed watermen. - It was stonking good fun. We cruised from the London Eye out to Greenwich (Value £13) and then came back into town on the DLR (Using our Oyster Cards) We picked up the tour at the Tower of London.

The tour is great for seeing bits of London, but does not by any means go to all the tourist hotspots. It is not very suitable (despite what the guides say) for going from one bit of London or attraction to another unless they are en route as it can take an age to get from one site to another because of London traffic and the Circuitous route that the bus takes. You need to check the map carefully as the bus routes cross over and interchange at various points.

If you want to go from a specific A to a specific B - Use the tube it will be far quicker

The bus tour makes a good destination in itself and hopping off for a quick cuppa or to take a few snaps is fine but using it to do London is self defeating because of the journey times

Their are several walking tours that are free - we did not take any of these.

Dubai is fairly spread out so this Big Bus Tour (with two separate routes) was a nice way to get an overview of the city. The blue route is the long route and stops at some of the most famous landmarks (Burj Al Arab, Burj Khalifa, Mall of the Emirates).

I would recommend buying the two day ticket because you really can't use both routes on the same day and actually get off and explore.

There were staff people at each stop so that it makes it easy to start at any point on the tour. The staff were very helpful and booked a tour of Burj Khalifa (the tallest building) so that we would save 300 AED (it costs 400 AED without a reservation).

The recorded commentary was informative.

They provide nice new headsets - you don't have to worry about having to use a "used" headset.

Good value for the money.
I saw everything I wanted to see and hopped on off at the places when i wanted! best service you can have in london

I had really only one full day in London and I had quite the list of things I wanted to see. The Big Bus Company let me see all the really touristy things you want to see when you go to London. The only con is I didn't get to really explore the sights. I was afraid that if I got off the bus I'd get lost and not be able to see the rest of the things I wanted to see but, its more of a self-doubt thing rather than the company's fault.
The ticket issuer was easy to see with his distinctive uniform, he was extremely helpful and easy to chat with. There were Big Bus stops all over London and the buses were easy to identify as well. The top of the bus was also open, which made for awesome pictures and uninterrupted views. There was also a choice between buses. There was the blue bus, which you plugged in earphones and listened to what you were seeing. They had 8 different languages to choose from. Then the red bus which had a live person explaining the sights, this was only in english.

Even though I had been to London many times, I did this tour with my elderly parents who were in the city for the first time. The staff who sell the tickets and work "on the ground" at the stops were all extremely nice and funny and always joking with us. The audio tour (on the Blue tours) was surprisingly decent, if not just a bit off in the timing. The live tour (Red tours) were somewhat disappointing. We hopped on three different Reds and so had three different guides who were all VERY different. One woman only pointed out shopping and celebrity joints, one guy kept talking about how government was interfering with everything, and other spoke so fast it was difficult to understand him. The best guide we had was actually the guy on the Thames River Cruise (included free with your ticket), and he wasn't even a proper tour guide!

Otherwise, the bus stops are convenient and take you to more or less every neighborhood in Zone 1. We never waited for more than about 10 minutes for our desired bus, which were always clean and had plenty of available seats both on the upper and lower levels. Also convenient was that our tickets were good for 48 hours, which I believe is only on offer during the winter months.

Excellent value with the 48 hour special. We used the tour to get our bearing on London. Took the Thames boat tour and two walking tours. Super. Walking tours recommended: Changing of the Guard and Harry Potter. Our guide Kevin was interesting, funny and we were lucky to have him on both tours. If this is your first trip to London, you should take a day to see the city with the bus and take a walking tour or two. Worth the price of admission.

The Big Bus Company runs a variety of tours in London. You pay for the day and can go on any tour at any stop whenever you want. Stay for a while at an attraction and then get back on and pick up where you left off. Great if you like to explore at your own pace. They also offer a number of fantastic guided tours with knowledgeable guides who give you an in depth look at the various attractions. I highly recommend you take a day on the Big Bus to see London. It's a bargain for all that they offer.

What a fantastic weekend and this was all down to the amazing staff at Big Bus Company. Staff of all ages, Bus Drivers, Attendants, Captains etc were all full of the most amazing knowledge and very amusing quips...... They alway made you feel a priority and always went that extra mile. Thank You so much Big Bus Company you should be very proud.
If you want to realx, take in the sites of London, learn the most interesting facts, cruise down the Thames on a river boat, completely stress free, then this company is without doubt the BEST company to be with.........

I absolutely enjoyed the Big Bus tour company in London. On several occasions, I needed to know what bus to take and where to get off for a particular attraction. The guide I talked to took me almost by the hand and as she was going to many of the same places told me exactly where to disembark for my destination. Thoroughly enjoyed the guides and their personalities.
great way to see london, you can hop on and off to see london
We used the Big Bus tours, as we only had a day and a half to see everything. Very handy as can hop on and off. Also the tour guides were very entertaining.

I really enjoyed the tour, I was a little lost finding the first bus stop near Victoria Station but once I found it the rest of the tour was a breeze. As you could listen to the tour (blue route) yourself, it was a great way to see the sights comfortably and enjoy the tour. I got off at Notting Hill, and when I returned I think I only waited 3mins for the next bus. The rest of the tour was with a tour guide who was fantastic and entertaining. I would highly recommend this to tourists who want to see the main sites of London. I also took up the cruise option which was a great way to see the sites too. When I have more time in London I will definately be using Big Bus' services again.

We bought a 2 day pass for £5 more than a 24 hour pass. Well worth the money to save our legs and hear about London's sights. Interesting to hear the different spin on sites from the different guides.
You can buy the passes at almost any Big Bus Stop; just look for an employee and they'll get you set up.
Also get discounts to attractions; can buy from the employee at the stops. Free walking tours are also included.
The buses are clean and comfortable. Go to the top for the best views.

Went to London for 10 year old daughters Birthday - Stayed in Weybridge and caught the Train into Waterloo - Thought we would do the Hop on Hop off bus - to save her legs and our ears - Bought train tickets with tube tickets inluded just in case - Arrived in Waterloo walked to London Eye and found the bus stop - This bus had a guide whom was very informative - Got off an Buckingham Palace - to see the Queen or 300 foreign tourists - there was also a half marathon going on just to confuse - We walked to Trafalgar Square to catch the bus again - We had E tickets which they validated and we got a free Thames boat trip - This was the problem with the bus it followed a single sort of route so unless you wanted to follow that route it didn`t quite work

The Big Bus Tour of London was good value for the money. Staff was very helpful. Buy the two day ticket for the best value and take the river tour that's included for free, which is the best way to see the London Bridge. Sit on top and enjoy the sunshine and the sites. One of the best ways to really see London and take advantage of all the shopping opportunities.

My son (23 yr) and I were in London in July; our first visit. We were only there a few
days so we decided to take the Hop on Hop off bus tour ... it was the perfect ... it was a guided tour - either in English with a live tour guid or in multiple languages using ear phones. The tour guides were very knowledgeable and lots of fun ... they interacted with the people on the bus ... they stopped at all the major sites ... if you wanted to get off ... you could get off or continue to an attraction that suited your fancy! For five pound more, you could use the bus the next day with was perfect for us. It is an awsome way to see London. I would definitely recommend this Bus Tour

We took the "blue line" of the Big Bus tour, which offers recorded commentary in a variety of languages (as opposed to live narration on the red line). The commentary was fine, and the route does cover a lot of ground. Our only complaint was long waits (up to 20 minutes) at bus stops while people bought tickets and loaded on. This was especially frustrating as several empty buses were parked near us but the company tries to fill one bus before letting people on another. I guess that makes sense from a business standpoint but for customers alreaddy on the bus, it meant a lot of idle time not spent sightseeing. We finally got off after the bus circled Marble Arch and the Wellington Memorial FOUR TIMES in about 45 minutes - and we saw very little inbetween. Understand that street closings and reroutes are not the company's fault, but this trip got a little stale after a while. We did not do any of the free walking tours or other incentives, so I can't speak to those.

Arrived in London on the Thursday afternoon, one of the pick up points on the green route was right outside our Hotel (Royal National). Spoke to the conductor and the bus driver who explained prices and asked us where we wanted to visit and explained what routes and stops we would get off at, both were very pleasant. We booked with them the next day, thoroughly enjoyed the live commentary, sat up top on the bus which was great and enjoyed hearing all about London, we hopped on and off the bus and experienced 3 different commentators, who were all great. We also went on the free boat cruise which you get when buying your bus tickets, which was also brilliant. When we arrived back at one of the stops to get our bus home on the green route we realised we had missed the last bus, after a few minutes a Big Bus came round the corner and the driver realised that we were still waiting for a bus, he pulled in and told us how we would get home using the underground. He then Very kindly took us back to our hotel even though his bus was not in service (Saidu is his name). We then saw him the next day and he even remembered us!!!! We also got chatting to a conductor at the Buckingham Palace stop who was also very pleasant and polite. Overall all the staff we spoke to couldn't have been more helpful or pleasant. I would definitely recommend using The Big Bus Coampany, you wont be disappointed. Great value for money.

The best way to see London, this 24 hour ticket allows you to hop on and hop off. The Live commentry by the friendly tour guides gives interesting facts with added humour. Just sit back with camera at the ready...brilliant.

If you have no idea what you want to see, Big Bus Tours will take you past all the major sitesand explain why you might want to see them. They also include free walking tours, such as The Harry Potter tour and the Gaslight Ghost Pub tour. The first of these was a huge disappointment, but the Ghost Pub tour is highly recommended. If you rely on these buses to get you to a certain attraction at a certain time though, you are likely to miss out. London traffic varies from hellish to gridlocked. It takes on average one hour to do 8 - 10 stops and there are over 35 on the whole route. If you know where you want to go already, catch the underground or local buses which are faster and cheaper. Big Bus also offer a second day option that you can only purchase on board which is worth doing if you want to do the walking tours and free Thames boat trip. You just cannot physically do those and do a full lap of London in the bus in a single day.

My 8 year old and I had such a great time on this bus . We choose to do this on our last day just to see what we had missed, It was so much fun to listen to the experienced guide. He was funny sweet and entertaining, We did the hop on hop off thing at many of the stops. It was great because my son loved the double decker buses and I loved the fact that it was a such a beautiful summer day and I could just relax and enjoy London with out walking or having to take the crowded tube. I highly recommend The Big Bus Company worth every pound!

Did the obligatory double-decker bus tour. Driver and guide were friendly. Guides were funny to begin with, with the accent, when they toss in a few jokes, it is hilarious. Like the hop on hop off, two day option and a Thames cruise tossed in for free. Would recommend for your first day so you know where everything is. We brought our own pancho, but apparently they give you one too as you know it will rain in London.

weather was awful but big bus tours made the day a fantastic experience nonetheless,the staff were very friendly and informative and i cant wait to do it again hopefully on a sunnier day,highly recommended
A great way to enjoy a day in London is with the Big Bus Tours. I had a tour guide that was very engaging and made the day that much more enjoyable.

In a word-FANTASTIC!! Our tour guide was hilarious and so knowledgeable about London!! We had a wonderful time and I didn't want to get off the bus! We had absolutely no issues and I highly recomnend this tour.
